# Progress toward finitely many exceptional filling assignments

Research record, updated 25 November 2026. The target is unchanged: for every
fixed tangle template in the stated strict Conway class, all but finitely many assignments
that produce hyperbolic knots should satisfy Kashaev's original volume
identity. This statement has not been proved. The manuscripts remain
frozen; the results below belong to the separate research notes.

The research priority is now the general theorem for fixed short partial
fillings. Further estimates for individual words are paused. The
[finite-branching argument](research_finite_exceptions_under_partial_fillings.md#3-a-finite-exception-lemma-for-one-template)
already explains how such a theorem would give finitely many exceptional
assignments: at every stage, fix any remaining bounded coefficient and
apply the theorem to the remaining long coefficients. The threshold may
depend on every coefficient fixed earlier.

The [definition note](research_strict_conway_family_definitions.md)
now spells out the literal construction, strict wire inequalities,
primitive crossing-circle slopes, knot-component test and order of
quantifiers without using “admissible” as an unexplained extra condition.
Its four-leaf example has strict state \(a_i=3/10\), two retained
outputs \(1/2\), and knot-producing pattern \((0,1,1,1)\).
The current frozen volume statement is the pure-source theorem in
the Conway asymptotics main file, not a restriction to the older
completed-root signed packet. This is exposition of the existing
statements, not a new volume proof. The final
\(\texttt{55662159ccd65ae3183bc55b4f17b414d15a18b6970e3d54a725ba16247eeb1a}\)
and all five complete direct files were read by author, independent
peer and root; their used definitions and reported statements were
checked and all six pins renewed and matched. This does not constitute
a fresh audit of the imported manuscript proofs.

There is an important qualification about the strength of this target.
For the enlarged strict grammar in the
[padding proposition](research_finite_exceptions_under_partial_fillings.md#8-a-consequence-of-counting-assignments-strict-padding),
finitely many exceptional assignments for every template would already
prove the volume identity for every hyperbolic strict core. A zero leaf
can turn a remaining twist into removable curls. The exact source
identity is
\[
 \phi_N[h(0)R^aTQ]
 =\phi_N[e_D R^aTQ]
 =(R^aTQ)(c_0)
 =\kappa_N^a\phi_N(Q),\qquad |\kappa_N|=1.
\]
Here \(h(0)=T1=e_D\), and \(e_D\) reproduces evaluation at \(c_0\)
under the original trace. Thus an arbitrarily long remaining twist
need not create any new analytic suppression: in this allowed
configuration its prescribed observation is exactly the unresolved
core scalar, up to a unit. Exact cap reductions must be made before
assuming a positive geometric saddle for an intermediate exterior.
This does not change the requested target or discard such assignments.

The current route combines the exact matrix presentation in
rivin-jones with Casson--Rivin angle-volume optimization. The
comparison must retain the original phases and closing functional.
An absolute-value maximum alone does not establish a lower bound.

## A filled cover cannot make its short meridian geometrically long, 25 November

The proposed cover shortcut has a necessary filling-compatibility condition.
It prevents using an unbranched cover to turn a fixed short filling into
a long one while retaining multiplication of the completed hyperbolic
volume by the covering degree. This is a check on that route, not a
quantum descent statement or a restriction of the finite-exception target.

Let \(X\) be a complete hyperbolic drilled exterior, and let \(Y=X(s)\)
denote some prescribed fillings along primitive slopes \(s_i\). Suppose
\(p:Y'\to Y\) is a finite unbranched cover of degree \(D\).
Drill every preimage of each filling core to obtain \(X'\to X\).
Equip \(X'\) with the pullback of the complete drilled metric on \(X\).
For a horotorus \(T_i\), let \(T'_{ij}\to T_i\) have degree \(d_{ij}\),
and define normalized slope length by
\[
 \mathcal L_T(s)=\frac{\operatorname{length}_T(s)}
                         {\sqrt{\operatorname{area}(T)}}.
\]
Changing the size of the horotorus does not change this ratio.

The primitive filling meridian \(s'_{ij}\) upstairs maps to
\(\pm s_i\), rather than to a higher multiple. Indeed each component
of the inverse image of the filled solid torus is an unbranched solid-
torus cover. A meridian disk downstairs lifts to disks mapped
homeomorphically to it, since the disk is simply connected. Their
boundaries are the primitive upstairs meridians. Equivalently, the
boundary subgroup contains \(s_i\), the kernel of the map from the
boundary fundamental group to that of the solid torus.

The lifted flat metric gives
\[
 \operatorname{area}(T'_{ij})=d_{ij}\operatorname{area}(T_i),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{length}(s'_{ij})=\operatorname{length}(s_i),
 \qquad
 \boxed{\mathcal L(s'_{ij})=\mathcal L(s_i)/\sqrt{d_{ij}}.}
\]
In particular the normalized length does not increase. If all the
preimage filling cores are retained, \(\sum_jd_{ij}=D\) for each \(i\).
For the simultaneous parameter
\(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}^{-2}=\sum_i\mathcal L(s_i)^{-2}\), this gives
\[
                 \mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}(X')
                      =\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tot}}(X)/\sqrt D.
\]

A cover of the unfilled exterior can instead have primitive lifted
slope mapping to \(ks_i\), \(k>1\). Its normalized length is
\(k\mathcal L(s_i)/\sqrt{d_{ij}}\), but that filling map cannot extend
unbranched across the core: its meridian has degree \(k\). A branched
completion does not supply the unbranched completed-volume law used by
the proposed descent. This distinction does not rule out a different
drilling construction or a separately proved branched quantum identity.

The [earlier cover analysis](regge_period_covers_and_a_curves.md) gives
peripheral isogenies, the marked regulator degree and quantum parameter
changes. It does not impose the filled-meridian condition above.
The proof here is disk lifting and flat area scaling; no invariant
identity is imported. The original source lower bound remains unproved.

## Finite coefficient projections preserve the cyclic norm, 24 November

The [Hardy norm comparison](research_cyclic_atom_hardy_head_comparison.md)
shows that the actual finite coefficients retain the exponential norm
of each cyclic function. This is a positive consequence of using the
orthogonal coefficient projection. It concerns the scalar functions;
the subsequent gluing and original marked closing remain to be estimated.

Let \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\),
\(F_a=\prod_{h=1}^a(1-Q^h)\), and \(F_0=1\). For the original
cyclic functions \(V_N,U_N=V_N^{-1}\) defined in the next section,
their projections to Taylor degrees below \(N\) are exactly
\[
 p_N^U(z)=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}\frac{z^a}{F_a},\qquad
 p_N^V(z)=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}
       \frac{(-1)^aQ^{a(a-1)/2}z^a}{F_a}.
\]
With \(\|\sum a_jz^j\|_{H^2}^2=\sum|a_j|^2\), there is a
universal \(C\) such that for every \(N\ge2\), every
\(0\le r\le1\), and either pair
\((A_N,p_N)=(U_N,p_N^U)\) or \((V_N,p_N^V)\),
\[
 \|p_N(r\,\cdot)\|_{H^2}
 \le\|A_N(r\,\cdot)\|_{H^2}
 \le N^C\|p_N(r\,\cdot)\|_{H^2}.
\]
At radius one each of these four norms satisfies
\(\log\|\cdot\|=Nv_3/(2\pi)+O(\log N)\), where \(v_3\)
is the regular ideal-tetrahedron volume. The radius may depend
arbitrarily on the level in the comparison; the stated rate is at
radius one.

The proof integrates the precise root exponents from the near-circle
estimate. Their endpoint contributions sum to only \(O(\log N)\).
One actual coefficient with \(a\) nearest \(N/6\) gives the matching
exponential lower bound for the projected norm. Finally the tail
starts in degree \(N\), whereas the retained part ends in degree
\(N-1\); shrinking the radius can only improve the squared norm ratio.
The same comparison applies to the reflected factorial function
\(Nz^{N-1}V_N(Q/z)\) on every circle of radius at least one, with
the original factor \(N\) and all coefficient phases retained.

This removes an exponential loss from passing between each full scalar
symbol and its physical finite coefficient vector. It does not give
a lower bound after coherent gluing, bound multiplication on arbitrary
Hardy inputs, or show that the geometric contribution survives the
original closing. The fixed-degree source formulations and the
finite-exception target are unchanged.

## Uniform estimates through the cyclic root divisors, 24 November

The [near-circle estimate](research_cyclic_atom_near_unit_circle.md)
extends control of the actual cyclic functions to arguments approaching
the unit circle and its level-dependent roots. The earlier disk
expansions alone did not give a uniform error there. The new estimate
retains the precise fractional zero or pole at each root.

Put \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), \(\zeta_j=Q^{-j}\),
\(\beta_j=(N-1-2j)/(2N)\), and
\(\delta=\operatorname{dist}(t,\{\zeta_j\})\). The original atom is
\[
 V_N(t)=\frac{(1-t^N)^{(N-1)/(2N)}}
 {\prod_{j=1}^{N-1}(1-Q^jt)^{j/N}},\qquad U_N=V_N^{-1}.
\]
Define its continuous rate by
\[
 F(t)=\begin{cases}
 \operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(t)/(2\pi),&0<|t|\le1,\\
 -\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(1/t)/(2\pi),&|t|>1.
 \end{cases}
\]
For every fixed annulus \(R^{-1}\le|t|\le R\), uniformly in
the level and argument away from the roots,
\[
 \log|V_N(t)|=NF(t)+
 \begin{cases}
 \beta_j\log(N|t-\zeta_j|),&|t-\zeta_j|<1/N,\\
 0,&\delta\ge1/N
 \end{cases}
 +O_R(\log N).
\]
The root in the first case is unique. Both signs on the right are
reversed for \(\log|U_N|\). In particular polynomial separation
\(\delta\ge N^{-A}\) gives the simpler error \(O_{A,R}(\log N)\).
For closer approaches the displayed root factor remains essential;
the assertion allows even superexponentially small distances.

There is an exact regular value as well. After removing only that
root factor, \(W_{N,j}(t)=V_N(t)(1-Q^jt)^{-\beta_j}\) is a holomorphic
unit on \(|t-\zeta_j|<1/N\), with
\[
 |W_{N,j}(\zeta_j)|=|(Q;Q)_j|\,N^{-(j+1/2)/N}.
\]
The proof combines a weighted logarithmic Riemann sum, including its
singular mesh cells, with the actual root exponents and a uniform
logarithmic-derivative bound for \(W_{N,j}\). It is a written
all-level proof, with no numerical assumptions on the argument.

The two chamber rates, resonant values and sharp per-atom constant
\(v_3/(2\pi)\) already occur in the earlier sources. The improvement
is the uniform error near and throughout the root neighborhoods.
It does not reduce the number of atoms in an original word, remove
matrix source flags, or replace the endpoint integrations. These are
estimates for the same scalar functions with their original norm
factor, not a lower bound for their coherent contraction. The selected
geometric cycle and the finite-exception theorem remain unproved.

## What the fixed-degree formulation has already simplified, 24 November

This is a coverage audit of the existing reductions, prompted by the
question whether further simplifications follow from the quartic minimum.
It does not announce another reduction or a new volume theorem.

The [linear-elimination proof](research_conway_orthogonal_linear_elimination.md)
removes all affine packet variables after one child of each binary gate
is retained. Their unconstrained least-squares solution lies strictly
inside the original packet balls. The exact reduced objective is
\[
 f(u)=\|\Pi(u)b(u)\|^2,
 \qquad
 \Pi=I-A(A^*A)^{-1}A^*.
\]
The original closing row is a component of this residual space.
The alternative boundary Gram has spectrum in \([1,226/225]\),
uniformly in the quantum level. Thus this particular Gram can be
compared with the identity with a proved constant loss; arbitrary
quantum channel metrics cannot be discarded on that basis.

The [branching reduction](research_conway_branching_quartic_source.md)
does better when prescribed leaf inputs and linear corridors are
contracted first. Suppose \(q\) product gates still have two unresolved
inputs. Keeping their \(2q\) input packets makes every other unknown
enter with constant linear coefficients. Exact elimination then leaves
a quartic objective on \(4Nq\) real coordinates, with Hessian between
\(I\) and \(3I\). With \(q=0\) no outer minimization remains.
The constant projection and its coherent coefficients are retained;
linearizing a product by inserting an unknown true child is not allowed.

There is also a proved formulation with no optimization at all. The
[positive matrix recursion](research_orthogonal_error_positive_conway_recursion.md)
propagates full covariance matrices through the original normalized
maps and their adjoints, with an explicitly prescribed small positive
error at each vertex. Its final scalar \(P_N\), with the original
closing row and all budgets restored, satisfies
\[
 1+|K_N|^2\le P_N\le1+|K_N|^2+1/128.
\]
This is a positive matrix construction, not an entrywise absolute-value
state sum. Its off-diagonal coefficients retain the original phases.
For a positive candidate volume \(V\),
\[
 \frac{\pi}{N}\log P_N\longrightarrow V
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|\longrightarrow V.
\]
The error scale can be exponentially small before budgets are restored;
bounded additive error is not permission to use fixed numerical precision.

The current [unitary source chart](research_true_cup_quantum_flag_source.md)
identifies the original closing with one precise cyclic coefficient.
A unitary change of coordinates is not, by itself, an elimination of
an unresolved binary gate. The auxiliary objective's degree four must not
be confused with bounded physical meridian degree; the selected clock
exponents still grow with \(N\).

The useful remaining task is therefore a geometric lower estimate for
the actual compressed source or the full positive matrix recursion,
after every required fixed short partial filling. No such estimate was
obtained in this audit. Further basis changes, exact semidefinite
reformulations and deletion of a direction seen as invisible only by
the final scalar row do not by themselves establish that estimate.
The finite-exception target and frozen manuscripts are unchanged.

## Positive matrix certificates retain a coherent alignment requirement, 24 November

This refines the earlier rank-one guard for the positive Conway recursion.
It applies to any positive matrix lower certificate, without ruling out
full-matrix methods or supplying a geometric lower bound.

Use the actual normalized compiler, its original closing row \(L\),
\(\sigma=1/16\), and unchanged total budget \(B_N\). The
[dimension-free covariance theorem](research_dimension_free_positive_conway_covariance.md)
gives, at every proper vertex and every \(0<\varepsilon\le1\),
\[
 S=a a^\dagger+V,\qquad
 \varepsilon I\preceq V\preceq2\varepsilon I.
 \tag{PC1}
\]
Here \(a\) is the true normalized packet. It is used in this proof,
not supplied as input to a certificate.

At the top let \(0\preceq Q\preceq S\) be any proposed matrix lower
certificate, and suppose \(c=LQL^\dagger>0\). Define
\[
 w=QL^\dagger/\sqrt c.
\]
The vector \(z=Q^{1/2}L^\dagger/\sqrt c\) has norm one, so
\[
 ww^\dagger=Q^{1/2}zz^\dagger Q^{1/2}\preceq Q,
 \qquad |Lw|^2=c.
 \tag{PC2}
\]
Thus extracting a coherent direction loses none of the certified root
observation. No invertibility of \(Q\) is required.

For \(a\ne0\), let \(P_{a^\perp}\) be orthogonal projection onto
its perpendicular complement. Compress (PC1),(PC2) to this subspace.
The operator norm, rather than the covariance trace, gives
\[
 \|P_{a^\perp}w\|^2\le2\varepsilon,\qquad
 \sin^2\angle(w,a)
 \le\frac{2\varepsilon\|L\|^2}{c}.
 \tag{PC3}
\]
Indeed \(\|w\|^2\ge c/\|L\|^2\). If \(a=0\), the same argument
gives \(c\le2\varepsilon\|L\|^2\), without defining an angle.

Calibrate \(\varepsilon=\theta/B_N^2\), \(0<\theta\le1\), and put
\(H_N=B_N^2c\). Then
\[
 \sin^2\angle(w,a)\le\frac{2\theta\|L\|^2}{H_N}.
 \tag{PC4}
\]
In particular a positive volume-rate lower observation,
\(\liminf \pi\log H_N/N\ge V_0>0\), forces
\(\limsup N^{-1}\log\sin\angle(w,a)\le-V_0/(2\pi)\).
The zero-angle case uses \(\log0=-\infty\). Thus polynomial angular
accuracy alone does not certify such a positive matrix lower bound.
The original recursion still gives its stated scalar certificate
\(|K_N|^2\ge\max(0,H_N-\theta/128)\); this argument constructs no
\(H_N\) at the required rate.

There is an exact check at every actual signed crossing leaf. Its
Newton coefficient packet is
\(R^{\pm1}_j=\kappa^{\pm1}(-q)^{\pm j}\), with norm \(\sqrt N\).
The original leaf budget is therefore \(16\sqrt N\), so
\[
 a_j=\kappa^{\pm1}(-q)^{\pm j}/(16\sqrt N),\qquad
 \|a\|^2=\sigma^2.
\]
Its message has eigenvalues \(\sigma^2+\varepsilon\) and
\(\varepsilon\) with multiplicity \(N-1\). For every coordinate \(j\),
\[
 \lambda e_je_j^\dagger\preceq S
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 0\le\lambda\le\lambda_*:=(e_j^\dagger S^{-1}e_j)^{-1}
 =\frac{\varepsilon}
 {1-\sigma^2/[N(\varepsilon+\sigma^2)]}
 \le\frac{N\varepsilon}{N-1}.
 \tag{PC5}
\]
The equivalence concerns nonnegative \(\lambda\).
This follows by conjugating the rank-one inequality by \(S^{-1/2}\)
and using the rank-one inverse formula. The same \(\lambda_*\) is
the scalar Schur complement after the other coordinates are removed.
It can be much smaller than the marginal
\(S_{jj}=\varepsilon+\sigma^2/N\). Thus positivity and a large signal
eigenvalue do not justify dropping the coherent complementary response.

The older ledger section already gave the rank-one domination formula
and explicitly left general full-matrix certificates available.
Equations (PC2)--(PC4) explain the necessary alignment of a direction
extracted from any such certificate; they do not show that constructing
it is impossible. Fixed short subtrees may still be contracted into
their actual leaf packets. The same original closing, budgets, phases
and full boundary directions remain. No arbitrary-short-filling lower
bound or finite-exception theorem follows from this audit.

## The original full source as a cyclic coefficient, 24 November

The [quantum flag source theorem](research_true_cup_quantum_flag_source.md)
uses the entire physical cup state. It gives polynomial difference
operators for all based quantum meridians at every width, and identifies
the original marked scalar as one specified cyclic Weyl coefficient.
The coordinate change is unitary. No conditional coideal mode replaces
the actual source.

Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(x=-q^{-1}\), and width \(2k\). Normalize the full cup by
\(\psi_0=\mathbf p^{\otimes k}/N^{3k/2}\). The exact Choi map
\(\mathscr C_k\) identifies the full physical space with
\(\operatorname{End}(V_N^{\otimes k})\), in normalized trace norm:
\[
 \mathscr C_k(I)=\psi_0,\qquad
 \langle\mathscr C_k(X),\mathscr C_k(Y)\rangle
       =\tau_k(X^\dagger Y),\qquad \tau_k=N^{-k}\operatorname{Tr}.
 \tag{TF1}
\]
In each matrix factor use the actual cyclic clock and shift
\(v e_a=Q^{-a}e_a\), \(T e_a=e_{a-1\ ({\rm mod}\ N)}\).
Then \(v^N=T^N=I\), \(Tv=Q^{-1}vT\), and
\[
 X_R=\mathscr C_k^{-1}R\psi_0
    =\sum_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}x_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}(R)
                         \prod_i v_i^{a_i}T_i^{b_i},\qquad
 \sum|x_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}(R)|^2=\|R\psi_0\|^2.
 \tag{TF2}
\]
This expansion is orthonormal for \(\tau_k\), with every index in
\(0,\ldots,d\). All coefficients are computed from the full actual
word and prescribed initial state, without its unknown closed value.

The correct finite quantum ordering is essential. With the actual
\(e=qE\), the original RLL meridian is
\[
 G=\begin{pmatrix}K&e\\FK&K^{-1}+Fe\end{pmatrix}
   =\begin{pmatrix}
   -q^{-1}v&q(Q^{-1}v-1)T\\
   q(1-v)T^{-1}&q(v-2)
   \end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{TF3}
\]
Its inverse is the existing bounded polynomial
\(G^{-1}=Q^{-1}(-2qI-G)\). The source theorem gives the exact
left module action of the second based meridian on every \(f(v)T^m\).
Its apparent negative powers cancel by polynomial divided differences.
The total Cartan and lowering of every preceding completed pair
preserve clock degree. Thus any ordered regular based-meridian word
of length \(L\), including inverse entries, has an unreduced polynomial
representative of total clock degree at most \(L\) on \(\psi_0\).
This holds at every width, before cyclic reduction.

For \(p=k-1\), the literal last-marked closing on total integer
degree \(kd\) gives the exact selected coefficient
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 K_N=\chi_N N^p x^{-dp}\,
              x_{(d,\ldots,d,0),\mathbf0}(R).
 \quad}                                                       \tag{TF4}
\]
The necessary degree condition holds for every original signed braid.
It cannot be dropped for arbitrary inserted operators. The proof keeps
all ordinary caps: their unitary clock insertion becomes
\(Q^{-p}v_1\cdots v_p\) under the Choi map. Consequently the
normalized trace selects exponent \(N-1\) in each ordinary-cap clock,
zero in the last clock, and zero shift exponents, all cyclically.
The prefactor is equivalently \(\chi_N x^{dp}N^pQ^{-p}\).
No peripheral, framing or external scalar is reset.

There is an exact degree selection rule. For a degree-preserving
sum \(W\) of regular words of length at most \(L\),
\[
 \ell_0Wu_0\ne0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
                     L\ge(k-1)(N-1).
 \tag{TF5}
\]
Every surviving polynomial term must supply at least \(N-1\) in
each of the first \(p\) clocks before cyclic reduction. A fixed braid
operator is not a bounded-degree regular meridian word. In particular,
the existing exact Hurwitz transport of regular observations does not
by itself evaluate (TF4).

The full positive cup has a separate holomorphic regular-boundary limit.
Writing
\[
 G_0(w)=\begin{pmatrix}0&-w^{-1}\\w&-2\end{pmatrix},\quad |w|=1,
\]
every fixed regular observation has, with error \(O(N^{-1})\), the
Haar integral over \(k\) inverse pairs
\((G_0(w_i),G_0(w_i)^{-1})\). This follows from the same polynomial
module by ordinary constant-term evaluation at clock zero.
It concerns the holomorphic regular algebra; it does not identify
the larger star-moment problem or remove (TF4)'s growing exponent.

The ordering audit ruled out using the apparent \(1/N\) clock leakage
of an unscaled Gauss lift as a canonical cap jet. In the original
\(e=qE\) meridian, (TF3)'s cancellation is exact. The surviving
root-of-unity coefficients must be retained instead. No failure note
or alteration of an earlier final was made for that audit.

The complete physical source and original observation are therefore
specified in one unitary coefficient chart. The unresolved general
estimate is the volume-rate asymptotic of its selected coefficient
after an arbitrary fixed short partial filling. No additional knot
volume theorem or finite-exception theorem is claimed.

The author, root and two independent peers read the complete final,
both complete proof inputs and the complete linked coverage text,
checked the used implications and renewed all four matching pins
after their reads.

## The complete crossing in Fourier coordinates, 24 November

The [full Fourier crossing theorem](research_coideal_full_fourier_crossing.md)
gives every entry of the actual reduced crossing between two unitary
Fourier bases. An existing full Toeplitz comparison then supplies all
neighboring heights and the entire deeper tail. This is an exact
operator formula with arbitrary coherent input, rather than propagation
of only the single initialized mode.

Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(\kappa=e^{i\pi d^2/(2N)}\). For a physical root
\(\nu=Q^r+qQ^{-r}\), define
\[
 t=-q^{2r-1},\quad \beta=t/q,\quad \gamma=t^{-1},\quad
 B=t^2/q,\quad v=Q^{-1},\quad
 V_j(a)=(\beta Q^{-j})^a,\quad Y_i(a)=\gamma^aQ^{ia}.
\]
Both normalized Fourier matrices
\(\mathcal V=N^{-1/2}(V_j)_j\) and
\(\mathcal Y=N^{-1/2}(Y_i)_i\) are unitary. The full
equal-neighbor graph crossing is
\[
 C_{\nu|\nu}=\kappa\mathcal Y T_B\mathcal V^\dagger,\qquad
 (T_B)_{ij}=
 \begin{cases}
 {j\brack i}_v B^iv^{i(i-1)}(Bv^i;v)_{j-i},&i\le j,\\
 0,&i>j.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{FC1}
\]
Here \((a;v)_m=\prod_{h=0}^{m-1}(1-av^h)\) and
\({j\brack i}_v=(v;v)_j/[(v;v)_i(v;v)_{j-i}]\).
All denominator indices are below \(N\). The proof uses the actual
finite continuant product, partial fractions and a finite Gaussian
Newton identity. It includes both parities, composite levels and
\(N=2\).

For arbitrary neighboring roots use the already established initialized
Toeplitz matrix \(A_{\nu,\sigma}=U_\nu U_\sigma^{-1}\). Then
\[
 C_{\nu|\sigma}=C_{\nu|\nu}A_{\nu,\sigma}.
 \tag{FC2}
\]
Writing \(A_{\nu,\sigma}=\sum_{m=0}^{d}\alpha_mZ^m\),
\(Ze_a=e_{a+1}\), \(Ze_d=0\), its complete recursion is
\[
 \alpha_0=1,\quad \alpha_{-1}=0,\qquad
 (1-Q^m)\alpha_m=(\nu Q^{m-1}-\sigma)\alpha_{m-1}
                    +q(Q^{m-2}-1)\alpha_{m-2}.
 \tag{FC3}
\]
For an entire deeper coideal \(S\), the same operator coefficients
give \(A_{\nu,S}\), without selecting one tail eigenvalue.
The actual full graph crossing and inverse are
\[
 C_\nu=(C_{\nu|\nu}\otimes I)A_{\nu,S},\qquad
 C_\nu^{-1}=A_{\nu,S}^{-1}(C_{\nu|\nu}^{-1}\otimes I).
 \tag{FC4}
\]
Thus both signs retain all multiplicity spaces. For any full input
\(z\), set \(\eta=(\mathcal V^\dagger\otimes I)A_{\nu,S}z\).
Its physical counting norm is exactly
\[
 \|C_\nu z\|^2=\sum_i\left\|\sum_{j\ge i}(T_B)_{ij}\eta_j\right\|^2.
 \tag{FC5}
\]
The coherent input sum remains inside each square. No orthogonality
of distinct deeper spectral projectors is assumed.

The original cup input also remains explicit. On one matched block,
with \(h_a=t^a\), the observed Fourier columns are
\(hC_{\nu|\nu}V_j/(N\kappa)=P_j=(B;Q^{-1})_j\). For the
actual graph endpoint \(e_d\), every Fourier channel is present and
\[
 P_N=2,\qquad \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}Q^{-j}P_j=B^d,\qquad
 hC_{\nu|\nu}e_d/(N\kappa)=t^d/N.
 \tag{FC6}
\]
The product endpoint \(P_N=2\) differs from the cyclic index value
\(P_0=1\). Retaining it recovers the exact original identity
\(C_\nu(e_d\otimes w)=\kappa(e_d\otimes w)\).

These full linear equations can be retained without increasing a
quartic energy's degree. The Toeplitz adapter is not assumed uniformly
conditioned, and the original full source, graph lift, last marked
closing and external scalar remain. No geometric lower bound for the
coherent closing follows from (FC5). The arbitrary-short-filling
finite-exception theorem is still open.

The complete final and all three selected complete inputs were read by
the author, root and two independent peers; their used implications
were checked and all four matching pins renewed after the reads.

## A movable marked observation and an analytic boundary response, 24 November

The [balanced marked-observation theorem](research_coideal_balanced_marked_height_observations.md)
allows both auxiliary boundary heights to be chosen, with a known
polynomial comparison to the same original scalar. At a matched choice
the selected boundary vectors are geometric progressions. Their response
to one scaled physical generator has a locally uniform analytic limit,
with a positive exponential density. This is boundary data; it does not
evaluate the global source minimum.

Use the physical conventions \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\),
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(x=-q^{-1}\), and width \(2k\).
Let \(\mathcal Qe_a=Q^ae_a\) be the physical clock and
\(m_r=m(\mathcal Q^r\otimes\mathcal Q^r)\), \(r\in\mathbb Z/N\).
The original cup source has integer degree \(kd\). After the unchanged
\(k-1\) ordinary caps, the final pair has degree \(d\). Thus
\[
 (\ell^{\otimes(k-1)}\otimes m_r)Ru_0=Q^{rd}Z_N(R),
 \qquad K_N=\chi_N Z_N(R).
 \tag{BM1}
\]
This equality retains the original last marked position. It is not an
equality of rows on the unrestricted physical space.

Write \(\mu_l=Q^l+qQ^{-l}\),
\(p_N(z)=\prod_l(z-\mu_l)\), and
\(A_\lambda=N^2q^dx^{-d}/p_N'(\lambda)\).
The charged diagonal seam, at every actual bottom root \(\sigma\), is
\[
 m_r[u_\sigma(\lambda)\otimes u_\lambda(\sigma)]
     =\delta_{\lambda,\lambda_r}T_r,\qquad
 \lambda_r=-q^{2r-1}-q^{2-2r},\quad
 T_r=Q^{rd}/A_{\lambda_r}.
 \tag{BM2}
\]
Both finite product strings survive at exactly one root. Their
coefficient is calibrated by \(m_r\mathbf p=Q^{rd}\), so its phase
is fixed, including both parities and \(N=2\).

In the full nested frame, let \(a_\sigma\) be the actual cup column
and let \(b_{\sigma,\lambda}\) impose the ordinary-cap even heights
\(\sigma\) and final odd height \(\lambda\), summing the other odd
heights. With \(\mathcal R_\sigma\) the actual word on its external
\(\sigma\) block, (BM1)--(BM2) give
\[
 \mathcal S_{\sigma,\lambda}(R)
   :=b_{\sigma,\lambda}\mathcal R_\sigma a_\sigma
      =A_\lambda A_\sigma^{k-1}Z_N(R),\qquad
 |Z_N(R)|\le|\mathcal S_{\sigma,\lambda}(R)|\le N^k|Z_N(R)|.
 \tag{BM3}
\]
Every internal word sum remains inside this contraction. Its two
root-grid Laurent degrees are \(1,k-1\); it is still one known
closed-family line with unknown coefficient \(Z_N(R)\).
No rank reduction of an open component or meridian identity follows.

For the matched bottom \(\sigma_r=Q^r+qQ^{-r}\), set
\(t_r=-q^{2r-1}\), \(\beta_r=q^{-1}t_r\),
\(B_r=q^{-1}t_r^2=q^{4r-3}\). The full one-head graph source and
literal marked row are
\[
 u_a=\beta_r^a,\qquad h_a=t_r^a,\qquad
 m_rL_{\sigma_r}=h/N,\qquad
 hu=\frac2{1-B_r},\quad T_r=\frac2{N(1-B_r)}.
 \tag{BM4}
\]
Both counting norms are \(\sqrt N\), and their normalized overlap
is \(|T_r|\ge1/N\). These are explicit initialized quantities.

Define the actual normalized boundary functional
\(\omega_{N,r}(O)=hOu/(hu)\), and retain the physical generator
\(Ee_a=(Q^{-a}-1)e_{a-1}\), with its missing endpoint arrow zero.
For \(m<N\), direct finite geometric sums give
\[
 \omega_{N,r}(E^m)
  =\beta_r^m\prod_{j=1}^m
                  \frac{Q^{-j}-1}{1-B_rQ^{-j}}.
 \tag{BM5}
\]
For \(\rho=r/N\) in any compact interval \(I\subset(1/2,1)\),
this strengthens to the analytic, rather than merely fixed-moment, result
\[
 \omega_{N,r}(e^{zNE})
   =\frac1{1-c(\rho)z}+O_I(N^{-1}),\qquad
 c(\rho)=-\frac\pi{\sin(2\pi\rho)}>0,
 \tag{BM6}
\]
uniformly on a sufficiently small fixed complex disk. The limit is
\(\int_0^\infty e^{zs}c^{-1}e^{-s/c}\,ds\).
For the proof, small-index denominator chords stay uniformly away from
zero. Any remaining product of \(m\) distinct odd-root chords is at
least \(m!/N^m\). Together these bounds control every exponential
coefficient by \(C_I^m\), including the long tail, and justify summing
the fixed-moment limits. No phase rotation of \(NE\) is used.

The initialized response is therefore explicitly nonzero near the
origin. The finite functional need not be positive. Degree four of a
variational energy does not bound the physical crossing's degree in
\(E\), which can be \(N-1\). Thus (BM6) cannot yet be passed through
an arbitrary short word. Its original observation and uniform relative
source bounds are still required. No new volume-equality class or
finite-exception theorem has been established by this boundary result.

## An auxiliary Fourier coefficient recovers the original scalar, 24 November

Every actual signed word has an exact auxiliary-height family after the
original cup and last marked cap are contracted. Its Laurent degree is
fixed by width. All word coefficients and shared internal-height sums
remain coherent inside each family value; the original scalar is its
unknown coefficient.

Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(x=-q^{-1}=q^d\), \(c=1+q\), and take width \(2k\), \(k\ge1\), \(p=k-1\).
Write \(\mu_l=Q^l+qQ^{-l}\), \(0\le l<N\),
\(p_N(z)=\prod_l(z-\mu_l)\), and use the full physical nested frame
\(\Psi_\sigma\) with bottom parameter \(\sigma\) and external height
also \(\sigma\). The continuant vectors are the original \(u_\lambda(\sigma)\).
Set
\[
 A_\lambda=\frac{N^2q^dx^{-d}}{p_N'(\lambda)},\quad
 \mu_*=-q^{-1}-q^2,\quad T_*=\frac{2}{N(1-q^{-3})}.
\]
The literal marked cap has the all-bottom-root identity
\[
 m[u_\sigma(\lambda)\otimes u_\lambda(\sigma)]
                       =\delta_{\lambda,\mu_*}T_*.
 \tag{AW1}
\]
Its two finite product strings survive simultaneously only at the
lengths \(a=d-l,b=l\); their phase-retaining product is
\((q^{-1};Q)_d/N=2/[N(1-q^{-3})]\). This includes N=2 and empty strings.
The unrestricted marked tensor still has no height delta when its
outer and deeper heights differ.

Let \(u_0=\mathbf p^{\otimes k}\),
\(\ell_0=\ell^{\otimes p}\otimes m\),
\(Z_N(R)=\ell_0Ru_0\), and \(K_N=\chi_N Z_N(R)\), with the original
cup, ordinary caps and last mark. Since R commutes with \(B_c\) and
\(\mathsf K\), it commutes with
\(B_\sigma=B_c+(\sigma-c)\mathsf K^{-1}\); also \(B_\sigma u_0=\sigma u_0\).
Construct the full frame first, then let \(\mathcal R_\sigma\) be R's
matrix on its external \(\sigma\) block. In that block the literal
cup column \(a_\sigma\) has even heights fixed to \(\sigma\) and odd
coefficients \(\prod_{i=1}^k A_{\nu_{2i-1}}\). The linear row
\(b_\sigma\) fixes the same even heights and the last odd height to \(\mu_*\),
leaving every other label summed. Ordinary-cap sewing and (AW1) give
\[
 u_0=\Psi_\sigma a_\sigma,\qquad
 \ell_0\Psi_\sigma=T_*A_\sigma^{-p}b_\sigma
 \quad\hbox{on that external block}.
\]
No projector is inserted at an intermediate face. With
\[
 \mathcal S_l=b_{\mu_l}\mathcal R_{\mu_l}a_{\mu_l},\quad
 w_l=Q^l-qQ^{-l},\quad \gamma_N=\tfrac N2q^dx^{-d},
\]
the actual whole-word identity is
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \mathcal S_l=\frac{\gamma_N^p}{T_*}Z_N(R)w_l^p,
 \qquad w_l^p\mathcal S_{l+1}=w_{l+1}^p\mathcal S_l .
 \quad}                                                       \tag{AW2}
\]
All \(w_l\ne0\), and cyclic indices are modulo N.
The auxiliary connection is word-independent; its coefficient Z is not.

For \(\widehat{\mathcal S}(n)=N^{-1}\sum_lQ^{-nl}\mathcal S_l\), define
\[
 b_n=\sum_{\substack{0\le j\le p\\p-2j\equiv n\ ({\rm mod}\ N)}}
                  \binom pj(-q)^j,\quad 0\le n<N,\qquad M_{N,p}=\sum_n|b_n|^2>0.
\]
Then, at every N including aliases,
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal S}(n)=\frac{\gamma_N^p}{T_*}Z_N(R)b_n,
 \qquad M_{N,p}=N^{-1}\sum_l|w_l|^{2p}.
 \tag{AW3}
\]
For \(N>2p\), the modes are distinct,
\(M_{N,p}=\binom{2p}{p}\), and the highest Fourier coefficient is
\(\widehat{\mathcal S}(p)=\gamma_N^p Z_N(R)/T_*\).
Parseval gives the exact positive energy
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 |K_N|^2=|\chi_N|^2|T_*|^2(2/N)^{2p}
       \frac{\sum_l|\mathcal S_l|^2}{N M_{N,p}} .
 \quad}                                                       \tag{AW4}
\]
Each absolute square encloses the entire coherent word contraction.
This is not the norm of an unclosed propagated state.

There is also a uniform pointwise comparison, including zero scalars:
\[
 |Z_N(R)|\le|\mathcal S_l|
                  \le(3\pi/2)N^p|Z_N(R)| .                  \tag{AW5}
\]
Indeed \(|A_\sigma|=N\sin\alpha_\sigma\in[1,N]\) for the sorted root
angle, and \(|T_*|^{-1}=N\sin(3\pi/(2N))\in[1,3\pi/2]\).
The sine concavity bound proves the lower estimates for N≥3;
N=2 is immediate. Equation (AW2) proves (AW5). Multiplying both sides
by \(|\chi_N|\) compares every chosen auxiliary-root contraction with
the original scalar at only polynomial cost.

This degree is in the bottom auxiliary root, not in an ordinary color
or a physical peripheral variable. The root-grid Laurent line gives no
off-grid spectral continuation or knot A-polynomial. Its bounded degree
applies after the full closing, so it gives no early projection or
bounded-rank replacement for an open component. The global quartic
compiler and its bilinear gates remain. The unknown inner contraction
still needs its geometric lower estimate; no finite-exception theorem
or nonzero scalar for every knot is asserted.

## Bidiagonal equations transport full height frames, 24 November

The full neighboring-height frames admit exact linear updates on each
parity of the physical grid. All N coordinates and coherent cross terms
remain. Use \(N\ge2\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(d=N-1\),
\(\lambda_s=q^{s+1}+q^{-s}\), \(U_s=U_{\lambda_s}\), and the nilpotent
coefficient shift \(Ze_a=e_{a+1}\), \(Ze_d=0\). Then
\[
 (I+q^{s+1}Z)U_{s+2}=(I+q^{-s-2}Z)U_s,
 \qquad 0\le s\le N-3.
 \tag{BT1}
\]
Both multipliers are unit lower bidiagonal; \(U_0,U_1\) generate both
parity sequences by linear solves. For N=2 no update is needed.
With the initialized period's exact gauge S, put \(W_s=U_sS\),
\(G_s=W_s^\dagger W_s\), and, for integers \(s,k\ge0\) with \(s+2k\le d\),
\[
 D_{N,k}=2^k\binom{N+k-1}{k},\qquad
 D_{N,k}^{-2}G_s\preceq G_{s+2k}\preceq D_{N,k}^{2}G_s.
 \tag{BT2}
\]
This is the full Gram comparison for arbitrary complex packets in the
coefficient-counting pullback metrics, not an assertion about \(G_{\rm ht}\).
The binomial bound gives \(\log D_{N,k}=o(N)\) whenever \(k=o(N)\),
uniformly in the starting height. The two parity bases remain separate.

For the marked primitive \(\nu=1+q\), the specified source and canonical
marked row satisfy
\[
 W_sf=q^{-d/2}e_d,\quad \|f\|_{G_s}=1,\quad
 \|\ell_s\|_{G_s^{-1}}=\sqrt N,\quad
 { |\ell_sf|\over\|f\|_{G_s}\|\ell_s\|_{G_s^{-1}}}=N^{-1/2}.
 \tag{BT3}
\]
The physical row is \(\beta_N\ell_s\); its original \(\beta_N\) and exterior
\(\chi_N\) are retained. The transport \(H=W_{s+2k}^{-1}W_s\) fixes f,
is an isometry between the displayed metrics, and carries the marked row.

The frame equations are linear, so their squared residuals are quadratic;
exact linear substitution preserves polynomial degree. Each relation
compares one common input vector. Independently summed physical height
sectors acquire no constraint from it. Original bilinear Conway gluing
still requires its full compiler. The initialized angle and Gram comparison
do not bound the marked angle after a short tangle or the closed scalar.

## An initialized coideal period has a finite boundary response, 24 November

The full actual coideal crossing now has a primitive initialized source,
a calibrated marked residue, and a two-row polynomial boundary response.
Both sorted folds, interior forcing and the prescribed observation remain.
The response can be evaluated at every pole with bounded local derivative
order. This does not give a closed-word scalar lower bound.

Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(\sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\),
\(\alpha_t=(t+\tfrac12)\pi/N\), \(\mu_t=\sin\alpha_t\), and
\(f_t=e^{i\pi t(t+1)/(4N)}\). Write
\(\lambda_t=2\sqrt q\cos\alpha_t\),
\(\nu=\lambda_v,\sigma=\lambda_s\), \(0\le v,s\le d\).
Use the full continuant matrix \(U_\sigma\), the original reversed
one-head operator \(J'_\nu\), and
\[
 S=\operatorname{diag}((-1)^t\mu_t/f_t),\quad
 L=q^{-1/2}S^{-1}U_\sigma^{-1}J'_\nu U_\sigma S,\quad
 \pi_N(\zeta)=2T_N(\zeta/2).
\]
The initialized actual crossing column is exactly
\[
 g(\zeta)={\kappa\over N}\operatorname{adj}(\zeta I-L)f,
 \qquad(\zeta I-L)g(\zeta)={\kappa\over N}\pi_N(\zeta)f.
 \tag{PB1}
\]
Its physical root values are the original crossing columns in this gauge.
The interior forcing \(f\) is universal, independent of both neighbors.
Over \(\mathcal O_N=\mathbb Z[\sqrt q,1/(2N)]\), the matrices \(U_\sigma,S\)
and the cyclic matrix \([f,Lf,\ldots,L^df]\) are unimodular. Thus the full
source module is the regular module of
\(\mathcal E_N=\mathcal O_N[\zeta]/\pi_N\), with rank N.
Its cyclic generators form the torsor \(\mathcal E_N^\times\).

For \(\nu=c=1+q\), the canonically normalized marked mode \(\ell_\sigma\)
satisfies
\[
 \ell_\sigma(\zeta I-L)^{-1}f={\omega_N\over\zeta-\zeta_*},\quad
 \ell_\sigma g(\zeta)={\kappa\omega_N\over N}
                  {\pi_N(\zeta)\over\zeta-\zeta_*},\quad
 \omega_N=i(-1)^{N-2}q^{-3/2},\quad |\omega_N|=1,
 \quad\zeta_*=2\cos\alpha_{N-2}.
 \tag{PB2}
\]
The physical four-head row is \(\beta_N\ell_\sigma\), where
\(\beta_N=(T_*/A_c)\kappa(1-q)/2\), with N's original boundary
constants \(T_*,A_c\) and its original \(\chi_N\) external.
Its residue is \(\beta_N\omega_N\), not a unit asserted for the physical
row. The polynomial in (PB2) vanishes at the other physical roots.
Mark-normalized cyclic generators correspond to units \(p\) with
\(p(\zeta_*)=1\); no row is rescaled.

Neighbor-frame changes also have an exact source calibration. For a
physical reference \(\sigma_0\),
\(A_\sigma=U_\sigma U_{\sigma_0}^{-1}\) is unit lower triangular Toeplitz:
a polynomial in the fixed nilpotent shift \(Ze_a=e_{a+1}\), \(Ze_d=0\).
Consequently \(H_{\sigma'\leftarrow\sigma}=S^{-1}U_{\sigma'}^{-1}U_\sigma S\)
forms an abelian unipotent family, intertwines L, fixes f, and transports
\(g_\sigma\) exactly; for \(\nu=c\) it transports the normalized marked
row as well. This conditional frame group is distinct from the
cyclic-generator torsor above. Neither is asserted to be the braid group
or a geometric cycle.

For the full sorted matrix take boundary indices \(B=\{0,d\}\) and
interior I. Both folds are retained in the full matrix, including their
upper \(\pm i\) factors; the literal \(N=2\) matrix is used separately.
Put
\[
 D=\det(\zeta I-L_{II}),\quad C=\operatorname{adj}(\zeta I-L_{II}),
\]
\[
 \widetilde H=D(\zeta I_2-L_{BB})-L_{BI}CL_{IB},\quad
 \widetilde h=Df_B+L_{BI}Cf_I,\qquad
 \det\widetilde H=D\pi_N.
 \tag{PB3}
\]
The following are exact polynomial quotients, not choices of finite parts:
\[
 N_B=\operatorname{adj}(\widetilde H)\widetilde h,\quad
 v_B=N_B/D,\qquad
 v_I={C[D\pi_Nf_I+L_{IB}N_B]\over D^2},\quad
 g={\kappa\over N}(v_B,v_I).
 \tag{PB4}
\]
For any prescribed row \(\eta\) independent of \(\zeta\), the original
period is \(\kappa(\eta_Bv_B+\eta_Iv_I)/N\). This includes
\(\eta=\ell A\) for a fixed actual short-component composition A;
its full operator, complementary channels and cap remain in \(\eta\).

Removing 0,d leaves two real sine-symmetrizable parity Jacobi paths,
with at most two zero cuts, hence at most four irreducible components.
Every root of D is real with multiplicity at most four. Exact division
therefore evaluates the raw boundary quotient with at most four
\(\zeta\)-derivatives, and the raw full-period quotient with at most eight,
even where \(D\) and \(\pi_N\) vanish together. These are auxiliary spectral
jets; the physical Casimir/Hermite normals have not been replaced.

A three-row option \(B_3=\{0,u,d\}\), with duplicates removed and
\(u=N-\max(v,s)-1\), isolates the cooriented interior \(1,\ldots,u-1\).
When that interior is nonempty, row 1 has a positive incidence to
boundary0; its reverse fold stays in the boundary matrix.
The natural upper cut and literal wall are retained.
For every cooriented physical input its sine-symmetrized pencil satisfies
\(cN^{-2}I\le M_r\le CN^2I\). The outside block and full boundary
response are not made positive. There are at most five interior Jacobi
components; the three-row raw boundary/full-period derivative bounds are
ten/fifteen. Empty interiors, duplicate boundaries, \(N=2,3\) are included.

The abelian frame family does not collapse the actual operator algebra.
For distinct physical \(\sigma,\sigma_0\), \(A_\sigma-I\) has unit first
subdiagonal \((\sigma-\sigma_0)/(1-Q)\), so finite compositional inversion
expresses Z as a polynomial in \(A_\sigma-I\) over \(\mathcal O_N\).
Also \(Z^d=e_de_0^{\mathsf T}\). The columns \((J'_\nu)^ke_d\) and rows
\(e_0^{\mathsf T}(J'_\nu)^l\), \(0\le k,l<N\), are unit triangular
bases: their diagonals are products of the original upper arrows
\(q(1-Q^{-a})\). Their outer products therefore give the unital algebra
\[
 \big\langle A_\sigma,J'_\nu\big\rangle_{\mathcal O_N}
       =\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathcal O_N).
 \tag{PB5}
\]
This is a statement about these actual boundary operators, not a theorem
that the braid-group image is the full matrix algebra.

Boundary matrix size and local pole order are now fixed, but their
polynomial degrees, paths and source rank still grow with N. Exact
sewing must retain the spectral response, source, full complements and
literal cap; constant two-row rank closure is not inferred. No phase
alignment, selected geometric coefficient, global scalar lower bound or
arbitrary-short-filling finite-exception theorem follows yet.

## One orthogonal basis retains coherent crossing sums, 24 November

For fixed actual neighboring heights, one Jacobi output basis now handles
every input of the cooriented crossing rectangle. It replaces the earlier
column-dependent description by exact coherent Cauchy sums. The sum over
inputs stays inside each absolute square; the full input Gram is retained.

Use the original conventions \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(\sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)}\),
\(\alpha_t=(t+\tfrac12)\pi/N\), \(\mu_t=\sin\alpha_t\), and the
actual amplitude \(J(r,t;v,s)\) from
[the cooriented crossing theorem](research_coideal_cooriented_volume_kernel.md).
Fix the original ordered neighboring indices \((v,s)\), and put
\[
 S=\max(v,s),\qquad T_0=N-S-2,\qquad
 \mathcal C=\{0,\ldots,T_0\},\qquad y_r=\cos\alpha_r.
\]
No physical neighbor swap is made. If \(\mathcal C\) is empty, the whole
actual block is retained literally. For \(p\in\{0,1\}\), \(p\le T_0\),
and a nonempty parity interior
\(I_p=\{p+2,p+4,\ldots\}\cap\mathcal C\), keep the literal lower
row \(p\), and the equality-wall row when the upper exit is nonzero.
Let \(L_p\) be the actual recurrence matrix on this interior, keeping its
original diagonal; omitted boundary couplings remain on the right side.
Then
\[
 A_p=D_p(2y_*I-L_p)D_p^{-1},\quad
 D_p=\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\mu_t}),\quad
 y_*=\cos\alpha_{T_0},\quad \tau_r=2(y_r-y_*)\ge0,
\]
\[
 cN^{-2}I\le A_p+\tau_rI\le CN^2I\qquad(r\in\mathcal C).
 \tag{JC1}
\]
The exact killing bound holds for all \(r,t\in\mathcal C\), without
ordering the middle labels. Detailed balance makes \(A_p\) real symmetric.
Thus one algebraic orthogonal matrix \(O_p\), independent of \(r\),
diagonalizes it with eigenvalues \(\kappa_j\).

Put \(K_{tr}=\sqrt{\mu_t\mu_r}J(r,t;v,s)\) for
\(t\in I_p\), \(r\in\mathcal C\).
The literal lower and possible wall incidences form a matrix \(B_p\)
with at most two columns. Their original boundary values form
\(\rho_r=\sqrt{\mu_r}(J(r,p;v,s),J(r,T_0+1;v,s))^T\), with the
right component omitted at a natural zero exit. The exact relation is
\[
 (A_p+\tau_rI)K_{\bullet r}=B_p\rho_r,\qquad
 A_pK+K\operatorname{diag}(\tau_r)=B_p(\rho_r)_r.
 \tag{JC2}
\]
Hence for every complex input \(\xi\) supported on \(\mathcal C\),
\[
 \|K\xi\|^2=\sum_j\left|
   \sum_{r\in\mathcal C}
   {(O_p^TB_p\rho_r)_j\xi_r\over\kappa_j+\tau_r}
                         \right|^2.
 \tag{JC3}
\]
This is not a sum of column energies.

The entire cross-input Gram also has a finite response formula. For real
\(s,t\ge0\), let \(R_p(s)=(A_p+sI)^{-1}\),
\(W_p(s)=B_p^TR_p(s)B_p\), and
\[
 \mathcal L_p(s,t)=\frac{W_p(s)-W_p(t)}{t-s}
                 =B_p^TR_p(s)R_p(t)B_p,\qquad
 \mathcal L_p(s,s)=-W_p'(s).
\]
Then
\[
 (K^\dagger K)_{rq}=\rho_r^T\mathcal L_p(\tau_r,\tau_q)\rho_q.
 \tag{JC4}
\]
The block kernel is positive because its quadratic form is
\(\|\sum_rR_p(s_r)B_ph_r\|^2\). Add the literal lower-row Grams
and the disjoint parity interiors to recover the complete corner Gram.
Two boundary forces do not imply a two-dimensional source or a rank-two
input Gram. The polynomial condition in (JC1) is not a conditioning
estimate for this Gram or for a coherent observation.

All source phases remain. In the common orthonormal \(G_{\rm ht}\)
coordinates, write \(f_r=e^{i\pi r(r+1)/(4N)}\); on the cooriented rectangle
\(r,t\in\mathcal C\) the original entries are
\[
 \widetilde B^\epsilon_{tr}
  =(f_vf_s)^\epsilon(-1)^t f_t^{-\epsilon}
      \sqrt{\mu_t\mu_r}\,J(r,t;v,s)f_r^{-\epsilon},\qquad\epsilon=\pm1.
 \tag{JC5}
\]
Extend each conditional \(O_p\) by identity on the literal boundary rows
and complementary heights, retaining the displayed diagonal phases.
These full changes are unitary in \(G_{\rm ht}\), including across
overlapping faces. Their interface operators remain explicit.
If the input is \(a=a_{\mathcal C}+a_Q\), the contribution from \(a_Q\)
to a cooriented output mode stays inside the same square as (JC3).
Complementary output rows remain too; no projection is inserted.

For a full change \(V\), the source becomes \(V^\dagger u\), the literal
marked row becomes \(\ell V\), and a source projector becomes
\(V^\dagger PV\). The original scalar and external \(\chi_N\) are unchanged;
source and cap norms are preserved in \(G_{\rm ht}\). This does not make
the braid unitary in the physical Hilbert metric, close the displacement
rank through a word, align its phases, or prove a closed-scalar lower bound.
The new result is an explicit common output basis and the complete coherent Gram.

## All cooriented coideal crossings have a positive volume amplitude, 24 November

The actual local coideal crossing now has a calibrated nonzero coefficient
throughout its strict cooriented domain. Neither the discriminant condition
nor an index parity is needed. Its logarithm has the sewn octahedral volume
as leading term, with a universal logarithmic error over all allowed labels.
This is a local source theorem; the original closed scalar remains separate.

Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(\delta=\pi/N\), \(\kappa=e^{i\pi d^2/(2N)}\), and use the principal
\(\sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)}\). All labels satisfy \(0\le r,t,v,s\le d\).
Write \(\lambda_j=2\sqrt q\cos\alpha_j\), \(\alpha_j=(j+\tfrac12)\delta\).
The original monic continuants are
\[
 D_{-1}=0,\quad D_0=1,\qquad
 D_{a+1}(\lambda;\sigma)=(\lambda+qQ^a\sigma)D_a(\lambda;\sigma)
                         -q(1-Q^a)^2D_{a-1}(\lambda;\sigma).
\]
Put
\[
 \Phi_{rs}(z)=\sum_{a=0}^dD_a(\lambda_r;\lambda_s)z^a/(q^2;q^2)_a,
 \quad f_j=e^{i\delta j(j+1)/4},\quad
 \gamma_{ij}=e^{i\pi d/4}f_i/f_j.
\]
For the original finite continuants define
\[
 J(r,t;v,s)=\frac{1}{\overline\gamma_{rv}\gamma_{ts}}
   \sum_{a=0}^d
   \frac{\overline{D_a(\lambda_r;\lambda_v)}D_a(\lambda_t;\lambda_s)}
        {|(q^2;q^2)_a|^2}.
 \tag{GC1}
\]
The theorem is
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \max(r,t)+\max(v,s)\le N-2
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 J(r,t;v,s)>0,\qquad
 |\log J(r,t;v,s)-NV_{\rm sew}/\pi|\le C\log N .
 \quad}
 \tag{GC2}
\]
Here \(C\) is universal, including labels approaching the boundary.
The known quadratic height phase has been retained in (GC1).

For completeness write \((\alpha_1,\alpha_2)=(\alpha_r,\alpha_t)\),
\((\beta_1,\beta_2)=(\alpha_v,\alpha_s)\),
\(a_i=\cos\alpha_i\), \(b_i=\cos\beta_i\), and
\[
 x_*={a_1a_2-b_1b_2\over a_1+a_2+b_1+b_2},\quad
 \Theta_*=\arccos x_*,\quad
 \psi_i={\pi-\alpha_i-\beta_i\over2},\quad
 u_i={\Theta_*-\alpha_i\over2}.
\]
Then \(0<u_i<\psi_i\). The volume \(V_{\rm sew}\) is the sum of the
volumes of the four tetrahedra
\[
 (u_i,\psi_i-u_i,\pi-\psi_i),\qquad
 (\alpha_i+u_i,\psi_i+\beta_i-u_i,\psi_i),\quad i=1,2.
 \tag{GC3}
\]
Their common edge closes in modulus and argument at \(x_*\), and their
supporting faces form one convex ideal octahedron. The closed-domain
maximum-energy definition retains collapsed and repeated wall equalities.

The proof has two explicit source boundaries and one Dirichlet argument.
Finite Parseval and the exact root intervals give positive quadratures
for the previously known parity and for equal or adjacent middle labels.
The latter two strips supply the lower boundary for every unresolved branch;
they are not separate assumptions on the final theorem.

By exact label symmetries take \(r\le t\), \(v\le s=S\).
At the upper equality boundary \(u=d-S\), \(\lambda_u=-\lambda_S\),
the original finite products give
\[
 J(r,u;v,S)={|\Phi_{rv}(-q^S)|\over R_S}\,\mathcal F>0,
 \qquad
 R_j=\prod_{h=1}^j{\sin(h\delta)\over\sin((h-\tfrac12)\delta)},
 \qquad 1\le R_j\le N.
 \tag{GC4}
\]
The exact balanced finite series \(\mathcal F\) transforms by the proved
finite Sears identity into a positive prefactor times a sum of positive
terms with squared numerator strings, for both parities of \(S-v\).
All factors that occur are nonzero; the one-term case is treated before
parameter checks. The source phase is exact, and
\(N^{-2}\le\mathcal F\le N^5\). Thus this boundary also has its calibrated
volume rate, rather than an assigned amplitude.

The actual sorted crossing recurrence steps by two. With
\(y=\cos\alpha_r\), \(x=\cos\alpha_t\),
\(a=\cos\alpha_v\), \(b=\cos\alpha_S\), its positive edge coefficients
\(c_t^\pm\) and diagonal \(d_t\) satisfy the exact defect identity
\[
 2y-d_t-c_t^+-c_t^-
 =2\left[y+\cos\delta-{(1-a)(1-b)\over\cos\delta+x}\right]
 \ge cN^{-2}.
 \tag{GC5}
\]
Starting at an equal or adjacent middle label avoids both sorted folds.
The resulting real tridiagonal Dirichlet matrix has a positive inverse;
its original boundary values are precisely the two calibrated ones above.
This proves positivity of every remaining actual coefficient.

There is also an exact local quadratic minimization. Put
\(\mu_t=\sin\alpha_t\) on a nonempty solved Dirichlet path. Its actual
coefficients obey detailed balance,
\[
 A_{t,t+2}:=\mu_t c_t^+=\mu_{t+2}c_{t+2}^-
 ={(\cos(\alpha_t+\delta)+a)(\cos(\alpha_t+\delta)+b)
       \over\sin(\alpha_t+\delta)}>0.
\]
For boundary edges use the incident interior row, and keep the two literal
Dirichlet values fixed. Writing \(\omega_t\) for (GC5), define
\[
 \mathscr D(z)=\frac12\sum_{\text{used edges }e=(i,j)}
                 A_e(z_j-z_i)^2
             +\frac12\sum_{\text{interior }t}\mu_t\omega_t z_t^2.
 \tag{GC5a}
\]
Both boundary-edge terms, including their constants, are retained.
Its Euler equation is \(\operatorname{diag}(\mu)(Mz-\mathrm{rhs})=0\),
so its unique real minimizer is the actual phase-removed amplitude column.
Since \(\mu_t\ge c/N\), \(\omega_t\ge c/N^2\), and \(c_t^\pm\le CN^2\),
its Hessian satisfies \(cN^{-3}I\le H\le CN^2I\), hence has condition
number at most \(CN^5\). Empty paths require no minimization.
This is an ordinary positive network energy for this local amplitude,
unlike the earlier complex kernel-Laplacian in the marked-mode problem.
The weight \(\mu\) is not a common positive physical braid metric.
This degree-two minimization does not replace the global quartic source
program or supply an original closed-scalar lower bound.

The rate does not follow merely from this polynomial inverse norm.
Match the unresolved interior to the known-parity path shifted by one index.
Its endpoint has zero outgoing coefficient. Positive finite forest
expansions of determinants and cofactors compare the two Green matrices:
the sum of absolute logarithmic ratios of matched weights is \(O(\log N)\).
This follows from monotone affine-cosine factors, unimodal sine factors,
and the monotone positive defect in (GC5); only two endpoint weights change.
Consequently corresponding Green entries differ by at most powers of \(N\).
The calibrated lower boundaries and equality boundary are likewise
polynomially comparable to the neighboring known-parity values.
The maximum principle bounds the right-boundary response by the known
positive column. Together these facts give \(N^{-C}g_i\le J_i\le N^Cg_i\).
The uniform log-sine modulus for a one-angle step then proves (GC2).

Both original same-frame signs therefore retain the exact formulas
\[
 B^+_{t,r}=(-1)^t\sin\alpha_t\,{f_vf_s\over f_tf_r}J(r,t;v,s),
 \qquad B^-_{t,r}=\overline{B^+_{t,r}}.
 \tag{GC6}
\]
The scalar identity \(\kappa q^{d/2}i^{-d}=1\) uses the specified original
lift. Both incident path-Haar weights remain compulsory and have their
known four-term volume correction. No Casimir normal is removed.

The theorem does not place a complete geometric character in rotated-real
coideal heights, or show that every intermediate quartet is cooriented.
The original input, last marked closing and external \(\chi_N\) remain.
The quadratic face phases do not by themselves align a whole coherent sum
or determine its contour intersection. No arbitrary-short-filling closed
scalar lower bound or finite-exception theorem follows from this local result.

## Exact parity-grid cancellation extends the signed volume chamber, 24 November

The actual signed coideal crossing has a larger proved positive domain.
Finite character orthogonality removes its unwanted samples exactly;
no comparison with the full absolute circle integral is needed.
This extends the earlier negative-discriminant chamber on one parity
class of the actual four height indices.

Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(\delta=\pi/N\),
\(\lambda_r=2\sqrt q\cos\alpha_r\), \(\alpha_r=(r+\tfrac12)\delta\), and
\[
 \Phi_{rs}(z)=\sum_{a=0}^{d}
       D_a(\lambda_r;\lambda_s)z^a/(q^2;q^2)_a,\qquad
 \Sigma_N=\sum_{a=0}^{d}
  \frac{\overline{D_a(\lambda_{r_1};\lambda_{s_1})}
                    D_a(\lambda_{r_2};\lambda_{s_2})}
       {|(q^2;q^2)_a|^2}.
 \tag{PQ1}
\]
The continuants, finite endpoint arrows and original crossing scalar
are those of the complete source proofs below.

Assume \(r_i+s_j\le N-2\) for every \(i,j\), put
\(R=\max(r_1,r_2)\), \(S=\max(s_1,s_2)\), and require
\(N+R+S\) even. Choose \(p\equiv1-R\equiv N+S-1\pmod2\).
On that \(N\)-point grid, the union of the two exact root strings is
\([1-R,N+S-1]\cap(p+2\mathbb Z)\). Its complement is
\[
 M=(N-R-S)/2,\qquad k_a=-N+S+1+2a,\quad0\le a<M.
 \tag{PQ2}
\]
Here \(M\ge1\); the last survivor \(-R-1\) is not a root.
All survivors lie in the same actual common root-free component.
The union follows from the finite root intervals: their lower endpoints
are \(1-r\) or \(r+2\), their upper endpoints \(N+s-1\) or \(N-s-2\),
and cross-coorientation makes the chosen step-two intervals overlap
or touch.

The frequency differences of
\(\overline{\Phi_{r_1s_1}}\Phi_{r_2s_2}\) lie in \([-d,d]\),
so direct finite Parseval is exact on this grid. With
\[
 f_r=e^{i\delta r(r+1)/4},\qquad
 \gamma_{rs}=e^{i\pi d/4}f_r/f_s,
\]
it gives the whole signed coefficient
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \Sigma_N=\overline{\gamma_{r_1s_1}}\gamma_{r_2s_2}J_N,\qquad
 J_N=\frac1N\sum_{a=0}^{M-1}
       |\Phi_{r_1s_1}(q^{k_a})\Phi_{r_2s_2}(q^{k_a})|>0.
 \quad}
 \tag{PQ3}
\]
Every excluded sample vanishes, and every survivor has this exact
common phase. Strict positivity holds at every allowed level.

Write \(a_i=\cos\alpha_{r_i}\), \(b_i=\cos\alpha_{s_i}\), and
\[
 x_*=\frac{a_1a_2-b_1b_2}{a_1+a_2+b_1+b_2},\quad
 \Theta_*=\arccos x_*,\quad
 \psi_i=\frac{\pi-\alpha_{r_i}-\alpha_{s_i}}2,\quad
 u_i=\frac{\Theta_*-\alpha_{r_i}}2.
\]
Cross-coorientation alone puts \(0<u_i<\psi_i\).
Let \(V_{\rm sew}\) be the volume of the convex ideal octahedron
formed by the four tetrahedra
\[
 (u_i,\psi_i-u_i,\pi-\psi_i),\qquad
 (\alpha_{r_i}+u_i,\psi_i+\alpha_{s_i}-u_i,\psi_i),
 \quad i=1,2.
\]
Their common edge closes in argument and modulus at \(x_*\).
The compact-uniform estimate of the new proof strengthens to
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \left|\log J_N-NV_{\rm sew}/\pi\right|\le C\log N
 \qquad}
 \tag{PQ4}
\]
with one universal constant for every cooriented good-parity quadruple.

Here is the additional uniform argument. At a surviving raw grid node,
its angular distance from every actual root is at least \(\delta\).
For each step-\(2\delta\) string, center cells at its root angles and
compare the sample of \(\log|2\sin(t/2)|\) with its cell average.
The boundedly many cells nearest a singularity have error \(O(1)\),
even when the singularity is a cell endpoint. On all remaining cells
the total oscillation is bounded by the integral of \(|\cot(t/2)|\)
outside distance \(c\delta\), hence by \(C\log N\).
This proves a two-sided log-cell estimate at every surviving node,
with universal constants; product multiplicities are at most two.
The actual finite-arc endpoint shift is \(O(\delta)\).
The uniform modulus \(|\Lambda(t+h)-\Lambda(t)|\le
C|h|\log(e/|h|)\), where \(\Lambda'=-\log|2\sin t|\),
therefore changes the \(N\)-scaled energy by at most \(C\log N\).
The sum of the two mean-zero energies in the new proof has its common-arc maximum
\(2V_{\rm sew}/\pi\). Every survivor lies in that closed arc,
and one is within \(\delta\) of its maximum, including when \(M=1\).
The same modulus controls that displacement. The upper bound on all
samples and the lower bound on this one sample, with the factor \(1/N\)
in (PQ3), prove (PQ4). No compactness margin or Hessian bound is needed.

For actual same-frame crossing indices \((r,r',v,s)\), take
\(R=\max(r,r')\), \(S=\max(v,s)\). The original phases give
\[
 B^+_{r',r}=(-1)^{r'}\sin\alpha_{r'}
       \frac{f_vf_s}{f_{r'}f_r}J_N,\qquad
 B^-_{r',r}=\overline{B^+_{r',r}}.
 \tag{PQ5}
\]
Here \(\kappa q^{d/2}i^{-d}=1\) for the specified original lift.
Both incident path-Haar weights remain, with their known two-label
volume corrections. No discriminant sign is required.

The other index parity is unresolved. This does not place a complete
geometric character in the real coideal heights, align word phases,
or prove a nonzero original marked closing. No original external
scalar, source constraint or complementary normal data is discarded.
The arbitrary-short-filling finite-exception target remains open.

## Direct spectral numerators also have persistent off-interval zeros, 24 November

A universal zero-free complement of the physical Casimir interval fails
for an actual direct spectral source, even eventually on compact sets.
This concerns the direct numerator variable \(\sigma\), not the Fourier
fugacity of the earlier finite color-window examples.
It leaves open a smaller domain following a specified geometric branch.

Use the fixed strict construction
\[
 \tau=C\bigl(h_1\,\mathscr T(h_2)\bigr),\qquad
 h_i=\mathscr T(L_{a_i}),\qquad \epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=0.
 \tag{DZ1}
\]
Here \(L_a\) is the literal ordinary-circle coupon with its original
pivot and \(\mathscr T\) is the genuine unscaled quarter-turn.
Both strict leaf coordinates may be \(1/4\): the closing children have
types \(L,H\) and complementary outputs. Their strand pairings are
\(U,I\), whose stack is \(U\), with no internal component; cylindrical
closure has one main component. No auxiliary link name is needed.

Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}\),
\(\chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2=\prod_{j=0}^d(z-c_j)\), and
\(s_r=\prod_{j=1}^r2\sin(\pi j/N)\), \(s_0=1\), \(s_d=N\).
The original full spectral coupon is
\[
 V_N(\sigma;z)=\frac{\chi_N(\sigma)-\chi_N(z)}{\sigma-z}.
 \tag{DZ2}
\]
In the full Casimir algebra it equals
\(\chi_N(\sigma)(\sigma-\Omega)^{-1}\), with polynomial continuation
at every node. All repeated-node derivatives remain.
The exact all-color identity in the Gaussian-resolvent proof expresses
this same coupon as a coherent finite combination of the original
\(L_a\), without an added half crossing.

Replacing both circle coupons in (DZ1) by (DZ2), its literal source is
\[
 F_N(\sigma,\tau)=
 \phi\bigl((\mathscr T V_N(\sigma))
                  \mathscr T(\mathscr T V_N(\tau))\bigr)
 =\phi\bigl(V_N(\sigma)\mathscr T V_N(\tau)\bigr).
 \tag{DZ3}
\]
This uses the proved full operator identity \(\mathscr T^2=I\) and
the symmetric turn/Gram identity from the Newton theorem, not a
topological erasure of turns.
The original cups, cap, mark and pivot are retained.

In the real normalized Newton basis
\(e_r=\prod_{j<r}(c_j-z)/s_r^2\), the exact turn/Gram theorem gives
\[
 V_N(\sigma)=\sum_{r=0}^d v_r(\sigma)e_r,\qquad
 v_r(\sigma)=(-1)^rs_r^2\prod_{j=r+1}^d(\sigma-c_j),\qquad
 F_N(\sigma,\tau)=\sum_{r=0}^dv_r(\sigma)v_r(\tau).
 \tag{DZ4}
\]
The coefficient formula follows by divided differences of the full
resolvent, and hence includes confluent nodes. In particular
\(v_0\) is monic of degree \(d\) and \(v_d=(-1)^dN^2\).
Thus the direct diagonal polynomial
\[
 D_N(\sigma)=F_N(\sigma,\sigma)=\sum_{r=0}^dv_r(\sigma)^2
 \tag{DZ5}
\]
is real and monic of degree \(2d\), with \(D_N(t)\ge N^4\) for real
\(t\). Every zero is nonreal. For example \(D_2(\sigma)=\sigma^2+16\).
A finite example alone would not exclude eventual compact zero-freeness;
the following argument supplies that stronger conclusion.

All zeros lie in \(|\sigma|<10\). Indeed, for \(|\sigma|\ge10\),
\[
 \left|\frac{v_r(\sigma)}{v_0(\sigma)}\right|
 \le\left(\frac4{|\sigma|-2}\right)^r\le2^{-r},\qquad
 \left|\frac{D_N}{v_0^2}-1\right|\le\sum_{r=1}^d4^{-r}<1.
 \tag{DZ6}
\]
For each fixed positive integer \(m\), the coefficient of
\(\sigma^{-m}\) in the Laurent expansion of \(\log(D_N/v_0^2)\)
is \(O_m(N^{-4})\). Only \(r\le m/2\) can contribute; for each fixed
such \(r\), \(s_r^4=O_r(N^{-4r})\), and the remaining coefficients
of \(\prod_{j=1}^r(\sigma-c_j)^{-2}\) are bounded independently of
\(N\). The finite logarithm expansion preserves this estimate.

Let \(\mu_N\) be the probability measure on the \(2d\) zeros of
\(D_N\), counted with multiplicity. Comparing Laurent logarithms yields
\[
 \int z^m\,d\mu_N(z)
   =\frac1d\sum_{j=1}^dc_j^m+O_m(N^{-5})
   \longrightarrow\int_{-2}^2x^m\,d\nu(x),\qquad
 d\nu(x)=\frac{dx}{\pi\sqrt{4-x^2}}.
 \tag{DZ7}
\]
The last limit is the ordinary cosine-grid Riemann sum.

There is nevertheless positive exponential growth at the endpoint.
Take \(r=\lfloor5N/6\rfloor\). Every factor \(2\sin(\pi j/N)\)
with \(j>r\) is at most one, and at least \(N/12-1\) of them are
at most \(\pi/6<2/3\). Since \(s_d=N\),
\(s_r\ge N(3/2)^{N/12-1}\).
For \(j>r\), \(2+c_j=4\cos^2((j+1/2)\pi/N)\ge3\), and there
are at least \(N/6-1\) such factors. Equation (DZ4) therefore gives
\[
 |v_r(-2)|\ge\frac4{27}N^2(9/2)^{N/6},\qquad
 D_N(-2)\ge\frac{16}{729}N^4(9/2)^{N/3}.
 \tag{DZ8}
\]

Suppose along some subsequence every zero approached \([-2,2]\).
The uniform bound (DZ6) gives a weakly convergent further subsequence;
its limit is supported on that real interval. Equation (DZ7) and
polynomial approximation identify that probability measure uniquely
with \(\nu\). For every \(M>0\), truncate the logarithm from below:
\(\max\{\log|-2-z|,-M\}\) is continuous on the fixed zero disk.
Consequently
\[
 \limsup\frac{\log D_N(-2)}{2d}
 \le\int_{-2}^2\log|-2-x|\,d\nu(x)=0.
 \tag{DZ9}
\]
The integral is zero by \(x=2\cos t\) and the elementary log-sine
integral. Monotone convergence of the truncated logarithms justifies
the displayed upper bound. It contradicts (DZ8), whose lower limit
is at least \(\log(9/2)/6>0\).

Hence there are \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(N_0\) such that for every
\(N\ge N_0\), \(D_N\) has a zero in the fixed compact set
\[
 \{z:|z|\le10,\ \operatorname{dist}(z,[-2,2])\ge\varepsilon\}.
 \tag{DZ10}
\]
At that zero \(F_N(z,z)=0\). The original spectral denominators
\(\chi_N(z)\) have all their zeros in \([-2,2]\), so they cannot
cancel these off-interval zeros.

This rules out a universal direct-spectral zero-free complement of
\([-2,2]\), including eventual zero-freeness on every compact subset,
for the stated actual strict source. It does not locate these zeros
relative to a particular short-filling geometric saddle or its path.
A narrower connected geometric corridor remains possible and requires
its own original-source estimate. No new finite-exception conclusion,
scalar asymptotic, or obstruction for every individual filling follows.

## A braid-compatible source projection has an explicit normal gap, 24 November

The [source-retraction proof](research_braid_natural_saturated_source_retraction.md)
gives a single source projection that works through the whole actual
braid representation. It also constructs a specified positive metric
with a quantitative bound for enforcing the complete source equation.
This goes beyond merely counting or preserving the genuine source.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and an even width \(b=2k\ge4\).
Put \(r=k-1\), \(W=V^{\otimes2r}\), \(D=rd\), and let \(W_D\)
be its physical integer-degree-\(D\) space. In the coherent corner
coordinates the actual source is
\[
 S=\ker(J_{E,W}:W_D\longrightarrow W_{D-N}).
 \tag{SR1}
\]
The \(J_E,J_F\) are the original regular divided currents:
generic \(E^N,F^N\) are divided by \(1-\zeta^{2N}\) before taking
the quantum root. They are not arbitrary root matrix quotients.

On \(W_D\), the explicit retraction is
\[
 P=I+\sum_{m=1}^{r-1}
       \frac{J_{F,W}^{m}J_{E,W}^{m}}
            {N^{2m}m!(m+1)!},\qquad
 P^2=P,\quad\operatorname{ran}P=S,\quad [P,B_i^{\pm1}]=0 .
 \tag{SR2}
\]
Here \(B_i^{\pm1}\) are the entire original reduced signed braid
matrices, including their repeated-root derivatives. Thus both source
and complement remain invariant under every overlapping crossing.

The proof uses the full tensor currents before reducing to the corner.
They preserve the small-quantum-group invariant sector across all
unrolled weights and give an ordinary \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) action there.
Both current extraction formulas have the sign \((-1)^d\); every
mixed divided-coproduct term vanishes by \(E_W^N=F_W^N=0\).
The two signs cancel in each \(J_F^mJ_E^m\) term of (SR2).
This proves commutation for this actual corner representation.

Regular generic linear cup, cap and sewing maps intertwine these
projections. This statement uses the complete incoming packet.
It does not permit independent projections of two arbitrary tensor
factors: nontrivial ordinary spins can couple to a trivial spin.

There are two useful metrics, with different norm comparisons.
First put \(Q=I-P\) and
\[
 G_{\rm split}=P^\dagger P+Q^\dagger Q\succeq\tfrac12 I .
 \tag{SR3}
\]
It makes source and complement orthogonal and agrees with the physical
metric on either separately. If \(AP=P'A\), then
\(\|A\|_{G_{\rm split}\to G'_{\rm split}}\le\|A\|_{\rm physical}\)
on those same actual packet spaces. No condition-number estimate is
needed for this inequality.

For the source-repair estimate use the full middle sector
\(\mathcal L_W=\ker(K_W-I)=\bigoplus_jW_{H_W=2Nj}\).
Its actual matrices
\[
 e=J_{E,W}/N,\qquad f=-J_{F,W}/N,\qquad h=H_W/N
\]
give an ordinary \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) representation with integer spins
\(0\le J\le r-1\). Let \(\rho\) be its integrated \(SU(2)\) action and,
with normalized Haar measure, define
\[
 \mathfrak G=\int_{SU(2)}\rho(g)^\dagger\rho(g)\,dg
       =\sum_{\nu=1}^{r(2r-1)^2}
                   w_\nu\rho(g_\nu)^\dagger\rho(g_\nu),
 \qquad w_\nu>0,\qquad\sum_\nu w_\nu=1 .
 \tag{SR4}
\]
The second equality is an exact finite rule, not a limiting quadrature.
Its group nodes and weights are algebraic and depend only on the width:
\(2r-1\) equally spaced angles on each Euler circle and \(r\) Gaussian
nodes for \(dt/2\), \(t=\cos\vartheta\). Fixed spin bounds make this
rule exact for every entry of the matrix product in (SR4).

In this metric \(e^\dagger=f\), \(h^\dagger=h\), and the source consists
of the trivial-spin vectors. On a nontrivial spin-\(J\) weight-zero
vector the raising coefficient is \(\sqrt{J(J+1)}\).
Consequently \(P\) is orthogonal and
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|z-Pz\|_{\mathfrak G}
      \le\frac{\|J_{E,W}z\|_{\mathfrak G}}{\sqrt2\,N},
                           \qquad z\in W_D .
 \quad}
 \tag{SR5}
\]
The residual norm uses its actual output weight \(H_W=2N\).
At four heads the complementary space is zero and this is vacuous.

At fixed width,
\(e^{-C_bN}I\preceq\mathfrak G\preceq e^{C_bN}I\).
The estimate follows from root Gaussian coefficients and the truncated
Gauss factorizations at the finitely many nodes in (SR4).
The gap (SR5) is in this specified metric; it is not a polynomial
physical singular-gap claim.

The literal corner row itself is fixed by the ordinary divided action:
\[
 \lambda_DJ_{E,W}=\lambda_DJ_{F,W}=0,\qquad\lambda_DP=\lambda_D .
 \tag{SR6}
\]
Indeed its interior ordinary caps intertwine both currents with those
on the final pair. That pair's corner has degree \(d=N-1\);
an incoming divided lowering would need degree \(d+N>2d\), while a
divided raising would need degree \(d-N<0\). Both are impossible.
This concerns the marked row after its proved whole-invariant
reduction; it does not call the raw marked cap a Hopf map.

Every actual source vector has exactly its physical norm in either
metric. With the original input \(z_{\rm in}\), corner row \(\lambda_D\)
and separate original factor \(\chi_N\),
\[
 \chi_N\lambda_D Bv
       =\chi_N\lambda_D BPv\quad(v\in W_D),\qquad
 \|z_{\rm in}\|\,\|\lambda_D\|_*
                         \le N^{k-2}.
 \tag{SR7}
\]
Here \(z_{\rm in}\) is the original cup input and the norms use the
same chosen metric. An included \(\chi_N\) multiplies the bound by
\(|\chi_N|\).
For \(\mathfrak G\), a commuting gate's norm is bounded by its physical
norm on the full graded sector \(\mathcal L_W\). A central-block-only
physical bound cannot be substituted. The split metric instead gives
the central-packet comparison stated after (SR3).

A linear residual compiler using the split metric and the literal
closing separates exactly into source and complementary energies.
Projecting all trial packets decreases its energy and preserves its
balls, so its minimum can be taken on the source. This uses the specified
metric; it does not equate older auxiliary minima in other metrics or
alter the nonlinear Conway quartic.

The remaining volume step is still quantitative and source-dependent:
estimate the source-projected word recursion or gradient and its
nonzero original closing at the required volume rate. Exact projection
requires no small-current-residual premise; (SR5) measures distance
when a trial comparison needs it. Classical gluing stationarity alone
does not supply the quantum estimate. Cancellation within \(S\) remains.
No new knot-volume class or finite-exception theorem is claimed.

## Choose the retained child by its nearest constant leaf, 24 November

There is a sharper degree bound for the actual compressed source in
[the logarithmic-degree proof](research_conway_logarithmic_reduced_residual_degree.md).
Use its complete packets, grouped original budgets and original closing.
There are \(q\) bilinear vertices, \(\ell=q+1\) constant leaves and
\(2q+1\) proper vertices. Only the choice of retained child changes.

For each vertex define
\[
 \delta(v)=0\quad(v\text{ a constant leaf}),\qquad
 \delta(v)=1+\min\{\delta(v_L),\delta(v_R)\}.
 \tag{DL1}
\]
At every product retain a child of greater \(\delta\), breaking ties
arbitrarily, and eliminate the other. Put
\(h=\max\{1,\max_v\delta(v)\}\).

Here degree bookkeeping means assigning degree zero to constants,
one to a retained independent packet, adding at a bilinear map and
taking a maximum under addition. It uses no coefficient cancellation.
The formal degree \(d(v)\) of a solved right-hand side obeys
\[
 d(v)=0\quad(v\text{ a leaf}),\qquad
 d(v)=1+d(v_{\rm eliminated\ child}).
 \tag{DL2}
\]
The choice (DL1) makes \(d(v)=\delta(v)\) at every vertex.
A retained row subtracts its own degree-one packet; a retained leaf
has its constant-minus-packet row. The original closing is linear.
Thus the resulting holomorphic reduced residual satisfies
\[
 F:\mathbb C^{Nq}\longrightarrow\mathbb C^{Nq+1},\qquad
 \deg F\le h,\qquad \deg_{\mathbb R}\|F\|^2\le2h .
 \tag{DL3}
\]

For \(q\ge1\), \(h\) is optimal for this formal bookkeeping.
Any orientation has \(d(v)\ge\delta(v)\), by induction in (DL2).
A vertex formula either appears in a retained row or the closing,
or feeds an eliminated ancestor, increasing the degree.
Thus its formal degree is counted; the degree-one subtraction
uses a maximum without cancellation. This rule attains the lower
bound at all vertices. Actual map coefficients can lower the degree.

If \(\delta(v)\ge r\), every descendant path has at least \(r\)
edges before a leaf, so the subtree contains at least \(2^r\) leaves.
Consequently
\[
 h\le\max\{1,\lfloor\log_2\ell\rfloor\}.
 \tag{DL4}
\]
The inequality can be strict. A comb has \(h=1\), at any length,
so its \(F\) is affine. At \(q=0\), \(F\) is constant and the
convention \(h=1\) is only a harmless upper bound.

The retained dimension and exact normalization remain
\(n=Nq\) and \(\widehat B_N=N^{2q+2}B_N\).
The residual \(F\) and its auxiliary integral depend on this new choice;
their numerical values can change, while the closed scalar is unchanged.
In particular
[the compact comparison](research_conway_compact_reciprocal_source.md)
applies with the unchanged unit packet balls and
\[
 \mathcal J_N=\frac{(Nq)!}{\pi^{Nq}}
       \int_{\prod_{i=1}^q\overline{\mathbb B}_N}
                     \|F(u)\|^{-2(Nq+1)}\,du,\qquad
 |K_N|^2=\frac{\widehat B_N^2}{\mathcal J_N}
                         (1+O_{\mathscr T}(N^{-1})).
 \tag{DL5}
\]
The comparison is for nonzero sources at sufficiently large levels;
at a source zero the integral is infinite and its reciprocal is zero.
The one-point convention covers \(q=0\).
All original phases, the marked closing and Casimir normals remain.

Affine \(F\) makes the unweighted compact proxy \(\|F\|^2\) quadratic.
It does not make the exact Schur energy \(F^*R(u)^{-1}F\) quadratic:
its response Gram can still vary with \(u\).
[The branching proof](research_conway_branching_quartic_source.md)
already treats exact linear-response minima after prescribed leaves
are inserted. The original scalar fiber degree is still \(\ell\)
when \(K_N\ne0\), as in the logarithmic proof.
No geometric rate or new finite-exception claim follows from (DL3).
