## A faithful degree slice removes the exponential boundary overestimate, 24 November

The [coherent corner proof](research_coherent_marked_cap_corner_reduction.md)
shows precisely how the orthogonality proposal applies to the actual source.
After the known coherent change of coordinates, one orthogonal integer-degree
slice retains the entire invariant tensor. The original closing becomes a
corner coordinate. In that smaller working packet the input and closing have
an exact polynomial norm product, at every fixed even width.

Use \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(\theta=\pi/(2N)\), and the actual \(S,\mathscr D_b,C_D,\tau\) of
(BT1)--(BT5). For \(b=2k\ge4\), put \(D=(k-1)d\) and
\(W=V^{\otimes(b-2)}\). Let \(P_t\) be physical orthogonal projection
onto integer degree \(t\). On the two-input pair the exact identity is
\[
 P_dS_A^{-1}\mathbf u=c_{\rm edge}|d,0\rangle,\qquad
 c_{\rm edge}=\frac{2C_D\tau^d}{1-q^3},\qquad
 |c_{\rm edge}|=N^2\sin3\theta .
 \tag{CQ1}
\]
The proof factors the finite Euler series only after taking this slice.
Every omitted term lowers degree by at least \(N\), and would need input
degree greater than the actual maximum \(2d\). A finite Gaussian sum
then collapses the first head to \(d\); the second gives exactly the
factor \(2/(1-q^3)\). No whole-operator factorization at the root is assumed.

The original transformed closing, restricted to the actual transformed
source \(\overline{\mathcal Y}_b=S_W^{-1}\mathscr D_b(\mathcal S_b)\),
is
\[
 \overline\Lambda_b(w)
   =c_{\rm edge}^{-1}\langle0,d|L_{\rm int}w,\qquad
 L_{\rm int}=I\otimes\ell^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes I .
 \tag{CQ2}
\]
Here \(\ell\) is the literal ordinary cap, and the last marked cap is
retained through this exact identity. It provides a different extension
of the same restricted functional from the full row \(\Lambda_bS_W\).
The intrinsic norm on the actual saturated source obeys
\[
 \frac{N^{-(3k-1)/2}}{\sin3\theta}
 \le \|\overline\Lambda_b\|_{\overline{\mathcal Y}_b^*}
 \le \frac{N^{-(k+2)/2}}{\sin3\theta}.
 \tag{CQ3}
\]
The lower bound uses an explicit regular cup matching in the saturated
source. Its seam caps contract by successive snake identities; no zero
ordinary bubble is divided out. These are bounds for the functional's
norm, not for its value on an arbitrary word state. The original
\(\chi_N\) scales the row if included.

The same calculation gives a complete reduced coordinate:
\[
 \mathscr F_b\Phi_f=P_DS_W^{-1}\mathscr D_b\Phi_f
                     =c_{\rm edge}f(|d,0\rangle),\qquad
 f(|d,0\rangle)=\frac{Q}{N^2}\Phi_{0,W,d}.
 \tag{CQ4}
\]
The ordered cup normalization fixes the displayed \(Q\).
The endpoint \(|d,0\rangle\) generates its whole pair module under
the actual \(E,F,K\) action, including all Casimir Jordan channels.
Thus this projection is faithful on every full unrolled invariant
source. The known dimension formula makes it an isomorphism onto
the middle central-degree space \(W_D\).

For the actual saturated source the image is the exact kernel
\[
 \mathscr F_b(\mathcal S_b)
  =\ker(\mathcal J_E^W:W_D\longrightarrow W_{D-N}),\qquad
 \mathcal J_E^W=
 \left[\frac{E_W(\zeta)^N}{1-\zeta^{2N}}\right]_{\zeta=q}.
 \tag{CQ5}
\]
A regular generic curried lift proves inclusion because its input
\(|d,0\rangle\) has degree \(d<N\). The previous divided-current
dimension and surjectivity theorem gives equality. Differentiated
source families retain their inhomogeneous equations.

The original input and closing in these degree coordinates are
\[
 z_{\rm in}=c_{\rm edge}|d\rangle\otimes
                      p^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes|0\rangle,\qquad
 \lambda_D=c_{\rm edge}^{-1}\langle0,d|L_{\rm int},\qquad
 \|z_{\rm in}\|\,\|\lambda_D\|=N^{k-2}.
 \tag{CQ6}
\]
The row norm here is that of its physical extension on \(W_D\).
The large full-packet norm in (BT5) is therefore unnecessary as a
boundary budget in this exact reduced representation. Faithfulness
requires transporting each original operator through \(\mathscr F_b\);
inserting \(P_D\) before untransported crossings is not justified.

The resulting Casimirs are explicit. Totals over proper blocks use the
original coproduct. With \(n=b-2\), on \(W_D\) they are
\[
 L=q^{-1}F_1K_1E_{2,\ldots,n}-K_1-K_1^{-1},\qquad
 R=qK_n^{-1}E_nF_{1,\ldots,n-1}-K_n-K_n^{-1},
 \qquad \|L\|,\|R\|\le4(n-1)+2 ,
 \tag{CQ7}
\]
at the two outer boundaries; every interior Casimir remains literal.
The original signed braid polynomials, including all repeated-root
derivatives, act on these matrices. Their degree still depends on \(N\),
and (CQ7) does not bound a coherent braid product at the volume rate.

Earlier source notes already construct central-degree modules,
polynomial boundaries and bounded-degree Casimirs. At four heads this
is the earlier opposite highest chart. The new result connects that
complete representation to this precise orthogonal slice of the
coherent marked observations and proves the intrinsic closing bounds.
It removes an exponential boundary overestimate without choosing a
replacement invariant.

The finite-exception problem is now the original coherent word estimate
in this source packet, with the polynomial boundary product (CQ6).
A geometric upper bound and a noncancellation lower bound must still
recover the knot-complement volume after every fixed short partial
filling. The finite-exception theorem remains unproved.

## Both boundary Casimirs and the original closing now have explicit formulas, 24 November

The [boundary transport proof](research_all_width_marked_boundary_casimir_transport.md)
gives the actual operators in the faithful observation coordinates.
Both outer pair Casimirs use one shared auxiliary vector. The
original closing is an explicit Fourier coefficient after the
interior ordinary caps. The formulas hold at every fixed even
width and retain the complete original source.

Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(\xi=q^{-3}\), and \(\theta=\pi/(2N)\). For \(b=2k\ge4\),
the middle physical space is \(W=V^{\otimes(b-2)}\).
Let \(E,F,K\) be its actual total operators, and let
\(E_j,F_j,K_j\) denote its individual heads. Define
\[
 C=E-\xi K,\qquad
 V_C=(1-\xi)(C+QI)^{-1},\qquad v=V_Cy .
 \tag{BT1}
\]
The inverse exists on the whole middle space, with the exact formula
\[
 C^N=(-1)^{N+1}I,\qquad
 (C+QI)^{-1}=\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(-C)^jQ^{N-1-j}.
 \tag{BT2}
\]
The denominator two is retained. This is a finite identity at
both parities and composite levels.

The four endpoint operators are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C_{L,0}&=-2K_1+q^3E_1-q^{-4}F_1K_1,\\
 C_{L,+}&=(1+q^{-2})K_1-q^3E_1+q^{-6}F_1K_1+2q^{-1}I,\\
 C_{R,0}&=qF_{b-2}-K_{b-2}^{-1}E_{b-2}-2K_{b-2}^{-1},\\
 C_{R,+}&=2qI+(1+q^2)K_{b-2}^{-1}
                         -q^3F_{b-2}+K_{b-2}^{-1}E_{b-2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Writing \(T_i=\mathscr D\Omega_{i,i+1}\mathscr D^{-1}\)
on the actual source image, the boundary formulas are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 T_1y&=C_{L,0}y+C_{L,+}QKv,\\
 T_{b-1}y&=C_{R,0}y+C_{R,+}v,\qquad
 (E-\xi K+QI)v=(1-\xi)y .
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{BT3}
\]
Every interior pair Casimir remains the literal middle operator.
The proof derives the two distinct cup transposes and their
endpoint coefficients directly; one inverse-clock contribution
cancels exactly. The shared vector \(v\) is kept in the full
middle space, since it need not satisfy the source constraints.

These Casimirs give the actual signed braid matrices through
\(\kappa r_N(T)\) and its literal inverse, where
\(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\) and \(r_N\) is the original braid polynomial.
All values and derivatives at repeated Casimir roots remain.
The bounded algebraic order in (BT3) concerns the Casimir
equations; the braid polynomial still depends on \(N\).
Their quadratic residuals describe these specified gate equations
without reconstructing the full invariant tensor at each boundary.

There is an exact orthogonal description of the shared denominator.
On a nilpotent argument define
\(\mathsf e_N(t)=\sum_{r=0}^d t^r/(Q;Q)_r\), and put
\[
 S=\mathsf e_N(EK^{-1}/\xi)^{-1},\qquad
 G_C=S^{-\dagger}S^{-1}.
\]
Then
\[
 C=-\xi SKS^{-1},\qquad
 V_C=S(1-\xi)(Q-\xi K)^{-1}S^{-1},\qquad
 \|V_C\|_{G_C}\le3,\quad \|V_C^{-1}\|_{G_C}\le N .
 \tag{BT4}
\]
The singular multipliers are
\(\sin(3\theta)/|\sin((2j-5)\theta)|\), \(0\le j<N\).
The metric and its inverse have norm \(e^{C_bN}\).
Internal braids commute with \(S\); outer coefficients, source
constraints, input and closing are all conjugated along with it.

The exact cost of the original cup input in this metric is now known.
Write
\[
 \tau=-Q^{-1},\qquad C_D=N^2\sin^2(3\theta)q^{3d},\qquad
 \mathbf u_{ac}=C_D\tau^a .
\]
On its two-head module,
\[
 \|S^{-1}\mathbf u\|^2
  =|C_D|^2\sum_{r+j\le d}|(q^{-1};Q)_r|^2
                       \left|{r+j\brack r}_Q\right|^2,\qquad
 \log\|S^{-1}\mathbf u\|=\frac{v_3}{\pi}N+O(\log N).
 \tag{BT5}
\]
Here \(v_3=3\Lambda(\pi/3)=2\Lambda(\pi/6)\) and
\(\Lambda(t)=-\int_0^t\log|2\sin s|\,ds\).
The positive identity follows by finite Euler summation and two
Parseval identities, with every cutoff and normalization retained.
An elementary half-grid product bound makes it polynomially
equivalent to \(\sum_{0\le j\le t<N}|(Q;Q)_t/(Q;Q)_j|^2\).
The action maximum occurs at \(j/N=1/6,\ t/N=5/6\).
Interior invariant cups add the exact squared norm factor
\(N^{3(k-2)}\), so the same exponential cost holds at every
fixed width. This is the prescribed input's metric cost.

The original marked closing has a polynomial physical extension
without using the full observation inverse. Put
\[
 \alpha_4(y)=\frac{c_\Lambda}{N}\sum_{a=0}^d Q^{-a}y_{0,a},
 \qquad c_\Lambda=\frac{(-1)^dN(1-q^3)}{2C_Dq^4}.
\]
Use the literal cap \(\ell_{ac}=(-q^{-1})^a\delta_{a+c,d}/N\)
and set \(L_{\rm int}=I\otimes\ell^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes I\).
Then
\[
 \Lambda(y)=\alpha_4L_{\rm int}y,\qquad
 \|\alpha_4L_{\rm int}\|_{\rm ph}
                  =\frac{N^{-(k+1)/2}}{\sin3\theta}.
 \tag{BT6}
\]
The proof compares the literal last-mark contraction with the full
Hermite functional of the pair Casimir, then extracts its top
coefficient by a finite Fourier row. The external original
\(\chi_N\) remains a multiplier. In the coherent coordinates
the row is \((\alpha_4L_{\rm int})S\); (BT6) does not estimate
that changed row.

The complete period is therefore specified by the actual input,
the transported signed generators and this original row, on
the constrained source image. A general original coherent
closing can still cancel. Neither the bound three nor (BT5)
proves its volume-rate lower bound after every fixed short
partial filling. That estimate and the finite-exception theorem
remain open.

## The marked-mode observations retain the complete source at every width, 24 November

The [source observation proof](research_all_width_marked_mode_observation.md)
settles the earlier question about losing information in the marked-mode
coordinates. These particular observations are faithful on the entire
actual invariant tensor, at every fixed even width. The proof has a
direct finite Fourier and Gaussian-binomial form. It replaces the
longer proposed argument through separate Casimir primary blocks.

Use \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(x=-q^{-1}\), \(\theta=\pi/(2N)\), and
\(\sigma=-q^{-1}-q^2\). The two endpoint rows are
\[
 \eta_a=\frac{1-q^3}{2}q^{3a},\qquad
 \zeta_a=\frac{1-q^{-3}}2x^a.
\]
For even \(b\), let \(\mathcal I_b\) be the full actual invariant
space with unrolled weight zero, and let \(\mathcal S_b\) be its
saturated generic source subspace. The observation
\[
 \mathscr D_b=(\eta\otimes I_{V^{\otimes(b-2)}}\otimes\zeta)
                   \big|_{\mathcal I_b}
 \tag{WM1}
\]
is injective on both spaces. Its explicit inverse satisfies
\[
 \|\Phi\|_{\rm ph}\le e^{C_bN}\|\mathscr D_b\Phi\|_{\rm ph},
 \qquad \|\mathscr D_b\|\le C/N .
 \tag{WM2}
\]
Thus its pullback norm is positive on the whole source, with
controlled exponential change of metric. Polynomial conditioning
is not asserted.

The source-specific reason for injectivity is elementary. Let
\(A=V\otimes V\), let \(W=V^{\otimes(b-2)}\), and use the literal
cups to write
\[
 \Phi_f=(I\otimes f\otimes I)(p\otimes p),\qquad
 \mathscr D_b\Phi_f=f(\mathbf u),\qquad
 \mathbf u_{ab}=C_D(-Q^{-1})^a,\quad
 C_D=N^2\sin^2(3\theta)q^{3d}.
 \tag{WM3}
\]
All scalars in this identity are retained. The \(N^2\) vectors
\(K_A^sE_A^r\mathbf u\), \(0\le r,s<N\), form a basis.
A Fourier transform in \(Q^{-(a+b)}\) and a triangular finite
Gaussian-binomial transform in \(Q^{-b}\) give its explicit inverse.

In that triangular transform the nonzero diagonal products are
\(L_k=\prod_{j=1}^k(Q^{-j}-q^{-3})\). Their bounds follow from
the complete product, without separate estimates at each channel:
\[
 \prod_{j=1}^N|Q^{-j}-q^{-3}|=2,\qquad
 2^{k-N+1}\le|L_k|\le2^k .
 \tag{WM4}
\]
The forward and inverse Gaussian-binomial formulas both have
\(e^{CN}\) coefficient bounds. Their Fourier normalizations add
only polynomial factors. The reconstruction uses known words in
\(E,K\) of length \(O(N)\); on any fixed-width physical middle
module these words have norm \(e^{C_bN}\). This proves (WM2)
without multiplying \(N\) separate inverse losses.

The image is also specified. Writing
\(B_\sigma=F-EK^{-1}+\sigma K^{-1}\) for the total middle
operators, there is a known polynomial \(\mathfrak a_H(E,K)\)
such that
\[
 \mathscr D_b(\mathcal I_b)
 =\{y:(B_\sigma-\sigma)y=0,\quad
              (H_W-\mathfrak a_H^W)y=0\}.
 \tag{WM5}
\]
Here \(H_W\) is the unrolled weight operator.
The polynomial is fixed by the explicit reconstructors and
\(\mathfrak a_H^A\mathbf u=H_A\mathbf u\).
The saturated source keeps the additional actual divided-current
equation \(\mathcal J_E^{(b)}\Phi_{f_y}=0\).
It is not replaced by the larger free coideal kernel. The
inhomogeneous equations for parameter derivatives remain separate.

At four heads the previously calibrated coefficients are exactly
the height coordinates of \(\mathscr D_4R_{12}^-\Phi\). If these
coefficients are \(a_l\), the original boundary identity is
\[
 (\ell_{12}\otimes m_{34})R_{23}^+\Phi
     =\beta_N\frac{2\kappa}{1-q^3}\sum_l a_l .
 \tag{WM6}
\]
The original factor \(\chi_N\) remains. Restoring a bare closing
requires the literal \(R_{23}^-\) in the preceding word; the
\(R_{12}^-\) already belongs to the coordinate map. All ordinary
caps, the marked cap and pair-Casimir derivative channels remain.

For general words the transported action is
\(\mathscr D_b R_i\mathscr D_b^{-1}\) on the constrained actual
image, and products transport exactly. There is no projection
between unrelated channels. These are linear coordinate changes,
so they preserve polynomial degree in packet variables; their
actual metric costs must still be included in any recompilation.
No estimate for the global recompiled minimum is inferred here.

This settles source faithfulness for the observations supporting
the local normal-gap and overlap estimates. It does not prove that
the original coherent closing has the hyperbolic-volume rate after
an arbitrary fixed short partial filling. That lower estimate,
and hence the finite-exception theorem, remains open.

## The marked overlap has an exact, conditioned quantum equation, 24 November

The [cyclic connection proof](research_coideal_cyclic_quantum_connection.md)
gives a further simplification of the actual opposed marked overlap.
Its entire array of height values is determined by a first-order
linear equation, including the endpoint. The inverse has polynomial
norm. This removes the need for an auxiliary minimization for this
specified coefficient; it does not eliminate the coherent closing
of a general short component.

Put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(z_l=Q^l\), and
\(G_l=\kappa\gamma_{N,l}\), with the original phase and overlap in
(OM1)--(OM2). On \(R_N=\mathbb Z[q,1/2][z]/(z^N-1)\), let
\(Sf(z)=f(Qz)\). The source equation is
\[
 \mathcal A G=h,\qquad
 \mathcal A=(q-z)^2-z^2(1-Qz)^2S,\qquad
 h=-2qz(1-qz^2).
 \tag{QC1}
\]
At the last clock point, the shift coefficient is zero. The
last row fixes \(G_{N-1}=2/(1-q^3)\); it does not identify a
nonperiodic tail with its first value.

Set \(a=(q-z)^2\), \(b=z^2(1-Qz)^2\), and
\(\mathcal T=M_{a^{-1}b}S\), where \(M_f\) means multiplication
by \(f\). Then \(\mathcal A=M_a(I-\mathcal T)\) and
\(\mathcal T^N=0\). Its exact finite inverse therefore retains
every boundary term. In the counting norm of the clock values,
\[
 \det\mathcal A=4,\qquad
 \|\mathcal A^{-1}\|_2\le CN^6,\qquad
 \|g-G\|_2\le CN^6\|\mathcal A g-h\|_2.
 \tag{QC2}
\]
The constants are uniform over both parities and composite
levels. The squared residual in (QC2) is a quadratic polynomial
in \(N\) complex coordinates, with a unique zero. It gives an
absolute error certificate for this actual block, rather than
a volume estimate for a supplied geometric trial field.

There is also a precise integral source line. The operator
\[
 \mathcal B=(1-qz^2)S-Q(1-qQ^2z^2)
\]
annihilates \(h\), and
\[
 \ker(\mathcal B\mathcal A)=\mathbb Z[q,1/2]\,G .
 \tag{QC3}
\]
The normalization (QC1) fixes the original vector. The proof
uses explicit geometric-series inverses and the characteristic-zero
domain; it does not invert \(N\), claim that \(G\) is a
multiplicative unit, or assert the same kernel after arbitrary
torsion base change. The auxiliary classical symbol is
\[
 (1-z)^2(1-z^2)(L-1)(1-z^2L).
\]
The coefficient factors remain in the exact equation. No knot
peripheral eigenvalue or geometric \(A\)-component is assigned
to this height clock.

Requiring the same displayed equation to hold in \(\mathbb C(z)\)
selects one rational representative \(\mathscr G_N(z)\).
Its cyclic determinant, before setting \(z^N=1\), is
\[
 \mathfrak D(Z)=(1+Z)^2-Z^2(1-Z)^2
             =(1+Z^2)(1+2Z-Z^2),\qquad Z=z^N .
 \tag{QC4}
\]
The representative agrees with every actual clock value and
obeys \(\mathscr G_N(z)=\mathscr G_N(q/z)\). It therefore descends
to \(\widehat G_N(\rho)\), where \(\rho=z+q/z\). For every fixed
compact set \(K\subset\mathbb C\setminus[-2,2]\),
\[
 \widehat G_N(\rho)=\frac{2}{2-\rho}+O_K(N^{-1}).
 \tag{QC5}
\]
This holds holomorphically, with the same order of error for
each fixed derivative on a smaller compact set. The function
is nonzero on a buffered neighborhood of \(K\) eventually.
Restoring the original boundary factor gives
\(c_K/N\le|\beta_N\bar\kappa\,\widehat G_N|\le C_K/N\);
any original \(\chi_N\) remains separate.

This continuation is specified by the exact rational equation.
It is not an arbitrary interpolation of a real-grid asymptotic.
Its possible poles satisfy \(p_N(\rho)=2,2i,-2i\), and approach
the limiting cut. A deformation across them must retain the
residues. Equality with an independently defined moving-color
period, its meridian derivatives, or its moving quantum parameter
has not been established.

For the finite-exception argument, this controls one actual
coherent boundary coefficient and its complex-height representative.
It does not yet control the original scalar after every fixed
short partial filling. The global noncancellation estimate and
the knot-complement volume rate remain unproved.

## The opposite-sign marked overlap has a uniform lower bound, 24 November

The [signed overlap proof](research_coideal_opposed_marked_mode_overlap.md)
now estimates the particular coefficient left open by the previous
normal-gap calculation. It is a lower bound for an actual coherent
coefficient of the two marked modes, with the original phases retained.
It holds uniformly over all height labels at sufficiently large levels.
It is not a lower bound for an arbitrary attached vector.

Use \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(\kappa=q^{(N-1)^2/2}\), and the marked
row \(r_l\), right mode \(s_l=B^+e_*\), and actual signed crossing
matrices of (NG1). Since \(B^-=\overline{B^+}\), the opposed
coefficient is
\[
 \gamma_{N,l}=r_lB^-e_*=r_l\overline{s_l}.
\]
There are universal constants \(N_0,c_0,C>0\) such that
\[
 \operatorname{Re}(\kappa\gamma_{N,l})\ge c_0N^{-3},
 \qquad c_0N^{-3}\le|\gamma_{N,l}|\le CN^4
 \quad(N\ge N_0,\ 0\le l<N).
 \tag{OM1}
\]
The phase correction is the same for every label. In particular,
sums with nonnegative real coefficients satisfy the same real-part
lower bound multiplied by the sum of their coefficients. No sign
condition on a general exterior packet has been inferred.
Restoring the original boundary factor gives
\(|\beta_N\gamma_{N,l}|\ge c_0N^{-4}\); an original factor
\(\chi_N\) remains explicit.

The exact reduction keeps the phase from the leading continuant
and the derivative of the coideal characteristic polynomial.
Put \(d=N-1\), \(Q=q^2\), and use the cumulative factors \(U_t,V_l\)
of (CC1). Then
\[
 \begin{split}
 W_t&=|U_t|^2,\qquad E_t=q^{2t^2-t},\\
 H_l&=\sum_{t=l}^{d}(E_t-E_{t+1})W_t,\qquad E_N=-1,\\
 \gamma_{N,l}
   &=\bar\kappa\,\frac{|V_l|^2}{2}\,\overline{E_l}H_l .
 \end{split}
 \tag{OM2}
\]
The factor \(\overline{E_l}\) follows from the original source;
it has not been chosen to align separate coefficients.

On the decreasing part of \(W_t\), an exact summation-by-parts
identity writes \(\operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_l}H_l)\) as a
positive weighted sum of squared distances on the unit circle.
It gives a lower bound \(1/(4N^2)\) there at every level.
For the remaining labels, the proof establishes the uniform estimates
\[
 W_t=N\sin(\pi t/N)+O(1),\qquad
 W_t-W_{t-1}=\pi\cos(\pi t/N)
                   +O(1/t+1/(N-t)).
\]
The first estimate includes \(0\le t<N\); the second uses \(1\le t<N\).
Thus the oscillatory remainder reduces to two quadratic Fourier sums.
Their exact paired identity is
\[
 \sum_{t=0}^{N-1}e^{2\pi it^2/N}
 +\sqrt q\sum_{t=0}^{N-1}e^{2\pi i(t^2-t)/N}
                  =(1+i)\sqrt N .
 \tag{OM3}
\]
The written proof derives its phase by Gaussian Fourier transformation;
it does not use a modulus estimate to guess the sign.
A uniform incomplete-sum bound controls the interior labels.
For \(l=O(\sqrt N)\), including the boundary term and the original
source phase gives an explicitly positive real Fresnel symbol,
with a uniform remainder. These estimates give one
threshold \(N_0\) for all labels, including both level parities and
composite levels. The classical methods and coverage references
are distinguished from the source-specific coefficient theorem.

Away from the two endpoints there is a more precise result:
for each fixed \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\),
\[
 \kappa\gamma_{N,l}
 =\frac{1+O_\varepsilon(N^{-1/2})}
          {2\sin^2((l-\tfrac12)\pi/N)}
 \quad(\varepsilon N\le l\le(1-\varepsilon)N).
 \tag{OM4}
\]
The error is complex; the displayed principal amplitude is positive.
For \(l/N\to a\in(0,1)\), it tends to \(1/(2\sin^2\pi a)\),
or \(-2z/(1-z)^2\) with auxiliary height parameter \(z=e^{2\pi ia}\).
This parameter has not been identified with a knot peripheral
eigenvalue. The endpoint proof is separate; (OM4) is not continued
into its poles or asserted for complex geometric colors.

The new scalar lower bound also repairs the original marked gauge
for the opposite-sign normal equation. Let
\[
 T_l^{\rm opp}=q\,\overline{J_l-\mu_*I},\qquad
 \Pi_l^{\rm opp}=\frac{\overline{s_l}r_l}{\gamma_{N,l}} .
 \tag{OM5}
\]
Then \(r_l\Pi_l^{\rm opp}=r_l\) and
\(\|\Pi_l^{\rm opp}\|_2\le CN^7\). The conjugated normal gap gives
\[
 \|(I-\Pi_l^{\rm opp})w\|_{\rm ht}
                      \le CN^{19}\|T_l^{\rm opp}w\|_{\rm ht}.
 \tag{OM6}
\]
For every compatible forcing \(\overline{r_l}f=0\), the equation
\(T_l^{\rm opp}w=f,\ r_lw=0\) has a unique solution with this bound.
The compatibility row is \(\overline{r_l}\); the preserved original
observation is \(r_l\). The projector need not commute with the operator.

This settles the specified opposite-sign marked-mode overlap and
its compatible local normal solve. All original cap, framing and
exterior factors remain. The preceding general crossing word must
still be kept before the final boundary observation. Neither
nonnegative coefficients nor small normal residuals have been
proved for every exterior produced by fixed short fillings.
Their complete coherent scalar and its geometric volume rate
remain the missing global estimate. The finite-exception theorem
has not been proved.

## A polynomial bound controls the error transverse to the marked mode, 24 November

The [marked-boundary normal estimate](research_coideal_marked_boundary_normal_gap.md)
now controls an actual crossing equation, rather than just the norm
of the cumulative matrix. At the literal marked boundary the equation
splits into paths. The compatible equation on the path selected by
that boundary can be solved with polynomial loss, even though its
edge weights are complex. This gives a specified positive metric in
which the original marked coefficient is an orthogonal coordinate.

Here “normal” means a vector component transverse to one specified
line. It does not mean a first derivative at a colliding Casimir root;
all those original derivative channels remain present.
Put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(\kappa=q^{(N-1)^2/2}\),
\(\mu_j=q^{2j}+q^{1-2j}\), and \(\mu_*=-q^{-1}-q^2\).
For each fixed neighboring height \(\rho=\mu_l\), the source selects
a path of \(N-l\) coordinates. Let \(J_l\) be the restriction of the
actual adjacent-crossing difference operator to that path.
The known boundary row \(r_l\) has entries
\(\Phi_{\mu_j,\rho}(-q)\) on its support. Its right partner is the
actual crossing column \(s_l=B^+_{c,\rho}e_*\), where \(c=1+q\)
and \(e_*\) is the coordinate at \(\mu_*\). Their exact equations are
\[
 r_lJ_l=\mu_*r_l,\qquad J_ls_l=\mu_*s_l,\qquad
             r_ls_l=\frac{2\kappa}{1-q^3}.
 \tag{NG1}
\]
The row is the literal marked boundary, divided only by its recorded
nonzero scalar factor. The latter is restored in the original source.
All the components of \(r_l,s_l\) on this path have polynomial
upper and lower bounds, uniformly over \(l\) and every level.

Set \(L_l=J_l-\mu_*I\), \(D_r=\operatorname{diag}(r_l)\),
and \(D_s=\operatorname{diag}(s_l)\). The exact factorization is
\[
 D_rL_lD_s=-D^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_i)D,
 \qquad
 (Dz)_i=z_{i+1}-z_i,\qquad
              c_0N^{-6}\le|\omega_i|\le CN^5.
 \tag{NG2}
\]
Here \(c_0,C\) are universal positive constants. The original
operator itself has zero couplings at the endpoints of this path.
The factorization does not remove a nonzero cyclic current.
On a path, \(D\) maps the complement of the constants bijectively
onto the edge space. Its transpose is injective there.
The two least singular values and the nonzero diagonal weights
therefore give an inverse bound for (NG2) without requiring
\(\omega_i\) to be positive.

Equivalently, for compatible data \(r_lf=0\), the edge currents
are the partial sums \(\sum_{a\le i}r_af_a\); dividing them by
\(\omega_i\) and integrating once gives a solution of \(L_lw=f\).
Compatibility is exactly the last-vertex equation, not an
additional terminal Dirichlet condition.
The resulting estimates are
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_2(w,\mathbb Cs_l)\le CN^{11}\|L_lw\|_2,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{dist}_{\rm ht}(w,\mathbb Cs_l)
                       \le CN^{12}\|L_lw\|_{\rm ht}.
 \tag{NG3}
\]
They hold at every \(N\ge2\). The two-dimensional endpoint is
checked directly in the written proof; a singleton has only zero
compatible forcing.

There is also a stable gauge preserving the actual marked row.
Define
\[
 \Pi_l=\frac{s_lr_l}{r_ls_l},\qquad
 H_{\rm mark}=\Pi_l^\dagger H_{\rm ht}\Pi_l+
                (I-\Pi_l)^\dagger H_{\rm ht}(I-\Pi_l).
 \tag{NG4}
\]
Then \(r_l\Pi_l=r_l\),
\(\tfrac12H_{\rm ht}\le H_{\rm mark}\le CN^7H_{\rm ht}\),
and \(\mathbb Cs_l\) is orthogonal to \(\ker r_l\) in this metric.
The exact coefficient on that line is \(r_lw/(r_ls_l)\), including
its original phase. In either prescribed metric,
\[
             \|(I-\Pi_l)w\|\le CN^{15}\|L_lw\|.
 \tag{NG5}
\]
Thus \(L_lw=f,\ r_lw=0\) has a unique polynomially bounded solution
for every compatible \(f\). The Gram equals \(H_{\rm ht}\) on
\(\ker r_l\), which is why changing to it introduces no extra
loss in (NG5). This supplies a quadratic boundary-error block for
the variational problem; it does not increase the degree of that
linear block or introduce an unknown word-dependent metric.

These formulas can be used at the final boundary of an arbitrary
incoming vector: coordinate projection onto the selected path
commutes with \(J\) and leaves the boundary row unchanged.
The full preceding word must still be retained. This is not
permission to project before other crossings, which can mix the
paths. The earlier ordinary caps, the boundary scalar \(\beta_N\),
and the original exterior factor \(\chi_N\) remain explicit.

The estimate controls transverse error but leaves the coefficient
in (NG4) free. A crossing of the opposite sign involves the marked
mode of \(J\) and the different operator \(q\overline J\); their
required signed overlap is not estimated here. Nor has a geometric
trial field with sufficiently small actual residual been constructed.
The closed-scalar lower bound after arbitrary fixed short partial
fillings, and hence the finite-exception theorem, remain unproved.

## The boundary between two cap pairs is a cumulative sum, 24 November

The [boundary calculation](research_coideal_cap_straddling_cumulative_kernel.md)
now treats a crossing between an ordinary cap and the original final
marked cap. This is different from the crossing between the two legs
of the marked pair in (HB6). The complete contraction of both caps
with this crossing has an exact triangular support and a weighted
cumulative-sum factorization. The calculation holds at every
\(N\ge2\), for both crossing signs and at arbitrary fixed width.

Here is its finite matrix. Put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(c=1+q\), \(d=N-1\), \(\theta=\pi/(2N)\), and
\(\mu_j=Q^j+qQ^{-j}\), \(0\le j<N\). Use the complete finite
polynomial \(\Phi_{\rho,\nu}\) defined by the continuant recurrence
in the linked proof, without a Casimir quotient. Permute the row
label \(l\) by
\[
 t(l)=
 \begin{cases}
 [N/2-l]_N,&N\ \text{even},\\
 [(N-1)/2+l]_N,&N\ \text{odd}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the matrix \(P_{t(l),j}=\Phi_{\mu_j,\mu_l}(q^{-1})\)
satisfies
\[
 \begin{split}
 P&=\operatorname{diag}(U_t)L\operatorname{diag}(V_j),
       &L_{tj}&=\mathbf1_{j\le t},\\
 U_t&=\prod_{h=1}^t\frac{1-Q^{-h}}{1-q^{2h-1}},
       &V_j&=\frac{2}{U_j(1-q^{2j-1})},\qquad U_0=1 .
 \end{split}
 \tag{CC1}
\]
Thus \(P_{t,j}=0\) exactly when \(j>t\). All the surviving entries
become positive after the displayed row and column phases are
removed; those phases must also be retained on an attached state.
The inverse is the explicit first difference
\[
 P^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(V^{-1})\nabla
                  \operatorname{diag}(U^{-1}),\qquad
 (\nabla z)_j=z_j-z_{j-1},\quad z_{-1}=0 .
 \tag{CC2}
\]
There is no additional terminal boundary condition.
The half-grid sine product and a finite Wallis-product bound give,
with universal positive constants \(c_0,C\),
\[
 1\le |U_t|\le C\sqrt N,\qquad
 c_0N^{-1/2}\le |V_j|\le N,\qquad
 \|P\|\le CN^{5/2},\quad
 \|P^{-1}\|\le C\sqrt N,\quad
 \det P=2^{N-1}.
 \tag{CC3}
\]
In particular every surviving entry has zero exponential rate.
This boundary contributes no additional positive cell volume.

For four heads the actual row is
\((\ell_{12}\otimes m_{34})R_{23}^{\pm}\) on the conserved
external channel \(\mathcal E_c\). Its remaining final height is
forced to \(\mu_*\); the two free heights \(\nu,\rho\) give
\[
 M^+_{\nu,\rho}=\beta_N\,
        \overline{\Phi_{\rho,\nu}(q^{-1})},\qquad
 \beta_N=\frac{T_*}{A_c}\frac{\kappa_N(1-q)}2,\qquad
 M^-=q^6\overline{M^+}.
 \tag{CC4}
\]
Here \(A_c,T_*,\mu_*\) are the original boundary constants in the
height-pairing proof. The marked cap has not been moved. Both
\(\nu\) and \(\rho\) are input coordinates of this boundary tensor;
its interpretation as a matrix is a declared reshaping.
In the orthonormal height coordinates the matrix is
\[
 \widehat M^+_{\nu,\rho}
  =g_0\sqrt{\sin\alpha_\nu}\,
       \overline{\Phi_{\rho,\nu}(q^{-1})}\sqrt{\sin\alpha_\rho},
 \qquad g_0=\beta_N\sqrt{\sin\theta\sin3\theta},\qquad
 |g_0|=\frac1{N^2}\sqrt{\frac{\sin\theta}{\sin3\theta}}.
 \tag{CC5}
\]
The angles \(\alpha_\xi=\arccos(\xi/(2\sqrt q))\) are the
sorted root angles. For either crossing sign,
\(\|\widehat M^\pm\|\le C\sqrt N\) and
\(\|(\widehat M^\pm)^{-1}\|\le CN^{7/2}\).
The conditioning is polynomial uniformly over every channel.

This gives a concrete positive boundary Gram rather than an
unspecified search over metrics. In the permuted order write
\(\widehat M^+=D_aLD_b\) using the known factors in (CC1) and
(CC5). Then
\[
 \begin{split}
 G_\partial&=(\widehat M^+)^{-\dagger}(\widehat M^+)^{-1},\\
 \|y\|_{G_\partial}^2
    &=\sum_{j=0}^d |(z_j-z_{j-1})/b_j|^2,\qquad
                  z_j=y_j/a_j,\quad z_{-1}=0 .
 \end{split}
 \tag{CC6}
\]
The Gram is tridiagonal, its eigenvalues lie in
\([c_0/N,CN^7]\), and
\((\widehat M^+)^\dagger G_\partial\widehat M^+=I\).
Its determinant is exactly \(|g_0|^{-2N}\) in the stated order.
This is a quadratic sum of local boundary residuals, useful in the
fixed-degree variational formulation. It concerns the output of
the matrix reshaping. For the original bilinear pairing
\(x^{\mathsf T}\widehat M^+v\), the corresponding primal metric
on \(x\) is \(G_\partial^{-\mathsf T}\).

At width \(2k\), the earlier ordinary caps retain their exact
height constraints and factors. Each has norm
\(1/(N\sin\theta)\) in its selected \(c\) sector. Their fixed-width
composition therefore has polynomial cost. The literal final
marked cap and the external factor \(\chi_N\) remain original;
no polynomial estimate for \(\chi_N\) is added here.

This settles the boundary factorization and its conditioning, not
the coherent scalar contraction with an arbitrary short component.
An invertible matrix can have zero pairing with a prescribed
exterior array. The missing finite-exception estimate still has
to control that actual scalar and recover the knot-complement
volume after every fixed short partial filling. The quadratic
boundary block does not by itself supply such a lower certificate.

## One height metric has polynomial original boundary costs, 24 November

The [height pairing and boundary proof](research_coideal_height_pairing_and_marked_boundary.md)
now gives one specified positive metric for the complete coideal path
basis. In this metric both original boundary packets have polynomial
norms, and the crossing normalization has no neighboring \(h_N\)-volume
corrections. This replaces the earlier choice of positive form; it does
not discard the large channels found in that earlier form.

Fix the same root conventions and put
\(\alpha_r=(r+\tfrac12)\pi/N\), \(d=N-1\),
\(\theta=\pi/(2N)\). The known physical Krein form admits the
explicit conserved half-Cartan twist
\[
 H'_N=H_NK^{1/2},\qquad
 H'_Ne_a=q^{1+d/2+a}e_{d-a}.
\]
For every conditional coideal eigenvector the exact signed pairing is
\[
 u_{\lambda_r}(\sigma)^\dagger H'_N u_{\lambda_t}(\sigma)
       =\delta_{rt}(-1)^{r+1}\csc\alpha_r .
 \tag{HB1}
\]
Its diagonal is independent of the neighboring height \(\sigma\).
Tensoring along the complete nested paths identifies this diagonal
with the physical tensor form \((H'_N)^{\otimes b}\). Existence of a
common indefinite form was already known; its exact expression in
these height coordinates is the additional calculation.

If \(\Psi\) has the complete path vectors as columns, define
\[
 D_{\boldsymbol\nu}=\prod_{j=0}^{b-1}\csc\alpha_{r_j},
 \qquad G_{\rm ht}=\Psi^{-\dagger}D\Psi^{-1},
 \quad \nu_j=\lambda_{r_j},\quad \nu_b=c .
 \tag{HB2}
\]
The external height is included. This takes the absolute values of
the diagonal in the specified nonunitary height basis; it is not
the physical spectral absolute value of \(H'_N\), which is the identity.
The complete basis and its inverse have \(e^{O_b(N)}\) physical
norms, while \(D\) has polynomial entries. Thus
\(\|\log G_{\rm ht}\|=O_b(N)\).

All actual braid generators now use this single positive form.
Normalizing a crossing that changes \(r\) to \(r'\) multiplies
its same-frame coefficient only by
\(\sqrt{\sin\alpha_r/\sin\alpha_{r'}}\). In the signed chamber
of (SC1) this gives
\[
 \widetilde B^+_{r',r}
  =(-1)^{r'}\sqrt{\sin\alpha_r\sin\alpha_{r'}}
       \frac{f_vf_s}{f_{r'}f_r}J_N,\qquad
 \widetilde B^-=\overline{\widetilde B^+},\qquad
 \log|\widetilde B^\pm|=NV_{\rm sew}/\pi+O(\log N).
 \tag{HB3}
\]
The neighboring heights are \(v,s\), and \(f_r\) is the explicit
quadratic phase in (SC4). No \(h_N\)-volume correction remains.
The positive form is not asserted to be preserved by the crossings;
their signed conserved form remains indefinite.

The original turns are also explicit in this basis. Put
\[
 A_\lambda=\frac{N^2q^dx^{-d}}{p_N'(\lambda)}.
\]
A cup in any tail sector has coefficients \(A_\lambda\);
an ordinary cap has coefficient
\(\delta_{\eta,\sigma}/A_\sigma\), independent of the middle
height. The proof uses the exact endpoint inverse row and a
degree-\(N-1\) Lagrange identity. It never divides by an ordinary
bubble, which is zero here. The exact sector map norms are
\[
 \|\operatorname{Cup}_\sigma\|^2
     =N^2\csc\theta\csc\alpha_\sigma,\qquad
 \|\operatorname{Cap}_\sigma\|^2
     =N^{-2}\csc\theta\csc\alpha_\sigma .
 \tag{HB4}
\]
These are polynomial uniformly over every allowed tail height.

For \(b=2k\), the actual cup tensor lies in the conserved full
external channel \(\mathcal E_c=\ker(B_c^{(2k)}-cI)\).
The literal last marked row is computed directly, without moving
the mark. Its even heights are \(c\), its final odd height is
\(\mu_*=\lambda_{N-2}\), and its other odd heights are free.
Writing \(\ell_0\) for the original unscaled row, the exact norms are
\[
 \|u_0\|_{G_{\rm ht}}^2=(N^2\csc^2\theta)^k,\qquad
 \|\ell_0|_{\mathcal E_c}\|_{G_{\rm ht}^{-1}}^2
   =(N^2\sin^2\theta)^{1-k}\frac{\sin\theta}{N^2\sin3\theta}.
 \tag{HB5}
\]
The first norm and the row's reciprocal size are polynomial at fixed
width; the row norm is \(\Theta_k(N^{-1})\).
The external original factor \(\chi_N\) remains explicit and multiplies
the row norm by \(|\chi_N|\). This is a source-exact restriction to a
conserved channel, not a bound on the marked row at every external height.

There is a uniform boundary coefficient calculation as well.
For a crossing between the two legs of the marked pair, the complete
mixed sum evaluates to a single finite product:
\[
 b^+_\lambda=\frac{\kappa_N}{N}
       \overline{\Phi_{\lambda,c}(-q)}
       =\eta_{N,A}W_{N,A},\qquad
 W_{N,A}=\frac1{N\sin\theta}
       \prod_{h=1}^A\frac{\sin(h\pi/N)}{\sin((h-\tfrac12)\pi/N)} .
 \tag{HB6}
\]
The integer \(A\) has the parity-correct value from the full finite
product, and \(\eta_{N,A}\) is its exact unit phase.
All factors are nonzero. Unimodality, the half-grid sine product and
\(\sin t/t\) monotonicity prove
\[
 2/\pi\le W_{N,A}\le C\sqrt N,\qquad
 b^-_\lambda=-q^3\overline{b^+_\lambda},\qquad
 c_0/N\le
 |b^\pm_\lambda\sqrt{\sin\theta\sin\alpha_\lambda}|
 \le C_0 .
 \tag{HB7}
\]
This holds for every \(N\ge2\) and every channel, not merely a
maximizing mode or the interior of (SC1).
Its phase is the same single-height chirp:
\(\eta_{N,A}=\zeta_N f_r^{-1}\),
\(\zeta_N=i^dq^{d(N-4)/4}\).
The entire original row after this pair-leg crossing has norm between
\(c_k\) and \(C_k\sqrt N\) on \(\mathcal E_c\), apart from \(\chi_N\).
It is an identity for arbitrary graph exteriors in that channel.
On actual invariant sources a terminal curl may already collapse;
this is not a new curl-survival assertion or a claim about a crossing
between two different cap pairs.

The fixed-degree variational problem can now use these specified spaces,
measures and polynomial boundary budgets. Recompilation must retain the
actual \(N^{b-1}\)-dimensional external channel; the earlier
\(N\)-dimensional Conway packet budgets are not silently reused.
What remains is a lower bound for the complete coherent matrix element,
including mixed phases and channels outside (SC1), and its identification
with the knot-complement volume. Nonzero entries of a boundary row do
not prevent its contraction with an exterior vector from vanishing.
The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## A signed overlap has a nonzero volume contribution, 24 November

The [signed chamber proof](research_coideal_crossing_signed_volume_chamber.md)
now gives a lower bound for an actual mixed coideal coefficient,
with its phases retained. This goes beyond the earlier positive
graph norm. It is a universal local estimate under explicit algebraic
conditions; arbitrary short components and the marked closing are
not yet controlled.

For the roots and continuants of (CT1)--(CT3), define
\[
 \Sigma_N=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}
 \frac{\overline{D_a(\lambda_1;\sigma_1)}
                   D_a(\lambda_2;\sigma_2)}{|F_a|^2},\quad
 a_i=\frac{\lambda_i}{2\sqrt q},\quad
 b_i=\frac{\sigma_i}{2\sqrt q}\in[-1,1].
\]
All four normalized coordinates are real. The chamber is
\[
 a_i+b_j>0\quad(1\le i,j\le2),\qquad
 \Delta=(b_1+b_2-a_1-a_2)^2-8(a_1a_2+b_1b_2)<0 .
 \tag{SC1}
\]
The constants below are uniform on any fixed compact subset
\(\mathcal C\) of this chamber, for every actual root quadruple
in it and all sufficiently large \(N\). There is no restriction
to one knot or one tangle word.

Let \(\Phi_i(z)=\sum_aD_a(\lambda_i;\sigma_i)z^a/F_a\), whose
finite product is in the complete proof, and put
\[
 A_N=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}|\Phi_1(e^{it})\Phi_2(e^{it})|\,dt .
\]
The signed estimate is
\[
 \Sigma_N=\eta_N A_N(1+O_{\mathcal C}(e^{-\epsilon_{\mathcal C}N})),
 \qquad
 \log A_N=\frac N\pi V_{\rm sew}+O_{\mathcal C}(\log N).
 \tag{SC2}
\]
Here \(\eta_N\) is an explicitly calibrated unit phase.
In particular \(\eta_N^{-1}\Sigma_N\) is exactly real and
strictly positive for large \(N\). This estimates the whole signed
integral, including its complementary arcs.

The algebraic criterion supplies both the saddle and its uniqueness.
Writing \(n(x)=(x-a_1)(x-a_2)\), \(d(x)=(x+b_1)(x+b_2)\),
one has \(n+d>0\) by \(\Delta<0\), while
\[
 n-d=(a_1+a_2+b_1+b_2)(x_*-x),\qquad
 x_*=\frac{a_1a_2-b_1b_2}{a_1+a_2+b_1+b_2}.
\]
Thus the circle energy has one global maximum on the
negative circle, inside a common zero-free arc of both products.
Their equal degrees and unit-circle zeros make their relative phase
exactly constant there. The rest of the circle has a uniform
exponential loss. This proves the signed lower bound, rather than
inferring it from an absolute-value maximum alone.

There is a genuine geometric seam. Put
\(\alpha_i=\arccos a_i\), \(\beta_i=\arccos b_i\),
\(\psi_i=(\pi-\alpha_i-\beta_i)/2\), and
\(u_i=(\arccos x_*-\alpha_i)/2\).
Take one tetrahedron of each of the following four types:
\[
 (u_i,\psi_i-u_i,\pi-\psi_i),\qquad
 (\alpha_i+u_i,\psi_i+\beta_i-u_i,\psi_i),\quad i=1,2.
 \tag{SC3}
\]
The four angles around their common diagonal sum to \(2\pi\).
The stationary equation \(n(x_*)=d(x_*)\) closes the product
of their shape moduli. Both equatorial links are convex; the proof
checks the eight supporting planes, using inversion to exchange
the two poles. Their developed convex ideal octahedron has volume
\(V_{\rm sew}\). Each half is allowed to exchange modulus with
the other half; neither half is maximized separately.

The phase also has a simple exact form. Sort the roots by
\(\alpha_r=(r+\tfrac12)\pi/N\), \(0\le r\le d=N-1\), and set
\[
 f_r=\exp\!\left(\frac{i\pi r(r+1)}{4N}\right),\qquad
 \gamma_{rs}=e^{i\pi d/4}f_r/f_s .
 \tag{SC4}
\]
For a pair with \(r+s\le N-2\), the polynomial on its negative zero-free
arc has phase \(\gamma_{rs}e^{idt/2}\), with \(t\) the raw circle
angle. Summing its two finite arithmetic strings of zeros proves
this at both parities, including \(N=2\). Consequently
\(\eta_N=\overline{\gamma_{r_1s_1}}\gamma_{r_2s_2}\).
The remaining oscillation is an explicit quadratic height phase.

For the actual crossing changing the middle height \(r\) to \(r'\),
with neighbors \(v,s\), the same-frame entries satisfy
\[
 B^+_{r',r}=(-1)^{r'}\sin\alpha_{r'}\,
                  \frac{f_vf_s}{f_{r'}f_r}\,J_N,\qquad
 B^-_{r',r}=\overline{B^+_{r',r}},\qquad J_N>0 .
 \tag{SC5}
\]
The positivity is in (SC1) at sufficiently large levels, and
\(\log J_N=NV_{\rm sew}/\pi+O_{\mathcal C}(\log N)\).
The common crossing scalar has canceled exactly through
\(\kappa_Nq^{d/2}i^{-d}=1\); the original external closing
normalization remains. The identity \(B^-=\overline{B^+}\)
actually holds at every root quadruple, without the chamber
condition. Its proof uses the middle coefficient of
\(\Phi_{\lambda',\sigma}\Phi_{\lambda,\nu}\): coefficients of
degree \(<N\) are determined by the product functional equation,
which is symmetric separately in the two middle and two neighbor
parameters.

These are entries in a complete nested coideal path basis.
Its physical joint Haar norm has product weight
\(\prod_i h_N(\nu_{i-1},\nu_i)\).
Changing a middle height therefore requires both incident metric
factors,
\[
 \left[
 \frac{h_N(\nu,\lambda')h_N(\lambda',\sigma)}
      {h_N(\nu,\lambda)h_N(\lambda,\sigma)}
 \right]^{1/2}.
 \tag{SC6}
\]
They are retained in the normalized coefficient and its volume
rate. The original cup and marked row must still be transformed
with the same complete basis.

Two checks explain the remaining global scope. The canonical
identity change between the conditional tail and crossed one-head Haar
frames at \(\nu=\sigma=c\) has ambient operator exponent \(4G_{\rm Cat}/\pi\);
its diagonal entry at four \(c\)-labels already has magnitude
\(\sin(\pi/(2N))h_N(c,c)\). Cauchy--Schwarz bounds each normalized
entry by \(\max_\lambda h_N(c,\lambda)\); the matrix has \(N\)
rows, giving the matching upper exponent. This is not a loss forced on
the source: the literal endpoint obeys \(C_c|d\rangle=
\kappa_N|d\rangle\), and its two Haar norms agree.
The large frame entries can cancel on this prescribed vector.
Also, the marked row in G observes
\(\mu_*=-q^{-1}-q^2\), whose normalized coordinate tends to \(-1\).
A raw transition from a near-\(c\) channel with two near-\(c\)
neighbors then approaches \((-1,1,1,1)\), where \(\Delta=4\).
That terminal configuration is outside (SC1). Exact cap
contractions or another boundary argument are needed before using
the chamber theorem there.

The finite-exception target is unchanged and unproved. The new
result establishes signed noncancellation for one universal overlap
kernel, together with an algebraic chamber and its sewn geometry.
It does not prove that every required channel stays in the chamber,
that the face phases cancel globally, or that the original marked
contraction has a nonzero geometric coefficient.

## Exact orthogonality transport for an actual crossing, 24 November

The [crossing transport proof](research_coideal_crossing_orthogonality_transport.md)
now computes a metric transition for the actual first crossing.
The calculation works at every fixed width and in every external
coideal channel. It retains the crossing phase and every original
pair-Casimir direction. The remaining problem is compatibility through
overlapping crossings and the lower bound for the original closing.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(b\ge2\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(c=1+q\), and \(F_a=(Q;Q)_a\). The deeper coideal is
\(S=B_c^{(b-2)}\); the neighboring total tail is
\(T=B_c^{(b-1)}\). Their common spectral nodes are
\(\mu_j=Q^j+qQ^{-j}\); for \(b=2\), the deeper \(S\) is just \(c\).
For any external node \(\nu\), the full \(\nu\)-kernel graph
\(L_\nu\) gives the actual reduced crossing
\[
 C_\nu=\pi_0R_1^+L_\nu
 =\kappa_N\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}(-1)^a|a\rangle_2
       \bigl[(\langle0|_2\otimes I)D_a(\nu;T)/F_a\bigr].
 \tag{CT1}
\]
Here \(D_a\) are the finite continuants in (CK1), now with external
argument \(\nu\), and \(\kappa_N=q^{(N-1)^2/2}\) is the original
crossing scalar. The phase-exact transform obeys
\[
 C_\nu T=J_\nu'C_\nu,\qquad [C_\nu,S]=0,\qquad
 J_\nu'=q\mathcal D\,\overline{B_\nu^{(1)}}\,\mathcal D^{-1},
 \quad \mathcal D|a\rangle=q^{-a}|a\rangle .
 \tag{CT2}
\]
Thus it decouples \(T\) into a specified one-head operator.
Its physical matrix is triangular, with diagonal
\(\kappa_N(-1)^a q^{a(a+1)}\), and can have nonzero off-diagonal entries.

For two spectral nodes the positive weight is explicit:
\[
 h_N(\lambda,\sigma)=
       \sum_{a=0}^{N-1}|D_a(\lambda;\sigma)/F_a|^2,
 \qquad h_N(\lambda,\sigma)=h_N(\sigma,\lambda).
 \tag{CT3}
\]
The proof gives a two-string finite product generating all these
coefficients and its exact Parseval integral. For
\(\lambda=2\sqrt q\cos\alpha\), \(\sigma=2\sqrt q\cos\beta\),
fold simultaneously by negation if \(\alpha+\beta>\pi\).
Writing \(\psi=(\pi-\alpha-\beta)/2\), the uniform formula is
\[
 \log h_N(\lambda,\sigma)=\frac N\pi\mathcal V(\alpha,\beta)
                                      +O(\log N).
 \tag{CT4}
\]
Here \(\mathcal V\) is the maximum of the strictly concave volume
functional for two tetrahedra with angles
\((u,\psi-u,\pi-\psi)\) and two with
\((\alpha+u,\psi+\beta-u,\psi)\).
The critical equation closes their moduli into the convex ideal
octahedron with vertices \(0,\infty,\pm1,\pm r e^{i(\pi-\psi)}\).
The flat case \(\psi=0\) has volume zero. A midpoint of the actual
root grid gives the lower estimate with only \(O(\log N)\) loss,
so (CT4) has no endpoint, parity or nondegeneracy restriction.

Let \(P_{\lambda,\sigma}\) be the full joint spectral idempotents of
\((T,S)\), and \(Q_{\lambda,\sigma}\) those of \((J_\nu',S)\).
The independently prescribed positive forms are
\[
 H_{\rm in}=\sum P_{\lambda,\sigma}^*P_{\lambda,\sigma},\qquad
 H_{\rm out}=\sum Q_{\lambda,\sigma}^*Q_{\lambda,\sigma}.
\]
The adjoint here is physical. These are joint Haar forms, distinct
from the earlier single-tail form unless separately proved equal.
On the joint channel \((\lambda,\sigma)\), the exact squared gain is
\[
 \frac{\|C_\nu v\|_{H_{\rm out}}^2}{\|v\|_{H_{\rm in}}^2}
          =\frac{h_N(\nu,\lambda)}{h_N(\lambda,\sigma)},\qquad
 C_\nu^*\!\left[H_{\rm out}h_N(J_\nu',S)\right]C_\nu
          =H_{\rm in}h_N(\nu,T).
 \tag{CT5}
\]
All multiplicity directions are retained. Both forms and their
specified reweightings have logarithmic radius \(O_b(N)\).
This is an exact isometry between different interfaces, with known
weights; no common positive unitarizing metric is asserted.
On a scalar deeper channel, the inverse also has a finite phase-exact
formula \(C_{\nu|\sigma}^{-1}=
\mathcal D\,\overline{C_{\sigma|\nu}}\,\mathcal D^{-1}\).
It exchanges the two conditional parameters, without moving a mark.

For the original source \(\nu=c\), both unweighted crossing norms
in (CT5) have logarithm \(2G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi+O_b(\log N)\) when
\(b\ge3\), where \(G_{\rm Cat}\) is Catalan's constant.
For \(b=2\) they are one, between the two specified forms.
For every other \(\nu\), the same exponent is a uniform upper bound.
This does not identify either local octahedron with a prescribed
cell of every knot complement, or justify telescoping mismatched
interface weights through a word.

There is also an exact check on the actual initial source in these
metrics. It prevents treating the costly graph channels as disposable
non-source directions. Put \(b=2k\), \(d=N-1\),
\(p_{\rm rest}=p^{\otimes(k-1)}\), and
\(z_0=Nx^{-d}|d\rangle\otimes p_{\rm rest}\), as in (CK3).
On \(V_N\otimes\mathbb Cp_{\rm rest}\), \(S=c\) and \(T\) acts
as \(T_1=B_c^{(1)}\).
For its spectral projector and the graph vector \(u_\lambda(c)\)
whose first coordinate is one, the endpoint expansion is
\[
 P_\lambda(T_1)|d\rangle
       =\frac{q^dN}{p_N'(\lambda)}u_\lambda(c).
 \tag{CT6}
\]
Indeed the \((0,d)\) entry of \(\operatorname{adj}(\lambda I-T_1)\)
is the product of the upper arrows, \(q^dN\). Divide by the simple
root derivative and reconstruct the eigenvector from its first coordinate.
Thus no unknown closed invariant is used in (CT6).
For \(\lambda=\mu_j=2\sqrt q\cos\alpha_j\) one has
\(|p_N'(\lambda)|=N/\sin\alpha_j\). Put \(g_j=h_N(c,\mu_j)\).
Orthogonality and reciprocity give the exact source energies
\[
 \|z_0\|_{H_{\rm in}}^2
   =N^2\|p_{\rm rest}\|^2\sum_j\sin^2\alpha_j\,g_j,\qquad
 \|z_0\|_{H_{\rm in}h_N(c,T)}^2
   =N^2\|p_{\rm rest}\|^2\sum_j\sin^2\alpha_j\,g_j^2 .
 \tag{CT7}
\]
Every \(\sin\alpha_j\ge\sin(\pi/(2N))\), while
\(\max_jg_j=e^{4G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi+O(\log N)}\). Consequently
the logarithm of the weighted source norm divided by the unweighted one is
\(2G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi+O_k(\log N)\). Here \(L_cz_0=u_0\) is
the literal cup tensor in the saturated source; the norm comparison
uses its graph coordinate \(z_0\).
It is a calibration of these particular forms, not an obstruction
to other geometric metrics.

The finite-exception theorem is still open. The positive transport
rule is now explicit locally, including both signs. The next global
step must match its forms through overlapping operations and retain
the original marked row with a volume-scale lower estimate.
No new signed source certificate or knot-volume equality is claimed.

## The coideal graph has an explicit positive volume profile, 24 November

The [graph Gram proof](research_coideal_graph_gram_and_octahedral_volume.md)
computes the positive metric of the actual corrected coideal graph on
every tail channel. It also computes its original marked closing row.
The result is uniform at the endpoint channels and at both level
parities. It is a local metric theorem, not a new knot-volume theorem.

Use \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(d=N-1\), \(c=1+q\), the
kernel map \(L\) in (CK1), and the full tail \(T=B_c^{(2k-1)}\).
Its distinct roots are \(\mu_j=Q^j+qQ^{-j}\). If \(P_j\) are the
full tail spectral idempotents, put \(G=\sum_jP_j^*P_j\), using
the physical adjoint. Thus \(\|v\|_G^2=\sum_j\|P_jv\|_{\rm ph}^2\).
The exact graph weight has a finite product and a positive integral:
\[
 A=[\lfloor N/2\rfloor-j]_N,\quad B=N-1-A,\qquad
 \mathscr F_{N,j}(z)=
       (-qQ^jz;Q)_A(-q^2Q^{-j}z;Q)_B,
\]
\[
 g_N(\mu_j)=
 \sum_{a=0}^{d}\left|\frac{D_a(c;\mu_j)}{(Q;Q)_a}\right|^2
 =\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}
                  |\mathscr F_{N,j}(e^{i\vartheta})|^2d\vartheta,
 \qquad L^\dagger L=g_N(T).
 \tag{OG1}
\]
Here \(L^\dagger\) uses \(G\) on the tail and \(I\otimes G\) on
the full graph space. The product follows from the finite continuant
recurrence; the integral is finite Fourier Parseval. No summand phase
is removed before this exact norm identity.

There is an explicit geometric profile. Put
\(\psi_j=\pi\min(A/N,1-A/N)\) and
\(\eta=\arcsin(\sin\psi_j/\sqrt2)\). With
\(\Lambda(u)=-\int_0^u\log(2\sin v)\,dv\), the proved estimate is
\[
 \log g_N(\mu_j)=\frac N\pi V(\psi_j)+O(\log N),\qquad
 V(\psi)=2\{2\Lambda(\eta)+\Lambda(\psi-\eta)
                              -\Lambda(\psi+\eta)\}.
 \tag{OG2}
\]
The error is uniform over all \(N\ge2\) and all \(j\).
For \(0<\psi\le\pi/2\), this is the volume of the convex ideal
octahedron with vertices
\[
 0,\ \infty,\ 1,\ v,\ -1,\ -v,\qquad
 v=\frac{\sin\eta}{\sin(\psi-\eta)}e^{i(\pi-\psi)}.
\]
The proof constructs all eight supporting planes. Its four-tetrahedron
angle-volume functional is strictly concave, and its unique maximum
satisfies \(2\sin^2\eta=\sin^2\psi\), exactly the modulus gluing
equation. Off-critical angle assignments are distinguished from
developed hyperbolic cells. The maximal volume is \(4G_{\rm Cat}\),
at the regular ideal octahedron, where \(G_{\rm Cat}\) is Catalan's
constant. Consequently \(\log\|L\|=2G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi+O(\log N)\)
in these specified metrics; the full projector has twice that rate.

The actual closing avoids that maximal graph weight. After the
existing legal relocation of the marked cap on the saturated generic
source, its graph row is exactly
\[
 a=(h/N)\otimes\ell^{\otimes(k-1)},\quad
 h_r=(-q^{-1})^r,\quad
 aT=(-q^{-1}-q^2)a,\quad g_N(-q^{-1}-q^2)=N .
 \tag{OG3}
\]
Here \(\ell\) is the original ordinary cap. The proof includes \(N=2\)
and does not move the mark on arbitrary root-only invariant tensors.
For \(G_{\rm graph}=Gg_N(T)\), it gives
\[
 \|a\|_{G,*}\le N^{-k/2},\quad
 \|a\|_{G_{\rm graph},*}\le N^{-(k+1)/2},\qquad
 \mathcal K_N=\chi_N a\mathcal R_cz_0 .
 \tag{OG4}
\]
The original external factor, reduced braid, and cup input are retained.
This removes an exponential worst-channel estimate from this particular
closing row. Polynomial control of the original closing was already
known in other frames; it is not a first scalar boundary bound.

There is a concrete consequence for a matrix-packet version of the
fixed-degree construction. In the physical tail metric the literal
input in (CK3) has
\(\|z_0\|=N^{(3k-1)/2}\), since each cup has norm \(N^{3/2}\).
Together with the exact physical row norm \(N^{-k/2}\), this gives
\[
 \|\Lambda_N\|_{\rm HS,*}=|\chi_N|N^{k-1/2},
 \qquad \Lambda_N(A)=\chi_N aAz_0
 \quad\bigl(A\in\operatorname{End}(W)\bigr).
 \tag{OG5}
\]
Indeed its Hilbert--Schmidt representing matrix is a rank-one outer
product, whose norm is the product of the two vector norms.
This supplies an explicit polynomial root budget in this graph
presentation. The tail has dimension \(N^{2k-1}\), so it is not
the earlier \(N\)-dimensional Conway packet compiler without a new
normalization of its other gates. Nor does (OG5) bound the input in
the different metric \(G_{\rm graph}\); that input can still have
exponential cost. No improvement of the total normalized budget is
inferred from this readout estimate alone.

The degree-four source minimum remains unevaluated. Equations
(OG1)--(OG4) supply actual positive local weights and their volume
profile, but not the joint estimate through an arbitrary short
component or a lower bound for its observed scalar. Those are still
needed for the fixed-short-partial-filling theorem. The local
octahedron is not identified with a cell in every knot complement.
Earlier centered-input Parseval estimates and native magnetic
octahedra are credited in the complete proof.

## An explicit coideal kernel calibrates the original cup, 24 November

The [continuant kernel proof](research_coideal_continuant_source_kernel.md)
gives polynomial kernel and cokernel maps for the actual conserved
coideal, including collisions. It also computes the nonzero coefficient
from a fixed endpoint seed to the original cup. The original closing
is retained; this is not yet a geometric scalar lower bound.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(b=2k\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(Q=q^2\), \(x=-q^{-1}\), and \(F_a=(Q;Q)_a\).
Write \(B_c=\mathsf F-(\mathsf E-cI)\mathsf K^{-1}\) and
\(T=B_c^{(b-1)}\). Its leading continuants obey
\[
 D_0=I,\quad D_{-1}=0,\quad
 D_{a+1}=(c+qQ^aT)D_a-q(1-Q^a)^2D_{a-1}.
\]
Let \(E_d\) be the trailing continuant on first-head indices \(1,\ldots,d\).
The actual even-width polynomial identity makes \(D_N=0\), and
the tridiagonal determinant identity gives
\[
 D_dE_d=q^dN^2I,\qquad
 L_c=\sum_{a=0}^d|a\rangle\otimes\frac{q^{-a}D_a}{F_a},
 \quad M_c=\sum_{a=0}^d\langle a|\otimes\frac{D_a}{F_a},
 \quad Q_c=E_dM_c .
 \tag{CK1}
\]
Thus the apparent tail inverse is another polynomial continuant.
For \(r_c(z)=(p_N(z)-p_N(c))/(z-c)\), put
\(p_N(z)=2q^{N/2}T_N(z/(2\sqrt q))\), with \(T_N\) Chebyshev
and \(\sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)}\). The exact factorization is
\[
 r_c(B_c)=L_cQ_c,\qquad Q_cL_c=p_N'(c)I,\qquad
 0\longrightarrow W\xrightarrow{L_c}V
 \xrightarrow{B_c-cI}V\xrightarrow{Q_c}W\longrightarrow0 .
 \tag{CK2}
\]
Here \(W\) is the full \((b-1)\)-head tail and \(V=\mathbb C^N\otimes W\).
This free exact sequence already holds over
\(\mathbb Z[\sqrt q,1/N][c]\), by unit-arrow elimination.
At \(p_N'(c)=0\), the natural kernel-to-cokernel comparison vanishes
and \(r_c(B_c)^2=0\). The graph map \(L_c\), split by first-coordinate
extraction \(\pi_0\), still carries the original source exactly.

Use the literal cup \(p=N\sum_a x^{a-d}|a,d-a\rangle\) and set
\(u_0=p^{\otimes k}\), \(\xi=|0,0\rangle\otimes p^{\otimes(k-1)}\).
The source calibration, including its phase, is
\[
 u_0=r_c(B_c)\xi=L_cz_0,\qquad
 z_0=Nx^{-d}|d\rangle\otimes p^{\otimes(k-1)} .
 \tag{CK3}
\]
For every original unmarked braid word \(R\), put \(R_c=\pi_0RL_c\).
Then \(RL_c=L_cR_c\) and the unchanged original scalar is
\(\mathcal K_N=\chi_N(\ell_0L_c)R_cz_0\), with its full marked
row \(\ell_0\) and external factor \(\chi_N\). The entire eigenspace
is not identified with the smaller saturated generic source.
The maps and continuant inverses have \(e^{O(N)}\) physical operator
cost at fixed width and bounded \(c\); those costs are retained.

At \(c=2\), the projected seed coefficient is
\(N^{3/2}/|p_N'(2)|=2\sqrt\pi\,e^{-\sqrt{\pi N/2}}(1+O(N^{-1/2}))\).
A quantum correction gives a polynomial coefficient:
\[
 c_N=1+q,\quad p_N(c_N)=0,\quad p_N'(c_N)=\frac{2N}{1-q},
 \qquad
 \frac{\|\Pi_{c_N}\xi\|}{\|\xi\|}
 =\sqrt N\sin\frac{\pi}{2N}\sim\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt N}.
 \tag{CK4}
\]
Here \(\Pi_{c_N}=r_{c_N}(B_{c_N})/p_N'(c_N)\) is over \(\mathbb C\).
Also \(B_{c_N}-c_NI=(B_2-2I)+(q-1)(\mathsf K^{-1}-I)\);
the generator correction is \(O(N^{-1})\) in physical operator norm.

There is an explicit finite cyclic clock. Define \(C_0=2,C_1=z\) and
\(C_{a+1}=zC_a-qC_{a-1}\). Then
\[
 V_N=\frac{B_{c_N}-qC_{N-1}(B_{c_N})}{2},\quad V_N^N=I,\quad
 \Pi_{c_N}=\frac1N\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}V_N^a,\qquad
             u_0=\frac2{1-q}\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}V_N^a\xi .
 \tag{CK5}
\]
For the full spectral idempotents \(\Pi_j\), character orthogonality gives
\(N^{-1}\sum_a(V_N^a)^*V_N^a=\sum_j\Pi_j^*\Pi_j\).

At this parameter the tail density has an exact metric bound. Its
odd-width tail also satisfies \(p_N(T)=0\). Put
\[
 \mathcal V=\frac{T-qC_{N-1}(T)}2,\qquad
 G_{\rm tail}=\frac1N\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}(\mathcal V^a)^*\mathcal V^a,
 \qquad A^{\dagger_G}=G_{\rm tail}^{-1}A^*G_{\rm tail}.
\]
The full tail spectrum is \(\lambda_j=Q^j+qQ^{-j}\), with
\(\overline{\lambda_j}=q^{-1}\lambda_j\), so \(T^{\dagger_G}=q^{-1}T\).
Also \(\overline{c_N}=q^{-1}c_N\). In the continuant, multiplication
of conjugated diagonals by \(q\) reverses \(a\mapsto d-a\);
conjugated edge products multiplied by \(q^2\) reverse \(a\mapsto N-a\).
Thus reflection and (CK1) give
\[
 E_d=q^dD_d^{\dagger_G},\qquad D_d^{\dagger_G}D_d=N^2I,\qquad
 \|D_d\|_{G_{\rm tail}}=\|E_d\|_{G_{\rm tail}}=N,\quad
 \|D_d^{-1}\|_{G_{\rm tail}}=\|E_d^{-1}\|_{G_{\rm tail}}=1/N .
 \tag{CK6}
\]
This removes the tail-density cost in this specified Haar metric.
The physical comparison, kernel graph, and original closing can still
have exponential cost; no compatible whole-component metric is inferred.

Abstract Chebyshev clock recovery was already proved in
[whole-source Newton transport, section 4](whole_source_newton_transport.md).
Here its actual coideal specialization retains the cup and closing.
Neither this finite averaging nor its coefficient is identified with
a geometric framing period. No geometric cycle coefficient, scalar
lower estimate, or finite-exception theorem is claimed.

## The metric scale required by an exact inverse block, 24 November

The polynomial local restriction Gram does not make the actual crossing
well conditioned in the physical source norm. Fix \(b=2k\ge4\) heads and
let \(\mathcal S_N\) be the saturated specialization of the generic
invariant source in the original balanced physical tensor space. Put
\(a=2G_{\rm Cat}/\pi\), where \(G_{\rm Cat}\) is Catalan's constant.
For any adjacent full signed crossing, the
[source-selected estimates](research_source_selected_coideal_gaussian_reduction.md)
give, as \(N\to\infty\) at fixed width,
\[
 A_N=R_i|_{\mathcal S_N},\qquad A_N^{-1}=R_i^{-1}|_{\mathcal S_N},
 \qquad \log\|A_N^{\pm1}\|_{\rm op}=aN+O_k(\log N).
 \tag{IC1}
\]
Thus \(\log\kappa(A_N)=2aN+O_k(\log N)\), where
\(\kappa(A)=\|A\|_{\rm op}\|A^{-1}\|_{\rm op}\). The exact identity
\(A_NA_N^{-1}=I\) has norm one; the product of these two norms has
exponential rate \(2a\).

Let \(H_0,H_1\) be any positive definite interface forms on
\(\mathcal S_N\), expressed in its physical orthonormal coordinates.
Their transformed crossing and its correctly ordered inverse are
\[
 T_N=H_1^{1/2}A_NH_0^{-1/2},\qquad
 T_N^{-1}=H_0^{1/2}A_N^{-1}H_1^{-1/2}.
\]
Submultiplicativity applied to \(A_N=H_1^{-1/2}T_NH_0^{1/2}\) proves
\[
 \kappa(T_N)\ge
 \frac{\kappa(A_N)}{\sqrt{\kappa(H_0)\kappa(H_1)}}.
 \tag{IC2}
\]
Consequently making \(\|T_N\|\|T_N^{-1}\|=\exp(o(N))\) requires
\[
 \log\kappa(H_0)+\log\kappa(H_1)\ge4aN-o(N).
 \tag{IC3}
\]
For the same form \(H_0=H_1=H\), this gives
\(\log\kappa(H)\ge2aN-o(N)\). In particular subexponentially
conditioned source-state interface forms cannot supply that reduction.
These are not claims about every tensor-packet gauge or compiler.

The two-interface cost is sharp. With \(H_0=I\), choose
\[
 H_1=(A_N^{-1})^*A_N^{-1}.
 \tag{IC4}
\]
Then \(T_N^*T_N=I\), \(\kappa(T_N)=1\), and
\(\kappa(H_1)=\kappa(A_N)^2\). This is an exact isometry between
different interface metrics, not unitarization in one common metric.
It is an open-operator construction and supplies no closing lower bound.

Two conserved structures do not remove this metric issue. The actual
[divided generators](actual_all_width_divided_source_projection.md)
\(J_E,J_F\) and the unrolled total weight annihilate \(\mathcal S_N\);
their exponentials and integrated group action are the identity there.
For the fixed tensor Krein form, write \(d=N-1\),
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and
\(H_Ne_j=qQ^je_{d-j}\). The
[prefix similarity](research_reduced_prefix_krein_descent.md) identifies
the actual total lowering operator \(\mathsf F\) with
\(F_1\otimes I\), where
\(F_1e_j=(1-Q^{j+1})e_{j+1}\) for \(j<d\), and \(F_1e_d=0\).
This is one length-\(N\) Jordan string.
For \([v,w]=v^*H_N^{\otimes b}w\), the
[actual adjoint identity](research_real_meridian_krein_transport.md)
is \(\mathsf F^\sharp=Q^{-1}\mathsf F\), with \(\sharp\) the adjoint
for this form. Hence
\[
 \ker\mathsf F=\operatorname{im}\mathsf F^{N-1}
       \subset\operatorname{im}\mathsf F,\qquad
 [v,\mathsf Fz]=[\mathsf F^\sharp v,z]=0
       \quad(v\in\ker\mathsf F).
 \tag{IC5}
\]
The tensor pairing therefore vanishes between every two vectors in
\(\ker\mathsf F\), including different braid images of actual source
states. The one-head kernel is the top endpoint \(e_d\).
The nondegenerate conserved form on the
[reduced complete multiplicity](actual_complete_source_krein_and_cauchy_metric.md)
is a different pairing; it is not this tensor-form restriction.

The existing [boundary-force dual](research_conway_boundary_force_mismatch_certificate.md)
also locates the required precision. Its normalized source minimum is
\(e_*=\min_x\{\sum_v\|\Phi_v-x_v\|^2+|Lx_{v_0}|^2\}\) on the recorded
unit packet balls. Its signed dual value \(d(p)\) and unique maximizing
force \(p^*\) satisfy
\[
 e_*-d(p)\ge\tfrac14\|p-p^*\|^2.
 \tag{IC6}
\]
This holds on the recorded force ball \(\|p_v\|\le1/3\). A positive
dual value requires \(\|p-p^*\|<2\sqrt{e_*}\). Polynomial local Gram
control and conserved forms do not supply such a signed geometric dual
value. No new scalar estimate or finite-exception theorem is claimed.

## The actual source and a polynomially controlled local Gram, 24 November

The [source-selected reduction](research_source_selected_coideal_gaussian_reduction.md)
gives quantitative control after restricting to the actual invariant
source. The restriction itself was already established in the complete
invariant and saturated-source notes. The new estimates concern its
physical norm, the source-selected coideal parameter, and the transfer
of whole-block approximations. The fixed-degree source minimum still
needs its geometric growth estimate.

Fix \(2k\) heads and let \(\mathcal S_N\) be the saturated specialization
of the generic invariant source, inside the original physical tensor
space. The actual incoming cup tensor \(u_0=p^{\otimes k}\) satisfies
\[
 \mathsf E u_0=\mathsf F u_0=0,\qquad \mathsf K u_0=u_0.
\]
For the earlier conserved operator, choosing the auxiliary parameter
\(c=2\) therefore gives \(B_2u_0=2u_0\) exactly. Every original
unmarked signed crossing preserves this channel. The original full
marked closing and external scalar remain
\[
 \mathcal K_N=\chi_N\ell_0Ru_0
             =\chi_N\ell_0\Pi_2R\Pi_2u_0 .
\]
The prescribed cups give this selection. On the central integer-degree space,
\(\ker(B_2-2)\) is the full root invariant space; the saturated source
can be smaller. Both were already available as stronger dimension
reductions than the whole coideal eigenspace.

At \(c=2\) all \(N\) conserved roots are simple at every level.
The new proof supplies projectors of norm \(e^{O_k(N)}\), including
this parameter which was outside the earlier stable range. The known
normalizing derivative satisfies
\[
 \log|p_N'(2)|=\sqrt{\pi N/2}+\tfrac32\log N+O(1).
\]
Its logarithm divided by \(N\) tends to zero. The orthogonalizing
coideal metric restricts exactly to the physical norm on
\(\ker(B_2-2)\). The flow generated by \(B_2-2\) acts as the
identity on this source; it does not construct a relative geometric
transport or select the discrete-faithful branch.

There is a useful quantitative statement for an entire short block.
Let \(A_N\) act on a contiguous block of \(1\le r\le k\) heads, with a
regular generic degree-preserving Hopf-intertwining lift. Put spectator
identities on the other heads. Then
\[
 N^{-r/2}\|A_N\|_{\rm HS}
 \le \|A_N|_{\mathcal S_N}\|_{\rm op}
 \le \|A_N\|_{\rm op}.
\]
The witness is a noncrossing matching of actual cups in which every
block head is paired to an outside head. It belongs to the saturated
source and has block reduced density \(I/N^r\) after normalization.
Thus this estimate uses the original source and holds for whole
supported blocks, with no restriction on their internal phases.

This also controls the correct local restriction Gram. On any linear
space of such supported operators with its physical Hilbert--Schmidt
norm, define \(\mathcal R_N(A)=A|_{\mathcal S_N}\) and
\(d_N=\dim\mathcal S_N\). The preceding bound and
\(\|T\|_{\rm op}\le\|T\|_{\rm HS}\le\sqrt{d_N}\|T\|_{\rm op}\)
on \(\operatorname{End}(\mathcal S_N)\) give
\[
 N^{-r}\|A\|_{\rm HS}^2
 \le \|\mathcal R_N(A)\|_{\rm HS}^2
 \le d_N\|A\|_{\rm HS}^2.
\]
Consequently, in an actual Hilbert--Schmidt orthonormal local basis,
\[
 N^{-r}I\le\mathcal R_N^*\mathcal R_N\le d_NI,\qquad
 \operatorname{cond}(\mathcal R_N^*\mathcal R_N)\le d_NN^r.
\]
The condition number is polynomial for fixed width. Restriction loses
no local operator direction, including any present Casimir Jordan
direction, and orthogonalizing this particular Gram has only polynomial
cost. This does not estimate an arbitrary Newton or fusion coordinate
Gram, or the restriction of operators with larger overlapping supports.
An additional projection of the output back to the source requires
the stated source-preservation hypothesis for this lower bound.

A relative Hilbert--Schmidt model error \(\varepsilon_N\) for the
whole block therefore gives a relative operator error at most
\(N^{r/2}\varepsilon_N\) after physical orthogonal source compression.
Such a whole-block estimate must be proved; multiplying relative letter
errors alone does not supply it.
For a single crossing with \(k\ge2\), the earlier order-\(J\) physical
Gaussian gives \(O(N^{-(J-1)/2})\). Spectator heads add no error factor. Projecting
first onto the full pair Casimir algebra gives a source-preserving
model retaining its Casimir derivative directions. This transfers all fixed
orders by increasing the number of correction terms.

The bare original closing row on
\(\operatorname{End}(\mathcal S_N)\), \(A\mapsto\ell_0Au_0\),
has Hilbert--Schmidt dual norm between \(1\) and \(N^{k-1}\).
The lower witness is the cyclic noncrossing cup matching, whose
literal marked pairing is one. Including the external scalar multiplies
both bounds by \(|\chi_N|\). These row bounds do not bound the
particular value \(\ell_0Ru_0\) from below. A whole-word scalar
estimate at the geometric rate, after arbitrary fixed short partial
fillings, remains necessary.

## Conserved channels for every complete-color braid, 24 November

The [conserved-channel proof](research_conserved_coideal_braid_channels.md)
gives a whole-boundary decomposition preserved by every original
crossing, with the original closing retained. It applies to every
fixed width and every signed braid word at the complete meridian.
This is a source-specific use of the established coideal structure,
not a geometric volume estimate.

Let \(N\ge2\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(\gamma=(-1)^{N+1}\), and
let \(\mathsf E,\mathsf F,\mathsf K\) be the actual width-\(b\)
ordered total generators in the stated factorial basis.
Here \(\mathsf E\) is the scaled generator of the Ward source.
For an auxiliary scalar \(c\), put
\[
 B_c=\mathsf F-(\mathsf E-cI)\mathsf K^{-1},\qquad
 p_N(z)=2i\,T_N\!\left(\frac{z}{2e^{\pi i/(2N)}}\right).
\]
On the full \(N^b\)-dimensional space the exact relation is
\[
 p_N(B_c)=\gamma^b p_N(c)I.
\]
The minimal polynomial is precisely \(p_N(z)-\gamma^bp_N(c)\).
An explicit change of basis gives its companion matrix, repeated
\(N^{b-1}\) times.
Both that change of basis and its inverse have norms \(e^{O(N)}\)
on bounded \(c\)-sets, including collisions. Thus the whole space
is a free rank-\(N^{b-1}\) module over this degree-\(N\) quotient
algebra. Every braid operator acts linearly over that algebra.

All repeated roots have multiplicity two, so the conserved operator's
Jordan blocks have length at most two, independently of the width.
The generalized eigenvectors are retained. This does not bound the
Jordan structure of every other operator or transport derivatives
in the meridian or quantum parameter. At the critical value
\(\gamma^bp_N(c)=-2i\), the rescaled quotient is exactly the full
Conway algebra \(\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2)\). Its transported
closing has not been identified with the canonical Frobenius row.

For \(4\le|c|\le C_*\), all eigenvalues are distinct and explicit
spectral idempotents \(\Pi_j\) give the positive metric
\[
 G_c=\sum_j\Pi_j^*\Pi_j,\qquad
 G_c\Pi_j=\Pi_j^*\Pi_j=\Pi_j^*G_c,\qquad
 \|\log G_c\|_{\rm op}=O_{b,C_*}(N).
\]
The full conserved eigenspaces are orthogonal in this metric.
The induced operator-packet Hilbert--Schmidt metric also has
logarithmic radius \(O(N)\); the proof keeps its distinction from
the metric on the head space.

For the original cut and pivotal matrix \(P\), set
\(P^{\rm diag}=\sum_j\Pi_jP\Pi_j\). Every unmarked original
braid word \(R\) commutes with \(B_c\), and hence
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}(PR)=\operatorname{Tr}(P^{\rm diag}R).
\]
Pinching does not increase either the operator norm or the
Hilbert--Schmidt root-dual norm in this metric. The pinched probe
commutes with \(B_c\), so its inner Ward boundary vanishes on
the commuting source algebra. It need not be positive. Arbitrary
marked insertions retain the exact correction
\(\operatorname{Tr}((P-P^{\rm diag})O)\).
At collisions one uses whole primary packets; their nilpotent
parts and their possible Ward boundaries remain.

There is also an explicit classical interpretation. For the ordered
total meridian
\(G=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}K&e\\Kf&K^{-1}+ef\end{smallmatrix}\right)\),
the Hamiltonian \(H_c=f-2-(e-c)/K\) generates simultaneous
conjugation by \(-J-H_cD/2\), with the matrices \(J,D\) specified
in the proof. On its zero level, in the specified noncentral cut frame,
this is the remaining parabolic framing translation. For bounded flow time
and bounded \(c\), the finite matrix exponential has norm \(e^{O(N)}\);
no finite-time geometric kernel or relative framing period is
inferred from its principal Hamiltonian.

The polynomial, companion form and source decomposition are proved
with the actual endpoint zero arrows, at even and composite levels
as well as odd levels. Coideal minimal-polynomial questions already
occur in the cited literature; no published proof is assumed here.
The remaining scalar channel sum can cancel. No geometric channel
coefficient, volume lower bound or finite-exception theorem follows
yet. In particular the construction does not justify selecting
only the classical \(H_c=0\) level in the finite source.

## Two physical colors suffice in a bounded metric problem, 24 November

The [color-preserving construction](research_main_color_block_regularized_compactness.md)
removes mixing between main colors from the bounded regularized
minimization at the volume scale. It also permits retaining only the
two actual main colors \(1,N\), whose original closed output is
\((1,K_N)\). This version needs no estimate for the discarded
ordinary-color remainder.

Fix a completed braid word whose marked closure is one knot. Let
\(m\) count its multiplication-tree vertices, including the original
root readout. Keep the two physical color spaces in full and restrict
each edge metric to preserve them. Write
\[
 L_N(H)=\sum_v\log\|T_{v,N}\|_H,\qquad
 Z(H)=1+\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(H_e+H_e^{-1}),\qquad
 j_{2,N}=\min_{\rm block}\{L_N(H)+N^{-2}\log Z(H)\}.
\]
The new finite-window estimate proves
\[
 j_{2,N}=\frac m2\log(1+|K_N|^{2/m})+O(N^{-1}),\qquad
 \sup_e\|\log H^{\rm block}_{e,N}\|_{\rm op}=O(N).
\]
The restricted minimum exists and is unique. The estimate includes
\(K_N=0\); neither its construction nor its bounds divide by a
closed color value.

The finite construction uses the invertibility of the actual open
word operators. Their norms and inverse norms have logarithms
\(O(N)\). Normalize their full directions on the proper edges,
then suppress the complementary coordinates by depth-dependent
filters. The retained coefficient slices and the errors are
orthogonal in the actual tensor norm. The root slice remains its
original \(c_j\), even when that value vanishes. All finite local
tensors remain nonzero, so scalar edge gauges can balance their
norms with controlled metric cost. This supplies the finite
near-minimizer that the earlier sector-infimum formula did not
quantify. It does not construct these directions from geometry.

For any selected \(r\) actual main colors containing \(1\), the same
proof approximates their exact sector infimum with error \(O(N^{-1})\)
and metric log-radius \(O(N)\). Restricting the regularized minimum
to those color blocks costs at most
\((m-1)\log r/2+O(N^{-1})\) compared with the unrestricted minimum
on the same selected source. It does not assert that pinching
improves an arbitrary metric, that the two minimizers coincide,
or that restricted stationarity gives full marginal balance.

For the same original Conway invariant, let \(Q_N\) be the earlier
anchored quartic minimum. Its proved bounds and the new estimate give
\[
 -\tfrac12\log(1+1/N)
 \le j_{2,N}-\tfrac12\log Q_N
 \le\tfrac{m-1}{2}\log2+O(N^{-1}).
\]
Thus the fixed-degree minimum and this bounded two-color matrix
problem have the same leading logarithmic value. Their minimizers
and pointwise objectives are not identified.

For every positive \(V\), proving
\((2\pi/N)j_{2,N}\longrightarrow V\) is equivalent to the original
full-sequence Kashaev volume identity with value \(V\).
The missing estimate is still the geometric value of this minimum,
after the arbitrary fixed short partial fillings in the target.
No additional volume case or finite-exception theorem is proved.
The argument concerns the raw multiplication tree of each fixed
completed word; arbitrary Conway packets containing partial traces
need not be invertible. Constants may depend on that fixed word,
braid width and filling assignment.
