## A prescribed leaf has a polynomial-cost full-matrix matching, 24 November

The [one-leaf construction](research_one_leaf_physical_capacity_calibration.md)
gives an explicit finite reference in which a known leaf and its parent
have nearly equal full density matrices. It works in the actual
all-main-color matrix-product compiler and preserves its original
root. It does not yet match the other input or the rest of the tree.

Write the operator space as
\(\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{\nu=1}^s\operatorname{Mat}_D(\mathbb C)\),
with its physical Hilbert--Schmidt norm. Its dimension is \(n=sD^2\).
In the actual source \(s=N,\ D=N^b\), for fixed braid width \(b\).
Let \(\mu(A\otimes B)=AB\) componentwise, and normalize a prescribed
nonzero crossing or blocked word leaf as \(A=\alpha a\), with
\(\alpha=\|A\|_{\rm HS}\) and \(\|a\|_{\rm HS}=1\). Set
\[
 P=|a\rangle\langle a|,\qquad
 G_t=P+t(I-P),\qquad B_t=\mu(G_t^{-1}\otimes I),\qquad t\ge1.
\]
Apply \(G_t\) to the leaf output and its inverse to the parent input.
Since \(G_tA=A\), the whole original contraction is exactly preserved.
This is a full bundled edge gauge, potentially mixing color and
matrix coordinates, rather than a separate gauge on each physical head.

Put \(L_a(B)=aB\). The canonical states on the selected input,
other input and output are
\[
 \tau_1=P,\qquad \tau_2=L_a^*L_a/D,\qquad
 \tau_o=L_aL_a^*/D.
\]
The actual normalized Hilbert--Schmidt marginals of \(B_t\) are
given by the same exact formula on each of its three legs:
\[
 \tau_{r,t}=\frac{\tau_r+t^{-2}(I-\tau_r)}
                        {1+(n-1)t^{-2}},\qquad r=1,2,o.
\]
The logical input matrices are transposed on the original dual
half-edges. The proof uses the three matrix-unit identities
\(\mu\mu^*=\operatorname{Tr}_1(\mu^*\mu)
=\operatorname{Tr}_2(\mu^*\mu)=D I\).
In particular, with
\[
 \eta_t=\frac{n-1}{t^2+n-1},
\]
the selected edge defect is exactly
\(\|\tau_{1,t}-P\|_1=2\eta_t\), and each other canonical
marginal error is at most \(2\eta_t\).
These are actual tensor marginals, not only independent dual witnesses.

There is also a local logarithmic lower bound. For arbitrary positive
metrics satisfying \(\|\log H_i\|_{\rm op}\le R\), \(i=o,1,2\),
write \(Z_t=D[1+(n-1)t^{-2}]\). Scalar spectral Jensen gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 \log\|H_o^{1/2}B_t(H_1^{-1/2}\otimes H_2^{-1/2})\|_{\rm HS}
 \ge{}&\tfrac12\log Z_t+\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(\tau_o\log H_o)\\
 &-\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(P\log H_1)
  -\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(\tau_2\log H_2)-3R\eta_t .
 \end{split}
\]
The original leaf inequality contributes
\(\log\alpha+\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(P\log H_1)\).
Thus its metric term cancels locally, while its possibly exponential
normalization \(\alpha\) is retained.

Choosing \(t=\sqrt n\,N^J\), for a fixed integer \(J\ge1\), gives
\[
 \eta_t\le N^{-2J},\qquad
 \log\|G_t\|_{\rm op}=(b+J+\tfrac12)\log N.
\]
The local logarithmic loss is \(O(RN^{-2J})\), in particular
\(O(N^{1-2J})\) on any supplied \(R=O(N)\) window.
The proof does not transfer an anchored Newton window to this larger
operator algebra or assert a new window theorem.

Any collection of prescribed-leaf edges with at most one selected
input per parent can be treated simultaneously. For \(M\) selections,
their total actual defect is at most \(2M\eta_t\); there is no
product-output gauge and the original root stays exact.
Unselected edges remain uncontrolled. In particular the remaining
canonical input state need not match the actual neighboring subtree.
No geometric volume rate or finite-exception result follows yet.

## Weighted crossing estimates beyond the small-weight region, 24 November

The [global weighted proof](research_global_weighted_crossing_gaussian_phase.md)
extends the whole physical crossing Gaussian to its entire region
with a strictly dominant interior maximum. It also gives an unbounded
range of boundary weights where the complete original Green source
is exponentially smaller than the crossing. These are local weighted
estimates; the general short-component and finite-exception theorems
remain unproved.

Give the two inputs real weights \(\rho_a,\rho_b\), and the outputs
real weights \(\rho_c,\rho_e\), with
\[
 R^\pm_\rho=W_{\rm out}R^\pm W_{\rm in}^{-1},\qquad
 W_{\rm in}|a,b\rangle=e^{\rho_a a+\rho_b b}|a,b\rangle,\quad
 W_{\rm out}|c,e\rangle=e^{\rho_c c+\rho_e e}|c,e\rangle.
\]
For a positive crossing its three amplitude weights are
\[
 \lambda=(\rho_e-\rho_a,\rho_c-\rho_b,\rho_c-\rho_a).
\]
In occupations \((u,v,t)\), its real amplitude profile is
\[
 S_\lambda=h(u+t)+h(v+t)-h(u)-h(v)-h(t)
                     +\lambda_u u+\lambda_v v+\lambda_t t,
 \quad h(y)=\int_0^y\log(2\sin\pi r)\,dr,
\]
on \(u,v,t\ge0,\ u+t\le1,\ v+t\le1\).
Define \(F_\lambda(t)=\max_{u,v}S_\lambda(u,v,t)\) on that slice,
and \(B_\lambda=(\lambda_u)_++(\lambda_v)_+\).

The full maximization now reduces to one quadratic and one comparison.
Put
\[
 A=\cosh\lambda_u,\quad B=\cosh\lambda_v,\quad
 E=e^{2\lambda_t-\lambda_u-\lambda_v},\qquad
 E_c=\sinh^2\!\left(\frac{|\lambda_u|+|\lambda_v|}{2}\right).
\]
There is an interior local maximum exactly when \(E>E_c\).
It is unique and nondegenerate, and \(c_*=\cos(\pi t_*)\) is the
smaller admissible root of
\[
 (1+E)c^2-(A+B)c+AB-E=0.
\]
The full strict interior region is
\(\mathcal I=\{\lambda:E>E_c,\ F_\lambda(t_*)>B_\lambda\}\).
The endpoint \(t=1\) is never maximal; the other boundary value
is exactly \(B_\lambda\). The proof does not assume global
concavity of \(S_\lambda\), which is false.

For every compact \(K\Subset\mathcal I\) and every fixed
correction order \(J\), the actual crossing has a whole-matrix
Gaussian-polynomial approximation with
\[
 \frac{\|R^\pm_\rho-\mathcal G^\pm_{N,J,\rho}\|_{\rm HS}}
      {\|R^\pm_\rho\|_{\rm HS}}
          \le C_{K,J}N^{-(J+1)/2}
\]
at all sufficiently large levels, when the corresponding induced
tilt lies in \(K\). The exact physical phase, support and all
repeated-root normals remain. The estimates are in the weighted
arrays themselves; undoing the metric is a separate operation.
The negative sign uses the literal flip-conjugation and
\(\lambda_-(\rho)=\lambda(\rho_b,\rho_a,\rho_e,\rho_c)\).

An explicit unbounded sufficient cone for the positive sign is
\[
 \mathcal C_+=\{\rho:\max(\rho_a,\rho_e)
                               \le\min(\rho_b,\rho_c)\}.
\]
It is equivalent to \(\lambda_t\ge B_\lambda\), so the interior
maximum \(M_\lambda\) satisfies \(M_\lambda>\lambda_t\).
The complete Green source \(L^\pm_\rho\), including both ground
terms and its degree-\(N\) carry, has the known norm exponent
\[
 \delta(\rho)=\max\{0,\max(\rho_c,\rho_e)-\min(\rho_a,\rho_b)\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal C_+\), this is \(\lambda_t\). Thus on every fixed
compact subset of \(\mathcal C_+\),
\[
 \frac{\|L^+_\rho\|}{\|R^+_\rho\|}
                       \le N^C e^{-\eta N},\qquad \eta>0.
\]
This holds for operator and Hilbert--Schmidt norms. The negative
sign has the reversed cone
\(\max(\rho_b,\rho_c)\le\min(\rho_a,\rho_e)\).
There is no uniform positive gap over the whole unbounded cone.

The new input is a classification and estimates in substantially
larger weighted metrics. It does not yet choose geometric weights
for an arbitrary fixed short component, prove compatibility of full
boundary marginals, or give a relative error after the original
closing. No additional knot-volume case is concluded.

## What the degree reduction leaves in the original closing, 24 November

Further written checks have not supplied a volume lower bound.
They identify limitations of two proposed simplifications: evaluating
an affine residual integral, and averaging the Newton metric under
common tensor symmetries. No new manuscript or standalone note is added.

Use the rescaled compressed source in [D], with \(\ell=q+1\)
input blocks and \(k_N=K_N/\widehat B_N\). Whenever its reduced
vector \(F\) is affine, write
\[
 F(u)=\binom{Au+b}{\gamma u+\delta},\qquad n=Nq.
\]
The first \(n\) rows are the retained gate residuals. Ancestry makes
\(A=-I+\) strictly triangular, so \(\det A=(-1)^n\).
Its unique gate-exact field is \(u_*=-A^{-1}b\), and the closing gives
\[
 k_N=\delta-\gamma A^{-1}b,\qquad
 \det\begin{pmatrix}A&b\\ \gamma&\delta\end{pmatrix}
                                      =(-1)^n k_N.
\]
The affine integral is consequently
\[
 \frac{n!}{\pi^n}\int_{\mathbb C^n}
          \|F(u)\|^{-2n-2}\,du=|k_N|^{-2}\qquad(k_N\ne0).
\]
Indeed change variables to \(v=Au+b\), whose real Jacobian is one,
then use the affine square completion in [C, (16)].
At \(k_N=0\) the integral diverges. This evaluation retains the
unknown scalar in the bordered determinant. The exact full integral
\(\mathcal P_N\) in [D, (11)] also retains its response Gram and
determinant; they are not removed by the affine calculation.

There is a separate orthogonality warning. Let \(f\) be the scalar
polynomial in the full residual variables, before linear integration.
Equation (14) of [D] proves \(\deg f=\ell\) when \(k_N\ne0\).
For a fixed tree, along nonzero-source levels tending to infinity,
the finite-fiber formula [F, (14)] and the affine comparison
[C, (18)] give, for the same full rescaled source,
\[
 \mathcal P_N=\frac{1}{\ell|k_N|^2}+\mathcal V_N,\qquad
 |k_N|^2\mathcal V_N=1-\frac1\ell+O_{\mathscr T}(N^{-1}),
 \qquad \mathcal V_N\ge0.
\]
Here \(\mathcal V_N\) is precisely the squared norm of the
zero-sum fiber component in [F]. For \(\ell>1\), that component
contributes at leading order. Its orthogonality to the constant
fiber component does not justify discarding its energy.
These are the full residual fibers, including the leaf residuals.
For fixed \(\ell>1\), both terms have the same exponential rate;
retaining only the constant fiber projection changes a known
constant factor at that scale. The missing geometric rate is still
the size of \(\mathcal P_N\), not this fiber projection angle.

The natural common Newton symmetry also does not reduce the metric
problem. Specifically, a complex-linear Newton-unitary algebra
automorphism \(U\) of \(\mathcal A_N\) satisfying
\[
 U1=1,\qquad U(fg)=(Uf)(Ug),\qquad
 U\mathcal T=\mathcal T U
\]
is the identity, for every \(N\ge2\).
Here [A,T] fix the full algebra and basis
\[
 \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2),\quad
 c_i=2\cos((2i+1)\pi/N),\quad
 b_r(z)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{j<r}(c_j-z),\quad
 S_r=\prod_{h=1}^r2\sin(\pi h/N),\quad S_0=1,
 \qquad \mathcal T b_r=b_{N-1-r}.
\]
The \(b_r\) are orthonormal. The symbol \(T_N\) is Chebyshev;
\(\mathcal T\) is the genuine turn.

To prove the claim, index distinct roots by
\(0\le i\le\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\), and set
\(v_i=(b_r(c_i))_r\). These vectors have strictly increasing norms:
\(b_r(c_i)>0\) for \(r\le i\), and zero for \(r>i\);
as \(i\) increases the existing positive factors increase and a new
positive term appears. An algebra automorphism permutes evaluation
characters, so \(U^{\mathsf T}v_i=v_{\pi(i)}\).
Unitarity forces \(\pi(i)=i\).
At a double root put \(w_i=(b_r'(c_i))_r\). The full local algebra
is \(\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\); fixing its character
leaves \(U^{\mathsf T}w_i=\beta_iw_i\), with \(\beta_i\ne0\).
For \(i\ge1\), differentiating the positive factors gives
\(v_i^{\mathsf T}w_i<0\), with a strictly negative \(r=1\) term.
Since \(U^{\mathsf T}\) is unitary, this forces \(\beta_i=1\).
The remaining double-root socle at \(c_0\) is spanned by
\[
 b_{N-1}(z)=\frac{(-1)^{N-1}P_N(z)}{N^2(z-c_0)}
                       =\mathcal T1,\qquad P_N=2T_N(z/2)+2.
\]
It is fixed by \(U\), so \(\beta_0=1\) too. The odd simple node
is already fixed by its value. Full primary decomposition proves
\(U=I\), including at \(N=2\).

This excludes averaging by that specified common unitary symmetry.
It does not classify edge-dependent stabilizers of a fixed network,
or symmetries of the larger physical spaces. Geometry-adapted
metrics and direct estimates of the original source remain possible.
None of these checks supplies the required volume rate after arbitrary
fixed short partial fillings; the finite-exception theorem remains open.

## Choosing the retained child lowers the residual degree, 24 November

The [degree reduction](research_conway_logarithmic_reduced_residual_degree.md)
simplifies the polynomial left after linear variables have been
integrated out. It retains Kashaev's original scalar, every complex
phase and every first-normal direction. It provides no new volume
estimate or finite-exception theorem.

First combine the known parts of the actual tangle recursion. A
product with two prescribed inputs becomes a known constant packet;
a product with one prescribed input becomes a known linear map.
Compose those maps with the intervening turns. Let \(q\) count
the original products whose two inputs both arrive from products.
The remaining literal source has \(\ell=q+1\) constant input
packets and \(q\) bilinear maps, hence \(2q+1\) proper vertices.
The original budgets can be grouped over these disjoint pieces:
their product \(B_N\) is exactly preserved and every normalized
map still has norm at most \(1/16\).
The fused maps are retained with their actual coefficients; no
unitarity of multiplication by a fixed packet is assumed.

At each remaining bilinear map, retain the child with more
descendant input packets. Solve the other gate equations exactly.
The resulting vector \(F\) consists of the retained residuals
and the original scalar closing. It satisfies
\[
 F:\mathbb C^{Nq}\longrightarrow\mathbb C^{Nq+1},\qquad
 \deg F\le d_\ell:=\max\{1,\lfloor\log_2\ell\rfloor\}.
\]
Every component is also affine separately in each retained packet.
To prove the degree bound, follow an eliminated child: its subtree
has at most half as many input packets as its parent. Each product
adds at most one to the degree, and a solved constant leaf has
degree zero. A retained gate's own residual adds only its linear
term \(-u_v\); the top closing adds no degree.

The compact reciprocal theorem therefore applies to this smaller
source with
\[
 \widehat B_N=N^{2q+2}B_N,\qquad
 \mathcal J_N=\frac{(Nq)!}{\pi^{Nq}}
       \int_{\mathcal U_N}\|F(u)\|^{-2(Nq+1)}\,du,
 \qquad \deg\|F\|^2\le2d_\ell.
\]
Here \(N\) is the quantum level, \(\mathcal U_N\) is the product
of retained unit packet balls, and \(F\) uses the rescaled maps.
For a fixed tree, at all sufficiently large levels with \(K_N\ne0\),
\[
 |K_N|^2=\frac{\widehat B_N^2}{\mathcal J_N}
                 (1+O_{\mathscr T}(N^{-1})).
\]
At a source zero the integral is infinite. For \(q=0\) it is a
one-point reciprocal and the equality is exact. The new auxiliary
energy and integral need not equal the earlier ones.
The original lifted objective still has degree at most four;
the logarithmic bound concerns the polynomial vector after elimination.

The degree improvement does not extend to the scalar polynomial
in the finite-fiber argument. For the full rescaled residual map
\(G\), put \(f(r)=c_N^{\rm new}(G^{-1}(r))_{\rm top}\) and
\(k_N=K_N/\widehat B_N\). Set internal residuals to zero and leaf
residuals to \(t\) times their prescribed rescaled constants.
Homogeneity gives \(f(r(t))=k_N(1-t)^\ell\). Thus
\(\deg f=\ell\) whenever \(K_N\ne0\).
Neither the remaining dimension \(Nq\) nor the original coherent
closing disappears. A geometric estimate of this particular
reciprocal integral is still required.

Author, root and two independent peers read the entire matching
final and all five complete selected source/coverage texts, checked
the implications used above, and renewed all six matching pins
after their reads. The elementary subtree-halving argument is not
claimed as a new general technique.

## The original turn-trace density has polynomial Newton norm, 24 November

The [full-normal operator proof](research_newton_turn_density_operator_bound.md)
upgrades the earlier pointwise estimates for the original turn-trace density
to a bound on its entire Newton multiplication operator. Use the actual
normalized Newton basis \(b_r\), the genuine unscaled turn \(\mathcal T\), and
\[
 \mathcal B_N(z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}b_r(z)^2,\qquad
 \mathfrak b_N=\mathcal B_N^{-1}\text{ in }\mathbb C[z]/P_N,
 \quad P_N=2T_N(z/2)+2,\quad \mathcal D_N=\mathcal T M_{\mathfrak b_N}.
\]
Here \(T_N\) is Chebyshev of the first kind and the inverse retains all
Hermite jets. At every \(N\ge2\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad \phi(f)=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal D_NM_f),\qquad
 \|M_{\mathfrak b_N}\|_{{\rm Newt}\to{\rm Newt}}=\|\mathcal D_N\|
       \le\lceil N/2\rceil(N+2).\quad}                    \tag{TD1}
\]
The trace identity is the original one; the global operator bound is the
new estimate. All first normals and original source factors remain.

For a canonical double node \(c_i=2\cos((2i+1)\pi/N)\),
\(0\le i\le\lfloor(N-2)/2\rfloor\), put
\(a_i=(-1)^{N-1}(4-c_i^2)\), \(\chi_i=c_i/(4-c_i^2)\). In the proof's
real orthonormal full-primary Newton frame \(E_i\), the normal scale obeys
\[
 \delta_i^2=\left.\partial_z\partial_w\log K_N(z,w)\right|_{(c_i,c_i)},
 \quad K_N(z,w)=\sum_r b_r(z)b_r(w),\quad
 \delta_i\le\frac{N-2i-1}{4\sin((2i+1)\pi/N)}.
\]
The source-residue matrix and the actual first derivative of \(\mathcal B_N\)
give the exact cancellation
\[
 C_i:=E_i^{\mathsf T}\mathcal T M_{\mathcal B_N}E_i
   =\frac1{a_i\delta_i}\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&\chi_i/\delta_i\end{pmatrix},
 \quad C_i^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}-a_i\chi_i&a_i\delta_i\\a_i\delta_i&0\end{pmatrix}.
                                                               \tag{TD2}
\]
Indeed \(a_i\chi_i=(-1)^{N-1}c_i\) and \(|a_i\delta_i|\le N\), so
\(\|C_i^{-1}\|\le N+2\). The odd simple block is exactly \(C_i=1\).
Distinct primary blocks have zero cross-pairing for this weighted turn.
The derivative is essential: scalar nodal replacement would not give (TD2).

Select any \(m\ge1\) full primary blocks and concatenate their frames as
\(V\). They are independent, and \(\|V\|^2\le m\); no lower joint-Gram
bound is used. For their sum \(I_J\), let \(P_J\) be its Newton orthogonal
projection. The actual measured weighted turn satisfies
\[
 H_J=P_J\mathcal T M_{\mathcal B_N}|_{I_J},\qquad
 H_J^{-1}=V\operatorname{diag}(C_i^{-1})V^{\mathsf T}|_{I_J},\qquad
                   \|H_J^{-1}\|\le m(N+2).                \tag{TD3}
\]
This holds for every selected size, not only sublinear windows. For the
whole algebra \(P_J=I\), so \((\mathcal T M_{\mathcal B_N})^{-1}
=M_{\mathfrak b_N}\mathcal T\). The original density is its conjugate
by \(\mathcal T\), not this inverse itself. This proves (TD1) with the
correct factor order and without a frame-condition loss.

The original closing direction is also fixed exactly. If \(s_N^2=\mathcal B_N\)
is the real Hermite unit with positive nodal values, then
\[
                    \phi M_{s_N}E_i=(1,0)                 \tag{TD4}
\]
at a double block, and equals \(1\) at the odd simple block. The first
coordinate is the nilpotent eigenvector direction. The other remains a
closing kernel. Recovering the unweighted source requires \(M_{s_N}^{-1}\);
no action factor has been deleted.

For fixed \(r\), the original tensor-source identity is
\(\phi^{\otimes r}(F)=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal D_N^{\otimes r}M_F)\).
Put \(C_N=\lceil N/2\rceil(N+2)\) and \(\|A\|_1=\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt{A^*A}\).
Every operator error on the full \(N^r\)-dimensional tensor algebra obeys
\[
 |\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal D_N^{\otimes r}\Delta A)|
 \le C_N^r\|\Delta A\|_1\le C_N^rN^r\|\Delta A\|_{\rm op}. \tag{TD5}
\]
The conversion factor from operator error to absolute source error is
polynomial, with the actual density retained in the leading trace.
The error itself is not asserted small, nor is this a relative scalar bound.

Already \(D_0=e_0e_d^{\mathsf T}\), where \(d=N-1\) and \(e_j\) are Newton
coordinate units, has \(\|D_0\|=1\) and \(\operatorname{Tr}(D_0M_f)=\phi(f)\).
A polynomial original closing density was also established in the [canonical cyclic-coproduct Gram](research_original_source_in_coproduct_graph_gram.md).
The present estimate concerns the specific invertible \(\mathcal D_N\)
in the fixed Newton metric with the kernel inverse from the turn-trace
theorem. Neither a first general co-source bound nor a comparison with
the cyclic-coproduct metric is asserted. The rank-one and canonical densities
agree on multiplication operators but need not on arbitrary inserted matrices;
(TD5) concerns the stated canonical extension.

The nodal weights \(\mathfrak b_N(c_i)\) can still be exponentially small.
The density remains indefinite, and no lower bound for its smallest
singular value or the prescribed scalar follows. Nor does (TD3) justify
inserting \(P_J\) into a closed source: its omitted component and exterior
remain. There is no new geometric lower bound or finite-exception theorem.
The weight and original Newton metric are retained, not a positive trace
substituted for the original source.

## Exact signed-twist transport on sublinear Newton windows, 24 November

The existing [Hermite filters](research_sublinear_physical_casimir_cluster_gram.md)
give an application of the [mixed metric bridge](research_conway_mixed_metric_source_compiler.md).
Fix \(N\ge2\), put \(Z=M_z\) on the full Newton algebra, and select \(m\ge1\)
distinct Casimir nodes \(c_i\) with their full multiplicities \(\nu_i\in\{1,2\}\).
Define
\[
 q_J(z)=\prod_{i=1}^m(z-c_i)^{\nu_i},\qquad I_J=\ker q_J(Z),\qquad
 \Lambda_{N,m}=m\log(eN/m)+\log N.                         \tag{NW1}
\]
Thus \(I_J\) is the sum of the selected full primary ideals. No bounded
ambient projector is assumed; every paired first normal remains.

There is a universal \(C\) such that, for every integer \(p\) and \(v\in I_J\),
\[
 \Gamma_{N,m,p}^{-1}\|v\|_{\rm Newt}\le\|R^pv\|_{\rm Newt}
       \le\Gamma_{N,m,p}\|v\|_{\rm Newt},\qquad
 \Gamma_{N,m,p}=(1+|p|)e^{C\Lambda_{N,m}}.                  \tag{NW2}
\]
The original crossing scalar is retained. The constant is independent of
\(p,N\), the selected nodes, and their multiplicities.

Here is an exact reciprocal construction. Put
\[
 \ell_i(z)=\frac{\prod_{k\ne i}(z-c_k)^{\nu_k}}
                       {\prod_{k\ne i}(c_i-c_k)^{\nu_k}},\qquad
 h_i=\begin{cases}\ell_i,&\nu_i=1,\\
 [1-\ell_i'(c_i)(z-c_i)]\ell_i,&\nu_i=2,\end{cases}\qquad
 k_i=(z-c_i)\ell_i\quad(\nu_i=2).                         \tag{NW3}
\]
The value-cardinals \(h_i\) have zero spectral derivative where that normal
exists. Each \(k_i\) has value zero and derivative one at its own double node.
They vanish to full multiplicity at every other selected node.

Let \(r_i=R(c_i)\), with its original common scalar, so \(|r_i|=1\).
The actual generic-confluence formula in the mixed-plat compiler gives
\(\rho_i=R'(c_i)/R(c_i)\) and \(|\rho_i|\le N^2/8\) at double nodes,
with both level parities retained. Define
\[
 g_{J,p}(z)=\sum_i r_i^{-p}h_i(z)
       -p\sum_{\nu_i=2}\rho_i r_i^{-p}k_i(z).             \tag{NW4}
\]
This polynomial matches the selected values of \(R^{-p}\) and its first
derivative at each selected double node. Its canonical representatives satisfy
\(g_{J,p}R^p\equiv1\pmod {q_J}\). Therefore
\[
              g_{J,p}(Z)M_{R^p}v=v\qquad(v\in I_J).      \tag{NW5}
\]
The forward interpolant is \(g_{J,-p}\); no source value defines either one.

For the bound, ordered selected cosine nodes satisfy
\(|c_i-c_k|\ge16|i-k|^2/N^2\). The actual Casimir is the orthogonal
direct sum of its physical degree blocks. The cluster theorem bounds
every block, including the high-degree mirror, by \(14\). Thus
\(\|\Omega\|_{\rm op}\le14\) and \(\|\Omega-c_i\|_{\rm op}\le16\).
Apply the same factorial filter proof on this whole operator:
\[
 \max_i\bigl(\|h_i(\Omega)\|_{\rm op}+\|k_i(\Omega)\|_{\rm op}\bigr)
       \le e^{C\Lambda_{N,m}},\qquad
 \|g_{J,p}(\Omega)\|_{\rm op}
       \le C m(1+|p|N^2)e^{C\Lambda_{N,m}}.               \tag{NW6}
\]
Omit \(k_i\) at simple nodes. Since \(mN^2\le e^{3\Lambda_{N,m}}\),
increasing \(C\) absorbs the polynomial factor into (NW2), uniformly in \(p\).
The mixed bridge bounds the Newton multiplier of this globally defined
surrogate by \(\|g_{J,p}(\Omega)\|_{\rm op}\). Apply it to (NW5) and
to the forward interpolant to prove both bounds, for arbitrary coherent \(v\).
This is the existing interpolation mechanism applied to the original source.

If \(m_N=o(N)\) and \(\log(1+|p_N|)=o(N)\), then \(\log\Gamma/N\to0\).
Thus these signed twists are bi-Lipschitz with subexponential cost on
full selected Newton windows, uniformly over their nodes and coefficients.
The filters are not ambient projectors and do not control the unselected part.

The genuine turn obeys \(\mathcal T I_J=\ker q_J(\mathcal TZ\mathcal T)\).
A following \(R(Z)\) acts on that transverse window; (NW2) does not
estimate its coupling to the original \(Z\)-window. Arbitrary short words
and the prescribed closing still need their original overlap estimate.
No geometric scalar lower bound or finite-exception result follows here.

## A mixed metric reduces the leaf normalization costs, 24 November

The [mixed compiler](research_conway_mixed_metric_source_compiler.md) gives a
quantitative bridge between the original physical and Newton packet metrics.
Write \(\|f\|_{\rm ph}=\|f(\Omega)\|_{\rm HS}\), with unnormalized physical
Hilbert--Schmidt norm. At every \(N\ge2\), on the full repeated-root algebra,
\[
 \|M_f\|_{{\rm Newt}\to{\rm Newt}}\le\|f(\Omega)\|_{\rm op},
 \qquad \|fg\|_{\rm Newt}\le\|f\|_{\rm ph}\|g\|_{\rm Newt}.
 \tag{MM1}
\]
Commutativity exchanges the inputs; taking \(g=1\) also gives
\(\|f\|_{\rm Newt}\le\|f(\Omega)\|_{\rm op}\le\|f\|_{\rm ph}\).
The literal head exchange \(S\) gives \(\Omega^*=S\Omega S\), while
\(M_f^\dagger=\mathcal T M_{f^\sharp}\mathcal T\) in the Newton metric;
\(f^\sharp\) is coefficient reflection. For \(B=M_f^\dagger M_f\), the
spectral radius is the squared Newton operator norm. Its operator norm
on the physical packet space is at most \(\|f(\Omega)\|_{\rm op}^2\).
The genuine turn is unitary in both metrics, so no condition-number
comparison enters. The same proof handles rectangular coefficient matrices:
\[
 \|[M_{f_{ij}}]\|_{{\rm Newt}^b\to{\rm Newt}^a}
                     \le\|[f_{ij}(\Omega)]\|_{\rm op}.
 \tag{MM2}
\]
This does not assert norm one for the Hilbert tensor flattening of the
mixed bilinear multiplication.

For a literal tree with \(s\) proper vertices and \(L\) leaves, choose one
leaf and put the Newton metric on its path to the root; every other packet
is physical. All products have bilinear norm at most one, all turns have
norm one, and both original root rows have dual norm one.

Two leaves can instead be chosen in opposite child subtrees of the highest
binary product. Use those two Newton paths below that product. At the
product, use the existing full multiplication quotient
\[
 C=MM^\dagger>0,\qquad \|y\|_{\rm quot}^2=y^\dagger C^{-1}y,
 \qquad C^{-1/2}M\text{ is a coisometry}.
 \tag{MM3}
\]
Transport this metric through the unary top turns. The final original row
has dual norm \(\gamma_N=1\) or \(\sqrt N\), according as its pulled-back
row is \(\lambda_0\) or \(\phi\). These exact costs are already in the
quotient theorem. Every boundary coordinate and original mark remains.

Let \(S_*\) be the selected one- or two-leaf set and retain the known external
factor \(\eta_N\). Use budget \(16\) at each internal gate, Newton leaf
budgets at selected leaves, physical leaf budgets elsewhere, and root budget
\(16\max(1,|\eta_N|\gamma_N)\). Here \(\gamma_N=1\) for one path. Thus
\[
 B_{\rm mix}=16^{s+1}\max(1,|\eta_N|\gamma_N)
  \prod_{\ell\in S_*}\max(1,\|A_\ell\|_{\rm Newt})
  \prod_{\ell\notin S_*}\max(1,\|A_\ell\|_{\rm ph}).
 \tag{MM4}
\]
Every normalized local norm is at most \(1/16\). The one-path budget never
exceeds the stated all-physical budget. Two selected leaf factors are
exchanged at only the possible root cost \(\sqrt N\).

For the two-path source itself, both separately bilinear closing rows
have norm one. Consequently
\[
 |K_N|\le|\eta_N|
     \prod_{\ell\in S_*}\|A_\ell\|_{\rm Newt}
     \prod_{\ell\notin S_*}\|A_\ell\|_{\rm ph}.
 \tag{MM5}
\]
The factor \(\sqrt N\) is needed for the quotient's linear row, not for
this decomposable-input upper bound.

The compact theorem applies in these prescribed metrics. Put \(n=N(L-1)\)
and \(\widehat B_{\rm mix}=N^{s+1}B_{\rm mix}\). After linear elimination
in the new compiler, its residual vector and original scalar row give
\[
 \mathcal J_{\rm mix}=\frac{n!}{\pi^n}\int_{\mathcal U_N}
                    \|F_{\rm mix}(u)\|^{-2(n+1)}du.
\]
The domain is the product of retained unit packet balls; the measure is
rebuilt in the chosen orthonormal coordinates. For nonzero sources at
sufficiently large levels,
\[
 |K_N|^2=\frac{\widehat B_{\rm mix}^{\,2}}{\mathcal J_{\rm mix}}
                        (1+O_{\mathscr T}(N^{-1})).
 \tag{MM6}
\]
At a source zero the integral is infinite and its reciprocal is zero;
the one-point convention covers \(L=1\). The actual \(R^{\pm1}\) leaves
have Newton norm \(\sqrt N\). Arbitrary fixed powers retain their actual
Newton norms; no polynomial bound for all powers is asserted.

This changes known leaf normalization costs while retaining the full
source. It defines a new normalized integral, not the numerical value of
the earlier physical one. Dimension and denominator power still grow
when \(L>1\). The geometric upper estimate on
\(\mathcal J_{\rm mix}/\widehat B_{\rm mix}^{\,2}\) remains missing.
There is no new volume lower bound or finite-exception theorem.

## What fixed degree still leaves to prove, 24 November

The adopted formulation has already simplified the original source
problem. Its objective has degree at most four. The polynomial inverse
of the triangular residual map gives \(f=cG^{-1}\) of degree at most
\(L\), the fixed number of leaf occurrences. These are degree bounds;
the number of complete packet coordinates still depends on \(N\).

Exact integration removes every packet that enters linearly. One child
packet remains for each of the \(L-1\) binary products, leaving
\(n=N(L-1)\) complex coordinates. Let \(s\) count proper vertices.
After the recorded polynomial budget change, the compact formulation is
\[
 \mathcal J_N=\frac{n!}{\pi^n}\int_{\mathcal U_N}
          \|F(u)\|^{-2(n+1)}\,du,\qquad
 \widehat B_N=N^{s+1}B_N .
\]
Here \(\mathcal U_N\) is the product of retained unit packet balls.
The known vector \(F\) lists their residual rows and the original scalar
closing after the eliminated gate equations have been solved exactly.
Every phase and first-normal direction remains. For nonzero sources,
at all sufficiently large levels,
\[
 |K_N|^2=\frac{\widehat B_N^2}{\mathcal J_N}
                    \bigl(1+O_{\mathscr T}(N^{-1})\bigr).
\]
At a source zero the integral is infinite and its reciprocal is zero.
When \(L>1\), its dimension, denominator exponent and factorial
normalization grow with \(N\). This does not determine the exponential
rate of \(\mathcal J_N/\widehat B_N^2\).

Contracting an already known short subtree can reduce \(L\) and the
retained packets, but its entire original boundary vector must remain.
Computing that vector is not a new volume estimate.

The prescribed leaves have more structure than arbitrary packets:
every signed crossing power \(R^p\) is an invertible element of the
full repeated-root algebra. The genuine quarter-turn does not preserve
the set of algebraic units. To see this, put \(d=N-1\), \(S_0=1\), and
\[
 c_j=2\cos\frac{(2j+1)\pi}{N},\qquad
 S_r=\prod_{h=1}^r2\sin\frac{\pi h}{N},\qquad
 b_r(z)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{j<r}(c_j-z).
\]
The full algebra is \(\mathbb C[z]/P_N\), with
\(P_N(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(z-c_j)=2T_N(z/2)+2\);
here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial, distinct from the turn
\(\mathcal T\). The exact turn identity is \(\mathcal T1=b_d\).
This element is nonzero because its degree is \(N-1\). But
\(c_d=c_0\) is a double root of \(P_N\), \(S_d=N\), and
\[
 b_d(z)=\frac{(-1)^dP_N(z)}{N^2(z-c_0)},\qquad
 b_d(z)^2=\frac{P_N(z)}{N^4}\,
                         \frac{P_N(z)}{(z-c_0)^2}.
\]
The last quotient is a polynomial, so \(b_d^2=0\) in the full
algebra at every \(N\ge2\). No first-normal direction was discarded.
Invertibility of the actual \(R^p\) leaves therefore supplies no
automatic reduction of arbitrary short subtrees to identity packets
through the turn. The unit property alone gives no bound on the
complete change of frame or the transformed closing row.

Geometry-adapted positive packet metrics remain allowed by the compact
theorem; their actual budgets, measure and original closing must be
retained. The observation above is a limitation of the proposed
reduction, not a vanishing claim for a prescribed knot.

This clarification adds no new volume bound or finite-exception
result. The noncancellation lower bound still needs an estimate using
the actual crossing phases and first normals with the original cap
retained. In the compact formulation, the missing estimate is a
geometric upper bound for \(\mathcal J_N/\widehat B_N^2\).

## A compact polynomial integral with a controlled source error, 24 November

The [compact integral proof](research_conway_compact_reciprocal_source.md)
removes the unbounded retained domain and its variable Gram weight
after an explicit polynomial change of normalization. For every fixed
literal Conway tree, the resulting compact integral gives a two-sided
relative approximation to the reciprocal squared normalized invariant.
This holds in any prescribed positive packet metrics, with all
normalizations retained. Its geometric volume rate is still unproved.

At level \(N\ge2\), let \(s\) count proper vertices, \(L\) leaf
occurrences, and \(p=L-1\) binary products. Start with known budgets \(b_v\) making
the leaf, linear, bilinear and closing norms at most \(1/16\).
Multiply every proper budget and the scalar root budget by \(N\):
\[
 B_N=\prod_vb_v,\qquad
 \widehat B_N=N^{s+1}B_N,\qquad \sigma_N=\frac1{16N}.
 \tag{CI1}
\]
The normalized maps and closing now have norms at most \(\sigma_N\).
This specifies a new normalized energy and integral; their numerical
values are not identified with an earlier normalization.

As in the exact linear elimination, retain one child packet at every
binary product, with coordinates \(u\in\mathbb C^n\),
\(n=Np\). Solve all eliminated gate equations by forward substitution.
Let \(F(u)\in\mathbb C^{n+1}\) consist of the remaining proper
residuals and the original scalar closing at that field. It is
computed from the original local tensors, with every phase and
first-normal direction retained. Every component has degree at most
\(L\). For the product \(\mathcal U_N\) of the retained unit packet
balls, define
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \mathcal J_N=\frac{n!}{\pi^n}
       \int_{\mathcal U_N}\|F(u)\|^{-2(n+1)}\,du .
 \qquad} \tag{CI2}
\]
No variable Gram matrix or determinant occurs in this compact
integrand. The denominator base can have degree \(2L\).

Here is why their removal is justified for this recompiled source.
Write \(D=Ns\), \(k=K_N/\widehat B_N\), and let \(\mathcal P_N\)
be the full reciprocal integral of its quartic residual energy.
On \(\mathcal U_N\), the exact boundary Gram \(R\) satisfies
\[
 I\le R\le(1+\eta_N)I,\qquad
 \eta_N=(16N-1)^{-2},\qquad
 \tau_N=(n+1)\log(1+\eta_N).
\]
Thus the exact reduced density and the density in (CI2) differ
pointwise by factors between \(e^{-\tau_N}\) and \(e^{\tau_N}\).
For the exterior, use the triangular polynomial inverse \(x=H(r)\)
of the original residual map, with real Jacobian one. If
\(\|r\|\le1/4\), every packet of \(H(r)\) has norm at most
\(\sigma_N+1/4<1\). Consequently the entire part outside
\(\mathcal U_N\) costs at most
\[
 \frac{D!}{\pi^D}\int_{\|r\|>1/4}\|r\|^{-2D-2}\,dr=16D .
\]
The true forward field obeys \(|k|\le\sigma_N^{s+1}\).
Finite-fiber orthogonality then gives
\[
 (1-\delta_N)e^{-\tau_N}\mathcal P_N
       \le\mathcal J_N\le e^{\tau_N}\mathcal P_N,\qquad
 \delta_N=16DL\sigma_N^{2s+2}\le\frac1{4096N^3}.
 \tag{CI3}
\]
These bounds include the zero-source case as an extended
nonnegative comparison.

A short affine calculation gives the two-sided calibration.
For \(f=cH\) on the residual ball, the same normalization gives
\(\|D^2f\|\le M_N=\sigma_N^2(8/7)^3\).
Completing the square for its affine part yields its exact reciprocal
integral \(|k|^{-2}\). The Taylor remainder and both exterior
bounds give, for nonzero sources,
\[
 \big||k|^2\mathcal P_N-1\big|
 \le \exp\!\left(\frac27(D+1)M_N\right)-1
                         +32D\sigma_N^{2s+2}.
\]
Together with (CI3), this proves an explicit
\(\epsilon_N=O_{\mathscr T}(N^{-1})\) such that, for all sufficiently
large levels,
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 (1-\epsilon_N)\frac{\widehat B_N^2}{\mathcal J_N}
 \le |K_N|^2\le
 (1+\epsilon_N)\frac{\widehat B_N^2}{\mathcal J_N}.
 \qquad} \tag{CI4}
\]
At \(K_N=0\), the compact integral is infinite and its reciprocal
is zero. No source lower bound is assumed. The error is uniform
over the normalized prescribed leaf packets for the fixed tree.
When \(p=0\), \(\mathcal J_N=|k|^{-2}\) exactly.

One may choose positive packet metrics from known geometric data
and normalize the actual tensors in those metrics before applying
(CI1). The proof requires no comparison to the old metrics.
All their actual budgets must still be included in \(B_N\).
For a fixed tree the additional factor \(N^{s+1}\) has logarithm
\(o(N)\).

The remaining geometric task is an upper estimate for
\(\mathcal J_N/\widehat B_N^2\) after an arbitrary fixed short
partial filling. The original signed closing is still a component
of \(F\). Both the dimension \(n=Np\) and the denominator exponent
grow with the level, and the prefactor \(n!/\pi^n\) remains.
This proof supplies neither a fixed-dimensional Laplace argument
nor a new volume-conjecture case. The finite-exception theorem
remains open.

## Finite leaf degree simplifies the lower bound and the positive integral, 24 November

The [finite-fiber proof](research_conway_reciprocal_finite_fiber_lower_bound.md)
gives two further simplifications. It proves the lower comparison with
the original invariant without the Gaussian calibration estimates,
and it integrates out all packets that enter linearly. The earlier
Wick theorem remains stronger as a two-sided relative asymptotic.
Neither result evaluates the integral from hyperbolic geometry.

Fix a literal Conway tree with \(s\) proper vertices and \(L\ge1\)
leaf occurrences. At level \(N\ge2\), each packet has its full \(N\)
complex physical coordinates, including all first-normal directions.
Keep the original normalized maps \(\Phi_v\), closing row \(c\),
and known budget product \(\mathcal B_N\). Put \(D=Ns\) and
\[
 G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_j)_j)-x_v,\qquad
 E_N(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|cx|^2,\qquad
 \mathcal P_N=\frac{D!}{\pi^D}
                 \int_{\mathbb C^D}E_N(x)^{-D-1}\,dx .
 \tag{FF1}
\]
The objective has degree at most four. A second degree bound supplies
the shorter proof: the triangular polynomial inverse \(H=G^{-1}\)
has real Jacobian one, and its original closing
\[
 f(r)=cH(r),\qquad \deg f\le L,\qquad
 k=f(0)=K_N/\mathcal B_N
 \tag{FF2}
\]
has degree bounded by the leaf count. This bound does not grow with
the quantum level or the magnitudes of the fixed filling coefficients.

For \(k\ne0\), set \(\nu=\max(1,\deg f)\le L\),
\(J(r)=f(r)-r\cdot\nabla f(r)\), and \(T(r)=r/f(r)\).
A generic fiber of \(T\) has \(\nu\) points \(r_j=t_jw\), where
\(f(t_jw)=t_j\). The exact partial-fraction trace is
\(\sum_j J(r_j)^{-1}=k^{-1}\).
With the probability measure
\[
 d\mu_D(w)=\frac{D!}{\pi^D}
                       \frac{dw}{(1+\|w\|^2)^{D+1}},
\]
change of variables and orthogonal projection in the counting inner
product on each fiber give
\[
 \mathcal P_N=\frac{1}{\nu|k|^2}
       +\int\sum_{j=1}^{\nu}
          \left|\frac1{J(r_j)}-\frac1{\nu k}\right|^2d\mu_D,
 \qquad
 \boxed{\quad |K_N|^2\ge
                  \frac{\mathcal B_N^2}{L\mathcal P_N}.\quad}
 \tag{FF3}
\]
The projection is independent of the ordering of the fiber points.
The proof accounts for the exceptional algebraic sets by ordinary
change of variables on inverse charts; it assumes no properness at
infinity. If \(K_N=0\), the integral diverges at the zero residual
field, and its reciprocal is zero. Thus the lower comparison holds
at all levels and for arbitrary complex prescribed leaf data.

It also holds after any prescribed positive Hermitian packet metrics
are chosen and the integral, its measure, and its known normalizations
are consistently rebuilt. The own-output residual coefficient remains
\(-I\), so the Jacobian and degree arguments remain valid. This
permits a metric chosen from geometric data without a conditioning
comparison to the physical metric. It does not preserve the numerical
integral or assert a two-sided approximation in the new metric.

For the exact integral reduction, retain one child packet at every
binary product. There are \(p=L-1\) such packets. Write their
coordinates as \(u\in\mathbb C^n\), \(n=Np\), and the remaining
coordinates as \(z\in\mathbb C^m\), \(m=D-n\). At fixed \(u\),
the original residuals split as
\[
 r_z=T(u)z+b_z(u),\qquad r_o=C(u)z+b_o(u).
\]
Here \(T=-I+\) a strictly triangular matrix has determinant of
modulus one for every complex \(u\); the scalar closing remains a
row of \(r_o\). Define
\[
 \mathsf D=CT^{-1},\quad F=b_o-CT^{-1}b_z,\quad
 R=I_{n+1}+\mathsf D\mathsf D^*,\quad q=F^*R^{-1}F .
\]
Hermitian square completion and radial integration give the exact
extended nonnegative identity
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \mathcal P_N=\frac{n!}{\pi^n}
       \int_{\mathbb C^n}\frac{du}{\det R(u)\,q(u)^{n+1}} .
 \qquad} \tag{FF4}
\]
This integrates over the whole complex spaces. No estimate restricted
to packet balls is used outside those balls. Both the Gram matrix
and its determinant remain in the formula. If \(p=0\), the scalar
Gram cancels and gives \(\mathcal P_N=|k|^{-2}\) exactly.

Since \(L\) is fixed, the loss in the logarithmic lower bound is
only \(\pi\log L/N\). For the lower-bound half of the volume identity,
one may therefore seek a geometric upper estimate for the smaller
positive integral (FF4), with every chosen metric and budget retained.
No such estimate after arbitrary fixed short partial fillings has
been established. The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## A connected holomorphic chamber of the complete filling source, 24 November

The [holomorphic source proof](research_holomorphic_long_filling_source.md)
establishes a nonzero asymptotic for the entire original source on
one connected complex domain. This domain contains every sufficiently
long real signed tuple, together with paths joining its sign patterns
through positive imaginary powers. It supplies an actual holomorphic
source and its logarithmic differential, with a nonzero coefficient.
It does not yet reach arbitrary short real partial fillings.

Fix a strict Conway construction with \(b\ge2\) crossing circles.
For \(N\ge3\), put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(\kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)}\), and
\(c_k=q^{2k+1}+q^{-2k-1}\), \(0\le k\le d\).
Use the exact crossing family in the original full pair algebra:
\[
 R_s(c_k)=\kappa^s e^{\pi i s k(k-d)/N},\qquad
 (w\partial_w)R_s(w+w^{-1})|_{w=q^{2k+1}}
       =-\frac{s}{2}(d-2k)R_s(c_k).
 \tag{HC1}
\]
The normal is retained at double nodes; the odd simple node has
only its value. The exponential lift specifies every power.
Full Hermite interpolation gives \(R_sR_t=R_{s+t}\), and the
original signed crossing powers are recovered at integers.
Let \(Z_N(s)\) be the unframed original tensor evaluation with
these coupons at the fixed disks. It is entire in
\(s\in\mathbb C^b\). Noninteger parameters here describe this
analytic source, not a new topological filling operation.

There are constants \(L>1\), \(\eta>0\), depending on the
construction, for which the theorem holds on
\[
 \Omega_{L,\eta}=\{s\in\mathbb C^b:
                   |s_j|>L,\ \Im s_j>-\eta\text{ for all }j\}.
 \tag{HC2}
\]
Let \(\Psi\) and \(B\) be the proved strict pure Fourier action
and its nonzero amplitude near zero, with
\(\Psi(0)=F_0\), \(\Psi''(0)=-2\operatorname{diag}(g_j)\),
\(g_j>0\). The unit-charge critical point \(z(s)\) is the unique
nearby solution of
\[
 \nabla\Psi(z)+2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(s)z
                       +2\pi i\mathbf1=0,
 \qquad \Im z_j(s)>0,
 \tag{HC3}
\]
where \(\mathbf1\) is the vector of ones. Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 S(s)&=\Psi(z(s))+\pi i\sum_js_jz_j(s)^2+2\pi i\sum_jz_j(s),\\
 \mathcal Q(s)&=-\Psi''(z(s))-2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(s),\\
 D(s)&=\frac{(-2i)^b(2\pi)^{b/2}B(z(s))
                        \prod_j\sin(2\pi z_j(s))}
                       {\sqrt{\det\mathcal Q(s)}},\\
 \Gamma_N(s)&=\exp\!\left(\frac{\pi i d^2}{4N}\sum_js_j\right).
 \end{split}
 \tag{HC4}
\]
The Gaussian square root uses \(\Re\mathcal Q>0\).
Both \(S,D\) are holomorphic throughout (HC2), and \(D\) is
nowhere zero with a specified logarithm. For every compact
\(K\Subset\Omega_{L,\eta}\), the entire original source satisfies
\[
 \Gamma_N(s)^{-1}Z_N(s)
    =N^{3/2}D(s)e^{NS(s)}(1+E_N(s)),\qquad
 \sup_K|\partial_s^\alpha E_N|=O_{K,\alpha}(N^{-1})
 \tag{HC5}
\]
for every fixed derivative multi-index \(\alpha\). In particular
the actual source is zero-free on a buffered neighborhood of
\(K\) for all sufficiently large integer levels, with both
parities and composite levels included.

The proof estimates the whole source before parameter differentiation.
For the normalized crossing \(\kappa^{-s/2}R_s\), the physical
values are \(e^{\pi i sNz_k^2}\),
\(z_k=(k+1/2)/N-1/2\). Finite Fourier-Hermite inversion gives
its ordinary-circle coefficient bound
\[
 \sum_{a<N}|\beta_a(s)|
       \le2N(1+|s|/2)e^{(\pi N/4)(-\Im s)_+},
 \qquad t_+=\max(t,0).
 \tag{HC6}
\]
Positive imaginary powers therefore introduce no exponential cost
in restoring the source outside its retained pure corridor. A fixed
small negative collar costs at most \(\pi b\eta/4\) in its rate.
The original endpoint currents and their quadratic endpoint zeros
are retained; their distant-charge sums are estimated before any
local contour is selected.

The connecting faces have a uniform estimate even at large positive
imaginary powers. For a local positive charge \(\ell\), put
\(f(z)=\Psi(z)+\pi i\sum_js_jz_j^2+2\pi i\ell\cdot z\)
and let its critical height be \(y=\Im z_\ell\). Translate the
whole real cube simultaneously by \(i\theta y\),
\(0\le\theta\le1\). Its real-phase maximum
\(H(\theta)=\max_x\Re f(x+i\theta y)\) has an interior
maximizer, controlled by a diagonally weighted contraction.
At that maximizer write \(A=\Re f''<0\), \(C=\Im f''\).
The exact envelope identity is
\[
 H''(\theta)=-y^{\mathsf T}Ay
                    -y^{\mathsf T}CA^{-1}Cy\ge0,
 \qquad H'(1)=0,\qquad H(0)=F_0.
 \tag{HC7}
\]
Thus \(H(\theta)\le F_0\). Strict horizontal concavity leaves
a fixed loss on every swept side face. This gives the actual
translated contour coefficient one. The other local charges have
a strict gap on each compact \(K\); the unit-sign contributions
are exactly equal, including their parity signs. The normalized
full-source remainder in (HC6) is below that same surviving action.

The resulting logarithmic differential is calibrated as a function:
\[
 \frac1N d\log(\Gamma_N^{-1}Z_N)
    =\pi i\sum_jz_j(s)^2\,ds_j
                +\frac1N d\log D(s)+O_K(N^{-2}).
 \tag{HC8}
\]
All fixed parameter derivatives satisfy the stated error. The action
has the absolute anchor \(S(s)\to F_0\) as
\(\min_j|s_j|\to\infty\) within the chamber. The known Cartan
factor \(\Gamma_N\) remains explicit throughout.

This is compact-local control on an unbounded connected domain.
The level threshold depends on \(K\); there is no uniform
zero-free assertion on all of (HC2), and parameters growing with
\(N\) are outside the theorem. At admissible integer tuples the
original framing convention is restored as in the frozen volume
theorem. No new knot-volume class or arbitrary-short-filling
continuation is inferred. The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## Coherent endpoint transport and exact boundary minimization, 24 November

The [crossing proof](research_coherent_endpoint_to_bulk_crossing_norm.md)
now gives a lower bound for an entire family of coherent boundary
states. Estimating each column separately would leave open the
possibility that their complex coefficients cancel. The proof instead
controls their actual Gram matrix, including all cross terms.

Use the original orthonormal head basis, put
\(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and let
\(R_N^\pm\) be the original signed checked crossings. Define
\[
 H_m^+=\operatorname{span}\{|d-a,a\rangle:0\le a<m\},\qquad
 H_m^-=\mathsf P H_m^+,\qquad
 h_*=\int_0^{5/6}\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt>0,
 \tag{CB1}
\]
where \(\mathsf P\) exchanges the two physical heads. There is an
absolute \(C\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\) and
\(1\le m\le N/2\),
\[
 e^{Nh_*-C\Lambda_{N,m}}\|v\|
 \le\|R_N^\pm v\|
 \le e^{Nh_*+C\Lambda_{N,m}}\|v\|,\qquad
 \Lambda_{N,m}=m\log(eN/m)+\log N,\quad v\in H_m^\pm .
 \tag{CB2}
\]
Thus every nonzero vector in a band of width \(m_N=o(N)\) has
the same outgoing norm exponent \(h_*\), even when its coefficients
and phases depend on \(N\). The outgoing vector includes the bulk;
it is not projected back onto the input band.

Here is the mechanism. With \(x=-q^{-1}\), the physical head
operators are
\(K|a\rangle=xQ^{-a}|a\rangle\),
\(E|a\rangle=(Q^{-a}-1)|a-1\rangle\), and
\(F|a\rangle=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1\rangle\), with missing arrows zero.
The exact checked crossing identity is
\[
 A=R_N^+K_1(R_N^+)^{-1}=K_2-qE_2K_1F_1,
 \qquad \|A\|\le5 .
 \tag{CB3}
\]
The columns \(f_a=R_N^+|d-a,a\rangle\) are eigenvectors of
\(A\) with eigenvalues \(-qQ^a\). Consecutive selected eigenvalues
are separated by at least \(4|a-b|/N\). Lagrange interpolation
in the bounded operator \(A\), retaining the factorial products
of these separations, gives
\[
 e^{-C\Lambda_{N,m}}I\preceq V_m^*V_m\preceq mI,
 \qquad V_mc=\sum_{a<m}c_a\frac{f_a}{\|f_a\|}.
 \tag{CB4}
\]
This uses operator products, not a spectral supremum for a nonnormal
matrix. The exact column moduli are
\(S_i^2/(S_{i-a}S_a^2)\) for \(i\ge a\), where
\(S_j=\prod_{r=1}^j2\sin(\pi r/N)\), \(S_0=1\).
Their column norms satisfy the two exponential bounds in (CB2).
Combining this with (CB4) proves (CB2). The negative crossing
follows from \(R_N^-=\mathsf P\overline{R_N^+}\mathsf P\).

The binomial boundary cut also has an exact realization in this
pair space. For real \(0\le\lambda\le L\), set
\(\beta_{N,a}=\binom da(\lambda/N)^a(1-\lambda/N)^{d-a}\),
\(H_N=\operatorname{diag}\sqrt{\beta_{N,a}}\), and
\(P_N=H_N^2\). For the original cup \(p\), ordinary cap \(\ell\),
and pivot \(g=K^{1-N}\), one has exactly
\[
 \Psi_N^+=\frac{(I\otimes H_N)p}{N}
     =\sum_a x^{-a}\sqrt{\beta_{N,a}}|d-a,a\rangle,
 \quad (\Psi_N^+)^*=N\ell(I\otimes gH_N),\quad
 (\Psi_N^+)^*(I\otimes C_N)\Psi_N^+=\operatorname{Tr}(P_NC_N).
 \tag{CB5}
\]
The pivot and both \(N\) factors are part of this equality.
Censoring the weights at \(m-1\), including the final accumulated
mass, changes \(\Psi_N^+\) by at most
\(\sqrt{2C_L(C_L/m)^m}\). The signed counterpart is
\(\Psi_N^-=\mathsf P\overline{\Psi_N^+}\). Choosing
\(m=\lceil cN/\log N\rceil\) with \(c>2(\log20+A_0)\)
makes the error after the actual crossing \(O(e^{-A_0N})\),
using \(\|R_N^\pm\|\le20^{N-1}\). Consequently
\[
 \frac1N\log\|R_N^\pm\Psi_N^\pm\|\longrightarrow h_*
 \tag{CB6}
\]
uniformly for \(0\le\lambda\le L\), for each fixed \(L<\infty\).
The exact finite weights are used before crossing; the algebraic
error of a Poisson limit is not propagated through a growing matrix.

The [transport proof](research_coherent_endpoint_sweep_norm.md) extends
the coherent norm estimate to overlapping crossings. Fix \(b\ge2\)
heads and the positive sweep
\(\mathsf W_{b,N}=R_{b-1,b}^+\cdots R_{12}^+\). For all sufficiently
large \(N\), \(1\le m\le N/(24b)\), and every vector in
\(\mathcal H_{m,b}=\operatorname{span}\{|d-a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_{b-1}\rangle:
0\le a_j<m\}\), it proves
\[
 e^{Nh_*-C_b\Lambda_{N,m}}\|v\|
 \le\|\mathsf W_{b,N}v\|
 \le e^{Nh_*+C_b\Lambda_{N,m}}\|v\|.
 \tag{CT1}
\]
All coefficients may depend on \(N\); entangled inputs are included.
Each matrix entry has a unique transfer path, and its factorial
modulus telescopes. On sublinear windows the column exponent is
\(h_*\), independently of \(b\). Conjugates of the prefix products
\(K_1\cdots K_j\) have norm at most \(1+4(b-j)\) for \(j<b\);
the total product remains unitary. Their selected eigenvalue
indices occupy consecutive intervals of length \(j(m-1)+1\).
The joint filters therefore have total degree \(O_b(m)\), while
separating all \(m^b\) columns. No endpoint projection is inserted
between these crossings. This extends the earlier whole-fan
calculation to every coherent endpoint input.

There is also an exact orthogonality and elimination calculation
for the original returned endpoint block. Extend \(H_m^+\) in
(CB1) to every \(1\le m\le N\), let \(\mathcal Q_m\) be its
orthogonal projection, and put
\(B_m=\mathcal Q_m R_N^+\mathcal Q_m|_{H_m^+}\). With
\(f_a=(Q;Q)_a=\prod_{j=1}^a(1-Q^j)\), define
\[
 D_{aa}=x^{-a}/f_a,\qquad
 L_{ak}=\frac{f_a}{f_k f_{a-k}}\ (k\le a),\qquad
 L_{ak}=0\ (k>a),\qquad J_{kk}=Q^{k^2},\qquad U=DL.
 \tag{CT2}
\]
Here \(0\le a,k<m\), and empty products are one. The existing
long-transfer kernel and the finite Gaussian-binomial identity give
\[
 B_m=\kappa N U J U^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 \|B_m^{-1}\|\le16^m/N\quad(1\le m\le N),\qquad
 \kappa=q^{d^2/2}.
 \tag{CT3}
\]
The transpose is bilinear, whereas \(*\) below is Hermitian adjoint.
All these returned blocks are invertible. The factorization also
holds when a numerator \(f_{a+k}\) vanishes at the root: the original
entry is zero there, and no vanishing denominator is introduced.
Set
\[
 G_{\rm out}=(U^{-1})^*U^{-1},\qquad
 G_{\rm in}=(U^{\mathsf T})^*U^{\mathsf T}.
 \qquad B_m^*G_{\rm out}B_m=N^2G_{\rm in}.
 \tag{CT4}
\]
Both metrics are positive. For \(m\le N/2\), they and their
inverses have norm at most \(e^{C\Lambda_{N,m}}\). Thus they
are equivalent to the physical metric with subexponential costs
on every sublinear window. They are two specified incident metrics;
compatibility across an arbitrary gluing has not been proved.

In these coordinates a local quadratic minimization is exact:
\[
 \min_{c\in\mathbb C^m,\ c_0=1}\|B_mc\|_{G_{\rm out}}^2
       =N^2/m\qquad(1\le m\le N).
 \tag{CT5}
\]
Indeed set \(y=U^{\mathsf T}c\). Then
\(c_0=\sum_k a_ky_k\), where
\(a_k=(U^{-1})_{k0}=(-1)^kQ^{k(k-1)/2}\) has modulus one.
The objective is \(N^2\|y\|^2\); Cauchy--Schwarz gives the
minimum at \(y_k=\overline{a_k}/m\). Linear elimination of the
other returned coordinates also gives the explicit Schur scalar
\[
 \operatorname{Schur}_{00}B_m
       =\frac{\kappa N}{\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}Q^{-k}}
                                      \qquad(1\le m<N).
 \tag{CT6}
\]
Its modulus is \(N\sin(\pi/N)/\sin(\pi m/N)\), asymptotic
to \(N/m\) for \(m=o(N)\). At \(m=N\) the corresponding
cofactor is zero, so this elimination is unavailable. These are
the weighted returned-block quadratic problem and its associated
linear elimination, not the full Conway source minimum. Inserting
the returned projection into an internal network would require
retaining the complementary excursions and the actual exterior.

There is also an explicit assembly estimate for the boundary cutoff
under the existing tensor-prefix change of coordinates. At the
complete root, on a fixed number \(b\ge1\) of heads, write
\[
 Z=x^{-1}L_1F_{\rm tail},\qquad
 S=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{Z^j}{(Q;Q)_j},\qquad
 C_{\rm pref}(b)=2\max(1,b-1).
 \tag{CB7}
\]
Here \(L_1|a\rangle=|a-1\rangle\), with zero at \(a=0\),
and \(F_{\rm tail}\) is the ordered raising coproduct on the
remaining heads. Its norm is at most \(2(b-1)\).
Both \(S\) and its inverse have norm at most \(C_{\rm pref}(b)^{N-1}\):
their inverse-series coefficients have the same moduli, and
\(|(Q;Q)_j|^{-1}\le2^{N-1-j}/N\).
For each of the four finite boundary operators
\(U_N=P_N,B_N,D_NB_N,B_ND_N\) in the endpoint result below,
put \(\widehat U_N=S^{-1}(U_N\otimes I)S\). Its exact censored
version satisfies, at \(u=0\) and for \(2\le m\le N\),
\[
 \|\widehat U_N-\widehat U_N^{[m]}\|_1
 \le N^{b-1}C_{\rm pref}(b)^{2(N-1)}C(C/m)^m .
 \tag{CB8}
\]
The same estimate holds for fixed \(\lambda\)-derivatives on compact
complex sets. This follows from the endpoint trace-norm estimate,
\(\|X\otimes I\|_1=N^{b-1}\|X\|_1\), and the two similarity
norms. Thus \(m=\lceil cN/\log N\rceil\), with
\(c>2\log C_{\rm pref}(b)+A_0\), gives absolute error \(O(e^{-A_0N})\).
The transformed commutator remains
\([\widehat D_N,\widehat B_N^{[m]}]
=\widehat P_N^{[m]}-\widehat P_0\), with the original
\(\widehat P_0=S^{-1}(P_0\otimes I)S\) retained.

If the entire original exterior is transformed at the same time,
cyclicity removes the similarity cost in its source pairing:
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}\bigl((\widehat P_N-\widehat P_N^{[m]})
                         S^{-1}WS\bigr)
 =\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(((P_N-P_N^{[m]})\otimes I)W\bigr).
 \tag{CB9}
\]
All tail pivots and marks belong to \(W\). The censored operators
have first-head output indices below \(m\), because \(S^{-1}\)
only lowers that index. Their incoming indices still range over
the full head. For example, exactly,
\[
 S^{-1}(P_0\otimes I)S
   =\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}\frac{x^{-a}}{(Q;Q)_a}
                       |0\rangle\langle a|\otimes F_{\rm tail}^a .
 \tag{CB10}
\]
No long incoming band has been removed.

These estimates settle cancellation inside the selected outgoing
packet in the physical norm, and quantify the prefix cost of the
exact cut approximation. The original invariant is still its
prescribed coherent closing. A lower bound for that closing, or a
nonzero selected geometric framing period, has not been obtained.
Arbitrary intervening crossings and Conway branchings are not
asserted to preserve the endpoint bands. The finite-exception
theorem remains open.

## What the boundary minimum controls in the original gluing, 24 November

The exact local minimum (CT5) remains valid. Its use in the whole
source requires both a specified outgoing boundary value and the
actual Conway packet interface. The following calculations check
these requirements directly. They do not evaluate the full source
minimum or disprove a knot-volume identity.

First let \(B=B_m\), \(G=G_{\rm out}\), and
\(r=e_0^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}\), with the notation of (CT2)--(CT5).
All vectors in this paragraph have \(m\) coordinates. The explicit
inverse gives \(rG^{-1}r^*=m/N^2\). For a prescribed outgoing
vector \(y\) and coefficient \(\alpha\), it follows that
\[
 \inf_{c:\ c_0=\alpha}\|Bc-y\|_G^2
       =\frac{N^2}{m}|\alpha-r y|^2.
 \tag{BG1}
\]
Indeed put \(w=Bc-y\). Its constraint is
\(r w=\alpha-r y\), so weighted Cauchy--Schwarz gives the
displayed minimum, attained along \(G^{-1}r^*\). This is the
unconstrained vector problem; additional packet-ball restrictions
would require their own check. Setting \(y=0\) recovers (CT5).

For the full original crossing, retain an incoming vector \(z\)
in the complementary space \((I-\mathcal Q_m)(V\otimes V)\).
The residual is then
\(Bc+\mathcal Q_mR_N^+(I-\mathcal Q_m)z-y\), and its same
constrained infimum is exactly
\[
 \frac{N^2}{m}
 \left|\alpha-r y+
           r\mathcal Q_mR_N^+(I-\mathcal Q_m)z\right|^2.
 \tag{BG2}
\]
This is a gate-consistency residual. It vanishes at the exact
forward field, where \(y\) is the actual outgoing component.
Consequently the positive value in (CT5) is not a nonzero forcing
term that can be added to the whole variational problem with a
free outgoing packet. The original closing row remains a separate
term. The existing orthogonal-elimination proof retains exactly
that distinction.

There is a genuine local cap match, with a precise ordering. Put
\(v_a^+=|d-a,a\rangle\), \(v_a^-=|a,d-a\rangle\).
On four legs in the displayed tensor order, let \(\mathscr E\)
be the nested ordinary evaluation: it pairs legs \((1,4)\) and
\((2,3)\), using \(\ell_{ij}=x^i\mathbf1_{i+j=d}/N\).
Direct substitution gives
\[
 \mathscr E(v_a^+,v_b^+)=\frac{x^d}{N^2}\delta_{ab},
 \qquad
 \mathscr E(v_a^+,v_b^-)=\frac{x^d}{N^2}\delta_{a+b,d}.
 \tag{BG3}
\]
The identity \(G_{\rm in}=\overline{G_{\rm out}}^{-1}\)
therefore gives the exact dual positive metrics for the first
pairing, with scalar \(x^d/N^2\) retained. The second pairing
uses complementary indices; it is zero on the two small bands
if \(2m-2<d\). A different routing is a different contraction.
No permutation of physical strands is omitted here, and the
marked cap is not substituted for the ordinary one.

A genuine quarter-turn bends one leg before a whole two-head
evaluation. For an arbitrary four-index array, the raw bend made
from the original cup and ordinary cap is
\[
 (\mathfrak TB)_{ab;ce}
 =\sum_{u,v}p_{au}B_{bv;uc}\ell_{ve}
 =x^{a-e}B_{b,d-e;d-a,c}.
 \tag{BG4}
\]
On actual Hopf boxes this is the recorded Conway turn. Its
extension to arbitrary arrays is kept explicit here. If a matrix
\(M\) is embedded only in the middle-degree endpoint block,
\[
 B_M=\sum_{\alpha,\beta<m}M_{\beta\alpha}
        |d-\beta,\beta\rangle\langle d-\alpha,\alpha|,
\]
then the same literal contraction yields
\[
 \mathfrak T B_M
  =\sum_{\alpha,\beta<m}x^{\alpha+\beta-d}M_{\beta\alpha}
       |\alpha,d-\beta\rangle\langle\alpha,d-\beta|.
 \tag{BG5}
\]
Thus a returned-vector matrix is turned into a diagonal corner
array, rather than another copy of the same vector packet.
It need not belong to the full invariant algebra \(\mathcal A_N\).
Even retaining its entire middle-degree block does not supply
the off-diagonal entries of the whole turned crossing; those
also use its other integer-degree blocks.

The extra data for one turned returned block can be located
exactly. For any \(B\) and \(0\le u,v<m\),
\[
 (\mathfrak TB)_{d-u,u;d-v,v}
     =x^{d-u-v}B_{u,d-v;u,d-v}.
 \tag{BG6}
\]
The entry on the right belongs to degree \(d+u-v\), within
\(m-1\) of the middle degree. A source-preserving extension of
the boundary calculation must retain these correlated degree
data and the excursion blocks in (BG2). The complete Pascal
source already supplies an all-degree crossing alphabet and
records its nontrivial three-head reassociation. Its diagonal
factorial factors and the marked source cannot be removed on
the basis of the returned-block inverse.

These checks leave the next task at the original source: obtain
a nonzero contribution after the prescribed closing, using an
interface valid for the whole Conway packet. They give no new
partial-filling class. The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## A controlled endpoint current and an exponentially accurate marked cut, 24 November

The [endpoint Ward proof](research_trace_class_endpoint_ward_model.md)
controls the actual boundary layer where an interior Gaussian cut
description is not uniform. It also gives a small boundary window
with exponentially accurate marked-source pairings. The endpoint
current and the artificial window's last-row contribution are both
retained. This is a boundary-source estimate, not a calculation of
the remaining geometric framing period.

Here is the scaling and the exact source. Fix an integer \(N\ge2\).
In the original orthonormal
head basis \(|a\rangle\), \(0\le a<N\), put
\(Q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}\), \(M=e^{u/N}\), and
\(\theta=\lambda/N\), with complex \(|u|<\pi\) and bounded
\(\lambda\). Let \(P_N\) be the diagonal cut with weights
\[
 p_{N,a}=\binom{N-1}{a}(\lambda/N)^a
                    (1-\lambda/N)^{N-1-a},\qquad
 T_{N,r}=\sum_{a>r}p_{N,a},\qquad P_0=|0\rangle\langle0|.
 \tag{EW1}
\]
The original lowering matrix has
\(\mathcal E_N|a\rangle=\epsilon_{N,a-1}|a-1\rangle\) for
\(a\ge1\), vanishes on \(|0\rangle\), and uses
\(\epsilon_{N,r}=e^{u/N}Q_N^{-r-1}-e^{-u/N}\).
Rescale the lowering matrix and its original Ward current in
opposite directions:
\[
 D_N=N\mathcal E_N,\qquad
 B_N=-\sum_{r=0}^{N-2}
       \frac{T_{N,r}}{N\epsilon_{N,r}}|r+1\rangle\langle r|.
 \tag{EW2}
\]
No finite source normalization changes. The exact identity is
\[
 [D_N,B_N]=P_N-P_0,\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}((P_N-P_0)C)
                 =\operatorname{Tr}(B_N[C,D_N]).
 \tag{EW3}
\]
The matrix \(C\) still contains its actual crossings, pivots, marks
and closing data. The second equality keeps the marked defect;
it does not replace an arbitrary marked cut by an unmarked one.

Embed the head into \(\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\) by extending finite
matrices by zero. Define
\[
 p_a=e^{-\lambda}\lambda^a/a!,\quad
 \tau_r=\sum_{a>r}p_a,\quad P=\operatorname{diag}(p_a),\qquad
 B=\sum_{r\ge0}\frac{\tau_r}{2(\pi i(r+1)-u)}
                                      |r+1\rangle\langle r|.
 \tag{EW4}
\]
The limiting lowering operator satisfies
\(D_u|0\rangle=0\) and
\(D_u|a\rangle=(2u-2\pi ia)|a-1\rangle\), on the domain
\(\sum_{a\ge1}a^2|v_a|^2<\infty\). Its two products with
\(B\) have trace-class extensions. Uniformly on compact complex
parameter sets, the proof establishes
\[
 \begin{split}
 \|P_N-P\|_1+\|B_N-B\|_1
 &+\|D_NB_N-D_uB\|_1\\
 &+\|B_ND_N-BD_u\|_1=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
 [D_u,B]=P-P_0 .
 \end{split}
 \tag{EW5}
\]
Here trace norm is the sum of singular values. These are whole
operator estimates, including every fixed derivative in \(u\) and
\(\lambda\). The meridian derivatives use
\(\partial_u=(M/N)\partial_M\); the root \(Q_N\) is not varied.
No operator-norm limit of the unbounded lowering generators is
asserted. The scalar Poisson approximation is classical; the
additional control is on the actual current, both products, and
their endpoint source normalization.

The exponential approximation uses the exact finite coefficients,
rather than substituting the limit in (EW4). For \(2\le m\le N\), retain indices
\(0,\ldots,m-1\), put the total weight from indices
\(a\ge m-1\) at the last retained index, and truncate the current
sum to \(r\le m-2\). Call the resulting operators
\(P_N^{[m]},B_N^{[m]}\). Then, exactly,
\[
 [D_N,B_N^{[m]}]=P_N^{[m]}-P_0,\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}P_N^{[m]}=1 .
 \tag{EW6}
\]
For real probabilities the new probe is still positive. The last
mass is the required cutoff current, rather than an omitted error.
The trace-norm errors of \(P_N,B_N,D_NB_N,B_ND_N\) under this
replacement are at most \(C(C/m)^m\), also for all fixed parameter
derivatives on compact sets. This follows from the actual factorial
bound \(|p_{N,a}|\le e^L L^a/a!\) for \(|\lambda|\le L\).

In particular \(m_N=\lceil cN/\log N\rceil=o(N)\) gives
error \(e^{-cN+o(N)}\). If an original marked exterior has operator norm
\(\|C_N\|\le e^{C_\Gamma N+O(\log N)}\), then choosing
\(c>C_\Gamma+A\), for any \(A>0\), gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 |\operatorname{Tr}((P_N-P_N^{[m_N]})C_N)|&=O(e^{-AN}),\\
 |\operatorname{Tr}((B_N-B_N^{[m_N]})[C_N,D_N])|
                                                    &=O(e^{-AN}).
 \end{split}
 \tag{EW7}
\]
These two traces are equal by the exact retained current identity.
At the original complete root, the required exterior growth bound
holds for every fixed literal crossing/cup/cap diagram with
polynomially bounded marks: signed crossing norms are at most
\(20^{N-1}\), and the remaining fixed contractions have polynomial
cost. Arbitrary fixed short fillings can be retained in that diagram.
The constants may depend on the fixed diagram and its fixed filling
integers. For families of meridians or exterior derivatives, (EW7)
requires their growth bound on a buffered parameter neighborhood.

For an unmarked one-cut knot operator, every trace-one probe already
gives its scalar exactly. The new exponential statement concerns
controlled comparisons of marked cuts and their entire currents.
It is an absolute error estimate. Neither it nor the Poisson limit
calculates a geometric contribution, a relative error in \(K_N\),
or the internal framing chain. In particular no Fourier alias,
other endpoint, or internal channel has been discarded from the
original source. The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## Low-degree observations do not repair the original closing, 24 November

The physical transport estimates below control a packet's norm, but
even optimizing over low-degree polynomial observations does not
turn that norm into a lower bound for its original closing. This can
be checked uniformly for the actual single-crossing packet. The
calculation determines a limitation of this proposed repair; it is
not a counterexample to a hyperbolic-knot volume statement.

Let \(\Omega\) be the physical pair Casimir and work in its complete
algebra \(\mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[\Omega]\), with \(N\ge3\),
\(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)\), and
\(\|B\|_{\rm ph}^2=\operatorname{Tr}(B^*B)\).
Write
\[
 s_j=2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad S_j=\prod_{a=1}^j s_a,\quad S_0=1,
 \qquad e_j(\zeta)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{a<j}(c_a-\zeta).
 \tag{LC1}
\]
These are the full Newton polynomials, not distinct-root value
coordinates. The two original normalized closing rows are
\(\lambda_d=\phi\) and \(\lambda_0(f)=f(c_0)\).
Let \(R_N\) be the original crossing and
\(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\). For \(\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}\), the exact
source identities are
\[
 R_N^\epsilon=\kappa^\epsilon
       \sum_{j=0}^d(-q)^{\epsilon j}e_j,\qquad
 \phi(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=d},\qquad
 \zeta e_j=c_je_j-s_{j+1}^2e_{j+1}.
 \tag{LC2}
\]
The missing last term in the recurrence is zero in the full
Hermite quotient. Its Newton coefficient matrix has column
\(\ell^1\) norm at most six. Thus, for an ordinary polynomial
\(P(\zeta)=\sum_{k=0}^D a_k\zeta^k\) of degree \(D<N\),
\[
 \|P(\Omega)\|_{{\rm Newt},1}
       \le\sum_k|a_k|6^k
       \le\sqrt{D+1}\,6^D\|P\|_2,
 \qquad \|P\|_2^2=\sum_k|a_k|^2.
\]
Every coefficient of \(R_N^\epsilon\) in (LC2) has modulus one.
The Frobenius identity in that display therefore gives
\[
 |\lambda(R_N^\epsilon P(\Omega))|
       \le\sqrt{D+1}\,6^D\|P\|_2,
       \qquad \lambda\in\{\lambda_0,\lambda_d\}.
 \tag{LC3}
\]
For \(\lambda_0\) this also follows directly, with \(2^D\) in
place of \(6^D\), from
\(\lambda_0(R_N^\epsilon P)=\kappa^\epsilon P(c_0)\).
These are scalar bounds in their original normalization. The
Newton norm was used only to prove (LC3); no equivalence with the
physical norm is assumed.

The [physical transport theorem](research_uniform_physical_rational_word_transport.md),
applied to the empty packet and \(W_N=L_{R_N^\epsilon}\), supplies
the other half of the comparison. For sufficiently large \(N\),
\(1\le D\le N/32\), and nonzero \(P\) of degree at most \(D\),
\[
 \|R_N^\epsilon P(\Omega)\|_{\rm ph}
       \ge e^{-CD}(D/N)^{12D}\|P\|_2
                                      \|R_N^\epsilon\|_{\rm ph}.
 \tag{LC4}
\]
The [whole physical crossing calculation](research_full_physical_crossing_gaussian_packet.md)
evaluates the denominator at zero tilt:
\[
 \|R_N^\epsilon\|_{\rm ph}^2
       =\frac{\sqrt N}{4}
          e^{4G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi}(1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad
 G_{\rm Cat}=\sum_{r\ge0}\frac{(-1)^r}{(2r+1)^2}>0 .
 \tag{LC5}
\]
Combining (LC3)--(LC5), and absorbing \(\sqrt{D+1}\) in
\(e^{CD}\), proves the uniform bound
\[
 \frac{|\lambda(R_N^\epsilon P(\Omega))|}
      {\|R_N^\epsilon P(\Omega)\|_{\rm ph}}
 \le C N^{-1/4}
       e^{-2G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi+CD}(N/D)^{12D}.
 \tag{LC6}
\]
The denominator is nonzero because \(R_N^\epsilon\) is a unit
and \(\deg P<N\). For \(D=0\) the ratio is exactly
\(1/\|R_N^\epsilon\|_{\rm ph}\); no convention for \(0^0\)
is required. Zero scalar closings are included in the upper bound.

Consequently, for every \(D_N=o(N)\), uniformly over all nonzero
polynomials of degree at most \(D_N\), even with coefficients
chosen separately at each level,
\[
 \frac{|\lambda(R_N^\epsilon P_N(\Omega))|}
      {\|R_N^\epsilon P_N(\Omega)\|_{\rm ph}}
       \le e^{-2G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi+o(N)}.
 \tag{LC7}
\]
Here \(D_N\log(N/D_N)=o(N)\), and coefficient scaling cancels
from the ratio. There is even one fixed \(\delta>0\) for which
the ratio is at most \(e^{-G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi}\) for every
\(\deg P\le\delta N\) and all sufficiently large \(N\).
Choose \(\delta\le1/32\) with
\(C\delta+12\delta\log(1/\delta)<G_{\rm Cat}/\pi\), and use
(LC6). If the closing functional is normalized as well, the
physical bound \(\|\lambda\|_*\ge1/N\) changes only a polynomial
factor and leaves these exponential conclusions unchanged.

Full-degree data can escape this particular limitation. For
\(\lambda_d\), take \(P=e_d\). The exact endpoint identities give
\[
 R_N^\epsilon e_d=\kappa^\epsilon e_d,\quad
\phi(e_d)=1,\quad \|e_d\|_{\rm ph}=\|T1\|_{\rm ph}=N,
\]
where \(T\) is the genuine unitary quarter-turn. Its ratio is
\(1/N\). For \(\lambda_0\), take the full
canonical polynomial \(P=R_N^{-\epsilon}\); the output is the
identity, again with ratio \(1/N\). Both choices have degree
\(N-1\). No first-normal direction or original source factor is
discarded in these identities.

This rules out a scalar lower-bound argument based only on the
physical norm, almost-invariance, and arbitrary sublinear-degree
polynomial observations of this packet. It does not rule out a
different family of observations or a proof that estimates the
assembled original scalar directly. In particular it does not
invalidate the source-exact quartic minimum: that objective has
degree at most four in all of its packet coordinates, whose number
grows with \(N\). Its degree is unrelated to the Casimir degree
\(D\) bounded here. A geometric estimate of that minimum or of
the coherent corrected closing is still needed. The finite-exception
theorem remains unproved.
