## Physical observables through fixed rational tangles, 24 November

The [physical transport proof](research_uniform_physical_rational_word_transport.md)
now controls polynomial observations in the same positive metric as the
quartic source minimum. It uses the original quarter-turn, signed
crossing powers, and full repeated-root algebra. It does not estimate
a change of metric from Newton coordinates.

Here are the operators and the quantitative statements. Fix \(N\ge3\). On
\(\mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[\Omega]\), give physical matrices their
original Hilbert--Schmidt norm
\(\|B\|_{\rm ph}^2=\operatorname{Tr}(B^*B)\). Let
\[
 X=L_\Omega,\qquad Y=TXT,\qquad
 \mathsf R=L_{R_N},\qquad c_0=2\cos(\pi/N).
 \tag{PT1}
\]
Multiplication is denoted by \(L\). The map \(T\) is the genuine
quarter-turn; \(R_N\) is the original positive crossing polynomial
with its full Hermite inverse. A fixed word \(W_N\) is a finite
composition of \(T\) and fixed integer powers of \(\mathsf R\).
The word is fixed before the level \(N\) tends to infinity.
Then
\[
 \|W_NXW_N^{-1}\|_{\rm ph}
       +\|W_NYW_N^{-1}\|_{\rm ph}\le C_W .
 \tag{PT2}
\]
These are operator norms on the physical packet space. Commutators
of any two such fixed transported observables are \(O(N^{-1})\).
Neither \(\|W_N\|\) nor \(\|W_N^{-1}\|\) is bounded here.

The proof realizes the two Casimirs on the actual four-index arrays
as fixed finite sums of cyclic shifts and phase multipliers. Every
wrap added by using cyclic indices has exactly zero coefficient at
the physical boundary, including at even levels. Such finite sums
have bounded norm and commutators of order \(N^{-1}\). The prior
exact Fricke identities propagate these bounds through the word.
Their apparent small denominator cancels term by term in this
realization. No adjoint or scalar closing is replaced in this argument.

For the actual coherent packet
\(w_N(y,z)=N^{-1}R_N^2A_N(y)A_N(z)\), where \(A_N\) is the
generating unit with the complete value and first-normal data in
section 6 of the proof, there is a word-dependent radius
\(\rho_W>0\). For \(|y|,|z|\le\rho_W\), sufficiently large
\(N\), \(1\le D\le N/32\), and \(\deg P\le D\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 e^{-C_WD}(D/N)^{24D}\|P\|_2^2\|W_Nw_N\|_{\rm ph}^2
 &\le\|W_NP(X)w_N\|_{\rm ph}^2\\
 &\le e^{C_WD}\|P\|_2^2\|W_Nw_N\|_{\rm ph}^2 .
 \end{split}
 \tag{PT3}
\]
Here \(\|P\|_2\) is the ordinary monomial coefficient norm.
For \(D=0\) the comparison is the exact constant-polynomial
identity; the zero polynomial is trivial. The same estimate holds
with \(w_N\) replaced by the identity packet \(1\). Indeed
\(w_N(0,0)=R_N^2/N\); applying the theorem to the fixed word
\(W_N\mathsf R^{-2}\) cancels that crossing power in both packets.
The physical identity has norm \(N\), which has not been normalized
away.

In particular, a coefficient-normalized observation of degree
\(o(N)\) changes the squared norm by \(e^{o(N)}\), uniformly
on the stated bidisc. Both the packet and its observation are
transported. The proof conjugates the existing finite-head extraction
identity by \(W_NL_{w_N}\) and bounds its two conjugated generators
using (PT2) and the exact generating-unit gauge identity. It never
bounds that conjugating operator itself.

### Repeated-root directions and almost-invariance

There is a further physical consequence, proved here. Let
\(A=W_NXW_N^{-1}\), and let \(\widetilde A\) be its ambient
finite cyclic-shift realization supplied by the transport proof.
Adjoints of those shift monomials are again such monomials, so
\[
       \|[\widetilde A,\widetilde A^*]\|\le C_W/N.
 \tag{PT4}
\]
Restriction requires care. If \(M\) is an invariant subspace, write
\(\widetilde A=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A_M&B\\0&C\end{smallmatrix}\right)\)
in its orthogonal decomposition. Direct multiplication gives
\[
 [A_M,A_M^*]
    =P_M[\widetilde A,\widetilde A^*]P_M-BB^*
    \le \varepsilon I,\qquad \varepsilon=C_W/N .
 \tag{PT5}
\]
Only this one-sided inequality is asserted after compression.
The distinct nodes are \(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)\),
\(0\le j\le\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\); let
\(\mathcal A_{N,j}\) be the corresponding primary ideal.
Apply (PT5) to the physical algebra and to its complete primary
subspace \(\mathcal S_j=W_N\mathcal A_{N,j}\). On a double block,
\(A_j=c_jI+J_j\), \(J_j^2=0\); in an orthonormal basis
\(J_j=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&n_j\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).
Its self-commutator has eigenvalues \(\pm|n_j|^2\). Consequently
\[
             \|J_j\|\le\sqrt{C_W/N} .
 \tag{PT6}
\]
A simple block has \(J_j=0\). This holds uniformly over all
actual nodes, with the full first-normal direction retained.
It strengthens the earlier constant bound on the restricted
nilpotent; it does not bound an ambient spectral projection.

For a unit vector \(u\in\mathcal S_i\), (PT5)--(PT6) give
\[
 \|(A^*-c_i)u\|^2
   =\|(A-c_i)u\|^2+\langle u,[A,A^*]u\rangle
   \le2\varepsilon .
\]
Taking the inner product with a unit vector in another complete
block, whose residual for \(A-c_j\) is at most
\(\sqrt\varepsilon\), proves that orthonormal block frames obey
\[
 \|E_i^*E_j\|\le
 \min\left\{1,
    \frac{(1+\sqrt2)\sqrt{C_W/N}}{|c_i-c_j|}\right\}
                  \qquad(c_i\ne c_j).
 \tag{PT7}
\]
Thus blocks separated by a fixed spectral distance become
orthogonal asymptotically in the actual metric. Close nodes still
require the full cluster estimate below.

On a double primary block, the conjugated signed crossing has the
original local formula
\(W_N\mathsf R^pW_N^{-1}|_{\mathcal S_j}
=\kappa^p\nu_j^p(I+p\rho_jJ_j)\), where
\(R_N(c_j)=\kappa\nu_j\),
\(\rho_j=R_N'(c_j)/R_N(c_j)\),
\(|\kappa|=|\nu_j|=1\), and \(|\rho_j|\le N^2/8\).
Equation (PT6) therefore improves its norm and inverse-norm bounds
on that complete block to \(1+C_W|p|N^{3/2}\). On a simple
block the action is just the unit scalar. All original phases and
raw packet normalizations remain present.

Finally the original empty packet satisfies \(Y1=c_0\,1\).
Hence the whole actual rational-word packet \(f_N=W_N1\) obeys
\[
 Y_Wf_N=c_0f_N,\qquad
 \|(Y_W^*-c_0)f_N\|_{\rm ph}
             \le\sqrt{C_W/N}\,\|f_N\|_{\rm ph},
 \qquad Y_W=W_NYW_N^{-1}.
 \tag{PT8}
\]
This follows directly from (PT5) for \(Y_W\), since its first
residual is zero. It is a statement about the entire original
packet, rather than a selected spectral truncation.

### What this simplifies and what remains

The metric in these estimates is the one already used for the
source-exact physical quartic. For fixed observation degree,
(PT3) permits at most polynomial loss in \(N\); for sublinear
degree it permits subexponential loss. This observation degree is
different from the degree at most four of the variational objective. The
number of coordinates of that objective still grows with \(N\).

The rate of \(\|W_Nw_N\|\), or of \(\|W_N1\|\), is not
evaluated here. Equations (PT6)--(PT8) give physical orthogonality
and almost-invariance estimates without a lower bound for the
original marked closing. Nor is a product of two independent
Conway children an invertible rational word. Its mixed forcing
still needs the corresponding assembly estimate. There is no new
knot-volume identity or finite-exception theorem in this entry.

## Sublinear Casimir clusters have a controlled full Gram, 24 November

The [selected-cluster proof](research_sublinear_physical_casimir_cluster_gram.md)
bounds the inverse Gram of a growing family of actual physical channels.
The nodes can be anywhere in the spectrum and need not be consecutive.
Both columns of every selected double block are retained. This controls
arbitrary coherent coefficient vectors, rather than just pairwise overlaps.

At level \(N\), select \(m\) distinct nodes in any physical pair-degree
block. Choose a Hermitian orthonormal basis \(E_i\) within each selected
simple or double generalized eigenspace, and put \(V=(E_1,\ldots,E_m)\).
Define
\[
 \Lambda_{N,m}=m\log(eN/m)+\log N .
 \tag{SC1}
\]
Uniformly in the physical degree, the selected nodes and their actual
multiplicities,
\[
       e^{-C\Lambda_{N,m}}I\le V^*V\le mI .
 \tag{SC2}
\]
In particular \(m=o(N)\) gives subexponential frame conditioning.
The actual value-normal columns divided by their respective value-column
norms have the same exponential bound, with polynomial extra factors.
Their raw value-column norms and inverse measures remain explicit.

The proof uses an existing interpolation estimate in a new physical
application. Actual cosine-node gaps satisfy
\(|c_a-c_b|\ge16|a-b|^2/N^2\). Their products retain the factorial
denominator \(\{(i-1)!(m-i)!\}^2\). Hermite value-cardinals have
zero first derivative at each selected double node, so their polynomial
functions of the actual bounded Casimir recover a whole selected block,
including its normal. Their operator norms cost
\(\exp(C\Lambda_{N,m})\). Applying them to \(\sum_iE_i a_i\)
proves (SC2). These filters are not ambient spectral projectors: their
values on unselected channels have not been set to zero.

The bound is uniform over all physical degrees, including the exact
high-degree mirror. Orthogonal direct sums over degrees cost the maximum
of (SC1). For any fixed number of disjoint physical pairs, tensor products
cost the sum of those maxima. The resulting estimates hold for arbitrary
coherent coefficient tensors. Overlapping pairings require their actual
recoupling map.

There is also a direct application to the space used by the quartic
minimum. Here is its proof. The [uniform physical source](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md)
identifies the full packet algebra faithfully as
\[
 \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[\Omega]\simeq\mathbb C[Z]/P_N(Z),
 \qquad \|A\|_{\rm ph}^2=\operatorname{Tr}(A^*A),
 \quad P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2 .
 \tag{SC3}
\]
The polynomial \(T_N\) is Chebyshev of the first kind. The physical
Casimir obeys \(\|\Omega\|_{\rm op}\le18\). Consequently left
multiplication \(L_\Omega\) has operator norm at most \(18\) in this
inherited Hilbert--Schmidt metric. Its minimal polynomial is exactly
\(P_N\): a polynomial relation applied to the identity matrix is the
same relation for \(\Omega\). Its primary ideals therefore have the
original dimensions one or two. Choose an internally Hilbert--Schmidt
orthonormal basis in each selected primary ideal. Applying precisely the
same cardinal proof, with \(20\) replacing the factor bound \(16\),
proves (SC2) for these full operator packets. This application does not
require transporting a magnetic column into the operator algebra or
claiming a polynomial normalization for its raw idempotent generators.

Fixed signed crossing powers also have controlled transport on this
selected ideal sum. Write the original crossing value as
\(R(c_j)=\kappa\nu_j\), where \(|\kappa|=|\nu_j|=1\), and let
\(\rho_j=R'(c_j)/R(c_j)\) at a double node. The actual bound is
\(|\rho_j|\le N^2/8\). On its primary ideal put
\(D_j=L_\Omega-c_j I\); then \(D_j^2=0\) and \(\|D_j\|\le20\).
Thus for every fixed integer \(p\), including either sign,
\[
 L_{R^p}|_{\mathcal A_{N,j}}
       =\kappa^p\nu_j^p(I+p\rho_j D_j),\qquad
 \max_{\epsilon=\pm1}\|L_{R^{\epsilon p}}|_{\mathcal A_{N,j}}\|
       \le1+C|p|N^2 .
 \tag{SC4}
\]
The simple ideal has only its unit scalar value. Conjugating these
block maps through the frame in (SC2) costs at most
\((1+C|p|N^2)e^{C\Lambda_{N,m}}\), hence \(e^{o(N)}\) when
\(m=o(N)\). All original crossing phases remain in (SC4).

For near-fold magnetic column clusters on a strict real degree compact,
the proof gives a further pairing estimate. Bilinear orthogonality
between different generalized eigenspaces and the exponentially small
self-pairing computed below imply that the whole orthonormalized cluster
\(U\) satisfies
\[
 U^*U=I,\qquad
 \|U^{\mathsf T}U\|
       \le C e^{-aN+C\Lambda_{N,m}} .
 \tag{SC5}
\]
For \(m=o(N)\), the frame \((U,\overline U)\) has Hermitian Gram
exponentially close to the identity and bilinear Gram exponentially
close to the block swap, in operator norm. The conjugate range is an
adjoint-Casimir carrier. This statement concerns the stated physical
column pairing; it does not replace the quartic algebra's closing row.

These estimates control synthesis inside a selected sum. They do not
bound the ambient projection onto it, discard its complement, or give
a lower bound for every contraction. In the packet algebra, products
of selected primary ideals stay in their intersection, but nonzero
nilpotents can multiply to zero. The genuine turn is unitary in the
physical metric but need not preserve a selected ideal cluster.
Controlling that recoupling and the original marked closing remains
necessary. The finite-exception theorem is still open.

The complete cluster proof, its five selected complete texts, and the
complete physical source used for (SC3)--(SC4) were read at these pins.
No earlier final or public manuscript was changed.

## The actual value and normal have a full physical Gaussian Gram, 24 November

The [physical-column Gram proof](research_q_hahn_physical_normal_gaussian_gram.md)
computes the positive Hermitian Gram of the original ordinary column and
its generic-confluent normal over every physical magnetic index. The
estimate includes their tails. Orthogonal projection cancels the scalar
part of the normal, so its transverse mode needs only the transport
derivative, rather than a sharper calibration of that scalar.

Keep actual integers \(0\le j<l\), \(j+l=N-1\),
\(s=l-j\), \(l\le t\le N-1\). Write \(C_u=C_j(t,u)\) and
\(w_u=w_{j,l}(t,u)\) for the original columns, with all physical indices
\(0\le u\le t\), and use their ordinary physical Hermitian product.
Let \(\tau=t/N\in I\Subset(1/2,1)\), \(\xi=j/N\), and set
\[
 \alpha_N=\frac{\langle C,w\rangle}{\|C\|^2},\qquad
 w^\perp=w-\alpha_N C,\qquad
 X_u=(u-t/2)/\sqrt N.
 \tag{HG1}
\]
There is a fixed \(\delta_I>0\) such that, for all actual
\(s\le\delta_I N\) and sufficiently large \(N\), the following
statements hold uniformly. Put
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 b=\sin(\pi\xi),\quad
 \varpi=\sqrt{1-2\cos(\pi\tau)+\cos^2(\pi\xi)},\\
 \lambda=2\pi b/\varpi,\quad
 a=i/(4b\varpi),\quad
 \gamma=1/(64\pi b^3\varpi).
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{HG2}
\]
The probability weights \(|C_u|^2/\|C\|^2\) have the Gaussian
limit proportional to \(e^{-\lambda X^2}\), with all fixed polynomial
moments. The mean of \(X_u\) is exactly zero. Moreover,
\[
 \|w^\perp-a(u-t/2)C\|\le C_I\|C\|,\qquad
 \frac{\|w^\perp\|^2}{N\|C\|^2}
       =\gamma+O_I(N^{-1/2}).
 \tag{HG3}
\]
Thus the actual value-normal Gram determinant is
\(N\gamma\|C\|^4(1+O_I(N^{-1/2}))\). In units of \(\|C\|\), centering
and scaling the normal by \(\sqrt{N\gamma}\) gives a bounded Gram; the raw
two-column Gram has condition number of order \(N^3\).

The tail bound is exact before taking limits. The original magnetic
polynomial factors as \(B_hA_n\), where \(h=N-1-t\) and \(A_n\)
has positive coefficients. Pairing the opposite phases in \(B_h\)
gives
\[
 \frac{|C_u|}{|\widehat C(t/2)|}
  \le \cos\!\left(\frac{\pi(u-t/2)}N\right)^h
  \le \exp[-c_I(u-t/2)^2/N].
 \tag{HG4}
\]
Here \(\widehat C(t/2)\) is the original finite continuation at the
possibly half-integral center. The global physical-grid polynomial
bound for \(w/C\) then controls every normal tail. On the central
range, the exact transport derivative and reflection symmetry prove
(HG3), including the cancellation of the scalar offset.

The proof also computes the Gram between ordinary columns in the wider
window \(s\le R N^{3/4}\). After their specified exact center phases
are removed, put \(r_j=s^2/N^{3/2}\) and
\(\varpi_0=\sqrt{1-2\cos(\pi\tau)}\). The unit-column overlaps are
\[
 \langle\psi_j,\psi_k\rangle
 =\exp[-\pi^3(r_j-r_k)^2/(128\varpi_0)]+O_{I,R}(N^{-1/2}).
 \tag{HG5}
\]
In particular columns in a \(\sqrt N\)-width channel window are
nearly parallel. This entrywise estimate alone is not an inverse
bound for their growing Gram matrix.

Finally let \(\mathcal U\) be the exact Hermitian orthonormal frame
obtained from \((C,w)\), and retain the original bilinear pairing.
The exact Hermite measures and their positive native-energy exponent
give \(\mathcal B=\mathcal U^{\mathsf T}\mathcal U=O_I(e^{-a_I N})\).
The doubled frame \(\mathcal D=(\mathcal U,\overline{\mathcal U})\)
therefore satisfies
\[
 \mathcal D^*\mathcal D=I_4+O_I(e^{-a_I N}),\qquad
 \mathcal D^{\mathsf T}\mathcal D
   =\begin{pmatrix}0&I_2\\I_2&0\end{pmatrix}+O_I(e^{-a_I N}).
 \tag{HG6}
\]
The second carrier is invariant under the adjoint Casimir. It is not
an extra eigenchannel of the original Casimir. These statements supply
a stable pairing for the two stated boundary types. They do not show
that an arbitrary original exterior supplies the adjoint carrier,
that turns preserve these packets, or that the marked closing has a
nonzero projection. The pair degree remains a physical integer in a
compact subset of \((N/2,N)\); the endpoint \(t=N-1\) is not a
uniform family here. No new knot-volume case follows yet.

## Both signed crossings have a nonzero local Jordan coefficient, 24 November

The [inverse-row and signed-node proof](research_q_hahn_inverse_row_nonvanishing_v2.md)
uses the calibrated normal below to complete the coherent subtraction
inside an actual repeated-Casimir contribution. The result holds for both
crossing signs and every integer auxiliary color, including complete
color. It estimates one double-node contribution before the sum over
different Casimir nodes.

Let \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(d=N-1\), and take actual integers
\(0\le j<l\), \(j+l=d\), \(s=l-j\), \(l\le t\le d\). Put
\(c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}\), \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\), and
\(\nu_j=(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)}\). The original double-block measure is
\(\sigma_{t,j}\ne0\), with its full complex phase retained. Its shear is
\[
 \eta_{t,j}=\rho_j+Q_{t,j}'(c_j)/Q_{t,j}(c_j),\qquad
 \rho_j=\frac{is}{4\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad
 Q_{t,j}(Z)=\frac{\prod_{m=0}^t(Z-c_m)}{(Z-c_j)^2}.
 \tag{SJ1}
\]
The last logarithmic derivative is real because \(t\) is a physical
integer. Write \(R_u=w_j(t,u)/C_j(t,u)\), with the original ordinary
column and generic paired normal. Define the actual color polynomial by
\(l_n(2\cos\theta)=(-1)^{n-1}\sin(n\theta)/\sin\theta\);
its prime denotes differentiation in the polynomial argument.
For \(\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}\), the entire double-node contribution
to the signed mixed crossing has the exact entry
\[
 \mathcal D_{t,j}^{\epsilon,n}(u,v)
  =\frac{\kappa^\epsilon\nu_j^\epsilon}{\sigma_{t,j}}
        C_j(t,u)C_j(t,v)\,\mathcal A_{t,j}^{\epsilon,n}(u,v),
 \qquad
 \mathcal A=l_n'(c_j)+l_n(c_j)(R_u+R_v+\epsilon\rho_j-\eta_{t,j}).
 \tag{SJ2}
\]
There is no conjugation of either column in this identity.

Fix any compact real family with
\(1/2<\tau<1\), \(0<\nu,\omega<\tau\). There is a fixed small
complex neighborhood in the two magnetic variables and a fixed
\(\delta>0\) such that, for physical \(t/N=\tau\),
\(u/N=\nu\), \(v/N=\omega\), and \(s\le\delta N\),
\[
             a\le |\mathcal A_{t,j}^{\epsilon,n}(u,v)|\le CN^4
 \tag{SJ3}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(N\), uniformly in both signs and all \(1\le n\le N\).
Replacing \(R_u,R_v\) in (SJ2) by their respective
\(N\mathcal F_{j/N}\) gives a relative \(1+o(1)\) formula,
uniformly in all these colors, with every fixed magnetic derivative
on smaller neighborhoods. The exact color polynomials, shear, measure
and phases remain in the leading formula.

The proof keeps the original coherent sum. On a real strict physical
compact the folded primitive satisfies
\(0<\Im\mathcal F_0<1/(4\pi)\), with uniform margins. These margins
persist on a small complex magnetic neighborhood and near-fold window.
Since \(\eta-\rho\) and the color polynomials are real, the imaginary
part of \(\mathcal A/l_n\) is bounded below by \(aN\) for the
positive crossing and above by \(-aN\) for the negative crossing.
If \(l_n(c_j)\ne0\), its root-of-unity sine formula gives
\(|l_n(c_j)|\ge2/N\). If it vanishes, the derivative instead obeys
\(|l_n'(c_j)|=n/(2\sin^2((2j+1)\pi/N))\ge1/2\).
Thus color zeros are included directly. The same argument also proves
\(aN\le|R_u-\eta_{t,j}|\le CN^3\) for the actual dual value row.

Consequently each stated signed double-node contribution has the two
ordinary-column exponential actions and the known inverse-measure
action, with no extra exponential loss from its two normal channels.
The unsigned case \(\epsilon=0\) is outside the theorem. The pair degree
remains a physical integer; no joint complex-degree or complex-color
continuation is claimed. Summing over nodes, subsequent gluings and
the original scalar closing may still cancel. The quartic minimum's
geometric rate and the finite-exception theorem remain open.

matching pins. No earlier final or public manuscript was changed.

## A nonzero leading coefficient for the actual near-fold normal, 24 November

The [calibrated normal transport proof](research_q_hahn_calibrated_normal_transport.md)
improves the earlier upper estimate to a complex leading-amplitude
formula. It concerns the original generic paired derivative, including
its large partner and its prescribed eigenvalue-gap divisor. Both magnetic
variables may vary on a fixed complex physical compact.

Keep the source, derivative and physical tube in (UT1) below. For actual
integers \(j<l\), \(j+l=N-1\), put \(s=l-j\) and \(\xi=j/N\).
For every compact \(K\Subset\mathcal P\), there is a fixed
\(\delta_K>0\) such that, uniformly for \(1\le s\le\delta_KN\),
\[
 w_{j,l}(N\tau,N\nu)
       =N\mathcal F_\xi(\tau,\nu)
          C_j(q_0;N\tau,N\nu)(1+o_K(1)).
 \tag{CN1}
\]
Here \(\mathcal F_\xi\) is a specified holomorphic function, uniformly
nonzero on \(K\) after decreasing \(\delta_K\). Thus the original
normal has the same exponential rate as the ordinary column, and their
ratio has magnitude between \(c_KN\) and \(C_KN\). Every fixed
holomorphic derivative of the relative error tends to zero on smaller
compacts. Both level parities and all actual channels in this window are
included; no finite complex-channel interpolation is made.

The coefficient is the primitive fixed by the original source. Write
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 z=e^{\pi i(\tau-2\nu)},\quad \sigma=e^{\pi i\tau},\quad
 c=\cos(\pi\tau),\quad b_\xi=\sin(\pi\xi),\\
 W_\xi=1-2cz+\cos^2(\pi\xi)z^2,\qquad
 H_\xi=-4ib_\xi\sqrt{W_\xi}/z,\\
 \mathcal F_\xi(\tau,\nu)
       =\int_0^1\frac{\nu}{H_\xi(\tau,\theta\nu)}\,d\theta .
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{CN2}
\]
The square root is the ordinary source branch, positive at real centers
\(\nu=\tau/2\), and continued holomorphically. The endpoint at
\(\theta=0\) is regular. At the fold this becomes the explicit unit
\[
 \mathcal F_{1/2}=\mathcal F_0
       =\frac{\sqrt{1-2cz}+i\sigma}{8\pi c}.
 \tag{CN3}
\]
Consequently every prescribed sublinear window \(s\le S_N=o(N)\)
satisfies \(w_{j,l}=N\mathcal F_0C_j(1+o(1))\) on each fixed
physical compact. In a fixed positive scaled window, (CN1) retains the
actual \(\xi=j/N\) in this coefficient and in the ordinary action.

Two exact generic source equations are essential. The magnetic Casimir
equation gives forcing exactly one for \(w/C_j\); a second, common
coproduct shift fixes its transport in \(\tau\). An analytic inverse
iterated a fixed positive multiple of \(N\) times suppresses the
earlier \(N^A\exp(Cs^2/N)\) bound when \(s/N\) is sufficiently
small. This determines the two derivatives of \(w/(NC_j)\), but
leaves an additive constant. One fixed small original physical prefix
fixes that constant: its resolvent has a uniformly convergent Neumann
series, and finite closed-walk sums compute its normalized trace as
\(\mathcal F_\xi\). No uniform estimate toward a physical boundary
is assumed.

This settles a local amplitude, not the full contracted tangle coupon
or its original scalar closing. The allowed \(\delta_K\) depends on
the chosen compact. Geometric placement of general short-filled boundary
data, contributing cycles and the global noncancellation estimate remain
unproved. There is no additional knot-volume case or finite-exception
theorem from (CN1) alone.

The complete proof and its five selected complete inputs were read at
these matching pins. Earlier final texts and public manuscripts are unchanged.

## The actual normal has polynomial cost on the Gaussian channel scale, 24 November

The [unipotent transport estimate](research_q_hahn_unipotent_fold_transport.md)
controls the original paired q-Hahn normal throughout a channel window
of width \(O(\sqrt N)\), with only polynomial relative cost. The proof
first retains the exact source normalization, then uses the column
value and its first difference as coordinates. It supplies an analytic
upper estimate, rather than another equivalent source representation.

Fix a compact subset \(K\) of the full strict physical tube
\[
 {\cal P}=\{(\tau,\nu)\in\mathbb C^2:
          \tfrac12<\Re\tau<1,\quad 0<\Re\nu<\Re\tau\}.
\]
Let \(q_0=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(t=N\tau\), \(u=N\nu\), and let
\(C_m(q;t,u)\) be the original finite generic highest-weight-\(N-1\)
column, as defined explicitly in the proof. For actual integers
\(0\le j<l\), \(j+l=N-1\), write \(s=l-j\). Keep the actual normal
\[
 w_{j,l}=
 \frac{D C_j(q_0;t,u)-D C_l(q_0;t,u)}{-2N\Delta_j},
 \qquad
 D=q\partial_q,\qquad
 \Delta_j=q_0^{2j+1}-q_0^{-2j-1}.
 \tag{UT1}
\]
The derivative fixes \(N,t,u\). Its original large partner is retained.
For sufficiently large \(N\), and \(1\le s\le\eta_KN\), the estimate is
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \sup_K\left|\frac{w_{j,l}(N\tau,N\nu)}
                    {C_j(q_0;N\tau,N\nu)}\right|
       \le C_K N^{A_K}\exp(C_Ks^2/N).
 \qquad}
 \tag{UT2}
\]
Here \(\eta_K>0\), \(C_K\) and \(A_K\) depend on the fixed compact.
The columns are holomorphic near \(K\), and the denominator is nonzero.
Both level parities are covered, with the actual integer-channel
constraint \(j+l=N-1\).

The earlier estimate was \(C_KN^8(C_KN^{16})^s\). The
[source-normalized recurrence](research_q_hahn_source_normalized_fold_transport.md)
first reduces that to \(C_KN^{100}C_K^s\): the scalar ratios cancel
the large monic recurrence coefficients at every nonresonant row.
The additional value/difference frame gives the quadratic exponent
in (UT2). The compact-dependent power \(A_K\) includes a harmonic
accumulation; it is not asserted to be the universal number \(100\).

The exact identity behind the second step is
\[
                         C_m(q;t,0)=1.
 \tag{UT3}
\]
It follows directly from the finite source, before specialization.
It is an algebraic anchor, not an asymptotic assertion at a boundary
point of \({\cal P}\). To state its consequence, put
\(Q=q^2\), \(B=Q^{-N}\), \(T=Q^t\), \(\sigma=q^t\) and
\(z=\sigma Q^{-u}\). The actual normalized recurrence is
\[
 C_{n+1}=a_n(z+\alpha_n)C_n+
                          a_na_{n-1}\beta_nC_{n-1},
 \qquad
 a_n=\frac{\sigma(1-B^2Q^{2n+1})(1-B^2Q^{2n+2})}
 {(T-Q^n)(1-B^2Q^{n+1})(1-BQ^{n+1})}.
 \tag{UT4}
\]
Here \(\alpha_n,\beta_n\) are the original monic recurrence
coefficients, whose complete rational formulas are retained in the
source-normalized proof. If \(\delta C_n=C_n-C_{n-1}\), (UT3) gives
\[
 \delta C_{n+1}=\varepsilon_nC_n+b_n\delta C_n,\qquad
 \varepsilon_n=a_n(z-\sigma),\qquad
 b_n=a_n(\sigma+\alpha_n)-1.
 \tag{UT5}
\]

Write \(r_n=1+|2n-N|\) and \(h_n=r_n/N+1/r_n\).
Outside the at most five rows with \(|2n-N|\le4\), the actual
generic circle \(|\epsilon|=c_KN^{-8}\), \(q=q_0e^\epsilon\),
satisfies
\[
 |\varepsilon_n|\le C_K(r_n/N)^2,\qquad
                         |b_n-1|\le C_Kh_n.
 \tag{UT6}
\]
The root coefficient calculation is algebraic; its continuation to
the circle uses derivatives of the original generic formulas.
No root-only identity is differentiated. In the frame
\((C_n,\delta C_n/h_n)\), each nonresonant transfer norm is at most \(1+C_Kh_n\).
The bound
\[
 \sum_{n=j}^{l-1}h_n
                \le C s^2/N+C(1+\log(s+2))
 \tag{UT7}
\]
then gives the quadratic cost. Initial coordinates, the finite bad
rows and Cauchy differentiation of the full holomorphic source
contribute polynomial factors.

Thus \(s=O(\sqrt N)\) has polynomial relative cost, and every
\(s=o(N)\) has subexponential relative upper cost. For a fixed
positive \(s/N\le\delta\), the upper action cost is at most
\(C_K\delta^2\); it can still be positive. The theorem supplies no
complex-channel interpolation, nonzero normal amplitude, or bound
for the full contracted coupon. Placement of the short-filled
geometric data and survival under the original closing remain
necessary. No additional knot-volume case or finite-exception
theorem is established by this estimate.

The complete proof and its six complete chosen inputs are fixed below.
The earlier four-coherent value theorem is methodological coverage for
rescaling a first difference; it does not prove this generic normal bound.

## Fixed leaf degree gives a vanishing error in the undamped integral, 24 November

The [relative undamped formula](research_conway_wick_undamped_reciprocal_asymptotic.md)
improves the earlier constant-error comparison without changing the
physical quartic, its closing row or any normalization budget. For every
fixed literal Conway tree, its relative error tends to zero uniformly
over all normalized prescribed leaf packets. Fixed short-filling packets
are included. This is a calibration of the original source integral;
its hyperbolic-volume rate has not been evaluated.

Let the tree have \(s\) proper vertices and \(L\ge1\) leaf occurrences.
Every packet belongs to the full \(N\)-dimensional physical pair algebra,
with all double-root derivative directions retained. Keep the original
budget product \(\mathcal B_N\), normalized recursion residuals \(G\),
and normalized original closing row \(c_N\). Put
\[
 D=Ns,\qquad E_N(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|c_Nx|^2,\qquad
 \mathcal P_N=\frac{D!}{\pi^D}
                  \int_{\mathbb C^D}E_N(x)^{-D-1}\,dx,
 \qquad k=K_N/\mathcal B_N.
 \tag{WA1}
\]
There is no damping parameter or selected temperature in this formula.
The integral is defined from the known local tensors and original
closing, without the value of \(K_N\) or a minimizing field.

For nonzero sources and all sufficiently large levels, the estimate is
\[
 \bigl||k|^2\mathcal P_N-1\bigr|
       \le C_{\mathscr T}\rho_L(N),\qquad
 \rho_L(N)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&L=1,\\
 N^{-1},&L=2,\\
 N^{-1}\log(2N),&L=3,\\
 N^{-2/(L-1)},&L\ge4.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{WA2}
\]
The constant depends on the fixed tree, and not on its normalized
leaf choices or a lower bound for their observed source. Both level
parities are covered. If \(K_N=0\), the integral is infinite and
its reciprocal is exactly zero. No eventual nonvanishing is assumed.
The vanishing-error estimate is not uniform over growing trees.

Two different degree bounds enter the argument. The objective \(E_N\)
has degree at most four. In the residual coordinates \(r=G(x)\), the scalar
\(f(r)=c_NG^{-1}(r)\) has degree at most \(L\). Its expansion is indexed
by sets of vertices with no member above another, called antichains.
For such a set \(A\), the coefficient \(C_A\) is the original scalar
context with those subtrees replaced by free packet inputs. Signs and
all other subtrees are retained before taking a norm. The new physical
estimate is
\[
                    \|C_A\|_{\rm HS}^2\le N^{|A|-3}
                            \qquad(|A|\ge2).
 \tag{WA3}
\]
It uses the original two closing forms. Write
\(\lambda_0(h(\Omega))=h(q+q^{-1})\) for Casimir evaluation and
\(\phi(F)=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}[(I\otimes g)F]\), where
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\) and \(g\) is the original unitary pivot.
Both obey
\[
 |\lambda(AB)|\le N^{-1}\|A\|_{\rm ph}\|B\|_{\rm ph},
                         \qquad \lambda\in\{\lambda_0,\phi\}.
 \tag{WA4}
\]
The genuine turn exchanges these two rows. At the first product below
the top turn corridor, fix all but two free inputs if both children
are used, or all but one if only one child is used. Equation (WA4)
then bounds the remaining coefficient matrix or row; summing over
the fixed orthonormal inputs proves (WA3). No small coefficient norm
for the full multiplication tensor is assumed.

Independent centered Gaussian residual blocks make distinct
antichains orthogonal. The coefficient estimate, fixed degree and
elementary fourth Gaussian moments control the nonlinear part of
\(f\). An exact Laplace identity then compares the whole integral
with its affine counterpart, whose value is exactly \(|k|^{-2}\).
Splitting its single Laplace variable into small, intermediate and
large ranges gives (WA2), including the entire large-variable tail.
No asymptotic formula at an unknown minimizer is needed.

The earlier constant-error comparison already gave the same exponential
rate as the original source. The new estimate strengthens that
calibration and simplifies a relative-error formulation. It does not
add a knot family to the proved volume results. For arbitrary fixed
short partial fillings, comparison of this particular positive integral
with the geometric volume remains necessary. The finite-exception
theorem remains unproved.

The complete proof and its four complete chosen source/coverage texts
are fixed below. Earlier finals and public manuscripts are unchanged.

## The macroscopic normal has a separate complex scale, 24 November

The following audit concerns the actual confluent q-Hahn normal. On
its supported physical integer grid its ratio to the ordinary column is
polynomially bounded. That conclusion cannot be extended uniformly
to the full complex physical tube at a fixed macroscopic channel.
Even after excluding the additional degree poles, the ratio can
grow exponentially. There is also a uniform exponential upper bound
on every fixed compact in the partner-admissible domain below.
This audit changes no earlier source theorem or frozen manuscript.

Fix integers \(j=j_N\), \(l=N-1-j\), with
\(j/N\to\xi\in(0,1/2)\). Put
\[
 q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=q^{N-1},\quad
 t=N\tau,\quad u=N\nu,\quad T=e^{2\pi i\tau},\quad
 X=e^{-2\pi i\nu},\quad
 \Delta_j=q^{2j+1}-q^{-2j-1}.
\]
All powers use \(\log q=\pi i/N\) and
\(\log x=(N-1)\pi i/N\), continued locally in the generic
parameter \(\zeta\) below.
Write \((a;Q)_k=\prod_{r=0}^{k-1}(1-aQ^r)\), and
\(s_k=|(Q;Q)_k|\), with \(s_0=1\).
The ordinary column has the exact root expression
\[
 C_j(t,u)=x^u F_j(X,T),\qquad
 F_j(X,T)=\sum_{k=0}^{j}
 \frac{(Q^{-j};Q)_k(Q^{-l};Q)_k(X;Q)_kQ^k}
      {(Q;Q)_k^2(T^{-1};Q)_k}.
 \tag{MN1}
\]
Use the actual generic columns of the
[collision calculation](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md),
with highest weight \(N-1\) fixed, to define
\[
 w_j(t,u)=
 \frac{[D C_j(\zeta;t,u)-D C_l(\zeta;t,u)]_{\zeta=q}}
      {-2N\Delta_j},\qquad D=\zeta\partial_\zeta,
 \qquad W_j(X,T)=x^{-u}w_j(t,u).
 \tag{MN2}
\]
No root-only identity is differentiated in this definition.
The same calculation gives its exact finite head and tail,
and shows that \(W_j\) has degree exactly \(l\) in \(X\).
Its leading coefficient \(\alpha_l\) has modulus
\[
 |\alpha_l|=
 \frac{s_j s_{l-j-1}}
      {|\Delta_j|s_l|(T^{-1};Q)_l|}.
 \tag{MN3}
\]
The finite offset \(l-j-1\) and original normalizer are essential.
In contrast, \(F_j\) has degree \(j\).

First consider any fixed compact \(\mathcal K\) in
\[
 \mathcal D_\xi=\{(\tau,\nu)\in\mathbb C^2:
       1-\xi<\Re\tau<1,\quad 0<\Re\nu<\Re\tau\}.
\]
There are constants \(A_{\mathcal K},N_{\mathcal K}\) such that
\[
 \left|\frac{w_j(N\tau,N\nu)}{C_j(N\tau,N\nu)}\right|
       \le e^{A_{\mathcal K}N}
       \qquad ((\tau,\nu)\in\mathcal K,
                              \ N\ge N_{\mathcal K}).
 \tag{MN4}
\]
Here and below the integer channel is always its actual value \(j_N\).

To prove the bound, sort any \(a\) distinct nonzero root factors
\(|1-Q^r|\). The \(k\)-th smallest is at least \(2k/N\): each
distance from a multiple of \(N\) occurs at most twice, and
\(2\sin(\pi v)\ge4v\) for \(0\le v\le1/2\). Therefore
\[
       s_a^{-1}\le\frac{(N/2)^a}{a!}\le e^{N/2},
                \qquad s_a\le2^N\quad(0\le a<N).
 \tag{MN5}
\]
Compactness in \(\mathcal D_\xi\) implies that every factor
\(1-Q^r/T\), \(0\le r<l\), has a uniform positive lower modulus
for all large \(N\). Indeed \(\Re\tau-r/N\) stays away from both
zero and one. Also \(|X|\) is uniformly bounded.
In the exact finite normal formula, collision equation (11),
the head has coefficients multiplied by differences of
\[
             L_k(y)=-\sum_{r=0}^{k-1}\frac{yQ^r}{1-yQ^r}
                \quad (y=Q^{-j},Q^{-l},\ k\le j).
\]
Their denominators are nonzero root factors, so these sums are
\(O(N^2)\). Every head or tail term contains a bounded number of
root products and inverse products of length at most \(N-1\),
factors \((X;Q)_k\) of modulus at most \((1+|X|)^k\), and the
separated degree factors. Equation (MN5) bounds every such term
by \(\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{A_{\mathcal K}N}\).
There are at most \(N\) terms, and \(|\Delta_j|\) stays bounded
below because \(j/N\to\xi\in(0,1/2)\).
Thus \(|W_j|\le\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{A_{\mathcal K}N}\).

The [ordinary complex packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md)
has a nonzero relative amplitude on \(\mathcal K\). Its action is
bounded there, uniformly in these integer channels. Absorbing the
same known factor \(x^u\) into that estimate gives
\(|F_j|\ge\operatorname{poly}(N)^{-1}e^{-A'_{\mathcal K}N}\).
It also ensures \(C_j\ne0\) for all sufficiently large levels.
The common factor cancels exactly in \(w_j/C_j=W_j/F_j\),
proving (MN4). This uses the actual finite normal formula, not a
generic monic determinant assumed regular at a collision.

An exponential scale is sometimes necessary, on a fixed compact
away from every extra pole. Set
\[
 \tau_*=1-\xi/2+i,\qquad a_*=\Re\tau_*,\qquad
 \mathcal K_R=\{(\tau_*,v+i\log R/(2\pi)):
                  a_*/2-1/8\le v\le a_*/2+1/8\},\quad R\ge1.
\]
This is a compact subset of \(\mathcal D_\xi\). It has
\(|T|=e^{-2\pi}\), so no degree factor can vanish. The corresponding
\(X\)'s lie on a radius-\(R\) arc of angular length \(\pi/2\).
We claim, for every sufficiently large \(N\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \sup_{\mathcal K_R}\left|\frac{w_j}{C_j}\right|
       \ge\frac1{2N}e^{-(7+2\pi)N}R^{l-j}.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{MN6}
\]

Equation (MN3) and (MN5) give
\[
 |\alpha_l|\ge\tfrac12
       e^{-N[1+\log2+\log(1+e^{2\pi})]}.
 \tag{MN7}
\]
For (MN1), each \((X;Q)_k\) has coefficient sum at most \(2^k\),
and \(|(T^{-1};Q)_k|\ge(e^{2\pi}-1)^k\ge1\).
Together with (MN5), this proves
\[
 \|F_j\|_{\text{coefficient }\ell^1}\le Ne^N8^j,
               \qquad |F_j(X,T)|\le Ne^N8^jR^j\quad(|X|=R).
 \tag{MN8}
\]
Choose \(l+1\) equally spaced nodes \(z_m\) on the arc. Their
chord distances satisfy \(|z_m-z_n|\ge R|m-n|/l\).
Lagrange interpolation of the leading coefficient of \(W_j\)
therefore gives, if \(M=\sup_{\rm arc}|W_j|\),
\[
 |\alpha_l|\le M(l/R)^l\sum_{m=0}^{l}\frac1{m!(l-m)!}
             \le M(2e/R)^l.
 \tag{MN9}
\]
The last step uses \(l!\ge(l/e)^l\). Dividing this lower bound
for \(M\) by the uniform bound (MN8), then applying (MN7), gives
(MN6). For the displayed safe constant, use \(j+l=N-1\),
\(\log(1+e^{2\pi})\le\log2+2\pi\), \(e<4\), and \(\log2<1\).

In particular, choose a fixed
\(\log R>(8+2\pi)/(1-2\xi)\). Then
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
       \log\sup_{\mathcal K_R}|w_j/C_j|
       \ge(1-2\xi)\log R-7-2\pi>0.
 \tag{MN10}
\]
This excludes a uniform subexponential normal/value comparison on
the full complex physical tube, even in the partner-admissible
range and away from degree poles. It is compatible with the
physical-grid polynomial theorem and the shrinking near-fold theorem.
The maximizing magnetic point may depend on \(N\). No fixed-point
normal amplitude, placement of a geometric saddle in this compact,
or noncancellation after the full coupon is sewn follows. A smaller
region containing the actual geometric data could still be tame.
The finite-exception theorem remains unproved.

The complete actual-source inputs and closest complete coverage are
fixed below. This audit is recorded here only; no separate negative
research note, mathematical program or numerical test was made.

## Gaussian crossing models in the actual cyclic source, 24 November

The [cyclic crossing estimate](research_cyclic_crossing_gaussian_morse_adapter.md)
connects the physical Gaussian approximation to the actual source-labeled
crossings used in the Morse construction. After a specified projection,
its error is an exact intertwiner. This removes an exponential metric
conversion from the error estimate, including with spectator strands.

First, the additional cyclic entries have a sharp smaller rate.
Let \(R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}\) be the actual changing-source crossing,
\(R^\sigma_0\) its nilpotent version, and
\(|\mu_1|=|\mu_2|=1/N\). For either crossing sign,
\[
 \log\|R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}-R^\sigma_0\|_{\rm op,ph}
 =\log\|R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}-R^\sigma_0\|_{\rm HS,ph}
 =\frac{Nv_3}{\pi}+O(\log N),
 \tag{CG1}
\]
where \(v_3\) is the volume of a regular ideal tetrahedron.
These are equal exponential rates, not equal finite norms.
The constants are uniform in the source phases. The full crossing's
physical Gaussian rate is \(M_0=2G_{\rm Cat}/\pi>v_3/\pi\), where
\(G_{\rm Cat}=\sum_{k\ge0}(-1)^k/(2k+1)^2\).

The difference consists exactly of one-wrap entries. A positive
wrapped transition with input \((a,b)\), Euler length \(k>a\), and
\(b+k\le N-1\) has modulus
\[
 \frac{s_a s_{b+k}s_{k-a-1}}{N s_b s_k},\qquad
             s_j=\prod_{h=1}^j2\sin(\pi h/N),\quad s_0=1.
\]
Its finite offset is retained. The negative inverse has the same
entry magnitudes after relabeling its recovered donor. The uniform
factorial estimate reduces the maximum to the two boundary donor
configurations. One maximizing choice has
\((a,b,k)/N\to(0,1/6,2/3)\), giving (CG1).
At Euler length \(2/3\), the unwrapped action is
\((5/3)(v_3/\pi)\), which proves the strict gap.

Let \(\mathfrak G^\sigma_{N,r}\) be the known untilted physical
Gaussian model at any fixed truncation order \(r\ge0\).
Define \(\Pi^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}\) to be the physical
Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal projection onto all pair matrices
intertwining the actual input and output \(E,F,K\) generators.
Their sources update as
\((\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(\gamma\mu_2,\gamma\mu_1)\), where
\(\gamma=(-1)^{N+1}\). Set
\[
 \widehat R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu,N,r}
          =\Pi^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}\mathfrak G^\sigma_{N,r},
 \qquad
 \mathcal E=R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}
                        -\widehat R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu,N,r}.
 \tag{CG2}
\]
The actual crossing lies in that full intertwiner space, so projection
cannot increase its physical approximation error. The wrap gap then
preserves every fixed-order Gaussian estimate. No repeated-root normal
or physical state direction is removed.

Crucially, \(\mathcal E\) is now an exact intertwiner. Embed it on
its neighboring pair in an opposite-source odd-width Morse slice.
The canonical averaging inequality applies to the error itself:
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|\mathcal E\otimes I_{\rm spec}\|
                       _{J_{\rm out}\leftarrow J_{\rm in}}
 \le\|\mathcal E\|_{\rm op,ph}
 \le\|\mathcal E\|_{\rm HS,ph}
 \le C_r N^{1/4-(r+1)/2}e^{NM_0}.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{CG3}
\]
The physical norms on the right are pair norms. There is no spectator
Hilbert--Schmidt dimension factor or Gram condition number. This also
works when that pair has zero total cyclic power: the averaging uses
the complete odd slice, whose total power is nonzero.

Physical intertwiner projections and the nilpotent Gaussian projection
were already available. The new ingredients are the sharp actual
cyclic-wrap gap and the updated-source estimate (CG3). Projection may
change the entrywise phase representation; no braid relations or
mutual-inverse identities are asserted for the projected models.
The truncation order is fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity.

The estimate is absolute at the local crossing norm scale. It may
still exceed the geometric contribution of an assembled short parent
or its original cap projection. A source-relative geometric packet,
its nonzero closing coefficient and the finite-exception theorem
remain unproved.

The complete proof and its complete chosen source and coverage texts
are fixed below. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations
were used; earlier finals and public manuscripts are unchanged.

## A compatible cyclic Gram through the original cups and caps, 24 November

The [opposite-source construction](research_opposite_source_morse_gram.md)
extends the canonical Gram to a fixed original one-cut Morse diagram,
including changes in its number of strands. The whole completed cut
remains the original knot operator. No boundary channel is discarded.

There is a genuine compatibility condition here. The earlier
all-equal normalized cyclic sources have nonzero total coproduct on
each pair, whereas an ordinary cup is annihilated by that coproduct.
Those pair sources cannot be used at a cup. The new construction
uses opposite sources at each birth or death and leaves one unpaired
source on the cut strand.

Here are the precise labels. Put \(N\ge2\), \(\gamma=(-1)^{N+1}\),
and choose \(|\mu|=1/N\). At a slice with \(b\) ordered heads set
\[
 \nu_i=\gamma^{i-1}\mu_i\in\{\mu,-\mu\},\qquad
                       \sum_i\nu_i=\mu .
\]
The signs follow the strand orientations, so \(b\) is odd.
Actual crossings exchange the adjacent \(\nu\)'s; a cup inserts
opposite labels and a cap removes them. In the original balanced
E-chart the dual parameter is \(\mu^\vee=-\gamma\mu\).
The literal original cup and ordinary cap are therefore still Hopf
intertwiners, with all their original scalars and pivot phases.

On every slice the total coproduct has the same central power:
\[
 E_\Sigma^N=\gamma N\mu I=cI,\qquad |c|=1.
 \tag{MG1}
\]
Choose one \(e^N=c\). The operators \(T=E_\Sigma/e\) satisfy
\(T^N=I\) across every width. The canonical positive Grams
\[
                 J_{\boldsymbol\nu}
                   =\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(T^k)^*T^k
 \tag{MG2}
\]
are consequently compatible with all the actual rectangular
intertwiners in this fixed diagram. More explicitly, any such map
\(A\), between its correctly labeled input and output fibers, obeys
\[
 \|A\|_{J_{\rm out}\leftarrow J_{\rm in}}
                                  \le\|A\|_{\rm ph}.
 \tag{MG3}
\]
This follows by intertwining each \(T^k\) before summing its physical
squared norm. A crossing and its actual inverse satisfy the estimate
between their respective Grams; no fixed-metric unitarity is asserted.

Let \(C\) insert the literal cup and \(B\) apply the ordinary cap.
Their exact physical squared norms are \(N^3\) and \(N^{-1}\).
The stronger identities are
\[
 C^*J_{\rm out}C=N^3J_{\rm in},\qquad
 B^*J_{\rm out}B\preceq N^{-1}J_{\rm in}.
 \tag{MG4}
\]
Thus \(N^{-3/2}C\) is an isometry and \(N^{1/2}B\) is a
contraction. If there are \(h\) births and \(h\) deaths, restoring
their original normalization multiplies the normalized word by
exactly \(N^h\). A normalized snake is \(I/N\).
The ordinary bubble remains \(\ell p=0\); the cap is not the
positive adjoint of the cup.

The proof also preserves the entire original cut matrix. A birth
adds integer degree \(N-1\), a death removes it, and each cyclic
wrap in either signed crossing adds \(N\). In a completed
\(1\to1\) diagram the births and deaths cancel. The remaining
one-head input and output degrees lie between zero and \(N-1\),
so no wrapped path survives. The completed operator is exactly its
original nilpotent value, with the original framing and assigned
external factors. This requires no local crossing-through-cup
identity or new semicyclic ribbon-invariant claim.

The construction works on the full physical spaces even when an
intermediate tail has zero cyclic power. It closes the stated
cup/cap compatibility gap in using these Grams for a fixed cut.
It does not prove preservation of the older cap-tree projections
by interior crossings or evaluate the actual crossing product at
the volume rate. The geometric contribution and scalar lower bound
after arbitrary short partial filling remain unproved; the
finite-exception theorem is still open.

## The unchanged quartic has an undamped reciprocal integral, 24 November

The [undamped source formula](research_conway_undamped_reciprocal_source.md)
removes the level-dependent damping from the earlier reciprocal
construction. It retains the original physical quartic, normalization
and marked closing. Its relative comparison constant is universal:
it depends on neither the quantum level nor the number of tangles.

Here are the objects being compared. At level \(N\ge2\), a literal
Conway tree has \(s\ge1\) proper vertices and \(D=Ns\) complex packet
coordinates. Every packet retains the full physical Casimir algebra,
including the derivatives at repeated roots. Let \(\mathcal B_N\)
be the known product of the physical normalization budgets, let
\(c_N\) be the normalized original closing row, and write
\[
 G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_j)_{j\text{ child of }v})-x_v,\qquad
 E_N(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|c_Nx|^2.
\]
The maps \(\Phi_v\) are the actual normalized leaves, products and
turns. Define the nonnegative integral
\[
 \mathcal P_N=\frac{D!}{\pi^D}
       \int_{\mathbb C^D}E_N(x)^{-D-1}\,dx,
 \qquad S_N^{\rm rec}=\frac{\mathcal B_N^2}{\mathcal P_N}.
 \tag{UR1}
\]
The measure is real Lebesgue measure in physical orthonormal
coordinates. The base polynomial has degree at most four; the
integration dimension and denominator exponent grow with \(N\).

For every nonzero original source, the integral is finite and
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \left|\frac{|K_N|^2\mathcal P_N}{\mathcal B_N^2}-1\right|
       \le\frac1{2048},\qquad
 \left(1-\frac1{2048}\right)S_N^{\rm rec}
       \le |K_N|^2\le
 \left(1+\frac1{2048}\right)S_N^{\rm rec}.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{UR2}
\]
If \(K_N=0\), then \(\mathcal P_N=+\infty\); its reciprocal is
zero, and the two source inequalities remain exact. The bound is
uniform in the prescribed leaf packets. In particular arbitrary fixed
short fillings retain their entire original operators.

Two features of the actual source make this possible. First, the
physical Casimir multiplicities give
\(\|c_N\|\le1/(16\sqrt{2N})\), using the same budgets as before.
Second, ordering children before parents makes \(G\) a polynomial
automorphism with real Jacobian one. Its inverse is the actual finite
recursion. In residual coordinates the denominator becomes
\(\|r\|^2+|c_NG^{-1}(r)|^2\).

On the proof ball \(\|r\|\le1/(4s)\), expanding the squared closing
term gives a relative energy error at most \(1/(8192D)\) against
its affine approximation. This controls the growing denominator
power. The exact forward recursion bounds the relative exterior
tail by \(1/8192\), without a lower bound on \(|K_N|\).
The affine reciprocal integral is exactly the inverse squared
normalized source. These facts prove (UR2). The ball is used only
in the proof; the integral has no adjustable parameter.

This shortens the dependency path for the reciprocal formulation.
It needs the physical operations, their norm bounds, the closing
estimate and triangular residual coordinates. It does not use the
convex minimum, Newton iteration, Gaussian determinant or
semidefinite-programming results. Those results remain available;
they are unnecessary for this representation of the source rate.

For nonzero sources the logarithmic error is explicitly bounded by
\[
 \left|\frac\pi N\log S_N^{\rm rec}
            -\frac{2\pi}N\log|K_N|\right|
        \le\frac\pi{2047N}.                                \tag{UR3}
\]
The corresponding bound with \(\log(1+S_N^{\rm rec})\) and
\(\log(1+|K_N|^2)\) includes zeros. Thus a positive volume-rate
limit for this undamped expression is equivalent to the original
Kashaev limit. The earlier damped formula retains its separate
advantage of a relative error tending to zero.

The remaining task is to estimate this particular positive integral
from the hyperbolic geometry, including after a fixed short partial
filling. Its denominator still contains the full signed source.
No such geometric estimate, additional knot family, or
finite-exception theorem is established here.

## An exact closing density with polynomial norm and inverse bounds, 24 November

The [original-source theorem](research_original_source_in_coproduct_graph_gram.md)
controls the actual marked pivotal closing in the canonical Gram of
the coproduct theorem below. Both its source density and its inverse
have polynomial bounds. The proof uses the metric inherited from an
explicit eigenspace graph; it assumes no comparison with a favorable
replacement metric.

Fix \(b\ge1\), and use the complete-color cyclic-source line with
\(N\ge2\). Here \(W_\mu\) is the genuinely transported braid operator,
including the finite source dependence of every crossing. The original
cut theorem identifies its completed cut with the original knot
operator. The unchanged nilpotent-head matrix \(W_0\) cannot simply be
substituted into the following cyclic identities.

The full physical space is \(\mathcal V=(\mathbb C^N)^{\otimes b}\);
the tail is \(\mathcal V_{\rm t}=(\mathbb C^N)^{\otimes(b-1)}\).
Write \(E_\Sigma=E_1K_{\rm t}+B\), where \(B\) is the tail coproduct,
and retain the original tail pivot \(g_{\rm t}=K_{\rm t}^{1-N}\).
On the chosen line,
\[
 E_\Sigma^N=bcI,\qquad B^N=(b-1)cI,\qquad |c|=1.
\]
For an actual eigenvalue \(\lambda^N=bc\), put \(Z=B/\lambda\).
The full \(\lambda\)-eigenspace is an explicit graph
\(L_\lambda:\mathcal V_{\rm t}\to\mathcal V\), uniquely specified by
\[
 E_\Sigma L_\lambda=\lambda L_\lambda,\qquad
 \pi_0L_\lambda=I.
\]
The map \(\pi_0\) extracts first-head color zero. It retains all
\(N^{b-1}\) tail coordinates and every intermediate Casimir channel.
Set \(W_\lambda=\pi_0W_\mu L_\lambda\).

Let \(P_0\) project the first head onto its zeroth basis vector.
The literal original closing
\(t_b(W_\mu)=\operatorname{Tr}[(P_0\otimes g_{\rm t})W_\mu]\)
then has the exact formula
\[
 t_b(W_\mu)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal V_{\rm t}}
                     (R_\lambda W_\lambda),\qquad
 R_\lambda=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} Z^k g_{\rm t}
            =\frac1b(I-Z)^{-1}g_{\rm t}.
                                                               \tag{SC1}
\]
The factor \(1/b\) follows from \(Z^N=(b-1)I/b\). No normalization
constant is suppressed. All \(N\) spectral sectors contribute equally
under the original total-clock symmetry; this is why one sector gives
the full formula (SC1), rather than an assumed dominant-sector truncation.
Existing exterior dimension and framing factors still multiply it.

Let \(G_\lambda=L_\lambda^*L_\lambda\) be the inherited graph Gram,
and put \(\rho=b^{-1+1/N}\). The theorem proves
\[
 \frac{\rho^2}{4}G_\lambda
 \preceq R_\lambda^*G_\lambda R_\lambda
 \preceq N^2\rho^2G_\lambda.
                                                               \tag{SC2}
\]
This is an explicit compensation identity. For \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\),
put \(\mathcal P_a(Z)=\prod_{h=0}^{a-1}(I-Q^hZ)\). Then
\[
 R_\lambda=g_{\rm t}\mathcal P_{N-1}(Z),\qquad
 \mathcal P_a(Z)R_\lambda
       =b^{-1}g_{\rm t}\mathcal P_{a-1}(Z)\quad(1\le a<N).
                                                               \tag{SC3}
\]
Applying (SC3) to every positive term of \(G_\lambda\) shifts its
weights by one place. The wrap contributes a retained final term.
The resulting coefficient ratios lie between \(\rho^2/4\) and
\(N^2\rho^2\), proving (SC2) at every level.

For \(T=E_\Sigma/e\), \(e^N=bc\), define the exact invariant density
\[
 J_{\rm av}=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(T^k)^*T^k,\qquad
 \overline D=\frac1N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}
       T^k(P_0\otimes g_{\rm t})T^{-k}.
\]
On actual braid intertwiners it gives the unchanged trace functional.
The canonical Gram satisfies
\(L_\lambda^*J_{\rm av}L_\lambda=NG_\lambda\); its spectral sectors
are orthogonal, and the block of \(\overline D\) is \(R_\lambda/N\).
Consequently
\[
 \|\overline D\|_{J_{\rm av}}\le\rho,\qquad
 \|\overline D^{-1}\|_{J_{\rm av}}\le2N/\rho,\qquad
 \operatorname{cond}_{J_{\rm av}}(\overline D)\le2N.
                                                               \tag{SC4}
\]
The last condition number is that of the source operator, not of the
Gram relative to physical coordinates. In the unnormalized matrix
Hilbert--Schmidt norm of this Gram, the original closing obeys
\[
 |t_b(W_\mu)|\le
       \rho N^{b/2}\|W_\mu\|_{{\rm HS},J_{\rm av}}.
                                                               \tag{SC5}
\]
These bounds have no sign or word-length restriction on the actual
braid, so fixed short components can retain their full operators.
They include \(b=1\), both level parities, and composite levels.

This settles a source-norm requirement in the same canonical Gram
whose physical distortion was computed below. It does not prove a
scalar lower bound. When \(b\ge2\), the invertible source density has
trace zero; its pairing with an operator can still cancel. The
geometric energy estimate, survival of the geometric trace contribution
and finite-exception theorem remain unproved.

## A positive coproduct period and the sharp cost of orthogonalization, 24 November

The [physical coproduct theorem](research_sharp_physical_coproduct_gram.md)
computes a canonical positive Gram and its optimal exponential scale
for every fixed number of heads. It supplies a positive norm identity
for actual spectral packets, with the cost of changing the physical
metric explicitly accounted for.

Fix \(b\ge1\) before taking \(N\to\infty\). Use the original physical
orthonormal basis, \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), and the regular complete-color
cyclic-source line \(\mu_i=\gamma^{1-i}\mu\), where
\(\gamma=(-1)^{N+1}\) and \(|\mu|=1/N\). The actual coproduct is
\[
 E_{\rm tot}=\sum_{i=1}^b E_iK_{i+1}\cdots K_b,\qquad
 K_{\rm tot}=\prod_{i=1}^bK_i,\qquad
 E_{\rm tot}^N=bcI,\quad c=\gamma^bN\mu.
\]
Choose \(e^N=bc\) and set \(T=E_{\rm tot}/e\). Then \(T^N=I\),
\(|e|=b^{1/N}\), and \(K_{\rm tot}T=QT K_{\rm tot}\).
The source-line freedom preserves the entire original selected knot
operator, with its existing exterior factors. This does not replace
the original closing by a new functional.

Define the known positive Gram and its scalar period by
\[
 J_{\rm av}=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(T^k)^*T^k,\qquad
 \mathcal H_N=\operatorname{Tr}J_{\rm av}.
                                                               \tag{CG1}
\]
Let \(\mathfrak d_N\) be the infimum of
\(\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(J)/\lambda_{\min}(J)}\) over positive Grams
making both \(T\) and \(K_{\rm tot}\) unitary. All these metrics are
compared with the original physical metric. With
\(\mathcal A_N=\max_{0\le k<N}\|T^k\|_{\rm op}\), the theorem proves
\[
 \mathcal A_N\le\mathfrak d_N\le\sqrt N\,\mathcal A_N,\qquad
 I\preceq J_{\rm av}\preceq N\mathcal A_N^2 I.
                                                               \tag{CG2}
\]
The same rate holds if only \(T\)-invariance is required.

Write \(n=2b+1\), \(\delta=\pi/n\), and
\[
 h(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi v)\,dv,\qquad
 M_b=-n h(1/n),\qquad
 C_b=\frac{2^{1-b}b^{-4b/n}\sin\delta}
                  {\sqrt n\,\sin(2\delta)^b}.
\]
The sharp asymptotics are
\[
 \log\mathfrak d_N=NM_b+O_b(\log N),\qquad
 \mathcal H_N=C_bN e^{2NM_b}(1+O_b(N^{-1})).
                                                               \tag{CG3}
\]
Here \(2\pi M_b\) is the volume of the regular ideal
\((2b+1)\)-gonal bipyramid. That familiar angle value already occurs
in divided-fusion calculations; the new assertions concern this
actual physical coproduct, its positive period and its optimal Gram.

The calculation retains every wrap. For \(k<N\), each nonzero power
entry has one allocation \(k_1+\cdots+k_b=k\), with output residues
\(r_i=[a_i-k_i]_N\), and exact modulus
\[
 |\langle\boldsymbol r|T^k|\boldsymbol a\rangle|
 =b^{-k/N}s_k\prod_i\frac{s_{a_i}}{s_{k_i}s_{r_i}},
 \qquad s_a=\prod_{j=1}^a2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad s_0=1.
                                                               \tag{CG4}
\]
The quantum multinomial has already combined the paths coherently.
The limiting entropy of this full wrapped array has its unique maximum
in the strict nonwrapped interior, at scaled coordinates
\(k_i/N=2/n\) and \(a_i/N=1/2+1/n\).
The negative entropy Hessian there has determinant \(n\pi^{2b}\).
Endpoint-uniform bounds control the complement and give (CG3);
the quadratic expansion supplies its displayed prefactor.

There is an exact orthogonality statement as well. The physical
unitary \(K_{\rm tot}\) gives different conjugation characters to
the \(N\) powers \(T^k\), so those matrices are Hilbert--Schmidt
orthogonal. Consequently their actual spectral projectors satisfy
\[
 P_j=\frac1N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}Q^{-jk}T^k,\qquad
 J_{\rm av}=N\sum_jP_j^*P_j,\qquad
 \|P_j\|_{\rm HS}^2=\frac{C_b}{N}e^{2NM_b}(1+O_b(N^{-1})).
                                                               \tag{CG5}
\]
The Gram identity is exact and retains all packets. The asymptotics
hold through both parities and composite levels, with fixed \(b\).

This is a coproduct metric scale, not a knot volume: already the
one-head construction has a positive rate while an unknot cut has
value one. The original pivotal tail, marked cut and incident
interfaces still require their transported estimates. Neither a
geometric coefficient for the original closing nor the theorem after
arbitrary short partial fillings follows from (CG3)--(CG5).

\(\texttt{6fcdfbece5d9f06c541649926345876aab8daf6dee09022160e79d99a02bafeb}\).
Its five complete matching texts are balanced source, 247 lines;

bounds, 306 lines; cyclic Wall conditioning, 257 lines; and divided

## Cyclic Fourier orthogonality retains the shifted pivotal source, 24 November

The cyclic-source freedom gives an exact test of another proposed
orthogonal basis. It preserves the original knot value, but its
orthogonality does not turn the prescribed tail closing into a norm.
This is a basis and source audit; no new volume estimate is asserted.

Put \(D=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(\gamma=(-1)^{N+1}\), \(x=-q^{-1}\), and
\[
 e_a=Q^{-a}-1,\qquad
 s_a=\prod_{h=1}^a2\sin(\pi h/N),\qquad s_0=1.
\]
The complete-color boundary chart in
[the balanced source proof](balanced_verma_coherent_braiding.md),
Section 5, has
\[
 E_\mu w_a=e_aw_{a-1}\quad(a>0),\qquad E_\mu w_0=\mu w_D.
\]
Its entire original one-cut operator is independent of the transported
source parameters, with the pivot, framing and meridian line retained.
Choose \(|\mu|=1/N\) on the fixed source line; the other head parameters
then have the same modulus. Since \(\prod_{a=1}^D e_a=\gamma N\),
choose \(\lambda^N=\gamma N\mu\), and set
\[
 c_a=\frac{\lambda^a}{\prod_{h=1}^a e_h},\qquad
 v_a=c_aw_a,\qquad H=\operatorname{diag}(s_a^2).
                                                               \tag{CF1}
\]
Then \(|\lambda|=1\), \(|c_a|=s_a^{-1}\), and \(E_\mu v_a
=\lambda v_{a-1}\), including the cyclic wrap. Thus the vectors
\[
 u_j=N^{-1/2}\sum_{a=0}^D Q^{ja}v_a,\qquad
 E_\mu u_j=\lambda Q^j u_j
                                                               \tag{CF2}
\]
are an \(H\)-orthonormal eigenbasis at every level \(N\ge2\).

The original pivot is different from the identity in this basis.
The literal formulas \(Kw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a\) and \(g=K^{1-N}\) give
\[
 Ku_j=xu_{j-1},\qquad gu_j=\eta u_{j-1},\qquad
 \eta=x^{1-N},\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}(gA)=\eta\sum_j(A_{\rm F})_{j+1,j}.
                                                               \tag{CF3}
\]
All Fourier indices are modulo \(N\), and \(A_{\rm F}\) is the
matrix in the \(u\) basis. If \(U\) has columns \(u_j\), the original
cut projection satisfies
\(U^{-1}P_0U=\boldsymbol1\boldsymbol1^*/N\). Consequently the
original \(b\)-head source becomes exactly
\[
 t_b(A)=\operatorname{Tr}\left[
 \left(\frac{\boldsymbol1\boldsymbol1^*}{N}
       \otimes(\eta S)^{\otimes(b-1)}\right)A_{\rm F}\right],
 \qquad Su_j=u_{j-1}.
                                                               \tag{CF4}
\]
Here each head uses its own transported basis. The existing exterior
normalization factors still multiply this expression. Equations
(CF3)--(CF4) sample shifted matrix entries; they are not Parseval
identities for the original scalar.

There is a quantitative distinction between this orthogonality and
the original physical metric. Let
\(\Pi_j=u_j u_j^*H\) be the \(H\)-orthogonal spectral projector of
\(E_\mu\). In the original physical metric it is generally oblique:
\[
 \|\Pi_j\|_{\rm op}=\|\Pi_j\|_{\rm HS}=B_N,\qquad
 B_N=\sum_{a=0}^D s_a^{-2},\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}(g\Pi_j)=0.
                                                               \tag{CF5}
\]
Indeed \(\|u_j\|^2=B_N/N\), while the squared physical norm of its
dual row is \(N B_N\), since
\(s_as_{D-a}=N\) implies \(\sum_a s_a^2=N^2B_N\).
Their product proves the norm identity; (CF3) proves the zero trace.
The projector has trace one, so it remains an allowed probe of the
unchanged scalar cut, with the existing normalization restored.

For scale, the endpoint-uniform bound in
[the crossing norm proof](weighted_crossing_source_gap.md) gives
\[
 \log\operatorname{cond}(\operatorname{diag}c_a)
 =\log B_N+O(\log N)
 =\frac{Nv_3}{\pi}+O(\log N),
                                                               \tag{CF6}
\]
where \(\Lambda(\theta)=-\int_0^\theta\log(2\sin u)\,du\) and
\(v_3=2\Lambda(\pi/6)\). To check the rate directly, the function
\(h(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du\) has minimum
\(-v_3/(2\pi)\) at \(1/6\) and maximum \(v_3/(2\pi)\) at \(5/6\).
Maximal terms bound \(B_N\) within a factor \(N\).
These factorial rates already occur in the earlier frame calculations.

The exponential factor in (CF5) is the error-amplification cost of
choosing this oblique spectral projector in the physical metric.
It is not an unavoidable cost for the original cap: in \(H\),
\(P_0\) is still orthogonal, \(g\) is unitary and
\(\|g\|_{\rm HS,H}=\sqrt N\). Physically Hermitian trace-one probes
also remain available. What has not been proved is a geometric lower
bound for the shifted contraction (CF4). Cyclic multiplicity-one on
one head does not compute the remaining knot-dependent period.
The [original reflection obstruction](original_reflection_gram_obstruction.md)
already excludes an automatic positive-functional interpretation.

## Joint fan optimization reduces to a degree-r polynomial, 24 November

The [joint fan proof](research_full_physical_fan_gaussian_packet.md)
combines any fixed number \(r\ge1\) of successive positive crossings in which
one donor strand meets \(r\) recipients. It estimates the original
physical matrix before any closing. Every nonzero entry has exactly
one transfer path, so the donor sine factorials telescope before any
estimate. The product of all original phases, including the Cartan
scalar, remains in the matrix and its Gaussian approximation.

Let \(A\in[0,1]\) be the donor input divided by the level \(N\), and
put
\[
 h(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi v)\,dv,\qquad m=2r+1.
\]
After maximizing over the recipient occupations and the individual
transfers at fixed \(A\), the maximal entry action is
\[
                         I_r(A)=h(A)-m h(A/m).
                                                               \tag{JF1}
\]
At positive interior transfers, the recipient optimizations are strictly
concave. Equalizing the
transfers and then solving one sine-ratio equation proves (JF1)
globally, including its endpoints.

Weight a donor input column by \(e^{\eta a}\), with fixed real
\(\eta\) and integer input \(a\). The joint maximum is that of
\(I_r(A)+\eta A\). Since \(I_r''(A)<0\), it has a unique interior
maximizer precisely when \(\eta>-\log m\). In that regime it reduces
to one polynomial equation:
\[
 P_r(y)=e^{-\eta},\qquad
 P_0(y)=1,\quad P_1(y)=4y-1,\quad
 P_{j+1}(y)=(4y-2)P_j(y)-P_{j-1}(y),
                                                               \tag{JF2}
\]
\[
 \cos^2(\pi/m)<y<1,\qquad
 A_\eta=\frac m\pi\arccos\sqrt y.
\]
Here \(P_r\) has integer coefficients and degree \(r\), independently
of \(N\); it is strictly increasing from zero to \(m\) on the stated
interval. For example \(P_2(y)=16y^2-12y+1\). At and below the
threshold the maximum has \(A=0\) and value zero. The interior
Gaussian theorem is not extended across that transition.

Write \(\mathsf F_{r,N,\eta}\) for this weighted fan matrix.
The proof also gives the full joint Hessian and the norm prefactor.
Write \(\theta=\pi A_\eta/m\) and
\(M_\eta=I_r(A_\eta)+\eta A_\eta\). Uniformly on every fixed compact
subinterval of the interior regime,
\[
 \|\mathsf F_{r,N,\eta}\|_{\rm HS}^2
 =\sqrt N\,e^{2NM_\eta}
 \frac{e^{-\eta}(2\sin2\theta)^{-r}}
 {\sqrt{\cot\theta-m\cot(m\theta)}}(1+O(N^{-1})).
                                                               \tag{JF3}
\]
The denominator is positive. The full matrix has a joint Gaussian
expansion to every fixed order \(J\ge0\), with relative Hilbert--Schmidt error
\(O_{r,J}(N^{-(J+1)/2})\); sufficiently small additional real boundary
weights are allowed. Both parities and the exact finite support are
retained. Neither \(r\) nor the expansion order grows with \(N\).

At zero weight, \(2\pi M_0\) is the volume of the regular ideal
\((2r+2)\)-gonal bipyramid. That volume already occurred in the
Fourier bridge calculation; the new assertion is the joint physical
matrix estimate. The proof additionally specifies unit product
Gaussian input and output vectors, with their phases determined from
the exact fan coefficient, for which
\[
 \langle\Psi_{\rm out,N},\mathsf F_{r,N}\Psi_{\rm in,N}\rangle
 =c_r e^{NM_0+i\Theta_N}(1+O_r(N^{-1/2})),\qquad c_r\ne0.
                                                               \tag{JF4}
\]
The constant and phase are explicit in the proof. Thus this open
coefficient has a proved nonzero leading term.

These prepared boundary vectors are not the prescribed knot closing.
The ordinary tail sewing already misses the flat joint maximum when
\(r\ge2\). General short-component propagation, geometric matching of
its boundary data, and a lower bound for the original closing remain
unproved. This fan result does not settle the finite-exception theorem
or reduce the whole-knot quartic to the polynomial (JF2).

## A whole physical Gaussian packet for an original crossing, 24 November

The [full physical packet proof](research_full_physical_crossing_gaussian_packet.md)
approximates the entire original crossing matrix in the uniform physical
Hilbert--Schmidt norm, to every fixed algebraic order. The matrix acts on
the physical pair of dimension \(N^2\). Its exact phases and all finite
support constraints remain in the approximation.

Put \(s_j=\prod_{h=1}^j2\sin(\pi h/N)\), \(s_0=1\).
The positive checked crossing has input \((a,b)\), output
\((b+k,a-k)\), and exactly one term at each nonzero entry.
Writing \(j=a-k\), its exact modulus is
\[
 |R^+_{(b+k,j);(j+k,b)}|
       =\frac{s_{b+k}s_{j+k}}{s_ks_bs_j}.
\]
The exact phase \(\chi_N(j,b,k)\), including the Cartan scalar, is retained.
The inverse has the exact flip-conjugate array.

For \(z=(u,v,t)=(j,b,k)/N\), set
\[
 h(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi r)\,dr,\qquad
 S(z)=h(u+t)+h(v+t)-h(u)-h(v)-h(t).
\]
The compact support is \(u,v,t\ge0\), \(u+t,v+t\le1\).
Real exponential diagonal weights on the input and output heads add
a known linear term \(\lambda\cdot z\) to \(S\).
On a fixed sufficiently small closed tilt ball, \(S+\lambda\cdot z\)
has a unique interior global maximum \(z_\lambda\).
Write \(M_\lambda\) for its value, \(H_\lambda=-S''(z_\lambda)>0\), and
\[
 a_\lambda^2=
 \left.\frac{\sin\pi(u+t)\sin\pi(v+t)}
 {\sin\pi u\sin\pi v\sin\pi t}\right|_{z_\lambda}.
\]
These quantities depend on the explicit \(S\), independently of a closed value.

For every fixed \(J\ge0\), the proof constructs real polynomials
\(P_{\lambda,l}(y)\), \(P_{\lambda,0}=1\), of degree at most \(3l\).
On the exact physical support the Gaussian model has entries
\[
 \mathcal G_{N,J,\rho}
 =\chi_N\,\frac{a_\lambda e^{NM_\lambda}}{\sqrt{2N}}\,
 e^{-y^{\mathsf T}H_\lambda y/2}
       \sum_{l=0}^J N^{-l/2}P_{\lambda,l}(y),\qquad
 y=\frac{(j,b,k)-Nz_\lambda}{\sqrt N}.
\]
The negative model uses the corresponding exact flip-conjugation
and permutation of the boundary weights. For both signs,
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \frac{\|R^\pm_\rho-\mathcal G^\pm_{N,J,\rho}\|_{\rm HS}}
      {\|R^\pm_\rho\|_{\rm HS}}
       \le C_JN^{-(J+1)/2}.
 \quad}                                                       \tag{PG1}
\]
This is uniform on the small tilt chamber through all sufficiently
large levels, including both parities. The order \(J\) is fixed;
no estimate for an order growing with \(N\) is asserted.
The squared norm has the explicit prefactor
\[
 \|R^\pm_\rho\|_{\rm HS}^2
 =\sqrt N\,\frac{\pi^{3/2}a_\lambda^2}
                  {2\sqrt{\det H_\lambda}}\,
       e^{2NM_\lambda}(1+O(N^{-1})).
                                                               \tag{PG2}
\]
At zero tilt \(z_0=(1/4,1/4,1/2)\), \(M_0=2G/\pi\),
\(\det H_0=4\pi^3\), so the right side is
\(\sqrt N\,e^{4GN/\pi}/4\,(1+O(N^{-1}))\);
\(G\) is Catalan's constant.

The proof uses all-order interior sine-factorial expansions and a
Gaussian polynomial remainder before summing its square. The unique
compact-domain maximum and endpoint-uniform factorial bounds control
every remaining matrix entry.

At zero tilt, orthogonal projection of the model onto the complete
physical algebra \(\mathcal A_N\) preserves (PG1), including every
double-root normal direction. Under nonzero tilts the correct projected
space is the exact image \(W_{\rm out}\mathcal A_NW_{\rm in}^{-1}\).
Undoing those gauges can have exponential cost; incident inverse
interfaces, original caps and actual compiler budgets remain necessary.
The models are not asserted to be exact mutual inverses.

The earlier Newton-coordinate crossing already has a full
Hilbert--Schmidt Gaussian operator limit. The present addition concerns
the uniform physical \(N^2\times N^2\) array, its three-dimensional
support, all fixed orders and small real tilts. No matching of these
tilts to arbitrary geometric Conway data is supplied.
The original closing can be exponentially smaller than the leaf norm,
so (PG1) alone gives no scalar lower or finite-exception theorem.

## One positive reciprocal integral replaces the quartic minimum, 23 November

The [reciprocal source formula](research_conway_reciprocal_quartic_source_formula.md)
gives a relative-error formula for the original squared modulus.
Its input is the known full physical quartic, with a prescribed
polynomial damping of its closing row. No minimizer, Hessian
determinant, chosen temperature or lower bound for \(K_N\) is supplied.

Use the actual uniform physical metric and budgets. If there are
\(s\) proper packets at level \(N\), put
\[
 D=Ns,\quad m=D+1,\quad \varepsilon=m^{-3},\quad
 B_\varepsilon=B/\varepsilon,\quad \delta=m^{-2}.
\]
The full \(N\)-dimensional packet spaces retain every Casimir normal.
Keep the normalized residuals \(G_v=\Phi_v-x_v\) and original closing
row \(c\). Its true normalized value is \(k=K_N/B\), with
\(|k|\le1/256\). Define
\[
 E_\varepsilon(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+\varepsilon^2|cx|^2,\qquad
 \mathcal P_\varepsilon=
       \frac{D!}{\pi^D}\int_{\mathbb C^D}
                           E_\varepsilon(x)^{-D-1}\,dx .       \tag{RI1}
\]
Here \(dx\) is real Lebesgue measure in physical orthonormal
coordinates. The base is polynomial of degree at most four;
the denominator power grows with \(D\). For the rational damping
specified above its coefficients are algebraic. The displayed
\(\pi^{-D}\) normalization is retained explicitly.

At every level \(N\ge2\), if \(K_N\ne0\), this integral is finite
and positive, and
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 (1-\delta)\frac{B_\varepsilon^2}{\mathcal P_\varepsilon}
 \le |K_N|^2\le
 (1+\delta)\frac{B_\varepsilon^2}{\mathcal P_\varepsilon}.
 \quad}                                                       \tag{RI2}
\]
If \(K_N=0\), the integral diverges to \(+\infty\); its reciprocal
is defined as zero, and both inequalities remain exact. There is
no parity restriction. For a fixed expression the relative error
is \(O(N^{-2})\), even when the nonzero source is exponentially tiny.

For a nonzero source, use the actual polynomial automorphism \(r=G(x)\),
whose real Jacobian is exactly one. On the fixed residual ball
\(\|r\|\le1/4\), its inverse remains in the packet unit balls.
Disjoint sibling maps give
\(\|D^2(cG^{-1})\|\le\sigma^2(8/7)^3<1\), \(\sigma=1/16\).
Thus the damped closing equals \(k'+d'r+p(r)\), with
\(k'=\varepsilon k\) and \(|p(r)|\le\varepsilon\|r\|^2/2\).

For the affine denominator
\(\|r\|^2+|k'+d'r|^2\), the normalized inverse-energy integral is
exactly \(1/|k'|^2\): its determinant and completed-square constant
cancel. The nonlinear and affine normalized tails outside that
fixed ball are each at most \(16D\). The inside comparison gives
\[
 \left||k'|^2\mathcal P_\varepsilon-1\right|
 \le e^{(2/7)m\varepsilon}-1+32D|k'|^2
 \le m^{-2}.                                                  \tag{RI3}
\]
Only the actual bilinear physical norm bounds are used; no
coefficient-Hilbert--Schmidt determinant estimate is transferred
to this metric. More generally, known damping
\(\varepsilon=m^{-p}\) with fixed integer \(p>1\) gives relative
error \(O(m^{1-p})\), with its budget factor restored.

There is also the exact positive Tonelli identity
\[
 \mathcal P_\varepsilon=\int_0^\infty Z_\varepsilon(t)\,dt,
 \qquad
 Z_\varepsilon(t)=(t/\pi)^D\int e^{-tE_\varepsilon(x)}\,dx .
                                                               \tag{RI4}
\]
It integrates all temperatures; the intrinsic small-source scale
remains in the resulting integral. All original signed tensors,
phases and the marked closing are still inside its denominator.
No hyperbolic-volume estimate of this integral, geometric source
coefficient, or finite-exception theorem is proved.
