## A fixed nearby color block determines the complete value, 23 November

The [terminal observation proof](research_near_complete_ordinary_jet_observation.md)
gives a simpler data problem than full-orbit reconstruction. For a fixed
actual recurrence of order \(d\), it uses only the colors
\(N-d,\ldots,N-1\), all strictly below the complete color. A fixed
number of their genuine quantum derivatives determines \(K_N\), with
polynomial observation cost. This does not estimate those derivatives.

Write the actual reduced color recurrence as
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^{d}a_j(Q,Q^m)\mathcal C_{m+j}(Q)=0,
 \qquad a_d\ne0,
\]
with fixed Laurent-polynomial coefficients after the recorded
denominator clearing. The original zero-framed period is
\(K_N=\mathcal C_N(Q_N)\), where \(Q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}\).
Factor the leading coefficient maximally as
\[
 a_d(Q,Y)=(1-Q^dY)^\mu b_d(Q,Y),\qquad
 B(Q)=b_d(Q,Q^{-d})\ne0,
 \quad v=\operatorname{ord}_{Q=1}B(Q).
\]
The integers \(d,\mu,v\) depend on the fixed recurrence, not on \(N\).

Use \(Q=Q_N(1+\zeta/N)\), keeping each color dimension fixed
during differentiation. Define
\[
\begin{split}
 J_{j,\ell,N}&=[\zeta^\ell]\mathcal C_{N-d+j}(Q),\\
 A_{j,r,N}&=[\zeta^r]a_j(Q,Q^{N-d}).
\end{split}
\]
For every sufficiently large level, through both parities,
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 K_N=\frac{(-1)^{\mu+1}}{B(Q_N)}
       \sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\sum_{\ell=0}^{\mu}
                   A_{j,\mu-\ell,N}J_{j,\ell,N}.
 \quad}                                                       \tag{NJ1}
\]
No derivative of the complete color appears on the right.
There are exactly \(d(\mu+1)\) supplied scalar entries, with
possible zero row weights retained.

The proof uses the recurrence row ending at \(N\). Its leading
factor becomes \((1-Q^N)^\mu\), and
\[
 1-Q^N=1-(1+\zeta/N)^N=-\zeta+O(\zeta^2).
\]
Thus its first nonzero coefficient isolates \(K_N\) exactly.
Every other fixed-order row coefficient \(A_{j,r,N}\) is bounded:
each substituted monomial has exponent \(O(N)\), canceled by
the specified derivative scale. Also
\(|B(Q_N)|\ge cN^{-v}\), because \(B\) is a fixed nonzero
Laurent polynomial. Consequently the total absolute row weight
in (NJ1) is at most \(CN^v\).

For arbitrary approximate jet data, let \(G_N\) be their observation
by the same row. Then
\[
 |G_N-K_N|\le CN^v
       \max_{j,\ell}|\widetilde J_{j,\ell,N}-J_{j,\ell,N}|.
                                                               \tag{NJ2}
\]
There is no arithmetic-coefficient hypothesis. The constants can
depend on the fixed knot, filling and recurrence; no bound uniform
over an unbounded filling family is claimed.

The ordinary-color polynomial bound controls only the \(\ell=0\)
part of this row. The higher quantum derivatives can have exponential
size, and their signed sum still needs a geometric estimate.
The prior peripheral-source theorem already explains the resonant
right factor required by positive growth. The new point here is
the bounded block of below-\(N\) colors and its polynomial row norm.
Earlier ordinary-orbit recovery used all noncomplete residue classes
and additional genuine high colors.

This is a different supplied-data problem from quantitative Mellin
reconstruction: it replaces global approximate source equations by
approximations to these actual nearby quantum derivatives. It does
not improve the Mellin bound from the same small-prefix information.
No geometric approximation to the required derivatives, nonzero
geometric coefficient or finite-exception theorem is established here.

## Quantum source reconstruction now has an error bound, 23 November

The [quantitative reconstruction proof](research_quantitative_cyclotomic_jet_reconstruction.md)
strengthens the earlier exact cyclotomic uniqueness theorem. It bounds
the error in the original Kashaev value by the errors in finitely many
quantum derivative orders of its actual source equations. The number
of color coefficients still grows with the level.

Keep a specified actual arithmetic recurrence
\[
 P=\sum_{j=0}^{d}a_j(Q,Y)T^j,\qquad TY=QYT,
\]
with fixed Laurent-polynomial coefficients over a fixed number field,
after its recorded denominator clearing. Use its original Mellin
source \(P^MZ=\mathcal B\), fixed color prefix and cutoff \(n_0\).
At \(Q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}\), the original period is
\[
 K_N=\operatorname{Res}_{X=\infty}Z_N(X)\,\frac{dX}{X}.
\]
Let \(D,s\) be the \(Y\)-span and number of collected monomials
of \(a_d\). The fixed quantum derivative budget is
\(k=D(s-1)+1\), or any larger fixed value.

The candidate \(W_N\) must have the same starting lattice and exact
cyclotomic pole/prefix condition:
\[
 W_N\in X^{n_0}\mathbb C[[X]],\qquad
 (1-X^N)(W_N+p_{<,N})\in X\mathbb C[X],\quad\deg\le N,
\]
where \(p_{<,N}\) is the original fixed-color prefix polynomial.
Lift its coefficients through degree \(N\), retaining the actual
prefix through quantum order \(k-1\). Measure the source-equation
defects on the window \(n_0-d\le m\le N-d\) in the scaled variable
\[
 Q=Q_N(1+\zeta/N).
\]
The norm is the sum of absolute Taylor coefficients through degree
\(k-1\) in \(\zeta\); suppose every defect has norm at most
\(\delta_N\). These are derivatives of the quantum parameter
\(Q\), distinct from the framing variable \(U\).

For all sufficiently large levels, without a parity restriction,
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \left|\operatorname{Res}_{\infty}W_N\frac{dX}{X}-K_N\right|
             \le C_1e^{C_2N^2}\delta_N.
 \quad}                                                       \tag{QR1}
\]
The same bound controls every root coefficient through degree \(N\).
The constants depend on the fixed recurrence and derivative budget.
No geometric approximation is an input to their definition.

There is a sharper conclusion under the explicit factorization
\[
 a_d(Q,Y)=cQ^uY^v\prod_t(1-Q^{a_t}Y^{b_t})^{m_t},
 \qquad c\ne0,\quad b_t\ne0,\quad m_t\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}.
\]
All other exponents are fixed integers.
Put \(M=\sum_t m_t\), \(B_0=\sum_t m_t|b_t|\), and use
\(k\ge B_0+1\). With the original cutoff chosen as in the proof,
\[
 \left|\operatorname{Res}_{\infty}W_N\frac{dX}{X}-K_N\right|
       \le C_1N^{1+kMB_0}e^{C_2N}\delta_N.                    \tag{QR2}
\]
This factorization has not been proved for every Conway operator.

The proof keeps singular propagation steps. Each zero pivot consumes
its vanishing order from the retained quantum derivatives; the total
loss is bounded independently of \(N\). At nonzero arithmetic pivots,
the algebraic-integer norm bounds the inverse by \(e^{CN}\).
The finitely many singular steps cost at most \(e^{CN\log N}\).
Propagation through at most \(N\) steps gives (QR1). Under the
binomial hypothesis, the exact product around a root-of-unity orbit
instead bounds the entire regular propagation by \(e^{CN}\);
the singular steps contribute only the displayed power of \(N\).
The pole condition makes the residue error exactly the last coefficient
error, with its original normalization.

The restriction \(b_t\ne0\) in (QR2) matters. A nonminimal actual
unknot annihilator with leading coefficient \(1-Q\) admits defects
\(e^{-N\log N+O(N)}\) preserving its prefix and pole lattice while
changing the residue by one. The general bound (QR1) allows this;
the stronger bound cannot be assigned to that operator.

This gives an explicit accuracy requirement for a proposed geometric
source comparison. Such a comparison must still construct \(W_N\)
with the stated lattice, prefix and sufficiently small defects.
Neither a geometric section nor a volume lower bound is supplied
here. The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## A small framing-kernel correction can contain the entire source, 23 November

The finite-root presentation of the
[relative framing source](relative_framing_source_transgression.md)
suggests an attractive shortcut: replace its residue kernel by its
leading logarithmic form away from the unit circle. The kernel error
is exponentially small there. The following exact calculation shows
why that estimate alone does not justify the replacement inside the
actual finite-source contraction.

Keep the full normal variable \(U\) and the clock relation
\(A^N=U\), with \(N\ge2\). For a polynomial \(F\) with coefficients
holomorphic near \(U=1\), the normalized trace of this clock algebra is
\[
 \tau_{N,U}(F)=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_{|A|=R}
       F(A)\frac{A^{N-1}}{A^N-U}\,dA,
 \qquad |U|<R^N.                                             \tag{FK1}
\]
At nonzero \(U\), each root has residue \(F(A)/N\). The
formula also gives the coefficientwise normal family. On this contour,
\[
 \frac{A^{N-1}\,dA}{A^N-U}
       =\sum_{w\ge0}U^w A^{-wN}\,d\log A,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{A^N}{A^N-U}-1\right|
       \le\frac{|U|R^{-N}}{1-|U|R^{-N}}.                      \tag{FK2}
\]
Thus the kernel correction is exponentially small on a fixed
\(R>1\), uniformly on a fixed normal collar for large \(N\).

Now use the literal product of two canonical factors,
\(F=A\cdot A^{N-1}=A^N\). Direct integration gives
\[
 \tau_{N,U}(A^N)=U,\qquad
 \frac1{2\pi i}\oint A^N\,d\log A=0.                       \tag{FK3}
\]
The entire source in this example comes from the first correction
\(UA^{-N}\,d\log A\). Its exponentially small contour size is
exactly offset by the factor \(|A^N|=R^N\). The first \(U\)-normal
is lost as well: differentiating the two values in (FK3) gives
one and zero. This is an exact finite-source test, not a knot
counterexample or a nonexistence statement about the framing map.

More generally, if \(F(A)=\sum_{j=0}^{D}f_j(U)A^j\), then
\[
 \tau_{N,U}(F)=
        \sum_{w=0}^{\lfloor D/N\rfloor}U^w f_{wN}(U).         \tag{FK4}
\]
This follows from the convergent expansion (FK2), or directly
from canonical reduction. A product of \(m\) canonical polynomials
has at most \(m\) such sectors. They remain a coherent sum;
at \(U=1\), the first normal need not discard the higher sectors.
After full canonical reduction to degree below \(N\), the leading
logarithmic contour gives the exact trace. Reducing \(A^N\) first
therefore gives \(U\) and repairs (FK3), as it must.

The required comparison is consequently a comparison of the
contracted numerator, its canonical carries and the contour together.
The isolated kernel estimate (FK2) gives no source-relative error.
The earlier relative-source note already records the algebraic carry
and the failure of an unreduced zero residue; (FK2)--(FK3) test the
stronger proposed exponential approximation of the actual rational
kernel. This does not supply the missing internal geometric
pushforward or a nonzero geometric coefficient. No new volume lower
bound or finite-exception result is claimed.

## Canonical multiplication has logarithmic boundary cost, 23 November

The [canonical crossing estimate](research_canonical_crossing_logarithmic_strip_bound.md)
gives a simpler bound directly on the original finite polynomials.
It applies to every signed integer crossing power, including zero,
at every level. Its interpolation keeps the first derivatives at
double roots and the value at the odd-level simple root.

Put \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\),
\(\kappa=e^{\pi i(N-1)^2/(2N)}\), and let \(r_{n,N}\) be the
degree-below-\(N\) representative of \(\kappa^{-n}R^n\) modulo
the full \(P_N\). If \(M(f)=\max_{[-2,2]}|f|\), then
\[
 M(r_{n,N})\le
 1+|n|\left\{\frac\pi2+\frac4\pi(1+\log N)\right\}
 =:M_{N,n}.                                                   \tag{LM1}
\]
The original scalar \(\kappa^n\) remains a unit phase. For
\(w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N)\), every fixed derivative obeys
\[
 \sup_{|\Re\alpha|\le r}
 |\partial_\alpha^k r_{n,N}(w_N(\alpha))|
                     \le k!e^{r+1}M_{N,n}.                    \tag{LM2}
\]
There is no restriction on the imaginary height: this is the
actual canonical periodic expression.

Here is why interpolation gives a logarithm. On the angular grid
\(t_j=(2j+1)\pi/N\), the values have modulus one and their angular
derivatives have modulus at most \(|n|N/2\). The exact trigonometric
Hermite interpolation has nonnegative value weights summing to one.
Its derivative weights have total absolute mass at most
\[
 \frac{A_N}{N},\qquad
 A_N=\pi+\frac8\pi(1+\log N).
\]
The paired physical derivatives sum to zero, removing the unwanted
frequency \(N\). This gives the full degree-below-\(N\) polynomial,
with its normal directions, rather than a distinct-root replacement.
The logarithm is necessary uniformly over all powers: the actual
sequence \(n=2N\) has
\(|r_{2N,N}(2)|=(4/\pi)N\log N+O(N)\).

For canonical polynomials \(f,g\), the same argument bounds multiplication.
Write \(\operatorname{can}\) for remainder modulo the full \(P_N\). Then
\[
\begin{split}
 M(\operatorname{can}(fg))
       &\le(1+2eA_N)M(f)M(g),\\
 M(\operatorname{can}(r_{n,N}f))
       &\le\{1+(e+|n|/2)A_N\}M(f).                          \tag{LM3}
\end{split}
\]
Thus a fixed collection of these operations has only a polylogarithmic
norm cost for fixed signed powers. Canonical reduction has already
included all quotient carries. For these bounds one can work directly
with the finite polynomial, without introducing an auxiliary cut.

The quartic minimum keeps its recorded Hilbert--Schmidt budgets.
These estimates use a separate canonical supremum norm. The genuine
turn, the assembled source and its prescribed closing still need
their geometric estimates. The nonnegative value weights above do
not remove the complex derivative contributions or establish a
positive lower bound. No new volume-identity case or finite-exception
theorem follows here.

## The genuine turn has an explicit cut term with a controlled endpoint, 23 November

The [full-cover and cut calculation](research_even_crossing_full_cover_and_left_cut.md)
extends the preceding local crossing work to an exact contour formula
for the original turn. It retains the outer contour, both banks of
the new cut, and the full odd-level simple-root contribution. The
new quantitative estimate controls the cut endpoint uniformly in
the level. It does not yet estimate the rest of the turn.

Keep \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), \(\eta=(-1)^{N-1}\),
\(\kappa=e^{\pi i(N-1)^2/(2N)}\), and the original turn kernel \(K_N\).
Use the entire even functions \(D,G_{n,N}\) defined below, the latter
with its original signed-power values and first normals. The new
partial-fraction formula proves
\[
 |D(x+iy)|\le\cosh(x/2)+
       \frac{24\cosh^2(x/2)}{x^2+(|y|+\pi)^2}.
                                                               \tag{TC1}
\]
Consequently, for fixed \(r,L>0\),
\[
 |G_{n,N}(\alpha)|\le C_r(1+|n|)
                    e^{|n|rL/(2\pi)}
 \quad (|\Re\alpha|\le r,\ |\Im\alpha|\le LN),                 \tag{TC2}
\]
uniformly in \(N\ge2\) and integer \(n\); buffered estimates retain
every fixed derivative. This covers the full physical logarithmic
window, whose height grows with \(N\).

Evenness gives a holomorphic function
\(g_{n,N}(z)=G_{n,N}(N\operatorname{arccosh}(z/2))\)
on \(\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,-2]\), including \(z=2\).
Choose \(R>2\), put \(z(a)=-2\cosh(a/N)\) and
\(r_R=N\operatorname{arccosh}(R/2)\), and define its cut jump by
\[
 J_{n,N}(a)=G_{n,N}(a+i\pi N)-G_{n,N}(-a+i\pi N).
\]
For any actual polynomial input \(f\), set
\(h(z)=f(z)K_N(z,w)\). The exact genuine turn is
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \mathsf T(R^nf)(w)=\frac{\kappa^n\eta N^2}{2\pi i}
 \left[
 \int_{\Gamma_R}\frac{g_{n,N}(z)h(z)}{P_N(z)}\,dz
 -\int_0^{r_R}\frac{J_{n,N}(a)h(z(a))}
                        {P_N(z(a))}z'(a)\,da
 \right].
 \quad}                                                       \tag{TC3}
\]
Here \(\Gamma_R\) is the positive outer slit circle, with its two
continued limits at \(-R\). Canonical products, the original mark
and scalar, all repeated-root normals and all boundary derivatives
are retained. At odd \(N\), the simple node \(-2\) contributes its
full original value; that residue is already included in (TC3)
and must not be added again.

The jump has an explicit finite-level expression from the identity
\[
 D(2\pi iN-\alpha)=(-1)^N
 \left[D(\alpha)+8\cosh^2(\alpha/2)
       \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{(-1)^j}{(\alpha-i\pi(2j+1))^2}\right].
                                                               \tag{TC4}
\]
All apparent poles in this formula are removable. In particular,
for each fixed \(n,r\), the endpoint jump is \(O(a)\) at even levels
and \(O(a^3)\) at odd levels, uniformly for \(0\le a\le r\).
The extra vanishing at odd levels follows from the exact
\(G'_{n,N}(i\pi N)=0\). Since the cut denominator is
\(4\cosh^2(a/2)\) at even levels and \(-4\sinh^2(a/2)\) at odd
levels, one obtains
\[
 N^2\left|\frac{J_{n,N}(a)}{P_N(z(a))}z'(a)\right|
                      \le C_{n,r}a^2.                        \tag{TC5}
\]
Thus the portion \(0\le a\le r\le r_R\) of the actual cut term
has norm at most
\(C_{n,r}\int_0^r a^2\|f(z(a))K_N(z(a),w)\|\,da\).
The complete neighboring source remains in this estimate.

The prior slit-coupon theorem already gave a general residue formula
with cut terms. The additions here are the specific crossing jump,
whole-cover bounds and parity-uniform integrable endpoint density.
No contour at infinity or limiting-kernel composition is used.
The outer integral, the remaining cut interval and the spectator
still require a joint geometric estimate. No new knot-volume case
or finite-exception theorem is claimed.

## One even analytic formula represents every integer crossing power, 23 November

The [full crossing calculation](research_microscopic_original_crossing_multiplier.md)
now supplies the actual signed crossing, its true first normals and its
multiplication kernel near the repeated Casimir endpoint. It also gives
a common analytic representation for every fixed signed integer power.
This is local source data for the short-component problem; the original
closing after a general short component is still unestimated.

Use that note's entire even functions
\[
 c(\alpha)=\cosh(\alpha/2),\qquad
 D(\alpha)=1+\sum_{m\ge1}
                [\mathsf E_m(\alpha)-\mathsf H_m(\alpha)],\qquad
 P(\alpha)=4c(\alpha)^2 .
\]
The two terms in each summand have the same \(1/m\) term and opposite
\(1/m^2\) terms. Their difference is normally summable. With
\(w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N)\) and the original Cartan scalar
\(\kappa=e^{\pi i(N-1)^2/(2N)}\), the proved full-sum estimate is
\[
 \kappa^{\mp1}R_N^\pm(w_N(\alpha))
       =D(\alpha)\pm ic(\alpha)+O_A(N^{-1}).                  \tag{AC1}
\]
It includes every fixed holomorphic derivative on \(|\alpha|\le A\),
through both parities. The imaginary term comes from the bulk of the
finite sum; it is lost by retaining only its two endpoint limits.
The same note proves the actual crossed Frobenius kernel limit, not
just an equality of selected nodal values.

There is a nonzero inverse carry:
\[
 \frac{\kappa^{-1}R_N^+(w_N(\alpha))\,
              \kappa R_N^-(w_N(\alpha))-1}{P(\alpha)}
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{D(\alpha)^2+c(\alpha)^2-1}{4c(\alpha)^2}.                \tag{AC2}
\]
Both sides have removable values at the zeros of \(c\), and convergence
has the same error and derivative control. The limit is strictly
positive on the real axis away from zero. Thus the limiting functions
are inverse modulo \(P\), not under ordinary pointwise multiplication.

Here is an exact all-level consequence, rather than a further limit.
For an integer \(n\), including negative powers and zero, define
\[
 U_n(\alpha)=
 \begin{cases}
 D(\alpha)+in c(\alpha),&n\ \text{odd},\\
 1+in c(\alpha)D(\alpha),&n\ \text{even},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 G_{n,N}(\alpha)=
 e^{-in(\alpha^2+\pi^2)/(4\pi N)}U_n(\alpha).                 \tag{AC3}
\]
These functions are entire and even. To specify their physical meaning
without assuming a global change of spectral variable, let
\(\alpha_j=i\pi(2j+1)\), \(z_j=w_N(\alpha_j)\).
For an entire even function \(F\), define \(\rho_N(F)\) to be the unique
canonical polynomial whose double-node data are
\[
 \rho_N(F)(z_j)=F(\alpha_j),\qquad
 \rho_N(F)'(z_j)=\frac{F'(\alpha_j)}{w_N'(\alpha_j)}
 \quad(0\le j<\lfloor N/2\rfloor).
                                                               \tag{AC4}
\]
At odd \(N\), also prescribe
\(\rho_N(F)(-2)=F(i\pi N)\), with no derivative there.
Hermite interpolation defines this projection uniquely.
The product rule makes \(\rho_N\) an algebra homomorphism into
\(\mathbb C[z]/P_N\), and \(\rho_N(P)=0\).

The new crossing theorem gives, for every integer \(j\ge0\),
\[
 D(\alpha_j)=(-1)^j,\quad D'(\alpha_j)=0,\quad
 c(\alpha_j)=0,\quad c'(\alpha_j)=\tfrac i2(-1)^j.
\]
Consequently
\[
 U_n(\alpha_j)=(-1)^{nj},\qquad
 U_n'(\alpha_j)=-\tfrac n2(-1)^{nj}.
\]
The exponential in (AC3) has value \(q^{nj(j+1)}\) and logarithmic
derivative \(n(2j+1)/(2N)\) at that point, where \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\).
It follows that
\[
 G_{n,N}(\alpha_j)=\nu_j^n,\qquad
 G_{n,N}'(\alpha_j)
       =-\frac{n(N-1-2j)}{2N}\nu_j^n,\qquad
 \nu_j=(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)}.
\]
These are exactly the original signed-power data. The value is correct
at the odd simple node as well. Therefore, for every \(N\ge2\),
\[
 \boxed{\qquad \rho_N(G_{n,N})=\kappa^{-n}R^n.\qquad}          \tag{AC5}
\]
All original scalar factors and first normals are retained. Since
\(D^2-1\) is divisible by \(c^2\), direct multiplication also gives
\[
 U_nU_m\equiv U_{n+m}\pmod P,\qquad
 G_{n,N}G_{m,N}\equiv G_{n+m,N}\pmod P .                      \tag{AC6}
\]
This is a congruence of entire functions and hence a genuine equality
after the physical projection.

The representation has quantitative bounds uniform in the level:
\[
 \sup_{|\alpha|\le A}|G_{n,N}(\alpha)|
 \le C_A(1+|n|)\exp\!\left(\frac{|n|A^2}{4\pi N}\right).
                                                               \tag{AC7}
\]
The polynomial bound for \(U_n\) and the modulus of the exponential
prove this directly. Buffered Cauchy estimates give every fixed
derivative, with \(A\) replaced by \(A+1\). On the real axis the
exponential has modulus one and
\[
 |G_{n,N}|^2=
 \begin{cases}
 D^2+n^2c^2,&n\ \text{odd},\\
 1+n^2c^2D^2,&n\ \text{even}.
 \end{cases}
 \qquad |G_{n,N}(\alpha)|\ge1\quad(\alpha\in\mathbb R).         \tag{AC8}
\]
On this real parameter line the formula has no zero or singular case
at a fixed short integer power, including zero.

The older real-power and even-Ward constructions already give exact
Gaussian representatives on a selected logarithmic sheet. The gains
here are evenness at \(\alpha=0\), holomorphy through \(z=2\), a prefactor
linear in \(|n|\) with the Gaussian factor in (AC7) retained, and the
real-axis bound (AC8). This is not the first source-exact Gaussian
representation.

There are still essential restrictions. A bounded \(\alpha\)-disk is
only an \(O(N^{-2})\) spectral window. The functions need not descend
holomorphically through \(z=-2\), nor have the canonical polynomial's
periodicity on the cover. Equations (AC4)--(AC5) justify their full
finite source projection; they do not justify a global contour
replacement, removal of endpoint currents, or control after a genuine
turn. The original closing is not made positive by (AC8). No
short-component volume lower bound or finite-exception theorem follows.

## Newton iteration has relative accuracy from the exact forward state, 23 November

The fixed-degree objective gives a stronger Newton estimate when its
initial point is the exact open tangle state. This concerns the accuracy
of the finite minimum. The initial state must still be computed by the
original coherent recursion.

Keep the full normalized Newton packets, maps, budgets and closing of
[the convex source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md). Write
\[
 E(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|cx|^2,\qquad
 G(a)=0,\qquad k=ca=K_N/B,\qquad \sigma=1/16.
\]
The product of unit packet balls is \(\mathcal D\).
The known source theorem gives
\[
 I\le D_{\mathbb R}^2E\le3I\quad\hbox{on }\mathcal D,\qquad
 \|a_v\|\le\sigma,\quad\|c\|\le\sigma,\quad |k|\le1/256,
 \qquad |k|^2/\gamma\le e_*\le|k|^2,\quad\gamma=197/196.
\]
Its unique minimum \(x_*\) has every packet of norm at most \(33/256\).
All norms in the argument below are the global Euclidean norms;
derivatives are real derivatives.

On \(\mathcal D\), disjoint sibling pairs give, for arbitrary variations \(h,u\),
\[
 \|D^2G[h,u]\|\le\sigma\|h\|\|u\|,\qquad
 \|DG\|\le9/8 .
                                                               \tag{RN1}
\]
For the first bound, a product contributes
\(\Phi_v(h_L,u_R)+\Phi_v(u_L,h_R)\). Its norm is at most
\(\sigma(\|h_L\|\|u_R\|+\|u_L\|\|h_R\|)\). Apply
Cauchy--Schwarz on each sibling pair and then sum over the disjoint
pairs. Since \(G\) is quadratic, the third derivative of \(E\) has
exactly three terms of the form
\(2\operatorname{Re}\langle D^2G[h,u],DGv\rangle\).
The closing adds none. Thus
\[
 \|D^3E\|\le6\sigma(9/8)=27/64 .                              \tag{RN2}
\]
For \(x\in\mathcal D\), define the exact real Newton map
\[
 \mathcal N(x)=x-[D_{\mathbb R}^2E(x)]^{-1}\nabla_{\mathbb R}E(x),
\]
Taylor's formula along the segment to \(x_*\) and the inverse-Hessian
bound consequently give
\[
 \|\mathcal N(x)-x_*\|\le\alpha\|x-x_*\|^2,\qquad\alpha=27/128.
                                                               \tag{RN3}
\]
This estimate is obtained before assuming feasibility of the new point.

Now start at \(x_0=a\) and put \(x_{j+1}=\mathcal N(x_j)\).
Strong monotonicity and the exact zero residual at \(a\) give
\[
 \delta_0:=\|a-x_*\|\le\|\nabla E(a)\|
                =2\|c^*k\|\le |k|/8\le1/2048.
\]
The bounds \(33/256+\delta_0<1\) and
\(\alpha\delta_0<1\) prove by induction that all iterates are feasible
and their errors decrease. For \(k\ne0\), solving (RN3), with
\(q=27/262144\), proves
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|x_j-x_*\|\le\frac{|k|}{8}
           \left(\frac{27|k|}{1024}\right)^{2^j-1}
 \le\frac{|k|}{8}q^{2^j-1}.
 \quad}                                                       \tag{RN4}
\]
If \(k=0\), then \(a=x_*\) and all iterates equal \(a\).
For \(k\ne0\), the upper Hessian bound and source comparison give
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 0\le\frac{E(x_j)-e_*}{e_*}
       \le r_j:=\frac{3\gamma}{128}q^{\,2(2^j-1)} .
 \qquad}                                                      \tag{RN5}
\]
In particular \(E(x_j)/(1+r_j)\le e_*\le E(x_j)\).
All constants are independent of the level, tree size and magnitude
of the nonzero source, with the original budgets retained.

Relative accuracy from the exact forward state was already proved
for the backward/forward contraction, equation (25) of
[the iteration note](research_conway_backward_forward_minimum_iteration.md).
The addition here is the doubly exponential relative error bound for
repeated real Newton steps, without a tree-size factor. At \(a\),
the internal residual-curvature part of the Hessian vanishes, so the
first step is exactly the previously proved rank-one Gauss--Newton
correction. Subsequent steps use the full real Hessian.

These are exact-arithmetic statements. They neither justify replacing
\(a\) by an absolute-accuracy approximation nor give a finite-precision
cost independent of \(|k|\). Most importantly, the coherent forward
state already contains the unknown closing. No geometric trial state,
new hyperbolic-volume rate or finite-exception case is established.

## A positive Mellin integral retains the original closing, 23 November

The [Mellin realization](research_positive_mellin_realization_of_original_gluing.md)
gives an exact regularized integral for the original bilinear gluing
and a positive approximation to its squared scalar closing. The
approximation has an error bound uniform in the quantum level and
includes zero sources. It is not a geometric evaluation of that closing.

Put \(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), and
\[
 P_N(x)=2T_N(x/2)+2,\qquad d\nu_N(x)=\frac{dx}{P_N(x)}
 \quad(x>2).
\]
This measure is positive. For every ordinary polynomial \(h\), of
arbitrary degree, polynomial division gives the meromorphic continuation
needed for the exact identity
\[
 \phi_N(h)=\eta N^2\operatorname*{Res}_{s=0}
                 \int_2^\infty x^{-s}h(x)\,d\nu_N(x).
                                                               \tag{PM1}
\]
Multiples of \(P_N\) have zero residue. Thus (PM1) retains the original
quotient multiplication and repeated-root normals in every finite
Conway contraction. Its residue pairing is bilinear and indefinite.

Write the original scalar, including its prescribed external factors
and closing turn, as \(K_N=\phi_N(f_N)\), where \(f_N\) is canonical,
\(\deg f_N<N\). Set \(M_N=\max_{[-2,2]}|f_N|\) and
\(C_N=3+\tfrac12\log N\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the positive integral
\[
 \mathcal A_{N,\varepsilon}
 =N^4\varepsilon\int_2^\infty
       (x/2)^{-\varepsilon}x^{-(N-1)}|f_N(x)|^2\,d\nu_N(x)
\]
satisfies
\[
 0\le\mathcal A_{N,\varepsilon}\le N^4M_N^2,\qquad
 |\mathcal A_{N,\varepsilon}-|K_N|^2|
                 \le\varepsilon N^4M_N^2C_N.                  \tag{PM2}
\]
For any known local-tensor budget \(B_N\ge\max(1,M_N)\), choosing
\(\varepsilon_N=(N^6B_N^2C_N)^{-1}\) makes the error at most \(N^{-2}\).
Consequently, for each \(V>0\), the original volume limit is equivalent
to \((\pi/N)\log\mathcal A_{N,\varepsilon_N}\to V\).
The finite-parameter integral is an approximation to the invariant;
it is not asserted to be invariant under a change of presentation.

There is an important limitation of this universal parameter choice.
Let \(\mathcal A_N^{\le R}\) restrict the integral to \(2\le x\le R\).
The proof of (PM2) writes its integrand using
\[
 w=\frac{x+\sqrt{x^2-4}}2,\qquad
 H(z)=z^D f_N(z+z^{-1}),\qquad
 R_N(x)=\frac{(1+w^{-2})^{-(N-2)}}{(1+w^{-N})^2},
\]
with \(|H|\le M_N\) on the unit disk and \(0<R_N\le1\).
Therefore, for every \(R\ge2\),
\[
 0\le\mathcal A_N^{\le R}\le\frac{\log(R/2)}{N^2C_N}.          \tag{PM3}
\]
For fixed \(R>2\), this sharpens by the factor
\((1+w(R)^{-2})^{-(N-2)}\), since \(w(x)\le w(R)\) on the interval.
If the total integral has positive rate \(V/\pi\), a window carrying
a fixed positive fraction must have
\(\log R_N\ge\exp(VN/\pi+o(N))\). Thus this regularization does not
supply a finite geometric window or a Casson--Rivin lower bound.
No filling case or finite-exception theorem is established by (PM1)--(PM3).

## The full endpoint kernel and its original Fourier gluing, 23 November

The [two-ended kernel theorem](research_two_ended_wilson_source_kernel.md)
now treats both free colors of the original ordinary kernel, including
every fixed holomorphic derivative. Its proof retains both ends of the
finite Newton sum. In particular it retains the complementary term
which vanishes at a fixed physical value but survives in its first
normal. This is a local source theorem, not a filled-knot asymptotic.

For \(N\ge2\), use that note's full basis \(e_i\), \(0\le i<N\), and put
\[
 d=N-1,\qquad \eta=(-1)^d,\qquad
 w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N),\qquad P(\alpha)=4\cosh^2(\alpha/2).
\]
In the finite recurrences below, \(c_i=2\cos((2i+1)\pi/N)\) and
\(s_m=2\sin(m\pi/N)\).
Its two entire coefficient families are
\[
 E_k(\alpha)=
 \frac{(\tfrac12+i\alpha/(2\pi))_k
       (\tfrac12-i\alpha/(2\pi))_k}{(k!)^2},\qquad
 H_m(\alpha)=\frac{\cosh^2(\alpha/2)}{\pi^2m^2E_m(\alpha)}.
\]
The apparent poles of \(H_m\) are removable. The original kernel satisfies
\[
 K_N(w_N(\alpha),w_N(\beta))
 =\mathcal K(\alpha,\beta)+O_A(N^{-1}),\qquad
 \mathcal K=\sum_{k\ge0}E_k(\alpha)E_k(\beta)
                  +\sum_{m\ge1}H_m(\alpha)H_m(\beta),
                                                               \tag{FK1}
\]
uniformly on every fixed complex bidisk and with every fixed mixed
derivative. Both series converge normally there. At a fixed physical
index \(j\), setting \(\beta=i\pi(2j+1)\) gives the normalized Wilson
polynomial. Differentiation retains the second series and gives the
true physical normal. The earlier \(O(N^{-1/2})\) endpoint-normal error
therefore improves to \(O(N^{-1})\).

There is also a simple formula for the original bilinear gluing.
Define its reverse kernel
\[
 B_N(z,w)=\sum_{i=0}^{d}e_i(z)e_{d-i}(w),\qquad
 P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2.
\]
The original Frobenius functional obeys
\(\phi_N(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=d}\). Consequently, for every
canonical polynomial \(f\) of degree less than \(N\),
\[
 \phi_{N,z}\bigl(B_N(z,w)f(z)\bigr)=f(w).
                                                               \tag{FK2}
\]
This is the unchanged bilinear source pairing, with every first normal.
The finite divided-difference identity, already present in the Ward
calculation, is
\[
 B_N(z,w)=\frac{\eta}{N^2}
                         \frac{P_N(z)-P_N(w)}{z-w}.
                                                               \tag{FK3}
\]
It can also be checked directly: multiply the sum by \(z-w\), use
\(ze_i=c_i e_i-s_{i+1}^2e_{i+1}\) below the top degree, and use
\((z-c_d)e_d=\eta P_N(z)/N^2\) at the top. Since
\(c_i=c_{d-i}\) and \(s_{N-i}=s_i\), all interior terms cancel.

For the scaled variables set \(u=(\alpha+\beta)/2\) and
\(v=(\alpha-\beta)/2\). Equation (FK3) gives the exact entire identity
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \eta B_N(w_N(\alpha),w_N(\beta))
 =\frac{\sinh u}{N\sinh(u/N)}
                   \frac{\sinh v}{N\sinh(v/N)} .
 \quad}                                                       \tag{FK4}
\]
Ratios are interpreted by their removable values. In particular
\[
 \eta B_N(w_N(\alpha),w_N(\beta))
 =\mathcal B(\alpha,\beta)+O_A(N^{-2}),\qquad
 \mathcal B=
 \frac{P(\alpha)-P(\beta)}{\alpha^2-\beta^2}
 =\operatorname{sinhc}u\,\operatorname{sinhc}v .
                                                               \tag{FK5}
\]
This estimate includes every fixed mixed holomorphic derivative:
on a fixed larger bidisk the product
\(\operatorname{sinhc}(u/N)\operatorname{sinhc}(v/N)\)
is a unit \(1+O_A(N^{-2})\), and Cauchy's formula applies.
Here \(\operatorname{sinhc}z=\sinh z/z\). The diagonal is
\(\mathcal B(\alpha,\alpha)=\operatorname{sinhc}\alpha\).

The same kernel has a finite Fourier description. Expanding each
factor in (FK4) as a finite geometric sum gives
\[
 \eta B_N(w_N(\alpha),w_N(\beta))
 =\frac1{N^2}\sum_{a,b=0}^{N-1}
  \exp\left\{\frac{N-1-a-b}{N}\alpha+\frac{b-a}{N}\beta\right\}.
                                                               \tag{FK6}
\]
Its limit is
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \mathcal B(\alpha,\beta)
   =\frac12\int_{|s|+|t|\le1}e^{s\alpha+t\beta}\,ds\,dt .
 \qquad}                                                      \tag{FK7}
\]
To verify the normalization, integrate first over the unit square
\(-1/2\le p,q\le1/2\), and set \(s=p+q,\ t=p-q\).
Then \(dp\,dq=\tfrac12\,ds\,dt\); the resulting diamond has area two.
For purely imaginary \(\alpha,\beta\), (FK6)--(FK7) are Fourier
averages. The entire identities retain their derivatives as well.

Finally, the two-ended coefficient bounds in (FK1) show directly that
\[
 \mathcal B(\alpha,\beta)
 =\sum_{k\ge0}\bigl\{
       E_k(\alpha)H_{k+1}(\beta)+H_{k+1}(\alpha)E_k(\beta)\bigr\}.
                                                               \tag{FK8}
\]
Indeed the two ends of the reverse finite sum give precisely these
terms; their products have summable \(O_A(k^{-2})\) bounds. In the
abstract two-sequence space, \(\mathcal K\) pairs like components,
whereas \(\mathcal B\) swaps the components. The factor \(\eta\)
in (FK4)--(FK6) records the original sign convention.
Thus positivity of the norm kernel does not replace the bilinear
gluing by a positive norm.

These statements give a local model with the actual gluing and normal
data. They assert neither injectivity of an infinite evaluation frame
nor convergence of arbitrary tangle coefficient vectors: their mass
may move to indices of order \(N\). Uniform composition through every
fixed short component, control of its original closing, and the
hyperbolic-volume lower bound still require proof. The finite-exception
theorem remains open.

## A microscopic contour height leaves a nonzero cosine current, 23 November

This sharpness calculation concerns the specified angular representative
in the exact trace rectangle. It rules out cancelling that rectangle's
vertical term merely by choosing physical integer colors and a height
of order \(N^{-1}\). It gives no new knot-volume bound.

Fix \(n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\), \(c>0\), \(N\ge3\), and an
integer \(0\le j\le N\). Put
\[
 A=N-j,\quad \theta=A/N,\quad \eta=(-1)^{N-1},\qquad
 C_{N,n}=\exp\{\pi i n(N-1)^2/(4N)\}.
\]
Let \(V_{N,j}(y)\) mean the full second line of
[the exact trace rectangle](research_exact_complete_trace_contour.md),
equation (8), with angular exterior \(f(t)=\cos(At)\), including the
prefactor \(\eta N^2C_{N,n}/\pi\). The exact paired density is already
equation (12) of
[the full-period current calculation](research_full_period_current_charge_convolution.md).
It gives
\[
 V_{N,j}(y)=
 \eta(-1)^AC_{N,n}e^{inN\pi/4}\frac{iN^2}{2\pi}
 \int_0^y
 \frac{\sinh v\,\sinh(nNv/2)\cosh(Av)}
      {\cosh^2(Nv/2)}e^{-inNv^2/(4\pi)}\,dv .
                                                               \tag{MC1}
\]
Indeed \(\sin(\pi+iv)=-i\sinh v\),
\(\cos(A(\pi+iv))=(-1)^A\cosh(Av)\), and the quadratic twist
contributes \(e^{inN\pi/4}e^{-nNv/2}e^{-inNv^2/(4\pi)}\).
Pairing \(v\) and \(-v\) proves (MC1), retaining the twist.

Define
\[
 M_{n,c}(\theta)=\int_0^c
  \frac{s\,|\sinh(ns/2)|\cosh(\theta s)}{\cosh^2(s/2)}\,ds.
                                                               \tag{MC2}
\]
For every \(0\le\theta\le1\),
\[
 0<M_{n,c}(0)\le M_{n,c}(\theta)
                            \le\cosh(c)M_{n,c}(0).              \tag{MC3}
\]
Set \(\alpha_N=|n|c^2/(4\pi N)\) and
\(h_N=\sinh(c/N)/(c/N)\). The following finite-level bounds hold
whenever \(\alpha_N\le\pi\):
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \cos(\alpha_N/2)M_{n,c}(\theta)
 \le 2\pi|V_{N,j}(c/N)|
 \le h_NM_{n,c}(\theta).
 \quad}                                                       \tag{MC4}
\]
To prove them, substitute \(s=Nv\) in (MC1), and remove its unit
outer factors and the constant sign of \(\sinh(ns/2)\).
The remaining integral has positive amplitude
\[
 \frac{N\sinh(s/N)|\sinh(ns/2)|\cosh(\theta s)}
      {\cosh^2(s/2)}
\]
and phase \(e^{-ins^2/(4\pi N)}\). Its arguments lie in an interval
of width \(\alpha_N\). Rotate the midpoint to argument zero; the
real part is at least \(\cos(\alpha_N/2)\) times the positive
amplitude integral. Finally use
\(s\le N\sinh(s/N)\le h_Ns\) on \(0\le s\le c\).
This proves both bounds without an asymptotic interchange.

Since \(h_N=1+O_c(N^{-2})\) and
\(\cos(\alpha_N/2)=1+O_{n,c}(N^{-2})\), (MC3)--(MC4) imply
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 |V_{N,j}(c/N)|
     =\frac{M_{n,c}((N-j)/N)}{2\pi}+O_{n,c}(N^{-2}),
 \qquad}                                                      \tag{MC5}
\]
uniformly over every physical integer color, at both parities.
Thus the full vertical term stays bounded above and bounded
away from zero for all sufficiently large levels. For \(n=0\) it
instead vanishes exactly.

The separate vertical term depends on the chosen representative.
For example \(j=0\) represents the quotient class \(\eta\cdot1\),
whereas \(j=N\) represents \(1\); their different vertical profiles
are compensated by the horizontal terms. Therefore (MC5) is not an
invariant sector of the knot source. An order-one current can be
exponentially smaller than a geometric contribution, and the rest
of a closed source can cancel it. No finite-exception case follows.
The existing microscopic upper bound and paired density are retained;
the added assertion is their explicit uniform nonzero calibration.

## Newton's method has a uniform quadratic error bound, 23 November

Use the full normalized Newton packets and unchanged original closing of
[the convex source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md). The tree
is literal and uncompressed, with distinct variables at distinct child
occurrences. Every local constant, linear map, bilinear map and closing
row has norm at most \(\sigma=1/16\). Write
\[
 r_v=\Phi_v((x_c)_c)-x_v,\qquad
 E(x)=\sum_v\|r_v\|^2+|Lx_{v_0}|^2,\qquad
 \mathcal D=\prod_v\{\|x_v\|\le1\}.
\]
The source comparison and all normalization budgets are unchanged:
\[
 B_{\rm tot}^2e_*\le |K_N|^2
       \le(197/196)B_{\rm tot}^2e_*,
 \qquad e_*=\min E.
\]
The complete source proof gives \(I\le D_{\mathbb R}^2E\le3I\) on
\(\mathcal D\). The
[global critical-point proof](research_conway_global_critical_point_localization.md)
gives the unique minimum \(x_*\in\sigma\mathcal D\).

Define the maximum packet norm and the real half-gradient iteration by
\[
 \|x\|_\infty=\max_v\|x_v\|,\qquad
 \mathscr F(x)=x-\tfrac12\nabla_{\mathbb R}E(x).
\]
All derivatives below are real, including derivatives of adjoints.
The following estimates are independent of \(N\) and of the tree size:
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|D\mathscr F(x)\|_{\infty\to\infty}\le a:=67/256,\qquad
 \|D^2\mathscr F(x)\|_{\infty,\infty\to\infty}
                                  \le b:=35/128
 \quad(x\in\mathcal D).
 \quad}                                                     \tag{NQ1}
\]
Indeed, at a nontop vertex with proper parent \(p\),
\(\mathscr F_v=\Phi_v-(D_v\Phi_p)^*r_p\).
At the top it is \(\Phi_{v_0}-L^*Lx_{v_0}\).
An own binary gate has first and second derivative bounds
\(2\sigma,2\sigma\) in this norm; an own unary gate has bounds
\(\sigma,0\), and an own leaf has zero derivatives.
A unary parent contributes \(U^*x_p-U^*Ux_v\), whose bounds are
\(\sigma+\sigma^2,0\). For a binary parent, with sibling \(y\), put
\(B_yh=B(h,y)\). Its contribution is
\(B_y^*x_p-B_y^*B(x_v,y)\).
The quadratic term has bounds \(2\sigma,2\sigma\); differentiating the
three real multilinear slots of the cubic term gives
\(3\sigma^2,6\sigma^2\). There is at most one parent. The closing
adds only \(\sigma^2\) to the first bound. Thus the worst cases are
\(4\sigma+3\sigma^2=67/256\) and
\(4\sigma+6\sigma^2=35/128\), proving (NQ1).

Consider exact, undamped Newton steps for the real stationary equations:
\[
 \mathcal N(x)=x-[D_{\mathbb R}^2E(x)]^{-1}
                                      \nabla_{\mathbb R}E(x).
\]
The Neumann series gives
\(\|(I-D\mathscr F(x))^{-1}\|_{\infty\to\infty}
\le1/(1-a)=256/189\).
Taylor's formula on the segment between \(x\) and \(x_*\), before
assuming feasibility of the new point, therefore gives
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \|\mathcal N(x)-x_*\|_\infty
       \le\frac{b}{2(1-a)}\|x-x_*\|_\infty^2
       =\frac5{27}\|x-x_*\|_\infty^2 .
 \qquad}                                                    \tag{NQ2}
\]
For \(x\in\mathcal D\), the old error is at most \(17/16\).
Consequently
\[
 \|\mathcal N(x)\|_\infty
 \le\frac1{16}+\frac5{27}\left(\frac{17}{16}\right)^2
 =\frac{1877}{6912}<1.
\]
Every Newton iterate from any \(x_0\in\mathcal D\) is thus well defined
and feasible. Iterating (NQ2), and using the upper real Hessian bound
for the energy estimate, proves
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|x_j-x_*\|_\infty
 \le\frac{27}{5}\left(\frac{85}{432}\right)^{2^j},
 \qquad
 0\le E(x_j)-e_*
 \le\frac{2187}{50}s
            \left(\frac{85}{432}\right)^{2^{j+1}},
 \quad}                                                     \tag{NQ3}
\]
where \(s\) is the number of proper packets. Here
\(\|x\|^2\le s\|x\|_\infty^2\). No energy-monotonicity claim is used.
The last upper bound also gives an explicit interval for \(e_*\):
subtract it from \(E(x_j)\) and clip the lower endpoint at zero.

The exact Newton system can be solved along the same tree. As already
recorded in
[the local gluing formulation](research_conway_gate_local_semidefinite_gluing.md),
each Hessian term involves one output and at most two child packets.
Adjacent such groups share one whole packet. Schur elimination from
leaves to root, followed by backsubstitution, therefore uses groups of
at most three packets and matrix messages on single-packet boundaries.
The sibling coupling must be retained. These are real \(2N\)-coordinate
packet blocks, not a removal of repeated-root derivatives.
Every elimination pivot is positive: for any Schur complement of the
full Hessian \(H\), the bounds \(I\le H\le3I\) imply
\[
 y^{\mathsf T}Sy=\min_z(z,y)^{\mathsf T}H(z,y),\qquad
                         I\le S\le3I.
\]
The lower bound drops \(\|z\|^2\), and the upper bound tests \(z=0\).
This concerns pivots of the global system; individual unshifted gate
Hessians and their separate messages need not be positive.
There are linearly many local block operations in the number of
vertices. No bound independent of packet dimension or arithmetic
precision is claimed.

For each fixed \(A>0\), (NQ3) attains absolute packet error
\(e^{-AN}\) in \(O(\log N)\) exact Newton steps. The earlier clipped
path sweep supplies a feasible start from any finite field.
This strengthens the minimization algorithm, not its geometric
evaluation. An exponentially small absolute error need not be small
relative to a still smaller or zero minimum. In particular no new
geometric lower bound, filling case or finite-exception theorem follows.
The polynomial degree is at most four; the number of real variables remains
\(2Ns\).

## The actual second meridian coupon has bounded contact curvature, 23 November

Keep the fixed balanced-source chart and original path sum of
[the derivative-coupon calculation](research_actual_microscopic_derivative_coupons.md):
\[
 f_N(\zeta)=F_N(e^{\zeta/N})
      =\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_N}W_\omega(\zeta),\qquad
 f_N(0)=K_N.
\]
Here \(N\ge2\), \(n=N-1\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), the braid has \(m\)
strands and \(\ell\) signed crossings, and the original cut, pivots,
phases and zero-framing factors are unchanged. At a positive crossing
put \(H_v=\{i_v-k_v+1,\ldots,i_v\}\); at a negative crossing use
\(H_v=\{j_v-k_v+1,\ldots,j_v\}\). Empty intervals contribute zero.
Every factor label lies in \(1,\ldots,N-1\); every Gaussian factorial
index is below \(N\). Thus all allowed path weights are nonzero at
completeness. Their logarithmic derivatives
\[
 L_\omega=\partial_\zeta\log W_\omega(0),\qquad
 C_\omega=\partial_\zeta^2\log W_\omega(0)
\]
are independent of logarithm choices. With crossing sign
\(\epsilon_v=\pm1\), direct differentiation gives
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 L_\omega=
 \frac{\sum_v\epsilon_v(n-i_v-j_v)-n(m-1)}{2N}
 +\frac{i}{2N}\sum_v\sum_{h\in H_v}\cot\frac{\pi h}{N},
 \qquad
 C_\omega=\frac1{4N^2}\sum_v\sum_{h\in H_v}
                              \csc^2\frac{\pi h}{N}.
 \quad}                                                    \tag{CC1}
\]
Indeed, for \(z=Q^{-h}\),
\[
 -\frac z{1-z}=\frac12+\frac i2\cot\frac{\pi h}{N},
 \qquad
 -\frac z{(1-z)^2}=\frac1{4\sin^2(\pi h/N)}.
\]
Each path factor is \(1-e^{\zeta/N}Q^{-h}\). Its first logarithmic
derivative adds \(1/(2N)\) to the real part; summing its \(k_v\)
factors cancels the \(-k_v/(2N)\) in either crossing monomial.
The \(m-1\) pivots contribute \(-n(m-1)/(2N)\), with zero second
logarithmic derivative. This proves (CC1) for both crossing signs.

Put \(\theta_N=(N^2-1)/(12N^2)\). There is the uniform bound
\[
                         0\le C_\omega\le\ell\theta_N\le\ell/12.
 \tag{CC2}
\]
To prove it, differentiate the finite sine product twice
logarithmically:
\[
 N^2\csc^2(Nx)=\sum_{h=0}^{N-1}\csc^2(x+h\pi/N).
\]
Subtract its \(h=0\) term and use
\(\csc^2x=x^{-2}+1/3+O(x^2)\). This gives
\(\sum_{h=1}^{N-1}\csc^2(\pi h/N)=(N^2-1)/3\).
Each crossing uses only a subset of that sum, proving (CC2),
including \(N=2\).

Actual Weyl symmetry and differentiation of the finite sum imply
\[
 \sum_\omega W_\omega(0)L_\omega=0,\qquad
 f_N''(0)=\sum_\omega W_\omega(0)(L_\omega^2+C_\omega).
\]
Use the canonical decomposition \(F_N=S_NR_N+P_N\), with
\(S_N(Y)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}Y^j\) and \(P_N\) the ordinary-color
interpolation polynomial of degree at most \(N-2\). Set
\(W_N(\zeta)=e^{(N-1)\zeta/(2N)}R_N(e^{\zeta/N})\) and
\(p_N(\zeta)=P_N(e^{\zeta/N})\). Then \(f_N=NH_NW_N+p_N\), where
\(H_N(\zeta)=\sinh(\zeta/2)/(N\sinh(\zeta/(2N)))\), and
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 NW_N''(0)=
 \sum_\omega W_\omega(0)(L_\omega^2+C_\omega-\theta_N)
       +\theta_Np_N(0)-p_N''(0).
 \quad}                                                    \tag{CC3}
\]
The ordinary-color coefficient bound gives
\(\lvert\theta_Np_N(0)-p_N''(0)\rvert\le3ND_N\), with
\(D_N=\sin(\pi/N)^{1-m}\le(N/2)^{m-1}\).
No division by \(K_N\) occurs.

The contact curvature is bounded in this specified chart. The remaining
second moment retains the original complex weights and the bilinear
square \(L_\omega^2\). It is not a positive variance, and no bound
by \(\operatorname{poly}(N)|K_N|+\operatorname{poly}(N)\) follows
from (CC2). The balanced second-jet estimate and finite-exception
theorem remain open.

## Habiro Taylor uniqueness does not settle the normalization, 23 November

This is a negative audit of an arithmetic shortcut, not a new geometric
source estimate. In the classical integral ring
\[
 \mathcal H_{\mathbb Z}
   =\varprojlim_m\mathbb Z[q]/((q;q)_m),\qquad
 (q;q)_m=\prod_{j=1}^m(1-q^j),
\]
the assertion
\(\mathcal H_{\mathbb Z}^{\times}=\{\pm q^k:k\in\mathbb Z\}\)
is explicitly Conjecture 7.2 in
[Habiro's original paper, §7.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0209324v1).
No later resolution has been verified here. A unit evaluates to a
nonzero algebraic-integer unit at every root, and to \(\pm1\) at \(1\);
these facts alone supply no archimedean rate proved in this audit.

There is a fixed-element distinction from the earlier
[level-dependent cyclotomic-unit example](research_normalized_cyclotomic_unit_small_observation.md).
Given any positive numbers \(H_N\), \(N\ge2\), there is one fixed
\(f\in\mathcal H_{\mathbb Z}\) satisfying
\[
 f(1)=1,\qquad
 |f(\zeta_N)|\ge H_N\quad(N\ge2),\qquad
 \zeta_N=e^{2\pi i/N}.
 \tag{HU1}
\]
Here \(\zeta_N\) has order \(N\), distinct from the physical convention
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\) elsewhere. To prove this, set \(a_0=1\).
Having chosen \(a_0,\ldots,a_{N-2}\), write
\[
 S_N=\sum_{n=0}^{N-2}a_n(\zeta_N;\zeta_N)_n
\]
and choose an integer \(a_{N-1}\ge1\) with
\(Na_{N-1}\ge H_N+|S_N|\). Define
\[
                         f(q)=\sum_{n\ge0}a_n(q;q)_n.
 \tag{HU2}
\]
The partial sums define a compatible inverse-limit element, since
all terms with \(n\ge m\) vanish modulo \(((q;q)_m)\).
At \(\zeta_N\), terms with \(n\ge N\) vanish and
\[
 (\zeta_N;\zeta_N)_{N-1}
       =\prod_{j=1}^{N-1}(1-\zeta_N^j)=N.
\]
The product identity is \((z^N-1)/(z-1)\) evaluated at \(z=1\).
Thus \(f(\zeta_N)=S_N+Na_{N-1}\), and the reverse triangle
inequality proves (HU1). Later choices preserve all earlier root
values. Also \(f(1)=1\); its formal Taylor series exists because
\((q;q)_n\) is divisible by \((q-1)^n\).

For example \(H_N=e^{N^2}\) excludes an archimedean growth bound
deduced solely from membership and injective formal Taylor expansion.
This construction is explicitly not a unit:
\[
                         f(-1)=1+2a_1\ge3,
\]
whereas evaluation at \(-1\) sends a Habiro unit to a unit of
\(\mathbb Z\). It therefore neither refutes the unit conjecture nor
settles the growth or decay of a fixed Habiro unit.

For the geometric torsor, the actual comparison ratio has not been
shown to be a unit of this classical ring. Both that identification
and the required normalization remain to be proved. A proved full
Taylor germ \(\pm q^k\) would determine an actual classical element
by Taylor injectivity; knowing its value at \(1\) does not.
An evaluation-compatible holomorphic germ near \(1\) would separately
give \(u(\zeta_N)=u(1)+O(N^{-1})\). No such analytic realization
follows from formal injectivity alone. This audit makes no statement
about a geometric coefficient of the actual knot source.

## The quartic has one real stationary point and a global initializer, 23 November

The [global path-scaling theorem](research_conway_global_critical_point_localization.md)
gives a further simplification of the full finite-level minimization.
Its only real stationary point in the entire packet space is the
minimum already constructed inside the unit balls. Moreover, one
explicit sweep moves any trial field into the radius-\(1/16\) packet
balls without increasing the energy. This holds at every \(N\ge2\)
and retains arbitrary prescribed short fillings as full leaf packets.

Keep the literal tree, distinct variables for each leaf occurrence,
the chosen metric and its budgets, and the original normalized closing
row \(L\). Put \(\sigma=1/16\) and
\[
 G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_c)_c)-x_v,\qquad
 E(x)=\sum_v\|G_v(x)\|^2+|Lx_{\mathrm{top}}|^2.
\]
Here \(\Phi_\ell=a_\ell\) at a prescribed leaf; internal maps are
homogeneous linear turns or bilinear products. Every normalized leaf
and map has norm at most \(\sigma\).

For a leaf \(\ell\), scale all trial packets on its ancestor path
\(P_\ell\), including the top packet, by one real scalar \(t\).
Each internal residual on this path scales by \(t\), as does the
closing. Only the leaf residual is \(a_\ell-tx_\ell\).
Consequently the line problem is the quadratic
\[
 E_\ell(t)=C_\ell-2b_\ell t+A_\ell t^2,\qquad
 b_\ell=\operatorname{Re}\langle a_\ell,x_\ell\rangle,\qquad
 A_\ell=\|x_\ell\|^2+
    \sum_{v\in P_\ell\setminus\{\ell\}}\|G_v(x)\|^2+
    |Lx_{\mathrm{top}}|^2.
\]
Minimize it on \([0,1]\): use
\(t=\min\{1,\max\{0,b_\ell/A_\ell\}\}\) if \(A_\ell>0\),
and \(t=1\) otherwise. The updated leaf has norm at most
\(\sigma\), and each updated internal residual has norm at most
\(\sigma/2\). Later paths preserve these bounds or establish them
again. After every leaf has been processed once, upward induction
places every packet in \(\sigma\mathcal D\), where \(\mathcal D\)
is the product of unit balls. All scaling factors lie in \([0,1]\).
The sweep is continuous, never enlarges a packet, and never increases
the energy. It changes trial fields, not source tensors or the cap.

The differentiated path identity also shows directly that every real
stationary point lies in \(\sigma\mathcal D\). Existing strict
convexity on \(\mathcal D\) therefore excludes any other ambient real
stationary point. More generally, with
\(g=\|\nabla E(x)\|\) and \(h=\|x\|\), the proof gives
\[
 gh\le899/512\ \Longrightarrow\ x\in\mathcal D,\qquad
 gh\le7/16\ \Longrightarrow\ x\in\tfrac12\mathcal D.
\]
These are bounds on \(gh\), not on the gradient alone.

After the sweep, the existing half-gradient iteration contracts.
For \(s\) proper vertices its absolute errors satisfy
\[
 \|x^j-x_*\|\le2\sigma\sqrt{s}\,2^{-j},\qquad
 0\le E(x^j)-E(x_*)\le6\sigma^2s\,4^{-j}.
\]
This gives a global initialization, not convergence of the unmodified
fixed step from arbitrary fields. The literal tree is essential:
identified repeated variables and compressed affine gates are outside
the path argument.

The original source comparison is unchanged:
\[
 B^2E(x_*)\le |K_N|^2\le(197/196)B^2E(x_*).
\]
The new theorem controls the optimization landscape and its
initialization. It does not determine the minimum's exponential rate,
give source-relative accuracy at that rate, or select a geometric
thimble of the original complex phase. Both the required filled-volume
rate and the finite-exception theorem remain open.

## A sharp polynomial resolvent bound on the tilted contour, 23 November

The original Newton-coordinate Casimir has a uniform quadratic
resolvent bound outside a specific disk. This gives quantitative
control on the whole tilted Gaussian line, including its point above
the spectral endpoint. The metric here is the Newton coefficient
metric, not the uniform physical metric of the quartic minimization.
No estimate for the full contracted source follows from this change.

Use the complete \(N\)-dimensional operator of the
[original resolvent theorem](research_original_casimir_resolvent_rate.md).
For \(N\ge2\), put \(d=N-1\), \(\theta=\pi/N\), and
\[
 (C_Nv)_j=c_jv_j-s_j^2v_{j-1},\qquad
 c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta),\quad s_j=2\sin(j\theta),
 \qquad 0\le j\le d,\quad v_{-1}=0 .
\]
The norm below is the Euclidean operator norm in these coordinates.
All repeated-root directions are retained. Then
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \frac{N^2}{4}\le\|(2I-C_N)^{-1}\|_2
 \le\sup_{|z+2|\ge4}\|(zI-C_N)^{-1}\|_2
 \le\frac{N^4}{4}\sin^2\frac{\pi}{2N}
 \le\frac{\pi^2N^2}{16}.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{QR1}
\]
In particular the power \(N^2\) is necessary for a bound on this region.

Here is a finite proof, uniform in \(z\) and \(N\). Define positive
numbers, with empty products equal to one,
\[
 H_j=\frac{\prod_{r=0}^j2\sin((r+\tfrac12)\theta)}
                 {\prod_{r=1}^j2\sin(r\theta)},\qquad
 R_i=\frac{H_i}{2\sin((i+\tfrac12)\theta)} .
\]
The two full sine products are
\(\prod_{r=1}^{N-1}2\sin(r\theta)=N\) and
\(\prod_{r=0}^{N-1}2\sin((r+\tfrac12)\theta)=2\).
They follow by taking absolute values in the factorizations of
\((X^N-1)/(X-1)\) at \(X=1\), and of \(X^N+1\) at \(X=1\),
respectively. Reflecting the remaining factors by
\(r\mapsto N-r\), or \(r+\tfrac12\mapsto N-r-\tfrac12\), gives
\[
                         H_jR_{d-j}=2/N .                    \tag{QR2}
\]
Triangular solution of the original operator, rather than spectral
diagonalization, gives
\[
 |[(2I-C_N)^{-1}]_{ji}|
 =\frac{\prod_{r=i+1}^j[2\sin(r\theta)]^2}
         {\prod_{r=i}^j[2\sin((r+\tfrac12)\theta)]^2}
 =\frac{R_i^2}{H_j^2}
 =\frac{N^2}{4}R_i^2R_{d-j}^2,\qquad j\ge i .                 \tag{QR3}
\]
Entries with \(j<i\) are zero.

For \(1\le r\le N-1\), the identity
\[
 \sin^2(r\theta)
 -\sin((r-\tfrac12)\theta)\sin((r+\tfrac12)\theta)
                         =\sin^2(\theta/2)
\]
has a positive right side. Multiplication of the resulting inequalities
for \(1\le r\le i\) telescopes to
\[
 R_i^2
 =\prod_{r=1}^i\frac{\sin^2((r-\tfrac12)\theta)}
                            {\sin^2(r\theta)}
 \le\frac{\sin(\theta/2)}{\sin((i+\tfrac12)\theta)} .
\]
The inequality also holds for \(i=0\), where both sides are one.
The sine multiplication formula, differentiated twice logarithmically
at \(x=\pi/(2N)\), gives
\[
 \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\csc^2((i+\tfrac12)\theta)=N^2.
\]
For completeness, the formula being differentiated is
\(\prod_{i=0}^{N-1}\sin(x+i\pi/N)=2^{1-N}\sin(Nx)\).
It follows from the same root factorization and holds on a neighborhood
of this \(x\), where all factors are positive. Consequently
\[
 \sum_{i=0}^{d}R_i^4
 \le N^2\sin^2(\theta/2)\le\pi^2/4 .                           \tag{QR4}
\]
Equation (QR3) is entrywise bounded by the full rank-one positive
matrix with entries \((N^2/4)R_i^2R_{d-j}^2\). Such domination also
bounds the Euclidean operator norm: apply the triangle inequality
entrywise to a vector and then Cauchy--Schwarz to its scalar product
with \((R_i^2)_i\). Its norm is
\((N^2/4)\sum_iR_i^4\). This and (QR4) prove the upper bound at \(2\).
Since \(R_0=1\), (QR3) gives the exact corner value
\(|[(2I-C_N)^{-1}]_{d0}|=N^2/4\), proving the lower bound.

If \(|z+2|\ge4\) and \(c\in[-2,2]\), then
\[
                  |z-c|\ge |z+2|-(c+2)\ge2-c .
\]
Every actual \(c_j\) is strictly below \(2\), so no denominator
vanishes. The exact bidiagonal inverse at \(z\) is entrywise bounded
by the absolute inverse at \(2\). The preceding rank-one argument
therefore proves all of (QR1), including real \(z\) and \(N=2\).

There is an immediate application to the tilted line. For
\(t=e^{i\sigma\pi/4}y\), \(y\in\mathbb R\), \(\sigma\in\{1,-1\}\),
put \(u=e^{-2\pi it}\) and \(z=u+u^{-1}=2\cos(2\pi t)\).
With \(a=\sqrt2\pi y\),
\[
 |z+2|=2(\cosh a+\cos a)\ge4 .
\]
Indeed \(\cosh a+\cos a
=2\sum_{k\ge0}a^{4k}/(4k)!\ge2\). Thus along the entire line
\[
 \|(zI-C_N)^{-1}\|_2\le\pi^2N^2/16,\qquad
 \|(I-uC_N+u^2I)^{-1}\|_2
                              \le\frac{\pi^2N^2}{16|u|}.      \tag{QR5}
\]
This is a bound for the full inverse, not just its values on distinct
Casimir roots. It does not bound a separately inserted radical
polynomial, the exterior functional, or a change to the physical
metric. Those factors must remain in a resummed source formula.

The earlier resolvent theorem proves a fixed-nonreal-parameter
exponential rate; its rate vanishes on this exterior region.
The added assertion here is the explicit uniform polynomial bound,
its inclusion of \(z=2\), and its sharp order in \(N\).
The [Gaussian numerator and cap note](actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.md)
already controls endpoint regions for the original physical blocks.
Its estimates concern a different metric and are not replaced by
(QR1). This result supplies no new filling class, lower source
estimate, or evaluation of the fixed-degree minimum.

## Operator norm and traced norm of the derivative term, 23 November

The quadratic resolvent bound above cannot be extended to the
radical multiplier left by the finite Chebyshev resummation.
In the same Newton metric this multiplier has exponential norm,
with an explicit rate. Contracting it with the original trace
instead leaves a polynomial cost and the actual exterior values.
This audit rules out estimating that multiplier separately by a
polynomial operator bound. It does not rule out a source estimate
that retains the original contraction.

Let \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\),
\(\eta=(-1)^d\), and \(\theta=\pi/N\). Use the complete algebra
\(\mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/P_N\), its original trace \(\phi\),
and its normalized Newton basis
\[
 P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\quad
 c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta),\quad
 S_i=\prod_{r=1}^i2\sin(r\theta),\quad
 e_i(z)=S_i^{-2}\prod_{h<i}(c_h-z).
\]
Here \(S_0=1\); the distinct double nodes are \(c_a\), \(0\le a<m\).
At odd levels there is also the simple node \(-2\).
Multiplication by \(z\) is the original bidiagonal matrix \(C_N\)
used in (QR1). Define
\[
 J_N(z)=2T_{N-1}(z/2)+z,\qquad M_N=J_N(C_N),
 \qquad (\Pi v)_i=v_{d-i}.
 \tag{DJ1}
\]
Thus \(\Pi\) is coefficient reversal, an orthogonal matrix in the
stated Euclidean coordinates. This \(J_N\) is not the
different, also radical polynomial in the even-threading note.

The Chebyshev recurrence gives the polynomial identity
\[
 J_N(z)=\frac z2P_N(z)+\frac{4-z^2}{2N}P_N'(z).
 \tag{DJ2}
\]
It has value zero at every physical node. At each double node its
derivative is \(N\): the Chebyshev differential equation gives
\((4-c_a^2)P_N''(c_a)=2N^2\). At the odd simple node its value
is zero as well. In particular \(J_N^2=0\) in the full algebra.
The original Hermite trace therefore gives, for every \(f\),
\[
 \phi(J_N f)=\eta N\sum_{a=0}^{m-1}(4-c_a^2)f(c_a).
 \tag{DJ3}
\]
The exterior's derivatives disappear here because \(J_N(c_a)=0\);
the surviving derivative is the original \(J_N'(c_a)\).

### The exact Gram matrix

Let \(V_{ai}=e_i(c_a)\) and
\(W=\operatorname{diag}(4-c_a^2)_{a<m}\). The original pairing
\(\phi(e_i e_j)=\delta_{i+j,d}\), applied to (DJ3), proves
\[
 H_N:=\eta\Pi M_N=N V^*WV\succeq0,\qquad
                         \|M_N\|_2=\lambda_{\max}(H_N).
 \tag{DJ4}
\]
The entries of \(V\) are real. Its first \(m\) columns form a
triangular invertible matrix, and every column with \(i\ge m\)
is zero. Hence \(H_N\) has rank \(m\). Its kernel consists of
polynomials vanishing at every double node, including the odd
simple component when present. It is not a positive definite
metric on \(\mathcal A_N\).

These normalizations include \(N=2\) directly:
\(P_2=z^2\), \(e_1=-z/4\), \(J_2=2z\), and
\[
 M_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\-8&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 H_2=\begin{pmatrix}8&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Here \(\phi(f)=-4[z]f\), so the pairing used in (DJ4) remains valid.

### The sharp exponential cost

Write \(G_{\rm Cat}=\sum_{r\ge0}(-1)^r/(2r+1)^2\).
Then, along all integer levels,
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \log\|J_N(C_N)\|_2=\frac{4G_{\rm Cat}}{\pi}N+O(\log N).
 \qquad}                                                     \tag{DJ5}
\]
To prove this, note that \(e_i(c_a)=0\) for \(i>a\), whereas
\(0\le e_i(c_a)\le e_i(-2)\) for \(i\le a<m\). Moreover
\[
 e_i(-2)=
 \left[
 \frac{\prod_{h=0}^{i-1}2\cos((h+\tfrac12)\theta)}
      {\prod_{r=1}^i2\sin(r\theta)}
 \right]^2,\qquad
 \log e_i(-2)=2N F(i/N)+O(\log N),\quad
 F(x)=\int_0^x\log\cot(\pi t)\,dt .
 \tag{DJ6}
\]
The error is uniform for \(0\le i<m\). For sine, split off the
logarithmic endpoint at zero and compare the remaining smooth
function with its integral. For the midpoint cosine sum, monotone
integral comparison costs at most the oscillation of its logarithm,
which is \(O(\log N)\) through \(i<m\). These give (DJ6) directly.

Since \(F'(x)=\log\cot(\pi x)\), its maximum on \([0,1/2]\)
is \(F(1/4)=G_{\rm Cat}/\pi\). The last value follows by integrating
the Abel-regularized cosine series for \(\log\cot t\) on
\([0,\pi/4]\): the integral is
\(\sum_{r\ge0}(-1)^r/(2r+1)^2\). The integrated series converges
absolutely; the logarithmic endpoint is integrable.
Taking the trace in (DJ4) now gives
\[
 \|M_N\|_2\le\operatorname{Tr}H_N
 \le4Nm^2\max_{i<m}e_i(-2)^2
 =\exp\{4G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi+O(\log N)\}.
\]

For the lower bound take \(i=\lfloor N/4\rfloor\) and \(a=m-1\).
For sufficiently large \(N\), \(i\le a\). This last double node has
\(\delta=c_a+2=O(N^{-2})\) and
\(4-c_a^2\asymp N^{-2}\), at both parities. Every \(h<i\) has
\(c_h+2\ge2\), so
\[
 \frac{e_i(c_a)}{e_i(-2)}
 =\prod_{h<i}\left(1-\frac{\delta}{c_h+2}\right)
 =\exp\{O(N^{-1})\}.
\]
The \(i\)-th diagonal of (DJ4) is therefore at least
\(N(4-c_a^2)e_i(c_a)^2
=\exp\{4G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi+O(\log N)\}\).
It is bounded above by \(\lambda_{\max}(H_N)\), proving (DJ5).

The resolvent does not remove this operator growth. Since
\(\|C_N\|_2\le6\), (QR1) gives, for every \(|\zeta+2|\ge4\),
\[
 \frac{\|M_N\|_2}{|\zeta|+6}
 \le\|M_N(\zeta I-C_N)^{-1}\|_2
 \le\frac{\pi^2N^2}{16}\|M_N\|_2 .
 \tag{DJ7}
\]
Thus the same logarithmic rate holds uniformly on every bounded
subset of that region, including \(\zeta=2\).

### The original contraction has a different cost

For an unchanged exterior polynomial \(A\in\mathcal A_N\), (DJ3)
instead gives the exact identity
\[
 \phi\!\left(J_N A(\zeta I-C_N)^{-1}\right)
 =\eta N\sum_{a<m}\frac{(4-c_a^2)A(c_a)}{\zeta-c_a}.
\]
For \(|\zeta+2|\ge4\), the estimate
\(|\zeta-c_a|\ge2-c_a\) and the identity
\(\sum_{a<m}(2+c_a)=N\) yield
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \left|\phi\!\left(J_N A(\zeta I-C_N)^{-1}\right)\right|
 \le N^2\max_{a<m}|A(c_a)|.
 \quad}                                                      \tag{DJ8}
\]
The node sum follows from \(\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j=0\), pairing the
double nodes and retaining the odd simple node \(-2\).
The constant is attained at \(A=1,\zeta=2\), when the value is
\(\eta N^2\), including \(N=2\).

For any exact exterior row, use its actual Frobenius carrier
\(A\), defined by that row applied to \(f\) being \(\phi(Af)\).
Nondegeneracy of the original pairing gives this carrier uniquely.
Equation (DJ8) retains its physical values; it does not bound them.
An intervening turn must therefore be included in that carrier.

There is also exact crossing invariance of (DJ4). If \(X_n\) is
multiplication by the original \(R^n\), then
\[
                         X_n^*H_NX_n=H_N,\qquad n\in\mathbb Z,
\]
because \(R(c_a)\) has modulus one. This statement concerns the
degenerate value form. It cannot control the original closing on
its kernel: \(J_N\) is in that kernel but \(\phi(J_N)\ne0\).
Nor does it permit replacing a bilinear gluing by a Hermitian norm.

Radical contraction to physical values and degenerate positive
weighted forms were already established in the complete high-radical
and even-threading notes below. The quantitative addition in this
audit is the sharp multiplier rate (DJ5), together with its
resolvent consequence (DJ7). It shows why (QR1) alone cannot bound
the resummed derivative term. No geometric lower certificate,
physical-metric transfer, or new filling theorem is obtained.

## An explicit substitute for the principal Gram vector, 23 November

For the Gram matrix in (DJ4), its principal vector can be compared
coordinate by coordinate with a known sine-product vector. The
comparison loses only a power of \(N\). Its original closing is
therefore nonzero and has a computable exponential rate. The same
closing rates can be obtained from the explicit vector without
solving an eigenvalue or minimization problem.

This concerns the specified derivative block. It does not identify
its principal vector with the boundary state of a knot or of an
arbitrary short component.

Keep the notation of (DJ1)--(DJ6), and put
\[
 a=m-1,\qquad w_a=4-c_a^2,\qquad
 v_i=e_i(-2)>0\quad(0\le i<m),\qquad
 b_N=Nw_a/4,\quad B_N=2N^2,\quad \kappa_N=B_N/b_N.
 \tag{PV1}
\]
Here \(H^{\rm low}\) denotes the nonzero \(m\)-by-\(m\) block of
\(H_N\). Then, entrywise,
\[
 b_Nv_iv_j\le H^{\rm low}_{ij}\le B_Nv_iv_j,\qquad
 b_N\ge4/N,\qquad \kappa_N\le N^3/2.
 \tag{PV2}
\]

To verify the uniform lower bound, compare the last double node
with the endpoint \(-2\). Writing \(\delta=c_a+2\), one has
\[
 \rho_i:=\frac{e_i(c_a)}{e_i(-2)}
 =\prod_{h<i}\left(1-\frac{\delta}{c_h+2}\right).
\]
All factors are positive and at most one; hence \(\rho_i\)
decreases for \(0\le i\le a\). The endpoint products give
\[
 \rho_a=
 \begin{cases}
  (2\cos\theta)^{-1},&N\text{ odd},\\
  (N/2)\tan(\theta/2),&N\text{ even}.
 \end{cases}                                                 \tag{PV3}
\]
Here is a direct derivation. Difference of cosines gives
\(e_a(c_a)=S_{2a}/S_a^2\). The product
\(\prod_{h<m}(c_h+2)\) is \(N\) at odd levels and \(2\) at even
levels: square it and use, respectively,
\(P_N'(-2)=N^2\) or \(P_N(-2)=4\).
Consequently \(\rho_a=\delta S_{2a}/N\) in the odd case and
\(\rho_a=\delta S_{2a}/2\) in the even case.
Now \(S_{N-3}=N/[s_1s_2]\), \(S_{N-2}=N/s_1\), where
\(s_r=2\sin(r\theta)\), and
\(\delta=s_1^2\) or \(4\sin^2(\theta/2)\), respectively.
These identities prove (PV3), including the empty products at \(N=2\).
In particular \(\rho_i\ge1/2\) for every \(i<m\).

Every summand of the Gram formula is nonnegative. Retaining just
the node \(c_a\) proves the lower comparison in (PV2).
For the upper comparison use \(e_i(c_h)\le v_i\) and
\(\sum_{h<m}(4-c_h^2)\le4m\le2N\).
At even levels \(w_a=4\sin^2\theta\); at odd levels
\(w_a=4\sin^2(2\theta)\).
The elementary sine bound gives \(w_a\ge16/N^2\), with \(N=3\)
checked directly. This proves all constants in (PV2).

### The principal vector and the original closing

There is a unique unit top eigenvector \(u\) of \(H^{\rm low}\)
with every coordinate positive. Indeed a real unit vector
maximizing its Rayleigh quotient can be replaced by its absolute
values. Strict positivity of every matrix entry forces all its
coordinates to be positive by the eigenvalue equation.
A second independent top eigenvector would be orthogonal to this
one and have both signs; taking its absolute values would strictly
increase the quotient. This proves uniqueness without assuming it.

Let \(\lambda_N\) be the top eigenvalue. If \(s=v^{\mathsf T}u>0\),
(PV2) gives \(b_Nsv_i\le\lambda_Nu_i\le B_Nsv_i\).
Taking Euclidean norms on both sides, then substituting back,
proves the coordinate bounds
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \kappa_N^{-1}\frac{v_i}{\|v\|_2}
 \le u_i\le
 \kappa_N\frac{v_i}{\|v\|_2},\qquad 0\le i<m .
 \qquad}                                                     \tag{PV4}
\]
Also \(b_N\|v\|_2^2\le\lambda_N\le B_N\|v\|_2^2\);
the lower bound tests the Rayleigh quotient at \(v/\|v\|_2\),
and the upper bound follows from rank-one domination.

Extend \(u\) and \(v\) by zeros to the full Newton space. Since
\(v_0=1\), (DJ6) and (PV4) give
\[
 \log\|v\|_2=\frac{2G_{\rm Cat}}{\pi}N+O(\log N),\qquad
 \phi(\Pi u)=u_0>0,\qquad
 \log u_0=-\frac{2G_{\rm Cat}}{\pi}N+O(\log N).
 \tag{PV5}
\]
The closing identity uses exactly \(\phi(e_d)=1\) and
\(\phi(e_j)=0\) for \(j<d\).
Since \(M_N=\eta\Pi H_N\),
\[
 \phi(M_Nu)=\eta\lambda_Nu_0\ne0,\qquad
 \log|\phi(M_Nu)|=\frac{2G_{\rm Cat}}{\pi}N+O(\log N).
 \tag{PV6}
\]
The analogous explicit vector \(\widehat v=v/\|v\|_2\)
requires no spectral solve:
\[
 \phi(\Pi\widehat v)=1/\|v\|_2,\qquad
 b_N\|v\|_2\le
       \eta\phi(M_N\widehat v)\le B_N\|v\|_2.
 \tag{PV7}
\]
It has the same two logarithmic closing rates.

These are observations of specified finite vectors with the
original functional. In particular they quantify the overlap,
rather than inferring it from the operator norm. They do not give
a lower bound for the projection of the actual knot state onto
either vector. There is also a concrete assembly limitation:
\(\Pi u\) and \(\Pi\widehat v\) lie in the square-zero radical.
Any two such outputs multiply to zero in the same pair algebra.
Thus positive local observations alone do not give a gluing rule
that preserves a nonzero original closing under unrestricted products.
No change to the physical metric, geometric boundary certificate,
or filling theorem is supplied.

The even endpoint comparison in (PV3) was already proved in the
regular circle-trace note, Section 9. The added assertions here are
the entrywise comparison of this \(J_N\)-Gram, its coordinatewise
principal-vector bounds, and the resulting original-closing rates.
The full source minimum has not been evaluated.

## A fixed twist can cancel the inserted positive observation, 23 November

The \(J_N\) observation in (DJ3) does not give a nonzero lower
bound for every actual short state obtained from positive low
input. The fixed two-crossing state already distinguishes it
from the original closing:
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \phi_N(J_NR^2)=0\quad\text{if }4\mid N,\qquad
 \phi_N(R^2)=N\quad\text{for every }N\ge2 .
 \qquad}                                                     \tag{TC1}
\]
This is an exact cancellation in the inserted observation,
despite the nonzero original closing. It is not a counterexample
to the principal-vector statement (PV4), or to a knot volume
conjecture.

Here is the calculation with the original scalar factors.
Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\), and \(\eta=(-1)^d\), using the displayed
exponential for the fractional power. The original crossing values
at the distinct double nodes are
\[
 c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N),\quad w_a=4-c_a^2,\qquad
 R(c_a)=\kappa(-1)^a q^{a(a+1)} .
\]
For \(N=4k\), write \(m=N/2\) and pair \(a\) with
\(a'=m-1-a\), for \(0\le a<m\). There are no fixed indices.
Then \(c_{a'}=-c_a\), \(w_{a'}=w_a\), and
\[
 a'(a'+1)-a(a+1)=m(m-1-2a),\qquad
 \frac{R(c_{a'})^2}{R(c_a)^2}
 =q^{2m(m-1-2a)}=(-1)^{m-1}=-1 .
\]
Thus the exact original trace (DJ3),
\[
                   \phi_N(J_N f)=\eta N\sum_{a<m}w_af(c_a),
\]
cancels pairwise for \(f=R^2\). More generally,
\(\phi_N(J_NR^{4\ell+2}F)=0\) for every integer \(\ell\) whenever
\(F(c_{a'})=F(c_a)\). This condition concerns the retained nodal
values; it is not assumed for an arbitrary exterior.

The full two-crossing expansion, with all Hermite directions, is
\[
 R^2=\kappa^2\sum_{r=0}^{d}(-q)^r(Q;Q)_r e_r .
\]
Since \(\phi_N(e_r)=\delta_{r,d}\), it gives
\[
 \phi_N(R^2)=\kappa^2(-q)^d(Q;Q)_d=N .
\]
Indeed \((Q;Q)_d=N\), by evaluating
\((X^N-1)/(X-1)\) at \(X=1\), and
\(\kappa^2(-q)^d=(-1)^d q^{d(d+1)}=1\).
This proves the second identity at both parities, including \(N=2\).

The input \(1=e_0\) is an actual low positive input; its multiplication
by \(R^2\) is the original signed-twist operation. The example rules
out extending nonzero \(J_N\)-observations to all such inputs merely
because crossing multiplication preserves the semidefinite form.
It does not assert cancellation for the particular explicit PV
vector. A proof for arbitrary short components must retain their
actual original closing and control the transported coefficients;
the inserted positive observation cannot replace that comparison.

## Optimal conditioning of finite twist-period recovery, 23 November

The actual twist-period sources give an exact optimum for linear
recovery of a short source from nonzero integer period shifts.
Fix a number \(d\ge1\) of incident edges and an integer power \(n\),
and evaluate the complete boundary source at \(\mathbf u=0\).
Here \(d\) is independent of \(N\), not the shift \(N-1\).
Using the full sources of the
[insertion-growth theorem](research_twist_period_insertion_growth.md), write
\[
 P=P_{d,n,N}(0),\qquad B=B_{d,n,N}(0),\qquad
 \eta=(-1)^{N-1}.
\]
Thus \(P\) uses the original trace with crossing \(R^n\), and \(B\)
uses the same trace and adjoining full edge kernels with the additional
insertion \(U_N=\eta R^{2N}-1\). No exterior kernel is omitted.
The exact full-Hermite period identity gives, at every \(N\ge2\),
\[
 y_k:=\eta^{-k}P_{d,n+2Nk,N}(0)=P+kB,\qquad k\in\mathbb Z.   \tag{PR1}
\]
The original crossing phases and normal directions remain.
Any external framing line must also be carried. The displayed
normalization has modulus one and preserves relative error radii.

Take finitely many nonzero integer shifts \(k_j\). A complex linear
rule recovering the intercept of every affine function has weights
\[
 \sum_jw_j=1,\qquad \sum_jw_jk_j=0,\qquad
                         P=\sum_jw_jy_{k_j}.
\]
These two conditions follow by testing the constant and linear
functions, and conversely imply exactness. The shifts, weights and
number of samples may depend on \(N\). Put
\[
 \Gamma=\sum_j|w_j|\,|y_{k_j}|,\qquad
 a=|P+B|,\quad b=|P-B|,\quad
 \alpha=(a+b)/2,\quad\beta=(a-b)/2.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \inf_{\substack{\text{finite affine-exact rules}\\
                         k_j\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}}}
       \Gamma
 =\frac{|P+B|+|P-B|}{2}
 \ge\max\{|P|,|B|\}.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{PR2}
\]

Indeed \(\alpha,\beta\) are real, the reverse triangle inequality gives
\(|\beta|\le|B|\), and
\[
 \alpha^2+\beta^2=|P|^2+|B|^2,\qquad
                 \alpha\beta=\operatorname{Re}(P\overline B).
\]
Consequently, for every real \(|k|\ge1\),
\[
 |P+kB|^2-|\alpha+\beta k|^2
                    =(k^2-1)(|B|^2-\beta^2)\ge0.
\]
Every admissible rule therefore satisfies
\[
 \Gamma\ge\sum_j|w_j|\,|\alpha+\beta k_j|
 \ge\left|\sum_jw_j(\alpha+\beta k_j)\right|=\alpha.
\]
The shifts \(k=\pm1\), with weights \(1/2,1/2\), attain this
bound. Finally the triangle inequality applied to the sum and
difference of \(P+B,P-B\) gives \(a+b\ge2|P|\) and
\(a+b\ge2|B|\). This proves (PR2), including all zero cases.

For \(u\ge0\) and independently selectable complex errors in the original
samples, \(|\delta y_j|\le u|y_{k_j}|\), the exact largest
recovered absolute error is \(u\Gamma\): choose the error phases
so that all \(w_j\delta y_j\) align. Thus, when \(P\ne0\), the
optimal relative condition number is \(\alpha/|P|\).

The complete insertion-growth theorem supplies fixed constants
\(b_0,C,c>0\) and \(p\), depending on \(d,n\), such that
\[
 |B|\ge b_0N^{-3(d-1)/2}e^{NW},\qquad
 |P|\le CN^p e^{N(W-c)}
\]
at all sufficiently large levels, including both parities.
Here \(W=4dG_{\mathrm{Cat}}/\pi\) and
\(G_{\mathrm{Cat}}=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^m/(2m+1)^2\).
Hence, at those levels where \(P\ne0\),
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \inf\frac{\Gamma}{|P|}
 =\frac{|P+B|+|P-B|}{2|P|}
 \ge\frac{|B|}{|P|}
 \ge C_0N^{-A}e^{cN}
 \qquad}                                                    \tag{PR3}
\]
for suitable fixed \(C_0>0,A\ge0\), uniformly over the allowed
sampling choices. If \(P=0\), relative conditioning is undefined,
but the exact absolute optimum in (PR2) remains \(|B|\).

A Fourier or orthogonal change of these sample coordinates followed
by linear recovery gives another rule on the original samples and
obeys the same bound. The original error set must be transported;
independent errors in the original samples need not remain independent
in the new coordinates. Correlated source errors can behave differently:
an error \(\delta y_k=k\,\delta B\) cancels exactly because
\(\sum_jw_jk_j=0\). The result does not exclude such estimates,
symbolic cancellation, nonlinear constructions, or a new geometric
argument controlling the recovered intercept. It is a conditioning
audit for the displayed actual boundary sources, not a hyperbolic-knot
counterexample or a finite-exception theorem.
