## One-head Ward identities do not distinguish exact Conway sectors, 23 November

This audit concerns exact finite decompositions in the full physical
pair algebra, including every repeated-root normal direction.
Fix \(N\ge2\), a literal Conway expression \(E\), and its original
root row \(\eta_N\lambda\), where \(\lambda=\phi\) or \(\lambda_0\).
Put \(d=N-1\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), and \(x=-e^{-\pi i/N}\).
The symbol \(\|\cdot\|_2\) below is the unnormalized
Hilbert--Schmidt norm in the uniform physical metric.
For each independent leaf occurrence choose any finite exact split
\[
 A_i=\sum_{s\in S_i}A_{i,s},\qquad A_{i,s}\in\mathcal A_N.
\]
Products and genuine turns preserve \(\mathcal A_N\).
Consequently the completed boxes
\(B_{\mathbf s}=B_E((A_{i,s_i})_i)\) satisfy
\[
 B_E((A_i)_i)=\sum_{\mathbf s}B_{\mathbf s},\qquad
 K_N=\sum_{\mathbf s}\kappa_{\mathbf s},\qquad
 \kappa_{\mathbf s}=\eta_N\lambda(B_{\mathbf s}).             \tag{ES1}
\]
The sums are over the finite product of the leaf index sets.
No bound on their cardinalities or on the summands is assumed.

Here is an elementary proof that each term has a scalar one-head
realization. Retain the original pivot
\(g=K^{1-N}=(-1)^dK\), \(d=N-1\), and put
\[
 C_d(B)=\operatorname{Tr}_2((I\otimes g)B),
                                      \qquad B\in\mathcal A_N.
\]
Write \(\mathcal E\) for the actual balanced lowering generator.
The pair box commutes with
\(\mathcal E_\Sigma=\mathcal E\otimes K+I\otimes\mathcal E\).
Partial trace is cyclic in operators acting only on the second
head, so
\[
 0=\operatorname{Tr}_2[\mathcal E_\Sigma,B]
   =[\mathcal E,\operatorname{Tr}_2((I\otimes K)B)].
\]
Thus \([\mathcal E,C_d(B)]=0\). Commutation of \(B\) with
\(K\otimes K\) and the same partial cyclicity give
\([K,C_d(B)]=0\). The distinct eigenvalues \(xQ^{-j}\) of \(K\)
force \(C_d(B)\) to be diagonal. Every arrow \(Q^{-j}-1\),
\(1\le j<N\), of \(\mathcal E\) is nonzero, so its diagonal
entries agree. This includes \(N=2\). Taking the ordinary trace
determines the scalar without another normalization:
\[
 C_d(B)=\phi(B)I,\qquad
 \phi(B)=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}((I\otimes g)B).             \tag{ES2}
\]
For the other original row use only the exact restricted sewing
identity \(\lambda_0=\phi\circ\mathcal T\) on \(\mathcal A_N\).
The genuine turn preserves this full algebra, so
\[
 C_0(B):=C_d(\mathcal TB)=\lambda_0(B)I.
\]
This does not declare the unrestricted marked cap equivariant
on arbitrary arrays or replace it by an ordinary cap. The
original cups, tail pivots and external normalizers remain.

Apply the appropriate \(C_d\) or \(C_0\) to each completed box
and multiply by the same original scalar \(\eta_N\).
The resulting one-head representatives are
\(C_{\mathbf s}=\kappa_{\mathbf s}I\). For the actual heat
\(T_t\) and softened cut \(\rho_t=T_t(P_0)\), at every \(t\ge0\),
\[
 T_t(C_{\mathbf s})=C_{\mathbf s},\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tC_{\mathbf s})=\kappa_{\mathbf s},
 \qquad
 \|C_{\mathbf s}\|_2=\sqrt N\,|\kappa_{\mathbf s}|.           \tag{ES3}
\]
All three one-head Ward defects vanish separately.
This applies in particular to an exact core/alias leaf split
made inside the full Hermite--Newton algebra.

The gluing Gram makes the surviving coherence explicit:
\[
 G_{\mathbf s,\mathbf t}
     =\operatorname{Tr}(C_{\mathbf s}^*C_{\mathbf t})
     =N\overline{\kappa_{\mathbf s}}\kappa_{\mathbf t},
 \qquad
 \left\|\sum_{\mathbf s}C_{\mathbf s}\right\|_2^2
     =\mathbf1^*G\mathbf1
     =N\left|\sum_{\mathbf s}\kappa_{\mathbf s}\right|^2.    \tag{ES4}
\]
Here \(\mathbf1\) is the vector of ones indexed by the sectors.
This Gram has rank at most one. Replacing it by its diagonal
would give \(N\sum_{\mathbf s}|\kappa_{\mathbf s}|^2\) and
discard the actual cross terms. Orthogonalizing the completed
one-head images leaves at most one scalar direction; it does not
estimate the coefficient in that direction.

Thus one-head Ward defects alone do not distinguish these
completed terms or prevent cancellation in (ES1). An independent
geometric estimate of their coherent sum would still be useful,
but is not supplied by the defects. A local geometric cutoff or
truncated period outside \(\mathcal A_N\) does not inherit this
argument, and still requires control of its original source
and boundary currents. This audit supplies no nonzero source
projection or new volume theorem.

## A sharper Ward bound for the actual heat-softened cut, 23 November

The [one-head Schur and cut-heat theorem](research_one_head_ward_coercivity_and_cut_heat_v2.md)
has a useful quantitative corollary. For the specified softened cut,
the relative commutator scale needed to control an observation improves
from \(N^{-3/2}\) to \(N^{-1}\). This concerns the softened observation;
its comparison with the original source still has to be retained.

Use the theorem's uniform physical metric, original generators and
heat flow. For an arbitrary matrix \(A\), put
\[
 V=\|A\|_2,\qquad c=\operatorname{Tr}A/N,\qquad B=A-cI,
\]
\[
 D=\frac N4\sqrt{3\|[\mathcal E,A]\|_2^2+
                       3\|[F,A]\|_2^2+\|[K,A]\|_2^2},
 \qquad \eta_t=e^{-16t/(3N^2)}.
\]
Let \(\rho_t=T_t(P_0)\) be the actual softened highest cut.
Here all norms are unnormalized Hilbert--Schmidt norms, and
\([u]_+=\max(u,0)\). At every \(N\ge2\) and \(t\ge0\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \left[\sqrt{\frac{[V^2-D^2]_+}{N}}-\eta_tD\right]_+
 \le|\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA)|
 \le\frac V{\sqrt N}+\eta_tD.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{HSO1}
\]

Indeed, the Schur estimate gives \(\|B\|_2\le D\), while
orthogonality gives \(V^2=N|c|^2+\|B\|_2^2\).
The heat estimate gives \(\|\rho_t-I/N\|_2\le\eta_t\).
Since \(\operatorname{Tr}B=0\),
\[
 |\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA)-c|
 =|\operatorname{Tr}((\rho_t-I/N)B)|
 \le\eta_t\|B\|_2\le\eta_tD.
\]
Combining these facts proves (HSO1), including \(A=0\).

Write
\[
 \mathfrak w(A)^2=\|[\mathcal E,A]\|_2^2+
                     \|[F,A]\|_2^2+\|[K,A]\|_2^2,
 \qquad t_N=\frac{3N^2}{16}\log(2N).
\]
For \(t\ge t_N\), if
\[
 \mathfrak w(A)\le aN^{-1}V,\qquad 0\le a<4/\sqrt3,
\]
then \(D\le\sqrt3aV/4\), and (HSO1) yields
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \left[\sqrt{1-\frac{3a^2}{16}}-
                   \frac{\sqrt3a}{8\sqrt N}\right]_+
 \frac V{\sqrt N}
 \le|\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA)|
 \le\left(1+\frac{\sqrt3a}{8\sqrt N}\right)\frac V{\sqrt N}.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{HSO2}
\]
For every fixed such \(a\), the lower coefficient is positive
for all sufficiently large \(N\). Positivity at every \(N\)
is not claimed when \(a\) approaches \(4/\sqrt3\).
In particular, for nonzero matrices \(A_N\) and \(t\ge t_N\),
\[
 \mathfrak w(A_N)=o(N^{-1}\|A_N\|_2)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \frac{|\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA_N)|}{\|A_N\|_2/\sqrt N}
                                      \longrightarrow1 .
\]

The power \(N^{-1}\) cannot be weakened for arbitrary matrices.
The actual trial \(A=|w_0\rangle\langle w_d|\), \(d=N-1\), has
\(V=1\) and \(\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA)=0\), since \(\rho_t\)
is diagonal. Direct multiplication, also at \(N=2\), gives
\[
 \|[\mathcal E,A]\|_2^2=0,\quad
 \|[F,A]\|_2^2=8\sin^2(\pi/N),\quad
 \|[K,A]\|_2^2=4\sin^2(\pi/N).
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak w(A)=2\sqrt3\sin(\pi/N)\asymp N^{-1}\).
For any \(\beta<1\), this is \(o(N^{-\beta})\) despite the zero
observation. This is an arbitrary trial, not a knot counterexample.

For the fully assembled original unmarked knot operator
\(A_N=K_NI\), softened observation equals \(K_N\) exactly.
For arbitrary marked matrices, the retained identity is instead
\(\operatorname{Tr}(P_0T_t(A))=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA)\).
Comparing this with the unsmoothed observation can cost \(O(D)\),
and therefore restore the earlier \(N^{-3/2}\) relative Ward
scale. The gain in (HSO2) concerns the specified softened probe;
it does not construct a finite geometric approximation, control
its source remainder, or prove a nonzero geometric contribution.
There is no new estimate of the quartic minimum's volume rate
or finite-exception theorem here.

## Actual one-head Ward defects control the marked observation, 23 November

The [quantitative Schur and cut-heat proof](research_one_head_ward_coercivity_and_cut_heat_v2.md)
provides a representation-theoretic almost-invariance estimate
for the original complete head. It uses the actual uniform physical
metric and the original zero arrows, at every \(N\ge2\).

Let \(d=N-1\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), \(x=-e^{-\pi i/N}\), and
\[
 \mathcal E w_a=(Q^{-a}-1)w_{a-1},\quad
 Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1},\quad
 Kw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a.
\]
The basis is orthonormal, and \(F=-\mathcal E^*\).
For any matrix \(A\), put \(c=\operatorname{Tr}A/N\).
In unnormalized Hilbert--Schmidt norm,
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|A-cI\|_2^2
 \le\frac{N^2}{16}
       \bigl(3\|[\mathcal E,A]\|_2^2+
             3\|[F,A]\|_2^2+\|[K,A]\|_2^2\bigr).
 \quad}                                                    \tag{WH1}
\]
The proof first projects orthogonally onto the clock's diagonal
grade. The clock controls the complementary grades; the lowering
and raising defects control the remaining diagonal by the actual
weighted-path Poincaré inequality. This proves a polynomial bound
without an exponentially conditioned fusion similarity.

Let \(\mathfrak w(A)\) be the square root of the sum of the three
squared defects in (WH1), without the coefficients \(3,3,1\).
For every positive trace-one probe \(P\), including the original
highest cut \(P_0=|w_0\rangle\langle w_0|\), the proof gives
\[
 \mathfrak w(A)\le\varepsilon N^{-3/2}\|A\|_2,\quad
          0\le\varepsilon\le1/4
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 (1-2\varepsilon)\frac{\|A\|_2}{\sqrt N}
 \le|\operatorname{Tr}(PA)|
 \le(1+\varepsilon)\frac{\|A\|_2}{\sqrt N}.
 \tag{WH2}
\]
This is an actual observation bound, not an assumed nonzero angle.
Its power of \(N\) matters. The arbitrary trial matrix \(A=I-P_0\)
has zero original-cut observation, norm \(\sqrt{N-1}\), clock
defect zero and each of its other defects equal to \(2\sin(\pi/N)\).
Thus the relative scale \(N^{-3/2}\) cannot be replaced by a
weaker power for arbitrary trials. This is not a knot counterexample.

The same generators give a concrete positive cut-softening flow.
With \(\operatorname{ad}_X(A)=[X,A]\), put
\[
 \mathscr L=\operatorname{ad}_{\mathcal E}^*
                       \operatorname{ad}_{\mathcal E}
            +\operatorname{ad}_{F}^*\operatorname{ad}_{F}
            +\operatorname{ad}_{K}^*\operatorname{ad}_{K}.
\]
Its kernel is \(\mathbb CI\), its positive gap is at least
\(16/(3N^2)\), and \(T_t=e^{-t\mathscr L}\) is a completely
positive, unital, trace-preserving flow. On the original cut,
\[
 \rho_t=T_t(P_0)
 =\operatorname{diag}(e^{-2t\Delta_{\mathrm{path},N}}\mathbf e_0),
 \qquad
 p_j=4\sin^2(\pi(j+1)/N)\quad(0\le j<d).
 \tag{WH3}
\]
Here \(\Delta_{\mathrm{path},N}\) is the undirected path
Laplacian with edge weights \(p_j\), with no closing endpoint edge.
In particular,
\[
 t\ge\frac{3N^2}{16}\log(2N)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \frac{I}{2N}\preceq\rho_t\preceq\frac{3I}{2N}.
 \tag{WH4}
\]
The actual highest cut becomes a positive definite probe of
condition number at most three in a specified polynomial time.

For the fully assembled unmarked one-cut knot operator,
including its recorded external normalization, \(A_N=K_NI\);
therefore \(\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA_N)=K_N\) exactly.
Scalarity and the qualitative freedom to use any trace-one
probe were already known. The new content is the quantitative
commutator estimate, positive flow and mixing bound.

For arbitrary marked operators the exact identity is instead
\(\operatorname{Tr}(P_0T_t(A))=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA)\).
The source must retain this dual transport. No many-head coproduct
gap, independent smoothing inside crossings, or scalar projection
of internal Casimir derivative channels is justified here.
An actual geometric approximation with the relative Ward estimate
and the required full norm growth has not been constructed.
The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## The expanded physical minimum has an explicit octahedral scale, 23 November

Two existing results determine the previously unspecified exponential
budget of one useful quartic presentation. The
[sharp crossing norm](weighted_crossing_source_gap.md), Sections 1--3,
is a theorem for the same uniform physical occupation metric as the
[physical quartic](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md).
Combining them gives the calibration below. This is a corollary of
those results, not a new crossing-norm theorem.

Fix a filled literal diagram \(D\). Expand every fixed integer power
\(R^n\) into \(|n|\) leaves \(R^{\operatorname{sgn}n}\), using an
identity leaf when \(n=0\). Retain the actual products and turns.
Let \(c=c(D)\) count these signed crossing occurrences, not the minimal
crossing number of the knot. Use exactly the physical budgets (18):
\[
 b_v=16\max(1,\|A_v\|_{\rm ph})\quad\hbox{at a leaf},\qquad
 b_v=16\quad\hbox{at products and turns},
\]
and root budget \(16\max(1,|\eta_N|)\) for its recorded original
scalar multiple \(\eta_N\lambda\).
Assume \(\log\max(1,|\eta_N|)=O_D(\log N)\), as for the
recorded framing phases and fixed powers of \(N\).
Write \(B_{D,N}\) for this budget product and \(e_{D,N}\) for this
expanded compiler's physical minimum.

Put \(v_8=4G_{\rm Cat}\), the regular ideal octahedron volume.
The sharp norm theorem gives, for either crossing sign,
\[
 \log\|R^{\pm1}\|_{\rm ph}
       =\frac{v_8}{2\pi}N+O(\log N).
 \tag{OB1}
\]
Here the norm is the full physical Hilbert--Schmidt norm on the
pair, as required by the leaf budget. The identity has norm \(N\).
The diagram has a fixed number of vertices. Consequently
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \log B_{D,N}=\frac{cv_8}{2\pi}N+O_D(\log N).
 \qquad}                                                   \tag{OB2}
\]
Indeed each crossing contributes (OB1) and its factor \(16\);
each identity contributes \(\log(16N)\); the fixed structural
and root factors contribute only \(O_D(\log N)\).

Keeping the source sandwich of the physical quartic now gives a
constant \(C_D\), enlarged to cover the finitely many small levels,
such that for every \(N\ge2\),
\[
 N^{-C_D}e^{cv_8N/\pi}e_{D,N}
 \le |K_N(D)|^2
 \le N^{C_D}e^{cv_8N/\pi}e_{D,N}.
 \tag{OB3}
\]
This includes exact zeros. Thus, with \(-\log0=+\infty\), the
volume identity for this fixed knot is exactly equivalent to
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 -\frac{\pi}{N}\log e_{D,N}
       \longrightarrow cv_8-\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K).
 \qquad}                                                   \tag{OB4}
\]
On nonzero levels this follows by taking logarithms in (OB3).
A finite limit on either side excludes an infinite subsequence
of zeros, and the zero sets agree.

This pins down the geometric scale the minimum would have to
recover. It neither computes that minimum nor proves that its rate
equals the displayed volume difference. The count \(c\), constants
and objective concern the fixed expanded filled diagram. They are
not uniform as its twist powers vary. Expanding a contracted power
can change the numerical minimum; no equality with a contracted
compiler or with the Newton-metric minimum is asserted.
The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## Real activity steps need not have small physical norm, 23 November

This is a limitation of a proposed continuation argument, not a
counterexample to the volume conjecture. Subdividing Euler activity
into real steps of size \(1/N\) does not by itself give tame
operator norms, even inside the interval \([0,1]\).

Use the actual complete-meridian arrows and coupled Euler factor
of the [fractional-time calculation](research_polynomial_seams_and_fractional_euler_time.md):
\[
 N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad
 X=E_1F_2,\qquad X^N=0,
\]
\[
 Ew_a=(Q^{-a}-1)w_{a-1},\qquad
 Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1}.
\]
The missing extreme arrows are zero. Put
\[
 F_n=(Q;Q)_n,\qquad
 U_N(t)=\sum_{n=0}^d\frac{t^nq^nX^n}{F_n}.
 \tag{AI1}
\]
At \(t=1\), this is the literal inverse Euler factor
\(\Theta_-\) in that calculation's ordered crossing.
For any complex \(a,b\), finite binomial convolution gives
\[
 U_N(b)U_N(a)^{-1}
 =\sum_{n=0}^d
       \frac{q^n\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(b-aQ^j)}{F_n}\,X^n.
 \tag{AI2}
\]
To verify it, multiply \(U_N(b)\) by the exact inverse
\(\sum_{n<N}(-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}(aqX)^n/F_n\).
The degree-\(n\) coefficient is the finite binomial product
\(\prod_{j<n}(b-aQ^j)\), divided by \(F_n\).
All higher degrees vanish by \(X^N=0\).

Take \(0<\delta<1\), \(a=1-\delta\), \(b=1\), and denote
this increment by \(V_N\). For \(n\ge1\),
\[
 |1-(1-\delta)Q^j|^2
       =\delta^2+(1-\delta)|1-Q^j|^2,
\]
so its degree-\(n\) coefficient in (AI2) has modulus at least
\[
 \frac{\delta(1-\delta)^{(n-1)/2}}{|1-Q^n|}
       \ge\frac{\delta}{2}(1-\delta)^{(n-1)/2}.
 \tag{AI3}
\]
Swapping \(a,b\) gives the same absolute products, so (AI3)
also holds for \(V_N^{-1}\).

Here is a literal test inside the physical middle degree.
Set \(A=\lfloor5N/6\rfloor\), \(k=2A-d\), and use input
\(w_A\otimes w_{d-A}\) and output
\(w_{d-A}\otimes w_A\). Then \(1\le k<N\), and only \(X^k\)
can connect them. Its entry has modulus
\[
 \prod_{h=d-A+1}^{A}|1-Q^h|^2.
 \tag{AI4}
\]
Every such \(h/N\) lies in \([1/6,5/6]\), so its individual
sine factor \(2\sin(\pi h/N)\) is at least one.
At least \(N/3-2\) of these indices lie in \([N/3,2N/3]\),
where that factor is at least \(\sqrt3\). Thus (AI4) is at least
\(3^{N/3-2}\). Also \(k-1\le2N/3\).

The input and output have equal norm both in the uniform physical
head metric and in the binomial metric
\(\|w_a\|^2=\binom da^{-1}\). A matrix entry between their
normalized vectors therefore gives, in either metric,
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \|V_N^{\pm1}\|_{\rm op}
 \ge\frac{\delta}{18}
            [\,3(1-\delta)\,]^{N/3}.
 \qquad}                                                   \tag{AI5}
\]
The same bound holds for \(V_N^{\pm1}-I\), because this is an
off-diagonal entry. All tested arrows stay strictly within their
allowed finite ranges.

In particular set \(\delta=1/N\). Then
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\|V_N^{\pm1}\|_{\rm op}
                    \ge\frac{\log3}{3}>0.
 \tag{AI6}
\]
The exponential rate of their condition number is at least
\(2\log3/3\). Orthonormal changes of basis preserve these norms.
More generally
\[
 \operatorname{cond}_2(S_1V_NS_0^{-1})
 \ge\frac{\operatorname{cond}_2(V_N)}
          {\operatorname{cond}_2(S_1)\operatorname{cond}_2(S_0)}.
 \tag{AI7}
\]
Thus input and output frame changes whose condition numbers are
subexponential cannot make both directions tame.
This does not rule out a selected microlocal packet estimate.
It rules out the proposed global small-step norm estimate.

The earlier fractional-time proof already gives exponentially
large logarithmic generators and failures on complex time disks.
The additional calculation here concerns actual real activity-ratio
increments ending at activity one, on every level, with explicit
finite bounds. Small-activity full-norm packet theorems do not
supply this missing estimate: an increment away from zero has
every transfer degree at first order in its step size.
The intermediate Euler arrays also need their full original
physical co-source; they are not automatically full commutant boxes.
No geometric packet or original knot closing is identified with
the test vectors in (AI4).

## The quartic has a uniform positive-integral approximation, 23 November

The [uniform Laplace estimate](research_conway_uniform_growing_level_laplace.md)
gives a further consequence of fixed degree. The quantum level and
the inverse temperature can now grow together, with a proved error.
Previously the Gaussian approximation was justified only at each
fixed quantum level.

Keep exactly the Hilbert--Schmidt budgets and full Newton packets
of the normalized source. If there are \(s\) proper vertices, put
\(D=Ns\), and write
\[
 E_N(x)=\|G_N(x)\|^2+|c_Nx|^2,\qquad
 e_N=\min E_N,\qquad
 g_N=\sqrt{\det_{\mathbb R}(D_{\mathbb R}^2E_N(x_*)/2)}.
\]
Here \(G_N\) is the original recursion residual and \(c_N\) the
original normalized closing row. Define
\[
 Z_N(\tau)=\left(\frac{\tau}{\pi}\right)^D
                 \int_{\mathbb C^D}e^{-\tau E_N(x)}\,dx.
\]
For every fixed literal construction,
\[
 Z_N(N^4)=g_N^{-1}e^{-N^4e_N}(1+o(1)),\qquad
 \sqrt{1-2^{-22}}\le g_N\le197/196 .
\]
The logarithmic error is
\(O_s((\log N)^{3/2}/\sqrt N)\).

The proof uses an exact Taylor formula: after its quadratic part,
the objective has only cubic and quartic terms, bounded respectively
by \(9\|h\|^3/128\) and \(\|h\|^4/1024\). A Gaussian tail estimate
controls a shrinking neighborhood. Outside that neighborhood, the
unit-Jacobian triangular residual map gives an integrable global
bound. Thus the growing number of coordinates causes no unrecorded
exponential normalization.

This result concerns the same numerical minimum, not a newly chosen
positive model. Its original source comparison is still
\[
 B_N^2e_N\le |K_N|^2\le(197/196)B_N^2e_N.
\]
The minimum and determinant have not been evaluated geometrically.
In particular the error above gives absolute, not source-relative,
precision for \(e_N\). It can exceed an exponentially small minimum.
The missing hyperbolic-volume rate and the fixed-short-filling lower
bound remain open.

## The faithful beta construction now includes even levels, 23 November

The [all-level local lift](research_all_level_faithful_beta_adapter.md)
extends the faithful-row construction below to every \(N\ge2\).
At odd levels it uses the earlier charged kernels. At even levels
it explicitly defines lifted local kernels, evaluates their selected
boundary packets, and proves their completion equals the original
physical crossings. It assumes no existing even-level charged invariant.

Put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(d=N-1\), \(x=-q^{-1}\)
and \(\gamma=-q\). The Gaussian
\[
 g(j)=\gamma^{j^2}
\]
is periodic modulo \(N\), and
\(g(j+k)=g(j)g(k)Q^{jk}\), for both parities.
Use this Gaussian in the displayed nine local kernels, keeping their
integer charge marks modulo \(2N\). The original decoration roots,
all nine finite normalizers, and every edge factor remain.

The two observed slices have \(k_2=0\), so the distinguished retained
beta quotient is one term by term. Three exact cyclic beta sums and
the remaining finite Fourier sums give, after the specified inverse
boundary factors,
\[
 w=x^{-d}e_d^{\mathsf T},\qquad v=x^de_0.
\]
These are exactly the first row of the stripped positive crossing
and the last column of its stripped inverse. The finite calculation
retains both endpoint coefficients of the rational rewrite; its
high coefficient does not vanish.

The continuant inverses \(I_+,I_-\) of the full middle-degree
Casimir therefore give
\[
 R_+=\kappa I_+(w)(\Omega),\qquad
 R_-=\kappa^{-1}I_-(v)(\Omega),\qquad
 \kappa=q^{d^2/2},
\]
at every level. Their full minimal polynomial retains the first
derivatives at double Casimir roots.

Reconstructing before assembly gives the same complete leaf operators
in every fixed Conway expression, including arbitrary fixed short
integer powers. Thus the original compiler, budgets, degree-four
objective and minimum are unchanged. This does not bound the inverse
reconstruction on arbitrary data or make its physical norm small.
At even levels the conclusion concerns this specified local lift and
completion; no global charged move theory is inferred.
The geometric lower bound remains open.

## Faithful boundary reconstruction removes the retained beta factor, 23 November

The [faithful boundary adapter](research_faithful_boundary_beta_adapter_v2.md)
gives an exact way to remove the large retained quotient from the first
cyclic beta elimination at a crossing. It uses a full boundary packet,
followed by an explicit reconstruction of the original operator. It
does not estimate that quotient by a smaller operator.

Let \(N\ge2\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(d=N-1\), and let
\(A=\Omega|_{W_d}\) be the original pair Casimir
on the physical middle degree
\[
 W_d=\operatorname{span}\{e_j=|j,d-j\rangle:0\le j\le d\}.
\]
This is a complex symmetric irreducible tridiagonal matrix with full
minimal polynomial \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), where \(T_N\) is the
Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. Consequently both maps
\[
 f\longmapsto e_0^{\mathsf T}f(A),\qquad
 f\longmapsto f(A)e_d,\qquad f\in H_N=\mathbb C[z]/P_N,
\]
are isomorphisms onto \(N\) coordinates. They retain the derivatives
at double Casimir roots. They are not observations of the cup alone.
Here \(H_N\) is the full algebra of two-head Hopf boxes.

The reconstruction is explicit. Write \(a_j=A_{jj}\) and
\(b_j=A_{j,j+1}\ne0\), and define
\[
 p_0=1,\quad p_1=z-a_0,\quad
 p_{j+1}=(z-a_j)p_j-b_{j-1}^2p_{j-1},\qquad
 B_j=\prod_{h<j}b_h .
\]
Then \(e_0^{\mathsf T}p_j(A)/B_j=e_j^{\mathsf T}\), so the row
inverse is \(I_+(w)=\sum_jw_jp_j/B_j\). Reversing the diagonal and
offdiagonal lists gives the last-column inverse \(I_-\); its product
denominator is \(\prod_{h<j}b_{d-1-h}\). These are full polynomial
reconstructions modulo \(P_N\), with no eigenvalue-only quotient.

The actual signed port maps select the following boundary differences:
\[
 \mathbf k_+(0,j)=(1,0,[j+1],[-j]),\qquad
 \mathbf k_-(i,d)=([-i],0,1,[i+1]).
\]
The first fixes the whole positive output to \((0,d)\) and varies
every middle-degree input. The second fixes the negative input to
\((d,0)\) and varies every middle-degree output. Brackets mean
reduction to \(0,\ldots,d\).

Both selections have \(k_2=0\). The retained beta quotient is therefore
\[
 \frac{\overline W_{0235}(K+L)}
      {\overline W_{0235}(K+L-k_2)}=1
\]
for every internal tuple, before summation. Strip the same nonzero
port scalars and use the same \(N^{-4}\) paired-fiber average as in
the original array. The ratio-deleted array then has the entire
positive row or negative column of the original stripped crossing.
If \(Y_\pm^\flat\) denotes its pulled-back middle-degree matrix, the
full crossing identities are
\[
 R_+=\kappa\,I_+(\rho_+Y_+^\flat)(\Omega),\qquad
 R_-=\kappa^{-1}I_-(\rho_-Y_-^\flat)(\Omega),
 \qquad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}.
\]
Here \(\rho_+\) extracts the first row and \(\rho_-\) the last column.
The inverse port scalars, charge phases, Cartan factors and all
decoration roots are retained in these identities.

At the proved odd levels, reconstruct each crossing before taking
products or genuine turns.
Every resulting subtree is then the same element of \(H_N\) as before,
so any fixed Conway construction has exactly its original marked
scalar. This includes arbitrary fixed short integer powers; it is
not a large-twist assertion. For the existing degree-four formulation,
the same leaf elements give the same local tensors, budgets, objective
and minimum. This statement concerns that same compiler, not a new
optimization over the raw beta variables.

The observed signed data are sparse: their Euclidean norms, with
Cartan factors restored, are one. Reconstruction gives
\(\|R_\pm\|_{\rm Newton}=\sqrt N\). This is only the norm ratio for
these particular original packets in the stated Newton metric.
The general reconstruction kernels and their physical norm costs
have not disappeared. In particular the raw ratio-deleted arrays
need not be Hopf boxes, and reconstruction is not omitted when they
are sewn. Individual ray-modified patterns also retain their own
transported co-source.

The algebraic observations and inverses hold at every \(N\ge2\).
The literal charged-array beta application proved here is at odd
\(N>2\), the scope of its source. Its normals are fixed-root Casimir
derivatives, not moving-meridian or quantum-parameter derivatives.
No even-level charged extension, positive global gluing, nonzero
geometric coefficient or new volume lower bound is inferred.
The finite-exception target remains open.

## Retained Pachner coupons can have exponential condition number, 23 November

The actual residual coupon in the first source-preserving beta move
need not be a scalar or a uniformly subexponential operator. This
statement concerns its full boundary action in a common Hermitian
metric. It does not estimate the assembled original observation.

Write \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), \(d=N-1\), and use the complete physical
flag adapter [PF, (19)--(23)]. For a recorded Fermat root
\(\beta^N=1-t^N\), the boundary coupon is
\[
 \mathcal F_t|m,s\rangle=R_m(tQ^s)|m,s\rangle,\qquad
 R_m(z)=\beta^{-m}\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-zQ^j),
 \qquad 0\leq m,s<N .
 \tag{PC1}
\]
The empty product is one. With the full invertible flag frame
\(\mathcal B\) of [PF], or its source-fixed rescaling
\(\widetilde{\mathcal B}\), its actual physical expression is
\[
 \mathcal O_t=\mathcal B\mathcal F_t\mathcal B^{-1}
   =\mathcal C_t\mathcal U^{-1}\mathcal C_t^{-1}\mathcal U .
 \tag{PC2}
\]
This equality retains the cyclic corner and all \(N^2\) boundary
coordinates. The complete exterior row is transported by the inverse
dual, as in [PF, (26)]; it is not replaced by a favorable cap.

Fix the nonreal regular central parameter and principal roots
\[
 A_0=\frac{1+i}{2},\qquad
 t_N=\exp\!\left(\frac{\operatorname{Log}A_0}{N}\right),\qquad
 \beta_N=\exp\!\left(\frac{\operatorname{Log}(1-A_0)}{N}\right).
 \tag{PC3}
\]
Then \(t_N^N+\beta_N^N=1\), neither root vanishes, and
\[
 |t_N|=|\beta_N|=\rho_N=2^{-1/(2N)},\qquad
 \arg t_N=\frac{\pi}{4N}.
\]
All factors in (PC1) are nonzero, since \(t_N^N=A_0\ne1\).
For \(N\geq4\), set \(m_N=\lfloor N/4\rfloor\) and
\(s_N=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\). For \(0\leq j<m_N\), the unreduced
angle of \(t_NQ^{s_N+j}\) satisfies
\[
 \frac{\pi}{2}
 <\pi-\frac{3\pi}{4N}
 \leq\frac{2\pi(s_N+j)}{N}+\frac{\pi}{4N}
 \leq\frac{3\pi}{2}-\frac{7\pi}{4N}
 <\frac{3\pi}{2}.
 \tag{PC4}
\]
The lower estimate uses \(s_N\geq(N-1)/2\), and the upper one uses
\(s_N\leq N/2\) and \(j\leq N/4-1\). Hence every displayed cosine
is negative. For its corresponding angle \(\theta_j\),
\[
 \frac{|1-t_NQ^{s_N+j}|^2}{|\beta_N|^2}
   =1+\rho_N^{-2}-2\rho_N^{-1}\cos\theta_j>2,
 \qquad
 |R_{m_N}(t_NQ^{s_N})|>2^{m_N/2}.
 \tag{PC5}
\]
Another eigenvalue is \(R_0=1\). Thus for every single positive
Hermitian Gram \(G\), with its induced operator norm,
\[
 \operatorname{cond}_G(\mathcal F_{t_N})
   >2^{m_N/2},\qquad
 \operatorname{cond}_G(\mathcal O_{t_N})
   >2^{m_N/2}.
 \tag{PC6}
\]
Indeed \(\|T\|_G\geq\max|\lambda(T)|\) and
\(\|T^{-1}\|_G\geq1/\min|\lambda(T)|\). The ratio of the two
specified eigenvalue moduli already exceeds \(2^{m_N/2}\).
Similarity preserves these eigenvalues, so this argument permits
every common positive Gram, without assuming a tame flag frame.
For any nonzero scalar \(c_N\), the condition number is unchanged;
consequently, for either operator \(T\) in (PC6),
\[
 \max\{\|c_NT\|_G,\|(c_NT)^{-1}\|_G\}>2^{m_N/4}.
 \tag{PC7}
\]
In particular a common peripheral scalar, including a factor
specializing to \(2\), cannot make both directions subexponential.

This coupon is the retained ratio of the actual source, not an
independent factorial partition function. In [R, (31)] and
[PF, (18),(19)], \(t=\alpha_{0235}Q^{r_0}\), where the internal
\(r_0=u_0+v_0+s_0+z_0+2\) is independent of the external
\((m,s)=([-k_2],[-k_1])\). Taking \(\alpha_{0235}=t_N\), replace
\(s_N\) above by \([s_N-r_0]\). This gives exactly the same eigenvalue
and bound for every internal tuple, with the same \(\beta_N\).
For the negative crossing the retained ratio is the mixed-index
Schur action \(R_{d-a}(tQ^c)\). The original ordered pivotal bend
in [NB, (4),(11)] makes it
\(\mathcal F_t\otimes I\) on the bent coefficient space; the physical
frame then gives \(\mathcal O_t\otimes I\). The bend has exact
Hilbert--Schmidt costs \(N\) and \(N^{-1}\), and its full exterior
is exactly [NB, (14),(15)]. No positive left-output placement is
asserted for the negative tensor before that bend.

The special cup column
\(\widetilde{\mathcal B}^{-1}p=N^2|0,1\rangle\) of [PF, (29)]
is fixed by (PC1). It does not imply that the whole remaining
source tensor takes values in \(m=0\). In fact [R, (8),(9)] gives
\((M_+^0)_{d,d;d,d}=d_d\ne0\): the endpoint inequalities force all
three transfers to be zero, and the diagonal factors of the
preparation and its inverse cancel. The actual port choice
\(\mathbf k=(1,1,0,0)\) in [R, (17)] maps to this entry, with
nonzero port scalar and \(\sum k_m=2\). If every remaining
\(Y_{r_0}\) had range in \(m=0\), multiplication by the diagonal
\(\mathcal F_{r_0}\) and summation could not produce this \(m=d\)
output. This only rules out a universal \(m=0\) range restriction
on the entire all-boundary tensor. It does not decide whether the
specific original cup-generated column, its Ward identities or a
coherent neighboring gluing avoids the growing eigenspaces.

The physical coupon and bend identities hold at all \(N\geq2\);
the estimate above holds at all \(N\geq4\). Their literal charged
nine-cell source occurrence is currently proved only for odd
\(N>2\), so the stated source application is at odd \(N\geq5\).
This does not show that the actual exterior samples the growing
eigenvector or that compensation fails after the complete gluing.
Independent input and output metrics, compensating neighboring
frames and the full co-source remain to be analyzed. No integrated
source-energy lower bound, scalar noncancellation or volume result

## Scalar budgets preserve exponential packet scales in the fixed physical metric, 23 November

Scalar redistribution of the physical budgets has a limited range when
their total product is preserved. The following estimate concerns the
fixed uniform physical Hilbert--Schmidt metric, with every short piece
retained as its literal crossing, product and turn circuit. It is not
a restriction on arbitrary nonuniform matrix Grams.

Fix a finite literal compiler with \(p\) proper product gates. Every
prescribed leaf is the full actual \(R^{n_\ell}\), with
\(n_\ell\in\mathbb Z\), including zero and negative powers. Its closing
is \(\eta_N\lambda\), where \(\eta_N\ne0\) is the original known scalar
and \(\lambda\in\{\lambda_0,\phi\}\). All normal channels remain.
Use the standard physical budgets
\[
 b_\ell=16\max(1,\|R^{n_\ell}\|_{\rm ph}),\qquad
 b_{\rm turn}=b_{\rm product}=16,\qquad
 b_\rho=16\max(1,|\eta_N|),\qquad B_{\rm ph}=\prod_vb_v .
 \tag{BR1}
\]
Consider any other positive scalar budgets \(\widehat b_v\) for these
same maps and this same metric. Assume every normalized leaf vector,
turn operator, separate-input bilinear product and original closing row
has norm at most \(1/16\), and
\(\prod_v\widehat b_v=B_{\rm ph}\). Only these norm conditions are
used below; no new semidefinite exactness assertion is needed.
Put \(\alpha_v=\widehat b_v/b_v\) and
\(\kappa_{\eta,N}=\max(1,|\eta_N|)/|\eta_N|\).

The actual crossing has unit-modulus values
\(\kappa(-1)^jq^{j(j+1)}\) at every Casimir root and is a unit in
the full Hermite algebra. Since \(P_N(\Omega)=0\), every eigenvalue
of the physical \(N^2\)-dimensional matrix \(R^{n_\ell}\) has
modulus one. Unitary triangularization bounds its squared
Hilbert--Schmidt norm below by the sum of squared diagonal entries.
Thus \(\|R^{n_\ell}\|_{\rm ph}\ge N\), also for \(n_\ell=0\).
The leaf budget in (BR1) is consequently \(16\|R^{n_\ell}\|_{\rm ph}\)
and is already minimal under the stated norm requirement. The
genuine turn is unitary, so its budget \(16\) is minimal too.

The physical identity box has norm \(N\). Testing multiplication on
the two unit inputs \(I/N,I/N\) gives bilinear norm at least \(1/N\).
Moreover \(\lambda_0(I)=1\), \(\phi(\mathcal TI)=1\), and
\(\|\mathcal TI\|_{\rm ph}=\|I\|_{\rm ph}=N\). Hence either original
closing has dual norm at least \(1/N\). These facts prove
\[
 \alpha_\ell\ge1,\qquad \alpha_{\rm turn}\ge1,\qquad
 \alpha_{\rm product}\ge N^{-1},\qquad
 \alpha_\rho\ge(\kappa_{\eta,N}N)^{-1},\qquad
 \prod_v\alpha_v=1 .
 \tag{BR2}
\]
No normal direction was replaced by a nodal-value quotient in deriving
the crossing spectrum or these physical norm bounds.

For a proper vertex \(v\), let \(B_v,\widehat B_v\) be the respective
budget products in its entire proper subtree, and let \(p_v\) count
that subtree's product gates. Multiplying (BR2) inside the subtree
gives its lower bound. Its complement contains \(p-p_v\) products
and the closing root, so multiplying there and using the last identity
of (BR2) gives its upper bound:
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 N^{-p_v}\le\frac{\widehat B_v}{B_v}
           \le\kappa_{\eta,N}N^{p-p_v+1}.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{BR3}
\]
This also checks the root bookkeeping: the top proper subtree has
\(p_v=p\), and its ratio is the reciprocal of
\(\widehat b_\rho/b_\rho\).

There are exact packet and residual identities behind this estimate.
Let \(\Phi_v\) and \(\widehat\Phi_v\) be the maps normalized by their
own local budgets, and put \(s_v=B_v/\widehat B_v\). For any packet
field \(x\), define \(\widehat x_v=s_vx_v\). The subtree products give
\(\widehat b_v/b_v=(\prod_cs_c)/s_v\), where the product runs over
the children. Constants, linear turns and bilinear products therefore
satisfy
\[
 \widehat\Phi_v((\widehat x_c)_c)=s_v\Phi_v((x_c)_c),\qquad
 \widehat G_v(\widehat x)=s_vG_v(x),\qquad
 \widehat L\widehat x_{\rm top}=Lx_{\rm top},\qquad
 \widehat k=K_N/B_{\rm ph}=k .
 \tag{BR4}
\]
The root identity uses preservation of the total budget.
These are ambient identities; a rescaled trial must still satisfy
its own packet-ball constraints. In particular
\(\widehat a_v=s_va_v\) for the true normalized forward fields.
Differences of any two associated packet fields scale by the same
\(s_v\).

For a fixed compiler, (BR3) gives
\[
 (\kappa_{\eta,N}N^{p-p_v+1})^{-1}\le s_v\le N^{p_v}.
 \tag{BR5}
\]
If \(\log\kappa_{\eta,N}=o(N)\), every multiplier has zero
exponential rate. This condition includes the recorded unit phases
and fixed powers of \(N\); nonzeroness of \(\eta_N\) alone would
not imply it. For every nonzero associated packet or residual error,
the scaled logarithms of its two norms consequently differ by
\(o(1)\). Since \(k\) is unchanged, the same holds for their error
ratios to \(|k|\) whenever \(k\ne0\). Exact zero errors stay zero.
If \(\kappa_{\eta,N}\) is polynomial, all bounds in (BR3),(BR5)
are polynomial. Scalar redistribution alone therefore cannot turn
an algebraic-size error into an exponentially smaller source-relative
error.

This does not compare different trial families or assert equality of
their variational minima. It does not apply unchanged after replacing
a short component by an arbitrary prescribed leaf, whose norm may be
below one. Nor does it exclude a genuinely anisotropic matrix Gram:
such a construction needs its own actual local norm, normal-channel
and closing estimates. The argument supplies no geometric lower
bound, positive dual witness or volume theorem.

## Analytic proofs replace the scalar comparison tables, 23 November

The [analytic gap estimates](research_conway_analytic_gap_estimates.md)
prove both scalar lemmas used in the frozen Conway source bounds with
their stated margins. The two-leaf comparisons have gap greater than
\(1/100\) throughout the closed output-slope interval
\([-\log4,\log4]\). The single-attachment comparison has gap greater
than \(1/2500\) whenever both its child and parent parameters are proper.
These proofs remove the 288 two-leaf and 880 attachment comparisons as
dependencies of the two lemmas.

Here the profiles are exactly those of the frozen source paper:
\[
 J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du,\qquad
 g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x),\quad
 \widetilde g(x)=g(\max(x,1/4)),\quad k(x)=-2J(x/2).
\]
The complete multiplication action and domain are unchanged. Equations
(4) and (7) of the new proof state the full dual comparisons explicitly;
in particular the alias input ranges and the core plateau are retained.

For an attachment, write \(X=\cot(\pi a)\),
\(Y=\sqrt{1+B^2-X^2}\), \(Y_p=Y/(X+B)\), where
\(1/2<X<1\), \(X+B>0\), and \(0<Y,Y_p<1\).
When \(X\le2/3\), the variables \(p=Y/X,r=Y_p/X\) satisfy
\[
 p,r>1,\qquad p^2<2r,\quad r^2<2p,\qquad
 X=\frac{\sqrt{1+p^2+r^2}-1}{pr}.
\]
An explicit feasible inner optimizer shows that increasing the smaller
of \(p,r\) until they agree, then increasing both toward \(2\), decreases
the pure-minus-alias gap. This path remains proper until its limiting
endpoint. A concave tangent and a convex-derivative integral bound at
that endpoint give the analytic margin
\[
 \Delta_{\rm attachment}>\frac{2303}{221760}>\frac1{100}.
\]
For \(X\ge2/3\), the existing one-leaf tangent argument is reproved
directly, with margin
\(57269/136687500>1/2500\).

For the two-leaf comparisons, the optimized alias output is strictly
larger than the pure output at the same slope. Envelope differentiation
therefore reduces both gaps to slope \(-\log4\), allowing boundary
maxima of the final conjugate. At that slope the one-alias gap dominates
the attachment endpoint above. For two aliases, a one-variable
curvature bound gives the separate margin
\[
 \Delta_{\rm two\ aliases}>\frac{169}{6820}>\frac1{100}.
\]
The proof derives the required stationary branches and verifies their
strict feasibility before using their derivatives.

There is a correction to the earlier
[two-leaf response note](actual_conway_two_leaf_monotone_alias_response.md),
equation (6). With \(U=\cot(\pi x)\), \(V=\cot(\pi y)\),
\(Z=\cot(\pi b)\), and \(w=V-Z\), the plateau relation is
\[
 U=\frac{1+Z^2-w^2}{2w},
\]
without the printed initial \(+Z\). The derivative and output-slope
formulas there remain correct. The new proof derives the corrected
relation and its matching at the plateau seam; the earlier final is
unchanged.

The attachment reduction uses its actual proper parameter region. It
does not reprove the older auxiliary inequality on the entire artificial
slope square. It suffices for the stated source lemma, whose hypotheses
include both proper inequalities. This is an analytic simplification of
the existing source upper bounds. It does not produce a nonzero
geometric contribution after arbitrary short partial filling or prove
a new knot volume identity.

## A finite boundary shell controls a connected component, 23 November

A connected short component can be replaced by an optimization over a
finite shell of its boundary, after one full reference solve. The error
is one-sided and decreases geometrically with the shell radius, with
constants independent of the quantum level and component size. The
replacement keeps the original quartic gates and their signed constants.
It does not give an explicit polynomial formula for their eliminated
boundary value or remove the reference solve.

Use either the complete Newton metric of the
[normalized source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md), or the
[uniform physical metric](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md)
with its own unchanged budgets. These are separate numerical minima.
In either choice every normalized leaf, turn, product and original
closing row has vector, linear or bilinear norm at most
\(\sigma=1/16\). All packets retain their full \(N\) complex coordinates,
including the repeated-root directions.

Let \(\Omega\) be any connected component of the literal tree, possibly
containing the closing root. Write \(b\) for its entering packets and,
for a proper component, its outgoing packet; write \(z\) for all
internal packets. All minima below impose the original packet unit
balls. With
\(t=1/4\), retain the redistributed potentials
\[
 V_v=\|\Phi_v-x_v\|^2-t\|x_v\|^2+
                 t\sum_{c\ {\rm child\ of}\ v}\|x_c\|^2,\qquad
 V_\rho=|Lx_{\rm top}|^2+t\|x_{\rm top}\|^2 .
\]
Set
\[
 F_\Omega(z,b)=\sum_{v\in\Omega}V_v,\qquad
 W_\Omega(b)=\min_z F_\Omega(z,b),\qquad z_*(b)=\arg\min_zF_\Omega .
 \tag{BS1}
\]
The internal quadratic shifts cancel. Thus the internal problem is the
original clamped residual problem of the
[connected-block theorem](research_connected_conway_block_boundary_energy.md).
Its minimizer is unique and each internal packet has norm at most
\(33/256\), for every feasible boundary. The same assertion holds when
any additional internal packets are fixed at feasible values: its
half-gradient components still have that bound and its internal Hessian
is a principal block of the original Hessian. Hence these minima are
interior and smooth on a neighborhood of the closed boundary domain.
No active-constraint inverse is used below.

Fix a feasible reference boundary \(b^0\), and retain its full solution
\(z^0=z_*(b^0)\). Distances mean undirected edge distances between packet
vertices in the original compiler tree. A parent and child have distance
one, siblings distance two; this is not distance between color indices.
For an integer \(h\ge0\), let
\[
 Z_h=\{v\ {\rm internal}:\operatorname{dist}(v,\partial\Omega)\le2h\},
 \qquad D_h=\{v\ {\rm internal}\}\setminus Z_h .
\]
Define the actual restricted boundary value
\[
 W_{\Omega,h}^{\,b^0}(b)
   =\min_{\|z_v\|\le1,\ v\in Z_h}
           F_\Omega(z_{Z_h},z^0_{D_h},b).
 \tag{BS2}
\]
Every frozen packet retains all its coordinates. In particular, every
gate whose arguments become fixed contributes its exact constant; if
the closing packet is frozen, its original marked closing term is kept.

**Boundary-shell estimate.** Put
\[
 q_0=\frac{67}{256},\qquad
 C_0=\frac{323}{256}\left(\frac{33}{95}\right)^2<\frac16,
 \qquad \epsilon_h=C_0q_0^{2h}.
\]
Uniformly for every feasible \(b,b^0\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 0\le W_{\Omega,h}^{\,b^0}(b)-W_\Omega(b)
                 \le\epsilon_h\|b-b^0\|^2 .
 \quad}                                                    \tag{BS3}
\]
Moreover these upper values decrease to the exact value as the shell
grows, and
\[
 W_{\Omega,h}^{\,b^0}(b^0)=W_\Omega(b^0),\qquad
 \nabla_bW_{\Omega,h}^{\,b^0}(b^0)=\nabla_bW_\Omega(b^0).
 \tag{BS4}
\]
If all internal vertices lie in the shell, equality holds for every
boundary. An empty boundary makes the assertion tautological: the
reference solve is already the whole component minimum.

Here is the complete quantitative proof. All Hessian blocks use real
coordinates with inner product \(\operatorname{Re}(u^*v)\). At any
feasible field an internal diagonal block is exactly
\[
 H_{vv}=2I+2T_v^*T_v,\qquad \|T_v\|\le\sigma ,
 \tag{BS5}
\]
where \(T_v\) is its derivative into its one parent residual, or the
original closing row at the root. A parent--child off-diagonal block
has norm at most \(2\sigma\). A sibling block has norm at most
\[
 2\sigma^2+2\sigma(1+\sigma)=2\sigma+4\sigma^2 .
\]
The latter terms come respectively from the product of the two first
derivatives and the residual paired with the bilinear second derivative.
Taking real parts introduces no additional factor. There are at most
three parent--child neighbors and one sibling at each packet. Thus the
absolute block row and column sums off the diagonal are at most
\[
 a=8\sigma+4\sigma^2=\frac{33}{64}.
\]
Boundary redistribution changes no mixed block. The block norm
inequality, and the same inequality on any clamped submatrix, give
\[
 m_0I\le H_{zz}\le M_0I,\qquad
 \|H_{zb}\|\le a,\qquad
 m_0=\frac{95}{64},\quad M_0=\frac{323}{128}.
 \tag{BS6}
\]
These estimates hold throughout the feasible internal balls, not only
at their minima. They use the bilinear norm of a product, so apply in
the uniform physical metric without changing its constant budgets.

At \(z_*(b)\), let \(R=I-H_{zz}/2\). Then \(\|R\|\le q_0\).
For \(h\ge0\), with the empty sum interpreted as zero, set
\[
 P_h=\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}R^j,\qquad
 H_{zz}^{-1}-P_h=H_{zz}^{-1}R^h,\qquad
 \|H_{zz}^{-1}-P_h\|\le m_0^{-1}q_0^h .
 \tag{BS7}
\]
A Hessian block can couple only vertices at distance at most two.
Consequently \(P_hH_{zb}\) has internal support within distance \(2h\)
of the boundary. Differentiate the interior stationary equations:
\[
 Dz_*(b)=-H_{zz}^{-1}H_{zb},\qquad
 \|\Pi_{D_h}Dz_*(b)\|\le\frac{33}{95}q_0^h .
 \tag{BS8}
\]
The second estimate follows by subtracting \(P_hH_{zb}\), whose deep
projection is zero. Integrating along the feasible boundary segment
from \(b^0\) to \(b\) proves
\[
 \|(z_*(b)-z^0)_{D_h}\|
                 \le\frac{33}{95}q_0^h\|b-b^0\| .
 \tag{BS9}
\]
As a trial in (BS2), keep the shell coordinates of \(z_*(b)\) and replace
only its deep coordinates by \(z^0\). This is feasible. Internal
stationarity at \(z_*(b)\) and the upper bound in (BS6), applied on the
segment to that trial, bound its extra cost by \(M_0/2\) times the
squared norm in (BS9). Restriction gives the opposite inequality.
This proves (BS3). Enlarging the shell enlarges the feasible set.
At \(b^0\), the full minimizer is feasible for every restriction.
The envelope formula at this same interior minimizer proves (BS4).

The restricted problem still has an exact degree-four local moment
description. In the
[gate-local formulation](research_conway_gate_local_semidefinite_gluing.md),
fix the first moments of the deep packets to \(z^0\), as well as the
specified boundary means. The local Jensen inequality bounds every
feasible moment objective from below by the corresponding consistent
mean-field cost, hence by (BS2); evaluation at its minimizer attains it.
Equivalently substitute the fixed deep packets into the local
polynomials first. No degree increases, and wholly fixed gates need
only their signed constants. For the physical metric, the local
matrix square identities of the
[physical certificate](research_conway_physical_matrix_degree_four_certificate.md)
give the same Jensen proof, as in the existing physical local-gluing
entry below. No small coefficient-tensor norm is assumed there.

For any connected partition, (BS3) can be summed on its consistent
boundary packets:
\[
 \sum_\Omega\!\left[
 W_{\Omega,h}^{\,b^0_\Omega}(b_\Omega)
                   -\epsilon_h\|b_\Omega-b^0_\Omega\|^2\right]
 \ \le\ \sum_\Omega W_\Omega(b_\Omega)
 \ \le\ \sum_\Omega W_{\Omega,h}^{\,b^0_\Omega}(b_\Omega).
 \tag{BS10}
\]
The middle minimum is the original \(e_*\). Every original budget and
closing stays unchanged, and no separate comparison loss is multiplied
for each short component. The errors use the full boundary direct-sum
norm; local negative constants must not be replaced by zero.

This also gives two convex boundary bounds. Set
\[
 \eta_h=\frac16q_0^{2h},\qquad
 U_{\Omega,h}=W_{\Omega,h}^{\,b^0},\qquad
 L_{\Omega,h}(b)=U_{\Omega,h}(b)-\eta_h\|b-b^0\|^2 .
\]
Then \(L_{\Omega,h}\le W_\Omega\le U_{\Omega,h}\).
The [coarse boundary proof](research_conway_coarse_boundary_force_certificate.md)
gives modulus \(\mu=45/128\) to the shifted fine component and hence
to its clamped partial minimum \(U_{\Omega,h}\); its pointwise proof
uses only the same bilinear norm bounds in either metric.
Thus \(D^2L_{\Omega,h}\ge(\mu-2\eta_h)I\ge(7/384)I\).
For \(h\ge1\), both bounds have exact degree-four local moment lifts.
Before taking moments, subtract each boundary quadratic from the local
polynomial of its unique bag. Its Hessian consumes at most \(2\eta_h I\)
in that bag, less than the local Hessian-certificate modulus \(31/128\).
The remaining local certificate and its integrated Jensen inequality
therefore retain degree four. With \(B\) the original budget for the
chosen metric and \(\gamma=197/196\), the consistent-boundary minima obey
\[
 B^2\max\!\left(0,\min\sum_\Omega L_{\Omega,h}\right)
       \le |K_N|^2
       \le\gamma B^2\min\sum_\Omega U_{\Omega,h}.
 \tag{BS11}
\]
All reference solves and signed constant terms remain in these programs.

The earlier block and coarse-force results already give exact convex
boundary values, their degree-four lifts and uniform conditioning.
The additional assertion here is the nonlinear frozen-interior estimate
(BS3): after one complete reference solve, only a boundary shell remains
free, with an explicit error for all other feasible boundaries. A shell
packet still has \(N\) complex coordinates. The reference packets are
not supplied by this theorem, storage for them has not disappeared,
and a fixed shell gives absolute rather than relative precision for an
exponentially small source. No scalar secular formula, geometric lower
bound or new volume theorem follows.

connected block

287857c29b2b0f8cbdc0a0fe71d05e16f7eaac0133e93936f2216a750c434eb3;

The finite-series inverse-decay method is standard; no general novelty
is claimed for it and no external proof is imported.
The finite-series and nonlinear value estimates above are proved here.

## A certified residual removes the exact shell reference solve, 23 November

The boundary-shell reduction above also works with any feasible reference
field. A nonnegative scalar certificate bounds its error and supplies
convex degree-four lower and upper programs. No exact internal reference
minimum is required. The price is an explicit additive residual term,
which must remain when components are assembled.

Keep \(F_\Omega(z,b)\), \(W_\Omega(b)\), the packet unit balls and the
original-tree shell \(Z_h,D_h\) of (BS1)--(BS2). The Newton and uniform
physical versions use their own unchanged metrics and budgets. Set
\[
 a=\frac{33}{64},\qquad m_0=\frac{95}{64},\qquad
 M_0=\frac{323}{128},\qquad
 \theta=\frac a2=\frac{33}{128}.
\]
Choose any feasible boundary \(b^0\) and any feasible internal field
\(\widetilde z\). For each internal packet define the known number
\[
 r_v=\|(\nabla_{z,\mathbb R}F_\Omega)(\widetilde z,b^0)_v\|.
 \tag{RS1}
\]
These are norms of the full real gradient blocks for the inner product
\(\operatorname{Re}(u^*v)\). They include the original closing term when
present. They are neither the recursion residuals nor the coherent
closing correction of the source-visible transport theorem.

Index a real symmetric scalar matrix \(\mathsf A\) by the component's
internal and boundary packets. Its diagonal is zero. Put
\(2\sigma=1/8\) on a parent--child pair in a component gate,
\(2\sigma+4\sigma^2=9/64\) on its two product inputs, and zero elsewhere,
where \(\sigma=1/16\). The real mixed-Hessian blocks have these norm
bounds by (BS5)--(BS6), uniformly throughout the feasible balls.
Each packet has at most three parent--child neighbors and one sibling,
so every row sum is at most \(a\). Write
\[
 \mathsf S=2I-\mathsf A_{zz},\qquad
 \mathsf C=\mathsf A_{zz}/2.
\]
Then \(\|\mathsf C\|\le\theta<1\), \(\mathsf S\ge m_0I\), and
\[
 \mathsf S^{-1}=\frac12\sum_{j\ge0}\mathsf C^j
 \quad\hbox{is entrywise nonnegative},\qquad
 \|\mathsf S^{-1}\|\le m_0^{-1},\qquad
 \|\mathsf A_{zb}\|\le a.                         \tag{RS2}
\]
All scalar vector inequalities below are componentwise.

Supply any nonnegative scalar vector \(w\) satisfying the finite
certificate
\[
                    \mathsf S w\ge r.            \tag{RS3}
\]
For example \(w=\mathsf S^{-1}r\) works and is the smallest such
nonnegative supersolution. An exact scalar solve is optional too.
For a nonempty internal list and any integer \(k\ge0\), the finite vector
\[
 w^{(k)}=\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\mathsf C^j r
       +\frac{\theta^k\|r\|_\infty}{m_0}\mathbf1
                                                        \tag{RS4}
\]
satisfies (RS3). Indeed applying \(\mathsf S\) to the finite sum gives
\(r-\mathsf C^kr\), while
\(\mathsf S\mathbf1\ge m_0\mathbf1\) and
\(\mathsf C^kr\le\theta^k\|r\|_\infty\mathbf1\).
The sum is zero for \(k=0\); each finite power uses only the scalar
packet adjacency. Empty internal lists require no certificate.

Freeze the deep packets at this feasible reference and define
\[
 U_{\Omega,h}(b)
   =\min_{\|z_v\|\le1,\ v\in Z_h}
           F_\Omega(z_{Z_h},\widetilde z_{D_h},b),\qquad
 \beta_{\Omega,h}=\|w_{D_h}\|.                    \tag{RS5}
\]
Every signed constant from a fixed gate, and the original marked
closing if its packet is fixed, remains in this objective.
For every integer \(h\ge0\) and every feasible \(b\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 0\le U_{\Omega,h}(b)-W_\Omega(b)
 \le\frac{M_0}{2}
       \left(\beta_{\Omega,h}
               +\frac{33}{95}\theta^h\|b-b^0\|\right)^2
 \le M_0\beta_{\Omega,h}^2
               +\frac13\theta^{2h}\|b-b^0\|^2 .
 \quad}                                                   \tag{RS6}
\]
The bounds are uniform in the level, component size and fixed short
coefficients after their original budgets are retained.

Here is the proof without an unknown reference minimizer. Put
\(z^*=z_*(b)\), \(\delta b=b-b^0\), and average the internal Hessian
and its mixed block along the feasible segment from
\((\widetilde z,b^0)\) to \((z^*,b)\). Denote these averages by
\(\overline H_{zz},\overline H_{zb}\). Internal stationarity gives
\[
 \overline H_{zz}(\widetilde z-z^*)
       =(\nabla_{z,\mathbb R}F_\Omega)(\widetilde z,b^0)
                            +\overline H_{zb}\delta b.    \tag{RS7}
\]
Each internal diagonal block of \(\overline H_{zz}\) is at least
\(2I\): it is the average of \(2I+2T_v^*T_v\).
All off-diagonal and mixed block norms are bounded by the corresponding
entries of \(\mathsf A\). Therefore, for
\(u_v=\|\widetilde z_v-z_v^*\|\) and
\(d_j=\|\delta b_j\|\), solving each diagonal block in (RS7) yields
\[
 2u\le r+\mathsf A_{zz}u+\mathsf A_{zb}d,\qquad
 u\le\mathsf S^{-1}(r+\mathsf A_{zb}d)
                         \le w+\mathsf S^{-1}\mathsf A_{zb}d.
 \tag{RS8}
\]
This uses the positive inverse (RS2) and the supplied inequality
(RS3), not values of the unknown averaged Hessian.

A nonzero entry of \(\mathsf A\) joins packets at original-tree
distance at most two. Hence
\(\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}\mathsf C^j\mathsf A_{zb}\) has no internal
support in \(D_h\). Its omitted tail has norm at most
\(m_0^{-1}\theta^h a\), by (RS2). Taking the deep direct-sum norm
in (RS8) proves
\[
 \|(\widetilde z-z_*(b))_{D_h}\|
       \le\beta_{\Omega,h}
                     +\frac{33}{95}\theta^h\|b-b^0\|.     \tag{RS9}
\]
Replace only the deep coordinates of \(z_*(b)\) by
\(\widetilde z_{D_h}\). This is a feasible trial in (RS5).
Stationarity at \(z_*(b)\) and \(H_{zz}\le M_0I\) bound its extra
cost by \(M_0/2\) times the square in (RS9). Restriction gives the
opposite inequality. Finally \((s+t)^2\le2s^2+2t^2\) and
\(M_0(33/95)^2=2C_0<1/3\) prove the last inequality of (RS6).
At \(b=b^0\) the sharper error is \(M_0\beta_{\Omega,h}^2/2\);
exact value and gradient matching are not asserted.

For \(h\ge1\), set
\[
 \eta_h=\frac13\theta^{2h},\qquad
 L_{\Omega,h}(b)=U_{\Omega,h}(b)
       -\eta_h\|b-b^0\|^2-M_0\beta_{\Omega,h}^2 .
 \tag{RS10}
\]
Then \(L_{\Omega,h}\le W_\Omega\le U_{\Omega,h}\), and both bounds
are convex. The coarse boundary proof gives
\(D^2U_{\Omega,h}\ge(45/128)I\), also after any feasible deep
clamping. Thus
\[
 D^2L_{\Omega,h}\ge
       \left(\frac{45}{128}-2\eta_h\right)I
                          \ge\frac{2517}{8192}I>0.
 \tag{RS11}
\]
The free shell minimizers remain interior by the same half-gradient
bound as (BS1), with the deep packets merely clamped at feasible values.
No active-constraint inverse is required. For \(h=0\), (RS6) still
holds, but no convexity assertion is made for (RS10).

Both bounds for \(h\ge1\) retain exact degree-four local moment lifts.
First substitute all fixed deep packets in the original local
polynomials. For the lower program subtract each boundary quadratic
inside its unique component bag, before taking moments, and subtract
the constant \(M_0\beta_{\Omega,h}^2\) once per component.
If \(P_B\) projects onto the boundary packets assigned to one bag,
extend \(b^0\) by zero on its other coordinates. The modified local
Hessian certificate follows from
\[
 D^2(V-\eta_h\|P_B(x-b^0)\|^2)
          -(\mu_0-2\eta_h)I
       =(D^2V-\mu_0I)+2\eta_h(I-P_B),\qquad
 \mu_0=\frac{31}{128}.
 \tag{RS12}
\]
The added constant positive semidefinite quadratic form is a sum of
squares, and
\(\mu_0-2\eta_h\ge1621/8192>0\).
After substitution, ball factors of fixed packets become nonnegative
constants. The gate-local integrated Jensen proof therefore applies
with unchanged degree and first-moment matching. In the physical
metric its local matrix square identities give precisely the same
certificate. Subtracting squared first means from the old moment
epigraph would not be this affine semidefinite program.

For any connected partition, choose these feasible references and scalar
certificates independently in each component and impose the original
boundary consistency. With the same budget \(B\) for the chosen metric,
\[
 B^2\max\!\left(0,\min\sum_\Omega L_{\Omega,h}\right)
       \le |K_N|^2
       \le\frac{197}{196}B^2\min\sum_\Omega U_{\Omega,h}.
 \tag{RS13}
\]
The signed gate constants and every residual constant in (RS10) are
included before the minima are taken. No comparison factor is
multiplied over components.

The earlier source-visible scalar flow estimates error from a trial
field to the exact forward quantum recursion. The Gauss--Newton
certificate controls the whole minimum by its normal and tangential
energies. The additional result here bounds a frozen clamped component
minimum for all boundary packets, using a checkable scalar supersolution
instead of an exact reference minimum. A feasible reference can be
supplied directly, including the zero field; its residual certificate
determines whether the bound is useful. Full packet coordinates and
their repeated-root directions remain. Distances concern the literal
tree, and the shell still contains \(N\)-coordinate packets.
The additive residual term can exceed an exponentially small source.
No relative precision, geometric lower rate, or volume theorem follows
without further estimates.

## Physical Casimir multiplicities sharpen the unchanged source minimum, 23 November

The uniform physical quartic has a better closing constant than the
level-independent bound used in its construction. The full physical
Casimir multiplicities give both original closing rows dual norm at
most \((2N)^{-1/2}\). Keeping exactly the same physical budgets and
numerical minimum then improves the source comparison factor to
\(1+1/(392N)\), at every level and including zeros.

Use the full physical algebra and uniform Hilbert--Schmidt metric of
the [physical source theorem](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md):
\[
 \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[\Omega]
       \subset\operatorname{End}(V_N\otimes V_N),\qquad
 \|F\|_{\rm ph}^2=\operatorname{Tr}(F^*F),\qquad
 P_N(t)=2T_N(t/2)+2,\qquad N\ge2 .
\]
Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and
\(c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}\), \(0\le j\le d\).
The characteristic polynomial on the entire \(N^2\)-dimensional pair is
\[
             \det(tI_{N^2}-\Omega)=P_N(t)^N.       \tag{PC1}
\]
In particular every distinct double Casimir node has physical
algebraic multiplicity \(2N\); the simple node \(-2\), present when
\(N\) is odd, has physical multiplicity \(N\).

Here is the all-level derivation from the
[complete pair proof](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md),
Section 4. In its analytic generic ordinary highest-weight family,
the explicitly constructed highest vectors and their descendants
give one summand of dimension \(2d-2j+1\) with Casimir eigenvalue
\[
 \xi_j(\zeta)=\zeta^{\,2d-2j+1}
                         +\zeta^{-2d+2j-1},\qquad 0\le j\le d.
\]
Their dimensions sum to \(N^2\). Thus the generic characteristic
polynomial is the product of
\((t-\xi_j(\zeta))^{2d-2j+1}\).
The finite matrices are analytic at \(\zeta=q\), where
\(\xi_j(q)=c_j=c_{d-j}\). The two dimensions in such a pair sum
to \(2N\). At the odd self-paired index \(j=d/2\) the dimension is
\(N\) and the eigenvalue is \(-2\).
Specializing the characteristic polynomial proves (PC1), for even
and composite levels as well. This uses no semisimple decomposition
at the root and makes no freeness assertion over \(\mathcal A_N\).

Consequently every full physical box \(F=f(\Omega)\) satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|f(\Omega)\|_{\rm ph}^2
    \ge N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}|f(c_j)|^2
    =2N\sum_{c\ {\rm distinct\ double}}|f(c)|^2
       +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}N|f(-2)|^2 .
 \quad}                                                   \tag{PC2}
\]
To verify this without a normality assumption, choose an invariant
complex flag for \(\Omega\) and orthonormalize it. Its matrix is upper
triangular, with the eigenvalues counted in (PC1). The same unitary
frame makes \(f(\Omega)\) upper triangular with diagonal entries
\(f(c_j)\) in those multiplicities. The sum of squared diagonal
entries is at most its full Hilbert--Schmidt norm squared.
All remaining entries stay in that norm. In particular (PC2) is a
lower bound using nodal values, not a deletion of the independent
first-normal directions.

The original closing rows are
\(\lambda_0(f(\Omega))=f(c_0)\) and \(\phi\), and the genuine
quarter-turn \(\mathcal T\) obeys
\(\lambda_0=\phi\circ\mathcal T\).
The physical source theorem proves that \(\mathcal T\) is a unitary
involution on this full physical algebra. Since \(c_0\) is a double
node at every \(N\ge2\), (PC2) gives
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
  N^{-1}\le\|\lambda_0\|_*=\|\phi\|_*
                                    \le(2N)^{-1/2}.
 \qquad}                                                \tag{PC3}
\]
For the lower bound use \(\lambda_0(I)=1\) and
\(\|I\|_{\rm ph}=N\); the turn transfers that same bound to \(\phi\).
The marked row and all original pivotal factors are the same ones
as in the physical source theorem.

Now retain exactly its physical compilation: prescribed leaf budgets
\(16\max(1,\|A_v\|_{\rm ph})\), product and turn budgets \(16\), and
root budget \(b_\rho=16\max(1,|\eta_N|)\) for the original scalar
multiple \(\eta_N\lambda\), \(\lambda\in\{\lambda_0,\phi\}\).
Let \(B_{\rm ph}\) be their unchanged product, let
\(L=\eta_N\lambda/b_\rho\), and write
\[
 G(x)=\Phi(x)-x,\qquad
 E_{\rm ph}(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|Lx_{\rm top}|^2,\qquad
 e_{\rm ph}=\min_{\text{original packet balls}}E_{\rm ph}.
\]
Equation (PC3) gives \(\|L\|\le1/(16\sqrt{2N})\).
If \(a\) is the true normalized forward field, then
\(G(a)=0\), \(La_{\rm top}=k=K_N/B_{\rm ph}\), and the existing
residual bound in the physical source proof is
\[
 \|a-x\|\le\frac87\|G(x)\| .
\]
Therefore every feasible \(x\) satisfies
\[
 |k-Lx_{\rm top}|
       \le\frac{\|G(x)\|}{14\sqrt{2N}},\qquad
 |k|^2\le\left(1+\frac1{392N}\right)E_{\rm ph}(x).
 \tag{PC4}
\]
The second inequality is the two-term Cauchy--Schwarz inequality.
Taking the minimum and using the feasible true field, whose cost
is \(|k|^2\), proves
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 B_{\rm ph}^2e_{\rm ph}\le |K_N|^2
       \le\left(1+\frac1{392N}\right)B_{\rm ph}^2e_{\rm ph}.
 \quad}                                                   \tag{PC5}
\]
No division by \(k\) occurs. The budgets, quartic objective, packet
balls, complete Hermite coordinates and original complex source
are unchanged.

The earlier explicit corridor factor gives a sharper comparison
after rescaling its Newton minimum by a known corridor factor.
That is a different numerical minimum and budget convention.
Equation (PC5) instead sharpens the direct comparison for the same
uniform physical minimum, without a corridor rescaling. It does not
evaluate this minimum, supply a geometric reference field, or prove
its hyperbolic-volume rate.

## Estimating multiplication after the original closing removes an exponential loss, 23 November

The [polar error bound](research_conway_source_polar_error_bound.md)
improves the nonlinear remainder in the finite Newton repair.
It keeps the same trial packets, coherent corrected closing and
normalization budgets. Its computable error radius is never larger
than the previous one. At the cylindrical closing, composing with
the original row before estimating a product removes a genuinely
exponential norm loss.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(D=N-1\), and the full normalized Newton space
with its coefficient Hermitian norm. Let \(J e_r=e_{D-r}\) be
the actual quarter-turn and let \(\phi(f)=f_D\) be the original
Frobenius closing, so \(\phi(fg)=f^{\mathsf T}Jg\).
At a product, the original normalized map is
\(\Phi_v(u,w)=uw/b_v\), where \(b_v\) is its recorded budget.
For a feasible trial field \(x\), write
\[
 r=\Phi(x)-x,\qquad A=D\Phi(x),\qquad
 \delta=(I-A)^{-1}r,\qquad d=c(I-A)^{-1}.
\]
Here \(L\) is the original normalized closing row, and \(c\)
is its extension by zero away from the top packet. The inverse
is a finite triangular sum. The prescribed scalar is
\(k=K_N/B_{\rm tot}\), with its full budget \(B_{\rm tot}\).
The earlier exact identity is
\[
 k=\widehat k+
       \sum_{v\ {\rm product}}d_v\Phi_v(e_L,e_R),
 \qquad \widehat k=Lx_{\rm top}+dr,\qquad e=a-x,
\]
where \(a\) is the true full packet field.

Define \(h_v=Jd_v^{\mathsf T}\), so that
\(d_v(f)=\phi(h_vf)\), and let \(M_h\) multiply by \(h\)
in the full algebra. A star denotes the coefficient Hermitian
adjoint; \(\mathsf T\) is ordinary transpose. The positive matrix
\[
 S_v=\frac{|M_{h_v}|}{b_v},\qquad
 |M_h|=(M_h^*M_h)^{1/2},
\]
gives the sharp bilinear estimate
\[
 |d_v\Phi_v(u,w)|
       \le\sqrt{u^*S_vu}\sqrt{w^*S_vw},\qquad
 \|S_v\|\le\|d_v\|\,\|\Phi_v\|_{\rm bil}.
\]
The reason is that the actual contracted matrix
\(JM_{h_v}/b_v\) is complex symmetric. Polar Cauchy--Schwarz
then uses the same positive matrix on both inputs. No inverse
of \(S_v\) is required. Its kernel is the annihilator
\(\{u:h_vu=0\}\) for this contraction. The bilinear norm is the
supremum on pairs of unit inputs. The carrier changes at every
actual turn.
Distinct sibling pairs are disjoint, so these local error Grams
also assemble into the block diagonal positive majorant proved
in equation (10a) of the note.

The bound is computable without the unknown errors \(e\).
The proof constructs scalar majorants
\(\|e_v\|\le\Delta_v\) and
\(\|e_v-\delta_v\|\le\omega_v\) by forward recursions.
At a product, put \(\gamma_v=\|S_v\|\) and
\[
 t_{vc}=\min\left\{\sqrt{\gamma_v}\Delta_c,\,
       \sqrt{\delta_c^*S_v\delta_c}+\sqrt{\gamma_v}\omega_c\right\}.
\]
Thus the new radius and the unchanged coherent center satisfy
\[
 |\widehat k-k|\le R_{\rm pol}:=\sum_v t_{vL}t_{vR}
                         \le R_{\rm loc},\qquad
 R=\min\{R_{\rm pol},\|r\|^2/343\},
\]
\[
 B_{\rm tot}(|\widehat k|-R)_+
       \le |K_N|\le B_{\rm tot}(|\widehat k|+R).
\]
The sum is over product vertices. The previous local radius
\(R_{\rm loc}\) charges a separate multiplication norm at each
such vertex. The new radius first combines that product with
its actual transported closing. Here \((t)_+=\max(t,0)\).

For a top product followed by the original cylindrical row
\(L=\chi\phi/b_\rho\), keep its recorded scalar \(\chi\)
and original closing budget \(b_\rho\). The matrix is exactly
\[
                  S_v=\frac{|\chi|}{b_\rho b_v}I.
\]
Write \(M(u,w)=uw\) for actual multiplication. The local error
coefficient drops from
\(|\chi|\|M\|_{\rm bil}/(b_\rho b_v)\) to
\(|\chi|/(b_\rho b_v)\), with every budget retained.
This is an exponential improvement: an actual multiplication
coefficient at \(j_N=\lfloor N/4\rfloor\) gives
\[
 \|M\|_{\rm bil}\ge \frac{s_{2j_N}^{\,2}}{s_{j_N}^{\,4}}
       =\exp\!\left\{\frac{2G_{\rm Cat}}\pi N+O(\log N)\right\},
 \quad s_j=\prod_{a=1}^j2\sin(\pi a/N).
\]
Here \(G_{\rm Cat}=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(\cot t)\,dt\).
The saving concerns decomposable product errors; the full tensor
row \(\phi M\) has norm \(\sqrt N\), rather than one.

Other products may still dominate a whole-tree radius. The
corrected center has not been estimated at the hyperbolic-volume
rate, and this sharper disk has not yet been shown smaller than
that center after arbitrary short partial fillings. Thus this
is a quantitative improvement in the required error estimate,
not a new volume identity or a finite-exception theorem.

### Internal products retain an intrinsic exponential cost

The preceding saving does not propagate freely through every product.
There is an exact transport inequality, but its remaining operator
cost can itself be exponential. This check narrows the next task to
the actual geometric packets and their residuals.

Use the same full Newton algebra, coefficient norm and Frobenius
functional. For an algebra element \(h\), let \(M_h\) be its
multiplication operator and write \(P_h=|M_h|\). Commutativity
gives, without commuting any operator past an adjoint,
\[
 (M_hM_x)^*(M_hM_x)
   =M_h^*M_x^*M_xM_h
   \preceq\|M_x\|^2 M_h^*M_h.
\]
Taking positive square roots proves
\[
 P_{hx}\preceq\|M_x\|P_h.
\]
Square-root monotonicity here has the elementary matrix proof
\[
 A^{1/2}=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty
       t^{-1/2}A(A+tI)^{-1}\,dt\qquad(A\succeq0).
\]
Inverse order makes \(A(A+tI)^{-1}=I-t(A+tI)^{-1}\)
order-preserving; integration proves the assertion, including
singular matrices. If \(x\) is a unit, applying the upper bound
to \(hx\) and \(x^{-1}\) also gives
\[
 \|M_{x^{-1}}\|^{-1}P_h
       \preceq P_{hx}\preceq\|M_x\|P_h.
\]
Along a sequence containing only product gates, the exact carrier
is \(h_{\rm out}=h_{\rm in}X/\prod_i b_i\), where \(X\) is
the product of the specified sibling trial packets. Thus
\[
 P_{h_{\rm out}}
       \preceq\frac{\|M_X\|}{\prod_i b_i}P_{h_{\rm in}}.
\]
The siblings can be combined before taking a norm, retaining their
cancellations. A genuine turn still uses the exact rule
\(h\mapsto Jh/b_i\); this order estimate does not move a turn
through a product.

The unnormalized closed trilinear form already has an exponential
norm in these Newton coordinates. Define
\[
 T(u,v,w)=\phi((uv)w),\qquad
 \|T\|_{\rm tri}=\sup_{\|u\|=\|v\|=\|w\|=1}|T(u,v,w)|.
\]
For a fixed \(a=uv\), the original identity
\(\phi(aw)=a^{\mathsf T}Jw\) gives
\[
 \sup_{\|w\|=1}|\phi(aw)|=\|a\|,\qquad
                  \|T\|_{\rm tri}=\|M\|_{\rm bil}.
\]
For \(a\ne0\), equality is attained at
\(w=J\bar a/\|a\|\); the zero case is immediate.
More explicitly, put \(D=N-1\) and \(j=\lfloor N/4\rfloor\).
The actual unit basis packets give, for \(N\ge4\),
\[
 T(e_j,e_j,e_{D-2j})
     =\mu_{j,j,2j}=\frac{s_{2j}^{\,2}}{s_j^{\,4}}
     =\exp\!\left\{\frac{2G_{\rm Cat}}\pi N+O(\log N)\right\}.
\]
This uses the same full Frobenius pairing and coefficient estimate
as the polar proof. Normalizing the product gates divides both
sides by their same recorded budgets. Thus the exponential cost
can return one product inward, even though the final binary
closing has bilinear norm one.

This is a test of estimates uniform over all boundary packets,
not a counterexample involving a knot or a specified geometric
trial. It leaves the sharper polar disk intact. Further progress
requires a bound for \(M_X\) on the selected errors, or localization
and forcing estimates for the residuals of a specified geometric
trial. No additional volume lower bound is proved by this audit.

### Projected trials retain an explicit backward error

Projecting the exact packet \(a_v\) onto a proposed geometric line
does not construct its amplitude: \(P_va_v\) already contains an
unknown coherent matrix element of the actual subtree. The
[projected forward recursion](research_conway_projective_direction_certificate.md)
is a different, explicit trial:
\[
 x_v=P_v\Phi_v((x_c)_c),\qquad P=\bigoplus_vP_v,\qquad Q=I-P.
\]
Here each \(P_v\) is an orthogonal packet projection chosen before
the recursion. Its actual local overlaps determine \(x\), and
every packet has norm at most \(\sigma=1/16\). Put
\[
 r=\Phi(x)-x,\quad A=D\Phi(x),\quad
 k=K_N/B_{\rm tot},\quad z=Lx_{\rm top}.
\]
Then \(Pr=0\) exactly. Let \(c\) be the original normalized closing
row on the top packet, extended by zero elsewhere, and define the
projected backward row and its defect by
\[
 \widetilde d=cP(I-PAP)^{-1}P,\qquad
 s=c-\widetilde d(I-A).
\]
The inverse is a finite triangular sum. Direct multiplication gives
\(\widetilde dP=\widetilde d\),
\(\widetilde d(I-A)P=cP\), \(sP=0\), and
\(\widetilde dr=0\). With \(e=a-x\), the exact bilinear
recursion therefore gives the original-source identity
\[
 k-z=s e+
       \sum_{v\ {\rm product}}\widetilde d_v\Phi_v(e_L,e_R).
\]
Thus orthogonality cancels the projected backward row applied to
the primal residual. The backward defect and the nonlinear error
remain. Their coarse bound is
\[
 |k-z|\le\frac{16}{15}\|s\|\|r\|
                       +\frac{8}{3375}\|r\|^2.
\]
Indeed the true and projected packets are all in their
\(\sigma\)-balls, so \(\|A\|\le\sigma\),
\(\|e\|\le(16/15)\|r\|\), and
\(\|\widetilde d\|\le1/15\). The quadratic remainder has norm
at most \(\|e\|^2/32\). The source-polar construction can bound
the last sum more sharply using the carriers of \(\widetilde d\).
This bound is not uniformly smaller than the earlier
\(\|r\|/15\) disk centered at \(z\).

The unresolved rows are explicit. With \(Q_v=I-P_v\),
\[
 s_{\rm top}=LQ_{\rm top},\qquad
 s_c=\widetilde d_v D_c\Phi_v(x)Q_c
       \quad(c\text{ a child of the proper vertex }v).
\]
These formulas retain the actual parent derivatives and the
original closing, with every turn in its prescribed place.
No geometric estimate making these rows sufficiently small
has been proved.
Moreover, if \(\delta=(I-A)^{-1}r\) and
\(d=c(I-A)^{-1}\) is the full backward row, then
\[
 d=\widetilde d+s(I-A)^{-1},\qquad dr=s\delta.
\]
Evaluating the coherent scalar \(s\delta\) thus recovers the
correction already retained in the polar proof. This calculation
identifies the remaining error; it supplies no new asymptotic
lower bound or finite-exception result.
