### A branch projector cannot cross the complete point unchanged

The proposed analytic projector must be tested at the original
complete point, not only on regular spectral arcs. The actual
figure-eight operator already requires a paired-block treatment
there. This tests a proposed general transport argument on a knot
whose volume identity is known; it is not a new knot case.

Fix \(N\ge2\) and use the original affine equation
\[
 C_QF_N=D(3-U-U^{-1}),\quad U=Y^N,\quad
 C_Q=c_-T^{-1}+c_0+c_+T,\quad TY=QYT,\quad
 Q=e^{2\pi i/N}.
\]
The complete coefficients are retained in the
[pointed Green proof](pointed_newton_green_barrier.md).
On the original orbit \(U=1\), where \(c_+\ne0\), the
forward state \(w(Y)=(F_N(Y),F_N(Q^{-1}Y))^{\mathsf T}\)
obeys \(w(QY)=T_Q(Y)w(Y)+f_Q(Y)\), with
\[
 T_Q=\begin{pmatrix}-c_0/c_+&-c_-/c_+\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad f_Q=\begin{pmatrix}D/c_+\\0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
On a regular arc its classical transfer, from the
[actual transfer calculation](actual_regulator_weighted_a_transfer.md),
is
\[
 T_0(Y)=\begin{pmatrix}P(Y)&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad P(Y)=Y^2+Y^{-2}-Y-Y^{-1}-2.
\]
At \(Y=1\), write \(J_0=T_0(1)+I\). Then
\[
 T_0(1)=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad J_0\ne0,\qquad J_0^2=0.
\]
For \(Y=e^s\), direct expansion gives
\(P(e^s)=-2+3s^2+O(s^4)\). The two eigenvalues can be
labelled on this logarithmic chart so that
\[
 \lambda_\pm=-1\pm i\sqrt3\,s+O(s^2),\qquad
 \Pi_\pm(s)=\frac{T_0(e^s)-\lambda_\mp I}
                  {\lambda_\pm-\lambda_\mp}
            =\pm\frac{J_0}{2i\sqrt3\,s}+O(1).
\]
For \(s\ne0\) these are the unique spectral projections onto
the separated eigenlines. Consequently no bounded analytic
rank-one spectral splitting extends them through completeness.
Their sum is the regular rank-two projector \(I\); the paired
Jordan block must be retained.

The actual finite-level coefficients add a boundary-layer issue.
Their exact formulas give
\[
 c_0(1)=0,\quad c_+(1)=c_-(1)=(Q-1)^2,\quad
 D(1)=2(Q-1)^2.
\]
Thus at \(Y=1\), where the forward equation is defined,
\[
 T_Q(1)=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad f_Q(1)=\begin{pmatrix}2\\0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Here \(f_Q\) is the actual affine source on \(U=1\).
In particular the expansion \(T_Q=T_0+O(1/N)\), valid on
compact regular arcs, is not uniform on a domain containing
the complete point. There is also an actual forward
leading-coefficient zero:
\[
 c_+(Y)=Y^2(QY-1)(Q-Y^2),\qquad c_+(Q^{-1})=0 .
\]
For \(N\ge4\), its source factor
\(D(Y)=Y(Y+1)(Q-Y^2)(QY^2-1)\) is nonzero at \(Q^{-1}\).
The full affine equation retains that value; dividing by
\(c_+\) cannot supply forward transport at that orbit step.

These calculations do not rule out paired or confluent
transport. They show why a regular separated-branch theorem
does not supply the missing complete-point and cut matching.
No new volume estimate follows. The two complete proof texts
used here retain pins

and cf7da5e73386d41ac9ce6b4e53c0b4e35ea343661f7953411eadf0bbac18ae46.

## One closing estimate controls the entire Conway tree, 23 November

The [global closing estimate](research_conway_global_closing_curvature.md)
extends the earlier endpoint saving to every bilinear correction in a
literal Conway tree. It gives a simpler uniform error bound: no polar
matrix has to be formed at any product.

Use the full Newton coefficient norm and the original budgets
\(b_v=16\max(1,\|T_v\|_{\rm HS})\). Write the original normalized
closing as \(L=\chi\lambda_\epsilon/b_\rho\), where
\(\epsilon\in\{0,N-1\}\) selects the marked or cylindrical closure.
Let \(v_*\) be the product nearest the closing root. Every gate above
it is a genuine turn. If \(\mathcal U\) is this list of turns, put
\[
 \alpha=\frac{\chi}{b_\rho\prod_{u\in\mathcal U}b_u},
 \qquad \zeta=\frac{|\alpha|}{b_{v_*}}.
\]
The parity of these turns may interchange the two endpoint rows;
it changes neither \(|\alpha|\) nor the following estimate.

For a feasible trial field \(x\), retain the exact backward row
\(d=c(I-D\Phi(x))^{-1}\), where \(c\) is \(L\) on the top packet
and zero elsewhere. The residual, corrected closing and true field are
\[
 r=\Phi(x)-x,\qquad
 \widehat k=Lx_{\rm top}+dr,\qquad a=\Phi(a).
\]
The exact bilinear remainder \(Q(h)\) is
\(Q_v(h)=\Phi_v(h_L,h_R)\) at products and zero elsewhere.
The new uniform estimate is
\[
 |dQ(h)|\le\frac{\zeta}{2}\|h\|^2
 \qquad\text{for every full packet variation }h.
\]
At the first product, the contracted bilinear matrix is
\(\alpha J/b_{v_*}\) or
\(\alpha e_0e_0^{\mathsf T}/b_{v_*}\), both of norm \(\zeta\).
Consequently each child row has norm at most \(\zeta\).
Every subsequent derivative block has norm at most \(1/16\),
including every later turn. A packet has just one parent, so the
backward recursion introduces no sum of competing paths.
Each lower contracted product therefore has norm at most
\(\zeta/16\). Disjoint sibling pairs give the displayed quadratic bound.

Since \(\|a-x\|\le8\|r\|/7\), the original source satisfies
\[
 \left|\frac{K_N}{B_{\rm tot}}-\widehat k\right|
       \le R_{\rm end}(x):=\frac{32\zeta}{49}\|r\|^2.
\]
Here \(B_{\rm tot}\) remains the full original budget product.
For actual multiplication \(M_N\) in the normalized Newton basis,
\[
 \zeta\le\frac{1}{256\max(1,\|M_N\|_{\rm HS})},\qquad
 R_{\rm end}(x)\le
 \frac{\|r\|^2}{392\max(1,\|M_N\|_{\rm HS})}.
\]
This improves the earlier inexpensive radius \(\|r\|^2/343\).
The explicitly computed polar radius can be sharper and remains
available. The advantage here is a uniform bound requiring only the
already recorded budgets, residual and backward row.
If the tree contains no product, the correction is exact.

The sine-product coefficient used in the earlier polar proof gives
\[
 \zeta_N\le
 \exp\!\left[-\frac{2G_{\rm Cat}}{\pi}N+O(\log N)\right],
\]
where \(G_{\rm Cat}\) is Catalan's constant.
Thus if the corrected center has size \(e^{-aN+o(N)}\), the
residual has norm at most \(e^{-bN+o(N)}\), and
\(\zeta_N\le e^{-gN+o(N)}\), the error is negligible whenever
\(2b+g>a\). The earlier constant-coefficient quadratic estimate
required \(2b>a\).

This is a global saving of one multiplication budget, rather than a
removal of every internal cost: the other budgets remain in
\(B_{\rm tot}\zeta\). Fixed short fillings may be retained in their
full leaf packets. General composed linear maps must not replace the
literal turn corridor in this proof. No source channel is deleted.
The nonzero geometric rate of \(\widehat k\), including after arbitrary
fixed short partial fillings, is still unproved. The finite-exception
theorem therefore remains open.

## The corrected closing shares the small endpoint scale, 23 November

The exponential coefficient in the preceding estimate does not by itself
make a bounded residual sufficient. The corrected closing is bounded by
the same endpoint scale. This follows from the actual Newton repair,
without a geometric assumption or a model counterexample.

Use the notation of the
[global closing proof](research_conway_global_closing_curvature.md).
Assume that the literal tree has a product, let \(v_*\) be its product
nearest the closing, and write
\[
 \mathscr B_*(u,v)=d_{v_*}\Phi_{v_*}(u,v),\qquad
 \|\mathscr B_*\|_{\rm bil}=\zeta.
\]
The row \(d_{v_*}\) depends only on the original closing and the turns
above this product. In particular, it is the same row for the true field
and for every trial field.

For any feasible trial \(x\), let
\[
 r=\Phi(x)-x,\quad A=D\Phi(x),\quad
 y=x+(I-A)^{-1}r .
\]
The complete
[residual transport proof](research_conway_source_visible_residual_transport.md),
equations (27), (30) and (31), gives
\[
 cy=\widehat k,\qquad
 (I-A)y=\Phi(x)-Ax,\qquad \|y_v\|\le1/14 .
\]
At a turn the last vector equation says exactly
\(y_v=Jy_{\rm child}/b_v\). Thus the repaired field satisfies every
turn above \(v_*\) exactly. At that product, bilinearity gives
\[
 y_{v_*}
 =\Phi_{v_*}(y_L,x_R)+\Phi_{v_*}(x_L,y_R)
                         -\Phi_{v_*}(x_L,x_R).
\]
Applying the unchanged turn corridor and original closing proves
the exact scalar identity
\[
 \widehat k
 =\mathscr B_*(y_L,x_R)+\mathscr B_*(x_L,y_R)
                         -\mathscr B_*(x_L,x_R).
\]
Since \(\|x_v\|\le1\) and \(\|y_v\|\le1/14\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad |\widehat k|\le\frac87\zeta.\quad}
\]
The true field has \(\|a_v\|\le1/16\) and
\(k=\mathscr B_*(a_L,a_R)\), so also
\[
                         |k|\le\zeta/256 .
\]
Both inequalities include zero scalars and both original closing types.
No source coordinate or repeated-root direction has been removed.

Consequently, if
\(|\widehat k_N|=\exp(-\alpha N+o(N))\) and
\(\zeta_N\le\exp(-\gamma N+o(N))\), then \(\alpha\ge\gamma\).
The hoped-for strict advantage \(\alpha<\gamma\) is impossible under
these normalized hypotheses. A valid change of metric must transform
the endpoint bilinear norm as well as the tensors; it cannot retain an
old favorable coefficient with a newly rescaled center.

This does not exclude polynomial relative accuracy when the two
exponential rates agree. For example, if \(\zeta_N>0\) and
\[
 \frac{|\widehat k_N|}{\zeta_N}\ge N^{-C},\qquad
 \|r_N\|\le N^{-(C+\delta)/2},\qquad \delta>0,
\]
then the preceding radius satisfies
\[
 \frac{R_{\rm end}(x_N)}{|\widehat k_N|}
                         \le\frac{32}{49}N^{-\delta}\longrightarrow0.
\]
No such relative-center lower estimate is proved for general geometric
trial fields. With no product the correction is already exact and this
endpoint-scale discussion is unnecessary. The finite-exception theorem
remains open.

## Division at the complete color depends on its ordering, 23 November

A bounded operator on the original color orbit would suffice to transfer
a proved geometric growth estimate to \(K_N\). A direct test
shows why a formal division by the meridian cannot supply such an
observation without its precise ordering and wall term.

Fix the original one-component, zero-framed knot source and put
\[
 q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad
 c=(K_N,C_1(q),\ldots,C_{N-1}(q))^{\mathsf T}
       =K_Ne_0+r_{\rm ord}.
\]
The complete [ordinary-color proof](ordinary_color_plancherel_bound_audit.md)
gives \(C_1(q)=1\) and
\(\|r_{\rm ord}\|^2=R_N\le(N-1)(N/2)^{2b-2}\) for a fixed
\(b\)-strand presentation. Use the actual squared-meridian labels
\(Y_j=Q^j\), and define
\[
 (Lc)_j=c_{j+1\bmod N},\quad
 D=\operatorname{diag}(Q^j-1),\quad
 D^+_{jj}=
 \begin{cases}(Q^j-1)^{-1},&j\ne0,\\0,&j=0.\end{cases}
\]
Here \(D^+\) is the explicitly specified diagonal pseudoinverse.
Let \(P_0=e_0e_0^*\). Then
\[
 DD^+=D^+D=I-P_0,\qquad
 \|D^+\|=\frac1{2\sin(\pi/N)}.
\]
The two orders
\[
 A_{\rm left}=D^+(L+I),\qquad
 A_{\rm right}=(L+I)D^+
\]
both have norm at most \(\csc(\pi/N)=O(N)\). Nevertheless, with
\(a_N=(Q^{-1}-1)^{-1}\), their complete-color columns are
\[
 A_{\rm left}e_0=a_Ne_{N-1},\qquad
                         A_{\rm right}e_0=0.
\]
Thus \(A_{\rm right}c\) has polynomial norm for every knot in the
stated scope. The other order retains the unknown complete sector:
\[
 A_{\rm left}c=a_NK_Ne_{N-1}+A_{\rm left}r_{\rm ord},\qquad
 \left|\,|a_N|^{-1}\|A_{\rm left}c\|-|K_N|\,\right|
                                                    \le2\sqrt{R_N}.
\]
This follows from the reverse triangle inequality and
\(\|A_{\rm left}\|\le2|a_N|\). A positive exponential rate for this
specific left-ordered observation would therefore imply the same rate
for the original scalar. No such geometric estimate is supplied by the
operator's boundedness.

The attempted division retains the exact forcing
\[
 DA_{\rm left}c=(L+I)c-(K_N+1)e_0.
\]
Indeed its omitted row is \(P_0(L+I)c=(K_N+C_1)e_0\).
It is not legitimate to discard this term as a small endpoint error.
The two orders have the same commuting fraction away from \(Y=1\),
but they act differently on the distinguished source.

The original peripheral normalization has the same issue. The complete
[ADO pointing calculation](kashaev_ado_pointing.md), equation (3.3),
gives
\[
 g(q,M)=-q^{-1}\frac{QM^2-1}{M^2-1},\qquad
                         (Tf)(M)=f(qM).
\]
Away from its pole this means, with \(Y=M^2\),
\[
                  g(q,M)T=-q^{-1}(Y-1)^{-1}T(Y-1).
\]
Simply replacing its inverse factor by the above pseudoinverse gives
\(-q^{-1}D^+LD\). This matrix annihilates \(e_0\), so its output on
\(c\) is polynomially bounded. It is only a value-level regularization:
it does not retain the meromorphic wall data of the original gauge.
The whole marked meridian germ and its prescribed finite part cannot be
replaced by assigning zero to the singular diagonal entry.

This test does not rule out a different bounded observation, or a
quantum-corrected construction retaining the full normal source.
It rules out using the commuting fraction or its pseudoinverse norm as
an exact source-preserving peripheral identification. No general
growing observation or finite-exception theorem has been obtained.

## Character coordinates make the full peripheral action bounded, 23 November

The [character-metric proof](research_actual_peripheral_character_metric.md)
gives a positive metric for the actual whole-meridian family in which
both elementary peripheral actions are uniformly bounded. The apparent
fusion division is handled in the Laurent-polynomial ring, with its
normal data retained, before evaluating at the complete color.

Fix \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\). Write the original reduced source as
\(F_N(M)=F_N(M^{-1})\), with \(K_N=F_N(1)\), and use the full
character ladder
\[
 \chi_n(M)=\frac{M^{n+1}-M^{-n-1}}{M-M^{-1}},\qquad n\ge0.
\]
The positive norm is
\[
 \|F\|_{\mathrm H}^2
  =\frac2\pi\int_0^\pi |F(e^{i\theta})|^2\sin^2\theta\,d\theta
  =\sum_n|a_n|^2,\qquad F=\sum_n a_n\chi_n.
\]
For the actual fundamental longitude \(\Lambda\) and meridian
\(\mathsf U\), the exact whole-source fusion identities give
\[
 \Lambda\chi_n=-2\cos((n+1)\pi/N)\chi_n,\qquad
 \mathsf U\chi_n=\chi_{n+1}+\chi_{n-1},\quad\chi_{-1}=0.
\]
Consequently both operators have norm at most two. The meridian
raises the allowed degree by one; no upper-degree compression is
inserted into compositions. Both meridian parities are retained.

On character degree at most \(D\), the original complete-color
functional has the sharp dual norm
\[
 \|\operatorname{ev}_1\|^2
     =\sum_{n=0}^D(n+1)^2
     =\frac{(D+1)(D+2)(2D+3)}6.
\]
Thus a fixed peripheral word \(\mathcal W\) of length \(s\), with
\(m\) meridian letters, satisfies
\[
 |F_N^{\mathcal W}(1)|
 \le 2^s
 \sqrt{\frac{(D+m+1)(D+m+2)(2D+2m+3)}6}\,
                                      \|F_N\|_{\mathrm H}.
\]
The actual finite crossing formulas give \(D=O(N)\) for each fixed
braid presentation. Hence all these peripheral closing costs are
polynomial in the level. Fixed-order meridian derivatives have
polynomial costs as well.

This statement keeps the original scalar and peripheral multiplier.
In the odd normal lattice, \(w_N=(M-M^{-1})F_N\), it still uses
\(K_N=\tfrac12\partial_{\log M}w_N(1)\). It concerns fixed-root
meridian data, rather than an off-root quantum-normal lift.

The character norm is polynomially equivalent to the full-circle
Fourier norm on the actual \(O(N)\) Laurent window. It is not thereby
equivalent to the norm of samples on one root orbit: those samples
can forget alias and normal data. The estimates above are upper
bounds for the specified closing, not a reverse estimate or a
hyperbolic-volume asymptotic. No new filling class follows.

## An explicit corridor factor calibrates the quartic minimum, 23 November

The [corridor-factor proof](research_conway_explicit_corridor_minimum_factor.md)
sharpens the fixed-constant comparison with the original squared source
to an exponentially small relative error. Its leading factor uses only
known closing and turn budgets, with no unknown internal response.

Let \(e_*=\min E\) be the original normalized quartic minimum and
\(k=K_N/B_{\rm tot}\), with all original budgets retained. Suppose
there is a product, and let \(v_*\) be the highest one. Above it are
only the original turns \(J/\beta_1,\ldots,J/\beta_m\), ordered
upward, followed by \(L=\chi\lambda_\varepsilon/b_\rho\), with
\(\varepsilon\in\{0,N-1\}\). Define
\[
 C=1+\nu_{\rm corr}
   =1+\frac{|\chi|^2}{b_\rho^2}
            \sum_{i=0}^m\prod_{j=i+1}^m\beta_j^{-2},
 \qquad
 \zeta=\frac{|\chi|}
             {b_\rho b_{v_*}\prod_{j=1}^m\beta_j}.
\]
Empty products equal one. The sum includes the output of \(v_*\)
as well as every turn output. Thus \(C\) is known explicitly and
\(1\le C\le256/255\).

For the full minimum and the prescribed-leaf smaller quartic
minimum \(e_{\rm cl}\) of the binary-skeleton reduction,
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \left(1-\frac{\zeta^2}{82C}\right)|K_N|^2
 \le C B_{\rm tot}^2e_*
 \le C B_{\rm tot}^2e_{\rm cl}
 \le |K_N|^2.
 \quad}
\]
The restricted minimum need not equal the full minimum. Any exact
elimination within the restricted problem preserves its own minimum
and the displayed comparison.

The proof first eliminates the final linear corridor exactly.
Its original ball constraints are inactive, and its least-squares
cost is \(|s|^2/C\). The remaining function is
\(F(u)=R(u)+|g(u)|^2\), with
\(R(u_a)=0\), \(g(u_a)=k/\sqrt C\) at the true field.
The original endpoint pairing bounds the highest product's
contracted bilinear matrix by \(\zeta\). Since both actual child
packets have norm at most \(\sigma=1/16\),
\[
 D^2F\succeq\frac{41}{32}I,\qquad
 \|\nabla F(u_a)\|^2
       \le\frac{8\sigma^2\zeta^2}{C}F(u_a).
\]
The Hessian bound survives the exact linear elimination by its
Schur-complement formula. Its quadratic minorant therefore gives
\(\min F\ge[1-\zeta^2/(82C)]F(u_a)\); the competitor \(u_a\)
gives the upper bound. The known leaf restrictions also contain
that competitor, proving the same estimate for \(e_{\rm cl}\).

The actual multiplication bound gives
\[
 \frac{\zeta^2}{82C}
 \le\exp\!\left\{-\frac{4G_{\rm Cat}}{\pi}N+O(\log N)\right\},
 \qquad
 G_{\rm Cat}=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(\cot t)\,dt.
\]
With no product, take the entire proper chain as the corridor and
\(\zeta=0\); then \(e_*=|k|^2/C\) exactly. Zeros of \(K_N\), and
\(\chi=0\), are included without dividing by the source.

The chosen variational presentation and its budgets depend on the
compiler. The original scalar, both endpoint closings and every
Hermite channel are unchanged. The minimum has not been evaluated:
a geometric lower witness or actual source rate is still required.
No finite-exception or volume theorem follows from this calibration.

## The actual charge normal has a nonzero complete-point initializer, 23 November

The [charge-normal proof](research_actual_charge_normal_initializer.md)
evaluates a derivative of the actual finite Hermite coupon source,
rather than differentiating a lattice-only asymptotic. Fix an integer
\(N\ge2\), and put
\(d=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^d\), \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), and retain
the original full trace
\(\phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f\).
For the actual analytic coupon \(\mathcal C_{N,\chi}\), define
\[
 \mathfrak d_N=\partial_\chi\mathcal C_{N,\chi}|_0.
\]
At every double node \(c_\tau=-2\cos\tau\), \(0<\tau<\pi\),
\(\mathfrak d_N(c_\tau)=0\) and
\(\mathfrak d_N'(c_\tau)=\eta N^2\tau/(2\sin\tau)\).
Its value at the odd simple root is zero. The original residue
formula therefore gives, exactly for every polynomial \(E\),
\[
 \phi_N(\mathfrak d_NE)
   =2N^2\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal T_N}\tau\sin\tau\,E(c_\tau),
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_N=\{\pi(N-1-2l)/N:0\le l<\lfloor N/2\rfloor\}.
\]
In particular \(\mathfrak d_N^2=0\) and
\(\phi_N(\mathfrak d_N\overline f f)\ge0\). This exact nodal
formula uses the original first normals.

Let \(\Gamma\) be a fixed finite graph carrying the original
same-index kernels \(K_N(t,u)=\sum_{a=0}^d e_a(-2\cos t)e_a(-2\cos u)\).
Select a nonempty set \(I\) of nonisolated vertices, fix all other
angles at zero, and fix integer crossing powers \(n_v\), of either
sign or zero. Write \(m=|I|\), \(e=|E(\Gamma)|\), and let \(d_v\)
be the original degrees, with loops counted twice. Repeated edges
and loops are allowed. Let \(Z_N(\boldsymbol\chi)\) be this
original finite source with the actual coupon at each selected
vertex. Then its whole mixed charge normal is
\[
 Z_N^{\rm nor}
 =\left.\left(\prod_{v\in I}\partial_{\chi_v}\right)
                        Z_N(\boldsymbol\chi)\right|_{\boldsymbol0}.
\]
Through both level parities,
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 Z_N^{\rm nor}=\varepsilon_N N^{3(m-e)/2}(2\pi)^m4^{-e}
    \prod_{v\in I}(d_v-in_v)^{-3/2}
    e^{NeM_\infty}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \quad}
\]
where \(M_\infty=4G_{\rm Cat}/\pi\),
\(G_{\rm Cat}=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(\cot s)\,ds\), and
\(\varepsilon_N=\prod_{v\in I}\exp[\pi in_v(N-1)^2/(4N)]\).
The powers use the branch in the right half-plane. The leading
coefficient is nonzero for every fixed signed power vector.

The proof uses literal Newton nodal positivity and an elementary
global tail bound, followed by the original local kernel expansion.
The positive half-grid has mesh \(2\pi/N\); its midpoint and integer
versions give the same half-Gaussian coefficient. All nodal weights,
crossing phases and odd-level endpoints are accounted for.

The [older charge-increment norm](research_charge_increment_graph_norm.md)
already gives the sharp positive norm of a vector of charge observations
at the same complete-edge rate, exactly independently of the powers.
Its written localization and local Gaussian analysis already supply
the relevant kernel estimates. The actual coupon jets of the
analytic-family proof specify the continuous mixed normal evaluated
here. Keeping its signed phases changes the Gaussian degree \(d_v\)
to \(d_v-in_v\). This is an incremental scalar evaluation, not a new
positive-norm or localization method.

This remains a different observation from the unit coupon:
\(\mathcal C_{N,0}=\eta\,1\), \(\mathcal C_{N,1}=1\), so no universal
division of the whole source by its charges is justified. Nor is the nodal
quotient preserved by turns. Indeed a retained reversed edge
\(\sum_a e_a(c_l)e_{d-a}(c_j)\) vanishes at all pairs of double
nodes. The theorem is explicitly for the stated same-index source.
Its rate is the complete-edge constant; no general graph-to-manifold
volume identification, unit-source continuation, filled-volume
lower bound or finite-exception theorem follows.

## Values and genuine turns reconstruct the full boundary packet, 23 November

The [completed charge-normal frame](research_charge_normal_completed_boundary_frame.md)
recovers every physical Newton coefficient from two complementary sets
of actual observations, with polynomial inverse cost. It includes all
first normals at repeated roots and both original closing directions.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(r=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), and use
\[
 c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\qquad
 e_k(z)=\frac{\prod_{h<k}(c_h-z)}
                  {\prod_{h=1}^k(2\sin(h\pi/N))^2},\qquad
 Je_k=e_{d-k}.
\]
For \(f=\sum_{k=0}^d\alpha_ke_k\), write
\(\|f\|_{\rm N}^2=\sum_k|\alpha_k|^2\). At the distinct double nodes put
\[
 \tau_j=\pi-(2j+1)\pi/N,\quad w_j=2N^2\tau_j\sin\tau_j,\qquad
 G_D(f)=\sum_{j<r}w_j|f(c_j)|^2
       =\phi_N(\mathfrak d_N f^\sharp f).
\]
Here \(f^\sharp(z)=\overline{f(\bar z)}\), and \(\mathfrak d_N\) is the
actual charge-normal coupon above. Complete its positive form by
\[
 \|f\|_{\rm D}^2=G_D(f)+G_D(Jf)
   +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}\bigl(|f(-2)|^2+|(Jf)(-2)|^2\bigr).
\]
The odd simple-node terms are explicit additional metric rows.
The completed form is positive definite on the full algebra, and
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
       \|f\|_{\rm N}\le N^2\|f\|_{\rm D},\qquad
       \|Jf\|_{\rm D}=\|f\|_{\rm D}.
 \qquad}
\]

The constructive inverse uses the triangular matrix
\(A_{jk}=e_k(c_j)=s_{j+k}/(s_{j-k}s_k^2)\), \(k\le j<r\), where
\(s_k=\prod_{h=1}^k2\sin(h\pi/N)\). Its exact node-gap inverse obeys
\(\|A^{-1}\|\le N^2/4\). Unturned values recover the low coefficients;
turned values recover the high coefficients. At odd levels the one
remaining middle coefficient is recovered from the simple value by
Lagrange extrapolation with every coefficient of absolute value at most
two. Thus no Hermite direction is removed in forming the metric.

For the original rows \(\lambda_0(f)=f(c_0)\) and
\(\phi_N(f)=(Jf)(c_0)\), and the original bilinear source, one obtains
\[
 |\lambda_0(f)|,\ |\phi_N(f)|\le(2\pi N)^{-1/2}\|f\|_{\rm D},
 \qquad
 |\phi_N(fg)|\le N^4\|f\|_{\rm D}\|g\|_{\rm D}.
\]
Any recorded closing scalar remains explicit. The last inequality is a
bilinear bound on two separate inputs, with no unit tensor-row claim.

In particular the full packet error satisfies
\[
 \|f-\widetilde f\|_{\rm N}\le
                         N^2\|f-\widetilde f\|_{\rm D}.
\]
The right side retains both actual value errors and genuinely turned
value errors, including the odd simple rows. The corresponding
observation map has a left inverse of norm at most \(N^2\).
This supplies a source-faithful synthesis and error adapter when those
complementary estimates are available.

No polynomial bound for the forward frame, its condition number, or
full multiplication is inferred. Every gate budget uses the same metric.
These are auxiliary pair-Casimir observations, without an identification
with ordinary main-meridian colors. The charge-normal scalar initializer
does not provide both observation sets or a lower bound for their
original marked closing coordinate. The geometric lower bound remains
unproved.

## A reported AJ multiplicity discrepancy does not replace the actual source, 23 November

The 19 November preprint by RJ Acuña reports, for \(8_{11}\),
\[
 \varepsilon^*(\widehat A)\asymp(L+M^6)A,
 \qquad \varepsilon(q,E,Q)=(1,L,M^2).
\]
Here its \(\widehat A\) is obtained by clearing denominators of the monic
minimal color-shift generator after Ore localization, and its \(A\) includes the abelian
factor \(L-1\). The paper states that \(L+M^6\) already divides \(A\): the
reported discrepancy is additional multiplicity, while the reduced
curve still satisfies its weak AJ formulation.
See the [primary abstract](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26905) and
[introduction, definitions, Conjectures 1–2 and Theorem 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.26905v1#S1).

Only the entire abstract and those specified introductory statements
were checked for this coverage update. The reported proof has not been
independently audited here and is not an input to the source argument.
In that paper \(\asymp\) permits a factor in \(\mathbb C(M)^\times\).
Such a factor can have a zero or pole at \(M=1\); this convention does
not authorize cancelling an original peripheral factor or its first
normal at completeness.

The [actual Weyl–Green calculation](research_actual_weyl_green_obstruction.md)
instead retains its specified whole cyclic operator and source:
\[
 B_N(U)v_N(U)=0,\qquad
 B_0v_1=-B_1v_0,\qquad K_N=N e_0^*v_1 .
\]
Here \(U=Y^N\), and the subscripts 0 and 1 are the actual constant
and first coefficients in \(U-1\). This source equation does not
require equality of a complete classical polynomial, its multiplicities,
or the minimal colored-Jones recurrence with an \(A\)-polynomial.
The reported external claim neither changes this identity nor supplies
the missing geometric projection or an original-source lower bound.
No new volume-conjecture result is asserted.

## Forward and backward recursion for the quartic minimum, 23 November

The [new iteration](research_conway_backward_forward_minimum_iteration.md)
replaces the half-gradient step by one backward transport of the actual
closing and one forced forward recursion. For the full normalized
quartic its contraction factor is at most \(15/2744\). After eliminating
the highest product's output and the turns above it, the factor is at
most \(5\zeta^2/C\), which decreases exponentially with the level.
Every packet still includes its repeated-root derivatives.

Here is the construction for that exactly eliminated problem. Write
\[
 F(u)=\|G(u)\|^2+|g(u)|^2,\qquad G(u)=\Phi(u)-u,\qquad
 g(u)=u_L^{\mathsf t}B u_R/\sqrt C,\quad
 \|B\|=\zeta,\quad t=\zeta/\sqrt C.
\]
The positive number \(C\) is the known closing-chain factor. Its original
scalar and budgets remain in \(B,\zeta\); the other recorded budgets
remain in their local maps and in the total source normalization.
For a prescribed forcing \(r\), the recursion
\[
 Y(r)_v=\Phi_v(Y(r)_{\rm children})-r_v
\]
uniquely solves \(G(Y(r))=r\). Put \(A_u=D\Phi(u)\). The row
\[
 d_u=Dg(u)(I-A_u)^{-1}
\]
is evaluated backward through the tree. The update is
\[
 \mathcal T_F(u)=Y(d_u^*g(u)).
\]
Its fixed-point equation is exactly the stationary equation for \(F\).
On the product of unit packet balls it stays in the packet balls of
radius \(1/16+2t^2\), and
\[
 \operatorname{Lip}(\mathcal T_F)\le5t^2
 \le5/65536<1/13000,\qquad
 5t_N^2\le
 \exp\{-4G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi+O(\log N)\}.
\]
Here \(G_{\rm Cat}=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(\cot s)\,ds\). The unique
fixed point is the minimizer of the same original quartic.

This also works on the smaller quartic with \(p-1\) packet variables,
where \(p\) is the number of products. This additional consequence uses
the exact scalar chain weights in the
[internal-edge reduction](research_conway_binary_skeleton_quartic.md).
After prescribing its known leaf inputs, write that objective as
\[
 F_{\rm cl}(u)=G(u)^*W^{-1}G(u)+|g(u)|^2,\qquad
 I\le W\le(256/255)I .
\]
Each block of \(W\) is the known positive scalar chain weight times
the packet identity. The maps in \(G=\Phi-u\) are the original products
followed by their known normalized turns, with prescribed leaf inputs
substituted. Their norms remain at most \(\sigma=1/16\); they form a
forest with one parent per variable. The same \(C,\zeta,t\) describe
the root term, which may become linear after a leaf is prescribed.
For \(p\le1\) there is no remaining minimization.

For \(p>1\), use the same \(d_u\) and replace the update by
\[
 \mathcal T_{\rm cl}(u)=Y(Wd_u^*g(u)).
\]
Indeed its stationary equation is
\(- (I-A_u)^*W^{-1}G(u)+(Dg(u))^*g(u)=0\), or
\(G(u)=Wd_u^*g(u)\). The inverse recursion satisfies
\(\operatorname{Lip}Y\le\rho=8/7\) on its feasible images.
The derivative bounds
\(\|Dg\|\le\sqrt2t\), \(\|D^2g\|\le t\), and
\(\|A_u-A_v\|\le\sigma\|u-v\|\) give
\[
 \|Wd_u^*g(u)\|\le(256/255)\rho\sqrt2\,t^2\le2t^2,
\]
\[
 \operatorname{Lip}(\mathcal T_{\rm cl})
 \le\frac{256}{255}
       \left(\frac{192}{49}+\frac{32\sqrt2}{343}\right)t^2
 \le5t^2.
\]
The first bound proves feasibility by forward induction before the
inverse Lipschitz estimate is used. Contraction and the established
strict convexity identify its fixed point with the smaller minimum.
That minimum need not equal the full one; it retains the source
comparison already proved for the prescribed-leaf restriction.

These are reductions in variables and in certified iteration error.
They supply no lower bound at the hyperbolic-volume rate. In particular
the first update from zero evaluates the actual open packets; it does
not bypass their coherent closing. The degree of the objective remains
at most four, while its packet dimension remains \(N\). The finite-exception
theorem is unchanged.

## A new Fourier comparison concerns the crossing matrices, 23 November

McPhail-Snyder's [12 November preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16987)
reports phase-controlled cyclic summation and a Fourier comparison of
holonomy braidings. For \(N\ge2\), put
\(\omega=e^{2\pi i/N}\), \(p=(N-1)/2\), and
\(\epsilon=(-1)^{N-1}\). At its pinched specialization
\(g_1=g_2=\epsilon I\), \(v_1=v_2\), \(\mu_1=\mu_2=p\),
the reported Kashaev and colored-Jones matrices obey
\[
 J=(F\otimes F)^{-1}K(F\otimes F),\qquad F_{jk}=\omega^{-jk}.
\]
Its Jones parameter is \(q=\omega^{1/2}\); the rescaled bases and
displayed framing/index conventions are part of the comparison.
See [Section 4.3, Propositions 4.6 and 4.8, and Corollary 4.10](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.16987v1#S4.SS3).

This is coverage of the entire abstract, notation, specialization setup
and those statements, not an audit of their proofs. They compare local
matrices; they do not assert a positive decomposition of the original
closed source over flat-connection sectors or geometric noncancellation.
No result from this paper is a proof input here. The finite-exception
theorem remains open.

## The squared marked source and the Weyl normalizer, 23 November

The [actual rank-one moment/source calculation](actual_rank_one_multiplicative_moment_and_orbit_source.md)
retains a divided moment and a separate orbit co-source. Their squared
normalizer agrees exactly, up to a minus sign, with the Weyl factor in
the corresponding Cartan three-form. This is a normalization calibration,
not a source-period comparison or a new volume theorem.

Write the actual clock and cyclic shift as \(X,Y\), and put
\[
 C=XYX^{-1}Y^{-1}=Q(I+dP),\qquad
 d=Q^{-N}-1,\qquad P=vw,\quad wv=1.
\]
The original orbit path is
\[
 S_Y=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}Y^r,\qquad \ell=wS_Y.
\]
For any supplied whole word matrix \(B\), keep that path and define
\[
 A_B=\operatorname{Tr}((Q^{-1}C-I)S_YB)
          =d\,\ell Bv.
\]
Every external framing or peripheral scalar stays attached to its
source. In particular, replacing \(\ell\) by \(w\) is not authorized.
Two independent holomorphic copies therefore satisfy
\[
 \frac{A_+A_-}{d_+d_-}
       =(\ell_+B_+v_+)(\ell_-B_-v_-).
\]
This quotient has removable singularities across both normal divisors.
To obtain a squared modulus, take the minus copy to be the conjugate
germ, including its recorded branches and external source line. Only
then restrict to \(|Q_+|=1,\ Q_-=Q_+^{-1}\). With
\[
 e^t=Q_+^{-N},\qquad
 \Delta^2=e^t+e^{-t}-2,
\]
the denominator is exactly
\[
                    d_+d_-=-\Delta^2.
\]

For comparison, let the marked projector \(P\) move on its orbit,
with \(P^2=P\), and regard \(C=Q(I+(e^t-1)P)\) as a family in
\((t,P)\). All differentials in the next calculation are exterior
differentials. Put \(\omega_P=\operatorname{Tr}(P\,dP\wedge dP)\).
Then
\[
 \chi_3(C):=\operatorname{Tr}((C^{-1}dC)^3)
          =3\Delta^2\,dt\wedge\omega_P .
\]
Here is a direct check. Set \(a=e^t-1\). Since \(P\,dP\,P=0\),
\[
 (I+aP)^{-1}d(I+aP)
 =\frac{da}{1+a}P
  +\frac{a}{1+a}P\,dP(1-P)+a(1-P)dP\,P.
\]
In the trace of its cube only the three cyclic products containing
one term of each type survive. Their sum is
\(3a^2da\wedge\omega_P/(1+a)^2\), which is the asserted formula.
The scalar factor \(Q\) adds nothing: the trace of the square of a
matrix-valued one-form is zero. Thus
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
       \frac{\chi_3(C)}{3\Delta^2}=dt\wedge\omega_P
       \qquad}
\]
extends regularly through \(t=0\) on the marked \((t,P)\) family.
It is not a descended formula at the central matrix \(C=Q I\)
after forgetting \(P\). The undivided form has quadratic vanishing
in its normal coefficient; its transgression with \(P\) fixed is
\(6(\sinh t-t)\omega_P=t^3\omega_P+O(t^5)\).

The relation with the ordinary RT dimension is equally exact. Put
\[
 [N]_q=\frac{q^N-q^{-N}}{q-q^{-1}},\qquad Q=q^2,\qquad
 q_N=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad t=-2N\operatorname{Log}(q/q_N),
\]
where the logarithm vanishes at the marked root. Then
\[
 \Delta^2=(q^N-q^{-N})^2,\qquad
 d(q^2)=-q^{-N}(q-q^{-1})[N]_q.
\]
On the unit circle,
\[
 |d(q^2)|^2=|q-q^{-1}|^2[N]_q^2=-\Delta^2.
\]
For \(q=e^{i(\pi+\theta)/N}\), \(|\theta|\le b<\pi\), the bounds
\[
 \frac{4(\pi-b)}{\pi N}\le |q-q^{-1}|
                         \le\frac{2(\pi+b)}N
\]
hold for every \(N\ge2\). They follow from
\(2\min(x,\pi-x)/\pi\le\sin x\le x\), \(0\le x\le\pi\).
After the exact removable factors are retained, the two squared
normalizers therefore differ by explicit factors of order \(N^{-2}\),
which do not change an established exponential rate of the same source.

The normalized form is not the ordinary regulator form. No equality
between its integral and the source energy has been proved. In the
canonical clock basis \(P\) is constant and \(\omega_P=0\); allowing
its orbit to move does not construct a geometric source cycle. The word
matrix, orbit path, marking and boundary currents remain necessary.
In particular this calculation supplies no geometric lower bound.

## The physical pairing is one coefficient extraction per head, 23 November

The [paired Gaussian proof](research_paired_bargmann_krein_sewing.md)
removes an unnecessary finite-exponential approximation from the
gluing calculation. There is also a shorter coefficient formula.
Set \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and use
the actual one-head matrix
\[
 H_N|a\rangle=qQ^a|d-a\rangle,\qquad 0\le a\le d.
\]
For full coefficient vectors \(u,v\), put
\(P_u(z)=\sum_{a=0}^d u_az^a\) and
\(P_u^\natural(z)=\sum_{a=0}^d\overline{u_a}z^a\). Direct
coefficient extraction gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 u^\dagger H_Nv
   &=q[z^d]P_u^\natural(z)P_v(Qz)\\
   &=\frac{q}{2\pi i}\oint_{|z|=\rho}
           P_u^\natural(z)P_v(Qz)\,\frac{dz}{z^N},
                    \qquad \rho>0 .
 \end{split}
\]
Indeed the extracted coefficient is
\(\sum_{b=0}^d\overline{u_{d-b}}Q^bv_b\).
The circle has positive orientation. Tensor products give one such
auxiliary coefficient extraction per head, retaining the quantum
shift and its phase.

The Gaussian version is equally explicit. With
\(h_a=a!/N^a\) and \(d\mu_N(z)=(N/\pi)e^{-N|z|^2}d^2z\),
the kernel representing this form is
\[
 \mathscr K_N(z,w)=q\frac{N^d}{d!}(z+Qw)^d,\qquad
 u^\dagger H_Nv=
 \iint\overline{P_u(z)}\mathscr K_N(z,\bar w)P_v(w)
                                      d\mu_N(z)d\mu_N(w).
\]
It represents the Gaussian Riesz matrix \(h^{-1}H_N\), where
\(h=\operatorname{diag}(h_a)\). It is different from the kernel
of the operator \(H_N\), which contains a truncated exponential.
The complete factor \(N^d/d!\) is kept.

The actual factorial frame also has an exact phased identity:
\[
 F_a=(Q;Q)_a,\quad G_F=\operatorname{diag}(F_a),\qquad
 F_a\overline{F_{d-a}}=N,\qquad
                    G_F^\dagger H_NG_F=NH_N .
\]
Thus its paired cost is exactly \(N\) per head. This is a congruence
of forms, not a positive condition-number estimate or the similarity
formula for a physical operator. An original row \(\lambda\) can
always be retained by its specified dual
\(H_N^{\otimes r}\lambda^\dagger\); it is not replaced by a cup.

The note computes both cap functions in this same calculus. In
particular the unrestricted marked cap retains the finite polynomial
\[
 \mathcal F_N(t)=\sum_{a=0}^d (Q;Q)_a\frac{t^a}{a!},
 \qquad
 \mathcal F_N'(t)=\mathcal F_N(t)-Q\mathcal F_N(Qt),
 \qquad \mathcal F_N(0)=1.
\]
It cannot be replaced by the nonzero local symbol of
\(\mathscr K_N\). The ordinary cap and a genuinely degree-restricted
marked cap instead have the explicitly retained quadratic chirp
given in the proof.

These identities simplify exact gluing and its auxiliary integrals.
The form is indefinite. The auxiliary Cauchy circles above are not
an identification with the original full-dilogarithm relative cycle;
no cut lip, endpoint, or competing source region has been removed.
The original cap's geometric contribution still requires an estimate.

## Prefix reduction preserves the physical adjoint, 23 November

The [prefix adjoint theorem](research_reduced_prefix_krein_descent.md)
supplies the pairing on the actual reduced braid representation.
For every \(N\ge2\), put \(d=N-1\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\),
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and
\[
 H_N|a\rangle=qQ^a|d-a\rangle,\qquad
 \mathscr H_b=H_N^{\otimes b},\qquad
 A^{\sharp_b}=\mathscr H_bA^\dagger\mathscr H_b .
\]
The common meridian is positive real, \(M>0\), with
\(x=-M/q\). These are the same physical forms on every head.

Let \(m\) be the original head count and \(r=m-1\).
The actual prefix change and its nilpotent argument are
\[
 S_m=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{Y^j}{(Q;Q)_j},\qquad
 Y=x^{-1}L_1F_{\rm r},\qquad Y^N=0.
\]
Here \(L_1\) is the unit lowering shift with its zero bottom
arrow and \(F_{\rm r}\) is the ordered remaining lowering
coproduct. Directly
\[
 L_1^\sharp=QL_1,\qquad F_{\rm r}^\sharp=Q^{-1}F_{\rm r},
 \qquad Y^\sharp=Q^{-1}Y,\qquad S_m^\sharp=S_m^{-1}.
\]
The finite Euler inverse proves the last equality, including
all endpoints.

For a matrix commuting with the original total lowering operator,
the transformed matrix has the unique expansion
\[
 S_m^{-1}WS_m=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}F_1^j\otimes B_j(W).
\]
Taking its constant coefficient is the existing actual reduction
\(\mathcal B_m(W)=B_0(W)\). Positive powers of \(F_1\) form a
nilpotent ideal preserved by the adjoint, since
\((F_1^j)^\sharp=Q^{-j}F_1^j\). Therefore
\[
 \mathcal B_m(W^{\sharp_m})
       =\mathcal B_m(W)^{\sharp_r},\qquad
 B_\beta(M)^\dagger\mathscr H_rB_\beta(M)=\mathscr H_r .
\]
The second identity applies to the original signed braid words.
It also polarizes to their complete holomorphic meridian germs,
so the reduced derivative pairings need no separate metric
construction. This descent uses the algebra of operators; the
first-head vacuum itself has zero norm for the physical form.

The scalar check is essential. In the actual reduced boundary
generator \(\kappa(M)S_rD_{\rm red}\),
\[
 D_{\rm red}^\sharp D_{\rm red}=M^{-2d}I,\qquad
 |\kappa(M)|^2=M^{2d}.
\]
Their product preserves the form. Stripping the original Cartan
scalar would give the wrong identity away from completeness.

The original pointed source is compatible with this adjoint too.
Its meromorphic trace density is
\[
 C_N(M)=\mathcal D_N(M)\mathcal D_N(MK_{\rm r}(M))^{-1},
 \qquad \mathcal D_N(z)=\frac{z^N-z^{-N}}{z-z^{-1}},
\]
with the Laurent-polynomial continuation understood.
For positive real \(M\), \(C_N^\sharp=C_N\); hence
\(\overline{\operatorname{Tr}(C_NB)}
 =\operatorname{Tr}(C_NB^\sharp)\).
The removable complete-color value retains the original first
meridian derivative and all external factors.

The forms remain indefinite, and this source functional is not
asserted positive. The theorem removes the unresolved adjoint
descent at the prefix reduction; it does not give a lower bound
for the prescribed closing, identify the two geometric eigenline
contributions, or prove the finite-exception theorem.

## The original pointed source has an exact adjoint sewing, 23 November

The [opposite-kernel adjoint proof](research_opposite_krein_adjoint_sewing.md)
uses the prefix descent above to identify the adjoint of the actual
opposite-polarization operator. The two sewn kernels are now a specified
single kernel and its adjoint, with the same original reduced word
between them.

Keep \(r=m-1\), \(d=N-1\), the frozen remaining Cartan \(K_0\),
and the actual opposite kernel \(T_M\). Its source-normalized version
and the additional fixed Cartan factor are
\[
 \mathcal H_M=\mathcal D_N(MK_{\rm r}(M)),\qquad
 J_M=\mathcal H_M^{-1}T_M,\qquad A_M=J_MK_0^{-1},
 \qquad \mathcal D_N(z)=\frac{z^N-z^{-N}}{z-z^{-1}} .
\]
Singular meridians are treated by the original continuation, with the
Laurent-polynomial continuation of \(\mathcal D_N\) understood, rather
than by separately specializing inverse factors. For positive real
common meridian \(M\), the exact
adjoints are
\[
 T_M^\sharp=T_{M^{-1}}K_0^{-2},\qquad
 J_M^\sharp=J_{M^{-1}}K_0^{-2},\qquad
 A_M^\sharp=A_{M^{-1}} .
\]
The proof includes the rectangular vacuum and top-row adjoints.
Their \(q\)-factors, the \(Q\)-factors from the ordered Cartan and
lowering power, and the two top-row factors \(N\) cancel explicitly.

Put
\[
 \sigma=(-1)^{d(m+1)},\qquad
 a_N(M)=\sigma N^{1-m}\mathcal D_N(M)^m .
\]
The original opposite-kernel composition gives
\[
 A_MA_M^\sharp=a_N(M)\mathcal H_M^{-1}.
\]
Consequently the original pointed source is exactly
\[
 \Phi_0(W_\beta(M))
   =\frac{\mathcal D_N(M)}{a_N(M)}
      \operatorname{Tr}_{U(M^{-1})}
        \bigl(A_M^\sharp B_\beta(M)A_M\bigr),\qquad
 \frac{\mathcal D_N(M)}{a_N(M)}
   =\sigma\left(\frac{N}{\mathcal D_N(M)}\right)^{m-1}.
\]
Here \(U(M^{-1})\) is the reflected remaining-head space.
The word \(B_\beta(M)\) and its meridian are unchanged.
The displayed sign, normalization, pivots and any additional external
lines retain their original positions. The complete-color value is
the finite part of this whole meromorphic trace.

For the actual unwindowed braid, its exact opposite intertwining
also makes the sandwiched matrix have at most a simple meridian
pole. If \(A(e^u)=R_A/u+A_0+\cdots\), then
\(R_A^\sharp=-R_A\), \(R_A^2=0\), and
\(R_AB_\beta(1)R_A=0\) as matrices. Arbitrary insertions or
separately restricted windows need not retain that cancellation;
their original relative defects and normal terms remain.
The earlier unadopted
\(\texttt{research\_opposite\_krein\_adjoint\_source.md}\)
incorrectly allowed a double matrix pole for the actual braid.
The corrected proof linked above supersedes that copy.

This is an indefinite Hermitian congruence for the original source,
not a positive Gram factorization. It settles the exact adjoint
sewing before geometric estimates are made. A nonzero geometric
degree, control of the complementary source, and the required
volume lower bound remain unproved.

## Physical coherent windows have explicit adjoint partners, 23 November

The compact source admits a positive resolution of the identity in the
original physical Euclidean basis. This makes adjoint windows explicit
without changing the original closing. Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\),
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and put
\[
 b_a=\binom da,\qquad G=\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{b_a}),\qquad
 u(z)_a=\sqrt{b_a}\,z^a,\qquad 0\le a\le d.
\]
On \(X=(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1)\setminus\{1+wz=0\}\), set
\[
 \Pi_s(w,z)=\frac{u(z)u(w)^{\mathsf T}}{(1+wz)^d},
 \qquad
 \nu=-\frac{dw\wedge dz}{2\pi i(1+wz)^2}.
\]
These expressions extend across the affine coordinate infinities.
On the compact sphere \(\Gamma=\{w=v,\ z=\bar v\}\), oriented by \(v\),
\[
                         N\int_\Gamma\Pi_s\,\nu=I.
\]
Angular integration kills unequal indices; the diagonal radial
integral is \(1/[N\binom da]\). Moreover \(\Pi_s\) on this sphere is
a positive rank-one Euclidean projector of trace one. Tensor products
give the full identity on every original physical tensor space.
If \(C\) is an oriented measurable subset of \(\Gamma^r\), with its
induced orientation, its partial resolution therefore satisfies
\(0\le P_C\le I\); it is not generally an idempotent.

Keep the physical tensor form \(\mathscr H_r=H_N^{\otimes r}\),
where \(H_N|a\rangle=qQ^a|d-a\rangle\), and its adjoint \(\sharp\).
The antiholomorphic involution
\[
             \iota(w,z)=(Q/\bar z,\ Q^{-1}/\bar w)
\]
preserves \(X\). On \(\Gamma\) it is the holomorphic Möbius map
\(v\mapsto Q/v\), so it preserves the sphere orientation. Direct
differentiation gives \(\iota^*\nu=\bar\nu\). The complete head
identities, with their phases retained, are
\[
 H_Nu(z)=q^{-1}z^d u(Q^{-1}/z),\qquad
 u(w)^{\mathsf T}H_N=q w^d u(Q/w)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
It follows, first in the displayed affine chart and then globally, that
\[
 \Pi_s(w,z)^\sharp=\Pi_s(\iota(w,z)),\qquad
 P_C^\sharp=P_{\iota C},\qquad
 P_C=N^r\int_C\Pi_s^{\otimes r}\,\nu^{[r]}.
\]
The last two formulas hold for every compact oriented real
\(2r\)-chain in \(X^r\). Here \(\nu^{[r]}\) is the ordered product
measure and \(\iota\) acts on each head. Boundaries go to
\(\iota(\partial C)\); none has been discarded.

For a physical one-head matrix \(L\), use the symmetric polynomial
kernel \(K_L(w,z)=u(w)^{\mathsf T}Lu(z)\). Its exact adjoint carrier is
\[
 K_{L^\sharp}(w,z)
       =(wz)^d\,\overline{K_L(\iota(w,z))}.
\]
The tensor formula has one such carrier per head. Normalizing by
\((1+wz)^d\), together with the transformed measure, accounts for
the carrier in the projector identity; it is not suppressed as an
amplitude of modulus one.

For the actual kernel \(A_M=J_MK_0^{-1}\) in the preceding adjoint
source proof, \(A_M^\sharp=A_{M^{-1}}\) at positive real meridians.
Thus its original window transport error
\[
 \mathcal E_{C,D}(M)=P_CA_M-A_MP_D
\]
has the exact symmetry
\[
 \mathcal E_{C,D}(M)^\sharp
             =-\mathcal E_{\iota D,\iota C}(M^{-1}).
\]
This does not make the error zero, even for \(D=\iota C\).
The reflected meridian in this formula is not the operator inverse.

The original asymmetric projector was
\(\Pi_{\rm old}=c(z)v(w)/(1+wz)^d\), with
\(c(z)_a=b_az^a\) and \(v(w)_a=w^a\). Exactly
\(\Pi_s=G^{-1}\Pi_{\rm old}G\). One can use this new identity
resolution while keeping every original physical matrix. Equivalently,
one can use the old resolution and conjugate every coupon \(L\) to
\(GLG^{-1}\), tensorwise. The constant frames cancel on complete
gluings. The original closing density, including the highest-cut and
tail-pivot density, commutes with these diagonal frames. Thus the
whole original scalar, its finite part and all fixed meridian
derivatives are unchanged. This is consistent with the existing
cyclic-frame theorem.

The local cost must still be retained. For an old partial window,
\[
 (P_{C,s})_{ab}=\sqrt{b_b/b_a}\,(P_{C,\rm old})_{ab}.
\]
Uniform Stirling bounds give its logarithmic frame factor as
\[
 \frac N2\{\mathfrak h(b/N)-\mathfrak h(a/N)\}+O(\log N),
 \qquad
 \mathfrak h(t)=-t\log t-(1-t)\log(1-t),
\]
with the continuous endpoint convention. Opposite frame factors
cancel term by term in complete occupation contractions. This need
not happen on a previously selected old geometric window. No new
boundary current is introduced by a constant frame, but equality or
smallness of the old and new geometric windows has not been proved.

The reflection also sends \(t=wz/(1+wz)\) to \(1-\bar t\).
The Cartan symbol is unchanged by the diagonal frame and obeys
\(\sigma_K(\iota)=\overline{\sigma_K}\); this follows directly from
\[
 \sigma_K(w,z)=x_0
       \left(\frac{1+Q^{-1}wz}{1+wz}\right)^d,\qquad x_0=-q^{-1}.
\]
Consequently adjoint reflection conjugates the clock. It is not
itself the Weyl exchange of two loxodromic eigenlines of one
geometric representation. Likewise it replaces an actual reduced
word \(B\) by \(B^{-1}\). These positive local resolutions and their
adjoint partners do not make the marked source a positive functional,
or prove its geometric degree or lower bound.

## The canonical primitive pairing has an exact signed decomposition, 23 November

The reciprocal lowering flags give a Hermitian pairing preserved
by the same actual reduced braid. Its occupation decomposition
shows why passing to this primitive quotient does not make that
pairing positive. This calculation applies at every fixed width
in its stated range, without an odd-level restriction.

Fix \(2\le r<N\), \(m=r+1\), \(d=N-1\),
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and \(x_0=-q^{-1}\). On the
remaining \(r\) heads put
\[
 \chi=x_0^r,\qquad s=N-r,\qquad D=rd,\qquad
 A=E_r^s:U_{\chi^{-1}}\longrightarrow U_\chi .
\]
Here \(U_\lambda\) is the actual remaining Cartan eigenspace
with eigenvalue \(\lambda\), and \(E_r\) is the ordered lowering
coproduct with head coefficient \(Q^{-a}-1\). All endpoint
arrows retain their original zero values. Since
\(\chi^2=Q^s\ne1\) and \(E_r^\sharp=QE_r\), the form
\[
                 g_\chi(u,v)=\chi\,u^\dagger\mathscr H_rE_r^s v
\]
is Hermitian on \(U_{\chi^{-1}}\). Indeed its matrix adjoint
multiplies \(E_r^s\) by \(Q^s=\chi^2\), canceling conjugation
of \(\chi\). The form \(\mathscr H_r\) pairs the two Cartan
spaces nondegenerately. Hence the radical is exactly \(\ker A\),
and \(g_\chi\) is nondegenerate on
\[
 \mathcal Q_\chi=U_{\chi^{-1}}/\ker E_r^s,\qquad
                  \dim\mathcal Q_\chi=rN^{r-2}.
\]
The dimension is the reciprocal-chain rank formula.

Write an actual reduced root braid's blocks on \(U_\chi\) and
\(U_{\chi^{-1}}\) as \(X\) and \(Y\). The division-free Ward
identity gives \(XA=AY\). Combined with the prefix isometry
for \(\mathscr H_r\), this gives
\(g_\chi(Yu,Yv)=g_\chi(u,v)\). In particular the radical is
invariant and the quotient carries the same word with all its
original crossing scalars.

The possible integer occupation degrees in \(U_{\chi^{-1}}\)
are precisely \(k_j=jN-r\), \(1\le j\le r\). The kernel of
\(E_r^s\) is graded, so the quotient splits into corresponding
spaces \(\mathcal Q_j\). Lowering by \(s\) followed by reflection
by \(\mathscr H_r\) shows
\[
 g_\chi(\mathcal Q_j,\mathcal Q_\ell)=0
                       \quad\hbox{unless}\quad j+\ell=r+1.
\]
Nondegeneracy makes each cross pairing of distinct paired degrees
nondegenerate. Their dimensions are equal and their sum has a
hyperbolic Hermitian form. The actual braid preserves every
summand because its prefix reduction preserves integer degree.
For even \(r\), there is no middle degree; the whole signature is
\[
               \left(\frac{rN^{r-2}}2,\frac{rN^{r-2}}2\right).
\]
For odd \(r\), only \(j=(r+1)/2\) can contribute a signature
imbalance.

There is already an explicit hyperbolic plane at every
\(2\le r<N\). For
\[
 u=|s,0,\ldots,0\rangle,\qquad v=|d,\ldots,d\rangle
\]
the two diagonal pairings vanish by degree, while
\[
 g_\chi(u,v)=
             (-1)^{r(s+1)}q^{(r-1)s}(Q;Q)_s\ne0 .
\]
Only the term lowering the first head \(s\) times contributes
to this coefficient. Its lowering product is
\((-1)^s(Q;Q)_s\), its remaining top Cartan factor is
\((-q)^{(r-1)s}\), and its tensor-reflection phase is \(q^r\).
Multiplication by \(\chi\) gives the displayed coefficient.
It is nonzero because \(s<N\). Both classes survive the radical
quotient, and their Gram matrix has one positive and one negative
eigenvalue. Thus neither changing the overall sign nor removing
the radical makes this canonical pairing positive.

This is an exact orthogonality decomposition, not a replacement
for the original closing. In particular the normal and off-diagonal
couplings in the actual word-source formula remain. Indefiniteness
of this particular invariant form does not rule out every other
metric on a selected packet, but it excludes deriving positivity
from this canonical quotient alone. A separate geometric source
estimate is still necessary.

## Fourier cancellation bounds every fixed signed filling source, 23 November

The [complete-source Fourier proof](research_complete_circle_source_fourier_cancellation.md)
gives an exponential cancellation estimate for the original closed
circle source. It applies to every fixed choice of signed crossing
powers, without assuming that any of them is large. Fix an original
circle template with at least one edge and edge set \(E\), at the quantum root
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and retain all its vertex traces and the prescribed
marked closing. Write \(K_N(\mathbf n)\) for that exact scalar, with
the original framing phase included. For a knot-producing assignment,
this is its original normalized knot invariant.

Define its unfilled source rate by
\[
 F_0=\frac{4|E|G_{\rm Cat}}{\pi},\qquad
 G_{\rm Cat}=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(\cot u)\,du .
\]
For every fixed signed assignment \(\mathbf n\), there are
\(C_{\mathbf n},A_{\mathbf n},\eta_{\mathbf n}>0\) such that
\[
 |K_N(\mathbf n)|
       \le C_{\mathbf n}N^{A_{\mathbf n}}
                           e^{N(F_0-\eta_{\mathbf n})}.
\]
The estimate holds along the whole sequence of levels; no parity or
coprimality condition enters. No hyperbolicity assumption is needed
for this upper bound on the finite source.

### One fixed coordinate gives a common loss in the exponential rate

There is a stronger consequence for a fixed short partial assignment.
Choose a vertex \(v_0\) incident to an edge and fix its signed power
\(n_0\). If \(\mathbf m\) denotes all remaining powers, then a single
\(\eta_{v_0,n_0}>0\) satisfies
\[
 \sup_{\mathbf m\in\mathbb Z^{\,V\setminus\{v_0\}}}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log|K_N(n_0,\mathbf m)|
                     \le F_0-\eta_{v_0,n_0},
\]
where \(V\) is the vertex set and \(\log0=-\infty\).
Each completion is fixed before the level tends to infinity.
The prefactors and the starting level may depend on that completion.
The supremum has not been moved inside the limit.
Restricting the other coordinates by any additional fixed partial
assignment preserves this bound, including restriction to completions
which give hyperbolic knots.

The proof selects its cancellation scale using only \(v_0,n_0\).
All other vertex powers enter through polynomial bounds for their
closing rows. They change prefactors, but do not reduce this selected
exponential loss. The original discarded-channel loss is also
independent of the fixed powers. This proves the common rate bound
without separate estimates for individual short filling patterns.

### Why the original closing cancels the central contribution

The exact full vertex trace is a sampled total derivative:
\[
 \phi_N(R^n A)=\eta C_{N,n}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}
 \left.\frac{d}{d\psi}
 \left\{\sin\psi\,e^{inN\psi^2/(4\pi)}
                         A(-2\cos\psi)\right\}
                                      \right|_{\psi=\psi_j},
\]
with \(\eta=(-1)^{N-1}\),
\(\psi_j=-\pi+(2j+1)\pi/N\), and
\(C_{N,n}=q^{n(N-1)^2/4}\).
This includes the original value and first-normal terms at double
roots and the value at the odd simple root.

After Gaussian Fourier transformation, Poisson summation of the
complete derivative gives a factor equal to its integer frequency.
The zero frequency therefore vanishes exactly. On the retained
angular lift \(-\pi<\theta<\pi\), the remaining bulk relations at
a vertex of valence \(h\) are
\[
 \theta_i=\epsilon_i\theta,\qquad
 \sum_{i=1}^{h}\epsilon_i\xi_i+
                          \frac{n\theta}{2\pi}
                         \in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\},
       \qquad \epsilon_i\in\{1,-1\}.
\]
Here \(\theta_i\) and \(\xi_i\) are the Gaussian frame's angle and
scaled Fourier coordinates. The angular cut and coefficient-band
boundary strips remain in the quantitative statement. The proof
does not discard them or commute a cutoff through the closing.

For the retained edge indices \(k/N\in[1/5,3/10]\), the exact
factor-pairing argument gives nonnegative Laurent coefficients.
Their exponential-moment bound controls frequency tails. The
Gaussian frame's angle marginal is exactly the heat convolution of
the squared original polynomial, so the full-period angular bound
also controls its angle tails. Together these concentrate the
retained source near zero angle and zero frequency. The complete
vertex row is exponentially small there because its zero Poisson
frequency has canceled.

Cauchy--Schwarz in the exact frame pairing then bounds the original
scalar on this central region and its complement. Restoring all
discarded index assignments with the original finite-source estimate
gives the displayed strict loss below \(F_0\). The first normal is
essential: bounding its terms separately would lose the cancellation.

### The remaining volume problem

These are upper bounds relative to the unfilled source rate.
The loss has not been identified with the change in hyperbolic volume
under a partial or complete filling. The result also gives no lower
bound for the surviving nonzero frequencies. The finite-exception
theorem still requires their sharp volume rate and a nonzero geometric
contribution after every required fixed short partial filling.

## Matrix conditioning independent of the level, 23 November

The [covariance estimate](research_dimension_free_positive_conway_covariance.md)
improves the positive matrix recursion without changing its original
closing. It permits fixed positive evaluation points and controls the
absolute error in extracting the original invariant. The evaluation
points depend on the expression's number of leaves, not on the quantum
level or the normalization budget.

Use the complete normalized compiler, with full tensor
Hilbert--Schmidt norms at most \(\sigma=1/16\), budget product \(B_N\),
and original normalized closing row \(L\). Let \(a_v\) be the true
normalized packet, \(S_v(\varepsilon)\) the existing positive recursion
with fresh error \(\varepsilon I\) at every proper vertex, and
\(V_v=S_v-a_va_v^\dagger\). The stronger estimate is
\[
 \varepsilon I\preceq V_v\preceq2\varepsilon I,\qquad
 \varepsilon I\preceq S_v
                    \preceq(\sigma^2+2\varepsilon)I,
                 \qquad 0<\varepsilon\le1 .
\]
These are bounds in positive matrix order. At a product, its full
tensor operator has norm at most \(\sigma\); the exact covariance
recursion consequently gives
\[
 V_v\preceq
   (\varepsilon+4\sigma^4\varepsilon+
                          4\sigma^2\varepsilon^2)I
 \preceq2\varepsilon I .
\]
The unary and leaf cases complete induction, with no factor for the
physical dimension or number of vertices. In particular the earlier
additive error bound \(\theta/128\) for the unnormalized square now
holds with \(\varepsilon=\theta/B_N^2\), instead of
\(\theta/(NB_N^2)\), for \(0<\theta\le1\).

There is a stronger consequence for exact extraction. If the expression
has \(l\ge1\) leaf occurrences, the already established polynomial
\[
 F_N(\varepsilon)=B_N^2LS_{\rm top}(\varepsilon)L^\dagger
      =|K_N|^2+\sum_{j=1}^l c_{N,j}\varepsilon^j
\]
has degree at most \(l\). Put \(a=(l+1)^{-2}\) and choose
\[
 x_j=\cos(j\pi/l),\qquad
 \varepsilon_j=(1+a)/2+(1-a)x_j/2,\qquad 0\le j\le l .
\]
Let \(w_j\) be the Lagrange interpolation weights for evaluation at
zero using these \(\varepsilon_j\). Then
\[
 |K_N|^2=\sum_{j=0}^l w_jF_N(\varepsilon_j),\qquad
 \sum_{j=0}^l|w_j|
  =\cosh\!\left(2l\,\operatorname{atanh}\frac1{l+1}\right)
  \le\cosh2<4 .
\]
Every intermediate positive matrix in these evaluations satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{cond}_2S_v(\varepsilon_j)
                         \le2+\frac{(l+1)^2}{256}.
\]
Thus the message conditioning is independent of \(N\), and extraction
amplifies absolute scalar errors by less than four, independently of
both \(N\) and \(l\). For errors in the normalized observations
\(LS_{\rm top}L^\dagger\), the bound is instead \(4B_N^2\) times
their absolute error. The full budget must be restored.

Fixed-degree extraction and removal of the auxiliary minimization
were already proved. The new ingredients are the operator covariance
bound and its combination with these sampling points. The polynomial
degree counts auxiliary errors; the physical boundary dimension
remains \(N\), with all phases and Hermite directions retained.
The final signed scalar combination can still be exponentially smaller
than its positive summands. These estimates therefore do not supply
relative precision or the missing geometric lower bound after arbitrary
fixed short partial fillings. The finite-exception theorem remains open.
