O639 `d52c6dd8e62f575a262fc7af460e258f7cb0e40b5a9c037ac46dd8d151002d44`,
I623 `abd8009aa0e0e729efe82450a4f838fe1bdf250574cedf82a7c84a51e2e1de8e`,
M482 `bf9bd5c282d478c9cfff7c93da5546a76177315724292c33dea528d5e1dd729f`,
and the marked Gauss calculus
`7f8c7c0be05331e7c0679c5a26374bbcb4b38b817c36a1f4ac4e16d4c1739095`.
The general periodic-prolate commuting-Jacobi method is established;
see [Dirckx--Huybrechs--Ongenae, section 2.3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.12583).
No estimate or unproved spectral assertion from that paper is used
here: (JF2)--(JF8) provide the complete finite calculation and ordering
for this actual flag.

## Actual Gauss flags and the projected-row Gram have exponential conditioning, 23 November

The actual two-head Gauss primary decomposition has an exponentially
small angle on the same macroscopic degree range as its initialized
kernel. This is a statement about the prescribed matrices, rather than
a generic nonnormal example. The finite Fourier Gram in the projected
boundary row also has an exponentially large inverse. Neither estimate
determines that particular signed row contraction or the knot scalar.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and
\(x_0=-q^{-1}\). In the original orthonormal basis
\(|a,T-a\rangle\), assume
\[
 0\le T\le d,\qquad \ell=d-T\ge1,\qquad
                    t=2T+2-N=N-2\ell>0.
 \tag{GA1}
\]
Thus \(1\le t<N\), \(\ell<N/2\), and the actual total Cartan
\(K_T=Q^{-T-1}\) is a present nonself weight satisfying
\(K_T^2=Q^{-t}\). Conditions (GA1), rather than an arbitrary choice
of a square root, specify every admissible level and parity below.
Write \(\mathcal H_T\) for this degree space and use the actual
ordered lowering and raising maps \(E,F\).

For an integer \(j\), define the entire capped vector
\[
 c_T^j(a)=q^{a^2}{T\brack a}_Q Q^{ja},\quad 0\le a\le T,
 \qquad {T\brack a}_Q=\frac{F_T}{F_aF_{T-a}},\quad
 F_a=(Q;Q)_a.
\]
The two nonzero contributions to an output coefficient of \(Ec_T^j\)
are
\((Q^{-a-1}-1)x_0Q^{-T+a+1}c_T^j(a+1)\) and
\((Q^{-T+a}-1)c_T^j(a)\). Their finite Gaussian ratio gives
\[
             Ec_T^j=Q^{-T}(1-Q^j)(1-Q^T)c_{T-1}^{j+1}.
 \tag{GA2}
\]
No outward endpoint arrow is included. Applying (GA2) repeatedly shows
that \(c_T^0,c_T^{-1},\ldots,c_T^{-t+1}\) lie in
\(\mathcal W=\ker(E^t|_{\mathcal H_T})\). They are independent by
the Vandermonde matrix in \(Q^{-a}\). The map
\(E^t:\mathcal H_T\to\mathcal H_{T-t}\) has full row rank: on
the input columns \(0\le a\le T-t\), its extreme term lowering
only the last head gives a triangular matrix with nonzero diagonal.
Every factor has an index between \(1\) and \(T<N\). Hence
\[
 \mathcal W=\operatorname{span}\{c_T^{-j}:0\le j<t\},
 \qquad \dim\mathcal W=t,\qquad T-t+1=\ell.
 \tag{GA3}
\]

Identify \(\mathcal H_T\) with its zero extension in \(\mathbb C^N\),
and let \(P_T\) be the occupation projection onto \(0\le a\le T\).
All orthogonal complements of flags below are taken within \(\mathcal H_T\).
The normalized twisted Fourier vectors
\[
 f_h(a)=N^{-1/2}x_0^aQ^{ha},\quad h\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z,
 \qquad P_\ell(z)=(Qz;Q)_\ell
\]
are an orthonormal basis at every parity. Root factorial reflection
gives the exact phase identity
\[
 c_T^{-j}(a)=\gamma\,x_0^aQ^{-(\ell+j)a}P_\ell(Q^a),\qquad
 \gamma=\frac{(-1)^\ell F_TQ^{-\ell(\ell+1)/2}}{N}\ne0.
 \tag{GA4}
\]
For \(a>T\) the product on the right contains \(1-Q^N\), so it
already vanishes; no extra tail has been dropped. Since \(P_\ell\)
has degree \(\ell\), (GA4) puts \(\mathcal W\) in the Fourier
band with indices \(-\ell-t+1,\ldots,0\). Define
\[
 Q_{\rm obs}=\sum_{h=1}^{\ell}f_hf_h^\dagger,\qquad Q_B=I-Q_{\rm obs}.
\]
The \(\ell\) vectors \(P_Tf_h\), \(1\le h\le\ell\), are
independent, again by Vandermonde. Comparing their dimension with
(GA3) proves the exact physical identifications
\[
 \mathcal W=\mathcal H_T\cap\operatorname{im}Q_B,
 \qquad
 \mathcal W^\perp=\operatorname{span}\{P_Tf_h:1\le h\le\ell\}.
 \tag{GA5}
\]
The transpose identities \(E^{\mathsf T}=x_0^{-1}KF\) and their
powers show that \((E^t)^{\mathsf T}\) is a nonzero scalar times
\(F^t\) between these two degree spaces. Also
\(\overline{f_h}=f_{1-h}\), since \(x_0^2=Q^{-1}\). Thus the
actual second flag is
\[
 \mathcal Y=\operatorname{im}(F^t|_{\mathcal H_{T-t}})
       =\overline{\mathcal W^\perp}
       =\operatorname{span}\{P_Tf_h:1-\ell\le h\le0\}.
 \tag{GA6}
\]
These are the actual \(E/F\) flags, with their original ordering.

The landing and transpose identities in the following section give
\(\operatorname{im}A_N(1)=\mathcal W\) and
\(\ker A_N(1)=\mathcal Y\) on this degree. The marked Gauss
factorization (17d) is a unit on the lower primary sum and is zero
on the upper primary sum at \(M=1\). Consequently
\(\mathcal H_T=\mathcal W\oplus\mathcal Y\), and its actual lower
primary Riesz projection \(\Pi_{\rm low}\) has range \(\mathcal W\)
and kernel \(\mathcal Y\). This identifies the projector whose
norm is estimated; an unrelated upper Fourier sector is not substituted.

For a quantitative angle test use the exact vector
\[
 w(a)=x_0^aQ^{-\ell a}P_\ell(Q^a)\in\mathcal W.
\]
Write \(P_\ell(z)=\sum_{n=0}^\ell p_nz^n\), so \(p_0=1\).
Its Fourier expansion is
\(w=\sqrt N\sum_{n=0}^\ell p_nf_{n-\ell}\). Removing only
the first Fourier term and then taking the physical time projection
gives
\[
 y=P_T(w-\sqrt N f_{-\ell})\in\mathcal Y,\qquad
 \|w-y\|=\sqrt{T+1}\le\sqrt N,\qquad
 \|w\|^2=N\sum_{n=0}^{\ell}|p_n|^2.
 \tag{GA7}
\]
Since \(\Pi_{\rm low}(w-y)=w\), for \(k=\lfloor\ell/2\rfloor\)
this yields the all-level bound
\[
 \|\Pi_{\rm low}\|
    \ge |p_k|=\left|{\ell\brack k}_Q\right|
    =\prod_{j=1}^k
       \frac{\sin(\pi(\ell-k+j)/N)}{\sin(\pi j/N)}
    \ge(4/\pi)^k.
 \tag{GA8}
\]
For the last inequality, \(\ell<N/2\) permits
\(\sin(\pi b/N)\ge2b/N\) for each numerator index and
\(\sin(\pi j/N)\le\pi j/N\) in the denominator. Each ratio
is at least \((2/\pi)(\ell-k+j)/j\ge4/\pi\).
The empty product at \(k=0\) is one. Equivalently the smallest
angle between these two actual flags has sine at most
\(\left|{\ell\brack k}_Q\right|^{-1}\).

For the initialized physical degrees
\(\sigma=(T+1)/N\in I\Subset(1/2,1)\), one has
\(\ell/N=1-\sigma\) in a fixed positive compact interval.
Thus (GA8) is an exponential lower bound, uniformly on that range
for all sufficiently large admissible levels. The two orthogonal
flag projections still have norm one. It is their actual oblique
primary splitting that cannot have a uniform polynomial norm bound.

The Hermitian Gram in the projected-row calculation has its own
quantitative bound. Let \(R\) extract the omitted occupations
\(T+1,\ldots,d\), and put
\[
 G=RQ_BR^\dagger=I_\ell-RQ_{\rm obs}R^\dagger>0.
 \tag{GG1}
\]
Positivity follows by evaluating degree-\((\ell-1)\) polynomials
at retained Fourier nodes. In particular \(R\) is onto on
\(\operatorname{im}Q_B\). The exact orthogonal projection is
\(P_{\mathcal W}=Q_B-Q_BR^\dagger G^{-1}RQ_B\); its restriction
to the physical time space is the one used in the actual boundary row.
The inverse in (GG1) is therefore a specified source calculation,
not an arbitrarily chosen Gram.

Set \(\nu=\ell-1\), \(\beta=\pi(\ell+1)/N\), and use the retained
indices \(B=\{\ell+1,\ldots,N\}\), with \(N\) representing zero.
The least eigenvalue is equivalently the minimum of
\(N^{-1}\sum_{h\in B}|p(Q^h)|^2/\|p\|_{\rm coeff}^2\)
over nonzero polynomials of degree at most \(\nu\).
Test \(p(z)=(1+e^{-i\beta}z)^\nu\). Every retained point has
angular distance at least \(\beta\) from its center, while
\(\|p\|_{\rm coeff}^2=\binom{2\nu}{\nu}\ge4^\nu/(2\nu+1)\).
It follows that
\[
       \|G^{-1}\|\ge
         \frac{1}{(2\nu+1)\cos^{2\nu}(\beta/2)}.
 \tag{GG2}
\]
There is also an elementary exponential upper envelope. Interpolate
at the \(\ell\) retained consecutive roots
\(Q^{\ell+1},\ldots,Q^{2\ell}\). Their Lagrange polynomials
\(L_j\), \(0\le j\le\nu\), satisfy
\[
 \|L_j\|_{\rm coeff}\le
       \frac{(N/2)^\nu}{j!(\nu-j)!},\qquad
 \sum_j\|L_j\|_{\rm coeff}\le\frac{N^\nu}{\nu!}.
\]
Indeed each numerator has coefficient norm at most \(2^\nu\),
and the denominator is at least
\((4/N)^\nu j!(\nu-j)!\), since every root separation is less
than half the circle. Consequently
\[
                 \|G^{-1}\|\le
                           N\left(\frac{N^\nu}{\nu!}\right)^2.
 \tag{GG3}
\]
Both bounds include \(\ell=1\). On the macroscopic initialized
range they show \(e^{c_I N}\le\|G^{-1}\|\le e^{C_I N}\) for
positive constants and sufficiently large levels. The upper estimate
uses \(\nu!\ge(\nu/e)^\nu\); the lower uses the fixed positive
margin in \(\beta\).

These bounds prevent treating either the actual oblique primary
projector or this whole inverse Gram as a polynomial-cost frame on
that range. They do not show that the particular signed projected
row attains the worst direction. Its two source vectors, both flags,
the complementary meridian normal, and the full marked sewing still
remain. No degree-complexification, original scalar lower bound,
or counterexample about knots or short fillings follows.

## The initialized Gauss packet lands in a lowering flag, but its full paired source does not compress, 23 November

The matched windows below allow an exact test on an already initialized
packet. At physical nodes the entire Gauss kernel lands in one lowering
flag. Its two interfaces are related by ordinary transpose. This does
not give a proper Hermitian window capturing the full reciprocal pair,
and its complementary first normal is nonzero.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(x_0=-q^{-1}\), and \(r\ge2\) remaining heads. Keep the original
finite occupation basis and the fixed-root meridian family \(M=e^\mu\).
The actual Gauss and opposite operators are
\[
 A_N(M)=q_F(M)E_\Sigma(M)^d i_d,\qquad
 T(M)=q_F(M)E_\Sigma(M)^d\mathscr C_m(M)i_0,
 \quad m=r+1.
 \tag{GK1}
\]
Here \(q_F=p_0S_m^{-1}\), and \(i_d\) inserts the first occupation
\(d\). These are the original capped maps, not scalar spectral values.
Write \(A_0=A_N(1)\). For a physical nonself weight \(\chi\), with
projector \(P_\chi\), choose
\(1\le t<N\) with \(\chi^2=Q^{-t}\). The resonant prefix row gives
\[
 E_r^tq_F=q_FE_\Sigma^t
 \quad\hbox{on full total weight }x_0\chi.
\]
The vector \(E_\Sigma^di_dP_\chi\) has precisely this weight:
\(i_d\) gives \(x_0Q\chi\), and \(E_\Sigma^d\) multiplies it by
\(Q^d=Q^{-1}\). Consequently the exact physical-node identity is
\[
             E_r^tA_0P_\chi
                =q_FE_\Sigma^{t+d}i_dP_\chi=0.
 \tag{GK2}
\]
Only the actual nilpotence \(E_\Sigma^N=0\) and the division-free
resonant row have been used. This holds at every level and for every
present nonself weight, with no small-occupation hypothesis.

On a whole reciprocal pair, use the two exact arrows
\(\mathsf a=E^s\), \(\mathsf b=E^{N-s}\), \(Q^s=\chi^2\), and
\(\delta=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&\mathsf a\\\mathsf b&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).
Set \(\mathcal Z=\ker\delta=\operatorname{im}\delta\).
The exact routing is
\[
 T(M)=L(M)A_N(M)R(M),\qquad
 L=\mathcal B_m(W_\tau^{-1}),\quad \tau=\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_r,\quad
 R=D_{\rm top}\mathscr C_r.
 \tag{GK3}
\]
Both endpoint factors are analytic and invertible near zero. At the
root they preserve the reciprocal pair as a set. The opposite-source
residue has rank half the pair dimension, and its diagonal factor relating it
to \(T(1)\) is invertible on this nonself pair. Thus \(T(1)\), and
hence \(A_0\), has rank half the pair dimension. Formula (GK2) and
exactness of the two arrows now give
\[
                    \operatorname{im}A_0=\mathcal Z.
 \tag{GK4}
\]
All spaces here retain their integer-degree grading. Since \(A_0\)
preserves that grading, (GK4) also holds after restriction to each
physical total degree.

Both kernel interfaces can be specified exactly. The literal root
formula is
\[
 A_0=(-1)^dN\sum_{n=0}^d
       \frac{(-1)^nq^{n^2}}{(Q;Q)_n^2}F^nE^nK^{d-n}.
 \tag{GK5}
\]
On one head, \(E^{\mathsf T}=x_0^{-1}KF\) and
\(F^{\mathsf T}=x_0EK^{-1}\); the ordered coproduct gives the
same identities on an interval. The powers in
\((F^nE^n)^{\mathsf T}\) have cancelling \(Q\)-factors and give
\(K^nF^nE^nK^{-n}=F^nE^n\). Since \(K\) commutes with this
product, every summand in (GK5) is symmetric. Thus
\(A_0^{\mathsf T}=A_0\), with ordinary bilinear transpose.
If \(P_{\mathcal Z}\) is the Euclidean orthogonal projection onto
\(\mathcal Z\), then
\[
       A_0=P_{\mathcal Z}A_0P_{\mathcal Z}^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{GK6}
\]
The right projection is onto \(\overline{\mathcal Z}\), not an
unidentified copy of the original incoming lowering flag.

This applies directly to the complete capped ordinary-binomial kernel
of the [initialized complex-degree packet](research_fixed_width_coherent_complex_degree_interpolation.md).
At each physical degree node with nonself weight, inserting the two
projections in (GK6) leaves \(v(w)A_0c_T(z)\) unchanged for all its
finite input and output variables. Its proved nodal asymptotic,
vacuum normalization, phases and amplitude are therefore unchanged.
No projector at noninteger or complex degree is defined by this
statement; the existing interpolation theorem is not an off-grid
operator-projection theorem.

The compatible matched windows are different. On the \(\chi\) output,
\(\mathcal Z_\chi=\operatorname{im}\mathsf a\), while on the
\(\chi^{-1}\) output it is \(\operatorname{im}\mathsf b\).
Thus the matched \(P_A\) retains only the first output block of
\(A_0\), and \(P_B\) only the second. The cycle projection itself
satisfies
\(P_{\mathcal Z}\delta=\delta\), \(\delta P_{\mathcal Z}=0\),
so it is not in \(V\). More strongly, if a Hermitian \(P\in V\)
obeys \(PA_0=A_0\) on the full pair, (GK4) makes it the identity
on \(\mathcal Z\). It commutes with both \(\delta\) and
\(\delta^\dagger\), so it is also the identity on
\(\operatorname{im}\delta^\dagger\). Exactness gives their orthogonal
sum as the whole pair. Hence
\[
       P=P^\dagger\in V,\quad PA_0=A_0
                         \quad\Longrightarrow\quad P=I.
 \tag{GK7}
\]
There is no proper Hermitian source-compatible compression of this
entire paired kernel by an unchanged-output argument.

The first meridian normal also retains complementary directions.
Write \(T(e^\mu)=T_0+\mu T_1+\cdots\). Its exact product is
\(T(e^\mu)T(e^{-\mu})=a_N(e^\mu)H(e^\mu)\), where
\(H=D_N(M^mK_0)\). On a nonself pair \(H(1)=0\),
\(a_N(1)\ne0\), and \(H_1=\partial_\mu H|_0\) is invertible.
Therefore
\[
            T_0^2=0,\qquad [T_1,T_0]=a_N(1)H_1.
 \tag{GK8}
\]
Its half rank gives \(\ker T_0=\operatorname{im}T_0\).
If \(w\in\ker T_0\) and \(T_1w\in\operatorname{im}T_0\),
then (GK8) forces \(H_1w=0\), hence \(w=0\). Equal dimensions
show that \(T_1:\ker T_0\to\operatorname{coker}T_0\) is an
isomorphism. The invertible analytic endpoints in (GK3) transfer
this induced isomorphism to \(A_1=\partial_\mu A_N|_0\).
Equivalently,
\[
 (I-P_{\mathcal Z})A_1(I-P_{\mathcal Z}^{\mathsf T}):
 (\overline{\mathcal Z})^\perp\longrightarrow\mathcal Z^\perp
                  \quad\hbox{is an isomorphism}.
 \tag{GK9}
\]
It cannot be dropped when forming the original meromorphic sewing
and its finite part. Root packet capture does not authorize
differentiating a projected root identity as a whole-meridian one.
The next question concerns a selected geometric portion with its
actual source normals, not compression of the whole paired kernel.
No new knot, filling, geometric occurrence or scalar lower bound is
proved here.

and I623, the [initialized packet](research_fixed_width_coherent_complex_degree_interpolation.md),

## Positive paired occupation windows need not preserve the source cancellation, 23 November

There is a distinction between a positive physical window and a window
compatible with the original quotient-normal source. It is visible in
the actual remaining-head Casimir, without choosing a knot or changing
the marked closing.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and
\(x_0=-q^{-1}\). On two remaining heads use the original orthonormal
occupation basis \(|a,b\rangle\), \(0\le a,b\le d\), with
\[
 E=E_1K_2+E_2,\qquad F=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2,\qquad K=K_1K_2,
 \quad \Omega=FE+qK+q^{-1}K^{-1}.
\]
Here \(E_i|a\rangle=(Q^{-a}-1)|a-1\rangle\),
\(F_i|a\rangle=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1\rangle\), and
\(K_i|a\rangle=x_0Q^{-a}|a\rangle\), with zero outward arrows.
The actual Casimir lift puts \(\Omega\) in the root prefix image
\(V\). Its exact diagonal, including the endpoint rows, is
\[
 K_{ab}=Q^{-a-b-1},\qquad
 \Omega_{ab}=2qQ^a+2q^{-1}Q^{-b}
                         -(q+q^{-1})Q^{a-b}.
 \tag{PW1}
\]
Indeed the diagonal of \(FE\) is
\(x_0Q^{-b}(Q^{-a}-1)(1-Q^a)
+x_0^{-1}Q^a(Q^{-b}-1)(1-Q^b)\); adding the two Cartan
terms gives (PW1). Complete root sums then give
\[
                  \operatorname{Tr}(K\Omega)
                 =\operatorname{Tr}(K^{-1}\Omega)=0.
 \tag{PW2}
\]
The only possibly exceptional character has exponent \(\pm2\).
It vanishes for \(N>2\); at \(N=2\) its coefficient
\(q+q^{-1}\) is zero. Thus (PW2) holds at every level here.

Choose a closed rectangle of positive area
\[
 U\Subset\{(p_1,p_2):0<p_1<p_2,\ p_1+p_2<1/2\},\qquad
 S=U\cup\{(1-p_1,1-p_2):(p_1,p_2)\in U\}.
\]
Let \(\Pi_N\) be the diagonal orthogonal projection selecting
\((a/d,b/d)\in S\). Its boundary has measure zero. With the
physical involution \(H_N|a\rangle=qQ^a|d-a\rangle\), the
reflection symmetry gives exactly
\[
 0\le\Pi_N\le I,\qquad
 \Pi_N^\sharp=\Pi_N,\qquad
 [\Pi_N,\Gamma_{\rm d}]=0,
 \quad \sharp=(H_N\otimes H_N)(\cdot)^\dagger(H_N\otimes H_N).
 \tag{PW3}
\]
Here \(\Gamma_{\rm d}\) is the diagonal donor matrix from the
selected-degree theorem below; the commutator is zero because both
matrices are diagonal. Nevertheless, a direct Riemann sum gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 \lim_{N\to\infty}N^{-2}
       \operatorname{Tr}((K-K^{-1})\Pi_N\Omega)
  =16\int_S &\sin(2\pi(p_1+p_2))\sin(\pi p_1)\sin(\pi p_2)\\
             &\hspace{13mm}\cdot\sin(\pi(p_2-p_1))\,dp_1dp_2>0.
 \end{split} \tag{PW4}
\]
For verification, the limiting imaginary part of (PW1) is
\(8\sin(\pi p_1)\sin(\pi p_2)\sin(\pi(p_2-p_1))\), while
\(K-K^{-1}\to-2i\sin(2\pi(p_1+p_2))\). The reflected terms
are complex conjugates, so their imaginary contributions cancel.
The displayed real integrand is positive on both rectangles.
All finite endpoint rows were retained before taking the limit;
no assertion for small \(N\) about the rank of \(\Pi_N\) is needed.

Thus positivity, the physical Krein reflection, and exact commutation
with the donor matrix do not suffice to localize
\(\operatorname{Tr}((K-K^{-1})v)=0\) for \(v\in V\).
The example uses an actual Casimir coupon, not a braid-image
surjectivity assumption. It is not a geometric window, an identified
opposite-kernel window, or a counterexample about knots or fillings.

## Matched reciprocal-arrow windows preserve the entire root source, 23 November

A narrower positive construction does preserve that cancellation.
It uses the actual reciprocal lowering complex, rather than imposing
a condition on an unknown scalar. Keep the root fixed and use the
fixed common-flattened coordinates of the actual word-normal source.
For \(r\ge2\) remaining heads set
\[
 \mathcal U=(\mathbb C^N)^{\otimes r},\quad m=r+1,\quad
 K^N=\varepsilon I,\quad \varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r},\qquad
 D_0=\frac{K+K^{-1}}{2\varepsilon},\quad
 D_{-1}=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{2\varepsilon m}.
\]
The actual root algebra is
\(\mathcal T=V\oplus(\operatorname{End}_K(\mathcal U)/V)\), with
\((b,[h])(b',[h'])=(bb',[bh'+hb'])\). Its original pointed row is
\[
                 \Phi(b,[h])=\operatorname{Tr}(D_0b)
                                  +\operatorname{Tr}(D_{-1}h).
 \tag{HW1}
\]
In particular \(\operatorname{Tr}(D_{-1}v)=0\) for every \(v\in V\).
The actual Cartan, crossing scalars, normal couplings and marked row
are those of this formula.

On a nonself reciprocal pair \(\{\chi,\chi^{-1}\}\), choose the unique
\(1\le s<N\) with \(Q^s=\chi^2\). The actual maps
\[
 A=E^s:\mathcal U_{\chi^{-1}}\longrightarrow\mathcal U_\chi,
 \qquad B=E^{N-s}:\mathcal U_\chi\longrightarrow\mathcal U_{\chi^{-1}}
\]
satisfy \(AB=BA=0\), \(\operatorname{im}A=\ker B\), and
\(\operatorname{im}B=\ker A\). The exact root-image classification is
\[
 (X,Y)\in V\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad XA=AY,\qquad YB=BX.
 \tag{HW2}
\]
Every adjoint in the next construction is the original coefficient
Euclidean adjoint, not the indefinite \(\sharp\). In the order
\((\mathcal U_\chi,\mathcal U_{\chi^{-1}})\), define
\[
 \delta=\begin{pmatrix}0&A\\B&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \Delta=\delta\delta^\dagger+\delta^\dagger\delta
 =\operatorname{diag}(AA^\dagger+B^\dagger B,
                         BB^\dagger+A^\dagger A).
 \tag{HW3}
\]
Exactness implies \(\ker\delta=\operatorname{im}\delta\). Hence
\(\Delta>0\): a vector in its kernel lies in both
\(\ker\delta\) and \(\ker\delta^\dagger\), which are orthogonal
complements along this exact complex. Also
\([\Delta,\delta]=0\), directly from \(\delta^2=0\).
The matrix \(\Delta\) preserves each Cartan weight and each total
integer occupation. Therefore every orthogonal spectral band
\(P_I=\mathbf1_I(\Delta)\) preserves those gradings, commutes with
both arrows, and belongs to \(V\) by (HW2). Its norm is one when
nonzero. No lower spectral-gap estimate is used.

There is an explicit classification of all Cartan-preserving
Hermitian members of \(V\). Use the orthogonal splittings
\[
 \mathcal U_\chi=\operatorname{im}A\oplus\operatorname{im}B^\dagger,
 \qquad
 \mathcal U_{\chi^{-1}}=\operatorname{im}B\oplus\operatorname{im}A^\dagger,
 \tag{HW4}
\]
and singular-value bases for the two nonzero arrows. Hermiticity
and (HW2), together with their adjoints, first preserve all four
summands. On an \(A\) block they give \(X\Sigma_A=\Sigma_A Y\)
and \(\Sigma_A X=Y\Sigma_A\); thus \(X\) commutes with
\(\Sigma_A^2\) and equals \(Y\) on each equal-singular-value
multiplicity space. The same argument applies to \(B\).
Conversely any such matched Hermitian matrices satisfy (HW2).
Positivity, contraction, or the projection property is precisely
the corresponding property on each multiplicity matrix.

For example, with \(A^+,B^+\) the Euclidean Moore--Penrose inverses,
\[
 P_A=\operatorname{diag}(AA^+,A^+A),\qquad
 P_B=\operatorname{diag}(B^+B,BB^+),\qquad P_A+P_B=I.
 \tag{HW5}
\]
They and their matched singular-value refinements are orthogonal
projections in \(V\). Formula (HW5) remains valid when an arrow
has rank zero. Choosing an orthonormal basis in each singular-value
multiplicity space gives matched rank-two projections and a complete
orthogonal resolution of the reciprocal pair. This basis choice need
not be unique at a repeated singular value. They can be chosen to
preserve integer occupation: \(A^\dagger A\) and \(B^\dagger B\)
preserve it, and each arrow has a fixed integer occupation loss.
On a self weight \(\chi=\pm1\), \(V\) is the whole matrix block and
\(D_{-1}=0\); occupation-preserving rank-one partitions there
complete the construction on \(\mathcal U\). The total number of
packets is allowed to grow with the physical dimension.

Let \(P\) be any positive contraction in this Cartan-preserving
Hermitian part of \(V\). Since \(Pv\in V\), the band source
\[
 \Phi_P(b,[h])=\operatorname{Tr}(D_0Pb)
                              +\operatorname{Tr}(D_{-1}Ph)
 \tag{HW6}
\]
is independent of the representative \(h\). For any finite positive
partition \(\sum_\nu P_\nu=I\) in this algebra,
\(\sum_\nu\Phi_{P_\nu}=\Phi\) exactly, including every first-normal
term. The class \((P,0)\) exists in the fixed flattened extension;
if \(P\) is a projection it is an actual root idempotent class.
This does not identify it with a meridian-constant literal matrix
mark. If the flattening derivative is \(\Gamma_{\rm flat}\), its
unflattened reduced first coefficient is
\(-[P,\Gamma_{\rm flat}]\) modulo \(V\). No analytic Hermitian lift
or equality with an uncorrected physical marked coupon is assumed.

The boundary-only donor formula below is valid in each band. Namely,
internal-letter normals and crossing-scalar derivatives are in \(V\);
positive and negative boundary-letter normals may respectively be
replaced modulo \(V\) by
\(2m b_i\Gamma_{\rm d}\) and \(-2m\Gamma_{\rm d}b_i\).
Multiplication by the other root letters and then by \(P\) leaves
the discarded terms in \(V\), so (HW6) annihilates them. The order
of \(P\) and of every remaining word factor is retained; \(P\)
is not commuted through the word. In particular, for a literal
signed word with \(L_\partial\) boundary letters,
\[
 |\Phi_P(\beta)|\le
 \operatorname{Tr}(P)\bigl[1+C L_\partial N\log(N+1)\bigr]
                                  \prod_i\|b_i\|.
 \tag{HW7}
\]
This uses \(\|P\|_1=\operatorname{Tr}(P)\le\operatorname{rank}(P)\),
\(\|D_0\|\le1\),
\(\|D_{-1}\|\le1/m\), and
\(\|\Gamma_{\rm d}\|\le C N\log(N+1)\), in the original coefficient
norm. In particular each rank-two packet has this polynomial trace
cost without an ambient dimension factor or an inverse singular
value. Every packet remains in the exact source sum. Any prescribed
external scalar line multiplies the identity and bound with its
original value.

These windows constructively retain the quotient-normal cancellation
that (PW4) loses. They need not commute with actual braid operators
or localize a geometric packet, and their spectral conditioning is
not estimated here. The separate complex band values may cancel.
Neither positivity of the windows nor their exact source partition
is a positive scalar formula or a lower bound after a short filling.

## The selected boundary degree has a protected nonzero component, 23 November

The [selected-degree proof](research_boundary_ward_selected_degree_commutator.md)
goes one step beyond the unprojected logarithmic-factor estimate below.
The actual boundary Ward sum collapses to a commutator with one diagonal
matrix. A particular Fourier component then gives a lower bound after
both total-degree selection and the physical Cartan-weight restriction.
This is a matrix lower bound; the knot's closing functional remains.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and
\(m=r+1\) with \(r\ge2\). Put \(x_0=-q^{-1}\) and
\(F_j=\prod_{h=1}^j(1-Q^h)\), \(F_0=1\). Use the original
orthonormal occupation basis on the remaining \(r\) tensor factors.
Write \(E,K_0\) for their complete lowering and Cartan matrices and
\(b=\kappa S_rD\) for the actual positive reduced boundary crossing.
Here \(S_r\) only lowers the first remaining occupation and has
zero-transfer term equal to the identity, while
\[
 D|j\rangle=(-1)^jQ^{j(j+1)/2}|j\rangle,
 \qquad 0\le j<N,
\]
is a unitary diagonal matrix. The scalar \(\kappa\) is retained.
Let \(L\) lower that first occupation by one, with
\(L|0\rangle=0\); call this the donor factor, and write \(E_{\rm T}\)
for the lowering coproduct on its ordered tail.

For an actual Cartan eigenvalue \(\lambda\) and its projector
\(P_\lambda\ne0\), assume \(\lambda^2=Q^{-t}\), \(1\le t<N\).
Thus the input weight is nonself-reciprocal. At even levels this
condition restricts which physical orders occur; no absent weight
is supplied. Define the diagonal matrix
\[
 \Gamma|j\rangle=\gamma_j|j\rangle,\qquad
 \gamma_j=-\sum_{h=1}^j\frac1{1-Q^h},\qquad \gamma_0=0.
\]
The complete physical Ward arrow satisfies the exact identity
\[
 \mathfrak D_tP_\lambda=2mb[\Gamma,E^t]P_\lambda.
\]
This follows by conjugating the whole-meridian lowering matrix
through the literal crossing, taking the resonant derivative before
specializing, and then using a diagonal deformation on the donor.
It includes the connection term of the frame that makes \(E\)
constant. It does not differentiate a root-only symbol.

Let \(\mathsf R_1\) retain matrix entries that lower the donor
occupation by exactly one. Averaging conjugation by
\(e^{-i\phi J}\), \(J|j\rangle=j|j\rangle\), against \(e^{-i\phi}\)
makes this a contractive operator-norm projection and an orthogonal
Hilbert--Schmidt projection. The selected entry formula is
\[
 \mathsf R_1(\mathfrak D_tP_\lambda)
  =2m\kappa(\lambda/x_0)[t]_Q
                  D E_{\rm T}^{t-1}LP_\lambda,\qquad
 [t]_Q=\frac{1-Q^t}{1-Q}.
\]
There is a short verification directly from the original Ward sum:
every transfer \(n\ge2\) lowers the donor at least twice. In its
\(n=1\) term, the selected loss forces the identity term of \(S_r\)
and the tail-only term of \(E^{t-1}\). Thus no higher transfer can
cancel this component.

Choose the last tail occupation to be \(d\), and all intervening
occupations to be \(d\). The input weight determines the donor
occupation modulo \(N\). If it is zero, change the last occupation
to \(d-1\), which makes the donor occupation one. The output that
lowers the donor once and the last head \(t-1\) times has a unique
contributing tail term. Its coefficient is, respectively,
\((-1)^{t-1}F_{t-1}\) or \((-1)^{t-1}F_t/F_1\).
Since \(|[t]_Q|\ge1\), both physical norms obey
\[
 \|\mathfrak D_tP_\lambda\|_{\rm op},\quad
 \|\mathfrak D_tP_\lambda\|_{\rm HS}
 \ \ge\ \frac{2m|\kappa|\,|F_t|}{|1-Q|}.
\]
In particular the packet divided by \(2mF_t\) has norm at least
\(|\kappa|N/(2\pi)\). The factorial has not been estimated away.
The witnessing entry is near occupation endpoints and has not been
identified with the geometric contribution.

### Only boundary letters need the diagonal insertion in the reduced source

There is a useful corollary for an entire unmarked literal word.
It concerns its original root source value, not a derivative of
the closed source. The
[normal-source proof](research_actual_word_normal_cocycle_and_source.md)
uses a common lowering frame. Write \(h_i\) for the first normal
of a signed reduced generator \(b_i\) in that frame, and \(V\)
for the algebra of root prefix images. The
[reciprocal flag classification](research_reciprocal_chain_flags_and_root_radical.md)
says that the two Ward arrows determine its class modulo \(V\).
The commutator identity above therefore gives
\[
 h_i\equiv
 \begin{cases}
  2m b_i\Gamma,&g_i=\sigma_1,\\
  -2m\Gamma b_i,&g_i=\sigma_1^{-1},\\
  0,&g_i=\sigma_j^{\pm1},\ j\ge2
 \end{cases}
 \pmod V .
\]
For the negative letter this follows by differentiating the actual
inverse. The self-reciprocal blocks have no normal quotient.

Put \(\varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r}\), so \(K_0^N=\varepsilon I\).
The same classification
gives \(\operatorname{Tr}((K_0-K_0^{-1})v)=0\) for \(v\in V\):
the two reciprocal block traces agree, and the weight factor is
zero on a self-reciprocal block. Since \(V\) is an algebra, this
remains true after multiplying an omitted \(V\) term on either
side by any original root-word factors.

More explicitly, let \(\beta=g_L\cdots g_1\),
\(B_\beta=b_L\cdots b_1\),
\(B_{<i}=b_{i-1}\cdots b_1\), and
\(B_{>i}=b_L\cdots b_{i+1}\). Define the two indicated cyclic
rotations by
\[
 C_i^+=B_{<i}B_{>i}b_i,\qquad
 C_i^-=b_iB_{<i}B_{>i}.
\]
The product rule for the first normal, followed by ordinary trace
cyclicity, gives the original pointed source exactly as
\[
 \begin{split}
 \Phi_0(W_\beta)={}&
  \operatorname{Tr}\left(\frac{K_0+K_0^{-1}}{2\varepsilon}
                                  B_\beta\right)\\
 &+\frac1{\varepsilon}\sum_{i:g_i=\sigma_1}
           \operatorname{Tr}((K_0-K_0^{-1})\Gamma C_i^+)\\
 &-\frac1{\varepsilon}\sum_{i:g_i=\sigma_1^{-1}}
           \operatorname{Tr}((K_0-K_0^{-1})\Gamma C_i^-).
 \end{split}
\]
Indeed the original first-normal source coefficient is
\((K_0-K_0^{-1})/(2\varepsilon m)\); substituting the three
congruences cancels exactly \(2m\). This retains both reciprocal
arrows and the normal off-diagonal couplings. It does not replace
their contractions by an inner product.

If \(L_\partial\) is the number of boundary letters, then
\(\|\Gamma\|\le C N\log(N+1)\), directly from the reciprocal-sine
sum. Since \(K_0\) is unitary in the physical basis, the reduced
trace has dimension \(N^r\), and hence
\[
 |\Phi_0(W_\beta)|
 \le N^r\bigl(1+C L_\partial N\log(N+1)\bigr)
                                     \prod_{i=1}^L\|b_i\|.
\]
Every \(b_i\) includes its original scalar and its actual inverse
when appropriate. A prescribed outside scalar multiplies this
root-value formula. Its meridian derivative is not silently used
to estimate the derivative of the closed source.

The earlier
[meridian-frame calculation](research_actual_meridian_source_frames.md)
already expressed physical crossing derivatives as root words with
diagonal insertions. The narrower simplification here is on the
reduced \(r\)-factor source: only boundary letters remain, with one
universal diagonal matrix and no meridian derivatives. Neither this
upper bound nor the protected matrix-entry lower bound proves a
lower bound for their final scalar contraction.

In particular a Ward arrow has total occupation loss \(t>0\), so
its direct trace against a degree-preserving exterior is zero.
The original source first reconstructs its normal blocks and then
closes them; it is not that direct arrow trace. In a one-boundary
stabilization, exact closing still gives the unchanged arbitrary
core scalar up to its prescribed framing factor. Thus no new knot
or short-filling case is established here. The missing assertion
remains survival of the geometric contribution under the original
closing, with the required volume rate.

## A positive Fourier Gram controls the complete boundary logarithmic factor, 23 November

The [boundary Ward proof](research_boundary_ward_positive_toeplitz.md)
resums every transfer in the actual first-normal boundary insertion
before estimating it. Its logarithmic factor has a positive Toeplitz
Gram after the one original endpoint shift is retained. This gives a
two-sided bound for full boundary norms, with no small-activity
assumption and no restriction on level parity.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and
\(m=r+1\) original heads. On the remaining occupation space let
\(L|a\rangle=|a-1\rangle\) for \(a>0\), with \(L|0\rangle=0\);
it acts on the first remaining head and leaves the others alone.
All norms here are the original physical Euclidean operator or
Hilbert--Schmidt norms. In particular \(\|L\|=1\). Define
\[
 \ell_N(T)=\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}T^n}{1-Q^n},
 \qquad
 U_N(T)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-2}(-1)^j
                    \frac{1-Q}{1-Q^{j+1}}T^j .
\]
For \(T^N=0\), exactly
\(\ell_N(T)=T U_N(T)/(1-Q)\). The second factor satisfies
\[
 \|U_N(zL)\|\le C\log N,\qquad
 \|U_N(zL)^{-1}\|\le2+2\pi,\qquad |z|\le1 .
\]
The constants are independent of the number of heads.

The positivity behind the inverse bound is explicit. For
\(\theta=\pi/N\), put
\[
 a_j=\frac{\sin\theta}{\sin((j+1)\theta)},\qquad 0\le j\le N-2.
\]
The phases in \(U_N(zL)\), for \(|z|=1\), are removed by a
diagonal unitary. On \(\operatorname{im}L\), the Hermitian part of
the resulting matrix is
\[
                         \frac12(I+T_a),\qquad
                  T_a=(a_{|i-j|})_{i,j=0}^{N-2}\ge0.
\]
To prove this Gram inequality, let \(p=N-2\). For \(N\ge3\),
\[
 a_j=\frac{N\sin\theta}{\pi}
       \int_0^1\frac{x^j+x^{p-j}}{1+x^N}\,dx .
\]
For each \(0<x<1\), the kernel
\(x^{|i-j|}+x^{p-|i-j|}\) is the pullback of a positive
\(p\)-cycle circulant, with indices \(0,p\) identified. Its
Fourier eigenvalues are
\[
       \frac{(1-x^p)(1-x^2)}
               {1-2x\cos(2\pi k/p)+x^2}>0.
\]
Integration gives \(T_a\ge0\). The one-cycle case is included;
\(N=2\) is handled directly by \(U_2=I\). Thus the restricted
inverse has norm at most two. The remaining triangular column
has norm at most \(\pi\), giving the full bound \(2+2\pi\).
The harmonic minimum principle extends it to the full unit disk.
No conditioned change of physical metric is used.

Consequently, for any compatible rectangular matrix \(B\) and
every \(|z|=1\),
\[
 cN\|BL\|\ \le\ \|B\ell_N(zL)\|\
                         \le CN\log N\,\|BL\|.
\]
This holds in either of the stated norms, with \(B\) already
containing any desired left exterior. Moreover
\(\ker\ell_N(zL)=\ker L\) and
\(\operatorname{im}\ell_N(zL)=\operatorname{im}L\).
Thus this complete normal factor cannot introduce an additional
exponential norm loss beyond the literal endpoint shift. This is
not a lower bound for applying a specified scalar co-source.

The factor occurs in the original Ward insertion as follows. Put
\(F_j=(Q;Q)_j\), let \(E\) be the actual remaining lowering
coproduct, and let \(b\) be the full reduced positive boundary
crossing. For a physical order \(1\le t<N\), with input weight
\(\lambda_0^2=Q^{-t}\), put \(a=\lambda_0/x_0\) and
\(x_0=-q^{-1}\), so \(|a|=1\). The exact ordered resummation is
\[
 \mathfrak D_t
       =2mF_t[\xi^t]\mathcal E_N(\xi E)b\ell_N(a\xi L),
 \qquad
 \mathcal E_N(w)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{w^j}{F_j}.
\]
The operators \(E,L\) lower integer occupation by one, while \(b\)
preserves it. Extraction of \([\xi^t]\) is therefore the Fourier
projection onto matrix entries that lower occupation by \(t\).
It is contractive in operator norm and orthogonal in
Hilbert--Schmidt norm. In particular
\[
 \|\mathfrak D_t\|
       \le Cm|F_t|N\log N\,\|\mathcal E_N(E)bL\|,
                         \qquad 1\le t<N .
\]
The factorial \(F_t\), which can have exponential size, remains
explicit. So do the full Euler matrix, crossing scalar and
original endpoint. Exterior matrices are not commuted through
the degree projection.

The exact coefficient integral still contains the original marked
co-source. Neither that projection nor its final closing has a
general lower bound. Negative letters and complete words also
retain the actual inverse and cocycle factors in the word-normal
source formula. The result controls a genuine entire normal factor;
it does not extend the small-activity Euler phase theorem to unit
activity or prove the finite-exception volume identity.

## Positive gluing has a quantitative full-gradient gap, 23 November

The [gradient estimate](research_positive_gluing_gradient_escape_bound.md)
settles one part of the classical escape question. Keep a supplied
positive solution of the full marked logarithmic gluing equations.
Positive cyclic quad choices give an invertible \(B\) block while
transforming the affine target, including its windings. In those
selected coordinates put
\[
 \mathcal S=\{x:0<\Im x<\pi\},\qquad
 v(x)=-\operatorname{Log}(1-e^x),\qquad
 P=B^{-1}A=P^{\mathsf T}\in M_t(\mathbb R),\qquad u=B^{-1}c,
\]
\[
 S(x)=\sum_{j=1}^t\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{x_j})
                +\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px-u^{\mathsf T}x,\qquad
 \nabla S=B^{-1}\{Ax+Bv(x)-c\}.
\]
Here \(t\) is the number of tetrahedra, \(c\) is the retained full
logarithmic target, and \(x_*\in\mathcal S^t\) is the supplied solution.
The logarithm is principal on this positive chart.

Choose \(r>0\) with \(\overline{B(x_*,r)}\subset\mathcal S^t\), and set
\[
 m=\min_{\substack{y\in\overline{B(x_*,r)}\\1\le j\le t}}
                        \Im v'(y_j)>0.
\]
Then throughout the entire positive product,
\[
                    \|\nabla S(x)\|
                          \ge m\min(\|x-x_*\|,r).
\]
The proof compares \(x\) to \(x_*\) along their straight segment.
Every contribution to
\(\Im\{(x-x_*)^*\nabla S(x)\}\) is positive. The initial portion
inside the fixed ball alone gives the stated bound. No gluing
equation is imposed along that segment.

For the growing height \(h=\Im S/(2\pi)\), normalized lowering
has \(dh/ds=-1\). Outside the ball its speed is at most
\(2\pi/(mr)\). Hence a trajectory remaining in this chart cannot
send a selected logarithmic coordinate to infinity during a finite
height drop. The constants can be uniform when the supplied critical
points remain in a compact positive family. Approximate full gluing
at the same fixed logarithmic target cannot escape either.

Finite flat-angle and cut-boundary exits remain. A quad rotation can
turn an old \(z\to0\) end into a finite \(z'\to1\) boundary, so this
is not an exclusion of all ideal degenerations under a new name.
It does not place the original quantum cycle in the positive chart,
bound its finite face periods, or prove its geometric coefficient.

## The positive chart has one relative cycle and an explicit coefficient, 23 November

The [positive-chart period theorem](research_positive_chart_relative_homology.md)
computes the whole ordinary relative homology of a supplied positive
gluing chart. This goes beyond constructing a particular local
descending contour.

Keep the marked potential
\[
 S(x)=\sum_j\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{x_j})
             +\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px-u^{\mathsf T}x,
 \qquad P=P^{\mathsf T}\in M_t(\mathbb R),
 \qquad X=\mathbb R^t+i(0,\pi)^t,
\]
with a supplied critical point \(x_*=\rho_*+i\theta_*\).
Write \(h=\Im S\), \(h_*=h(x_*)\), and
\(A_c=\{x\in X:h(x)\le c\}\). For a cutoff \(c<h_*\)
sufficiently close to \(h_*\), there is an explicit compact
Legendre disk \(\Gamma_c\), with boundary in \(A_c\), such that
\[
 H_j(X,A_c;\mathbb Z)=
 \begin{cases}\mathbb Z,&j=t,\\0,&j\ne t.\end{cases}
\]
The disk, oriented by its angle coordinates, generates the group.
For every finite relative cycle \(\Gamma\), its coefficient is
\[
 [\Gamma]=k[\Gamma_c],\qquad
 k=\deg_{\theta_*}(\Im\Gamma).
\]
The degree is the local relative homology class of the angle
projection. For transverse smooth chains it is the signed count
of intersections with the fiber \(\{\Im x=\theta_*\}\).
Thus this coefficient can be computed without choosing a full
basis of descending contours.

The proof uses two convexity properties of the same whole action:
it is strictly convex in the logarithmic radii and strictly concave
in the angles. Near the high fixed-radius slice, move the radii to
their unique Legendre minimum; away from it, retain the geometric
radii. A smooth cutoff joins these choices. Radial convexity makes
the resulting homotopy preserve \(A_c\). The graph then retracts
to the compact convex Legendre-height superlevel and its boundary. This is
a deformation of the whole pair, rather than an assertion about
an unspecified integration cycle.

There is a corresponding compact-period conclusion. Let \(N\) tend
to infinity through positive integers and let \(\mu\) be fixed.
For actual holomorphic forms
\[
 \omega_N=N^\mu e^{NS/(2\pi i)}a_N(x)\,
                                      dx_1\cdots dx_t,
\]
assume polynomial amplitude bounds on the compact chains used by
the deformation and a uniform holomorphic expansion
\(a_N=a_0+O(N^{-1})\) near \(x_*\), with \(a_0(x_*)\ne0\).
The constructed connecting chains are compact, and Stokes gives
\[
 \int_\Gamma\omega_N
 =kC_*N^{\mu-t/2}e^{NS(x_*)/(2\pi i)}(1+O(N^{-1}))
                         +O(N^C e^{Nc/(2\pi)}),
 \qquad C_*\ne0.
\]
The proof retains the original density, contour Jacobian and
Gaussian determinant in \(C_*\). For complex peripheral targets,
the Legendre height retains the term
\(-(\Re u)^{\mathsf T}\theta\); a hyperbolic-volume calibration
must apply to that same marked action.

This settles the finite-chain topology and compact period assembly
inside this one positive chart. It does not supply a representative
of the original quantum source with boundary below the cutoff,
prove that its degree is nonzero, or remove cut-bank, alias or
noncompact currents outside the chart. In fact every compact
closed cycle entirely inside the unpunctured \(X\) has degree zero.
The finite-exception theorem therefore remains open.

## An assembled endpoint retains an arbitrary Conway core, 23 November

The exact ground-output channel in the
[sewn Newton/Rogers source](actual_rogers_sink_opposite_beta_source.md),
equation (21), cannot be discarded even with genuine Conway exteriors.
At complete color use \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(x=-q^{-1}\), and \(F_a=(Q;Q)_a\). That channel is
\[
 H_0|a,b\rangle=
 \begin{cases}
 x^{-b}\dfrac{F_{a+b}}{F_b}|a+b,0\rangle,&a+b<N,\\
 0,&a+b\ge N.
 \end{cases}
\]
Keep the original cup, unrestricted marked row, and ordinary cap:
\[
 p=N\sum_{a=0}^d x^{a-d}|a,d-a\rangle,\qquad
 m|a,b\rangle=\frac{x^b}{N^2},\qquad
 \ell_o|a,b\rangle=\frac{x^a}{N}\delta_{a+b,d}.
\]
In particular \(mp=1\) whereas \(\ell_op=0\).

There is an all-level exact evaluation
\[
              H_0p=N|d,0\rangle,\qquad
              mH_0p=\frac1N,\qquad \ell_oH_0p=x^d .
\]
To check the first equality, put \(U_N(z)=\sum_{a=0}^d z^a/F_a\).
Its finite recurrence is
\[
 U_N(Qz)=(1-z)U_N(z)+z^N/F_d .
\]
Thus \(U_N(Q)=1/N\), and substitution of the cup in \(H_0\)
gives \(N^2U_N(Q)|d,0\rangle=N|d,0\rangle\).
This retains the final Euler coefficient and works at every parity
and composite level.

More strongly, let \(A=f(\Omega)\) be any actual Conway pair box,
where \(\Omega=F_tE_t+qK_t+q^{-1}K_t^{-1}\) is the pair Casimir and
\(E_t,F_t,K_t\) are its total raising, lowering, and Cartan operators.
The full pair-commutant and genuine-turn theorems give this
description with all repeated-root derivatives retained. Set
\(c_0=q+q^{-1}\). The genuine invariant cup and ordinary cap
independently obey
\[
 \Omega p=c_0p,\qquad \ell_o\Omega=c_0\ell_o.
\]
For example the total raising and lowering operators annihilate
them on their respective sides, while their total Cartan eigenvalue
is one. The cap assertion does not follow by cancelling the zero
bubble \(\ell_op\). Consequently
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
       mH_0Ap=\frac1N\,mAp,\qquad
       \ell_oAH_0p=x^d\,mAp .
       \qquad}
\]
No division by \(mAp=f(c_0)\) is used. These formulas also hold at
its zeros. For a cylindrical Conway closure, first use the genuine
quarter-turn \(\mathscr R\): the original Newton source identities
give \(\phi(f)=m(\mathscr R f)(\Omega)p\). The same calculation then
applies to that entire core. All external framing and normalization
factors stay attached. If \(H_0\) comes from a newly exposed crossing
cell, that cell's original Cartan scalar remains separate.

Thus this assembled endpoint can carry the whole unknown core scalar,
with only polynomial or unit factors. It is not universally killed
by genuine caps or Conway gluing. This concerns the coupled endpoint
channel of the exact Green identity; it does not assign the same
behavior to every separated beta or Rogers current. The required
analysis must keep the coherent sum containing this endpoint.
It supplies no new volume lower bound or finite-exception class.

## Whole meridian germs replace separate derivative calculations, 23 November

The [meridian-family proof](research_real_meridian_krein_transport.md)
extends the common physical pairing from the complete color to the
original mixed-color family. The same one-head matrix works at every
positive real meridian:
\[
 N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\qquad
 H_N=q^{-1}Z^{-1}R_d,
\]
where \(Z|a\rangle=Q^a|a\rangle\) and
\(R_d|a\rangle=|d-a\rangle\). It is Hermitian and squares to the
identity. For a signed word of width \(b\), put
\(\mathscr H_b=H_N^{\otimes b}\).

Choose positive real base meridians \(M_i^0\), write
\(M_i=M_i^0e^{t_i}\), and let \(W(t)\) be the full original braid
matrix, carrying the colors through its actual permutation. With
\(W^\natural(t)=\overline{W(\bar t)}^{\mathsf T}\), the exact
holomorphic identity is
\[
                    W^\natural(t)\mathscr H_bW(t)=\mathscr H_b.
\]
The proof uses the original finite Euler factor and the full unrolled
Cartan diagonal. Its separate highest-entry scalar generally does not
have modulus one away from completeness and is not discarded.
Arbitrary signed overlapping crossings are included.

This identity supplies all mixed meridian derivative relations at
once. There is also a simple inverse formula: if
\(W(t)=\sum_\alpha W_\alpha t^\alpha\) in normalized Taylor
coordinates, then
\[
             [t^\alpha]\,W(t)^{-1}
                         =\mathscr H_bW_\alpha^\dagger\mathscr H_b.
\]
Inverse derivative packets therefore need no separate matrix-inversion
recursion. Imaginary meridian shifts are paired with their conjugate
shifts; an individual such shift is not declared an isometry.

For rectangular truncation orders \(r_i\), keep the full jet algebra
\[
 A_{\boldsymbol r}=\mathbb C[t_1,\ldots,t_b]/
                         (t_1^{r_1+1},\ldots,t_b^{r_b+1}).
\]
The pairing
\[
 [u,v]_{\boldsymbol r}
   =[t_1^{r_1}\cdots t_b^{r_b}]\,u(t)^*\mathscr H_bv(t)
\]
is nondegenerate and preserved by multiplication by the truncated
original \(W(t)\). Here the star conjugates coefficients and fixes
the formal variables. Its matrix is the tensor product of the
anti-diagonal identity matrices on Taylor coefficients and
\(\mathscr H_b\); its singular values are all one. This packages every
retained derivative cross term without a quotient by derivative
directions or a separate form at each order.

These forms are indefinite. They do not replace the positive norm in
the quartic variational problem. The original observed scalar remains
\(\Lambda(t)W(t)p(t)\), with its actual marked row, cups, pivots and
normalization factors. The marked row is not replaced by a Hermitian
adjoint. The jet dimension is still \(N^b\prod_i(r_i+1)\), and no
word-norm estimate follows from the unit singular values of the form.
The parameter \(q\) stays fixed: these are meridian derivatives, not
derivatives away from the quantum root.

This simplifies the exact transport needed for a fixed-degree
description. It gives no new filling class or geometric scalar lower
bound. The finite-exception theorem remains unproved.

## One physical pairing works on overlapping crossings, 22 November

The [physical tensor-form proof](research_physical_tensor_krein_crossing_form.md)
gives a common indefinite Hermitian pairing on the original heads.
It works across overlapping pairs, before any change to local flag
coordinates. This supplies an exact global conservation law for
signed braid words. It is not a positive energy estimate.

Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and
\(k=(-1)^d\). On the original one-head basis define
\[
 Z|a\rangle=Q^a|a\rangle,\qquad
 R_d|a\rangle=|d-a\rangle,\qquad
 H_N=q^{-1}Z^{-1}R_d .
\]
Then \(H_N^\dagger=H_N\) and \(H_N^2=I\).
For every actual signed crossing \(R_i^{\pm1}\) on adjacent
heads, and every signed word \(\mathcal W\) of width \(b\),
\[
 (R_i^{\pm1})^\dagger H_N^{\otimes b}R_i^{\pm1}
       =H_N^{\otimes b},\qquad
 \mathcal W^\dagger H_N^{\otimes b}\mathcal W
       =H_N^{\otimes b}.
\]
The original Cartan scalars have modulus one and remain present.
The same physical \(H_N\) is used on each wire.

The relation to the explicit flag frame is proved on every basis
entry, not inferred just from its value on the cup:
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}^{\dagger}
          [-Nk(H_N\otimes H_N)]\widetilde{\mathcal B}=J,\qquad
 J=q\mathcal Rv^{-1},\quad
 \mathcal R|m,s\rangle=|d-m,1-s\rangle .
\]
The finite root-binomial sum kills every off-reflection entry;
its remaining scalar is exactly the displayed one. Both parities
and composite levels are included.

The marked full matrix \(F_v\), including its \(\phi_N\) scalar,
preserves this same form on its physical pair. The cyclic matrix
has the paired identity
\[
 \mathcal C_t^\dagger(H_N\otimes H_N)\mathcal C_{\bar t}
                       =H_N\otimes H_N
\]
on conjugate-compatible marked root paths. A single arbitrary
complex-\(t\) factor is not asserted to be an isometry.

The ordinary cup and cap match this pairing exactly:
\[
 p^\dagger(H_N\otimes H_N)=N^2\ell_o,\qquad
 p^\dagger(H_N\otimes H_N)p=0 .
\]
Thus \(p/N\) and \(N\ell_o\) are adjoints for the indefinite form,
with their actual orders. The original marked cap is different:
\(\ell_m p=1\), whereas \(\ell_o p=0\). It is retained separately.
No pivot or marked boundary line is removed.

This settles a common-pairing question for arbitrary overlapping
crossings. The conserved form is blind to every scalar multiple
of the isotropic cup. It therefore supplies no lower bound for
the marked observation and does not make a general knot source
a positive norm square. The actual paired-face wire is still
the identity contraction with its inverse-dual frames, not \(J\)
inserted by convention. Geometric survival remains unproved.

## The negative residual has a genuine ordered pivotal adapter, 22 November

The [negative-adapter proof](research_negative_pachner_residual_pivotal_adapter.md)
removes the mixed input/output restriction left in the earlier
physical flag result. Its bend uses the original ordered cup
and ordinary evaluation, while keeping the full marked exterior.

For a tensor \(T:V_a\otimes V_b\to V_c\otimes V_e\), put
\(x=-q^{-1}\) and use
\[
 p_{m,a}=Nx^{m-d}\delta_{m+a,d},\qquad
 \varepsilon_{a,m}=x^a\delta_{a+m,d}/N .
\]
Their two snake contractions are the identity. The genuine bend is
\[
 \mathfrak B(T)=(I_m\otimes T)(p_{m,a}\otimes I_b),\qquad
 \mathfrak B(T)_{m,c,e;b}=Nx^{m-d}T_{c,e;d-m,b}.
\]
Its identity test gives the native cup, \(\mathfrak B(I)=p\otimes I\).
Feeding the other cup leg and then using an ordinary flip would
introduce the additional clock \(x^dZ_m\); that clock is not dropped.
The right-dual identification is checked against the original
antipode, so the ordered pair \((m,c)\) consists of actual complete
heads. No Hopf-intertwining assumption on \(T\) is needed.

In the literal negative nine-cell source the first retained ratio is
\[
 R_{d-a}(tQ^c),\qquad R_j(Z)=\beta^{-j}(Z;Q)_j,\qquad
 t=\alpha_{0235}Q^{r_0},\quad \beta^N=1-t^N ,
\]
where \(r_0=u_0+v_0+s_0+z_0+2\) contains only internal indices.
After the bend this is the diagonal factor
\(\mathcal F_t|m,c\rangle=R_m(tQ^c)|m,c\rangle\).
The physical frame from the earlier adapter therefore gives
\[
 \mathfrak Q(\mathcal R_t^-(T))
       =(O_t\otimes I_e)\mathfrak Q(T),\qquad
 \mathfrak Q=(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{m,c}\otimes I_e)\mathfrak B,
 \quad O_t=\mathcal C_t\mathcal U^{-1}\mathcal C_t^{-1}\mathcal U .
\]
Here \(\mathcal R_t^-\) multiplies each original entry by
\(R_{d-a}(tQ^c)\). All \(N^4\) entries and both spectator indices remain.

For any original exterior row its bent coefficients are exactly
\[
 \widehat\eta_{m,c,e;b}
       =x^{d-m}\eta_{c,e;d-m,b}/N .
\]
The subsequent row is
\(\widehat\eta(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{m,c}^{-1}\otimes I_e)\).
This preserves the original scalar bilinearly, including its
sector phase, face factors and full marked cap. The bend alone
has Hilbert--Schmidt norm cost \(N\), and its inverse \(1/N\);
no norm bound for the separate flag frame is claimed.

The local operator statement holds for every \(N\ge2\).
Its literal charged-source occurrence is established for odd \(N>2\).
Together with the positive adapter, both signs now have typed
commutator realizations before the remaining sums and circle/ray
integrals. This does not identify the remaining full nine-cell
product with a positive geometric cycle or prove noncancellation.

## The original crossing has a closed flag exchange, 22 November

The [crossing exchange proof](research_actual_crossing_flag_euler_exchange.md)
identifies an explicit nilpotent argument in the actual crossing.
Unlike the earlier pure-\(\Delta\) factors, it moves the multiplicity
clock. This removes the fixed-clock restriction when transporting the
retained cyclic factor through an original crossing. The source and
the completed endpoint arrow remain explicit.

Use the original two complete heads at \(N\ge2\), with
\[
 d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad
 \lambda=-q,\quad F_h=(Q;Q)_h .
\]
Retain the coupled flags \(\Delta,\gamma,v\) and the multiplicity clock
\(M=Z_1Z_2v\) of the physical adapter below. This \(M\) is not a
peripheral meridian eigenvalue. Put
\[
 S=S_1v^{-1},\qquad
 B_0=(1-Q^{-1}M^{-1})S^{-1},\qquad X=B_0\Delta .
\]
In the explicit orthogonal frame these have the entries
\[
 S=S_m,\qquad
 X|m,s\rangle=(1-Q^{-m})(1-Q^{1-s})|m-1,s-1\rangle .
\]
Thus \(X^N=0\), \([X,\Delta]=0\), and \(Xv=QvX\), with
both zero endpoint arrows retained.

Define the finite Euler inverse and the marked Gaussian by
\[
 \mathcal E_N(Y)=\sum_{h=0}^dY^h/F_h,\qquad
 \mathcal G=\sum_{j=1}^N(-1)^{j-1}Q^{j(j-1)/2}E_j(v),
 \qquad E_N(v)=E_0(v).
\]
For the original crossing \(\kappa W\), with its common Cartan
scalar \(\kappa\) retained, the exact full-space factorization is
\[
                         W=\mathcal G\mathcal E_N(X).
\]
Its proof is short. The candidate and the original \(W\) have
the same conjugations of \(S_1\) and \(\Delta\), and both fix
\(|0,0\rangle\). Hence they agree first on every
\(S_1^m|0,0\rangle=|m,0\rangle\), then on the full basis
\(\Delta^a|m,0\rangle/F_a\). This fixes the scalar as well
as all \(N^2\) entries.

In particular the original crossing gives the explicit updates
\[
 \begin{split}
 v'&=v+X,&\Delta'&=-Q\Delta v^{-1},\\
 S_1'&=S_1+\Delta,&M'&=M+(Z_1Z_2)X,\\
 \gamma'&=-\gamma v-\lambda Q^{-1}B_0v .
 \end{split}
\]
The completed shift has no untracked endpoint correction. If
\(\Gamma=\gamma+c_*\Delta^d\), where
\(c_*=[(-\lambda)^dF_d]^{-1}\), then
\[
             W\Delta^dW^{-1}=\Delta^d,\qquad
             \Gamma'=\gamma'+c_*\Delta^d .
\]
The finite top terms in these formulas vanish by \(\Delta^N=0\)
or \(B_0^N=0\). The cyclic sign is checked at even levels too.
The retained commutator from the physical adapter therefore
transports using these explicit primed clocks and shift; an
unspecified conjugated crossing matrix is no longer needed there.

There are actual cyclic and full-dilogarithm exchange identities.
For \(\beta^N=1-t^N\), on the original nondegenerate marked cover,
\[
 \mathcal C_tW
  =\mathcal G\mathcal E_N(-\beta^{-1}Q^{-1}tXv)
               \mathcal E_N(\beta^{-1}X)\mathcal C_t,\qquad
 \mathcal C_t=\mathfrak d_N(tv).
\]
The inverse Euler factors occur in the displayed order.
The same marked cyclic function occurs on both sides, with its
full normalization. At the physical root the regular marked
matrix \(F_v\) gives instead
\[
             F_vW=\mathcal G\mathcal E_N(-Q^{-1}Xv)
                            \mathcal E_N(X)F_v .
\]
For the original cup \(p\) and full marked cap \(\ell\),
the second equality has common observation
\[
 \ell F_vWp=\phi_N,\qquad
 \phi_N=\sqrt N\exp\!\left\{i\pi\left[
                  \tfrac14-\tfrac{N+N^{-1}}{12}\right]\right\}.
\]
The full crossing retains the additional factor \(\kappa\).

These identities hold for every level and every actual exterior.
They identify a crossing argument and its endpoint-preserving
transport, rather than merely another scalar-parameter oscillator.
The remaining nine-cell factors have not all been matched.
Compatible geometric source cycles and a nonzero general closing
at the hyperbolic-volume rate are still required. The
finite-exception theorem remains unproved.

## The flag Fourier labels are not ordinary-color fusion labels, 22 November

The new orthogonal flag frame does not identify its shifted-cap
observations with the ordinary-color invariants. A local obstruction
holds at every level, including both parities and composite levels.
Here is the complete calculation, using the actual physical matrices.

Retain \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), and \(\lambda=-q\)
with \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), so \(\lambda^2=Q\). The original balanced
lowering operator and Cartan inverse are
\[
 f|a\rangle=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1\rangle\quad(a<d),\qquad
 f|d\rangle=0,\qquad K^{-1}|a\rangle=\lambda Q^a|a\rangle .
\]
The relevant coproduct is
\[
                   F_{\mathrm{tot}}=f_1+K_1^{-1}f_2 .
\]
Use the original first auxiliary wrap \(S_1^N=1\), not a nilpotent
replacement. Let \(C\), \(v\), and \(M=CZ_1C^{-1}\) be the
preparation and clocks in the
[physical flag adapter](research_retained_pachner_ratio_physical_flags.md).
Its preparation argument \(-S_1e_2Z_2\) commutes with \(Z_1Z_2\):
the weight factors from \(S_1\) and \(e_2\) cancel. Thus
\[
 Mv^{-1}=Z_1Z_2,\qquad
 M=Z_1Z_2v=Z_1+Z_1Z_2S_1e_2 .
\]
This identity includes the cyclic arrow of \(S_1\).

Every element of \(\mathbb C[M]\) is \(h(M)\) for a polynomial
of degree below \(N\), since \(M\) is similar to \(Z_1\). Put
\(h_a=h(Q^a)\). For \(0\le a<d\), the invariant two-dimensional
span of \(|a,1\rangle\) and \(|a+1,0\rangle\) gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 M|a,0\rangle&=Q^a|a,0\rangle,\\
 M|a,1\rangle&=Q^a|a,1\rangle+
                 \lambda Q^a(Q-1)|a+1,0\rangle,\\
 h(M)|a,1\rangle&=h_a|a,1\rangle+
                 \lambda(h_{a+1}-h_a)|a+1,0\rangle .
 \end{split}
\]
The last formula is the divided difference at the two distinct
eigenvalues \(Q^a\) and \(Q^{a+1}\). Meanwhile
\[
 F_{\mathrm{tot}}|a,0\rangle
   =(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1,0\rangle+
                    \lambda Q^a(1-Q)|a,1\rangle .
\]
Using \(\lambda^2=Q\) therefore gives
\[
 \langle a+1,0|[h(M),F_{\mathrm{tot}}]|a,0\rangle
       =(1-Q^{a+2})(h_{a+1}-h_a).
\]
If the commutator vanishes, the indices \(0\le a\le N-3\)
force \(h_0=\cdots=h_{N-2}\). This range is empty at \(N=2\).

The remaining equality uses the retained cyclic arrow:
\[
 \begin{split}
 M|d,1\rangle&=Q^d|d,1\rangle+
                       \lambda(1-Q^{-1})|0,0\rangle,\\
 h(M)|d,1\rangle&=h_d|d,1\rangle+
                       \lambda(h_0-h_d)|0,0\rangle,\\
 F_{\mathrm{tot}}|d,0\rangle
       &=\lambda Q^d(1-Q)|d,1\rangle .
 \end{split}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \langle0,0|[h(M),F_{\mathrm{tot}}]|d,0\rangle
                 =(1-Q)(h_0-h_d).
\]
Since \(Q\ne1\), \(h_d=h_0\), also at \(N=2\). We have proved
\[
             \mathbb C[M]\cap\operatorname{Comm}(F_{\mathrm{tot}})
                        =\mathbb C I .
\]
In particular, a nontrivial clock power or nonconstant Fourier
projector of \(M\) is not a Hopf intertwiner on these original
complete-color heads. It cannot be identified locally with an
ordinary-color fusion coupon. The polynomial bounds for actual
ordinary-color invariants therefore do not apply through that
identification. This calculation does not exclude a separately
proved scalar identity after a constrained whole-source closure.
It also does not obstruct an entangled positive Gram on complete
boundary packets.

## The retained Pachner factor has an explicit orthogonal flag frame, 22 November

The [physical flag adapter](research_retained_pachner_ratio_physical_flags.md)
identifies one factor retained by the first nine-cell beta move with an
operator on the original two quantum-group heads. It keeps the factor
and the original exterior covector. The same calculation gives a positive
inner product in which the completed internal shifts are unitary and
the original cup and marked cap have polynomial norms.

Fix \(N\ge2\), put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(\lambda=-q\), and \(F_a=(Q;Q)_a\). The physical space has dimension
\(N^2\). Its actual coupled flags satisfy
\[
 \Delta^N=\gamma^N=0,\qquad v^N=1,\qquad
 \Delta\gamma=\lambda(v-1),\qquad v\gamma=Q\gamma v .
\]
Write \(E_1(v)=N^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^dQ^{-j}v^j\). The missing cyclic
arrow can be supplied explicitly:
\[
 \Gamma=\gamma+
       \frac{E_1(v)\Delta^d}{(-\lambda)^dF_d},\qquad
 \Gamma^N=1,\qquad v\Gamma=Q\Gamma v .
\]
The added term sends the last vector of every nilpotent string back
to its first. It retains the endpoint data; it does not invert a
nilpotent matrix. The auxiliary flag wraps are fixed to \(1\) and
\((-1)^d\), respectively, including even levels.

Here are the actual boundary indices in the positive crossing.
Set \(m=[-k_2]\), \(s=[-k_1]\), and
\(r_0=u_0+v_0+s_0+z_0+2\), with the four latter variables internal
to the first beta move. The retained ratio is
\[
 \frac{\overline W_{0235}(K+L)}
      {\overline W_{0235}(K+L-k_2)}
   =R_m(tQ^s),\qquad
 R_m(Z)=\beta^{-m}(Z;Q)_m,\qquad t=\alpha Q^{r_0}.
\]
The Fermat coordinates satisfy \(\alpha^N+\beta^N=1\), and the
connector's recorded root \(\beta\) is retained. These are full
physical color indices, not derivative orders.

Let \(\mathcal F_{r_0}\) be diagonal with these entries. The proof
gives an explicit invertible frame \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}\), a
commuting multiplicity clock \(M\), and
\[
 \mathcal U=\sum_{m=0}^d E_m(M)\Gamma^m,\qquad
 \mathcal C_t=\mathfrak d_N(tv),
\]
where \(\mathfrak d_N\) is the existing marked cyclic dilogarithm.
Then, on every boundary coordinate,
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}\mathcal F_{r_0}
             \widetilde{\mathcal B}^{-1}
       =\mathcal C_t\mathcal U^{-1}\mathcal C_t^{-1}\mathcal U .
\]
The full periodic arrow is checked: \(R_N(tv)=1\) uses precisely
\(\beta^N=1-t^N\). No scalar or peripheral factor is dropped.

The orthogonal coordinates are particularly simple. For \(a=[-s]\),
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}|m,s\rangle
       =\frac{\Delta^a|m,0\rangle}{F_a}.
\]
In these coordinates \(v=Z_s\), \(M=Z_m\), and
\(\Gamma=\lambda S_sZ_s\), where \(Z\) is the unitary clock and
\(S_s\) is the unitary cyclic shift. Thus \(v,M,\Gamma,\mathcal U\)
are unitary. The original cup \(p\) and full marked cap \(\ell\)
become
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}^{-1}p=N^2|0,1\rangle,\qquad
 (\ell\widetilde{\mathcal B})_{m,s}=Q^{-ms}/N^2 .
\]
Their norms are \(N^2\) and \(N^{-1}\), and their pairing is one.
This fixes a positive Gram from the original flags, without using
the unknown closed invariant. No bound on the frame's condition
number in the original balanced metric is asserted.

For an arbitrary actual exterior row \(\eta\) and remaining tensor \(Y\),
the preserved scalar is
\[
 \eta\mathcal F_{r_0}Y
  =(\eta\widetilde{\mathcal B}^{-1})
    (\mathcal C_t\mathcal U^{-1}\mathcal C_t^{-1}\mathcal U)
    (\widetilde{\mathcal B}Y).
\]
This is a bilinear identity with the complete original row, before
the remaining finite sums and pattern integrals. The transformed
exterior is not replaced by the special cap above.

The flag construction holds for every \(N\ge2\). Its literal charged
nine-cell source occurrence is currently established for odd \(N>2\)
and the positive crossing; the negative crossing has a mixed
input/output placement requiring its own typed dual transport.
The remaining \(W\)-factors have not been matched to the neighboring
nilpotent factors of the flag pentagon. Compatible frames across
further gluings, a sharp whole-source norm estimate, and nonvanishing
of the original closing at the geometric action remain to be proved.
The finite-exception theorem is still open.

## Global uniqueness in the positive marked gluing domain, 22 November

The geometric uniqueness argument no longer needs a small neighborhood
of the complete point or the special circle-tree edge coordinates.
The [global logarithmic gluing theorem](research_global_positive_log_gluing.md)
compares any two positive ideal-shape assignments directly.
It applies to any supplied actual ideal triangulation with torus cusp
links and its full marked incidence equations.
Existence of a positive assignment is still a separate requirement.

Here is the entire comparison. For one positively oriented ideal
tetrahedron use the principal logarithms
\[
 \mathcal S=\{x\in\mathbb C:0<\operatorname{Im}x<\pi\},\qquad
 z=e^x,\qquad v(x)=-\operatorname{Log}(1-e^x).
\]
Both logarithms have imaginary part between zero and \(\pi\), and
\[
       v'(x)=\frac{e^x}{1-e^x},\qquad
       \operatorname{Im}v'(x)>0\quad(x\in\mathcal S).
\]
If two configurations have \(t\) tetrahedra, write
\(\Delta x=x-x'\) and \(\Delta v=v(x)-v(x')\).
The strip is convex, so
\[
 \operatorname{Im}\sum_{j=1}^t
                  \overline{\Delta x_j}\Delta v_j
 =\sum_{j=1}^t|\Delta x_j|^2
       \int_0^1\operatorname{Im}v'(x'_j+s\Delta x_j)\,ds>0
                      \quad\text{unless }x=x'.
\]
The joining segment is used only to evaluate \(v\).
It need not satisfy any gluing equation.

Take real \(t\)-by-\(t\) matrices \(A,B\) with
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(A\ B)=t,\qquad
                    AB^{\mathsf T}=BA^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Their real kernel is Lagrangian for
\(\Omega((a,b),(c,d))=a^{\mathsf T}d-b^{\mathsf T}c\).
If \(Ax+Bv(x)=Ax'+Bv(x')\), both
\((\Delta x,\Delta v)\) and its conjugate lie in that kernel's
complexification. Their symplectic pairing is zero, contradicting
the strict comparison unless the configurations agree. The same
argument on tangent vectors proves that
\[
              A+B\operatorname{diag}(v'(x_j))
\]
is invertible everywhere. Thus \(x\mapsto Ax+Bv(x)\) is a
biholomorphism onto its open realized image.
No convexity of the peripheral image is assumed.

For an actual triangulation with \(c\) torus cusps, retain
\(t-c\) independent edge rows and one nonzero real peripheral
direction at each cusp. The existing marked incidence theorem
proves exactly the rank and isotropy conditions above.
For surgery these directions can be the original
\(\mu_i+p_i\lambda_i\), with arbitrary fixed integer \(p_i\),
including zero and mixed signs. Keep the chosen meridian rows at
unfilled cusps. Consequently each fixed full logarithmic target,
with its original edge windings and primitive peripheral marking,
has at most one positive solution, across all positive components.
Every such solution has nonsingular gluing Jacobian.

This is a statement about fixed logarithms. Exponentiated equations
can have other positive solutions with different targets differing
by \(2\pi\mathrm i\) times integers.
Changing quad conventions must transform the affine constants along
with the rows. Neither operation can be suppressed when comparing
primitive filling branches.

There is also a direct algebraicity conclusion. When the rows are
integral and the exponentiated targets \(\gamma_i\) are algebraic,
the shapes satisfy
\[
       \prod_j z_j^{A_{ij}}(1-z_j)^{-B_{ij}}=\gamma_i .
\]
The rational Jacobian is invertible at a positive solution.
Over a number field containing the \(\gamma_i\), differentiation
therefore forces every \(dz_j\) to vanish. The generated field has
transcendence degree zero in characteristic zero, so every shape
is algebraic. This is a nonsingular algebraic point; no quantum
limit or torsor identification is needed for this classical fact.

The earlier global theorem treated the explicit eight-tetrahedron
circle-tree edge blocks. The new proof works directly with arbitrary
positive ideal tetrahedra and the same actual incidence data.
It rules out a collision or singular Jacobian inside this fixed
positive gluing domain. If a target path has solutions remaining
in a compact subset of the shape strips, their continuation extends
past a finite endpoint.
It does not prove that a given hyperbolic short filling has a
positive realization on the original triangulation, that a cone
path stays in this domain, or that primitive metric completion
follows from multiplier equations alone.

The quantum task is unchanged: the geometric branch must contribute
with a nonzero coefficient to the whole original partially filled
source, with the other source terms controlled at its own action.
The positive gluing theorem supplies neither that coefficient nor
the required source gap. The finite-exception theorem remains
unproved.

## An explicit fusion dual gives a linear derivative budget, 22 November

The [factorial dual theorem](research_factorial_fusion_dual_and_linear_confluence.md)
sharpens the numerical confluence bound in the next section.
It also gives a controlled factorial expansion for a full original
marked contraction. The source space is unchanged. In particular,
this does not assert that the original cup is cyclic in that entire
space, or replace it by the larger root invariant space.

Fix an even number \(b\ge2\) of physical boundary strands,
\(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q_0=e^{\pi i/N}\), and
\(u=\zeta-q_0\). Let \(\mathcal O=\mathbb C\{u\}\) and
\(\mathcal K=\operatorname{Frac}\mathcal O\).
For the actual balanced generic leaf \(V_d(\zeta)\), retain the
saturated invariant lattice
\[
 \Lambda=
 \operatorname{Inv}_{\mathcal K}(V_d(\zeta)^{\otimes b})
                  \cap V_d(\zeta)^{\otimes b}_{\mathcal O},
 \qquad \mathcal V=\Lambda/u\Lambda.
\]
Here the intersection is inside the generic physical tensor.
The embedded space \(\mathcal V\) contains the original cup state
and every state obtained from it by regular original braid operators.

For every binary fusion tree, keep all admissible generic intermediate
colors and root color zero. If \(B_T\) is its column frame and \(L_T\)
its exact dual, the new bounds are
\[
 L_TB_T=I,\qquad
 u^pB_T,\ u^qL_T\ \text{regular},\qquad
 p=b-1,\quad q=2(b-1),\quad m=p+q=3(b-1).
\]
These are bounds for each summand of the specified formulas, as well
as for the matrices themselves. They hold at all levels, including
even and composite levels.

The improvement comes from cancelling factorials before estimating
their orders of vanishing. Write
\[
 [a]_\zeta=\frac{\zeta^a-\zeta^{-a}}{\zeta-\zeta^{-1}},
 \qquad
 \binom ar_\zeta=\frac{[a]_\zeta!}{[r]_\zeta![a-r]_\zeta!}.
\]
Every valid Gaussian binomial has valuation zero or one:
\[
 \operatorname{ord}_{u=0}\binom ar_\zeta
  =\lfloor a/N\rfloor-\lfloor r/N\rfloor
                         -\lfloor(a-r)/N\rfloor\in\{0,1\}.
\]
An inclusion summand has one Gaussian denominator. The proof derives
its exact dual using a diagonal bilinear form and a finite
Vandermonde identity, with the normalization fixed by the highest
vector's first coefficient. Two further factorial cancellations
leave only two Gaussian denominators in each dual summand.
Thus the local pole bounds are one and two. Adding them over the
\(b-1\) vertices proves the displayed bounds. This bilinear form is
used to calculate the dual; it is not claimed to be a positive
Hermitian metric.

Set \(\mathcal C_T=u^pB_T\) and
\(g=\dim_{\mathcal K}\operatorname{Inv}_{\mathcal K}
(V_d(\zeta)^{\otimes b})\). Then the exact source is
\[
 \mathcal V=
 \left\{[u^m](\mathcal C_Tz):
 \begin{array}{l}
 z\in(\mathcal O/u^{m+1})^g,\\
 [u^j](\mathcal C_Tz)=0\quad(0\le j<m)
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
Only Laurent coefficients of \(B_T\) from order \(-p\) through \(q\)
are needed. The lower equations define a finite vector space \(Z_T\);
the last coefficient map \(E_Tz=[u^m]\mathcal C_Tz\) has image
exactly \(\mathcal V\). Consequently
\(Z_T/\ker(E_T|_{Z_T})\simeq\mathcal V\).
If a minimization uses these variables only through the resulting
physical root state, eliminate this kernel before forming its Gram.
The redundant jet variables then disappear. The remaining dimension
is \(g\), which may still grow with \(N\), and this elimination has no
proved conditioning bound.

For a whole regular original word \(W\),
\[
                  \operatorname{ord}_{u=0}(L_{T'}WB_T)\ge-m.
\]
This depends on width, rather than word length. Root-value operations
can use \(W(q_0)\) restricted to the reconstructed source.
An independently prescribed quantum-normal derivative still needs
its differentiated word and cap; the root restriction does not
determine that separate germ.

There is also an analytic consequence for the full marked scalar.
Keep the word and all filling powers fixed before \(N\to\infty\).
Use one complete frame identity inside the original ambient word,
and expand the original finite crossing matrices there.
Every raw crossing term is root-regular. The resulting raw pole
budget is \(m\); it is not obtained by adding apparent poles from
many sequential changes of fusion coordinates.

The potentially large balanced leaf gauges cancel in the full
degree-preserving contraction before absolute values are taken.
The last marked row is restricted to its degree only after the
whole invariant word and the other ordinary caps have been assembled.
The proof retains the original phases and marked cap. Its auxiliary
regular cap lift is used only to recover the prescribed root value;
it is not identified with a separate generic Jones or ADO family.

With \(F_n(\zeta)=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-\zeta^{2j})\), the resulting
finite sum has explicit terms consisting of a phase, powers of \(N\),
and a fixed number of ratios of these factorials.
There are polynomially many terms for a fixed word, and all factorial
indices are \(O_b(N)\).
Removing root zeros and extracting the constant Laurent coefficient
requires at most \(m\) derivatives. The existing factorial estimate
therefore adds only a polynomial cost:
\[
 |K_N|\le |\chi_N|\,C_WN^{A_W}
       \sum_\nu\prod_a
          S_{\,n_{\nu,a}\bmod N}^{\,\epsilon_{\nu,a}},
 \qquad
 S_r=\prod_{j=1}^r2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad S_0=1.
\]
Here \(\chi_N\) is the unchanged original external factor; \(\nu\)
indexes the specified expansion; \(n_{\nu,a}\) and
\(\epsilon_{\nu,a}\) are its factorial indices and integer exponents.
The number of factors per term, the polynomial exponent and constants
may depend on the fixed word and its filling powers. The source-frame
derivative order \(m\) does not.

This removes an unspecified large-minor inverse from the chosen
closed expression. It does not bound inverses of arbitrarily selected
saturated root bases or the conditioning of their positive Grams.
Nor is the factorial envelope proved sharp: its maximum need not be
the hyperbolic volume, and the original coherent sum can have a
smaller rate. The general geometric estimate after fixed short
partial fillings, its nonzero contribution to the original closing,
and the finite-exception theorem remain unproved.
