## Bounded quantum jets determine the physical fusion source, 22 November

The generic fusion source now has a uniform bound on the order of
its confluence at a root of unity. The bound depends on the number
of physical strands, and is independent of the level and the number
of regular crossing operators in a word.
This resolves the unspecified jet order in the earlier deformable
source construction. It supplies no bound on the large-\(N\) sizes
of the resulting matrices.

Here is the precise statement of the
[uniform confluence theorem](research_uniform_fusion_confluence_source.md).
Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q_0=e^{\pi i/N}\), and an even
number \(b\ge2\) of physical strands.
Use \(u=\zeta-q_0\),
\(\mathcal O=\mathbb C\{u\}\), and
\(\mathcal K=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal O)\).
For the actual generic balanced \(N\)-dimensional leaf family set
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathcal O}=V_d(\zeta)^{\otimes b},\qquad
 \mathcal I_{\mathcal K}=
       \operatorname{Inv}_{\mathcal K}
          (\mathcal M_{\mathcal O}\otimes\mathcal K),\qquad
 \Lambda=\mathcal I_{\mathcal K}\cap\mathcal M_{\mathcal O}.
\]
Its embedded root fiber \(\mathcal V=\Lambda/u\Lambda\) is the
already established saturated source containing every state reached
from regular original cups and tangle operators. It can be smaller
than the entire root invariant space, which is not substituted for it.

For every binary fusion tree, retain every admissible generic
intermediate color and root color zero. The proof constructs its
column frame \(B_T\) and an exact dual \(L_T\), with
\[
 \operatorname{im}B_T=\mathcal I_{\mathcal K},\qquad
 L_TB_T=I,\qquad
 u^JB_T,\ u^JL_T\ \hbox{regular},\qquad
                    J=(5b+4)(b-1).
\]
The dual is defined by actual generic Casimir projectors and
coefficient extraction after divided raising. It uses no inverse
of an unspecified large minor.
The physical balanced leaf gauge, including its phases, is written
explicitly and is a unit over \(\mathcal O\).
Its complex norm is not assumed bounded.

The valuation calculation is elementary and uniform in the level.
For \([m]_\zeta=(\zeta^m-\zeta^{-m})/(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})\),
\[
 \operatorname{ord}_{u=0}[m]_\zeta!=\lfloor m/N\rfloor.
\]
Every intermediate color is less than \(bN\).
The difference of two generic Casimir eigenvalues factors as
\[
 \lambda_c-\lambda_e
    =\zeta^{-c-1}(1-\zeta^{c-e})(1-\zeta^{c+e+2}).
\]
There are only \(O(b)\) vanishing factors in each projector
denominator, even when a gap has a double zero.
The local inclusion and dual have pole bounds \(2b\) and
\(5b+4\), respectively. Adding these bounds along the \(b-1\)
vertices proves the stated tree bound. No prime or parity
restriction on \(N\) is needed.

Put \(g=\dim_{\mathcal K}\mathcal I_{\mathcal K}\),
\(\Lambda_T=B_T^{-1}\Lambda\), and \(C_T=u^JB_T\).
The two frame bounds give
\[
       u^J\mathcal O^g\subset\Lambda_T\subset u^{-J}\mathcal O^g.
\]
More importantly the entire root source is the following finite
kernel/image calculation:
\[
 \mathcal V=
 \left\{[u^{2J}](C_Tz):
 \begin{array}{l}
 z\in(\mathcal O/u^{2J+1})^g,\\
 [u^k](C_Tz)=0\quad(0\le k<2J)
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
Thus only the Laurent coefficients of \(B_T\) from order
\(-J\) through \(J\) are required.
In one direction, if \(\psi\in\Lambda\), then
\(z=u^JL_T\psi\) is regular and \(C_Tz=u^{2J}\psi\).
In the other direction, a polynomial representative satisfying
the displayed finite equations gives the regular invariant lift
\(\psi=u^{-2J}C_Tz\).
This proves the formula without computing an unknown full
Smith basis.

For any whole regular original braid word \(W(\zeta)\),
\[
             \operatorname{ord}_{u=0}(L_{T'}WB_T)\ge-2J.
\]
Multiplying many meromorphic recoupling matrices separately would
hide the cancellations behind this bound.
The physical word is regular before recoupling, so the whole-word
bound follows directly from the two frame bounds, independently
of its number of letters.

Once \(\mathcal V\) is determined, root values of the original
physical generators suffice for its root-value contractions.
For example, choose an orthonormal column basis \(U\) of
\(\mathcal V\) in the original physical metric.
If \(p\in\mathcal V\) is the original cup state and \(\lambda\)
the original final row, then
\[
 \lambda W(q_0)p
       =(\lambda U)\,(U^*W(q_0)U)\,(U^*p).
\]
Every regular original letter preserves this source, so these
restrictions compose exactly. Also
\(\|\lambda U\|\le\|\lambda\|\) and \(\|U^*p\|=\|p\|\).
The full marked cap, pivots and original external factors remain
in this expression. Independently prescribed quantum-normal
derivatives of a word or cap still need their own derivative data.

Higher-spin generic fusion and nonsemisimple centralizer bases
are established subjects; see
[Flores--Peltola](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.06038) and
[Andersen--Stroppel--Tubbenhauer](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.00224)
for literature coverage. No theorem from those papers is imported
into the proof of this bound.
The already known source filter is also not claimed as a new result.
The addition is the explicit dual, uniform pole budget and finite-jet
construction for the actual physical fusion frames.

The number of coordinates still grows with \(N\), and a bounded
valuation gives no subexponential bound on nonzero coefficients
or Gram matrices. The full observed geometric asymptotic after
arbitrary fixed short components remains unproved.
So does the finite-exception theorem.

## The initialized formula extends while the root stays inside the unit circle, 22 November

The small coefficient interval is no longer an arbitrary restriction
coming from a small activity disc.
The [transport theorem](research_crossing_coefficient_interior_transport.md)
proves the same canonically normalized asymptotic throughout
\[
 (h,k)\in\Omega,\qquad 0<t=\frac nN<\frac{h+k}{2}.
\]
The inequalities are strict: estimates are uniform on compact subsets,
and the theorem makes no assertion at the unit-circle boundary itself.
Here \(\Omega\), the actual coefficients \(c_{n,N}\), the origin
factor \(\Gamma_{0,N}\), and the phase \(a(C)\) are those defined
in the coefficient section below.
With \(C_ta'(C_t)=t\),
\(\alpha(C)=[(1-HC)(1-KC)]^{-1/2}\), and
\(\beta_t=C_ta'(C_t)+C_t^2a''(C_t)\), the formula is
\[
 c_{n,N}=
 \Gamma_{0,N}
 \frac{\alpha(C_t)e^{Na(C_t)}C_t^{-n}}
      {\sqrt{2\pi N\beta_t}}
                       (1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
All logarithms, factorials and square roots retain their small-index
initialization. The normalized error has fixed parameter derivatives
of the same order on smaller complex neighborhoods.

There is an explicit geometric reason the recurrence is stable
through this whole interval. Put \(R=h+k\),
\(H=e^{-2\pi ih}\), \(K=e^{-2\pi ik}\), and
\[
 B(C)=\frac{(1-HC)(1-KC)}{(1-C)^2},\qquad
 w=\frac{1+C}{1-C},\quad
 A=\frac{\cot\pi h+\cot\pi k}{2},\quad
 D=\frac{\cot\pi h-\cot\pi k}{2},\quad
 s=\sin\pi h\sin\pi k .
\]
The exact identity
\[
       e^{\pi iR}B(C)=-s\{(w-iA)^2+D^2\}
\]
maps the unit disc conformally onto
\(\mathbb C\setminus e^{-\pi iR}[-sD^2,\infty)\).
For \(0<t<R/2\), the rotated target
\(e^{\pi iR}e^{-2\pi it}\) lies strictly in the upper half-plane.
Consequently the characteristic quadratic has exactly one root
\(C_t\) inside the unit disc and its other root outside.
Its reciprocal eigenvalues satisfy
\[
                     |\lambda_t|>1>|\mu_t|.
\]
This strict modulus gap is uniform on compact subsets and persists
on small fixed complex parameter neighborhoods.

The proof then uses the exact finite recurrence, not a continued
coefficient contour. Write \(\epsilon=1/N\) and \(T=e^{-2\pi it}\).
For \(2\le n<N\),
\[
 c_n=a_\epsilon(t)c_{n-1}+b_\epsilon(t)c_{n-2},\qquad
 a_\epsilon=\frac{2Te^{\pi i\epsilon}-H-K}{T-1},\quad
 b_\epsilon=\frac{HK-Te^{2\pi i\epsilon}}{T-1}.
\]
The explicit trial \(W_n\) on the right of the asserted asymptotic
has relative recurrence residual \(\rho_n=O(\epsilon^2)\).
The proof verifies the first-order amplitude equation algebraically,
including both half-step factors.
For \(y_n=c_n/W_n\) and \(d_n=y_n-y_{n-1}\), the exact error equation is
\[
 d_n=-\widetilde b_n d_{n-1}-\rho_n y_{n-1},\qquad
 \widetilde b_n=b_\epsilon W_{n-2}/W_n
                   =-\mu_t/\lambda_t+O(\epsilon).
\]
The modulus of this multiplier is at most a fixed \(r<1\).
Two consecutive actual source values in the earlier small-index
interval initialize \(y_n=1+O(\epsilon)\).
Summing the geometric error bound over at most \(N\) steps gives
\(\sup|y_n-1|=O(\epsilon)\).
The argument divides only by the known nonzero trial, and proves
nonvanishing of the actual coefficients.

Combining this result with the bounded-index and small-index formulas
also controls every index from zero through
\(\lfloor N((h+k)/2-\delta)\rfloor\), for any fixed positive margin
\(\delta\), uniformly on compact subsets of \(\Omega\) wherever
that index range is nonempty.
The restriction \(V(h,k)>0\) in \(\Omega\) is still needed for the
proved source initialization.

This is a source estimate in the centered Fourier index \(n\).
That index has not been identified with a Newton wire angle of the
strict Conway construction. The unit-modulus boundary, arbitrary
short-component assembly and the original full closing remain
outside this theorem. In particular the cancellation calculation
below continues to rule out discarding the complementary coordinates.
The finite-exception theorem is still unproved.

## The original cap requires cancellation with the complementary coordinates, 22 November

The newly controlled low coordinates cannot be kept as a dominant
part while treating the remaining coordinates as a small cap error.
This fails for the literal source and closing, throughout an open
parameter region. The calculation also gives a noncancelling
observation of each retained initial interval, without requiring
a specially phase-aligned row.

Use the source, coefficients and phase from the next section:
\(x_N=f_0U_{-H}U_{-K}\),
\(c_{n,N}=(-1)^n(x_N)_n\),
\(H=e^{-2\pi ih}\), and \(K=e^{-2\pi ik}\).
Write \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(d=N-1\), and
\(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\).
The exact original cap from the centered compiler is
\[
 \phi(f_n)=\frac{\kappa^{-1}}{\sqrt N}(-q^{-1})^n,\qquad
 \phi(P_Dx_N)=\frac{\kappa^{-1}}{\sqrt N}
                  \sum_{n=0}^Dq^{-n}c_{n,N}.
\]
Here \(P_D\) is orthogonal coordinate projection onto
\(f_0,\ldots,f_D\); no cap has been changed.

First shrink the coefficient theorem's \(t_0\).
Uniformly on a compact subset of its parameter region, for all
sufficiently large levels there is a fixed \(r<1/4\) with
\[
 |c_{n-1,N}|\le r|c_{n,N}|,\qquad
                         1\le n\le\lfloor t_0N\rfloor .
\]
Here is the argument for growing indices.
Set \(S(t)=a(C_t)-t\Log C_t\), with
\(\Log C_t=\log t+\Log(C_t/t)\) near zero, and let
\[
 B_{n,N}=
 \frac{\alpha(C_t)e^{NS(t)}}{\sqrt{2\pi N\beta_t}},
 \qquad t=n/N .
\]
The saddle equation gives \(S'(t)=-\Log C_t\), exactly.
For \(n\ge2\), the exponential part of
\(|B_{n-1,N}/B_{n,N}|\) is therefore at most
\[
 \exp\!\left(N\int_{(n-1)/N}^{n/N}\log|C_u|\,du\right)
                              \le M n/N .
\]
Since \(\beta_t=t\,b(t)\), with \(b\) analytic and nonzero,
the remaining amplitude ratio is at most
\(M_1\sqrt{n/(n-1)}\).
Choose a fixed index threshold large enough that the relative
\(O(1/n)\) errors in the coefficient theorem and their inverses
are bounded, and then decrease \(t_0\).
This proves the ratio inequality above that threshold.
For the finitely many smaller indices, its fixed-index formula gives
\[
 \left|\frac{c_{n-1,N}}{c_{n,N}}\right|
       =\frac{n}{N|z|}(1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad z=a'(0)\ne0 .
\]
This proves the same bound there.
Consequently all preceding terms of the cap sum have total
magnitude at most \(r/(1-r)\,|c_{D,N}|\), and hence
\[
 \frac{2|c_{D,N}|}{3\sqrt N}
       \le|\phi(P_Dx_N)|
       \le\frac{4|c_{D,N}|}{3\sqrt N},
 \qquad 0\le D\le\lfloor t_0N\rfloor .
\]

Now fix a compact set of real pairs
\((h,k)\in(0,1/2)^2\).
With \(J(u)=\int_0^u\log|2\sin\pi s|\,ds\), put
\[
 T(h,k)=J(h+k)-J(h)-J(k),\qquad
 V(h,k)=T(h,k)-J(h)-J(k).
\]
On this compact set \(T>0\) and \(V-T>0\).
In particular it lies in the origin theorem's region \(\Omega\).
The exact full observation is
\[
             \phi(x_N)=\mathcal C_N(0,-H,-K).
\]
The single-leg source theorem gives
\(\log|\phi(x_N)|=NT(h,k)+O(1)\).
Its strict prism hypotheses can be met uniformly by choosing
\[
 a=1-h-k+\frac{hk}{h+k};
 \quad
 a+h=1-\frac{k^2}{h+k},\quad
 a+k=1-\frac{h^2}{h+k},\quad
 a+h+k=1+\frac{hk}{h+k}.
\]
All these inequalities have positive margins on the fixed compact set.

Choose any sufficiently small fixed \(0<\tau<t_0\) and
\(D=\lfloor\tau N\rfloor\).
The origin and coefficient theorems, together with the endpoint
cap bound above, give
\[
 \log|\phi(P_Dx_N)|=N W_\tau(h,k)+O(\log N),\qquad
 W_\tau=V+\operatorname{Re}a(C_\tau)-\tau\log|C_\tau|.
\]
The floor changes this expression by \(O(1)\), since
\(\tau>0\) is fixed. Shrinking \(t_0\) ensures
\(\operatorname{Re}a(C_t)\ge t/2\) and \(|C_t|<1\).
Thus \(W_\tau>V>T\), uniformly on the compact set.
For some \(\gamma>0\), the exact complementary observation is therefore
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \phi((I-P_D)x_N)
      =-\phi(P_Dx_N)\bigl(1+O(e^{-\gamma N})\bigr).
 \quad}
\]
The head and complement are orthogonal vectors in the positive
coefficient norm. Their original scalar observations nevertheless
cancel at an exponential scale. The coefficient theorem remains
valid; the failed inference is a cap approximation by that head
with a small complementary cap error. A full observed sum must
be assembled before its geometric rate is inferred.
This is not a knot counterexample or a new filling result.

## One quadratic equation controls a linear number of boundary coordinates, 22 November

The fixed-degree error expansion already has an exact finite Fourier
filter, so its auxiliary minimization is unnecessary. There is now a
different simplification for the original boundary coordinates.
A single analytic phase controls a positive fraction of them, with
their actual coefficient integrals and phases retained.

Write
\[
 \Phi_N(C,H,K)=\phi(f_0U_{-C}U_{-H}U_{-K})
              =\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}c_{n,N}(H,K)C^n,
 \qquad U_t=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}t^jf_j .
\]
Here \(\phi(f_if_j)=\delta_{ij}\),
\(H=e^{-2\pi ih}\), and \(K=e^{-2\pi ik}\).
Thus \(c_{n,N}=(-1)^n(x_N)_n\) for the original output
\(x_N=f_0U_{-H}U_{-K}\).
The parameter region is
\[
 J(u)=\int_0^u\log|2\sin\pi s|\,ds,\qquad
 \Omega=\{h,k>0:\ h+k<1,\
             J(h+k)-2J(h)-2J(k)>0\}.
\]
For every fixed compact subset of \(\Omega\), the
[coefficient theorem](research_crossing_linear_head_coefficient_source.md)
gives a fixed complex neighborhood and a number \(t_0>0\)
such that all
\[
               c_{n,N},\qquad 0\le n\le\lfloor t_0N\rfloor ,
\]
are nonzero for every sufficiently large integer level.
The estimate includes both level parities and composite levels.
It is proved in the full repeated-root algebra.

The phase and its leading amplitude are
\[
 a(C)=-\frac{2\operatorname{Li}_2(C)
                 -\operatorname{Li}_2(HC)-\operatorname{Li}_2(KC)}
                 {2\pi i},\qquad
 \alpha(C)=[(1-HC)(1-KC)]^{-1/2},\quad \alpha(0)=1 .
\]
Set \(t=n/N\), \(z=a'(0)=(2-H-K)/(-2\pi i)\), and
\(T=e^{-2\pi it}\). The branch \(C_t=t/z+O(t^2)\) solves
\[
 (HK-T)C_t^2+(2T-H-K)C_t+1-T=0.
\]
Its logarithmic lift is fixed by \(C_ta'(C_t)=t\);
the exponentiated quadratic alone would not fix that lift.
This is a local coefficient relation, not a knot peripheral polynomial.
With \(\beta_t=C_ta'(C_t)+C_t^2a''(C_t)=t+O(t^2)\),
\[
 c_{n,N}=
 \Gamma_{0,N}
 \frac{\alpha(C_t)e^{Na(C_t)}C_t^{-n}}
      {\sqrt{2\pi N\beta_t}}
 \bigl(1+O(n^{-1})+O(e^{-\delta N})\bigr).
\]
Here \(\Gamma_{0,N}\) is the canonically normalized origin value
in the next section, and
\(\sqrt{\beta_t}=\sqrt t\,\sqrt{\beta_t/t}\), continued from
\(\beta_t/t=1\). The formula is uniform as \(n\to\infty\)
with \(0<n/N\le t_0\), including \(n/N\to0\).
For fixed \(m\), the separate expansion is
\[
 c_{m,N}=\Gamma_{0,N}\frac{(Nz)^m}{m!}
                     (1+O_m(N^{-1})+O(e^{-\delta N})).
\]

The proof starts with the analytic source comparison
\(\Phi_N=\Gamma_{0,N}A_N(1+O(e^{-\delta N}))\)
from the fixed-disc theorem below.
The exact series for \(A_N\) gives
\(A_N=\alpha e^{Na}(1+O(N^{-1}))\), including the
near-resonant series tail and the original half-step amplitude.
On the entire original coefficient circle,
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\{a(C_te^{i\theta})-a(C_t)-it\theta\}
       \le-\frac t2(1-\cos\theta),\qquad -\pi\le\theta\le\pi .
\]
This supplies the complementary-arc bound as well as the nonzero
Gaussian contribution. Rescaling the phase by \(t\) makes the
effective large parameter \(n=Nt\), which proves the uniformity
at small \(t\). The actual source error is integrated on the
same circle, so it remains a relative exponential error.

There is also an ordinary coefficient-norm consequence.
Put \(\pi_{n,N}=[C^n]A_N\),
\(v_D=\sum_{n=0}^D(-1)^n\pi_{n,N}f_n\), and let \(P_D\)
be orthogonal coordinate projection onto \(f_0,\ldots,f_D\).
Uniformly for \(D\le\lfloor t_0N\rfloor\),
\[
 \|P_Dx_N-\Gamma_{0,N}v_D\|
       \le Ce^{-\delta N}|\Gamma_{0,N}|\,\|v_D\| .
\]
The canonical phase therefore controls a growing part of the
actual vector, rather than only a fixed number of test coefficients.
The phase-aligned nonnegative rows specified in the proof also
have noncancelling contractions with this vector.

The auxiliary error degree, the quartic optimization degree, and
the physical boundary degree remain different quantities.
A fixed short component need not have bounded physical degree
or a phase-aligned closing row. The omitted coordinates and the
original full closing still require control. This theorem does
not establish general Conway gluing or finitely many exceptional
filling assignments.

## The origin normalization and a fixed complex activity disc, 22 November

The coefficient \(\Phi_N(0,H,K)\) in the earlier origin formula
now has a proved canonical normalization on its whole positive-action
region. This also controls the full original crossing polynomial
on a fixed small complex activity disc. Both estimates concern the
actual source, with all Fourier coordinates retained.

Use \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\), \(H=e^{-2\pi ih}\), and \(K=e^{-2\pi ik}\).
Write
\[
 \Phi_N(C,H,K)=\phi(f_0U_{-C}U_{-H}U_{-K}),\qquad
 \Phi_{0,N}(H,K)=\phi(f_0^2U_{-H}U_{-K}),
\]
\[
 L(t)=\int_0^t\log|2\sin\pi u|\,du,\qquad
 V(h,k)=L(h+k)-2L(h)-2L(k),
\]
\[
             \Omega=\{h,k>0:\ h+k<1,\ V(h,k)>0\}.
\]
Here \(U_t=\sum_{j=0}^d t^jf_j\), and \(f_j\) is the complete
centered basis with \(\phi(f_if_j)=\delta_{ij}\).
The comparison is the specified origin value
\[
 \Gamma_{0,N}(h,k)=\frac{\kappa^2}{N^2}
 \frac{\mathfrak F_N(N(1-h)-1/2)^2
       \mathfrak F_N(N(1-k)-1/2)^2}
      {\mathfrak F_N(N(1-h-k))}.
\]
Its factorial and phase have the canonical normalization already
fixed above. Activity \(C=0\) is distinct from the physical
grid value \(C=q^{-1}\) used by the original cap.

The [origin normalization theorem](research_crossing_origin_fourier_normalization.md)
proves that for every compact \(\mathcal K\subset\Omega\), there
are a fixed complex neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) and \(\delta>0\)
such that
\[
       \sup_{\mathcal U}
       |\Phi_{0,N}/\Gamma_{0,N}-1|=O(e^{-\delta N}).
 \tag{N1}
\]
Every fixed-order derivative has the same property on a smaller
neighborhood. Both parities, composite levels, original phases
and all Hermite directions remain included. In particular,
on the real compact set,
\[
            \log|\Phi_{0,N}|=NV(h,k)+O(\log N).
\]

There is one normalization seed for the whole region. On the
full two-variable Fourier grid \(h=(j+1/2)/N\),
\(k=(\ell+1/2)/N\), the original data are exact factorial products
with magnitude
\[
       N\,\frac{S_{j+\ell}}{S_j^2S_\ell^2},\qquad
       S_a=\prod_{b=1}^a2\sin(\pi b/N),
                      \quad j+\ell\le d,
\]
and zero outside that support. Their uniform exponential profile
is \(V\). Its unique global maximum on the closed triangle is
\((1/4,1/4)\); the boundary has a strict lower maximum.
The canonical phase near that point lies strictly inside the
physical Fourier band. The exact cardinal remainder therefore
selects the normalization there, including generic fractional
offsets. This is a two-variable argument for these data; it does
not specialize a three-variable interior theorem at a boundary.

The rest of the region is reached by balancing. At fixed
\(R=h+k<1\),
\[
 \frac{d^2}{dt^2}V(t,R-t)
       =-\frac{2\pi\sin\pi R}{\sin\pi t\sin\pi(R-t)}<0.
\]
Moving to \((R/2,R/2)\) increases the action. On the diagonal,
\[
                  \frac d{dt}V(t,t)=2\log\cot(\pi t),
\]
so moving toward \(t=1/4\) increases it again.
Thus \(\Omega\) is connected, and every target has a path
to the seed along which \(V\) never falls below its target value.
For compact target sets these paths have uniformly buffered
coordinate staircases, preserving both fractional offsets and
using fewer than \(3N/2+3\) steps.
The exact affine source equation makes the normalized error
additive along those steps. Its forcing is \(O(1/N)\) on real
angles, while the canonical denominator grows exponentially
because \(V>0\). This proves (N1) throughout the region.
The complete proof also gives the fixed complex neighborhood.

The [fixed-disc theorem](research_crossing_origin_disc_normalization.md)
then proves more than a statement at the center.
For the same compact target set, after shrinking \(\mathcal U\)
there is a fixed \(r>0\), independent of \(N\), with
\[
 \frac{\Phi_N(C,e^{-2\pi ih},e^{-2\pi ik})}
      {\Gamma_N(C,e^{-2\pi ih},e^{-2\pi ik})}
       =1+O(e^{-\delta N}),
 \qquad (h,k)\in\mathcal U,\quad 0<|C|\le r .
 \tag{N2}
\]
This holds on every fixed bounded-argument marked sector, and
at the continuous origin value. The Gamma section can still
have its \(C^N\Log C\) term; no all-orders holomorphic germ is
asserted.

The proof uses the exact finite identity
\(\Phi_N=\Phi_{0,N}P_N+j_{0,N}\mathcal Q_N\) and the explicit
factorization \(\Gamma_N=\Gamma_{0,N}A_NB_N\) from the preceding
origin calculation. On a sufficiently small fixed outer circle,
\(A_N\) and its inverse are bounded by \(e^{aN}\), with \(a\)
as small as required. Ordinary Hardy projection controls the
Taylor truncation \(P_N\). The diagonal Fourier inverse has
norm at most \(N/4\) and bounds \(\mathcal Q_N\) on a smaller
circle. The positive rate of \(\Gamma_{0,N}\) then dominates
this explicit source correction and its central characters.
The marked factor \(B_N\) is also estimated explicitly.
The proof retains all multiplication and projection costs.

These results remove the previously unresolved origin
normalization on \(\Omega\), and establish a nonzero actual
source on the stated fixed disc. A pointwise disc estimate
does not give a relative bound for an arbitrary boundary
covector or its subsequent Conway contraction. The original
cap activities lie on the unit circle, and a reciprocal change
of basis also changes the source being compared.
The general gluing and closing estimate, and hence the
finite-exception theorem, remain unproved.

## The actual Gamma remainder has an origin formula and a controlled connector, 22 November

The [origin and cap calculation](research_crossing_origin_jet_and_cap_adapter.md)
now concerns the specific Gamma remainder, rather than an arbitrary
function invisible on the finite grid. It separates the remainder's
first \(N\) coefficients from the integral across its marked cut.
The latter has a bound against every full boundary covector.
The finite polynomial contribution still needs its geometric estimate.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(p=q^{-2}\),
\(\eta=(-1)^d\), and \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\).
Let \(H=e^{-2\pi ih}\), \(K=e^{-2\pi ik}\), where \(h,k>0\)
and \(h+k<1\). The activity \(C\), rather than its angle, tends
to zero below. Keep a bounded-argument branch of \(\Log C\).
The full original polynomial is
\[
 \Phi_N(C,H,K)=\phi(f_0U_{-C}U_{-H}U_{-K}),\qquad
 U_t=\sum_{j=0}^d t^j f_j .
\]
The centered basis is orthonormal, and
\(\phi(f_if_j)=\delta_{ij}\); it contains the whole nonreduced
boundary space.

There is an explicit nonzero origin value for the canonical
section:
\[
 \Gamma_0=\frac{\kappa^2}{N^2}
 \frac{\mathfrak F_N(N(1-h)-1/2)^2
       \mathfrak F_N(N(1-k)-1/2)^2}
      {\mathfrak F_N(N(1-h-k))}.
\]
Here \(\mathfrak F_N\) is the same normalized canonical factorial
as in the earlier source formulas. Define the analytic unit
\[
 A_N(C)=\exp\sum_{\substack{n\ge1\\N\nmid n}}
    \frac{2q^{-n}-H^n-K^n}{n(p^n-1)}C^n,\qquad |C|<1.
\]
The exact factorization is
\[
 \Gamma_N(C)=\Gamma_0 A_N(C) B_N(C),\qquad
 \log B_N=O_\rho\!\left(|C|^N(1+|\Log C|)\right)
                           \quad(0<|C|\le\rho<1).
\]
The complete proof specifies \(B_N\), including its central
logarithms and dilogarithms, with no unspecified periodic unit.
In particular \(B_N=1+O_\rho(\rho^N)\) on a fixed marked turn.
The first possible logarithmic term of \(\Gamma_N\) itself is
\[
          \frac{\Gamma_0(2+H^N+K^N)}{2\pi i}\,C^N\Log C .
\]
An ordinary holomorphic germ to all orders is therefore not
being assumed.

Put \(P_N=[A_N]_{<N}\), where brackets retain degrees \(0,\ldots,d\),
and \(j_0=\eta(2+H^N+K^N)/N\).
There is a second explicitly defined polynomial \(\mathcal Q_N\)
of degree at most \(d\), with zero constant term, such that
\[
 \Phi_N=\Phi_0P_N+j_0\mathcal Q_N,\qquad
 \Phi_0=\Phi_N(0,H,K).
 \tag{O1}
\]
Both polynomials are given by finite recurrences in the proof;
\(\Phi_0\) is a coefficient of the cleared cyclic product sum,
not an unknown normalization chosen to match \(\Gamma_0\).
Thus the difference of the first \(N\) coefficients is exactly
\[
              (\Gamma_0-\Phi_0)P_N-j_0\mathcal Q_N .
 \tag{O2}
\]
There are still \(N\) coefficients here. Varying \(H,K\) does
not give a two-dimensional physical boundary module.

### The inhomogeneous polynomial also has a direct Fourier primitive

The second recurrence in (O1) can be replaced by one diagonal
inverse. This is a further calculation from the exact origin
formula. Work in the coefficient algebra
\(\mathbb C[C]/(C^N)\), and set \(\sigma F(C)=F(pC)\).
This is a calculation with generating coefficients, not a change
of the Conway multiplication algebra.
Write \(A=P_N\) in this quotient; it is a unit because \(A(0)=1\).
Define
\[
 V=\left[\frac{C}{(1-HC)(1-KC)A}\right]_{<N},\qquad
 V=\sum_{n=1}^d v_n C^n .
\]
The exact homogeneous identity for \(A_N\), reduced modulo \(C^N\),
and the original affine source equation give
\[
        (\sigma-I)(\Phi_N/A)=j_0V .
\]
The constant coefficient is retained as \(\Phi_0\). On the
remaining coefficients, the inverse is explicit:
\[
 \mathcal Q_N
 =\left[A\sum_{n=1}^d\frac{v_n}{p^n-1}C^n\right]_{<N},
 \qquad
 \sum_{n=1}^d\frac{v_n}{p^n-1}C^n
       =\frac1N\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}r\,V(p^r C).
 \tag{O3}
\]
For the last equality, use
\(\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}r p^{rn}=N/(p^n-1)\) for \(1\le n<N\).
Equivalently, applying \(\sigma-I\) to the finite average gives
\(V-N^{-1}\sum_rV(p^rC)=V\).
In the orthonormal monomial coefficient norm, this inverse has
operator norm at most \(N/4\), since
\(|p^n-1|\ge2\sin(\pi/N)\ge4/N\).
Multiplication by \(A\) and \(A^{-1}\) has not been bounded by
this estimate; it cannot be omitted when returning to the
original boundary norm.

### The original caps retain an explicit cut integral

Set
\[
 J_N=\frac{\eta}{N}
 [2+H^N+K^N+C^N(1-(HK)^N)],\qquad
 \beta=[1-(CH)^N][1-(CK)^N].
\]
Across one counterclockwise marked turn, the exact Gamma jump is
\[
 \Gamma_- -\Gamma_+
       =\frac N\eta\,\frac{C^N J_N\Gamma_+}{\beta}.
\]
For any full boundary row \(\ell=(\ell_0,\ldots,\ell_d)\),
the kernel extracting its original observation is
\[
                  K_\ell(C)=\sum_{n=0}^d(-1)^n\ell_n C^{-n-1}.
\]
The marked Cauchy observation of \(\Gamma_N-\Phi_N\) is the
observation of (O2), with the same coefficient signs, plus
\[
          \Delta_\ell(0,\rho)=\frac1{2\pi i}
             \int_0^\rho(\Gamma_- -\Gamma_+)K_\ell(C)\,dC .
 \tag{O4}
\]
The original cap rows have the explicit finite kernels
\[
 K_\phi=\frac{\kappa^{-1}}{\sqrt N}
                  \frac{1+C^{-N}}{C-q^{-1}},\qquad
 K_m=\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt N}
                  \frac{1+C^{-N}}{C-q}.
\]
They retain the high Fourier modes; their apparent poles at
\(q^{\pm1}\) are removable.

For each fixed \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large \(N\), choosing
\(0\le\rho\le c/N\) gives the uniform bounds
\[
 |\Delta_\ell(0,\rho)|\le
       C_c|\Gamma_0|\,\|\ell\|/N,\qquad
 |\Delta_\phi(0,\rho)|,\ |\Delta_m(0,\rho)|
                \le C_c|\Gamma_0|N^{-3/2}.
 \tag{O5}
\]
Indeed \(|\log A_N(C)|\le-N\log(1-|C|)\le2c\)
on this shrinking disc, the central factor stays bounded, and
\(|\Gamma_--\Gamma_+|\le C_c|\Gamma_0||C|^N\).
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\(|K_\ell(C)|\le\|\ell\||C|^{-N}/\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\).
The factors cancel before integration over a segment of length
at most \(c/N\). Each original cap contributes its additional
\(N^{-1/2}\) through its displayed kernel.
All \(N\) boundary coordinates are included in (O5).

The scale in (O5) is the explicit origin value \(|\Gamma_0|\).
It is not the filled knot's volume rate or its final scalar.
The finite block (O2), its subsequent gluing, and its original
closing remain to be estimated. The result supplies no new
filling class and does not prove the finite-exception theorem.

The complete 388-line origin proof has SHA-256
b804ff01db1fec35851fec8b0f875aef742a71d60cade31d61b4684899f1ad9a.
Its four complete direct sources are recorded in that proof.
The Fourier primitive (O3) and its precise norm qualification
are proved above. Only written mathematics and text/hash
operations were used.

## Cardinal interpolation and orthogonal Fourier projection differ, 22 November

The proposed cancellation on a tree needs an additional property of
the actual source. The exact Gamma remainder vanishes when any two
boundary arguments are grid values, but cardinal interpolation is not the orthogonal
frequency projection used by the ordinary circle pairing. Their
discrepancy can reach every physical boundary coordinate.
The calculation below rules out an inference from orthogonality alone;
it does not rule out a more specific cancellation of that remainder.

Write \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and
\[
 V_N=\operatorname{span}\{1,C,\ldots,C^d\},\qquad
 D_N(C)=1+C^N,\qquad C_j=q^{-1}Q^{-j}.
\]
Let \(P\) be cardinal interpolation at the \(N\) distinct roots
\(C_j\) of \(D_N\), with values in \(V_N\), and put \(Q_{\rm card}=I-P\).
Let \(P_0\) instead be the orthogonal projection onto \(V_N\)
in \(L^2\) of the unit circle, with normalized Haar measure.
The two projections agree on \(V_N\), but need not agree outside it.

First, the exact two-grid identity really does imply that the Gamma
remainder has at least two complementary cardinal factors. Here are
the ingredients so this assertion does not rely on an analogy.
For the original crossing source \(\Phi_N\) and its specified
canonical \(\Gamma_N\), fix
\[
 h=(j+1/2)/N,\qquad k=(\ell+1/2)/N,\qquad 0\le j,\ell\le d.
\]
If \(j+\ell\le d\), its exact canonical formula and single-step
factorial identity give
\[
 \Gamma_N(c,h,k)=
 \frac{\kappa^2}{N^2}
 \frac{(Q;Q)_{d-j}^2(Q;Q)_{d-\ell}^2}
      {(Q;Q)_{d-j-\ell}}
 \prod_{a=0}^{j-1}(1-Cq^{-1}Q^{-a})
 \prod_{b=0}^{\ell-1}(1-Cq^{-1}Q^{-b}),
 \quad C=e^{-2\pi ic},\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}.
 \tag{P1}
\]
The variable factorial argument is \(u=N(1-c)-1/2\);
the quotient \(\mathfrak F(u)^2/
[\mathfrak F(u-j)\mathfrak F(u-\ell)]\) is exactly the two
finite products in (P1), before any specialization in \(C\).
Thus this is a polynomial of degree at most \(d\).
If \(j+\ell>d\), the fixed pair denominator has its canonical
pole at \(d-j-\ell\); after canceling the same variable ratios,
the Gamma section on this entire slice is zero.
In either case it equals \(\Phi_N\) at every remaining \(C_i\)
by the full-grid tensor identity. Polynomial interpolation proves
equality for the whole remaining variable. Permutation gives all
three two-variable identities, with their original marks.

Consequently the commuting cardinal projections in the three variables
satisfy
\[
 P_iP_j\Gamma_N=\Phi_N\quad(i\ne j),\qquad
 \Gamma_N-\Phi_N
 =Q_1Q_2P_3\Gamma_N+Q_1P_2Q_3\Gamma_N
   +P_1Q_2Q_3\Gamma_N+Q_1Q_2Q_3\Gamma_N,
 \tag{P2}
\]
where \(Q_i=I-P_i\). These are statements on the marked domain
where the sections and evaluations are defined, followed by their
meromorphic continuations. They do not identify the Gamma section
with an ordinary single-valued Fourier series on a whole circle.

If a proposed continuous extension of the gluing pairing had zero
mixed \(P/Q_{\rm card}\) blocks, (P2) would give a useful tree
argument: each surviving remainder vertex would require at least
two complementary incident edges, and such a subgraph cannot
terminate on physical boundary data in a finite tree. The known
unitary Fourier pairing does not provide that mixed-block property.

Indeed, for every \(f\in V_N\), ordinary polynomials already give
\[
              P(D_N f)=0,\qquad P_0(D_N f)=f,\qquad
              \|D_N f\|_{L^2}=\sqrt2\,\|f\|_{L^2}.
 \tag{P3}
\]
The first identity is evaluation at the nodes. The second and
third follow because \(f\) has frequencies \(0,\ldots,d\)
whereas \(C^Nf\) has frequencies \(N,\ldots,2N-1\).
Thus the cardinal-complementary space has a full \(N\)-dimensional
component visible to the orthogonal Fourier-band projection.

This is detected by the original source coordinates, not just an
unrelated polynomial functional. For a complete boundary packet
\(x=\sum_jx_jf_j\), define its centered coherent analysis
\[
             Sx(C)=\phi(xU_{-C})=\sum_{j=0}^d(-C)^j x_j .
\]
The centered basis is Hermitian orthonormal, so \(S\) is an
isometry onto \(V_N\) with its circle norm.
For any original finite boundary operator \(T\), its extension
using ordinary coefficient projection is
\[
                  E_T=S T S^{-1}P_0 .
\]
On the \(N\)-dimensional polynomial subspace \(D_N V_N\),
(P3) gives the exact identity
\[
        P E_T Q_{\rm card}(D_N f)=S T S^{-1}f .
 \tag{P4}
\]
For an invertible \(T\) this mixed block has rank \(N\);
for \(T=I\) or the genuine turn it preserves the physical norm
up to the displayed factor \(\sqrt2\) on its input.
In particular \(S f_0=1\), and the original cap detects
the two elementary outputs:
\[
             \phi(f_0)=\kappa^{-1}/\sqrt N,\qquad
             \phi(Jf_0)=\phi(f_d)=\kappa/\sqrt N .
 \tag{P5}
\]
Both are nonzero at every level. The full Hermite boundary space
is used throughout.

Sampling on the nodes would make \(Q_{\rm card}\) null, but that
chooses a different extension outside \(V_N\). It is the exact
discrete tensor presentation already available; it does not
justify discarding connectors when the Gamma period is moved to
a continuous geometric contour. The specific remainder in (P2)
may have additional correlated cancellations not shared by all of
\(Q_{\rm card}\). Establishing those cancellations with the
original closing remains the task. No new scalar bound or
finite-exception theorem follows from (P2) alone.

## A cleared cyclic formula and the large-activity source, 22 November

The [cleared cyclic formula](research_crossing_cleared_cyclic_source.md)
expresses the entire original crossing polynomial as a sum of \(N\)
explicit products. Its apparent division by \(C^N\) is exact polynomial
division. No cyclic-norm difference, forcing polynomial or individual
shift coefficient is a denominator. This includes their resonances,
and retains the full open tensor through its coherent coefficients.
The general Conway contraction still has to be estimated.

Use \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(p=Q^{-1}\), and \(\eta=(-1)^d\). For the original source put
\[
 \Phi_N(C,H,K)=\phi(f_0U_{-C}U_{-H}U_{-K}),\qquad
 J_N=\frac{\eta}{N}[2+C^N+H^N+K^N-(CHK)^N],
\]
\[
 A_r=(1-Cq^{-1}p^r)^2,\qquad
 B_r=(1-CHp^r)(1-CKp^r),\qquad
 \mathscr S_N=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}
      Cp^r\prod_{s<r}A_s\prod_{s>r}B_s .
\]
The product indices lie in \(0,\ldots,N-1\). Then, identically,
\[
                 C^N\Phi_N=\frac{\eta}{N}\mathscr S_N .
\]
Indeed the \(N\) cleared source equations telescope, and
\[
 \prod_r A_r-\prod_r B_r
 =(1+C^N)^2-[1-(CH)^N][1-(CK)^N]
 =\frac N\eta C^NJ_N .
\]
One cancels the nonzero polynomial \(J_N\) in the polynomial ring,
rather than dividing by its value at a chosen parameter.
The complete proof also obtains \(C^N\mid\mathscr S_N\)
independently, by cyclically rotating a product of triangular
two-by-two matrices. The quotient has degree at most \(N-1\)
separately in all three activities. Its value at \(C=0\) is its
polynomial value; no pole is present.

Adjacent summands have the exact cleared relation
\(B_{r+1}T_{r+1}=pA_rT_r\). Their generic classical ratio is
\[
       \frac{(1-s)^2}{(1-Hs)(1-Ks)},\qquad s=Cp^r.
\]
The nonzero stationary-symbol root, when defined, is
\[
                   s_*=\frac{2-H-K}{1-HK}.
\]
This gives a one-index finite sum with known endpoints, not an
accessible saddle or a nonzero saddle coefficient. The summands
retain their original phases.

### Why an arbitrarily tall Gamma chart cannot replace this source

There is a source-specific estimate in a different regime. Fix
\(|H|=|K|=1\) with \(r=HK\ne1\). There are constants \(R_0,c_1,c_2>0\)
and infinitely many integer levels such that, for all sufficiently
large levels in that subsequence,
\[
 \frac{c_1}{N}|C|^{N-1}\le|\Phi_N(C,H,K)|
                    \le\frac{c_2}{N}|C|^{N-1}
                     \qquad(|C|\ge R_0).
 \tag{E1}
\]
This statement concerns the original off-grid coherent polynomial.
Here is a proof, including the tail estimate needed to use its top
coefficient when \(N\) grows.

Reverse its \(C\)-coefficients:
\[
 F_N(z)=z^d\Phi_N(1/z,H,K)=\sum_{\ell=0}^d f_\ell z^\ell.
\]
Substitution into the exact coordinate equation gives
\[
 (1-qz)^2F_N(Qz)
 -r(1-z/H)(1-z/K)F_N(z)
 =\frac{\eta}{N}
    [1-r^N+(2+H^N+K^N)z^N].
 \tag{E2}
\]
Its constant term and coefficients in degrees \(1\le\ell\le d\),
with \(f_{-1}=0\), give
\[
 f_0=\frac{\eta(1-r^N)}{N(1-r)},\qquad
 (Q^\ell-r)f_\ell
 =[2qQ^{\ell-1}-H-K]f_{\ell-1}
       +(1-Q^{\ell-1})f_{\ell-2}.
 \tag{E3}
\]
Choose \(0<\delta<\min(1/4,|1-r|/(4\pi))\), and put
\(\Delta=|1-r|\), \(L=1+12/\Delta\).
For \(1\le\ell\le\delta N\),
\(|Q^\ell-r|\ge\Delta/2\). The other two coefficient moduli
in (E3) are at most four and two. Induction therefore gives
\[
                   |f_\ell|\le L^\ell|f_0|
                         \qquad(0\le\ell\le\lfloor\delta N\rfloor).
 \tag{E4}
\]
Indeed \(8/(\Delta L)+4/(\Delta L^2)<1\).
This induction uses no division at a possible later resonant row.

There is also a coarse bound for every coefficient:
\[
                         |f_\ell|\le N^B e^{MN}.
 \tag{E5}
\]
Here \(B,M\) are fixed constants. To see this, the exact full grid
and its uniform factorial profile in the Fourier-normalization
proof bound every grid datum by \(N^{B_0}e^{MN}\).
On the three unit activity circles each cardinal polynomial has
modulus at most one. The full cardinal formula consequently bounds
\(\Phi_N\) there by \(N^{B_0+3}e^{MN}\).
Cauchy's coefficient formula in \(C\), with the present fixed
unit \(H,K\), proves (E5), after increasing \(B\).

Choose a fixed \(0<\rho<1\) such that
\[
                   L\rho<1/4,\qquad M+\delta\log\rho<-2.
\]
On \(|z|\le\rho\), the part of \(F_N-f_0\) with
\(\ell\le\lfloor\delta N\rfloor\) has modulus at most
\(|f_0|/3\), by (E4). By (E5), its remaining part has modulus
at most \(N^{B+1}e^{-2N}\).
Infinitely many levels satisfy \(|1-r^N|\ge\Delta/3\):
otherwise two consecutive large powers would give
\[
 \Delta=|r^{N+1}-r^N|
       \le|r^{N+1}-1|+|r^N-1|<2\Delta/3.
\]
At these levels \(1/(3N)\le|f_0|\le2/(N\Delta)\).
For all sufficiently large such levels the tail is at most
\(|f_0|/6\). Thus
\[
 \tfrac12|f_0|\le|F_N(z)|\le\tfrac32|f_0|
                         \qquad(|z|\le\rho).
\]
This proves (E1), for example with
\(R_0=\rho^{-1}\), \(c_1=1/6\), and \(c_2=3/\Delta\).
In particular, for each fixed \(|C|\ge R_0\), the rate along
this subsequence is exactly \(\log|C|\).

Compare this with the specified canonical Gamma section.
Fix real \(h,k>0\), \(h+k<1\), and \(a>0\) with
\(a+h,a+k<1\). Set
\[
 H=e^{-2\pi ih},\quad K=e^{-2\pi ik},\quad
 c=a+iY,\quad C=e^{-2\pi ic},\quad |C|=e^{2\pi Y}.
\]
For each fixed \(Y\), the canonical strip estimate gives
\(N^{-1}\log|\Gamma_N|\to\Re\mathcal S(c,h,k)\).
Its marked logarithmic derivative is
\[
 \partial_c\mathcal S
 =\Log(1-CH)+\Log(1-CK)-2\Log(1-C).
\]
The branches continue from the positive real pair domain.
As \(Y\to+\infty\), this derivative is
\(-2\pi i(h+k)+O(e^{-2\pi Y})\); the strict pair-angle
inequalities fix the arguments of all three logarithms.
Integration in \(Y\) proves
\[
                \Re\mathcal S=(h+k)\log|C|+O(1).
 \tag{E6}
\]
Since \(h+k<1\), choose one sufficiently large fixed \(Y\).
Then (E1) and (E6) show that \(|\Phi_N/\Gamma_N|\) grows
exponentially along an infinite subsequence. Thus the earlier
relative Gamma estimate cannot be extended to all positive
heights merely by analytic continuation.

This does not contradict the exact Gamma values on the physical
half-grid. On that grid \(H^N=K^N=-1\), so \(r^N=1\) and the
leading coefficient in
(E3) vanishes. Nor is it a knot counterexample: the subsequent
inverse pairing and original closing can cancel the exterior
contribution. It shows why that cancellation must be proved for
the complete contraction. The source channels cannot be omitted
when composing local Gamma approximations.

## Both signs have one orthogonal Burau operator model, 22 November

The [signed orthogonal dilation](research_burau_signed_orthogonal_dilation.md)
gives an exact way to use one local operator alphabet for both
auxiliary crossing signs. Every negative marked row space embeds
isometrically into two copies of the existing positive row space.
Its image is an explicit reducing charge subspace. This proves
compatibility through every ordered word and through the full
principal-minor source formula, with the original boundary vectors
retained. It is a finite operator identity, not a volume estimate.

Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\).
The positive row space has orthonormal rows \(f_{r,l}\), with
\(r\in\mathbb Z/N\), \(0\le l\le d\), and actual right actions
\[
 f_{r,l}a=\rho_l f_{r,l+1},\qquad
 f_{r,l}b=Q^{-2r}f_{r,l},\qquad
 f_{r,l}c=Q^l f_{r+1,l}.
\]
The raising action is zero at \(l=d\). Here
\[
 \rho_l=w_{l+1}/w_l,\qquad
 w_l^2=\sum_{h=0}^l\left|{l\brack h}_Q\right|^2.
\]
The negative orthonormal rows \(F_{p,j}\), \(p\in\mathbb Z/N\),
\(0\le j\le d\), embed by the row-isometry
\[
 V(F_{p,j})=\alpha_{p,j}
               f_{p,j}\otimes f_{-j,d-j},\qquad
 \alpha_{p,j}=i^jQ^{pj}q^{j(j+5)/2}.
\]
Define, with the actual Hilbert adjoints in this row metric,
\[
 \mathsf A=a\otimes(a^*c^*),\qquad
 \mathsf B=b\otimes b,\qquad
 \mathsf C=Q(c^*\otimes I).
\]
Then \(V\mathsf A=a_-V\), \(V\mathsf B=b_-V\),
\(V\mathsf C=c_-V\), and the same identities hold for adjoints.
The displayed order in \(a^*c^*\) matters.

The earlier reflection identity
\(\rho_j\rho_{d-1-j}=2\sin(\pi(j+1)/N)\) supplies the
amplitude of \(\mathsf A\). The explicit phase \(\alpha\)
supplies the remaining negative coefficient
\(Q^{-p}(1-Q^{j+1})\). Along \(j\) height steps, the paired
magnitude is exactly
\[
       w_jw_d/w_{d-j}=S_j,\qquad
       S_j=\prod_{h=1}^j2\sin(\pi h/N).
\]
Thus the lift retains the original negative factorial scale.

Its orthogonal image projection is
\[
 \Pi=\mathbf1_{\{l_1+l_2=d\}}
       \mathbf1_{\{r_2+l_1\equiv0\pmod N\}}.
\]
It is the average of the two commuting cyclic characters:
\[
 \Pi(r_1,l_1;r_2,l_2)=
   \frac1{N^2}\sum_{u,v=0}^{N-1}
       Q^{u(l_1+l_2-d)+v(r_2+l_1)}.
\]
The congruence in the first charge is an equality because
\(0\le l_1+l_2\le2d\) excludes \(d\pm N\). This works at
even and composite levels. The image reduces each complete
grouped letter \(\mathsf A,\mathsf B,\mathsf C\) and its
adjoint. It does not reduce each separate factor inside them:
for example \(\Pi(a\otimes I)\Pi=0\), although
\(\Pi\mathsf A\Pi\ne0\). No extra projection may be inserted
inside a lifted letter.

The original negative initial row becomes
\[
 N^{-1/2}\sum_p\alpha_{p,p}
                 f_{p,p}\otimes f_{-p,d-p}.
\]
The terminal column has coefficient
\(\sqrt N\,\overline{\alpha_{0,j}}\) on
\(f_{0,j}\otimes f_{-j,d-j}\), and is zero off the image.
Their norms remain \(1,N\), and their pairing is one.
Both normalized vectors have Schmidt rank \(N\): their
displayed summands use distinct orthonormal vectors in each
factor and all coefficients have modulus \(N^{-1/2}\).
In particular they cannot be replaced by independent positive
terminal columns.

Tensor these maps at the negative occurrences and leave the
positive ones unchanged. Every ordered quantum minor intertwines
exactly. With \(k\) crossing occurrences, \(b\) physical braid
heads and writhe \(w\), the original scalar remains
\[
 K_N=\zeta\,\widetilde E^{\mathsf T}
                  (I-\widetilde C_N)^{-1}\widetilde H,\qquad
 \zeta=Q^{(b-1+w)/2}.
\]
The auxiliary word is still the reversed, sign-mirrored one
specified in the original source theorem. The endpoint norms
remain \(1,N^k\). Every surviving monomial in the lifted
principal-minor operator increases the sum of the first positive
heights, so
\(\widetilde C_N^{\,k(N-1)+1}=0\) even on the full ambient
space. The inverse is therefore a finite polynomial, with no
source limit or intermediate projection.

This is a common model for the bounded auxiliary letters and
their adjoints. It enlarges a negative \(N^2\)-dimensional
module to a reducing subspace of a positive \(N^4\)-dimensional
tensor square; it is not a dimension reduction. The full
scalar is still complex. Its selected inverse element and
entangled closing still require a geometric lower estimate.
No additional filling class or finite-exception theorem is
proved. Isometry here concerns the finite root-grid Hilbert
spaces; no isometric continuation at arbitrary complex
peripheral parameters is asserted.

### A common eigenbasis would be a different claim

The ordinary commuting-family shortcut does not apply uniformly to
all gluing operators. In the full Newton algebra, let \(M_z\)
denote multiplication by its generator and let \(J_e e_i=e_{d-i}\).
If a linear map \(T\) commutes with both, then it is scalar.
Indeed commutation with \(M_z\), whose cyclic vector is the unit,
gives \(T=M_p\), where \(p=T1\). Commutation with \(J_e\) on
the unit then gives
\[
                J_ep=pe_d=m(p)e_d,\qquad p=m(p)1.
\]
Here \(m(p)\) is the coefficient of \(e_0\); the identity uses
the full product \(e_de_j=0\) for \(j>0\).
This check uses the complete pairwise source at
470c9df0384274623a1aa0b6939067021894f2fea41595dfa7440081ca77f1d1.
It excludes a nontrivial common commuting family for these
operators, not word-dependent or covariant spectral constructions.
It places no restriction on the orthogonal gluing pairing itself.

Primary coverage was checked for that alternative:
[Tarasov--Varchenko](https://arxiv.org/html/hep-th/9411181v1)
uses an \(R\)-twisted complex bilinear Shapovalov form and generic
parameters for its Bethe basis. It does not supply a positive
Hermitian basis for our complete root-specialized source.
[Varchenko's root-of-unity qKZ paper, 19 November 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.26375v1)
fixes the physical lowering degree, weights and root order in its
connection theorem; its stated chamber-basis limits specialize
further to degree one. Those are not the fixed auxiliary-error
degrees of our recursion. In our physical complete color,
\(q_N^{N-1}\to-1\), whereas fixed weights in that limit give
\(q^{\Lambda}\to1\). Neither stated result identifies its
loaded pairing with the original closing and all its Hermite
directions. No theorem from either paper is a proof input here.

## Fourier interpolation replaces the fractional initializer, 22 November

The [Fourier normalization proof](research_crossing_fourier_normalization.md)
gives a simpler proof of the full pair-domain theorem recorded in the
next section. It uses the complete exact grid and the canonical
factorial expansion. The 705-line fractional-rigidity theorem,
its growing-order Gevrey estimates, and the separate real-to-complex
barrier are no longer inputs to this proof. Earlier final proofs
remain unchanged.

The result is still an estimate for the original crossing source:
for every compact
\[
 \mathcal K\subset\mathcal D
   =\{c,h,k>0:\ c+h,c+k,h+k<1\},
\]
there is a fixed complex neighborhood \(V\) and \(\delta>0\) such that
\[
             \sup_V|\varphi_N/\Gamma_N-1|=O(e^{-\delta N}).
\]
Fixed-order derivatives have the same property on a smaller
neighborhood. All original phases, closing factors, repeated-root
coordinates and integer levels remain included.

The Fourier bandwidth now performs a selection that was missing
from the earlier phase-only discussion.

1. The exact source has degree at most \(N-1\) in each activity.
   Its full \(N^3\) cardinal interpolant is known on the original
   Newton grid, including its zero support.
2. The grid magnitude has the uniform profile
   \(\log|G_{ijk}|=N A_0(a_i,a_j,a_k)+O(\log N)\), even on
   the support faces. The function \(A_0=\sum_{\{a,b\}}T(a,b)\)
   is jointly strictly concave, not merely positive: each
   two-variable Hessian of \(T\) is negative definite with
   determinant \(\pi^2\). Its unique global maximum is
   \(p=(1/3,1/3,1/3)\). Thus the actual grid outside a small
   neighborhood of \(p\) has a strict exponential gap.
3. Near \(p\), the canonical action satisfies
   \(0<\partial_{\Im a_j}\Re\mathcal S<2\pi\).
   The exact local cardinal remainder is
   \[
    f(t)-\sum_{\text{local }i}f(C_i)\ell_i(t)
       =\frac{1+t^N}{2\pi i}
          \int_{\mathcal C_N}
             \frac{f(z)}{(z-t)(1+z^N)}\,dz .
   \]
   Choose the angular vertical sides at multiples of \(1/N\).
   Then \(|1+z^N|=1+e^{2\pi N\Im a}\) there. The two
   horizontal sides are suppressed at the two edges of the
   physical frequency band; the vertical sides retain the
   strict grid-action gap. This bounds the actual interpolation
   error, rather than assuming it from the local phase.
4. Tensorizing these identities proves an exponentially accurate
   normalization near \(p\) for every fractional offset. A
   sufficiently small fixed complex seed follows from the same
   contour estimates. The exact additive coordinate equations
   then propagate it to any compact subset of \(\mathcal D\).
   Keeping the imaginary parts fixed along the path gives the
   complex theorem directly.

This also explains why the central countergauge in the next
section is not a counterexample to the new proof. Grid values,
shift ratios and a rough complex bound alone permit that gauge.
The strict frequency condition and the two-sided cardinal
remainder estimate are additional information; the wrong
frequency shift does not preserve them.

### An exact partial interpolation reduction

There is also an elementary exact simplification. Fix two grid
angles \(h=a_j=(j+1/2)/N\), \(k=a_k=(k+1/2)/N\).
If \(j+k\le d=N-1\), then for every complex \(c\), meromorphically
on its marked cover,
\[
 \begin{split}
 \Phi_N(C,C_j,C_k)=\Gamma_N(c,a_j,a_k)
  ={}&\frac{\kappa^2 F_{d-j}^2F_{d-k}^2}
             {N^2F_{d-j-k}}\\
    &{}\cdot
       \prod_{r=0}^{j-1}(1-Cq^{-1}Q^{-r})
       \prod_{r=0}^{k-1}(1-Cq^{-1}Q^{-r}).
 \end{split}
\]
Empty products are one. To prove this, put
\(X=N(1-c)-1/2\) in the literal Gamma quotient. Its only
\(C\)-dependent ratio is
\(\mathfrak F_N(X)^2/
 [\mathfrak F_N(X-j)\mathfrak F_N(X-k)]\).
The exact factorial recurrence turns it into the two displayed
products. Their total degree is \(j+k\le d\). The resulting
polynomial agrees with the original polynomial at all \(N\)
values \(C_i\), so they agree identically. If \(j+k>d\),
the original polynomial is identically zero by its full grid;
the canonical quotient is also identically zero, since its
constant pair factorial has a negative-integer pole and the
remaining ratio is the same finite polynomial. This last
statement is interpreted after the displayed meromorphic
cancellation, not by multiplying an uncanceled pole and zero.

Thus two discrete boundary parameters eliminate interpolation
in the third parameter exactly. The written normalization proof
uses the symmetric three-coordinate argument; a future
expository version can use this reduction to shorten it further.

### The next estimate must retain the closing projection

The analogous concavity calculation for the exact pair kernels
does not yet prove the closed-source theorem. With indices
scaled by \(N\), their limiting magnitude actions are
\(T(x,y)\) for \(g\), \(T(1-x,1-y)\) for \(h\), and
\(T(x,y-x)\) for \(J_eh\), on their strict support interiors.
Each is strictly concave. These are profiles before summation,
not estimates of the contracted boundary grid.

The original Frobenius closing gives a direct algebraic test:
\[
          (\phi h)g=\phi,\qquad
          \sum_i(\phi h)_iA_{abi}=\delta_{a+b,d}.
\]
The first identity follows from \(hg=I\). For the second,
the weighted vertex is \(g\) applied to the original product,
so the contraction is \(\phi(e_ae_b)\), exactly the displayed
Kronecker delta. In particular every \(g\)-column \(j<d\)
is annihilated by this closing despite its interior magnitude
profile. A final multiplication without a unary corridor can
be removed exactly, leaving the original bilinear pairing
\(\sum_a x_a y_{d-a}\).

Thus the next Fourier estimate must apply to the assembled
boundary data with this charged projection retained. The
interior normalization theorem does not bound the selected
projection merely by controlling the separate packet norms.
This is an exact compatibility issue for every construction,
not an additional knot case or a claimed counterexample to
the proposed finite-exception theorem.

This progress simplifies a source estimate; it supplies no
additional knot filling class by itself. General Conway gluing
still requires the nonzero geometric contribution with the
actual inverse pairings, support projections and closing.
The finite-exception theorem remains unproved.

## Three coordinate equations remove the target gap restriction, 22 November

The [full-parameter transport proof](research_crossing_full_parameter_transport.md)
extends the original crossing-source estimate to the entire real domain
\[
 \mathcal D=\{c,h,k>0:\ c+h,c+k,h+k<1\}.
\]
For every compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal D\), the original
scalar and the specified canonical Gamma section satisfy
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \varphi_N(c,h,k)/\Gamma_N(c,h,k)
        =1+O(N^A e^{-\delta N})
                 \quad\hbox{uniformly on }\mathcal K.
 \qquad}
\]
There is also a fixed complex neighborhood of \(\mathcal K\)
with exponentially small relative error and fixed-order derivatives.
The original framing, phases, Frobenius closing, repeated-root
directions, both level parities and composite levels remain included.

The exact equation behind the extension is simpler than the earlier
balanced shift. Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(Q=q^2\), \(\eta=(-1)^d\), and
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \Phi_N(C,H,K)=\phi(f_0U_{-C}U_{-H}U_{-K}),\\
 C=e^{-2\pi ic},\quad H=e^{-2\pi ih},\quad K=e^{-2\pi ik},\\
 J_N=\frac{\eta}{N}
       [2+C^N+H^N+K^N-(CHK)^N].
 \end{gathered}
\]
Then, as a polynomial identity at every \(N\ge2\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 (1-C/q)^2\Phi_N(C/Q,H,K)
       -(1-CH)(1-CK)\Phi_N(C,H,K)=CJ_N.
 \quad}
\]
There are two further equations obtained by permutation. Their
shift coefficients have degree two, independent of \(N\).
Their inhomogeneous polynomial is explicit and is retained.
The proof uses the full Newton-grid identity from the pairwise
source theorem, then fixes the polynomial remainder by its three
leading coefficients. The cyclic wrap and every support wall
are checked before division.

The same coordinate shift multiplies \(\Gamma_N\) by
\((1-CH)(1-CK)/(1-C/q)^2\). Thus, for
\(E_N=\varphi_N/\Gamma_N-1\),
\[
 E_N(c+1/N,h,k)-E_N(c,h,k)
    =\frac{CJ_N}{(1-C/q)^2\Gamma_N(c+1/N,h,k)}.
\]
The action in its denominator is
\[
 \begin{split}
 A_0&=T(c,h)+T(c,k)+T(h,k)>0,\\
 T(a,b)&=L(a+b)-L(a)-L(b),\qquad
 L(x)=\int_0^x\log|2\sin\pi t|\,dt .
 \end{split}
\]
At fixed \(s=a+b<1\), the second derivative of
\(L(s)-L(a)-L(s-a)\) is
\(-\pi\sin(\pi s)/[\sin(\pi a)\sin(\pi(s-a))]<0\);
its endpoint values are zero. This proves positivity throughout
\(\mathcal D\), not just on the older region.

Choose a seed near \((1/6,1/6,1/6)\) with the same three
fractional classes modulo \(1/N\) as the target. First lower
coordinates above their seed values, then raise the others.
This gives fewer than \(3N\) coordinate steps inside one fixed
compact subset of \(\mathcal D\). Each normalized increment is
exponentially small because \(|J_N|\le6/N\) and
\(\log|\Gamma_N|=N A_0+O(\log N)\). Summing the increments
propagates the proved fractional normalization from the seed.
Polynomial interpolation supplies a rough complex bound; a
maximum-modulus barrier then supplies a fixed complex neighborhood.
The complete proof writes out both arguments.

The target no longer needs \(c+h+k<1\) or
\(L(c+h+k)-L(h+k)>0\). The earlier fractional-rigidity theorem
is used only on the one seed neighborhood. The full cyclic norm
is still
\[
 M_C=\frac{[1-(CH)^N][1-(CK)^N]}{(1+C^N)^2}.
\]
The propagation never divides by this norm's numerator,
\(1+C^N\), \(1-M_C\), or \(J_N\). Resonant fractional classes
are consequently retained.

### What the fixed degree does and does not simplify

The auxiliary-error degree and the physical boundary degree are
different. In the positive recursion, the auxiliary degree is at
most the fixed number \(l\) of leaf occurrences. The already
proved phase filter with \(m=l+1\) therefore extracts its constant
mode exactly. Equivalently, storing \(l_v+1\) positive coefficient
matrices at a subtree with \(l_v\) leaves avoids the phase-copy
cross blocks. This removes the auxiliary minimization; it does
not evaluate the selected coefficient's exponential rate.
The physical boundary polynomials still have degree \(N-1\)
and contain all \(N\) coordinates.

Two tempting shortcuts have been checked and do not supply the
missing lower bound.

First, grid values and transport alone do not replace the generic
fractional normalization. The multiplier \(-C^{-N}\) is invariant
under all three coordinate shifts, equals one on every full grid
point \(C_i^N=-1\), has modulus one on real angles, and is
nonzero holomorphic on a fixed activity neighborhood in
\((\mathbb C^*)^3\). Multiplying \(\Gamma_N\) by it preserves
the grid values, shift ratios, real exponential rate and rough
complex exponential bounds, while changing generic fractional
phases. The canonical definition is fixed; this calculation
explains why its fractional calibration cannot be inferred
solely from those other properties.

Second, there is an exact quadratic polynomial reconstruction,
but it is exponentially ill-conditioned. On the space
\(V_N\) of polynomials separately of degree at most \(d\), with
the coefficient \(\ell^2\) norm, let
\[
 \mathcal L_C P=(1-C/q)^2P(C/Q,H,K)
                       -(1-CH)(1-CK)P(C,H,K).
\]
It is injective: the homogeneous equation and an \(N\)-step
cycle give \((1-M_C)P=0\), and \(M_C\) is not identically one.
Consequently \(\min_{P\in V_N}\|\mathcal L_C P-CJ_N\|^2\)
has the unique zero \(P=\Phi_N\). However
\[
 \|\mathcal L_C\|\le8,\qquad
 \|\mathcal L_C1\|=\sqrt8,\qquad
 \|\mathcal L_C\Phi_N\|=\sqrt8/N.
\]
The first bound follows from the two coefficient \(\ell^1\)
multiplier bounds, each equal to four. The other two equalities
follow by listing their five monomials, with one coefficient
of modulus two and four of modulus one.
At a half-grid triple within \(O(1/N)\) of the seed, the exact
Gamma-grid formula and its strip expansion give
\[
 |\Phi_N|\ge cN^{-1/2}e^{NM_0},\qquad
 M_0=A_0(1/6,1/6,1/6)>0.
\]
Evaluation on the unit activity torus has norm \(N^{3/2}\)
on \(V_N\), so \(\|\Phi_N\|\ge cN^{-2}e^{NM_0}\).
It follows that
\[
 \sigma_{\min}(\mathcal L_C)\le CN e^{-NM_0},\qquad
 \operatorname{cond}(\mathcal L_C^*\mathcal L_C)
                         \ge cN^{-2}e^{2NM_0}.
\]
This quadratic reconstruction has \(N^3\) complex unknowns.
It is not a uniformly conditioned substitute for the earlier
convex formulation. The useful new step is the direct additive
transport of the known solution, rather than minimization
over polynomial coefficients.

General Conway gluing still requires a nonzero geometric
contribution to its original closed scalar. The new complex
neighborhood need not contain every geometric continuation;
pair-strip walls, larger complex heights, support constraints
and the actual closing remain to be controlled. No further
filling class or finite-exception theorem is claimed here.

## Exact pairwise weights for every finite Conway construction, 22 November

The [pairwise source theorem](research_exact_pairwise_conway_source.md)
gives closed formulas for the weighted vertex and its inverse gluing
pairing on the entire original Newton space. This is an exact finite
identity for arbitrary literal Conway trees, including their fixed
short components. It is not an asymptotic replacement of their source.

Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\), and
\(S_r=\prod_{a=1}^r2\sin(\pi a/N)\), with \(S_0=1\).
Let \(e_0,\ldots,e_d\) be the complete Hermitian-orthonormal
Newton basis, \(\phi\) the original Frobenius closing, and
\(u=f_0=R^+/\sqrt N\). Define
\[
 g_{ij}=\phi(ue_ie_j),\qquad
 A_{ijk}=\phi(ue_ie_je_k),\qquad h=g^{-1}.
\]
The two pair kernels are
\[
 \begin{split}
 g_{ij}&=\frac{\kappa^{-1}}{\sqrt N}
    (-1)^{i+j}q^{-i-j-ij}\frac{S_{i+j}}{S_iS_j}
                         &&(i+j\le d),\\
 h_{ij}&=\frac{\kappa^{-1}}{\sqrt N}
    q^{ij}\frac{S_iS_j}{S_{i+j-d}}
                         &&(i+j\ge d).
 \end{split}
\]
Each kernel is zero outside its displayed support. The vertex factors
exactly as
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 A_{ijk}=\kappa^2N(-q)^{i+j+k}g_{ij}g_{ik}g_{jk}.
 \qquad}
\]
In particular its support is given by the three inequalities
\(i+j,i+k,j+k\le d\). All displayed sine-product magnitudes
are positive. Their phases are retained.

The proof is a cleared finite summation applied to the original
Newton multiplication. It never divides by the vanishing root
factorial \((q^2;q^2)_N\). Both level parities, composite levels,
and every repeated-root derivative coordinate remain included.
The summation is the standard second
[\(q\)-Chu--Vandermonde identity](https://dlmf.nist.gov/17.6.E3);
the note supplies its own finite proof and its root specialization.

For coefficient columns \(x,y\), write
\(A(x,y)_i=\sum_{a,b}A_{abi}x_ay_b\). Their original product
column is exactly \(hA(x,y)\). Thus an ordered unary corridor
\(T\) between multiplication vertices gives the edge matrix
\(Th\). The genuine turn is the reversal
\(J_e e_i=e_{d-i}\); its edge is \(J_eh\), supported on
\(i\le j\) with the parent index first. An original root row
\(\ell\) becomes \(\ell T_0h\) after its actual root corridor
\(T_0\). A leaf corridor contributes \(Tb\) for the original
leaf column \(b\). An expression with no multiplication has
value \(\ell Tb\), with no extra inverse pairing. These typed
identities retain the original cap and all normalization factors.

There is also an exact link to the canonical Gamma section. At
\[
 x_i=-q^{-1}(q^2)^{-i},\qquad
 U_{x_i}=\kappa\sqrt N(-q)^i e_i,
\]
the original coherent crossing kernel equals its explicit Gamma-grid
formula for every triple of indices, including all support zeros.
These samples form the full Newton basis; they are not evaluations
only at distinct Casimir roots. The whole coherent polynomial is
the tensor-product cardinal interpolant of those specified data.
This does not equate it to the meromorphic Gamma section off the grid.

### The exact Fourier space and its projections

The pair phases \(q^{\pm ij}\) are characters on
\(\mathsf G=\mathbb Z/(2N)\). Extend the physical index window
\(0,\ldots,d\) by zero to that group. Introducing a charge
\(a=d-i-j\) for each \(g\) pair and
\(b=i+j-d\) for each \(h\) pair makes every factorial magnitude
a one-variable weight. The remaining couplings are affine delta
constraints. There is no support alias: \(i+j+a\in[0,3d]\)
and \(i+j-b\in[-d,2d]\) contain only \(d\) among the numbers
\(d+2N\mathbb Z\).

The quadratic phases can likewise be placed in one-variable chirps,
using
\[
 -ij=\tfrac12[i^2+j^2-(d-a)^2],\qquad
 ij=\tfrac12[(d+b)^2-i^2-j^2].
\]
These half-square chirps are \(2N\)-periodic for every integer
\(N\). All other affine index maps keep their actual window
projections. Consequently the complete original scalar has an exact
presentation
\[
 Z_N=C_N\sum_{x\in\mathsf G^v}
       \prod_{r=1}^v w_r(x_r)
       \prod_{s=1}^f\delta_{\mathsf G}((Bx)_s-\beta_s),
\]
where each \(w_r\) is a specified factorial magnitude times a
one-variable phase and its support window. The constants \(C_N\)
retain the original framing, cap factors and powers of \(N\).
The integer matrix \(B\) and vector \(\beta\) record the actual
constraints; \(v\) and \(f\) count variables and constraints.

For \(m=2N\), use the unitary transform
\(\mathcal F_mw(\xi)=m^{-1/2}\sum_xq^{\xi x}w(x)\).
Character orthogonality gives the exact dual formula
\[
 Z_N=C_Nm^{v/2-f}
       \sum_{\xi\in\mathsf G^f}q^{-\langle\beta,\xi\rangle}
       \prod_{r=1}^v
           (\mathcal F_mw_r)((B^{\mathsf T}\xi)_r).
\]
No rank assumption on \(B\) is needed. Every factor of \(m\)
is explicit. Zero extension is an isometry, the Fourier transform
and chirps are unitary, and the normalized addition map is a
coisometry. Its adjoint followed by itself is an orthogonal
projection. Those projections, support windows and original closing
remain part of the source; unitarity alone does not supply a lower
bound for the closed scalar.

This makes vertices, inverse pairings and boundary factors explicit
in one universal finite model. The remaining volume argument must
control its original oscillatory contraction at the geometric rate.
The finite-exception theorem remains unproved.

## Polynomial rigidity fixes the fractional normalization, 22 November

The [fractional-rigidity proof](research_crossing_gamma_fractional_rigidity.md)
settles the local normalization left open in the preceding research
step, recorded below. Write \(\Phi_N(c,h,k)\) for the original
positive-crossing scalar and \(\Gamma_N(c,h,k)\) for the exact
canonical Gamma product in that proof. Fix a compact set of pairs
\[
 c,R>0,\qquad c+R<1,\qquad
 L(c+R)-L(R)>0,
 \qquad L(x)=\int_0^x\log|2\sin\pi t|\,dt.
\]
There are constants \(A,\kappa>0\), independent of the quantum
level \(N\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \frac{\Phi_N(c,h,R-h)}{\Gamma_N(c,h,R-h)}
       =1+O(N^A e^{-\kappa N}),\qquad 0\le h\le R.
 \qquad}
\]
This is uniform through the fold and at the two real endpoints.
The endpoint Gamma factors remain in the denominator; the interior
WKB amplitude is not substituted there.

The proof first treats \(h=(a-1/2)/N\) for \(a\) in a fixed
compact subset of \((0,\infty)\). At every fixed order, the
normalized coefficients are polynomials in \(a\). This is proved
for the original finite head and its retained Barnes integral,
including the finite prefactor multiplying that integral. The exact
first-order equation makes these polynomials 1-periodic. They are
therefore constant, and the known \(a=1\) normalization makes
every correction coefficient zero.

To obtain the displayed exponential error, the proof also gives a
remainder \(C^{p+1}p!N^{-p}\), uniformly for \(p\le c_0N\).
Exact convergent integral formulas for the canonical factorial
justify this growing-order bound. Keeping the factorial bound
graded by the degree of the integration variable prevents a second
factorial during exponentiation and Barnes integration. Choosing
\(p\) proportional to \(N\) then gives exponential accuracy.
The original vertical current, right connector and infinite ends
retain their separate bounds throughout. Finally the exact
first-order equation propagates the initializer along each real
fractional orbit by direct summation.

### A fixed complex neighborhood

There is a further consequence useful for contour gluing. Define the
open real region
\[
 \mathcal U=\{(c,h,k):c,h,k>0,\ c+h+k<1,
                   L(c+h+k)-L(h+k)>0\}.
\]
For every compact \(K\subset\mathcal U\), there is a fixed open
complex neighborhood \(V\) of \(K\) and a number \(a>0\) such
that
\[
 \Phi_N/\Gamma_N=1+O(e^{-aN})\quad\hbox{on }V.
\]
Both \(V\) and \(a\) are independent of \(N\). Here is an
elementary proof of this consequence; it does not assume that a
real asymptotic automatically holds on a complex contour.

Work first near one real product box with closure in \(\mathcal U\).
The original \(\Phi_N\) is a polynomial of degree at most
\(d=N-1\) separately in
\(C=e^{-2\pi ic},H=e^{-2\pi ih},K_0=e^{-2\pi ik}\).
Its real-box bound is at most \(e^{b_0N}\), after enlarging
\(b_0\). In each angular coordinate choose \(d+1\) equally
spaced points on a fixed interval of length \(s<1/2\) inside
the box. If their activities are \(C_j\), then
\[
 \prod_{i\ne j}|C_j-C_i|
 \ge(4s/d)^d j!(d-j)!\ge(2s/e)^d.
\]
The first inequality uses
\(|e^{2\pi ix}-e^{2\pi iy}|\ge4|x-y|\) when
\(|x-y|\le1/2\); the second uses
\(j!(d-j)!\ge d!/2^d\) and \(d!\ge(d/e)^d\).
On \(|C|\le B\), each Lagrange numerator is at most
\((1+B)^d\). Interpolation in all three variables therefore
gives \(|\Phi_N|\le N^3e^{b_1N}\) on any fixed bounded
activity polydisk. No estimate of unknown boundary packets is
being supplied as input.

Choose a small fixed complex angle box on which every single and
pair real part stays strictly between zero and one. The canonical
factorial strips make \(\Gamma_N\) holomorphic and nonzero
there for large \(N\). Its uniform strip expansion bounds its
reciprocal by \(N^Ce^{b_2N}\). Thus
\(E_N=\Phi_N/\Gamma_N-1\) is holomorphic with rough bound
\(e^{bN}\) on this complex box. Its real restriction has bound
\(e^{-a_0N}\), after absorbing the polynomial factor in the
real theorem and decreasing \(a_0>0\).

For one centered coordinate \(z=x+iy\), use the rectangle
\(|x|<R_0,0<y<R_0\) and the harmonic polynomial
\[
 W(x,y)=2y/R_0+(x^2-y^2)/R_0^2.
\]
It is nonnegative on the bottom and at least one on the other
three sides. Apply the maximum-modulus principle to
\[
 E_N(z)\exp\{a_0N-(a_0+b)N
                    (z^2/R_0^2-2iz/R_0)\}.
\]
Its boundary modulus is at most one. Consequently
\(\log|E_N|\le-a_0N+(a_0+b)NW\). On a smaller fixed
square \(|x|,y\le r_0\), choose
\(2r_0/R_0+(r_0/R_0)^2\le a_0/[2(a_0+b)]\).
The bound there is \(e^{-a_0N/2}\). The lower rectangle uses
\(z^2/R_0^2+2iz/R_0\) and gives the same result. Apply this
argument successively in the three coordinates, with the other
coordinates held as parameters. The exponent decreases by at most
a factor of eight, while all three resulting radii remain fixed.
A finite covering proves the claim for compact \(K\).

Cauchy's formula on a smaller neighborhood also gives
\(\partial^\alpha(\Phi_N/\Gamma_N-1)=O_\alpha(e^{-aN})\)
for every fixed multi-index \(\alpha\), with a possibly smaller
\(a>0\). This does not bound derivative orders growing with
\(N\). Nor is a fixed complex neighborhood asserted at the
real endpoints \(h=0\) or \(k=0\), where the factorial-strip
margin shrinks with \(N\).

This supplies a local kernel with an exponentially controlled
holomorphic remainder. It retains the original scalar and the full
cyclic factors of the Gamma section. General attachment through an
arbitrary fixed short component still needs control of the prescribed
gluing pairing and the competing regions of the whole source.
The finite-exception theorem remains unproved.

## The crossing transport reduces to a first-order sourced equation, 22 November

The [exact Gamma-source proof](research_crossing_exact_gamma_source_extension.md)
gives a simpler transport argument for the original crossing scalar.
Its homogeneous comparison is an exact solution, and the difference
from the physical source has explicit forcing. This replaces the
second-order tracking problem by a sum once a fractional-orbit
normalization has been fixed.

Put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(\eta=(-1)^{N-1}\), and
\[
 C=e^{-2\pi ic},\quad H=e^{-2\pi ih},\quad K=e^{-2\pi ik},
 \qquad \Phi=\phi(f_0U_{-C}U_{-H}U_{-K}).
\]
The basis, multiplication and closing are the original ones. The
shift \(\sigma\) sends \((H,K)\) to \((H/Q,QK)\), or
\((h,k)\) to \((h+1/N,k-1/N)\). Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 P_1&=(1-H/q)^2(1-QCK),\\
 P_2&=(1-qK)^2(1-CH),\\
 J&=\frac{\eta}{N}
        [2+H^N+K^N+C^N(1-(HK)^N)].
 \end{split}
\]
The exact original polynomial satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\qquad P_1\,\sigma\Phi-P_2\Phi=J(H-QK).\qquad}
\]
This cleared equation includes the coefficient-zero and fold loci.
Its proof uses the original source's extreme coefficient and its
socle evaluation to determine every term of \(J\).

The explicit canonical Gamma product \(G_N\) in the proof satisfies
\(\sigma G_N=(P_2/P_1)G_N\) exactly. For
\(E_N=\Phi/G_N-1\), the remaining equation is therefore
\[
 \sigma E_N-E_N
          =\frac{J(H-QK)}{P_1\,\sigma G_N}.
\]
All phase and cyclic factors remain. In particular,
\[
 \prod_{j=0}^{N-1}\sigma^j(P_2/P_1)
  =\frac{(1+K^N)^2[1-(CH)^N]}
         {(1+H^N)^2[1-(CK)^N]}
\]
need not be one. The Gamma solution on its angle cover and the
periodic physical polynomial are distinct sections.

There is a uniform real estimate behind direct summation. Fix a
compact set \(c,R>0,c+R<1\), put \(k=R-h\), and let
\(0\le h\le R\). With \(L(x)=\int_0^x\log|2\sin\pi t|\,dt\),
define
\[
 \begin{split}
 M_0&=L(c+R)-L(c)-L(R)>0,\\
 \mathcal A_0&=L(c+h)+L(c+k)+L(h+k)
                              -2[L(c)+L(h)+L(k)].
 \end{split}
\]
Exact factorial shifts and reflection give
\(\log|G_N|=N\mathcal A_0+O(\log N)\), uniformly even at
the two endpoints. Concavity in \(h\), together with equal
endpoint values, gives \(\mathcal A_0\ge M_0\). The forcing
and its denominator cost only a power of \(N\). Consequently
\[
 |E_N(h_2)-E_N(h_1)|
       \le N^C e^{-NM_0},\qquad
 h_1,h_2\in[0,R],\quad N(h_2-h_1)\in\mathbb Z.
\]
The constant \(C\) is uniform on the fixed compact parameter
set. No division by a fold distance occurs.

On the anchored grid \(h=(j+1/2)/N\), the retained initializer
current also fixes the normalization. Under the additional compact
gap hypothesis \(L(c+R)-L(R)>0\), it yields
\[
                    \Phi/G_N=1+O(N^C e^{-NM_0})
\]
throughout that grid. For other fractional orbits the displayed
variation estimate alone leaves an undetermined constant. Controlling
that constant is the remaining local initializer problem.

These two solution/source coordinates do not replace the original
\(N\)-dimensional boundary packet. General attachment with the actual
closing, competing regions, and the volume of the knot complement
still require proof. No new knot class or finite-exception theorem
is asserted here.

## Keeping the error degrees separately, 22 November

The fixed degree also simplifies the positive recursion before the
closing is taken. This is a consequence of the existing
[orthogonal-error proof](research_orthogonal_error_positive_conway_recursion.md),
rather than a new volume estimate. It avoids storing all the cross
blocks in the finite Fourier construction below.

For a subtree rooted at \(v\), let \(l_v\) be its number of leaf
occurrences and write its full second moment as
\[
 S_v(\varepsilon)=\sum_{j=0}^{l_v}\varepsilon^j C_{v,j}.
\]
The index \(j\) counts error vertices, not physical colors. Every
\(C_{v,j}\) is a positive semidefinite matrix on the complete
\(N\)-dimensional boundary space. Use the same normalized leaf
vectors \(a_v\), unary maps \(A_v\), binary maps \(M_v\), budget
product \(B_N\), and original closing row \(L\) as in that proof.
The coefficient recursion is
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 C_{v,0}=a_va_v^*,\quad C_{v,1}=I,
     &v\text{ a leaf},\\[1mm]
 C_{v,j}=A_v C_{c,j}A_v^*+\delta_{j1}I,
     &v\text{ unary},\\[1mm]
 C_{v,j}=\displaystyle\sum_{p+q=j}
       M_v(C_{l,p}\otimes C_{r,q})M_v^*+\delta_{j1}I,
     &v\text{ binary}.
\end{array}
\]
An absent coefficient is zero. Here \(\delta_{j1}\) is one
when \(j=1\) and zero otherwise. Omitting the fresh internal
errors simply omits the last term at internal vertices. The
formulas follow by multiplying the finite matrix polynomials;
each summand is positive semidefinite. Unary corridors do not
increase the degree, and the degrees add at a branching vertex.

This stores \(l_v+1\) matrices of size \(N\), instead of a
matrix with all pairs of phase indices. To see the exact relation,
use the common-noise phase copies with
\(m=l+1\), \(\omega=e^{2\pi i/m}\), where \(l\) is the total
number of leaves. Their second-moment cross block at \(v\) is
\[
 \mathcal S_{v,ab}
   =\sum_{j=0}^{l_v}\varepsilon^j
                       \omega^{j(a-b)}C_{v,j}.
\]
The unitary Fourier transform in the phase index makes these
blocks diagonal, with diagonal blocks
\(m\varepsilon^j C_{v,j}\) and zero blocks for \(j>l_v\).
There is no wraparound because every subtree degree is less
than \(m\). All physical coordinates, including the derivative
coordinates at repeated roots, remain inside each block.

At the original closing,
\[
 c_{N,j}=B_N^2LC_{\mathrm{top},j}L^*,\qquad
 c_{N,0}=|K_N|^2.
\]
Keeping only degree zero throughout gives the original rank-one
contraction exactly. It also removes the positive error floor:
it cannot inherit conditioning or lower bounds supplied by the
discarded error blocks. Likewise, averaging
\(|Z(\theta\omega^a)|^2\) retains every error variance;
extracting the original scalar requires the correlated phase
projection already described below. Thus the simplification is
an exact local way to organize the same source, with no auxiliary
minimization. The geometric lower estimate is still needed.
