## An original crossing source has a nonzero regulator asymptotic, 22 November

The [crossing-source theorem](research_crossing_source_continuous_transport.md)
now treats an actual signed-crossing insertion with its original
closing. It gives a nonzero leading coefficient and a marked
regulator limit. This is a universal local source theorem; it does
not prove the volume identity after arbitrary short fillings.

Put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(d=N-1\),
\(\kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)}\), and
\(U_x=\sum_{j=0}^d x^j f_j\) in the complete centered basis.
Since the original positive crossing is \(R^+=\sqrt N f_0\),
the scalar is
\[
 \Phi_N^+(c,h,k)=
   \phi(f_0U_{-e^{-2\pi ic}}U_{-e^{-2\pi ih}}U_{-e^{-2\pi ik}}).
\]
Here \(\phi\) is the original Frobenius closing; all internal
value and first-derivative directions remain.

Let \(L(x)=\int_0^x\log|2\sin\pi v|\,dv\), with its odd
one-periodic extension. Work on compact subsets of
\[
 c,h,k>0,\qquad T=c+h+k<1,\qquad
                         L(T)-L(h+k)>0.
\]
Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal A&=L(c+h)+L(c+k)+L(h+k)-2[L(c)+L(h)+L(k)],\\
 \mathcal S&=\mathcal A-\pi i(ch+ck+hk),\\
 \mathcal B&=
 \frac{e^{\pi iT}}
      {2\sqrt{2\sin\pi(c+h)\sin\pi(c+k)\sin\pi(h+k)}}.
 \end{split}
\]
The square root is positive real. The actual finite scalar satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \Phi_N^+=\kappa^2 N^{-1/2}\mathcal B\,e^{N\mathcal S}
                                      (1+O(N^{-1})).
 \qquad}
\]
The leading coefficient is nonzero, with its explicit phase.
The result includes the central fold \(h=k\), both parities,
and composite levels.

For fixed \(R=h+k\), the logarithmic estimate
\(\log|\Phi_N^+|=N\mathcal A+O(\log N)\) and nonvanishing
are also uniform for every real \(0<h<R\), on compact
\((c,R)\)-sets with \(c,R>0,c+R<1\) and
\(L(c+R)-L(R)>0\). This includes level-dependent approaches
to the endpoints. The relative formula above has a narrower
compact-positive-angle scope; the endpoint layers retain their
separate Gamma factors.

The proof uses the
[fractional crossing initializer](research_four_coherent_zero_radius_boundary_source.md),
which evaluates the complete original moving-pole packet with
its current and right connector retained. The condition
\(L(c+R)>L(R)\) supplies a genuine upper-end gap there.
The source recurrence is complex. After rescaling its first
difference, the ratio of the original scalar to that difference
tracks an explicit comparison function with positive real part.
A reflection identity cancels the leading fold defect, leaving
an error \(O(N^{-1}\delta)\), where \(\delta=k-h\) on the
first half-interval. Its contraction then gives uniform \(O(N^{-1})\)
tracking by induction. No singular terminal equation is used.
This controls the scalar itself, including its possible cancellation.

The remaining correction product has an exact logarithmic primitive.
The four explicit sine products and the boundary Gamma factors
then cancel every fractional-offset phase and power, yielding
the closed coefficient \(\mathcal B\). Thus the displayed
marked action is selected by the actual finite period; it is
not chosen solely from an exponentiated classical equation.
The framing \(\kappa^2\) is retained.

The [marked-regulator proof](research_one_crossing_marked_bloch_regulator.md)
derives that classical equation directly from the same finite
source. With \(C=e^{-2\pi ic}\), \(H=e^{-2\pi ih}\), and
\(r=e^{-2\pi i(h+k)}\), its local boundary polynomial is
\[
 A_\times=(\ell-1)
 \left[H(1-H)^2(H-Cr)\ell-(H-r)^2(1-CH)\right].
\]
Here \(\ell\) is the multiplier for the forward boundary shift
\(h\mapsto h+1/N,\ k\mapsto k-1/N\).
Both components are retained. This is a local source polynomial,
not the peripheral A-polynomial of a knot.

Its nonconstant critical point gives a reduced Bloch class
\[
 \beta_\times=[CH]+[CK]+[HK]-2[C]-2[H]-2[K],
       \qquad K=e^{-2\pi ik}.
\]
Exact five-term substitutions identify it with
\(\sum_{\{a,b\}}([z_{ab}]-[\overline{z_{ab}}])\), where
\[
 z_{ab}=\frac{1-e^{-2\pi ib}}{1-e^{-2\pi i(a+b)}},
                    \qquad \{a,b\}\subset\{c,h,k\}.
\]
Pair sums here count the three labelled pairs \((c,h),(c,k),(h,k)\),
also when two numerical angles coincide.
These are positive ideal-tetrahedron shapes, with angles
\(\pi(a,b,1-a-b)\). For the Bloch--Wigner regulator \(D\),
the actual-source limit is therefore
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}
        \log\left|\frac{\Phi_N^+}{N^{3/2}}\right|
       =D(\beta_\times)
       =2\sum_{\{a,b\}}\operatorname{Vol}(\infty,0,1,z_{ab}).
\]
The factor of two records conjugate antisymmetry. The positive
tetrahedral chain has not been identified with a convex union
or with the complement of an arbitrary filled knot.

The negative crossing is \(R^-=\sqrt N f_d\). Its scalar
\(\Phi_N^-=\phi(f_dU_{-e^{-2\pi ic}}U_{-e^{-2\pi ih}}U_{-e^{-2\pi ik}})\)
follows from an exact full-algebra reflection. If
\(p=-e^{-2\pi iT}\), then
\(\Phi_N^-=p^d\overline{\Phi_N^+}\); its carrier is retained
and its modulus has the same rate. Symmetry also patches the
relative formula over the three permuted gap regions. Their
union contains every positive triple with \(1/4<T<5/6\).

The remaining step is a general attachment theorem with the
original closing: the known local kernels must be assembled
through arbitrary fixed short components while controlling the
full scalar and competing regions. Multiplying local amplitudes
or taking a positive norm does not establish that statement.
No new filled-knot class or finite-exception theorem is claimed.

## The four-input geometric estimate no longer requires a grid, 22 November

The [continuous-angle theorem](research_four_coherent_continuous_angle_transport.md)
removes both the sampling restriction and the fixed fold margin
in the earlier source estimates below. It concerns the original
four-input scalar, with its original phase and closing. It does
not enlarge the proved class of filled knots.

Fix a compact set of triples satisfying
\[
 b,c>0,\qquad S=b+c<1,\qquad
                    1-S<R<1-\max(b,c).
\]
For every real \(0<h<R\), let
\[
 y=-e^{-2\pi ib},\quad z=-e^{-2\pi ic},\quad
 s=-e^{-2\pi ih},\quad t=-e^{-2\pi i(R-h)}.
\]
Use \(U_a=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}a^jf_j\) in the full centered basis
and \(\Phi_N=\phi(U_yU_zU_sU_t)\), where \(\phi\) is the
original Frobenius closing. For all sufficiently large \(N\),
uniformly in these three shape parameters and in every such \(h\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \Phi_N=e^{-\pi i(N-1)(S+R)}P_N,\qquad P_N>0,\qquad
 \log P_N=N\mathcal F(b,c,R,h)+O(\log N).
 \quad}
\]
Here \(\mathcal F\) is explicitly defined by the two-prism
maximum in the theorem, and
\(\pi\mathcal F=\operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal Q)\) for its
actual convex ideal cube. The original normalized closing is
\(\Phi_N/N^2\). Both parities and composite levels are included.
The bound is uniform even for level-dependent approaches to
either endpoint or the central fold.

The new analytic input is the
[fractional boundary theorem](research_four_coherent_fractional_boundary_source.md).
Put \(u=1-R\) and
\[
 g=\frac{\sin^2\pi u\,\sin\pi b\,\sin\pi c}
          {\pi^2\sin\pi(u-b)\sin\pi(u-c)}>0.
\]
Let \(V_a\) denote the same source at
\(s_a=-e^{-2\pi i(a-1/2)/N}\),
\(t_a=e^{-2\pi iR}/s_a\). For \(a\) in any fixed compact
subset of \((0,\infty)\),
\[
 \frac{V_a}{V_1}
     =\frac{N^{2a-2}g^{a-1}}{\Gamma(a)^2}
                                     (1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
This is a relative estimate for the actual original scalar,
including its phase. Its proof retains the entire moving pole
family of the source interpolation. A second finite Barnes
rectangle evaluates that packet. Both infinite tails have
explicit integrable bounds; the retained right connector has a
strictly smaller exponential rate. No unsigned envelope replaces
the packet, and integer parameters are handled by canceled
identities before division.

For each offset, choose two adjacent parameters
\(a_0\in[3/2,5/2)\) and \(a_0-1\in[1/2,3/2)\).
After removal of the common original phase, these give positive
values with predecessor-to-current ratio
\[
                     \frac{(a_0-1)^2}{N^2g}(1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
Their first difference is therefore positive. The same rescaled
flux used at the fold now propagates that offset to its target,
with logarithmic error \(O(\log N)\). Angles at most \(2/N\)
are covered directly by the fractional boundary estimate;
interchanging the last two inputs covers the second half of the
interval. This is why a result for every offset, rather than one
initial value on each offset, was needed.

The chamber restriction \(R<1-\max(b,c)\) remains essential
to this proof. Other initial prism faces, derivatives normal to
the folded boundary coordinate, and arbitrary short-component
attachments have not been covered. The result is a universal
four-boundary source estimate, not the missing theorem for every
fixed short partial filling. The finite-exception theorem remains
open.

## A finite Fourier projection removes the auxiliary minimization, 22 November

The fixed-degree scalar Gram has a simpler exact form. In the
[positive recursion](research_orthogonal_error_positive_conway_recursion.md),
let \(l\) be the number of leaf occurrences, put \(m=l+1\), and set
\(\omega=e^{2\pi i/m}\), \(\theta=\sqrt\varepsilon\).
Here \(\varepsilon>0\) is the auxiliary error variance. Use the
independent centered error vectors \(\xi_v\) of that proof, now with
covariance \(I_N\). Errors at different tree vertices remain
independent; every phase copy below uses the same \(\xi_v\) at a
given vertex.

Write \(Z(\theta)=B_N L X_{\rm top}(\theta)\) for the original
closed noisy scalar. The local maps, their budget product \(B_N\),
and the closing row \(L\) are those of the positive recursion.
The antichain expansion makes \(Z\) a polynomial in \(\theta\)
of degree at most \(l\), with constant term \(K_N\). Thus,
pointwise in every auxiliary error variable,
\[
 Z_a=Z(\theta\omega^a),\qquad
                  \frac1m\sum_{a=0}^{m-1}Z_a=K_N.
\]
The auxiliary root \(\omega\) is unrelated to the physical root
\(Q\) or to a physical color. This finite average removes every
nonconstant error term before taking an absolute value.

Let \(F_N(\varepsilon)=\sum_{j=0}^l c_{N,j}\varepsilon^j\)
be the polynomial in the positive recursion, where
\(c_{N,0}=|K_N|^2\) and all coefficients are nonnegative.
Orthogonality of distinct error antichains gives the positive
circulant Gram
\[
 G_{ab}=\mathbb E[Z_a\overline{Z_b}]
       =\sum_{j=0}^l c_{N,j}\varepsilon^j\omega^{j(a-b)}.
\]
For the unitary Fourier matrix \(\mathsf U_{aj}=m^{-1/2}\omega^{aj}\),
\[
 G=\mathsf U\,\operatorname{diag}
                 (m c_{N,j}\varepsilon^j)_{j=0}^l\,\mathsf U^*,
 \qquad
             |K_N|^2=\frac1{m^2}\mathbf1^*G\mathbf1.
\]
A known Fourier coordinate therefore replaces the constrained
quadratic minimum, derivatives, and Vandermonde coordinates in
the earlier extraction. Averaging the separate energies
\(|Z_a|^2\) would give \(F_N(\varepsilon)\); the correlations
between phase copies are essential.

This Gram also has an exact positive local construction. Stack
the \(m\) phase packets at each vertex. A leaf has mean
\(\mathcal a_v=(a_v,\ldots,a_v)\) and fresh noise
\(\theta(\omega^a\xi_v)_{a=0}^{m-1}\). A unary map is
\(\mathcal A_v=I_m\otimes A_v\). On the standard phase basis
\(e_0,\ldots,e_{m-1}\), define the lifted binary map by
\[
 \mathcal M_v((e_a\otimes u)\otimes(e_b\otimes w))
       =\delta_{ab}\,e_a\otimes M_v(u,w).
\]
Put \(\upsilon_a=\omega^a\) and
\(\mathcal E=\varepsilon\,\upsilon\upsilon^*\otimes I_N\).
Independence of the child subtrees and of the fresh error gives
the full second moments
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
 \mathcal S_v=\mathcal a_v\mathcal a_v^*+\mathcal E,
                                      &v\text{ a leaf},\\
 \mathcal S_v=\mathcal A_v\mathcal S_c\mathcal A_v^*+\mathcal E,
                                      &v\text{ unary},\\
 \mathcal S_v=\mathcal M_v(\mathcal S_l\otimes\mathcal S_r)
                    \mathcal M_v^*+\mathcal E,
                                      &v\text{ binary}.
 \end{array}
\]
At the unchanged closing,
\[
 G=B_N^2(I_m\otimes L)\mathcal S_{\rm top}(I_m\otimes L)^*.
\]
The block size is \(mN\). Individual cross blocks need not be
positive; the complete block matrix is positive. Independent
errors in different phase copies would change this construction
and destroy the exact filter.

The simplification concerns scalar extraction. It gives no
geometric lower bound on its own. The constant Fourier eigenvalue
can vanish or be exponentially smaller than the other eigenvalues.
Since the total degree is below \(m\), nonzero error degrees
cannot wrap into degree zero during assembly. The selected mode
remains precisely the original source with its original closing.
Its full boundary dimension and contraction precision still have
to be controlled. In particular, positivity of \(G\) does not
prove noncancellation of \(K_N\).

The complete direct proof source is the 407-line positive recursion
at SHA-256
5506f489642f2ec118c4fef25cccc0485fecdc32ffccf09c700ac923c9da98dd.
The finite phase filter and lifted construction are proved above.
Only written mathematics and text operations were used.

## The anchored source estimate reaches the central fold, 22 November

The [fold-value extension](research_four_coherent_fold_value_transport.md)
removes the fixed distance from the fold required in the previous
anchored-grid theorem. Keep
\[
 b,c>0,\quad S=b+c<1,\qquad 1-S<R<1-\max(b,c),
\]
and its original four-input scalar
\(\Phi_J=\phi(U_yU_zU_{s_J}U_{t_J})\). Uniformly on compact
sets of these three shape parameters, for all sufficiently large
\(N\), the conclusion now holds for every integer \(J\ge0\) with
\(h_J=(J+\tfrac12)/N\le R/2\):
\[
 \Phi_J=e^{-\pi i(N-1)(S+R)}P_{N,J},\qquad P_{N,J}>0,
 \qquad
 \log P_{N,J}=N\mathcal F(b,c,R,h_J)+O(\log N).
\]
The action \(\mathcal F\) is the ideal-cube action defined in
the anchored-grid entry below. Its geometric value is
\(\pi\mathcal F=\operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal Q)\).
The bound is uniform when the sampled angle tends to zero or to
\(R/2\), and includes an exact central grid value whenever it
occurs. Both parities and composite levels remain included.

The proof rescales the first difference rather than bounding it
uniformly away from the fold. After removing the same source
phase, put \(H_j=e^{\pi i(N-1)(S+R)}\Phi_j\),
\(\Delta_j=H_j-H_{j-1}\), and
\[
 \alpha_j=\sin\pi(R-2j/N),\qquad E_j=\Delta_j/\alpha_j.
\]
The exact recurrence becomes
\[
 E_{j+1}=q_jE_j
       \left(1+\beta_j\frac{H_j}{E_j}\right),\qquad
 q_j-1\ge c(R-2h_j),\quad
 0<\beta_j\le\frac C N(R-2h_j).
\]
Every row actually used has \(j<J\), hence
\(R-2h_j\ge2/N\). No singular terminal row is used.
Telescoping the positive increments of \(E_j\) gives
\(c/N\le H_j/E_j\le C\), including the target point.
The total logarithmic correction in the displayed recurrence
is bounded. Thus \(\log H_J\) differs by \(O(\log N)\)
from the logarithm of its initial value plus \(\sum_{j<J}\log q_j\).
This product has no divided fold factor. Its log-sine integral
is the same geometric action, continuous at the central fold.

This proves an actual value estimate. Derivatives normal to the
folded coordinate, arbitrary fractional grid offsets, other
initial prism faces and arbitrary attached tangles are outside
this extension. It does not prove the finite-exception theorem.

Its complete direct sources are the anchored-grid proof at
d79b3f5bb0f2cb325214015cf9b4b15ca4ac8892ff5d1d42df794b89f7d2771d
and the actual prism/cube theorem at
c29321805df39a49854665df1255db1ec7180397a5dd689f19289d61335871c9.
Only written mathematics and text operations were used.

## Positive transport proves a four-input geometric rate, 22 November

The [anchored-grid transport theorem](research_four_coherent_anchored_grid_volume.md)
now proves noncancellation and the geometric rate for an original
four-input scalar. This goes beyond the polynomial equation: the
actual closing has a positive coefficient after its explicit
source phase is removed.

Write \(S=b+c\), and assume
\[
 b,c>0,\qquad S<1,\qquad
            1-S<R<1-\max(b,c),\qquad 0<h<R/2.
\]
Take
\[
 y=-e^{-2\pi ib},\quad z=-e^{-2\pi ic},\quad r=e^{-2\pi iR},
 \qquad h_j=(j+\tfrac12)/N,
\]
\[
 s_j=-q^{-1}Q^{-j},\qquad t_j=-qrQ^j,\qquad
                       q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2.
\]
Thus the two remaining angles are \(h_j,R-h_j\), and their product
is fixed. In the original centered basis put
\(U_a=\sum_{\ell=0}^{N-1}a^\ell f_\ell\), and let
\(\Phi_{N,j}=\phi(U_yU_zU_{s_j}U_{t_j})\), with the original
full boundary algebra, phases and Frobenius closing. Uniformly
on compact subsets of the displayed domain, for sufficiently
large \(N\) and targets \(h_j\) in the compact set,
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \Phi_{N,j}=e^{-\pi i(N-1)(S+R)}P_{N,j},\qquad
 P_{N,j}>0,\qquad
 \log P_{N,j}
   =\frac N\pi\,\operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal Q_{b,c,h_j,R-h_j})
                                      +O(\log N).
 \quad}
\]
Here \(\mathcal Q\) is the actual convex ideal cube of the
positive Newton composition theorem. The normalized original
closing of the two turned products is \(\Phi_{N,j}/N^2\), with
the same rate. Both level parities and composite levels are included.

The proof starts at two exact source values. The entry \(j=-1\)
is an elementary finite product of size \(O(N^{-1})\).
The entry \(j=0\) is \(\kappa\sqrt N\) times the original
three-input scalar in a compact strict prism family. Its known
asymptotic supplies a growing initial value with its correct phase.
After division by the common phase, call these real values \(H_j\)
and put \(\Delta_j=H_j-H_{j-1}\). The exact boundary equation gives
\[
 \Delta_{j+1}=\rho_j\Delta_j+
                   \frac{\Lambda_N}{\mathsf d_j}H_j,\qquad
 \rho_j=\mathsf b_j/\mathsf d_j>1+c.
\]
The coefficients are positive along this path. Although
\(\mathsf d_0\) is of order \(N^{-2}\), the useful quantity is
\(\Lambda_N/\mathsf b_j=O(N^{-1})\). Geometric summation bounds
\(H_j/\Delta_j\) above and below by fixed positive constants.
Consequently
\[
 c\prod_{m<j}\rho_m\ \le\ \frac{\Phi_{N,j}}{\Phi_{N,0}}
                   \le C\prod_{m<j}\rho_m .
\]
The ratio in this display is real and positive. This is a bound
on the original scalar, rather than on a separately squared norm.

Finally the finite product has a log-sine Riemann approximation
with error \(O(\log N)\). Its rate derivative is the envelope
derivative of the ideal-cube volume action. A cotangent
factorization of the stationary equation proves that equality.
At \(h=0\), the action reduces to the same prism action as the
three-input initial value, fixing the additive constant. Thus
the positive transport selects the actual geometric contribution.

The sampling and geometric restrictions are essential to the
proved statement. Only \(s_j\) is required to be on this anchored
half-grid; the other three inputs can be generic unit parameters.
The proof stops a fixed distance before \(h=R/2\), and its
initial value requires \(R<1-\max(b,c)\). Arbitrary fractional
grid offsets, a start on another prism face, the fold derivatives,
and subsequent arbitrary tangle attachments remain outside this
theorem. In particular it does not establish the finite-exception
knot theorem or a new knot-volume class.

## The original four-input scalar has a selected polynomial boundary equation, 22 November

The [four-input source theorem](research_four_coherent_boundary_polynomial_source.md)
gives an exact equation for the original closing of two coherent
products. The calculation uses their complete Newton coefficients,
then proves a finite polynomial operator identity. It introduces
neither a cyclic extension of the summand nor a replacement closing.

Write \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and
\(U_a=\sum_{j=0}^d a^jf_j\) in the full centered basis. The scalar is
\[
 \Phi_N(y,z;s,t)=\phi(U_yU_zU_sU_t).
\]
All internal repeated-root derivative coordinates are included.
The exact Frobenius identity also gives
\(\phi(J(U_yU_z)J(U_sU_t))=\Phi_N\), with the original genuine
turns. Dividing by the four known input norms gives the normalized
two-product closing.

For \(\sigma(s,t)=(Qs,Q^{-1}t)\), set
\[
 B=\frac{(t+q)^2(1-Qys)(1-Qzs)}{(t-s)(t-Qs)},\qquad
 D=\frac{(s+q)^2(1-Qyt)(1-Qzt)}{(Qt-s)(t-s)}.
\]
Then the actual scalar satisfies
\[
 B(\sigma\Phi_N-\Phi_N)
   +D(\sigma^{-1}\Phi_N-\Phi_N)
                =(Q-1)(1-Qyz)\Phi_N.
\]
Multiplying by \((t-s)(t-Qs)(Qt-s)\) gives a polynomial identity
in all four parameters. The whole identity and its derivatives
remain valid at its folds; an equation involving values alone
does not replace that family.

Here is the source normalization. At fixed \(r=st\ne0\), the
scalar is a polynomial of degree at most \(d\) in
\(\mu=-q(s+t)/r\). Its highest coefficient is explicitly
\[
 [\mu^d]\Phi_N
   =\frac{\kappa^2r^d}{N}\sum_{a=0}^d(yz)^a,\qquad
                      \kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)}.
\]
This follows directly from \(f_df_0=1/N\) and the original
bilinear orthogonality, by taking the extreme \(s^d\) coefficient.
The boundary operator is triangular on this polynomial space,
with diagonal entries
\[
                \lambda_k=(Q^{-k}-1)(1-Q^{k+2}yz),
                           \qquad 0\le k\le d.
\]
Unless \(yz\) is a nontrivial \(N\)-th root of unity, the
equation and highest coefficient select a unique polynomial.
At \(yz=Q^{-h}\), \(1\le h\le d\), the actual source instead
has degree at most \(h-1\). Its original parameter family
retains the source and its normals there. Dividing by the vanished
highest coefficient would lose those data.

Two readouts fix the same source directly. Put
\(F_N(a)=\sum_{j=0}^d(-qa)^j\), and write
\(\mathcal C_N(y,z,t)=\phi(U_yU_zU_t)\). Then
\[
 \Phi_N(y,z;-q,t)=\frac{\kappa^2}{N}F_N(y)F_N(z)F_N(t),
 \qquad
 \Phi_N(y,z;-q^{-1},t)=\kappa\sqrt N\,\mathcal C_N(y,z,t).
\]
The first input is a known multiple of the Newton socle \(e_d\);
the second is a known multiple of the unit. These are exact
original boundary values, including their phases.

The finite sum has the standard terminating \(q\)-Racah parameter
pattern; the general definition and difference equation are
recorded in [Koekoek--Swarttouw, section 3.2](https://tudelft.roelofkoekoek.nl/documents/as98.pdf).
The source-specific statement is the equation with its actual
normalization and complete resonant family. Its finite operator
proof is written out in the note. It is an auxiliary boundary
operator, not an identification of a knot's peripheral
\(A\)-polynomial. No new geometric lower bound or knot-volume
class follows from the polynomial equation alone.

The complete 409-line proof is at SHA-256
`93241074830ff4b844ba5baafd06a15bf08ec6bddc3a1498727f110ebe297d84`.
Its two complete direct proof sources are the coherent-product theorem
at `73152328a77ba5d63a2a8eaa17647ed38b7683c613e0947e3bda9e451dda76e2`
and the centered compiler at
`0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413`.

## The full boundary cycle has a nontrivial balance factor, 22 November

For \(N\ge3\), the same equation cannot be treated as an ordinary diagonally
reversible cyclic Jacobi problem on generic source parameters.
This can be checked by an exact product, retaining all color
factors. Work on the open set where every displayed coefficient
and denominator is nonzero. Let
\[
 s_j=Q^js,\quad t_j=Q^{-j}t,\quad
 Y=y^N,\ Z=z^N,\ S=s^N,\ T=t^N,\quad
 \eta=(-1)^{N-1}.
\]
Write \(B_j=B(y,z;s_j,t_j)\), \(D_j=D(y,z;s_j,t_j)\), and
\(D_N(a)=1-\eta a^N\). Direct multiplication gives
\[
 \prod_{j=0}^{N-1}B_j
 =\frac{D_N(t)^2(1-YS)(1-ZS)}{(T-S)^2},\qquad
 \prod_{j=0}^{N-1}D_j
 =\frac{D_N(s)^2(1-YT)(1-ZT)}{(T-S)^2}.
\]
Indeed \(\prod_j(q+t_j)=-D_N(t)\) and
\(\prod_j(1-Qys_j)=1-(ys)^N\). For the denominator, the even
and odd powers in
\[
 \prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(t-sQ^{2j})(t-sQ^{2j+1})
\]
give \((t^N-s^N)^2\), at both parities. The remaining phase is
\(Q^{-N(N-1)}=1\); no parity sign is omitted.
The two denominator products are also equal directly by
\(Qt_j-s_j=t_{j-1}-Qs_{j-1}\).

A nonzero diagonal balance of the two directed channels would require
\(w_jB_j=w_{j+1}D_{j+1}\). Multiplication around the original
periodic cycle would force
\[
 1=\mathfrak h_N
   :=\frac{D_N(t)^2[1-(ys)^N][1-(zs)^N]}
           {D_N(s)^2[1-(yt)^N][1-(zt)^N]}.
\]
This rational function is not identically one. For example, at
\(y=z=0\) it is \(D_N(t)^2/D_N(s)^2\). Therefore it also cannot
be identically one on an open unit-angle chamber: apply the
one-variable polynomial identity theorem successively in the four
parameters. The failure is generic, rather than an issue at just one fold.
For \(y=-e^{-2\pi ib}\), \(z=-e^{-2\pi ic}\),
\(s=-e^{-2\pi ih}\), \(t=-e^{-2\pi ik}\), expressing each
factor as a sine shows that \(B/g,D/g\) are real, where
\(g=-4e^{\pi i(2/N-b-c)}\). For \(N\ge3\), the two neighboring
coordinates are distinct, so the same balance condition is necessary
for a diagonal Hermitian metric for \(L/g\). At \(N=2\), the
forward and backward shifts coincide; matrix selfadjointness tests
their sum instead. The product formula remains valid there, but
the stated metric obstruction is restricted to \(N\ge3\).
Allowing indefinite diagonal weights does not remove it.

This external balance factor is different from the monodromy
obtained by formally continuing the internal finite-sum index.
Neither is silently set to one. At a zero of one of its factors,
the divided product formula is not a substitute for the original
polynomial source and its derivatives.

This audit rules out that diagonal-cycle shortcut. It does not
rule out a nonlocal positive Gram at generic real simple spectrum,
and it gives no scalar volume counterexample. Such a Gram would
still need quantitative control of its conditioning and of the
original closing. Root-of-unity Askey--Wilson orthogonality is
established subject matter; see
[Spiridonov--Zhedanov](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9605034).
No positivity theorem or proof from that reference is used here.
The product and its consequence have been derived above.

## Stable transport replaces local eigenline selection by an exact solve, 22 November

The [pinned Green formula](research_unit_source_pinned_green_formula.md)
gives a simpler construction of the same full unit coherent product.
The construction is now a positive quadratic solve with explicit source
amplitude. Its conditioning proof uses no geometric lower estimate,
no approximate eigenvector, and no separation into nonzero and zero
source coordinates.

Here \(y=-e^{-2\pi ib}\), \(z=-e^{-2\pi ic}\), and
\((b,c)\) ranges in a fixed compact subset of
\(b,c>0,\ b+c<1\). The assertions about this coherent product
hold uniformly for all sufficiently large \(N\).

Use the normalized adjacent-coordinate rows
\[
 (Ax)_j=(a_jx_{j+1}-n_jx_j)
                    /\sqrt{|a_j|^2+|n_j|^2}
\]
from the unit-source theorem. Orient an edge forward if
\(|n_j|<|a_j|\), and backward otherwise. In the chosen direction,
the preceding-coordinate coefficient has modulus at most one and
the error coefficient at most \(\sqrt2\). The two-crossing profile
has exactly two vertices with no incoming edge: \(0\) and the
explicit interior index \(k\). Every coordinate has a directed
path of length at most \(N-1\) from one of them. Cauchy--Schwarz
along that path, and then summation, prove
\[
 T=A^*A+|e_0\rangle\langle e_0|
           +|e_k\rangle\langle e_k|,
       \qquad \frac1{2N^2}I\preceq T\preceq3I.
\]
The backward equality convention retains the same \(k\) at an
exact grid tie. The proof treats an exact zero coefficient just
as any other coordinate; no direction is deleted.

For the actual source \(w=\sum_j b_je_j\), the cleared relation
\(Aw=0\) therefore gives the exact formula
\[
                  w=T^{-1}(b_0e_0+b_ke_k).
\]
Both forcing coefficients are known finite products. Equivalently,
\(w\) is the unique minimum, of value zero, of
\(\|Ax\|^2+|x_0-b_0|^2+|x_k-b_k|^2\).
This local quadratic minimum is separate from the global quartic
minimum that estimates the closed invariant.

The same path proof works for any normalized first-order chain whose
row denominators are nonzero. Pin all vertices with no incoming edge.
If the comparison function \(F=|n|^2-|a|^2\) is a trigonometric
polynomial of degree at most \(m\),
at most \(2m+2\) pins suffice, with the same condition bound
\(6N^2\). A bounded recurrence degree thus bounds the number of
source coefficients required by this reconstruction. No new
recurrence for an arbitrary short tangle is asserted.

The original closing remains a matrix coefficient. For any specified
exterior row \(\ell\), solve \(Tz=\ell^*\); then
\[
             \ell w=\overline{z_0}b_0+\overline{z_k}b_k.
\]
This retains an arbitrary actual exterior, its phases and its
derivative coordinates. There is also a residual certificate with
a known source scale. For any exterior trial \(\widetilde z\),
put \(s=\ell^*-T\widetilde z\) and
\(f=b_0e_0+b_ke_k\). Then
\[
 |\ell w-\widetilde z^*f|^2
       \le (|b_0|^2+|b_k|^2)\,s^*T^{-1}s.
\]
Indeed the difference is \(s^*w\), and
\(w^*Tw=|b_0|^2+|b_k|^2\); Cauchy--Schwarz in this
energy gives the inequality. This avoids an unknown packet norm
in the source factor, while preserving the complex trial closing.

The actual closing can vanish. Positivity of \(T\) does
not prove a noncancelling geometric asymptotic for this scalar.
That estimate, after arbitrary fixed short partial fillings,
remains necessary for the finite-exception theorem.

The complete 299-line proof is at SHA-256
`5578a2df80e183f0d3c76089517e292f08763c72df0536a7f6d7fc81539cfa4f`.
Its sole complete direct proof source is the unit-source theorem at
`cb5d4e0af1b74f2e6740d2ecced5356666f24a6f59067e6a669f889adb5b9277`.
Only written mathematics and text operations were used.

## A fixed-size scalar Gram extracts the original invariant, 22 November

The fixed-degree statement in the
[positive matrix recursion](research_orthogonal_error_positive_conway_recursion.md)
has a further elementary consequence. For a fixed template with \(l\)
leaf occurrences, its root scalar is
\[
 F_N(\varepsilon)=\sum_{j=0}^l c_{N,j}\varepsilon^j,
 \qquad c_{N,0}=|K_N|^2,\qquad c_{N,j}\ge0.
\]
Here the error variables are auxiliary independent Fourier variables;
the original quantum phases and closing have already been contracted
inside each coefficient. The index \(j\) counts the number of error
vertices in an antichain, rather than a physical color or a Casimir
eigenvalue.

Choose any \(\varepsilon>0\), let
\(D=\varepsilon\,d/d\varepsilon\), and form the real symmetric
\((l+1)\)-by-\((l+1)\) matrix
\[
 \mathsf M_N(\varepsilon)_{rs}
       =D^{r+s}F_N(\varepsilon),\qquad 0\le r,s\le l.
\]
Define \(v(j)=(1,j,\ldots,j^l)^{\mathsf T}\), with the first
entry equal to one also at \(j=0\). Then
\[
 \mathsf M_N=\sum_{j=0}^l c_{N,j}\varepsilon^j
                           v(j)v(j)^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.
\]
For a polynomial \(p(t)=\sum_{r=0}^l p_rt^r\), with coefficient
column \(\mathbf p\), this gives the exact identity
\[
 \mathbf p^*\mathsf M_N\mathbf p
     =\sum_{j=0}^l c_{N,j}\varepsilon^j|p(j)|^2.
\]
If \(p(0)=1\), the right side is at least \(|K_N|^2\).
The fixed polynomial
\[
                  p_*(t)=\prod_{j=1}^l(1-t/j)
\]
attains equality. Consequently
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 |K_N|^2=\min_{p(0)=1,\ \deg p\le l}
                      \mathbf p^*\mathsf M_N\mathbf p
          =\max\{\lambda\ge0:
                \mathsf M_N\succeq\lambda e_0e_0^*\}.
 \quad}
\]
In this display \(e_0=(1,0,\ldots,0)^{\mathsf T}\) belongs to
the scalar coefficient space \(\mathbb C^{l+1}\), not the
Newton boundary space. The second equality follows by testing the
matrix inequality on every coefficient column: for \(p_0\ne0\)
divide by \(p_0\), and for \(p_0=0\) use positivity. These
formulas include vanished error coefficients and \(K_N=0\),
without taking an inverse of a singular matrix. In the invertible
case the common value is \((e_0^*\mathsf M_N^{-1}e_0)^{-1}\).

This scalar extraction does not require an exponentially small
regularization. At \(\varepsilon=1/N\), the existing recursion
has \(S_v\succeq I/N\), while its covariance bound gives
\(\|S_v\|\le2+\sigma^2\), where \(\sigma=1/16\).
Thus every intermediate positive matrix has condition number at
most \((2+\sigma^2)N\). The scalar Gram still needs moments
through order \(2l\); its dimension and the required derivative
order depend on the fixed template, not on \(N\). Its entries
are obtained from the full boundary contractions, so their
evaluation has not been reduced to bounded work.

There is also a positive construction of the Gram that does not
differentiate numerical scalar values. Write
\(\theta=\sqrt\varepsilon\) and use the finite Fourier errors
\(\xi_v\) of the recursion, now with covariance \(I\).
Add \(\theta\xi_v\) at every proper vertex, and call the resulting
closed random scalar \(Z(\theta)=B_NLX_{\rm top}(\theta)\).
Its antichain terms of size \(j\) have degree \(j\) in
\(\theta\). Distinct antichains are orthogonal. With
\(\mathcal D_\theta=\theta\,d/d\theta\), therefore,
\[
 \mathsf M_{rs}=\mathbb E[(\mathcal D_\theta^rZ)
                         \overline{\mathcal D_\theta^sZ}],
                \qquad p_*(\mathcal D_\theta)Z=K_N.
\]
This is a literal Gram, not a declaration that arbitrary expanded
quantum coefficients are orthogonal.

To compile it, retain \(l+1\) derivative packets
\(X_v^{[r]}=\mathcal D_\theta^rX_v\), for \(0\le r\le l\).
At a leaf their deterministic parts are
\((a_v,0,\ldots,0)\), and their common random part is
\((\theta\xi_v,\ldots,\theta\xi_v)\).
A unary map acts as \(I_{l+1}\otimes A_v\). At a product the
lifted bilinear map is
\[
 (\mathcal M_v(U,V))_r
       =\sum_{p=0}^r\binom rp M_v(U_p,V_{r-p}).
\]
At every proper vertex add the common random part just described.
Its covariance is
\(\mathcal E=\varepsilon\,\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}
\otimes I_N\). Independence of distinct child occurrences gives
an exact deterministic recursion for their full second moments:
\[
 \mathcal S_v=\mathcal a_v\mathcal a_v^*+\mathcal E,
 \quad
 \mathcal S_v=\mathcal A_v\mathcal S_c\mathcal A_v^*+\mathcal E,
 \quad
 \mathcal S_v=\mathcal M_v(\mathcal S_l\otimes\mathcal S_r)
                       \mathcal M_v^*+\mathcal E
\]
at leaves, unary vertices, and binary vertices, respectively.
Here \(\mathcal a_v=(a_v,0,\ldots,0)\) and
\(\mathcal A_v=I_{l+1}\otimes A_v\). At the root,
\[
 \mathsf M_N=B_N^2(I_{l+1}\otimes L)\mathcal S_{\rm top}
                                      (I_{l+1}\otimes L)^*.
\]
The block size is \((l+1)N\). All cross
moments and phases remain; the added covariance has rank one in
the derivative index, so no positive lower bound on the entire
lifted matrix is asserted.

The orthogonality is particularly explicit in the Lagrange basis
on the nodes \(0,1,\ldots,l\). In that basis the Gram is diagonal
with entries \(c_{N,j}\varepsilon^j\). The change from monomials
is a fixed Vandermonde change of basis, independent of \(N\).
This removes the auxiliary error sectors exactly; it does not make
the signed terms within the original invariant positive.

For estimates, matrix order is the useful requirement. If
\(e^{-\eta_N}\mathsf M_N\preceq\widetilde{\mathsf M}_N
\preceq e^{\eta_N}\mathsf M_N\), with \(\eta_N=o(N)\), then
minimizing the same constrained quadratic form gives its value
between \(e^{-\eta_N}|K_N|^2\) and
\(e^{\eta_N}|K_N|^2\). Entrywise estimates do not imply this
order comparison. In particular, polynomially conditioned
intermediate messages do not imply a polynomially conditioned
scalar Gram or a nonzero original invariant.

This is the finite-support Christoffel minimum; the standard
variational definition appears in
[Lasserre, equation (2.3)](https://arxiv.org/html/2203.16238v1#S2.E3).
The calculation above proves the needed statement directly,
including its singular cases. It gives a smaller positive
certificate for the same scalar, rather than a new volume estimate.
The remaining task is still a geometric lower estimate in matrix
order, with the original closing retained.

The complete direct proof source is the 407-line positive-recursion
note at SHA-256
`5506f489642f2ec118c4fef25cccc0485fecdc32ffccf09c700ac923c9da98dd`.
Its normalized compiler source remains at
`6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c`.
Only written mathematics, a primary-literature coverage lookup,
and text operations were used.

## A tridiagonal matrix constructs the full source at unit parameters, 22 November

The [unit-parameter source theorem](research_unit_coherent_product_source_gap.md)
supplies a full boundary direction in the unit-circle regime used by
the geometric scalar theorem. Its definition uses an explicit
tridiagonal matrix, and one known finite-product coefficient fixes its
source amplitude. The resulting error is polynomial in absolute norm,
not an error measured relative to the exponentially large packet norm.

Take the original normalized coherent product
\[
 w_N=u_N(y)u_N(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}b_j e_j,\qquad
 y=-e^{-2\pi ib},\quad z=-e^{-2\pi ic},\quad
 b,c>0,\quad b+c<1.
\]
The angles range in a fixed compact subset of this open triangle.
The proof first cancels the finite-product denominators to obtain
polynomial formulas for all \(b_j\), including at exact resonances.
Put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(d=N-1\), and define
\[
 a_j=(1+qQ^{j+1}y)(1+qQ^{j+1}z),\qquad
 n_j=-q(1-Q^{j+1})(1-yzQ^{j+1}),
\]
\[
 (A_Nx)_j=\frac{a_jx_{j+1}-n_jx_j}
                    {\sqrt{|a_j|^2+|n_j|^2}}
                 \quad(0\le j<d),\qquad
 H_N^0=A_N^*A_N+|e_0\rangle\langle e_0|.
\]
The row denominators stay uniformly away from zero for large \(N\).
The fixed endpoint pin makes \(H_N^0\) an explicitly known,
smooth, positive tridiagonal matrix, including at the exact zero
blocks of the original source. No full-state projector is used to
construct it.

Let \(\lambda_{0,N}\le\lambda_{1,N}\le\cdots\) be its eigenvalues.
The theorem proves, uniformly for large \(N\),
\[
 0\le\lambda_{0,N}\le C e^{-2N\delta},\qquad
 \lambda_{1,N}\ge\frac1{8N^2},\qquad \delta>0.
\]
Its lowest eigenline is therefore simple. If \(P_N\) is its
orthogonal projection, then
\[
 \|(I-P_N)w_N\|\le8N^2|b_0|\le C.
\]
This controls the entire coefficient vector and all repeated-root
derivative coordinates. The proof uses a separate exact operator
\(H_N=A_N^*A_N+C_N^*C_N\), where
\[
 C_Nx=\frac{b_kx_0-b_0x_k}{\sqrt{|b_k|^2+|b_0|^2}}.
\]
Here \(k\) is the explicit interior maximum selected by a fixed-degree
crossing equation; \(b_0,b_k\) are the corresponding known finite
products. Weighted paths control the nonzero support, while actual
root rows and stable forward/backward propagation control its zero
blocks. This gives
\(H_N\ge(4N^2)^{-1}(I-P_{w_N})\) without deleting coordinates.
The geometric scalar theorem makes \(b_0/b_k\) exponentially small,
so the reset projection differs exponentially little from the fixed
endpoint pin in \(H_N^0\). Finally
\(H_N^0w_N=b_0e_0\), which gives the absolute error bound above.

The scale and phase can also be specified without knowing the full
packet. For any unit lowest eigenvector \(v_N\),
\[
 |v_{N,k}|\ge\frac1{2\sqrt N},\qquad
 \widehat w_N=\frac{b_k}{v_{N,k}}v_N,\qquad
 \|\widehat w_N-w_N\|\le C(1+2\sqrt N).
\]
The definition is invariant under rephasing \(v_N\). For the two
geometric coherent closing families already proved, with or without
one genuine turn, the rows have dual norm one and their actual values
are at least \(cN^{-3/2}e^{N\delta}\). Thus this explicitly scaled
lowest state preserves those original observations with relative
error at most \(CN^2e^{-N\delta}\).

This gives a separate unit-boundary construction, including all exact
resonances. A bounded original cap can still have a small or zero
value, and an arbitrary later component can have exponential dual
norm. Neither is controlled by the last relative estimate. General
composition and the finite-exception theorem remain open.

The complete 467-line proof is at SHA-256
`cb5d4e0af1b74f2e6740d2ecced5356666f24a6f59067e6a669f889adb5b9277`.
Its three complete direct sources are the
[coherent-product theorem](research_centered_coherent_product_energy.md)
at `73152328a77ba5d63a2a8eaa17647ed38b7683c613e0947e3bda9e451dda76e2`,
the [centered compiler](research_centered_fourier_conway_compiler.md)
at `0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413`,
and the [single-leg source theorem](research_single_leg_radial_turn_source.md)
at `c624e0edbaadb57279c00420d3f552e93c67cb84972926aad27ff51c2c973e7e`.
Only written mathematics and text operations were used.

## Three diagonal tilts do not always expose the cube saddle, 22 November

An exact source-profile calculation rules out one proposed shortcut
for the next composition. Reassociating four coherent inputs gives
three pairings. It is not always possible to choose one of them and
opposite exponential diagonal weights so that the geometric cube
saddle is a global norm maximum of both factors. This is a test of
that auxiliary metric argument, not a counterexample to a knot-volume
statement.

Take all four unit angles equal to \(a=5/11\), and put
\(y=-e^{-2\pi ia}\). All six pair sums are less than one, and
the total is greater than one. The
[positive cube theorem](actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity.md)
therefore applies. All three pairings are identical. Their positive
composition action is symmetric under \(u\mapsto1-u\), so its
unique interior maximum is \(u=1/2\).

Let \(L(t)=\int_0^t\log|2\sin\pi s|\,ds\), extended as an odd
one-periodic function. For the actual normalized unit product
\(w_N(y,y)=\sum_j b_j e_j\), the coefficient rate near \(u=1/2\)
is
\[
 \frac1N\log|b_{\lfloor Nu\rfloor}|\longrightarrow P_a(u),
\]
\[
 P_a(u)=L(u)+L(u-2a)+L(2a)-2L(a)-2L(u-a).
\]
This follows directly from the finite products in the unit-parameter
theorem: the numerator products give \(L(u)\) and
\(L(u-2a)+L(2a)\), and the two denominator products give
\(2L(u-a)+2L(a)\). Since the denominator angle has fixed odd
denominator eleven, its half-grid distances are at least a fixed
multiple of \(1/N\); splitting off the logarithmic singularity
gives a Riemann-sum error \(O(\log N)\). There is no vanishing
numerator in a fixed neighborhood of \(u=1/2\).

The slope there is
\[
 p=P_a'(1/2)
 =\log\frac{\cos(\pi/11)}{\sin^2(\pi/22)}>\log47>3.
\]
Indeed \(\pi<22/7\) gives
\(\cos(\pi/11)>47/49\) and \(\sin(\pi/22)<1/7\).
Also \(|L|<1/4\): its largest absolute value is \(-L(1/6)\),
and \(2\sin\pi s\ge4s\) on \([0,1/6]\) gives
\[
 -L(1/6)\le\frac{1+\log(3/2)}6<\frac14.
\]
Consequently
\[
 P_a(1/2)=L(2a)-2L(a)-2L(1/2-a)-L(2a-1/2)<\frac32.
\]

Multiply the first coefficient vector by \(e^{\lambda j}\) and
the reversed second vector by \(e^{-\lambda j}\), retaining their
original bilinear contraction. Making both stationary at \(u=1/2\)
forces \(\lambda=-p\). But the first tilted amplitude at that
point has rate
\[
                    P_a(1/2)-p/2<0.
\]
Its zeroth coefficient has rate zero. In fact its exact value is
\[
 b_0=\frac{\kappa^2D_N(y)^2}{N^2(1+qy)^2},\qquad
 D_N(y)=1+e^{-10\pi iN/11}.
\]
The latter lies in a finite set of nonzero values because eleven
is odd, so \(|b_0|\) is bounded above and below by positive
multiples of \(N^{-2}\) for all large \(N\). The tilt leaves
that coordinate unchanged. The proposed saddle therefore fails
global exposure for the actual coefficients along the full sequence.
All three pairings coincide in this example.

This excludes that particular diagonal-weight and reassociation
shortcut. It does not exclude more general boundary metrics or give
a lower estimate for the original signed four-boundary period.
The complete matching proof inputs read for this calculation are
the unit-source theorem above, its coherent-product and centered
sources, and the 377-line cube theorem at
`c29321805df39a49854665df1255db1ec7180397a5dd689f19289d61335871c9`.
The countercalculation is written out here. Only written mathematics
and text operations were used; no numerical test was run.

## The original geometric contribution survives one radial leg and its turn, 22 November

The [single-leg source theorem](research_single_leg_radial_turn_source.md)
proves a nonzero geometric asymptotic for an actual scalar family,
including its zero-radius endpoint and the corresponding observation
after one genuine turn. This verifies a local source coefficient on
that family; it does not yet control arbitrary short components.

Let \(U_N(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}t^j f_j\) in the full centered
basis and let
\(\mathcal C_N(x,y,z)=\phi(U_N(x)U_N(y)U_N(z))\), with the
original Frobenius closing. Here \(N\ge2\) and
\(\kappa=\exp(\pi i(N-1)^2/(2N))\). Fix a strict prism shape
\[
 a,b,c>0,\quad a+b,a+c,b+c<1,\quad a+b+c>1,
\]
and put
\[
 x_r=-r e^{-2\pi ia},\quad y=-e^{-2\pi ib},\quad
 z=-e^{-2\pi ic},\qquad 0\le r\le1.
\]
Here any of the three legs may be chosen as radial; its angle need not
be largest. The calibrated dilogarithmic action \(\Psi\) and
nonzero amplitude \(B\) are the original prism-source ones, defined
explicitly in the new proof. Uniformly on compact strict shape
families and the whole interval,
\[
 \mathcal C_N(x_r,y,z)=
 \kappa e^{i\pi/4-\pi i/(2N)}B(x_r,y,z)
                  e^{iN\Psi(x_r,y,z)}(1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
The height has the strictly positive bound
\[
 -\operatorname{Im}\Psi(x_r,y,z)
 \ge J_0(b+c)-J_0(b)-J_0(c)>0,\qquad
 J_0(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du.
\]
It increases strictly with \(r\) on \((0,1)\).
The logarithmic radial derivative is minus the argument of an explicit
cross ratio, divided by \(2\pi\). That ratio has negative imaginary
part throughout the interval. The endpoint inequality follows by
differentiating the displayed log-sine expression in \(b\).

The zero-radius step retains an initialized source contribution.
The existing canceled prism identity is
\(\mathcal C_N=\mathcal G_N+O(N^{-1})\).
Inspection of its full-vertical-strip estimates shows that its
constants remain uniform as this radius tends to zero. The canonical
Gamma quotient \(\mathcal G_N\) has a nonzero limit: two upper
factorial limits cancel two matching denominator limits, leaving a
specified three-factor quotient. The positive height makes the
remaining current exponentially smaller than that contribution.
One must take the limit of the canceled identity. In a representation
using the radial leg as the Cauchy leg, setting the radius to zero
inside the uncanceled rectangle would discard its escaping pole.

The turn is controlled by an exact full-tensor identity. With
\(d=N-1\) and \(|y|=|z|=1\),
\[
 t^d\mathcal C_N(1/t,y,z)
   =\phi\bigl[J(U_N(y)U_N(z))U_N(t)\bigr]
   =(yz)^d\overline{\mathcal C_N(\bar t,y,z)}.
\]
This is a reciprocal-polynomial equality, including \(t=0\).
At \(t=\bar x_r\) it gives the same positive rate and an explicit
nonzero leading coefficient for the turned observation. The original
carrier \((yz)^d\) is retained. Unit-normalizing the three inputs
divides this scalar by \(N\sqrt{Z_N(t)}\), where
\(Z_N(t)=\sum_{j=0}^d|t|^{2j}\); that known polynomial factor
does not alter its rate. The claims hold along the full large-level
sequence, including both parities and composite levels.

The theorem concerns a scalar observation with two unit parameters.
It does not give the entire next output, arbitrary further gluings,
or a closed-knot volume theorem. In particular it must not be combined
with the compact-open-bidisk vacuum estimate below by assuming that
estimate is uniform at the unit boundary. The remaining general
composition problem still includes products of two turned composite
packets with their original exterior and closing retained.

The complete 326-line proof is at SHA-256
`c624e0edbaadb57279c00420d3f552e93c67cb84972926aad27ff51c2c973e7e`.
Its two complete proof sources are the
[full prism source](research_centered_tensor_full_prism_source_transport.md)
at `eb43e287eca5933b70de3b6362a81f92d46bb2e121f0eb5716793c107adaef10`
and the [centered compiler](research_centered_fourier_conway_compiler.md)
at `0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413`.
Only written mathematics and text operations were used.

## An explicit cyclic equation selects the entire coherent-product line, 22 November

The [cyclic product theorem](research_cyclic_coherent_product_vacuum_gap.md)
gives an actual source-derived direction with a polynomial coercivity
bound for one universal multiplication step. It retains all Newton
coefficients, including the tails and repeated-root coordinates.

Fix \(|y|,|z|\le r<1\), independently of \(N\), and let
\(d=N-1\) and
\(w_N=u_N(y)u_N(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}b_j e_j\), where the two
centered coherent inputs have norm one. Their exact finite wall
products give \(b_j\ne0\) and the consecutive ratios
\[
 \rho_j=-q\frac{(1-Q^{j+1})(1-Q^{j+1}yz)}
                 {(1+qQ^{j+1}y)(1+qQ^{j+1}z)}
                   \quad(0\le j<d),
\]
\[
 \rho_d=\frac{b_0}{b_d}
 =\frac{\kappa^2D_N(y)D_N(z)(1-yz)}
        {N(1+qy)(1+qz)(1-(yz)^N)},\qquad
 D_N(t)=1-(-1)^d t^N.
\]
Here \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and
\(\kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)}\). The last ratio is a known
nonzero endpoint factor of size \(O_r(N^{-1})\), not an unknown
knot invariant. Define
\[
 (A_Nv)_j=v_{j+1}-\rho_jv_j\quad(j<d),\qquad
 (A_Nv)_d=v_0-\rho_dv_d.
\]
This bounded operator has kernel exactly \(\mathbb Cw_N\) at
every level. Uniformly for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\[
 A_N^*A_N\ge N^{-2}(I-P_{w_N}),\qquad
 \operatorname{dist}(v,\mathbb Cw_N)\le N\|A_Nv\|.
\]
The projection is orthogonal in the declared full Newton coefficient
metric. The input coherent lines are themselves kernels of explicit
rectangular difference operators with positive gap at least
\((1-r)^2\).

The output gap follows from an exact weighted-cycle calculation.
The finite ratios have only two modulus-one crossings, by a uniform
\(C^1\) perturbation of the previously proved single-cosine identity.
Thus the weights \(|b_j|^2\) have one cyclic peak, allowing tied
steps. Write \(v_j=b_jg_j\) and follow weakly increasing paths
to one fixed peak. The conductance of every edge on such a path
is at least its starting weight. Cauchy--Schwarz and summation give
the variance bound with factor \(N^2\), without any lower bound
on the smallest coefficient. The prescribed wrap is part of this
cycle and is retained in the operator.

The genuine turn is unitary, so \(JA_NJ\) selects the full turned
line with the same gap. This is a proved primitive with known source
normalization. It is not a gap assertion for arbitrary short words
or further products of composite outputs. The original endpoint
observations can still be exponentially small relative to the packet
norm; a gap for the direction does not establish their volume rate.

The complete 336-line proof is at SHA-256
`fb94dcc9fd6bb92935eadb3522b900652487b3c1bb46948c36535525ef295a0c`.
Its complete proof sources are the
[whole coherent-product theorem](research_centered_coherent_product_energy.md)
at `73152328a77ba5d63a2a8eaa17647ed38b7683c613e0947e3bda9e451dda76e2`
and the centered compiler at
`0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413`.
Only written mathematics and text operations were used.

## Boundary directions give an explicit scalar certificate, 22 November

The [projective-direction certificate](research_conway_projective_direction_certificate.md)
simplifies the finite-level problem further. Once one supplies a full
boundary direction at every gate, a product of local complex overlaps
and a sum of squared discarded components give a direct error bound
for the original invariant. This particular certificate needs no
minimization. Choosing the directions and proving the required relative
error remain substantive tasks.

Use the original normalized tree, its known budget product \(B_N\),
maps \(\Phi_v\) of norm at most \(\sigma=1/16\), and original
closing row \(L\), also of norm at most \(\sigma\). The top proper
vertex is \(v_0\). At every proper vertex choose a unit vector
\(u_v\) in the entire physical Newton space, including its
repeated-root derivative coordinates. Define
\[
 c_v=u_v^*\Phi_v((u_c)_c),\qquad
 \alpha_v=c_v\prod_{c\text{ child of }v}\alpha_c,
 \qquad
 \widetilde a_v=\alpha_vu_v.
\]
At a leaf \(\Phi_v\) is its prescribed constant and the product
is empty. These equations are exactly the forward recursion with
orthogonal projection onto the supplied line after each gate.
They give the explicit complex closing
\[
 k_\parallel=L\widetilde a_{v_0}
       =(Lu_{v_0})\prod_{v\text{ proper}}c_v.
\]
The original phases remain in this product. Rephasing any supplied
unit representative leaves the projected packets and closing unchanged.
The squared norm of the discarded components is
\[
 H_0=\sum_{v\text{ proper}}
 \left(\|\Phi_v((u_c)_c)\|^2-|c_v|^2\right)
                  \prod_{c\text{ child of }v}|\alpha_c|^2.
\]
Every summand is nonnegative by orthogonality. It is the squared
residual at that gate, rather than a sum of separately squared
terms in an unassembled quantum expression.

The exact comparison is
\[
                  \boxed{\quad
 \left|K_N/B_N-k_\parallel\right|\le\frac{\sqrt{H_0}}{15}.
                  \quad}
\]
Here is the improvement behind the constant. The true and projected
forward packets all have norm at most \(\sigma\). On the segment
between those fields, the derivative of the forward map has unary
blocks of norm at most \(\sigma\) and binary input blocks of norm
at most \(\sigma^2\). Each child belongs to only one parent, so
the derivative norm is at most \(\sigma\). The residual map is
therefore bounded below by \(1-\sigma\) on this segment.
Applying the original closing, whose norm is at most \(\sigma\),
gives \(\sigma/(1-\sigma)=1/15\). No original closing row is
replaced by a norm observation in this argument.

For example, if \(H_0\le|k_\parallel|^2\), then
\[
 \frac{196}{225}B_N^2|k_\parallel|^2
       \le |K_N|^2
       \le\frac{256}{225}B_N^2|k_\parallel|^2.
\]
Thus a geometric choice of directions would suffice if the explicit
product \(B_N|k_\parallel|\) has the volume rate and the discarded
components obey this relative bound. More generally the direct error
estimate allows any eventual fixed ratio
\(\sqrt{H_0}/|k_\parallel|<15\), bounded away from fifteen.
Neither estimate has been proved after the arbitrary short partial
fillings required by the finite-exception target. A Gaussian valid
only in an interior window does not supply these full boundary vectors
or control the tails seen by the original closing.

The same note proves an optional amplitude refinement. For fixed
boundary lines, all overall packet phases align by a single upward
tree pass. The remaining quartic is strongly convex with Hessian
between \(I\) and \(3I\), and has one real radius per proper
vertex. At its minimum the full complex gradient along every supplied
line vanishes, including at zero radii. Consequently the existing
gradient lower certificate needs only the perpendicular gradient
components. This removes separate phase and amplitude fitting;
it does not remove the full-dimensional problem of constructing the
directions. The explicit product certificate above requires neither
this scalar optimization nor a full-gradient evaluation.

The complete proof is the 351-line note at SHA-256
`a6313c251f93b18ebcff4acb8eae3a3bb63889226f1b7c1e00f923a5d47fb42d`.
Its sole complete proof source is the
[normalized compiler](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) at
`6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c`.
Orthogonal tensor truncation is an established method; the note cites
primary coverage and proves the closing-specific comparison directly.
No new volume-conjecture class or finite-exception theorem follows here.
Only written mathematics and text operations were used.

## Fixed degree removes the small error parameter, 22 November

The [positive matrix recursion](research_orthogonal_error_positive_conway_recursion.md)
has an exact finite-difference consequence. Its artificial errors can be
removed by evaluating the recursion at finitely many inverse-polynomial
error sizes. This removes the exponentially small error parameter from
the matrix evaluations, but retains cancellation in the final scalar
combination.

Use the original normalized compiler, its full Newton/Hermite spaces,
budget product \(B_N\), and original closing row \(L\). Put
\(\sigma=1/16\). Add \(\varepsilon I\) at every proper vertex,
including unary and binary vertices; no error is added at the closing
root. Thus
\[
 S_v=a_va_v^*+\varepsilon I\quad\text{at a leaf},\qquad
 S_v=A_vS_cA_v^*+\varepsilon I\quad\text{at a unary vertex},
\]
\[
 S_v=M_v(S_l\otimes S_r)M_v^*+\varepsilon I
       \quad\text{at a binary vertex},\qquad
 F_N(\varepsilon)=B_N^2 L S_{\rm top}(\varepsilon)L^*.
\]
Every displayed map is the prescribed original normalized map; its
complex entries and the original root observation are retained.

Let \(l\ge1\) be the number of leaf occurrences and set \(r=l+1\).
The recursion makes \(F_N\) a polynomial of degree at most \(l\)
with \(F_N(0)=|K_N|^2\). Indeed the matrix polynomial has degree
one at a leaf, no larger leaf-count degree after a unary operation,
and at most the sum of the two child degrees at a binary operation.
The fresh linear term does not increase those bounds. Define
\[
 \varepsilon_j=\frac{j}{rN},\qquad
 w_j=(-1)^{j-1}\binom rj,\qquad 1\le j\le r.
\]
The \(r\)-th forward difference of a polynomial of degree less
than \(r\) is zero. Applying this to \(F_N\), with step
\(1/(rN)\), proves the exact identity
\[
                  \boxed{\quad
 |K_N|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r w_j F_N(\varepsilon_j).
                  \quad}
\]
It holds also when the invariant is zero. There is no variational
solve or division by the invariant.

All intermediate matrices in these evaluations have polynomial spectral
conditioning. The complete covariance estimate in the recursion proof
gives, at \(h=N\varepsilon_j=j/r\le1\),
\[
 S_v=a_va_v^*+V_v,\qquad V_v\succeq0,\qquad
 \operatorname{tr}V_v\le2h,\qquad \|a_v\|\le\sigma.
\]
The added error at every proper vertex also gives
\(S_v\succeq\varepsilon_j I\). Consequently
\[
 \frac1{rN}I\preceq S_v(\varepsilon_j)
       \preceq(\sigma^2+2)I,\qquad
 \operatorname{cond}_2 S_v(\varepsilon_j)
       \le(\sigma^2+2)rN.
\]
These estimates concern the entire physical packet, including its
repeated-root directions. They do not use a distinct-root quotient.

The scalar extrapolation has coefficient sum
\(\sum_j|w_j|=2^r-1\), independent of \(N\) for the fixed
template. If the evaluated \(F_N(\varepsilon_j)\) have absolute
errors at most \(\delta\), the recovered square has error at most
\((2^r-1)\delta\). Errors of size \(\eta\) in the normalized
observations \(LS_{\rm top}L^*\) instead give error at most
\(B_N^2(2^r-1)\eta\).

Thus this is an exact simplification of the finite-level calculation,
not a positivity or relative-error estimate for its signed scalar sum.
The evaluated matrices can be well conditioned while the scalar
combination is much smaller than its summands. The identity does not
evaluate the volume rate or prove an additional filling case.

## Interior norm localization does not retain the closing, 22 November

The exact centered kernels suggest using analytic Fourier-integral
composition to attach short components. Two explicit tests show why
the existing local kernel and forward Gaussian estimates do not
yet justify that step. These are tests of the proposed general
composition argument, not additional knot-volume cases.

Use the complete orthonormal centered basis \(f_0,\ldots,f_{N-1}\)
and the original Newton basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_{N-1}\). Put
\[
 U_{N,\theta}=N^{-1/2}\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}e^{ia\theta}f_a,\qquad
 u_N(y)=\frac{\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}y^af_a}{\sqrt{Z_N(y)}},\qquad
 Z_N(y)=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}|y|^{2a}.
\]
Circle orthogonality gives the exact positive resolution
\[
       N\int_0^{2\pi}|U_{N,\theta}\rangle
          \langle U_{N,\theta}|\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}=I.
\]
However its density on the stated input family is
\[
 N|\langle U_{N,\theta},u_N(y)\rangle|^2
 =\frac{|1-(ye^{-i\theta})^N|^2}
        {Z_N(y)|1-ye^{-i\theta}|^2}
 \longrightarrow
               \frac{1-|y|^2}{|1-ye^{-i\theta}|^2}
\]
uniformly for \(|y|\le r<1\) and all \(\theta\).
This follows from the finite geometric sum,
\(Z_N(y)=(1-|y|^{2N})/(1-|y|^2)\), and
\(|1-ye^{-i\theta}|\ge1-r\).
The limit is a positive Poisson density on the whole circle,
not a Gaussian concentrated on one fixed arc.

For an arc \(I\) with positive-length complement, let
\[
 \mathsf E_{N,I}
   =N\int_I|U_{N,\theta}\rangle
                    \langle U_{N,\theta}|\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}.
\]
It is a positive contraction, not generally a projection.
The omitted mass converges to the integral of that Poisson
density over \(I^c\), bounded below by
\[
                   \frac{1-r}{1+r}\frac{|I^c|}{2\pi}>0.
\]
Since \(u_N(y)\) is unit,
\(\|u_N(y)-\mathsf E_{N,I}u_N(y)\|\) is at least this
omitted mass, up to a quantity tending uniformly to zero.
Thus this exact circle resolution cannot localize these incoming
states exponentially to a fixed arc.

There is a complementary source-level test for the genuine
forward Gaussian. Let
\[
           w_N=u_N(0)^2=(R^+)^2/N.
\]
The [whole-output theorem](research_centered_coherent_product_energy.md)
gives its unique Newton norm maximum at \(u_*=5/6\).
Fix \(0<\delta<1/12\), and let \(\mathsf P_N\) be the
orthogonal Newton-coordinate projector onto
\[
       \left|(j+1/2)/N-5/6\right|<\delta.
\]
Its full concentration estimate gives constants \(C,c>0\) with
\[
              \|(I-\mathsf P_N)w_N\|
                          \le Ce^{-cN}\|w_N\|.
\]
But for sufficiently large \(N\), this window omits both endpoint
coordinates. The original closings satisfy
\[
 \phi(e_j)=\delta_{j,N-1},\qquad m(e_j)=\delta_{j,0},
 \qquad
 \phi\mathsf P_N=m\mathsf P_N=0.
\]
The exact endpoint formulas of the same theorem give
\[
       \phi(w_N)=1,\qquad m(w_N)=\kappa^2/N.
\]
Consequently the norm-small omitted tail carries the **entire**
original value of either closing. A full-vector relative Gaussian
approximation, even with exponentially small tails away from its
peak, does not itself justify inserting its bulk projector in
the original scalar source.

The original closing is explicit also in centered polynomial
coordinates. If \(p_v(t)=\sum_a v_at^a\), the
[compiler](research_centered_fourier_conway_compiler.md) gives
\[
       \phi(v)=\kappa^{-1}N^{-1/2}p_v(-q^{-1}),\qquad
       m(v)=\kappa N^{-1/2}p_v(-q).
\]
Here \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\) and \(\kappa=q^{(N-1)^2/2}\), with their
original phases. These formulas follow directly from its
closing coefficients and are not Hermitian norm evaluations.

An attachment argument must therefore control the actual
adjoint context on the discarded packet directions, together
with the state itself. Interior ellipticity and orthogonality
alone supply no such source-relative estimate. No new general
short-component attachment theorem or finite-exception result
was obtained in this test.

and the 405-line centered compiler at
\(\texttt{0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413}\).

## The cyclic color trace does not yet give critical descent, 22 November

The exact [regularized-source trace](regularized_kashaev_period.md)
already gives a positive norm for the original main-color orbit.
The following tests restrict the kind of source descent that can
use it. They do not yield a new geometric lower bound.

At a fixed principal root \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), write \(Y=M^2\)
for the squared meridian and
\[
 A_N=\mathbb C[Y^{\pm1}]/(Y^N-1),\qquad
 \tau_N=\operatorname{Tr}_{A_N/\mathbb C}/N,\qquad
 e_0=\frac{1+Y+\cdots+Y^{N-1}}{N}.
\]
The element \(e_0\) is the primitive idempotent at the complete
color \(Y=1\). The original reduced source \(F_N\) satisfies
\[
 F_N(1)=K_N,\qquad F_N(Q^j)=C_j(q_N)\quad(1\le j<N).
\]
With coefficient conjugation and \(Y^\sharp=Y^{-1}\), the exact
color energy is
\[
 E_N=N\tau_N(F_N^\sharp F_N)
       =|K_N|^2+\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}|C_j(q_N)|^2.
\]
The second term has the proved polynomial bound. But the
source-weighted trace on the complete idempotent is
\[
                 \tau_N(F_N^\sharp e_0F_N)=|K_N|^2/N.
\]
Faithfulness of the unweighted color trace therefore does not
supply nonzero geometric source coefficients.

This distinction cannot be removed using only the color algebra,
its degree bound, and the ordinary-color anchor. For any chosen
numbers \(a_N\), the algebraic test family
\[
             F_N^{(a)}=1+(a_N-1)e_0
\]
has degree less than \(N\), every ordinary color equal to one,
and complete value \(a_N\). Its energy is
\(|a_N|^2+N-1\). Its generic representative is a nonzero element
of \(\mathbb C(Y)\) for every \(a_N\). This is not asserted to
be a knot source: its point is that the additional actual
Ward, endpoint and closing relations must do essential work.

There is also a degree restriction on one proposed algebraic
identification. At this fixed root,
\[
                \mathbb C(Y)/\mathbb C(U),\qquad U=Y^N,
\]
is a cyclic field extension of degree \(N\), with automorphism
\(Y\mapsto QY\). If a geometric field of degree \(d\) over
the **same** base \(\mathbb C(U)\) embeds as a unital subfield,
the tower law gives \(d\mid N\). Hence a fixed degree \(d>1\)
cannot be realized by this subfield construction at all
sufficiently large levels. This does not exclude a different
relative-period module, a changed base, or a separately constructed
critical action on a larger operator space. Nor is the cyclic
color average a number-field Galois average over geometric
critical points. With indeterminate \(Q\), the shift need not
fix \(Y^N\); the displayed cyclic extension is a fixed-root
construction.

The need for a relative module can also be seen in an existing
exact source identity. In the original figure-eight sum from
[the source-quotient theorem](actual_source_quotient_and_critical_relation.md),
work on \(\mathcal C_N=\mathbb C[Z^{\pm1}]/(Z^N-1)\), with
\[
 A(Z)=(1-Z)(1-Z^{-1}),\qquad
 B_Q=A(QZ)\sigma_Q,\qquad \sigma_Q f(Z)=f(QZ).
\]
The actual source functional obeys
\[
 B_Q^N=0,\qquad
 \mu_N((I-B_Q)f)=f(1),\qquad
 \mu_N=\operatorname{ev}_1\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}B_Q^j.
\]
Thus \(I-B_Q\) is invertible and its finite homogeneous cokernel
is zero. Before the finite root specialization, the expression
\(I-A(QZ)\sigma_Q\) has classical multiplication symbol
\[
                      1-A(Z)=(Z^2-Z+1)/Z.
\]
The degree-two critical algebra cannot be obtained as that
finite homogeneous cokernel. Retaining the endpoint gives
the vector-space complex
\[
 f\longmapsto((I-B_Q)f,-f(1))
       \quad\text{in } \mathcal C_N\oplus\mathbb C,
\]
whose cokernel is one-dimensional: its map is injective and
the nonzero functional \((g,c)\mapsto\mu_N(g)+c\) annihilates
its image. Neither this dimension count nor the classical
critical polynomial constructs a critical Frobenius algebra.
The example is used to test the general descent proposal;
it is not another proof of an individual knot-volume case.

The missing construction is consequently still a source-compatible
relative reduction before final closure, retaining the affine
endpoint, Gaussian contractions and normal currents. The faithful
trace on colors cannot replace that construction. No new volume
case or finite-exception conclusion follows from these audits.

## Algebraic finiteness requires the marked peripheral data, 22 November

The [marked-curve lemma](research_marked_peripheral_curve_finite_slopes.md)
proves a small algebraic part of a possible finite-exception argument.
Let \(C\) be an integral finite-type algebraic curve, \(s\) a nonzero
regular section of a line bundle, and \(U,V:C\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)\)
commuting regular peripheral matrices. Suppose the subgroup
\(\langle U(z),V(z)\rangle\) is infinite at every zero of \(s\).
Then
\[
 \#\left\{\text{unoriented primitive }(p,q):
       U(z)^pV(z)^q\in\{I,-I\}
                 \text{ for some }z\in Z(s)\right\}
                  \le \# Z(s)<\infty .
\]
This is a theorem about marked algebraic data, not a newly proved
statement about quantum coefficients.

The proof is elementary. The nonzero section has a proper closed
zero set on the integral curve; this set is zero-dimensional and
Noetherian, hence finite. Two distinct primitive slope classes at
one zero have determinant \(d\ne0\). Their commuting matrix
equations imply \(U^{2d}=V^{2d}=I\), so their generated group
would be finite. Thus each zero contributes at most one slope.
Singular and nonproper finite-type curves are allowed. Finitely
many coefficient sections or finite algebraic covers are also
allowed; an unrestricted logarithmic cover is not such a curve.

The full matrices matter at unit eigenvalues. For \(E\ne0\),
\(E^2=0\),
\[
 U=I+uE,\qquad V=I+vE,\qquad
                   U^pV^q=I+(pu+qv)E .
\]
At a noncentral pair, the projective translation ratio \([u:v]\)
retains the slope equation, although both eigenvalues are one.
For example, \(U=I+E\), \(V=I+\varepsilon E\) realizes
the distinct slopes \((1,n)\) at \(\varepsilon=-1/n\).
An eigenvalue-only map sends all of them to the same point.
The infinite-group condition is separate; it cannot be inferred
from hyperbolicity of a final ambient manifold when a filling
circle can become trivial.

There is a concrete limit to extending this curve argument by
induction. On \(\mathbb A^3\), use the same matrices separately
in coordinates \(\varepsilon_i\). For a fixed nonzero \(n_0\),
the regular function
\[
                   s=\varepsilon_1+1/n_0+
                                      \varepsilon_2-\varepsilon_3
\]
is a unit at the total origin and is nonzero on every
positive-dimensional coordinate fiber. Nevertheless
\[
              s(-1/n_0,-1/n,-1/n)=0
\]
for every nonzero integer \(n\). These points satisfy the full
matrix filling equations for \((1,n_0),(1,n),(1,n)\), with
infinite peripheral images. Thus neither nonzero restrictions
nor last-curve finite zero counts imply a finite total
exceptional set. This is an algebraic countermodel, with no
claimed hyperbolic-knot realization.

There is relevant arithmetic literature to audit for the
higher-dimensional part. The printed statement of
[Habegger, Corollary 2](https://user.math.uzh.ch/habegger/bhc.pdf)
asserts finiteness of
\[
       D^{\rm oa}\cap
          \bigcup_{\operatorname{codim}H\ge\dim D+1}H
\]
for an irreducible torus subvariety \(D\) over
\(\overline{\mathbb Q}\). Here \(D^{\rm oa}\) removes the
positive-dimensional intersections with torus cosets that are
larger than expected. For a coefficient-zero component of
dimension \(k-1\), the \(k\) independent filling equations meet
this codimension threshold. The divisor's own excluded anomalous
locus can still contain an infinite filling family. This is
coverage of a possible arithmetic input; its proof has not been
adopted into our source argument.

Even a finite set of peripheral eigenvalue points does not itself
give finitely many assignments. Torsion points can satisfy
infinitely many exponentiated slope equations. One must either
retain enough full marked peripheral data to use the infinite-image
argument, prove an appropriate finite-fiber property, or handle
the collapsed filling families separately.

The remaining source premise is substantial: construct the
coefficient of the whole original selected quantum expansion
as a nonzero regular section on the relevant marked algebraic
space, with its complementary contributions controlled and its
action calibrated to the actual filled volume. A local
algebraic Gaussian prefactor alone does not establish that
premise. Nor has the higher-dimensional anomalous locus been
controlled after arbitrary fixed short partial assignments.
The finite-exception theorem remains open.

The complete new 133-line elementary proof has SHA-256
\(\texttt{52d6efaee2a1285233b1643e55fe1841909d2ff3a4ff74904f677eaad728a30f}\).
It has no imported proof premise. Only written mathematics,
source reads, literature coverage and text operations were used.
Frozen manuscripts and earlier final notes remain unchanged.

## Testing a positive reconstruction of the closed source, 22 November

Two follow-up tests clarify what the positive recursion still needs.
Neither supplies a geometric rate or a new knot-volume theorem.

First, a covariance square root can make a proposed packet into a
valid lower matrix, but this alone does not construct a geometric
approximation. For a known nonzero packet \(w\), choose a unit vector
\(\psi\), with phase adjusted so
\(c=\langle w/\|w\|,\psi\rangle\ge0\). The vector
\[
 q=\frac{\|w\|}{\sqrt{\|w\|^2+\varepsilon}}
                (ww^*+\varepsilon I)^{1/2}\psi
   =cw+\frac{\|w\|\sqrt{\varepsilon}}
                 {\sqrt{\|w\|^2+\varepsilon}}
                     \left(\psi-c\,\frac{w}{\|w\|}\right)
\]
satisfies \(qq^*\preceq ww^*+\varepsilon I\), \(\|q\|\le\|w\|\),
and \(\|q-cw\|\le\sqrt{\varepsilon}\). These follow by separating
the line through \(w\) from its orthogonal complement.
However, \(q=cw\) already gives \(qq^*\preceq ww^*\) without
an error. Applying the latter rule through the normalized tree
produces exactly \(q_v=\alpha_v a_v\), where \(\alpha_v\) is the
product of the chosen \(c\)'s in its subtree. Its closing is
exactly \(\alpha_{\rm top}K_N/B_N\). Both constructions still use
the full actual packet direction. They do not turn a polynomially
accurate proposed Gaussian into an independently controlled
source contribution. No separate completion note was added.

Second, a natural positive state obtained by projecting onto the
original cap fails to satisfy the knot's meridian relations. This
can be checked exactly for every level using a single presentation;
it tests the proposed general construction rather than another
knot-volume case.

Use the zero-framed closure of the actual positive two-braid
\(\sigma_1\), whose knot is the unknot and whose original reduced
invariant is \(K_N=1\). Write \(\widetilde W\) for its full
original braid operator, including its framing and pivotal scalar
phases. Put \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\). The
[original cap formula](research_main_color_cap_projection_energy.md)
fixes the vectorization and its unit cap vector as
\[
 \begin{split}
 \operatorname{vec} A
   &=\sum_{a,a',i,j}A_{(a,i),(a',j)}
                     e_a\otimes e_{a'}\otimes e_i\otimes e_j,\\
 r&=e_0\otimes e_0\otimes
                 \frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}Q^a e_a\otimes e_a,
       \qquad \Pi=|r\rangle\langle r|,\\
 \Pi\operatorname{vec}\widetilde W&=N^{-1/2}r .
 \end{split}
\]
Therefore the normalized cap-projected positive Gram is exactly
\[
 \Gamma_{\rm cap}
 =\frac{\Pi|\operatorname{vec}\widetilde W\rangle
                  \langle\operatorname{vec}\widetilde W|\Pi}
              {\|\Pi\operatorname{vec}\widetilde W\|^2}
 =|r\rangle\langle r|.
\]
Its reduced state on the two input heads is
\(\rho_{\rm in}=|e_0\rangle\langle e_0|\otimes I/N\).

Use the exact matrices from the
[bounded meridian theorem](actual_bounded_quantum_meridian_transport.md):
\[
 x=-e^{-\pi i/N},\qquad Ke_a=xQ^{-a}e_a,\qquad
 f e_a=(1-Q^{a+1})e_{a+1},
\]
with the last raising arrow zero. Its based meridians are
\[
 H_1=G_1,\qquad H_2=L_{-,1}^{-1}G_2L_{-,1},\qquad
 G=\begin{pmatrix}K&e\\fK&fe+K^{-1}\end{pmatrix},
 \quad L_-=\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\-Kf&K\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The actual Hurwitz identity is
\(\operatorname{Ad}_{\widetilde W}H_1=H_2\), so the first
closed-braid matching relation is \(H_2-H_1=0\). Its upper-left
entry is
\[
                         D=K_2-K_1-e_2K_1f_1 .
\]
Since \(f_1^*e_0=0\),
\[
 D^*(e_0\otimes e_a)
       =\overline{x}(Q^a-1)e_0\otimes e_a,\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{\rm in}DD^*)
       =\frac1N\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}|Q^a-1|^2=2 .
\]
The last equality uses \(\sum_aQ^a=0\), valid for every \(N\ge2\).
Right insertion on the input acts as
\(\mathsf R(D)=I_{\rm out}\otimes D^{\mathsf T}_{\rm in}\)
after the fixed factor permutation. Since \(\rho_{\rm in}\) is
real diagonal, its positive mean-square defect is thus
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\Gamma_{\rm cap}
                      \mathsf R(D)^*\mathsf R(D)\bigr)
 =\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\rho_{\rm in}(DD^*)^{\mathsf T}\bigr)
 =2 .
 \qquad}
\]
It does not tend to zero. In particular bounded quantum Hurwitz
transport cannot, by itself, turn this cap-projected positive Gram
into a state supported on the knot-character relations.

This conclusion concerns this specified positive reconstruction.
The original inserted source is
\(\Pi\mathsf R(D)\operatorname{vec}\widetilde W\), whereas
applying the insertion after projecting gives
\(\mathsf R(D)\Pi\operatorname{vec}\widetilde W\).
They cannot be interchanged without a proved insertion adapter.
The calculation neither changes the original invariant nor
excludes a different annotated positive lift. It also gives no
counterexample to the volume conjecture.
