## Positive matrix propagation without minimization, 22 November

The [orthogonal-error theorem](research_orthogonal_error_positive_conway_recursion.md)
gives an explicit positive matrix recursion for the same filled
source. It removes the variational solve. Its gain over simply
squaring the source is a positive regularization with a controlled
additive error in the original, unnormalized invariant.

Use the normalized complete compiler, with full boundary spaces
\(H_N\cong\mathbb C^N\), normalized leaf vectors \(a_\ell\), unary
maps \(A_v\), binary maps \(M_v\), and the original closing row
\(L\). Every normalized map and leaf has norm at most \(1/16\).
The known product of the original local budgets is \(B_N\), so
the true closed normalized scalar is \(K_N/B_N\). No closed source
value is needed to choose these budgets.

The simpler version adds orthogonal errors only at the original
leaves. Put \(\varepsilon_N=(NB_N^2)^{-1}\), and propagate
\[
 S_\ell=a_\ell a_\ell^*+\varepsilon_N I,\qquad
 S_v=A_vS_cA_v^*,\qquad
 S_v=M_v(S_l\otimes S_r)M_v^*.
\]
These are complete positive semidefinite matrices, including their
off-diagonal entries. At the unchanged original closing, define
\[
                       P_N=1+B_N^2 L S_{\rm top}L^* .
\]
The proved comparison is
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 1+|K_N|^2\le P_N\le1+|K_N|^2+\frac1{256}.
 \qquad}
\]
It includes zeros, even and composite levels, all phases and all
repeated-root derivative directions.

The orthogonality can be made literal Fourier orthogonality. At
each original leaf, use the \(N\) nonconstant characters of
\(\mathbb Z/(N+1)\) as vector-valued error directions with
covariance \(\varepsilon_N I\). Use independent character variables
at different leaf occurrences. The constant Fourier component of
the original assembled scalar is \(K_N/B_N\); every nonconstant
component is orthogonal to it. At a product the full second-moment
matrix is exactly \(M_v(S_l\otimes S_r)M_v^*\), rather than a sum
of separately squared entries of \(M_v\).

For completeness, let \(t_v\) be the trace of the error covariance
and \(h=N\varepsilon_N=B_N^{-2}\le1\). At a leaf \(t_v=h\);
a unary map gives \(t_v\le\sigma^2h\), where \(\sigma=1/16\).
At a binary map, the two single-child fluctuations and their product
are pairwise orthogonal, giving
\[
 t_v\le\sigma^4(t_l+t_r)+\sigma^2t_lt_r
       \le\sigma^2(2\sigma^2h+h^2)\le h.
\]
The root excess is therefore at most
\(B_N^2\|L\|^2h\le1/256\). There is no accumulated loss
per vertex. An alternative version adds the error also at every
internal vertex; it gives a strictly positive intermediate matrix
without any surjectivity assumption, with additive error \(1/128\).

There is another fixed-degree statement here. For a template with
\(l\) original leaf occurrences, the scalar obtained at variable
error variance \(\varepsilon\) is a polynomial of degree at most
\(l\):
\[
 B_N^2LS_{\rm top}(\varepsilon)L^*
      =|K_N|^2+\sum_{j=1}^l c_{N,j}\varepsilon^j,
       \qquad c_{N,j}\ge0.
\]
Each coefficient is a sum of squared norms of complete original
exterior contractions. The bound is independent of \(N\) and of
the lengths of unary corridors. The original scalar coefficients
have not been declared nonnegative.

The theorem also supplies local lower certificates. In the version
with errors at every vertex, take positive semidefinite \(Q_v^-\)
whose leaf values are at most \(a_\ell a_\ell^*+\varepsilon_N I\),
whose unary values are at most
\(A_vQ_c^-A_v^*+\varepsilon_N I\), and whose binary values are at
most \(M_v(Q_l^-\otimes Q_r^-)M_v^*+\varepsilon_N I\).
Induction in the positive-matrix order gives
\[
 |K_N|^2\ge
       \max\left(0,B_N^2LQ_{\rm top}^-L^*-\frac1{128}\right).
\]
Reversing the local inequalities gives upper certificates.
This keeps the full gluing Gram at every attachment. Constructing
such matrices at the Casson--Rivin volume rate is now a concrete
possible route to the missing lower bound.

The representation alone does not give that rate. At zero error,
the matrix recursion is simply the source contracted with its
conjugate. Also, \(\varepsilon_N\) can be exponentially small.
A rank-one approximation to an outgoing packet cannot be used as
a lower matrix just from a polynomially accurate angle estimate.
Explicitly, for \(\|\psi\|=1\) and \(w\ne0\),
\[
 s\psi\psi^*\preceq ww^*+\varepsilon I
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 s\le
 \frac{\varepsilon(\varepsilon+\|w\|^2)}
      {\varepsilon+\|w\|^2\sin^2\angle(\psi,w)}.
\]
Indeed conjugating by \((ww^*+\varepsilon I)^{-1/2}\)
reduces the condition to
\(s\,\psi^*(ww^*+\varepsilon I)^{-1}\psi\le1\);
decomposition along \(w\) gives the displayed formula.
General full-matrix certificates remain available.

Thus a positive limit \(\pi\log P_N/N\) is equivalent to the
original volume limit, and the recursion applies after any fixed
short partial assignment. Its geometric limit, including the
needed uniform local matrix inequalities, is still unproved.
The finite-exception theorem remains open.

The complete new 407-line proof is
\(\texttt{5506f489642f2ec118c4fef25cccc0485fecdc32ffccf09c700ac923c9da98dd}\).
Its complete sole direct proof source is the normalized compiler at
\(\texttt{6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c}\).
The general second-moment and transfer-operator method is standard;
the note gives a primary-literature pointer and proves the particular
source comparison in full. Only written mathematics, source reads
and text operations were used. Frozen manuscripts and public
documents remain unchanged.

## Sublinear observations through a fixed short word, 22 November

The [joint transport theorem](research_short_word_coherent_observation_transport.md)
now controls polynomial observations through every fixed sequence of
original crossings and turns. The packet and the observation must
be transported together. The comparison uses the norm of the newly
transported packet, whose rate can differ from its initial rate.

Let \(Z\) be multiplication by the original Casimir coordinate, let
\(J\) be the genuine turn, and let \(W\) be any fixed finite word
in \(J\) and integer powers of the original crossing \(R\).
The word and its exponents are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity;
all source scalars remain included. Use the coherent product packet
\(w_N(y,z)\) defined below. Its scalar input normalization cancels
from the following inequalities. All vector norms are the declared
Newton coefficient norm.

For each such word there are a radius \(0<\rho_W<1\), a constant
\(C_W<\infty\), and a level threshold such that
\[
 \begin{split}
 &e^{-C_WD}(D/N)^{24D}\|P\|_2^2\,\|Ww_N\|^2\\
 &\hspace{12mm}\le\|WP(Z)w_N\|^2
       \le e^{C_WD}\|P\|_2^2\,\|Ww_N\|^2
 \end{split}
\]
for \(1\le D\le N/32\), \(\deg P\le D\), and
\(|y|,|z|\le\rho_W\). Here \(\|P\|_2\) is its ordinary
monomial coefficient norm. For constant polynomials the comparison
is exact. Consequently every sequence of coefficient-normalized
observations with \(D_N=o(N)\) satisfies
\[
 \frac1N\log
 \frac{\|WP_N(Z)w_N\|^2}{\|Ww_N\|^2}\longrightarrow0
\]
uniformly on this small input bidisk. This conclusion does not
require knowing whether the denominator already has a volume limit.

The lower bound comes from an exact recovery operator, rather than
from a bound on the condition number of \(W\). Put \(L=JZJ\).
For every nonzero polynomial \(P\) of degree at most \(D\), the
proof constructs a polynomial in the two noncommuting operators
\(Z,L\) which sends \(P(Z)1\) to \(1\). Its degree is at most
\(5D\), and the sum of its absolute coefficients is at most
\[
             e^{CD}(N/D)^{12D}/\|P\|_2.
\]
The construction uses the actual monic kernel polynomials, their
positive three-term lowering coefficients, and finite spectral
filters on polynomial degree at most \(2D\). Every intermediate
degree stays in that range. The resulting operator identity acts
on the full original module.

Conjugating this recovery operator by \(WM_{w_N}\), where
\(M_{w_N}\) denotes multiplication by the actual packet, recovers
\(Ww_N\) from \(WP(Z)w_N\). Its two conjugated generators have
uniformly bounded norms on the stated small bidisk. The additional
source identity that proves this bound is
\[
 b_t(Z)M_tL_nM_t^{-1}
       =L_n-c_0tL_{n+1}+t^2L_{n+2}+8tI,
\]
where \(M_t\) is multiplication by the exact generating unit
\(A_N(t,\zeta)\), \(b_t(\zeta)=1+t\zeta+t^2\),
\(L_n=R^{-n}LR^n\), and \(c_0=2\cos(\pi/N)\).
This is an exact identity in the full repeated-root algebra.
The proof checks the spectral first normals, coalescing middle
points, endpoint seams and both level parities. These identities
bound the conjugated recovery operator and give the displayed
energy inequality after squaring.

This settles a compatibility estimate through fixed linear words
on a word-dependent small input bidisk. Binary tangle compositions
still need a compatible estimate, as does continuation to the
required geometric input domain. The new rate of \(\|Ww_N\|\)
and its prescribed scalar closing have not been evaluated. The
original closing row stays unchanged throughout the proof; no
lower bound for that scalar follows from the vector inequality.
The finite-exception theorem remains open.

The complete new proof is the 509-line note at
`ff2fbaaa56c48bc6845bd58f964e10de66483df550a4b30005aed244ff0a0398`.
Its complete direct sources are the generating-tensor theorem at
`8426410354feb509c2780e1207613899bda8ab5eb46ad22fd4ab008bf5841bf1`,
the full crossing transport at
`f81b9fc3edc2504c5250ad283bf0ceff191a1fc3a310c00fdb57602362f0bf4a`,
the finite-band conjugation at
`31d9f574c7dc3aaac07e4eb50c131b3328be46b3c2a2ef46f9dae7f0c4ddb9cb`,
and the kernel difference theorem at
`5d0d07d4d97d82cca66e0e0c3bf2cecad8e5f58ef8329178278b297cf0d6c5da`.
Only written mathematics and text operations were used. Frozen
manuscripts and public documents remain unchanged.

## Observation degree may grow sublinearly with the level, 22 November

The [exact rational Newton calculation](research_sublinear_casimir_observation_energy.md)
removes the restriction in the earlier fixed-degree observation
argument. It applies to the same actual packet
\(w_N(y,z)=u_N(y)u_N(z)\) and the same centered/Newton coefficient
norm, with the normalized inputs defined in the next section and
\(\zeta\) the original Casimir coordinate. Every polynomial
observation of degree \(D_N=o(N)\), with
coefficient norm one, has the same exponential energy rate as
\(w_N\). The polynomial and its coefficients may change at every
level. The statement is uniform on compact input bidisks.

More precisely, fix \(|y|,|z|\le\rho<1\). There are constants
\(\delta_\rho,c_\rho,C_\rho>0\) and \(N_\rho\), independent of
the observation degree, such that for \(N\ge N_\rho\),
\(0\le D\le\delta_\rho N\) and \(\deg P\le D\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 &c_\rho N^{-1/2}
 e^{-C_\rho D-C_\rho(D+1)^2/N}
 \left(\frac{D!}{N^D}\right)^2
 \|P\|_2^2\,\|w_N\|^2\\
 &\hspace{12mm}\le\|P(\zeta)w_N\|^2
 \le(D+1)36^D\|P\|_2^2\,\|w_N\|^2.
 \end{split}
\]
Here \(\|P\|_2\) is its ordinary monomial coefficient norm,
and \(0!=1\). The negative logarithm of the lower factor is
\[
 O_\rho\!\left(\log N+D+(D+1)^2/N+D\log(N/D)\right)
\]
when \(D\ge1\). It is \(o(N)\) for \(D=o(N)\).
Thus, for coefficient-normalized \(P_N\) of sublinear degree,
\[
 \frac1N\log
 \frac{\|P_N(\zeta)w_N(y,z)\|^2}{\|w_N(y,z)\|^2}
                  \longrightarrow0.
\]
The same conclusion allows \(\log\|P_N\|_2=o(N)\); an upper
bound alone would permit an exponentially small scalar multiplier.

The proof uses exact formulas, rather than substituting a growing
degree into the constants of the earlier fixed-degree estimate.
In the monic Newton basis, the observed packet divided by its
nonzero output rows is a rational Newton polynomial. Its numerator
has degree at most \(D\), and recovering the observation coefficients
costs at most \(C_\rho^D\), uniformly for every \(D<N\).
Interpolation on \(D+1\) actual consecutive rows near the positive
energy maximum costs at most \(N^D/D!\). The exact positive row
weights give the displayed lower bound. All output coefficients and
the full Hermite algebra remain present.

There is an exact reason not to extend this to arbitrary short
fillings by calling their polynomial degree bounded. At \(y=z=0\),
\[
 w_N(0,0)=R^2/N,\qquad
 R^{-1}w_N(0,0)=R/N,\qquad \|R/N\|^2=1/N.
\]
The first packet has positive exponential norm rate by the output
theorem, whereas the last has rate zero. Multiplication by one
genuine inverse crossing therefore changes this forward rate.
This uses the Newton coefficient norm of \(R\); it makes no claim
about its ordinary monomial coefficient norm. A fixed crossing can
require Casimir degree \(N-1\). Its short word length does not put
it in the sublinear-degree theorem.

For a short word \(W\), transporting an observation means retaining
\(WP(\zeta)w_N\), together with the actual closing row. Replacing
this by \(P(\zeta)Ww_N\) changes the observation family. The
untransported observation result and bounded conjugated operator norms
alone do not give the needed lower bound. The joint theorem above
supplies it on a word-dependent small input bidisk using the additional
exact recovery operator. Binary composition, the changed geometric
action and the final scalar observation still require proof. No new
knot-volume identity or finite-exception conclusion has been obtained.

The complete new proof is the 350-line note at
`6aa7861fcd10eac082f04b2c9e4af17dd47c118fe4c7a9a704ceeabbb1ce4539`.
Its complete direct sources are the output theorem at
`73152328a77ba5d63a2a8eaa17647ed38b7683c613e0947e3bda9e451dda76e2`
and the centered compiler at
`0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413`.
The scope calculation above follows from their exact signed crossing
and normalized input identities. Only written mathematics and text
operations were used; frozen manuscripts and public documents remain
unchanged.

## A full output norm from one positive sum, 22 November

For two explicit input packets, an intermediate norm calculation can
now be completed directly. It requires neither a variational solve nor
separate estimates on the output coefficients. This is a forward
estimate in the centered coefficient norm, equivalently the positive
Newton Gram; it does not use the uniform physical Hilbert--Schmidt
metric.

At level \(N\ge2\), in the full centered basis, put
\[
 Z_N(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}|t|^{2a},\qquad
 u_N(t)=\frac{\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}t^af_a}{\sqrt{Z_N(t)}},\qquad
 w_N(y,z)=u_N(y)u_N(z),\quad |y|,|z|<1.
\]
The product is the original algebra multiplication. Fourier Parseval
and the exact wall products express \(\|w_N\|^2\) as one finite
positive sum, with every output channel retained. Its rate is
\[
 E(u;y,z)=2\int_0^u\log\left|
 \frac{(1-e^{2\pi is})(1-yze^{2\pi is})}
 {(1+ye^{2\pi is})(1+ze^{2\pi is})}\right|\,ds.
\]
For every complex input pair in the open bidisk, \(E\) has exactly
one global maximum \(E_*>0\), at a point \(u_*\in(0,1)\), and
\(E''(u_*)<0\). The proof reduces \(E'=0\) to one cosine
equation. Its two roots are simple; the second is the unique maximum.
The exact products also give an endpoint-uniform envelope, so neither
end of the finite sum is omitted.

The [full-output proof](research_centered_coherent_product_energy.md)
then gives
\[
 \|w_N(y,z)\|^2
   =N^{-1/2}c_N(y,z)e^{NE_*}(1+O(N^{-1})),
\]
where \(c_N\) is explicit and bounded above and away from zero on
every compact input bidisk. The entire normalized Newton output has
a complex Gaussian approximation with error \(O(N^{-1/2})\) in
\(\ell^2\). Its original carrier and overall phase are specified.
These assertions hold along the full sequence of levels.

There is also stability under a fixed algebraic operation. The
[insertion proof](research_casimir_inserted_coherent_product_energy.md)
establishes, for every fixed nonzero polynomial \(P\) in the original
Casimir coordinate \(\zeta\),
\[
 \frac1N\log\|P(\zeta)w_N(y,z)\|^2\longrightarrow E_*(y,z)
\]
locally uniformly in the input bidisk. It proves an exact inserted
Pearson identity whose finite boundary source includes both a value
and its first normal. On the generating sampling grid, that source
vanishes exactly. The inserted observation is then uniformly
\(P(\Lambda)+O(N^{-1})\), with an explicit nonconstant rational
Casimir \(\Lambda\). A zero at the maximizing point does not remove
the rate: a nearby interval still contributes to the positive sum.

There is a quantitative consequence which also permits the coefficients
of \(P\) to depend on \(N\). Fix an integer \(D\ge0\) and a compact
input bidisk \(|y|,|z|\le\rho<1\). Write
\(\|P\|_{2}^{2}=\sum_{k=0}^D|p_k|^2\) for
\(P(\zeta)=\sum_{k=0}^Dp_k\zeta^k\). There are constants
\(c,C>0\) and \(N_0>D\), depending only on \(\rho,D\), such that
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 cN^{-D}\|P\|_2^2\,\|w_N\|^2
 \le \|P(\zeta)w_N\|^2
 \le C\|P\|_2^2\,\|w_N\|^2
 \quad(N\ge N_0,\ \deg P\le D).
 \quad}
\]
Equivalently, the actual Hermitian Gram matrix of
\(w_N,\zeta w_N,\ldots,\zeta^Dw_N\), divided by
\(\|w_N\|^2\), lies between \(cN^{-D}I\) and \(CI\).
It retains the cross terms between these observations. A coefficient
vector of norm one therefore loses at most a polynomial factor in
energy, even if it is chosen separately at every level to cancel
the leading value at the maximum.

Here is a complete proof from the two cited theorems. In the insertion
proof set \(\mathbf t=(x,y,z)\), with
\[
 q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad X_j=-qQ^j,\qquad
 \Lambda(x,y,z)=1-\frac{x+y+z+xy+xz+yz}{1+xyz}.
\]
Its exact wall multiplier has the form
\[
 r_{N,P}(x,y,z)=\frac{B_{N,P}(x;y,z)}{A_{N,D}(x;y,z)},\qquad
 A_{N,D}=\prod_{k=0}^{D-1}(qQ^k+xyz),\quad \deg_xB_{N,P}\le D.
\]
Every coefficient of the inserted Pearson operator is affine in \(x\).
Induction in its triangular recurrence, using the displayed common
denominator, proves the numerator degree assertion. This is valid
also for a polynomial of degree less than \(D\), by inserting the
remaining denominator factors. On \(|x|=1\),
\[
 (1-\rho^2)^D\le |A_{N,D}|\le(1+\rho^2)^D.
\]
The linear coefficient map \(P\mapsto B_{N,P}\) converges uniformly
on the input bidisk to
\[
             P\longmapsto(1+xyz)^DP(\Lambda(x,y,z)).
\]
This follows either from that finite recurrence or its fixed-degree
limit. The limiting map is invertible on the \((D+1)\)-dimensional
polynomial coefficient space. Indeed \(\Lambda\) is a nonconstant
Möbius function of \(x\), since
\[
 \partial_x\Lambda=
 -\frac{(1+y)(1+z)(1-yz)}{(1+xyz)^2}\ne0.
\]
A polynomial with zero image would consequently vanish on an open
set. Continuity and compactness give uniform upper and lower singular
value bounds for the limiting coefficient map, and then for the exact
map at all sufficiently large \(N\). In particular
\(\|B_{N,P}\|_2\ge c\|P\|_2\).

Let \(\mu_{N,j}\) be the normalized output weights from the first
theorem. The exact Fourier identity in the insertion proof says
\[
 \frac{\|P(\zeta)w_N\|^2}{\|w_N\|^2}
       =\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\mu_{N,j}|r_{N,P}(X_j,y,z)|^2.
\]
The upper bound follows from the coefficient-map bound and the
denominator lower bound. For the lower bound retain the actual peak
window
\[
 s_j=\frac{j+1/2-Nu_*}{\sqrt N},\quad |s_j|\le1,\qquad
 x_*=-e^{2\pi iu_*}.
\]
The bulk amplitude and full norm asymptotic give
\(\mu_{N,j}\ge c/\sqrt N\) uniformly on this window.
Expand \(B_{N,P}(x)=\sum_{k=0}^Db_k(x-x_*)^k\) and put
\(a_k=N^{-k/2}b_k\). At its sampling points this expansion is
\[
 B_{N,P}(X_j)=\sum_{k=0}^Da_k
 \left[\sqrt N\,x_*(e^{2\pi is_j/\sqrt N}-1)\right]^k.
\]
The functions in brackets, raised to powers \(0,\ldots,D\),
converge uniformly on \([-1,1]\) to \((2\pi ix_*s)^k\).
Their sampling mesh has spacing \(N^{-1/2}\). Thus their discrete
Gram matrices with weights \(N^{-1/2}\) converge uniformly, including
all mesh shifts and \(|x_*|=1\), to the positive definite monomial
Gram on \([-1,1]\). Their least eigenvalues are bounded below by
a positive constant depending only on \(D\). Consequently
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{|s_j|\le1}|B_{N,P}(X_j)|^2
 \ge c_D\sum_{k=0}^D|a_k|^2
 \ge c_DN^{-D}\sum_{k=0}^D|b_k|^2
 \ge c_D' N^{-D}\|B_{N,P}\|_2^2.
\]
The last step uses the uniformly invertible Taylor change of
coefficients at \(|x_*|=1\). Combining this with the actual positive
weights, the denominator upper bound and the coefficient-map lower
bound proves the boxed inequality. No error from a Gaussian vector
approximation has been divided by a small observation.

Here \(D\) is independent of \(N\). This is a different condition
from degree four of the variational objective. A general short
component can require Casimir degree \(N-1\), and the Gram estimate
supplies no uniform constants for that sequence.

The original closing is still a separate observation. Indeed this
same family satisfies exactly
\[
 \phi_N(w_N(y,z))=
 \frac{\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}(yz)^a}{\sqrt{Z_N(y)Z_N(z)}},
\]
which stays bounded on compact bidisks while the internal norm grows
exponentially. Thus the new result supplies a controlled forward
packet and its phase; it does not establish a scalar volume lower
bound. Compatibility through general short components and their
prescribed closing remains open, as does the finite-exception theorem.

The complete proof texts are the 393-line output theorem at
`73152328a77ba5d63a2a8eaa17647ed38b7683c613e0947e3bda9e451dda76e2`
and the 450-line insertion theorem at
`b89c9c0ded6d6f68bb6c4581f0445573cece022718eea86e4a5a95b84c9e697e`.
Their complete direct sources are the wall theorem at
`3cda6a170c46abf27a1c8c15b110780ebcb6017a5aa18758a4e51ba0a271892c`,
the centered compiler at
`0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413`,
and the full tensor theorem at
`8426410354feb509c2780e1207613899bda8ab5eb46ad22fd4ab008bf5841bf1`.
Only written proofs and text operations were used. Frozen manuscripts
and public documents remain unchanged.

## Closed products for the full branching tensor, 22 November

The [full-tensor proof](research_centered_fourier_full_tensor_source.md)
extends the calculation from signed slices to every coefficient of
the universal Conway tensor. Its generating polynomial is one finite
sum over the physical Casimir nodes, with closed products, explicit
quadratic Gaussian weights and all first-normal terms. The same proof
gives an actual complex upper bound on fixed parameter discs. Its
exponent is not yet the selected geometric action of a filled knot.

Keep \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\),
\(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), where \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial
of the first kind. Use the complete algebra
\(\mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N)\) and its original Frobenius
closing \(\phi_N\). Write \(R=R^+\) for the
original positive crossing. The centered modes have
\(f_a=N^{-1/2}R p_a(z)\), with \(p_a\) an ordinary polynomial
of degree \(a\). Define
\[
 A_N(t,z)=\sum_{a=0}^dp_a(z)t^a,\qquad
 \mathscr C_N(t_1,t_2,t_3)=\sum_{a,b,c=0}^d
                    \phi_N(f_af_bf_c)t_1^at_2^bt_3^c.
\]
The exact polynomial equation is
\[
 (1+zt+t^2)A_N(t,z)-(1+q^{-1}t)^2A_N(Q^{-1}t,z)
       =\frac{(-1)^d}{N}P_N(z)t^N.
\]
The proof solves it at every physical node by closed finite products
and separately solves its differentiated equation at every double
node. Substitution into the original trace gives all tensor
coefficients through the identity
\[
 \mathscr C_N(\mathbf t)
       =N^{-3/2}\phi_N\!\left(R^3\prod_{i=1}^3A_N(t_i,z)\right).
\]
The Gaussian-node sum is formula (22) of that proof. In particular,
ordinary values have not replaced the independent spectral normals.

There is a concrete algebraic cyclic equation behind these products.
Put \(g(t,z)=(1+zt+t^2)/(1+q^{-1}t)^2\). Then
\[
 \prod_{r=0}^{N-1}g(Q^{-r}t,z)
 =1-\frac{(-1)^NP_N(z)t^N}{[1+(-1)^Nt^N]^2}.
\]
Thus its cyclic product is one on the full nonreduced algebra.
In \(\mathcal H_N\otimes\mathbb C(t)\), the equation
\(A(Q^{-1}t,z)=g(t,z)A(t,z)\) has the explicit invertible
solution \(A_N\). All invertible solutions differ from it by an
invertible element of \(\mathcal H_N\otimes\mathbb C(t^N)\).
This describes the solution torsor without assuming a Hilbert 90
theorem for a nonreduced ring. Polynomial degree less than \(N\)
and value one at \(t=0\) select the original solution. It is a
local generating kernel, not an identification of the whole knot
invariant with a regulator.

For \(|v|=1\) and \(|t|<1\), set
\[
 \mathcal S(v,t)=\frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(-vt)
       +\operatorname{Li}_2(-v^{-1}t)-2\operatorname{Li}_2(-t)}{2\pi i},
 \qquad v_j=e^{(2j+1)\pi i/N}.
\]
Here \(\operatorname{Li}_2(w)=\sum_{k\ge1}w^k/k^2\).
The actual node products satisfy
\(\log A_N(t,v_j+v_j^{-1})=N\mathcal S(v_j,t)+O_r(1)\)
uniformly on every fixed \(|t|\le r<1\). Their relative first
normals at the double nodes cost at most \(C_rN\). Consequently
\[
 |\mathscr C_N(\mathbf t)|\le C_rN^{1/2}
   \exp\!\left\{N\max_{0\le j\le\lfloor d/2\rfloor}
        \Re\sum_{i=1}^3\mathcal S(v_j,t_i)\right\},
                         \qquad |t_i|\le r<1.
\]
This is an estimate for the exact polynomial on complex discs, not
an estimate obtained by substituting a formal factorial expansion.
Taking absolute values of the node sum may lose cancellations, so
sharpness is not asserted.

There is also a useful consequence for genuine turns on any of the
three attaching legs. Let \(\sharp\) conjugate polynomial coefficients
and fix the formal variables \(t,z\). The compiler gives
\(f_a^\sharp=f_{d-a}\) and \(R^\sharp=R^{-1}\), hence, in the
full algebra,
\[
                  t^d A_N(t^{-1},z)=R^{-2}A_N^\sharp(t,z).
\]
For a subset \(I\subset\{1,2,3\}\), let \(\mathscr C_N^I\)
be the polynomial obtained by replacing the exponent \(a_i\) by
\(d-a_i\) on exactly those legs. Then
\[
 \mathscr C_N^I(\mathbf t)=N^{-3/2}\phi_N\!\left[
 R^{3-2|I|}\prod_{i\notin I}A_N(t_i,z)
                    \prod_{i\in I}A_N^\sharp(t_i,z)\right].
\]
Indeed the displayed reciprocal identity follows by conjugating
\(f_a=N^{-1/2}Rp_a\), and substitution proves the formula.
This attaches the literal turn to a tensor leg; it does not commute
a turn through multiplication. All spectral normals are retained.

For \(|v|=1\), \(\overline{\mathcal S(v,\bar t)}=-\mathcal S(v,t)\).
The same node proof therefore gives the preceding upper bound with
\(\sum_i\varepsilon_i\mathcal S(v_j,t_i)\), where
\(\varepsilon_i=-1\) for \(i\in I\) and \(+1\) otherwise.
The crossing power \(n=3-2|I|\) is always one of \(3,1,-1,-3\).
At a double node \(c_j=v_j+v_j^{-1}\), its weighted contribution
\((4-c_j^2)(R^n)'(c_j)/R^n(c_j)\) to the original trace is
\(O(N)\), which preserves the \(N^{1/2}\) bound. This handles all
eight leg orientations at the generating-polynomial level. It supplies neither
a full geometric metric nor a sharp whole-component comparison.

The complete proof is the 482-line full-tensor note at
`8426410354feb509c2780e1207613899bda8ab5eb46ad22fd4ab008bf5841bf1`.
Its two complete direct sources are the centered compiler at
`0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413`
and the Hermite phase-transport proof at
`0985159d134d82a404bd07973cf5ee55eb78c115e154465cbeac1b201c1c2686`.
The mixed-turn consequence is derived above. Generic Al-Salam--Chihara
generating functions are standard and credited in the proof; no
infinite-product specialization at a root of unity is assumed.

## A fixed fraction of signed crossing modes has a bounded Hardy chart, 22 November

The [Hardy-chart proof](research_signed_fourier_contracting_hardy_chart.md)
also gives a phase-sensitive estimate for individual signed-block
entries. For every fixed \(0<\alpha<1/6\), it covers all output
channels and the input modes \(f_{N-m}\),
\(1\le m\le M_N=\lfloor\alpha N\rfloor+1\).
The normalized entries are exact polynomials satisfying
\[
 A_1^{\rm band}(w)=1,\qquad
 A_{m+1}^{\rm band}(w)=1+w(1-Q^{-m})A_m^{\rm band}(w).
\]
On a fixed disc containing the unit circle, this recurrence is
contracting on the stated band. It proves the uniform relative
approximation
\[
 A_m^{\rm band}(w)
       =\frac{1+O_\alpha(N^{-1})}{1-(1-Q^{-(m-1)})w}
\]
and zero-freeness for sufficiently large \(N\). With
\(\rho_\alpha=2\sin(\pi\alpha)<1\) and \(\Pi_{\alpha,N}\)
the projection onto those input modes, the exact operator obeys
\[
 \|M_{R^+}\Pi_{\alpha,N}\|_{\rm op}
       \le\sqrt{\frac{M_N}{N(1-\rho_\alpha^2)}}.
\]
The output has not been projected: every Hermite channel remains.
The proof constructs its exact polynomial Hardy Gram and its Szegő
kernel approximation, retaining both original closing functionals.
In particular the original Frobenius closing annihilates the exact
crossing outputs: \(\phi_N M_{R^+}\Pi_{\alpha,N}=0\).
The rational kernel approximation generally does not. It therefore
cannot be substituted for the exact polynomial to obtain a lower
source bound. No invariance of the input band under subsequent
turns or branching is proved.

The 332-line proof has SHA-256
`7825174a942d38d9cb09b4f8ef389a5fda77f45bfd51ef4f0653b21b9da0b3f4`.
Its complete direct sources are the signed-slice proof at
`71abfe35c8c005589762b9a5dc672dfa4c5ce95d0c7a12fddae8ad2f1586336d`
and the centered compiler at
`0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413`.
Neither result proves a new knot class or the finite-exception theorem.

## One factorial Fourier sum for each signed crossing block, 22 November

The [signed-block proof](research_centered_fourier_signed_slice.md)
now evaluates a universal part of the Conway compiler without expanding
its multiplication paths separately. This is a calculation of the
same block at every level and Fourier index, not a list of knot cases.
Its individual complex entries retain their phases, while their full
row energies have a positive formula.

Use the centered orthonormal basis \(f_a\) of the complete Newton
algebra and its original Frobenius functional \(\phi_N\), and put
\[
 C_{abc}=\phi_N(f_af_bf_c),\qquad
 d=N-1,\quad Q=e^{2\pi i/N},\quad
 F_r=(Q;Q)_r=\prod_{j=1}^r(1-Q^j),\quad s_r=|F_r|.
\]
Empty products are one. The signed crossings are \(\sqrt N f_0\)
and \(\sqrt N f_d\). The exact formula for \(C_{0bc}\) in the
proof expresses it through the single finite sum
\[
 \mathcal S_c(x)=\sum_{r=c}^dF_rx^r,\qquad x=Q^{-b},
\]
with every carrier and Fourier phase specified. Finite Parseval then
gives the entire row energy
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \sum_{b=0}^d|C_{0bc}|^2
       =\frac1{N^2s_c^2}\sum_{r=c}^ds_r^2.
 \qquad}
\]
For the negative crossing, replace \(c\) by \(d-c\).
The proof also gives a uniform exponential profile for all these
energies, including both endpoints, from the single real function
\(J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du\).
It does not infer the rate of an individual complex entry from its
row energy.

There is an exact equation for the remaining phase-sensitive sum:
\[
       (1-x)\mathcal S_c(x)+Qx\mathcal S_c(Qx)=F_cx^c.
\]
It follows from \(F_r=(1-Q^r)F_{r-1}\); the upper-end remainder
vanishes because \(Q^N=1\). The lower-end term is retained.
Writing \(g_b=\mathcal S_c(Q^{-b})\) gives
\[
 (1-Q^{-b})g_b+Q^{1-b}g_{b-1}=F_cQ^{-bc},
                         \qquad b\pmod N.
\]
The row \(b=0\) fixes \(g_{N-1}=F_c/Q\); the remaining rows
determine all the other values by backward substitution without
dividing by \(1-Q^{-b}\). This is exact boundary transport, not
an inverse-norm estimate.

The same equation records a small source extension explicitly. Put
\(\xi_c(x)=F_cx^c\) and \((\sigma h)(x)=h(Qx)\). Away from
\(x=0\),
\[
 \binom{\mathcal S_c(Qx)}{\xi_c(Qx)}
 =\begin{pmatrix}(x-1)/(Qx)&1/(Qx)\\0&Q^c\end{pmatrix}
       \binom{\mathcal S_c(x)}{\xi_c(x)}.
\]
Thus a homogeneous annihilator is the ordered operator
\[
              (\sigma-Q^c)\bigl[(1-x)+Qx\sigma\bigr].
\]
These statements follow by applying \(\sigma-Q^c\) to the exact
forcing equation; the relation \(\sigma x=Qx\sigma\) fixes the
order. The inhomogeneous equation and its polynomial normalization
specify the original sum. The homogeneous annihilator alone does
not retain that normalization. This two-component description is
for one fixed \(c\); it does not replace the full \(N\)-dimensional
boundary algebra or the arbitrary-input crossing matrix.

The full three-index tensor \(C_{abc}\) at a genuine branching
vertex still needs a compatible estimate, and the original closing
functional remains part of the source. Neither the positive row
energy nor the local annihilator supplies that missing comparison.
No new knot class or finite-exception conclusion is drawn.

The complete proof is the 319-line signed-block note at
`71abfe35c8c005589762b9a5dc672dfa4c5ce95d0c7a12fddae8ad2f1586336d`.
Its two complete direct sources are the
[centered compiler](research_centered_fourier_conway_compiler.md) at
`0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413`
and the [crossing covariance proof](research_actual_newton_crossing_gaussian_covariance.md)
at `ce2b1b8efbbcffa8bafe0d0de4f7ce12febf193e433d8e3291f7d2a8c826fa3f`.
The two-component transport and ordered annihilator are derived above.

## A local calibration controls its own metric window, 22 November

An explicit change of reference gives a quantitative lower certificate
without estimating a spectral cutoff at an unknown minimizer. A small
constant density mismatch suffices if the local calibration constants
nearly attain the known norms in that reference. The required geometric
reference and witnesses have not been constructed.

Use the exact anchored tree with output \(Y_N=(1,K_N)\), including
its original closing, phases and full Hermite spaces. Let \(m\ge2\)
count all vertices and \(n_e\) be the edge-space dimensions. Choose
prescribed invertible edge changes \(G_e\), with the inverse acting at
the other end of each bilinear contraction. Write \(\overline T_v\)
for the resulting tensors. This retains \(Y_N\) exactly. All metrics
below are relative to this supplied reference; the reference changes
themselves need not be well conditioned. Put
\[
 L(H)=\sum_v\log\|\overline T_v\|_H,\quad L_0=L(I),\quad
 Z(H)=1+\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(H_e+H_e^{-1}),\quad R(H)=\log Z(H),
 \quad Q=Z(I)=1+2\sum_en_e,\quad \ell=\log\|Y_N\|.
\]
The original finite tensors and the specified reference determine
\(L_0\) before evaluating the closed scalar.

Choose valid full-metric local calibrations, including the literal
leaf and original closing calibrations. The
[ordered-density inequality](research_ordered_density_bilinear_calibration.md)
supplies such families for the transformed surjective maps after their
positive factors are recomputed. A nonunitary change of reference does
not automatically transport an old calibration density.
Suppose their sum is
\[
 L(H)\ge B+\frac12\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(\Delta_e\log H_e)
 \qquad\hbox{for every }H>0,\qquad
 B=\sum_v\beta_v,\quad
 \Delta_e=\rho_{{\rm child},e}-\rho_{{\rm parent},e}^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The transpose is prescribed by the original bilinear pairing. All
half-edge densities are Hermitian positive semidefinite of trace one;
they are independent calibration data, not asserted actual tensor
marginals. Define
\[
                    E=L_0-B\ge0,\qquad
                    \delta=\sum_e\|\Delta_e\|_1 .
\]
The inequality \(E\ge0\) follows by setting \(H=I\).

Fix \(0<t\le s_0=1/(512m^2)\), independently of \(N\), and let
\[
 H_t=\operatorname*{argmin}_{H>0}\{L(H)+tR(H)\},\qquad
 L_t=L(H_t),\quad R_t=R(H_t).
\]
The [capacity](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md) and
[regularization](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md)
proofs apply in this reference because \(\|Y_N\|\ge1\). They give
existence, uniqueness, full marginal mismatch at most \(2t\), and
\[
                         \ell\le L_t\le\ell+\log2 .
\]
Indeed the tree comparison factor is at least
\(1-4m\sqrt{2t}-10mt>1/2\).

If \(\delta<2t\), the self-calibrating estimates are
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 R_t\le\frac{E+t\log Q}{t-\delta/2},\qquad
 0\le L_0-\ell
 \le\frac{2t}{2t-\delta}E
          +\frac{t\delta}{2t-\delta}\log Q+\log2 .
 \quad}
\]
For proof, every eigenvalue of \(H_e\) and its reciprocal is at most
\(Z(H)\), hence \(\|\log H_e\|_{\rm op}\le R(H)\).
The assembled calibration and comparison with the identity trial give
\[
 L_t\ge B-\frac{\delta}{2}R_t,\qquad
 L_t+tR_t\le L_0+t\log Q .
\]
Subtracting proves
\((t-\delta/2)R_t\le E+t\log Q\). Then
\(\ell\ge L_t-\log2\ge B-\delta R_t/2-\log2\)
gives the second bound. Its nonnegative left side is tree Cauchy at
the supplied reference. No metric derivative or limit interchange is
used, and no penalty of order \(N\) has been discarded.

In particular, if \(\delta\le t\), then
\[
 R_t\le 2E/t+2\log Q,\qquad
              0\le L_0-\ell\le2E+t\log Q+\log2 .
\]
For a fixed template \(Q\) is polynomial in \(N\). Thus
\(E=O(\log N)\) gives \(R_t=O(\log N)\) and polynomial spectral
conditioning relative to the supplied reference. It does not bound
the raw-coordinate condition numbers of the \(G_e\).
More generally \(E=o(N)\) suffices for \(L_0\) and the anchored norm
to have the same leading rate. A positive common rate is also the
original scalar rate. These conclusions require the stated
calibrations on the entire metric cone, not only near a Gaussian
stationary point.

This accommodates mixed ordered witnesses. For pure maximal singular
witnesses much of its rate consequence is already covered by the
compatible-singular-vector criterion below. An arbitrary normalized
geometric Gaussian is not automatically an ordered density for the
actual full positive factor. We have constructed neither a suitable
geometric reference, matching witnesses with small \(E,\delta\), nor
the Casson--Rivin rate of \(L_0\). No new knot class or finite-exception
theorem follows.

The four complete matching proof texts are:

- [Ordered-density calibration](research_ordered_density_bilinear_calibration.md),
  SHA-256 928322373f35eee6692949953a91a592d9486b3507ffa439db5fbbc5729e516a.
- [Full tree capacity](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md),
  SHA-256 2997b732aa73e063c66e81d6487a1d9927509609d61842c1dbb43d9345df1d6d.
- [Regularized capacity](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md),
  SHA-256 0cea0d52182eb24b4610538f354dbe5158fa54aa6f9cf7f9fc280c72ab090ff8.
- [Anchored compiler](research_anchored_conway_positive_variational_period.md),
  SHA-256 e83c35d16c79faa13ac6556db78b9b57da2a2371d3fc04c4673ecd74e1d336f7.

The quantitative comparison is proved above. Only written mathematics
and text operations were used; earlier finals and public documents
are unchanged.

## Two fixed penalty strengths remove the regularizer from the rate problem, 22 November

The fixed-degree formulation admits a further simplification at the
exponential scale: the rate problem can be stated without a quartic
objective. Two fixed penalized minimum values suffice; we need not
differentiate those
values or estimate and subtract a penalty at an unknown minimizer.
The statement is a finite-level comparison with the original source,
not an evaluation of its geometric rate.

Use the [anchored compiler](research_anchored_conway_positive_variational_period.md)
with output \(Y_N=(1,K_N)\), including its original closing map,
phases and full physical boundary spaces. Let its fixed tree have
\(m\ge2\) vertices, and set
\[
 \ell_N=\log\|Y_N\|=\tfrac12\log(1+|K_N|^2).
\]
For positive full edge metrics \(H\), define
\[
 L_N(H)=\sum_v\log\|T_{v,N}\|_H,\qquad
 R(H)=\log\left(1+\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(H_e+H_e^{-1})\right),
 \qquad j_N(s)=\min_{H>0}\{L_N(H)+sR(H)\},\quad s>0.
\]
All tensors in these definitions are prescribed before evaluating
\(K_N\). The [capacity proof](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md)
and [regularization proof](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md)
apply to this compiler because \(\|Y_N\|\ge1\). They give a unique
minimizer \(H_{N,s}\) and full marginal defect at most \(2s\).
Put \(s_0=1/(512m^2)\). For \(0<s\le s_0\), the tree estimate gives
\[
 \frac{\|Y_N\|}{\exp L_N(H_{N,s})}
 \ge 1-4m\sqrt{2s}-10ms
 \ge\frac34-\frac5{256m}>\frac12.
\]
Tree Cauchy gives the other inequality. Thus
\[
             \ell_N\le L_N(H_{N,s})\le\ell_N+\log2
                         \qquad(0<s\le s_0).
\]

Fix \(r>1\) and \(t>0\) with \(rt\le s_0\), independently of
\(N\). Define a number using only two penalized minimum values:
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 A_N(t,r)=\frac{rj_N(t)-j_N(rt)}{r-1}.
 \qquad}
\]
Then the exact comparison is
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \ell_N\le A_N(t,r)\le\ell_N+\log2.
 \qquad}
\]
In particular one may take \(r=2\), \(t=1/(1024m^2)\), so that
\(A_N=2j_N(t)-j_N(2t)\). Neither strength tends to zero.

The proof uses only optimality at these two strengths. Abbreviate
\(L_s=L_N(H_{N,s})\), \(R_s=R(H_{N,s})\), and put
\(\Delta L=L_{rt}-L_t\), \(\Delta R=R_t-R_{rt}\).
Using each minimizer as a trial for the other problem gives
\[
 L_t+tR_t\le L_{rt}+tR_{rt},\qquad
 L_{rt}+rtR_{rt}\le L_t+rtR_t,
 \qquad t\Delta R\le\Delta L\le rt\Delta R.
\]
In particular \(\Delta R\ge0\). Direct subtraction now yields
\[
 A_N(t,r)-L_t=\frac{rt\Delta R-\Delta L}{r-1}\ge0,
 \qquad
 A_N(t,r)-L_{rt}=\frac{r(t\Delta R-\Delta L)}{r-1}\le0.
\]
Hence \(L_t\le A_N(t,r)\le L_{rt}\), which proves the bounds.
No differentiation, interpolation between the minimizers, or uniqueness
is needed for this last argument. It retains a penalty that can be
of order \(N\), rather than declaring that penalty negligible.

Equivalently, \(P_N=\exp(2A_N(t,r))\) is a positive proxy satisfying
\[
                  1+|K_N|^2\le P_N\le4(1+|K_N|^2).
\]
These logarithmic metric problems are not being assigned a
degree-four semidefinite formulation by this comparison.

For any \(V>0\), including the volume of a hyperbolic knot
complement, we have therefore proved the equivalence
\[
 \frac{2\pi}{N}A_N(t,r)\longrightarrow V
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|\longrightarrow V.
\]
The positive limiting rate removes the anchor and gives eventual
nonvanishing; nonvanishing is not a premise. More explicitly, if the
two limits \(2\pi j_N(t)/N\to J(t)\) and
\(2\pi j_N(rt)/N\to J(rt)\) have independently been proved, the
anchored source-norm rate is
\[
                         \frac{rJ(t)-J(rt)}{r-1}.
\]
It is also the original scalar rate when this number is positive.
Approximate minimum values with absolute errors \(o(N)\) give the
same conclusion, since \(r\) is fixed. No interchange of a minimum
and a level limit is contained in these statements.

This gives a concrete alternative to describing the optimizing
metrics: establish the large-level values of two coercive, geodesically
convex problems at fixed strengths, then take the displayed
combination. We have not established those values or compared them
with Casson--Rivin volume optimization. The formula remains valid
after every fixed short partial filling, but that validity alone
provides no threshold for the remaining fillings and proves no new
volume-conjecture class. The finite-exception theorem remains open.

The three complete direct proof texts are the anchored compiler at
`e83c35d16c79faa13ac6556db78b9b57da2a2371d3fc04c4673ecd74e1d336f7`,
the full tree capacity proof at
`2997b732aa73e063c66e81d6487a1d9927509609d61842c1dbb43d9345df1d6d`,
and the regularization proof at
`0cea0d52182eb24b4610538f354dbe5158fa54aa6f9cf7f9fc280c72ab090ff8`.
The two-strength identity and its consequences are proved in full
above. No general novelty is claimed for comparing penalized minima
at two strengths. Frozen manuscripts and public documents are
unchanged.

## The absorbed zero-power Hardy source cannot satisfy the continuation upper bound, 22 November

There is now an exact reason to avoid one apparently simpler source
representative. The [absorbed Hardy construction](research_standard_crossing_hardy_source.md)
puts the standard crossing classes into a canonical numerator of degree
less than \(N\) in each selected variable, then applies zero-power
Hardy caps. It retains the original invariant at unit charge and all
Hermite normals. Nevertheless it cannot satisfy the proposed geometric
subexponential upper bound on a regular seed-to-unit domain with a
nonzero continued leading coefficient.

First, its universal plus cap has the exact row identity
\[
 \mathscr T_{+,0,1+j/N}[p]=0
       \qquad(j=1,2,\ldots,\quad\deg p<N).
\]
To verify it, use the literal
[Hardy derivative-grid definition](research_hardy_reduced_polarized_source.md).
At this charge the projected function is
\[
 f(t)=\sin t\,p(-2\cos t)e^{-ijt}.
\]
Its highest positive Fourier frequency is at most \(N-j<N\).
The cap projects onto positive frequencies and sums their derivatives
on the \(N\) original physical angular grid points. That sum kills
every positive frequency except a multiple of \(N\), so the entire
row vanishes. This is the full derivative readout, not a value-only
quotient. Tensoring shows that the absorbed source
\(\mathscr S_{N,\mathbf+}^{\boldsymbol b}(\boldsymbol\chi)\) is zero
whenever any selected coordinate equals \(1+j/N\), independently
of its other charges.

Now fix a holomorphic charge curve from a small-charge seed to unit
charge at \(s_*\). Some coordinate is nonconstant. Locally write
\[
 \chi_v(s)-1=(s-s_*)^q h(s),\qquad q\ge1,\quad h(s_*)\ne0.
\]
A local holomorphic \(q\)-th root of \(h\) gives an invertible
coordinate \(\psi(s)\) with \(\chi_v(s)-1=\psi(s)^q\).
Hence \(s_N=\psi^{-1}(N^{-1/q})\to s_*\), and the actual absorbed
source vanishes at every \(s_N\).

These zeros contradict a uniform nonzero geometric leading term
near the target. More precisely they rule out the complex upper
hypothesis on an entire connected regular continuation domain.
The actual exponentially accurate seed is retained: the
[numerator reduction](research_hermite_reduced_polarized_initializer.md),
zero-height limit, and crossing absorption have exponential errors
near a sufficiently small fixed seed. They therefore preserve the
Gevrey remainder obtained from the full-midpoint initializer and the
generic factorial/Gaussian estimates. All those comparison errors
are independent of the truncation order.

Let \(S(s)\) be its marked action and put
\(f_N=N^{-\beta}e^{-NS}\mathscr S_{N,\mathbf+}^{\boldsymbol b}\), with
\(\beta=3(|I|-|E|)/2\). Let \(a_r\) be the continued full
stationary coefficients on this marked regular curve. Suppose
\(a_0\) is nonzero at \(s_*\), as on the supplied positive component.
On a fixed buffered compact chain from seed to a target disk, the
Gevrey estimates give a bounded truncation
\(P_N=\sum_{r<\lfloor cN\rfloor}a_rN^{-r}
       =a_0+O(N^{-1})\).
The seed remainder is \(O(e^{-\kappa N})\), whereas
\(|f_N(s_N)-P_N(s_N)|\ge c_0>0\). After \(J\ge1\)
three-circles steps, \(\theta=2^{-J}\), one obtains
\[
 c_0\le C e^{-\kappa\theta N}
       \max\{1,\sup_{\rm chain}|f_N-P_N|\}^{1-\theta}.
\]
Consequently the normalized absorbed source has a strictly positive
exponential excess somewhere on this fixed chain compact. In
particular the subexponential upper condition on all compact sets
of that domain is impossible for this representative. This argument
does not locate that excess in an arbitrarily small target disk.

There is also an exact orthogonality calculation near the unit charge.
Keep the other charges equal to one and put \(z=\chi_v-1\).
Let \(u_N(z)\) be the absorbed source, optionally multiplied by a
nonvanishing holomorphic action normalization, on a neighborhood of
\(|z|\le r\). Set \(J_N=\lfloor rN/2\rfloor\) and
\[
 \mathcal B_N(z)=\prod_{j=1}^{J_N}
       \frac{r(z-j/N)}{r^2-(j/N)z},\qquad
 |\mathcal B_N(0)|=\frac{J_N!}{(rN)^{J_N}}\le2^{-J_N}.
\]
This finite Blaschke product has modulus one on the circle and its
listed zeros are zeros of \(u_N\). Dividing them out gives a
holomorphic function with the same boundary squared norm. Cauchy's
mean inequality therefore proves
\[
 |u_N(0)|^2\le
 \left[\frac{J_N!}{(rN)^{J_N}}\right]^2
 \frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}|u_N(re^{i\theta})|^2\,d\theta .
\]
For the full radius-\(r\) Hardy space subject only to these listed
zero constraints, this is sharp: take \(u=c\mathcal B_N\).
Its evaluation dual norm is exactly \(|\mathcal B_N(0)|\), with
the empty product equal to one when \(J_N=0\). The actual source
can satisfy further constraints, so equality of its smaller space's
evaluation norm is not asserted.

In particular
\(\sup_{|z|=r}|u_N(z)|\ge2^{J_N}|u_N(0)|\).
If an independently supplied unit-value rate gives
\(\log|u_N(0)|=o(N)\), the boundary supremum has lower rate at
least \((r/2)\log2\). This local rate conclusion needs that
unit-value hypothesis; the exact relative inequality does not.
The charge-function Hardy norm is not being identified with a
physical gluing norm. Its explicit exponential evaluation factor
must be retained in any argument using this particular boundary norm.

The quantitative seed and propagation steps use the complete
[full-midpoint proof](research_full_midpoint_polarized_initializer.md),
[generic growing-order estimates](research_full_charge_grid_exponential_remainder.md)
and [Gevrey continuation proof](research_gevrey_initialized_source_upper_propagation.md),
together with the three exponential source comparisons cited above.
Their phase, prefactor and both parity conventions are retained.

The zeros occur at off-endpoint charges depending on \(N\), not at
new filling assignments. The original scalar at charge one and the
volume conjecture are not contradicted. Nor does this argument rule
out canonical numerators with the crossing Gaussian retained inside
their caps, or the unreduced centered source below. It excludes the
specific simultaneous absorption into degree-less-than-\(N\) numerators
and use of universal zero-power caps for this continuation route.

## A centered contour formula for the remaining upper estimate, 22 November

The geometric upper estimate need not be proved for the original table
of frozen partial-row contours. The
[full-midpoint source](research_full_midpoint_polarized_initializer.md)
already gives a simpler exact representative with one horizontal and
one vertical functional per selected vertex. The new
[Gevrey propagation argument](research_gevrey_initialized_source_upper_propagation.md)
applies to its centered, moving-height version as well.

Fix the same-index graph and real crossing powers \(b_v\), and keep
outside angles complete. Assume a supplied positive unit-charge
primitive target. The full-midpoint proof constructs a fixed marked
holomorphic curve from a small-charge seed to that target, with angular
critical points \(t_v(s)\), charges \(\chi_v(s)\), and
\[
 h_v(s)=i t_v(s),\qquad \Re h_v(s)>0.
\]
On a complex neighborhood \(D\) of this curve define
\[
 \widehat G_N(s)=
 \left[\bigotimes_{v\in I}
 \left(\mathcal H_{+,b_v,\chi_v(s)}^{h_v(s)}
           +\mathcal V_{b_v,\chi_v(s)}^{h_v(s),\epsilon_v}\right)\right]F_N,
 \qquad F_N(\boldsymbol\theta)=\prod_{e=vw}K_N(\theta_v,\theta_w).
\]
The functionals are exactly the full-midpoint horizontal and cosine
vertical functionals of that source, with cuts at \(-\pi,\pi\)
and fixed side choices \(\epsilon_v\in\{1,-1\}\). They act on
the full ordinary polynomial \(F_N\). The horizontal path is
\(t=t_v(s)+x\), \(-\pi\le x\le\pi\); the slanted vertical path
uses \(t=\epsilon_v\pi+i h_v(s)r\), \(-1\le r\le1\), including
its measure factor \(h_v(s)\,dr\). No vertical piece is deleted.

This is a holomorphic new off-endpoint representative. At its target,
\[
 Z_N^{\rm original}=\varepsilon_N\widehat G_N(1),\qquad
 \varepsilon_N=\prod_v e^{\pi ib_v(N-1)^2/(4N)}.
\]
Equality with the old frozen family and its simple heat equation
are not assumed.

Its actual seed expansion has the same quantitative Gevrey remainder.
Indeed the central wire and angle variables lie on buffered analytic
charts near the complete quarter-point wires. Apply only the generic
factorial and growing-order Gaussian estimates in Sections 2--3 of the
[exponential-remainder proof](research_full_charge_grid_exponential_remainder.md).
The exact slanted wings and verticals already have a fixed seed loss
in the full-midpoint proof, independent of the truncation order.
The exponentially small correction in the rational trace denominator
is kept as a remainder, rather than differentiated to growing order.
Full Gaussian integration identifies the same marked formal coefficients.

Consequently, with \(S(s)\) the marked critical action and
\(\beta=3(|I|-|E|)/2\), it suffices to establish
\[
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\sup_{s\in C}
       |N^{-\beta}e^{-NS(s)}\widehat G_N(s)|\le0
                            \qquad(C\Subset D),
\]
or the corresponding complex-area squared-norm upper estimate.
This uses the general analytic theorem in Section 4 of the Gevrey
proof, not its application to a different frozen family.
Both level parities and the complete-only edge factors remain included.

Thus the upper problem can be stated with one centered trace functional
per vertex, without a removed-row height table or a global comparison
with the old contours. Its full currents still require an action-relative
estimate. Centering alone does not give that estimate, and the supplied
positive target hypothesis does not cover every required short filling.
No new filling class is concluded.

## The raw charge stencil does not give a universal maximum principle, 22 November

The exact [Hardy charge relation](research_standard_crossing_hardy_source.md)
retains the insertion of multiplication by the Casimir coordinate
\(z\). Its unmodified homogeneous left side on a finite charge window
therefore has the form
\[
 B_M=C_M\otimes I+I\otimes Z,\qquad M\ge2,
\]
where \(C_M\) is the nearest-neighbor adjacency matrix on \(M\)
sites with zero Dirichlet exterior, and \(Z\) is multiplication by
\(z\) on the full \(N\)-dimensional algebra
\(\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2)\). This auxiliary boundary condition
is being used to test a proposed universal comparison argument; it is
not asserted to be the original source's boundary condition.

The eigenvectors \(u_k(j)=\sin(kj\pi/(M+1))\) of \(C_M\) have
eigenvalues \(2\cos(k\pi/(M+1))\), \(1\le k\le M\).
The real Casimir spectrum has minimum at most zero and maximum at
least zero for every \(N\ge2\). Tensor products of corresponding
eigenvectors show that \(B_M\) has both a positive and a negative
real eigenvalue. Hence neither \(B_M\) nor \(-B_M\) is accretive in
any positive Hermitian inner product: testing a negative-eigenvalue
vector would give a negative real quadratic form. Nor can a similarity
turn either sign into a real M-matrix, whose spectrum would have
nonnegative real parts. In particular a diagonal exponential change of
unknowns preserves these eigenvalues and does not fix this problem
for the same finite window.

This excludes that direct, uncoupled maximum-principle shortcut.
It does not exclude a different operator after the actual graph
relations and boundary forcing have been incorporated. Replacing
\(Z\) by the geometric scalar before proving such a reduction would
remove physical Hermite channels. No upper bound for the original
source follows from this check.

The author, root and two independent peers have read all three complete
sections and all six complete direct proof sources, checked the used
implications, and renewed matching source hashes. The frozen manuscripts
and earlier author-final notes are unchanged.

## A sharp complex upper rate suffices on the initialized regular component, 22 November

The [Gevrey continuation proof](research_gevrey_initialized_source_upper_propagation.md)
weakens the upper estimate needed on a supplied marked regular source
component. The actual initializer is accurate to an exponentially small
error when its expansion is truncated at a sufficiently small multiple
of \(N\). This makes a subexponential upper loss sufficient; a fixed
polynomial loss is no longer needed.

Keep the same frozen all-plus contour family, including every removed
row and endpoint current. Fix the graph and real crossing powers before
taking the level limit, and keep outside angles complete. Let
\(G_N(s)\) be that family on a fixed connected complex parameter domain
\(D\). Suppose its full critical point and marked action \(S(s)\)
continue regularly from the actual seed. For \(m\) selected vertices
and \(e\) retained edges, including outside-only edges, put
\[
 \beta=3(m-e)/2,\qquad f_N(s)=N^{-\beta}e^{-NS(s)}G_N(s).
\]
The continued stationary coefficients \(a_j\) have the compact bounds
\[
 \sup_K|a_j|\le C_KA_K^j j!\qquad(K\Subset D).
\]
These are Gevrey-1 bounds: the factorial controls how the constants
grow with the expansion order. Near the seed the actual remainder is
\[
 \left|f_N-\sum_{j<L}a_jN^{-j}\right|
      \le CA^LL!N^{-L}+Ce^{-\delta N},\qquad 1\le L\le aN.
\]
The proof applies the quantitative local factorial and Gaussian
estimates to this same initialized source. It does not apply the
separate zero-power full-grid theorem to nonzero powers.

It now suffices to prove the locally uniform complex upper rate
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\sup_K|f_N|\le0
                         \qquad(K\Subset D).
 \qquad}
\]
Indeed, on a compact buffered chain from seed to target choose
\(L_N=\lfloor cN\rfloor\) small enough that the truncated series is
uniformly bounded. Its seed error is \(O(e^{-\kappa N})\).
After \(J\) fixed three-circles steps the difference between the
actual function and that truncation has exponential rate at most
\(-\kappa2^{-J}\). Adding back any fixed tail gives the full
initialized expansion throughout the domain. In particular a
nonzero continued \(a_0\) gives a nonzero leading term at the target.
The statement holds through both level parities.

A subexponential upper bound on the complex-area integral
\(\int_K|f_N|^2\,dA\) also suffices, by the holomorphic submean
inequality on buffered disks. Therefore a positive quadratic upper
trial for the exact frozen row needs only the correct leading
exponential rate. Its trial vectors need not be holomorphic.
The original ordinary polynomial numerator and full frozen row must
be retained; reduction to the physical quotient away from unit charge
is not permitted.

For a supplied positive unit-charge target, the existing marked
formal-component theorem gives a suitable regular curve and nonzero
leading coefficient. A successful complex upper trial on that curve
would therefore also give its lower asymptotic. This is an alternative
to proving a lower bound uniformly over all orthonormal bases.
It has not supplied that upper trial or a positive lift of every
required short filling. Source-to-knot identification and the marked
action-volume equality remain necessary. No new filling class or
finite-exception theorem is concluded. The author, root and two
independent peers have read the complete final proof, this entire
section and all four complete direct sources, checked the used
implications, and renewed matching source hashes.

## Optimizing the boundary metrics does not increase projective speed, 22 November

The [horizontal-response proof](research_horizontal_source_metric_response.md)
controls the motion of the canonical metrics when the prescribed source
tensors vary. Choose a smooth anchored tensor family, keep the positive
regularization parameter \(\varepsilon\) fixed while differentiating,
and minimize \(L+\varepsilon\log Z\) at each parameter value, where
\(L=\sum_v\log\|T_v\|_H\) is the sum of the gauged local log norms
and \(Z=1+\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(H_e+H_e^{-1})\). The
minimizer is smooth. Its gauges can be chosen with
\(g_e'=X_eg_e\), \(X_e=X_e^*\); this fixes their arbitrary moving
unitary rotations.

For each normalized local tensor, split its derivative orthogonally
to its own complex line. Let \(q_v\) be this part when the gauges
are frozen and only the physical tensor is differentiated. Let
\(a_v\) be the additional part from the moving gauge. Define
\[
 P_{\rm phys}^2=\sum_v\|q_v\|^2,\qquad
 P_{\rm gauge}^2=\sum_v\|a_v\|^2,\qquad
 P_{\rm tot}^2=\sum_v\|q_v+a_v\|^2.
\]
The regularizer's second derivative along this gauge direction is
\({\cal H}_R(X)\ge0\). Differentiating the full stationary metric
equation, including the physical variation, proves exactly
\[
 \boxed{\qquad P_{\rm phys}^2=P_{\rm tot}^2+
                 P_{\rm gauge}^2+\varepsilon{\cal H}_R(X).\qquad}
\]
Thus the optimized horizontal motion has no larger projective speed
than the frozen-gauge physical variation. The proof uses no inverse
metric-Hessian bound and assumes no commutativity of the edge metrics.

For the original anchored closing, the earlier purity estimate supplies
an output spectral gap at least \(1-8\varepsilon\), when
\(0<\varepsilon<1/8\). If \(\psi_v\) are the principal output
vectors, with their derivative phases chosen orthogonally, then
\[
 \sum_v\|\psi_v'\|^2
          \le\frac4{(1-8\varepsilon)^2}P_{\rm phys}^2.
\]
The vectors here are in the horizontal metric frames. This is not a
bound on their derivatives in the original Newton coordinates.

The remaining input is the physical variance in those same optimized
metrics. It has not been bounded for all required short fillings.
The speed identity supplies neither its geometric limiting mean nor a
nonzero coefficient in the original closing. Its use is to avoid a
separate estimate for the motion of the optimizing frames once the
physical variation is controlled. No new filling class follows.

## An exact positive formula using only orthonormal bases, 22 November

One further simplification is available at a fixed quantum level. In the
[orthonormal partition construction](research_orthonormal_boundary_partition.md),
replace the sum of squared index terms by the sum of their magnitudes,
keeping the root output as a vector. The minimum then equals the source
norm exactly. This is a corollary of the same elementary tree argument;
the earlier note already established the reduction at the volume scale.

Here are the definition and proof. Root a finite tensor tree at its
output \(Y\in F\), where \(F\) is a fixed Hilbert space. An internal
edge \(e\) has dimension \(n_e\). Choose an orthonormal vector basis
with columns \(U_e\): use \(U_e^*\) on the child vector coordinates
and \(U_e^{\mathsf T}\) on the parent covector coordinates. Their
bilinear contraction and the original output are unchanged. If \(k\)
assigns one index to every internal edge, define the vector
\[
 A_k(U)=T_\rho(U)_{k|\rho}
                 \prod_{v\ne\rho}T_v(U)_{k|v}\in F,
 \qquad Y=\sum_k A_k(U).
\]
Here \(\rho\) is the root; its coefficient at the incident internal
indices is a vector in \(F\), and every other displayed coefficient
is a scalar. Put
\[
 \mathcal A(U)=\sum_k\|A_k(U)\|,
 \qquad \mathcal W(U)=\max_k\|A_k(U)\|,
 \qquad D=\prod_e n_e.
\]
Both functions are continuous on the compact product of unitary groups.
They are specified entirely by the original tensors and trial bases.
Triangle inequality gives \(\|Y\|\le\mathcal A(U)\) for every
choice of bases.

For the reverse bound, contract all tensors below edge \(e\) in
the original coordinates, leaving its vector \(a_e\) uncontracted.
When \(a_e\ne0\), choose the first basis vector
along \(a_e/\|a_e\|\); choose an arbitrary basis when \(a_e=0\).
If all proper messages are nonzero, every nonzero index term is forced
from the leaves to have all its indices zero. At a proper vertex its
remaining coefficient is the outgoing message norm divided by the
product of the incoming message norms. These positive factors telescope;
the single surviving vector term is exactly \(Y\).
The zero case also holds: inductively the absolute contraction of a
zero-message subtree vanishes. Either a child message is zero, or all
children have nonzero messages and the remaining zero-input slice is
the zero outgoing vector. Consequently
\[
 \boxed{\quad \min_U\mathcal A(U)=\|Y\|,\qquad
 \frac{\|Y\|}{D}\le\min_U\mathcal W(U)\le\|Y\|.\quad}
\]
The second assertion follows from
\(\mathcal W\le\mathcal A\le D\mathcal W\) and the adapted bases
just constructed. Both minima are attained. No tensor direction was
removed, and absolute values were taken after the basis changes.

For the [original anchored compiler](research_anchored_conway_positive_variational_period.md),
\(Y_N=(1,K_N)\) and \(D=(N+1)^{m-1}\), where \(m\) counts its
fixed tensor vertices. Thus
\[
 \min_U\mathcal A_N(U)=\sqrt{1+|K_N|^2}
\]
at every level, with the full closing, phases and Hermite coordinates.
The constant reference is optional for this particular formula: apply
the abstract result directly to the unaugmented source with scalar root
\(Y=K_N\). Its edge spaces have dimension \(N\), and if
\(a_k(U)\) are its scalar index terms, then
\[
             |K_N|=\min_{U_e\in\mathrm U(N)}\sum_k|a_k(U)|.
\]
The zero-case proof above includes levels at which \(K_N=0\).
This removes the extra reference coordinate from the absolute-sum
formulation; it does not remove the anchor needed in the separate
regularized metric theorems.

Compared with the squared partition, the absolute-sum identity has no
polynomial comparison loss. Its unitary optimization is nonconvex and
the objective generally nonsmooth. The strongly convex quartic's
degree-four semidefinite exactness does not transfer to this different
problem. Nor does this identity replace the smooth
metric-response argument.

The volume lower bound must hold under the minimum over all bases.
A favorable geometric basis supplies an upper bound on that minimum.
The adapted bases prove equality but depend on the actual proper
messages, whose geometric asymptotics remain unproved. Accordingly this
is a simpler finite-level identity, not a new asymptotic estimate or an
additional filling case. The author, root and two independent peers
have read this entire section and both complete direct sources, checked
the used implications, and renewed matching source hashes.

## Canonical metrics already satisfy the singular-vector test, 22 November

The existence of compatible quantum metrics is not a separate missing
theorem. The canonical regularized metrics already pass the
maximal-singular-vector test below. What is missing is a geometric
description of their norm budget and its leading value.

Here is the deduction, including the vector-valued closing. Let
\(S_{\rm HS}\) be the sum of the actual normalized tensor marginal
mismatches at the canonical metrics, with the prescribed input
transposes. The purity argument in the full-capacity proof gives
\[
 1-\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{v,e}^2)\le2S_{\rm HS}
\]
at every half-edge. In particular
\(\eta_v=1-\lambda_{\max}(\rho_{v,\rm out})\le2S_{\rm HS}\)
for every nonroot output: for a density matrix,
\(\operatorname{tr}\rho^2\le\lambda_{\max}(\rho)\).
The original anchored root has one input and output \(\mathbb C^2\).
Its two marginals have the same nonzero eigenvalues, so the same
bound holds for its maximal left singular vector.

For a normalized local tensor, the actual joint input density is
its Schmidt mixture \(\sum_j\lambda_j\xi_j\xi_j^*\).
Its trace distance from the maximal right singular state
\(\xi_1\xi_1^*\) is \(2\eta_v\). Partial trace cannot increase that
distance: decompose a Hermitian difference into positive and negative
parts and use preservation of their traces. On an edge from child
\(c\) to parent \(v\), the triangle inequality therefore gives
\[
 \delta_{{\rm top},e}
 \le\delta_{{\rm HS},e}+2\eta_v+2\eta_c
 \le\delta_{{\rm HS},e}+8S_{\rm HS}.
\]
There are \(m-1\) internal edges in the tree. Consequently
\[
 S_{\rm top}\le(8m-7)S_{\rm HS}.
\]
The fixed regularizer \(\varepsilon=1/(512m^2)\) gives
\(S_{\rm HS}\le2\varepsilon\), hence
\[
        mS_{\rm top}\le\frac{8m-7}{256m}<\frac1{32}.
\]
This is stronger than the sufficient bound \(S_{\rm top}\le1/(4m)\).
Near purity also implies
\(\lambda_1-\lambda_2\ge1-4S_{\rm HS}>0\); a spectral gap is
obtained here, not assumed.

Thus the exact canonical quantum construction provides matching
singular states at every level, after any fixed filling assignment.
This does not calculate the product of their singular values.
It is a consequence of the earlier capacity estimates, not an
additional volume estimate or a new knot case.
The complete proof sources are the
[capacity purity estimate](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md),
[regularized metric construction](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md)
and [anchored compiler](research_anchored_conway_positive_variational_period.md).
The author, root and two independent peers have read this entire
section and its complete direct proof sources, checked the used
implications, and renewed matching source hashes.

## Parameter response and the remaining Schläfli comparison, 22 November

The [projective response proof](research_projective_conway_parameter_response.md)
gives an error estimate for parameter variation of the unchanged
source. Fix a parameter value and freeze the boundary gauges there.
For the local tensor \(U_v\) and its prescribed derivative \(U_v'\), put
\[
 \tau_v=\frac{U_v}{\|U_v\|},\qquad b_v=\frac{U_v'}{\|U_v\|},
 \qquad z_v=\langle\tau_v,b_v\rangle,\qquad
 Q_v=\|b_v-\tau_vz_v\|.
\]
Let \(Y=(1,K)\), \(F=\prod_v\|U_v\|_{\rm HS}\),
\(r=\|Y\|/F\), and
\(w_v=\langle Y,Y_v'\rangle/\|Y\|^2\), where \(Y_v'\) is the
original contraction with that one tensor differentiated. Then
\[
 |w_v-z_v|\le\frac{\sqrt{1-r^2}}r Q_v,\qquad
 \left|\partial_t\log\|Y\|-\operatorname{Re}\sum_vz_v\right|
       \le\frac{\sqrt{1-r^2}}r\sum_vQ_v .
\]
The error uses only the orthogonal part of the tensor variation.
In the proof, the environment contraction gives an error vector
exactly orthogonal to \(\tau_v\); no approximate phase cancellation
is being assumed.

If the frozen-gauge insertion acts on one leg by an operator \(B\),
the quantity needed is the actual variance
\[
 Q_v^2=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_vB^*B)
                         -|\operatorname{tr}(\rho_vB)|^2.
\]
Here \(\rho_v\) is the normalized local tensor's true marginal.
The formula retains all nilpotent terms, dual orientations and
carrier contributions. A scalar change of the whole tensor is
parallel and cancels from the error; a carrier acting only on its
physical block need not be parallel.

At the canonical metrics with \(\varepsilon_N=1/(m^2N^2)\),
let \(j_N\) be the minimum of the full penalized objective
\(L_N+\varepsilon_N\log Z\). Its envelope derivative is
\(j_N'=\operatorname{Re}\sum_vz_{v,N}\). For \(N\ge8\), the norm
comparison gives
\[
 \frac1N\left|\partial_t\log\|Y_N\|-j_N'\right|
          \le C_mN^{-3/2}\sum_vQ_{v,N}.
\]
In particular a bound \(O(\sqrt N)\) on this sum would give an
\(O(N^{-1})\) scaled derivative error. No such variance bound is
proved for the general short-filled source.
The derivative here is that of the penalized minimum. The total
derivative of its unpenalized part additionally contains
\(-\varepsilon_N\partial_t\log Z(H_N(t))\).

There is also a weak identity not requiring a variance bound.
On a compact parameter interval with uniform input norm growth
\(\prod_v\max(1,\|T_{v,N}\|)\le e^{CN}\), the existing compactness
proof gives
\(0\le j_N-\log\|Y_N\|\le C/N\).
Thus for every \(C^1\) test function \(\varphi\) supported inside
that interval,
\[
 \left|\int\varphi(t)\,
       \frac{j_N'(t)-\partial_t\log\|Y_N(t)\|}{N}\,dt\right|
       \le\frac{C}{N^2}\|\varphi'\|_{L^1}.
\]
This follows by integration by parts, not by differentiating a
uniform value error pointwise.

The missing geometric statement is now explicit: these scaled
quantum means must recover the marked real-action derivatives from
the Schläfli formula along an appropriate initialized parameter path,
with enough endpoint control
to recover the desired values. For the source phase terms
\(in_vt_v^2/(4\pi)-i\chi_vt_v\), the classical targets are
\(\operatorname{Re}(it_v^2/(4\pi))\) and \(\operatorname{Im}t_v\).
Here \(t_v\) is the complex angle of a supplied geometric stationary
point. Matrix balance alone supplies neither mean identification,
the required path, nor pointwise endpoint convergence.
No additional filling case or finite-exception theorem is concluded.
