## Two checked routes which do not yet supply the geometric comparison, 22 November

The full-clock positive-angle count was already proved in
[the angle majorant](positive_angle_majorant_and_integer_winding.md).
It requires the correct global edge characters. The
[marked five-cell dictionary](research_marked_five_cell_edge_peripheral_lattice.md)
supplies continued logarithmic lifts and retains two auxiliary
spherical ends. It does not supply the principal-angle conversion
on a torus-cusped ideal triangulation. Its zero internal log lifts
are not themselves statements that the principal windings vanish.
Thus inserting further exact Frobenius or Hardy resolutions does
not, by itself, prove all the required principal winding inequalities.
No new angle-majorant theorem is adopted from that shortcut.

A proposed comparison with the regular knot-group trace also needs
a new adapter. In particular the bare clock-and-shift monomial
group has central commutators, since its two generators commute up
to a scalar root of unity. Any knot-group homomorphism into it has
cyclic image. Indeed its image \(H\) has cyclic abelianization
(a quotient of the knot group's \(\mathbb Z\)), and \([H,H]\)
is central. Writing any two elements as powers of one lift of that
cyclic generator times central commutators proves that they commute.
The image is therefore abelian and hence cyclic.
For a nontrivial knot-group commutator, every such representation has
normalized matrix trace one, whereas its regular group trace is zero.
This excludes that particular moment approximation. It does not
exclude a nonmonomial matrix realization, a different trace adapter,
or a separate asymptotic formula for the original marked source.
No \(L^2\)-torsion result is used as a proof premise.

These checks concern the proposed arguments, not counterexamples
to the volume conjecture. The author, root and two independent peers
have read this entire section and its complete direct proof sources,
checked the used implications, and renewed matching source hashes.
No frozen manuscript or public document was edited.

## A simpler lower bound from compatible maximal singular vectors, 22 November

For the maximal-singular-vector choice, the local calibration argument
has a more direct form. A single forward contraction estimate gives
both bounds, without a logarithmic metric window or a separate upper
trial. This is a sufficient test; the geometric changes of reference
needed to pass it have not been constructed.

Take the exact anchored compiler, including its actual closing map
with output \(Y_N=(1,K_N)\). Make any prescribed invertible boundary
changes of basis, acting inversely at the two ends of each edge.
All original contractions, phases and Hermite channels remain.
Let \(m\) count the vertices, including leaves and closing root.
At a leaf with nonzero vector \(a_v\), set
\[
 s_v=\|a_v\|,\qquad \psi_v=a_v/s_v.
\]
At every nonleaf, regard its nonzero multilinear tensor as a linear map
\(A_v:\bigotimes_{c\ {\rm child}}H_c\to H_v\), where the root space
is the original \(\mathbb C^2\). Choose a unit maximal left singular
vector and its corresponding right vector:
\[
 s_v=\|A_v\|_{\rm op},\qquad
 A_vA_v^*\psi_v=s_v^2\psi_v,\qquad
 \xi_v=A_v^*\psi_v/s_v.
\]
Then \(\|\xi_v\|=1\) and \(A_v\xi_v=s_v\psi_v\).
No spectral gap or simple largest singular value is required.

For an edge \(e\) from a child \(c\) into its parent \(v\), let
\(\sigma_{v,e}\) be the input marginal of the pure state
\(\xi_v\xi_v^*\) on \(H_c\). Define
\[
 \delta_e=\|\sigma_{v,e}-\psi_c\psi_c^*\|_1,\qquad
 d_v=\sum_{e\ {\rm input\ to}\ v}\delta_e,\qquad
 S_N=\sum_e\delta_e,\qquad \mathcal B_N=\prod_vs_v.
\]
These densities are on the input Hilbert spaces. If expressed instead
on the parent's dual tensor indices, transpose them once according to
the original bilinear pairing.
The joint state \(\xi_v\xi_v^*\) is retained when taking its marginals;
it is not replaced by their tensor product.

The exact tree estimate is
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \left[1-\sum_{v\ {\rm nonleaf}}\sqrt{d_v}\right]_+\mathcal B_N
 \ \le\ \|Y_N\|\ \le\ \mathcal B_N,\qquad
 \sum_{v\ {\rm nonleaf}}\sqrt{d_v}\le\sqrt{mS_N}.
 \qquad}
\]
Here \([x]_+=\max(x,0)\). To prove it, put
\(u_v=\bigotimes_c\psi_c\). A projection tested against the traceless
difference of two density matrices has absolute trace at most half
their trace-norm distance. The commuting input projections therefore
give
\[
 1-|\langle\xi_v,u_v\rangle|^2
 \le\sum_c\{1-\langle\psi_c,\sigma_{v,e}\psi_c\rangle\}
 \le d_v/2.
\]
Consequently a phase \(\alpha_v\), with \(|\alpha_v|=1\), can be
chosen so that \(\|\xi_v-\alpha_vu_v\|\le\sqrt{d_v}\).
Indeed its squared minimum is
\(2-2|\langle\xi_v,u_v\rangle|\le d_v\); if \(d_v\ge2\),
the same assertion follows from the universal bound two on that
squared minimum. Applying the contraction \(A_v/s_v\) proves
\[
 \|(A_v/s_v)u_v-\overline{\alpha_v}\psi_v\|
 \le\sqrt{d_v}.
\]

Normalize each exact subtree output by the product of the \(s_w\)
in that subtree. These normalized outputs have norm at most one.
At a nonleaf, telescoping the tensor product of its normalized child
outputs changes the output by at most the sum of the child errors.
Choose the comparison phase at \(v\) to be
\(\overline{\alpha_v}\) times the product of its child phases.
Induction thus bounds the root's error from a unit vector by
\(\sum_v\sqrt{d_v}\). This comparison tracks phases; it does not
alter them in the original source. Cauchy--Schwarz, with each edge
counted once, gives the final bound by \(\sqrt{mS_N}\).
The upper estimate is the ordinary product of operator norms.

For a fixed construction, the level-independent condition
\(S_N\le1/(4m)\) gives
\[
             \tfrac12\mathcal B_N\le\sqrt{1+|K_N|^2}\le\mathcal B_N .
\]
Thus constant matching accuracy already suffices for the exponential
rate. If a geometric reference gives this condition eventually and
\(2\pi N^{-1}\sum_v\log s_v\to
\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K)>0\), the original volume identity
follows. If \(S_N\to0\), the ratio \(\|Y_N\|/\mathcal B_N\) tends to one.
The same product \(\mathcal B_N\) supplies the upper bound; no additional
upper estimate is needed in this specialization.

The earlier [line-and-complement composition criterion](research_source_adapted_observation_composition.md)
already gave general source-sensitive transport conditions. This
is an elementary specialization to maximal singular pairs, for which
every normalized map is a contraction and the actual closing is one
of those maps. Its \(\delta_e\) are not the actual normalized
Hilbert--Schmidt tensor marginals in the full-capacity theorem.
Neither a good reference nor the stated geometric rate follows from
the existence of these singular pairs. This does not prove a new
filling case.

The physical compiler is the
[anchored construction](research_anchored_conway_positive_variational_period.md);
the local spectral family is also covered by the
[bilinear calibration proof](research_ordered_density_bilinear_calibration.md).
The estimate above is proved directly, without importing a transport
or spectral-gap theorem. The root and three peers have read this
whole section and its complete matching source texts, checked the
used implications and renewed matching hashes.

## Local lower certificates on a finite logarithmic metric window, 22 November

The fixed regularizer permits a weaker requirement than an affine
calibration valid on the entire positive cone. One only needs local
inequalities on a known finite window. Approximate matching of their
full density matrices then has a controlled cost at the volume scale.
The local inequalities themselves still need a geometric construction.

Use the exact anchored tree with \(Y_N=(1,K_N)\), \(m\ge2\) vertices
and full boundary spaces \(\mathbb C\oplus H_N\). At each edge orient
the positive metric action toward the child output. Set
\[
 \varepsilon=\frac1{512m^2},\quad
 L_N(H)=\sum_v\log\|T_{v,N}\|_H,\quad
 Z(H)=1+\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(H_e+H_e^{-1}),\quad
 R_N=\frac{L_N(I)}{\varepsilon}+\log Z(I).
\]
All of these inputs are prescribed by the original tensors. The
unique minimizer \(H_N^*\) of \(L_N+\varepsilon\log Z\) satisfies
\[
 \|\log H_{e,N}^*\|_{\rm op}\le R_N=O(N),\qquad
 \|Y_N\|\le e^{L_N(H_N^*)}\le2\|Y_N\|.
\]
Indeed \(L_N(H_N^*)\ge\log\|Y_N\|\ge0\), so comparison with
\(H=I\) gives \(\log Z(H_N^*)\le R_N\). Each eigenvalue and its
reciprocal are at most \(Z\). The constant comparison follows from
the full-marginal estimate and \(S_N\le2\varepsilon\), as in the
fixed-regularizer argument below. Original anchored input norms give
\(L_N(I)=O(N)\), while \(\log Z(I)=O(\log N)\).

Here is a sufficient lower certificate. On each half-edge choose
a positive semidefinite Hermitian matrix \(\rho_{v,e,N}\) of trace
one. They are calibration parameters, not presumed to be the actual
marginals of a common gauged tensor field. At vertex \(v\), suppose
a known real number \(\beta_{v,N}\) satisfies
\[
 \begin{split}
 \log\|T_{v,N}\|_{e^X}\ \ge\ \beta_{v,N}
 &+\frac12\sum_{e:\,v\ \mathrm{child}}
                \operatorname{tr}(\rho_{v,e,N}X_e)\\
 &-\frac12\sum_{e:\,v\ \mathrm{parent}}
                \operatorname{tr}(\rho_{v,e,N}X_e^{\mathsf T})
 \end{split}
\]
for every simultaneous tuple of Hermitian matrices with
\(\|X_e\|_{\rm op}\le R_N\) on its incident edges. The notation
\(e^X\) means \(H_e=e^{X_e}\) with the original bilinear edge
pairing: the parent's dual factor uses \(e^{-X_e^{\mathsf T}}\).
The original closing tensor is included among these vertices.
Define the full matching error
\[
 \delta_{e,N}=\|\rho_{{\rm child},e,N}
                   -\rho_{{\rm parent},e,N}^{\mathsf T}\|_1.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \log\|Y_N\|\ge\sum_v\beta_{v,N}
                    -\frac{R_N}{2}\sum_e\delta_{e,N}-\log2.
 \quad}
\]
To prove this, evaluate all the assumed local inequalities at
\(X_e=\log H_{e,N}^*\). Their linear terms sum to
\(\frac12\sum_e\operatorname{tr}
 [(\rho_{{\rm child},e,N}-\rho_{{\rm parent},e,N}^{\mathsf T})X_e]\).
The trace-norm/operator-norm inequality bounds this from below by
\(-R_N\sum_e\delta_{e,N}/2\). The preceding comparison with
\(\|Y_N\|\) proves the result. No exchange of a limit and an
infimum is used.

This gives a quantitative allowance for approximate geometric data.
Replacing any calibration matrix by one at trace-norm distance
\(\eta_{v,e,N}\) decreases its valid local constant by at most
\(R_N\eta_{v,e,N}/2\). On a fixed tree, a total error \(o(1)\)
therefore costs \(o(N)\) in the logarithmic lower bound. This is an
additive estimate for logarithmic certificates; it is not a bound
on the error in the original complex scalar.

In particular, for \(V>0\), such local certificates would give the
desired lower volume rate if
\[
 \sum_e\delta_{e,N}=o(1),\qquad
 \liminf_N\frac{2\pi}{N}\sum_v\beta_{v,N}\ge V.
\]
A separate full-metric trial with product of local norms
\(\widetilde F_N\) and
\(\limsup_N 2\pi N^{-1}\log\widetilde F_N\le V\)
would give the upper rate by tree Cauchy. Together these prove the
original volume identity: \(\|Y_N\|^2=1+|K_N|^2\), and a positive
rate implies \(|K_N|\to\infty\). No such geometric certificates
or trial are supplied here for arbitrary fixed short partial fillings.

The distinction from an unrestricted entropy calibration matters.
For an actual nonzero anchored leaf \(a\), an inequality
\[
 \log\|H^{1/2}a\|\ge c+\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\rho\log H)
 \qquad\hbox{for every }H>0
\]
with a finite constant \(c\) forces
\(\rho=aa^*/\|a\|^2\). Set \(H=e^{tP}\), where \(P\) is the
orthogonal projection onto \(a^\perp\), and let \(t\to\infty\).
The left side is constant, hence \(\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)=0\);
positivity and trace one force the asserted projector. With matched
densities on a tree this condition propagates to exact forward
subtree projectors: in a unitary basis with \(a/\|a\|=e_0\), the
same limit suppresses the parent's orthogonal child slices while its
linear calibration term on that edge is zero. The remaining local
inequality is that of the contracted normalized leaf. Repeat from
the leaves; the anchor ensures that these forward messages are nonzero.
Thus this unrestricted route requires exact quantum message projectors;
it does not rule out other calibration methods.

On the finite window the leaf has a valid approximate certificate.
Writing \(p=aa^*/\|a\|^2\), scalar Jensen in a spectral basis of
\(X\) gives
\[
 \log\|e^{X/2}a\|\ge\log\|a\|+\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(pX)
 \ge\log\|a\|-\frac{R_N}{2}\|p-\rho\|_1
                              +\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\rho X).
\]
There is also a useful necessary test: any valid leaf constant obeys
\(\beta\le\log\|a\|-R_N\{1-\operatorname{tr}(p\rho)\}\).
Substitute the allowed matrix \(X=R_N(I-2p)\) to obtain it.
Thus the bounded window permits approximate source alignment; it
does not make an arbitrary bulk Gaussian into a valid sharp witness.

The actual unscaled turns also have explicit calibrations. If \(U\)
is unitary, then for arbitrary positive \(H_o,H_i\) and every density
matrix \(\rho\),
\[
 \log\|H_o^{1/2}UH_i^{-1/2}\|_{\rm HS}
 \ge\frac12\operatorname{tr}(U\rho U^*\log H_o)
             -\frac12\operatorname{tr}(\rho\log H_i).
\]
This has constant \(\beta=0\), output density \(U\rho U^*\), and
dual input half-edge density \(\rho^{\mathsf T}\). It holds on the
entire positive cone, with no simultaneous diagonalization assumption.
For proof, set \(c=\|H_o^{1/2}UH_i^{-1/2}\|_{\rm op}^2\).
Then \(U^*H_oU\le cH_i\), hence
\(U^*\log H_oU-\log H_i\le(\log c)I\). Trace against \(\rho\)
and use the Hilbert--Schmidt norm's lower bound by the operator norm.
The logarithm preserves positive-matrix order because inverses reverse
it and
\[
 \log A=\int_0^\infty
       \{(1+t)^{-1}I-(A+tI)^{-1}\}\,dt.
\]
The integral identity follows by scalar integration in a spectral
basis; it converges in norm for every fixed positive matrix. This
proves the needed order statement without assuming that exponentiation
preserves matrix order. In the anchored compiler
\(U=\operatorname{diag}(1,J)\) is exactly unitary, since the physical
quarter-turn \(J\) reverses the complete normalized Newton basis.

The original closing also has an explicit full-metric family. Write
\(C(a,u)=(a,\ell_Nu)\), where \(\ell_N\ne0\) is the actual physical
closing row with its recorded phase and normalization. Put
\[
 r=(0,\ell_N),\qquad p_\ell=r^*r/\|\ell_N\|^2,\qquad
 p_\star=e_\star e_\star^*,\qquad
 \rho_\theta=(1-\theta)p_\star+\theta p_\ell,
 \quad 0\le\theta\le1.
\]
With \(h(\theta)=-(1-\theta)\log(1-\theta)-\theta\log\theta\)
and \(0\log0=0\), one has for every positive \(H=e^X\)
\[
 \log\|CH^{-1/2}\|_{\rm HS}
 \ge \theta\log\|\ell_N\|+\frac12h(\theta)
                         -\frac12\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\theta X).
\]
Use \(\rho_\theta^{\mathsf T}\) as the dual input half-edge density.
Indeed the squared norm is the sum of the two squared row norms.
Jensen bounds these below by
\(e^{-\operatorname{tr}(p_\star X)}\) and
\(\|\ell_N\|^2e^{-\operatorname{tr}(p_\ell X)}\). The two-term
log-sum inequality gives the displayed bound, including the endpoints
by continuity. The full closing tensor is unchanged; choosing
\(\theta=1\) for a lower estimate does not declare its actual
marginal pure. The leaf and closing projectors retain their complex
phases, since they are the full outer products, not diagonal entries.

An explicit family for the bilinear multiplication is now provided
by the [full-matrix proof](research_ordered_density_bilinear_calibration.md).
For a surjective tensor \(A\), write \(D=(AA^*)^{1/2}\) and
\(V=D^{-1}A\). Choose a density \(\rho\) commuting with \(\log D\)
and similarly ordered: in a common eigenbasis its weights \(w_i\)
and the eigenvalues \(k_i\) of \(\log D\) satisfy
\((w_i-w_j)(k_i-k_j)\ge0\).
Then the valid constant is
\(\beta=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\log D)\), the output density is
\(\rho\), and the two logical input densities are the marginals of
\(V^*\rho V\). They are transposed on the dual input half-edges.
This joint state is allowed to be entangled. The proof gives the
inequality on the full positive cone, not only diagonal metrics.
It applies to the original full anchored multiplication, which is
surjective by its unit. The family is restricted: compatible geometric
densities and the volume rate of their summed constants are not proved.

There is a concrete failed choice which should not be mistaken for
geometric matching. In the untransformed anchored Newton frame, a
literal unit crossing leaf \(a=(1,R^{\pm1})\) satisfies
\(\|a\|^2=N+1\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}a=1\).
Indeed \(R^{\pm1}_r=\kappa^{\pm1}(-q)^{\pm r}\),
where \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(|\kappa|=1\), and the sum of
\(q^{\pm2r}\), \(0\le r<N\), is zero.
Writing \(p=aa^*/(N+1)\), the largest eigenvalue of
\(\Re p\) is \((N+2)/(2N+2)\): if \(a=x+iy\) with real \(x,y\),
then \(x\perp y\), \(\|x\|^2=(N+2)/2\), and \(\|y\|^2=N/2\).
Thus every real density \(\sigma\) obeys
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(p\sigma)\le\frac{N+2}{2N+2}.
\]
Allow any complex leaf witness \(\rho\), but suppose its matching
parent logical density \(\sigma\) is real. For
\(\delta=\|\rho-\sigma\|_1\), trace zero gives
\(|\operatorname{tr}(p(\rho-\sigma))|\le\delta/2\).
The necessary leaf test above therefore yields
\[
 \beta_{\rm leaf}-R_N\delta/2
 \le\tfrac12\log(N+1)-R_N\frac{N}{2(N+1)} .
\]
At identity metrics every other local constant is at most
\(\log\|T_v\|\). Consequently the entire lower certificate is at most
\[
 L_N(I)-R_Nc_N-\log2<0,\qquad c_N=\frac{N}{2(N+1)}\ge\frac13.
\]
The strict inequality uses \(R_N=L_N(I)/\varepsilon+\log Z(I)\),
\(L_N(I)\ge0\), \(\log Z(I)>0\), and \(\varepsilon<1/3\).
It is weaker than the known anchor bound. A real covariance recipe
cannot fix this by choosing the correct complex leaf separately and
charging the mismatch to the error allowance.
Covariant unitary relabelling of that same recipe preserves this
limitation. It does not exclude new complex witnesses or nonunitary
reference changes. In particular the explicit leaf shear in section 5
of the new proof sends \(a\) to \(e_\star\) at polynomial cost,
with the inverse applied to the parent. It removes the hypothesis of
this raw-frame test without claiming global geometric matching.

Thus all local operation types now have explicit inequalities for
specified data. The remaining problem is geometric compatibility
and the volume rate, or the maximal-singular-vector test above.
In particular geodesic convexity does not automatically provide affine
supporting planes in all noncommuting coordinates \(X=\log H\).
This is a sufficient certificate with controlled error, not an asserted
exact entropy dual, a geometric comparison theorem or a new knot case.

The complete proof sources are the
[tree capacity theorem](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md),
[regularized metric theorem](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md)
and [anchored compiler](research_anchored_conway_positive_variational_period.md).

## A fixed regularizer and a uniformly positive quartic minimum, 22 November

There is a useful simplification of the fixed-degree problem. It can
be normalized so that its minimum is bounded above and below by positive
constants independent of the quantum level. The exponential growth then
lies in the normalization budget. This does not evaluate that growth.

Use the exact anchored compiler with output
\(Y_N=(1,K_N)\), including the original marked closing map and all
physical Hermite directions. Let its fixed tree have \(m\ge2\)
vertices. For positive full edge metrics \(H\), put
\[
 L_N(H)=\sum_v\log\|T_{v,N}\|_H,\qquad F_N(H)=e^{L_N(H)},
 \qquad Z(H)=1+\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(H_e+H_e^{-1}).
\]
The full-capacity and regularization proofs apply to this anchored
compiler: their needed lower bound is \(\|Y_N\|\ge1\).
Choose the fixed number
\[
 \varepsilon=\frac1{512m^2},\qquad
 J_{N,\varepsilon}(H)=L_N(H)+\varepsilon\log Z(H),
 \qquad H_N^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{H>0}J_{N,\varepsilon}(H),
 \qquad F_N=F_N(H_N^*).
\]
There is a unique minimizer. Its full trace-norm marginal mismatch
satisfies \(S_N\le2\varepsilon=1/(256m^2)\). Hence the tree estimate
gives
\[
 1-4m\sqrt{S_N}-5mS_N
       \ge\frac34-\frac5{256m}>\frac12,
 \qquad
 \boxed{\ \|Y_N\|\le F_N\le2\|Y_N\|.\ }
\]
Thus vanishing regularization is unnecessary for the exponential rate.
It gave a sharper relative approximation in the earlier theorem; a
constant comparison is enough here. The quantity used is the
unpenalized \(F_N\) at the minimizer, not the penalized minimum.

The fixed regularizer also gives a short proof of spectral control.
The original anchored tensor bounds give \(L_N(I)=O(N)\), and its
\(m-1\) edge spaces have dimension \(N+1\). Since \(L_N(H_N^*)\ge0\),
comparison with the identity metrics gives
\[
 \varepsilon\log Z(H_N^*)
 \le J_{N,\varepsilon}(H_N^*)\le J_{N,\varepsilon}(I)
 =L_N(I)+\varepsilon\log\{1+2(m-1)(N+1)\}=O(N).
\]
Thus, for this fixed construction, some \(C>0\) satisfies
\(e^{-CN}I\le H_{e,N}^*\le e^{CN}I\) at every edge.
Spectral bounds of this order were already available for the earlier
vanishing-regularizer construction; here they follow just from this
comparison. They give no geometric description of the eigenvectors.
Also, an \(O(N)\) penalty cannot be discarded in a volume limit.

An additional scalar change of gauge makes all \(m\) local tensor
norms equal to \(t_N=F_N^{1/m}\ge1\). To see this, take logarithms
of the desired norm changes. Their sum is zero, and the incidence
matrix of a tree maps its edge scalars onto exactly that zero-sum
subspace. Positive scalar edge gauges therefore realize the changes.
They preserve the contraction, product of norms and normalized marginal
matrices. No output value is needed to choose them.

Normalize each resulting tensor by \(16t_N\). Their total budget is
\(B_N=16^mF_N\). Use the ordinary quartic residual energy, retaining
the two-component closing map, and let its minimum be \(e_N\).
The normalized-source proof is unchanged for a vector closing:
the closing Hessian is still positive with operator norm at most
\(2/256\), and the source comparison uses the vector triangle
inequality followed by the same two-term Cauchy inequality. Therefore,
with \(\gamma=197/196\),
\[
 \frac{\|Y_N\|^2}{\gamma B_N^2}\le e_N
       \le\frac{\|Y_N\|^2}{B_N^2},\qquad
 \boxed{\quad
 \frac1{4\gamma16^{2m}}\le e_N\le\frac1{16^{2m}}.
 \quad}
\]
This is a new anchored, gauged quartic, not the earlier scalar-source
minimum. It remains quartic and has the same uniform Hessian bounds.
Its closing has two components, so the earlier rank-one source-normal
formula is not being applied to it. All its coefficients are specified
by the original tensors and the unique regularized metric problem.
This construction uses no assumed value or nonvanishing of \(K_N\).

For a hyperbolic knot, the remaining equation is still
\[
       \frac{2\pi}{N}\log F_N
                \longrightarrow\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K).
\]
The displayed comparison with \(\sqrt{1+|K_N|^2}\) makes this
equivalent to the original volume identity. The uniform positive
minimum has not supplied that equation: its unknown exponential scale
has moved into \(B_N\). In particular the full metric minimizers
still need a geometric description and an asymptotic estimate.

There is also a precise limit to ordinary covariance whitening.
The full multiplication \(M:H_N\otimes H_N\to H_N\) is surjective,
because the algebra has a unit. Put \(C=MM^*>0\). The whitened tensor
\(\widetilde M=C^{-1/2}M\) has normalized output marginal \(I_N/N\).
An adjacent nonzero closing row has a pure marginal after every
invertible inverse-transpose gauge. Their mismatch is consequently
\(2(1-1/N)\) in trace norm, with the prescribed transpose included.
This whitening alone cannot provide the small full-marginal defects
needed above. Likewise, rank-one moment matrices of an optimizing
packet field are not the reduced density matrices of its local
coefficient tensors; moment rigidity does not prove capacity balance.

[tree capacity theorem](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md),
[regularized metric theorem](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md),
[anchored compiler](research_anchored_conway_positive_variational_period.md)
and [normalized quartic source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md).

## Keeping the crossings in the finite algebra, 22 November

The [standard-crossing source](research_standard_crossing_hardy_source.md)
puts every original crossing power into the full repeated-root algebra.
The charged closing rows are then universal: they use the zero-power
Hardy projection. In the notation of that proof, the numerator is
\[
 A_{N,\mathbf b}=R_I\!\left(Q_N\prod_{v\in I}V_{b_v,N}\right),
 \qquad
 \mathscr S^{\mathbf b}_{N,\sigma}(\chi)
       =\bigotimes_v\mathscr T_{\sigma_v,0,\chi_v}
                   [A_{N,\mathbf b}] .
\]
Here \(V_{b_v,N}\) is the carrier-removed original crossing, with all
Hermite derivatives retained; the carriers are restored in the invariant.
This moves the powers into the state without replacing the actual
marked closing functional.

The comparison with the initialized Hardy source has an absolute gap:
for fixed real powers, locally uniformly in complex charges,
\[
 |\mathscr G-\mathscr S|
 \le C N^A\prod_v(1+|\chi_v|)^2
       \exp N\!\left(M_0-c+\pi\sum_v|\Im\chi_v|\right),
 \qquad c>0.
\]
Consequently the full nonzero expansion at sufficiently small fixed
positive charges is preserved. The sign average, unit-charge value,
original phases and prescribed signed Gaussian heat readouts are exact.
The old off-endpoint heat differential equation is not asserted for
this new family.

Its charge-shift equation has rank-one forcing. Crucially, that forcing
uses the same filled row \(p\mapsto\phi_N(V_bp)\). At a face
\(\chi_v=1\), the exact original filled trace is applied at \(v\),
while the other charged Hardy rows remain intact. There is no change
to a zero-power filling in this boundary operation. The rank-one
forcing does not eliminate the remaining \(N\)-dimensional module.

The error above is measured from the complete action \(M_0\).
At a short filling the geometric action may be smaller than \(M_0-c\),
so this comparison alone supplies no sharp bound at that filling.
The missing estimate remains a coherent bound at the filled geometric
action, including all boundary and alias contributions.

The complete final proof has 431 lines and SHA-256
`a861b2210a3dc02f5a59f383ee9c82dc6019357cb745dd7285eaf1607549ecc6`.
Its author, root and two independent peers have read the whole matching
final and all three complete direct proofs, checked the used implications
and renewed matching pins. Both new ledger sections have also received
whole-text root and two independent peer checks against their complete
matching proof sources.

## Larger positive primitive charges have smaller action, 22 November

There is a quantitative comparison at the same fixed real crossing
powers. Keep a finite original same-index graph, every retained edge,
complete outside angles, and a nonempty selected set \(I\) with every
vertex incident. Let \(d_v\) be its incidence degree. Repeated edges
remain distinct and loops count twice.
Suppose two configurations on the original marked positive branches
solve the full primitive equations at real charges
\(0<\boldsymbol\chi\le\boldsymbol\lambda\). Define
\[
 M(\boldsymbol\mu)=\Re\left[
   \sum_{e=vw}\psi(t_v,t_w)+
   \sum_{v\in I}\left(\frac{in_vt_v^2}{4\pi}-i\mu_vt_v\right)\right],
 \qquad t=t^\mu,\qquad H_v^\chi=-\Im t_v^\chi .
\]
All powers \(n_v\) are unchanged in this comparison. The original
complete constants and logarithmic periods are unchanged too.
The sign-flip comparison in the full angular contour proof gives
\(H_v^\chi>0\).

Here is an inline extension of the convex-energy argument to this
graph, including loops. The frozen variational theorem is stated for
circle trees, and the frozen absolute-action identity for paths; their
local formulas suffice for the following argument. Give each endpoint
incidence \(\iota\) its own return coordinates
\(r_\iota=k_\iota+ig_\iota\), and write \(v(\iota)\) for its vertex.
The two incidences \(\iota,\bar\iota\) of an edge remain separate
even for a loop. Its open angle conditions are
\[
 |s_{v(\iota)}|+2|g_{\bar\iota}|<\pi,\qquad
 |s_{v(\bar\iota)}|+2|g_\iota|<\pi,\qquad s_v=\Re t_v .
\]
These define a common convex domain, independently of the charge.
The sum \(\mathcal E=4\sum_e(E_{P,e}+E_{Q,e})\) of the original
strictly convex square energies is convex there. This follows by
their real linear incidence pullbacks; identifying the two vertex
labels of a loop does not affect convexity. At a positive geometric
configuration their local differential gives
\[
 d\mathcal E=\sum_\iota
   \{k_\iota\,ds_{v(\iota)}+h_{v(\iota)}\,dg_\iota\},
 \qquad h_v=\Im t_v .
\]
Outside angles are fixed and complete, so their terms vanish.
Put
\[
 C_v(X)=\sum_{\iota:\,v(\iota)=v}g_\iota-\frac{n_v}{2}s_v .
\]
At a primitive stationary point,
\(C_v(X^\mu)=-\pi\mu_v\) and
\(\sum_{\iota:\,v(\iota)=v}k_\iota=-n_vh_v/2\).
Consequently
\(\nabla\mathcal E(X^\chi)\cdot dX=\sum_{v\in I}h_v^\chi\,dC_v\).
The convex supporting-plane inequality at \(X^\chi\), applied to
\(X^\lambda\), proves
\[
 \mathcal E(X^\lambda)-\mathcal E(X^\chi)
 \ge \pi\sum_v H_v^\chi(\lambda_v-\chi_v).
\]
The absolute local edge identity, summed over all original edges with
both endpoint incidences retained,
gives at either positive endpoint
\(\mathcal E(X^\mu)=\pi\{M_0-M(\boldsymbol\mu)\}\), where
\(M_0=|E|M_\infty\). Indeed the terms
\(\sum_{v\in I}h_v\sum_{\iota:\,v(\iota)=v}g_\iota\) become
\(\sum_v(n_vs_vh_v/2-\pi\mu_vh_v)\), exactly canceling the
quadratic filling and charge terms. Complete-only edges retain their
action constants. Thus
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 M(\boldsymbol\lambda)\le M(\boldsymbol\chi)
       -\sum_v H_v^\chi(\lambda_v-\chi_v).
 \quad}
\]
No stationary solution at an intermediate charge is required.

For a positive Hardy index vector \(a_v\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\), the formal
effective charges are \(\lambda_v=\chi_v+a_v-1\). If that sector is identified
with an original positive marked stationary configuration, its action
is bounded by the displayed inequality. A nonprincipal index then has
a gap at least \(\min_vH_v^\chi>0\). Positivity also gives
\[
 0<\lambda_v<\frac{d_v+|n_v|}{2},
\]
because \(|s_v|<\pi\), \(|g_\iota|<\pi/2\), and
\(\pi\lambda_v=n_vs_v/2-\sum_{\iota:\,v(\iota)=v}g_\iota\).
Only finitely many index vectors can have such positive stationary
configurations, independently of \(N\).

Likewise, if \(0<\chi_v\le1\) and a same-powers face sets the charges
at \(v\in S\) to one, two supplied positive marked endpoints have
action gap at least \(\sum_{v\in S}H_v^\chi(1-\chi_v)\).
This is strict when a changed charge was below one.

These are positive-endpoint action comparisons. They prove neither
existence at the higher charges or faces nor a classification of all
Hardy sectors. Quotient aliases, radical channels, nonpositive
stationary points and source boundaries still require their actual
coupled source analysis. No quantum coefficient, integral upper
estimate, new knot class or volume-conjecture conclusion follows.

## Orthogonal Fourier projections with no contour heights, 22 November

The [Hardy source proof](research_hardy_reduced_polarized_source.md) now
gives an initialized reduced source without any contour-height choices.
For a canonical degree-less-than-\(N\) polynomial \(p\), put
\[
 f(t)=\sin t\,p(-2\cos t)
       e^{iN\{nt^2/(4\pi)+(1-\chi)t\}},\qquad -\pi\le t\le\pi.
\]
Join its endpoints periodically, and let \(P_+\) and \(P_-\) be the
orthogonal projections onto positive and negative integer Fourier
frequencies in ordinary angular \(L^2\). With
\(\eta=(-1)^{N-1}\) and \(\tau_j=\pi(N-1-2j)/N\), the exact local rows are
\[
 \mathscr T_{\pm,n,\chi}[p]
             =2\eta\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(P_\pm f)'(\tau_j).
\]
This retains the original derivative sampling, including the repeated
root normals and odd simple node. The derivative row is not replaced by
an \(L^2\) norm. The Fourier projections themselves are orthogonal.

The proof takes the height to zero at each fixed level before taking
any level limit. It controls the seam where the periodically joined
Gaussian can have a derivative jump. A Hilbert-transform estimate gives
the actual Chebyshev coefficient-row bound
\[
 \|\boldsymbol\ell^0_{\pm,n,\chi}\|_2
 \le C N^{5/2}\log(2N)(1+|n|+|\chi|)^2
          e^{\pi N|\Im\chi|+\pi N|\Im n|/4}.
\]
The original Frobenius coupons have a finite parity-sum formula and
coefficient norm bounded by the same expression with \(N^{3/2}\)
in place of \(N^{5/2}\). In particular all these local norms are
polynomial at fixed real powers and charges. These bounds concern
Chebyshev coordinates, not physical Hilbert--Schmidt norms.

The sign average, original unit-charge value with its crossing carriers,
and independent signed heat readouts are exact. An endpoint-current
estimate compares this source with the positive-height reduced source
at a sufficiently small fixed positive charge. Its error has a strict
exponential gap. Thus the nonzero starting expansion and every fixed
order survive. This comparison uses the actual endpoint estimates;
it does not follow from the common endpoint value alone. Outside
variables are complete for this analytic statement.

There is also a clean global complete-action bound for the whole new
source. Let \(f_N^{\mathrm{coef}}\) denote the Chebyshev coefficient vector
of the original numerator. The real profile and cosine Parseval give
\(\|f_N^{\mathrm{coef}}\|_2\le C_\Gamma N^A e^{NM_0}\), where
\(M_0=|E|M_\infty\) counts every retained edge. The uniformly bounded
Chebyshev remainder map gives the same bound for the reduced coefficient
vector. Apply the displayed local row bound in every selected coordinate.
After absorbing logarithms into a fixed power of \(N\),
\[
 |\mathscr G_{N,\boldsymbol\sigma}(\boldsymbol n,\boldsymbol\chi)|
 \le C_\Gamma N^{A_\Gamma}
     \prod_v(1+|n_v|+|\chi_v|)^2
 \exp N\left[M_0+\pi\sum_v|\Im\chi_v|
                         +\frac\pi4\sum_v|\Im n_v|\right].
\]
This is for the carrier-removed source, with complete outside data.
It removes the artificial height cost. It is a complete-action bound;
the required filled geometric action can be strictly smaller. No
Rivin-relative upper estimate or new volume-conjecture case follows.

## A bounded metric does not supply the sharp upper rate, 22 November

There is an exact limit on estimating the reduced source by one
full-vector Cauchy inequality. Consider the literal same-index star
with one selected vertex of fixed even valence \(d\ge4\), all its
neighbors complete, and crossing power \(n=1\) or \(n=-1\). Put
\(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), and
\[
 F_N(t)=K_N(t,0)^d,\qquad M_0=dM_\infty,\qquad
 Q_N=\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}F_N
      =\sum_{j=0}^{D}q_j B_j,\qquad B_j=T_j(-z/2).
\]
Here \(z=-2\cos t\). This is the actual ordinary numerator and its
full Hermite remainder, with the original complete factors retained.
It is a test of a proposed estimate, not an identification of this
star with a knot case.

The constant coefficient of the unreduced cosine expansion is
\[
 c_0=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}K_N(t,0)^d\,dt
                       =e^{NM_0+O(\log N)}.
\]
Indeed the integrand is nonnegative because \(d\) is even.
The actual nonzero complete-kernel expansion gives a polynomial
times \(e^{NM_0}\) on a window of width \(N^{-1/2}\) about zero;
the global real profile gives the matching upper bound.
The high-Fourier estimate and exact aliases in the
[reduction proof](research_hermite_reduced_polarized_initializer.md)
show that reduction changes this coefficient by at most
\(CN^A e^{N(M_0-c)}\), for a fixed \(c>0\). Consequently
\[
                         |q_0|=e^{NM_0+O(\log N)}.       \tag{M1}
\]
Thus this large coordinate survives the polynomial quotient.

At unit charge write the carrier-removed reduced source as
\(rq=\sum_jr_jq_j\), retaining its literal complex row
\[
 r_j=C_{N,n}^{-1}\phi_N(R^n B_j).
\]
The exact Newton expansion is
\[
 R^\pm=\kappa^{\pm1}\sum_{j=0}^{D}(-q_N)^{\pm j}e_j,
 \qquad q_N=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad |\kappa|=1.
\]
Since \(\phi_N(e_j)=\mathbf1_{j=D}\) and the carrier is a unit,
\[
 |r_0|=|\phi_N(R^\pm)|=1.                               \tag{M2}
\]
The positive isolated-vertex cone branch exists here because
\(d+|n|>2\). Its correctly marked real stationary action satisfies
\[
 S=M_{d,n}(1)<M_0,\qquad
 M_{d,n}'(\lambda)=\Im t_{d,n}(\lambda)<0
                          \quad(0<\lambda\le1).         \tag{M3}
\]
This uses the original primitive periods and action normalization.

All unadorned norms below are Euclidean norms in these Chebyshev
coefficient coordinates, before inserting the displayed metric.
For any positive diagonal coefficient metric \(W\), even depending
on \(N\), its Cauchy upper envelope obeys
\[
 B_W:=\|rW^{-1/2}\|\,\|W^{1/2}q\|
       \ \ge\ |r_0q_0|=|q_0|.                          \tag{M4}
\]
The two factors containing \(W_{00}^{1/2}\) cancel in this lower
bound. More generally, for any positive definite Hermitian Gram
\(H\), let \(\kappa(H)=\lambda_{\max}(H)/\lambda_{\min}(H)\).
The exact source still satisfies \(|rq|\le B_H\), but
\[
 B_H:=\|rH^{-1/2}\|\,\|H^{1/2}q\|
 \ge\kappa(H)^{-1/2}\|r\|\,\|q\|
 \ge\kappa(H)^{-1/2}|q_0|.                              \tag{M5}
\]
Hence every subexponentially conditioned Gram leaves this envelope
with lower exponential rate at least \(M_0>S\). In particular the
uniformly conditioned Chebyshev quotient Gram cannot by itself
supply the sharp rate. An estimate \(B_H\le CN^A e^{NS}\) would require
\[
 \log\kappa(H)\ge2N(M_0-S)-O(\log N).                    \tag{M6}
\]
This does not exclude intrinsically exponential geometric metrics.
It also does not exclude coherent trial or sum-of-squares
certificates, which retain cancellations that this single norm
envelope discards. No growth assertion for the exact scalar \(rq\),
knot counterexample, or failure of the volume conjecture is inferred.

## Hermite reduction preserves the starting expansion, 22 November

The [reduction proof](research_hermite_reduced_polarized_initializer.md)
now justifies removing polynomial relation directions before polarizing
the source. In each selected variable it takes the ordinary remainder
modulo \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\). This is the full Hermite quotient: it keeps
the repeated-root derivatives and every Jordan channel. It does not
replace that algebra by its distinct-root values.

The analytic point is a uniform exponential bound on every continuous
Fourier coefficient of the original graph numerator having a selected
frequency at least \(N\) in absolute value. Shifting one entire angular
period cancels its vertical sides exactly. The actual local kernel
expansion controls the central cube; the global real-angular profile
controls its complement. Exact Chebyshev folding, including first
derivatives, then proves that the remainder changes the numerator by
an exponentially smaller term on sufficiently thin complex strips.

Consequently the reduced polarized source has the same actual nonzero
starting expansion, to every fixed order, at sufficiently small fixed
positive charges. It also has the exact original cosine source and
unit-charge endpoint, with all crossing carriers retained. Fixed heights
preserve the signed heat readouts; a moving-height composition keeps its
endpoint and holomorphy without acquiring the old heat equation. The
analytic expansion is asserted with outside variables at their complete
values; exact algebraic congruences retain ordinary outside polynomials.

There is now a precise positive quotient metric for the polynomial
relations. Let \(R\) be the tensor Chebyshev remainder matrix, acting on
the original finite coefficient box. Its low-degree columns are the
identity and its row and column sums have bounds depending only on the
fixed graph. Thus, in these coefficient coordinates,
\[
 G=(RR^*)^{-1},\qquad C_\Gamma^{-2}I\preceq G\preceq I,
 \qquad R^*GR=\operatorname{Proj}_{(\ker R)^\perp}.
\]
The bounds are independent of the quantum level. This auxiliary positive
Gram is distinct from the original bilinear Frobenius trace, which is
retained literally. No monomial-coordinate or physical Hilbert--Schmidt
norm bound is inferred.

This gives an exact simplification of the quadratic upper trial. For raw
Chebyshev coefficient data \(f\), the reduced closing row \(\ell\), and
any \(\lambda>0\),
\[
 \min_x\{\lambda\|x-f\|^2+|\ell Rx|^2\}
 =\min_q\{\lambda(q-Rf)^*G(q-Rf)+|\ell q|^2\}.
\]
Indeed fix \(q=Rx\) and apply the minimum-lift identity to \(x-f\).
The relation variables disappear without increasing polynomial degree.
This is elimination for the new reduced-source quadratic; it is not an
equality with the previous unreduced polarization's quadratic minimum.

The reduced local rows also have explicit coupons in the original finite
Frobenius algebra, including their original endpoint phases. Only ideal
relations are killed; a direction merely invisible to one closing row
cannot be deleted on this argument. Ideal relations cannot return under
quotient multiplication. No new boundary-turn adapter is asserted.

The remaining sharp geometric upper estimate concerns this new reduced
family. Neither quotient conditioning nor the proved starting expansion
supplies that estimate along the full critical curve. No new knot class,
volume lower bound or finite-exception theorem is claimed.

## Full angular contours and a critical-point-centered family, 22 November

The [full angular contour proof](research_full_midpoint_polarized_initializer.md)
removes the artificial angular cutoff and the table of heights indexed by
removed subsets. For every fixed finite same-index graph, with every
selected vertex incident, and every fixed real choice of crossing powers,
it constructs a genuine polarized source using the full interval
\([-\pi,\pi]\) and one positive height per selected vertex. All original
edges, including complete-only factors, first normals and both level
parities are retained. The original unit-charge value is exact.

The starting expansion is proved at sufficiently small fixed positive
charges, with a nonzero leading coefficient and every fixed inverse-level
order. The allowable charge can depend on the graph and powers. The proof
uses the global ordinary-real kernel estimate and a weighted maximum
principle on a polydisk. Every added horizontal wing and vertical side
then has a strict exponential gap near the starting point. There is no
claim that endpoint equality alone preserves an asymptotic expansion.

This also simplifies the coefficient-space upper trial. The exact closing
row is a single tensor product \(\ell_N=\bigotimes_v r_v\), so
\(\|\ell_N\|^2=\prod_v\|r_v\|^2\). No subset-dependent row sum is needed.
The positive quadratic upper trial has coefficient condition number below
two. Its size can nevertheless be exponential; no trial with the required
geometric growth estimate has yet been constructed.

At fixed powers there is a second exact simplification. For any supplied
positive unit-charge primitive solution, the sign-flip comparison gives
\(\Im t_v<0\). A marked holomorphic critical curve from a small positive
seed to that solution can therefore be kept in the lower half-plane.
Choosing the complex contour heights \(h_v(\zeta)=i t_v(\zeta)\) puts each
horizontal contour through its critical point for every parameter. The
slanted contour still encloses exactly the original physical grid, and its
unit-charge endpoint is the same original source with the prescribed
crossing carriers restored. Its actual starting
expansion is proved by uniform bounds on all slanted boundary pieces.

This moving-height family generally loses the fixed-height heat equation
and the all-even heat-readout comparison. The generic analytic continuation
criterion for a fixed filling needs neither property. Its formal
coefficients continue along the chosen curve and the leading coefficient
is nonzero. What remains to be proved for this concrete family is
\[
 \sup_{\zeta\in K}
 \left|N^{-\beta}e^{-NS(\zeta)}
                  \widehat{\mathcal G}_{N,+}(\zeta)\right|
 \le C_K N^{B_K},\qquad K\Subset D_* ,
 \qquad \beta=\frac{3(m-e)}2.
\]
Here \(S\) is the original marked critical action, \(m\) counts selected
vertices, and \(e\) counts all retained edges. A local complex-area squared
norm bound also suffices. The fixed-height upper criterion applies to this
new holomorphic family through its general analytic statement, not through
the discarded heat equation.

The construction does not supply this sharp upper estimate, an actual
global kernel expansion at every new center, or positive geometric charts
for arbitrary short fillings. The source-to-knot marking and volume
calibration must also be retained. No new class of knots satisfying the
volume identity is claimed, and the finite-exception theorem remains open.

## A relative Hessian bound enlarges the proved filling range, 22 November

The [relative Hessian proof](research_network_relative_sector_source.md)
gives an additional range of actual fillings, including adjacent selected
vertices. The original general network condition
\[
 n_v^2+d_v^2\ge4096
\]
can be replaced by
\[
 \boxed{\quad n_v^2+d_v^2\ge1024
                    \quad\text{at every selected vertex.}\quad}
\]
Here \(d_v\) is the actual incidence degree, with loops counted twice,
and \(n_v\) is the original fixed signed crossing power. Any fixed finite
graph and selected adjacency are allowed. In particular, degree at
least \(32\) now permits every fixed power, including zero, even beside
other selected vertices. No edges or incidences are added to meet the
condition.

The new estimate uses the edge's own positive real Hessian as its
reference metric. Write
\[
 K=-2\pi\psi''=H+iJ,\qquad
 y=\big(\Im\tan(t/2)\big)^2+\big(\Im\tan(u/2)\big)^2 .
\]
The exact two-by-two determinant identity gives, whenever \(y<1\),
\[
 H>0,\qquad \det H\ge1-y,\qquad
 \|H^{-1/2}JH^{-1/2}\|^2
       =(\det H)^{-1}-1\le\frac{y}{1-y}.
\]
The resulting bilinear bound on \(|a^TJb|\) survives averaging along
the Taylor segment and summing all original edge incidences. It avoids
the loss from bounding the real and imaginary parts separately in the
ambient norm.

On the enlarged contour, with real angles between \(-\pi/2\) and
\(\pi/2\) and imaginary heights at most \(1/5\), the proof obtains
\[
 \tfrac12I<H<2I,\qquad
 |a^TJb|\le\tfrac3{10}
                 \sqrt{(a^THa)(b^THb)} .
\]
For each charge in the full cube there is a unique critical point
within \(|t_v|\le1/5\), namely the continued positive branch.
Every nonempty vertical-current set \(S\) is then below
the geometric stationary rate by more than
\((1/60)\sum_{v\in S}d_v\). Completing the charges on a removed
set costs at most \((7/2048)\sum_{v\in S}d_v\); the original centered
row loss still leaves a gap greater than
\((1/10)\sum_{v\in S}d_v\).

These are estimates on the original finite source. Its rows, trace
aliases, first and mixed normals, both level parities, and small complex
outside colors are retained. The geometric term has the same specified
nonzero amplitude and original phases as in the earlier network
theorem. Thus this result proves survival of the contribution; it does
not merely construct a critical point.

For an original marked circle-tree realization, use the original
carriers and filling slopes, so \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\).
The positive primitive solution satisfies the marked completion
theorem and its absolute volume identity. If all auxiliary vertices
are filled and the original strand tracing gives one main component
and no internal closed component, the resulting knot satisfies the
original full-sequence Kashaev volume identity under the new condition.
An arbitrary graph is not thereby a knot presentation.

This is a genuine enlargement of the proved parameter range, but the
finite-exception theorem remains open. The argument does not cover
arbitrary fixed short components containing vertices with
\(n_v^2+d_v^2<1024\). The graph and powers are fixed before taking
the quantum-level limit.

## The Hessian metric does not supply global continuation, 22 November

The relative sector bound above controls the imaginary Hessian in its
real metric. That metric can nevertheless reach the boundary of the
original positive chart in finite length, even when the imaginary
Hessian vanishes throughout the path.

Take two adjacent selected vertices of degree three and power zero,
each with two edges to complete outside vertices. Put both selected
angles equal to \(t_1=t_2=-ih\), and define
\[
 h_0=2\operatorname{arsinh}1,\qquad
 \tau=\tanh(h/2),\qquad q=\sqrt{1-2\tau^2},\qquad
 s=\operatorname{sech}(h/2),\qquad 0<h<h_0 .
\]
The original returns are
\[
 r(t_1,t_2)=-i\arcsin(\sinh(h/2)),\qquad
 r(t_v,0)=-i\arcsin\tau .
\]
Thus the original zero-power equations with equal charges hold at
\[
 \chi(h)=\frac{\arcsin(\sinh(h/2))+2\arcsin\tau}{\pi}.
\]
This function increases from zero to one as \(h\uparrow h_0\).
The [positive-edge criterion](research_positive_edge_global_monotonicity.md)
makes every edge strictly positive before that limit: the internal
square root is \(q>0\), and each outside square root is \(s>0\).

The exact edge Hessian in the
[relative-sector proof](research_network_relative_sector_source.md)
is real on this path. On the internal edge it is
\[
 K=q^{-1}
 \begin{pmatrix}1-\tau^2&\tau^2\\ \tau^2&1-\tau^2\end{pmatrix},
\]
with eigenvalues \(q\) and \(q^{-1}\). Each outside edge contributes
\(K_{tt}=s\) in its selected coordinate. Consequently the assembled
real Hessian metric has path speed
\[
 \left\|\frac{d(t_1,t_2)}{dh}\right\|_{H_\Gamma}^2
       =\frac2q+4s,\qquad J_\Gamma=0 .
\]
Yet
\[
 q^2=\frac{h_0-h}{\sqrt2}+O((h_0-h)^2),
 \qquad
 \int^{h_0}\sqrt{2/q+4s}\,dh<\infty .
\]
The unit-charge limit therefore reaches a degenerate original edge
at finite metric distance despite a perfect relative sector bound.
This audits an attempted extension beyond the proved filling range;
it asserts neither failure of the volume identity nor a topological
obstruction to hyperbolicity. Continuing the quantum argument needs
an actual source-preserving change of chart with its endpoint currents
retained. Classical strict concavity alone does not provide it.

## The midpoint cutoff meets the gluing equation at the fold, 22 November

The [exact edge-difference source](research_edge_kernel_difference_and_endpoint_bound.md)
identifies an equation that separated cutoff pieces do not retain. Put
\(N\ge2\), \(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), and
\[
 c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\quad s_j=2\sin(j\pi/N),\quad
 S_j=\prod_{r=1}^j s_r,\quad
 e_j(z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{r<j}(c_r-z),\quad S_0=1.
\]
Write \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), where \(T_N\) is Chebyshev's polynomial,
and \(K_{\le L}(z,w)=\sum_{j=0}^L e_j(z)e_j(w)\). The original
Askey--Wilson operator obeys
\(\mathscr L_z e_j=c_je_j-s_j^2e_{j-1}\), with \(e_{-1}=0\).
Together with \(we_j=c_je_j-s_{j+1}^2e_{j+1}\) for \(j<D\), this telescopes to
\[
 (w-\mathscr L_z)K_{\le L}
       =-s_{L+1}^2e_L(z)e_{L+1}(w)\qquad(0\le L<D).
\]
This is nonzero even in the full tensor algebra
\(\mathcal A_N\otimes\mathcal A_N\), where
\(\mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N)\): both factors are nonzero Newton
basis elements and \(s_{L+1}\ne0\). In contrast the full kernel satisfies
\[
 (w-\mathscr L_z)K_N
   =(w-c_0)e_D(z)e_D(w)=\frac{\eta}{N^2}P_N(w)e_D(z).
\]
Its defect vanishes in the full physical quotient, including every
required first normal. The complementary sector cancels the cutoff
forcing upon recombination; neither piece separately has that equation.

For \(T_{j,N}(t,u)=e_j(-2\cos t)e_j(-2\cos u)\), the exact finite relation is
\[
 T_{j+1,N}=
 \frac{[\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)+\cos t][\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)+\cos u]}
      {4\sin^4((j+1)\pi/N)}\,T_{j,N}\qquad(j<D).
\]
The multiplicative identity retains Newton zeros. As \(j/N\to x\in(0,1)\),
its ratio tends locally to
\[
 \mathcal R(x;t,u)=
 \frac{[\cos(2\pi x)+\cos t][\cos(2\pi x)+\cos u]}{4\sin^4(\pi x)}.
\]
On a regular logarithmic chart the product of finite ratios gives a
local action with \(A_x=\Log\mathcal R\) modulo \(2\pi i\mathbb Z\).
Thus original interior wire gluing requires \(\mathcal R=1\),
independently of the integer Fourier alias or logarithmic lift.

Set \(a=\tan(t/2)\), \(b=\tan(u/2)\), \(q_e^2=1+a^2+b^2\).
Where these half-angle coordinates and displayed denominators are regular,
\(\mathcal R=1\) gives
\[
 \cos(2\pi x)=\frac{a^2+b^2}{2+a^2+b^2},
 \qquad \cot^2(\pi x)=q_e^2.
\]
The two local wire branches therefore meet at \(x=1/2\) when \(q_e^2=0\).
For the low-sector cutoff \(L/N\to1/2\), the limiting defect is exactly
\[
 \mathcal R(1/2;t,u)-1
 =\sin^2(t/2)\sin^2(u/2)-1
 =-\frac{q_e^2}{(1+a^2)(1+b^2)}.
\]
This is a classical limit, not an exact replacement of the parity-shifted
finite cutoff. Away from the fold it is a classical local unit, not a
uniformly bounded quantum inverse or an estimate making the current small.
One cannot apply same-filled-group volume rigidity independently to cut
pieces without restoring their missing relations. Recombination
restores the exact equation above; no full-cycle coefficient or new filling
case follows from this calculation.

## Formal continuation is settled for supplied positive targets, 22 November

The [marked positive-source theorem](research_positive_source_formal_component.md)
discharges the formal continuation and leading-coefficient conditions in
the upper-bound criterion below for the following class: a fixed finite
original same-index graph with no isolated selected vertex, complete
outside angles, fixed real powers,
and a supplied solution of the original unit-charge primitive equations
with every original edge block positive. This is not a claim that every
hyperbolic short partial filling has such a solution.

The proof retains independent wire and angle variables. Put
\[
 w_v=\tan(t_v/2),\qquad q_e=\cot(\pi x_e),\qquad
 q_e^2=1+w_v^2+w_u^2,
 \qquad H=-\Phi''_{(x,t)},\quad\Delta=\det H.
\]
Every post-leading factorial coefficient and every phase derivative of
order at least two is rational in these coordinates. Finite Gaussian
contractions therefore give the actual initialized formal coefficients.
Their leading density is
\[
 a_0=\left(\frac{i}{\pi}\right)^m(2\pi)^{(e+m)/2}
       \frac{\displaystyle\prod_{v\in I}\sin t_v
                    \prod_e\frac{1+q_e^2}{4}}{\sqrt\Delta},
\]
where \(m\) counts selected vertices and \(e\) counts retained edges.
Edges with both endpoints outside the selected set keep their exact
complete-kernel factors and are included in \(e\).
The determinant root has its original seed mark. The coefficients
themselves stay holomorphic through zero selected tangents; dividing by
\(a_0\) can introduce artificial poles there. At a vanishing wire square
root, the formal continuation remains regular if the incidence factors
stay nonzero and the full Hessian stays nonsingular.
No global asymptotic for the exact factorials is inferred from this.

The original positive tangent domain is star shaped. Its canonical wire
and return logarithms therefore have the same complete marking throughout.
For the primitive map
\[
 P_v=\sum_{e\ni v}r_{v,e}-in_vt_v/2,
 \qquad \chi_v=iP_v/\pi,
\]
the positive edge matrices give \(\Re P_t>0\). The real powers do
not change that Hermitian part. The wire Hessian block is invertible,
and its full Schur complement is \(P_t/\pi\), so \(\Delta\) never
vanishes on this domain. Global edge comparison also proves that the
complex charge map is injective. It is a biholomorphism onto an open
contractible complex charge image, with the original marked action and
all formal coefficients holomorphic there.

A vertex sign flip changes only the corresponding charge sign. It follows
that \(\chi_v=0\) exactly when \(w_v=0\). Hence the formal leading
density is nonzero at every supplied positive unit-charge target. A fixed
holomorphic curve from the actual small-charge seed to that target can be
chosen inside the positive domain while avoiding all those zeros. The
charges on this curve vary independently and can be complex; a common
real radial charge path is unnecessary.

The source along the curve is still the same initialized contour family,
with its heights and complete source data frozen at the seed. Its actual
all-order coefficients agree with the rational Gaussian formulas there,
at both level parities, and their marked continuations are now supplied
by the theorem. Thus, for this positive-target class, the remaining
analytic requirement in the criterion below is the sharp complex upper
estimate for that source, with any fixed polynomial loss. That estimate
has not been proved. Source identification and marked action-volume
calibration remain necessary for a knot statement; arbitrary nonpositive
short-filling configurations are not covered. No new volume-conjecture
case or finite-exception theorem is claimed.

## Polynomial upper bounds can propagate the initialized source, 22 November

The [polynomial upper-bound criterion](research_polarized_polynomial_upper_criterion.md)
gives a different sufficient target for the cancellation problem. Use the
fixed, actually initialized contour polarization, with its complete outside
data and all original currents retained. Fix the powers before taking the
level limit. On a connected complex charge domain \(D\), suppose \(S\)
is holomorphic and continues the initialized marked action. Write
\[
 f_N(\chi)=N^{-\beta}e^{-NS(\chi)}\mathscr G_N(\chi),
 \qquad \beta=3(m-e)/2.
\]
Suppose its initialized formal coefficients extend holomorphically along
that domain. A locally polynomial upper bound
\[
                  \sup_K|f_N|\le C_KN^{B_K}
                  \qquad(K\Subset D)
\]
then propagates the actual all-order starting expansion to the target.
It need not have the exact asymptotic power of the desired answer.

The proof subtracts a high but fixed truncation of the starting expansion.
Its remainder is \(O(N^{-L})\) on the initial disk and \(O_L(N^B)\)
on a buffered chain, with \(B\) independent of \(L\). After \(J\)
three-circles steps its bound is
\[
 O_L\!\left(N^{-L\theta+B(1-\theta)}\right),
 \qquad \theta=2^{-J}.
\]
Choosing \(L\) sufficiently large proves every fixed asymptotic order.
For the leading term alone it suffices to continue the finite jet with
\[
                     L\ge\max\{1,2^J(B+1)-B\}.
\]
Neither this order nor the disk chain depends on \(N\). If the continued
leading coefficient is nonzero at charge one, the literal endpoint identity
gives a nonzero asymptotic for the original marked scalar. Both level
parities must have that property. The marked action and all original
normalization factors remain part of the statement.

A local complex-area \(L^2\) upper bound with polynomial loss also suffices,
by the holomorphic submean inequality. This connects the criterion to
positive estimates without inferring a lower bound from positivity alone.
Bounds only on real charges or physical samples do not supply the required
complex-neighborhood estimate.

The same note gives an explicit quadratic upper trial for the correct
off-endpoint representative. Retain the full unreduced ordinary polynomial
coefficient vector \(f_N^{\rm coef}\), and let \(\ell_N(\chi)\) be the
sum of the exact tensor rows from its frozen contour construction. Thus
\(\mathscr G_N=\ell_Nf_N^{\rm coef}\), including physical first normals.
With \(\lambda_N=1+\|\ell_N\|^2\), put
\[
 J_{N,\chi}(x)=\lambda_N\|x-f_N^{\rm coef}\|^2+|\ell_Nx|^2.
\]
Its coefficient condition number is below two, and every trial satisfies
\( |\mathscr G_N|^2\le2J_{N,\chi}(x)\).
The ordinary coefficient dimension is \(O_\Gamma(N^m)\); this is not an
extension of the linear-dimensional cyclic compression to arbitrary charge
coupons. The row norms and forcing can still have exponential size.

The missing estimate is now a possible upper trial bound: its complex-area
energy, multiplied by \(N^{-2\beta}e^{-2N\Re S}\), should have only
polynomial growth on buffered compact charge sets. No such general trial
bound is proved here. Holomorphic continuation of the required formal jet,
its nonzero target coefficient, and the geometric value of the marked
action also remain separate requirements. This deduction adds no filling
class and does not establish the finite-exception theorem.

## The quadratic needs only linearly many unknowns, 22 November

The [cyclic reduction](research_burau_cyclic_quadratic_reduction.md)
reduces the Euclidean quadratic from \(N^{2k}\) complex variables to
at most \(k(N-1)+1\), with exactly the same minimum. Here \(k\) is the
number of crossing occurrences in the fixed completed knot braid,
chosen before letting \(N\) tend to infinity. The bound is not a
uniform bound over different filling assignments.

The reduction uses the actual terminal vector \(v\), rather than
discarding internal channels during the tangle construction. For the
contracted operator \(C\), let
\[
 \mathcal K=\operatorname{span}\{v,Cv,\ldots,C^{L-1}v\},
 \qquad L=k(N-1)+1.
\]
Nilpotence gives \(\dim\mathcal K=m\le L\). An orthonormal basis,
starting with \(v/\|v\|\), gives a compressed operator \(B\) and a
forcing vector \(a\) with
\[
 B^m=0,\qquad \|B\|\le\tfrac12,\qquad a_0=1.
\]
The complementary variables can be eliminated by solving their
residual equations exactly. Merely restricting the old variable to
\(\mathcal K\) would not have the same effect. After a scalar
rescaling, the exact remaining problem is
\[
 j_\tau(z)=4\tau\|(I-B^*)z-a\|^2+|z_0|^2,\qquad
 z\in\mathbb C^m,\quad \tau\ge1.
\]
Its original closing and minimum satisfy
\[
 K_N=\zeta a^*(I-B)^{-1}e_0,\qquad
 \mu_\tau=\min_zj_\tau(z),\qquad
 \mu_\tau\le |K_N|^2\le(1+\tau^{-1})\mu_\tau.
\]
The positive correction factor and the complex phase are exactly
those of the preceding full-space quadratic. These statements
include zeros and all even or composite levels.

The complex quadratic coefficient lies between \(\tau I\) and
\((9\tau+1)I\); its Euclidean condition number is at most ten.
For the explicitly specified half-gradient
\[
 g_\tau(z)=4\tau(I-B)\big((I-B^*)z-a\big)+e_0z_0,
\]
every trial gives the lower and upper certificates
\[
 [j_\tau(z)-\tau^{-1}\|g_\tau(z)\|^2]_+
 \le |K_N|^2\le(1+\tau^{-1})j_\tau(z).
\]
Thus the degree remains two while the number of unknowns is now
linear in the quantum level. There is no exponential scale in the
Hessian coefficient. The forcing can still have exponential size.

The basis is obtained from the vectors \(C^rv\). Constructing its
Gram matrix and the projected source can still require the original
large tensor calculation; their small eigenvalues are not controlled
here. In particular, their entries retain the coherent power
coefficients. This is a reduction of the minimization problem, not
a claim of linear computational cost or a new geometric lower bound.
The condition \(a_0=1\) does not prevent cancellation in the prescribed
closing. No additional filling case or finite-exception theorem is
proved.

## An exact limit on the contraction argument, 22 November

The height contraction is valid, but optimizing its norm budget cannot
by itself give a volume-sharp estimate in every permitted presentation.
This can be proved for every positive metric, including full matrix
gauges, in the original normalization diagram. The issue survives
removing all states invisible to the complete sequence of observations.
It is a test of a general proposed method, rather than an additional
knot family.

First, for any specified matrix \(C\), source row \(\ell\), endpoint
\(H\), and invertible similarity \(S\), put
\[
 \rho=\|SCS^{-1}\|<1,\qquad
 P=\|\ell S^{-1}\|\,\|SH\|.
\]
Submultiplicativity gives the source-invariant inequalities
\[
 |\ell C^rH|\le P\rho^r,\qquad
 |\ell(I-C)^{-1}H|\le\frac{P}{1-\rho}.
 \tag{C7}
\]
Thus every such resolvent budget is at least
\(\max_r|\ell C^rH|\). A positive Hermitian metric gives a
similarity of this form by taking its positive square root.
The assertion consequently includes every same-space positive
Hilbert metric, rather than just diagonal height weights.

**The literal normalization source.** At level \(N\ge2\), put
\(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\). Take a physical positive curl:
\(b=2,k=1,w=1\). Its auxiliary crossing is negative. The bridge
gives \(C=Qa_-\) and \(\zeta=Q\). In the Fourier-height basis the
endpoint has only \(p=0\), and \(C\) preserves \(p\). The other
blocks can therefore be removed exactly. The factors \(\sqrt N\)
and \(N^{-1/2}\) in the remaining endpoint and source cancel.
The resulting \(N\)-dimensional system has source \(e_0^*\),
endpoint \(\mathbf1\), and matrix
\[
 C_{j,j+1}=Q(1-Q^{j+1})\quad(0\le j<N-1),
 \qquad C_{ij}=0\text{ otherwise}.
 \tag{C8}
\]
Put \(F_r=(Q;Q)_r=\prod_{a=1}^r(1-Q^a)\), with \(F_0=1\).
Its exact observed powers are
\[
 \alpha_r=e_0^*C^r\mathbf1=Q^rF_r\quad(0\le r<N),
 \qquad \alpha_r=0\quad(r\ge N).
 \tag{C9}
\]
Since \(F_N=0\),
\[
 Q^rF_r=Q^{-1}(F_r-F_{r+1}),\qquad
 e_0^*(I-C)^{-1}\mathbf1=Q^{-1},\qquad K_N=1.
 \tag{C10}
\]
There is also a complete bounded solution before closing:
\[
 (I-C)g=\mathbf1,\qquad g_j=Q^{-j-1},\qquad \|g\|=\sqrt N.
\]
The interior equations and the last equation \(g_{N-1}=1\)
verify this directly.

The discrepancy in a norm budget is sharp. Write \(s_r=|F_r|\),
\(M_N=\max_{0\le r<N}s_r\), and define
\[
 \mathcal B_N=
 \inf_{\substack{S\ {\rm invertible}\\\|SCS^{-1}\|<1}}
 \frac{\|e_0^*S^{-1}\|\,\|S\mathbf1\|}
                  {1-\|SCS^{-1}\|}.
\]
Then, at every level \(N\ge2\),
\[
 M_N\le\mathcal B_N\le eN^{3/2}M_N.
 \tag{C11}
\]
The lower bound is (C7). For the upper bound choose
\(\rho=1-1/N\) and \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s_j\rho^{-j})\).
Every entry of \(SCS^{-1}\) on its strict superdiagonal has
modulus \(\rho\), so its norm is \(\rho\). The source norm is
one, and the endpoint norm is at most
\(\sqrt N M_N\rho^{-(N-1)}\le e\sqrt N M_N\).
Dividing by \(1-\rho=N^{-1}\) proves (C11).

For completeness the exponential rate is positive:
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathcal B_N
 =\max_{0\le t\le1}\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du
 =\int_0^{5/6}\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du>0.
 \tag{C12}
\]
Indeed subtracting \(\log u+\log(1-u)\) from the integrand
leaves a smooth function on the closed unit interval. Integral
comparison for the two logarithms, or Stirling's formula, gives
\(\log s_r=NJ(r/N)+O(\log N)\) uniformly in \(r<N\), where
\(J(t)\) is the displayed integral. Its derivative has zeros
\(1/6,5/6\), respectively a minimum and a maximum. The root
product \(s_{N-1}=N\) and the same uniform estimate give
\(J(1)=0\); reflection of the integrand gives
\(J(5/6)=-J(1/6)>0\). Now use (C11).
No parity or composite-level restriction is needed.

A quotient preserving all these powers cannot remove the example.
The \(N\)-by-\(N\) Hankel matrix \((\alpha_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<N}\)
has zeros beyond its anti-diagonal and the nonzero value
\(\alpha_{N-1}=NQ^{-1}\) on that anti-diagonal. It has rank \(N\).
Every realization preserving all \(\alpha_r\) must therefore
have dimension at least \(N\): its Hankel matrix factors through
its state space. A coherent identity at the selected parameter,
such as (C10), can still remove the entire normalization cell.

The same test excludes assuming that the raw step polynomial
\[
 f_N(t)=e_0^*(I-tC)^{-1}\mathbf1
       =\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}Q^rF_rt^r
\]
is zero-free on the unit disk. Its constant coefficient is one
and its leading coefficient is \(NQ^{-1}\). Vieta's formula
gives product of root moduli \(1/N\), so at least one zero lies
strictly inside that disk at every level. Nevertheless
\(f_N(1)=Q^{-1}\). This raw parameter scales all powers of
\(C(1)\); in a general braid it differs from the physical
MacMahon parameter in \(C(t)\), which weights a principal minor
of size \(j\) by \(t^j\). No peripheral interpretation of the
raw step parameter is being assumed.

These calculations retain the original source. They do not
disprove the volume identity for a reduced hyperbolic core,
or exclude a sharp estimate after exact source resummation.
They rule out replacing that resummation by a better
contractive similarity budget for the same observed powers.
The Euclidean quadratic and its trial-gradient certificate
remain valid. A useful trial must capture the coherent
closing, rather than only the individual power norms.

**A separate assembly check.** Minimality of a weighted tree
does not let the isolated-vertex theorem finish the argument.
The complete theorem covers \(d+|n|>2\), but its multi-vertex
consequence explicitly requires an independent selected set.
After eliminating one vertex, an adjacent vertex receives its
full boundary polynomial in place of an original bare edge.
The theorem does not state that this input has the same
integer-degree isolated form. The existing joint-component
theorems still need their own hypotheses. Hyperbolicity has
not been shown to supply an eligible alternative presentation.

## A Fourier basis makes the finite transport triangular, 22 November

The [height-coordinate derivation](research_burau_fourier_height_contraction.md)
removes the nonlocal history matrix from the direct quadratic
formulation. It gives an explicit orthonormal basis, a diagonal
weight, and an ordinary Euclidean Hessian condition bound of ten.
The diagonal weight has exponential size, and its full cost is
retained in the endpoint vector. No new filling case is proved.

Fix a knot braid with \(b\ge2\) strands and \(k\ge1\) crossing
occurrences. The additional basis change is local and exact. At level \(N\ge2\)
put \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\). For one negative auxiliary crossing use its
original point rows \(\xi_{r,h}\) at
\(z=Q^{-1}\), and set
\[
 F_{p,j}=N^{-1/2}\sum_{h=0}^{N-1}Q^{ph}\xi_{j-p,h},
 \qquad p\in\mathbb Z/N,\quad 0\le j<N.
\]
Fourier orthogonality gives an orthonormal basis. Its right actions
are
\[
 F_{p,j}a_-=Q^{-p}(1-Q^{j+1})F_{p,j+1},\qquad
 F_{p,j}b_-=Q^{2(j-p)}F_{p,j},\qquad
 F_{p,j}c_-=QF_{p-1,j}.
 \tag{H1}
\]
The first action is zero at \(j=N-1\). The initial row and endpoint
are exactly
\[
 \xi_{0,0}=N^{-1/2}\sum_p F_{p,p},\qquad
 H^-_{\mathrm{new}}(p,j)=\sqrt N\,\delta_{p,0}.
 \tag{H2}
\]
The entire diagonal initial sum is retained.

The positive crossing already has a strict height-increasing
\(a_+\)-action. In the tensor product basis every \(a\) increases
total height, and every \(b,c\) preserves it. The bridge's
two-sided ideal statement then makes the full operator \(C\)
strictly increase total height \(0,\ldots,k(N-1)\).
Its height bandwidth is at most \(k(b-1)\), for a physical braid
with \(k\) crossings and \(b\) strands. This gives an exact
bounded-width block recurrence; the blocks themselves still grow
with \(N\).

Here is the explicit contraction. Put
\[
 B=\sum_{j=1}^{b-1}\binom{b-1}{j}j!4^{kj},\quad
 R=2B+1,\quad D=R^{\mathcal H},
\]
where \(\mathcal H\) is the total-height diagonal. The local generator
norms and principal-minor formula give \(\|C\|\le B\).
Each component \(C_m\) of height increase \(m\) is a Fourier
coefficient of unitary height conjugations, so \(\|C_m\|\le B\).
Consequently
\[
 C_R=DCD^{-1}=\sum_{m\ge1}R^{-m}C_m,\qquad
 \|C_R\|\le B/(R-1)=1/2.
 \tag{H3}
\]
Let \(E,H_1\) be the source and endpoint after the unitary basis
change. The original scalar is
\[
 K_N=\zeta u^*(I-C_R)^{-1}v,\qquad
 u=D^{-1}E,\quad v=DH_1.
 \tag{H4}
\]
All phases and both observations remain prescribed. In particular
\[
 \|v\|^2=\left(N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}R^{2j}\right)^k,
 \qquad u^*v=1.
\]
The exponential boundary cost is therefore an explicit geometric
series, rather than an unestimated history Gram.

With \(A=I-C_R^*\), \(\tau\ge1\), and
\(\beta=4\tau\|v\|^2\), define
\[
 J_\tau(x)=\beta\|Ax-u\|^2+|v^*x|^2,\qquad
 \mu_\tau=\min_xJ_\tau(x).
\]
The note proves
\[
 \mu_\tau\le|K_N|^2\le(1+\tau^{-1})\mu_\tau,\qquad
 \operatorname{cond}_2(D_{\mathbb R}^2J_\tau)
                         \le9+1/\tau\le10.
 \tag{H5}
\]
For the explicit half-gradient
\(g=\beta A^*(Ax-u)+v(v^*x)\), every trial satisfies
\[
 \max\{0,J_\tau(x)-4\|g\|^2/\beta\}
       \le|K_N|^2\le(1+\tau^{-1})J_\tau(x).
 \tag{H6}
\]
The statement uses ordinary Euclidean coordinates, all levels and
the original complete color. It does not use ordinary-color
estimates. The choice \(\tau=N\) retains the relative factor
\(1+1/N\).

The exponential factor in \(v\) still matters: a fixed absolute
state error does not control its closing relative to \(|K_N|\).
Complex path phases also remain. Neither strict height increase
nor contraction proves a nonzero geometric contribution, or
justifies discarding a tail before comparing its endpoint cost
with the volume scale. A geometric trial satisfying (H6) at that
scale after every fixed short partial filling is still missing.

## The quadratic comparison needs only the original closing, 22 November

The [single-closing quadratic note](research_burau_single_closing_quadratic.md)
removes the ordinary colors from this reduction. It uses the exact
complete-color row model, including the phase of its terminal column.
The minimum can approximate \(|K_N|^2\) within \(1+1/N\), using a
polynomial penalty. The finite-exception theorem remains open.

Here are the data and the full comparison. For a fixed knot braid with
\(k\ge1\) crossing occurrences, the prescribed matrix \(C\) acts on
\(\mathbb C^{N^{2k}}\), satisfies \(C^L=0\) with
\(L=k(N-1)+1\), and has source vectors \(e,H\) of norms \(1,N^k\).
The original invariant is
\[
 K_N=\zeta e^*(I-C)^{-1}H,\qquad |\zeta|=1.
\]
Keep that matrix and those columns, and put
\[
 T=C^*,\quad A=I-T,\quad
 G=\sum_{r=0}^{L-1}(T^*)^rT^r,\quad h=N^{-k}H.
\]
The new objective and minimum are
\[
 J_N(x)=NL\|Ax-N^ke\|_G^2+|h^*x|^2,\qquad
 \mu_N=\min_{x\in\mathbb C^{N^{2k}}}J_N(x).
 \tag{S1}
\]
There is one complex closing component. The objective is strictly
convex, unconstrained, and quadratic. With \(M=NL G\), square completion
and finite-history Cauchy--Schwarz give exactly
\[
 \mu_N=\frac{|K_N|^2}{1+\eta_N},\qquad
 \eta_N=h^*A^{-1}M^{-1}A^{-*}h,\qquad
 0<\eta_N\le N^{-1}.
 \tag{S2}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \mu_N\le |K_N|^2\le(1+N^{-1})\mu_N.
 \tag{S3}
\]
This includes zeros and every parity and composite level. No division
by the invariant occurs. The only direct proof input is the complete
marked row model; the ordinary-color bounds and all-color frame are
unnecessary for (S1)--(S3). The earlier all-color energy remains useful
when a positive polynomial floor is wanted: \(\mu_N\) itself vanishes
exactly when \(K_N\) does.

The orthogonality also becomes particularly simple. The linear part
of the affine map
\[
 x\longmapsto\big(M^{1/2}(Ax-N^ke),h^*x\big)
\]
has image of complex codimension one. Its normal is
\[
 \big(-M^{-1/2}A^{-*}h,1\big).
\]
Its squared normal component is \(\mu_N\). This projection is made
after assembling the complete ordered operator; it does not delete
directions during the crossing transport. The normal still contains
the full adjoint inverse.

There is also a direct lower certificate for any trial field. Define
the complex half-gradient
\[
 g_N(x)=A^*M(Ax-N^ke)+h(h^*x).
\]
Then the note proves
\[
 \max\{0,J_N(x)-L^2\|g_N(x)\|_{M^{-1}}^2\}
 \le |K_N|^2\le(1+N^{-1})J_N(x).
 \tag{S4}
\]
Thus a geometric trial field with the required energy rate and
\(L^2\|g_N(x)\|_{M^{-1}}^2\le\theta J_N(x)\), for a fixed
\(0\le\theta<1\), would give both volume bounds. Such fields have not
been constructed for arbitrary fixed short partial fillings.
The large dimension, full-word history metric, and source propagation
are still present. In particular the metric can have exponential
size; polynomial conditioning in that metric is not Euclidean
conditioning.
