## Calibrating the geometric weight against the actual endpoint, 22 November

The local weights in the new orthogonal row model have a tetrahedron
volume profile. That fact does not give the volume growth of the
original source. The following exact identities explain how the
profile enters the original normalization and specify the endpoint
which a propagation argument must reach.

Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), and
\[
 S_j=\prod_{a=1}^j2\sin(\pi a/N),\quad S_0=1,\qquad
 w_l^2=\sum_{h=0}^l\left|{l\brack h}_Q\right|^2.
\]
The Gaussians have their standard polynomial meaning. On the complete
marked row model let \(\rho_l=w_{l+1}/w_l\), \(0\le l<d\).
There is an exact reflection identity at every level:
\[
 w_{d-r}^2=\frac{Nw_r^2}{S_r^2}\quad(0\le r\le d),
 \qquad
 \rho_l\rho_{N-2-l}=2\sin\frac{\pi(l+1)}N.
 \tag{C1}
\]
For the first equality use \(S_jS_{d-j}=N\) to write
\[
 \frac{S_{d-r}}{S_hS_{d-r-h}}
       =\frac1{S_r}\prod_{a=1}^r2\sin\frac{\pi(h+a)}N.
\]
For \(h>d-r\), the product contains a zero, so its squared sum
can be extended to all \(h\in\mathbb Z/N\). It is the sampled
squared modulus of \(P_r(T)=\prod_{a=1}^r(1-Q^aT)\), divided by
\(S_r^2\). Since \(\deg P_r=r<N\), character orthogonality gives
the sum as \(N\) times the squared coefficient norm, namely
\(Nw_r^2\). This proves the first assertion. Taking the ratio of
two consecutive identities proves the second. No parity or prime-level
restriction is used.

**The local action is an exact change of Gram normalization.** In the
positive orthonormal row basis \(f_{r,l}\), let \(S\) be the strict
shift in \(l\), with zero output at \(l=d\), and put
\(D_w=\operatorname{diag}(w_l)\). The actual right-action matrices obey
\[
 a_+=D_w^{-1}SD_w,\qquad [D_w,b_+]=[D_w,c_+]=0.
 \tag{C2}
\]
Take the tensor product \(D\) of these diagonals at the positive
auxiliary occurrences and identities at the negative ones. Let
\(\widehat C_N\), \(H_N\), and \(\mathfrak e^{\mathsf T}\)
be the full operator, terminal column, and initial row of the adopted
orthogonal model. Its retained phase is
\(\zeta_N=Q^{(b-1+w)/2}\), where \(b\) is the number of physical
braid strands and \(w\) its writhe. Ordered substitution of (C2) into the entire quantum
minor formula gives exactly
\[
 \widehat C_N=D^{-1}C_{{\rm flat},N}D,\qquad
 \mathfrak e^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}=\mathfrak e^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
 K_N=\zeta_N\mathfrak e^{\mathsf T}
                 (I-C_{{\rm flat},N})^{-1}D H_N.
 \tag{C3}
\]
Here \(C_{{\rm flat},N}\) uses the unweighted strict shift in
place of each positive \(a\), with the other letters unchanged.
Thus products of the weights telescope to the endpoint. The factor
\(1/w_l\) in its positive terminal column cancels that transport
normalization in each source monomial. The remaining Pochhammer
products are still present and can have exponential growth. This does
not say that their geometric action disappears from the source.
It says that flattening and unflattening transport only redistributes
it, and provides no independent gain for a lower bound.

For reference, the entire earlier covariance proof already gives,
uniformly on compact subsets of \(0<t<1\),
\[
 w_l^2=\sqrt{\frac{\cot(\pi t/2)}{2N}}
       e^{2NB(t)}(1+o(1)),\quad t=l/N,\qquad
 B(t)=J(t)-2J(t/2),\quad
 J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du.
\]
Taking a consecutive ratio yields \(\rho_l\to2\cos(\pi t/2)\)
uniformly on such compacts. The same proof identifies \(\pi B(t)\)
as the volume of the ideal tetrahedron with angles
\((\pi t/2,\pi t/2,\pi(1-t))\). These are existing local results,
not a new volume theorem. In particular the bulk formula cannot be
used at the actual initial index: \(\rho_0=\sqrt2\) exactly,
whereas its bulk continuation at zero equals two. The change \(D\)
can have exponential condition number. Its metric, endpoint and
boundary projection must therefore be transported together.

**The prescribed endpoint is a reflected crossing row.** At
\(z=Q^{-1}\), the positive terminal column is exactly zero for
\(r+l\ge N\). For \(r+l<N\) it is
\[
 H^+_{r,l}=e^{i\vartheta_{r,l}}
                         \frac{S_{r+l}}{S_rw_l},\qquad
 \vartheta_{r,l}=\frac{\pi l}2
           -\frac\pi N\left((3l+2)r+\frac{l(l+1)}2\right).
 \tag{C4}
\]
This is obtained by writing
\(1-Q^{-a}=2i e^{-\pi ia/N}\sin(\pi a/N)\) in the actual
terminal product. Set \(i=d-l\), and write
\(\beta_{i,r}=S_i/(S_rS_{i-r})\), extended by zero outside
\(0\le r\le i\). Reflection of the factorials and (C1) give
\[
             |H^+_{r,l}|=\sqrt N\,\frac{\beta_{i,r}}{w_i}.
 \tag{C5}
\]
Thus \(|H^+_{r,l}|^2/N\), for fixed \(l\), is exactly the
normalized positive row distribution of the old crossing covariance.
It is not an independently chosen coherent state.

For \(t=l/N\) in a fixed compact subset of \((0,1)\), and
\(v=(r-(N-l-1)/2)/\sqrt N\) bounded, its proved Gaussian estimate
therefore gives
\[
 H^+_{r,l}=e^{i\vartheta_{r,l}}
       (2N\tan(\pi t/2))^{1/4}
            e^{-\pi\tan(\pi t/2)v^2}(1+o(1)).
 \tag{C6}
\]
The error is uniform on these ranges, without a parity subsequence;
the same strict-concavity estimates control the tails. Moreover,
\(\sum_r|H^+_{r,l}|^2=N\) exactly for every \(l\). The normalized
terminal vector consequently has a uniform \(l\)-marginal, not
concentration at the regular tetrahedron index \(2N/3\).

These statements initialize the boundary packet and rule out counting
its Gram normalization as an additional bulk contribution. They do not
control the actual inverse state arriving on that packet. In particular
neither (C1) nor (C6) gives a geometric-rate dual certificate for the
quadratic minimum below, or a new short-filling volume estimate.
The next analytic step still concerns propagation by the full ordered
operator, with the prescribed projection retained at the closing.

Both entire direct proof texts were read with matching renewed pins:
the [orthogonal row model](research_burau_orthogonal_marked_row_model.md)
`faade30be18b475de010b68cef3a5c5438e727fb17c599f38b97578ad369e4be`,
and the [Gaussian crossing covariance](research_actual_newton_crossing_gaussian_covariance.md)
`ce2b1b8efbbcffa8bafe0d0de4f7ce12febf193e433d8e3291f7d2a8c826fa3f`.
The new exact reflection, full-operator gauge identity, endpoint phase
and reflected-row comparison are proved above. The bulk action and
Gaussian estimates are the stated consequences of the matching
covariance proof.

## Local degree-four gluing with constant physical budgets, 22 November

The local moment formulation also works in the improved uniform physical
metric, with the constant structural budgets of the
[physical source theorem](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md).
This joins two earlier results whose normalizations must not be confused:
the earlier local theorem assumed small coefficient tensors, whereas
physical multiplication only has a small bilinear norm after division
by sixteen. The matrix identities in the
[physical degree-four certificate](research_conway_physical_matrix_degree_four_certificate.md)
give the stronger local conclusion directly. No change to the physical
budget, leaf data, or original closing is required.

Here is the complete additional argument. All coordinates are real and
imaginary parts in the prescribed physical orthonormal basis of the
full algebra \(\mathcal A_N\), of complex dimension \(N\). Set
\(\sigma=1/16\) and \(t=1/4\). A proper vertex \(v\) has
output \(x_v\), at most two distinct child packets, normalized map
\(\Phi_v\), and residual energy
\[
 E_v=\|\Phi_v-x_v\|^2.
\]
A leaf map is its prescribed constant, a turn is the genuine linear
turn divided by sixteen, and a product is actual matrix multiplication
divided by sixteen. The root has energy
\(E_\rho=|Lx_{v_0}|^2\). The feasible packets are unit balls.
The original budget is \(B=B_{\rm ph}\), and its unchanged comparison is
\[
 B^2e_*\le |K_N|^2\le(197/196)B^2e_*,\qquad
                         e_*=\min E,\quad E=\sum_vE_v.
\]
Let a local group contain a proper output and its children, or just the
top packet at the root. It has at most \(6N\) real coordinates. Define
\[
 V_v=E_v-t\|x_v\|^2+t\sum_{c\text{ child of }v}\|x_c\|^2,
 \qquad V_\rho=E_\rho+t\|x_{v_0}\|^2.
\]
Their sum is exactly \(E\) on a consistent field. The individual
\(V_v\) can have negative minima; their signs are retained.

**Local certificate.** Put \(\mu=31/128\). For every local group
\(C_v\) and every feasible local center \(b\),
\[
 V_v(x)-V_v(b)-\nabla V_v(b)\cdot(x-b)
                     -\frac\mu2\|x-b\|^2\in Q_2(C_v),
 \tag{P1}
\]
where \(Q_2(C_v)\) consists of sums of squares of local quadratics
plus each local ball constraint \(g_w=1-\|x_w\|^2\) times a sum
of squares of local affine polynomials.

To prove this, consider a product, with output index \(0\) and input
indices \(1,2\). Its half-Hessian is
\[
\begin{split}
\tfrac12D^2V_v[h,h]={}&
 (1-t)\|h_0\|^2+t(\|h_1\|^2+\|h_2\|^2)\\
 &-2\operatorname{Re}\langle h_0,
                   \sigma h_1x_2+\sigma x_1h_2\rangle
             +\|\sigma h_1x_2+\sigma x_1h_2\|^2\\
 &+2\operatorname{Re}\langle\sigma x_1x_2,\sigma h_1h_2\rangle
             -2\operatorname{Re}\langle x_0,\sigma h_1h_2\rangle.
\end{split}
\]
Apply identities (6)--(8) of the physical degree-four proof. The two
derivative cross terms consume
\(2\sigma\|h_0\|^2+\sigma(\|h_1\|^2+\|h_2\|^2)\);
the two curvature terms consume respectively
\(\sigma^2(\|h_1\|^2+\|h_2\|^2)\) and
\(\sigma(\|h_1\|^2+\|h_2\|^2)\).
Each remainder is a local sum of squares plus local ball constraints
times constant positive semidefinite quadratic forms in \(h\).
The unused half-Hessian coefficients are
\[
 1-t-2\sigma=5/8,\qquad
                         t-2\sigma-\sigma^2=31/256.
\]
At a turn the corresponding coefficients are \(11/16\) and
\(3/16\); a leaf has coefficient \(3/4\), and the root at least
\(1/4\). Thus in every group
\[
 h^{\mathsf T}(D^2V_v-\mu I)h
   =\sum_j|W_j(x)h|^2+\sum_{w\in C_v}g_w(x)h^{\mathsf T}A_wh,
\]
with affine \(W_j\) and constant \(A_w\succeq0\), all locally
supported. Integration along \(b+s(x-b)\), with weight \(1-s\),
proves (P1). In particular use
\[
 g_w(b+s(x-b))=(1-s)g_w(b)+s g_w(x)
                                      +s(1-s)\|x_w-b_w\|^2.
\]
The first and last pieces give squares of degree at most four, and the
middle piece is the original ball times squares of affine polynomials.
This proves the degree assertion without a small multiplication
coefficient tensor.

**Local moments.** Introduce one functional \(\mathcal L_v\) through
degree four in each group, with
\[
 \mathcal L_v(1)=1,\quad \mathcal L_v(p^2)\ge0\ (\deg p\le2),
 \quad \mathcal L_v(g_wp^2)\ge0\ (w\in C_v,\ \deg p\le1).
\]
Match only first moments of the shared packet across each tree edge.
Those means form a feasible global field \(m\): moment positivity and
the ball localizer imply
\(\|\mathcal L_v(x_w)\|^2\le\mathcal L_v(\|x_w\|^2)\le1\).
Applying (P1) at the local means gives
\[
 \sum_v\mathcal L_v(V_v)\ge
 E(m)+\frac\mu2\sum_v
       \mathcal L_v(\|x_{C_v}-m_{C_v}\|^2)\ge e_*.
\]
Evaluation at the unique physical minimizer attains equality. Therefore
the exact minimum is
\[
 e_*=\min_{\{\mathcal L_v\}}\sum_v\mathcal L_v(V_v).
 \tag{P2}
\]
Use the redistributed objective here: its shifts need not cancel for
arbitrary moments when only first moments are matched. The largest
moment block has size at most \(\binom{6N+2}{2}\), a localizing
block at most \(6N+1\), and the matching conditions use \(2N\)
real equalities per edge. All structural budgets remain sixteen.

The optimal local moments are uniquely evaluation at that one field.
Indeed equality above forces the means to be the unique minimizer and
every centered coordinate \(p_i\) to satisfy
\(\mathcal L_v(p_i^2)=0\). For every coordinate \(x_j\) in a
local packet, its ball localizer gives
\[
 0\le\mathcal L_v(x_j^2p_i^2)\le\mathcal L_v(p_i^2)=0.
\]
Moment-matrix Cauchy--Schwarz kills the rows of \(p_i\) and
\(x_jp_i\). Every quadratic monomial minus its value at the mean
is a sum of these rows. Factoring a degree-at-most-four monomial into
two quadratics then determines its moment as its value at the mean.
Thus every local moment matrix at the optimum has rank one. No physical
packet coordinate has been discarded.

**Eliminating a fixed short component.** For any connected set of gate
groups, keep its entering and outgoing packet means and minimize the
sum of its \(V_v\) over the internal packets. This is a jointly
strongly convex boundary function: interpolate two internal minimizers,
apply local strong convexity, and discard the nonnegative internal
displacement term. Its epigraph has an exact degree-four local moment
description from (P2), with the boundary means prescribed. The lower
bound is the same mean-field argument, and evaluation at the clamped
minimizer proves equality. At a proper component its boundary shifts
are \(t\sum\|u_j\|^2-t\|y\|^2\); internal shifts cancel.
At a component containing the closing there is no outgoing negative
shift. The boundary functions can be nonpolynomial and their values
can be negative. Their original local degree-four descriptions remain
exact. This handles a fixed short component without removing its
original boundary data or changing the source comparison factor.

The additional simplification is therefore precise: the small local
problems and first-mean gluing now use the improved physical metric
and constant structural budgets simultaneously. The missing volume
estimate is still a positive lower certificate at the correct
exponential rate. For instance, locally feasible affine-force
certificates with signed total \(\lambda_N>0\) give
\(B_{\rm ph}^2\lambda_N\le|K_N|^2\); their existence at a specified
geometric rate has not been proved by (P1)--(P2). Rank-one optimal
moments and fixed degree do not supply that rate or a finite-exception
theorem.

Both entire direct proof texts were read and their matching pins renewed:
the physical degree-four proof is
`55b09c698207663866bec909a52055f338a00ea1277f57940c8d23981a6a9ae9`,
and the physical source theorem is
`39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8`.
The entire earlier local and moment notes were read for coverage, at
`8b3241f9cc8a9e740aa4223345e39932f3a2096fcdab60f55458a6266857e8e9`
and `6c05525ce9a7e277457510b7a3f4e624e3bfd020adfbd8a0918ecd9ed3ef0b82`.
Their local small-tensor theorems are not imported with a changed norm.
The matrix-specific replacement needed for (P1) is checked above.

## The finite Burau inverse now has the original marked source, 22 November

The [completed source comparison](research_burau_cyclic_marked_source_bridge.md)
derives the original normalized knot scalar from the finite model. It
checks the actual crossings, operator order, selected cut, tail pivot
and framing directly; a colored-Jones determinant formula is not used
in place of those checks.

In detail, let the physical column-operator word have \(b\) strands,
\(k\) crossing occurrences and writhe \(w\). Its rightmost factor acts
first. Form the auxiliary Burau product from the reversed list with
every crossing sign changed. For \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), the specified
operator \(C_N\) on \(\mathbb C[(\mu_N)^{3k}]\) then gives
\[
 K_N=Q^{(b-1+w)/2}\,
       \ell_N\left(\sum_{r=0}^{k(N-1)}C_N^r\right)\mathbf1,
 \qquad C_N^{k(N-1)+1}=0.
\]
Here \(\ell_N\) is point evaluation at every
\(x_j=y_j=Q^{-1},\ u_j=1\), and \(\mathbf1\) is the constant
function. The displayed power of \(Q\) is integral by knot parity.
Both parities and composite levels are retained. A central grading
parameter makes the quantum-MacMahon inverse polynomial before that
parameter is set to one. The observed trace also has a direct finite
color cutoff. Thus no infinite root-level trace is exchanged with
evaluation.

Set \(A_N=I-C_N\) and \(\zeta_N=Q^{(b-1+w)/2}\). Since
\(\det A_N=1\), the same source is the ordinary bordered determinant
\[
 K_N=\det\begin{pmatrix}
            A_N&\mathbf1\\-\zeta_N\ell_N&0
          \end{pmatrix}.
\]
This completes the source comparison that was still absent when the
separate nilpotence calculation below was recorded. It does not estimate
the selected inverse element. In particular, the unbordered ordinary
determinant remains one and cannot be substituted for the source in a
volume-growth argument. No new knot-volume family follows here.

The complete source proof is at
`7edce1a2c39ddf213066de0026fa60b44545f9eaab25679580926e842092c496`.
Its three complete internal proof sources have matching pins
`d8b21fa8db909120035e86e997a0e02cb84f8dce2dcf6fb244bb5c85c17e28a3`,
`c4a9a92ec22f31a035036642e0621ef9abe569646b2488dbac2d2add786500f0`,
and `1b0e105ffb67b2b8552f5fddc5f0a3ac009e9795b33e27599ac4726ebd74079e`.

## Orthogonal marked rows with two registers per crossing, 22 November

The [orthogonal row model](research_burau_orthogonal_marked_row_model.md)
reduces the exact source from \(N^{3k}\) to \(N^{2k}\) coordinates.
It uses the actual right orbit of the marked row, rather than the full
orbit of the constant input. At each crossing that row orbit has
dimension exactly \(N^2\), including at even and composite levels.

For a positive auxiliary crossing the rows \(\ell c^r a^l\) have
disjoint grid supports. Their explicit norms are
\[
 w_l^2=\sum_{h=0}^l\left|{l\brack h}_Q\right|^2.
\]
Division by \(w_l\) gives an actual orthonormal basis. For a negative
crossing the row orbit consists of all coordinate observations on
\(xu=Q^{-1}\); its point basis is orthonormal. Thus redundant
coefficient directions are not being counted as independent states.
Both signs have an initial row of norm one, terminal column of norm
exactly \(N\), and generator norms at most \(2,1,1\) for \(a,b,c\).
The nonzero singular values of each local \(a\) are at least \(1/N\).

Tensoring these exact right actions gives the same original source,
with its word order, phase and nilpotence unchanged, and terminal norm
\(N^k\). This is a genuine reduction of the source representation.
It supplies no lower bound for the selected inverse element.
The entire final proof is at
`faade30be18b475de010b68cef3a5c5438e727fb17c599f38b97578ad369e4be`;
its sole entire proof direct is the source bridge
`7edce1a2c39ddf213066de0026fa60b44545f9eaab25679580926e842092c496`.

## A positive boundary norm for the same finite inverse, 22 November

The cyclic inverse also realizes the already established whole-color
Fourier energy, with a specified orthogonal boundary projection. This
does not replace coherent intermediate coefficients by independent
squares.

Use the physical word, reversed sign-mirrored auxiliary word and finite
operator of the [source bridge](research_burau_cyclic_marked_source_bridge.md).
Write \(\alpha=(w+b-1)/2\in\mathbb Z\) and
\(\mathcal R_N=(I-C_N)^{-1}\). For \(0\le s<N\), let
\(\ell_s\) evaluate every crossing copy at
\(x_h=y_h=Q^s,\ u_h=1\). Then
\[
 \ell_s\mathcal R_N\mathbf1
                  =Q^{s\alpha}C_{s+1}(q_N),
 \tag{B1}
\]
where \(C_j\) is the original reduced ordinary color for \(j<N\),
and the terminal reduced cut \(C_N\) in (B1) means the original
\(K_N\). No ordinary quantum dimension is divided out at the terminal
color. In this paragraph the ordinary-color symbol is distinguished
by its argument \(q_N\); the operator \(C_N\) retains the notation
of the source bridge.

Here is the additional color comparison. Set \(z=Q^s\) in the
bridge's actual coaction kernels. The positive product kills an output
\(j+l>s\) from an input \(j\le s\); its factor with \(h=s-j\)
is zero. The negative product similarly kills \(i+l>s\) from
\(i\le s\). The other output follows the other incoming strand
and is automatically within range. Following the single knot component
from the pinned input zero therefore forces every contributing trace
index into \(0,\ldots,s\). The observed graded trace terminates at
degree \((b-1)s\). The operator inverse is already finite, so this
argument introduces no interchange with an infinite sum.

The generic-color crossing comparison requires one extra diagonal;
the complete-color root reflection cannot simply be reused. In the
ordinary balanced color of dimension \(s+1\), set
\[
 t_i=\frac{[i]![s-i]!}{[s]!},\qquad 0\le i\le s,
 \qquad [i]=\frac{q_N^i-q_N^{-i}}{q_N-q_N^{-1}}.
\]
For \(s=0\) all empty factorials are one. Every factorial is nonzero
because \(s<N\). Compose the bridge's reversal and position-dependent
clock with this diagonal on each head. At a positive coaction output
the extra ratio is
\(t_{j+l}t_{i-l}/(t_it_j)\); it converts the factorial product
\[
 \frac{[i]!}{[i-l]!}\frac{[s-j]!}{[s-j-l]!}
 \quad\hbox{to}\quad
 \frac{[j+l]!}{[j]!}\frac{[s-i+l]!}{[s-i]!}.
\]
At a negative output the ratio is
\(t_{j-l}t_{i+l}/(t_it_j)\), with the corresponding inverse
conversion. These are exactly the generic balanced crossing
coefficients, before using any complete-color reflection. The phase
differences are respectively
\(-s^2/2+s(i-j-l)\) and \(s^2/2+s(i-j+l)\), supplied by
\(\kappa_s=q_N^{s^2/2}\) and the same position clock. This checks
both full crossings. The additional diagonals preserve the selected
pin and commute with the diagonal pivot, so cancel from its trace.

Consequently the selected observation is
\[
 q_N^{s(b-1)}\kappa_s^{-w}
       \operatorname{Tr}[(P_s\otimes K_s^{\otimes(b-1)})W_s].
\]
The actual partial pivotal trace is scalar: \(K_s\) has distinct
weights, and all its internal lowering arrows are nonzero. Its ordinary
twist is \(q_N^{s(s+2)/2}\). Restoring that zero-framing convention
gives \(q_N^{s(b-1+w)}=Q^{s\alpha}\), proving (B1) for ordinary
colors. At \(s=N-1\), all \(t_i=1\) and
\(Q^{-(N-1)\alpha}=Q^\alpha\); the adopted complete-source formula
gives precisely the same assertion without division by \([N]\).

For \(k\ge1\), these \(N\) grid points are distinct. Their
coordinate restriction \(P_{\rm diag}\) obeys
\(P_{\rm diag}P_{\rm diag}^*=I_N\) in counting \(\ell^2\).
Thus an explicit positive boundary norm is
\[
 \begin{split}
 E_N&=\|P_{\rm diag}\mathcal R_N\mathbf1\|^2\\
 &=\mathbf1^*\mathcal R_N^*P_{\rm diag}^*P_{\rm diag}
                                      \mathcal R_N\mathbf1\\
 &=|K_N|^2+\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}|C_j(q_N)|^2.
 \end{split}
 \tag{B2}
\]
The ordinary-color comparison and positive-trace proof give
\[
 1\le E_N-|K_N|^2\le (N-1)(N/2)^{2b-2}.
 \tag{B3}
\]
The lower bound uses the trivial color \(C_1=1\). If \(k=0\), the
knot is the one-strand unknot and the direct convention gives \(E_N=N\).
For every fixed \(V>0\), (B2)--(B3) therefore imply exactly
\[
 \frac\pi N\log E_N\longrightarrow V
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|\longrightarrow V.
\]
No eventual nonvanishing is assumed in this equivalence; the positive
rate and polynomial remainder imply it.

**One compressed operator for all colors.** The two-register row model
also makes this boundary norm explicit in its smaller coordinates.
For the remainder of this construction assume \(k\ge1\); the empty
unknot convention was handled above.
Its positive right-action matrices are already independent of the
marked root \(z\in\mu_N\). Its negative point rows can be rephased
unitarily by
\[
 \xi'_{r,h}=z^{h-r}\xi_{r,h}.
\]
Their right actions become
\[
 \xi'_{r,h}a_- =\xi'_{r+1,h+1}-Q^r\xi'_{r+1,h},\quad
 \xi'_{r,h}b_-=Q^{2r}\xi'_{r,h},\quad
 \xi'_{r,h}c_-=Q^{-h}\xi'_{r+1,h}.
\]
All three are independent of \(z\), and the initial row is still
\(\xi'_{0,0}\). Thus the same compressed operator
\(\widetilde C_N\) and the same initial coordinate row
\(\mathfrak e^{\mathsf T}\) serve every color. At the complete
root this is a known unitary diagonal change of the adopted row model,
so \(\widetilde C_N^L=0\), \(L=k(N-1)+1\).
Only the terminal columns change:
\[
 \begin{split}
 h^+_{r,l}(z)&=\frac{Q^{-rl}z^r}{w_l}
                        \prod_{j=0}^{l-1}(1-zQ^{-r-j}),\\
 h^-_{r,h}(z)&=z^{h-r},\qquad
 h_N(z)=\bigotimes_{j=1}^k h^{\sigma_j}(z).
 \end{split}
 \tag{B4}
\]
The disjoint-support and invariant-surface arguments in the row proof
apply at every \(z\in\mu_N\); these are its actual terminal
columns in the stated gauges. The same finite character calculation
gives \(\|h^\pm(z)\|=N\), hence \(\|h_N(z)\|=N^k\).
In particular, with
\[
 v_N=\mathfrak e^{\mathsf T}(I-\widetilde C_N)^{-1},\qquad
 \mathsf H_N=(h_N(z))_{z\in\mu_N},\qquad
 \Gamma_N=\mathsf H_N^*\mathsf H_N,
\]
equation (B2) is exactly \(E_N=\|v_N\mathsf H_N\|^2\).
All ordered products are the original right actions.

The boundary frame has polynomial condition number, uniformly in the
number of crossings. For one positive occurrence, the \(l=0\) block
in (B4) has entries \(z^r\), so character orthogonality gives its
Gram matrix \(NI\). The remaining blocks are positive semidefinite,
and every diagonal entry of the full Gram is \(N^2\).
For a negative occurrence the Gram is exactly \(N^2I\), because
\(\sum_{r,h}(z'/z)^{h-r}=N^2\delta_{z,z'}\).
The tensor-column Gram is the entrywise product of these local Grams.
Entrywise products preserve positivity: they are Gram matrices of
tensor products of the original Gram vectors. Applying this also to
\(A-NI\succeq0\) proves, for \(k\ge1\),
\[
 N^{2k-1}I\le\Gamma_N\le N^{2k+1}I.
 \tag{B5}
\]
Indeed the lower bound is \(N\) times the diagonal of the product of
the other local Grams, namely \(N^{2k-1}I\); the upper bound is the
trace, \(N^{2k+1}\). If there is any negative auxiliary occurrence,
its diagonal Gram makes the product exactly \(N^{2k}I\).

The explicit rank-\(N\) orthogonal projection is therefore
\[
 \Pi_N=\mathsf H_N\Gamma_N^{-1}\mathsf H_N^*.
\]
It retains all color observations. Its definition uses only known
endpoint columns. From (B5),
\[
 N^{2k-1}\|v_N\Pi_N\|^2\le E_N
                          \le N^{2k+1}\|v_N\Pi_N\|^2.
 \tag{B6}
\]
For a negative occurrence the middle quantity equals
\(N^{2k}\|v_N\Pi_N\|^2\) exactly. The projection cannot be omitted
or applied prematurely between generators: its range has not been
shown invariant under their transport.

**A quadratic minimum with polynomial comparison factors.** This norm
also has a positive quadratic minimization formulation. Put
\[
 T_N=\widetilde C_N^*,\quad A_N=I-T_N,\quad
 G_N=\sum_{r=0}^{L-1}(T_N^*)^rT_N^r\succeq I,
\]
and let \(\mathfrak e\) be the canonical column corresponding to the
initial row. Define the known quadratic objective on the whole complex
space of dimension \(N^{2k}\) by
\[
 m_N=\min_x\{\|A_Nx-\mathfrak e\|_{G_N}^2
                                      +\|\Pi_Nx\|^2\}.
 \tag{B7}
\]
This has a unique minimum. It has degree two in real coordinates;
all coefficients use the known finite operator and endpoints, with
no invariant value supplied as input.

To prove the comparison, set
\(t=\Pi_NA_N^{-1}\mathfrak e=\Pi_Nv_N^*\) and
\(a=\Pi_NA_N^{-1}\). Substituting \(r=A_Nx-\mathfrak e\)
into the objective and completing its quadratic square gives
\[
 m_N=\min_r\{\|r\|_{G_N}^2+\|t+ar\|^2\}
          =t^*(I+aG_N^{-1}a^*)^{-1}t.
\]
Moreover, the finite inverse and Cauchy--Schwarz across its \(L\)
terms give
\[
 \|ar\|^2
   =\left\|\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}\Pi_NT_N^jr\right\|^2
       \le L\sum_j\|T_N^jr\|^2=L\|r\|_{G_N}^2.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \frac{\|v_N\Pi_N\|^2}{L+1}\le m_N
                              \le\|v_N\Pi_N\|^2,
 \quad
 \frac{E_N}{N^{2k+1}(L+1)}\le m_N
                              \le\frac{E_N}{N^{2k-1}}.
 \tag{B8}
\]
Every factor here is polynomial in \(N\) for a fixed word. In
particular \(E_N\ge1\) implies
\(m_N\ge[N^{2k+1}(L+1)]^{-1}>0\) at every level.
For each fixed \(V>0\),
\[
 \frac\pi N\log m_N\longrightarrow V
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|\longrightarrow V.
 \tag{B9}
\]
Thus positivity of this minimum is established; its required positive
exponential rate remains to be proved.

For completeness, its Hessian has condition number at most \(5L^2\)
in \(G_N\) coordinates. The identity
\(T_N^*G_NT_N=G_N-I\) gives \(\|T_N\|_{G_N}\le1\),
\(\|A_N\|_{G_N}\le2\), and
\(\|A_N^{-1}\|_{G_N}\le L\). Since \(G_N\succeq I\), the
closing term has norm at most one in those coordinates. The real
Hessian eigenvalues therefore lie between \(2/L^2\) and \(10\).
This is a statement in the specified metric, not a bound on its
Euclidean condition number or on the size of its coefficients.

An explicit lower certificate is a pair \(u,y\) satisfying the
linear adjoint equation
\[
                     A_N^*u=\Pi_Ny.
\]
Completing the two squares in (B7) proves
\[
 d_N(u,y)=2\operatorname{Re}(u^*\mathfrak e)
                        -u^*G_N^{-1}u-\|y\|^2\le m_N.
 \tag{B10}
\]
Equality is attained at
\(u=G_N(\mathfrak e-A_Nx_*),\ y=\Pi_Nx_*\), where \(x_*\)
is the minimizer; its stationarity is exactly the displayed equation.
The unknown minimizer proves attainment and is not needed to check a
supplied feasible certificate. Equations (B3), (B6), and (B8) then give
\[
 \max\{0,N^{2k-1}d_N(u,y)-(N-1)(N/2)^{2b-2}\}
                                     \le |K_N|^2.
 \tag{B11}
\]
A feasible trial in (B7) gives the matching upper estimate through
\(|K_N|^2\le N^{2k+1}(L+1)m_N\).

The degree drops from four to two at the expense of the larger
\(N^{2k}\)-dimensional presentation and its full-word history metric.
Neither the history matrix nor its input energy is polynomially
bounded here. The new polynomial comparison is with the specified
projected response, not with the full inverse-state norm. This is the
existing original Plancherel energy in explicit finite-inverse
coordinates. It is not a sum of separately squared powers, an
unpointed operator trace, or a positive path-weight expansion.
Coherent cancellation inside the inverse remains.
No geometric family of dual certificates (B10) with the positive
volume rate has been constructed, and no new filling class or
finite-exception theorem follows yet.

## A finite nilpotent realization of the standard Burau operator, 22 November

There is a useful finite algebraic fact behind the determinant route.
The operator definitions here are those of
[Huynh--Lê](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0503296), Sections 0.1.1--0.1.3.
The following root-level calculation is proved directly; it does not
use their colored-Jones determinant theorem as a premise.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), and a braid word with \(k\)
crossing occurrences on \(b\) strands. Give each occurrence its own
variables \(x_j,y_j,u_j\). Work on the finite function space
\[
 \mathcal F_N=\mathbb C[(\mu_N)^{3k}],\qquad
                         \dim\mathcal F_N=N^{3k},
\]
where \(\mu_N\) is the set of \(N\)-th roots of unity. Multiplication
and shifts act literally; for example
\(\tau_x f(x,y,u)=f(Qx,y,u)\). Thus
\(x^N=y^N=u^N=\tau_x^N=\tau_y^N=\tau_u^N=I\).
At a positive or negative crossing use respectively
\[
\begin{aligned}
 a_+&=(u-y\tau_x^{-1})\tau_y^{-1},&
 b_+&=u^2,&c_+&=x\tau_y^{-2}\tau_u^{-1},\\
 a_-&=(\tau_y-x^{-1})\tau_x^{-1}\tau_u,&
 b_-&=u^2,&c_-&=y^{-1}\tau_x^{-1}\tau_u .
\end{aligned}
\]
The displayed actions fix the multiplication/shift convention; in
particular \(\tau_x x=Qx\tau_x\).

Direct multiplication gives the homogeneous relations
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
 a_+b_+=b_+a_+,&a_+c_+=Qc_+a_+,&b_+c_+=Q^2c_+b_+,\\
 a_-b_-=Q^2b_-a_-,&c_-a_-=Qa_-c_-,&c_-b_-=Q^2b_-c_- .
\end{array}
\]
Different crossing copies commute. Also \(a_+^N=a_-^N=0\).
For example split \(a_+=U-V\), with
\(U=u\tau_y^{-1}\), \(V=y\tau_x^{-1}\tau_y^{-1}\).
Then \(UV=Q^{-1}VU\), \(U^N=I\), and
\(V^N=(-1)^{N-1}I\). The intermediate coefficients of the
quantum binomial formula vanish at the primitive root, giving
\((U-V)^N=I+(-1)^NV^N=0\).
For the negative crossing use
\(U=\tau_y\tau_x^{-1}\tau_u\),
\(V=x^{-1}\tau_x^{-1}\tau_u\); now \(UV=QVU\), with the same
two \(N\)-th powers. These signs retain even and composite levels.

Let \(\mathcal S_N\) be the unital subalgebra generated by the
specified crossing triples, and let \(J\) be its two-sided ideal
generated by all \(a_j\). This is not an ideal in the full ambient
endomorphism algebra. Normal-ordering by the homogeneous relations
shows that every product of \(k(N-1)+1\) elements of \(J\)
contains some \(a_j^N\). Consequently
\[
                         J^{\,k(N-1)+1}=0.
\]

Embed the local blocks
\[
 S_+=\begin{pmatrix}a_+&b_+\\c_+&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 S_-=\begin{pmatrix}0&c_-\\b_-&a_-\end{pmatrix}
\]
at the actual adjacent strand positions and multiply them in braid
order to obtain \(\rho_N\). Delete the first row and column to get
\(\rho_N'\). For a square operator matrix use the ordered definition
\[
 \det_Q A=\sum_{\pi}(-Q)^{\operatorname{inv}(\pi)}
                         A_{\pi(1),1}\cdots A_{\pi(r),r},
\]
and set
\[
 C_N=\sum_{\emptyset\ne L\subset\{2,\ldots,b\}}
       (-1)^{|L|-1}\det_Q((Q\rho_N)_{L,L}).
\]
Thus \(I-C_N\) is the finite representation of the specified
modified quantum determinant \(\widetilde{\det}_Q(I-Q\rho_N')\).

If the braid closure is a knot, then \(C_N\in J\). Indeed modulo
\(J\) every crossing block is a weighted transposition, and their
product is a weighted permutation with one cycle. No nonempty proper
set of its vertices is invariant under that cycle. Each nonempty
principal submatrix after deleting a strand therefore has zero
ordered quantum determinant, purely by its zero pattern. This proves
the asserted membership and hence
\[
 C_N^{k(N-1)+1}=0,\qquad
 (I-C_N)^{-1}=\sum_{r=0}^{k(N-1)}C_N^r,\qquad
                         \det(I-C_N)=1.
\]
The last determinant is the ordinary determinant on \(\mathcal F_N\).
Nilpotency order grows with \(N\); this is not a uniform finite
transport bound as the quantum level tends to infinity.

The finite evaluation also retains its literal source. If \(P\) is
a finite polynomial in the crossing operators, the Laurent-function
quotient defining \(\mathcal F_N\) is respected by all shifts.
Therefore applying \(P\) to \(1\), then evaluating at
\(x_j=y_j=Q^{-1},u_j=1\), gives exactly
\[
 \left.\mathcal E_N(P)\right|_{Q}
       =\ell_N\,\pi_N(P)\,\mathbf1.
\]
Here \(\pi_N\) is this finite representation and \(\ell_N\) is the
specified point-evaluation row. The identity concerns finite operator
polynomials before importing any completed inverse or invariant theorem.
The inverse above is already finite in this representation.

This separates two determinant questions. The ordinary determinant of
the unipotent root operator is one, while a selected inverse matrix
element can still have exponential growth. The calculation does not
identify that element, including its framing, with the original
Kashaev invariant. Such an identification still requires the actual
crossing, quantum-MacMahon and marked-source comparison; it is not
assumed from the literature theorem here. In particular no
Fuglede--Kadison determinant comparison or volume lower bound has been
proved. The existing [pointed quantum-A Gram period](pointed_a_gram_period.md)
already retains the original invariant in a different positive
determinant ratio; its source-growth estimate remains open as well.

## Required accuracy of the full-field gradient witness, 22 November

The new certificate is exact, but its usual trial-field witness still
requires precision on the scale of the normalized source. This can be
checked quantitatively in the physical metric, without an asymptotic
assumption about the knot. The calculation concerns this particular
witness, not every possible sum-of-squares lower certificate.

Use the [physical objective](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md),
write \(B=B_{\rm ph}\), \(k=K_N/B\), and let \(a\) be its true
normalized forward field. Let \(u_*\) minimize \(E=E_{\rm ph}\).
The source proof's stronger Hessian estimate carries over unchanged:
\[
 \mu I\le D^2E\le3I,\qquad \mu=41/32.
\]
Indeed its proof uses only the separate-input bilinear and linear
operator bounds. Put \(d(u)=E(u)-\|\nabla E(u)\|^2/2\).
The embedded normalized closing row \(c\) has norm at most \(1/16\).
At the true field,
\[
 E(a)=|k|^2,\quad \nabla E(a)=2c^*k,\quad
 \|\nabla E(a)\|\le |k|/8,\quad
 d(a)\ge127|k|^2/128.
\]
For a feasible \(u\), let \(\varepsilon=\|u-a\|\). Along the
feasible segment from \(a\) to \(u\), use
\(\nabla d=(I-D^2E)\nabla E\),
\(\|I-D^2E\|\le2\), and
\(\|\nabla E(a+t(u-a))\|\le |k|/8+3t\varepsilon\).
Integration gives
\[
 |d(u)-d(a)|\le |k|\varepsilon/4+3\varepsilon^2.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \|u-a\|\le |k|/2
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad d(u)\ge15|k|^2/128.
\]

There is also a necessary precision bound. Strong convexity gives
\(\|\nabla E(u)\|^2\ge2\mu(E(u)-e_*)\), where \(e_*=E(u_*)\).
Combining this with its quadratic growth inequality yields
\[
 d(u)\le e_*-\frac{369}{2048}\|u-u_*\|^2.
\]
Since \(e_*\le |k|^2\) and strong monotonicity gives
\(\|u_*-a\|\le\|\nabla E(a)\|/\mu\le4|k|/41\),
\[
 d(u)>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|u-a\|<\left(\sqrt{2048/369}+4/41\right)|k|
                                      <\tfrac52|k|.
\]
When \(k=0\), the preceding inequality for \(d\) instead rules out
a positive witness altogether, as required by the source comparison.

This does not lower-bound any actual approximation error. It shows
which error estimate would suffice, and which precision a positive
witness necessarily achieves. An \(O(N^{-M})\) error bound alone
cannot certify this route when \(|K_N|/B\) is exponentially smaller.
Even an exponential error bound must be compared with the actual
normalized source scale, retaining prefactors when rates coincide.
The calculation gives no new lower bound for that scale.

The next constructive task is therefore a direct phase-sensitive dual
certificate, or control of the initialized original cycle/source
coefficient, unless a full packet approximation at the required scale
can be proved. Further fixed-order local approximations alone do not
complete this trial-field argument. The finite-exception theorem and
the frozen manuscripts are unchanged.

and the [normalized source estimate](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md)
at `6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c`.

## An exact degree-four certificate with the constant physical budgets, 22 November

The [matrix certificate theorem](research_conway_physical_matrix_degree_four_certificate.md)
now proves finite-order semidefinite exactness for the physical quartic
below. The objective \(E_{\rm ph}\), its packet balls, its original
complex closing, and its budget \(B_{\rm ph}\) are unchanged. In
particular products and turns still use budget \(16\); multiplication
does not acquire an additional factor depending on \(N\).

The extra ingredient is actual matrix structure. For physical matrices,
\[
 \mathfrak C(A,B)=\|A\|_{\rm HS}^2\|B\|_{\rm HS}^2-\|AB\|_{\rm HS}^2
\]
is an explicit sum of row--column Lagrange squares. Together with
\(\langle XY,HK\rangle=\langle H^*X,KY^*\rangle\), this gives
polynomial sum-of-squares identities for all mixed and curvature terms
in the Hessian. The identities remain valid on the full pair algebra;
the ambient adjoint matrices need not lie in that algebra.

Write \(g_v(x)=1-\|x_v\|^2\), and let \(Q_2(g)\) consist of sums
of squares of quadratics plus \(g_v\) times sums of squares of linear
polynomials. The theorem proves, for every fixed feasible trial \(u\),
\[
 E_{\rm ph}(x)-E_{\rm ph}(u)
 -\nabla E_{\rm ph}(u)\cdot(x-u)-\tfrac12\|x-u\|^2\in Q_2(g).
\]
In particular, if \(e_N=\min E_{\rm ph}\), then
\[
 e_N=\max\{\lambda:E_{\rm ph}-\lambda\in Q_2(g)\}
\]
with attainment, and the matching order-two moment problem has the same
attained value. Its coefficients require only the known physical tensors
and packet balls. The unknown minimizer is used in the existence proof,
not supplied as data to the optimization problem.

At a specified feasible trial put
\(d(u)=E_{\rm ph}(u)-\|\nabla E_{\rm ph}(u)\|^2/2\).
Then \(E_{\rm ph}-d(u)\in Q_2(g)\), and
\[
 B_{\rm ph}^2\max(0,d(u))\le |K_N|^2.
\]
Here \(d(u)\) is a number once the trial is fixed. The polynomial
certificate has degree four even though the expression for \(d\) as a
function of a varying trial can have higher degree.

There is therefore no relaxation-degree error in this finite physical
problem. Matrix sizes and the accuracy needed for a small optimum still
grow with \(N\). A geometric family of positive lower certificates at
the hyperbolic-volume rate, after every required short partial filling,
has not been constructed. The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## Polynomial gluing costs in the physical metric, 22 November

The [uniform physical metric theorem](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md)
provides a simpler exact setting for the quartic. Declare the balanced
physical basis orthonormal and give the full pair algebra
\(\mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[\Omega]\) its inherited Hilbert--Schmidt
norm. This is still the complete \(N\)-dimensional algebra, with
all repeated-root derivative directions. The literal turn permutes
physical matrix entries with unit phases. Consequently
\[
 \|\mathcal T A\|_{\rm ph}=\|A\|_{\rm ph},\qquad
 \|AB\|_{\rm ph}\le\|A\|_{\rm ph}\|B\|_{\rm ph}.
\]
Both original normalized closing rows have dual norm between
\(1/N\) and one. The marked row is retained through its exact identity
\(\lambda_0=\phi\mathcal T\) on the full physical algebra.
Cups and caps are contracted exactly here; they are not approximated
by low-occupation states.

Let \(B_E\) be the synthesis map of a fixed unfilled Conway tree
with \(p\) products, keeping every leaf as an independent full packet.
An explicit right inverse inserts the physical identity box, whose
norm is \(N\), and reverses the genuine turns. It proves
\[
 N^{-2p}I\le C_E:=B_EB_E^*\le N^{2p}I,
 \qquad \operatorname{cond}_2(C_E)\le N^{4p}.
\]
Thus the synthesis quotient norm and this fixed physical norm differ
by polynomial factors for every fixed template. Either original
closing has squared quotient-dual cost between
\(N^{-2p-2}\) and \(N^{2p}\).
These are properties of the unfilled synthesis map. Its right inverse
need not respect a prescribed short leaf, so this is not a conditioning
bound for a partially specialized channel.

For the quartic, separate-input bilinear norm is enough: products,
turns, and a normalized original closing can each use budget \(16\).
For \(m\) vertices, prescribed leaf packets \(A_j\), and the known
external scalar \(\eta_N\), the new total budget is
\[
 B_{\rm ph}=16^m\max(1,|\eta_N|)
                      \prod_j\max(1,\|A_j\|_{\rm ph}).
\]
The sum \(E_{\rm ph}\) of squared normalized recursion errors and
the original closing term is quartic. It has a unique interior
minimum, Hessian between \(I\) and \(3I\), and
\[
 B_{\rm ph}^2\min E_{\rm ph}\le |K_N|^2
       \le\frac{197}{196}B_{\rm ph}^2\min E_{\rm ph}.
\]
The budget and the raw minimum differ from those in the Newton metric.
No small tensor-coefficient norm or degree-four semidefinite exactness
is inferred from these constant bilinear budgets.

This removes exponential structural Gram costs from the new formulation.
The actual filled leaf tensor can still have an exponentially small
projection or closing overlap. Neither that lower bound nor the
hyperbolic-volume rate has been proved after arbitrary short partial
fillings. Existing binomial-metric packet estimates also require their
actual conversion cost before use here. The finite-exception theorem
therefore remains open; the frozen manuscripts are unchanged.

## The original cup sector and the geometric boundary, 22 November

The small-input packet theorems are valid, but their hypothesis has
not been established for the incoming state of the original knot
contraction. The [literal bridge source](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md)
gives, at \(M=1\),
\[
 p_N=N\sum_{a=0}^{d}x^{-a}w_{d-a}\otimes w_a^{\rm dual},
 \qquad d=N-1,\quad |x|=1.
\]
Here the standard-dual color equals the original root color.
Equip both indexed head copies with the prescribed binomial metric
\(\|w_a\|^2=\binom da^{-1}\). This is a choice of positive
head metrics, not the categorical Hilbert-dual metric.
Every term of this cup has total occupation \(d\); a tensor of
\(k\) original cups has total occupation \(kd\).

In fact these cups have little mass in the low boxes used by the
[small-input proof](research_bounded_activity_small_input_packets.md).
For one cup let \(P_m\) restrict both occupations to
\(m=\lfloor\delta d\rfloor\), with fixed \(0<\delta<1\).
Directly from the displayed source,
\[
 \|p_N\|^2=N^2\sum_{a=0}^d\binom da^{-2}\ge2N^2.
\]
If \(\delta<1/2\), then \(P_mp_N=0\). If
\(1/2\le\delta<1\), only \(d-m\le a\le m\) survive and
\[
 \frac{\|P_mp_N\|^2}{\|p_N\|^2}
 \le\frac{(d+1)^3}{2}e^{-2dH(\delta)},\qquad
 H(t)=-t\log t-(1-t)\log(1-t)>0.
\]
For completeness, the binomial probability at \(a\) with parameter
\(a/d\) is a mode and hence at least \(1/(d+1)\). Thus
\(\binom da\ge e^{dH(a/d)}/(d+1)\). On the retained interval
\(H(a/d)\ge H(\delta)\); summing at most \(d+1\) terms proves
the bound. The original incoming cup is therefore not approximated
by this low box in the stated norm.

Analytic reconstruction does not automatically remove the problem.
In unnormalized holomorphic coherent coordinates, recovering a cup
requires total degree \(d\). The norm of extracting the coefficient
of \(z_1^d\) from a radius-\(\rho\) polydisk is
\(\rho^{-d}\), as the monomial itself shows. Applying this Cauchy
estimate to the truncation bound proportional to \(\rho^{m+1}\)
leaves \(\rho^{m+1-d}\). For \(m\sim\delta d<d\), shrinking
\(\rho\) no longer improves that bound. This is a limitation of
the estimate, not a lower bound on the actual reconstruction error.

There is a related geometric restriction on a whole generating tuple.
The actual [coherent holonomy chart](research_actual_coherent_polarization_transport.md)
at \(M=1\) has
\[
 t=\frac{wz}{1+wz},\quad A=e^{2\pi it},\quad K=-A^{-1},\quad
 e=\frac{A^{-1}-1}{w},\quad f=(1-A)w,\quad
 G=\begin{pmatrix}K&e\\Kf&K^{-1}+ef\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The apparent quotient defining \(e\) is removable:
\(e=z[(e^{-2\pi it}-1)/t]/(1+wz)\).
Consequently \(G\to-I\) uniformly when \(z\to0\) and \(w\)
stays in a fixed bounded chart. The actual Borel prefix factors
\(b_-\) tend to \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\), so their finite
products and inverses remain bounded. The based meridians
\(H_j=B_{-,j-1}^{-1}G_jB_{-,j-1}\) therefore all tend to \(-I\)
if every incoming coordinate is small and every paired row coordinate
is bounded.

Such a tuple cannot generate a discrete nonelementary complete
hyperbolic image once the neighborhood is sufficiently small.
Here is a direct matrix proof. If noncommuting trace-two parabolics
\(A,B\) satisfy \(\|A-I\|,\|B-I\|\le\varepsilon=1/20\) in the
Euclidean operator norm on \(2\times2\) matrices, put
\(B_0=B\), \(B_{n+1}=[A,B_n]\). The exact commutator identity gives
\[
 \|B_{n+1}-I\|\le
 \frac{2\varepsilon\|B_n-I\|}
      {(1-\varepsilon)(1-\|B_n-I\|)},
\]
so \(B_n\to I\). Conjugating \(A\) to
\(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\)
only to check nontriviality, its parameter satisfies \(a\ne0\).
Distinct fixed points give a nonzero lower-left entry \(c_0\) of
\(B\); the exact recurrence is \(c_{n+1}=a c_n^2\ne0\).
Thus the group contains nonidentity elements converging to identity,
contradicting discreteness. A nonelementary parabolic generating
tuple contains such a pair. Apply this to the lifts \(-H_j\).

This excludes only an entire generating tuple in the stated chart.
An individual cusp or a selected short-component boundary tuple can
be elementary and can have small inputs. Complex paired row coordinates
or adapted frames may also escape the bounded chart. Those possibilities
still need their original source estimates. In particular completeness
of peripheral eigenvalues alone does not justify the small-input
hypothesis for the whole geometric state.

The next source estimate must address the forced cup-degree sector
and its original marked closing. Further vacuum estimates alone do
not supply it. No new volume lower bound is asserted by this audit;
the frozen manuscripts are unchanged.

## Bounded activities with small physical inputs, 22 November

The [bounded-activity packet theorem](research_bounded_activity_small_input_packets.md)
extends the full-vector estimate to any fixed bound on the Euler
activities, including activity one. The extra hypothesis is on the
actual incoming vector: its coherent coordinates must lie in a fixed
sufficiently small neighborhood of the lowering vacuum. The theorem
allows every fixed finite word in the stated lowering factors.

The local kernel follows from an exact diagonal change of coordinates.
One first fixes its compact coordinate domain, then chooses the
diagonal scale, then restricts the original input. The dimensionless
interaction is unchanged; its smallness comes from that genuine input
restriction. A separate estimate in the original binomial metric
controls the entire complementary coherent region, so no exponentially
conditioned metric comparison is used.

The global estimate uses a simple invariant subspace. Each factor
only lowers its donor occupation, so the box \(a_i\le m\) is
preserved throughout the word. Small coherent inputs have exponentially
small mass above this box. Binomial tail bounds and the exact inverse
norm estimate show that this remains a small relative output error.
The exact coherent resolution then gives the full-vector packet
approximation with relative error \(O(N^{-1})+O(e^{-cN})\).

There is also arbitrary exponential accuracy for a finite quantum
approximation. Fix \(\Lambda>0\) and \(0<\delta<1\), and truncate
each Euler factor at \(\lfloor\delta(N-1)\rfloor\). After making
the original input neighborhood smaller, the resulting word obeys
\[
 \frac{\|(W_N-W_N^{[\delta]})\psi_z\|}{\|W_N\psi_z\|}
                                      \le Ce^{-\Lambda N}.
\]
The retained coefficients are exact quantum coefficients and their
number still grows with \(N\). This is separate from the classical
phase-and-amplitude approximation, whose proved error remains
\(O(N^{-1})\). The same truncation preserves exactly the low input
box and the high output box specified in the theorem, at every
activity. Those boxes have not been identified with the original
pivotal closing.

For any specified closing row \(\mathcal L_N\), Cauchy--Schwarz
therefore gives the actual absolute error bound
\[
 |\mathcal L_N(W_N-W_N^{[\delta]})\psi_z|
 \le Ce^{-\Lambda N}\|\mathcal L_N\|\,\|W_N\psi_z\|.
\]
In this input regime the truncation rate can thus pay any known
fixed exponential norm cost of the exterior. It supplies no nonzero
leading value for the retained closing.

This supplies controlled finite vectors at physical activity one
for the lowering-operator class. It does not show that a generic
short-filling geometric state lies in the required input neighborhood,
or extend the alphabet to all original signed crossings and turns.
The Newton-metric and original-closing estimates required by the
finite-exception theorem therefore remain unproved.

## Full-vector approximations from coherent orthogonality, 22 November

The [finite Euler packet note](research_small_activity_full_norm_packet_transport.md)
now constructs actual vectors from the previously proved generating
kernels. It uses the positive binomial metric on the physical heads.
For a fixed finite word \(W_N\) of the stated Euler factors and a
normalized coherent input \(\psi_z\), it gives a vector
\(v_N^{\mathrm{app}}\) such that
\[
 \|W_N\psi_z-v_N^{\mathrm{app}}\|
   \le \left(\frac{C}{N}+Ce^{-cN}\right)\|W_N\psi_z\|.
\]
The activities, meaning the coefficients multiplying the nilpotent
lowering operators, must lie in a sufficiently small fixed polydisk.
The estimate is uniform on the stated compact input sets and runs
through all sufficiently large integer levels. The positive coherent
mass outside a fixed small output window is exponentially small
relative to the squared output norm.

The orthogonality is the exact coherent-frame identity
\[
 N^r\int |\langle\psi_y,v\rangle|^2\,d\mu^{[r]}(y)=\|v\|^2,
\]
where \(r\) is the fixed number of heads and \(\mu\) is the
normalized sphere measure. Applying its adjoint to the local kernel
approximation gives the finite vector. The previous whole-compact-cycle
estimate pays the complementary region before this reconstruction.
The proof treats the full word together, rather than propagating
individual vector errors through exponentially large operator norms.

There are also sharper explicit norm budgets at every complex activity:
\[
 \|U_{i,N}(\lambda)^{\pm1}\|\le(1+|\lambda|)^{N-1},\qquad
 \|\mathcal E_N(\lambda\textstyle\sum_iX_i)^{\pm1}\|
                     \le(1+|\lambda|)^{r(N-1)}.
\]
They follow from ordinary binomial bounds for the quantum divided
powers, the exact finite Euler inverse, and the ordered quantum
multinomial formula. In particular the word's output norm has an
explicit lower bound from its inverse. This makes the complementary
kernel estimate relative without assuming a nonzero closing value.
Coarser exponential budgets were already available; these inequalities
give explicit binomial constants and retain the inverses.

This is a full-vector estimate in the physical head metric. Transport
into the Newton pair-algebra norm and through the original closing
still requires control. A relative \(O(N^{-1})\) vector error alone
does not resolve a closing which is exponentially smaller than the
vector norm. The packet theorem also has not been extended to arbitrary
physical signed crossings: a diagonal gauge preserves its dimensionless
activity parameter and cannot establish that extension. No new volume
lower bound or finite-exception theorem is claimed.

## What the quartic minimum says about the complex closing, 22 November

There is a useful direct consequence of the
[unweighted branching theorem](research_conway_unweighted_branching_source.md):
the closing at the minimizing field approximates the original complex
source, including its phase. The following calculation records that
consequence without introducing another optimization problem.

First suppose the theorem's branching count is \(q\ge1\).
Use its notation: \(k=K_N/B\), \(a=f(a)\) is the actual
forward field, \(G(w)=f(w)-w\), and
\(U(w)=\|G(w)\|^2+|g(w)|^2\). The scalar map \(g\) retains
the original closing functional. For a feasible field define
\[
 S_w=I-Df(w),\qquad d_w=Dg(w)S_w^{-1},\qquad
 h_w=G(w)-d_w^*g(w),\qquad \delta=\frac1{\sqrt{32512}}.
\]
The same disjoint-depth argument as in that theorem gives
\(\|d_w\|\le\delta\) at every feasible field. Each derivative
row has at most two child blocks of norm at most \(1/16\), and
each child belongs to one parent. Thus
\(\|Df(w)\|\le\sqrt2/16<1/8\) and
\(\|S_w^{-1}\|\le8/7\).

All gradients below use real and imaginary packet coordinates. Direct
differentiation gives
\[
 \nabla U(w)=-2S_w^*G(w)+2Dg(w)^*g(w)=-2S_w^*h_w,
 \qquad \|h_w\|\le\frac47\|\nabla U(w)\|.
\]
Put \(b=(w+a)/2\). The theorem's exact midpoint identity is
\(k=g(w)+d_bG(w)\). Substituting the definition of \(h_w\)
therefore proves the complex error estimate
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \left|\frac{K_N}{B}-g(w)\right|
 \le\frac{|g(w)|}{32512}
       +\frac{4}{7\sqrt{32512}}\|\nabla U(w)\|.
 \quad}
\]
This is an estimate for complex numbers before their phases are
discarded. The midpoint field is used only in its proof; evaluating
the right side requires the trial field and the known compiler maps.

In particular, at the unique interior minimum \(w_*\),
\[
 \frac{K_N}{B}=g(w_*)(1+\varepsilon_N),\qquad
 |\varepsilon_N|\le\frac1{32512},
\]
whenever \(g(w_*)\ne0\). If \(g(w_*)=0\), the same estimate
gives \(K_N=0\); conversely \(K_N=0\) forces \(g(w_*)=0\).
For a nonzero trial closing, a bound
\(\|\nabla U(w)\|\le c|g(w)|\) gives a relative error at most
\[
 \frac1{32512}+\frac{4c}{7\sqrt{32512}}.
\]
If this number is less than one, the trial closing is a certified
nonzero approximation to the original source. This criterion keeps
every packet coordinate, including derivative directions.

The minimum is also close to the actual forward field on the scale
of the source itself. The midpoint identity for the proper recursion
gives \(\|w_*-a\|\le(8/7)\|G(w_*)\|\), while stationarity
gives \(G(w_*)=d_{w_*}^*g(w_*)\). Consequently
\[
 \|w_*-a\|\le\frac{8}{7\sqrt{32512}}|g(w_*)|.
\]
For \(q=0\), use the theorem's empty-field convention:
\(g_0=K_N/B\) exactly, with zero gradient and field-distance terms.

Known exact short subtrees can also be removed together, without
multiplying comparison losses. Choose disjoint rooted subtrees and
fix all their packets to their exact normalized forward values.
Their internal residuals then vanish. Let \(m_S\) be the minimum
over the remaining packets, with the original maps and budget \(B\)
unchanged. Restriction raises the minimum, and the full actual field
is still feasible, so
\[
 m_U\le m_S\le |k|^2,\qquad
 B^2m_S\le |K_N|^2\le
       \left(1+\frac1{32512}\right)B^2m_S.
\]
The same single factor works for any number of these subtrees. Their
full boundary packets must be retained, including phases and derivative
coordinates. A short component with unknown incoming boundary packets
instead needs the existing convex boundary energy; it cannot be
replaced by one independently evaluated packet.

Thus the minimization has not replaced the full quantum field by
classical angles. Its useful simplification is an explicit closing
and a relative stationarity test. We still need geometric fields
passing this test, or the existing tangential-energy test, with a
proved hyperbolic-volume rate for their nonzero closing. No new
filling class or finite-exception theorem follows from this calculation.

## Where the geometric trial must differ from the old window, 22 November

The relevant comparison in the frozen proof is quantitative. Its
[full filling estimate](../papers/conway-asymptotics/filling.tex)
bounds the omitted source by
\[
 P_{\boldsymbol n}(N)e^{N(\Phi_0-\gamma)},\qquad \gamma>0,
\]
with a polynomial prefactor for every fixed filling tuple. It makes
this negligible using the small action drop of long fillings.
After a fixed short partial filling, write \(\Phi_S\) for the new
complete source height. Reusing that old estimate would require
\[
 \Phi_0-\Phi_S+
       O\!\left(\sum_{j\ \mathrm{remaining}}n_j^{-2}\right)<\gamma.
\]
A polynomial cost from a change of basis or a constant comparison
between energies does not establish this exponential inequality.
This does not prove that the actual remainder is large: it identifies
what the old bound fails to decide. The
[complex-boundary theorem](research_long_fillings_complex_boundary_phase.md)
instead assumes a new local expansion and a whole-source angular gap
measured from \(\Phi_S\). Both assumptions still need verification.

For some allowed short fillings, that theorem's specific nonvanishing
local-amplitude hypothesis is false. The existing
[source-rebasing identity](research_short_fillings_require_source_rebasing.md)
provides a direct example. Let \(Q_N\) be the full polynomial of
the retained core, let \(d=N-1\), and consider the padded boundary
polynomial
\[
 B_N^{\mathrm{pad}}(z)=e_d(z)(JQ_N)(z),\qquad
 e_d(z)=\frac{(-1)^d[2T_N(z/2)+2]}{N^2(z-c_0)},\qquad
 c_0=2\cos(\pi/N).
\]
The product displayed here is an ordinary polynomial. Its equality
to \(\phi_N(Q_N)e_d\) holds in the full quotient algebra, not
necessarily in the ordinary polynomial ring. At every odd level
\(N\ge3\), however, \(T_N(-1)=-1\) and \(-2\ne c_0\), so
\[
 B_N^{\mathrm{pad}}(-2)=0.
\]
The same value holds for its canonical representative, since \(-2\)
is then a root of the quotient polynomial. Thus its angular source
at \(t=0\), with \(z=-2\cos t\), cannot have the theorem's
eventually nonzero form with an \(N\)-independent amplitude
\(a(0)\ne0\).

This example is handled by the exact contraction
\[
 \phi_N(R^a B_N^{\mathrm{pad}})=\kappa_N^a\phi_N(Q_N).
\]
It retains the original core period rather than producing a new
Gaussian source for that removable twist. A universal short-filling
argument therefore needs exact endpoint reductions alongside any
geometric bulk estimate. The identity does not estimate the core
period, and no new lower bound or exceptional-filling theorem is
claimed here. This calculation checks the scope of the trial-field
route; it does not change the frozen long-filling theorem.

## Nearby closing observations have comparable costs, 22 November

The [boundary-cost comparison theorem](research_conway_boundary_cost_local_comparison.md)
now applies to every fixed finite expression built from the original
Conway multiplication and turns. Keep each filled crossing block as
a full leaf input. Its universal synthesis \(B_E\) and positive
covariance \(C_E=B_EB_E^*\) then depend on the unfilled expression.
Define
\[
 a_r(E,N)=(C_E)_{rr}=\|e_r^{\mathsf T}B_E\|^2.
\]
These are squared norms of closing maps before the actual filled
leaf states are inserted. The theorem proves, for all levels and
all root indices,
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 N^{-A_E|r-s|}\le\frac{a_r(E,N)}{a_s(E,N)}
                         \le N^{A_E|r-s|}.
 \qquad}
\]
Here \(A_E\) depends only on the fixed expression. Thus any fixed
number of steps from either original endpoint cap changes its cost
by at most a polynomial in \(N\).

The proof uses the exact positive doubled synthesis tree. Its support
is a fixed integer system with nonnegative labels and slacks; the
quantum level changes only its right side. A finite conformal integer
generation argument moves any configuration from root \(r\) to root
\(s\), changing each label by at most a constant times \(|r-s|\).
The exact sine-factorial coefficients change by a polynomial factor
under these bounded shifts, and the map has bounded multiplicity.
This proves the finite-level comparison without an entropy limit or
an assumption about the conditioning of the full covariance.

For a matrix \(H_N\) of fixed bandwidth \(b\), with entries bounded
by \(C_HN^p\), the theorem gives the original-cap estimate
\[
 \|e_r^{\mathsf T}H_N\|_{G_E,*}
 \le (2b+1)C_HN^{p+A_Eb/2}\|e_r^{\mathsf T}\|_{G_E,*},
 \qquad G_E=C_E^{-1},\quad
 \|\lambda\|_{G_E,*}^2=\lambda C_E\lambda^*.
\]
It applies to either endpoint cap and to the already verified
finite-band Casimir observations. For these closing observations,
a bound for every operator on the full quotient space is unnecessary.

The same result holds for strictly positive diagonal leaf metrics
whose adjacent weights have polynomial ratios. The proof retains
the exact scalar by rescaling the leaf vectors inversely. It does
not cover arbitrary coherent nondiagonal metrics or zero weights.

The fiber map changes shared leaf labels inside a covariance sum.
It is therefore not a comparison of periods with their signed filling
coefficients held fixed. The actual leaf projection and its angle
with the original closing row still need a lower estimate at the
hyperbolic-volume rate. No new volume-conjecture class or finite
exception theorem is claimed.

## Testing the configuration coupling against the signed source, 22 November

The new positive covariance comparison was checked against the actual
crossing phases. Expand each fixed physical power into its original
signed unit crossings. The remaining multiplication and turn weights
are nonnegative, but the leaf character is exactly
\[
 \chi_N(\xi)=(-q)^{S(\xi)},\qquad
 S(\xi)=\sum_\ell\varepsilon_\ell i_\ell,
 \quad \varepsilon_\ell\in\{1,-1\},\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},
\]
apart from the retained common Cartan and framing factors. The
bounded-displacement fiber map used for covariance estimates does
not preserve this character or provide an exact cancellation rule.

The original inverse relation gives an immediate source test:
\[
 \phi(R^+R^-)=(-q)^{-d}\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}Q^i=0,
 \qquad d=N-1,\quad Q=q^2.
\]
At odd levels no two terms of this cyclic sum have opposite phases.
More generally \(-q\) has odd order \(N\) at odd levels, so a
positive-weight pairwise phase-reversing involution cannot account
for the exact source cancellation. At even levels phase reversal
requires a charge change congruent to \(N\) modulo \(2N\);
a bounded configuration move cannot supply it for large \(N\).
These checks use the original crossings and closing, not a replacement
model or a hyperbolic-knot counterexample.

This audit does not exclude multi-term quantum Pascal identities or
the existing full Fourier construction. It shows why the covariance
comparison cannot itself be summed as a comparison of signed periods.
Any further reduction must keep the complete cyclic relations, their
logarithmic lifts and initialized boundary currents. No new geometric
coefficient lower bound was obtained from this attempted extension.

## Checking positive state sums against the original root, 22 November

The exact [ordinary-color Plancherel identity](ordinary_color_plancherel_bound_audit.md)
still gives the relevant positive target:
\[
 E_N=|K_N|^2+\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}|C_j(q_N)|^2,
 \qquad q_N=e^{\pi i/N}.
\]
The ordinary remainder has the proved polynomial bound. A positive
geometric state sum could therefore help only after its finite
definition is related to this complete-color norm with the original
marked source retained.
The index \(j\) changes the main color on the entire knot. It is not
the Newton boundary index \(r\) in the preceding covariance theorem,
where the full main module remains fixed. That theorem therefore does
not compare \(|K_N|^2\) with an adjacent ordinary-color value.

The standard compact TV comparison was checked at the matching root.
[Detcherry--Kalfagianni--Yang, Theorem 1.1(1)](https://users.math.msu.edu/users/kalfagia/QT.pdf)
states, for its admissible levels and in these variables,
\[
 \mathrm{TV}_N(S^3\setminus K;q_N)
   =\eta_N^2\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}[j]^2|C_j(q_N)|^2,
 \qquad \eta_N^2=\frac{2\sin^2(\pi/N)}N.
\]
Their colored Jones values are unreduced and the unknot value is
\([j]\), explaining the displayed weights. The complete color
\(j=N\) is absent. Its ordinary quantum dimension is zero at this
root, whereas its marked reduced source is retained in \(K_N\).
The exponential TV regime discussed there uses a different root.
This is a check of the primary definitions, normalizations and theorem
statement; their TV/Jones identity was not independently reproved or
used as a premise for a new volume assertion here.

The [2026 modular-double construction](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.16560v1)
was likewise checked from its introductory definitions. It integrates
continuous edge-length colors modulo changes of horospheres. Its
proposed Jones-function relation in section 1.3 is announced as future
work and has the reflected pairing
\(\int J_b(x)\overline{J_b(-x)}\,dx\). It supplies no stated
identity with the finite norm \(E_N\). No asymptotic theorem from
that paper has been assumed.

These comparisons do not exclude a suitable modified or relative
state-sum construction. They do exclude substituting either displayed
object for \(E_N\) without an additional source-preserving theorem.
The exact doubled original source remains available, but its coherent
sewing and its marked ideal-edge constraint still need the geometric
estimate. No new signed lower bound was obtained from this comparison.

## What the fixed degree has simplified, 21 November

The finite-level source problem now needs only a quartic objective and
degree-four certificates. The [local gluing theorem](research_conway_gate_local_semidefinite_gluing.md)
already reduces the semidefinite formulation to one small group of
packets at a time, with only first means matched across an attaching
edge. Its [moment theorem](research_conway_moment_rigidity_and_error_bounds.md)
shows that the optimum describes one deterministic packet field.
There is no further moment degree or independent moment distribution
to determine. The later unweighted branching theorem removes the
covariance matrices and retains only genuine branching inputs.

For a proposed geometric field, solving that optimization problem is
optional. The exact original-closing error estimate is
\[
 \left|K_N/B-g(w)\right|
       \le \frac{\|G(w)\|}{\sqrt{32512}}.
\]
Thus a nonzero geometric closing and a smaller relative residual would
give the desired lower bound directly. This estimate retains the
complex closing; replacing it by a packet norm would lose precisely
the information still needed. Neither fixed degree nor the uniform
positive Hessian supplies the exponential rate of the minimum.

## A uniform operator through an actual branching vertex, 22 November

The [Newton product-lift theorem](research_conway_uniform_newton_product_lift.md)
now supplies an exact bounded operation on the two inputs of a product.
This is stronger than the earlier angular product rule, whose separated
shifts had poles and did not define a bounded operator on the Newton
tensor space.

Let \(M\) be the original multiplication, \(Z\) multiplication by
the Casimir coordinate, \(J\) the genuine turn, and \(L=JZJ\).
Put \(d=N-1\), \(s_r=2\sin(\pi r/N)\),
\(p_r=s_r^2\), and \(c_r=2\cos((2r+1)\pi/N)\).
On the full Newton basis, with negative subscripts interpreted as zero,
define
\[
\begin{split}
 \Delta_NL(e_i\otimes e_j)={}&c_{i+j}e_i\otimes e_j\\
 &-p_{i+j}(e_{i-1}\otimes e_j+e_i\otimes e_{j-1})\\
 &-s_{i+j}s_{i+j-1}e_{i-1}\otimes e_{j-1}.
\end{split}
\]
Then, at every level and on the entire repeated-root algebra,
\[
 M\Delta_NL=LM,\qquad \|\Delta_NL\|\le14.
\]
The completed current \(L-c_0I\) consequently has a lift of norm
at most sixteen. The other Casimir has the elementary lift
\(\Delta_NZ=Z\otimes I\), of norm at most six. Substitution gives
an exact lift for any specified noncommutative polynomial in \(Z,L\),
with the written order retained. Any original exterior row can be
applied after these identities; no source or derivative channel changes.

The proof is a direct calculation with the actual positive Newton
product coefficients. Two asymmetric formulas initially contain
\(p_j/p_i\); taking a specified weighted average cancels every
ratio. The resulting operator has one diagonal and three strict-shift
terms, of norms at most \(2,4,4,4\). The proof checks every lower
support endpoint and the exact zero products at total indices
\(N,N+1\) and above. It does not assume a semisimple root or
infer a tensor-space bound from an angular supremum norm.

This settles one previously missing local transport estimate. It does
not yet give transport through a whole arbitrary short component.
The explicit lift contains joint degree-clock and strict-shift
operators; bounded lifts for their coupled continuations through
further branches are not supplied by this theorem. It is not asserted
to be a coassociative coproduct. In particular no new geometric closing
estimate or volume-conjecture class follows yet.

## Exact boundary estimates in the original closing direction, 21 November

The [wall-cap theorem](research_conway_wall_cap_visibility.md)
gives a concrete simplification of one boundary contribution. Write
\(d=N-1\), \(s_r=2\sin(\pi r/N)\),
\(S_r=\prod_{h=1}^r s_h\), and \(S_0=1\).
The lower-total boundary current is the exact trilinear form
\[
 \mathcal W_N(A,B,C)
   =-N^2\sum_{i+j+k=d-1}
                   \frac{A_iB_jC_k}{S_i^2S_j^2S_k^2}
\]
in the full original Newton coordinates. If its exterior closing
has Frobenius-dual vector \(v\), put
\(W_v(A,B)=\mathcal W_N(v,A,B)\). Then
\[
 W_v=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v\in\mathbb C e_d.
\]
The original marked cap has precisely this dual vector and kills
the current. The bare Frobenius cap has dual vector \(1=e_0\)
and gives a weighted reversal of norm at most four.

There is also an explicit positive Gram matrix for detecting the
other cap coordinates:
\[
 E_{\rm wall}(v)=\sum_{i<d}s_{i+1}^4|v_i|^2,\qquad
 \frac{256}{N^4}\|P_{<d}v\|^2
       \le E_{\rm wall}(v)\le16\|P_{<d}v\|^2.
\]
The missing line is still needed by the original source, since
\(\phi(e_d)=1\). Retaining \(|\phi(v)|^2\) completes this
observation energy to a full positive diagonal norm.

For an actual exterior word \(T\), propagate its original cap first:
its exact dual vector is \(T^\dagger1\) or \(T^\dagger e_d\),
using the bilinear Frobenius adjoint and the reversed operator order.
Multiplication by any actual packet preserves \(\mathbb C e_d\),
including a possible zero scalar; the genuine turn sends \(e_d\)
to \(1\). Thus this is an exact criterion at the given attachment,
not an invariant deletion rule through arbitrary later turns.

The distinction between observation and full contraction is essential.
A single actual signed crossing from the unit cap already has a full
wall operator with positive exponential growth, as proved from an
explicit factorial entry. The diagonal observation energy does not
upper-bound that operator. The ordinary-color theorem also cannot
be applied to these corrected complete-color Newton probes without
a new argument. No arbitrary-short boundary gap or nonzero geometric
closing follows here.

## One common quantum trace equation, with its source, 21 November

The [shared Casimir equation](research_centered_tensor_common_casimir_source.md)
expresses the original multiplication tensor in a particularly simple
form. Set \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(a=q^{-1}\),
\(d=N-1\), and \(D_N(t)=1-(-1)^dt^N\). For its centered
generating polynomial \(\mathcal C_N(x,y,z)\), let
\[
 \mathscr Z_xF=
 \frac{(1+ax)^2F(x/Q,y,z)-(1+x^2)F(x,y,z)}x.
\]
This is the actual Casimir action on the full degree-below-\(N\)
space; both endpoint arrows have their original zero coefficients.
With \(s_1=x+y+z\), \(s_2=xy+xz+yz\), \(s_3=xyz\),
\[
 h=1+as_3,\qquad L=a-s_1-as_2+s_3,\qquad
 \beta_N=(-1)^{N+1}q^{3d^2/2}N^{-3/2},
\]
the three legs satisfy the same exact polynomial identity
\[
 h\mathscr Z_i\mathcal C_N-L\mathcal C_N
 =-\frac{\beta_N}{Q}D_N(x)D_N(y)D_N(z),
 \qquad i=x,y,z.
\]
It follows by one shift and an elementary symmetric expansion from
the initialized Rogers equation. This is an explicit common potential
for the known source, rather than an additional constraint or a new
geometric estimate.

The distinction between the two finite representations matters. On
the invertible generating grid \(t_j=-q^{-1}Q^{-j}\), the displayed
right side vanishes. In the Taylor coefficient quotient used for
assembly, every \(D_N\) instead equals one, so the source remains.
Even on the generating grid, division by \(h\) can lose a real
boundary current: at \(i+j+k=d-1\), both \(h\) and the tensor
entry vanish, but its common Casimir current is nonzero. The grid
equation there reads \(0=0\). These terms must remain in a
source-sensitive gluing argument.

## Orthogonal packets with a remaining-context budget, 21 November

The [filtered observation compiler](research_filtered_conway_observation_compiler.md)
now gives an exact gluing rule for smaller observable packets. The
restriction to reachable states is essential at a binary product.
A projection defined only from closing rows in the whole boundary
space need not preserve this restriction and need not allow the
second child to be replaced safely.

Give every elementary crossing, turn and product a positive syntax
cost. A fixed filled leaf may retain its original atomic tensor and
normalization while receiving the cost of its finite crossing-word
realization. This bookkeeping does not change the original compiler.
Let \(\mathcal R_r\) span the actual open states of cost at most
\(r\), and let \(\mathcal Z_{r,m}\subset\mathcal R_r\) consist
of states killed by every original-cap context of cost at most \(m\).
The contexts include all well-defined cap completions, also those
which close to links. For a fixed total budget \(L\), set
\[
 V_r^L=\mathcal R_r/\mathcal Z_{r,L-r}.
\]
Represent this quotient by the orthogonal complement of its kernel
**inside** \(\mathcal R_r\). The note constructs its positive
Gram projector and proves the exact maps
\[
 V_r^L\otimes V_s^L\longrightarrow V_{r+s+1}^L,
 \qquad V_r^L\longrightarrow V_{r+1}^L
\]
for products and turns whenever the indicated budgets fit.

The product proof retains the actual exterior. Inserting a reachable
sibling of cost at most \(s\) enlarges the test context by at most
\(s+1\). The first child's representative is still reachable, so
the same argument justifies replacing the second child. Every
completed term of cost at most \(L\) therefore has exactly its
original marked scalar. These graded maps are not claimed to be
an invariant quotient of the full physical operator algebra; the
graded turn need not be unitary or invertible.

Isometric input inclusions and orthogonal output projections cannot
increase the local Hilbert--Schmidt norms. Keeping all original
budgets gives the same quartic residual comparison
\[
 B_{\rm tot}^2\min E\le |K_N|^2
   \le\frac{197}{196}B_{\rm tot}^2\min E
\]
on these heterogeneous packet spaces. Only their quotient residuals
are charged. Directions genuinely invisible to the allowed future
contexts need not contribute their full physical norm.

This also corrects a possible quantifier misunderstanding. Fixed-level
irreducibility asks for one quotient preserving every exterior at
that \(N\). A slowly growing syntax budget can instead preserve
every **fixed** completed term eventually as \(N\to\infty\).
For example the note's budget of order \(\log N\) has a sum of
packet-dimension bounds \(o(N)\). This uses the original order in
which filling coefficients are fixed before the quantum level grows;
it provides no uniform estimate for coefficients growing with \(N\).

The analytic limitation is substantial. The reachable/context pairing
matrix has entries \(C(t)\), which are actual closed periods. An
entry can already be the target \(K_N\), and constructing the
reachable basis can require the target open state. Thus the theorem
proves safe algebraic composition, not independently known geometric
coefficients, cheap computation, Gram conditioning, or a nonzero
geometric contribution. The elementary fixed-cost dimension bound
already holds for the reachable space before quotienting.

The attempted full-packet route has not supplied a new lower bound:
the exact bottom product and its short-word transforms retain an
initialized finite source whose further branching and closing are
still uncontrolled. The remaining target is a geometric estimate
for that actual retained source, including its connection coefficient
and returning terms. No additional volume case or finite-exception
theorem is claimed.
