## An unweighted branching quartic with a uniform source comparison, 21 November

The [unweighted source theorem](research_conway_unweighted_branching_source.md)
removes covariance matrices from the reduced objective. Keep the known
linear transfers and original complex closing row. If \(q\) counts
products with two internal inputs, the resulting tree has \(2q\)
full packets, or \(4Nq\) real coordinates. Its proper maps \(f_i\)
are constant or bilinear, and its scalar root is \(g\). With
\(\sigma=1/16\), their bilinear coefficient norms are bounded by
\(\sigma\) and \(\sigma^2\), respectively. Define
\[
 G_i(w)=f_i((w_j)_{j\text{ child of }i})-w_i,\qquad
 U(w)=\sum_i\|G_i(w)\|^2+|g(w)|^2,\qquad
 m_U=\min_{\|w_i\|\le1}U(w).
\]
This known objective is quartic. Its coefficients require no inverse
Gram matrix, covariance or square root. All original phases, full
Newton packets and the normalization product \(B=B_{\rm tot}\) remain.
The theorem proves
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 B^2m_U\le |K_N|^2\le
                 \left(1+\frac1{32512}\right)B^2m_U.
 \quad}
\]
This includes exact zeros. The comparison is uniform in the level and
tree size; it does not multiply a loss at every product. The constant
is small because the local tensors were normalized to be small. It
does not establish a geometric positive lower bound.

The useful orthogonality is especially simple. Let \(a\) denote the
true forward field, used only in the proof. Linearize at the midpoint
\((w+a)/2\). Since every map is constant or bilinear, the midpoint
difference formula is exact, and
\[
 K_N/B=g(w)+dG(w),\qquad d=c(I-A)^{-1}.
\]
Here \(A\) is the derivative of the proper recursion and \(c\)
the derivative of the scalar root at that midpoint. The matrix \(A\)
is nilpotent. The rows \(cA^j\) occupy disjoint tree depths, so
their squared norms add, giving
\[
 \|d\|^2=\sum_j\|cA^j\|^2
   \le2\sigma^4\sum_j(2\sigma^2)^j\le\frac1{32512}.
\]
Thus no orthogonal crossing eigenbasis or deletion of derivative
channels is needed for this transport bound.

For any explicit feasible trial the same proof also gives the direct
error bound
\[
 \left|K_N/B-g(w)\right|\le\frac{\|G(w)\|}{\sqrt{32512}}.
\]
A geometric trial whose nonzero closing has the desired exponential
rate and whose displayed error is relatively smaller would therefore
suffice without solving the minimization. Such trials have not been
constructed after arbitrary fixed short partial fillings.

The [preceding branching certificate](research_conway_branching_degree_four_certificate.md)
also proves that exact linear elimination preserves a degree-four
sum-of-squares certificate on the smaller original packet balls.
The unweighted objective inherits the same fixed-degree property.
For a fixed feasible trial \(u\), the number
\[
 d_U(u)=U(u)-\tfrac12\|\nabla U(u)\|^2
\]
is a certified lower bound for \(m_U\), and
\[
 B^2\max(0,d_U(u))\le |K_N|^2\le
            \left(1+\frac1{32512}\right)B^2U(u).
\]
Only the retained packets enter this gradient. No growing-degree
moment hierarchy is needed, although matrix sizes and the precision
needed to resolve a small optimum still grow with \(N\).

These are general finite-level reductions for the prescribed source,
including its fixed short fillings. They prove no additional volume
case. The outstanding task is to construct geometric trials with the
stated relative error, or equivalent positive certificates at the
hyperbolic-volume rate, for every required partial filling. The
finite-exception theorem remains unproved and the manuscripts stay
frozen.

## A growing sample family now has both exact orthogonalities, 21 November

The [reflection-symmetric frame theorem](research_reflection_symmetric_geometric_frame.md)
combines the local growth estimates with the original gluing pairings.
Use the shorter angle weight
\[
 w(x)=\min(x,1-x),\qquad
 t(x,r)=-r^{w(x)}e^{-2\pi ix}.
\]
Both the actual trivalent source and the crossing kernel have strictly
positive initialized height on this path throughout their strict prism
and tetrahedron domains. The symmetry \(w(x)=w(1-x)\) treats reflected
angle labels with the same damping. Uniform source asymptotics hold on
strict shape compacts and \(r\in[r_0,1]\), for fixed \(r_0>0\).

The folded prism proof again uses angle concavity and a weighted
secant comparison. In the difficult notation of the path theorem below,
its five positive angle/exponent pairs are
\[
 (b,b),\quad(c,c),\quad(u,\delta+s),\quad
 (p,\delta+b),\quad(q,\delta+c).
\]
Their total weight is \(\delta+s\), their first moment is
\(\delta^2+s^2\), and their exponents lie outside \([\delta,s]\).
The two negative terms are precisely the endpoint terms of that
secant comparison. This proves growth for the folded rule, rather
than assuming that reflection preserves the earlier unfurled path.

For \(\xi_j=(j+1/2)/N\), form the complete sampled packets with
\[
 B_{aj}=N^{-1/2}
       [-e^{-h w(\xi_j)-2\pi i\xi_j}]^a,
       \qquad 0\le a,j<N,
\]
in the original centered basis. Let \(P\) reverse the sample index,
\(P_{ij}=\mathbf1_{i+j=N-1}\). For \(0\le h_N\le c/N\),
\(c<2\log2\), all singular values of \(B\) lie in
\([2-e^{c/2},e^{c/2}]\), independently of the level. Define
\[
 H=B^*B,\qquad S=B^{\mathsf T}B,\qquad U=BH^{-1/2}.
\]
Complementary samples are conjugate, so \(\bar B=BP\),
\(S=PH\), and \(\bar H=PHP\). The positive inverse square root
respects that symmetry, proving exactly
\[
                    U^*U=I,\qquad U^{\mathsf T}U=P.
\]
Thus \(\widehat E_j=\sum_aU_{aj}f_a\) is orthonormal for the
original positive norm and obeys
\(\phi(\widehat E_i\widehat E_j)=P_{ij}\) for the original
bilinear source. Every Casimir first-normal direction remains.

The physical turn remains its literal matrix
\(\mathsf J_U=U^*\mathsf J_fU\); it is not identified with the
sample permutation \(P\). All multiplication tensors, signed leaves,
framing factors and closing rows are transported through the same
unitary \(U\), so all original norms and budgets are unchanged.
In particular this basis can be used in the existing quartic source
minimum by a unitary change of its packet coordinates: the balls,
polynomial degree and Hessian bounds are preserved. The signed crossing
operators also retain the exact identity
\[
                 A_U^-=\mathsf J_U(A_U^+)^*\mathsf J_U.
\]
This is not a claim that either crossing is unitary.

There is a necessary limit to the conclusion. The geometric asymptotic
is proved for the raw sampled tensors \(T^E\). Their tensors in the
orthogonal basis contain the full polar matrix on every leg:
\[
 T^{\widehat E}_{ijk}
   =\sum_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}
    (H^{-1/2})_{\alpha i}(H^{-1/2})_{\beta j}
    (H^{-1/2})_{\gamma k}T^E_{\alpha\beta\gamma}.
\]
The uniform bound on \(H^{-1/2}\) does not justify keeping only the
summands in a chosen geometric neighborhood, or transfer a particular
raw entry's asymptotic to a particular orthogonal entry at an arbitrary
positive damping. Those coherent terms must remain if that frame is
used.

A separate polar-localization theorem is nevertheless unnecessary for
the present critical path: take \(h_N=0\). Then \(H=I\), \(U=V\),
and the raw boundary frame is already exactly orthogonal for both
required pairings. The full prism and crossing estimates explicitly
include these physical unit-grid points and their norm-wall collisions.
Thus we may work directly in this frame, with no polar mixing to
estimate. The remaining problem is the actual signed finite source
and its marked closing, including contributions outside a proposed
geometric neighborhood. The new frame construction does not turn
that problem into positivity or prove the finite-exception theorem.

## An actual signed crossing now has a tetrahedron kernel, 21 November

The [crossing endpoint theorem](research_centered_signed_crossing_endpoint_source.md)
contracts a signed leaf before doing any asymptotic assembly. At level
\(N\ge2\), put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\), and \(D_N(t)=1-(-1)^dt^N\).
If \(\mathcal C_N\) is the original centered multiplication tensor,
then
\[
 A_N^+(y,z)=\mathcal C_N(0,y,z),\qquad
 \mathcal K_N^+(y,z)=\sqrt N A_N^+(y,z)
\]
is the actual positive-crossing matrix kernel. This keeps its original
bilinear pairing and all \(N\) boundary coordinates.

For \(b,c>0\), \(b+c<1\), set
\(y=-r_ye^{-2\pi ib}\), \(z=-r_ze^{-2\pi ic}\). On each strict
angular compact, uniformly for \((r_y,r_z)\in[0,1]^2\), the theorem
proves the exact source formula
\[
 A_N^+(y,z)=G_N^+(y,z)
       -\frac{\kappa}{N}D_N(y)D_N(z)J_N^+(y,z),
                         \qquad |J_N^+|\le C.
\]
The nonzero \(G_N^+\) is an explicit quotient of three canonical
factorials. Its asymptotic is
\[
 G_N^+=\kappa e^{i\pi/4-\pi i/(4N)}
             (1-yz)^{-1/2}e^{iN\Psi_0(y,z)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
\]
where the branches are anchored at zero and
\[
 \Psi_0(y,z)=-\frac\pi{12}
  +\frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(-y)+\operatorname{Li}_2(-z)
                         -\operatorname{Li}_2(yz)}{2\pi}.
\]
This is the relative asymptotic of \(A_N^+\) wherever
\(-\operatorname{Im}\Psi_0\ge0\). For the physical matrix kernel
\(\mathcal K_N^+\), both the geometric term and the error must be
multiplied by \(\sqrt N\); its absolute correction is
\(O(N^{-1/2})\), rather than \(O(N^{-1})\).

The source term comes from the upper horizontal side of the exact
canonical rectangle when the first generating coordinate is zero.
It is not assigned as the value of a prospective saddle. The same
outer-pole cancellation remains exact. A modified lower-current
argument covers the full tetrahedron region, including an angle
greater than \(1/2\). Uniform complete-strip factorial bounds and
the regular final current include both zero and unit moduli.

At unit moduli, let
\[
 L(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi v)\,dv,\qquad
 T(b,c)=L(b+c)-L(b)-L(c).
\]
Then
\[
 i\Psi_0=T(b,c)-i\pi bc,\qquad
 \operatorname{Vol}(\Delta_{b,c})=\pi T(b,c),
\]
where \(\Delta_{b,c}\) has dihedral angles
\(\pi b,\pi c,\pi(1-b-c)\). The standard volume formula and its
normalization were checked against Milnor's Chapter 7 in Thurston's
notes, Theorem 7.2.1. The real Hessian of \(T\) is negative definite
with determinant exactly \(\pi^2\), so its inverse is explicit.
Writing \(\Phi=T-i\pi bc\), the actual source amplitude satisfies
\[
 \left|(1-yz)^{-1/2}\right|^2
        =\frac1{2\sin\pi(b+c)}=\frac{|\Phi_{bc}|}{2\pi}.
\]
This fixes the mixed-Hessian density of the geometric kernel. It
does not by itself imply unitarity or a bound for full boundary-vector
transport.

There is a single explicit growing path for every strict tetrahedron:
\[
              r_y=r^b,\qquad r_z=r^c,\qquad 0<r\le1.
\]
Its proof uses strict angle concavity and convexity in the logarithmic
radius of the radial Clausen function. If one angle exceeds \(1/2\),
the two unequal exponents are essential to this proof; arbitrary
independent moduli need not have nonnegative height. These paths have
not yet been made compatible on all shared edges of a whole source.

For the inverse crossing, coefficient conjugation \(\sharp\) gives
the exact identity
\[
 \mathcal K_N^-(y,z)
       =(yz)^d(\mathcal K_N^+)^\sharp(1/y,1/z).
\]
Its reciprocal chart and monomial remain. Thus the two signs cannot
be put into the same interior disk chart just by conjugating a phase.
The endpoint theorem is a source-calibrated local crossing result,
not a new knot-volume family. A compatible whole coefficient cycle,
control outside the selected geometric neighborhoods, and the original
closing lower bound remain necessary for arbitrary fixed short partial
fillings.

## One angle-weighted growing path works for both local kernels, 21 November

The [angle-weighted path theorem](research_angle_weighted_geometric_source_path.md)
gives the same local deformation for both the trivalent source and the
crossing kernel. For a leg of angle \(x_i\), use
\[
                      t_i(r)=-r^{x_i}e^{-2\pi i x_i}.
\]
On the whole strict prism region
\(x_i>0\), \(x_i+x_j<1\), \(\sum_i x_i>1\), its initialized
height \(-\operatorname{Im}\Psi\) is strictly positive for every
\(0<r\le1\). The crossing theorem already establishes the same
rule for two strict tetrahedron angles. The actual source asymptotics
therefore remain nonzero along these paths, uniformly on strict shape
compacts and \(r\in[r_0,1]\), with any fixed \(r_0>0\).

The proof uses angle concavity and convexity in logarithmic radius.
In the difficult prism case, put
\(a=1-\delta>1/2\), \(s=b+c<1/2\),
\(u=s-\delta\), \(p=\delta-b\), and \(q=\delta-c\).
After reflecting the large angle, the five positive terms have
angle weights and radius exponents
\[
 (b,b),\quad(c,c),\quad(u,1+u),\quad(p,1-p),\quad(q,1-q).
\]
Their total weight is \(\delta+s\), and their weighted first
moment is \(\delta(1-\delta)+s^2\). All five exponents lie
outside \([s,1-\delta]\). The secant line of the convex radial
function at those two endpoints therefore bounds the weighted sum
from below by the two negative terms. Strict angle concavity supplies
the positive remainder. This is a general weighted convexity argument;
no knot or filling enumeration is used.

The result supplies a common rule for local coordinates, not a common
global contour. Shared-edge reversals, reciprocal charts and the
original coefficient pairing still have to be retained. Letting the
angle vary along this rule traces a spiral rather than a closed Taylor
circle. Nor is a uniform level-dependent approach to the origin proved.

## The full spiral sampling Gram has a uniform inverse, 21 November

The [spiral sampling theorem](research_spiral_boundary_sampling_gram.md)
turns the local path rule into a controlled finite boundary frame.
Let \(\xi_j=(j+1/2)/N\),
\(t_j(h)=-e^{-(h+2\pi i)\xi_j}\), and
\[
 E_j(h)=N^{-1/2}\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}f_a t_j(h)^a,
 \qquad B(h)_{aj}=N^{-1/2}t_j(h)^a.
\]
At zero damping, \(V=B(0)\) is unitary. With
\(A=\operatorname{diag}(a)\), \(X=\operatorname{diag}(\xi_j)\),
the exact operator series is
\[
 B(h)=\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{(-h)^k}{k!}A^kVX^k,
 \qquad \|B(h)-V\|\le e^{h(N-1)}-1.
\]
Thus for \(0\le h_N\le c/N\), \(c<\log2\), every singular
value lies between \(2-e^c>0\) and \(e^c\), uniformly in the
level. The full Hermitian Gram \(H=B^*B\) and its inverse are
controlled. If \(Nh_N\to0\), this Gram tends to the identity.
Every physical boundary direction, including the Casimir first
normals, is retained.

The original bilinear sewing uses \(S=B^{\mathsf T}B\), with
the dual matrix \(S^{-1}\), whereas \(H\) controls the positive
norm. Both matrices, all turns, signed leaves and the original
closing are transported exactly. The original normalization budgets
are unchanged when the transported positive metric is used. Actual
covariant source tensors are precisely the finite tensor evaluated
at the spiral nodes, with their recorded powers of \(N\); the local
geometric estimates therefore apply on the strict angle regions.

A diagonal correction that fixes complementary node pairs is
insufficient: the note computes its nonzero off-pair entries
explicitly. The full inverse Gram is required. Likewise, sampling
on a spiral is an exact finite basis change, not a deformation of
the original coefficient contour. Uniform conditioning does not
remove the signed phases or establish a lower bound for the final
closing. The unit grid was already orthogonal; the additional fact
is control of a whole damped geometric frame in the same thin layer
where the initialized source estimates now hold.

## The geometric tensor now reaches the unit boundary, 21 November

The [complete prism transport theorem](research_centered_tensor_full_prism_source_transport.md)
settles the radial transport problem for the original universal
three-boundary tensor. At level \(N\ge2\), put
\[
 d=N-1,\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad
 \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\qquad D_N(t)=1-(-1)^dt^N.
\]
Fractional powers of \(q\) use the displayed exponential. Write
\[
 a,b,c>0,\qquad a+b,a+c,b+c<1,\qquad a+b+c>1,
\]
and put \(x=-r_xe^{-2\pi ia}\), \(y=-r_ye^{-2\pi ib}\),
\(z=-r_ze^{-2\pi ic}\). On each compact set of these angular
shapes, uniformly for independent \(r_x,r_y,r_z\in[r_0,1]\)
with \(r_0>0\), the actual source has the exact decomposition
\[
 \mathcal C_N(x,y,z)=\mathcal G_N(x,y,z)
 -\frac{\kappa}{N}D_N(x)D_N(y)D_N(z)\mathcal I_N(x,y,z),
 \qquad |\mathcal I_N|\le C.
\]
Here \(\mathcal G_N\) is a specified nonzero quotient of the
canonical factorials, rather than a freely chosen homogeneous solution.
With the initialized action and amplitude defined in that theorem,
\[
 \mathcal G_N=
 \kappa e^{i\pi/4-\pi i/(2N)}B(x,y,z)e^{iN\Psi(x,y,z)}
                              (1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
This is also the relative asymptotic of \(\mathcal C_N\) wherever
\(-\operatorname{Im}\Psi\ge0\). The common-radial family
\(r_x=r_y=r_z\) has strictly positive height throughout, by the
prism action theorem below. Hence its initialized geometric
contribution survives along the entire path up to the unit boundary,
including all level-dependent approaches to the physical norm walls.
If any \(D_N(t_i)=0\), the correction vanishes exactly.

The proof starts from the exact finite Cauchy source. In the canonical
factorial interpolation, the retained source factors cancel both
outer pole families, with their multiplicities, before estimates are
taken. A moving residue supplies \(\mathcal G_N\). The two remaining
vertical currents are controlled by a full-strip factorial estimate,
an exact half-step modulus, and an elementary argument inequality.
All singular norm factors disappear from the final integral. Dominated
convergence therefore includes the unit boundary without moving an
uncanceled pole through a sampling point. This removes the local
boundary-layer problem on strict angular compact sets; it does not
control angular degenerations or moduli tending to zero.

This result concerns one universal tensor. It neither contracts an
arbitrary short-filled tangle nor proves that its final marked closing
retains the same rate. The remaining task is the geometric lower bound
for the assembled source after every fixed short partial filling.
The finite-exception theorem remains open.

The factors \(D_N\) do not remove this last task algebraically.
In the original positive-power coefficient quotient,
\(D_N(t)\equiv1\pmod{t^N}\), whereas at the physical sampling
points \(D_N(t)=0\). These are different operations. Exact
\(N\)-point quadrature on each edge is valid for the finite incident
tensors, whose product has edge degree at most \(2N-2\); it returns
the full Newton network, with its signed phases. Applying that same
quadrature to an untruncated analytic or logarithmic section can
alias higher coefficients. Nor does its canonical geometric block
automatically qualify as a Taylor replacement of the full tensor.
Consequently the current cannot be discarded from the assembled
source merely because its displayed norm factors vanish on a grid.

## The source action has the ordered prism volume and a growing path, 21 November

The [prism boundary and radial theorem](research_centered_tensor_prism_radial_bridge.md)
connects the new source potential to the existing ideal-prism geometry.
Let
\[
 x_i>0,\qquad x_i+x_j<1\ (i\ne j),\qquad
 S=x_1+x_2+x_3>1,
\]
and put \(t_i(r)=-r e^{-2\pi i x_i}\). If \(\tau(\mathbf x)\)
is the symmetric Newton action, then
\[
 i\Psi(\mathbf t(1))=\tau(\mathbf x)+i\pi(1-S),\qquad
 \pi\tau(\mathbf x)=\operatorname{Vol}(\operatorname{Prism}_{\mathbf x}).
\]
The directed prism has input labels \(x_1,x_2\) and output
\(1-x_3\), as required by the original Frobenius pairing.
For \(R_i=\exp(2\pi t_i\partial_{t_i}\Psi)\), its actual ordered
quadrilateral metrics are
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{in},1}=-R_1^{-1},\qquad
 \kappa_{\mathrm{in},2}=-R_2^{-1},\qquad
 \kappa_{\mathrm{out}}=-R_3.
\]
All are positive on this boundary. This gives the local volume
and marked face-metric comparison; it is not an identification
of the knot's full peripheral period.

For the entire strict prism domain, the theorem also proves
\[
             \operatorname{Im}\Psi(\mathbf t(r))<0
                                      \quad(0<r\le1).
\]
Its proof uses strict concavity in the angle and convexity in the
logarithmic radius of the radial Clausen function. A two-coordinate
majorization inequality handles the possible angle greater than
\(1/2\); this is a uniform shape argument, not a knot-by-knot
calculation. Each radial path starts in the initialized complex
growing domain established below and reaches the geometric unit
boundary without crossing the zero-height set.

The unit boundary itself has an exact source initializer. For
\(d=N-1\), set
\[
 x_{j,N}=(j+1/2)/N,\quad
 t_{j,N}=-e^{-2\pi i x_{j,N}},\quad
 \gamma_{j,N}=e^{-\pi i d(j-d/2)/N}.
\]
The centered Fourier identity is
\(\sum_a f_a t_{j,N}^a=\sqrt N\,\gamma_{j,N}e_j\).
Thus the full polynomial at three such grid arguments is exactly
\(N^{3/2}\prod_i\gamma_{j_i,N}\) times the original positive
Newton tensor \(\phi(e_{j_1}e_{j_2}e_{j_3})\). Its sharp
sine-factorial asymptotic, with both parity normalizations fixed
at the middle index, yields uniformly on strict compact shape sets
\[
 \mathcal C_N(\mathbf t_{\mathbf j,N})
   =L_Ne^{i\pi/4}B(\mathbf t_{\mathbf j,N})
      e^{iN\Psi(\mathbf t_{\mathbf j,N})}(1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
The note records the exact phase discrepancy before absorbing its
\(1+O(N^{-1})\) factor. Here \(D_N(t_{j,N})=0\). The full
polynomial is evaluated, and there is no factor \(\prod_iD_N\)
in this boundary formula. Substituting these arguments into the
interior formula with that factor would be invalid.

The same geometric source packet is therefore initialized near the
origin and, independently, on the physical unit grid. The complete
prism transport theorem above now connects these along every strict
common-radial path, including the level-dependent unit-boundary layer.
The assembled marked Conway coefficient still needs its geometric
lower bound. No additional knot-volume family or finite-exception
theorem is claimed by these local results.

## The exact finite Cauchy source and its wall values, 21 November

The [wall and finite Cauchy theorem](research_centered_tensor_wall_cauchy_source.md)
proves an exact consequence of the forced Ward equation.
Write \((a;Q)_j=\prod_{h=0}^{j-1}(1-aQ^h)\), with empty product
one, and \(x_j=-qQ^j\). The last forced step on this wall gives
\[
 \mathcal C_N(-q,y,z)=\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt N}
           \frac{D_N(y)D_N(z)}{(1+qy)(1+qz)}.
\]
All the other wall steps are homogeneous and give the residues
\[
 \mathcal C_N(x_j,y,z)=\mathcal C_N(-q,y,z)
       \frac{(Q;Q)_j(Qyz;Q)_j}
            {(-q^3y;Q)_j(-q^3z;Q)_j}.
\]
Proper rational partial fractions in \(x\) consequently give
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal C}_N(x,y,z)=
 \frac{\kappa}{N^{3/2}(1+qy)(1+qz)}
 \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}
   \frac{(Q;Q)_j(Qyz;Q)_j}
        {(-q^3y;Q)_j(-q^3z;Q)_j}
   \frac1{1+q^{-1}Q^{-j}x}.
\]
This identity holds on the open unit polydisk with all original
norm factors retained in the definition of
\(\widehat{\mathcal C}_N\). Its poles are the actual norm wall;
there is no auxiliary root derivative or unknown initializer.
The \(1/N\) in partial fractions follows from
\(D_N'(x_j)=-N/x_j\). At the origin it recovers the finite
factorial initializer below. Root and both independent agents
checked the whole derivation against the complete matching Ward
and full-section texts.

This removes a misleading analytic shortcut. Off the boundary
coefficient quotient, the cyclic norm defect is nonzero for
\(x\ne0\) in the polydisk. An exact single-valued homogeneous
solution on a q-orbit-invariant open set there must be zero.
The actual source is selected by its forced cycle, not by choosing
an arbitrary exact homogeneous function. Directly iterating that
cycle divides by \(x^ND_N(y)D_N(z)\); an absolute estimate loses
the compensating cancellation. The displayed Cauchy representation
avoids that explicit small denominator. By itself it gives no sharp
estimate of the canceling sum; the canonical contour argument above
now supplies that estimate on the strict prism tube.

At each of the \(N\) prescribed wall arguments \(x_j\), the exact
source value is nonzero for every level and all \(y,z\) in the open
unit disk. This assertion concerns those discrete wall points, not
the entire unit circle. The same note proves a uniform geometric
asymptotic when \((j+1/2)/N\) remains away from the endpoints.

## An initialized affine connection for the whole gluing tensor, 21 November

The [forced Rogers connection](research_centered_tensor_forced_rogers_connection.md)
gives exact source equations, including the endpoint term which a
homogeneous product would miss. Put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(Q=q^2\), \(\kappa=q^{(N-1)^2/2}\),
\(D_N(t)=1-(-1)^{N-1}t^N\), and
\(\beta_N=(-1)^{N+1}\kappa^3N^{-3/2}\). For the original tensor,
write \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_N=\mathcal C_N/\prod_iD_N(t_i)\).
One of its three permuted exact equations is
\[
 (1-Qxy)(1-Qxz)\widehat{\mathcal C}_N(Qx,y,z)
 -(1+qx)(1+qxyz)\widehat{\mathcal C}_N(x,y,z)
                       =\beta_N\frac{x}{1+qx}.
\]
The proof is a finite telescoper followed by the prescribed root
derivative. Its nonzero right side comes from the terminal summand.
Derivatives of the moving auxiliary argument vanish because the
undifferentiated finite sum is identically zero at the root. The
polynomial equation retains the full product of the \(D_N\).

In \(\mathscr R_N=\mathbb C[x,y,z]/(x^N,y^N,z^N)\), an explicit
finite cyclic-dilogarithm unit \(H_N\), with constant one, solves
the homogeneous equations. Dividing by this known unit leaves three
compatible additive shift equations. The note constructs their
unique zero-constant potential \(A_N\) by diagonal finite Fourier
inversion. Its inverse norm is at most
\(1/(2\sin(\pi/N))\le N/4\) in the stated coefficient norm.
The full initialized tensor is exactly
\[
 \mathcal C_N=a_NH_N+\beta_NH_NA_N
                 \quad\text{in }\mathscr R_N,
 \qquad
 a_N=-\frac{\beta_N}{q}
          \sum_{r=0}^{N-1}\prod_{h=1}^{r}(1-Q^h).
\]
The initializer is derived from the terminal degree-\(N\)
coefficient of the original polynomial equation. It is a known
universal finite sum, rather than an unknown knot invariant. Before
this terminal condition is imposed, the compatible affine system
has one free constant. The cyclic norm defect is also explicit:
it is a multiple of \(x^ND_N(y)D_N(z)\), not an omitted zero
off the boundary quotient.

This representation retains all \(N^3\) original tensor entries.
After the prescribed finite-index reversals, it can replace every
vertex in the original positive-power coefficient formula exactly.
The stable ideal is killed by that coefficient; no peripheral factor
or physical Casimir normal is discarded. Multiplication by
\(H_N^{\pm1}\) can have exponential condition number. Thus the
polynomial Fourier bound and the small factor \(\beta_N\) do not
make the forced contribution negligible in an assembled knot source.

## The initialized complex saddle and its surviving endpoint, 21 November

The [complex connection theorem](research_centered_tensor_complex_source_connection.md)
extends the actual source estimate beyond real evaluations. For each
compact real cube inside \((-1,1)^3\), there is a fixed complex
neighborhood on which
\[
 \frac{\mathcal C_N}{L_N\Delta_N}
  =e^{i\pi/4}B\,e^{iN\Psi}
       +N^{-3/2}A_0
       +O\!\left(N^{-1}e^{-N\operatorname{Im}\Psi}+N^{-5/2}\right).
\]
Here \(\Psi\) and \(B\) are the explicit dilogarithmic action and
amplitude of the real-source theorem,
\(A_0=\prod_i(1+t_i)^{-1}\),
\(\Delta_N=\prod_iD_N(t_i)\), and
\(L_N=(-1)^N\kappa^3e^{-3\pi i/(4N)}\).
Every original scalar and required first normal is retained.

The proof uses analytic interpolation on a complex angular strip.
For nonstationary Fourier charges it constructs fixed-endpoint
contours with real phase. For the two stationary charges a global
analytic Morse coordinate separates the critical rays from the
endpoint rays; the connecting contours are exponentially small.
All endpoint coefficients are summed with their actual source
weights. Their sum is \(2\pi\), giving the nonzero coefficient
\(+1\) of the second term above. The endpoint action is constant,
since \(\Phi(t,2)=0\) exactly.

Consequently the initialized saddle has a nonzero coefficient
uniformly on the part of this neighborhood with
\(\operatorname{Im}\Psi\le0\). At fixed
\(\operatorname{Im}\Psi\ge\epsilon>0\), the endpoint term instead
dominates. Both sides occur arbitrarily close to every real point.
A single relative saddle formula on a whole complex neighborhood
would therefore be false. The shrinking region where the two
contributions compete is not declared zero-free.

This is an actual noncancellation result for the universal vertex
on a proved complex parameter domain. The required domain and
coefficient contour for arbitrary short-filled geometric components
have not been supplied, and gluing the vertices still needs its
geometric lower bound. No knot-volume class is added here.

## Reciprocal real charts distinguish the two source mechanisms, 21 November

The [reciprocal-chart theorem](research_centered_tensor_reciprocal_real_charts.md)
keeps an exact full-algebra identity,
\(t^{N-1}G_N(1/t)=R^{-2}G_N^\sharp(t)\), where \(\sharp\)
conjugates coefficients. Moving \(m\) legs outside the unit disk
therefore changes the spectral crossing power from \(3\) to
\(k=3-2m\) and contributes the original monomial
\(\prod_{\rm exterior}t_i^{N-1}\). These are retained exactly.

If the real inside/exterior choices are mixed, \(k=\pm1\).
After writing exterior variables as \(t_i=1/s_i\), every nonzero
Fourier charge is nonstationary on a fixed real compact
\(s\)-cube. The zero charge is killed exactly by the original
source derivative. The entire normalized chart therefore has
the endpoint asymptotic
\[
 F_{\varepsilon,N}(\mathbf s)=
 \kappa^{-k}e^{3k\pi i/(4N)}
 \prod_iD_N(s_i)\,N^{-3/2}\prod_i(1+s_i)^{-1}
                    (1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
It is nonzero for all sufficiently large levels. The same-side
charts retain the initialized oscillatory packet and its conjugate.
This covers real evaluations away from \(t_i=\pm1\), after the
displayed exterior monomials are restored.

For the classical cleared critical trace, set
\(x_i=(1-t_i)/(1+t_i)\) and \(E_2=\sum_{i<j}x_ix_j\).
Then \(z_*=2-4/(1+E_2)<-2\) precisely when
\(-1<E_2<0\); a real such point requires mixed inside/exterior
choices. Thus real negative trace algebraicity does not by itself
place the source on its oscillatory saddle. Reciprocal-pair
divisors \(t_it_j=1\) can also create spurious roots when
the critical equation is cleared. The original source remains
regular through those divisors. The note's tangent-circle triangle
interpretation is auxiliary and makes no marked global-gluing claim.

## A quartic minimum on the internal Conway edges, 21 November

The [internal-edge reduction](research_conway_binary_skeleton_quartic.md)
removes the linear corridors while preserving degree four. For a
literal construction with \(p\ge1\) binary products, only
\(p-1\) full boundary packets need remain free: one on each
connection between binary products. There are \(2N(p-1)\) real
coordinates. The reduced polynomial \(\widetilde F_N\) has
\[
 I\le D^2\widetilde F_N\le3I
\]
on the retained packet balls. Its half-gradient step stays strictly
inside those balls and contracts by \(1/2\). With
\(\widetilde e_N=\min\widetilde F_N\), the original source obeys
\[
 B_{\rm tot}^2\widetilde e_N\le |K_N|^2
       \le\frac{197}{196}B_{\rm tot}^2\widetilde e_N.
\]
The same original normalization product is retained. All statements
include exact source zeros and both level parities.

The proof first retains both inputs at every product. Every omitted
variable then occurs linearly with a constant coefficient matrix,
while the forcing is quadratic in the retained inputs. Exact
orthogonal elimination therefore leaves a quartic polynomial on
\(2p\) packets, with exactly the original minimum. Its coefficients
can be assembled from explicit corridor least-squares formulas and
one scalar root response, with no trial-dependent linear solve.
In the actual Conway compiler each turn is a normalized isometry,
so every corridor metric is a known positive scalar times the
identity. These formulas require no matrix inversion.

Of the \(2p\) inputs, \(p+1\) are known transports of prescribed
leaves through turns alone. Fixing those inputs at their known values
sets their corridor residuals to zero and leaves the \(p-1\)
internal connections. This restriction can change the auxiliary
minimum: if \(e_N\) is the original minimum, the proof gives
\[
 e_N\le\widetilde e_N\le|K_N/B_{\rm tot}|^2.
\]
That inequality, together with the original source comparison,
proves the unchanged sandwich above. No unknown binary-subtree
packet or invariant value is inserted as boundary data.

Every free packet still has all \(N\) physical coefficients,
including repeated-root normals. The reduction removes auxiliary
linear transport, rather than replacing the quantum boundary by
scalar shape variables. Neither the geometric exponential rate nor
a new knot-volume class has been established. Exactness of a
degree-four semidefinite relaxation for this reduced objective is
not inferred from its convexity.

## Only genuine branching products need nonlinear variables, 21 November

The [branching reduction](research_conway_branching_quartic_source.md)
simplifies the \(p-1\)-packet quartic further. After the original
leaf transports are prescribed, a product with one internal input
is a known linear map, and a product with no internal input is a
known constant forcing. Let \(q_{\rm br}\) count products with two
internal inputs, and let \(u\) count those with one. The tree gives
\[
                         p-1=u+2q_{\rm br}.
\]
Retain both input packets at each of the \(q_{\rm br}\) products.
Every omitted variable then enters the residuals linearly, with a
constant coefficient matrix. After the fixed corridor metrics are
included, the objective has the exact form
\[
 \widetilde F(w,z)=\|Az+b(w)\|^2,
 \qquad
 F_{\rm br}(w)=b(w)^*
       [I-A(A^*A)^{-1}A^*]b(w).
\]
The vector \(b\) has degree at most two, and \(A\) is independent
of the trial field. The omitted balls are inactive by the original
inward contraction; their unconstrained quadratic minimum is therefore
the exact partial minimum of the stated problem.

Only \(2q_{\rm br}\le p-1\) full packets remain, or
\(4Nq_{\rm br}\) real coordinates. The polynomial still has degree
at most four, with Hessian between \(I\) and \(3I\), inward
half-gradient contraction by \(1/2\), and exactly the same minimum
as \(\widetilde F\). Its comparison with \(|K_N|^2\) retains the
same \(B_{\rm tot}\) and \(197/196\). If \(q_{\rm br}=0\),
no outer minimization remains. The resulting known linear response
still retains all coherent phases and needs its own asymptotic estimate.

This is exact elimination, not a further clamp of an unknown subtree
output. Multiplication by a prescribed packet can enter the new linear
responses; its constant Gram matrix need not be scalar or unitary.
Those matrices remain in the formula. There is no trial-dependent
linear solve and no new degree-four semidefinite exactness claim.

## An exact scalar response survives the internal-edge reduction, 21 November

There is a separate [scalar-response theorem](research_conway_internal_edge_scalar_response.md)
for the \(p-1\)-packet quartic before the branching elimination.
Write that actual objective as
\[
 E(u)=R(u)+|g(u)|^2,\qquad m_N=\min E.
\]
Here \(R\) is the nonnegative sum of nonroot corridor costs, and
\(g\) is the original scalar root-corridor bilinear form divided by
the positive square root of its recorded response denominator.
Neither that denominator nor the original normalization is dropped.
The forward field shows \(\min R=0\). The root form is small enough
that the scalar-forced objectives
\[
 J_\lambda(u)=R(u)+2\operatorname{Re}(\bar\lambda g(u)),
                  \qquad |\lambda|\le(1/16)^2,
\]
remain uniformly strongly convex and have unique interior minimizers
\(u(\lambda)\). Define
\[
 s_N(\lambda)=g(u(\lambda)),\qquad
 q_N(\lambda)=\min_uJ_\lambda(u)-|\lambda|^2.
\]
Then
\[
 m_N=\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb C}q_N(\lambda),\qquad
 E(u(\lambda))-q_N(\lambda)=|s_N(\lambda)-\lambda|^2.
\]
The unique maximizing scalar is the fixed point of \(s_N\).
The response acts on two real coordinates, with derivative norm
at most \(\vartheta=1/16382\) in the retained normalization.
This separates the final closing without assuming complex holomorphy
or removing any physical packet from the inner problem.

In particular, for a nonzero scalar trial in this disk, suppose
\[
 |s_N(\lambda_N)-\lambda_N|
                      \le\epsilon|\lambda_N|,
                        \qquad 0\le\epsilon<1/2.
\]
The theorem gives the original-source bounds
\[
 B_{\rm tot}^2(1-2\epsilon)|\lambda_N|^2
 \le |K_N|^2
 \le\frac{197}{196}B_{\rm tot}^2
             [\vartheta+(1+\epsilon)^2]|\lambda_N|^2.
\]
Thus a geometric family of such responses with
\(2\pi N^{-1}\log(B_{\rm tot}|\lambda_N|)\to V\)
would prove the same limit for \(K_N\). All constants are independent
of the level and the tree size. Their smallness comes from the
recorded normalization, not from a new noncancellation theorem.

This result is proved for the original clamped quartic. It does not
assume that the later branching partial minimum preserves the displayed
root-square decomposition. Fixed polynomial degree alone would not
justify this scalar dual; residual convexity and the small actual root

## The closing-response error in the original full-field problem, 21 November

There is a useful direct connection between the existing
[scalar closing response](research_conway_scalar_cap_response.md)
and [normal projection](research_conway_source_normal_gauss_newton_certificate.md).
It simplifies the lower-bound test without introducing another
variational model. Write \(E(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|cx|^2\),
\(e_* =\min E\), \(B=B_{\rm tot}\), and
\(\gamma=197/196\), so that
\(B^2e_*\le |K_N|^2\le\gamma B^2e_*\).

For \(|\lambda|\le1/16\), let \(x(\lambda)\) be the exact
internal minimizer of
\[
 \|G(x)\|^2+2\operatorname{Re}(\bar\lambda cx).
\]
It is the unique interior response proved in the scalar theorem.
Set \(s=cx(\lambda)\), \(r=G(x(\lambda))\),
\(S=-DG(x(\lambda))\), \(d=cS^{-1}\), and
\(\nu=\|d\|^2\le1/196\). Its stationary equation is
\(S^*r=c^*\lambda\), hence \(r=d^*\lambda\).
The scalar dual value and the remaining error therefore satisfy
\[
 q_{\rm cap}(\lambda)
   =(1+\nu)|\lambda|^2
        +2\operatorname{Re}\{\bar\lambda(s-\lambda)\},
 \qquad
 q_{\rm cap}(\lambda)\le e_*
       \le q_{\rm cap}(\lambda)+|s-\lambda|^2.
\]
The normal and tangential energies simplify to
\[
 \mathfrak n=\frac{|s+\nu\lambda|^2}{1+\nu},\qquad
 \mathfrak t=\frac{\nu}{1+\nu}|s-\lambda|^2
                  \le\frac{|s-\lambda|^2}{197}.
\]
Thus, after the internal response has been solved, its entire remaining
primal--dual gap is bounded by one complex fixed-point defect. This
does not discard any internal boundary direction.

In particular suppose \(\lambda\ne0\) and
\(|s-\lambda|\le\varepsilon|\lambda|\), for a fixed
\(0\le\varepsilon<1/2\). Since
\(E(x(\lambda))=\nu|\lambda|^2+|s|^2\),
\[
 B^2(1-2\varepsilon)|\lambda|^2
 \le |K_N|^2
 \le\gamma B^2\{1/196+(1+\varepsilon)^2\}|\lambda|^2.
\]
Consequently a supplied full-sequence family of such responses gives
\[
 \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|
   =\frac{2\pi}{N}\log(B_N|\lambda_N|)+O_\varepsilon(N^{-1}).
\]
To prove the volume identity by this test, one must still construct
\(\lambda_N\) at the geometric rate and prove the stated relative
response defect after every fixed short partial filling. Computing
the internal response retains the original coherent source; the
scalar reduction does not establish that estimate on its own.

This is an algebraic consequence of existing results, rather than a

## A nonzero asymptotic for the full real three-boundary source, 21 November

The [real-source theorem](research_centered_tensor_real_source_packet.md)
now estimates the entire initialized universal tensor, rather than
only locating its stationary points. Write
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(\kappa=q^{(N-1)^2/2}\), and
\(D_N(t)=1-(-1)^{N-1}t^N\). Uniformly on every fixed real cube
\([-\rho,\rho]^3\), \(\rho<1\), the original tensor satisfies
\[
 \mathcal C_N(\mathbf t)=
 (-1)^N\kappa^3e^{i\pi/4-3\pi i/(4N)}
 \prod_{\nu=1}^3D_N(t_\nu)
 \prod_{\mu<\nu}(1-t_\mu t_\nu)^{-1/2}
 e^{iN\Psi(\mathbf t)}(1+O_\rho(N^{-1})),
\]
where
\[
 \Psi(\mathbf t)=-\frac\pi{12}+\frac1{2\pi}
 \left[\sum_\nu\operatorname{Li}_2(-t_\nu)
 +\operatorname{Li}_2(-t_1t_2t_3)
 -\sum_{\mu<\nu}\operatorname{Li}_2(t_\mu t_\nu)\right].
\]
Here \(\Psi\) is real and the displayed amplitude is positive.
The actual polynomial is consequently nonzero throughout each such
cube for all sufficiently large levels, including both parities.

The nonzero coefficient is obtained from the original Frobenius
closing. Its full-circle derivative sampling removes the zero
Poisson charge exactly. The two stationary unit charges add with the
same source sign; all other charges have a summable bound that retains
their endpoint terms. The stationary trace and amplitude can then be
eliminated algebraically. Both physical values and first Casimir
normals are calibrated, and the odd simple node is included.

This is a value estimate on compact real cubes. It asserts neither
relative estimates for parameter derivatives nor a fixed complex
neighborhood. Complex endpoints can have different exponential
scales. The geometric boundary data of an arbitrary short-filled
component have not been placed in the proved real domain, and
whole-tree gluing has not been shown to preserve its nonzero
coefficient. No new knot-volume class or finite-exception theorem
follows yet.

## The universal gluing tensor is one initialized finite sum, 21 November

The [finite hypergeometric source theorem](research_centered_tensor_finite_6phi5_source.md)
reduces the whole centered multiplication tensor to one prescribed
finite sum and its root derivative. It applies to the common vertex
of every literal Conway compiler, rather than to a list of short
filling words.

Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(\eta=(-1)^d\), \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\), and
\(D_N(t)=1-\eta t^N\). For the exact tensor
\(C_{abc}=\phi(f_af_bf_c)\), let
\(\mathcal C_N(\mathbf t)=\sum C_{abc}t_1^at_2^bt_3^c\).
The proved identity is
\[
 \mathcal C_N(\mathbf t)=
 \frac{(-1)^N(q-q^{-1})\kappa^3}{2N^{5/2}}
 \prod_{\nu=1}^3\frac{D_N(t_\nu)}{1+qt_\nu}
 \left.(\xi\partial_\xi)S_N(\xi;\mathbf t)\right|_{\xi=q}.
\]
Here \(S_N\) is the explicitly defined \(N\)-term canceled
very-well-poised \({}_6\phi_5\) partial sum in the note. Its
value at \(\xi=q\) is identically zero. The displayed derivative
is essential: it is exactly the original Frobenius source after
calibrating the values and first normal derivatives of the auxiliary
generic-node interpolation. The normalization is proved again by
paired node limits and residues of the Chebyshev polynomial, including
the odd simple node. No infinite Rogers sum is substituted at the
root, and no unproved generic quantum-source identification is used.

After reversing the finite arrays as specified in the next section,
the entire original closed source has the coefficient representation
\[
 K_N=[\,\prod_e t_e^{N-1}\,]\prod_v V_v((t_e)_{e\ni v}),
\]
with its original scalar framing factors and caps retained. All powers
are nonnegative. On this coefficient cycle only, the \(D_N(t_\nu)\)
factors in a vertex can be removed: they equal one modulo the stable
ideal generated by \(t_e^N\). The resulting analytic vertex uses the
same finite sum, its prescribed normal, and the simple factors
\((1+qt_\nu)^{-1}\). This is an exact source-preserving simplification
in auxiliary generating variables, not a rule for omitting peripheral
factors or evaluating a parameter at one.

The remaining analytic task is now an asymptotic and noncancellation
estimate for this initialized expression through a general short
component, followed by the geometric volume comparison. The identity

## Full generating sections and exact independence of central units, 21 November

The [full-degree section theorem](research_full_degree_centered_generating_section.md)
supplies an analytic estimate as well as an exact algebraic section.
With \(p=q^{-2}\) and \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), the actual
degree-\(N-1\) generating polynomial satisfies
\[
 (1+q^{-1}t)^2G_N(pt;z)-(1+zt+t^2)G_N(t;z)
      =\frac{(-1)^N}{N}P_N(z)t^N.
\]
The forcing and its normalization are retained. In the complete
nonreduced Casimir algebra \(\mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[z]/P_N\),
its shift ratio has cyclic norm one. All normalized formal unit
solutions are exactly
\[
 G_N(t;z)H(t;z),\qquad
 H\in1+t^N\mathcal H_N[[t^N]].
\]
This is an explicitly trivialized local section torsor, including
the nilpotent coordinates. An anchored finite-product analytic
cochain and its norm correction are also given. The statement concerns
an internal Casimir section; it is not an identification with the
knot's peripheral A-polynomial or its regulator.

At every physical Casimir node, \(G_N\) factors into products whose
zeros lie on \(t^N=\eta\). Its actual first normal derivative is
computed by a finite cyclic primitive with a necessary central term.
This gives an explicit nonzero analytic function \(U_N\) such that,
on every fixed disk \(|t|\le\rho<1\),
\[
 \left|G_N/U_N-1\right|
  +\left|\partial_z(G_N/U_N)\right|
       \le C_\rho N^2\rho^N
\]
at all physical double nodes. Only values are required at the odd
simple node. The estimate is in these full Hermite coordinates;
it is not a uniform Newton-norm estimate. A separate exponentially
accurate germ includes any fixed compact set of off-spectrum labels
after choosing a sufficiently small generating disk. Its size is
not asserted to contain the required geometric point.

There is also an exact whole-source statement. On the compiler tree,
one can reverse finite vertex indices recursively so that each edge
contracts indices summing to \(N-1\). Forming the ordinary generating
polynomial of each resulting vertex gives the coefficient formula
above. The ideal generated by the \(t_e^N\) is stable under the
entire nonnegative-power product and is killed by that coefficient.
Consequently \(G_N\), its stated analytic sections and the central
units just described give exactly the same original assembled source.
First transform the finite arrays; reversing an untruncated section,
introducing negative powers or using sectorial logarithms invalidates
this argument. The small Taylor-circle cycle is fixed; a geometric
contour deformation still requires its own proof.

This controls the full generating section and its physical first
normals with exponential accuracy. It does not prove a geometric
asymptotic for the triple source period or a lower certificate for
arbitrary short partial fillings. The frozen volume theorem is unchanged.

## Exact signed Fourier modes and a single gluing tensor, 21 November

The [centered Fourier compiler](research_centered_fourier_conway_compiler.md)
answers a concrete version of the basis question. Put \(d=N-1\),
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and let \(e_r\) be the full normalized Newton
basis. The vectors
\[
 f_a=\frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{r=0}^d
  \exp\!\left(\frac{2\pi i}{N}(a-d/2)(r-d/2)\right)e_r
 \qquad(0\le a\le d)
\]
are orthonormal for the established positive packet metric and also
satisfy
\[
 \phi(f_af_b)=\delta_{ab},\qquad Jf_a=f_{d-a},\qquad
 R^+=\sqrt N\,f_0,\quad R^-=\sqrt N\,f_d.
\]
Thus both signed unit crossings are exact coordinate vectors at every
level parity, with their original phases already included. This is
different from truncating a flat Newton vector to a narrow window.
Every fixed short power can be retained by a finite product of these
exact signed inputs. The original two closing rows remain dense,
explicit phase vectors of dual norm one.

All multiplication is carried by one symmetric tensor
\(C_{abc}=\phi(f_af_bf_c)\), given by the explicit centered Fourier
transform of the positive Newton triple tensor. The actual Casimir
also becomes tridiagonal. With \(Q=q^2\),
\[
 zf_a=(Q^{-a-1}-1)f_{a+1}
       +2q^{-1}Q^{-a}f_a+(Q^{-a}-1)f_{a-1}.
\]
Both out-of-range terms vanish by their coefficients. Moving \(z\)
between the three tensor legs gives three-term equations for \(C\).
The associated monic polynomials satisfy the Al-Salam--Chihara
recurrence, derived directly in the note with all root endpoints
retained. The standard name was checked against
[Koornwinder, equation (5)](https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/t.h.koornwinder/art/informal/ASC.pdf);
no positive-measure theorem is imported at the unit root.

This exact preparation removes the previously tested leaf-truncation
error. It does not automatically improve a trial field: a unitary
coordinate change preserves its source-normal and tangential energies.
Nor does it turn the remaining tensor into a positive one. In fact
the note proves that no basis diagonalizing the original bilinear
Frobenius form can make the whole multiplication tensor real up to
one common phase. The obstruction already follows from
\(\phi(1)=0\): if the tensor were real up to phase, uniqueness of
the unit would make its correspondingly rephased coordinates real,
contradicting their zero sum of squares. This statement does not
apply to all Hermitian orthonormal bases; the old Newton basis has
real positive multiplication and anti-diagonal Frobenius gluing.

The next analytic object is therefore the common phase-sensitive
tensor \(C\), with its exact source rows and recurrences. A general
geometric lower estimate after short partial fillings is still
missing. No new knot-volume case or finite-exception theorem is
claimed. Norm budgets are preserved on the same algebraic tree;
expanding a short power changes that tree and requires its budgets
to be recomputed. No filling assignments are discarded.

## One complex normal gives a tangential-error source test, 21 November

The [source-normal theorem](research_conway_source_normal_gauss_newton_certificate.md)
gives a more selective test of a geometric trial field. In the original
quartic formulation write
\[
 F_N(x)=(G_N(x),cx),\qquad E_N(x)=\|F_N(x)\|^2,
 \qquad e_N=\min E_N.
\]
Here \(G_N\) lists all normalized recursion residuals, and \(c\)
is the original normalized closing row. Every packet coordinate,
including repeated-root derivatives, remains present. The complex
linearization of \(F_N\) is injective with a one-dimensional complex
orthogonal complement in this lifted residual space.

At a feasible field put \(r=G_N(x)\), \(z=cx\),
\(DG_N=-S\), and \(d=cS^{-1}\). The row \(d\) is obtained by
one backward pass through the actual tree. The exact orthogonal
normal and tangential energies are
\[
 \mathfrak n_N(x)=\frac{|z+dr|^2}{1+\|d\|^2},\qquad
 \mathfrak t_N(x)=E_N(x)-\mathfrak n_N(x)\ge0.
\]
The coherent correction \(dr\) is summed before taking its modulus.
No physical boundary channel is discarded. The proved bound is
\[
 \left[\sqrt{\mathfrak n_N}-\frac{325}{2048}\mathfrak t_N\right]_+
 \le\sqrt{e_N}\le
 \sqrt{\mathfrak n_N}+\frac{2}{49}\mathfrak t_N.
\]
The lower proof projects the exact quadratic expansion onto the
normal line, so its linear error vanishes. The upper proof uses a
feasible Gauss–Newton correction. Both constants are independent of
the quantum level and the number of vertices. Unlike a full-residual
radius, this radius vanishes at the minimizing field even when its
recursion residual is nonzero.

Together with
\(B_{\rm tot}^2e_N\le|K_N|^2\le(197/196)B_{\rm tot}^2e_N\),
this controls both sides of the original invariant. In particular,
if actual feasible fields satisfy
\(\mathfrak n_N>0\),
\(\mathfrak t_N\le a\sqrt{\mathfrak n_N}\) for a fixed
\(a<2048/325\), and
\[
 \frac{2\pi}{N}\log\bigl(B_{\rm tot}\sqrt{\mathfrak n_N}\bigr)
       \longrightarrow\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K),
\]
the volume identity follows. The remaining research task is to build
such fields after arbitrary fixed short partial fillings. No such
general construction or new filling case has been proved. The retained
budget can be exponential, so polynomial absolute errors cannot be
assumed small enough for this relative test.

## A convex reduced objective without inverse Gram matrices, 21 November

The [compressed-source theorem](research_conway_compressed_convex_source.md)
strengthens the earlier elimination result. Retain one complete packet
at each of the \(p\) binary products and determine every other packet
by the original forward recursion. Let \(\Psi(u)-u\) be the remaining
gate residuals and \(c(u)\) the original normalized closing scalar.
Then
\[
 H_N(u)=\|\Psi(u)-u\|^2+|c(u)|^2,\qquad
 \frac32 I\le D^2H_N\le\frac52 I.
\]
The unweighted objective itself is strongly convex. Its half-gradient
step stays in the packet balls and contracts by \(1/4\). No inner
normal equations or inverse boundary Gram are needed. This does not
set the Gram of exact least-squares elimination equal to the identity:
it proves additional properties of the separately defined unweighted
objective, with the original comparison
\[
 B_{\rm tot}^2\min H_N\le |K_N|^2
   \le(1+224^{-2})B_{\rm tot}^2\min H_N.
\]
At any feasible retained field there is the lower witness
\[
 B_{\rm tot}^2
   \max\left\{0,H_N(u)-\tfrac13\|\nabla H_N(u)\|^2\right\}
 \le |K_N|^2.
\]
The key estimate is a sum-of-packet-norms bound for all direct second
variations. Each binary gate has one retained and one eliminated
child, and different gates have disjoint child occurrences. Their
total second forcing is at most \(\|h\|^2/120\); propagation through
the eliminated corridors introduces no dimension or depth factor.

There are \(2Np\) real variables. The reduced polynomial is quadratic
in each packet separately but can have total degree above four.
Keeping the original auxiliary variables preserves the fixed-degree
quartic formulation. Neither representation supplies a geometric
trial family or a new volume-conjecture case.

## A global zero-free shortcut fails for an actual source, 21 November

The [finite-window Fourier calculation](research_pure_conway_fourier_constant_feature.md)
rules out a proposed universal real-stability or Lee–Yang argument.
It uses the original source of the admissible strict construction
\(C(h_1\mathcal T(h_2))\), including its signed aliases. For
\(N\ge3\) and any color window \(1\le H\le\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\),
its even Fourier polynomial is exactly
\[
 \mathscr F_{N,H}(z_1,z_2)
   =K_{N,H}(z_1+z_1^{-1},z_2+z_2^{-1}),\qquad
 K_{N,H}(u,v)=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}p_r(u)p_r(v).
\]
The real features satisfy \(p_0=N^2\), and at least one has
degree \(H\). Hence \(K_{N,H}(u,u)\) has degree \(2H\) and is
at least \(N^4\) on the real line. All its zeros are nonreal.
The quadratic equation \(z+z^{-1}=u\) then gives zeros with each
fugacity independently inside or outside the unit disk. A separate
exact argument establishes the corresponding obstruction for the
positive wire corridor; zeros are not transferred through an
asymptotic approximation.

This excludes that global zero-free proof strategy. It says nothing
about whether the zeros meet a particular geometric saddle or its
local analytic neighborhood. The literal oscillatory Gaussian factor
also fails the elementary Hermitian-symmetry test for a
positive-definite function. No new volume identity, counterexample to

## The original source as a full function and an orthogonal Fourier mode, 21 November

The [cap-current theorem](research_middle_cap_full_current_connection.md)
sums the complete family of fixed-root cap currents exactly. This
addresses a specific failure of a jet approximation: a physical cap
correction of order \(1/N\) can become order one after the actual
Euler change of coordinates. The calculation keeps that whole family.

Use \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), \(d=N-1\), the physical middle-weight
clock \(Zv_a=Q^av_a\), and the literal marked row
\(m(v_a)=x^{d-a}/N^2\), where \(x=-e^{-\pi i/N}\).
For any physical boundary vector \(w\), define
\[
 (\mathcal B_Nw)(t)=m(I-tZ)^{-1}w
      =\frac{p_w(t)}{1-t^N},\qquad
 p_w(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(mZ^jw)t^j.
\]
The map is an isomorphism onto the displayed rational-function space.
Its numerator coefficients are an explicitly normalized finite Fourier
transform, with
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}|mZ^jw|^2=N^{-3}\|w\|_{\rm physical}^2.
\]
Thus no internal cap current is discarded or reconstructed from a
short Taylor expansion.

Let \(C_N\) be the established cyclic-column matrix, and set
\(\mu_r=(mC_N)_r\ne0\). The exact transformed kernel is
\[
 \frac{(\mathcal B_NC_Ne_r)(t)}{\mu_r}
       =\frac1{(t;Q)_{r+1}},\qquad
 (t;Q)_{r+1}=\prod_{j=0}^{r}(1-tQ^j).
\]
This includes both endpoints. At \(r=N-1\) the kernel is exactly
\((1-t^N)^{-1}\); its central factor remains in the source. In
these coordinates the original clock and cyclic shift act by
\[
 \mathcal D_Zf=\frac{f(t)-f(0)}t,\qquad
 \mathcal D_Xf=Q^{-1}f(t/Q).
\]
The evaluation term in \(\mathcal D_Z\) supplies the original cyclic
endpoint. The strict Euler argument has a separate, explicitly retained
top-coefficient subtraction. Its finite Euler polynomial sends the
reciprocal-product basis to explicit Cauchy kernels. The correct Newton
Gram also has a full-function realization: the functions
\(\mu_r/(t;Q)_{r+1}\) are an orthonormal basis in its transported
Hilbert space. This norm is distinguished from the flat physical
Fourier norm above.

The distinction between the three original boundary functionals is
essential. If \(b_j=[t^j]p_w\), then exactly
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 mw&=b_0=(\mathcal B_Nw)(0),\\
 m_{\rm pkt}(w)&=N^2x^{-d}b_d,\\
 \phi_{\rm pkt}(w)&=Np_w(Q)
       =-N^2Q^{-1}\operatorname{Res}_{t=Q}\mathcal B_Nw(t).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \(m_{\rm pkt}\) and \(\phi_{\rm pkt}\) are the marked and
Frobenius packet rows, respectively. The original Conway root closing
is the residue, with the same exterior framing and peripheral factors.
It has not been replaced by the literal cap's value at zero.

The reciprocal product has a uniform nonzero dilogarithmic asymptotic
on every fixed disk \(|t|\le\rho<1\), at every index, including
both ends. Its exact ratio of the literature-normalized cyclic
dilogarithms keeps the factor \((1-t^N)^{-(r+1)/N}\).
There is an explicit norm-one cyclic cocycle behind this formula.
On \(\eta^N=1-t^N\), away from the norm divisor, it is
\(a(t,\eta)=\eta/(1-t)\):
\[
 \prod_{j=0}^{N-1}a(Q^jt,\eta)
      =\frac{\eta^N}{1-t^N}=1.
\]
This is a cocycle of the actual boundary source. The original root
lies on the excluded divisor, so the norm factor cannot be removed
before taking its residue. The parameter \(t\) remains a
source-resolvent coordinate, not the knot meridian or a filling
parameter.

The [boundary-layer theorem](research_middle_cap_moving_root_pole.md)
now controls that moving source pole itself. Write \(w=C_N\alpha\),
with the full Newton vector \(\alpha=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_d)\),
and define
\[
 t_N(\zeta)=\exp\!\left(\frac{2\pi i(1-\zeta)}N\right),
 \qquad
 \mathscr F_N(\zeta;\alpha)
       =N(\mathcal B_NC_N\alpha)(t_N(\zeta)).
\]
Fix \(0<\rho<1/2\). At every level there is the exact decomposition
\[
 \mathscr F_N(\zeta;\alpha)
   =\frac{\alpha_d}{1-e^{-2\pi i\zeta}}
       +L_N(\zeta)\alpha_\perp,\qquad
 \sup_{|\zeta|\le\rho}\|L_N(\zeta)\|\le C_\rho,
\]
where \(\alpha_\perp=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{d-1})\), and
\(L_N\) is holomorphic with uniform fixed-derivative bounds on
smaller disks. The norm is the ordinary Newton norm, equivalently
the previously fixed physical packet Gram. There is no
level-dependent condition number in this source estimate.

The proof factors both ends of the finite sine product into Gamma
ratios and leaves a smooth zero-free factor. If
\(e_{r,N}(t)=\mu_r/(t;Q)_{r+1}\), its quantitative bound is
\[
 |N e_{r,N}(t_N(\zeta))|
   \le C_\rho\min(r+1,N-r-1)^{\rho-1}\quad(r<d).
\]
The squares are summable uniformly in \(N\), which proves the
operator bound while keeping both endpoint ranges. The top term is
retained separately and exactly. Multiplying the full family by
\(1-e^{-2\pi i\zeta}\) gives a holomorphic row which equals
\(e_d^{\mathsf T}\) at zero and differs from it by
\(O_\rho(|\zeta|)\) in operator norm.

This supplies an exact version of the proposed orthogonality argument
at the original closing. Let \(P_-\) keep only the negative Fourier
frequencies on \(\zeta=\rho e^{i\theta}\), with normalized measure
\(d\theta/(2\pi)\). Then
\[
 P_-\mathscr F_N(\rho e^{i\theta};\alpha)
    =\frac{\alpha_d}{2\pi i\rho}e^{-i\theta},\qquad
 \|P_-\mathscr F_N\|_{L^2}^2
       =\frac{|\alpha_d|^2}{4\pi^2\rho^2}.
\]
Indeed subtracting \(\alpha_d/(2\pi i\zeta)\) leaves a function
holomorphic in the disk. All regular terms are removed by an actual
orthogonal projection. Multiplying by the original external framing
and normalization line once gives the same identity for the original
reduced invariant \(K_N\).

The projection is made after full assembly. A physical shift sends
\(\zeta\) to \(\zeta+1\); a term regular at the current root can
return to the root through a later crossing. It cannot be deleted
at an intermediate gate. Nor does the uniform regular-row bound
compare the projected and unprojected norms from below. The remaining
finite-exception problem is the geometric exponential estimate for
this actually projected source after arbitrary fixed short partial
fillings. The local boundary normalization and pole estimate are now
explicit; the global geometric noncancellation theorem is still open.

## Explicit orthonormal coordinates and geometric localization, 21 November

The [explicit turn calculation](research_middle_weight_turn_gram_kernel.md)
identifies the positive metric that belongs to the faithful physical
model. Write a physical packet as \(y=C_N\alpha\), where \(\alpha\)
is its full Newton coefficient vector. The matrix \(C_N\) is explicit
and triangular; it retains the repeated-root derivative channels.
If \(P\) reverses the indices, the genuine physical turn satisfies
\[
 \mathcal J_N=C_NPC_N^{-1}=H_NP,\qquad
 H_N=C_NC_N^*>0,\qquad PH_NP=H_N^{-1}.
\]
The physical packet metric is therefore \(G_N=H_N^{-1}\). In this
metric the turn is an isometry, and both original packet closing rows
have dual norm one. These are the rows reconstructed on whole Hopf
boxes. The literal two-head marked cap on arbitrary face operators
is a different functional and must be transported separately.
The off-diagonal phases of \(H_N\) are part of the
metric; it is not an entrywise-positive matrix.

The [Euler-factor theorem](research_middle_face_euler_orthonormalizer.md)
identifies the orthonormalizing operator itself with a factor already
present in the literal crossing identity. Put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(Q=q^2\), and \(F_h=\prod_{j=1}^h(1-Q^j)\), with \(F_0=1\).
In the physical basis \(v_a=|a,N-1-a\rangle\), let \(X\) be the
original cyclic face shift and \(Zv_a=Q^av_a\) the diagonal clock.
The literal argument \(n=(Q-Z^{-1})X\)
has its original missing arrow and satisfies \(n^N=0\). Define
\[
 \mathcal E_N=P_Q(n)=\sum_{h=0}^{N-1}
       \frac{(-1)^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}n^h}{F_h}.
\]
Then exactly, at every level,
\[
 G_N=\mathcal E_N^*\mathcal E_N,\qquad
 \mathcal E_N\mathcal J_N\mathcal E_N^{-1}=P,
 \qquad
 \mathcal E_N\mathcal H_{\rm face}\mathcal E_N^{-1}=Z.
\]
Here \(\mathcal H_{\rm face}=Z(1-n)\) is the actual fifth face
clock, distinct from the positive matrix \(H_N\). The formula uses
finite Euler polynomials, not a specialization of separate infinite
products. It keeps every endpoint and every repeated-root Casimir
direction. Thus the same prescribed face factor supplies Euclidean
boundary coordinates, reversal for the turn and a diagonal face clock.
The literal five-point marked cap becomes an explicit factorial row
in these coordinates; it is not replaced by a packet coordinate row.
Its amplitude, phase and endpoint recurrence are retained in the note.

This makes the relation to the fixed-degree minimum precise. Transport
every gate, every packet ball and the original closing by \(C_N\),
using \(G_N\) on physical packets. The gate norms, normalizing
budgets and quartic objective agree exactly with their Newton versions.
Their minimum is unchanged. A flat physical norm or a diagonal
replacement for \(G_N\) would instead change the problem.
Equivalently use \(\mathcal E_N\) throughout: since
\(\mathcal E_NC_N=D_\nu\), where
\((D_\nu)_{aa}=(-1)^aQ^{a(a+1)/2}\), this is only a unitary
rephasing of all Newton gates and boundary data. No
unknown invariant enters the construction of the metric or the frame.

The [localization theorem](research_middle_weight_gram_geometric_localization.md)
then gives an actual geometric estimate for this metric. Put
\(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and
\[
 s_r=\prod_{j=1}^r2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad s_0=1,
 \qquad
 (H_N)_{aa}=\sum_{r=a}^{d}
                  \left(\frac{s_r}{s_as_{r-a}}\right)^2.
\]
Uniformly for \(a/N\) in a compact subinterval of \((0,1)\),
\[
 \log(H_N)_{aa}=Nh(a/N)+O(\log N),\qquad
 h(\xi)=\frac2\pi\left[
  \Lambda(\pi\xi)+2\Lambda\!\left(\frac{\pi(1-\xi)}2\right)
 \right],
\]
where \(\Lambda(\theta)=-\int_0^\theta\log(2\sin u)\,du\).
The bracket is the volume of the ideal tetrahedron with angles
\(\pi\xi,\pi(1-\xi)/2,\pi(1-\xi)/2\), by
[Milnor's volume formula, Theorem 7.2.1 in Thurston's notes](https://library.slmath.org/nonmsri/gt3m/PDF/Thurston-gt3m.pdf#page=174).
This local volume profile is already contained, after index reversal,
in the earlier Newton covariance calculation. It is not a new volume
identity for a knot.

The additional estimate is uniform separation in the correct Gram.
Let \(R_{ab}=(H_N)_{ab}/\sqrt{(H_N)_{aa}(H_N)_{bb}}\). Fix
\(0<\delta<1/2\). For
\(a/N,b/N\in[\delta,1-\delta]\),
\[
 |R_{ab}|\le C_\delta N^{M_\delta}
   \exp\!\left[-\frac{\pi\sin(\pi\delta)}{16N}(a-b)^2\right].
\]
Thus two separated interior intervals have exponentially small
normalized overlap. Both exact endpoints also have exponentially
small overlap with every fixed compact interior interval. Their
mutual overlap is only \(|R_{0d}|=N^{-1/2}\), so the two endpoints
must be kept together when using exponential separation. The proof
uses the actual factorial coefficients, their strictly concave row
action and a Hellinger-affinity bound. The endpoint-to-interior
estimate uses the exact phases. Earlier near-diagonal Gaussian and
fixed endpoint-window estimates apply by the exact identity
\(H_N=P(T_1T_1^*)P\), where \(T_1\) is the original Newton crossing.

These estimates help separate parts of the boundary space. They do
not supply the missing lower bound for the original closing. For
example, if \(m\) is the original marked packet closing row, then
\(mC_N=e_0^{\mathsf T}\), hence \(mH_N=e_0^{\mathsf T}\).
It annihilates every interior column of \(H_N\) exactly. A unit
packet in the correct metric can therefore carry the displayed
geometric weight while its prescribed cap value is zero. No
particular knot packet is claimed to equal such a column. The point
is that a source estimate must follow the assembled packet and its
closing, not infer visibility from its local norm.

The fixed-degree formulation still gives the exact target in a
positive variational form. With its original normalization budget
\(B_N\), minimum \(e_N^*\) and the original reduced Kashaev
invariant \(K_N\) of the fixed knot \(K\),
\[
 B_N^2e_N^*\le |K_N|^2\le\frac{197}{196}B_N^2e_N^*.
\]
Consequently the required volume statement is equivalent to
\[
 \frac{2\pi}{N}\log B_N+
 \frac{\pi}{N}\log e_N^*
 \longrightarrow \operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K).
\]
What remains is a lower certificate for this minimum at that rate,
together with the matching upper estimate, after an arbitrary fixed
short partial filling. The local Gram theorem does not yet produce
that certificate or prove a new short-filling case.

A separate [classical gauge theorem](research_middle_weight_classical_gauge_torsor.md)
also makes the proposed torsor explicit. For ordered meridians
\(A,B\in\mathrm{SL}_2\) with traces \(-2\), put
\(\tau=\operatorname{tr}(BA)\). The pair is irreducible precisely
when \(\tau\ne2\). Seven fixed rational projective charts put its
product into the same companion form. The changes between frames
belong to the exact matrix centralizer of that companion matrix,
modulo scalars. Away from \(\tau^2=4\) this becomes a torus after
adjoining the eigenvalues; the nontrivial unipotent case is retained
separately. The admissible flag charts are open subsets of this frame
torsor. This is a classical representation-theoretic construction;
\(\tau\) is an internal trace, not the peripheral meridian variable.
Neither a quantum lift of this companion-frame torsor nor the surviving
coefficient of the knot period is supplied by this construction. The
Euler theorem above treats a particular preserved face clock, not the
whole companion gauge.

## A faithful physical sector removes one face correction, 21 November

The [middle-weight model](research_conway_middle_weight_face_model.md)
gives a constructive simplification of the local face presentation.
Inside the original two-head physical space take
\[
 \mathcal M_N=\operatorname{span}\{|a,N-1-a\rangle:0\le a<N\}.
\]
It is the entire eigenspace \(ZT=Q^{N-1}\), so the displayed
local \(X,Z,T\) face operators preserve it. On this whole subspace,
not just on its cup vector, the first and middle Euler arguments obey
\[
 n=c=n(I-E_{N-1}(T)),\qquad P_Q(n)=P_Q(c).
\]
The Casimir on this \(N\)-dimensional space still has minimal polynomial
\(2T_N(z/2)+2\). Thus this representation retains every repeated-root
Casimir derivative of \(H_N\); it is not a distinct-eigenvalue quotient.

One cyclic endpoint column reconstructs the complete Newton coefficients.
It gives both original closing rows and the genuine turn explicitly.
Whole Hopf boxes can therefore be multiplied, turned and closed in this
model throughout a literal Conway expression. Individual face factors
must remain full matrices until their complete Hopf box is assembled;
they are not individually replaced by polynomial packets.

The first and middle factorial interfaces also have an exact relation:
they differ by the known unit scalar \(N/\varpi_N^2\) and diagonal
\[
 (D_\nu)_{aa}=(-1)^aQ^{a(a+1)/2}.
\]
The reconstructed Frobenius closing is a fixed scalar times the
outermost matrix entry. Since \(\nu_0=\nu_{N-1}=1\), an exterior
\(D_\nu\), or conjugation of the whole middle-block word by it,
leaves that closing unchanged. Its cyclic conjugation still has an
endpoint reflection, which the note retains. Its physical-basis
unitarity does not give a uniform bound after an arbitrary Newton
coordinate change. Other strict endpoint projectors remain nonzero.

This result resolves one local correction exactly instead of asking a
volume gap to suppress it. The remaining geometric task is to transport
these source-preserving face operators and the actual turn to compatible
positive angle contours, retaining their complete relative coefficient
cycles and surviving endpoints. No such global transport or new
short-filling volume identity is proved.

The complementary [full-space overlap calculation](research_first_middle_face_overlap_contact.md)
explains why the choice of source representation matters. On the
original tensor square,
\[
 P_Q(n)P_Q(c)^{-1}=I+V,\qquad V^2=0,\quad V\ne0,
\]
and the same original averaged physical functional has
\[
 \Phi_N(V)=0,\qquad \Phi_N(X^{-1}V)=\frac{Qg_{N-1}}{Q-1}\ne0.
\]
Thus its present kernel cannot be quotiented out before arbitrary
face-unit transport. This does not contradict the middle-weight
reduction: the old all-array \(\Phi_N\) does not descend to arbitrary
middle blocks. The reduction reconstructs the correct Conway source
on whole Hopf boxes. In particular the overlap calculation is not an
obstruction to the new faithful Conway representation or a failure of
either exact whole-crossing identity.

A separate [common-cone theorem](research_signed_crossing_common_cone_obstruction.md)
rules out a universal entrywise-positive basis for arbitrary signed
packets. With all original phases retained,
\[
 R^{4N}=1+2U_N,\qquad U_N^2=0,\qquad
 \phi_N(U_N)=\frac{i(-1)^{N-1}N^2}{\sin(\pi/N)}\ne0.
\]
Any closed real cone containing the unit and invariant under both
\(R\) and \(R^{-1}\) contains \(U_N\) and \(-U_N\), and so is not
pointed. This excludes one common linear positivity compiler; it does
not exclude word-dependent frames, positive doubled matrix actions,
or the residual Gram minimization. The witnessing word lengths grow
with \(N\), so it is not a counterexample for a fixed filling.

Two attempted shortcuts were checked against the existing complete
notes and produced no additional estimate. Local geometric packets on
supplied chains do not yet provide full Newton packets with relative
closing-scale errors. Finite Newton repair computes coherent source
corrections whose leading rate still has to be estimated. Also the
root-channel \(X(p_N)\) boundary profile is already known: it amounts
to a coherent-position tilt. It does not replace the actual compensated
head--tail insertion \(L_1^n\otimes F_{\rm tail}^{\,n}\) in the framing
infinity source. No duplicate note or new kernel claim was made for
those attempts.

## Orthogonal elimination and smaller boundary problems, 21 November

Three finite-level results simplify the fixed-degree minimum while keeping
the original marked source and every boundary coordinate. None evaluates
its hyperbolic-volume rate.

The [linear-elimination theorem](research_conway_orthogonal_linear_elimination.md)
retains exactly one child packet at each binary product. If there are
\(p\) products and \(s\) proper vertices, the retained variables \(u\)
have \(2Np\) real coordinates. All other packets \(z\) enter the
stacked recursion residuals and the original closing row linearly:
\[
 E(u,z)=\|A(u)z+b(u)\|^2,\qquad
 \tfrac12I\le A(u)^*A(u)\le\tfrac32I.
\]
The unconstrained normal-equation solution lies strictly inside every
original packet ball. Thus it is the exact inner minimum, without
active-boundary cases. The remaining objective is
\[
 f(u)=\|\Pi(u)b(u)\|^2,\qquad
 \Pi=I-A(A^*A)^{-1}A^*,\qquad I\le D^2f\le3I.
\]
This is an actual orthogonal projection, including the prescribed
closing row. Its range has complex dimension \(Np+1\).

Equivalently, let \(F(u)\) list the retained gate residuals and the
original closing value after the eliminated gate equations have been
solved exactly. Then
\[
 f(u)=F(u)^*G(u)^{-1}F(u),\qquad
 G=I+DD^*,\qquad I\le G\le(226/225)I.
\]
These Gram bounds justify a constant comparison with the ordinary
norm of this particular residual vector. A direct argument gives the
sharper source comparison
\[
 B_{\rm tot}^2\min_u\|F(u)\|^2
 \le |K_N|^2
 \le (1+224^{-2})B_{\rm tot}^2\min_u\|F(u)\|^2.
\]
It includes zeros. The budgets are retained; this residual Gram is
different from the physical synthesis quotient metric, whose condition
number can grow exponentially.

The exact reduced function \(f\) is rational and strongly convex.
The explicitly propagated \(F\) is polynomial, but its degree can grow
with the expression. Keeping the original local variables preserves the
degree-four formulation. A reduced trial field also has the witness
\[
 f(u)-\tfrac12\|\nabla_u f(u)\|^2\le e_*\le f(u).
\]
Only the retained derivatives appear. This removes an inner optimization
and unnecessary trial coordinates, rather than an asymptotic estimate.

The [moment-rigidity theorem](research_conway_moment_rigidity_and_error_bounds.md)
shows that all optimal local moments through degree four are evaluation
at the unique minimizing packet field. Every optimal moment matrix
therefore has rank one. This is a statement about optimization packet
coordinates; each packet can still have all \(N\) Newton coefficients.
It does not concentrate physical colors at one index. The minimizing
field need not be the exact zero-residual forward field.

For a feasible moment family with objective gap \(\Delta\), its local
centered second moments obey
\[
 \sum_C\mathcal L_C(\|x_C-x_{*,C}\|^2)
                  \le (256/31)\Delta.
\]
All recorded moments and whole local matrices have quantitative error
bounds, with constants independent of the packet dimension. A certified
primal--dual gap can replace the unknown \(\Delta\). These are additive
bounds; an exponentially small source still requires relative precision.
Ball localizers are essential and are not discarded.

The [coarse boundary-force theorem](research_conway_coarse_boundary_force_certificate.md)
permits an arbitrary connected partition of the compiler tree, including
the closing root. Every component is replaced exactly by its shifted
boundary cost. Its boundary Hessian remains between \(45I/128\) and
\(4I\), independently of the component size and number of boundary
packets. With forces of packet norm at most \(1/3\), only cut packets
need be matched, and the same signed dual bound holds:
\[
 d_{\mathcal P}(p)\le e_*
       \le d_{\mathcal P}(p)+\|m_{\mathcal P}(p)\|^2.
\]
There is no internal mismatch term or new comparison loss. The costs
and their local minima retain their signs. A calibration using the
exact forward packets gives
\(d_{\mathcal P}=t|K_N/B_{\rm tot}|^2/(t+\|L\|^2)\) when the
root is a singleton. It illustrates why the algebraic construction
alone does not independently determine the closing coefficient.

The remaining general task is to construct full quantum boundary data
from the geometry, with a positive lower certificate and a matching
upper estimate at the hyperbolic-volume rate after an arbitrary fixed
short partial filling. The reductions above simplify the data and
error estimates needed for that task. They do not prove another
volume-conjecture case or the finite-exception theorem.
