## Arbitrary fixed short powers reduce to unit powers, 21 November

The [strict unit-leaf expansion](research_strict_conway_unit_leaf_expansion.md)
gives an exact reduction of the numerical alphabet in the partial-filling
target. Write \(h(n)=T(R^n)\), where \(T\) is the physical quarter-turn.
For \(n=\sigma k\), \(\sigma\in\{1,-1\}\), \(k\ge2\),
\[
 h(n)\simeq T\bigl(h(-\sigma)^k\bigr),\qquad
 h(0)\simeq T\bigl(h(1)h(-1)\bigr).
\]
The first identity is a stack of actual single-crossing rotations;
the second uses a Reidemeister-II cancellation. The full original
Newton packets agree, with no missing phase or dimension factor.
No arbitrary physical half-turn is erased.

Each replacement has open-output type \(A=(0,1)\), which contains
the original leaf type \(L=(0,1/2)\). An old strict feasible state
therefore extends through the new subtree while keeping every outside
variable fixed. The filled tangles, endpoint order, components, ribbon
marking and zero-framed reduced invariant are unchanged.

Expanding only already fixed leaves produces one enlarged strict
template for that partial assignment. All newly fixed physical powers
are \(+1\) or \(-1\); every original free power, disk neighborhood
and primitive surgery coordinate is unchanged. The equivalence holds
for every completion. Thus the general arbitrary-short partial-filling
theorem is equivalent to that theorem with only fixed unit physical
powers, in arbitrary positions of arbitrary strict templates. At each
new fixed leaf its retained carrier equals its unit power, and its
surgery coefficient is zero. Unit physical powers must not be confused
with unit surgery coefficients.

This is a reduction of coefficients, not of interaction complexity.
Every fixed strict core itself has such a unit-only presentation.
The number of new leaves grows with the fixed powers, so the result
does not supply finitely many universal templates or place these
fillings in the frozen all-long regime. Arbitrarily connected unit
components still require a general geometric source theorem.

## Short fillings can annihilate the old complete-color window, 21 November

The [source-window audit](research_short_fillings_require_source_rebasing.md)
checks the exact finite expansion and the explicit longness comparisons
in the frozen proof. The complete-color corridor keeps
\(j=N-1-h\ge1\), whereas the full original circle expansion at a
zero physical crossing power is
\[
 R^0=1=L_1,\qquad \beta_j^0=\delta_{j0}.
\]
Consequently one permitted zero power annihilates that entire corridor,
for every adjoining exterior and all other filling powers. This is an
identity in the full Hermite quotient, not an asymptotic estimate.
The full invariant need not vanish: the already proved strict padding
construction includes hyperbolic cores with a nonzero full source and
such a zero leaf. Their contribution is carried by the old complement.

The general short-filling theorem therefore cannot always preserve the
old complete-color corridor as its surviving geometric source. A source
adapted to the partial filling, or a full-source calculation retaining
the old complement, is necessary. This does not affect the stated
all-long theorem.

The audit also identifies why the fixed remainder bound does not
automatically control a continued geometric saddle. It has rate
\(F_0-\gamma_*\), relative to the complete value \(F_0\).
To place it below a candidate filled action \(S\), that bound alone
requires \(F_0-\Re S<\gamma_*\). The frozen proof obtains a stricter
margin from \(F_0-\Re S_{\mathbf n}=O(\sum_jn_j^{-2})\) in
its proved local germ. Its contour, finite-charge and distant-charge
estimates likewise use fixed complete-source gaps. Real Rivin
concavity or convergence of the infinite charge sum does not extend
those comparisons to an arbitrary short filling.

The new exact convex boundary formulation retains the low colors and
all other sectors, so it does not suffer the annihilation of that
chosen window. Its geometric value and relative error still require
proof. No new volume-conjecture class or finite-exception theorem is
obtained by this audit.

## Testing an actual geometric boundary candidate, 21 November

The [geometric resolvent test](research_geometric_resolvent_source_return.md)
checks a specific candidate for the missing boundary packets. Let
\(Z\) be actual Casimir multiplication in the full Newton basis,
\(P_N(X)=2T_N(X/2)+2\), and \(z<-2\). Its canonical resolvent vector
\[
 g_{N,z}(X)=\frac{1-P_N(X)/P_N(z)}{X-z}
\]
has strictly positive Newton coefficients. For \(z<-6\), its norm
is bounded by \(1/(-6-z)\). These parameters include actual complete
crossing-circle targets \(z=2-4/c^2\) with
\(0<c<1/\sqrt2\). The vector is source driven:
\((Z-z)g_{N,z}=1\). It cannot be replaced there by a homogeneous
approximate eigenvector, since \(\|Z\|\le6\).

The original marked functional obeys the exact identity
\[
 \phi_N(fg_{N,z})=s_N(z)f(z),\qquad
 s_N(z)=\frac{(-1)^NN^2}{P_N(z)}>0
\]
for canonical \(f\). Turning this positive probe gives
\(\phi_N(p_{\alpha,N}Jg_{N,z})=1/(c_\alpha-z)>0\), a bounded
pairing of zero exponential rate. The known resolvent and reproducing
identities are not new; their full earlier coverage is recorded in
the note.

The new transport test explains why this candidate has not supplied the
required geometric lower bound. For an actual positive crossing put
\[
 q_{N,z}(X)=\frac{R_N^+(X)-R_N^+(z)}{X-z}.
\]
Then \(\phi_N(q_{N,z})=0\) exactly, and
\(R_N^+g_{N,z}=R_N^+(z)g_{N,z}+q_{N,z}\). One following actual
inverse crossing makes that discarded part visible:
\[
 \phi_N(R_N^-q_{N,z})
    =\{1-R_N^+(z)R_N^-(z)\}s_N(z)
    =(-1)^{N+1}N^2 C_N(z),
\]
where \(C_N=(R_N^+R_N^--1)/P_N\) is the previously retained
polynomial carry. For fixed \(z<-6\) its returned source rate is
\(+\log|w|\), with \(w+w^{-1}=z\), \(|w|>1\), while the exact
initial source \(s_N(z)\) has rate \(-\log|w|\). The inverse word
is still exactly the identity: the large returning term cancels
the large scalar approximation.

This rules out transporting the tested candidate modulo the kernel
of the current closing row. It does not rule out positive resolvent
vectors themselves or a full boundary-force construction. The next
geometric estimate must retain the whole coherent returning component;
its invisibility to one present cap is insufficient. No new volume
lower bound or finite-exception class has been obtained from this test.

## Boundary disagreement gives a quantitative source certificate, 21 November

The [boundary-force error theorem](research_conway_boundary_force_mismatch_certificate.md)
makes the local gluing result quantitative. Keep the redistributed
local energies and give neighboring gates separate copies of their shared
full Newton packet. Add a real force paired with the parent's copy and
subtract the same pairing at the child's copy. Every force has \(2N\)
real coordinates; no physical Hermite direction is removed.

For forces \(p_v\) with \(\|p_v\|\le1/3\), let \(d_N(p)\) be the
signed sum of the independent local minima. Let \(m_N(p)\) be the
vector of differences between the two minimizing copies of each shared
packet. If \(e_N=\min E_N\), the theorem proves
\[
 d_N(p)\le e_N\le d_N(p)+\|m_N(p)\|^2.
\]
Averaging the two boundary copies gives a feasible global field. The
local gradients vanish, so their disagreement incurs only the displayed
quadratic error. Restoring the original normalization gives
\[
 B_N^2\max(0,d_N(p))\le |K_N|^2
   \le\frac{197}{196}B_N^2\{d_N(p)+\|m_N(p)\|^2\}.
\]
This is a statement about the original marked source, including all
phases. Positivity of an unrelated envelope is not used.

The local problems are uniformly well conditioned on that explicit force
domain. Their real Hessians lie between \(45I/128\) and \(4I\).
The matrix which takes differences of copied packets satisfies
\(BB^*=2I\), so the negative dual Hessian lies between
\(I/2\) and \(256I/45\), independently of the level and the number
of tangles. The maximizing force is inside this domain. The written
proof gives a projected gradient iteration with contraction
\(467/557\); no iteration has been run.

There is a directly checkable version without exact local minima.
Choose feasible trial copies \(b_v\), arbitrary forces, and let
\(F_v\) be the corresponding force-adjusted local potentials. Put
\[
 C_N=\sum_v F_v(b_v),\qquad q_v=\nabla F_v(b_v),\qquad
 m_N=Bb,\qquad
 A_N=C_N-\frac{64}{31}\sum_v\|q_v\|^2.
\]
The lower bound \(|K_N|^2\ge B_N^2\max(0,A_N)\) has explicit
degree-four local sum-of-squares certificates. A matching upper witness
is
\[
 U_N=C_N+\frac{\|q\|\|m_N\|}{\sqrt2}+\|m_N\|^2,
 \qquad |K_N|^2\le\frac{197}{196}B_N^2 U_N.
\]
Thus a geometric candidate can now be tested by local values, gradients,
and full boundary disagreements, without first solving the global
minimum.

The missing estimate remains substantive. We need such actual quantum
data with \(A_N>0\),
\[
 \log(U_N/A_N)=o(N),\qquad
 \frac\pi N\log(B_N^2 A_N)
                    \longrightarrow\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K),
\]
after every fixed short partial filling in the target. Uniform
conditioning alone does not provide this relative accuracy. In fact
the dual loss is bounded above and below by fixed multiples of the
squared distance to its maximizing force. If the normalized minimum
is exponentially small, obtaining a positive dual value requires
accuracy on its square-root scale. No geometric family satisfying
these estimates has been constructed, and the finite-exception theorem
is not concluded.

## Local convexity gives exact assembly of arbitrary short components, 21 November

The [gate and boundary gluing theorem](research_conway_gate_local_semidefinite_gluing.md)
simplifies the fixed-degree minimum further. It applies to every fixed
literal Conway compiler with the full original Newton packets and
the recorded tensor budgets, without a restriction on its fixed short
filling coefficients.

At a proper vertex let \(x_v\) be its full complex boundary packet
and \(\Phi_v\) its normalized local operation. Set
\[
 V_v=\|\Phi_v((x_w)_w)-x_v\|^2
             -\tfrac14\|x_v\|^2
             +\tfrac14\sum_{w\text{ child of }v}\|x_w\|^2.
\]
At the closing root use
\(V_\rho=|Lx_{\rm top}|^2+\|x_{\rm top}\|^2/4\).
These terms sum exactly to the original quartic energy \(E_N\).
Each is jointly \(31/128\)-strongly convex on its local product
of unit balls. Its Hessian has a local degree-two polynomial
sum-of-squares certificate. The values of the individual terms can be
negative; all their constants remain in the assembled problem.

This yields three exact simplifications.

1. **The matrices are local.** There is one degree-four moment problem
   per gate, involving at most three complete packets. Its largest
   matrix has size at most \(\binom{6N+2}{2}\), independently of the
   number of tangles. There are linearly many such blocks.
2. **Only boundary means need match.** Adjacent problems require
   \(2N\) real equalities for their shared packet. These are means
   of every full Newton/Hermite coordinate, not values at distinct
   Casimir roots. Higher auxiliary moments need not match. A local
   Jensen inequality proves exactness. The objective must use the
   redistributed \(V_v\); unmatched second moments do not permit
   cancelling its quadratic shifts inside arbitrary moment functionals.
3. **Short components have exact convex boundary descriptions.**
   For a connected proper component with cut inputs \(u_j\), output
   \(y\), and unshifted residual boundary value \(C_\Omega\),
   \[
    \widetilde C_\Omega(u,y)=C_\Omega(u,y)
           +\tfrac14\sum_j\|u_j\|^2-\tfrac14\|y\|^2
   \]
   is jointly strongly convex and has an exact finite semidefinite
   epigraph. Such components can be eliminated with no comparison
   factor. The quadratic boundary terms cancel upon actual assembly.
   The unshifted \(C_\Omega\) is still not asserted jointly convex.

There is also an explicit local dual. On each shared boundary choose
a real force vector with \(2N\) coordinates. Add its linear pairing
at the parent and subtract it at the child. If each resulting local
polynomial is bounded below by a constant \(\alpha_v\), certified
by degree-four sums of squares and the local ball constraints, then
\[
                         |K_N|^2\ge B_{\rm tot}^2\sum_v\alpha_v.
\]
The best signed total is exactly \(\min E_N\). Affine forces suffice;
there is no need to search over boundary polynomials of increasing
degree. Every prescribed force also has an exact local semidefinite
minimization. No unknown invariant is supplied as input to these
problems.

This settles a finite-level assembly issue for arbitrary connected short
components. It does not establish their geometric noncancellation.
The missing volume argument is now expressible as a concrete family of
local feasible certificates with a positive signed total at the
hyperbolic-volume rate, together with a matching upper bound. No
Casson--Rivin construction of these full-coordinate forces has yet been
proved. The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## The quartic minimum has an exact degree-four semidefinite formulation, 21 November

The [degree-four certificate theorem](research_conway_degree_four_semidefinite_certificate.md)
strengthens the normalized source minimum. Write
\[
 E_N(x)=\|G_N(x)\|^2+|Lx_{\rm top}|^2,\qquad
 g_v(x)=1-\|x_v\|^2,\qquad e_N=\min_{g_v\ge0}E_N.
\]
Every packet here is the complete original Newton packet, and the
budgets and original marked closing row are unchanged. There is an exact
polynomial identity
\[
 E_N-e_N=S_0+\sum_v g_vS_v,
\]
where \(S_0\) is a sum of squares of polynomials of degree at most
two and each \(S_v\) is a sum of squares of affine polynomials.
Consequently
\[
 e_N=\max\{\lambda:E_N-\lambda
                  \text{ has such a degree-four certificate}\}.
\]
This is one exact semidefinite program, rather than the limit of
increasing relaxation degrees. If there are \(s\) proper vertices,
the dense construction uses \(n=2Ns\) real coordinates and a largest
Gram matrix of size \(\binom{n+2}{2}\). Its matrix sizes, precision
requirements, and unknown optimum still depend on \(N\).

The proof keeps the local Hilbert--Schmidt tensor budgets. After a
coefficient reshuffling, the residual-curvature terms have a polynomial
sum-of-squares bound. This gives a degree-two matrix certificate for
\(D^2E_N-I\) on the product of balls, with constant positive
semidefinite multipliers. Integrating that identity along the segment
from the interior minimum proves the degree-four certificate. Convexity
alone would not establish this fixed degree.

The original comparison remains
\[
 B_{\rm tot}^2e_N\le |K_N|^2
           \le\frac{197}{196}B_{\rm tot}^2e_N.
\]
Thus any explicit feasible \(\lambda_N>0\) yields the rigorous
lower bound \(|K_N|^2\ge B_{\rm tot}^2\lambda_N\).
The critical remaining task is to construct such feasible certificates
at the hyperbolic-volume rate after arbitrary fixed short partial
fillings. Exact finite-level optimization does not establish that rate.

General convexity and sum-of-squares methods are established literature;
the primary coverage records of
[Helton--Nie](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4068),
[Lasserre](https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.3784), and
[Kriel--Schweighofer](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.07231) were checked.
The specific local tensor certificate and its fixed degree are proved
in the new note without importing those papers' proofs.

## Scalar response and the Gaussian normalization, 21 November

The [scalar closing theorem](research_conway_scalar_cap_response.md)
separates the last rank-one closing from the residual energy. Put
\(R_N=\|G_N\|^2\) and \(cx=Lx_{\rm top}\). Then
\[
 e_N=\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb C}
 \left[-|\lambda|^2+
    \min_{x\in\mathcal D}\{R_N(x)+2\operatorname{Re}(\bar\lambda cx)\}
 \right].
\]
For \(|\lambda|\le1/16\), the inner minimum has a unique
interior state \(x(\lambda)\). Its scalar response
\(s(\lambda)=cx(\lambda)\) contracts by at most \(1/128\),
and the maximizing scalar is its fixed point. Each response evaluation
still retains the internal quantum packets; this is not their elimination
into a known scalar formula.

Let \(a\) be the exact normalized open recursion,
\(k=ca=K_N/B_{\rm tot}\), and
\(\nu=\|c(DG_N(a))^{-1}\|^2\le1/196\). The same theorem proves
\[
 \left|e_N-\frac{|k|^2}{1+\nu}\right|
       \le\frac{|k|^3}{4096}.
\]
It also improves the explicit trial-field lower certificate to
\[
 D_{\rm cap}(x)=E_N(x)-\tfrac12\|\nabla E_N(x)\|^2
       +\frac{|c\nabla E_N(x)|^2}{1+2\|L\|^2}
       \le e_N.
\]
The extra term is nonnegative. Neither this correction nor the scalar
response estimates the original coherent value \(k\) geometrically.

The separate
[Jacobian and determinant theorem](research_conway_residual_jacobian_gaussian_determinant.md)
removes a possible loss caused by the growing number of variables.
The residual map \(G_N\) is a triangular polynomial automorphism
with real Jacobian exactly one. At the unique minimum \(x_*\),
\[
 1-2^{-22}\le
   \det_{\mathbb R}\bigl(D^2E_N(x_*)/2\bigr)
                         \le(197/196)^2.
\]
Thus its local Gaussian prefactor stays within universal constants.
The note proves the positive-integral change of variables exactly and
the large-temperature expansion at each fixed \(N\). It supplies no
simultaneous temperature/level estimate and does not determine \(e_N\).

## A rational frame removes a universal outer growth factor, 21 November

The [rational Newton frame](research_rational_newton_frame_opposite_fibre.md)
replaces a canonical representative \(f\) by
\[
                       \frac{4f(z)}{4-P_N(z)}.
\]
The multiplying function is exactly one modulo \(P_N\), so all
physical Hermite data and both original closing values are unchanged.
For every compact \(K\subset\{\operatorname{Re}z<-6\}\), its full
Newton frame satisfies
\[
 \sup_{z\in K}\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}
           \left|\frac{4e_r(z)}{4-P_N(z)}\right|
                                  \le C_KN^{-2}.
\]
This removes the common outer Chebyshev exponential from the whole
frame, rather than only from one signed crossing. The coefficients of
an actual knot packet still have to be estimated.

The price is explicit: the representatives have poles on the opposite
fibre \(P_N=4\). For \(\deg f<N\), the identity
\[
 \frac{4f}{P_N(4-P_N)}=\frac f{P_N}+\frac f{4-P_N}
\]
transfers the original physical residue period to that opposite fibre
with reversed orientation. Products and turns retain their transported
finite-algebra operations. Pointwise multiplication of the new outer
leading terms still loses an essential carry. No source contribution or
cycle has been discarded, and no general volume rate is concluded.

## Outer crossing values must be contracted with their source, 21 November

The [outer crossing estimate](research_canonical_crossing_outer_chart_carry.md)
now controls the actual canonical positive and negative crossing
polynomials on compact subsets of \(\operatorname{Re}z<-6\). Write
\(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\),
\(c_0=2\cos(\pi/N)\), and \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\). Uniformly on
each such compact set,
\[
 R_N^\epsilon(z)=
 \frac{\kappa^\epsilon q^{\epsilon d}P_N(z)}{N^2(z-c_0)}
                  (1+O(N^{-2})),\qquad \epsilon\in\{1,-1\}.
\]
Every fixed endpoint-tail order has a corresponding uniform expansion,
including fixed spectral derivatives. Both signs have the same outer
exponential rate. This does not contradict their being exact inverses
in the physical quotient algebra. Their ordinary polynomial product is
\[
 R_N^+R_N^-=1+P_N C_N,\qquad
 C_N(z)=\frac{P_N(z)}{N^4(z-c_0)^2}(1+O(N^{-2})).
\]
Thus the quotient reduction cancels two terms at the same large
exponential scale. An asymptotic calculus for short components must
retain this reduction or an equivalent exact source-period operation.
Multiplying the displayed leading functions pointwise loses it.

There is also an exact contraction before estimation. Let
\(e_j\) be the normalized Newton basis, \(Je_j=e_{d-j}\),
\(\phi_N\) the original Frobenius source, and
\(p_{\alpha,N}=\sum_j e_j(c_\alpha)e_j\) the actual recoupling
polynomial. For every full canonical packet \(f\),
\[
 \phi_N(p_{\alpha,N}f)=(Jf)(c_\alpha).
\]
In particular,
\[
 \phi_N(p_{\alpha,N}R_N^\epsilon)
 =\left[\kappa(-1)^\alpha
                     q^{\alpha(\alpha+1)}\right]^{-\epsilon},
\]
which has modulus one. The large outer value of a crossing therefore
does not describe its marked source contribution. The endpoint class
itself cannot be discarded either: \(\phi_N(p_{\alpha,N}e_d)=1\)
and \(Je_d=1\).

This is a uniform actual-operator estimate and a restriction on any
proposed continuation, rather than a new knot-by-knot volume result.
Off-spectrum continuation is one possible route. The exact contracted
formula instead evaluates the whole turned exterior at a physical
channel. Neither formula yet proves its general geometric exponential
rate or a nonzero coefficient. The required short-partial-filling
theorem, and hence the finite-exception theorem, remain open.

## The marked matching block needs only scalar Hermite data, 21 November

The [pivotal scalarization theorem](research_matching_edge_pivotal_ward_scalarization.md)
removes a separate obstacle in the actual matching-edge source. The
ordinary complementary network is contracted before any estimate of
moving projectors is taken. After the original marked first normal,
only scalar value and nilpotent data of that exterior remain.

The pivotal ordering matters. Write \(K\) for the physical diagonal
weight matrix, \(P=K\otimes K\), and
\(\operatorname{tr}_q X=\operatorname{Tr}(PX)\).
Write the ordinary exterior as \(C_t(Z)=\operatorname{tr}_q(Y_tZ)\).
For the literal
cup bend and cyclic turn \(A=B^{-1}RB\), the identity on arbitrary
matrix arrays contains an extra clock:
\[
 \operatorname{tr}_q(YA(X))
   =\operatorname{tr}_q((K^{-2}\otimes I)A(Y)X).
\]
Deleting that clock on arbitrary arrays is false. If \(X,Y\) are
actual Hopf intertwiners, however, the right partial pivotal trace of
\(A(Y)X\) is scalar. Since
\(\operatorname{Tr}K=\operatorname{Tr}K^{-1}\), the complete
trace then satisfies
\[
                    C_t(A_tX_t)
              =\operatorname{tr}_q(\widetilde Y_tX_t),
                  \qquad \widetilde Y_t=A_t(Y_t).
\]
This is an identity for the entire analytic Hopf family. It is
differentiated only after that replacement. No division by a vanishing
quantum dimension is used. In particular it does not say that the
original exterior annihilates an isolated moving-projector derivative.

Here is the resulting root formula. Put \(d=N-1\),
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(\zeta=qe^t\), and
\(\lambda_g(t)=\zeta^{2g+1}+\zeta^{-2g-1}\). For a paired
target \(g'=d-g>g\), let \(y_g(t)\) and \(y_{g'}(t)\)
be the scalar eigenvalues of the regular rotated exterior
\(\widetilde Y_t\). Their common root value is \(y_g\), and
their regular divided difference has root value
\[
 z_g=\left.
       \frac{y_g(t)-y_{g'}(t)}{\lambda_g(t)-\lambda_{g'}(t)}
                                                    \right|_{t=0}.
\]
This \(z_g\) is the actual exterior nilpotent coefficient.
Let \(R=R_N(\alpha,g)>0\) and \(H=H_{\alpha g}(0)\) be the
known scalar and divided difference of the completed recoupling block
at original folded label \(\alpha\). Put
\(a_g=2g+1\), \(\Delta_g=q^{a_g}-q^{-a_g}\).
The pair's normalized marked first normal is exactly
\[
 (-1)^N\left[
   (q^{a_g}+q^{-a_g})Ry_g
                  +\Delta_g^2(Rz_g+Hy_g)\right].
\]
For odd \(N\), the simple middle target contributes
\(R_N(\alpha,(N-1)/2)y_{(N-1)/2}(0)\). The full formula in
the note retains the original sector multiplicity, factor \(N\),
half-twist phase and physical marked normalization.

Here \(Q_g\) is the paired spectral projector and \(M_g\) its
nilpotent companion. There is no separate norm of \(Q_g'\), \(M_g'\), or a moving
projector frame in this formula. Common first moving-parameter
derivatives cancel; the genuine exterior Hermite response \(z_g\)
and scalar divided difference \(H\) remain. Primitive normal channels
have not been discarded: their literal normalized trace coefficient is
\((-1)^N\Delta_g^2\), nonzero at every paired target.

This changes the next analytic task. The uncontrolled native
projector-frame energies need not be estimated before closing the
block. What is needed is a sharp coherent scalar estimate for the
exterior data \(y_g,z_g\), with the prescribed source and geometric
branch retained, followed by control of their sum. The scalarization
does not itself prove positivity or a nonzero geometric coefficient.
The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## Exact short-block absorption and source-visible errors, 21 November

Two general estimates now address the quantum assembly after a short
partial filling. Neither changes the original filling coordinates,
mark, phases or full Newton boundary spaces.

The [connected-block boundary theorem](research_connected_conway_block_boundary_energy.md)
keeps the normalization of the convex source below. Take any connected
block \(\Omega\), clamp its cut input packets to \(u\) and its top
output to \(y\), and minimize its internal squared recursion errors.
Call this boundary energy \(C_\Omega(u,y)\), and let
\(F_\Omega(u)\) be the exact composite of its original normalized
maps. For all unit-ball inputs and outputs,
\[
 \frac{63}{64}\|y-F_\Omega(u)\|^2
 \le C_\Omega(u,y)\le\|y-F_\Omega(u)\|^2.
\]
The comparison is pointwise, before the outside boundary variables are
optimized. Its proof eliminates a unique interior minimum and computes
the output Hessian by a Schur complement:
\(63I/32\le D_y^2C_\Omega\le2I\).
The inputs are clamped in this assertion; joint input convexity is not
claimed.

Several vertex-disjoint short blocks can be absorbed together. Keep
all their cut variables, exact coherent composites and the original
normalization \(B_{\mathrm{tot}}\). If \(E_{\mathrm{comp}}\)
replaces their internal energies by the displayed squared boundary
residuals, then
\[
 \frac{63}{64}\min E_{\mathrm{comp}}
       \le\min E_N\le\min E_{\mathrm{comp}}.
\]
The factor occurs once, independently of the number of blocks,
because the nonnegative local energies add. This removes an internal
metric loss as a separate exponential obstacle. It does not estimate
the exact composite \(F_\Omega\) on geometric boundary data.

The [source-visible error theorem](research_conway_source_visible_residual_transport.md)
also weakens the earlier full-norm certificate. At a feasible normalized
trial field \(x\), write
\[
 r=G(x),\qquad A=D\Phi(x),\qquad z=Lx_{v_0}.
\]
Here \(\Phi\) is the full upward recursion and \(L\) is the
original normalized closing row. Let \(c\) be \(L\) on the top
block and zero elsewhere. The row
\[
 d=c(I-A)^{-1}
\]
is computable by one backward tree recursion. The inverse is a finite
sum since \(A\) is strictly triangular. Its correction
\[
                   \widehat k=z+dr=z+\sum_v d_vr_v
\]
retains the complex sum before taking absolute values. The actual
source obeys
\[
 \left|\frac{K_N}{B_{\mathrm{tot}}}-\widehat k\right|
                                    \le\frac{\|r\|^2}{343}.
\]
There is also a sharper radius obtained from local forward error
majorants and the actual rows \(d_v\).

The proof keeps the nonlinear remainder exactly. If \(e=a-x\)
is the unknown difference from the true field, then
\[
 (I-A)e=r+Q(e),\qquad
 Q_v(e)=\Phi_v(e_L,e_R)
\]
at products, with \(Q_v=0\) at leaves and turns. Thus the first
error seen by the source is the coherent scalar \(dr\). Only the
remaining quadratic term is estimated in a norm. An invisible
first-order error is not deleted without paying that remainder.
Where one sibling subtree is exact, its contribution to \(Q_v\)
is zero, so chains of exact short attachments transport the remaining
error linearly.

A direct source lower bound is now
\[
 |K_N|\ge B_{\mathrm{tot}}
          \left(|\widehat k|-\|r\|^2/343\right)_+.
\]
For example, if \(|\widehat k_N|=\exp(-\alpha N+o(N))\),
a residual bound
\(\|r_N\|\le\exp(-(\alpha/2+\varepsilon)N+o(N))\)
with \(\varepsilon>0\) makes the quadratic remainder strictly
smaller. The corrected closing itself must still have a proved
nonzero leading coefficient and the hyperbolic-volume rate.

The same note proves an exact repair mechanism. Solve
\((I-A)\delta=r\) and replace \(x\) by \(x+\delta\).
This stays feasible, has closing \(\widehat k\), and satisfies
\[
               \|G(x+\delta)\|\le\frac2{49}\|G(x)\|^2.
\]
On a bilinear tree with \(n\) leaves, at most
\(1+\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor\) such repairs recover the exact field;
the sharper count is its Strahler rank. This is a finite evaluation
and error-control statement, not a volume theorem. Its asymptotic
use still requires control of the coherent corrected closings.

The general techniques are established: see the publisher's account of
[Becker--Rannacher's dual-weighted residual method](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0962492901000010)
and the authors' paper on
[Newton iteration and derivation-tree analysis](https://archive.model.in.tum.de/um/bibdb/esparza/tcs-bergstra.pdf).
This was a coverage check, not an imported proof. The notes prove the
actual complex Conway identities and constants directly.

The remaining task is to construct the full geometric boundary field
and prove its corrected closing and error estimates after the required
fixed short assignments. The two estimates above resolve neither that
geometric coefficient nor the finite-exception theorem.

## An unweighted strongly convex source energy, 21 November

The [normalized convex formulation](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md)
removes the reference coordinate, the depth weights and the
level-dependent penalties from the quartic argument below. It applies
to the original complete Conway boundary spaces and closing row.

For each local physical tensor, including leaves and the root, choose
the explicit budget
\[
 b_v=16\max(1,\|T_v\|_{\mathrm{HS}}),\qquad
 B_{\mathrm{tot}}=\prod_v b_v.
\]
Normalize a proper boundary packet by the product of the budgets in its
subtree. The normalized local maps \(\Phi_v\), prescribed leaf
vectors, and closing row \(L=\ell_N/b_{\mathrm{root}}\) all have
norm at most \(1/16\). The true normalized field \(a\) obeys
the exact recursion and \(K_N=B_{\mathrm{tot}}La_{v_0}\).
Here \(v_0\) is the child of the closing root.

For trial fields \(x_v\) in the unit balls, put
\[
 G(x)=(\Phi_v((x_c)_c)-x_v)_v,\qquad
 E_N(x)=|Lx_{v_0}|^2+\|G(x)\|^2.
\]
The variable \(x_v\) retains all \(N\) complex Newton coordinates,
including repeated-root derivatives. This is an unweighted degree-four
real polynomial on \(2N(m-1)\) real variables. No unknown closed
invariant is used in its coefficients.

There are two useful uniform estimates:
\[
 I\le D^2E_N(x)\le3I,\qquad
 \left|\frac{K_N}{B_{\mathrm{tot}}}-Lx_{v_0}\right|
                                      \le\frac1{14}\|G(x)\|.
\]
Both hold throughout the product of unit balls. The proof writes
\(DG=-I+A\). Each child enters just one parent, each parent has
at most two children, and all normalized derivative blocks have norm
at most \(1/16\). Hence \(\|A\|\le1/8\). The bilinear
residual-curvature term is small enough to give the Hessian bounds.
The second estimate follows by integrating this derivative bound and
using the original closing row.

If \(\gamma=197/196\), the resulting minimum satisfies
\[
 |K_N|^2\le Q_N:=
 \gamma B_{\mathrm{tot}}^2\min E_N
                         \le\gamma|K_N|^2.
\]
This includes zeros and requires no added constant or ordinary-color
anchor. The fixed comparison factor disappears at the volume scale.
The degree-four statement concerns the objective in its boundary
variables; it is not a bound of four on the algebraic degree of its
minimizer or minimized value.

The optimizer is obtained by a plain local iteration
\[
                  x^{(j+1)}=x^{(j)}-\tfrac12\nabla E_N(x^{(j)}).
\]
Each block uses its own residual and the adjoint contribution of its
parent, with the original closing contribution at the top. The update
maps every unit-ball field into balls of radius \(33/256\), and
contracts the Euclidean distance by a factor at most \(1/2\).
There is one fixed point, it is strictly interior, and it is the
unique global minimizer on the stated domain. No projection or
boundary multiplier is required. This is an exact finite-source flow;
no numerical iteration was run.

There is now a lower certificate from a single feasible trial field.
Define the degree-six polynomial
\[
 C_N(x)=E_N(x)-\tfrac12\|\nabla E_N(x)\|^2.
\]
Strong convexity and the interior stationary point prove
\[
 C_N(x)\le\min E_N\le E_N(x),\qquad
                       \min E_N=\max_x C_N(x).
\]
The maximum is over the same unit balls; concavity of \(C_N\) is
not asserted. In particular
\[
 B_{\mathrm{tot}}^2\max(0,C_N(x))
       \le|K_N|^2\le\gamma B_{\mathrm{tot}}^2E_N(x).
\]
Thus a geometric trial field with a controlled full quantum gradient
can supply an actual lower bound, rather than only evaluate a positive
upper envelope.

The amplitude estimate gives another immediate certificate. Write
\(z=Lx_{v_0}\) and \(r=\|G(x)\|\). Then
\[
 B_{\mathrm{tot}}(|z|-r/14)_+
       \le|K_N|\le B_{\mathrm{tot}}(|z|+r/14).
\]
For example, \(r\le7|z|\) and \(z\ne0\) give a two-sided
comparison within fixed factors \(1/2\) and \(3/2\). A full
geometric boundary field with this relative transport control and the
correct closing-amplitude rate would prove the volume identity.

This is the remaining geometric requirement, not a consequence of the
Hessian bounds. An exponentially small minimum can be uniformly
strongly convex. Scalar angle stationarity does not bound the full
Newton residual vector or full real gradient at that scale. No such
trial field is constructed here for arbitrary fixed short partial
fillings, so the finite-exception theorem remains open.

## Orthonormal bases and a positive gluing partition, 21 November

The [orthonormal partition theorem](research_orthonormal_boundary_partition.md)
gives a direct version of the proposed basis argument on an entire
source tree. It applies to arbitrary finite edge dimensions \(n_e\);
write \(D=\prod_e n_e\). At each internal boundary choose an
orthonormal basis with unitary matrix \(U_e\). Use \(U_e^*\) on
the child vector and \(U_e^{\mathsf T}\) on the parent covector,
so the original bilinear gluing is unchanged.

Let \(T_v(U)\) be the resulting local tensors. For an internal index
assignment \(k\) and output index \(o\), their product is the original
path amplitude \(A_o(k;U)\). Define
\[
 Z(U)=\sum_{o,k}|A_o(k;U)|^2
     =\sum_{o,k}\prod_v|T_v(U)_{\alpha_v(k,o)}|^2 .
\]
Here \(\alpha_v(k,o)\) lists the indices incident at vertex \(v\).
The squared magnitudes are taken after the basis change. Their
dependence on \(U\) therefore retains the original complex phases.
If the original vector output is \(Y\ne0\), the compact unitary
minimum satisfies
\[
                \frac{\|Y\|^2}{D}\le\min_U Z(U)\le\|Y\|^2.
\]
The first inequality is pathwise Cauchy--Schwarz. For the other,
choose the first vector of each boundary basis along its true proper
subtree message. Only the all-zero internal index assignment then
survives, and its output is exactly \(Y\). These messages exhibit
a competitor; they are not extra inputs to the minimization.

For the actual anchored Conway output \(Y_N=(1,K_N)\), the edge
dimensions are \(N+1\). Thus a construction with \(m\) vertices has
\[
 \frac{1+|K_N|^2}{(N+1)^{m-1}}
       \le Z_N^{\mathrm{orth}}:=\min_U Z(U)
       \le1+|K_N|^2.
\]
At fixed \(m\), its logarithmic error is at most
\((m-1)\log(N+1)\), which disappears at the volume scale.
This formulation uses only compact orthonormal frame choices, with
no metric eigenvalues or regularization penalty.

There is an exact variational formula for the positive partition in
each fixed frame. Put \(a_{v,\alpha}=|T_v(U)_\alpha|^2\), and
let \(p_v\) be probabilities on its nonzero coefficients. Require
the two probabilities at each edge to have the same marginal \(p_e\).
With \(H(p)=-\sum p\log p\), \(0\log0=0\), the formula is
\[
 \log Z(U)=
 \max_{p\ \mathrm{balanced}}
 \left\{
   \sum_v\left[H(p_v)+\sum_\alpha p_{v,\alpha}\log a_{v,\alpha}\right]
          -\sum_e H(p_e)
 \right\}.
\]
The edge subtraction is necessary: the two adjacent vertex distributions
share that index. The note proves the formula from the finite Gibbs
identity and a tree probability construction, including zero marginals.
It also gives a minimum/maximum path formulation at the same leading
scale. Neither formulation permits removing the minimization over bases.

This identifies the next estimate more sharply. A geometrically
favorable basis supplies an upper bound on the optimized partition.
The required volume lower bound must survive all allowed bases, or
come from a dual certificate. Positivity in one basis alone does not
give that bound. In particular the original Newton-frame partition
for elementary crossing leaves is unchanged by flipping their signs;
their phase interactions reappear when the bases vary. No new
hyperbolic-volume case or finite-exception conclusion is claimed.

## A quartic residual formula, 21 November

The [compact variational note](research_anchored_conway_positive_variational_period.md)
shortens the finite-source argument substantially. The original closing
row is kept throughout. Neither ordinary-color estimates nor the earlier
matrix flow is needed for its main theorem.

Fix a literal Conway expression with \(m\) vertices, including the
closing row \(\ell_N\) at the root. Each of its \(m-1\) proper
vertices has a full \(N\)-dimensional Newton boundary packet. Give
that packet a variable \(w_v\), constrained by \(\|w_v\|\le B_N\),
where \(B_N\ge1\) is an explicit product of local tensor norms.
It bounds every actual proper packet and every local operation needed
in the proof. If \(r_v\) is the depth of a proper vertex, define
its residual to be
\[
 \mathcal R_v=
 \begin{cases}
 f_v-w_v,&\text{at a prescribed leaf},\\
 Jw_c-w_v,&\text{at a quarter-turn},\\
 M(w_L,w_R)-w_v,&\text{at a multiplication}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Here \(J\) and \(M\) are the actual full Newton turn and
multiplication; repeated-root derivatives remain in their boundary
spaces. Write \(v_0\) for the child of the closing root, and set
\[
 \mathcal J_N(\boldsymbol w)
 =1+|\ell_Nw_{v_0}|^2
   +N(m-1)\sum_{v\ne\mathrm{root}}
              B_N^{4r_v-2}\|\mathcal R_v(\boldsymbol w)\|^2,
\]
\[
 Q_N=(1+1/N)\min_{\|w_v\|\le B_N}\mathcal J_N(\boldsymbol w).
\]
This is a compact minimization of a positive real polynomial, of
degree at most four on \(2N(m-1)\) real variables. The degree remains
four as the number of turns and products increases.
Its exact finite-level bound is
\[
             1+|K_N|^2\le Q_N\le(1+1/N)(1+|K_N|^2).
\]
The proof propagates each residual along its unique path to the root,
then uses weighted Cauchy--Schwarz. Inserting the true proper packets
makes every residual zero and proves the other inequality. Thus exact
contraction of a fixed proper short subtree, or a different valid
choice of \(B_N\), changes the logarithmic minimum by at most
\(\log(1+1/N)\). This is stability of the optimized value, not
pointwise equality of the two polynomial objectives.

The same note explains the orthogonality behind an alternative product
formula. Adjoin a separate constant reference to each physical boundary
space. At depth \(r\), with a positive scale \(t\), use
\[
       \|(a,u)\|_{w,t}^2=|a|^2+t^{2r}\|u-aw\|^2.
\]
The line through \((1,w)\) is orthogonal to every \((0,h)\),
while all physical directions remain. At the true proper packet this
centers the actual message. The local squared norms are explicit
positive sums, and their compact product minimum lies between
\(1+|K_N|^2\) and \(e^{2/N}(1+|K_N|^2)\). Its lower
bound also has an exact polynomial sum-of-squares certificate. These
metric and product interpretations are optional for the shorter quartic
proof.

For every \(V>0\), the quartic theorem gives
\[
 \frac\pi N\log Q_N\longrightarrow V
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{2\pi}N\log|K_N|\longrightarrow V.
\]
The new formulation is phase-sensitive: the original phases remain
inside its residuals and closing row. Positivity supplies the constant
lower bound one; it supplies no positive exponential rate. The remaining
task is to prove the hyperbolic-volume value of this minimum after the
required fixed short partial assignments. No new filling class or
finite-exception theorem follows from this reformulation alone.

## A canonical positive matrix flow for the original energy, 20 November

The [tree capacity theorem](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md)
and its [regularized construction](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md)
give a general formulation retaining the original closing functional.
For a tensor contraction whose contraction graph is a tree, including
one with a vector-valued output \(Y\),
\[
 \|Y\|=\inf_{H_e>0}\prod_v\|T_v\|_H.
\]
The two ends of each internal edge use reciprocal transpose gauges.
The infimum allows full matrices on the edge spaces. Compiling the
physical braid products into a tree can require bundled spaces; this
does not replace them by separate single-wire metrics. A leaf-peeling
proof includes zero outputs and permits singular limiting gauges.

There is a dimension-independent lower comparison for a specified
gauge. Normalize its local tensors and let \(\rho_{v,e}\) be their
full reduced density matrices. If \(m\) is the number of vertices and
\(S=\sum_e\|\rho_{v,e}-\rho_{w,e}^{\mathsf T}\|_1\), then
\[
 \frac{\|Y\|}{\prod_v\|T_v\|_H}
       \ge [1-4m\sqrt S-5mS]_+.
\]
The proof propagates linear entropy from the pure leaves and compares
the resulting product tensors. It keeps the off-diagonal entries and
the original bilinear pairing. Diagonal probability balance is not
enough.

Apply this to the actual all-main-color vector \(Y_N=(c_1,\ldots,c_N)\).
The [physical cap-projection calculation](research_main_color_cap_projection_energy.md)
retains the prescribed cut and pivots and gives
\(\|Y_N\|^2=E_N=|K_N|^2+R_N\), with polynomial \(R_N\).
Its trivial ordinary color is one. Hence \(\|Y_N\|\ge1\), including
levels where nothing is known about nonvanishing of \(K_N\).
Put
\[
 L_N(H)=\sum_v\log\|T_{v,N}\|_H,\qquad
 Z(H)=1+\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(H_e+H_e^{-1}).
\]
The objective \(L_N+\varepsilon\log Z\) is strictly geodesically
convex, has compact sublevel sets, and has a unique positive minimizer.
Its full marginal defect obeys \(S\le2\varepsilon\). Thus the choice
\(\varepsilon_N=(m^2N^2)^{-1}\) supplies the required matrix balance
by an explicit optimization using known tensors alone. At its minimizer,
write \(\widehat F_N=\exp L_N(H_N)\). Then
\[
 \left(1-\frac{4\sqrt2}{N}-\frac{10}{mN^2}\right)\widehat F_N
       \le\sqrt{E_N}\le\widehat F_N.
\]
In particular \(\log\widehat F_N=\tfrac12\log E_N+O(N^{-1})\).
The matrices are algebraic at each fixed level, with no asserted
uniform degree bound. A specified full matrix gradient flow converges
to this minimizer. This is a flow for the original finite source;
it is not yet identified with a dihedral-angle flow.

Exact contraction of any connected short subtree preserves the output.
Reapplying the construction before and after this contraction changes
the unpenalized logarithmic objective by only \(O(N^{-1})\), with
the stated uniform bound independent of block complexity. This permits
short components to be contracted before further analysis without
requiring separate bounds for their intermediate closing angles.
The [quantitative tree normal form](research_regularized_source_metric_compactness.md)
now also controls the penalty. If
\(B_N=\prod_v\max(1,\|T_{v,N}\|)\), the trivial-color anchor bounds
every proper subtree message between \(B_N^{-1}\) and \(B_N\).
Gauges sending these messages to a coordinate vector, followed by
explicit depth-dependent filters, give near-minimizers with controlled
condition numbers. The original finite crossing formulas give
\(\log B_N=O(N)\) for every fixed completed braid. Comparison with
these competitors proves
\[
 \log Z(H_N)=O(N),\qquad
 \sup_e\|N^{-1}\log H_{e,N}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(1),\qquad
 \varepsilon_N\log Z(H_N)=O(N^{-1}).
\]
Thus the entire penalized minimum, not just the unpenalized norm,
equals \(\tfrac12\log E_N+O(N^{-1})\). These bounds control spectra;
they do not give a classical description of the eigenspaces.

The remaining theorem is now a specific variational comparison:
\[
 \frac{2\pi}{N}\min_H J_{N,\varepsilon_N}(H)\longrightarrow
                       \operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K).
\]
It is equivalent to the original volume identity for a hyperbolic knot.
It has not been proved for arbitrary fixed short partial fillings.
The construction applies separately to every completed assignment
giving a one-component knot; no trivial-color anchor is asserted for
an unfilled intermediate link. The finite-branching argument will give
finite exceptions only after the geometric comparison holds on its
required partial-assignment branches. Strictly positive geometric
critical points, scalar angle balance and algebraicity of \(H_N\)
do not by themselves establish that comparison.

One restriction of the metric class is justified at the leading scale.
For a direct sum of \(r\) tree sectors, the infimum over sector-preserving
gauges is exactly \((\sum_j\|Y_j\|^{2/m})^{m/2}\). It lies between
the unrestricted capacity and \(r^{(m-1)/2}\) times that capacity.
For the actual \(N\) main colors this costs only \(O(\log N)\) in
the logarithm at fixed \(m\). It is an estimate for infima, not a claim
that pinching an arbitrary gauge improves it or that the canonical

## Orthogonality through the full Conway boundary, 20 November

The [boundary quotient metric](research_conway_full_boundary_quotient_gram.md)
now gives an exact construction for every finite expression made from
the actual Conway multiplication and quarter-turn. Let \(B_E\) assemble
arbitrary full Newton packets at the leaves into the boundary packet of
an expression \(E\). Every \(B_E\) is surjective, because the boundary
algebra has a unit and the turn is invertible. Thus
\[
 C_E=B_EB_E^*,\qquad G_E=C_E^{-1},\qquad
 P_E=B_E^*C_E^{-1}B_E
\]
are defined independently of the numerical filling assignment. Here
\(P_E\) is an orthogonal projection on the expanded leaf space, and
\[
 \|B_Ev\|_{G_E}^2=\|P_Ev\|^2
                 =\min_{B_Ec=B_Ev}\|c\|^2.
\]
It removes exactly the presentations that assemble to the zero boundary
operator. Every true boundary channel, including each repeated-root
derivative, remains. The actual multiplication matrix \(M\) and turn
\(J\) give the closed recursion
\[
 C_{EF}=M(C_E\otimes C_F)M^*,\qquad C_{\mathscr RE}=JC_EJ.
\]
Normalized multiplication is a coisometry between these expression-dependent
metrics; its projection loss is explicit. One multiplication already has
exponentially conditioned covariance, so this is not a polynomial-cost
replacement by a fixed metric.

For either original closing row \(\lambda=e_0^{\mathsf T}\) or
\(e_{N-1}^{\mathsf T}\), the squared dual cost is the explicit positive
contraction \(a_\lambda(E)=\lambda C_E\lambda^*\). If \(v\) is the
tensor of the actual leaf packets, the scalar satisfies exactly
\[
 |\lambda B_Ev|^2
 =a_\lambda(E)\,\|v\|^2\,\eta_E(v)\,
                         \gamma_{E,\lambda}(v).
\]
Here \(\eta_E\in[0,1]\) is the fraction surviving boundary synthesis,
and \(\gamma_{E,\lambda}\in[0,1]\) is its squared normalized overlap
with the prescribed closing vector. Neither factor has a general lower
bound. Orthogonal changes of coordinates leave their product unchanged.
The required geometric estimate must control their combined exponential
rate as well as the explicit positive costs. Long powers also have the
same exact cyclic span as the full nonnegative half-line, even with
Jordan blocks; their advantage must therefore be quantitative.

The [adjacent-crossing calculation](research_cap_packet_hermite_overlap_leakage.md)
rules out a smaller proposed packet system. On three physical heads,
take the normalized ordinary-cap packet space and adjoin both overlapping
two-dimensional source Hermite planes. A single original adjacent crossing
of its root-zero cap packet has at least \(1/128\) of its squared norm
outside this enlarged space, at every \(N\ge32\). A bounded second
difference detects that part and annihilates the entire enlarged space,
including its derivative directions and all Gram cross terms. The escaping
energy has rate \(Nv_3/\pi+O(\log N)\), where \(v_3\) is the regular
ideal tetrahedron volume. This concerns that particular compression; it
does not obstruct the full boundary metric above or bound a closed knot
invariant from below.

The new results settle exact metric compatibility for this full Conway
compiler and test a proposed smaller packet. They do not prove a new

## Whole-polynomial Fourier transport and the crossing-continuation gap, 19 November

The [polynomial transport and fractional-time calculation](research_polynomial_seams_and_fractional_euler_time.md)
clarifies where the proposed Fourier route still needs an estimate.
Retaining the entire physical polynomial removes a separate Fourier
adapter problem. It does not establish the required asymptotic after

For a polynomial \(P_N(z)=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}p_a z^a\), the exact
change from samples at \(rQ^j\) to samples at
\(re^{\alpha/N}Q^j\) is simply
\[
                       P_N(z)\longmapsto P_N(e^{\alpha/N}z).
\]
The coefficient multiplier and its inverse have norm at most
\(e^{|\alpha|}\). If the actual whole polynomial already has a
buffered holomorphic expansion \(e^{NS}A(1+O(N^{-1}))\), with
\(A\) a unit, then the new leading amplitude is
\(A\exp(\alpha z\partial_zS)\), again a unit. The same statement
holds for finitely many variables. On buffered scaled meridian
collars, the normalized remainder \(\epsilon_N\) satisfies
\(N^{-\ell}\partial_\mu^\ell\epsilon_N=O(N^{-1})\) for every
fixed \(\ell\), where \(M=e^\mu\). Every endpoint source adapter
remains in the exact matrix
identity. This restates an existing one-port principle for an
initialized whole function; it does not substitute the raw
four-\(\Psi\) expression for an unknown multivariable interpolant.

In particular, the long tails of an individual Dirichlet adapter
entry are not an additional error once the actual full polynomial
and its asymptotic have been retained. The unresolved step is
propagating that actual asymptotic through crossings outside the
proved small-activity domain, followed by the original closing-cycle
analysis.

The new negative result concerns the actual capped Euler factor
\(\Theta_N\) in a crossing. At \(M=1\), put \(X_N=E_1F_2\), so
\(X_N^N=0\), and define its unambiguous nilpotent logarithm by
\[
 L_N=\log\Theta_N
     =-\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}\frac{q^nX_N^n}{n(1-Q^n)}.
\]
For \(N=4k+1\), the matrix entry transferring occupations
\((3k,k)\) to \((k,3k)\) contains only the term \(n=2k\).
The literal arrow products give
\[
                 \|L_N\|\ge
                    \frac{2^{(N-1)/2}}{N-1}.
\]
This holds separately in the coefficient Euclidean metric and the
original binomial metric: the exchanged input and output have equal
binomial weights, so no exponential metric comparison is used.

For \(B_N(t)=\exp(tL_N)\), Cauchy's inequality consequently gives
\[
 \sup_{|t|=1/N}\|B_N(t)-I\|
             \ge\frac{2^{(N-1)/2}}{N(N-1)}.
\]
Thus no bound \(C N^p e^{cN|t|}\) holds uniformly on a fixed
complex time disk. An explicitly specified two-state expectation
even has a complex zero within \(16k^2\,2^{-2k}\) of time zero,
although the matrix \(B_N(t)\) is invertible at every time.
This expectation is not a geometric packet or the original knot

The coarser bound \(e^{C_{T,\eta}N}\) does hold on
\(|t|\le T,\ |N\mu|\le\eta\), including the actual meridian family.
On smaller buffered domains, a fixed true \(\mu\)-derivative of

\(C_\ell N^\ell e^{CN}\). This does not become a small-time estimate of the form
just ruled out. Small Euler activity damps the \(n\)-th transfer by
\(\lambda^n\); differentiating fractional time retains every transfer
at first order. Those two initializations therefore require different
proofs.

The obstruction is about complex fractional time and these specified
metrics. It is not a counterexample at time one, along real time, or
at a faithful geometric point. The finite-exception theorem and the
nonzero geometric coefficient remain open. The next analytic duty is
the actual large-activity crossing continuation, rather than another

## The original source now has an exact cutoff representation, 19 November

The [source-repair theorem](research_source_preserving_commutant_projection_and_window_repair.md)
removes the scalar remainder from the preceding localization argument.
It applies at every fixed width to the actual meridian family, with
constants independent of the word length and integer filling powers.
The correction is explicit and small relative to the full matrix norm.
No geometric lower bound is needed to construct it.

Here is the simplest form. Write \(\Phi_M(C)=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{\rm pt}(M)C)\)
for the original highest-cut source, including its prescribed pivot.
Let \(\mathcal L_\chi\) be the correlated coherent cutoff defined in
the next entry, and put \(\mathcal R_\chi=I-\mathcal L_\chi\).
There is a known matrix \(T_M\) which commutes with the actual total
lowering operator and satisfies \(\Phi_M(T_M)=1\). It is constructed
from the explicit two-head radical coupon, with every pivotal partial
trace retained. At \(M=1\) its operator norm is exactly \(N\), its
rank is \(N^{m-2}\), and its Hilbert--Schmidt norm is \(N^{m/2}\).
The actual meridian frame gives polynomial bounds on a buffered disk
\(|N\log M|<\pi\).

The localization estimate gives
\[
 z_N(M):=\Phi_M(\mathcal L_\chi(T_M))
                  =1+O(N^B e^{-cN}).
\]
Thus \(z_N\) is a holomorphic unit for all sufficiently large levels,
uniformly on any fixed smaller scaled disk. For an actual lowering
intertwiner \(W_N(M)\), set
\[
 W_N^\sharp
   =W_N+
       \frac{\Phi_M(\mathcal R_\chi(W_N))}{z_N(M)}T_M.
\]
Then the exact identity is
\[
                  \Phi_M(\mathcal L_\chi(W_N^\sharp))
                         =\Phi_M(W_N).
\]
The amplitude changes in one explicitly known matrix direction.
There is no division by the unknown knot invariant or by a selected
geometric coefficient. Both \(W_N^\sharp-W_N\) and
\(\mathcal L_\chi(W_N^\sharp)-W_N\) have Hilbert--Schmidt norm at
most \(C N^B e^{-cN}\|W_N\|_{\rm HS}\). All fixed true meridian
derivatives satisfy the buffered estimates with their \(N^k\) costs;
differentiating the source also differentiates its actual pivot.

Equivalently, the original source is exactly the coherent integral
with cutoff \(\chi\), amplitude \(W_N^\sharp\), and the original
coupon \(Q_{\rm pt}(M)\). This is a cutoff in the integral formula,
not a claim that the coherent kernel of the resulting matrix has
hard support in that region.

The proof also constructs a polynomially bounded, source-preserving
projection onto the lowering commutant. Composing it with the small
discarded part and summing a convergent series gives the stronger
matrix identity \(W_N=\mathcal P_M\mathcal L_\chi(V_N)\).
Neither construction assumes a commutator spectral gap or projects
onto the simultaneous raising and lowering commutant.

This settles an exact finite-source localization step. It does not
settle the finite-exception theorem. The retained region still
contains the entire real matching locus and every occupation endpoint.
The correction is controlled relative to \(\|W_N\|_{\rm HS}\), which
may be exponentially larger than the desired volume contribution.
Its geometric phase and the contribution of the original relative
cycle still need proof. In particular, the positive contraction used
in the proof acts on the space of matrices; it does not make the
original scalar integrand nonnegative.

The distinction is necessary even at finite level: an allowed cutoff
can give a nonzero discarded source on the identity matrix, although
the identity's original pointed source is zero at width at least two.
Thus norm localization alone does not descend to the one-dimensional
source quotient. The explicit correction repairs this defect, without
establishing a lower bound for a specified knot.

## An actual correlated window has a small Euclidean current, 19 November

The [Euclidean localization theorem](research_euclidean_correlated_intertwiner_localization.md)
constructs an actual marked operator with an exponentially small current.
Its error is measured against the full word norm. This supplies a
concrete localization in the correct metric, but does not yet select

Fix the width \(m\ge2\), take \(N\ge2\), and put \(d=N-1\).
The quantum root \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\) stays fixed. Use the unit vectors
\[
 \psi_z=(1+|z|^2)^{-d/2}
          \sum_{a=0}^d\sqrt{\binom da}\,z^a w_a,\qquad
 d\nu(z)=\frac{d\Re z\,d\Im z}{\pi(1+|z|^2)^2}.
\]
For tensor products write \(\psi_{\mathbf z}\). On strict
occupation charts, set \(p_j=|z_j|^2/(1+|z_j|^2)\) and
\[
 e(z_j)=\frac{z_j}{|z_j|}(e^{-2\pi i p_j}-1),\qquad
 k(z_j)=-e^{-2\pi i p_j},\qquad
 \epsilon(\mathbf z)=\sum_j e(z_j)\prod_{\ell>j}k(z_\ell).
\]
These are the real Euclidean coherent principal values, not the weak
values of an arbitrary mixed kernel.

Choose a fixed smooth cutoff \(\chi(\mathbf y,\mathbf z)\) equal
to one near every pair with
\(\epsilon(\mathbf y)=\epsilon(\mathbf z)\), and near every
occupation endpoint. Its removed part is supported on a strict compact
chart where \(|\epsilon(\mathbf y)-\epsilon(\mathbf z)|\ge\gamma>0\).
For the actual whole-meridian intertwiner \(W_N(M)\), define
\[
 C_{\chi,N}=N^{2m}\int\chi(\mathbf y,\mathbf z)\,
 |\psi_{\mathbf y}\rangle
 \langle\psi_{\mathbf y},W_N(M)\psi_{\mathbf z}\rangle
 \langle\psi_{\mathbf z}|\,
                         d\nu^{[m]}(\mathbf y)d\nu^{[m]}(\mathbf z).
\]
This is a specified finite matrix integral; its cutoff may correlate
input and output variables. It is not asserted to be a projection.
The theorem proves, on \(|N\mu|\le\eta'<\pi\), \(M=e^\mu\),
\[
 \|W_N-C_{\chi,N}\|_1+
       \|[E_\Sigma(M),C_{\chi,N}]\|_1
       \le C N^{2m}e^{-cN}\|W_N(M)\|.
\]
The positive constants depend on the width, cutoff and collar, but
not on \(W_N\), its word length or its integer filling powers.
The whole-family identity \([E_\Sigma(M),W_N(M)]=0\) is essential.
For a holomorphic family on a larger buffered collar, every fixed
true meridian derivative has the same estimate after its \(N^r\)
derivative cost, with the supremum of the actual word norm on that
larger collar.

The proof uses the literal finite-difference rows in the Euclidean
coherent frame. A protected local analytic estimate controls powers
through order \(\delta N\). Exact finite propagation and binomial
tails separately control every path that could meet a cap. The local
and tail errors are kept as a sum during the intertwining expansion.

No binomial-metric norm estimate is transferred into this argument.

\[
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N

\]

## Polynomial cost for the original marked-source correction, 19 November

The [polynomial Ward theorem](research_polynomial_top_source_ward_transport.md)
now compares the original pointed source with the literal top source
for an arbitrary marked matrix. Its explicit primitive acts on just two
heads. At the complete meridian its operator norm is at most \(N/2\),
independently of total width. The entire meridian family and every fixed
true derivative have polynomial bounds on the buffered scaled collar
\(|N\mu|\le\eta<\eta'<\pi\).

Fix \(m\ge2\), \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and \(M=e^\mu\), with the
quantum root \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\) fixed. Let \(Z\) be the last \(m-2\) heads, with
ordered Cartan \(K_Z\); when \(m=2\), take \(Z=\mathbb C\) and
\(K_Z=1\). Write \(E_\Sigma\) for the full actual lowering
operator. The two retained source matrices are
\[
 Q_{\rm pt}=|0\rangle\langle0|\otimes K_2^{-d}\otimes K_Z^{-d},
 \qquad
 Q_{\rm top}=|0\rangle\langle d|
              \otimes|d\rangle\langle0|\otimes K_Z^{-d}.
\]
Thus \(\Phi_M(C)=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{\rm pt}C)\) is the original
pointed source.
There is an explicit holomorphic primitive \(\mathcal A(M)\) with
\[
 [\mathcal A,E_\Sigma]=Q_{\rm pt}-Q_{\rm top},\qquad
 \|\mathcal A(1)\|\le N/2.
\]
Consequently every full matrix \(C\), without an intertwining
assumption, satisfies
\[
 \Phi_M(C)=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{\rm top}C)
                +\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal A[E_\Sigma,C]).
\]
The top trace is exactly
\(\operatorname{Tr}_Z(K_Z^{-d}\langle d,0|C|0,d\rangle)\).
All prescribed scalars and pivots remain in these expressions.

For example, at \(M=1\) the correction obeys
\[
 \left|\Phi_1(C)-\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{\rm top}(1)C)\right|
 \le \min\!\left\{
       \frac N2\|[E_\Sigma(1),C]\|_1,\,
       \frac{N^m}{2}\|[E_\Sigma(1),C]\|
     \right\}.
\]
Here \(\|\cdot\|_1\) is trace norm and \(\|\cdot\|\) is operator
norm in the physical coefficient Euclidean metric. The two bounds
give alternative hypotheses; no estimate in a coherent kernel
metric has been substituted for them.

The resulting transfer of a leading term is quantitative. Suppose the
actual top trace is \(L_N(1+o(1))\), \(L_N\ne0\). If its actual
trace-norm current is at most \(|L_N|N^{-2}\), the correction has
relative size \(O(N^{-1})\). Thus sufficiently small errors of fixed
algebraic order can preserve a nonzero leading term in this source
comparison. Establishing that current bound for a geometric
localization is still required.

The proof uses the unweighted capped raising shift on the second head,
not a general inverse for \([E_\Sigma,\cdot]\). Its middle blocks cancel,
and its two remaining blocks are precisely the source matrices above.
The actual two-head meridian frame extends this identity
holomorphically. Tensoring by \(K_Z^{-N}\), which is scalar at the
fixed quantum root, gives the full-width identity. No Laurent pole
occurs at \(M=1\); every true meridian derivative retains the moving
arrows, primitive, marked matrix and the two distinct pivot derivatives.

This polynomial bound belongs to the top-source comparison. It does
not identify the separate opposite-polarization return or replace every
earlier quotient-source primitive by a polynomial one. The remaining
analytic task is to estimate the actual geometric boundary contribution,
its current and its competing regions. The original source must still
have a nonzero geometric coefficient. No new volume-conjecture case is
claimed here.

## The finite-level source quotient has a bounded section, 19 November

The [source-quotient theorem](research_top_column_source_quotient_and_bounded_section.md)
solves the linear lifting problem associated with the top coefficient.
It gives the exact image and kernel, an explicit section with uniformly
bounded norm on the scaled meridian collar, and a finite homotopy.
This is an algebraic source reduction for every width, before any
identification with a geometric critical algebra.

Use the notation of the top-column observation below:
\(d=N-1\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), \(M=e^\mu\), \(x=-M/q\), with
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(g=K^{-d}\), and
\(\mathcal B=\iota_dK_Z^{-d}\pi_0\). Let
\[
 \mathcal A_j=\{X:KX=Q^jXK\},\qquad
 \delta X=[E,X],\qquad
 \mathcal Y=\{Y\in\mathcal A_d:\delta Y=0\}.
\]
For a seed \(H\in\mathcal A_0\), denote its actual top coefficient by
\[
 \mathcal C(H)=C_d(H)
     =\eta_d^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^d E^k(gH)E^{d-k},\qquad
 \eta_d=\prod_{a=1}^d(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1}).
\]
The theorem proves \(\operatorname{im}\mathcal C=\mathcal Y\), with
the literal right inverse
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \mathcal R(Y)=g^{-1}\mathcal B Y
       =x^dQ^{-1}\iota_d\pi_0Y,\qquad
 \mathcal C\mathcal R(Y)=Y.
 \quad}
\]
All spectator Cartans cancel from this section. For every Schatten
matrix norm,
\[
 \|\mathcal R(Y)\|_p\le |M|^d\|Y\|_p
                 \le e^\eta\|Y\|_p
                 \quad (|N\mu|\le\eta<\pi).
\]
At \(M=1\) it is a contraction, independently of the number of heads.
In the coefficient Hilbert--Schmidt norm, this implies
\(\sigma_{\min}^{+}(\mathcal C)\ge |M|^{-d}\ge e^{-\eta}\).
This is a bound for the top integral map on the complement of its
kernel. It is not a bound for \(E\) or for \([E,\cdot]\).

The kernel and the source-preserving change of representative are exact:
\[
 \ker\mathcal C=g^{-1}\delta(\mathcal A_d),\qquad
 H=\mathcal R(\mathcal C H)+g^{-1}\delta\mathfrak h(gH).
\]
Here \(\mathfrak h\) is the explicit finite sum in the note; no
dimension argument or unsolved transport equation replaces it.
Its norm can still be exponential. Thus the bounded lift does not
provide a polynomial bound for every commutator primitive.
For integer-degree-zero seeds, the top coefficient has degree \(-d\)
and its commutator primitive has degree \(+1\); these are not identified
modulo \(N\).

The original source descends by the prescribed functional
\[
 \tau(H)=\lambda(\mathcal C H),\qquad
 \lambda(Y)=\operatorname{Tr}_U(\mathcal B Y).
\]
Every compatible fiber is explicitly
\(\mathcal R(Y)+g^{-1}\delta(\mathcal A_d)\).
This is the split finite-level affine lifting torsor. The section is
holomorphic, and its true meridian derivatives have polynomial cost;
the moving coefficient \(Y(\mu)\) is retained. This construction
depends on \(N\), is linear rather than multiplicative, and does not
construct a fixed A-polynomial torsor.

The remaining scalar \(\lambda(Y)\) can vanish. The chosen representative
is supported on the first remaining output row \(d\), so its bounded
norm supplies neither the previously required low-output analytic seed
nor a geometric boundary amplitude. The outstanding task is to estimate
the actual knot's class and its specified spectator contraction, with
the original cycle and competing regions retained. The finite-exception
theorem remains open.

## The original source is a bounded top-column observation, 19 November

The [top-column source theorem](research_top_column_integral_and_bounded_source.md)
identifies the boundary quantity left unestimated by the preceding
ordinary-column and Fourier arguments. It is an exact identity for
the original pointed source, with polynomial observation cost at every
fixed width. The exponential conditioning of the auxiliary lowering
frame cancels from the observation entirely.

Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and \(M=e^\mu\) at fixed
\(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\). There are one opened head and \(r\ge1\)
remaining heads. On their tensor \(U\), let \(E,K\) be the actual
ordered lowering and Cartan operators. For an actual intertwiner
\(W_H\), put \(H=(W_H)_{00}\), \(g=K^{-d}\), and
\(C_d=(W_H)_{d0}\); these indices concern the opened head.
Split \(U=V\otimes Z\), where \(V\) is its first head and
\(Z\) has \(r-1\) heads. Let \(\iota_a\) insert and
\(\pi_a\) extract occupation \(a\) on \(V\). The specified
observer is the literal physical matrix
\[
 \mathcal B=\iota_d K_Z^{-d}\pi_0.
\]
With \(Z=\mathbb C\), \(K_Z=1\) if \(r=1\), the theorem gives
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \Phi_0(W_H)=\operatorname{Tr}_U(gH)
       =\operatorname{Tr}_U(\mathcal B C_d)
       =\operatorname{Tr}_Z(K_Z^{-d}\pi_0C_d\iota_d).
 \quad}
\]
Every crossing, framing and peripheral scalar already in the word is
retained. No new pivot is put on the opened head.

The proof uses the exact finite integral and operator partition
\[
 C_d=\eta_d^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^d E^k(gH)E^{d-k},\qquad
 \sum_{k=0}^d E^{d-k}\mathcal B E^k=\eta_d I_U,
\]
where \(\eta_d=\prod_{a=1}^d(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})\), nonzero on
\(|N\mu|<\pi\). The lowering frame fixes both endpoints of
\(\mathcal B\); conjugating the partition therefore leaves the
observer unchanged. Trace cyclicity then proves the source formula.
All finite caps occur in these identities.

In the coefficient Euclidean metric,
\[
 \|\mathcal B\|=|M|^{-(r-1)d},\qquad
 \|\mathcal B\|_{\rm HS}=N^{(r-1)/2}|M|^{-(r-1)d}.
\]
For example, on \(|N\mu|\le\eta<\pi\),
\( |\Phi_0(W_H)|\le e^{(r-1)\eta}N^{(r-1)/2}
\|C_d\|_{\rm HS}\).
All true meridian derivatives are retained exactly by
\[
 \partial_\mu^k\Phi_0(W_H)
   =\operatorname{Tr}_U\!\left(
       \mathcal B(\partial_\mu-(r-1)d)^k C_d\right).
\]
For one remaining head the sharper identity is
\(C_d=|0\rangle\langle d|\,\Phi_0(W_H)\) throughout the
meridian family.

This supplies a concrete boundary observation, not a lower bound from
a Fourier norm. At larger width the prescribed spectator trace still
has to be estimated. In particular, moving to the reciprocal or
factorial-output chart cannot provide its nonzero geometric coefficient
for free: that boundary contains the original source itself. The
complementary occupations zero and \(d\), their meridian derivatives,
and the original contributing cycle remain part of the analytic task.
No additional filling assignments have been proved.

A coverage-only literature check found the general trace/integral
framework in Beliakova--Blanchet--Gainutdinov,
[Modified trace is a symmetrised integral](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.00321).
Its abstract concerns modified traces and integrals for finite-dimensional
unimodular pivotal Hopf algebras. No proof from that paper is used here,
and no novelty claim for that general framework is made.

## Analytic propagation and meridian Fourier norm control, 19 November

Two estimates now go beyond the scalar-preserving replacement discussed
below. They concern the actual highest-block completion, with all its
finite coefficients retained. Neither supplies a previously unproved
volume-conjecture case.

There are \(r\ge1\) remaining heads and one opened head. At level
\(N\ge2\), put \(d=N-1\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\) and
\(f_n=(Q;Q)_n=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-Q^j)\), with \(f_0=1\).
For a Cartan-preserving remaining-head seed \(H_M\), write
\(W_{H_M}\) for its exact intertwiner completion and
\(C_n(M)=p_nW_{H_M}i_0\). Here \(i_0\) inserts occupation zero
on the opened head and \(p_n\) extracts occupation \(n\).
In particular \(C_0=H_M\).

The [ordinary-column theorem](research_highest_block_ordinary_column_kernel.md)
starts with an actual seed estimate at \(M=1\): its remaining-head
kernel must have a uniform expansion \(\gamma_N e^{NS}a(1+O(N^{-1}))\)
on a buffered complex polydisk, with \(a\ne0\), and its matrix norm
must be at most \(|\gamma_N|e^{cN}\). Remaining output coordinates
are monomials and remaining input coordinates have ordinary binomial
weights; the output coordinates stay away from zero. These are explicit
hypotheses, not a conclusion about an unspecified short component.

For the ordered remaining lowering and Cartan operators \(E,K\), put
\(\mathcal L(X)=K^{-1}[E,X]\) and
\(E_N(Z)=\sum_{n=0}^{d}Z^n/f_n\), and let
\(H_*=H_M|_{M=1}\). The exact ordinary output column is
\[
 \Psi_N(t)=\sum_{n=0}^{d}t^nC_n(1)
           =E_N(Qt\mathcal L)^{-1}H_*,\qquad \mathcal L^N=0.
\]
The inverse is an actual finite operator inverse. On a fixed small
\(t\)-disk, the scalar kernel of this column has a selected analytic
phase and nonzero amplitude,
\(\gamma_Ne^{NV}b(1+O(N^{-1}))\), initialized by \(S,a\).
The proof controls the low logarithm using the actual short clock
rotations, and then bounds the entire remaining cap. Every fixed
coherent derivative of the normalized error has the same order.
This theorem concerns ordinary first-head output; no factorial output
weight or meridian differentiation is included in that local estimate.

The separate [meridian norm theorem](research_completion_column_meridian_fourier_norm.md)
controls the whole column for \(M=e^\mu\), on
\(|N\mu|\le\eta<\pi\) at fixed width. Let \(A(M)\) be the exact
diagonal lowering frame, so that
\(E(M)=A(M)E(1)A(M)^{-1}\), \(K(M)=M^rK(1)\), and set
\(\widetilde H_M=A(M)^{-1}H_MA(M)\). If \(C_n^0(X)\) denotes the
root completion coefficient with seed \(X\), the exact transport is
\[
 C_n(M)=h_n(M)M^{-rn}A(M)C_n^0(\widetilde H_M)A(M)^{-1},\qquad
 h_n(M)=M^{-n}\frac{f_n}{(M^{-2}Q;Q)_n}.
\]
Here \((b;Q)_n=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1-bQ^j)\).
Both this map and its inverse have polynomial norms, uniformly through
\(0\le n<N\). Consequently, for arbitrary positive weights \(w_n\)
independent of \(\mu\), the weighted coefficient norms
\[
 \left(\sum_n w_n^2\|C_n(M)\|_{S_2}^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad
 \left(\sum_n w_n^2\|C_n^0(\widetilde H_M)\|_{S_2}^2\right)^{1/2}
\]
are comparable in both directions by powers of \(N+1\).
Here \(S_2\) is the Hilbert--Schmidt matrix norm. Thus their logarithms
differ by at most \(O(\log N)\) whenever the norms are nonzero.
The corresponding coefficient comparison also holds for every
Schatten norm. Parseval identifies the displayed Hilbert norms with
actual circle \(L^2\) norms: weights \(R^n\) give the ordinary column,
and weights \(R^n/|f_n|\) give its factorial-output transform.
For a seed family holomorphic on a larger scaled disk, all fixed true
meridian jets satisfy the same two-sided comparison when derivative
order \(k\) is weighted by \(N^{-k}\). The actual
derivatives of the frame and transformed seed remain in the formula.
No comparison with a fixed unchanged seed is inferred.

The remaining geometric boundary is explicit. The exact factorial
transform is a finite contour integral selecting the constant Laurent
coefficient. Its reciprocal ordinary column starts with
\(C_d=(-1)^dQ^{d(d+1)/2}\mathcal L^dH_*/f_d\), whose local phase
and nonzero amplitude are not supplied by the small ordinary-output
theorem. A Fourier norm does not give a lower bound at a prescribed
endpoint or for the original pivotal trace. The geometric contribution
and global bounds for competing regions still need proof.

## What the current-free replacement does and does not settle, 19 November

This pass checked whether the remaining lowering correction could be
bypassed by replacing an assembled mark with a genuine intertwiner.
The existing [physical-block reconstruction](research_physical_highest_block_endpoint_coordinates.md)
already does this at the level of the closed scalar. Fix \(m\ge2\)
heads and \(N\ge2\). For a degree-preserving analytic marked
operator \(C\), let \(i_a\) insert
first-head occupation \(a\), let \(p_a\) extract it, and put
\[
 H=p_0Ci_0,\qquad C^{\rm int}=W_H.
\]
The reconstruction gives a holomorphic operator \(W_H\) commuting
with the actual total \(E,F,K\), with \(p_0W_Hi_0=H\). Consequently
\[
 \Phi(C^{\rm int})=\Phi(C)
       =\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm r}(K_{\rm r}^{1-N}H)
\]
as a whole fixed-root meridian germ, including all its derivatives.
Its Ward currents vanish exactly. This is a positive algebraic result
already in the notes; it is not a new estimate for a geometric window.
At fixed width its proved uniform reconstruction cost is \(e^{cN}\)
on \(|N\mu|\le\eta<\pi\), where \(M=e^\mu\). The replacement
generally changes the prefix quotient mark.

The analytic comparison that is still needed can be written explicitly.
Use \(E_\Sigma=E_1K_{\rm r}+E_{\rm r}\),
\(e_a=MQ^{-a}-M^{-1}\) for \(1\le a<N\), and
\(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\). Set
\[
 D_a=p_a(C-W_H)i_0,\qquad
 Y_a=p_a[E_\Sigma,C]i_0.
\]
Taking first-head blocks, using \(E_\Sigma i_0=i_0E_{\rm r}\), gives
\[
 D_0=0,\qquad
 e_{a+1}K_{\rm r}D_{a+1}=Y_a-[E_{\rm r},D_a]
       \quad(0\le a<N-1),\qquad
 Y_{N-1}=[E_{\rm r},D_{N-1}].
\]
Thus every forcing term and the last capped row remain visible.
The equal closed sources do not give a bound for this forced kernel
relative to the proposed geometric phase.

There is an elementary reason not to infer that bound from source
preservation alone. The actual degree-preserving coupon
\(C=i_1E_{\rm r}p_0\) has \(H=0\), zero pointed source and zero
completion, while \(Ci_0=i_1E_{\rm r}\ne0\). Completion can therefore
erase a nonzero local kernel. This coupon is neither a knot
counterexample nor a claim about the faithful geometric window.

No additional filling assignments have been proved in this pass.
The outstanding positive step is a controlled comparison for the
actual geometric window in the forced system above, or a construction
of a current-free window with a controlled complex kernel and the
original contributing cycle. This local comparison would still need
the global bounds for competing regions. Repeating the algebraic
completion or its closed symmetry does not supply these estimates.
The existing written theorems and both frozen manuscripts are unchanged.

## Closed degree averaging removes lower-section parameter dependence, 19 November

The [closed-source reduction](research_closed_source_degree_averaging.md)
settles an algebraic part of the return problem without a smallness
estimate. Let \(J\) be total integer occupation, and let \(P_j\)
project onto its degree \(j\). For the entire assembled marked matrix
\(C\), put
\[
 \mathcal A(C)=\sum_jP_jCP_j
 =\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}e^{i\theta J}Ce^{-i\theta J}\,d\theta.
\]
This preserves the original pointed source, both quotient source rows,
and all true meridian derivatives. It contracts operator and trace
norms and the corresponding norms of the full lowering and raising
commutators. The averaging is applied after assembling the marks;
averaging their factors separately would generally change their product.

For every complex section parameter \(a\), the original source has
the exact form below. At level \(N\), write \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\) and
\(E_N(Z)=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}Z^n/(Q;Q)_n\), with
\((Q;Q)_n=\prod_{k=1}^n(1-Q^k)\).
\[
 \Phi(C)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm r}
    \bigl(D_N(M)H^{-1}q_F\mathcal A(C)i_a\bigr)
 +\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\mathcal W_E[E_\Sigma,\mathcal A(C)]\bigr),
 \qquad H=D_N(MK_{\rm r}).
\]
Here \(D_N(z)=(z^N-z^{-N})/(z-z^{-1})\), \(q_F\) is the exact
quotient map, and \(i_a=E_N(aF_\Sigma)i_0\) is the actual lower
section. The first trace is exactly independent of \(a\): every
positive power of \(F_\Sigma\) raises integer degree and has zero
closed trace against the retained weight. Its unclosed current need
not vanish. No small-activity condition or concentrated head profile
is required for this closed identity.

Thus lower-section parameter dependence is no longer an independent
closed-source obstruction. The original \(E_\Sigma\) correction is
still present and has the same scalar value after averaging. The
opposite-polarization return and the geometric value of the quotient
pairing have not been settled by this argument. In particular averaging
does not select a contributing geometric window or prove that its
contribution survives the complement.
