## Bounded nearby transport for unclosed marks, 19 November

The [nearby-return theorem](research_nearby_section_return_and_bounded_source.md)
provides a quantitative tool when an unclosed matrix or individual
window must still be retained. For \(B=F_\Sigma(M)\), define
\[
 T_N=E_N(ae^{-s/N}B)E_N(aB)^{-1}.
\]
On buffered actual matrix-norm domains \(\|aB\|<\rho<1\), the
completed return, its inverse and all fixed true meridian derivatives
are bounded independently of the level. Its scalar divided function
\(g_N(z;s)=(f_N(z;s)-1)/z\), where \(T_N=f_N(aB;s)\), has a removable
value at zero and norm \(O(|s|)\). The bounded quotient coupon satisfies
the exact single-current row
\[
 Q_{\rm b}C(T_N-I)=Q_{\rm b}[C,T_N]
                  =aQ_{\rm b}[C,B]g_N(aB;s).
\]
The source change also has an explicit bounded homotopy:
\[
 Q_s=T_NQ_{\rm b},\qquad
 \mathcal V_s=-a g_N(aB;s)Q_{\rm b},\qquad
 [\mathcal V_s,B]=Q_s-Q_{\rm b},\qquad
 \|\mu\mathcal V_s\|\le C|as|,\quad\mu=\log M.
\]
It uses neither the large prefix norm nor a right inverse of the
many-head current. Its square-zero section similarity is bounded
on this local family. The theorem retains the complete root residue,
finite part, moving current and moving return. Comparisons with the
analytic operator model are \(O(1/N)\) only after pole regularization;
a finite-part comparison does not automatically retain that rate.

The original pointed source still requires its previous lowering
correction and the raising correction adjusted by \(-\mathcal V_s\).
The new bound applies to the added homotopy, not to that whole error.
Nor does it give free composition of \(O(N)\) steps to a finite
classical displacement. For assembled degree-preserving closed marks
the scalar transport error vanishes by the preceding exact result.

## The full section at coalescing endpoints and its transport, 19 November

The [full-section theorem](research_full_section_coalescent_kernel.md)
now estimates both endpoint terms of the actual quotient section
together. Write \(N\ge2\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\),
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(x=-M/q\), and
\[
 E_N(Z)=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\frac{Z^n}{(Q;Q)_n},\qquad
 A_N=x^{-1}F_{\rm r},
\]
where \(F_{\rm r}\) is the literal ordered recipient raising
coproduct. Its actual caps give \(A_N^N=0\). The section is
\(i_a=E_N(aF_\Sigma)i_0\). For first-head evaluation \(y\), put
\(v=ay\). Its exact recipient operator is
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal S}_N(a,v)=
 \frac{E_N(aA_N)-v^N E_N(aA_N/v)}{1-v},\qquad
 \widehat{\mathcal S}_N(a,1)=(N-a\partial_a)E_N(aA_N).
\]
Both endpoints remain, including the removable value at \(v=1\).
The theorem proves a phase and nonzero amplitude for the actual
total-recipient Euler polynomial at small fixed \(a\), retaining
all coproduct carries, recipient caps and true meridian derivatives.
It then obtains a uniform coalescent profile for \(v=e^{s/N}\):
\[
 \mathcal L(s,H)=\frac{e^{sH}-1}{s},\qquad
 \mathcal L(0,H)=H,\qquad H=1-a\partial_aV,
\]
where \(V\) is the proved Euler-kernel phase. Denote the section and
Euler coherent kernels by \(\mathcal K_N\) and \(\mathcal E_N\).
The estimate is
\[
 \frac{\mathcal K_N(a,e^{s/N})}{N\mathcal E_N(a)}
                 =\mathcal L(s,H)+O(N^{-1}).
\]
The error is absolute, including at zeros of \(\mathcal L\). Where
\(\mathcal L\ne0\), it gives a relative estimate and nonvanishing.

Retaining the affine vacuum term also yields an exact connection.
The completed operator
\[
 Y_N(a,v)=I-(1-v)\widehat{\mathcal S}_N(a,v)E_N(aA_N)^{-1}
\]
satisfies
\[
 Y_N(a,Q^{-1}v)=(I-aA_N/v)Y_N(a,v),\qquad Y_N(a,1)=I.
\]
The complete clock-cycle product is exactly \(I\). In the coefficient
Euclidean operator norm, on a buffered
small-coupling domain \(\|aA_N\|\le\rho<1\), the stronger actual
operator estimate is
\[
 Y_N(a,e^{s/N})=e^s(I-aA_N)^{-s/(2\pi i)}
                                      +O_{\rm op}(N^{-1}).
\]
It includes uniformly bounded inverses and every fixed true meridian
jet. The proof uses the exact finite logarithm of the nilpotent Euler
polynomial, so no estimate of a separate coherent inverse symbol is
assumed. In the retained Euler-weighted scalar pairing the same
completion recovers the recipient Gauss transport factor
\(1-a f_{\rm r,out}/x_{\rm cl}\), with \(x_{\rm cl}=-M\).

This is a section profile, not a single geometric head state. Its
weak occupation at coalescence tends to \(H/2\); clock insertion
shifts \(s\) by \(2\pi i\) and must retain the entire profile.
The actual returning \(q_F\) pairing has not yet been estimated on
a geometric window. Nor is an arbitrary section parameter covered by
the small-coupling domain. No original-cycle coefficient or new volume
case is inferred.

## The actual finite-series input through either crossing, 19 November

The [finite-series crossing theorem](research_physical_crossing_qexponential_section_kernel.md)
estimates a boundary column that occurs in the section-change problem.

geometric series. In the factorial donor basis it is
\(\sum t^ae_a/(Q;Q)_a\), rather than an ordinary binomial column.
Here \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\). The theorem treats both literal crossing
signs, with their Cartan factors and checked flips, for sufficiently
small fixed \(t\).

The new argument uses the exact capped donor equation. Below degree
\(N\), its logarithm is solved by a q-difference inverse whose
coefficient at degree \(n\le\delta N\) costs at most \(C_\delta/n\).
An analytic positive majorant controls these low degrees; a separate
bound on the whole finite polynomial restores the high degrees,
including the explicit top forcing. It proves a nonzero local
amplitude and its first transport. Every recipient cap and every fixed
true meridian derivative of the normalized remainder is included.
This is not a deduction from a formal power series alone.

The input coordinate is the actual physical flag coordinate \(p=t\)
at completeness, with \(f=(1-A)/t\). The lower limit is regular with
nonzero \(f\), and the mixed Hessian is nondegenerate. This pays the
local crossing calculation for the actual finite-series input. It
does not estimate the complete section \(S_m\sum t^ae_a\), its
returning quotient row, a coalescing pair of section endpoints, or an
arbitrary nonlower geometric donor. Their boundary currents and the
original closing cycle remain.

## A bounded representative of the original quotient source, 19 November

The [bounded quotient-source theorem](research_bounded_quotient_source_and_ward_homotopy.md)
removes the large prefix conditioning from a representative of the
unmarked source. Let \(q_0=q_F(1)\) be the exact quotient map at
completeness. Its first block is the identity, so \(q_0q_0^*\ge I\).
The explicit least-norm section
\[
 j_\perp=q_0^*(q_0q_0^*)^{-1},\qquad P_\perp=j_\perp q_0
\]
has norm at most one, and \(P_\perp\) is the orthogonal projection
with kernel \(\operatorname{im}F_\Sigma(1)\). Here the occupation
coefficient basis is orthonormal. Transporting this fixed projection
by the actual Cartan frame gives a holomorphic projection \(P(M)\)
and a bounded section on each scaled meridian disc
\(|N\log M|\le\eta<\pi/m\). No adjoint is differentiated in the
complex meridian.

With \(K_\Sigma\) the ordered total Cartan, the new coupon is
\[
 Q_{\rm b}(M)=D_N(M)D_N(-qK_\Sigma(M))^{-1}P(M),

## Boundary corrections reduce to physical crossing-degree sectors, 19 November

The [crossing-sector theorem](research_crossing_wall_degree_sectors.md)
identifies the two integrated cross-wall corrections exactly. On a
pair of \(N\)-dimensional heads, let \(J_1,J_2\) be their integer
occupation indices and put
\[
 \Pi_0=\mathbf1_{J_1+J_2<N},\qquad
 \Pi_1=\mathbf1_{J_1+J_2\ge N}.
\]
For every holomorphic germ \(f\), the two wall periods are
\(f(T)\Pi_0\) and \(f(T)\Pi_1\), where \(T\) is the original
truncated transfer. All three transfer slots within one crossing
preserve that pair degree, so inconsistent wall choices have zero
complete period. A fixed word with \(c\) crossings therefore has at
most \(2^c\) sectors, one low/high choice per crossing, instead of
\(2^{3c}\) independent slot histories. Overlapping crossings retain
their original order.

Each sector has an exact nilpotent completion with ordinary convergent
Hankel banks. Its full period equals the original regularized cyclic-wall
period, including the endpoint finite parts and unramified cyclic-pole
residues. This changes the auxiliary completion; it does not delete
those currents or identify integrals over arbitrary subregions. The
norm-one degree projectors preserve the meridian transport
estimates sector by sector, with the original diagonal point cut and
all scalar factors fixed. This gives separate radial infinity bounds
for the completed sectors and every fixed true meridian derivative.

The sectors are not homogeneous intertwining sources. If
\(E_{\rm pair}\) lowers pair degree by one and \(F_{\rm pair}\)
raises it by one, their exact commutators are
\[
 [E_{\rm pair},\Pi_0]=-E_{\rm pair}\mathbf1_{J_1+J_2=N},
 \qquad
 [F_{\rm pair},\Pi_0]=F_{\rm pair}\mathbf1_{J_1+J_2=N-1}.
\]
Thus source identities requiring total intertwining cannot be applied
to a separately marked sector by definition.

The same theorem supplies an explicit complex chamber for the actual
binomial coherent kernels of these projectors. Write \(v_i=z_iw_i\)
for the two coherent contractions, with \(1+v_i\ne0\), and define
\[
 \Gamma(v_1,v_2)=
 \frac{(\sqrt{|v_1|}+\sqrt{|v_2|})^2}
 {|1+v_1|\,|1+v_2|}.
\]
On compact sets with \(\Gamma<1\), the low projector has normalized
kernel \(1+O(\gamma^{N-1})\) if \(|v_1v_2|<1\); the high projector
does so if \(|v_1v_2|>1\), for some \(\gamma<1\). The complementary
kernel and every fixed holomorphic derivative are exponentially small.
This is a single-kernel estimate, without a rule for composing
normalized symbols.

An exact counterexample shows why this chamber must be checked.
For equal contractions \(v_1=v_2=u/(1-u)\), take \(u=1/4+i\).
The real occupation sum is \(1/2<1\), and the limiting Cartan kernel
is off the unit circle. Nevertheless both low and high normalized
kernels grow exponentially and cancel to one: the high kernel has
rate \(|4u(1-u)|=5\sqrt{17}/4>1\). This is a literal finite-projector
calculation, not a claim about a faithful geometric representation.
It excludes selecting a sector from these real-part inequalities
and clock regularity alone.

The reduction removes redundant boundary histories and supplies
source-preserving contours for each remaining degree sector. It
does not turn the contraction into a determinant or positive scalar:
the integrated projectors have ranks \(N(N+1)/2\) and \(N(N-1)/2\).
The nonzero geometric coefficient and the arbitrary-short-partial-filling
theorem remain unproved. No new volume-conjecture case follows.

## The finite axis trace and its prescribed meridian filling, 19 November

The [axis-trace theorem](research_actual_braid_axis_trace_and_filling.md)
constructs a finite family directly from the actual reduced braid
operator. For an \(m\)-strand braid, let \(J\) be the sum of the
remaining \(m-1\) occupation indices, as an integer rather than a
residue class. Fix \(N\ge2\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(Q=q^2\), and \(x=-M/q\), where \(M\) is the original
meridian parameter. The family is the polynomial
\[
 T_{\beta,N}(s,M)
   =\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(s^J\mathcal B_m(W_\beta(M))\bigr).
\]
The original pointed and pivotal source is recovered exactly from
its two values at \(s=Q^{-1}\) and \(s=Q\), with the original
Cartan weights. Put \(c_N=(-q^{-1})^{m-1}\) and define
\[
 \Lambda_N(\mu)
 =c_Ne^{m\mu}T_{\beta,N}(Q^{-1},e^\mu)
  -c_N^{-1}e^{-m\mu}T_{\beta,N}(Q,e^\mu).
\]
At \(M=e^\mu=1\), this difference has a zero, and its
prescribed filling is
\[
 \Phi_{\beta,N}(1)
       =\frac{\Lambda_N'(0)}{2\varepsilon m},
 \qquad \Lambda_N(0)=0,
 \qquad \varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)(m-1)}.
\]
The derivative is the true meridian derivative of the whole finite
family, including the prefix, word and crossing scalars. Every outside
normalization line is retained before taking this limit. An arbitrary
shift of both sample points need not have a removable meridian pole.
This is a specified filling operation on a finite braid family; no
new topological invariant or Markov invariance of the polynomial is
asserted.

The same polynomial has an exact signed full-twist action, obtained
by identifying the reduced space with the quotient by the image of
the total lowering operator. The twist multiplier in degree \(j\)
is \(x^{-2mj}Q^{j(j-1)}\), before restoring the crossing and framing
scalars. This keeps the distinct meridian slopes at \(j\) and
\(j+N\). The constant and highest coefficients of an unmarked braid
are explicit nonzero units, but these units give no geometric lower
bound.

There is also a universal root symmetry. Applying the exact residue
identity to powers of the total Casimir and separating its distinct
root eigenvalues gives
\[
 T_{\beta,N}(s,1)
       \equiv s^{-(m-1)}T_{\beta,N}(s^{-1},1)
                                      \pmod{s^N-1}.
\]
It pairs sums of coefficients with labels related by
\(j\mapsto-j-(m-1)\) modulo \(N\). It does not identify the
individual integer-degree coefficients or their meridian derivatives.
This writes the previously established
[reciprocal-Casimir source pairing](research_reduced_casimir_pair_localizer.md)
in the axis variable. No positivity or equality of geometric period
coefficients follows.

The whole-meridian rational coefficient graph also checks: after
the remaining common diagonal conjugation is quotiented, the twisted
fixed scheme is the marked axis scheme with \(z_\beta=s\). The
proof extends the resolved first-head calculation explicitly in

Artin rings. This supplies the finite-state and rational-equation
comparison left open in the next entry. It does not supply a uniform
kernel expansion or a contour carrying the geometric contribution.
The smooth \((\mu,\log s)\) germ still requires the positive complete
gluing certificate specified there.

The residue gives a useful restriction on the next analytic theorem.
A single uniformly dominant nonzero root packet with the geometric
axis moment would make its two sample values differ by a nonzero

total-product eigenvalue. That contradicts \(\Lambda_N(0)=0\).

or other nonnegligible contributions to the exact cancellation, must

to the prescribed first-jet filling is not proved. Neither the
arbitrary-short-partial-filling theorem nor a new volume case follows.

## Absorbing supplied Seifert pieces, 19 November

The [marked Seifert reduction](research_marked_seifert_leaf_absorption.md)
now supplies a general topological rule for some degenerate short-filling
exteriors. Its input is a supplied planar Seifert piece with one retained
boundary, its actual section curves, and its primitive fiber \(h\).
It does not infer that input from a strict-template diagram.

Fill its other boundaries by nonfiber slopes. A slope meeting the fiber
once is a regular filling; a slope meeting it \(\alpha\ge2\) times
creates an exceptional fiber of that order. Count both the original
exceptional fibers and the ones just created. With none or one left,
the piece is a solid torus. If the regular slopes are
\(\mu_i+p_i h\), its exact outgoing meridian is
\[
 \mu_0-\Bigl(\sum_i p_i\Bigr)h,
 \qquad\text{or}\qquad
 \alpha\mu_0-\Bigl(\alpha\sum_i p_i+\beta\Bigr)h
\]
in the one-exceptional case with marked pair \((\alpha,\beta)\).
The proof constructs the disk/collar homeomorphism before calculating
homology. With at least two exceptional fibers, the outgoing boundary
injects on fundamental groups. If the attaching boundary of the rest
also injects after its own fillings, the resulting exterior cannot be
hyperbolic: it contains a nonabelian subgroup centralizing an infinite
fiber, whereas hyperbolic holonomy has abelian nontrivial centralizers.

For independently varying slopes \(m_i+n_i\ell_i\) in actual primitive
peripheral bases, write the fiber as \(h=r_i m_i+s_i\ell_i\).
Their fiber distances are \(|s_i-r_i n_i|\). Fiber-parallel directions
have distance one for every integer, while transverse directions have
distance at least two throughout a sufficiently long coordinate region.
This classifies the supplied leaf there by its count of exceptional
fibers. It is not asserted for a forest's rational effective parameters
without recomputing their actual vectors.

The rule can be iterated from the leaves of any supplied marked forest
when each child has become a solid torus. Fiber fillings and unabsorbed
children are explicit stopping branches. Replacing an absorbed piece
with the same retained boundary attachment preserves the final marked
knot, and hence its zero-framed Kashaev invariant at every level. All
original assignment fibers remain recorded; cancellation of outgoing
slopes does not settle the volume identity of an unresolved core.

This is an explicit application of standard Seifert-filling topology,
not a new volume theorem. Recognition of arbitrary short descendants,
the stopped branches, and their general source lower bound remain open.

## Which source comparison is still missing, 19 November

The latest coverage check rules out making the next task another local
crossing formula or a direct quotient onto the geometric shape field.
The [faithful-cut obstruction](actual_source_quotient_and_critical_relation.md)
already proves that a proper multiplicative quotient cannot preserve the
original source and all coupon products. This includes finite meridian
jets. Its exact sourced difference equation also shows how the classical
critical relation appears without being a relation of the raw insertion
algebra: the shift and its endpoint current must remain together.

The [twist-period insertion](research_twist_period_insertion_growth.md)
is an all-level witness inside the actual braid algebra. Its square is
zero but its original source is nonzero. The new radical coordinates
locate that witness; they do not remove it. Likewise, the fixed-level
meridian expansion in \(\mu=\log M\) and the selected semiclassical
expansion in \(1/N\) are different filtrations. A bound on the former's
nilpotence does not bound the first surviving coefficient of the latter.

The literal crossing matrices, finite boundary operations and the
actual-word normal covector are available. So is the
[formal critical observable](actual_pointed_commutant_and_critical_observable.md)
on the local transverse Gaussian module. What is missing is a comparison
from the **whole original relative cycle**, with its meridian normal, to
that module. Such a comparison must transport the accumulated endpoint,
cyclic-carry, alias and framing currents through the prescribed closing
functional. Local Gaussian integration does not establish that comparison.
It is an action-normalized comparison to each required semiclassical
order, with a controlled remainder; it need not kill a raw finite
insertion exactly.

For critical-shape insertions, the test must use the
[forced marked-source formula](research_forced_source_and_opposite_kernel_transport.md#a-simple-pole-primitive-for-the-full-marked-current),
not just the homogeneous word formula. For an analytic finite marked
family \(A(M)\), with \(q_N\) fixed, write
\(C_0(A)=p_0S^{-1}ASi_0=C_{00}+\mu C_{01}+O(\mu^2)\),
\([E_\Sigma,A]=Q_0+\mu Q_1+O(\mu^2)\), and expand the two
known source matrices as
\(D_\mu=\mu^{-1}d_{-1}+d_0+O(\mu)\) and
\(\mathcal W_E=\mu^{-1}W_{-1}+W_0+O(\mu)\). The exact root
moment is
\[
 \Phi_0(A)=\operatorname{Tr}_U(d_0C_{00}+d_{-1}C_{01})
              +\operatorname{Tr}_V(W_0Q_0+W_{-1}Q_1),
\]
where \(U\) is the space of remaining heads and \(V\) that of all
heads. All moving-prefix derivatives are retained
in these coefficients. The last two terms vanish for a whole-\(M\)
intertwining word but generally survive for inserted critical
observables. A proposed formal critical relation must therefore be
tested against this full moment, together with its original boundary
currents, to the claimed order in \(1/N\). The formula provides that
test; it does not prove its required vanishing or a geometric image.

Afterwards one still needs a nonzero geometric image and a bound for
the total competing contribution. The
[irreducible critical-trace criterion](irreducible_critical_source_and_whole_norm.md)
can be used only after this descent and a nonzero actual moment have
been supplied. It is not a consequence of the existence of the shape
field.

This is a coverage correction and a restriction on the proposed proof
route, not a new nonvanishing theorem. The manuscript and the scope of
the frozen long-filling theorem are unchanged.

For current literature coverage only, Haibin Hang's preprint
[*Cable Knot Counterexamples to the All-Knot Volume Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09063v1),
posted 6 November 2026, claims full-sequence failures for specified
cables of connected sums of figure-eight knots. Its abstract was
checked; its proof has not been audited here and is not used. These are
satellite knots, outside the final hyperbolic-knot target. In particular
this report supplies no counterexample to that target and no theorem
for the intermediate nonhyperbolic exteriors that its proof must handle.

## The actual word source has an explicit normal cocycle, 19 November

The [actual-word source theorem](research_actual_word_normal_cocycle_and_source.md)
now computes the normal datum for signed braid words. Here \(N\)
is the level, \(m\) the number of strands,
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(M=e^\mu\), and \(x=-M/q\).
The algebra \(\mathcal A\) is the commutant of the remaining
Cartan matrix \(K_0\) at \(M=1\); \(V\) is the image of the
root prefix map, and \(\varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)(m-1)}\).
Let
\(\rho_\mu(\beta)\) be the literal reduced matrix family and
\(b_\beta=\rho_0(\beta)\). Its logarithmic quotient normal is
\[
 c_\beta=[\rho'_0(\beta)b_\beta^{-1}]\in\mathcal A/V,
 \qquad
 c_{\beta\gamma}=c_\beta+\operatorname{Ad}(b_\beta)c_\gamma.
\]
It is a cocycle of the full root braid operators. The reduced
matrix \(b_\beta\) alone can lose precisely this datum.

There is one common analytic frame, equal to the identity at
\(\mu=0\), making the remaining lowering operator constant.
In this frame every internal crossing has zero quotient-normal
class. A different arbitrary moving frame adds the exact inner
coboundary; its contribution cancels in the complete original
trace. No frame derivative is discarded from a local kernel.

The boundary class is explicit from the original finite matrices.
Its entire prefix expansion satisfies
\[
 B_n(R_1)=\frac{x^{-n}}{(Q;Q)_n}\,B_0(R_1)L_2^n,
                     \qquad 0\le n<N,
\]
where \(L_2\) is the physical lowering shift, including its zero
bottom arrow. A division-free differentiated Ward equation gives
both reciprocal-arrow defects directly from these root
coefficients. Their negative-generator formula is the exact
cocycle inverse. This retains every cap, crossing scalar and
fixed-root meridian factor, without estimating an internal word's
unknown first derivative.

For each nonself physical Cartan pair, the prescribed source is
\[
 \Phi_{\mathfrak o}(\beta)
   =\operatorname{Tr}(d_0b_\beta)
       +\operatorname{Tr}(d_{-1}c_\beta b_\beta),
 \quad d_0=\frac{K_0+K_0^{-1}}{2\varepsilon},
 \quad d_{-1}=\frac{K_0-K_0^{-1}}{2\varepsilon m},
\]
with the traces restricted to that pair. The explicit flag-block
formula includes diagonal matrix characters and normal terms,
as well as a root off-diagonal paired with a normal off-diagonal.
Those quadratic couplings survive the trace. They cannot be
replaced by an adjoint or a positive norm.

In a presentation with one boundary crossing, the whole normal
term is therefore one specified boundary covector applied to the
actual internal root word. This removes unknown internal
quotient-normal insertions from the finite source formula. The
boundary covector retains the lowering-frame connection through
its full Ward sum. Its analytic behavior is not supplied merely
by the separate local estimate for \(\kappa S D_{\rm red}\).
In particular this statement does not establish a nonzero value
for that covector on the geometrically selected state.

## First-order prefix data and a uniform nilpotence bound, 19 November

The [first-normal source-order theorem](research_prefix_first_jet_source_order.md)
sharpens the earlier recursive reconstruction substantially. Write
\(\mu=\log M\), at fixed \(q_N\), and let \(\mathscr B_\mu\)
send a physical highest block \(H\) to the actual reduced prefix
matrix \(Z\). Its full inverse has at most a simple pole:
\[
 \mathscr B_\mu^{-1}=\frac{\mathscr R}{\mu}+\mathscr Q+O(\mu).
\]
Consequently, for an actual analytic reduced family
\(Z=Z_0+\mu Z_1+O(\mu^2)\),
\[
                    H(0)=\mathscr R Z_1+\mathscr QZ_0.
\]
Thus the prefix value and first meridian derivative recover the
entire root intertwiner, including every physical row and column.
Recovering its first derivative generally requires the second
prefix derivative. This is a statement about the true fixed-root
meridian family, not a quantum-parameter differentiation rule.

The proof uses the exact original cut pairing, rather than bounding
each step of a resonant recursion separately. If
\(V=\operatorname{im}\mathscr B_0\), an analytic proposed prefix
matrix is admissible exactly when its value at zero belongs to
\(V\). Its entire image order is
\[
 \mathcal I=V\otimes\mathcal O+\mu\mathcal A_{\mathcal O},
 \qquad \mathcal O=\mathbb C\{\mu\},
 \quad\mathcal A=\operatorname{End}_{K_0}(U).
\]
The part lost by the root prefix map has square zero. More
explicitly the full root algebra is the split extension
\(V\oplus(\mathcal A/V)\), with product
\[
 (b,[c])(b',[c'])=(bb',[bc'+cb']).
\]
The second component is retained in the original closing; dropping
it would lose actual source values.

The [lowering-flag classification](research_reciprocal_chain_flags_and_root_radical.md)
identifies \(V\) explicitly. On each reciprocal pair of actual
Cartan weights \(\chi,\chi^{-1}\), choose \(s\) with
\(Q^s=\chi^2\). The two maps \(E^s\) and \(E^{N-s}\) between
their weight spaces form an exact two-periodic complex. The
admissible pair matrices are exactly its endomorphisms. A
division-free Ward calculation proves necessity; the dimension
forced by the original polar cut pairing proves equality.

This yields a uniform algebraic conclusion for the full actual
root intertwiner algebra. Its Jacobson radical satisfies
\[
                             \mathfrak R^3=0.
\]
The bound is independent of the quantum level and strand count.
The subgroup \(1+\mathfrak R\) has nilpotence class at most two, so its
logarithms, exponentials and transport products truncate at
quadratic order. This realizes a precise nilpotence statement in
the finite source algebra. The general linear matrix factors of
the quotient remain, and the whole unit group is not declared
nilpotent. The classification concerns the full Cartan-preserving
algebra; no separate classification of the exact integer-degree
subalgebra is asserted.

## A pole-free coordinate for both physical endpoints, 19 November

The [physical highest-block theorem](research_physical_highest_block_endpoint_coordinates.md)
gives a regular coordinate for the entire finite intertwiner near
the complete meridian. For a word operator \(W\), let
\(H=W_{00}\) be its physical first-head highest block, an operator
on the remaining heads. Every operator \(H\) commuting with their
total Cartan extends uniquely to a total \(E,F,K\)-intertwiner.
The extension is holomorphic at \(M=1\). Exact integer occupation
degree can also be retained.

This is stronger endpoint information than a reconstruction from
the transformed constant term \(B_0\). Its first-column recurrence
divides only by the physical head coefficients
\[
 e_a=M Q^{-a}-M^{-1},\qquad 1\le a<N,
\]
which are nonzero at completeness. The first row follows from the
corresponding raising recurrence. Both terminal rows are proved
from the actual nilpotence \(E_\Sigma^N=F_\Sigma^N=0\), rather
than omitted at the finite cap. There is no inversion of a resonant
remaining Cartan eigenvalue.

On every strict collar \(|\log M|\le\eta/N\), \(\eta<\pi\),
the exact extension satisfies
\[
 \|H\|\le\|W_H\|\le e^{C N}\|H\|.
\]
The proof also gives a coupled low-degree bound for both endpoint
indices, an exponentially small high-degree tail on a sufficiently
small fixed physical coordinate disk, and Cauchy bounds for the
true meridian derivatives. The factor \(e^{CN}\) has an exponential
cost; it is not a zero-rate error in a volume comparison. An actual
phase and a lower bound still need additional information about the
seed.

The coordinate is linear, and its multiplication is explicit. If
\(U_a(H)=(W_H)_{0a}\) and \(V_a(H)=(W_H)_{a0}\) are its
reconstructed endpoint rows and columns, then
\[
 H_1\star H_2=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}U_a(H_1)V_a(H_2),\qquad
 W_{H_1\star H_2}=W_{H_1}W_{H_2}.
\]
All physical paths and their caps remain in this finite product.
The original pointed closing is exactly
\(\tau(H)=\operatorname{Tr}(K_{\rm r}^{1-N}H)\), including its
specified scalar lines and pivot derivative. Thus a finite word can
be studied through its actual endpoint operators without replacing
the closing by an unmarked trace.

This does not make the seed a scalar or fix its amplitude.
Intertwining permits arbitrary Cartan multiplicity operators.
In particular it supplies no lower bound for \(\tau(H)\), and
the seed is generally not an intertwiner on the remaining heads.
The construction therefore cannot be iterated to erase those
heads. Its next analytic use must estimate the seeds selected by
actual braid words, with their original closing.

The [lowest-block identity](research_lowest_physical_block_cut_pairing.md)
then identifies the duality operator explicitly. With the same
literal pivot and finite product,
\[
 \tau(H\star J)=\operatorname{Tr}(K_{\rm r}^{1-N}H\mathscr L J),
 \qquad \mathscr L J=(W_J)_{N-1,N-1}.
\]
The lowest physical block is another holomorphic coordinate on the
whole intertwiner space. Its downward raising recurrence and a
finite quantum-binomial inverse reconstruct the original operator,
with all terminal rows. Consequently \(\mathscr L\) and its inverse
have \(e^{CN}\) norm bounds on strict scaled meridian collars, and
the original bilinear cut pairing is perfect at completeness.
Exact integer degrees and true meridian derivatives remain.

The abstract perfect cut form was already established in
integral_projective_cut_duality.md. The new result gives its
explicit opposite-endpoint operator and a direct finite proof with
conditioning bounds. No projectivity theorem is used in that proof.
Perfection says a nonzero element has some nonzero pairing; it does
not force its pairing with the prescribed identity to be nonzero.
Thus the result supplies neither positivity nor the missing
geometric contribution to the original knot closing.

## One Euler operator and an exact trace density, 19 November

The reduced source now has a simpler presentation and a compatible
analytic description, without restricting the knot to a particular
braid word.

The [left-stabilization theorem](research_left_stabilized_single_euler_presentation.md)
puts the braid into a presentation whose reduced operator has exactly
one Euler star, together with its specified diagonal factor and scalar.
Every other crossing is an ordinary physical crossing on the remaining
strands. At the complete faithful representation,
at most three positive left stabilizations suffice to make the total
meridian product regular while retaining this form. Conjugations and
stabilizations preserve the actual normalized pointed source as a
whole fixed-root meridian family, including its prescribed derivative.

Here the Euler star is the finite change of basis used to eliminate
the selected strand. It acts on one donor strand and the remaining
recipient strands. The presentation theorem makes its geometric
donor a lower row: its Gauss coordinates satisfy
\(A_1=1\), \(p_1=0\), and \(f_1\ne0\). These symbols denote,
respectively, the Cartan coordinate and the upper and lower
off-diagonal coordinates, with \(1-A_1=p_1f_1\). Thus the needed
Euler estimate has a specified initial row. It need not cover
arbitrary donor coordinates. Recipients with coincident selected
meridian flags can also be lower rows; they are retained.

The [common radial dual](research_reduced_common_radial_first_jet_dual.md)
gives one finite coherent integrand for both terms of the prescribed
Cartan trace. Their different Cartan weights are carried by scalar
radial densities. If \(P_N(\mu)\) denotes that common integrand,
with \(M=e^\mu\), the exact root value has the form
\[
 \Phi_N(0)=\int
 \bigl(c_N P_N(0)+d_N\,\partial_\mu P_N(0)\bigr)\,d\gamma_N.
\]
The derivative is the derivative of the actual operator family,
including every scalar and change of basis. The apparent simple pole
has zero integrated residue; its residue is not set to zero on an
arbitrary part of the integration cycle. Every occupation cap remains.

The scalar \(d_N\) has only real zeros in the common radial variable,
and it and its reciprocal are uniformly bounded on fixed compact
sets separated from the real axis. The complete geometric total
moment is nonreal in this presentation. The scalar normal density
therefore does not kill that point. This statement concerns the
specified density, not the integral over its other variables:
it does not yet give a lower bound for the knot invariant.

The [hybrid spin estimate](research_hybrid_spin_euler_star_lower_chart.md)
then proves the actual Euler kernel is nonzero on a fixed complex
neighborhood of its initialized donor row. A physical recipient can
range over any fixed compact set where its identity kernel is
nonzero. A resolved lower recipient uses a factorial change of basis;
its finite output cap is recovered with an exponentially small
relative error. The theorem gives the phase, a nonzero leading
amplitude and uniform derivatives in the actual meridian family.
Both signs of the Euler operator are included. Its proof uses an
exact finite donor recurrence, analytic majorants and finite Cauchy
tails, rather than an uncapped infinite operator approximation.

The [combined boundary estimate](research_hybrid_spin_reduced_generator_lower_chart.md)
includes the diagonal factor in the same calculation. It proves the
actual kernel of \(\kappa S_rD_{\rm red}\), in its original order,
on the initialized donor chart. The proof derives its changed finite
recurrence directly and retains the scalar \(\kappa\), the Cartan
half-steps and the endpoint \(N-1\). It therefore completes the local
estimate for the entire boundary factor introduced by the presentation
theorem. No separate estimate or pointwise cancellation of a change
of basis is needed inside this factor. All fixed derivatives of its
normalized remainder are \(O(N^{-1})\) on smaller complex charts.

For a coincident recipient flag this supplies a lower logarithmic
coordinate chart at the geometric point. It does not show that the
original closed integration cycle selects that logarithmic lift.
Every interface between its basis choices and the other operators
must also remain. These qualifications are part of the remaining
global problem, not additional short-filling exclusions proved here.

The [common spin dual](research_reduced_common_spin_first_jet_dual.md)
places the exact Cartan trace and first finite part in this same
spin-coherent polarization. It works with arbitrary cyclic diagonal
basis frames, so using the hybrid Euler estimate requires no unproved
passage between spin and Bargmann kernels. An elementary rotated beta
integral supplies both Cartan densities, including the endpoint
occupations. The scalar normal weight is uniformly nonzero on compact
complex charts with nonreal total spin moment. The rational incidence
divisors, all moving-frame terms and the integrated residue identity
remain. In particular, neither that scalar unit nor the nonzero local
Euler amplitude asserts that the combined finite part or its closed
integral is nonzero.

The matching finals are \(\texttt{e5ee05ad…e17d3}\),
\(\texttt{f710940e…46f0c}\), \(\texttt{1575d7ce…620b93}\),
\(\texttt{1ba0870e…10b9f6f}\) and \(\texttt{dd21d1ab…4329b5d}\).
Each received complete author, independent peer and root review
together with both of its complete direct sources; the matching pins
were renewed. The manuscripts and the established range of the
volume theorem are unchanged.

The remaining analytic task includes the ordinary internal crossings,
the comparison of the full phase with its marked geometric primitive,
and the original closed integration cycle. In particular, local
nonzero factors do not prove that the cycle contains the geometric
contribution or that other contributions cannot cancel it. Those
global statements remain necessary for arbitrary fixed short partial
fillings. None of the results in this section adds a new such filling
to the frozen volume theorem.

## The geometric critical value and the framing directions, 19 November

The [charged geometric comparison](research_charged_geometric_critical_value.md)
now identifies the complete geometric critical point in the actual
charged-source coordinates and fixes its marked critical value.
For the alternating closed-braid formula, the exact correspondence
at a crossing is
\[
 I=d-u,\qquad V=z,\qquad J=B,\qquad
 \delta=d-u-z,\qquad J+\delta=d-A,
 \qquad d=N-1.
\]
Here \(I,V\) are the overstrand's input and output occupations,
\(J\) is the understrand's input, and \(\delta\) is its transfer.
This is a bijection of the actual finite states, including the
closing occupations. Substituting it into the physical crossing
action gives the charged action exactly on their common marked
branches. The corresponding singleton-clock comparison applies
to general signed braid words; the simpler charged coordinates
here still require an actual alternating closed diagram.

Write \(M=S^3\setminus K\), and let \(W(w)\) be the calibrated
charged potential whose exponential is \(e^{NW/(2\pi i)}\).
At the complete geometric point \(w_*\), retain the actual
integer critical character \(n\), so that
\(\nabla W(w_*)=2\pi i n\). The comparison proves
\[
 \operatorname{Re}
 \frac{W(w_*)-2\pi i n\cdot w_*}{2\pi i}
             =\frac{\operatorname{Vol}(M)}{2\pi}.
\]
The proof uses the explicit physical crossing Bloch class and its
degree-one fundamental-cycle comparison. It checks the primitive
constant and the sign of the integer character. This is a critical
value identity for the original function, not a volume asymptotic
for its sum. The original outside normalization remains separate.

The same comparison settles an important limitation of the proposed
positive chart. The geometric representation retains a locally free
two-dimensional framing orbit after its selected meridian flag is
fixed. Both directions survive in the full charged coordinates.
Consequently the full geometric Hessian has at least two null
directions. In the five-shape positive chamber of the charged
Legendre argument, the imaginary part of that Hessian is positive
definite. The two
facts are incompatible: no regular complete geometric point lies
in this full positive chamber, on any integer character. Changing
the character adds a linear term and leaves the Hessian unchanged.

This sharpens the preceding status of the boundary estimates.
Their nonzero coefficients and their positive angle examples remain
valid, but those examples cannot be full geometric critical points
of this unreduced charged formula. Extending that particular full
positive chart until it contains the geometric point is therefore
not a possible route to the desired theorem.

There is already an actual finite reduction available in
[the reduced braid source](research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md),
with its [resolved critical scheme](research_actual_reduced_braid_critical_scheme.md).
It uses \(\mathcal B_m(W)=p_0S_m^{-1}Wi_0\) and the prescribed
Cartan trace with its first meridian derivative. Its geometric
correspondence removes the framing directions under the conditions
stated there. The full trace and derivative must remain: deleting
two integration coordinates, or replacing the trace by an orbit
volume, would not preserve the original invariant. The next analytic
work must use that genuine reduction, retain the framing modes in
a larger domain, or find another exact polarization. The coefficient
of the geometric contribution and control of the rest of the source
remain open for arbitrary fixed short partial fillings.

The comparison final is
\(\texttt{53f5dde6b44bc09da1f8521eb0675c71f41617fe7b391b2b5a40743eed8ee8d9}\).
Author, independent peer and root read the entire matching final
and all five complete direct sources, checked the used implications,
and renewed all six matching hashes. Root's full J-source read was
repeated separately after a combined display was truncated. No
manuscript or public document was changed; no new volume-conjecture
case is claimed.

## A controlled nonzero boundary sum, 19 November

The [exterior closing theorem](research_exterior_fiber_zero_free_closing.md)
now proves a nonzero contribution for the full finite boundary
polynomial, under explicit conditions on its remaining charges.
This goes beyond uniqueness of its difference-equation solution:
the proof evaluates its prescribed closing and determines its
Gaussian coefficient from the original finite residue contour.
It does not establish noncancellation of the final knot invariant.

Here is the precise class. Let \(k\ge2\) be the number of
crossings on the rightmost circuit of the actual alternating
closed-braid diagram. Write \(A_i=a_i/N\) for its fixed charges
and \(B_i=b_i/N\) for the offsets of its moving charges. Set
\[
 J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi v)\,dv,\qquad
 R(y)=\sum_i[J(A_i+B_i+y)-2J(B_i+y)].
\]
At a real base with \(A_i>0\), \(B_i\ge0\), \(\min B_i=0\)
and \(A_i+B_i<1\), the inequalities
\(\cot^2(\pi A_i)<8\) make \(R\) strictly concave on its
entire physical interval. Its derivative tends to opposite
infinities at the two endpoints, so it has one interior maximum
\(y_0\). The additional condition is
\[
 k y_0+\sum_i B_i-\sum_i A_i-k/2=2n,
 \qquad n\in\mathbb Z.
\]
This says that the derivative of the original quadratic phase
at that maximum is an integer lattice Fourier frequency.
It is a checkable condition on the finite source, rather than
an assumption that a preferred saddle contributes.

For every literal integer-offset array in a fixed neighborhood
of such a base, the whole polynomial has the uniform asymptotic
\[
 F_{\gamma,N}(t)=\mathcal E_{\gamma,N}
    N^{(1-k)/2}e^{N\Psi_\gamma(t)}
                    \bigl(C_\gamma(t)+O(N^{-1})\bigr),
 \qquad |C_\gamma(t)|\ge c>0,
\]
on a fixed complex disk about \(t=1\). Here \(\gamma\) labels
the other charges, \(\mathcal E_{\gamma,N}\) is the exact
retained initial factor, \(\Psi_\gamma\) is the selected critical
value, and \(C_\gamma\) is the explicit Gaussian amplitude in
the theorem. The finite cotangent rectangle gives this contribution
with coefficient \(+1\). The rest of the physical interval,
both endpoints, the contour connectors and the other Fourier
terms have a uniform exponential loss. Consequently the actual
\(F_{\gamma,N}\) has no zeros on that disk for sufficiently
large \(N\). The conjugation formula covers the opposite
crossing sign with its original pivot.

The admissible base class is nonempty for every fixed \(k\ge2\),
and the note realizes it in the honest flow polytope. For every
\(k\ge6\) it also gives a choice inside the five-shape positive
angle chamber at every crossing. This is compatibility with
positive angles, not identification with geometric holonomy.
For \(k=1\) a separate exact finite identity gives the nonzero
closing value; a uniform disk is not inferred from that point value.

The [complex-offset completion](research_exterior_fiber_complex_offset_completion.md)
then removes a practical obstruction to using this result in a
larger contour calculation. The original upper cutoff depends
on \(\min_i(N-1-a_i-b_i)\). On a neighborhood of the chosen
base, extend the sum to one fixed cutoff. At every admissible
integer offset, each added term contains a numerator factorial
zero and a nonzero denominator. Thus the extension has exactly
the original values. It is holomorphic in the complex offsets,
and the proof bounds the entire added interval, so the nonzero
Gaussian and its uniform relative error persist on a complex
parameter neighborhood. The off-lattice difference equation
has explicit endpoint forcing, which is retained. Derivatives
of this specified interpolation are not asserted to be meridian
derivatives or Casimir Hermite partners.

The remaining knot sum still includes every \(\gamma\), its
exact outside factor and its phase. We have not shown that the
geometric offsets of an arbitrary short partial filling belong
to the controlled neighborhood, or that the other fibers have
a smaller action. Cancellation in the sum over \(\gamma\)
therefore remains open. The frozen volume theorem has not
gained an additional short-filling case.

For literature coverage, related radial asymptotics of
\(q\)-hypergeometric series are treated in
[Garoufalidis--Zagier, *Asymptotics of Nahm sums at roots of unity*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.07690).
No theorem or proof from that paper is an input to the two
arguments above; their finite source, endpoint and contour
calculations are written out. This coverage check is not a
novelty assessment of the exact boundary results.

The matching closing final is
\(\texttt{8b7d5a5eae77b98fb9f531fb1a8d03ad5e5a808978e66eb854431b468ce25d92}\)
and the completion final is
\(\texttt{127e8cae7bdba6f102f98d4fbd9aee603692465139b2e97c52065653fcb89062}\).
For both, author, independent peer and root checked the entire
matching final and every complete direct source and renewed

and public documentation remain unchanged.

## Exact cut identities and a finite boundary equation, 19 November

The new results concern the original finite expression for Kashaev's
invariant, with its closing factors and framing normalization retained.
They do not extend the frozen long-twist volume theorem. In particular,
the theorem for every fixed short partial filling is still open.

The [fixed-cut identity](research_highest_cut_charged_endpoint_reduction.md)
now gives an explicit polynomial formula for any prescribed occupation
at the strand where the braid is cut. Here an occupation is an integer
between zero and \(d=N-1\), and \(N\) is the quantum level. The pivotal
partial trace is a scalar matrix, so every such diagonal entry gives
the same normalized knot invariant. In the propagated Fourier basis,
fixing occupation \(a\) replaces the closing polynomial by the single
monomial \(Z^{d-a}Y^a\), where \(Y,Z\) are its two endpoint variables.
The complete coefficient formula retains the original factors; the
finite root sums introduce no additional alias terms. At \(a=0\),
one anchor variable can be set to zero after its exact coefficient has
been extracted. This is polynomial evaluation, rather than a proposed
contour deformation through a singular endpoint. The identity applies
to arbitrary signed braid words. It does not make the remaining sum
positive or establish a lower bound.

The [finite difference equations](research_exterior_pivotal_fiber_quantum_curve.md)
provide a second exact description. For an arbitrary signed word and
fixed bridge clocks, shifting one anchor variable \(X\) to \(QX\),
where \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), gives a rational identity between its finite
products. Clearing denominators gives a coefficient recurrence whose
width is bounded by the number of incident blocks, independently of
\(N\). These equations retain the actual polynomial degree bounds.
Their coefficients depend on the bridge clocks, so the same equation
cannot simply be pulled through the remaining clock sum.

There is a more explicit equation when the actual closed-braid diagram
is connected and alternating. Fix the other charges and vary the
charges along the rightmost braid position. Their allowed values form
one consecutive interval \(0\le l\le K\). The corresponding exact
finite polynomial is
\[
 F_\gamma(t)=\sum_{l=0}^{K}T_{\gamma,l}t^l.
\]
Here \(\gamma\) records all the fixed charges and \(T_{\gamma,l}\)
is the original complex summand, including the pivot at that boundary.
The note proves its finite difference equation in the shift
\((\mathsf T F)(t)=F(Qt)\). Both endpoints satisfy the equation:
no residual cap term is discarded. Its constant coefficient and degree
bound determine this polynomial uniquely. The original invariant is
the unchanged scalar factor times \(\sum_\gamma F_\gamma(1)\).
This is an equation for an auxiliary boundary variable, not yet a knot
A-polynomial. Uniqueness of the polynomial does not prove that its
value at one, or the subsequent sum over \(\gamma\), is nonzero.

The [integral-flow criterion](research_uniform_angle_integral_character_flows.md)
also makes one part of the volume optimization explicit. It concerns
the same alternating diagram, at the uniform angle assignment
\(\theta_{U_j}=\theta_{Z_j}=2\pi/3\). Form the dual graph of its
regions. Each diagram edge meets exactly one overcrossing; orient its
dual edge from white to black, reversing that direction when the
overcrossing is negative. A candidate integer Fourier character has
a strictly feasible Legendre constraint exactly when this graph has
real currents \(r_e\) satisfying
\[
 0<r_e<\tfrac12,\qquad
 |r_{u_j}-r_{z_j}|<\tfrac13,\qquad
 \operatorname{div}r=\nu\in\mathbb Z^{V}.
\]
The two currents in the middle inequality belong to the over-input
and over-output at crossing \(j\). Divergence means incoming current
minus outgoing current, and the integral vector \(\nu\) specifies
the character in the original face lattice. The note proves both
directions and a sufficient construction using strict inequalities
on every graph cut. A successful test supplies the proper radial
minimum in the Legendre problem. It does not supply the remaining
critical equations, geometric peripheral data, or a coefficient in
the original integration cycle.

These results separate three questions that had been conflated:
an exact finite source equation, feasibility of its volume
optimization, and a nonzero geometric contribution to its prescribed
closing value. The first is now explicit in these representations;
the second has the stated exact test at uniform angles. The third
remains unresolved. The alternating-diagram results do not apply
automatically to arbitrary signed short partial fillings.

The existing [short-contraction criterion](research_physical_window_short_contraction_class.md)
states the remaining analytic requirement explicitly. Each contraction
needs one holomorphic representative agreeing with the actual finite
source on its selected color window. The contour through its saddle
must stay inside that representative's proved domain. Both original
end connectors and the complete sum over colors outside the window,
including the required derivatives, must have a strict action loss.
Large twists supply these controls in the long-twist argument.
For arbitrary fixed short components they have not been established.
Preservation of a local Hessian inequality does not establish them.

The [combined-corner calculation](research_combined_low_kernel_corner_cancellation.md)
now removes one specific excessive rate in the original source.
On any fixed graph satisfying its degree and power condition,
the low-kernel vertical current's artificial upper endpoint cancels
against the adjoining horizontal pieces, before absolute values.
The resulting local chain has a strict exponential loss, with
every coupled edge factor retained. This is a loss from that
corner's rate, not yet a bound by hyperbolic volume. The remaining
contour and the original closed observation of the matching terms
still need estimates.

The [finite-kernel fold theorem](research_actual_low_newton_fold_packet.md)
now computes another local source coefficient. When a stationary wire
reaches the midpoint of its index interval, the ordinary endpoint
geometric-series estimate fails. The exact low-index sum has a uniform
cubic half-line profile instead. Its overlap with the original positive
stationary wire has coefficient \(+1\), with both level parities and
the endpoint forcing retained. This is a coefficient of that local
low kernel. It is not the coefficient of the closed knot invariant;
the high-index terms and original angular/current contraction remain.

The [full matching transport](research_full_radical_matching_unit_transport.md)
now combines all high-index correction terms into one explicit
unipotent map. On a fixed graph its inverse terminates after finitely
many matching terms, and both operator norms are polynomial in the
quantum level when all physical values and first derivatives are kept.
The original closing row is transported explicitly as \(\ell\mapsto\ell U\).
This is actual nilpotent transport on a fixed physical network.
It neither discards the derivative channels nor makes the final
scalar pairing positive.

With each first derivative divided by the quantum level, the
[scaled full-jet estimate](research_semiclassical_matching_unit_corollary.md)
sharpens this to \(U^{\pm1}=I+O(N^{-1})\) for every fixed graph.
The actual closing row changes by the same relative operator bound.
Its error after application to the source is still absolute:
it is bounded by \(O(N^{-1})\|\ell\|\|F_<\|\), rather than by
\(O(N^{-1})|\ell(F_<)|\). Exponential cancellation in that last
pairing remains the central issue.

On sufficiently short physical color windows away from \(c=2\), the
[analytic matching lift](research_analytic_matching_unit_window_lift.md)
now strengthens this comparison: both the matching unit and its
reciprocal have holomorphic representatives \(1+O(e^{-\gamma N})\)
on any prescribed fixed complex compact. Their complete window values
and derivatives are exact. They preserve a supplied nonzero local
Gaussian contribution, including its leading coefficient. The source
outside those windows and the occurrence of that local contour in the
original closing still require estimates.

The [relative Stokes calculation](research_actual_fold_relative_stokes_transport.md)
also computes how the local fold coefficient changes. In a controlled
complex overlap, the selected low-kernel saddle can lose its coefficient
while its eight geometric shapes stay positive. The endpoint period
and its integer transition matrix account for the change. Thus
positivity of the shapes cannot replace transport of the original
relative cycle. This is not a vanishing theorem for a closed knot source.

The actual filling equations do exclude that particular middle-endpoint
mechanism in the same-sign path family with powers of magnitude at
least three. The [filled-path separation theorem](research_filled_path_middle_endpoint_phase_separation.md)
shows that the geometric wire and its canonical middle endpoint have
strictly different imaginary actions throughout the full charge cube.
This concerns solutions of the filling equations, whereas the fold
counterexample used free complex boundary parameters.
The [zero-endpoint supplement](research_filled_path_zero_endpoint_phase_separation.md)
also proves, on every active edge of this family,
\[
       0<\Im\psi(t,u)<(\Re t+\Re u)/2 .
\]
Thus both specified fixed-endpoint alignments are excluded. This
does not compare a boundary whose angular variables have been
restationarized, other logarithmic branches, or the original
closed contour.

The [wire-endpoint angle comparison](research_wire_endpoint_angle_comparison.md)
now gives a general strict action gap for an entire family of boundary
assignments. It applies to any fixed graph with a supplied positive
parent solution, independent of the signs or sizes of its powers.
Every closed assignment obtained by setting a nonempty collection of
internal wire indices to zero lies strictly below the parent action,
with one uniform positive margin. All vertex equations remain in
force, including those made isolated by the deletion. These zero
indices are internal summation indices; the filling integers stay fixed.

For middle or mixed endpoints, an exact incidence-capacity test gives
the same gap whenever the missing angle data can be restored to the
original rows. Outside that test, the proof isolates an explicit
half-charge work term. Reflecting negative boundary charges shows that
only middle-incidence counts \(1,2,3\) have an adverse local charge
coefficient; larger counts have the favorable sign. This is a uniform
angle comparison, not a bound on the entire quantum boundary term.
The remaining source theorem must still control boundaries outside
this angle domain and prove that the geometric contribution survives
the original closing.

The [deleted-graph core theorem](research_deleted_graph_core_endpoint_gap.md)
now strengthens that test by moving the surviving angles. Repeatedly
remove selected vertices of deleted degree zero or one, retaining
complete outside vertices. If every selected middle-edge endpoint
survives this pruning, the entire closed boundary-angle maximum has
the same strict gap. In particular every pattern whose selected
middle degrees are zero or at least two is covered, including
branching of degree three. Zero-endpoint edges can also supply enough
support to cover some middle-degree-one vertices. The remaining
unpaid angle patterns have a middle endpoint on a pruned branch.
The construction is an energy comparison; it does not perform a
quantum source deletion or settle the original contour coefficient.

The [single-middle source adapter](research_middle_leaf_half_charge_adapter.md)
also identifies the actual remaining interface on a degree-two
middle path. Its even-level normal is exactly the already controlled
half-charge interpolation defect; the odd-level interface is the
retained top coefficient. The resulting whole-period bounds hold
at both parities for each fixed power of magnitude at least three,
including all ordinary outside derivatives. Interior path vertices
contribute explicit polynomial factors. The subsequent
[joint interface theorem](research_multileg_half_charge_source_bound.md)
now bounds any fixed number of retained edges at every fixed signed
power, including zero. It retains the mixed outside derivatives needed
by the original traces. The [product-and-trace theorem](research_half_charge_coupon_product_trace_bound.md)
now carries these bounds through shared outside variables and the full
original closing row. Its explicit weighted exterior norm remains
unestimated for an arbitrary short component. The
[turn-gluing calculation](research_turn_gluing_cost_in_coupon_norm.md)
shows why a direct norm argument does not close that step: the
actual joining kernel has exponential rate \(M_\infty\) in this
norm. Ordinary multiplication of the two output polynomials would
give a different connection.

There is now a source-specific replacement for that unrestricted
norm estimate. The [coherent turn-graph theorem](research_low_degree_coherent_turn_graph_bound.md)
uses the actual degree bound on the outside variables of the A/B
sources. It gives an exact physical-data Gram formula and polynomial
cost for all internal turns of any fixed graph of those sources,
including loops, fixed oriented edge powers, and the full remaining
exterior trace. Thus the extra \(M_\infty\) per turn is removed on
this prescribed class. The sum of local actions is still only an
upper bound; its comparison with the parent volume and a nonzero
joint leading coefficient are not established.
The [one-low-incidence extension](research_degree_cover_turn_graph_bound.md)
requires the degree condition at only one end of each untwisted edge.
The other tensors may keep their full degree and joint physical data.
Thus A/B-marked vertices forming a vertex cover suffice for the exact
polynomial-cost contraction, while their unmarked partners' source
bounds remain explicit requirements.

The [global low-halfwire boundary map](research_global_low_halfwire_boundary_pushforward.md)
now lifts the full/low matching relation to an exact differential
identity before integrating the wires. It retains an explicit finite
Laurent primitive, the ordinary physical-ideal remainder, and the
derivative of a wire-dependent co-source. Complete moving wire seams
cancel; partial arcs keep their actual endpoint values. The corrected
low residue is still the original full kernel. This constructs a
source-preserving boundary map without estimating those partial values
at the geometric action.

The [partial-wire observation theorem](research_partial_wire_boundary_observability.md)
now gives a polynomially conditioned Fourier reconstruction of the
entire original source from actual real partial-period observations.
Complete-period evaluation alone retains one Newton coefficient;
the partial-current frame recovers all \(N\), including the physical
normal data. Period plus finitely many primitive endpoint values also
suffice. This makes a full-source bound equivalent, at exponential
scale, to a bound on that whole real boundary family. It does not
make the specified complete period nonzero or control a complex
contour with the same bound.

The [continuous-filling rank/width theorem](research_continuous_filling_rank_fourier_width.md)
now rules out one proposed exact scalar simplification. Even the original
constant-input source needs differential order growing with \(N\) if
the coefficients have bounded Fourier width in the specified filling
parameter. Rational dependence on that parameter does not remove the
tradeoff. This concerns continuous filling, not the quantum recurrence
in the main color. An asymptotic geometric quotient still requires its
own source and boundary proof.

The [mixed low/radical theorem](research_mixed_low_radical_coupon_trace_bound.md)
now also treats the literal cutoff forcing \(A\otimes B\). The
radical factor \(B=e_{L+1}\) has the same half-charge action and a
nonzero complete local coefficient as \(A=e_L\), rather than only
an absolute-value envelope. Its bounds retain mixed physical
derivatives and the full joint exterior. This improves a real source
term in the recurrence, while leaving the homogeneous source and
the final coherent assembly unresolved.

The [ratio corollary](research_half_charge_period_ratio_geometric_coordinate.md)
now recovers the selected algebraic coordinate from those two actual
complete local sums: their ratio tends to
\(\rho_*=-\sin^2(t_*/2)\), and \(z_*=-2-4\rho_*\).
Their common exponential and normalization cancel in the quotient.
This gives an observed algebraic point of the local critical equation,
without asserting a knot \(A\)-polynomial identification or a global
nonzero coefficient.

The [even complete-row extension](research_even_complete_low_slit_relative_transport.md)
also proves that the actual low row divided by its last physical row
is \(1+O(N^{-1/2})\) on every fixed compact subset of
\(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\). Its normalized logarithm therefore
continues with the geometric phase throughout that slit domain.
This is a relative estimate for the actual finite polynomial, rather
than an upper bound obtained by continuation. It supplies neither an
arbitrary exterior contraction nor a coefficient for the closed knot.

The [holomorphic jet-quotient construction](research_bergman_jet_quotient_phase_transport.md)
now gives an exact functional model for the same finite source.
Holomorphic representatives carry a phase-weighted Bergman norm,
and their least-norm projection preserves every original physical
value and mixed normal. Every signed crossing power is an exact
isometry between the corresponding phase-dependent norms.
The original closing remains its prescribed bilinear row, with
an explicit positive Gram formula for its dual norm. This makes
weighted Cauchy--Schwarz precise without changing the invariant.
On the selected short windows, combining it with the analytic
matching lift gives exponentially near-identity full/low transport
uniformly in every holomorphic phase norm, retaining the actual
source and dual row.
The geometric bound for that fixed row, general turn transport,
and controlled global assembly of window representatives remain
unproved.

The [integral clock quotient](research_original_clock_quotient_and_affine_winding.md)
now distinguishes the auxiliary summation variables from the physical
color paths without passing to a finite cover. Its exact finite sums
retain the signed crossing matrices and the original closing. In the
stationary equations, a positive crossing has a compulsory clock
winding of one. Subtracting this specified character leaves a winding
on the physical-path lattice. Thus the exact cancellation of unwanted
finite sampling aliases does not justify discarding every nonzero
logarithmic winding. The marked edge comparison below now identifies
the residual winding, including its integer corrections. The original
cycle and closing estimate remain necessary.

The [reduced logarithmic presentation](research_reduced_physical_marked_logarithmic_lattice.md)
makes the remaining source equations integral as well. For every signed
diagram it gives explicit matrices \(A,B\), a parity vector \(\nu\),
and the exact equation
\(A\lambda+B\mu=\pi i(2\bar\chi-\nu)\), where \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\)
are the retained logarithms of the five source arguments and their
complements. Together with the physical monomial relations, these rows
form a primitive Lagrangian lattice for the signed shape form. This
retains integer data absent from the rational Bloch comparison. It does
not identify the rows with a positive triangulation's marked edge
equations or prove that the geometric contribution survives closing.

The [region-coordinate assembly](research_physical_region_logarithmic_assembly.md)
now writes those equations directly on the planar diagram, with both
crossing signs. Each physical index is an integer difference of the
adjacent region potentials. The original averaged marked cut already
sums its color, so this change of coordinates introduces no new
summation variable. The new calculation gives the local logarithmic
rows and their integer constants, then adds their actual region
occurrences. Planar flow duality itself was already established.
This makes the source equations explicit in the region coordinates
used by the geometric comparison. It does not supply the nonzero
coefficient of the final scalar.

The [crossing-tunnel construction](research_crossing_tunnel_shadow_cellulation.md)
now justifies the individual geometric face pairings inside the
original three-sphere. Cutting the added tunnel handles back out
recovers the original knot neighborhood and its peripheral curves.
This supplies an explicit proof of the earlier classical cellulation
claim and places the five source arguments on the same labeled
crossing ball. It does not make its developed tetrahedra positive
or replace the finite factorial endpoint sources by homogeneous
tetrahedron states. The selected contribution of the remaining
physical-flow sum is still the principal unresolved step.

The [sphere-vertex removal](research_free_sphere_vertex_lens_deletion.md)
now turns that crossing cellulation into a generalized ideal
triangulation of the same marked knot exterior. A two-tetrahedron
lens first creates an embedded disk in each spherical link. Replacing
the cone on that sphere by a cone on its complementary disk removes
the free vertex. Doing this twice leaves the original \(4c\)
tetrahedra and only the knot's torus end. The construction retains
every boundary face map, the meridian and the longitude, even when
edges or tetrahedra have repeated incidences. It supplies no quantum
identity for these replacements and no positive developed shapes.

The [local-move refinement](research_free_vertex_deletion_by_local_moves.md)
also removes both vertices using only lenses, \(2\leftrightarrow3\)
moves and one terminal \(4\to1\) per vertex. It handles nonregular
links by realizing two barycentric refinements without adding global
vertices. This localizes the types of quantum identities that would
be needed. Some introduced tetrahedra have coincident developed
vertices, so a regular-chart pentagon identity alone does not cover
the construction.

The [paired-face adapter from Kashaev's original definition](research_kashaev_paired_face_boundary_adapter.md)
now has an explicit inverse, cyclic boundary term and normalization.
Complementary charged face-pair sewing recovers the original wire
clock, including its \(N^2\) factor. The original fixed-index cut
also has an explicit image. For equidistant noncoinciding decorations,
its one-face marginal is positive with a polynomial lower bound.
This is a lower bound for positive observations on one face; it does
not control the full signed contraction. The crossing identity and
its global charge and cut comparison are now evaluated below. The
geometric contribution to that signed contraction still needs a
lower bound.

The [literal charged tetrahedron calculation](research_literal_charged_tetrahedron_bubble.md)
also proves Kashaev's inverse and three-face bubble directly from
the finite definitions, including the normalization sums. At odd
levels and regular decorations, its edge weights and vertex measure
cancel the bubble factor exactly under the specified link detour.
This verifies the published face-state identity. Assigning that
charged state and detour to our original marked free vertices,
including singular source limits, remains unfinished.

The [complete crossing evaluation](research_nine_cell_canonical_crossing_evaluation.md)
now evaluates that array at every allowed odd level and every boundary
index. The nine charged tetrahedron tensors give the specified planar
crossing tensor times an explicit nonzero scalar and a specified charge
phase. For any six distinct real vertex decorations, with real odd
roots, the scalar has modulus exactly \(N^{-2}\). No ordering of their
real values is required. The proof starts from the
[literal six-variable sum](research_nine_tetrahedron_boundary_source_reduction.md)
and evaluates it by three finite cyclic convolutions and finite binomial
identities. It retains the zero entries as well as the nonzero entries.
The earlier normalization obstruction is therefore resolved by an exact
scalar formula, whose phase is still retained. This settles a local
source comparison; it does not provide the geometric contribution to
the complete signed knot sum.

The [recoupling calculation](research_literal_clebsch_gordan_recoupling.md)
also derives the normalized change of basis and its pentagon directly
from the finite definitions. The
[protected-collision calculation](research_nine_cell_protected_collision_valuation.md)
proves that the actual crossing source vanishes to order at least
\(N-1\) when its two protected vertices coincide, canceling the
denominator of its inverse boundary adapter. These statements keep
their charge, root and normalization choices. The global construction
below now retains the original marked cut. Transport of its geometric
contribution, including arbitrary fixed short fillings, remains
unfinished.

The [two-cell wire calculation](research_literal_hamiltonian_wire_subdivision.md)
now supplies an exact interface for introducing a material vertex along
a strand. Its physical tensor is \(K=Z^{-1}/N\), where
\(Z_{jj}=q^j\). The actual normalized joining disk is \(S=NZ\), so
\(SKS=S\). Both possible orders of the strand's endpoints are covered
by explicit charges, and the original fixed-index cut \(E_{00}\) is
preserved. This compares fixed physical exterior arrays, with all
their decoration-dependent crossing scalars retained; it is not an
invariance theorem for changing those exterior decorations.

The [planar charge-change proof](research_planar_sector_gauge_and_open_cut.md)
also keeps both open-edge colors fixed. It expresses the difference
between two admissible corner-charge assignments as differences of
edge potentials that vanish at both ends. Changing the summation colors
by those potentials changes the entire open array by one explicit root
of unity. This is proved for every \(N\ge2\), including composite
levels, and counts repeated corner occurrences explicitly.

The [global sewing proof](research_braid_cut_and_global_nine_cell_sewing.md)
now assembles those finite identities for any supplied braid
presentation of a knot. At every odd level, the actual closed charged
tetrahedral source, with its original vertex normalization, has exactly
the absolute value of the original fixed-cut planar invariant. The
proof specifies the individual face maps, charges, global vertex order
and Hamiltonian closing arc; its explicit multiplier has modulus one.
This settles the constructed finite-source comparison. It supplies no
new filling assignment satisfying the volume identity and does not
improve the required large-level lower bound.

The [reciprocal-wall calculation](research_actual_reciprocal_wall_nine_cell_boundary.md)
now transports the specified finite five-point collision wall and its
nonzero lowering current to the actual nine-cell boundary. Their
physical norms are \(N\) and \(N|q^{-1}-1|\le2\pi\), respectively.
The explicit factorial endpoint factor, direction of the Fourier
shift and cyclic seams are retained. This local map does not identify
that finite wall with the entire negative-ray current of an analytic
period.

The [completed beta elimination](research_literal_beta_current_and_stationary_flags.md)
also transports arbitrary attached finite arrays, rather than only
the unit input used in the crossing evaluation. Its polynomial
continuation retains a nonzero multiple of \(1-k^N\); although this
term vanishes at the sampled roots, all its positive Fourier-normal
derivatives remain. The proof gives the associated local five-flag
stationary primitive and subexponential normalization on specified
fixed-log root paths. It does not identify the original analytic ray
cycle with a positive geometric cycle.

The [marked closing formula](research_marked_cap_for_arbitrary_open_observations.md)
now retains any prescribed linear observation after an insertion.
The bare closing cap agrees with the fixed cut on the unmodified
scalar knot operator; that comparison cannot be reused on an
arbitrary modified operator. An explicit diagonal boundary coupon
implements the supplied covector, with no additional exponential
norm cost. It keeps an averaged observation distinct from the
fixed-zero observation until their actual boundary coordinates have
been compared.

The [uniform ray estimate](research_uniform_full_dilogarithm_ray_transport.md)
now controls every physical degree: the actual negative-ray moments
have modulus between \(c/N\) and \(C/N\) for all sufficiently large
levels. The last degree has a second endpoint term, which the proof
keeps. The resulting finite transfer and its inverse have
polynomial norms, by the consecutive-moment improvement below.
This is a local operator result, not a lower
bound after closing a knot.

The [full ray-pattern comparison](research_full_psi_ray_crossings_and_nine_cell_boundary.md)
also transports the entire specified ray functional, rather than only
the finite collision wall. It gives both signed crossing arrays,
the actual original exterior observation, and an exact first beta
elimination under the original ray integrals. No ray contour is
replaced by a geometric contour. Choosing rays at all nine atoms
gives a crossing of norm \(O(N^{-3})\), with inverse norm \(O(N^6)\).
The mixed circle/ray patterns and the nonzero geometric coefficient
of their complete signed sum still require control.

The [consecutive-moment calculation](research_polynomial_ray_transport_and_normal_endpoint.md)
improves the ray-transfer inverse bound to \(CN\). Its Fourier
conjugate and inverse have counting-measure operator bounds
\(C\log(eN)/N\) and \(CN\log(eN)\), respectively, even after an
actual beta transform on that transform's own input index.
The same calculation finds zeros of a specified Mellin deformation
of the top ray moment at distance \(O(1/\log N)\) from its physical
value. This deformation has not been identified with a knot-meridian
parameter. Physical invertibility therefore gives no fixed complex
zero-free neighborhood for this ray, and no scalar lower bound.

The [nine-cell stationary calculation](research_nine_cell_regular_stationary_gate.md)
locates a separate problem with an interior stationary-phase argument.
After the exact shared-root relations are imposed, a regular limiting
stationary point forces all four physical boundary clocks to one.
If the commuting shift coordinates have finite nonzero limits, the
associated classical meridian matrices are then central.
Compatible auxiliary roots with finite nonzero limits do not change
this conclusion. A noncentral geometric contribution must instead
involve a boundary term, a singular chart, or another regime outside
those hypotheses. This is a statement about this nine-cell phase,
not an obstruction to the original invariant.

The [boundary residue calculation](research_nine_cell_pentagon_boundary_and_residue.md)
now gives an exact alternative to that interior chart. A specified
finite sampling sum is the negatively oriented residue at shape one,
with an arbitrary attached finite array retained as a polynomial
evaluation. Keeping the final coefficient's two cyclic contributions
then recovers the original five-factor crossing formula, with both
crossing signs and their phases. The simplest finite boundary surface
has constant normalized action; it is not the physical crossing
action. That action occurs in the retained boundary coefficient.
This supplies a rational residue representative of the local source,
not the global geometric contribution's nonzero coefficient.

The [endpoint transport formula](research_physical_packet_endpoint_cosource.md)
also retains the original boundary observation explicitly. A finite
product gives every clock-weighted cap and all its derivatives before
sampling. Some cap coefficients vanish on the physical grid but have
nonzero first derivatives there. In particular a specified rank-one
cap has a full-rank first clock derivative with polynomial condition
number. The inserted clock and flip are part of the formula; this
does not replace the original pivotal trace or prove a lower bound.

The [marked edge and peripheral comparison](research_marked_five_cell_edge_peripheral_lattice.md)
now proves that the five-cell edge equations, with one full meridian
equation added, generate exactly the source's integral stationary
lattice. The index is one. It also computes the logarithmic constants:
the internal edges have winding zero, the two arc families have
their actual encounter counts, and a region has winding
\(\xi_f+k_f/2\), where the explicitly computed \(k_f\) is even.
The remaining meridian coordinate is \(2\Log M\); the longitude
retains the writhe correction. This closes the integral comparison
at the complete character. It neither supplies positive tetrahedra
nor transports the generic quantum source or its integration cycle.

The [marked boundary calculation](research_marked_cusp_boundary_and_cut_residue.md)
also distinguishes the exact protected-face coefficient from the
geometric framing form. In the classical determinant chart, the two
protected zeros meet a divisor. Its logarithmic coefficient form is
regular on the finite part of the second exceptional divisor, whereas
the principal geometric form has a pole there. A section change toward
that boundary introduces a retained endpoint current at \(A=1\).
