The centered-clock comparison below now supplies the global
multiplicative labels across cups and caps, with their actual carry.
It does not supply the transverse or relative-cycle comparison.
No nonzero geometric coefficient follows from this boundary calculation.

The [quadratic-cover residue identity](research_protected_residue_quadratic_cusp_cover.md)
now transports the entire finite coefficient, keeping all ordinary
face variables independent. The boundary at \(r=\infty\) carries
twice the protected residue; the exact coefficient is half the
pulled-back integral. Relative to the geometric framing form, its
amplitude contains \(xW_r\), which changes sign between the two
branches and cancels one order of the pole at infinity. Dropping
that factor would instead give a zero algebraic trace. This
computes the full algebraic change of variables, but does not
justify specializing its transverse variables to the geometric
critical family or interchanging that specialization with the
boundary residue.

The [centered-clock adapter](research_centered_clock_checkerboard_adapter.md)
resolves the former global unit ambiguity by using \(X_i=qQ^i\).
Its dual is exactly \(X_{N-1-i}=X_i^{-1}\). One checkerboard sign
per face then matches the complete determinant ratios throughout
the original Morse diagram. The original coefficient keeps its
known checkerboard phase, and the two protected signs are opposite.
The finite relation \(X_i^N=-1\) remains separate from the
arbitrary geometric determinant assignment.

The [Jackson boundary calculation](research_crossing_jackson_boundary_jets.md)
now reconstructs every signed crossing from its protected-face
specialization by exact finite \(q\)-differences. It also proves
uniform local asymptotics with nonzero leading factors in explicit
neighborhoods. Retaining the physical half shift changes an
exponential limit into a confluent hypergeometric function. The
ordinary face-ratio contrast has curvature of order \(N^2\), so
its local scale is \(1/N\). These are estimates for the original
crossing polynomial, with all scalar phases retained. They do not
yet control the final signed coefficient after shared-face assembly.

The [choice-of-mark theorem](research_unique_main_mark_protected_corner_normal_form.md)
now bounds the number of boxes containing both protected faces
independently of the diagram size. Every connected original projection
has an allowed mark for which there are two adjacent-corner boxes, or
one box with three protected slots. For literal signed crossings,
the existing full-block fusion eliminates these factors exactly
against the entire attachment, retaining the \(q\)-shifts and any
cycle filter. Thus their narrow contrast layers need not be treated
by a new Gaussian integration. The remaining attachment, including
boxes with one protected face in one or two slots, still needs the
general geometric estimate.

The [full cap adjoint](research_protected_cap_all_jet_attachment_transform.md)
extends that exact corner elimination to all restored protected
variables. It is a finite Jackson operator on the entire attachment,
followed by the known phased merge. The operator depends on
derivatives transverse to the merged-face relation: even an
attachment vanishing identically on that relation can contribute
a nonzero first restored derivative. This identifies the data a
boundary asymptotic reduction must retain. It does not establish
their asymptotics or a nonzero final coefficient.

The [invertible cap translation](research_invertible_cap_normal_translation.md)
now retains the attachment in its exact two-variable coefficient
module. The Jackson lowerings are nilpotent, so the transport and
its inverse are finite sums with explicit coefficients. Both have
uniform norm bounds at the \(1/N\) protected scale and are
\(I+O(1/N)\) at scale \(1/N^2\). The bounds concern the whole
coefficient vector before its prescribed scalar closing.

The [minimal restored-cap module](research_minimal_restored_cap_normal_module.md)
identifies exactly which transverse coefficients that cap can
observe. There are \(N\) independent moments. Their quotient has
one nilpotent Jordan block, and its transport has an explicit
fundamental frame and exact composition law. After the remaining
original coefficient targets are extracted, the actual source
lies on the constant line of this module. Its coefficient
\(\gamma_N\) remains unknown, and the original scalar is
\(\lambda\gamma_N\). Neighboring face multiplication or individual
clock shifts need not preserve this cap-specific quotient.

The [compensated raising calculation](research_cap_observable_q_weyl_endpoint.md)
gives a genuine finite \(q\)-Weyl pair on that module and computes
the endpoint term in its exact conjugation. That term preserves
nilpotence even though its norm is superexponentially small on
the \(1/N\) boundary scale. A separate check against the original
small-circle operator shows that the whole neighboring Casimir
does not preserve the reduced cap kernel. Thus the local normal
transport is explicit, while its propagation through the original
neighboring operations remains an additional source comparison.

The [full phase-orbit construction](research_root_orbit_cap_observable_operators.md)
now supplies a larger quotient preserved by the two original
Casimir operators centered on the retained faces. It keeps all
root phases of the cap and has rank \(N(N+1)/2\). The full
signed Hermite crossing operators act invertibly on it, with
their original endpoints and closing row. Its exact single-crossing
coefficient-norm rate is still \(v_{\rm oct}/(2\pi)\); the larger
quotient retains the exponential cost. Operations centered on a
third face can leave its scope, and the selected closing value
still needs its geometric asymptotic estimate.

The [initialized endpoint calculation](research_terminal_phase_endpoint_connection.md)
now gives every local value and Jordan-normal observation weight
explicitly. All are nonzero and bounded above and below by powers
of \(N\). Its finite generating equation retains the last-row
current, and a literal cap-prepared source becomes a normalized
return amplitude \(N(U_{\rm phase})_{00}\).
This removes an unspecified initial cofactor from the local problem.
It does not control changes between successive operator bases or
the selected coherent sum for a whole diagram.

The [fixed-contour reciprocity formula](research_complex_color_mordell_gauss_reciprocity.md)
now expresses each signed full twist through \(2|p|\) explicit Gaussian
terms and one absolutely convergent Mordell integral, with its original
derivative data and all residues from contour translation. This is an
alternative to the already proved
[entire complex-color formula](research_complex_color_fresnel_fusion.md),
not a first construction of that continuation. Its benefit is that
finitely many twist slots can be combined using ordinary absolutely
convergent integrals at each level. It does not discharge a geometric
bound or noncancellation hypothesis in the short-component composition
theorem. The [existing endpoint estimate](research_complex_circle_endpoint_noncancellation.md)
shows why the attached exterior must remain in the argument: moving
the whole local coefficient to nonreal color retains an endpoint
exponential, rather than isolating the desired quadratic surgery action.

The [geometric transport bound](research_geometric_transport_level_dependent_metric_obstruction.md)
rules out one proposed way of avoiding that combined estimate. Even
positive inner products that depend arbitrarily on \(N\) cannot make
all symmetric-power transports of the complete geometric holonomy
subexponential. A fixed loxodromic loop forces exponential norm growth,
and every finite cover retains a power of that loop. This concerns
flat geometric transport, not an identification of quantum crossings
with holonomy matrices. It leaves contour choices based on the full
assembled phase available, and gives no conclusion about the knot
scalar's growth or cancellation.

The [physical-row product formula](research_physical_row_alternating_linearization.md)
now gives exact signs for every product whose degree stays at most
\(\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). Its coefficients alternate across their full
triangle support. An odd signed turn cancels those signs, leaving
positive amplitudes with explicit quadratic phases. Products of higher
degree require the derivative rows at repeated roots; those rows have
a triangular, rather than scalar, crossing action. The formula
preserves the original finite source but does not supply its closing
lower bound.

The [full product formula](research_physical_row_full_product_normal_support.md)
now also covers the higher degrees. Its derivative coefficient at
node \(\ell\) is a fixed sign times the positive original triple trace
\(\Gamma_{jk\ell}=\phi_N(F_jF_kF_\ell)\), and is nonzero exactly when
\(j+k+\ell\ge N-1\). The
[triple-trace estimate](research_physical_triple_row_pressure.md)
gives a uniform logarithmic rate on this entire support and a positive
\(N^{-3}\) Gaussian amplitude on strict interior ranges. Its action
is a strictly concave sum of nine ideal-tetrahedron volume functions.
The actual value coefficients still contain alternating derivative
tails, and the crossed closing still sums the original phases.
No signed knot-scalar lower bound follows from the positive triple
trace alone.

The [fold calibration](research_triple_row_fold_full_normal_calibration.md)
now controls the actual closing derivative as well as the values near
the midpoint of the color range. It uses one polynomial obtained from
the positive saddle window. The additional Newton terms activated by a
derivative have a strict boundary gap there. Near the simultaneous
midpoint it controls all eight mixed value and first-derivative entries.
The [finite fold trace estimate](research_triple_row_fold_alias_suppression.md)
then proves that the complete original closing over a small midpoint
window has a strictly smaller exponential rate than the positive
maximum, for every fixed signed crossing power and both level parities.
The remaining colors and the nonzero leading coefficient of the full
closing are still unresolved.

The [positive coefficient representation](research_physical_products_positive_coefficient_saddle.md)
now treats any fixed number of physical value rows together. It
expresses their original trace as one positive coefficient and gives
a uniform leading term by Fourier inversion of an exact sum of
Bernoulli and geometric variables. The estimate includes midpoint
rows and any fixed-degree polynomial inserted into the trace.
For three rows, the [common characteristic](research_triple_row_common_characteristic.md)
is selected by one strictly monotone algebraic equation. This ties
the pressure to the original Jacobi source equations. A filling
crossing still has degree growing with \(N\), and its cancellation
is not covered by the fixed-degree observation theorem.

The [general scalar pressure](research_physical_products_scalar_pressure.md)
now identifies that trace's exponential rate explicitly for every
fixed number of rows, including zero and midpoint indices with a
fixed support margin. A unique internal height solves a sum of
inverse-sine equations; the rate is the sum of the normalized row
actions minus that height. The variance of the coefficient
distribution equals the corresponding height Hessian after the
specified change of variable.

The [coherent mixed-normal theorem](research_physical_products_full_normal_coherent_contour.md)
also removes the value-only restriction before a crossing is
inserted. Every allowed mixed first normal is polynomially bounded
relative to the positive trace on that support range. In the bulk,
its leading coefficient is nonzero. One scalar contour packet
approximates all physical mixed jets with an exponential error
coming from the omitted circle arc and the explicitly paid branch
cut. This is a local bulk construction, not continuation to every
charged saddle or a lower bound after a further signed closing.

The [analytic insertion theorem](research_analytic_hermite_coupon_trace.md)
allows full Hermite interpolants of functions holomorphic on the
entire coefficient disk, even when their polynomial degree grows
with \(N\). Slowly varying exponentials have a nonzero relative
asymptotic and remain in this class under fixed ordinary products.
For slit representatives, the formula retains their cut, pole and
endpoint contributions. An actual filling crossing has an
exponential cut jump, so it is outside that slow class.

The [crossed physical-row theorem](research_crossed_physical_products_radial_contour.md)
retains an actual crossing phase in a complete scalar asymptotic.
Its two extensions now establish the following ranges for
\(Z_{p,N}=\phi_N(R^p\prod_i F_{j_i})\):

* [Powers of magnitude at least four](research_crossed_physical_products_bounded_minimax.md):
  any fixed number \(m\ge1\) of rows with
  \(\sum_i j_i\ge\delta N\), for fixed \(\delta>0\).
* [Powers of magnitude two or three](research_crossed_physical_products_two_three_radial_contour.md):
  any fixed \(m\ge3\), with
  \(\sum_i j_i-(N-1)\ge\varepsilon N\), for fixed \(\varepsilon>0\).

In both ranges the original scalar has a uniformly nonzero leading
coefficient. The contour proof bounds the reflected half, outer
intervals, endpoint connectors and every Fourier alias. It also
controls all allowed mixed first boundary derivatives: each has at
most a polynomial loss relative to the value trace, and derivatives
at interior indices have explicit nonzero leading multipliers.
Locally in those interior indices, one holomorphic function
approximates all the physical values and derivatives with an
exponentially small relative error. These are one-vertex results.
The complete signed contraction across a shared boundary, the
remaining power and index ranges, and the general geometric volume
identification still require proof.

The [continuation of a crossed block](research_crossed_block_regular_saddle_source_window.md)
now carries its actual values and first boundary derivatives along a
supplied regular family of geometric critical points. On a sufficiently
short consecutive range of boundary colors, these data have one exact
holomorphic representative with a nonzero Gaussian leading coefficient.
The construction includes the terms produced by moving the integration
endpoints. It removes the earlier restriction to a thin neighborhood of
the real boundary colors. It does not construct the required family for
an arbitrary short component or bound the complete next contraction.
The exterior sides of the window and the omitted colors remain.

The [fixed-fiber counterexample](research_strict_feasible_nonregular_angle_fiber.md)
also rules out a proposed geometric shortcut. A positive filling center
can coexist with strictly feasible real angles whose minimizing fiber
has degenerate cells. Thus strict linear feasibility cannot replace the
regularity hypothesis in the continuation theorem. This is a limitation
of that contour construction, not a counterexample to the volume identity.

The [compact-base bounds](research_strict_base_fiber_compactness_and_corner_subgradients.md)
make the remaining geometry more precise. On a compact subset of the
strict feasible real-angle domain, the original regular solutions have
bounded heights and periods. Their genuine degenerate limits have a
strict classical action gap from a supplied positive filling center.
The proof also computes the larger set of convex supporting vectors at
a corner; only its boundary corresponds to limits of geometric
gradients. Thus extending the convex minimization problem does not by
itself extend the geometric contour. The quantum estimate at those
degenerations remains to be proved.

The [composition theorem](research_physical_window_short_contraction_class.md)
now treats already contracted incoming boundary functions. Its inputs
are bounds on their physical values and first derivatives, together
with an exact holomorphic representative on a specified window.
Explicit inequalities on the incoming phases pay the untouched colors
and the complete deformed contour. Under those inequalities, the
outgoing function has the same type of bounds and an exact smaller
window with a nonzero leading coefficient. A separate root statement
proves noncancellation for the prescribed final scalar. Thus finite
composition is established when the stated domains and inequalities
hold at every step. They have not been verified for arbitrary fixed
short partial fillings.

The [positive Ward measure](research_positive_ward_measure_and_coherent_cauchy_tail.md)
gives an additional estimate valid without those composition hypotheses.
Its physical row polynomials are exactly orthogonal for a positive
measure on the spectral cut. The difference between a turned canonical
polynomial and its Ward representative is one Cauchy integral.
Orthogonality bounds that difference by reciprocal physical rows,
for arbitrary products and every integer crossing power. This keeps
the cancellations between the two Ward terms intact. The original
closing remains indefinite: the positive norm does not give a lower
bound for the knot invariant.

The [physical-row factorization](research_physical_rows_positive_ward_remainder.md)
now separates the zeros forced by the finite spectrum from a positive
Cauchy integral. For every physical value row, including the odd simple
row, the normalized integral is bounded above and below by powers of
\(N\) on each compact subset of the slit plane. The same identity
retains the original derivative rows by differentiating in the input
color. Its exact continuation also contains a term proportional to
\(P_N(c)\), which vanishes at the physical colors but must be retained
away from them. This proves control of the positive remainder for an
entire family of rows; arbitrary products and signed sums of those rows
still require a separate noncancellation argument.

The [Christoffel–Darboux calculation](research_physical_ward_cd_action_and_normals.md)
also identifies the remaining exponential factor, uniformly over the
whole real input interval \([-2,c_0]\). The ratio \(U_c(C)\) between
the Ward and canonical physical rows has logarithm
\(N[\Psi(c)-\Psi(C)]+o(N)\), with an \(O(\log N)\) error on compact
subsets of \(\Re C<2\). Here \(\Psi\) is the existing calibrated
complete-edge action. The original derivative rows have polynomial
upper bounds relative to this factor. These estimates describe the
chosen representatives of individual rows. Applying them to an
arbitrary input still requires its original turned coefficients and
the prescribed closing; the action difference cannot simply be
cancelled along a tangle diagram.

The [full Ward crossing theorem](research_ward_cut_jet_crossing_propagation.md)
now retains the information lost by that positive value norm. Both
polynomial Ward channels, together with the odd simple value, give a
positive norm on the entire original finite algebra. Their normal
connection has operator norm \(O(N^3(1+\log N))\). Every integer
crossing and its inverse act with polynomial cost in this norm, and
the original scalar closing has dual norm at most \(\sqrt5\).
The explicit evolution contains both the quadratic phases and the
normal shear. This supplies a full source for Fourier estimates;
it gives no bound for a subsequent turn or product and no scalar
lower bound.

The critical task is now to obtain the composition theorem's global
contour inequalities from the geometry of an arbitrary short partial
filling, or replace them by a proved contour argument that covers it.
The Ward correction estimate supplies part of the required control;
it does not bound the remaining representative. A positive geometric
critical point and a classical volume gap alone still do not bound all
terms of the finite quantum sum.

The follow-up comparison with Fourier analysis locates the missing
estimate more concretely. Crossing acts unitarily on the finite
orthogonal-row space, but point evaluation has the same norm for every
crossing power; this loses the cancellation needed for the charged
action. Summation by parts leaves a bulk oscillatory sum. Its bound
must use the actual coefficients of the received short component and
their first-normal connection. On the geometric contour, the analogous
unpaid term is the primitive along a moving corner face: a local bound
for its derivative does not bound its value fixed by integration from
the original endpoint. Neither observation is a counterexample to
the desired identity. They identify estimates not supplied by the
present positive norms or local geometric gaps.

The return to the torsor construction also rules out a tempting
algebraic shortcut. The
[positive-tetrahedron calculation](research_positive_tetrahedron_pointed_projection_zero.md)
exhibits, at level three, a positive regular tetrahedron whose
distinguished vector is killed by a nonzero primitive monomial
projector. Thus positive central shapes and nonzero reduced-module
rank do not by themselves prove a nonzero projected state. This is
not a knot-gluing counterexample: the displayed local incidence has
angle sum \(\pi\), and no full interior edge is supplied. A useful
global theorem must retain the actual \(2\pi\) edge equations,
their prescribed characters, and the comparison with the original
source. The existing invertible local ordering and pentagon maps
transport a supplied state; they do not replace this missing
projection argument.

The [single-edge nonvanishing theorem](research_single_edge_pointed_nonvanishing.md)
now proves what those additional conditions give for one genuine edge.
With positive tetrahedra, an angle sum of \(2\pi\), paired face
occurrences, and a primitive nonzero edge row, every compatible
single-edge projector is nonzero on the original tensor pointing.
The statement holds at all levels, including even and composite ones.
For one-ideal-vertex knot triangulations, the integral edge theorem
supplies the required individual primitivity. This repairs the
one-edge inference using actual incidence data. It does not yet
prove nonvanishing of the simultaneous edge projection: the first
projection generally produces an entangled tensor, so the same
support proof cannot be iterated without a new argument.

The [joint character theorem](research_joint_edge_character_bootstrap.md)
now supplies such an argument under an explicit incidence condition.
The exact tetrahedron equations relate the simultaneous character
components of the original tensor. They force the set of zero components
to be invariant under a subgroup computed from the integral edge
incidences. If that subgroup contains the kernel of restriction to one
genuine edge, a zero component would make a whole single-edge projection
zero, contradicting the preceding theorem. An integral subgroup
inclusion makes this conclusion valid at every level. The condition has
now been checked against complete geometry, with a negative result:
the [complete geometric incidence theorem](research_complete_positive_no_axis_incidence.md)
shows that this propagation cannot even start at any level \(N\ge3\).
For edge rank at least two, the criterion therefore cannot prove
joint nonvanishing on a complete positive geometric triangulation.
Its algebraic proof remains valid under its stated condition, and the
rank-one single-edge result is unchanged. It supplies no new knot
coverage. The original scalar and its exponential lower bound remain
separate tasks.

The geometric obstruction has a short direct proof. Complete cusp
holonomy permits equivariant nonzero vectors modulo sign at the lifted
ideal vertices. Their squared determinants give one nonzero number
\(d_e\) on each global unoriented edge. Each squared tetrahedral shape
is a ratio of the products on two opposite edge pairs. The repeated
label multisets required to start the propagation would force that
shape to have square one, contradicting positivity. A further consequence
is that every tetrahedron whose full local edge constraints have rank one
is regular. In a connected triangulation with \(T>2\), their edge-label
pairs are disjoint, so at least \(\lceil T/2\rceil\) tetrahedra have
rank-two local constraints. Thus complete geometry requires a substantial
number of tetrahedra with two independent local edge directions.
The next joint argument must handle their interaction, including their
level-dependent commutators, or supply a different exact source
representation.

The [finite-cover theorem](research_complete_positive_cover_neighbor_matching.md)
also tests a stronger local proposal. A zero component gives three
invertible relations between neighboring character components for each
tetrahedron. Loops among those relations could in principle impose
incompatible holonomies. However, every complete positive geometric
triangulation has a finite normal cover in which these immediate
relations form a disjoint matching at every \(N\ge3\), with no loops.
The cover need not be a knot exterior, and no quantum state is
identified between cover and base. The result shows that these initial
loops are not a universal consequence of complete geometry. Longer
relations involving several tetrahedra would be needed.

Returning to the original finite source gives a separate restriction.
The [open threading theorem](research_open_star_even_threading_scalar.md)
proves the even-thread identity with every tangle boundary index left
uncontracted. If the auxiliary loop has relative linking number zero,
its \(2N\)-th Chebyshev threading multiplies the entire array by two.
The difference from twice the unthreaded array is therefore identically
zero, including every meridian derivative at fixed \(q\). This holds
with the original marked cap, despite that cap not being a quantum-group
intertwiner. Leaving the boundary open does not recover a hidden
coefficient from this particular difference. A derivative in \(q\)
would require a specified off-root family and a separate calculation;
neither its nonvanishing nor a geometric contribution follows here.

That derivative has now been computed for the specified zero-framed
annulus around a pair of strands. The
[pair normal theorem](research_even_threading_first_normal_casimir_radical.md)
gives a nonzero square-zero operator at every level. It is precisely
\(J_N=4(I-(-1)^{N-1}R^{2N})\), where \(R\) is the original crossing
with its full scalar normalization. Its prescribed closing is
\(-4i(-1)^{N-1}N^2/\sin(\pi/N)\). This supplies an exact connection
between the derivative of the threading and the already retained
Jordan data of the crossing. It adds no independent transport estimate:
one original quarter-turn followed by closing annihilates \(J_Nf\)
for every pair polynomial \(f\). A nonzero local normal therefore
does not establish the required nonzero contribution after the
particular short component is attached.

The [full row and closing calculation](research_confluent_row_closing_and_positive_quotient.md)
now identifies the coefficient that the original closing extracts.
It also classifies every positive semidefinite form preserved exactly
by the conjugated crossing \(V_1\). All such forms lose directions
that one original multiplication crossing can restore to the closing.
Consequently no such exactly invariant norm can both control the
closing and propagate every input through that crossing, even with
an arbitrarily large finite level-dependent bound. Approximate
invariance on the particular knot source remains a separate possibility.

The separate microscopic-endpoint result covers every fixed filling power
\(|n|\ge2\) for one original trace with any fixed product of bounded
real microscopic endpoint factors and complete output. The two-power
case now includes the full endpoint contribution, not just its local
critical point. This is a source theorem; it does not yet cover an
arbitrary short partially filled component.

There is also a proved obstruction to one proposed extension.
The [exact real-zero theorem](research_microscopic_common_circle_real_zeros.md)
shows that a general upper-bound class cannot be given a uniform
nonzero scalar closing for arbitrary real endpoint marks. Some
original finite sums in that class vanish exactly, even when the
mark tends to zero and the local amplitude has a nonzero derivative.
The next lower-bound statement must therefore use the boundary
data and closing prescribed by the actual knot construction.
These continuous-mark examples are not counterexamples to the
knot volume conjecture.

The subsequent source audit fixes the role of those parameters.
The real marks are actual variables in the vertical-current
integrals, not extra choices in the knot. Those integrals need
upper estimates. The required lower estimate concerns the
original geometric contribution after its prescribed closing,
or the coherent total if other contributions remain at the
same rate. Pointwise nonvanishing of every current integrand
is unnecessary.

The [full-height angle comparison](research_saturated_current_full_height_angle_envelope.md)
now extends the classical boundary gap over the entire height box
when every removed power has magnitude at least two. For arbitrary
powers it gives an exact finite collection of convex minimizations.
This is a classical result conditional on a positive parent geometry.
The same note disproves a proposed pointwise quantum transfer:
an edge joining two removed vertices has an additional positive
exponential rate that the classical envelope does not include.

The [integrated-current estimate](research_integrated_unit_current_norm.md)
shows that this distinction survives integration. A single vertical
current has an explicit exponential norm rate,
attained by original endpoint-kernel products. Its horizontal
companion cancels that growth in the original trace. Separately,
[integration of shared microscopic modes](research_shared_microscopic_current_mode_integration.md)
gives sharp powers of \(N\) and \(\log N\) for a bounded microscopic
height interval. Those gains are subexponential. Neither result
supplies the general partial-filling volume theorem.

The [joint vertical-current theorem](research_all_removed_vertical_current_asymptotic.md)
now also evaluates the term in which every vertex of a fixed graph
is integrated vertically. For nonzero powers and no isolated vertex,
its leading coefficient is nonzero and its rate includes the full
internal-edge cost. Integrating these vertices together therefore
does not remove that cost. The cancellation question concerns the
original combination with the horizontal terms.

The [remaining low-kernel integral](research_low_kernel_all_removed_current_asymptotic.md)
has now been evaluated as well. Contracting the entire high Newton
radical halves the internal-edge endpoint rate but does not eliminate
it. Under the precise condition \(d_v+|n_v|>2\), its joint vertical
integral still has a nonzero leading coefficient at both parities.
Thus the next estimate must control the original recombination,
rather than assume that radical removal has already removed every
exponentially large endpoint contribution.

The [physical-residue estimate](research_compact_positive_contour_residue_control.md)
now bounds the complete contribution of any specified set of physical
poles in a fixed graph. It includes every physical color, edges joining
two frozen vertices, and the derivatives required at repeated roots.
After the remaining original traces are retained, these derivatives
have the same exponential upper rate as the physical row values.
The remaining complex angles must stay in a fixed compact part of
the positive domain. This removes a local cost from contour transport;
it does not yet connect the geometric contour to the entire original
integration cycle.

The [normal-connection theorem](research_physical_row_slit_normal_connection.md)
also fixes the derivative normalization of the analytic row interpolant.
Its value and derivative now come from one scalar function, with the
original mixed derivatives preserved at the physical grid. The second
color can range over any fixed compact subset of its slit plane; the
interpolated first degree still lies in a thin neighborhood of a real
bulk interval.

The [regular positive continuation theorem](research_physical_row_regular_positive_continuation.md)
now extends the constructed, correctly normalized mode to complex
charts reaching every positive pair away from the first-degree fold.
It does not require that the selected recurrence root remain larger
in modulus than the other root. One-sided Hermite correction preserves
the exact original window values and derivatives with an exponentially
small normalized error on its designated side. Opposite-side closing,
exterior window sides and all rows outside the window remain.

The [endpoint-role comparison](research_physical_row_endpoint_role_overlap.md)
now compares constructions made by treating opposite endpoints as
the degree variable. Their normalized difference is exponentially
small on connected common domains with a shared physical seed and
the same calibrated action. The proof uses both physical grids;
agreement of local source classes alone would not give this bound.

The [product-window construction](research_positive_product_window_gluing.md)
now joins these local functions into one holomorphic baseline on a
fixed product domain. A finite Cauchy integral performs the joining;
comparison with the opposite-endpoint construction controls its error.
An explicit finite correction then restores both families of physical
row values and derivatives exactly. Its exponential upper bound holds
in each designated quadrant. This result covers the selected bulk
windows; the remaining rows and the full original contour still matter.

The [fold-window extension](research_positive_product_fold_window_extension.md)
also includes the midpoint and every nearby physical row. Its proof
compares the common baseline with the actual kernel on a small complex
neighborhood of completeness, then propagates the row errors using
uniform row bounds. A contour enclosing both angular lifts has half
the earlier prefactor. It counts the odd-level central value exactly
once and does not introduce a derivative at that simple spectral root.

The [short spectral-window theorem](research_short_spectral_window_repair.md)
now removes the real repair interface entirely on sufficiently short
blocks of consecutive physical colors. After symmetrizing the common
baseline, ordinary spectral Hermite interpolation restores the exact
values and normals with an exponentially small error throughout the
fixed complex product domain. The same function works on both angular
sides. The remaining terms are the exterior boundaries of these blocks
and their differences when adjacent blocks use different representatives.

The [coherent Fourier alias theorem](research_coherent_window_fourier_alias_transport.md)
gives an exact cancellation that an absolute real-profile estimate misses.
When normalized value and derivative errors come from one analytic
function, subtracting its actual endpoint cubic removes the zero
Poisson alias from the interior pairing. The remaining interior has
the original unit filling charge and an exponential saving. The cubic
and vertical endpoint integrals remain an explicit finite packet;
controlling that packet after the original closing is still necessary.

The [overlapping-window theorem](research_overlapping_spectral_window_seam_transport.md)
now joins these estimates at the level of the exact trace. Enlarge each
repair window slightly beyond its assigned color block. Neighboring
representatives then agree in value and required derivative on the shared
colors, so their difference cancels those trace poles. Their boundary
integrals can be transported through the overlap without new residues
at its physical colors. All endpoint terms and the bounds for the full
remaining integrand are still required.

The [finite-partition endpoint identity](research_partitioned_window_endpoint_regrouping.md)
now combines the Fourier endpoint terms exactly. The auxiliary cubics
cancel, and each internal cut contributes one joined chain carrying
the neighboring error difference divided by the original trace
polynomial. Passing to the common union pairing also changes the
exterior half-boundaries; the formula retains that change. Its top
terms have the unit-charge estimate, while the joined internal chains,
outer terms, common baseline and unmatched rows remain explicit.

The [higher-face theorem](research_window_higher_faces_and_edge_cover.md)
now supplies an exact cancellation for finite networks. A changed edge
is annihilated by the closed trace at its unchanged neighboring window.
Consequently a surviving set of opened vertices has no isolated vertex
in its induced represented graph. Its error coefficient gains the sum
of the interpolation rates over a minimum weighted edge cover. Mixed
corners remain even on one edge, and the estimate precedes the remaining
closing and the outer contour terms.

The [signed-turn calculation](research_physical_row_fourier_positivity_under_turns.md)
also settles a proposed positivity shortcut. Individual physical kernel
rows are exact turn eigenvectors. Their ordinary two-incidence product,
however, loses Fourier positivity after either unit turn at every
level \(N\ge5\), and has a nonreal spectral zero. Those zeros approach
the endpoint \(+2\); they are not a counterexample to a fixed geometric
chart or to a knot volume identity.

The [additive half-wire regularization](research_additive_half_wire_source_regularization.md)
is a second concrete step toward changing the representation before
estimating it. It replaces the reflected half of an internal edge
integral by an inverse-kernel term, with the exact difference invisible
to the original full trace. A finite collection of thin contours gives
this inverse term an arbitrarily small exponential upper rate locally
in the angular parameters. Its moving poles, contour transitions and
endpoint segments are explicit. The main half and the bounded assembly
of these local representations remain to be controlled.

The [fixed-wire collar reduction](research_fixed_wire_collar_source_reduction.md)
now isolates a fixed interior wire segment. The remaining two local
endpoint pieces have arbitrarily small exponential upper rates on
buffered angular compacts. The exact replacement has zero primitive
on fixed wire cuts, but retains its primitive integrals on additional
angular or exterior faces. The action at the interior segment's fixed
endpoints and the full contribution of those faces still need control.

The [absolute-wire barrier](research_positive_wire_absolute_barrier.md)
rules out a proposed shortcut for that last step. On an open family
of positive edge parameters, every bounded-height wire contour
crossing a specified interior strip has absolute integral growing
faster than the selected saddle rate. Moving the fixed cut transfers
the excess to the inverse piece. This concerns the sum of absolute
integrals, not their signed sum or the knot invariant. The remaining
argument must retain coherent cancellation or coupled angular motion.

The [inverse-contour estimate](research_inverse_half_strip_contour_bounds.md)
extends that small rate to detours around moving poles, grouped
collision residues and both endpoint connectors. The distance from
the poles may shrink as a fixed inverse power of the level. This
controls all inverse pieces of the contour transitions, while
retaining their exact orientations and parameter derivatives.

The [finite Sears source theorem](research_finite_sears_full_normal_source.md)
now supplies an exact four-factorial representation with the original
independent first and mixed spectral derivatives. Its finite recurrence
retains the cutoff flux and fixes the derivative normalization. The
representation is local: its diagonal poles and off-grid cutoff
transitions still require a coherent contour treatment.

The [slit-domain comparison](research_inverse_half_slit_domain_source_comparison.md)
also constructs common even holomorphic domains for complete periods
at different inverse-half heights. The original full traces cancel
the entire difference exactly. This does not require an estimate of
the main-half primitive, but it does require the full angular contour
and its slit detours. Individual interface faces of a patched
geometric contour have not been deleted by this result.

The current boundary analysis contains several proved components. The
[fixed-height comparison](research_fixed_parent_height_global_calibration.md)
places the geometric maximum above every other point of its positive
horizontal domain. The
[all-top current estimate](research_microscopic_all_top_current_gap.md)
gives an actual quantum gap for its stated microscopic terms and
certified remaining forests. The
[marked-forest theorem](research_marked_forest_full_endpoint_current_gap.md)
now bounds the entire microscopic current when a specified
leaf-removal sequence keeps endpoint factors at their marked
vertices until exact evaluation or an isolated trace.
The [single-factor turn theorem](research_full_endpoint_unit_turn_polynomial_bound.md)
now permits one unit turn of one full microscopic endpoint
factor, with polynomial cost and all original normals retained.
The [repeated-turn comparison](research_repeated_endpoint_unit_turn_action_growth.md)
shows that this polynomial bound cannot be iterated: two turns
of the same sign already acquire positive exponential growth.
For any fixed number of turns, the transformed endpoint norm
and the corresponding original terminal-source norm differ only
by polynomial factors. General composition must retain this
terminal action, rather than assuming repeated polynomial closure.
The [finite operator theorem](research_unit_turn_finite_band_branching_operator.md)
now gives exact conjugation formulas, a quantum cubic, and a
denominator-free recurrence for every integer twist power.
At a vertex with several endpoint factors, it also identifies the
additional mixed forcing and both initial data needed to bound
the resulting polynomial. The derivative datum is a genuine
generalized eigenvector of the conjugated operator. These identities
retain the quantities whose exponential growth still needs control.
The [terminal characteristic theorem](research_terminal_twist_characteristic_geometry.md)
classifies the associated classical branches for every nonzero
integer twist power. Distinct physical shift roots cannot collide
in the interior, although each still has double multiplicity.
This removes interior collisions for this operator from the list
of unresolved issues; it does not establish bounds on transport
between the branches or on their source coefficients.
The [bulk transfer theorem](research_terminal_twist_bulk_transfer_bound.md)
now supplies an actual upper bound for the terminal value and
derivative system on each compact interior interval. Its exponent
is the integral of the largest characteristic growth, with
an \(O(\sqrt N+\log N)\) loss. The
[modulus-order theorem](research_terminal_twist_global_modulus_order.md)
proves that the same branch is largest throughout the interval,
for every fixed nonzero twist power.
The [whole-terminal theorem](research_whole_terminal_characteristic_upper_bound.md)
now joins this interior estimate to polynomial source initialization
and coarse propagation through both endpoint regions.
It bounds the entire terminal polynomial and its derivative
companion by the integrated characteristic action, for every fixed
signed power. Both original boundary anchors have this same upper
rate when multiplied by a polynomially bounded spectator.
No lower coefficient or filled-volume identity follows.
For a product of endpoint factors, the
[tensor closure theorem](research_endpoint_product_tensor_annihilator.md)
now gives an exact system of rank bounded independently of \(N\),
including the original forcing and first derivatives.
Its bounded-order operator relation survives the original turns.
The [divided-difference construction](research_endpoint_product_divided_difference_module.md)
now gives a more controlled system: its leading characteristic
contains only the transported endpoint condition and the original
terminal condition. A polynomial change of channels removes
spurious denominator factors without dividing out the source.
The [whole-product estimate](research_turned_endpoint_product_characteristic_upper_bound.md)
first bounded every fixed product after a fixed signed number of
turns by twice the terminal characteristic action. The
[first-turn initialization theorem](research_first_turn_endpoint_product_initialization.md)
now removes the initial exponential cost and improves that upper
rate to the terminal action itself. It proves a subexponential
bound simultaneously for the actual first turn and every gauged
source channel needed in the later recurrence.
One unit turn therefore has subexponential cost.
The [literal filled-leaf estimate](research_filled_leaf_endpoint_product_upper_bound.md)
now gives the same terminal upper rate for \(T(R^nB_N)\), with the
crossing and all original endpoint factors inside the leaf trace.
Its actual initial values and derivatives have polynomial bounds.
The [physical-color refinement](research_filled_leaf_physical_color_profile.md)
retains the exposed color: at row \(j\), the upper exponent is
\(\int_0^{j/N}L_n(u)\,du\), rather than its maximum
\(\mathcal I_n\). This partial integral equals the real part
of the normalized stationary leaf action at that boundary angle.
It controls actual physical values and first normals.
The [weighted window formula](research_filled_leaf_weighted_window_current.md)
now constructs holomorphic representatives of those exact data
on either half-plane, with the calibrated leaf phase as an upper
exponent. Their use in the original trace is exact, but introduces
an explicit real interface and retains both outer vertical sides.
The bound for this whole joined contour at the parent volume rate
is still missing.
The [normalized leaf adjoint](research_filled_leaf_normalized_jet_adjoint.md)
now uses the exact recurrence to control its Fourier observation.
Away from the specified characteristic frequencies, the interior
sum reduces to two actual endpoint packets with exponentially
small error. For powers of absolute value at least two, the
calibrated phase places the sole normalized characteristic
frequency at zero modulo integers. The integer-frequency
contributions and the external endpoint packets still require
their original closing estimates.
The [slow-state reduction](research_filled_leaf_slow_graph_reduction.md)
now also treats the characteristic sector for \(|n|\ge2\).
After a fixed left buffer, the actual normalized state is
exponentially close to a holomorphic graph of rank \(4\,6^r\),
where \(r\) is the fixed endpoint-factor count. This rank is
independent of the twist magnitude. The graph retains the
independent first-normal copy. Its transfer and inverse cost
only subexponentially. The
[regular-amplitude theorem](research_filled_leaf_regular_amplitude_transport.md)
now improves that cost to a polynomial in \(N\) for each fixed
bulk interval. An exact symmetry of the finite difference operator
removes the first-order error at its double geometric root.
The remaining slow transfer becomes \(I+N^{-1}B_N\), with bounded
\(B_N\), after a polynomially conditioned change of coordinates.
A nonzero initial projection and a noncancelling scalar closing
are still required.
The [ordinary-residual theorem](research_filled_leaf_exact_bivariate_residual.md)
also determines the term hidden by reduction to the physical algebra.
For a single endpoint kernel the filled source is a symmetric
polynomial of total degree \(N-1\); its ordinary difference-equation
residual is an explicit multiple of \(P_N(Z)\). Subtracting the
undecorated terminal removes that residual exactly. The same
cancellation holds for an endpoint difference in a product, with
the original mixed forcing retained. This gives ordinary polynomial
uniqueness, but no bound for the inverse.
For undecorated terminals and fixed physical endpoint marks, the
[scalar compatibility theorem](research_terminal_bulk_scalar_compatibility.md)
now supplies one holomorphic function matching both the original
values and first derivatives on every fixed interior color interval.
After removal of the calibrated phase, its amplitude is polynomially
bounded on a fixed narrow complex neighborhood. The proof uses the
actual terminal asymptotic near complete output as its initial scalar
data. Products at a shared color therefore need no separate
derivative-mismatch term on such an interval. The prescribed complex
heights of a parent geometry and the exterior boundaries remain
outside this result.
The [complex continuation theorem](research_terminal_one_sided_characteristic_continuation.md)
now continues a common approximate amplitude through any supplied
regular complex domain where the selected double characteristic
remains separated. An analytic differential equation approximates
the finite recurrence with exponential accuracy. Exact corrections
on the two sides of the real interval then differ by an exponentially
small interface. This saving has a fixed size determined by the
domain; it must still be compared with the remaining source's rate.
Neither the required complex domain nor an exterior-current bound
is asserted for an arbitrary short component.
For the unturned microscopic insertion, the
[common-baseline theorem](research_unturned_endpoint_complex_baseline_and_window.md)
now verifies continuation on every bounded buffered subdomain of
\(0<\Re x<1/2\). Its balanced original recurrence is already
\(I+O(N^{-1})\), so no additional characteristic-separation
hypothesis is needed there. The theorem also bounds the entire
positive-endpoint physical window with both outgoing-kernel channels.
The opposite endpoint and exterior currents remain outside that
result. The sharper bulk error estimates are described below.
The [partial-kernel Green estimate](research_partial_endpoint_green_boundary_budget.md)
now propagates the actual truncation forcing at its product rate,
uniformly through its zeros and with first normals. Its formula
retains the specifically normalized baseline's boundary mismatch
on every fractional grid, and the baseline's own ordinary residual.
That Green formula does not supply the required sharper bounds for
those two terms. The newer local construction below bypasses this
comparison with the older baseline.
The [exact period calculation](research_unturned_endpoint_exact_period_monodromy.md)
now determines the two-dimensional transfer around one whole angular
period. Its determinant is one and its trace is
\(2+P_N(w)\cot^2(\pi Nx)\), with every repeated physical eigenvalue
retained. For \(w=2\cosh(\alpha/N)\), its two multipliers approach
\(-e^\alpha\) and \(-e^{-\alpha}\) at fixed nonzero imaginary height.
This identifies the available branches. The original kernel has an
inhomogeneous forcing term, so these multipliers alone neither select
its continuation coefficients nor bound the remaining Green terms.
The [fixed-height source asymptotic](research_unturned_endpoint_forced_off_real_asymptotic.md)
does determine the leading term of the actual kernel away from the
real axis:
\[
 \frac{N^2K_N(2\cosh(\alpha/N),c_N(x))}{P_N(c_N(x))}
 =-\frac{\cosh^2(\alpha/2)}{\pi^2+\alpha^2}\csc^2(\pi x)
   +O(N^{-1}).
\]
It holds uniformly on fixed nonreal bands for bounded complex
\(\alpha\), through the removable physical parameters, with
derivatives. The proof retains the forcing and uses the bounded
periodic inverse. It describes an exponentially large part of the
canonical kernel; it does not yet isolate the smaller homogeneous
contribution needed near the physical line.
The [sine-factor construction](research_endpoint_sine_factor_sharp_truncation.md)
now gives an explicit approximate homogeneous basis with the sharp
residual exponent \(J_*\), on bulk rectangles of any fixed height.
It uses the normalized factorial interpolation and a finite descending
index expansion. Matching two actual physical values gives a sharp
value comparison. This statement retains a separate first-normal
anchor and does not assert a sharp comparison between nodes.
The [reflection argument](research_reflected_endpoint_sharp_normal_connection.md)
now controls that first-normal anchor too. A spectral divided difference
removes the apparent singularity where adjacent colors coincide.
Reflection reverses the derivative of the connection coefficients,
whereas the recurrence changes it only by the sharp residual.
Together these facts force the derivative coefficient to be exponentially
small. Thus the same explicit scalar approximates both actual physical
jets with the sharp local rate, while remaining moderate at fixed
complex height. This does not estimate the older baseline between
nodes or establish a filled-current bound.
The [sharp one-sided assembly](research_sharp_endpoint_one_sided_window_assembly.md)
now turns this approximation into exact local representatives of both
physical jets. On a sufficiently small fixed window about any bulk
point, their real interface has every rate strictly below the local
\(J_*\). Both designated half-plane amplitudes remain moderate at
fixed height. Thus this local construction bypasses the old
fractional-grid comparison; its exterior sides, the joint spectator,
and the nonzero geometric contribution still require estimates.
The [finite parameter atlas](research_endpoint_sharp_local_parameter_atlas.md)
extends these sharp local results to every bounded complex endpoint
parameter set. At the apparent index poles it subtracts an explicit
reflected finite sum with the same eigenvalue; the other resonances
terminate. The resulting analytic bases and exact representatives are
local in parameter space, with uniform estimates on a finite cover.
No agreement of their off-grid choices on chart overlaps is asserted.
The [nonreal insertion theorem](research_endpoint_nonreal_insertion_lower_bound.md)
now also controls the actual leading coefficients of the new baseline.
On a fixed nonreal compact it and the exact designated-half
representative have magnitude at least \(c/N\), uniformly for bounded
real endpoint parameters, including zero. Their conjugate modes have
unequal magnitudes there, so their oscillation in \(\log N\) cannot
cancel the insertion. Fixed products therefore preserve an already
supplied nonzero local Gaussian contribution. This does not establish
that the original global cycle contains that contribution or prevent
cancellation with its other terms.
The [compact contour theorem](research_sharp_endpoint_compact_interface_and_seams.md)
now bounds the real interfaces and joins between neighboring spatial
patches for every fixed signed power with \(|n|\ge2\). It retains the
outgoing high Newton sector as a separate polynomially bounded
original trace. For the remaining low kernel, convexity in contour
height and concavity along the calibrated horizontal contour give
strict bounds for the internal seams and all horizontal corrections.
The positive spectral endpoint is also controlled.
The [fold-cap theorem](research_endpoint_uniform_fold_cap.md) now
joins the remaining negative-end boundary currents to those compact
patches. Its error has rate at most \(\mathcal I_2+CT^4\), where
\(T\) is the angular width of the cap. For every fixed \(|n|\ge3\),
a sufficiently small fixed cap therefore lies strictly below
\(\mathcal I_n\). At \(|n|=2\) the shrinking-cap estimate reaches
the same rate as the saddle and supplies no noncancellation theorem.
The [whole microscopic-product trace](research_microscopic_endpoint_filled_leaf_scalar_asymptotic.md)
now combines those estimates with an actual local coefficient.
For fixed \(|n|\ge3\), bounded real endpoint parameters and complete
output, the reflected saddle pieces add with the original trace
normalization and every complementary piece has a strict gap.
Thus this entire scalar source has rate \(\mathcal I_n\), with a
nonzero coefficient of polynomial size. The
[boundary extension](research_microscopic_endpoint_filled_leaf_boundary_packet.md)
now proves its asymptotic on a fixed complex output neighborhood
for \(|n|\ge3\), together with an upper bound on the whole output
period. The resulting functions retain their actual, possibly
level-dependent, nonzero coefficients.
The [composition estimate](research_microscopic_upper_packet_composition.md)
propagates upper bounds when sufficiently many such inputs meet
at one circle, including fixed microscopic insertions. The filling
power at that circle can be any fixed signed integer.
It does not propagate a lower bound.

For \(|n|=2\), the
[shortened-kernel calculation](research_two_power_shortened_wire_packet.md)
now proves the nonzero local contribution with its original
normalization. The
[optimized fold estimate](research_critical_fold_optimized_block_assembly.md)
controls the fixed endpoint interval up to its four retained
exterior contour sides. Its error is
\(O(N^{-r-1/4}(1+\log N)^{2r}e^{N\mathcal I_2})\), smaller than
the local contribution \(cN^{-r}e^{N\mathcal I_2}\).
The [complete scalar assembly](research_two_power_microscopic_endpoint_scalar_asymptotic.md)
now joins those four exterior sides to the compact contours.
It proves the whole nonzero scalar asymptotic for \(n=\pm2\).
Together with the earlier scalar theorem this covers every
fixed \(|n|\ge2\) for this specific microscopic-product source.
These results do not identify a new knot-complement volume or
cover arbitrary received factors.
The [ordinary-operation theorem](research_endpoint_pre_turn_analytic_alias_class.md)
also retains the analytic coefficients of the aliases through fixed
products, half shifts, positive-endpoint division, and canonical
reduction. These operations precede an outer turn; estimates after
that turn remain a separate problem.
Its [actual alias coefficient](research_endpoint_analytic_alias_leading_coefficient.md)
now has an explicit leading term through the real interval and the
negative endpoint. A thin-rectangle maximum principle transfers the
known nonreal asymptotic to the real interval without changing the
chosen source. This identifies the constant corrections produced
by odd numbers of half-shift operations; those corrections remain
in subsequent contractions.
The [retained-boundary energy profile](research_retained_boundary_leaf_energy_profile.md)
now specifies the corresponding classical comparison problem. It
keeps the neighbor's incidence variable and the constraints from
deleted edges. Minimizing over the leaf preserves the exact parent
gap, whereas replacing that profile by a single terminal constant
loses a nonnegative coupling term.
The [full-step interface](research_full_step_repeated_turn_tensor_interface.md)
also gives exact finite equations for products of already transformed
factors followed by another turn. It retains the repeated-root
derivatives and the original initial data.
The [regular-arc source bound](research_repeated_turn_regular_arc_source_bound.md)
now supplies a finite-root upper estimate between two interior
colors where its stated leading classical coefficient is nonzero.
It retains higher-order quantum terms and controls their fast modes
using the actual source on a right buffer. Propagation across the
exceptional colors and control of the macroscopic initial packet
remain open.
The [projective monic certificate](research_repeated_turn_projective_monic_certificate.md)
now makes the possible interior exceptions explicit. Away from the
finite union of resonant cosine grids, it constructs a monic member
of the full principal maximal-minor ideal. The resulting local bound
retains all source channels and all higher-order quantum terms.
The [support-envelope refinement](research_principal_support_envelope_on_regular_arcs.md)
removes roots introduced only by the choice of monic certificate
from the integrated bound. The remaining envelope belongs to
the full principal presentation and is not yet the geometric action.
The [exact rank-loss lemma](research_simple_rank_loss_full_normal_transport.md)
also distinguishes value recovery from full transport. At a simple
loss of rank in an actual finite-level row, its derivative equation
recovers the missing value but leaves a first-normal component.
The original trace can detect that component. The full stacked
equations, including their higher-order quantum terms, must be used
to determine whether it is present in the repeated-turn problem.
For a fixed window at a rational exceptional phase, the
[conditioning theorem](research_resonant_physical_window_conditioning.md)
reduces polynomial recovery cost to nonvanishing of an actual
finite-level minor in each of finitely many residue classes.
The [holomorphic recovery theorem](research_holomorphic_parameter_recovery.md)
then extends that upper estimate across parameter-specific minor
zeros, provided the supplied bounds hold on complex parameter
neighborhoods. Generic nonvanishing of a suitable window minor
is still required, and no supplied boundary rate is improved
by this continuation.
The [quantum-binomial criterion](research_repeated_turn_quantum_binomial_rank_criterion.md)
now expresses generic rank failure as an exact divisibility question:
all full-column minors must share the binomial defining the physical
color trajectory. The criterion uses the finite quantum equations,
including the translated rows and first normals. It does not yet
exclude that divisor for every short component.
The [parameter-leading theorem](research_single_kernel_parameter_leading_window_rank.md)
now proves the required generic rank for an enlarged system when
each transformed input contains one independently parameterized
kernel. It permits arbitrarily many fixed factors and arbitrary
fixed nonzero signed powers. The proof uses all equations touching
the finite unknown window, including those centered outside it.
The complete transformed terminal sector and both collars remain
supplied data. That terminal sector contains a central branching-star
source whose volume-rate estimate is still missing; generic rank
does not supply that estimate.
The [product recovery theorem](research_multikernel_parameter_leading_projected_recovery.md)
now treats a product of independently parameterized kernels inside
one inner turn. A finite sequence of ordinary polynomial divisions
provides enough additional equations to determine the original
interior packet generically. The auxiliary quotient packets need
not be uniquely determined. This extension requires the transformed
terminal sources, fixed-degree remainders, and both boundary collars
of every quotient as supplied data. Their rates remain in the bound.
An [exact contour reduction](research_endpoint_quotient_dual_contour_reduction.md)
now expresses those quotient collars after all turns in terms of
mixed original and dual endpoint factors. Its prefactors cost only
powers of \(N\). It retains both endpoint signs and all derivative
terms. The new mixed family still needs an estimate: a negative
dual factor can grow exponentially after one turn, so bounding
its pieces separately at the positive endpoint's rate is invalid.
The [coherent quotient theorem](research_negative_endpoint_quotient_first_turn_growth.md)
now proves that the exact subtraction does not generally remove
this growth. Dividing even one microscopic kernel by a negative
endpoint factor produces a first-turn rate \(4G_{\rm Cat}/\pi\),
although the unquotiented first turn is bounded. This is an
obstruction to giving the enlarged auxiliary family the original
rate. The recovery theorem remains valid with its supplied budgets;
using it for the volume bound now requires different auxiliary
data or a cancellation estimate before taking their separate norms.
There is a contrasting [positive-division theorem](research_positive_endpoint_quotient_source_bounds.md).
Ordinary division at \(2+O(N^{-2})\) costs only a polynomial in
the joint norm of an input and its first turn. For the original
microscopic products and their specified source channels, any fixed
number of such divisions also preserves the signed physical-color
profile after \(V_n\). The forcing and its propagation share one
characteristic integral. The
[positive-pole presentation](research_positive_pole_parameter_leading_product_module.md)
now constructs selected-parameter leading equations whose clearing
roots all lie at \(2+O(N^{-2})\). It retains all four selected
coordinates and the two prescribed source columns. This avoids the
negative divisors at the inner ordinary-division stage. The
[assembly theorem](research_positive_pole_projected_recovery_assembly.md)
now inserts these equations into projected recovery on all selected
coordinates. Its auxiliary inner quotient profiles are proved.
The resulting estimate retains the actual lower-factor sources,
remainders and both outer collars of every quotient; their composed
rates remain to be established.
The [exact weighted observation](research_outer_turn_weighted_jet_observation.md)
now shows the limit of using only the incoming physical value and
first-normal profile. Its dual norm is, up to polynomial factors,
the positive physical-kernel sum. That bound is sharp over the
whole corresponding jet ball, so positive reweighting alone cannot
improve its exponential rate. The saturating inputs are arbitrary
Hermite data, not asserted to be actual received sources. A sharper
estimate must use additional information about the coherent source.
The [Newton-degree calculation](research_resonant_newton_graded_carrier.md)
also retains the linear quantum phase at a reciprocal resonance.
Its binomial involves a degree variable, which has not been identified
with the physical color. The original trace fixes one degree, while
the resonant translation changes that degree. The resulting finite
boundary terms and the higher-degree canonical terms remain necessary.
The [quantum indicial calculation](research_repeated_turn_quantum_indicial_physical_hits.md)
also shows why a finite quantum shift cannot simply remove the
exceptional colors. For the ordered single-kernel equations, primitive
resonant phases still meet nearby physical rows at infinitely many
levels. Such a candidate need not survive the complete equations;
their full minors remain the relevant test.
The [projective resonance criterion](research_terminal_product_projective_resonance.md)
now classifies one possible obstruction to regular propagation.
For a terminal product followed by \(U_\sigma\), an old branch
at infinity reaches a new interior physical color precisely when
the signed reciprocal sum is \(-\sigma\) and the least common
multiple of the active magnitudes is at least three.
This is a classification of possible characteristic branches,
not of their coefficients in the actual source.
The [finite-core corollary](research_terminal_resonance_finite_core.md)
shows that at fixed arity every such resonance contains one
of finitely many bounded minimal cores. Its remaining factors
have reciprocal sum zero. Those remaining powers and their
phase denominator can be unbounded, so they remain part of
the general source problem.
For matched opposite powers, the
[spectator reduction](research_opposite_power_spectator_reduction.md)
now gives an exact simplification inside the original closing
trace. An additional insertion is conjugated, rather than
discarded. Fixed-degree insertions have polynomial bounds;
the first-normal insertion after the next turn still has degree
growing with the quantum level and is retained.
The endpoint-product and first-turn estimates yield an enlarged
[forest reduction theorem](research_endpoint_product_forest_current_certificate.md):
an original endpoint product may pass through a unit leaf,
provided a vertex receiving that transformed factor is not
turned again. The entire corresponding microscopic boundary
current has rate at most zero, strictly below a supplied
positive parent action.
The [action calibration](research_terminal_characteristic_action_calibration.md)
also identifies the terminal growth integral with a fully normalized
stationary action. It is strictly less than \(4G_{\mathrm{Cat}}/\pi\),
increases with the absolute twist power, and approaches that ceiling
with deficit \(\pi/n^2+O(n^{-4})\).
This does not identify it with the volume budget of an arbitrary
partially filled parent: the original boundary marking and outside
work must still be carried through the turn.
The [boundary-action covariance](research_unit_turn_boundary_action_covariance.md)
now supplies that local transformation law, with the original
quadratic primitive and its additive constant. It preserves
the boundary Legendre energy on the transformed domain.
Identifying that domain with the actual marked geometry
after general composition remains open. The
[first-turn capacity criterion](research_endpoint_first_turn_angle_capacity.md)
rules out the literal positive square-incidence interpretation
near microscopic endpoints: its first unit-charge row has
insufficient angle capacity. The first-turn source estimate
works without that geometric interpretation.
For the complementary endpoint factors,
[exact value/normal interpolation](research_microscopic_endpoint_two_channel_interpolation.md),
[bulk Fourier interpolation](research_endpoint_bulk_fourier_interpolation.md),
and the [midpoint profile](research_endpoint_fourier_fold_transition.md)
provide controlled analytic expressions.

The local derivative-compatibility question is now settled by the
[bulk scalar theorem](research_microscopic_endpoint_bulk_scalar_compatibility.md).
Both intrinsic normal-defect coefficients are exponentially small
on every fixed interior interval. A single scalar analytic function
with polynomial norm can therefore reproduce the original endpoint
values and first derivatives there, including shared products.
The [value connection theorem](research_endpoint_value_connection_and_overlap.md)
also gives explicit value asymptotics; its derivatives now give the
actual spectral-normal asymptotics. The earlier endpoint-normal
calculation remains valid, but individually matching its large
components is no longer needed to prove this local compatibility.
The [fixed-neighborhood extension](research_endpoint_fixed_strip_asymptotics.md)
now makes the explicit asymptotic valid on a sufficiently thin
fixed complex neighborhood. At the complete endpoint its leading
factor is nonzero there.
The [shrinking-buffer theorem](research_microscopic_endpoint_shrinking_buffer_compatibility.md)
also quantifies the interpolation as the physical endpoints approach:
at distance \(\rho\), its width is \(c\rho\) and its compatibility
error is a polynomial factor times \(e^{-cN\rho}\).

The [bulk contour assembly](research_endpoint_bulk_annulus_full_trace.md)
places this scalar in the original double-pole trace on any fixed
interior angular window. Artificial subdivision boundaries cancel
exactly. The two outer vertical integrals, complementary physical
rows, and all shared source factors remain in the formula.

These statements do not yet prove the theorem for arbitrary short
partial fillings. Their complex neighborhoods can be thin; neither
physical endpoint is included. The remaining endpoint regions,
external connecting integrals and shared source factors must still
be controlled in the original closed expression. A general nonzero
geometric contribution is required as well. The improvements address
this common obstruction, rather than additional isolated fillings.

## The retained filling theorem and the extension now sought

The research priority is the filling-parameter extension, not further
analysis of the complete acute crossing presentation below.
The retained theorem already covers every independently sufficiently
long tuple in its stated families. For a fixed strict
Conway expression with at least two crossing circles and a retained
half-twist pattern giving one knot, there is \(P_0\) such that every
fixed tuple \(|p_i|>P_0\) has the original reduced Kashaev volume
limit through all integer levels. The signs and relative magnitudes
are unrestricted. The physical crossing powers are
\(n_i=\varepsilon_i-2p_i\), with the original primitive surgery
slopes \(\mu_i+p_i\lambda_i\).
See [the companion theorem](../papers/conway-asymptotics/main.tex).
The frozen reference's main Conway theorem uses the narrower
completed/completed closing grammar; its separate tree chapters
give the explicit degree-and-twist criteria. The retained
companion statement covers the enlarged strict grammar.

For fixed dimension, density one follows by counting the complement
of this all-long region. It is not a probabilistic premise of the
theorem. With two or more parameters, the unproved sets where one
coordinate remains bounded are still infinite.
The desired next theorem fixes any short partial assignment and
proves the identity for every independently sufficiently long tuple
of the remaining coordinates that gives a hyperbolic knot.
Thresholds may depend on the entire fixed partial assignment.
Repeated application gives finite exceptions by the
[finite-branching lemma](research_finite_exceptions_under_partial_fillings.md#3-a-finite-exception-lemma-for-one-template).

The [retained geometric theorem](../papers/strict-conway-geometry/main.tex)
already permits a subset of cusps to be filled with long slopes
while the other cusps remain complete. It does not supply arbitrary
short partial fillings. For a partially filled parent with a verified
marked positive geometric certificate,
[the geometric continuation theorem](finite_geometric_certificate_uniform_filling_existence.md)
supplies all sufficiently long remaining primitive fillings.
The further quantum requirements are a nonzero holomorphic
boundary asymptotic for the actual partially filled source and a
bound on its entire complementary contribution. The
[complex-phase transfer](research_long_fillings_complex_boundary_phase.md)
already handles independently long remaining powers when those
requirements hold. It does not prove the requirements for an
arbitrary short component.

There is a second, distinct density-one result:
[a nonzero amplitude germ](general_long_filling_source_divisor.md)
allows long tuples outside its pulled-back zero set. In several
variables that set can contain infinitely many long integer tuples.
A unit, or a coordinate monomial times a unit, eliminates this
additional exclusion. The retained strict-Conway theorem already
proves its nonzero leading coefficient for every sufficiently long
tuple; it does not have this extra divisor exclusion.

Finally, arbitrary short partial fillings can collapse the diagram
and make some parameters inessential. The
[original-tree padding theorem](research_original_tree_padding_equivalence.md)
shows that infinite families of parameter assignments can represent
the same fixed hyperbolic core. Such branches cannot be discarded
as finitely many exceptions, or removed by silently assuming every
intermediate exterior hyperbolic. The full assignment-counting
target must prove the relevant core identities or control these
branches by another exact argument. Restricting the target to
hyperbolic intermediate parents would be a useful intermediate
theorem, but a weaker one.

The recent acute-domain obstruction concerns a different proposed
representation of the complete source. It changes none of these
retained filling conclusions.

## Continuing through regular cell degenerations

The [primitive-period calculation](research_regular_corner_period_assembly.md)
now treats a boundary of the positive cell domain where one square of
an edge block reaches a regular corner and the other remains interior.
Four tetrahedra flatten there, but their vertices and the original
face maps remain distinct and regular. Two-square corners and
singular face charts are excluded.

At such a corner the Hermitian part of the two-variable edge
Jacobian has rank one. Its kernel gives an explicit nonzero real
ratio between the variations at its endpoints. A positive edge
forces both variations to vanish. These constraints assemble over
the original graph: a zero at any fixed outside vertex propagates
through every corner edge. Consequently, for every proper selected
subset of a connected graph, the complete selected period Jacobian
has positive definite Hermitian part. The signed filling powers
contribute only an imaginary diagonal, so no restriction on their
size or sign is needed for this conclusion.

Thus, at a supplied solution of the primitive equations with these
regular corner types, the marked solution continues holomorphically
through the corner. Its reduced phase still has a strict local
maximum in the horizontal real directions. The exact factorial
integral also admits fixed-endpoint wire contours through its
stationary point at the corner. These conclusions address the
coupled equations and the original integral, with all physical
derivative data retained.

The [uniform end theorem](research_regular_corner_uniform_end_tubes.md)
supplies a second geometric control along a positive approach to
the same corners. If the core heights stay bounded above and away
from zero and the cone charges have positive limits, the original
ends contain disjoint cone tubes of a common positive radius.
The complete cusps also have uniform nondegenerate neighborhoods.
The essential calculation shows that the second peripheral fixed
point stays away from every collapsed similarity-link triangle.
The logarithmic link maps then converge, with their original
periods, to a map whose fibers can be collapsed to obtain the
limiting flat torus.

The [compact-middle estimate](research_regular_corner_compact_middle_bounds.md)
adds control away from these ends. After fixed tube and cusp
truncations, the retained part of each tetrahedron lies in a uniformly
compact developed region, even when that tetrahedron flattens.
The proof bounds its height in every ideal-vertex frame; strict
convexity of the Klein ball then excludes escape towards any other
ideal point. Paths through the finite dual graph give a uniform
diameter bound in the completed metric. A tetrahedron that remains
positive contains an embedded hyperbolic ball of fixed radius.
The [ball-volume comparison](research_regular_corner_uniform_ball_volumes.md)
now transfers that surviving volume to every point in the retained
filled core \(C_j\). If its diameter is at most \(D_1\) and it
contains an ordinary hyperbolic ball of radius \(r_*>0\), then
\[
 \operatorname{Vol}B(p,\rho)\ge
 V_{\mathbb H}(r_*)\,
 \frac{V_{\mathbb H}(\rho)}{V_{\mathbb H}(D_1+r_*)},
 \qquad p\in C_j,\quad 0<\rho\le D_1+r_*.
\]
Here \(V_{\mathbb H}(r)=\pi(\sinh(2r)-2r)\) is the volume of a
radius-\(r\) ball in hyperbolic three-space. The bound is uniform
along the supplied positive sequence, including centers on cone
axes. Its constants depend on the fixed gluing and regular limit.

The comparison is the familiar Bishop--Gromov argument, justified
here directly at cone angles at most \(2\pi\). A minimizing path
between regular points cannot pass through a genuine cone axis:
its incoming and outgoing directions can be joined by an angle
less than \(\pi\), giving a shorter path. Ordinary radial Jacobi
fields therefore give the polar volume formula up to the cut
time. The resulting volume ratios decrease with radius; simple
ball inclusions extend the inequality to axis centers. This
