## The fixed geometric heights give a global positive-domain comparison

The [fixed-parent-height calibration](research_fixed_parent_height_global_calibration.md)
strengthens the local phase comparison. Let a supplied positive
unit-charge parent solution have heights \(H_v^0>0\), angle assignment
\(z_0\), and action \(M_G\). Let \(D_0\) be the raw ambient angle
energy after subtracting its value and supporting affine function
at \(z_0\). For every point of the original positive horizontal
slice \(t=s-iH^0\),
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\Phi_1(s-iH^0)
       =M_G-\frac{D_0(z(s))}{\pi}.
\]
Thus the geometric point is the unique global maximum on that
whole slice. This requires neither connectedness nor convexity
of the slice. Every fixed region away from the geometric point
has a strict gap, and every positive-boundary limit loses at
least \(\delta_0/\pi\), where
\(\delta_0=\min_{\partial X}D_0>0\).

The same computation retains the endpoint work for a saturated
set \(C\). Leave the removed charge rows free, write their induced
values as \(c_v\), and keep the surviving rows at one. The classical
rate \(A_C(h;z)\), including the appropriate signed exponential
of the actual paired current, satisfies
\[
 M_G-A_C(h;z)=\frac{D_0(z)}{\pi}
       +\sum_{v\in C}(H_v^0-h_v)(c_v-1).
\]
At \(h=H_C^0\) this gives the same boundary gap without restricting
the removed powers or imposing their old row-capacity condition.
The theorem also supplies an explicit terminal-height collar
retaining half the gap.

The correction is retained at other heights. The exact vertical
current still integrates from zero to \(H_C^0\), with its original
positive sign in the trace decomposition. The terminal-height
bound does not estimate that whole integral or identify the
quantum endpoint factors with weak-angle assignments.

## An actual upper gap for one class of microscopic current terms

The [microscopic all-top theorem](research_microscopic_all_top_current_gap.md)
now estimates a specified part of the original quantum current,
including its integration. This estimate uses the exact source and
does not assume a corresponding bound for a smaller filled source.

Let \(C\) be the vertices evaluated by microscopic vertical currents,
with heights between zero and \(A/N\), where \(A<\pi\) is fixed.
Assume every selected vertex adjacent to an ordinary outside
variable belongs to \(C\). At each surviving vertex adjacent to
\(C\), first multiply all incident endpoint kernels and retain their
full Hermite remainder. In that remainder, take the Newton terms
\(e_{N-1-r}\) with \(0\le r\le\lfloor\varepsilon N\rfloor\).
This choice is made at every such surviving vertex.

The exact radical trace turns these terms into physical evaluations
with indices at most \(\varepsilon N\). One index is shared by all
edges incident to an evaluated vertex, and edges joining two
evaluated vertices remain in the expression. The unevaluated
vertices therefore carry ordinary physical-row polynomials of
degree at most \(d_*\varepsilon N\), where \(d_*\) bounds the
original valence.

If the remaining closed forest has a fixed reduction order using
the proved zero-leaf, unit-leaf and isolated-vertex operations,
the entire integrated term satisfies
\[
 |I_{C,N}^{\mathrm{top}}|
       \le C N^p \exp\!\bigl(N\omega_C(\varepsilon)\bigr),
 \qquad
 \omega_C(\varepsilon)
       =O_G\!\left(\varepsilon\log(1/\varepsilon)\right).
\]
The theorem gives the constants explicitly. The coefficient estimate
uses the original first spectral derivatives as well as the values.
It also includes all crossing factors, the current densities, and
the ordinary outside variables on their real intervals. Fixed
outside derivatives have the same exponential rate. A complex
outside strip costs the stated amount
\(\sum_b d_b|\operatorname{Im}u_b|\), rather than being treated as
free.

A supplied positive parent has action \(M_G>0\). Choosing
\(\varepsilon\) sufficiently small makes this term strictly smaller
than \(\exp(NM_G)\). This proves a quantum upper gap for that term.
That theorem alone does not handle complementary Newton parts.
The marked-forest result below treats the full product under its
separate, stronger combinatorial hypothesis. Residual forests
without an applicable certificate and macroscopic current heights
still require estimates. Neither result supplies a lower bound for
the full geometric contribution.

## A whole microscopic current bound for marked forests

The [marked-forest theorem](research_marked_forest_full_endpoint_current_gap.md)
controls full endpoint products without selecting a Newton band.
It allows arbitrarily many vertices, with a fixed finite reduction
sequence satisfying an explicit condition.

Mark every surviving vertex that carries an endpoint factor.
The permitted reductions are:

* An isolated vertex can be traced, with any current integer power.
* An unmarked leaf of power \(\sigma=\pm1\) can be removed,
  subtracting \(\sigma\) from its neighbor's power.
* An unmarked zero-power leaf and its neighbor can be removed
  together. The neighbor may be marked.

The sequence must remove the entire forest. A marked leaf cannot
be used for a leaf operation. Thus its endpoint product stays at
its original vertex until an isolated trace or exact endpoint
evaluation consumes it. This condition is stronger than the
unmarked reduction condition in the earlier theorem.

The proof uses exact source identities. A unit leaf transmits
\(R^{-\sigma}\). A zero leaf inserts the top radical \(e_{N-1}\);
the next trace evaluates its entire remaining factor at \(c_0\).
Every endpoint kernel and every other incident kernel then equals
one. At an isolated vertex, the full endpoint product has
polynomial real norm; the polynomial Markov inequality and the
original trace formula bound its values and first derivatives.
All signed crossing factors and shared endpoint parameters remain.

For a closed forest with \(v\) vertices and \(r\) full endpoint
factors at bounded complex microscopic parameters, this gives
\[
                         |Z_N|\le C N^{p_A r+3v}.
\]
For an original microscopic current at vertices \(C\), assume
that every selected vertex incident to an ordinary outside
variable belongs to \(C\), and that the remaining forest \(Y\)
has the marked reduction sequence above. Integrating all current
heights from zero to their prescribed bounds \(A/N\), \(A<\pi\),
then gives
\[
 |I_{C,N}|\le C N^{\,2(e_C+b_C)+3|Y|}.
\]
Here \(e_C\) counts edges within \(C\), while \(b_C\) counts
edges with exactly one endpoint in \(C\), including outside
edges. This is a bound for the entire current, with all surviving
traces already evaluated. Fixed outside derivatives cost only
additional powers of \(N\). Ordinary complex outside variables
incur the explicit rate \(\sum_b d_b|\Im u_b|\).

A supplied positive parent has action \(M_G>0\), so this
polynomial bound lies strictly below its exponential rate.
The result does not cover a reduction requiring a marked leaf
to be turned, arbitrary remaining forests, macroscopic current
heights, or the nonzero coefficient of the full geometric term.
No such additional estimate is assumed in the proof.

## One unit turn preserves a full microscopic endpoint factor

The [exact operator identities](research_full_endpoint_unit_turn_identities.md)
and the [polynomial turn theorem](research_full_endpoint_unit_turn_polynomial_bound.md)
treat a leaf operation excluded from the static marked reduction
above. Let \(T\) be the original turn, \(R\) the original crossing,
\(\kappa=q^{(N-1)^2/2}\), and
\[
 U_\sigma=\kappa^\sigma T R^{-\sigma}T,\qquad \sigma=\pm1.
\]
For every fixed bounded complex set of parameters \(\alpha\),
\[
 \sup_{Z\in[-2,2]}
 \left|(U_\sigma^{(Z)}K_N)(2\cosh(\alpha/N),Z)\right|
                         \le C_A N^{p_A}.
\]
All fixed spectral and parameter derivatives obey polynomial
bounds. The assertion includes both level parities and the
actual first normals at the double physical roots.

The proof does not estimate the triangular coefficient sum term
by term. With \(J=T Z T\), the turn commutes with \(J\), and the
actual transformed kernel \(F\) satisfies
\[
 (w-J)F=\frac{\eta P_N(w)\kappa^\sigma}{N^2}R^\sigma.
\]
This is the original finite difference operator with an explicit
forcing term. Its endpoint value and derivative are controlled
by canonical multiplication in the endpoint variable; a finite
Fourier reconstruction bounds that multiplication while preserving
the full derivative data.

On the physical rows the recurrence has
\[
 0\le q_j=C(j)/A(j)<1,\qquad
 |d_j|+|f_j|\le C_A/(j+1)^2.
\]
Balancing the state as \((h_j,(j+1)(h_j-h_{j-1}))\) makes each
forward matrix have norm at most \(1+C_A/(j+1)\).
Their product therefore grows polynomially. Differentiating the
ordinary source identity gives the same homogeneous recurrence
for the actual index derivative, with polynomial forcing.
This proves the bound through the last required physical root;
the singular next row is never used.

Consequently a unit-power leaf carrying exactly one such endpoint
factor can be removed, shifting its neighbor's power by
\(-\sigma\) and inserting the transformed factor there. This is
an exact source operation. The resulting factor is polynomially
bounded, but has not been identified with a microscopic endpoint
kernel. The repeated-turn comparison below shows that a second
same-sign turn has positive exponential growth. Products with
other endpoint factors still require a separate propagation
argument.

## A polynomial real norm alone is not preserved by the turn

The [unit-turn obstruction](research_unit_turn_real_norm_obstruction.md)
rules out a shortcut for the next composition step. For
\(f_k(Z)=T_k(Z/2)\), if \(2k(2k+1)<N\), then
\[
 \|f_k\|_{[-2,2]}=1,\qquad
                  |(U_\sigma f_k)(-2)|\ge 3^k/4.
\]
The proof keeps the exact finite phases. The original Newton
coefficients have alternating signs because their interpolation
nodes lie above every root of \(f_k\). In the transformed value
at \(-2\), these signs cancel the explicit triangular signs.
All resulting amplitudes are positive and their phases lie in
an arc of width less than \(\pi/3\). The highest-degree term
already supplies the displayed lower bound.

Taking \(k=\lfloor c\sqrt N\rfloor\), \(0<c<1/2\), gives
superpolynomial growth for the actual shrinking-charge cosine
coupons, whose input norm is one. An existing upper estimate
still makes this example subexponential. Thus this obstruction
does not refute a volume-rate estimate or the special endpoint
product bound; it shows why the next proof cannot use only the
real norm of its input.

## Repeated turns preserve the terminal rate, not a polynomial bound

The [repeated-turn theorem](research_repeated_endpoint_unit_turn_action_growth.md)
identifies the growth which must be retained in a general reduction.
For a fixed integer \(n\), set
\[
 V_n=\kappa^nTR^{-n}T,\qquad
 G_{n,N}=T(R^{-n}),\qquad
 F_{n,N,\alpha}=V_nK_N(2\cosh(\alpha/N),\cdot).
\]
Thus \(V_nV_\ell=V_{n+\ell}\), including the original signed
unit turns. For real \(|\alpha|\le A\), the theorem proves
\[
 c_A N^{-5}\|G_{n,N}\|_{[-2,2]}
 \le \|F_{n,N,\alpha}\|_{[-2,2]}
 \le C_{A,n}N^{p_{A,n}}\|G_{n,N}\|_{[-2,2]} .
\]
This comparison holds at every level, with constants depending
on the fixed power and parameter interval. In particular the two
norms have the same exponential rate whenever either rate exists.

The lower bound is a finite operator estimate. The exact source
equation is
\[
 (w-\mathcal L)F_{n,N,\alpha}
       =\eta P_N(w)\kappa^nG_{n,N}/N^2,\qquad
                  \mathcal L=TZT .
\]
An explicit cosine calculation removes the apparent singularities
of the difference operator and proves
\(\|\mathcal L p\|_{[-2,2]}\le34N^3\|p\|_{[-2,2]}\)
for every canonical polynomial. For real microscopic parameters,
\(P_N(w)=4\cosh^2(\alpha/2)\ge4\); this factor is retained.
The lower bound follows immediately. The upper bound uses the
same forced recurrence as the single-turn theorem, with the
actual terminal polynomial \(G_{n,N}\) in its forcing and all
its first derivatives controlled by Markov's inequality.
The initial jets remain polynomial for each fixed \(n\).

For two same-sign turns the previously established terminal
asymptotic supplies both bounds needed to identify the rate:
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
 \log\|U_\sigma^2K_N(2\cosh(\alpha/N),\cdot)\|_{[-2,2]}
                 =\frac{2G_{\mathrm{Cat}}}{\pi}>0,
 \qquad \sigma=\pm1.
\]
The convergence is uniform on compact real parameter intervals
and includes both parities. The original kernel and its first
unit-turn image are polynomially bounded; its second same-sign
image is exponentially large. Therefore even the actual
microscopic endpoint family cannot be enlarged by repeated turns
while keeping a universal polynomial bound.

This is an ordinary polynomial norm statement before further
graph closure. Additional traces can cancel these large values.
It proves neither a lower bound for the closed invariant nor
the arbitrary-short-partial-filling theorem. Its role is to
replace an invalid polynomial-closure target by transport of the
correct terminal action. The next composition estimate must
account for that action and then establish the coefficient of
the geometric contribution in the original closed trace.
At complex parameters where \(P_N(w)=0\), the lower comparison
is not asserted.

## Exact quantum operators for turns and branching

The [operator and branching theorem](research_unit_turn_finite_band_branching_operator.md)
is an exact statement about the original finite algebra, including
the derivative at each double root. Put \(C f=Zf\bmod P_N\),
\(J=TCT\), and \(D_n=V_nCV_{-n}\). For
\(X=C,\ Y=J,\ Z=D_1\), the three cyclic relations begin with
\[
 qXY-q^{-1}YX=8(q-q^{-1})I-(q^2-q^{-2})Z,
 \qquad q=e^{\pi i/N}.
\]
Their central relation is
\[
 qXYZ+q^2X^2+q^{-2}Y^2+q^2Z^2
       -8qX-8q^{-1}Y-8qZ
       =\bigl((q+q^{-1})^2-32\bigr)I.
\]
Both formulas hold at every \(N\ge2\). The proof uses the full
triangular crossing matrix, checks every entry of the conjugated
multiplication, and evaluates the central scalar on a cyclic vector.
No value-only specialization or limit is used.

For every integer \(n\), the resulting twist recurrence is
\[
 qD_{n+2}+q^{-1}D_n+D_{n+1}J=8I.
\]
There is also the corresponding identity with the factors in the
opposite order. It gives an explicit finite Chebyshev formula.
For each fixed \(n\), the operator \(D_n\) has polynomial norm on
canonical polynomials with their norm on \([-2,2]\).
This does not bound \(V_n\), whose exponential growth was established
above. The commuting leading symbols satisfy
\[
 X^2+Y^2+Z^2+XYZ-8(X+Y+Z)+28=0.
\]
This classical cubic already occurs elsewhere in the notes. The
additional result here is its exact finite operator lift and its
compatibility with the original turns.

For a product \(P_r=\operatorname{can}\prod_{i=1}^rK_N(w_i,Z)\),
let \(\lambda_r=\sum_iw_i-(r-1)c_0\). The exact product rule gives
\[
 (\lambda_r-J)V_nP_r
   =\frac{\eta\kappa^n}{N^2}
       \left(\sum_iP_N(w_i)\right)T(R^{-n})+V_nM_r,
\]
where \(M_r\) is the explicitly displayed sum of products of
two or more finite differences. It vanishes for one factor.
For microscopic \(w_i\), the whole output norm is equivalent,
up to polynomial factors in \(N\), to the norm of this
**combined** forcing together with
\((V_nP_r)(c_0)\) and \((V_nP_r)'(c_0)\).
Thus a bound on the mixed term before applying \(V_n\) is
insufficient, and cancellation within the forcing must be retained.

The derivative datum involves
\(H_n=T(R^{-n}Q_N)\), where
\(Q_N=\partial_wK_N(c_0,\cdot)\). It satisfies
\[
 (D_n-c_0)H_n=G_n,\qquad
 (D_n-c_0)G_n=0,\qquad G_n=T(R^{-n}).
\]
It is not obtained by replacing \(H_n\) with \(V_nQ_N\).
These formulas give a polynomial-loss lower comparison with
\(\|G_n\|\), but no corresponding upper comparison.
Control of the combined forcing, this derivative datum, and
the final geometric coefficient remains necessary for arbitrary
short partial fillings. The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## All integer terminal powers have separated interior branches

The [terminal characteristic theorem](research_terminal_twist_characteristic_geometry.md)
uses the exact operator identities above. Its statements apply to
every fixed nonzero integer \(n\), without enumerating individual
fillings. On the classical cubic, define
\[
 x_0=x,\qquad x_1=z,\qquad
 x_{k+2}=8-yx_{k+1}-x_k.
\]
The terminal condition is \(x_n=2\). Define
\[
 f_0=2,\quad f_1=4-y,\quad
 f_{m+1}=8-yf_m-f_{m-1}.
\]
Its reduced locus has \(x=f_{|n|}(y)\), with
\(z=f_{n-1}(y)\) for \(n>0\) and
\(z=f_{|n|+1}(y)\) for \(n<0\).
Thus the signed information is retained after projection to
the same equation in \(x,y\).

The proof gives the polynomial expression
\[
 f_m(y)=\frac{8+2(y-2)T_m(-y/2)}{y+2},
\]
with the value at \(y=-2\) supplied by its removable extension.
Chebyshev factorizations show that every critical point is real
and simple, and every critical value is at least \(2\).
Consequently \(f_{|n|}(y)=x\) has \(|n|\) distinct roots for
every real \(x<2\), with holomorphic labels on
\(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\).

The actual physical shift coordinate is checked separately.
For \(x=2\cos\nu\), \(0<\nu<\pi\), put
\(a=(2-x)/(2+x)\). The original operators give
\[
 y=2+2a-a(\tau+\tau^{-1}),\qquad
 z=2+2a+a(e^{-i\nu}\tau+e^{i\nu}\tau^{-1}).
\]
These formulas parametrize the cubic slice by
\(\tau\in\mathbb C^\times\). The selected terminal shifts are
therefore distinct, nonzero and finite, uniformly on compact
physical intervals. None equals \(1\) or \(-1\).
There is exactly one unit-circle shift for odd \(|n|\),
and none for even \(|n|\).

The unreduced terminal section remains double:
at \(x_n=2\) the cubic is
\((x_{n-1}+y-4)^2=0\). The proof follows this nilpotent
coordinate through every recurrence step and shows that each
interior terminal shift has multiplicity exactly two.
It does not replace these double roots by simple eigenvectors.
Separation of the distinct branches alone neither controls
transport between them nor determines the coefficient selected
by the original finite source. Those analytic questions, and
the mixed forcing at branching vertices, remain on the critical
path to arbitrary short partial fillings.

## Actual terminal transport and a fixed maximal branch

The [bulk transfer theorem](research_terminal_twist_bulk_transfer_bound.md)
uses the original polynomials
\[
 G_n=T(R^{-n}),\qquad H_n=T(R^{-n}Q_N),
\]
with their value and first-derivative data at the physical nodes.
For \(m=|n|\ge1\), the recurrence has order \(2m\).
Its two extreme coefficients are explicit products of the
original Askey--Wilson coefficients and are nonzero on every
fixed compact interior interval. Ordinary operator residuals
are multiples of \(P_N\), whose values and first angular
derivatives vanish on the physical grid. This gives exact
nodal recurrences without assuming an off-grid eigen-equation.

In the scaled row variable \(t=j/N\), the four blocks are the
values of \(G_n\), their derivatives, the values of \(H_n\),
and their derivatives. Their triangular couplings retain the
forcing from \(G_n\) into \(H_n\). A confluent Vandermonde
basis retains each double characteristic root. Scaling its
generalized-eigenvector column by \(N^{-1/2}\), and scaling
the four blocks by \(1,N,N,N^2\), bounds each transformed
step by its largest root modulus plus \(O(N^{-1/2})\).
The resulting literal finite-\(N\) propagator satisfies
\[
 \|\Phi_N(k,j)\|
 \le C N^{5/2}
 \exp\left\{N\int_{j/N}^{k/N}
            \max_\ell\log|\tau_\ell(t)|\,dt
                 +C(k-j)/\sqrt N+C\right\}.
\]
There is a corresponding backward bound with inverse roots.
The constants depend on the fixed power and interior interval.

The [strict modulus-order theorem](research_terminal_twist_global_modulus_order.md)
then removes the maximization over changing branches.
For every \(|n|\ge2\), exactly one selected forward shift has
largest modulus throughout \(0<t<1/2\). For \(|n|=1\), the
only shift has modulus one. The proof writes
\[
 y=2-4\zeta^2,\qquad
 f_m(2-4\zeta^2)-2=4[\zeta U_{m-1}(\zeta)]^2.
\]
For each conjugate pair, the growing modulus is
\(\exp(2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{asinh}(\zeta/\sqrt a))\),
where \(a=\tan^2(\pi t)\) and \(\zeta\) is in the first quadrant.
On each fixed-modulus ellipse, the modulus of
\(\zeta U_{m-1}(\zeta)\) increases strictly along the quadrant.
Two distinct pairs therefore cannot have the same growing
modulus. Endpoint labels order all the branches once and for all.
The reciprocal pairing also identifies the largest backward rate.

Thus the upper-bound integral on a compact interior interval
is the action of one globally labeled branch. Its improper
integral over the entire physical interval is finite.
The separate whole-terminal argument below handles the
endpoints by coarse estimates before taking the shrinking-region
limit; it does not assume a uniform interior transfer estimate
there. A nonzero coefficient on the maximal branch remains unproved.

## Whole terminal upper rate and both original boundary anchors

The [whole-terminal theorem](research_whole_terminal_characteristic_upper_bound.md)
closes the endpoint initialization and upper propagation for
every fixed signed power \(n\). With
\[
 \mathcal I_n=\int_0^{1/2}\log\rho_{1,|n|}(t)\,dt
 \quad (|n|\ge2),\qquad
 \mathcal I_0=\mathcal I_{1}=\mathcal I_{-1}=0,
\]
it proves
\[
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
   \log\bigl(\|T(R^{-n})\|_{[-2,2]}
         +\|T(R^{-n}Q_0)\|_{[-2,2]}\bigr)
                  \le\mathcal I_n,
 \qquad Q_0=\partial_wK_N(c_0,\cdot).
\]
The integral uses the single maximal branch already identified.
This is an upper rate, not an equality of rates.

The initialization is taken from the actual source. The
kernel values \(K_N(c_j,\cdot)\) and first derivatives at every
fixed initial row have polynomial real norm, by finitely many
steps of the original forced recurrence. Their trace formulas
with \(R^{-n}\), and with \(R^{-n}Q_0\), therefore give
polynomial initial data for both \(G_n\) and \(H_n\).
No smallness assumption is imposed on an arbitrary solution.

For \(m=|n|\), the row coefficients and their first derivatives
are bounded by a fixed power of \(N/d_j\), where
\[
 d_j=\min\{j-m+1,\ \lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor-m-j+1\}.
\]
Products across an endpoint region of width \(\epsilon N\)
cost at most
\(\exp\{N C_n\epsilon\log(e/\epsilon)+O_n(\log N)\}\).
The last admissible step produces the final physical value;
no singular next row is used. At odd levels that value is
the simple node \(-2\), where no spectral derivative is imposed.
Full-Hermite reconstruction recovers the ordinary polynomial
norm from these values and the retained double-root derivatives.
Taking \(N\to\infty\) first and then \(\epsilon\downarrow0\)
gives the displayed whole-interval rate.

There is also an immediate bound for the two actual anchors
in the ordinary branching equation. For any canonical
\(p_N\) of polynomial real norm, put
\[
 \mathcal A_{0,N}=\kappa^n\phi_N(G_n p_N),\qquad
 \mathcal A_{1,N}=\kappa^n\phi_N(H_n p_N).
\]
Then
\[
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
 \log(1+|\mathcal A_{0,N}|+|\mathcal A_{1,N}|)
                  \le\mathcal I_n.
\]
The proof bounds canonical multiplication and the original
trace with polynomial cost, including product-rule normals.
Thus the earlier missing arbitrary-power derivative-anchor
upper bound is now supplied by \(H_n\) itself.
For a fixed product of microscopic endpoint kernels, the
previously established polynomial real-norm estimate supplies
the hypothesis on \(p_N\).

This terminal theorem alone does not bound the mixed forcing
\(V_nM_r\) in the ordinary branching equation. The later
whole-product theorem supplies a rate for its coherent sum,
as recorded below. The terminal theorem does
not compare \(\mathcal I_n\) with the filled geometric volume,
prove a nonzero coefficient, or establish the finite-exception
theorem.

## Exact algebraic closure for any fixed number of endpoint factors

The [tensor closure theorem](research_endpoint_product_tensor_annihilator.md)
addresses an ordinary product of \(r\) endpoint kernels.
The exact forced equation for each kernel becomes a rational
three-dimensional recurrence after adjoining
\(p(v)=P_N(v+v^{-1})\), which is invariant under \(v\mapsto q^2v\).
Its third component retains the source
\(p/(v+v^{-1}-c_0)\) with its removable continuation.
Tensoring these recurrences gives rank \(3^r\);
differentiating gives rank \(2\cdot3^r\) and retains the
literal product-rule derivatives.

Finite elimination, performed at the actual specialized
parameters, yields a polynomial relation
\[
 \sum_{k=0}^{2\cdot3^r} A_k(C)J^k P_r=0,\qquad
 P_r=\operatorname{can}\prod_{i=1}^rK_N(w_i,Z).
\]
The coefficients are not all zero, and their degrees have
a bound depending only on \(r\), independent of \(N\).
At rank changes the construction chooses a nonzero minor
for the actual rank; it does not assume that one generic
minor survives every specialization. The corresponding
finite-dimensional operator need not be nonzero at small levels.

Original turns give the exact ordered relation
\[
 \sum_k A_k(D_n)J^k V_nP_r=0.
\]
This bounds the number of operator bands for fixed \(r,n\).
It gives neither a nonvanishing leading coefficient on a
propagation interval nor a norm bound for the solution.
Even for one factor the source produces the essential factor
\((D_n-c_0)(w-J)\); retaining only the homogeneous microscopic
roots would discard the terminal growth already established.
The original inhomogeneous equation and initial data remain
necessary to select the actual source.

## A controlled product system retains the source under turns

The [divided-difference module](research_endpoint_product_divided_difference_module.md)
replaces the large generic elimination by an explicit construction.
For an ordinary polynomial \(f\), its half-shift average
\(\mathcal Sf\) and divided difference \(\mathcal Df\) are taken
at the two points
\[
 z_\pm=q^{\pm1}v+q^{\mp1}v^{-1},\qquad Z=v+v^{-1}.
\]
For each endpoint kernel, six polynomial channels suffice:
\[
 (f,\mathcal Df,\mathcal Sf,\mathcal S\mathcal Df,P_N,1).
\]
The last two are necessary. Although
\(\mathcal DP_N=0\), the average satisfies
\(\mathcal SP_N=4-P_N\); setting \(P_N=0\) before applying
these operations would lose an actual source term.

For \(r\) factors the resulting system has \(6^r\) channels.
A diagonal polynomial change of channels makes its rational
coefficient degrees controlled. Clearing denominators gives
\[
 [d(C)(J-c_0)I-(q-q^{-1})^2E(C)]\mathcal W=0,
 \qquad \deg d=33r,\quad\deg E_{ab}\le33r.
\]
The coefficients stay bounded for bounded complex microscopic
endpoint parameters, and \(d(Z)\to(Z-2)^{33r}\).
After an original turn \(V_n\), replace \(C\) by its exact
conjugate \(D_n=V_nCV_n^{-1}\). Recovery of the ungauged
product remains a forced equation,
\[
 (D_n-2)^rY=\mathcal F_*,
 \qquad
 Y=V_n\operatorname{can}\prod_iK_N(w_i,\cdot).
\]
It is never obtained by inverting \(D_n-2\).

The principal characteristic is
\((x_n-2)^{33r}(y-2)\). In particular this construction
introduces no additional characteristic at \(x_n=-2\).
All ordinary equations are established before canonical
reduction. Their residual multiples of \(P_N\) then yield
the exact physical values and first-normal equations.
This algebraic result controls the system to which an
analytic transfer estimate can be applied; it does not
by itself bound its solution or its leading coefficient.

## A whole-product upper bound and the actual mixed forcing

The [whole-product theorem](research_turned_endpoint_product_characteristic_upper_bound.md)
first proved, for every fixed number \(r\) of factors, every
fixed integer \(n\), and bounded complex parameters \(\alpha_i\),
\[
 B_N=\operatorname{can}\prod_{i=1}^r
              K_N(2\cosh(\alpha_i/N),\cdot),\qquad
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
   \log\left(1+\sup_{\boldsymbol\alpha}\|V_nB_N\|_{[-2,2]}\right)
                  \le2\mathcal I_n.
\]
All fixed parameter and spectral derivatives retain this rate.
Since \(\mathcal I_{\pm1}=0\), one unit turn of any fixed
endpoint product is subexponential. The proof does not assert
a polynomial bound.

There are two separate costs. The actual fixed initial rows
are bounded by the terminal functions \(G_n,H_n\), with
rate \(\mathcal I_n\). Transfer across the interior has
another cost \(\mathcal I_n\). The product system's terminal
Jordan chains have length \(66r\); rescaling these chains
and the derivative/source blocks makes every additional
coupling cost \(O(N^{-1/(66r)})\) per row. Coarse endpoint
bounds cost \(O(N\epsilon\log(e/\epsilon))\), after which
\(N\) tends to infinity before \(\epsilon\) tends to zero.
The proof separately completes the shorter product-recovery
window at the last physical rows. These steps retain the
actual source and both parities throughout.

There is a direct consequence for the mixed term in the
original branching equation. Denote that combined canonical
forcing by \(M_r\), put \(w_i=2\cosh(\alpha_i/N)\), and set
\(\lambda_r=\sum_iw_i-(r-1)c_0\). The exact operator theorem gives
\[
 V_nM_r=(\lambda_r-J)V_nB_N
       -\frac{\eta\kappa^n}{N^2}
                    \left(\sum_iP_N(w_i)\right)G_n.
\]
Here \(P_N(w_i)=4\cosh^2(\alpha_i/2)\) is uniformly bounded,
\(\lambda_r=2+O(N^{-2})\), and \(\|J\|\le34N^3\).
Consequently the combined forcing also has upper rate
\(2\mathcal I_n\). Cauchy and Markov inequalities retain
the rate for fixed derivatives. This conclusion concerns
the coherent sum \(M_r\); it does not separately estimate
every mixed summand or an uncontrolled spectator.

## The first turn removes the extra terminal cost

The [first-turn theorem](research_first_turn_endpoint_product_initialization.md)
sharpens both upper bounds in the preceding section. For every
fixed original microscopic endpoint product \(B_N\), it proves
\[
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
       \log\left(1+\sup_{\boldsymbol\alpha}\|TB_N\|_{[-2,2]}\right)=0.
\]
The same bound holds simultaneously for the first turns of
all gauged channels in the exact product module. This simultaneous
statement matters: the later recurrence needs their actual initial
values and derivatives, not only those of the product.

Conjugating the module by \(T\) gives
\[
 [d(J)(C-c_0)I-(q-q^{-1})^2E(J)]\mathcal F=0,\qquad
 (J-2)^rY=\mathcal F_*,
\]
where \(Y=TB_N\), \(\mathcal F=T\operatorname{can}\mathcal W\),
and \(k=\deg d=33r\).
The forward leading matrix includes the correction
\[
 d_k(c_{j+k}-c_0)I-(q-q^{-1})^2E_k.
\]
It cannot be discarded at the first rows. Instead, since
\[
 |c_l-c_0|\ge16l^2/N^2\qquad
       (1\le l\le\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor)
\]
at both parities, a sufficiently large fixed starting index
makes its scalar part dominate the uniformly bounded correction.
All initial rows are still fixed rows and have polynomial bounds
from the literal traces \(\phi_N(F_jp)\), \(\phi_N(Q_jp)\).
In the interior, the limiting companion has only the shift root
\(1\). The same full-normal transfer and endpoint recovery
therefore give the displayed subexponential estimate.

For the subsequent signed turn, the actual initial values are
\[
 (V_np)(c_j)=\kappa^n\phi_N(R^{-n}(Tp)F_j),\qquad
 (V_np)'(c_j)=\kappa^n\phi_N(R^{-n}(Tp)Q_j).
\]
The crossing's physical values have modulus one and its
derivatives cost polynomially. The simultaneous first-turn
bound makes these initial vectors subexponential. Only the
terminal transport action remains:
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
   \log\left(1+\sup_{\boldsymbol\alpha}\|V_nB_N\|_{[-2,2]}\right)
             \le\mathcal I_n.
 \quad}
\]
The preceding exact branching identity likewise improves the
upper rate of the combined mixed forcing \(V_nM_r\) to
\(\mathcal I_n\). Fixed spectral and parameter derivatives
retain these rates.

This removes an actual overestimate of the source initialization;
it does not assume a small initial vector from its characteristic
equation. It also gives no lower coefficient and no closure
under turning a product of already transformed factors.
A subexponential real norm is not a bound on an arbitrary
fixed complex neighborhood.

## An enlarged forest reduction controls an entire boundary current

The [forest certificate theorem](research_endpoint_product_forest_current_certificate.md)
allows an original endpoint product at a unit-power leaf.
Removing that leaf uses the exact identity
\[
 T(R^\sigma Q)=R^{-\sigma}U_\sigma Q,\qquad \sigma=\pm1.
\]
It changes the neighboring power by \(-\sigma\) and puts
the complete factor \(U_\sigma\operatorname{can}Q\) at
that neighbor. The whole-product theorem bounds this factor
subexponentially. Several such factors may meet at one vertex.

The restriction is precise: a vertex which has received one
of these factors is not itself turned. It can receive more
factors and can eventually be removed by an isolated trace
or by evaluation against an adjacent undecorated zero leaf.
The latter operation retains its actual scalar:
\[
 \kappa^{n_w}\widetilde Q_w(c_0)
 =\kappa^{n_w+\sum_v\sigma_v}
       \prod_v\phi_N(R^{\sigma_v}Q_v).
\]
The original endpoint product at \(w\) evaluates to one,
but the received factors need not. Each displayed trace
has a polynomial bound; nothing is divided out when it
vanishes.

Any fixed forest admitting this reduction sequence has
an entire source of rate at most zero, uniformly in the
shared bounded complex endpoint parameters, with all first
normals retained. This strictly enlarges the previous
static-mark certificate. It includes arbitrarily many
decorated unit leaves meeting a common vertex with an
arbitrary fixed power and its own endpoint product.

For the original microscopic current, take a nonempty
current set containing every selected vertex adjacent to
an untraced outside vertex. If the surviving closed forest
admits this certificate, the theorem bounds the entire
current \(I_{C,N}\), without a Newton-band projection:
\[
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}N^{-1}\log|I_{C,N}|\le0.
\]
For a supplied positive parent action \(M_G>0\), this is
a strict gap below \(M_G\). Ordinary outside continuation
costs at most
\(\exp\{N\sum_b d_b|\operatorname{Im}u_b|+o(N)\}\),
where \(d_b\) is the original outside incidence degree.

The next unbounded operation is explicit:
\[
 U_\tau\operatorname{can}
       \left(Q_w\prod_v U_{\sigma_v}Q_v\right).
\]
Its input is no longer an original endpoint product.
Already \(U_\sigma U_\sigma=V_{2\sigma}\) can produce
positive exponential growth. Thus the proved reduction
cannot be iterated without keeping the additional action.
Macroscopic heights, other current patterns, and the
nonzero full geometric coefficient remain outside this theorem.

## The terminal growth integral is a normalized stationary action

The [action calibration](research_terminal_characteristic_action_calibration.md)
identifies the previously bounded terminal growth integral.
For \(m=|n|\ge2\), let \(\zeta_m(h)\) be the dominant
first-quadrant solution of
\[
 \zeta U_{m-1}(\zeta)=ih,\qquad 0<h<1.
\]
Its label is fixed by continuation from \(\cos(\pi/m)\)
at \(h=0\), with the separately specified square-root
branch when \(m=2\). The characteristic integral is
\[
 \mathcal I_m=\int_0^{1/2}
   2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{asinh}
       \bigl(\zeta_m(\sin\pi v)\cot\pi v\bigr)\,dv.
\]
The proof constructs a stationary action \(\mathcal S_m(u)\)
with the original primitive Fourier charge and the exact
endpoint normalization \(\mathcal S_m(\pi)=-i\pi/m\).
It then proves
\[
 \mathcal I_m=\operatorname{Re}\mathcal S_m(0).
\]
Thus the additive real constant is fixed; this is not
merely equality of action derivatives.

Writing \(G_{\mathrm{Cat}}\) for Catalan's constant, the
same note proves
\[
 \mathcal I_2=\frac{2G_{\mathrm{Cat}}}{\pi},
 \qquad
 0<\mathcal I_m<\frac{4G_{\mathrm{Cat}}}{\pi},
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_m=\frac{4G_{\mathrm{Cat}}}{\pi}
                  -\frac{\pi}{m^2}+O(m^{-4}).
\]
The actions increase strictly with \(m\). To prove this,
the stationary point is continued to every real \(p\ge2\);
if \(t_p=2A_p-2iB_p\), its real action has derivative
\(2A_pB_p/\pi>0\). The endpoint expansion then gives the
displayed deficit.

The result calibrates one transported boundary action.
It neither asserts that this boundary continuation is
a positive ideal-cell subdivision nor assigns its
deficit to removed edges in an arbitrary parent.
A marked geometric comparison and a nonzero coefficient
in the closed original source remain separate requirements.

## Exact transformation of the boundary period and work

The [boundary covariance theorem](research_unit_turn_boundary_action_covariance.md)
relates the turn operator to a local geometric action without
changing its normalization. In the polarization where \(J\)
is diagonal, \(Z=-2\cos t\) and
\[
 TV_nT=\kappa^nR^{-n}
       =d_{N,n}\exp\{Ng_n(t)\},\qquad
 g_n(t)=\frac{in}{4\pi}(\pi^2-t^2),\quad
 d_{N,n}=e^{-i\pi n/2+i\pi n/(4N)}
\]
as full physical jets. The additive constant comes from
the original crossing carrier.

For a local phase \(S\), write \(p=S'(t)\). The state
map is
\[
 (t,p)\longmapsto(t,p-int/(2\pi)).
\]
The conjugated operator uses the inverse pullback.
Distinguishing these signs gives the exact classical
twist recurrence and sends the endpoint condition
\(C=2\) to \(D_n=2\).

Write \(t=s+ih\) and \(-\pi S'=K+iG\). Then
\[
 K_n=K-nh/2,\qquad G_n=G+ns/2,\qquad
 \operatorname{Re}(S+g_n)-\operatorname{Re}S
                         =nsh/(2\pi).
\]
The boundary Legendre expression
\[
 E_b=E_*-\pi\operatorname{Re}S+hG
\]
is therefore unchanged. Its differential is
\(K\,ds+h\,dG\), which is unchanged as well.
An independently supplied convex energy pulls back
under the real affine shear \((s,G)\mapsto(s,G+ns/2)\);
its positive Hessian is preserved on that transformed
domain.

Returning to the original polarization retains both exact
turn kernels in a double Frobenius trace. The note writes
the selected unit-charge Fourier action and its period rows,
while retaining the other Fourier terms and vertical
currents in the exact source formula. It does not assert
that the selected action estimates the whole trace.

This makes the remaining geometric requirement precise.
One must match the transformed domain, rows and logarithmic
lifts to the actual marked parent geometry after composition.
The unchanged parent angle domain cannot simply be reused.
At a saturated endpoint its removed-edge energy constants
already cancel from the surviving action; they cannot also
pay for a transported source bound.

## Why the literal positive first-turn decomposition is unavailable

The [first-turn capacity theorem](research_endpoint_first_turn_angle_capacity.md)
checks the proposed geometric interpretation against the actual
source identity
\[
 (TQ_N)(Z_t)=\phi_{Z_u}
       \left[K_N(Z_u,Z_t)\prod_{i=1}^rK_N(w_i,Z_u)\right].
\]
At \(u\) this has zero crossing power. Its selected lower
Fourier sector of charge \(\ell\) requires
\[
 \sum_i g_{u,i}+g_{u,t}=-\pi\ell.
\]
Fix all real angles, and fix admitted opposite incidence
variables. The original closed square inequalities allow
exactly the local capacity
\[
 2\pi|\ell|\le
       \sum_i(\pi-|s_i|)+\pi-|s_t|.
\]
This is an if-and-only-if statement for those free row
variables; in a surrounding network it is only a necessary
condition, since other rows and matching conditions remain.

For real microscopic endpoints
\(w_i=2\cosh(\alpha_i/N)=-2\cos(\pi-i\alpha_i/N)\),
the original real endpoint angles are \(s_i=\pm\pi\).
Thus all \(g_{u,i}\) vanish and the new edge has capacity
at most \(\pi/2\), whereas a unit row needs magnitude \(\pi\).
There is no closed assignment in any nonzero lower Fourier
sector. The obstruction also holds for any fixed number of
endpoints in shrinking real-angle collars around saturation.

This does not make the exact turn vanish.
The original product satisfies \(Q_N(c_0)=1\), and \(T^2=1\).
For one factor its exact turn is the dualizing divided difference
\[
 TK_N(w,\cdot)(Z)
        =\frac{P_N(Z)-P_N(w)}{\eta N^2(Z-w)}.
\]
The separately proved first-turn theorem above now bounds
general fixed products directly. It avoids identifying this
source with a nonexistent positive minimizer of its literal
first-turn square diagram. A geometric comparison after
recoupling still requires a compatible marked representation.

## A filled leaf with arbitrary fixed twist power

The [literal leaf theorem](research_filled_leaf_endpoint_product_upper_bound.md)
estimates the expression that occurs when a leaf is integrated out:
\[
 F_N(Z)=\phi_W\left[
 K_N(Z,W)R^n(W)\prod_{i=1}^rK_N(w_i,W)\right],
 \qquad w_i=2\cosh(\alpha_i/N).
\]
Here \(n,r\) are fixed and the complex parameters \(\alpha_i\) lie
in a fixed bounded set. The crossing is multiplied inside the
original trace. This placement matters: the expression is
\(T(R^nB_N)\), not \(V_nB_N\).

The theorem proves
\[
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
 \log\left(1+\sup_{\boldsymbol\alpha}\|F_N\|_{[-2,2]}\right)
 \le \mathcal I_n.
\]
The same rate holds for fixed derivatives. In particular,
\(n=0,\pm1\) gives a subexponential bound.

The proof conjugates the entire endpoint-product system by
\(TR^n\). Its two operator coordinates become \(J,D_{-n}\), and
the forced recovery equation becomes \((J-2)^rF_N=\mathcal F_{N,*}\).
The leading coefficients have explicit nonzero products of the
original physical shift coefficients. Polynomial bounds for the
input channels give polynomial initial values and first derivatives.
Propagation through the interior costs the integrated terminal
characteristic action. Coarse bounds near both ends have vanishing
exponential cost as those neighborhoods shrink. The remaining
recovery rows and full value-and-derivative interpolation complete
the real-interval estimate.

This is an upper bound for an arbitrary fixed leaf power. It
does not supply a lower coefficient, permit arbitrary repeated
branching, or compare \(\mathcal I_n\) with the volume budget of a
surrounding partially filled knot complement.

## Retaining the exposed color in the leaf estimate

The [physical-color theorem](research_filled_leaf_physical_color_profile.md)
sharpens the preceding norm bound. Let
\[
 \mathcal J_n(u)=\int_0^uL_n(v)\,dv,\qquad
 c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N).
\]
Uniformly over all original physical rows, the actual leaf values
and angular first derivatives have upper exponent
\(\mathcal J_n(j/N)\). Fixed exterior-parameter derivatives have
the same bound, as do first spectral derivatives at the double
nodes. The odd simple node requires only its value.

The proof stops the existing value-and-normal recurrence at the
requested row. Initial rows have polynomial bounds, the left
endpoint contributes a vanishing rate, and the compact portion
costs only the corresponding partial characteristic integral.
Near the last endpoint, the whole norm estimate suffices because
the remaining integral tends to zero. No new choice of initial
solution or phase coefficient is made.

The normalized stationary action supplies the exact identity
\[
 \mathcal J_n(u)
   =\operatorname{Re}S_{|n|}(\pi-2\pi u),\qquad |n|\ge2.
\]
The actual angular color has the additional half-row shift
\(1/(2N)\), which changes this continuous exponent uniformly
by \(o(1)\).

This preserves information that the scalar ceiling
\(\mathcal I_n\) discards. It does not establish the same
profile between physical nodes or on a complex boundary contour.
It also does not identify the continued stationary action with a
positive geometric minimum at every boundary angle.

## The leaf's boundary energy and the parent comparison

The [retained-boundary profile theorem](research_retained_boundary_leaf_energy_profile.md)
keeps the variables that a scalar terminal ceiling discards.
Let \(u,g\) be the leaf angle and outgoing incidence, let \(s,G\)
be the neighboring angle and opposite incidence, and let
\(\beta_i\) be the incidences on the deleted side of its cut edges.
The original unit row is \(g-nu/2=-\pi\). For \(n=\sigma m\ne0\),
its complete weak feasible fiber is
\[
 u=\sigma v,\qquad g=mv/2-\pi,\qquad
 \frac{\pi+|s|}{m}\le v\le
 \min\left\{\pi-2\max(|G|,|\beta_i|),
                      \frac{3\pi-|s|}{m}\right\}.
\]
Its capacity condition is
\[
 |s|+2m\max(|G|,|\beta_i|)\le(m-1)\pi.
\]
An empty interval does not imply a zero quantum source.

Minimizing the actual edge energy on this interval gives a
convex retained-boundary function \(\mathfrak e_n\). At a regular
interior minimum its differential is
\(d\mathfrak e_n=k_w\,ds+h_w\,dG\). In particular, a real
external angle requires stationarity in \(G\); it does not
generally require \(G=0\). Near the complete neighbor, with
inactive cut constraints, minimizing over \(G\) recovers the
normalized stationary leaf action. The note does not extend
that identification beyond its positive regular neighborhood.

On a saturated deletion face, several nonadjacent leaf fibers
can be minimized simultaneously while all shared neighboring
variables remain fixed. This infimal projection preserves
exactly the parent-energy comparison and its endpoint-work
terms. At the parent's specified heights, it retains the
already proved strict boundary gap.

For \(|n|\ge2\), the complete-neighbor terminal constant is
\(\pi(M_\infty-\mathcal I_n)\). The difference
\[
 \mathfrak d_n=\mathfrak e_n-\pi(M_\infty-\mathcal I_n)
\]
is nonnegative. Replacing the full profiles by these constants
raises the projected action by \(\sum_\ell\mathfrak d_{n_\ell}/\pi\).
This is the exact coupling cost that a scalar norm estimate
must pay. The parent gap alone does not pay it automatically.

The result is a classical comparison with all constraints and
work retained. A quantum upper bound on the relevant complex
boundary with that same profile is still needed.

## Exact equations for combining transformed boundary factors

The [full-step interface](research_full_step_repeated_turn_tensor_interface.md)
treats
\[
 U_\tau\operatorname{can}
 \left(Q_{\rm base}\prod_{i=1}^{b}V_{n_i}Q_i\right),
 \qquad \tau=\pm1,
\]
where each \(Q_i\) and \(Q_{\rm base}\) is an original fixed product
of microscopic endpoint kernels. The numbers of factors and all
twist powers are fixed before \(N\) grows.

The central algebraic point is that the full angular shift
\(v\mapsto q^2v\) preserves
\[
 \mathcal B_N=\mathbb C[v,v^{-1}]/((v^N+1)^2).
\]
This quotient retains both the values and first derivatives at the
physical angular roots. Its decomposition
\[
 \mathcal B_N=\mathcal A_N\oplus(v-v^{-1})\mathcal A_N
\]
also retains the odd derivative at \(v=-1\). Ordinary half shifts
would not preserve this quotient.

The proof builds full-shift equations for each actual factor,
multiplies their columns at the shared variable, and descends the
result to the two spectral components above. Explicit polynomial
identities then express the full-shift mean and divided difference
in the original operators \(C,J,D_1\). Conjugating their ordered
products performs the final turn exactly. All denominator factors,
original source equations and forced recovery data are retained;
clearing a factor is not treated as an inverse at its zeros.

Before the final turn, every constructed component has upper rate
\(\sum_i\mathcal I_{n_i}\). The same rate bounds its actual fixed
initial rows after the turn. This follows from the previously proved
whole-product estimates and the original trace formulas, with
polynomial losses for multiplication and derivative interpolation.

The resulting equations have ranks and orders bounded independently
of \(N\). Their highest shift coefficients after the final turn
have not been shown uniformly invertible. Thus this result gives
exact equations and controlled initial data; it does not yet give
a growth bound for the final output, a geometric parent comparison,
or the nonzero contribution required for the volume identity.

## Which terminal products reach an interior color from infinity

The [projective resonance theorem](research_terminal_product_projective_resonance.md)
classifies the reduced characteristic correspondence of a product
with fixed nonzero signed powers \(n_1,\ldots,n_r\). Put
\[
 \gamma=\sum_i\frac1{n_i},\qquad
 L=\operatorname{lcm}_i|n_i|,\qquad M=\prod_i|n_i|.
\]
For an actual outer unit turn \(U_\sigma\), a branch over old
spectral infinity has a finite new spectral limit if and only if
\[
 \gamma=-\sigma.
\]
The minus sign comes from the inverse action on characteristic
points. Conjugation substitutes operators in equations; points
transform by the inverse substitution.

There are \(M/L\) labeled normalization branches at old infinity,
each with old ramification order \(L\). In the resonant case
the possible new limits are exactly
\[
 2\cos(2\pi k/L),\qquad 0\le k<L.
\]
Each phase occurs on \(M/L^2\) labeled branches. Interior cosine
values pair two inverse phases; the endpoint values have one
phase each. Thus an interior limit occurs exactly when resonance
holds and \(L\ge3\). Away from resonance the new coordinate
instead has pole order \(L|\gamma+\sigma|\).

The proof uses convergent Puiseux expansions of the already
identified terminal curves and the exact twist automorphism.
It retains repeated factors as labeled factors. Their generic
normal algebra has dimension \(2^r\), with maximal nilpotent
order \(r+1\); these numbers are not image-curve multiplicities.
Some entire reduced branches contract to an endpoint, and the
note gives an exact identity detecting that contraction.

If separate source branches are also admitted, apply the
criterion to every active terminal subset. A sufficient condition
excluding all such interior infinity points is
\[
 \sum_{\sigma n_i<0}|n_i|^{-1}<1.
\]
This permits any fixed number of factors. It neither proves
the chosen finite matrix regular nor controls its finite-level
perturbations. A possible characteristic branch need not occur
with nonzero coefficient in the quantum source.

## Finitely many minimal resonances, with unbounded complements retained

The [finite-core corollary](research_terminal_resonance_finite_core.md)
organizes the signed reciprocal condition without enumerating
individual knots. If \(\sum_i1/n_i=\epsilon\), \(\epsilon=\pm1\),
choose an inclusion-minimal subset with the same sum. Its
complement has reciprocal sum zero.

For a core of length \(s\), order the magnitudes
\(m_1\le\cdots\le m_s\). Every proper prefix has nonzero residual
\(R_k=\epsilon-\sum_{i\le k}1/n_i\). Since its denominator divides
\(\prod_{i\le k}m_i\), and its remaining terms have magnitudes
at most \(1/m_{k+1}\),
\[
 m_{k+1}\le(s-k)\prod_{i\le k}m_i,\qquad
 m_k\le s^{2^{k-1}}.
\]
Thus fixed arity permits only finitely many minimal cores.
Same-sign resonant tuples are themselves minimal and hence
form a finite set at that arity.

Mixed signs retain an essential infinite part. For example
\((\epsilon,p,-p)\) is resonant for every \(p\ge3\); its
minimal core is the singleton \((\epsilon)\), but its full
phase denominator is \(p\). The corresponding characteristic
limits include \(2\cos(2\pi k/p)\), whose union is dense in
\([-2,2]\). The complement cannot be discarded from the
projection or from the original finite source.

This is a bound on minimal arithmetic resonances. It is not
a Dehn-filling length threshold, a topological cancellation
theorem, or a proof of finitely many exceptional fillings.

## An opposite pair transports its insertion exactly

The [opposite-power theorem](research_opposite_power_spectator_reduction.md)
uses the original bilinear Frobenius trace \(\phi_N\).
For arbitrary complex inputs \(f,g\), every integer \(n\), and an
ordinary polynomial insertion \(h\), it proves
\[
 \phi_N\!\left(h(V_nf)(V_{-n}g)\right)
              =\phi_N\!\left(f\,h(D_n)g\right).
\]
Here \(D_n=V_nCV_{-n}\), and all coefficients of \(h\) are
held as external scalars. The proof transfers the self-adjoint
operator \(V_n\) across the bilinear pairing and conjugates
multiplication by \(h\). It preserves every physical first normal.

For \(h=1\) the powers disappear exactly. If \(f,g\) are fixed
microscopic endpoint products, the resulting trace is polynomially
bounded. More generally, fixed-degree insertions with polynomial
coefficients obey the same type of bound, using the existing
polynomial operator bound for \(D_n\). Consequently fixed-row
values after the next \(T\) have polynomial bounds.

This last statement does not include the next output normal.
At a double physical row \(c_j\), its required insertion
\(\partial_wK_N(c_j,Z)\) has degree exactly \(N-1-j\).
A full boundary kernel or a crossing insertion likewise has
degree growing with \(N\). The conjugated insertion remains
explicit and cannot be dropped.

For one equal endpoint kernel, the closing is particularly simple:
\[
 \phi_N((V_nK_w)(V_{-n}K_w))
 =\eta\frac{P_N'(w)}{N^2}
 =\eta\frac{\sinh\alpha}{N\sinh(\alpha/N)},
 \qquad w=2\cosh(\alpha/N),\quad \eta=(-1)^{N-1}.
\]
For bounded real \(\alpha\), its modulus is between one and
a fixed constant. This nonvanishing concerns precisely this
closing. It is not a statement about an arbitrary attached
exterior or a general reciprocal-zero product.

## Actual propagation on a regular interior arc

The [regular-arc theorem](research_repeated_turn_regular_arc_source_bound.md)
turns the exact repeated-product equations into a quantitative
bound for their actual source. Choose a square minor of the
commuting principal row matrix and lift its adjugate as an ordered
shift operator. This gives an exact equation
\[
 \{p(v,E)I+N^{-1}K_N(v,E)\}\mathcal Y_N=0.
\]
The scalar polynomial \(p\) is the chosen principal determinant;
all higher-order shift terms remain in \(K_N\). A maximal-minor
Bezout construction can replace this determinant by the generic
gcd, while retaining its coefficient denominators. No quantum
leading coefficient is inverted.

On a compact physical arc where the highest surviving coefficient
of \(p\) is uniformly nonzero, the original values and first normals
form a finite block recurrence. Its classical spectral radius
\(\rho(u)\) is the largest modulus of the roots of \(p\).
An explicit extra factor \(E-1\), if needed, ensures
\(\rho\ge1\) in the stated upper envelope.

The existing slow-forward/fast-backward argument applies to this
block. The actual entire column has a coarse \(\exp(CN)\) ceiling.
With a fixed positive-length right buffer, its terminal fast data
therefore contribute only \(\exp[-cN\log N+O(N)]\) at the target.
If \(A_a\) is the actual exponential budget of the initial
value-and-normal packet at a positive color fraction \(a\), then
\[
 \limsup_N N^{-1}\log
 \bigl(\|y_N(t_N)\|+\|y_N'(t_N)\|\bigr)
 \le A_a+\int_a^t\log\rho(u)\,du .
\]
Every terminal datum is retained in this comparison.

The construction produces regular arcs outside a finite algebraic
exceptional set on each valid fixed parameter chart. The roots are
those of the displayed principal presentation; their envelope has
not been identified with the geometric action. The theorem also
does not supply \(A_a\) from the fixed initial rows, cross the
exceptional colors, or establish a lower coefficient.

## The possible interior failures of a monic equation are explicit

The [projective certificate](research_repeated_turn_projective_monic_certificate.md)
concerns a fixed product of transformed endpoint factors followed
by a unit turn \(U_\tau\), with \(\tau\in\{1,-1\}\). If the nonzero
powers in the factors are \(n_1,\ldots,n_b\), define
\[
 \mathcal E_\tau=
 \bigcup_{\substack{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,b\}\\
                    \sum_{i\in S}1/n_i=-\tau}}
 \left\{2\cos(2\pi k/L_S):\,k\in\mathbb Z,\ 0<k<L_S/2\right\},
 \qquad L_S=\operatorname{lcm}_{i\in S}|n_i|.
\]
This is a finite set for each fixed list of powers.

The proof checks the full principal presentation, including the
recovery channels, the base alias and the polynomial clearings.
Away from the old finite clearing colors, its support consists
of products of active terminal branches and source shifts equal
to one. Under the unit turn, a new interior color with unbounded
shift forces the old color to infinity. The projective resonance
classification then places that new color in \(\mathcal E_\tau\).
Old components at finite clearing colors cannot create another
such limit.

On the complement of this set, the leading coefficients of all
members of the maximal-minor ideal generate the unit ideal locally.
A finite combination gives a monic polynomial in that actual ideal.
Its adjugate certificate therefore lifts to the exact equation used
by the regular-arc bound. This preserves nilpotent multiplicities;
it does not replace the ideal by its radical.

An exceptional phase \(a/b\) in lowest terms can meet the original
physical grid exactly when \(b\) is even. In that case it does so
at infinitely many levels. For odd \(b\), the nearest physical
colors are still at distance of order \(1/N\). Thus none of these
colors can be omitted without an additional argument.

This theorem removes unspecified leading-coefficient failures on
the remaining compact intervals. It does not cross
\(\mathcal E_\tau\), provide the initial-packet budget, identify
the finite-root envelope with hyperbolic volume, or prove a
nonzero geometric coefficient. Its finite exception set concerns
colors, not knot or filling assignments.

## The regular-arc exponent can use the full principal support

The [support-envelope theorem](research_principal_support_envelope_on_regular_arcs.md)
removes an avoidable loss from the preceding monic construction.
At a fixed color, separate the roots of a monic ideal member into
those present in the full rank-drop support and those absent from
it. Coprime factorization gives holomorphic factors nearby.
A finite Bezout identity in the quotient by the original monic
polynomial proves that the factor containing the support still
belongs to the actual maximal-minor ideal. Multiplicities and
all source channels remain; this is not radical reduction.

The resulting local exact equation has a root radius arbitrarily
close to the radius of the full principal support at its center.
Finite overlapping intervals and the buffered source estimate
then give, at fixed microscopic parameters,
\[
 \limsup_N\frac1N\log
       \bigl(\|y_N(t_N)\|+\|y_N'(t_N)\|\bigr)
 \le A(a)+\int_a^t\log r(u)\,du ,
\]
where
\[
 r(u)=\max\bigl(\{1\}\cup
 \{|t|:\operatorname{rank}
             \mathcal R_0(e^{2\pi iu},t)<d,\ t\ne0\}\bigr).
\]
Here \(A(a)\) is a common actual bound for every fixed-size
initial value-and-normal packet at \(a\). It is finite, but
no smaller value is supplied by this argument.

Extra finite roots of an arbitrary certificate no longer enlarge
this integral. Any clearing or recovery components actually
present in the full principal support still do. The intervals
must avoid the explicit projective exception set; the argument
does not transport through a root at infinity or identify the
remaining envelope with a geometric action.

## A singular value equation need not determine the next normal

The [exact rank-loss theorem](research_simple_rank_loss_full_normal_transport.md)
describes what happens if an actual finite-level leading matrix
loses rank. Once known data have been moved to the right, the
original value and first-normal equations are
\[
 Ax=b,\qquad Ay+A'x=b'.
\]
If \(A\) has one-dimensional kernel generated by \(r\), left
kernel generated by \(\ell\), and \(\ell A'r\ne0\), compatibility
of the first equation and the second equation determine \(x\)
uniquely. They leave \(y\) undetermined by a multiple of \(r\).

For all actual rows aligned on the same unknown packet, replace
\(A\) by the stacked matrix \(B\). The full value-and-normal
packet is uniquely determined by those equations exactly when
\(B\) has full column rank. Additional future values cannot
be treated as known merely to obtain that rank.

This missing normal is visible in the original trace. At a double
physical node \(c\), the canonical polynomial
\[
 R_c(Z)=\frac{(4-c^2)P_N(Z)}{N^2(Z-c)}
\]
has derivative one there and every other physical jet zero.
For any actual spectator \(g\),
\[
                    \phi_N(R_cg)=\eta(4-c^2)g(c).
\]
The quotient by \(Z-c\) is ordinary exact polynomial division.
This identity does not assert that adding \(R_c\) to an actual
source preserves its other shifted equations.

A second differentiated residual does not supply another
homogeneous row. If the ordinary residual is
\(P_N(C_N(u))H_N(u)\), its second derivative at \(j/N\) is
\(8\pi^2N^2H_N(j/N)\); that additional source term must remain.

The theorem supplies a precise local test for the complete
finite-level system. A classical exceptional color, even if it
coincides with a physical grid point, does not itself establish
such a rank loss. Smaller quantum terms and further rows can
restore it. Their actual rank and conditioning remain to be
proved for general resonant products.

## Conditioning at a rational exceptional color

The [finite-window theorem](research_resonant_physical_window_conditioning.md)
uses the complete finite-level equations, including first normals.
Fix a rational exceptional phase \(a/b\), let
\(j_N=\lfloor Na/b\rfloor\), and keep a fixed number of neighboring
rows. On each residue class of levels, every angular color in
that window has the exact form
\[
 v_{j_N+k}=e^{2\pi ia/b}q^{\delta+2k},
 \qquad \delta=2\lfloor Na/b\rfloor+1-2Na/b.
\]
The rational number \(\delta\) is fixed on the residue class.
A further finite refinement keeps any original parity and
Gaussian carrier phases fixed. All matrix coefficients then
have meromorphic germs in \(h=1/N\), with only finite-order poles.

Specify the unknown packet \(X_N\), all supplied boundary data
\(B_N\), and the true forcing \(F_N\) before forming the matrix:
\[
                  \mathsf A_NX_N=F_N-\mathsf L_NB_N.
\]
If an actual full-column minor has first nonzero expansion
\[
              h^\nu(c(\boldsymbol\alpha)+O(h))
\]
with \(c\) a unit on the chosen compact parameter chart, the
adjugate gives a polynomial bound for the inverse. Thus
\[
       \|X_N\|\le C N^k(\|F_N\|+\|B_N\|).
\]
This uses all finite-level terms. The classical exceptional
color does not decide whether the required minor is zero.

A right boundary supplied only at rate \(C\) remains at that
rate in this estimate. The theorem does not convert a two-sided
recovery problem into propagation from lower-rate left data.
It also does not prove that a suitable window has full rank
for every resonant product.

## Exact quantum divisibility detects generic window rank failure

The [quantum-binomial criterion](research_repeated_turn_quantum_binomial_rank_criterion.md)
treats a fixed window of the exact repeated-turn equations. Its unknowns,
supplied boundary packets, first-normal equations and polynomial
clearings are specified before taking minors. The number of rows and
columns is fixed as the level \(N\) grows.

Write \(h=1/N\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and let \(v\) be the physical
angular variable. Near a rational phase \(\zeta=e^{2\pi ia/b}\),
the chosen row on a fixed level residue class has
\[
v=\zeta q^\delta,\qquad \delta=p'/b',\qquad
\gcd(p',b')=1,\quad b'>0.
\]
Neighboring rows are already included through their shifts
\(v\mapsto q^{2k}v\). The coefficients of the fixed window have
bounded degree in \(h^{\pm1},q^{\pm1},v^{\pm1}\) and the endpoint
parameters \(w_i,p_i\).

The theorem proves that the microscopic window loses column rank
identically in its independent parameters if and only if every
full-column minor is divisible by
\[
v^{b'}-\zeta^{b'}q^{p'}.
\]
The proof uses two explicit independence arguments. First, the
substitution \(p_i=P_N(w_i)\) is injective on the bounded coefficient
space when \(N\) exceeds its \(w_i\)-degrees. Second, a finite
exponential polynomial in \(h\) cannot vanish on infinitely many
levels approaching zero unless its grouped polynomial coefficients
vanish. These statements connect the exact finite-level rows to the
formal Laurent-polynomial divisibility test.

A minor without this divisor gives polynomial conditioning on each
compact parameter set where its leading \(h\)-coefficient is nonzero.
This does not establish such a minor for every component, remove a
physical nonunit clearing, or lower the exponential cost of a supplied
boundary packet. The adjacent holomorphic-recovery result concerns
the actual source after this generic nonvanishing has been proved.

## Independent endpoint parameters give a nonzero actual window minor

The [parameter-leading rank theorem](research_single_kernel_parameter_leading_window_rank.md)
proves a generic-rank statement for the exact source
\[
U_\tau\operatorname{can}\prod_{i=1}^r
V_{n_i}K_N(w_i,\cdot),
\qquad \tau=\pm1,\quad n_i\ne0 .
\]
The number of factors and their powers are arbitrary but fixed.
The endpoint parameters are independent in the coefficient argument.
Each input contains one kernel, and there is no additional base
product. The theorem does not yet cover several kernels inside
one transformed input.

For each factor the original equation is
\[
(w_i-J)f_i=p_i g_i,\qquad
(D_{n_i}-c_0)g_i=0,\qquad
p_i=P_N(w_i).
\]
The scalar crossing normalization is retained in \(g_i\).
Tensoring these companion systems and setting the formal symbols
\(p_i\) to zero separates them according to the choice of \(f_i\)
or \(g_i\) at each factor. Supply the entire sector containing
only \(g_i\), including its reflected and shifted coordinates,
even and odd components, outer turn, and first normals.

Every remaining sector contains an \(f_i\). Multiplying its
one-factor equation by the other companions gives additional
exact source equations. After polynomial clearing, descent and
the outer turn, their dependence on \(w_i\) has the form
\[
\bigl[w_i d_i(D_\tau)I-\mathcal P_i\bigr]X=0
\quad\text{at }\mathbf p=0,
\]
where \(d_i\ne0\) and both operators are independent of \(w_i\).
These equations are appended to the finite system; their inclusion
is part of the theorem.

On a formal physical trajectory
\(v_j=\zeta q^{\delta+2j}\), with \(\zeta\ne\pm1\), the extreme
coefficient of \(d_i(D_\tau)\) is nonzero at every translated row.
It therefore has no nonzero finitely supported solution. If the
augmented window had a rational-function kernel, its highest
Laurent coefficient in \(w_i\) would give exactly such a solution.
All rows whose shifts touch the unknown window are included, so
extension by zero is legitimate. This proves full value rank;
the triangular first-normal equations then give full normal rank.

The resulting nonzero minor is a minor of the actual augmented
system. The preceding bounded-degree criterion transfers its
formal nonvanishing to generic microscopic parameters at physical
levels. On compact sets where the leading minor coefficient
does not vanish, recovery costs only a power of \(N\).
The existing holomorphic-recovery theorem can extend an actual-source
upper bound across parameter-specific zeros when its required
complex-neighborhood bounds for the supplied data are available.
Generic rank on the shared-parameter diagonal itself is not asserted.

The supplied terminal sector contains
\[
U_\tau\operatorname{can}\prod_i T(R^{-n_i}),
\]
together with all of its specified companion insertions. This is
an undecorated branching source, not a product of terminal norms
after the outer turn. Its rate remains an explicit obligation.
Both exterior collars also retain their actual rates. The theorem
removes a generic algebraic ambiguity in recovery for this class;
it does not yet give propagation at the geometric volume rate or
a nonzero coefficient in the closed invariant.

## A finite division chain recovers an inner product through a turn

The [product recovery theorem](research_multikernel_parameter_leading_projected_recovery.md)
extends the algebraic argument to
\[
U_\tau\operatorname{can}\left[
 V_n\left(\operatorname{can}\prod_{i=1}^rK_N(w_i,\cdot)\right)y_\nu
\right],
\qquad \tau=\pm1 .
\]
Here \(y\) is a fixed received state with its full difference
equation, including source and derivative coordinates. It is
independent of the endpoint parameters of the displayed product.
Every number of factors and every power is fixed independently
of \(N\).

Selecting one parameter \(w_i\) gives an inner equation
\[
(w_i d(C)I-\mathcal B)\mathcal P=\mathcal S,
\]
where \(d\ne0\) is a polynomial of fixed degree and \(\mathcal B\)
does not depend on \(w_i\). The vector \(\mathcal P\) contains the
original product and the shifted coordinates needed for its
equation. The source \(\mathcal S\) retains the terms in which a
kernel has been replaced by its original forcing. After the inner
turn, those terms contain actual terminal sources and fixed
insertions, still coupled to \(y\).

After coupling and the outer turn, the leading operator becomes
a matrix operator \(\mathcal L\). The scalar argument used for a
single kernel no longer applies to it. The new proof instead
divides the ordinary canonical polynomials a fixed number of times:
\[
\mathcal P_j=d(C)\mathcal P_{j+1}+\mathcal R_j,\qquad
\deg\mathcal R_j<\deg d .
\]
Applying the original operations to each identity gives
\[
\mathcal L X_{j+1}=\mathcal A X_j-\mathcal A Y_j ,
\]
where \(X_j\) is the transformed quotient, \(Y_j\) the transformed
remainder, and \(\mathcal A=a(D_\tau)I\) has no nonzero compactly
supported kernel on the interior physical trajectory. No division
by a physical nonunit is used.

Let \(d_I\) be the dimension of one interior packet, including its
first normals. Take \(d_I\) divisions and include every equation
whose shifts meet the unknown interval. In a homogeneous ambiguity,
the highest Laurent coefficient in \(w_i\) of the original packet
would give vectors satisfying
\[
\mathcal L x_0=0,\qquad
\mathcal L x_{j+1}=\mathcal A x_j
\quad(0\le j<d_I).
\]
If \(x_0\ne0\), these \(d_I+1\) vectors must be independent:
applying \(\mathcal L\) to a shortest dependence and using the
injectivity of \(\mathcal A\) gives a shorter dependence.
This contradicts the dimension. The same argument uses the full
value-and-normal packet throughout.

Thus the original packet is determined, even if the auxiliary
quotients are not. A rational row-space identity expresses this
precisely as
\[
\Delta\Pi=H\mathsf M,\qquad \Delta\ne0,
\]
where \(\mathsf M\) is the enlarged equation matrix and \(\Pi\)
selects the original packet. The identity has degree bounded
independently of \(N\). The bounded-degree specialization argument
then gives a polynomial recovery cost on generic microscopic
parameter neighborhoods. It is the projection identity itself
that is specialized; no full-rank claim for the auxiliary variables
is needed.

The estimate retains three kinds of supplied data: the entire
transformed terminal sources, every transformed remainder, and both
exterior collars of every quotient packet. Remainder coefficients
and quotient norms before turning are polynomially bounded.
This does not bound their outer images at the desired volume rate.
In particular, the clearing polynomial can have roots tending to
the negative endpoint, and those roots have not been removed.
The theorem therefore enlarges the exact recovery mechanism;
it does not prove the missing source-rate or noncancellation
estimate.

## Quotient boundary data have an exact contour representation

The [dual-contour reduction](research_endpoint_quotient_dual_contour_reduction.md)
expresses the extra quotients in the preceding recovery theorem
after every original operation has been applied. Write
\[
\delta_z(C)=TK_N(z,C)
 =\frac{P_N(C)-P_N(z)}{\eta N^2(C-z)},\qquad
Q_a(C)=\frac{P(C)-P(a)}{C-a},\qquad \eta=(-1)^{N-1}.
\]
Here \(P\) is the specified ordinary canonical input polynomial.
For any parameter contour \(\Gamma\) enclosing \(a\) and avoiding
zeros of \(P_N\) on its boundary, the full physical algebra gives
\[
Q_a=-\frac{\eta N^2}{2\pi i}
\oint_\Gamma\frac{\delta_zP-P(z)\delta_z}{P_N(z)(z-a)}\,dz .
\]
The numerator is divisible by \(P_N(z)\) in that algebra.
Thus the apparent internal poles at physical parameter values
are removable, including their repeated-root data.

Every later turn, shared multiplication, and original trace is
linear in this input and commutes with the parameter integral.
The formula therefore represents the actual transformed quotient
and both of its derivative channels. It is not just a pre-turn
norm comparison.

For divisor roots \(a_N=\pm(q^k+q^{-k})\) with fixed \(k\), choose
circles \(z=\pm2+\lambda/N^2\), \(|\lambda|=R\), avoiding the fixed
limiting zero radii. On them \(|P_N(z)|\) is bounded below,
\(|z-a_N|\) is comparable to \(N^{-2}\), and the contour length
is comparable to \(N^{-2}\). One division costs at most \(CN^2\)
times the transformed integrand norm.

Repeated divisions introduce products of the \(\delta_z\).
Whenever the integral construction evaluates an intermediate class,
it uses its canonical value
\[
[\operatorname{can}F](z)=\phi_N(\delta_zF).
\]
These are original traces, with all aliases and derivatives
retained. Replacing them by products of separate factor values
would give the wrong repeated-division formula. For a fixed
number \(\ell\) of divisions, the exact construction has a coarse
polynomial prefactor \(C_\ell N^{5\ell}\). Thus a common rate
bound for these mixed original/dual families would supply the
quotient-collar rates needed above.

The endpoint signs have a concrete difference. Although
\(\|\delta_{-2}\|_{[-2,2]}\le1\), its actual first transform satisfies
\[
T\delta_{-2}=K_N(-2,\cdot),\qquad
K_N(-2,-2)=\sum_j e_j(-2)^2 .
\]
The nonnegative summand with \(j=\lfloor N/4\rfloor\) already gives
\[
\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\|T\delta_{-2}\|_{[-2,2]}
\ge 4\int_0^{1/4}\log\cot(\pi x)\,dx
=\frac{4G_{\rm Cat}}{\pi}>0 .
\]
In contrast, \(T\delta_2=K_N(2,\cdot)\) has polynomial real norm.
This rules out treating every individual dual factor as having
zero first-turn rate. It does not prove growth of the full quotient:
the exact subtraction and contour integral can cancel that channel.
Indeed fixed positive physical endpoint marks give fixed-degree
input polynomials, whose actual divided quotients still have
polynomial first transforms for either divisor sign.

The reduction identifies the precise larger source family requiring
control. It does not establish that family's common rate or its
nonzero final coefficient.
The next result determines the rate of an actual coherent quotient,
so the possibility of cancellation in this formula is not used as
an assumed zero-rate estimate.

## The coherent negative quotient has an actual exponential rate

The [coherent quotient theorem](research_negative_endpoint_quotient_first_turn_growth.md)
tests the exact source introduced by ordinary division, including
its subtraction. For fixed bounded real \(\alpha,\beta\), let
\[
w_N=2\cosh(\alpha/N),\qquad a_N=-2+\beta/N^2,\qquad
Q_N(C)=\frac{K_N(w_N,C)-K_N(w_N,a_N)}{C-a_N}.
\]
The quotient is an ordinary polynomial, including at \(C=a_N\).
Its real norm is polynomially bounded. Nevertheless, for the
original turn \(T\),
\[
\frac1N\log\|TQ_N\|_{[-2,2]}
\longrightarrow \frac{4G_{\rm Cat}}{\pi}.
\]
The limit is uniform on each fixed real parameter rectangle.
It also holds for
\(\|TQ_N\|+N^{-2}\|(TQ_N)'\|\).
In contrast, \(TK_N(w_N,\cdot)\) has bounded real norm.
The allowed divisor parameters include every fixed negative
clearing root \(-(q^k+q^{-k})\).

The proof identifies the growing contribution in the actual finite
source. Write \(Y=TQ_N\). The exact equation, with its full
derivatives still retained, is
\[
(J-a_N)Y=\delta_{w_N}-K_N(w_N,a_N)e_{N-1}.
\]
Since \(\deg Q_N\le N-2\), the original trace gives \(Y(c_0)=0\).
At physical value rows the last term vanishes, and
\[
Z_j=-\frac{(-1)^{N-1}N^2}{P_N(w_N)}Y(c_j)
\]
satisfies
\[
\Delta Z_{j+1}
 =\frac{B_j}{A_j}\Delta Z_j
  +\frac{c_0-a_N}{A_j}Z_j
  +\frac1{A_j(w_N-c_j)},\qquad Z_0=0,\quad Z_1>0.
\]
All displayed coefficients and forcing terms are positive before
the final folded row. Thus the exact subtraction cannot cancel
this value channel. On each compact interior interval the positive
two-dimensional transfer has Perron root
\[
\rho(u)=\cot^2(\pi u/2).
\]
Positive left eigenvectors give a lower bound with rate
\(\int\log\rho\), and enlarging the interval yields
\[
\int_0^{1/2}\log\rho(u)\,du
=\frac{4G_{\rm Cat}}{\pi}.
\]
This argument uses the actual initialization and forcing; it does
not infer a nonzero coefficient from a characteristic root alone.

For the matching upper bound, the physical-row interpolation and
radical estimates imply
\[
\sup_{z,C\in[-2,2]}|K_N(z,C)|
\le N K_N(-2,-2)+N^2,\qquad
\log K_N(-2,-2)=\frac{4G_{\rm Cat}}{\pi}N+O(\log N).
\]
The original trace bound therefore gives this same exponential
ceiling for \(T\) on any polynomially bounded canonical input.
The ordinary divided-difference formula bounds \(Q_N\)
polynomially, and Markov's inequality supplies the first-normal
upper bound.

The original reset derivative in the exact equation has not been
removed: \(e_{N-1}\) has zero physical values but can have nonzero
first normals. Only the value projection was used for the lower
bound. Later turns, shared factors and a final trace can still
cancel this large unclosed source. Consequently the theorem
does not contradict a volume identity.

It does rule out one proposed route to it: negative spatial
quotients cannot all inherit the first-turn rate of the original
microscopic products. Nor can bounds at fixed physical endpoint
marks prove that inheritance. Those marks have \(P_N(w)=0\) and
give fixed-degree quotients with polynomial transforms, whereas
the real microscopic family above has positive rate. The source
enlargement itself changes the estimate that must be proved.
