## Positive division preserves the original turn budget

The [positive-division theorem](research_positive_endpoint_quotient_source_bounds.md)
gives a different outcome at the other spectral endpoint. Let \(f\)
be any canonical polynomial and define its joint norm by
\[
\mathfrak B_N(f)=\|f\|_{[-2,2]}+\|Tf\|_{[-2,2]}.
\]
For a fixed number of ordinary divisions
\[
f_0=f,\qquad
f_\ell(C)=\frac{f_{\ell-1}(C)-f_{\ell-1}(a_{\ell,N})}
                         {C-a_{\ell,N}},\qquad
a_{\ell,N}=2+\beta_\ell/N^2,\quad |\beta_\ell|\le B,
\]
the theorem proves
\[
\max_{\ell\le s}\mathfrak B_N(f_\ell)
\le C N^p\mathfrak B_N(f).
\]
The parameters may be complex and may coincide. The result is
unconditional for this joint norm. It is not a polynomial bound
for \(T\) on arbitrary inputs.

For one division, \(Y=Tf_1\) satisfies the exact equation
\[
(J-a_{1,N})Y=Tf-f(a_{1,N})e_{N-1}.
\]
The existing graph-norm estimate for \(J\) applies because
\(a_{1,N}-c_0=O(N^{-2})\). Its two original anchors,
\(Y(c_0)\) and \(Y'(c_0)\), are bounded by the trace formulas
and the ordinary polynomial norm of \(f_1\). A Bernstein-ellipse
estimate supplies that polynomial norm uniformly through coincident
division points. Iterating gives the displayed joint estimate.
The full first-normal norm is equivalent by Markov's inequality.

For a canonical microscopic kernel product, or any of its actual
six-state tensor channels, the theorem proves more. Let \(P_\ell\)
be these ordinary quotients and \(F_\ell=V_nP_\ell\). Then their
physical values and first normals retain the existing profile
\[
|F_\ell(c_j)|+|\dot F_{\ell,j}|
\le \exp\{N\mathcal J_n(j/N)+o(N)\},\qquad
\mathcal J_n(u)=\int_0^u L_n(v)\,dv ,
\]
uniformly over all rows and bounded complex parameters. The
whole-real norm has upper rate \(\mathcal I_n=\mathcal J_n(1/2)\).
All powers and numbers of divisions are fixed independently of
the level.

The actual first-turn estimate initializes each quotient at fixed
physical rows. Its signed recovery equation is
\[
(D_n-a_{\ell,N})F_\ell
=F_{\ell-1}-P_{\ell-1}(a_{\ell,N})1 .
\]
The second term is polynomially bounded. A forcing contribution
from row \(k\) acquires the exponent
\[
\mathcal J_n(k/N)+\int_{k/N}^{j/N}L_n(u)\,du
=\mathcal J_n(j/N).
\]
Thus variation of constants does not spend a second terminal
integral. The proof includes the original derivative equation,
both endpoint strips and the final physical row at both parities.

Ungauged tensor channels are included through exact forced
identities for
\(p_b=\operatorname{can}((C-2)^b Z_N)\):
\[
(J-2)Tp_b=Tp_{b+1},\qquad
(D_n-2)V_np_b=V_np_{b+1}.
\]
Descending from the already estimated gauged channel keeps every
alias. Ordinary division of its canonical representative is not
silently identified with the original ungauged channel.

This provides actual estimates for positive spatial quotient
inputs. It does not estimate a subsequent shared product after
another turn, prove a complex contour bound, or provide a nonzero
closing coefficient. The following algebraic construction now supplies
a parameter-leading presentation using only these divisors; its
subsequent assembly must retain the actual source columns and collars.

## Parameter-leading equations with only positive-endpoint divisors

The [positive-pole construction](research_positive_pole_parameter_leading_product_module.md)
proves an exact ordinary identity which, after clearing and canonical
reduction, has the form
\[
[w_i d_N(C)I-\mathcal B_i(C,J,D_1)]\operatorname{can}\mathcal P
   =\operatorname{can}\mathcal R_i.
\]
Here \(\mathcal P\) contains the selected kernel, its divided difference,
its half-step average and its averaged divided difference, each
multiplied by the full tensor of the other factors. The polynomial
\(d_N\) is independent of the endpoint parameters, has bounded degree,
and has all roots at \(2+O(N^{-2})\). The operator matrix is independent
of the selected parameter \(w_i\). The lower-factor columns \(P_Ng,g\)
remain prescribed actual data, including their half-grid aliases.

The construction uses backward transport on the actual six-coordinate
module; it does not invert that module on arbitrary formal data.
An even divided-difference operator can then be expressed in the
original full-step operators with coefficient poles only near \(+2\).
The proof cancels the apparent negative-endpoint poles at the
coefficient level, before applying the equation to a solution.

These are necessary source equations. Clearing a physical-root factor
can annihilate an endpoint-supported forcing term, so the defining
source identities and the original endpoint data must accompany them.
No denominator is inverted in the finite physical algebra. Every
original first normal is retained.

Combined with the preceding division theorem, this supplies estimates
for the associated inner ordinary quotient inputs and their \(V_n\)
images. It does not yet supply the outer-turn collar bounds required
by projected recovery, nor a nonzero coefficient in the closed invariant.

## Positive-pole projected recovery retains the composed boundary data

The [assembly theorem](research_positive_pole_projected_recovery_assembly.md)
combines the positive-pole presentation, finite-chain recovery and
the proved positive-division estimates. All four selected coordinates
are unknowns; the two lower-factor columns are prescribed actual
sources. Clearing the ordinary aliases makes the right side a
fixed-degree polynomial insertion in that lower-factor tensor.
Its half-grid data are not replaced by bounded-degree physical rows.

Write \(P_j=d_NP_{j+1}+R_j\) for each ordinary division, and let
\(\mathfrak F\) apply the inner turn \(V_n\), coupling to the entire
received source \(y\), full descent, and the outer turn \(U_\tau\).
For every fixed chain length the inputs \(P_j\) have polynomial real
norm, subexponential first-turn norm, and the same \(V_n\) physical-color
profile \(\mathcal J_n\). This holds through collisions of the positive
division points. The remainder coefficients have polynomial cost.

For a fixed interior window, the exact recovery rows determine
\(X_0=\mathfrak F(P_0)\) from the supplied sources and the complete
two-sided collars of all \(X_j=\mathfrak F(P_j)\). On the specified
microscopic parameter unit charts the recovery cost is polynomial.
The highest Laurent coefficient in the independent selected parameter,
together with the finite-chain injectivity lemma, proves recovery
of \(X_0\); uniqueness of every auxiliary packet is unnecessary.

The remaining estimate is for
\[
 U_\tau\operatorname{can}[(V_nP_j)y]\big|_{\partial I},
\]
including its first normals and all shared coordinates. It is not a
value of \(V_nP_j\) at the inner color. The same issue applies to the
composed lower-factor and remainder packets. The theorem's upper rate
is the maximum of these actual supplied rates; it does not replace
them by the inner profile. Parameter identifications and minor-zero
loci also retain the specialization qualifications of projected recovery.

## The outer observation has a sharp positive weighted norm

The [outer-observation theorem](research_outer_turn_weighted_jet_observation.md)
uses the exact original identity \(U_\tau=R^\tau T R^\tau\).
For a physical output \(c_b\), write \(r=R^\tau\). Then
\[
 (U_\tau f)(c_b)
   =r(c_b)\phi_N\!\left(K_N(c_b,C)r(C)f(C)\right).
\]
Differentiating the output retains both the kernel derivative and
the crossing derivative. For \(f=(V_nQ)y\), bilinear
self-adjointness moves \(V_n\) to the entire observation:
\[
 (U_\tau f)(c_b)
   =r(c_b)\phi_N\!\left(Q\,V_n(rK_N(c_b,\cdot)y)\right).
\]
The shared received factor \(y\) remains inside this expression.

At each double node use the jet
\((f(c_j),(4-c_j^2)f'(c_j))\). The local Frobenius matrix is
\(\eta\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-c_j&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\);
it is nondegenerate and indefinite. At the odd simple node only
the value occurs.
For arbitrary positive weights \(W_j\), bound each of these
coordinates by \(W_j\) and denote the resulting norm by \(\|f\|_W\).
The value observation \(\mathcal L_b(f)=(U_\tau f)(c_b)\) satisfies
\[
 \sum_j K_N(c_b,c_j)W_j
 \le \|\mathcal L_b\|_W^*
 \le C N^p\sum_j K_N(c_b,c_j)W_j .
\]
The normalized output derivative has the same upper bound.
All kernel mixed derivatives cost only a polynomial relative to
the positive physical values.

The lower bound is an exact Hermite-interpolation test: set all
double-node values to zero and align their independent normal
coordinates with the original crossing phases. Include the odd
simple value separately. This constructs a canonical input attaining
the displayed positive sum. It is not an input asserted to arise
from a knot source or a positive-pole quotient.

For a continuous profile \(A\), weights
\(W_j=e^{NA(\theta_j)}\), and an interior output angle \(t\), the
value-observation norm consequently has rate
\[
 \max_{u\in[0,\pi]}\{\psi(t,u)+A(u)\}.
\]
Thus this positive kernel criterion is necessary and sufficient at
the exponential scale for a bound uniform on that whole weighted
jet ball. It does not recover the sharper filled action merely by
choosing different names for the weights. The actual source equations
and cancellations can still yield a stronger bound on their smaller
family; that is the remaining analytic problem.

## A reciprocal resonance retains a quantum phase and changes degree

The [filtered-carrier calculation](research_resonant_newton_graded_carrier.md)
uses the monic Newton basis \(p_k\) of the original finite algebra.
For a product of factors transformed by powers \(n_1,\ldots,n_r\),
followed by a unit turn of sign \(\tau\), its top-degree coefficient
at total input degree \(K<N\) is
\[
\Phi_N(\mathbf k)=(-1)^{\ell(\mathbf k)}
q^{-\{\sum_i n_i k_i^2+\tau K^2+\ell(\mathbf k)\}},
\qquad
\ell(\mathbf k)=\sum_i(n_i+\tau)k_i .
\]
At \(\sum_i1/n_i=-\tau\), put
\(L=\operatorname{lcm}_i|n_i|\) and \(a_i=L/n_i\).
Translation by \(\mathbf a\) leaves the quadratic part unchanged
but multiplies this full coefficient by \(q^{-L(r-1)}\) and changes
the total degree by \(-\tau L\).

Keeping a degree variable \(z\) therefore gives the exact factor
\(1-q^{-L(r-1)}z^{-\tau L}\), together with finite boundary terms
and differences of the actual factorial amplitudes. The latter
differences are not uniformly small merely because \(N\) is large.
The variable \(z\) has not been identified with the physical \(v\)
of the preceding rank criterion.

The original trace annihilates degrees below \(N-1\). Its first
possible nonzero degree-marked coefficient is exactly the
top-degree sum at \(K=N-1\), multiplied by \((-1)^{N-1}N^2\).
The resonant translation leaves that fixed-degree slice, so it is
not a symmetry of this trace coefficient. The full source also
contains terms with \(K\ge N\), whose canonical reductions and
normal contributions are not determined by the graded formula.
Thus the calculation records the exact resonance phase without
claiming cancellation or noncancellation of the original source.

## Quantum phase shifts can move an exceptional row without removing it

The [indicial calculation](research_repeated_turn_quantum_indicial_physical_hits.md)
retains the exact ordered scalar equations at the old spectral
infinity. Write \(Ef(v)=f(q^2v)\). A candidate with
\(Ef/f\sim a v^{1/n}\), for a fixed nonzero signed \(n\), obeys
\[
(-1)^n\bigl(q^{n-1}a^n+q^{1-n}a^{-n}\bigr)=\lambda
\]
for the raw equation \(D_n-\lambda\). This is a coefficient balance
of an ordinary difference expression, not an assertion about the
asymptotic behavior of the canonical source.

The distinction between the terminal forcing and its kernel matters.
The actual single-kernel equation has the ordered consequence
\((D_n-c_0)(w-J)f=0\). Applying \(w-J\) changes the leading shift
ratio by \(q^{2/|n|}\). At a reciprocal resonance
\(\sum_i1/n_i=\epsilon\), followed by the inverse outer pullback,
the corresponding candidates therefore have angular coordinates
\[
v_{\mathrm{new}}=\zeta q^\beta,\qquad
\beta=1-r-\epsilon+2\sum_i e_i/n_i-2\sum_i1/|n_i|,
\quad e_i\in\{0,1\},\quad \zeta\in\mu_L ,
\]
where \(L=\operatorname{lcm}_i|n_i|\). Their reciprocals remain
part of the calculation.

For \(\zeta=e^{2\pi ik/L}\), a physical hit is equivalent to
\[
2Nk\equiv L(1-\beta)\pmod{2L}.
\]
The resonance makes \(L(1-\beta)\) even. Every primitive phase
therefore has an infinite residue class of such levels; if
\(L\ge3\), the phase \(k=1\) is interior. Its row lies a fixed
number of steps from \(\lfloor Nk/L\rfloor\). Comparing the
exponent only with the center row would miss these hits.

Neither this arithmetic nor the indicial equation proves that
the candidate survives the exact forcing, full first normals,
recovery constraints and other rows. The full stacked-window
minor question is unchanged. Products of several endpoint
factors before a turn also retain their mixed forcing and
cannot be replaced by this single-kernel scalar model.

## Parameter-specific rank loss need not spoil an actual-source upper bound

The [holomorphic recovery theorem](research_holomorphic_parameter_recovery.md)
weakens the parameter restriction in the preceding conditional
estimate. Assume a full-column minor is not identically zero as
a germ in \((h,\boldsymbol\alpha)\) in each level residue class.
Its leading coefficient may vanish at the parameter of interest.

For finitely many nonzero leading coefficients and any parameter
\(\alpha_0\), choose a complex line through \(\alpha_0\) on which
their product is not identically zero. A sufficiently small
circle on that line avoids all their zeros. The same circle,
translated to nearby centers, still avoids them uniformly.
The finite-window inverse estimate applies on these circles.
Cauchy's formula for the actual holomorphic source transfers
the bound to their centers.

Consequently, for every compact parameter set \(K\) in the stated
coefficient domain, there is a fixed larger compact set \(K'\)
such that
\[
 \sup_K\|X_N\|\le C N^k
                  \sup_{K'}(\|F_N\|+\|B_N\|).
\]
This is a source estimate even where the pointwise matrix is
singular; it does not claim an inverse of that singular matrix.
It also shows uniqueness among holomorphic source families
with the same supplied data, once generic full rank is known.
An algebraically free normal at one parameter then cannot be
chosen independently of its surrounding family.

The premise still concerns an actual full-column minor, not
generic rank of the classical characteristic matrix.
The source bounds must hold uniformly on a complex neighborhood.
Their right-boundary cost is retained. This continuation also
does not preserve a lower bound: the family
\(\alpha e^{NA}\) has rate \(A\) away from zero and vanishes
at zero. A nonzero geometric coefficient needs its own proof.

## A filled leaf has exact weighted representatives on a trace window

The [weighted window theorem](research_filled_leaf_weighted_window_current.md)
uses the actual values and first derivatives of a filled leaf, rather
than assuming that its canonical polynomial has a controlled complex
continuation. On a compact physical window, write its row coordinate
as \(u_j=j/N\), and let \(\mathcal S_N\) be the calibrated terminal
phase with the physical half-row displacement included.
After division by \(e^{N\mathcal S_N(u_j)}\), both prescribed jets
have subexponential bounds.

One-sided sinc-square interpolation gives two holomorphic functions
\(H_N^\pm\). Each agrees exactly with both prescribed jets.
In its own half-plane it satisfies
\[
 |H_N^\pm(z)|\le e^{N\Re\mathcal S_N(z)+o(N)}.
\]
Fixed derivatives cost only polynomial factors. These functions are
representatives inside the trace window; they are not identified
with the canonical source away from the physical grid.

For an actual retained spectator \(p_N\), put
\[
 g_\pm(z)=\sin(2\pi z+\pi/N)\,
          H_N^\pm(z)p_N(2\cos(2\pi z+\pi/N)),
 \qquad D_N(z)=(\pi N)^2\csc^2(\pi Nz).
\]
If \(E_-\) is the lower exterior half-boundary oriented from the
left midpoint to the right midpoint and \(E_+\) the upper
half-boundary oriented back, the original window trace is exactly
\[
 -\frac{\eta}{2\pi^2i}
 \left\{
   \int_{E_-}D_Ng_-\,dz+\int_{E_+}D_Ng_+\,dz+
   \int_{a_N}^{b_N}D_N(g_+-g_-)\,dz
 \right\}.
\]
Here \(\eta=(-1)^{N-1}\). Both outer vertical sides are part of
the exterior contours. The real interface is holomorphic at every
grid point, since the two representatives have matching first jets.
Its absolute bound has the same real leaf profile. The exterior
bound has the additional sampling factor
\(e^{-2\pi N|\Im z|}\). Every Fourier alias remains in \(D_N\).

On the calibrated positive regular branch, this exponent has the
retained-boundary geometric interpretation
\[
 \Re S_n(s+i h_w)
 =M_\infty-\frac1\pi
       \min_G\{\mathfrak e_n(s,G;\boldsymbol\beta)-h_wG\},
 \qquad h_w=-2\pi\Im z.
\]
The cut constraints and shared neighbor variables are retained.
The identity is asserted only where the stated minimizers are
interior and the cut constraints inactive. Products of finitely
many messages preserve the exact shared-color trace formula.

The real interface lies at \(h_w=0\). The positive-height parent
gap does not automatically bound it. Neither that interface nor
the outer vertical sides have been discarded, and this theorem
does not yet prove the required bound for the full partially
filled source.

## The remaining interface is an exact Fourier and normal pairing

The [midpoint pairing](research_leaf_interface_midpoint_fourier_pairing.md)
rewrites the real interface of the weighted-window formula.
Let \(a_j,b_j\) be the exact phase-normalized value and derivative
of the leaf at the physical row \(j\), and set
\[
 A_N(x)=e^{N\mathcal S_N(x)}
           \sin(2\pi x+\pi/N)\,p_N(c_N(x)).
\]
The spectator \(p_N\) remains the original one, including the
receiving crossing and every remaining coupled variable.
Define
\[
 \mathfrak c_N(\xi)=
       \sum_j(b_j-2\pi iN\xi a_j)e^{-2\pi i\xi j},
 \qquad
 \widehat A_N(\xi)=
       \int_{a_N}^{b_N}A_N(x)e^{2\pi iN\xi x}\,dx .
\]
If \(\Lambda_N\) denotes the original remaining closing
functional, the closed real-interface contribution is exactly
\[
 -\frac{\eta N}{\pi}
       \int_{-1}^{1}
       \Lambda_N\!\left(\mathfrak c_N(\xi)
                              \widehat A_N(\xi)\right)\,d\xi .
\]
This keeps the derivative term, signs, normalization and shared
variables. It follows by writing the interface kernel as
\(\sin(2\pi N(x-u_j))/(x-u_j)\).
The midpoint endpoints are zeros of every such kernel, so
integration by parts has no endpoint term. The exterior
half-boundaries from the weighted-window formula remain.

The coefficients \(\mathfrak c_N\) have a polynomial-times-
subexponential bound, but their frequency interval includes zero.
No uniform oscillatory gain follows from this bound. The required
estimate is for this whole pairing with \(\Lambda_N\), or for
its combination with the exterior contributions.

There is also a general geometric reason to retain these phases.
For genuine disjoint terminal leaves with powers \(|n_\ell|\ge2\),
complete every retained vertex and keep each terminal leaf at
its complete-neighbor reference. If at least one selected
retained vertex remains, strict energy convexity gives
\[
 M_G<
 (e_G-|L|)M_\infty+\sum_{\ell\in L}\mathcal I_{n_\ell}.
\]
The right side is the real reduced phase at zero retained angles,
and it persists as an excess on nearby real windows.
Thus minimizing the terminal incidences and then taking an
absolute real-profile bound cannot give the desired parent
comparison in general. This is a statement about that classical
upper budget, not a lower bound on the actual quantum interface.

## The filled-leaf recurrence controls its Fourier observation

The [normalized adjoint theorem](research_filled_leaf_normalized_jet_adjoint.md)
uses the entire finite companion for
\(F_N=T(R^nB_N)\): gauged channels, recovered product,
shifted values and first physical normals. Scale the normals
by \(1/N\) and divide the full state by its calibrated leaf
phase. The actual normalized state \(X_j\) then satisfies
\[
 X_{j+1}=\mathsf Q_h(u_j)X_j,\qquad
 \max_{u_j\in I_0}\|X_j\|=e^{o(N)}
\]
on every buffered compact interior interval. The matrix
coefficients, rather than the source between rows, are
holomorphic on a fixed complex neighborhood.

The phase argument is now checked with its sign.
For \(|n|\ge2\),
\[
 e^{\mathcal S_0'(u)}=\tau_{\max,-n}(u),
\]
the largest-modulus forward root of the literal leaf equation
\(D_{-n}=2\). It follows that the only unit-modulus root of
the normalized principal matrix is one, with its full
multiplicity retained. For \(n=\pm1\), the frequency set is
\(\{0,\frac12-nu\}\) modulo integers; for \(n=0\), it is
\(\{0\}\).

Away from these frequencies, solve the adjoint equation by
a finite analytic iteration on nested complex neighborhoods.
It produces bounded rows \(v_N\) and exponentially small
residual rows \(r_N\) satisfying exactly
\[
 v_N(u,\xi)-e^{-2\pi i\xi}v_N(u+h,\xi)\mathsf Q_h(u)
       =\ell_h(u,\xi)-r_N(u,\xi).
\]
Here \(\ell_h\) selects the actual normalized combination
\(b_j/N-2\pi i\xi a_j\). Therefore the Fourier coefficient
from the midpoint interface satisfies
\[
 \begin{split}
 N^{-1}\mathfrak c_N(\xi)
 ={}&e^{-2\pi i\xi j_0}v_N(u_{j_0},\xi)X_{j_0}\\
   &-e^{-2\pi i\xi(j_1+1)}
           v_N(u_{j_1+1},\xi)X_{j_1+1}
     +e^{-\kappa N+o(N)} .
 \end{split}
\]
The exact finite remainder is written in the proof. No endpoint
packet is set to zero. A single adjoint used across adjacent
windows cancels their artificial common packets exactly; the
two outer packets remain.

For a fixed product of leaf messages at a shared color, tensor
their full states and retain the product normal. The possible
unit frequencies are the sums of the individual frequency sets.
When all powers have absolute value at least two, the sole
normalized sector remains zero modulo integers.

This supplies phase-sensitive control before the remaining
closing functional is applied. That closing can still have an
exponential cost. The observation is not asserted to be small
at integer frequencies or at its two external packets.
In particular the normal copy of the principal matrix has
its own unit eigenspace; phase centering alone does not prove
compatibility of the normalized values with their derivatives.

## The normalized leaf state approaches its entire unit cluster

The [slow-graph theorem](research_filled_leaf_slow_graph_reduction.md)
concerns the same actual leaf state for every fixed
\(|n|\ge2\) and every fixed number \(r\) of microscopic
endpoint factors. The complete principal matrix, after
division by the calibrated dominant root, has a unit
generalized eigenspace of dimension \(4\,6^r\). Its
restriction is \(I+J_0\), with \(J_0^2=0\).
Every other eigenvalue has modulus less than one on a
fixed compact interior interval.

Both the value and first-normal copies contribute to this
dimension. Recovery has a different eigenvalue and does not
lengthen the unit Jordan blocks. A holomorphic spectral
projection and an explicitly transported frame give the
exact finite-level matrix in the form
\[
 Q_h=
 \begin{pmatrix}A_h&B_h\\C_h&D_h\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad B_h,C_h=O(h).
\]
In this formula the frame is evaluated at the two ends
of the step; its variation is included in the coefficients.

The theorem constructs a holomorphic matrix \(R_h=O(h)\)
with exponentially small defect in the graph equation
\[
 R_h(u+h)\bigl(A_h(u)+B_h(u)R_h(u)\bigr)
               =C_h(u)+D_h(u)R_h(u).
\]
The construction is a finite nonlinear iteration with
controlled loss of complex-neighborhood width. It keeps
the exact shift and the quadratic term in \(R_h\).

For the actual state \((x_j,y_j)\), the difference
\(\eta_j=y_j-R_h(u_j)x_j\) satisfies a stable recurrence
with that exponentially small defect as forcing.
The already proved subexponential bound for the entire
normalized source implies that \(\eta_j\) is exponentially
small after any fixed positive left buffer. The original
left packet remains in the formula and is suppressed by
the stable evolution.

The retained slow matrix is \(I+J_0+O(h)\).
The norm
\[
             |v|_{u,h}=\|v\|+h^{-1/2}\|J_0(u)v\|
\]
bounds each forward step and inverse step by
\(1+C\sqrt h\). Hence transport over a fixed physical
interval, in either direction, costs \(e^{O(\sqrt N+\log N)}\).
An already established normalized lower norm \(e^{-o(N)}\)
at one slow packet therefore persists on such an interval.
The theorem does not establish that initial lower norm.

For a fixed shared product of \(q\) leaf messages, the unit
cluster is their tensor product. Its nilpotent part has
power \(q+1\) equal to zero; the same graph construction
and a weighted nilpotent norm give subexponential two-sided
transport. The original joint first normal remains the
product-rule selector on this tensor.

The reduction gives the actual state on a fixed interior
interval, including its normal data. It supplies neither
endpoint initialization nor a lower bound for the original
scalar closing. A vector can have a large norm while its
specified linear observation vanishes.

## The actual leaf amplitudes have polynomial bulk transport

The [regular-amplitude theorem](research_filled_leaf_regular_amplitude_transport.md)
strengthens the preceding slow-state estimate for every fixed signed
power \(|n|\ge2\) and every fixed number of microscopic endpoint
factors. It uses the literal filled leaf \(T(R^nB_N)\), including
all gauged source channels, forced product recovery and independent
first normals.

In the centered physical coordinate \(x=(j+1/2)/N\), conjugate
the scalar operator by \((\sin 2\pi x)^{-1/2}\).
The coefficients at the midpoints of its shifts are then even in
\(h=1/N\). This follows first from the explicit coefficients of
\(J,D_1,D_{-1}\), and then for every signed \(D_n\) from the exact
anticommutator recurrence. A fixed-degree interpolation argument
justifies that recurrence for the ordinary difference lifts,
without turning the source's residual into an off-grid equation.

Let \(\mathcal S(x)\) be the previously calibrated geometric phase.
Its characteristic root is double. The first-order error when the
operator acts on the test amplitude
\((\sin2\pi x)^{-1/2}e^{\mathcal S(x)/h}\) is therefore
\[
\frac h2\frac{d}{dx}
\partial_\xi P_0(x,\mathcal S'(x))=0.
\]
The actual matrix coupling in the full source equation starts at
order \(h^2\), so the same second-order residual holds for every
constant source-channel vector.

This extra order controls the first columns of the slow graph.
Scaling each generalized eigenvector by \(h\) puts its transfer
in the form
\[
I+hB_h(x),\qquad \|B_h\|\le C .
\]
Both forward and inverse products across a fixed bulk interval
are bounded in these coordinates. Changing back costs only a
fixed power of \(N\). Forced recovery has strictly stable
principal roots and is included in the embedding. Differentiating
the embedding retains a second, independent normal coordinate;
the resulting dimension is still \(4\,6^r\).

For the actual normalized packet \(X_j\), after a fixed positive
left buffer, the quantitative conclusion is
\[
\|X_j\|\le C N^p\|X_l\|+e^{-cN}\mathcal B_N,
\qquad
\|X_l\|\le C N^p\|X_j\|+e^{-cN}\mathcal B_N,
\]
where \(\mathcal B_N=e^{o(N)}\) bounds the actual packet on the
larger buffer. The exponentially small term retains the initial
stable component and the graph's invariance error.

Thus a lower packet bound, if established above that error, can
be transported with polynomial loss. The theorem does not supply
the initial lower bound, identify independent normals with a
single amplitude derivative, control the ends of the full color
interval, or prove noncancellation under the original closing.

## The filled source has an explicit ordinary polynomial residual

The [ordinary-residual theorem](research_filled_leaf_exact_bivariate_residual.md)
starts with the literal one-kernel source
\[
F_n(w,Z)=T(R^nK_N(w,\cdot))(Z),\qquad
c_{n,N}=(-1)^{N-1}\kappa^n/N^2 .
\]
Its original trace expression is symmetric in \(w,Z\).
The terminal Newton ideals show that its total degree is \(N-1\)
and that both top coefficients are \(c_{n,N}\), independently
of the other variable.

Let \(\widetilde D_{-n}\) be the ordinary polynomial lift of the
original conjugated operator. Its action on degree \(d\) raises
degree by exactly one, with coefficient
\((-1)^nq^{2n(d+1)}\). The full physical equation and the top
coefficient therefore determine the entire ordinary residual:
\[
(w-\widetilde D_{-n})F_n
=c_{n,N}\bigl(P_N(w)-(-1)^nP_N(Z)\bigr).
\]
This is an identity for all complex \(w,Z\), not only at
physical grid values or modulo \(P_N\).

For \(G=T(R^n)=F_n(c_0,\cdot)\), subtraction gives
\[
(w-\widetilde D_{-n})(F_n-G)
=c_{n,N}P_N(w)-(w-c_0)G .
\]
The difference has degree at most \(N-2\) and is the unique
ordinary polynomial of that degree satisfying the displayed
equation. Parameter differentiation also gives the actual
ordinary Jordan identity
\((\widetilde D_{-n}-c_0)T(R^nQ_N)=G\).

For any fixed product of endpoint kernels, the same top
\(P_N(Z)\) term is independent of all endpoint parameters.
Setting one endpoint to \(c_0\) and subtracting cancels it.
The remaining equation explicitly retains
\(T(R^n(M_r-M_{r-1}))\), where \(M_r\) is the mixed source from
the original product rule. No estimate of that term is inferred.

The single-kernel source also has an exact parameter expansion.
For \(w=2\cosh(\alpha/N)\), the coefficient of
\(e^{k\alpha/N}\), \(0\le k\le N-1\), is
\[
c_{n,N}U_{N-1-k}(D_{-n}/2)1 ,
\]
of degree exactly \(N-1-k\). Removing the ordinary interpolation
of all distinct physical values leaves only frequencies
\(|k|\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\), with a nonzero top polynomial
coefficient at both parities. This is a statement about the
global interpolation remainder; it does not estimate the
derivative mismatch relative to a moderate local scalar amplitude.

The theorem supplies exact source identities and uniqueness,
not an estimate of the inverse or a noncancellation theorem.

## One scalar amplitude now represents both terminal channels in the bulk

The [scalar compatibility theorem](research_terminal_bulk_scalar_compatibility.md)
concerns the actual terminal polynomial \(G_N=T(R^n)\) for every fixed
signed power \(|n|\ge2\). Let \(x_j=(j+1/2)/N\), let
\(c(x)=2\cos(2\pi x)\), and put
\[
f_N(x)=(\sin 2\pi x)^{-1/2}e^{N\mathcal S_n(x)},
\]
where \(\mathcal S_n\) is the calibrated terminal phase. For every
fixed interval \(I\Subset(0,1/2)\), the theorem constructs a function
\(\mathcal A_N\), holomorphic on a fixed neighborhood of \(I\), such that
\[
\|\mathcal A_N\|\le C N^p,\qquad
f_N(x_j)\mathcal A_N(x_j)=G_N(c(x_j)),\qquad
\frac{(f_N\mathcal A_N)'(x_j)}{c'(x_j)}=G_N'(c(x_j)).
\]
The exponent and neighborhood may depend on \(n\) and \(I\).
Both level parities are included.

The value interpolation alone does not prove the last equality.
To establish it, write \(a_j=f_N(x_j)^{-1}G_N(c(x_j))\) and
\[
b_j=f_N(x_j)^{-1}c'(x_j)G_N'(c(x_j))
             -\frac{f_N'(x_j)}{f_N(x_j)}a_j .
\]
The ordinary terminal equation, with its explicit \(P_N\) residual,
gives a homogeneous equation for these values and first normals
only after restriction to the physical rows. Its normalized scalar
operator \(\mathsf P_h\), \(h=1/N\), has one double unit root; its
other roots are strictly stable. The preceding amplitude theorem
puts the slow transfer in the form \(I+hB_h\).

The known holomorphic terminal asymptotic near complete output
provides a scalar initial function on a small interval to the right
of \(I\). Forward contraction from a retained left buffer controls
the stable part. Backward transport is then applied only to the
slow part, whose inverse has bounded products. This gives
polynomial bounds for both actual channels throughout the intervening
interval.

Construct a moderate holomorphic interpolation \(A_N\) of the
values \(a_j\). Its residual \(r_N=\mathsf P_hA_N\) vanishes at all
interior grid points. A disk Blaschke estimate makes \(r_N\) and
its derivative exponentially small on a narrower neighborhood.
The original normal equation then gives the exact relation
\[
\mathsf P_h\bigl(b-A_N'\bigr)(x_j)=-r_N'(x_j).
\]
At the right initial interval the same zeros estimate compares
\(A_N\) with the actual scalar terminal function. Their derivative
difference is exponentially small there. Forward stable contraction
and backward slow transport now propagate that estimate to \(I\).
A derivative interpolation correction, itself exponentially small
on a sufficiently narrow fixed neighborhood, gives \(\mathcal A_N\)
with both required equalities exactly.

For each fixed physical mark \(b\), the identity
\[
T(R^nK_N(c_b,\cdot))=K_N(c_b,J)G_N
\]
transfers the result through a difference operator of fixed order.
Fixed products at a shared color also inherit it by the ordinary
product rule. Consequently these terminal inputs can enter the
original double-pole trace on a bulk interval with one scalar
amplitude and no derivative-mismatch contribution.

The result does not control the prescribed complex height of that
trace in a parent geometry, either endpoint of the full color
interval, or its exterior boundary terms. It does not identify
the local representative with the canonical polynomial at arbitrary
complex colors, and it does not give a nonzero closing coefficient.
Generic microscopic endpoint parameters and general products inside
the terminal remain outside its scope.

## A common terminal amplitude gives an exponentially small interface

The [complex continuation theorem](research_terminal_one_sided_characteristic_continuation.md)
strengthens the preceding scalar result under explicit conditions on
the original characteristic equation. Choose a bounded simply
connected complex domain containing the real interval and the proposed
contour, together with fixed surrounding buffers. The original phase
and scalar gauge must extend holomorphically there. The finite
difference coefficients and inverse extreme coefficients must remain
bounded, and the selected double characteristic must stay separated
from every other root. The theorem does not assume modulus ordering
away from the real axis.

These conditions extend the regular slow graph and its step
\(T_h=I+hB_h\) through the domain. A bounded holomorphic differential
equation can then approximate this step with error \(e^{-c/h}\).
The proof constructs it, rather than using a formal matrix logarithm.
If \(\Phi_h(A;x)\) is the length-\(h\) flow of \(Y'=A(x)Y\), put
\[
Q_h(A)=\frac{\Phi_h(A)-I}{h}-A.
\]
On a domain reduced by a distance \(\delta\), this map has Lipschitz
constant \(C(h/\delta+h)\) on bounded matrix functions. Iterating
\(A\mapsto B_h-Q_h(A)\), with \(\delta=Mh\) for fixed sufficiently
large \(M\), permits \(c/h\) contracting iterations inside the
available buffer. Its resulting flow agrees with \(T_h\) to
exponential accuracy.

Start this differential equation with the actual slow data at a
real row. Its bounded fundamental matrix gives one holomorphic
normalized amplitude \(A_N^0\) of polynomial size on the complex
domain. Real stable contraction and comparison with the preceding
scalar theorem show that both its value errors and derivative errors
are exponentially small at the physical nodes:
\[
e_j=a_j-A_N^0(x_j),\qquad
d_j=b_j-(A_N^0)'(x_j),\qquad
|e_j|+|d_j|\le Ce^{-\kappa N}.
\]

The exact corrections use
\[
L_j^\sigma(x)=e^{\sigma2\pi i(x-x_j)/h}
                  \operatorname{sinc}^2((x-x_j)/h),\qquad
C_N^\sigma=\sum_j
\left[e_j+\left(d_j-\frac{\sigma2\pi i e_j}{h}\right)(x-x_j)\right]
L_j^\sigma(x).
\]
Their values and derivatives are precisely \(e_j,d_j\).
The Fourier support of \(L_j^+\) lies in \([0,2/h]\), so its norm
is at most one throughout the upper half-plane; the corresponding
statement for \(L_j^-\) holds below. Thus each correction remains
exponentially small throughout its designated half of the fixed
complex domain. Only a continuation to the opposite side spends
the exponential estimate.

Both exact representatives share the same \(A_N^0\). Their difference,
after multiplication by the original double-pole sampling kernel,
therefore has an exponentially small removable real interface.
This is the new conclusion: separate one-sided representatives
with polynomial bounds were already available.

If the actual remaining spectator has rate \(E(x)\), the interface
has upper rate
\[
\sup_{x\in I}\{\operatorname{Re}\mathcal S_n(x)+E(x)\}-\kappa_1
\]
for some fixed \(\kappa_1>0\). A parent-volume gap follows only
when this expression is smaller than the parent action.
The error exponent is determined by the available analytic domain
and cannot be increased on demand. Both vertical boundaries,
the omitted endpoint rows, and all original sampling aliases
remain in the exact trace formula.

Fixed physical marks and fixed products at shared colors inherit
the result, with their full derivatives and sum of phases.
The note does not establish the required complex domain or the
remaining action comparisons for arbitrary short partial fillings.
In particular this is not an additional terminal-plus-long-remainder
volume theorem: that case was already proved in the verified-terminal
results. Making the remaining filling powers long makes their own
heights and action corrections small. It does not make the internal
heights of a fixed short component small. Its internal contour
contributions must still be estimated before applying the long-filling
transfer.

## An unturned insertion has a common baseline at fixed complex height

The [unturned baseline and window theorem](research_unturned_endpoint_complex_baseline_and_window.md)
applies directly to \(B_N(C,\alpha)=K_N(2\cosh(\alpha/N),C)\).
On every bounded buffered rectangle inside \(0<\Re x<1/2\), its
actual balanced value recurrence has the form \(I+N^{-1}B_N(x)\)
with a uniformly bounded holomorphic matrix. The bounded modified
differential equation therefore supplies a common polynomially bounded
baseline. The scalar compatibility theorem verifies exponential
accuracy for both the value and the original first normal on real
interior rows.

One-sided Hermite corrections give exact representatives above and
below the real interval, with exponentially small corrections on their
respective sides. Their difference has an exponentially small removable
real interface in the original trace formula. All vertical sides,
the spectator and the crossing phase remain in that formula. Positive
powers use the upper \(x\)-half-plane; negative powers use its reflected
lower counterpart and the reflected Fourier sector. The estimate does
not assign an arbitrary size to the interface's positive error exponent.

The theorem also estimates a literal positive-endpoint row window of
the filled trace, including the derivative of the outgoing kernel.
For rows \(0\le a\le\varepsilon N\), the resulting output polynomial
satisfies
\[
 |W_{N,\varepsilon}(-2\cos u)|
 \le C N^p\exp\{N[h_0(2\varepsilon)+|\Im u|]\},\qquad
 h_0(t)=2t\log((\pi e^2/2)/t).
\]
Since \(h_0(t)\to0\), this window is below a fixed positive terminal
rate on a sufficiently small output disk. The full outgoing normal
can have degree \(N-1\), so its continuation cost is \(|\Im u|\),
not \(\varepsilon|\Im u|\).

A separate exact central-product calculation gives
\[
 J_*(t)=\frac1\pi\int_t^\pi\operatorname{asinh}(\sin(s/2))\,ds,
 \qquad \psi(t,0)-J_*(t)\le\mathcal I_2.
\]
This is a diagnostic for a possible sharper error estimate. The proof
does not identify \(J_*\) with the baseline or interface error.
The opposite endpoint and all remaining currents still need their
actual terminal-action estimates; a generic-parameter filled-leaf
scalar seed has not been proved.

## The truncation forcing has a sharp rate; its boundary packet remains

The [Green estimate](research_partial_endpoint_green_boundary_budget.md)
uses the actual partial Newton polynomial
\[
 H_K(C)=\sum_{a=0}^{K}e_a(w)e_a(C),\qquad
 K=\lceil N/2\rceil+\lfloor\delta N\rfloor,\quad 0<\delta<1/2.
\]
Its ordinary defect telescopes exactly:
\[
 (J-w)H_K=s_{K+1}^2e_{K+1}(w)e_K(C).
\]
On a buffered physical bulk interval with \(0<t<2\pi\delta\),
the defect and its fixed derivatives have upper bound
\[
 C N^p e^{-N J_\delta(t)},\qquad
 J_\delta(t)=-\int_0^\delta
  \log\left|\frac{\sin^2(t/2)-\sin^2(\pi v)}
                  {\cos^2(\pi v)}\right|\,dv .
\]
Small complex disks and shifted factorial bounds prove this uniformly
even at the product zeros. No lower distance from a zero is assumed.

For a chosen holomorphic baseline \(H\), put
\(E=H_K(c_N(x))-H(x)\) and retain
\(r_H=(\mathscr J_N-w)H\). A four-component state contains two
adjacent values of \(E\) and their two derivatives. Its exact backward
Green formula on any fractional grid \(x=(j+\vartheta)/N\) gives
\[
 \|Z_E(x)\|
 \le C\|Z_E(x_b)\|
      +CN^p e^{-N J_\delta(t_N(x))}
      +CN\sum_{x_l\ge x}(|r_H(x_l)|+|r_H'(x_l)|).
\]
The first term is the actual right-boundary packet on that same
fractional grid. The monotonic increase of \(J_\delta(t_N(x))\)
along the grid proves that backward propagation does not lose the
forcing exponent.

For the existing common baseline \(A_N^0\), the missing boundary
estimate is therefore explicit: it concerns
\(Z_{H_K\circ c_N-A_N^0}\) near the right end of the interval,
uniformly for all \(0\le\vartheta<1\). Initializing at one physical
row does not supply that off-grid estimate. The baseline's residual
must also have a sufficient rate. Optimizing the cutoff controls the
forced term, not these two independent terms.

The normalization qualification is essential. At \(w=c_0\), the
partial kernel equals \(1\), but
\(1+e^{-cN}P_N(C)/4\) is another ordinary homogeneous solution with
identical full physical jets and bounded size on a sufficiently thin
strip. Its between-node difference is \(e^{-cN}\), although the
truncation defect vanishes. This is not the constructed baseline,
which preserves the constant solution. It shows why an arbitrary
moderate representative cannot replace that normalization. The ideal
multiple vanishes in the entire original trace; separated contour
pieces must retain their cancellation.

## Exact continuation around one angular period

The [period transfer theorem](research_unturned_endpoint_exact_period_monodromy.md)
concerns the ordinary second-order recurrence for the unturned kernel.
Write \(h=1/N\), \(c_N(x)=2\cos(2\pi x+\pi/N)\), and
\(P_N(w)=2T_N(w/2)+2\). At a generic starting point
\(2Nx\notin\mathbb Z\), let \(M_N(x,w)\) carry the state
\((F(x),F(x-h))^t\) to \((F(x+1),F(x+1-h))^t\) for a
homogeneous solution. Then
\[
 \det M_N(x,w)=1,\qquad
 \operatorname{tr}M_N(x,w)=2+P_N(w)\cot^2(\pi Nx).
\]
Both formulas extend meromorphically. The excluded orbits contain
singular individual recurrence coefficients; the formulas do not
replace their original removable limits.

The proof uses the whole cyclic characteristic polynomial. Evaluation
of polynomials of degree below \(N\) at the generic orbit is invertible.
It identifies the periodic recurrence with the triangular Newton
operator, whose characteristic polynomial is exactly \(P_N(w)\).
Imposing the boundary condition \(F(x+1)=\mu F(x)\) changes its
determinant to
\[
 P_N(w)+\tan^2(\pi Nx)(2-\mu-\mu^{-1}).
\]
The two winding terms in the determinant give this identity; at
\(N=2\), where the two neighbors share one matrix entry, their sum is
retained explicitly. Thus repeated eigenvalues and both parities enter
the proof with their full multiplicities.

For the microscopic parameter \(w=2\cosh(\alpha/N)\), one has
\(P_N(w)=4\cosh^2(\alpha/2)\). On either line
\(|\Im x|=H>0\), the trace tends exponentially to
\(-2\cosh\alpha\). Consequently the two multipliers tend to
\(-e^\alpha,-e^{-\alpha}\), with multiplicities retained at collisions.
This provides exact branch data for a possible homogeneous
continuation. At \(P_N(w)=0\), the trace is two, but a nontrivial
Jordan part may remain.

The original kernel instead satisfies
\[
 (w-\mathscr J_N)K_N(c_N(x),w)
 =\frac{P_N(w)P_N(c_N(x))}
        {N^4(c_N(x)-c_0)}.
\]
This ordinary polynomial source is retained. The transfer trace does
not determine a homogeneous representative matching the physical
values and first normals, or give the sharp boundary and residual
estimates required by the preceding Green formula.

## The actual kernel has an explicit leading term away from the real axis

The [fixed-height theorem](research_unturned_endpoint_forced_off_real_asymptotic.md)
uses the preceding period identity for the original inhomogeneous
kernel. For \(w_N=2\cosh(\alpha/N)\), define
\[
 r_N(x,\alpha)
 =\frac{N^2K_N(w_N,c_N(x))}{4\sin^2(\pi Nx)},\qquad
 r_0(x,\alpha)
 =-\frac{\cosh^2(\alpha/2)}{\pi^2+\alpha^2}\csc^2(\pi x).
\]
For any \(0<H_0<H_1<\infty\) and bounded complex parameter disk,
\(r_N=r_0+O(N^{-1})\) uniformly on
\(H_0\le|\Im x|\le H_1\), with every fixed spatial and parameter
derivative. The expression at \(\alpha=\pm i\pi\) is removable;
the assertion is an absolute estimate at all physical parameters.

The proof divides the exact ordinary source equation by its
\(1/N\)-periodic physical relation. Its balanced transfer is
\(I+N^{-1}B+O(N^{-2})\). The displayed function \(r_0\) solves the
limiting forced differential equation, so its error in one discrete
step is \(O(N^{-2})\). Both the actual function and \(r_0\) are
periodic. Their difference over one period is therefore determined
by \(I-M_N\), whose inverse is bounded on these bands away from
the discrete exceptional parameters. Summing \(N\) step errors gives
\(O(N^{-1})\). Holomorphy and a surrounding parameter circle extend
the estimate through those parameters.

The original spectral derivative is also retained:
\[
 \frac{N}{P_N(c_N(x))}
       \partial_CK_N(w_N,c_N(x))
 =\frac{i\,\operatorname{sgn}(\Im x)}{2\sin(2\pi x)}
       r_0(x,\alpha)+O(N^{-1}).
\]
For bounded real \(\alpha\), the leading terms are nonzero and give
pointwise bounds of order \(N^{-2}e^{2\pi N|\Im x|}\) for the
kernel, and \(N^{-1}e^{2\pi N|\Im x|}\) for its derivative.
This concerns the actual canonical polynomial, not a selected
homogeneous solution. A moderate homogeneous contribution would
be exponentially smaller here and cannot be recovered from this
power-size error.

## An explicit approximate basis reaches the sharp residual rate

The [sine-factor theorem](research_endpoint_sine_factor_sharp_truncation.md)
uses the already normalized interpolation \(G_N\) of the finite sine
factorials. Set
\[
 \mathcal F_{z,N}(x)
   =4^{-z}\frac{G_N(Nx+z)}{G_N(Nx-z)},\qquad
 z_\pm=-\frac12\pm\frac{i\alpha}{2\pi}.
\]
The original ordinary operator satisfies the exact lowering rule
\[
 \mathscr J_N\mathcal F_{z,N}
 =c_z\mathcal F_{z,N}-\frac{s_z^4}{4}\mathcal F_{z-1,N}.
\]
Consequently a finite sum \(U_m=\sum_{k=0}^m a_k\mathcal F_{z-k,N}\),
with
\[
 a_0=1,\qquad
 \frac{a_k}{a_{k-1}}
 =\frac{s_{z-k+1}^4}{4(c_{z-k}-c_z)},
\]
has a single uncanceled final term in \((\mathscr J_N-w)U_m\).
This is an ordinary identity of the explicitly normalized functions.

For a target \(x_0\in(0,1/2)\), choose
\[
 \delta=\frac1\pi\arcsin\frac{\sin(\pi x_0)}{\sqrt2},
 \qquad m=\lfloor N\delta\rfloor .
\]
The successive summand ratios give the rate
\[
 \mathcal I_\delta(X)=
 \int_0^\delta
 \log\frac{\sin^2(\pi X)-\sin^2(\pi u)}{\sin^2(\pi u)}\,du.
\]
The functions remain bounded on a buffered rectangle of any fixed
height about \(x_0\). Their ordinary residuals and fixed derivatives
are at most a polynomial times \(e^{-N\mathcal I_\delta(\Re x)}\).
At the target,
\(\mathcal I_\delta(x_0)=J_*(\pi-2\pi x_0)\).
The proof checks this identity including its additive constant.

Taking the sum and divided difference of the two modes gives a
basis regular at \(\alpha=0\). The parameter statement holds on
bounded rectangles \(|\Re\alpha|\le A\),
\(|\Im\alpha|\le\pi-\epsilon\); other complex-index resonances are
not included. Its balanced frame is uniformly invertible on the
chosen bulk domain. Two actual kernel values at a right physical
anchor determine polynomially bounded coefficients. Backward
propagation then gives a sharp comparison at the physical values.
The first-normal comparison in this note still retains its actual
normal anchor. An estimate between physical nodes is also separate.

## Reflection controls the actual first normal at the sharp rate

The [reflected connection theorem](research_reflected_endpoint_sharp_normal_connection.md)
closes the normal-anchor gap in the preceding sine-factor construction.
It uses the same scalar \(V_N\), fixed by two actual physical values.
On the stated bulk window and parameter rectangles
\(|\Re\alpha|\le A,\ |\Im\alpha|\le\pi-\epsilon\), it proves
\[
 |K_N(w,C_N(x_j))-V_N(x_j)|
 +|\partial_xK_N(w,C_N(x_j))-V_N'(x_j)|
 \le CN^p e^{-NI_\delta(x_j)} .
\]
Here the first derivative denotes differentiation of the composed
kernel in \(x\). Dividing by the nonzero \(C_N'(x_j)\) gives the
original spectral normal. The exponent equals
\(J_*(\pi-2\pi x_0)+O(N^{-1})\) at rows tending to the target
\(x_0\). Fixed parameter derivatives and outside endpoint normals
cost only powers of \(N\).

The key step concerns the actual source. The canonical factorial
reflection makes every approximate mode, as well as the kernel,
invariant under \(x\mapsto1-N^{-1}-x\). For a symmetric function,
use the state
\[
 \left(f(x),
 \frac{f(x)-f(x-N^{-1})}{C_N(x)-C_N(x-N^{-1})}\right)^t .
\]
The quotient extends as a spectral derivative at coincident colors.
In these coordinates the recurrence remains \(I+O(N^{-1})\)
through the fold. The two approximate modes give a uniformly
invertible frame, including at \(\alpha=0\).

Write the actual state in this frame with coefficients
\(\mathbf a_N(x)\). Exact reflection gives
\(\mathbf a_N(1-x)=\mathbf a_N(x)\).
At every physical row in the reflected interval, both the original
ordinary forcing and its first angular derivative vanish. The
coefficient recurrence and its derivative therefore differ from the
identity only by the sharply bounded mode residual. Propagating from
\(j/N\) to \((N-j)/N\) changes \(\mathbf a_N'\) by an exponentially
small amount, while reflection changes its sign. The resulting
matrix equation has leading matrix \(2I\), and proves the required
bound on \(\mathbf a_N'(j/N)\).

## The sharp local estimates extend across the complex parameter resonances

The [finite-atlas theorem](research_endpoint_sharp_local_parameter_atlas.md)
removes the parameter-strip restriction from the preceding physical-jet
and one-sided estimates. For every compact complex \(\alpha\)-set it
constructs finitely many local analytic bases, with uniform constants.
The anchored scalar and exact representatives are chosen on each
chart. No global off-grid identification between charts is needed
for the stated estimates.

In the descending-index expansion the only possible poles on a bounded
parameter set are \(2z+1=L\), with fixed positive integers \(L\).
At odd \(L\), a numerator zero removes the pole and the sum terminates.
At even \(L\), put \(z_0=(L-1)/2\). The complete residue is
\[
 \operatorname*{Res}_{z=z_0}U_{m,N}(z,x)
   =R_{N,L}\,U_{m-L,N}(-z_0-1,x),\qquad
 R_{N,L}=
 \frac{\prod_{j=1}^L s_{z_0-j+1}^4}
      {4^L S_LS_{L-1}(4\pi/N)}=O(N^{-2L}).
\]
Subtracting
\(R_{N,L}U_{m-L,N}(-z-1,x)/(z-z_0)\) removes the pole
holomorphically. The moving reflected index has exactly the same
eigenvalue, so the residual regularizes as well. The fixed cutoff
change preserves the sharp exponential rate. Maximum principles on
fixed parameter disks preserve the leading mode and its regular
spectral frame through the fold.

Each chart retains exact reflection, so the same coefficient argument
proves the actual sharp value and first-normal comparison. Exact
one-sided Hermite repair then preserves both original jets, shared
products, all crossing factors and the full contour decomposition.
The real-interface rate remains arbitrarily close to the local
\(J_*\). Fixed original endpoint derivatives cost powers of \(N\).

## The actual endpoint insertion cannot vanish on a fixed nonreal saddle neighborhood

The [nonreal insertion theorem](research_endpoint_nonreal_insertion_lower_bound.md)
combines the new explicit baseline with the existing actual endpoint
connection constants. Put \(\nu=\alpha/\pi\),
\[
 k_\pm(\nu)=\frac{\Gamma(\pm i\nu)}
                  {\Gamma(1/2\pm i\nu/2)^4},\qquad
 S_N(x)=\frac N\pi\sin(\pi x).
\]
For real bounded \(\alpha\), the two-value anchor fixes the baseline's
two coefficients with an error \(O(N^{-1-\epsilon})\).
Its explicit modes then give, on any prescribed fixed-height bulk
rectangle,
\[
 V_N(x,\alpha)
 = k_+ S_N(x)^{-1+i\nu}
   +k_- S_N(x)^{-1-i\nu}+O(N^{-1-\epsilon}).
\]
The sum has its removable logarithmic value at \(\alpha=0\).
The same estimate holds for fixed spatial derivatives. It is obtained
by transporting two actual coefficients, not by extending a small
real-axis error without a bound.

For a fixed nonreal compact in \(0<\Re x<1/2\), write
\(\beta=\Im\Log\sin(\pi x)\). Its absolute value is bounded
away from zero. Since \(k_-=\overline{k_+}\) for real \(\nu\),
the two leading terms have unequal magnitudes, giving
\[
 |k_+S_N^{-1+i\nu}+k_-S_N^{-1-i\nu}|
 \ge \frac{2\pi|k_+|\,|\sinh(\nu\beta)|}
              {N|\sin(\pi x)|}\ge \frac cN .
\]
The last inequality extends uniformly through zero because
\(|\nu k_+|\to1/\pi^2\). The exact designated-half representative
differs from \(V_N\) exponentially, so it has the same lower bound.
Its fixed spatial derivatives are at most
\(C(1+\log N)/N\).

For a fixed product of \(r\) such factors at a supplied local saddle,
the value is at least \(cN^{-r}\), and derivatives are at most
\(C((1+\log N)/N)^r\). Under the stated bare local Gaussian
hypotheses, replacing the product by its saddle value costs a
relative \(O((1+\log N)^r/\sqrt N)=o(1)\).
Thus these insertions preserve that already specified nonzero local
coefficient. The proof explicitly assumes the bare cycle, its nonzero
coefficient, and its absolute Gaussian bound.

## The compact contour joins are controlled for every fixed power of magnitude at least two

The [compact interface and seam theorem](research_sharp_endpoint_compact_interface_and_seams.md)
applies to the original leaf source
\[
 L_{N,n}(Z)=
 \phi_N^{(C)}
 \left[R_N(C)^n
   \prod_{i=1}^{r}K_N(2\cosh(\alpha_i/N),C)\,K_N(C,Z)\right].
\]
The number of endpoint factors, the signed integer \(n\), and the
bounded parameter set are fixed. Every fixed ordinary output
derivative at \(Z=-2\) is retained.

For any compact angular interval \(K\Subset(0,\pi)\), put
\[
 d_K=\mathcal I_2-\max_{t\in K}\{\psi(t,0)-J_*(t)\}>0.
\]
A finite choice of sufficiently small sharp patches gives the real
interfaces a bound
\(CN^p e^{N(\mathcal I_2-d_K/2)}\).
Their baselines are normalized at one common physical anchor.
Subtracting two cutoff expansions gives an exact finite tail, and
the same anchor then bounds the actual difference between neighboring
baselines. The repaired representatives inherit that exponential
overlap estimate at every prescribed fixed height.

The outgoing kernel is split exactly at \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor\).
All high-index polynomials, including the odd middle polynomial, have
polynomial real norms and fixed derivative bounds. The literal full
Hermite trace therefore bounds their entire contribution by a
polynomial, also on restricted sets of rows. They are kept as a
separate estimated source. The remaining low kernel has the coherent
slit-domain bound with phase \(\psi(t,0)\).

For a vertical seam at angular real part \(t\), height \(H\), and
half-plane sign \(\sigma\), its low-kernel phase is bounded by
\[
 \mathcal P_{n,\sigma}(t,H)
 =\Re\psi(t-i\sigma H,0)
        +\left(\frac{\sigma nt}{2\pi}-1\right)H.
\]
It is convex in \(H\), since
\(\psi''(t,0)=-1/(2\pi\cos(t/2))\).
At height \(H_n=|\Im t_{|n|}(0)|\), the designated horizontal
phase is strictly concave in \(t\), with maximum \(\mathcal I_n\)
at the calibrated saddle. The opposite half has a smaller value.
The seam's real endpoint is paid by the compact interface gap;
its top endpoint is paid by the horizontal bound and the strictly
positive overlap saving. Convexity pays the whole seam. The exact
rational sampling kernel, all aliases, and both signs of \(n\) remain.

The same argument controls horizontal repair errors and the outer
vertical near the positive spectral endpoint; its remaining physical
window has an arbitrarily small positive rate. The negative-end
vertical is joined by the fold-cap result below.
This theorem gives no strict cap estimate for \(|n|=2\), and no
whole-leaf lower asymptotic.

The [uniform fold-cap theorem](research_endpoint_uniform_fold_cap.md)
uses the regular spectral divided-difference frame at \(C=-2\).

The [whole scalar theorem](research_microscopic_endpoint_filled_leaf_scalar_asymptotic.md)

derivative at every double physical root and the odd simple

\(|n|\ge3\), are fixed. The real parameters \(\alpha_i\)
range over any fixed bounded interval.

for some fixed \(b\), uniformly over those parameters and

\[

rate is strictly smaller near the selected saddle.

## Ordinary operations retain the analytic alias coefficients before a turn

The [pre-turn analytic class](research_endpoint_pre_turn_analytic_alias_class.md)
gives an exact local decomposition of the original endpoint kernel:
\[
 K_N(w_N(\alpha),C_N(x))
     =V_N(x)+P_N(C_N(x))Q_N(x)+E_N(x).

Here \(V_N\) is the sharply normalized scalar baseline.
The quotient \(Q_N\) is holomorphic with polynomial bounds
on prescribed bounded-height rectangles. The error \(E_N\)
has the sharp real full-jet bound. No moderate off-real
bound is asserted for that error.

Finite sums and products, the ordinary half-shift average
\(\mathcal S\), and its divided difference \(\mathcal D\)
preserve a finite polynomial in \(P_N\) with such analytic
coefficients and sharp real errors. The exact rule is
\[
 P_N(C_+)=P_N(C_-)=4-P_N(C).
\]
Thus a half shift can turn an alias into a constant term.
That term must remain in the source. Fixed-degree ordinary
division at roots \(2+O(N^{-2})\) also preserves the class
locally away from \(C=2\), with the actual remainders retained.

When canonical reduction is prescribed, full Hermite
interpolation preserves the physical values and normals.
A new exact repair then resets the alias degree to one.
Reduction and half shifts cannot be interchanged: the
half-shift operators do not preserve the ideal \((P_N)\).

This is closure under the stated ordinary operations, not
under a turn or arbitrary composition of short components.
It supplies neither a nonzero coefficient after subtraction
nor a comparison with the filled hyperbolic action.

## The actual alias coefficient has an explicit leading term through the real interval

The [alias coefficient theorem](research_endpoint_analytic_alias_leading_coefficient.md)
keeps the same baseline, symmetric repair and quotient \(Q_N\)
as the ordinary-operation theorem. For every fixed
\(\varepsilon>0\), on buffered spectral domains away from
\(C=2\), including \(C=-2\), it proves
\[
 Q_N(C,\alpha)=
 -\frac{4}{N^2(2-C)}
       \frac{\cosh^2(\alpha/2)}{\pi^2+\alpha^2}
       +O_{\rm hol}(N^{-3+\varepsilon}).
\]
This includes fixed derivatives and bounded complex
parameters. The apparent singularities at
\(\alpha=\pm i\pi\) are removable; the assertion is
absolute at these and the other physical imaginary marks.

The actual fixed-height asymptotic gives the comparison
on two horizontal lines. The already fixed polynomial
bound controls the vertical sides. In a thin rectangle
the harmonic measure of those sides is exponentially
small in width divided by height. The two-constants
maximum principle therefore transfers an almost
\(N^{-1}\) error for \(N^2Q_N\) across the real axis.
Reflection permits spectral differentiation through
the negative endpoint. The height is chosen only after
fixing the polynomial exponent; no new source is selected.

For an ordinary word \(\mathcal W\) of length \(\ell\)
in the half-shift operators, with \(d\) divided
differences, the exact alias term is
\[
 \begin{cases}
 P_N\,\mathcal WQ_N,&\ell\ \text{even},\\
 (4-P_N)\,\mathcal WQ_N,&\ell\ \text{odd}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The odd case therefore has the explicit constant-channel
correction
\[
 -\frac{16\,d!}{N^2(2-C)^{d+1}}
       \frac{\cosh^2(\alpha/2)}{\pi^2+\alpha^2}
       +O_{\rm hol}(N^{-3+\varepsilon}).
\]
It cannot be dropped before contraction. The calculation
does not bound an outer turn or rule out cancellation
with the other source channels.

## Boundary estimates and the critical two-power endpoint

The scalar theorem for \(|n|\ge3\) now has a
[fixed-output-neighborhood extension](research_microscopic_endpoint_filled_leaf_boundary_packet.md).
For the actual full trace with \(r\) microscopic endpoint factors,
its leading term is the calibrated exponential \(e^{NW_n(u)}\)
times a nonzero analytic geometric factor and the actual product
of endpoint coefficients. For bounded real parameters the latter
has modulus at least \(cN^{-r}\). The relative error is
\(O((1+\log N)^{r+1}N^{-1/2})\), uniformly on a fixed complex
output neighborhood. Fixed derivatives follow there. The whole
output period also has a Gaussian upper envelope in the angular
distance from the complete color.

This is an estimate for the literal finite source. It retains
the shortened outgoing sum, the odd middle term in its proper
complement, and every original trace normal. Its phase is the
previously calibrated terminal action. It is not a new
identification of that action with the volume of an arbitrary
partially filled exterior.

The [upper-bound composition theorem](research_microscopic_upper_packet_composition.md)
takes finitely many actual polynomial inputs with such local
exponential bounds and whole-period decay. After inserting
finitely many microscopic factors, a sufficiently large number
of attached inputs preserves this class of upper bounds for any
fixed signed filling power at the common circle. The threshold
on that number is explicit in the incoming phase curvature and
contour constants. This can be iterated through eligible joins.
It does not assume
or prove a nonzero leading coefficient. At a purely imaginary
common saddle, the imbalance used in the terminal lower bound
may disappear; an upper estimate alone does not settle that issue.

The two-power problem needs a different endpoint estimate.
The [actual trace error](research_critical_fold_actual_trace_error.md)
first retains the vanishing sine factor in the original trace
and the sharper independent-normal bound. On an interval of
angular width \(T\asymp N^{-1/4}\), this gives a saving
\(N^{-1/4}\), up to logarithms, relative to the local
\(N^{-r}e^{N\mathcal I_2}\) scale.

The [optimized block argument](research_critical_fold_optimized_block_assembly.md)
extends the estimate to a fixed endpoint interval. It chooses
the literal integer cutoff nearest the optimal cutoff at each
physical row, then groups equal cutoffs into consecutive blocks.
Only the analytic baseline on each block is moved along a contour.
At a common boundary the two contour integrals subtract, leaving
one exact last-summand difference and the correction to its actual
fold normalization. Summing these differences gives
\(O(N^{-r-5/4}(1+\log N)^{2r}e^{N\mathcal I_2})\) and
\(O(N^{-r-1}(1+\log N)^{2r}e^{N\mathcal I_2})\), respectively.
The physical replacement error is larger, of order
\(N^{-r-1/4}(1+\log N)^{2r}e^{N\mathcal I_2}\), but still
smaller than the local term. Four exterior sides remain explicit
for the join to the compact part of the contour.

The [two-power local calculation](research_two_power_shortened_wire_packet.md)
proves the needed nonzero local coefficient directly for
\(n=\pm2\). An explicit contour for the shortened Newton sum has
a unique strict maximum. The reflected factorial is continued
with its exact scalar, and the reflected sampling terms have a
strictly smaller rate. This yields the original local Gaussian
with a nonzero endpoint multiplier, uniformly on a fixed output
neighborhood. The
[whole two-power scalar theorem](research_two_power_microscopic_endpoint_scalar_asymptotic.md)
now combines this with the optimized endpoint estimate. It
compares the actual fold and bulk normalizations, retains the
finite cutoff tail and one-sided repair at their common boundary,
and joins all four exterior sides with a strict gap. The reflected
local integrals add with the original half-normalization; the
high outgoing sector is restored exactly once.

For \(n=\pm2\), the entire original scalar therefore equals its
nonzero local leading term times
\[
 1+O\!\left(
       N^{-1/4}(1+\log N)^{2r}
       +N^{-1/2}(1+\log N)^{r+1}
      \right).
\]
Its modulus lies between \(cN^{-r}e^{N\mathcal I_2}\) and
\(CN^{-r}(1+\log N)^r e^{N\mathcal I_2}\). This is uniform for
bounded real microscopic parameters, including parameters
depending on \(N\), and for both parities. It completes the
scalar microscopic-product theorem for every fixed \(|n|\ge2\).
A fixed output-neighborhood theorem for the whole two-power
source does not follow from this scalar estimate: the remaining
margin is polynomial, not exponential.

There is now a limited
[output-uniform version of the endpoint estimate](research_critical_fold_output_tube.md).
It holds on a complex spectral tube of width \(A/N\) around a
fixed small real interval starting at \(Z=-2\). The normalized
endpoint remainder and its \(q\)-th output derivative are bounded by
\[
 C_{A,q}N^{q-r-1/4}(1+\log N)^{2r}e^{-cNu_s^2},
\]
where the nearest real point is \(Z_s=-2\cos u_s\).
The proof compares the actual Newton factors at \(Z\) and \(Z_s\);
it preserves their sharp prefactor without continuing the scalar
estimate. Continuation with an exponential loss is used only for
pieces that already have a fixed gap.

This gives all fixed output normals at the complete color and
control on angular disks of radius \(O(N^{-1/2})\). It cannot yet
be used at a parent's fixed nonreal saddle. For a fixed parent,
that saddle eventually lies outside the shrinking tube, even if
the parent has very many pieces. At fixed imaginary output \(u=ib\),
the available endpoint envelope exceeds the desired filled action
by \(b^2/(8\pi)+O(b^4)\). This comparison does not determine whether
the actual endpoint terms cancel there.

## An exact cancellation obstruction for arbitrary real endpoint marks

The [real-zero theorem](research_microscopic_common_circle_real_zeros.md)
tests the proposed lower-bound class on an original finite source.
Choose a sufficiently large fixed number \(m\) of bare incoming
edges, a zero filling power at their common circle, and one
microscopic endpoint factor. Its exact scalar is
\[
 Z_{N,m}(\alpha)=
 \phi_N\!\left[
    K_N(2\cosh(\alpha/N),C)\,K_N(C,-2)^m
 \right].
\]
Here \(K_N\) is the original Newton kernel and \(\phi_N\) is the
full physical trace, including its first normals and the odd
simple value. All coefficients are real when \(\alpha\) is real.
The selected common critical point is \(t_*=-iH_m\), where
\(\tanh(H_m/2)=\sin(\pi/m)\).

The actual normalized amplitude contains
\[
 g_\alpha(Ns_m)=
 \frac{2|k_+(\alpha/\pi)|}{Ns_m}
 \cos\!\left(
       \frac{\alpha}{\pi}\log(Ns_m)+\arg k_+(\alpha/\pi)
      \right),\qquad
 s_m=\frac{\cosh(H_m/2)}{\pi},
\]
where \(k_+(\nu)=\Gamma(i\nu)/\Gamma(1/2+i\nu/2)^4\).
The proof retains the exact positive Gaussian prefactor and
estimates every complementary current. It gives an absolute
amplitude error \(o(N^{-1})\), without division by the cosine.
Consequently the sign changes of this expression give exact
zeros of the original scalar.

For every fixed positive real interval, such zeros occur at
every sufficiently large level, at both parities. There are
also choices of exact zeros satisfying
\(\alpha_N\log N\to\pi^2\), so convergence of the mark to zero
does not suffice for a uniform lower bound. At these zeros
in a fixed positive interval the first spatial amplitude
derivative still has magnitude at least \(c/N\). Nonvanishing
of a finite collection of local amplitude derivatives therefore
does not by itself force a nonzero scalar closing.

A separate nested-interval argument constructs one fixed
positive real mark in every positive interval for which
\[
 \liminf_N N^{-1}\log|Z_{N,m}(\alpha_*)|=-\infty,
 \qquad
 \limsup_N N^{-1}\log|Z_{N,m}(\alpha_*)|=M_m,
\]
where \(M_m=m\psi(-iH_m,0)-H_m\) is the calibrated common
action. The construction uses exact zeros and the actual
parameter-derivative upper bound. It claims no arithmetic
property of this mark.

This rules out the arbitrary-real pointwise lower bound.
It does not refute a lower bound for the prescribed knot
closing, an estimate for an integrated current, or the volume
conjecture. The roles of integration variables, physical
colors and fixed geometric boundary data must be distinguished
before using it in the partial-filling argument.

## The lower bound belongs to the original closing

The [exact compiler](research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md)
defines the partially filled source without any arbitrary real
mark: apply the original functionals \(\phi_v(R^{n_v}\,\cdot)\)
at the fixed filled vertices and retain the entire ordinary
polynomial at every remaining boundary variable. Original edge
kernels, phases and first normals stay in that expression.

Real microscopic marks appear only after the
[full-current decomposition](research_full_period_current_charge_convolution.md).
Its unit-charge vertical side evaluates a removed color at
\(w=2\cosh h\) and integrates \(0\le h\le H\). Setting
\(\alpha=Nh\) gives the exact weight
\[
 \rho(h)\,dh=
 \frac{i\eta C_{N,n}e^{inN\pi/4}}{2\pi}
 [N\sinh(\alpha/N)]e^{-in\alpha^2/(4\pi N)}
 \frac{\sinh(n\alpha/2)}{\cosh^2(\alpha/2)}\,d\alpha ,
 \qquad
 C_{N,n}=e^{\pi i n(N-1)^2/(4N)},\quad
 \eta=(-1)^{N-1}.
\]
One \(\alpha\) is shared by every edge incident to that removed
vertex. The source inside the integral still includes all
surviving traces and all edges between removed vertices.
Different removed sets carry their original inclusion–exclusion
signs. The resulting correction is a coherent integral, not
a positive sum of independent endpoint values.

At \(n=0\) this vertical current vanishes exactly. The zero-power
vertex in the real-zero theorem is instead a surviving traced
vertex, so that theorem does not contradict this identity.
At nonzero \(n\), the displayed density vanishes quadratically
at \(\alpha=0\). That single endpoint is not a separate
positive-measure contribution.

Physical colors have a different origin:
\(c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N)=w_N(i(2a+1)\pi)\).
For a fixed early row the Newton sum terminates at \(a\), and
at \(a=0\) its endpoint factor is exactly one. This does not
replace the real integration variables above by imaginary
discrete marks. Complete outside color is \(Z=-2\), distinct
from this \(+2\) endpoint.

For a fixed parent height, the full integration range is
\(\alpha\in[0,NH]\). Bounded microscopic marks cover only its
initial segment. The
[parent calibration](research_fixed_parent_height_global_calibration.md)
gives a classical gap on the positive horizontal slice and
near the final heights, but explicitly leaves the full
quantum currents and the rest of their height intervals
to be estimated.

The general partial-filling obligation is therefore to retain
the actual free-boundary source, prove that its prescribed
geometric contribution has a sufficiently large nonzero
coefficient, and bound the joined complementary terms from
above. If they are not smaller, noncancellation must be
proved for their coherent sum. Subsequent long fillings
require these estimates on the boundary domains they use;
a scalar value at complete output alone is insufficient.
Neither the new scalar theorem nor the real-zero theorem
settles this obligation for every fixed short assignment.

This clarification follows from complete reads of the compiler,
full-current identity, parent calibration and real-zero theorem.
It introduces no new volume theorem or additional hypothesis
on the original knot.

## Classical full-height comparison and the cost of the actual currents

The [saturated-face theorem](research_saturated_current_full_height_angle_envelope.md)
keeps a supplied positive parent geometry, its original edges and all
surviving unit-charge equations. Let \(C\) be the removed vertices,
\(H_v^0>0\) the parent heights, \(M_G\) the parent action, and
\(\delta_0>0\) its boundary Bregman gap, the positive margin supplied
by the parent action comparison. Each cut edge \(vw\),
with \(v\in C\) and \(w\notin C\), leaves a free incidence at \(v\).
Optimizing these incidences gives
\[
 \lambda_v(s)=\frac{|n_v|}{2}-1+
       \frac12\sum_{\substack{vw\\w\notin C}}
                        \left(1-\frac{|s_w|}{\pi}\right).
\]
Here \(s_w\) is the surviving real angle; complete outside angles
are zero. If every removed \(|n_v|\ge2\), all these coefficients
are nonnegative. The optimized action is then nondecreasing in
each height. The known gap at \(h_v=H_v^0\) consequently bounds
the entire box \(0\le h_v\le H_v^0\) by \(M_G-\delta_0/\pi\).
For arbitrary powers, the exact maximum occurs at one of the
\(2^{|C|}\) height corners. Each corner is an explicit convex
minimization on the shared retained angle body. An empty retained
body does not imply that the quantum descendant vanishes.

The actual finite source has an extra cost. For one edge whose
two vertices are removed, it contains the original Newton kernel
\(K_N(2\cosh h_1,2\cosh h_2)\). At fixed positive heights,
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
       \log K_N(2\cosh h_1,2\cosh h_2)=h_1+h_2.
\]
Every Newton summand is positive here, and the final one dominates.
The note also constructs a positive parent satisfying the stated
hypotheses. Thus transferring the classical envelope to the
pointwise quantum descendant with no additional rate is false.
This calculation neither disproves a gap for the integrated total
nor supplies a lower bound for its oscillatory current.

The [single-current theorem](research_integrated_unit_current_norm.md)
makes the distinction precise in an operator norm. Write
\[
 V_{n,N}^{H}[f]=\int_0^H \rho_{N,n,1}(h)f(2\cosh h)\,dh
\]
for the original vertical current, with \(n\ne0\), \(H>0\) fixed.
On ordinary polynomials of degree at most \(r(N-1)\), \(r\ge1\),
equipped with the supremum norm on \([-2,2]\), it proves
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\|V_{n,N}^{H}\|
                   =\left(r-1+\frac{|n|}{2}\right)H.
\]
Products of \(r\) original kernels with bounded real microscopic
endpoint parameters attain this rate. Reduction modulo the physical
polynomial cannot be performed before this off-grid integral.
If \(L_{n,N}\) is the original full trace and
\(H_{n,N}^{H}=L_{n,N}-V_{n,N}^{H}\) its horizontal companion, then
\(L_{n,N}\) has only polynomial operator cost in this norm.
On the stated products, the horizontal term therefore cancels the
vertical term to exponential relative accuracy. Taking absolute
values before recombining them loses that cancellation.

There is a separate improvement on the interval \(0\le h\le A/N\),
where \(A>0\) is fixed. The
[shared-mode integration theorem](research_shared_microscopic_current_mode_integration.md)
integrates all \(d\) incident factors using the same variable
\(\alpha=Nh\), with the original paired density and local
representatives retaining their physical values and first derivatives.
Uniformly on its specified interior complex windows, the bounds are
\[
 \begin{cases}
 O(N^{-1}/\log N),&d=1,\\
 O(N^{-2}),&d=2,\\
 O\!\left(N^{-d}(\log N)^{d-3}\right),&d\ge3.
 \end{cases}
\]
For \(d\ge3\) and \(n\ne0\), the leading coefficient is explicit
and nonzero. The two-factor coefficient is nonzero for coincident
positive real local coordinates. The one-factor formula retains its
oscillating upper-endpoint term and gives no uniform lower bound.
This local result does not estimate edges joining two removed
vertices or the rest of a fixed positive height interval. In
particular these logarithmic gains are not an exponential volume gap.

The [all-removed theorem](research_all_removed_vertical_current_asymptotic.md)
settles one of those integration questions exactly. Let
\(\Gamma=(V,E)\) be a fixed finite simple graph with no isolated
vertices, no outside vertices and no additional factors. Give every
vertex a fixed nonzero signed power \(n_v\) and a fixed height
\(H_v>0\). Write \(d_v\) for its degree. For the actual integral
\[
 I_{\Gamma,N}=
 \int_{\prod_v[0,H_v]}
  \prod_v\rho_{N,n_v,1}(h_v)
  \prod_{\{v,w\}\in E}
        K_N(2\cosh h_v,2\cosh h_w)\,\prod_v dh_v,
\]
the theorem proves
\[
 I_{\Gamma,N}
 =A_{\Gamma,N}N^{|V|-4|E|}
   \exp N\sum_v
    \left[
      \left(d_v-1+\frac{|n_v|}{2}\right)H_v
                   -\frac{i n_vH_v^2}{4\pi}
    \right]\bigl(1+O(N^{-1})\bigr).
\]
The coefficient retains all original phases, has an explicit
formula, and has modulus bounded above and below by positive
constants on compact positive height sets. A global Newton-product
bound controls every small-height region; near the upper corner,
the last Newton term dominates and ordinary endpoint integration
gives the displayed coefficient.

For one edge this has rate \((|n_1|H_1+|n_2|H_2)/2\), so the
additional \(H_1+H_2\) survives the actual joint oscillatory
integration. More generally the additional internal-edge rate is
\(\sum_v d_vH_v\). The theorem assumes no geometric parent and
makes no claim that this rate exceeds a particular parent's action.
It determines one term of the exact contour expansion; horizontal
terms can cancel it. Zero powers, isolated vertices, surviving
traces and additional factors are outside this statement.
