## What remains after contracting the entire high Newton sector

The [low-kernel current theorem](research_low_kernel_all_removed_current_asymptotic.md)
starts with the exact split
\[
 K_N=K_N^{\rm low}+H_N^{\rm rad},\qquad
 K_N^{\rm low}(w,w')=\sum_{k=0}^{L}e_k(w)e_k(w'),\qquad
 L=N-1-\lfloor N/2\rfloor .
\]
The full high radical has already been treated by the exact matching
contraction; its contributions remain separate. The theorem concerns
the low kernel that this algebraic step leaves behind.

At fixed positive heights it proves
\[
 K_N^{\rm low}(2\cosh h,2\cosh h')
 =N^{-2}e^{N(h+h')/2}
   \left(\mathcal K_{\epsilon}(h,h')+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-2})\right).
\]
Here \(\epsilon\) is the parity of the level,
\[
 r(h)=\operatorname{sech}^2(h/2),\quad
 a_{\rm ev}(h)=r(h)/2,\quad a_{\rm odd}(h)=\sqrt{r(h)}/2,\quad
 \mathcal K_{\epsilon}(h,h')
   =\frac{a_{\epsilon}(h)a_{\epsilon}(h')}
          {1-r(h)r(h')}>0.
\]
The global bound
\[
 0<K_N^{\rm low}(2\cosh h,2\cosh h')
       \le (L+1)e^{N(h+h')/2}\qquad(h,h'\ge0)
\]
includes every small-height region. It follows from the exact
product over the distinct double nodes, without extrapolating the
positive-height asymptotic to zero.

For a fixed finite simple graph with no isolated vertex, no outside
vertices and no additional factors, give each vertex a nonzero
integer power and assume
\[
 \lambda_v=\frac{d_v+|n_v|}{2}-1>0.
\]
Replacing every kernel by \(K_N^{\rm low}\) in the all-removed
integral then gives
\[
 I_{\Gamma,N}^{\rm low}
 =B_{\Gamma,N}N^{|V|-2|E|}
       \exp N\sum_v
          \left(\lambda_vH_v-\frac{i n_vH_v^2}{4\pi}\right)
             \bigl(1+O(N^{-1})\bigr).
\]
The exact coefficient is nonzero, uniformly over compact positive
height sets, at both parities. The proof retains the coupled edge
amplitude at the upper corner; it does not assume that this
amplitude factors by vertex. Every other height region has a
strict exponential loss because every \(\lambda_v>0\).

The extra rate beyond the current densities is therefore
\(\frac12\sum_vd_vH_v\). In particular, contracting the radical
does not justify assigning the classical saturated-face envelope
to the remaining low integral without paying an additional rate.
The excluded degree-one, absolute-power-one case has
\(\lambda_v=0\); a zero power makes its unit current vanish.
Neither case is included in the displayed asymptotic.

The adopted final pin is
\(\texttt{e9261e460fe52989ea298f423acc699a4e4b34c00805efbe52c5bee8eb2c1161}\).
This establishes an integrated obstruction for general fixed graphs,
not a new knot volume limit.

The accompanying coverage check keeps two existing routes distinct.
For radical matchings, the matched edges must be omitted before
estimating the remaining physical-color component sources. Restoring
their full kernels and then taking a supremum can lose an entire
edge action. The archived alternating observation gives a strict
loss when those actual components already have joint boundary
envelopes; those envelopes and their comparison with the parent
action remain unproved for arbitrary short components.

For continuation from small charges, the existing initializer and
the nonzero local companion factor are already available. The
classical convexity argument excludes competitors in the same
positive charge fiber. A general proof still has to show that the
original quantum cycle, with all its boundary and alias terms,
has the required nonzero projection onto the geometric contribution.
The finite trace identity and positivity of the angle optimizer
alone do not supply that assertion.

## Physical residues retain their own edge action

The [compact-contour residue theorem](research_compact_positive_contour_residue_control.md)
controls the derivatives at repeated spectral roots without replacing
their physical colors by a complete-color maximum.
Let \(K_N(z,w)\) denote the original edge polynomial, let
\(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)\) be a physical spectral value, and set
\[
 F_j(w)=K_N(c_j,w),\qquad G_j(w)=\partial_zK_N(c_j,w).
\]
The first quantity is a physical row value. The second is the
independent derivative required by the original trace at a double
root; it cannot be obtained by differentiating a sum after its
vanishing terms have been removed.

The Jacobi determinant identity gives a representative
\[
 \widehat G_j(w)=
 \frac{c'(0)F_j(w)\widetilde Q_N(w)+R_j(w)}{c'(j)}.
\]
Here \(c(x)=2\cos((2x+1)\pi/N)\), \(R_j\) is the derivative of
the normalized Jacobi determinant under a common shift of its
indices, and \(\widetilde Q_N\) is the logarithmic-factorial
representative of the endpoint derivative \(G_0\).
The determinant derivative \(R_j\) is a polynomial. Apparent
resolvent poles therefore cancel before any estimate is made.
The resulting representative is holomorphic on
\(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\), including \(-2\).

It agrees with \(G_j\) in every value and first derivative
required at the next physical endpoint. Consequently substitution
preserves the original remaining traces and every mixed derivative
in them. This is not equality at an arbitrary free complex endpoint;
untraced boundary polynomials remain literal.

On every fixed compact subset of the slit plane, for every fixed
derivative order \(r\), the proof gives
\[
 |\partial_w^r\widehat G_j(w)|
 \le C_rN^{6+r}(1+\log N)|F_j(w)|.
\]
The row's normalized logarithm converges uniformly to its own
action \(\Psi_{j/N}\). The physical angle is
\(\tau_j=\pi-(2j+1)\pi/N\), and the exact calibration is
\[
 \Psi_{j/N}(-2\cos t)=\psi(t,\tau_j+\pi/N).
\]
Monotonicity of the real part of \(\Psi_x\) gives an upper bound
by the action at \(\tau_j\), uniformly even for colors approaching
the ends of the physical grid. For edges with both endpoints
physical, the previously proved real entropy and full-normal
estimates supply the same conclusion directly.

For a fixed set \(S\) of vertices frozen at arbitrary physical
nodes, let \(E_S\) be the edges incident to \(S\), counted once.
Apply the full residue trace at every vertex in \(S\), including
its crossing value and first derivative. The resulting packet
has a representative \(\widehat A_{S,N}\) satisfying
\[
 |\partial_{\mathbf w}^{\beta}\widehat A_{S,N}|
 \le C N^M
 \exp N\left\{\sum_{vw\in E_S}\operatorname{Re}\psi(t_v,t_w)
                    +\epsilon\right\}
\]
for every fixed \(\epsilon>0\) and derivative multi-index \(\beta\).
The remaining traced angles range over a fixed compact positive
family; no buffer is required for the frozen physical colors.
All mixed normals on internal frozen edges, coincident colors,
both level parities, and arbitrary fixed signed powers are included.
A polynomial number of physical-node assignments can be summed
with the same exponential bound. On compact subsets of
\(\operatorname{Re}w<2\), the \(\epsilon\) can be replaced by a
polynomial prefactor. On a general slit compact only the stated
arbitrary fixed tolerance has been proved.

The final proof is pinned at
\(\texttt{cac1016d5f515510b95071a25c8d97345b334043492a6b430c4e924f87d82bb0}\).
Its complete proof and four complete direct sources were read
at matching versions before adoption.

This gives a quantitative estimate for crossed physical poles
whenever a compact contour construction already provides a strict
action gap. It does not bound edges disjoint from \(S\), supply a
global contour construction, or establish a nonzero geometric
coefficient. In particular, connecting a small geometric contour
straight to the real integration domain can increase the real
action above the target. The required further argument must
control the original combined contour and its boundary terms.
The finite-exception theorem remains open.

## The value interpolant has the original derivative normalization

The [normal-connection theorem](research_physical_row_slit_normal_connection.md)
resolves a compatibility issue in constructing a representative of
the full edge kernel. Interpolating its values and bounding its
derivatives separately would not establish that both arise from the
same analytic function.

Let \(h=1/N\), let \(x=j/N\) be the scaled row index, and write
\[
 C_N(x)=2\cos(2\pi x+\pi/N),\qquad
 F_j(w)=K_N(C_N(j/N),w).
\]
Fix \(0<a<b<1/2\) and a compact subset \(\mathcal K\) of
\(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\). The new theorem constructs a
holomorphic unit \(A_N(x,w)\), anchored at one actual row, for which
\[
 \frac{A_N(j/N,w)}{F_j(w)}=1+O(e^{-\kappa N}),\qquad
 \frac{\partial_x A_N(j/N,w)
       -C_N'(j/N)\widehat G_j(w)}{F_j(w)}
             =O(e^{-\kappa N})
\]
uniformly for \(j/N\in[a,b]\) and \(w\in\mathcal K\).
Here \(\widehat G_j\) is the source-preserving normal representative
from the preceding theorem. The estimates include any fixed number
of derivatives in \(w\).

The proof first extends attraction of the actual Riccati ratios to
the spectral slit. Their inverses are last diagonal entries of
Jacobi resolvents, hence Stieltjes transforms of probability measures
on a fixed real interval. This bounds the ratios above and away
from zero on slit compacts. Analytic continuation from the known
half-plane limit identifies the limiting root; the Riccati equation
then improves convergence to \(O(1/N)\). Finite iteration and an
anchored Euler--Maclaurin primitive give exponentially accurate
row values.

Differentiating the exact recurrence under a common index shift
leaves one scalar normalization constant. With
\(D_j=R_j/F_j\), where \(R_j\) is the shifted determinant
derivative, and an actual anchor \(x_*=j_*/N\), that constant is
\[
 a_N(w)=c'(0)\widetilde Q_N(w)+D_{j_*}(w)
                 -N^{-1}\partial_x\log A_N(x_*,w).
\]
It is determined by the original kernel, not chosen as an
asymptotic initial condition. Exact symmetry at pairs of physical
colors forces \(a_N\) to be exponentially small on a real spectral
interval. Two analytic estimates finish the argument: many equally
spaced approximate zeros give exponential smallness on a smaller
complex disk, and a finite chain of overlapping disks propagates
that smallness to \(\mathcal K\). Polynomial bounds on \(a_N\)
throughout the connecting domain are essential here.

A finite Hermite correction then produces a single scalar function
\(\mathfrak F_N\) with exact identities
\[
 \mathfrak F_N(j/N,w)=F_j(w),\qquad
 \partial_x\mathfrak F_N(j/N,w)
                    =C_N'(j/N)\widehat G_j(w).
\]
Differentiating in the second color retains the original mixed
normal, including the contribution of high Newton terms.
The correction is exponentially small on a sufficiently thin
fixed degree strip and preserves the original row action, with
an arbitrary fixed exponential tolerance on general slit compacts
and a polynomial prefactor on half-plane compacts.

The adopted proof is pinned at
\(\texttt{a5084adb4ff25cb08020e5f9485bd1aaea5b49468c6ab0af311ebc1c0c504d99}\).
Its entire proof and both complete direct sources were checked at
matching versions.

This removes an undetermined derivative coefficient from the
proposed complete-kernel construction. It does not extend the
interpolated degree to arbitrary complex height. There the selected
Riccati root can have modulus one even within a positive geometric
configuration, so the real-degree contraction argument no longer
applies. The exact identities also cover only the specified bulk
subgrid; all other rows and the original closing remain part of
the full source problem.

## An additive replacement for the reflected wire half

The [half-wire regularization theorem](research_additive_half_wire_source_regularization.md)
gives an exact change of representation before taking absolute values.
It uses the original factorial interpolation \(B_N(x,t)\) of a
Newton polynomial. Put
\[
 D=N-1,\quad a_N=-\frac1{2N},\quad b_N=\frac D{2N},
 \quad \mathcal R x=\frac DN-x,\qquad
 F_N(x;t,u)=B_N(x,t)B_N(x,u),
\]
and define
\[
 d_t(x)=\cos t+\cos(2\pi x+\pi/N),\qquad
 c_N(x)=\cos(2\pi Nx).
\]
The exact factorial reflection yields
\[
 B_N(x,t)B_N(\mathcal R x,t)
 =\frac{\cos(Nt)-(-1)^{N-1}c_N(x)}{N^2d_t(x)}.
\]
Writing \(P_t=P_N(-2\cos t)\), the difference between
\(F_N(\mathcal R x;t,u)\) and
\[
 I_N(x;t,u)=
 \frac{(1-c_N(x))^2}
 {N^4d_t(x)d_u(x)F_N(x;t,u)}
\]
is explicitly a sum of terms divisible by \(P_t\) or \(P_u\).
Its coefficients are holomorphic near the full physical grid
when the prescribed nonreal wire contours are used.

For \(H>0\), orient
\(\gamma^\pm=[a_N,b_N]\pm iH\) from left to right. Then
\[
 K^{\rm reg}_{N,H}(t,u)
   =N\int_{\gamma^+}F_N(x;t,u)\,dx
        +N\int_{\gamma^-}I_N(x;t,u)\,dx
\]
has exactly the original internal edge's values and all required
first and mixed spectral derivatives. It is holomorphic for
\(|\Re t|,|\Re u|<\pi\) and
\(|\Im t|,|\Im u|<2\pi H\).
The claim concerns an edge whose endpoints will be traced.
It does not change an ordinary free-boundary polynomial.

The inverse term has moving poles at
\[
 x=b_N\pm\frac{t}{2\pi}+\frac rN,\qquad
 x=b_N\pm\frac{u}{2\pi}+\frac rN,\qquad r\ge0,
\]
with the exact possible multiplicities determined from the
factorial divisor. Residues at colliding poles must be grouped
before they are evaluated. On the stated parameter neighborhoods,
their grouped sums are again in the full physical Hermite ideal.
Height changes retain both endpoint segments as well as these
residues; the inverse integrals alone do not have vanishing
transition terms.

There is a quantitative local estimate. On a fixed compact
angular set, choose five heights between \(\epsilon\) and
\(2\epsilon\). At least one stays a fixed multiple of
\(\epsilon\) away from both moving pole heights. These choices
give a finite open cover on whose smaller closed pieces
\[
 \left|N\int_{\gamma^-}I_N\,dx\right|
 \le C_\epsilon N^{-1}
      \exp\{N[8\pi\epsilon+\omega(2\epsilon)]\},
 \qquad \omega(s)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Fixed derivatives cost only powers of \(N\).
The estimate follows from the two-sided factorial bounds and
the nonnegative real-wire logarithmic potential
\[
 \int_0^x\log|2\cos(2\pi r)-w|\,dr
       -2\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi r)\,dr\ \ge0,
       \qquad 0\le x\le\tfrac12 .
\]
The latter inequality holds for every complex \(w\): first prove
it on \([-2,2]\), then compare distances with the projection of
\(\Re w\) to that interval.

On a compact positive edge domain the original
\(\Re\psi(t,u)\) has a positive minimum, by the volume identity
and global monotonicity. Choosing \(\epsilon\) sufficiently small
puts the local inverse rate strictly below that minimum.
This is a bound for the inverse half only. The main half can
retain larger endpoint contributions, and the local meromorphic
representations have not been assembled into one globally bounded
holomorphic representative.

The adopted final pin is
\(\texttt{af8daf3eaa16303f8297b4a712ee9debe31cabc7326776fc34c9b185f0d216a0}\).
The complete proof and all six complete direct sources were
checked at matching versions. The result supplies an exact
representation change and a local exponential estimate; it does
not establish a further filling volume theorem.

## Continuing actual row windows to regular positive configurations

The [regular positive continuation theorem](research_physical_row_regular_positive_continuation.md)
extends the correctly normalized physical-row mode beyond a thin
real-degree tube. In centered degree coordinates
\[
 X_j=(j+\tfrac12)/N,\qquad t=\pi-2\pi X,\qquad
 a=\tan(t/2),\quad b=\tan(u/2),\quad q_*^2=1+a^2+b^2,
\]
its selected characteristic is
\[
 \lambda=\frac{q_*+a}{q_*-a},\qquad
 \partial_X\psi(\pi-2\pi X,u)=\operatorname{Log}\lambda.
\]
The logarithm and action keep their original real calibration.
The positive product domains supply buffered paths from real
physical windows to any positive target with \(t\ne0\). On these
paths \(q_*\) and \(q_*\pm a\) are units, and
\[
 1-\lambda^{-2}=\frac{4q_*a}{(q_*+a)^2}
\]
does not vanish. Points with \(|\lambda|=1\) cause no failure of
this algebraic separation.

The proof constructs an analytic approximate Riccati solution on
the complex chart by iteration on nested domains. Cauchy estimates
make the iteration contract after a fixed multiple of \(1/N\) is
reserved at each step; a fixed domain buffer permits order \(N\)
steps and an exponentially small residual. Comparison with the
actual row is made only on a real buffer where contraction is
already proved. An Euler--Maclaurin primitive is anchored at the
actual row value. Consequently the continued function has the
original action and exponentially accurate physical values and
independent derivatives.

Phase-normalized one-sided Hermite correction then matches the
window data exactly. On its designated complex half-domain it
has exponentially small norm, regardless of the fixed target
height within the supplied chart. The resulting source upper
bound is \(\exp\{N\Re\psi+o(N)\}\), including all prescribed mixed
data when the other endpoint is physical. Same-coordinate charts
have exponentially small normalized differences on buffered
overlaps connected to a shared physical seed.

The exact contour formula is for the explicitly defined finite
residue expression \(\Phi^\sharp\), formed using \(F_j\) and the
holomorphic representative \(\widehat G_j\). Its difference from
the original window trace is a multiple of \(P_N(w)\), holomorphic
on the second spectral slit. Thus it becomes the original
expression after the required second trace, with the spectator's
derivative and every mixed datum retained. Root review corrected
an earlier formula that displayed equality with the original
untraced expression; the corrected final distinguishes these
objects explicitly in equations (37a)--(38a).

The one-sided representative need not be even in the first angle.
It enters a closed window contour with both horizontal sides,
all four vertical half-sides and the real interface. The common
baseline gives an exponential saving on that interface; the
remaining spectator still has to be bounded. The theorem does
not cover the whole first grid, make an individual chart cross
its fold, compare role-swapped charts without a shared joint
seed, or prove a gap for the exterior currents.

The adopted final pin is
\(\texttt{3a7d81d55f60396c2e3058d5ebe967ae625ff47c4b527b4e102e37fa8f28d644}\).
Author, peer and root read the complete corrected final and all four
complete direct sources at matching pins. Root checked the source
type in the residue identity, the recurrence normalization, the
analytic iteration, its real-only source comparison and the
one-sided correction. No mathematical program or numerical test
was used.

## Comparing the two endpoint choices on a common domain

The [endpoint-role overlap theorem](research_physical_row_endpoint_role_overlap.md)
compares the actual regular continuation constructions with the
first and second endpoint roles interchanged. Choose fixed bulk
intervals in both centered coordinates,
\[
 X_j=(j+\tfrac12)/N,\qquad Y_k=(k+\tfrac12)/N,
\]
contained in the respective matched windows. The two local
second-parameter domains must also contain the opposite seed
intervals. The normalized constructions are bounded by
\(e^{o(N)}\) on a buffered complex product about these intervals,
and their phases agree with
\(\Psi(X,Y)=\psi(\pi-2\pi X,\pi-2\pi Y)\).

At every joint physical node, their values, both first derivatives
and mixed first derivative agree with the original kernel.
For each fixed second node, the normalized difference therefore
has order \(N\) exact zeros in the first coordinate. A disk
Blaschke estimate gives an exponentially small bound on an open
first-coordinate neighborhood. Its values at the second grid
are now small rather than identically zero. Subtracting their
finite sinc interpolant before a second Blaschke estimate gives
an exponentially small bound on a two-complex-variable seed.
This approximate-zero step is necessary.

On any connected common domain with the same holomorphic action
and locally uniform \(e^{o(N)}\) bounds for both normalized
constructions, a finite chain of buffered holomorphic-ball
estimates propagates this saving to every compact subset:
\[
 \left|\partial_X^a\partial_Y^b
       \left[e^{-N\Psi}(A_N-B_N)\right]\right|
       \le C_{K,a,b}e^{-c_KN}.
\]
All derivative orders here are fixed. The same argument applies
to the unrepaired baselines, using their exponentially small
nodal errors in both stages.

The theorem requires a shared seed and a connected common
domain on which both designated-side bounds hold. It neither
identifies arbitrary off-grid representatives nor constructs a
global scalar from these local functions. It retains the exact
\(\Phi^\sharp\) versus original-trace distinction from the
continuation theorem, as well as all unmatched rows, fold
neighborhoods, opposite closures and exterior currents.

The adopted final pin is
\(\texttt{67478e66259712bc648c23241c3c3e93bc4342c54b2dbcea39be97ee7b83edec}\).
Author, peer and root read the complete final and both complete
direct sources at matching versions. Root checked the joint
normal identities, the exact and approximate dense-grid stages,
and the connected-domain propagation. Only written mathematics,
source reads and hash checks were used.

## Joining the local functions while preserving both row families

The [positive-product window theorem](research_positive_product_window_gluing.md)
constructs a common holomorphic baseline on a fixed product neighborhood
of any positive pair. The product contains two real physical seed
intervals. Its discriminant has the original square-root branch, and
the action \(\psi(t,u)\) has the original additive constant.

Choose a buffered Jordan contour in the first angular domain. Cover
its boundary by finitely many regular first-degree constructions,
normalize each by \(e^{-N\psi}\), and combine their boundary values
with a fixed partition of unity. Their Cauchy integral defines one
holomorphic function \(H_N(t,u)\), bounded by \(e^{o(N)}\) on smaller
product compacts. This is an explicit finite projection.

To control the projection error, compare every boundary function with
a second-degree construction. The latter is holomorphic throughout
the enclosed first-parameter domain. The endpoint-role theorem makes
their normalized differences exponentially small, and Cauchy's formula
therefore compares \(H_N\) with that second-degree construction.
Comparison at the second real seed followed by analytic propagation
gives the corresponding estimate against every first-degree
construction. In particular, the baseline has exponentially small
errors in both entire physical row families, not just at their
intersections.

Write \(X=(\pi-t)/(2\pi)\), \(Y=(\pi-u)/(2\pi)\), and
\(\Psi(X,Y)=\psi(t,u)\). Let \(E_X^\sigma\) and \(E_Y^\tau\)
be the finite one-sided Hermite corrections for the two row families.
Their common array of values, first derivatives and mixed derivatives
defines a tensor correction \(E_{XY}^{\sigma,\tau}\). The representative
\[
 \mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau}
 =e^{N\Psi}\bigl(H_N+E_X^\sigma+E_Y^\tau
                         -E_{XY}^{\sigma,\tau}\bigr)
\]
has both prescribed row families exactly. Indeed, on a first row the
last two corrections have the same value and derivative and cancel;
on a second row the first and tensor corrections cancel. Compatibility
of the mixed original physical derivatives is essential here.

The finite cardinal functions have polynomial bounds on their
designated half-planes. Consequently
\[
 |\mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau}|
 \le \exp\{N\Re\Psi+o(N)\}
\]
on compact subsets of the designated quadrants and sufficiently thin
opposite collars. All fixed derivative orders have buffered estimates.
The first spectral normal is the prescribed \(\widehat G_j\), so a
single window trace is still \(\Phi^\sharp\); its comparison with the
original trace requires the complete subsequent trace stated in the
source theorem. Double selected-window traces retain all original
mixed jets exactly.

The baseline is holomorphic at the simultaneous fold, but this theorem
alone prescribes physical data only in the chosen bulk windows.
Neither evenness of the repaired functions nor removal of exterior
contour sides is asserted. The original spectator multiplies every
interface difference. A local exponential saving does not establish
the required bound for the full graph.

\(\texttt{ace4f667038c494e2690a77496ce32e8bc8538535356b78600e8ad8ced8183d5}\).

## Including the physical rows at the midpoint

The [fold-window theorem](research_positive_product_fold_window_extension.md)
extends the common positive-product construction through the simultaneous
angular midpoint. The proof uses the full original kernel only where
its established three-fifths-disk expansion applies. Outside that
neighborhood it uses the bounds for physical rows; it does not assume
an off-grid bound for the canonical polynomial.

Choose the two seed intervals inside a small disk about completeness.
The normalized baseline and normalized canonical kernel have
subexponential bounds there and exponentially small differences on
the two seed grids. Two dense-grid estimates followed by analytic
propagation give
\[
 H_N(t,u)-e^{-N\psi(t,u)}
                 K_N(-2\cos t,-2\cos u)=O(e^{-cN})
\]
throughout a smaller bidisk, with every fixed angular derivative.
The canonical first spectral normal and the prescribed
\(\widehat G_a\) also have the same physical second-color data.
Their uniform polynomial bounds on this bidisk and a dense-zero
estimate make their normalized difference exponentially small,
uniformly over all nearby double rows.

These comparisons supply the correct baseline errors in every row
near the midpoint. The all-row bounds then propagate those errors
as holomorphic functions of the opposite parameter over the fixed
product chart. The exact two-family Hermite correction can therefore
include a whole mirror window about \(X=1/2\). A reflected angular
index \(j\) uses the original distinct row
\(a(j)=\min(j,N-1-j)\); it is not a new high-degree normal.

The trace multiplicity is separate from this analytic comparison.
With \(D_h(X)=(\pi N)^2\sec^2(\pi NX)\), the closed mirror
window has prefactor \(-\eta/(4\pi^2 i)\). Every double spectral
root has two angular lifts, so their two equal residues give
one original trace term. At odd \(N\), the central residue is
\(-2\pi f(-2)\), and the same prefactor gives exactly \(f(-2)\).
Its angular derivative does not contribute. The optional zero
angular derivative in the interpolant is not an additional
spectral normal.

The real interface, exterior window sides and all original
spectators remain in the exact contour formula. A single window
still gives the sharp trace with \(\widehat G_a\), whose comparison
with the original requires the specified subsequent complete trace.
Double selected-window traces preserve all original mixed data.
No general noncancellation or full-contour estimate follows here.

## Removing the real repair interface on short color windows

The [short spectral-window theorem](research_short_spectral_window_repair.md)
uses a different repair from the preceding one-sided cardinal functions.
It constructs one even holomorphic function with the required estimates
on both angular sides, provided the selected block of consecutive
physical colors is sufficiently short. Shortness is chosen after the
baseline error exponent has been established on a larger fixed interval.

First, the common baseline is exponentially close to the separately
even canonical kernel on the small complete bidisk. Its reflection
defects have subexponential bounds on the symmetric positive product
domain. Analytic propagation makes those defects exponentially small
on any fixed inner compact. Averaging the four reflections therefore
gives an even baseline with the same accuracy, which descends to the
spectral coordinates \(z=-2\cos t,\ w=-2\cos u\).

The quantitative interpolation estimate is explicit. For \(m\)
consecutive distinct physical colors \(c_j\), their actual spacing
satisfies
\[
 |c_j-c_k|\ge\frac{16(j-k)^2}{N^2}.
\]
The resulting product bound includes the factorials
\[
 \prod_{k\ne j}|c_j-c_k|
 \ge(16/N^2)^{m-1}
       \bigl[(j-j_0)!\,(j_0+m-1-j)!\bigr]^2.
\]
Consequently the ordinary confluent Hermite interpolation operator,
with multiplicity two at double roots and one at the odd simple root,
has norm at most
\[
 C N^B\exp\!\left\{C_Km\left(1+\log\frac Nm\right)\right\}
\]
on a fixed complex compact. This bound remains uniform at the midpoint.
When \(m\le\delta N\), its exponential cost is at most
\(C_K\delta(1+|\log\delta|)N\), which tends to zero with
\(\delta\).

Apply this interpolation to the normalized baseline errors in each
endpoint variable, subtracting the common mixed correction once.
Choose both window widths so their combined interpolation cost is
smaller than the previously proved error exponent. The result is one
spectral function \(\mathcal K_{I,J,N}\) with exact physical line
data
\[
 \mathcal K_{I,J,N}(c_j,w)=F_j(w),\qquad
 \partial_z\mathcal K_{I,J,N}(c_j,w)=\widehat G_j(w)
\]
at double rows, and the symmetric second-endpoint identities. Only
the value is prescribed at an odd simple row. On the whole fixed
smaller product compact,
\[
 |\mathcal K_{I,J,N}|\le e^{N\Re\Psi+o(N)},\qquad
 e^{-N\Psi}\mathcal K_{I,J,N}-h_N=O(e^{-c'N}).
\]
These estimates do not require choosing an angular half-plane.

The exact single-window trace is the ordinary closed spectral integral
\[
 \Phi^\sharp_{I,N}(w)=
 \frac{\eta N^2}{2\pi i}
 \oint_{\gamma_I}
       \frac{P(z)\mathcal K_{I,J,N}(z,w)}{P_N(z)}\,dz.
\]
Here \(P\) is the entire original spectator, including its derivative
in the residue calculation. In a mirrored angular contour the upper
and lower halves now use the same function, so their real repair
interface is exactly zero. The sharp-versus-original trace distinction
is unchanged; the specified later complete trace is still needed.

This result does not construct one bounded exact interpolant for a
large union of windows. A finite cover by short cells retains its
exterior sides and the differences between adjacent representatives.
Those differences are exponentially small after normalization, but
their full original spectators and filling phases still require a
joint estimate. No global source coefficient follows from the local
construction alone.

## Transporting boundaries between overlapping color windows

The [overlapping spectral-window theorem](research_overlapping_spectral_window_seam_transport.md)
assigns disjoint color cells to the trace, but repairs each cell on a
slightly larger window. These enlarged windows overlap. For a fixed
finite network of edges admitting the short spectral representatives,
simultaneous replacement preserves every tensor cell trace exactly:
each edge receives its value, either first derivative, or their mixed
derivative at a physical tuple. The ordinary product rule then preserves
all original shared-vertex normals and crossing factors.

If two neighboring choices differ only at vertex \(v\), their bounded
repaired-edge products have difference \(\Delta_N\). At every shared
color \(c_j\), this difference has the original root multiplicity:
\[
 \Delta_N=Q_{v,N}B_{v,N},\qquad
 Q_{v,N}(z)=\prod_{j\in I_v\cap I_v'}(z-c_j)^{\nu_j}.
\]
Here \(\nu_j=2\) at double roots and \(1\) at the odd simple root.
The coefficient is jointly holomorphic. Consequently
\(\Delta_N/P_N\) has no pole at any shared color, even before the
other endpoint variables are traced. Other, unbounded source factors
are kept in the full spectator, not included in the repaired-product
estimate.

On a buffered angular rectangle through the shared real grid, with
\(\Psi_{\rm rep}\) the sum of the represented edge phases,
\[
 \left|e^{-N\Psi_{\rm rep}}
       \frac{\Delta_N(-2\cos t,\mathbf z')}{P_N(-2\cos t)}\right|
 \le e^{-cN-N|\Im t|+o(N)}.
\]
Away from an \(N^{-1}\)-thin real strip this follows directly from
\[
 |P_N(-2\cos t)|\ge
 e^{N|\Im t|}(1-e^{-N|\Im t|})^2.
\]
Inside that strip, the quotient is holomorphic, and a maximum-principle
argument with midpoint vertical sides gives the same bound. Fixed
derivatives cost only powers of \(N\); the simple spectral node at the
fold needs no extra normal.

Multiplying by the entire original spectator gives an exact seam
form. Its contour may move through the shared grid without residues
at those nodes. If its endpoints move as well, the exact identity
retains both endpoint connectors and any residues of other factors.
A joint deformation retains the corresponding additional boundary
faces. This is a transport identity and estimate, not deletion of
the seam integral.

Even spectral representatives also give a simpler original contour.
On a symmetric union of angular cells,
\[
 q_N(t)=\sin t\,W_N(t)\,E_N(t)\,A_N(t)
\]
is odd: the trace kernel, original quadratic/charge carrier and
spectral source are even. Reflection preserves the one-form
\(q_N(t)\,dt\), so the upper mirror integral equals the lower one.
The exact trace therefore uses twice the lower paths, with original
coefficient \(-N^2C_{N,n}/(\pi i)\). This works both for paired
disjoint cells and for a cell containing the fold. The odd center
contributes one value. No ordinary real integral through its poles
is introduced.

The remaining global task is to choose the coupled contour and bound
its actual spectators, endpoint connectors, unmatched rows and
exterior faces at the parent action. The estimate above retains the
unit trace-density decay; it does not establish that global inequality.

## The coherent Fourier estimate and its exact endpoint packet

The [coherent window Fourier theorem](research_coherent_window_fourier_alias_transport.md)
uses the derivative compatibility that was absent from a bound on
arbitrary arrays of physical values and normals. In centered coordinates
\(X_j=(j+1/2)/N\), suppose those normalized errors are exactly
\(d_j=f_N(X_j)\) and \(e_j=f_N'(X_j)\) for one analytic function.
The same function must be controlled on both signed height contours.
Distinct one-sided completions cannot be substituted separately.

Let \(I=[k_0/N,k_1/N]\). Subtract the cubic \(p_N\) matching
\(f_N,f_N'\) at both ends and put \(g_N=f_N-p_N\).
The zero extension of \(g_N\) is continuously differentiable.
Writing
\[
 \widehat g_N(\omega)=\int_I g_N(y)e^{-2\pi i\omega y}\,dy,
\]
the exact normal Fourier combination is
\[
 \sum_{j=k_0}^{k_1-1}
 [g_N'(X_j)-2\pi iN\xi g_N(X_j)]e^{-2\pi iN\xi X_j}
 =
 -2\pi iN^2\sum_{m\ne0}m(-1)^m
                    \widehat g_N(N(\xi-m)).
\]
The \(m=0\) term vanishes algebraically. The endpoint subtraction
gives absolute convergence; it does not discard the four endpoint
data, whose original pairing is retained separately.

For positive and negative aliases, move the same function \(g_N\)
to height \(\sigma H\), \(\sigma=\operatorname{sgn}m\).
The alias sum is then the explicit meromorphic function
\[
 W_{\sigma,N}(y)
 =-\sigma\frac{e^{2\pi i\sigma Ny}}
                 {(1+e^{2\pi i\sigma Ny})^2}.
\]
Its endpoint segments start at integer multiples of \(1/N\),
so their bases are regular. This gives an exact decomposition
of the original Fourier/normal pairing into an interior double
integral and a finite endpoint packet. The latter consists of
the original cubic pairing and the oriented vertical segments
from the two contour deformations. Any crossed poles add their
actual residues.

If \(|f_N|\le e^{-\kappa N+o(N)}\) on a buffered rectangle
containing both height contours, and the actual spectator \(A_N\)
is moved to an admitted contour \(\gamma_\sigma\) with
\(0\le\sigma\Im z\le H\), the interior satisfies
\[
 |\mathfrak B_N|
 \le e^{-\kappa N+o(N)}
 \sum_{\sigma=\pm1}\int_{\gamma_\sigma}
            |A_N(z)|e^{-2\pi N|\Im z|}\,|dz|.
\]
Indeed the frequency integral has kernel
\(L_N(z-y)=\sin(2\pi N(z-y))/(\pi N(z-y))\), and
\[
 |W_{\sigma,N}(y)L_N(z-y)|
 \le\frac{2e^{-2\pi N|\Im z|}}
              {(1-e^{-2\pi NH})^2}.
\]
The original angle is \(t=\pi-2\pi X\); the leading character
is exactly \(e^{i\sigma\pi N}e^{-i\sigma Nt}\).
Together with the unchanged quadratic carrier this is the
original unit-charge filling phase. Thus an admitted parent-phase
bound for that spectator gives the same rate minus \(\kappa\),
without requiring \(\kappa\) to exceed the complete-to-filled
action loss.

The estimate is before the remaining closing functional. The full
endpoint packet, original exterior sides and shared trace normals
remain. Their joint recombination is not bounded here. The short
spectral repair supplies a common two-sided function on each eligible
small cell, but this alone does not prove cancellation of endpoint
packets between different cells.

## Combining the endpoint terms of a finite partition exactly

The [partitioned-window theorem](research_partitioned_window_endpoint_regrouping.md)
places the preceding local formulas in one finite source identity.
Let consecutive midpoint cells \(I_l\) carry scalar normalized
errors \(f_l\), all with the same phase weight and unchanged spectator
\(A_N\). Write \(P_{lr}\) for the normal Fourier data from cell
\(l\) paired with the spectator integral over cell \(r\).
The union pairing is
\[
 P_U=\sum_{l,r}P_{lr},
\]
not just the sum of the diagonal cell pairings.

This change of pairing has an exact source compensation. A cardinal
correction associated to cell \(l\) has zero value and first derivative
at every other cell's centered nodes. Its residue functional on
cell \(r\ne l\) is therefore zero, giving
\[
 \mathcal E_{lr}=\eta\pi^{-2}P_{lr}\qquad(l\ne r).
\]
Here \(\mathcal E_{lr}\) is its actual exterior half-boundary term,
including vertical sides. Subdivision with one common representative
then gives
\[
 \mathcal E_U-\sum_l\mathcal E_{ll}
       =\eta\pi^{-2}\sum_{l\ne r}P_{lr}.
\]
Thus the cross-window pairings are compensated by a recorded change
of exterior terms; they are not discarded.

The endpoint cubic can be eliminated algebraically. Put
\[
 W_{+,N}(y)=-\frac1{4\cos^2(\pi Ny)},\qquad
 W_{-,N}=-W_{+,N}.
\]
The residue theorem on each cell rectangle expresses its exact normal
Fourier combination directly through \(f_l\) on its top, bottom and
vertical sides. Applying this identity to the subtracted cubic cancels
the auxiliary cubic packet from the earlier formula. At a shared cut
\(a_l\), the two signed vertical contributions join into the single
chain \(S_l=[a_l-iH,a_l+iH]\). Its coefficient is
\(\delta_l=f_{l+1}-f_l\).

With \(C(y)=2\cos(2\pi y)\) and
\(L_N(s)=\sin(2\pi Ns)/(\pi Ns)\), the internal packet is exactly
\[
 J_l=2\pi^2iN^3\int_{S_l}
 \frac{\delta_l(y)}{P_N(C(y))}
       \left\{\int_I A_N(z)L_N(z-y)\,dz\right\}dy.
\]
The quotient is holomorphic through the shared physical rows, by
the overlap theorem. The point \(a_l\) is no longer an endpoint of
this combined chain. Its two endpoints are at heights \(\pm H\).
A deformation confined to the actual overlap introduces no shared-row
residue. A larger deformation enclosing nonshared rows must retain
their original residue packet.

The complete decomposition is
\[
 P_U=B_U+O_U+\sum_lJ_l.
\]
The top term \(B_U\) has the earlier unit-charge estimate. The finite
outer packet \(O_U\) contains the two unpaired outer verticals and
the spectator's external endpoint connectors. Those terms and the
internal packets have not acquired the top-term bound.

Let \(\Lambda_N\) be the original remaining joint closing. Because
the \(f_l\) are errors, the full source identity must also retain
the covered baseline trace \(Z_{U,N}^{\rm base}\) and the unmatched
rows \(Z_{O,N}\):
\[
 Z_N=Z_{O,N}+Z_{U,N}^{\rm base}
 +\Lambda_N\!\left[
     \mathcal E_U-\eta\pi^{-2}
                  \left(B_U+O_U+\sum_lJ_l\right)\right].
\]
Consequently the unmatched rows plus outer terms alone are not an
unmatched-row trace; regrouping them carries the top and internal
terms with a plus sign on the other side of this equality. The
original half multiplicity is retained for mirrored source windows.
The theorem supplies exact endpoint bookkeeping, not a global
parent-action estimate or a nonzero coefficient.

## Which mixed window faces can survive the closed neighboring traces

The [higher-face and edge-cover theorem](research_window_higher_faces_and_edge_cover.md)
applies to any fixed finite loopless graph of represented same-index
edges, with repeated edges allowed. All other original factors stay
in a window-independent spectator. It uses the exact line identities
of the short spectral representatives, not an estimate of a closing
functional.

For each vertex let \(D_v\) be the original sum of closed cell
traces. Its exact opening is \(D_v=H_v+I_v\), where \(I_v\)
is the sum of internal window differences and \(H_v\) includes
every other piece, including outer connectors. On fixed product
chains these operators commute. Hence
\[
 Z_{\rm cov}=Z_H+
 \sum_{\varnothing\ne A\subseteq V}(-1)^{|A|+1}
       \left(\prod_{v\in A}I_v\right)
       \left(\prod_{w\notin A}D_w\right)F_N.
\]
This form deliberately leaves the complement of \(A\) closed.

Expand the simultaneous window differences by the exact Boolean
product rule. Every changed edge receives a nonempty subset of
its opened endpoints, and those subsets cover \(A\). If a changed
edge meets a vertex outside \(A\), its value and required first
normal vanish on that unchanged neighboring window as identities
in all other complex variables. Multiplication by the remaining
factors preserves those zero jets. The closed neighboring trace
therefore kills the entire summand, including all product normals.

All surviving changed edges lie inside the induced graph \(G[A]\).
In particular, an isolated vertex of \(G[A]\) forces that whole
face term to vanish. For a single edge the singleton terms vanish,
but the two-vertex corner remains. Its coefficient is exactly
\[
 -e^{N\Psi_e}
   (\mathscr L_{v,i}-\mathscr L_{v,i+1})
   (\mathscr L_{w,j}-\mathscr L_{w,j+1})\mathcal C_e,
\]
where the two \(\mathscr L\)'s are the actual spectral Hermite
operators and \(\mathcal C_e\) carries the compatible mixed
baseline errors. Two-line compatibility does not set this expression
to zero. Thus acyclicity alone does not remove all mixed faces.

If edge \(e\)'s normalized error is at most
\(e^{-\kappa_eN+o(N)}\), either a single or double endpoint
jump costs one factor with that exponent. The surviving changed
edges form an edge cover of \(A\). Consequently their kernel
coefficient, before the remaining spectator and closing, has bound
\[
 e^{N\Re\Psi_{\rm rep}-N\tau_\kappa(A)+o(N)},\qquad
 \tau_\kappa(A)=
 \min_{\substack{E'\subseteq E(G[A])\\\bigcup_{e\in E'}e=A}}
                        \sum_{e\in E'}\kappa_e .
\]
For equal rates \(\kappa\), this is
\(\kappa(|A|-\nu(G[A]))\), where \(\nu\) is the maximum
matching size. A single-edge corner has one error factor, not two.
The number of cells and graph size are fixed, so their finite sums
do not change the exponential rate.

This is a general cancellation and coefficient estimate. It does
not identify \(H_v\) with its top part alone, bound the remaining
closing, or compare the \(\kappa_e\)'s with a geometric filling
loss. Coupled deformations retain their additional boundary faces;
uncovered physical rows and free polynomials are unchanged.

## Physical-row eigenvectors do not give a positive class under composition

The [physical-row signed-turn theorem](research_physical_row_fourier_positivity_under_turns.md)
checks this question in the actual full algebra
\(\mathbb C[Z]/(P_N)\), including its repeated roots. Put
\(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(\kappa=q^{(N-1)^2/2}\),
\(F_j(Z)=K_N(c_j,Z)\), and \(V_n=\kappa^nTR^{-n}T\).
The exact reproducer gives
\[
 TF_j=\frac{P_N(Z)}{\eta N^2(Z-c_j)}.
\]
Multiplication by any polynomial on the right acts by its value
at \(c_j\), modulo the entire relation. Together with the original
turn matrix this proves the ordinary polynomial identity
\[
 V_nF_j=(-1)^{nj}q^{-nj(j+1)}F_j
\]
for every signed integer \(n\), at both parities. It retains
all first-normal data.

Multiplication destroys the proposed positive class. For every
\(N\ge5\), let \(c=2\cos(\pi/N)\). The first two exact Jacobi
steps give
\[
 F_1^2=aF_2+bF_1+d,\qquad
 a=\frac{c^4}{(c^2-1)(c^2-2)}>0,\quad
 b=-\frac4{c^2-2}<0,\quad
 d=\frac1{c^2-1}>0.
\]
The input \(F_1^2(-\zeta-\zeta^{-1})\) has five strictly
positive Laurent coefficients, and its repeated spectral root
is \(4/c>2\). The exact signed turn instead gives
\[
 q^{6n}V_n(F_1^2)
       =aF_2+b(-1)^nq^{4n}F_1+dq^{6n}.
\]
Its leading Laurent coefficient is positive real. The next
coefficient has nonzero imaginary part whenever
\(\sin(4\pi n/N)\ne0\). No common nonzero scalar can make
all coefficients real. In particular either unit turn fails
at every \(N\ge5\); every fixed nonzero power fails for
all sufficiently large levels.

The same quadratic has a nonreal spectral zero, so the
real-root/zero-free class is not preserved either. For fixed
power its roots satisfy \(Z=2+O_n(N^{-2})\).
This last restriction matters: the calculation gives no zeros
on a fixed compact positive-parent chart. It is an exact
two-incidence source calculation, not a complete knot scalar
or a failure of the volume-conjecture lower bound.

## Exact signs in physical-row products and the required derivative rows

The [linearization theorem](research_physical_row_alternating_linearization.md)
uses the original polynomials \(F_j(Z)=K_N(c_j,Z)\), where
\(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)\) and \(0\le j\le J=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\).
For \(j+k\le J\) it proves the ordinary polynomial identity
\[
 F_jF_k=\sum_{\ell=|j-k|}^{j+k}
       (-1)^{j+k-\ell}A_{jk\ell,N}F_\ell,
 \qquad A_{jk\ell,N}>0.
\]
The coefficients have an explicit finite positive recursion. After
the monic normalization \(p_j=(-1)^jH_jF_j\),
\(H_j=S_j^4/S_{2j}\), the proof uses strictly increasing Jacobi
coefficients and the difference
\(p_mp_n-p_{m-1}p_{n+1}\). It proves positivity at every index
in the triangle, including its endpoints.

For the original operator \(V_n=\kappa^nTR^{-n}T\), an odd signed
integer \(n\) gives
\[
 V_n(F_jF_k)=(-1)^{j+k}
    \sum_{\ell=|j-k|}^{j+k}
        A_{jk\ell,N}q^{-n\ell(\ell+1)}F_\ell .
\]
This removes the alternating coefficient signs but retains the
quadratic phases. It is not a noncancellation assertion.

When \(j+k>J\), an expansion using only \(F_0,\ldots,F_J\) is
impossible by ordinary degree; reduction modulo \(P_N\) does not
change this. At each double node the polynomial
\(G_j(Z)=\partial_wK_N(c_j,Z)\) has degree \(N-1-j\).
The \(F_j\)'s and these \(G_j\)'s give a basis of the full algebra,
including both parity cases, and
\[
 V_nG_j=\lambda_{n,j}G_j+
       \kappa^n(R^{-n})'(c_j)F_j,\qquad
 \lambda_{n,j}=(-1)^{nj}q^{-nj(j+1)}.
\]
The derivative is the actual spectral normal of the original
crossing. No off-grid phase is substituted for it.

## The full derivative coefficients and a precise limit of positive norms

The [confluent closing theorem](research_confluent_row_closing_and_positive_quotient.md)
retains the full value/derivative basis \(F_j,G_j\). For a double node,
put \(\beta_j=\eta/(4-c_j^2)\) and
\(\gamma_j=\eta c_j/(4-c_j^2)^2\). The original bilinear closing
has block
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}\phi(F_j^2)&\phi(F_jG_j)\\
                 \phi(F_jG_j)&\phi(G_j^2)\end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}0&\beta_j\\\beta_j&\gamma_j\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Different nodes are orthogonal. The odd simple row has square one.
For \(f=\sum_j(A_jF_j+B_jG_j)\), with its odd simple term included,
the prescribed closing is exactly \(\phi(f)=\beta_0B_0\).
The theorem recovers every coefficient from the values and first
derivatives of \(Tf\), so this does not omit any normal direction.

There is an exact positive seminorm
\[
 \|f\|_{\mathcal Q_N}^2=\sum_j|(Tf)(c_j)|^2,\qquad
 |\phi(f)|\le\|f\|_{\mathcal Q_N},
\]
with closing dual norm one. Every \(V_n=\kappa^nTR^{-n}T\)
is an isometry. Its nullspace is precisely the span of the
double-node value rows \(F_j\). The theorem proves that every
positive semidefinite \(V_1\)-invariant form must kill that same
space; all remaining forms are positive matrices on the quotient,
with blocks restricted to equal crossing phases.

This exact invariance cannot propagate an original multiplication
crossing while controlling the closing on every input. Indeed
\(F_0=1\) is null, whereas \(|\phi(R^{\pm1})|=1\).
Any finite crossing bound would make \(R^{\pm1}\) null as well,
contradicting closing control. This is a source-specific obstruction
to exact universal isometry, not to a lower estimate or approximate
invariance for the particular knot source.

## All-degree products and strictly signed derivative coefficients

The [full product theorem](research_physical_row_full_product_normal_support.md)
extends the calculation to every physical pair \(0\le j,k\le
J=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\), retaining the full \(F/G\) basis. Write
\(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), \(c_\ell=2\cos((2\ell+1)\pi/N)\).
The coefficient of \(G_\ell\), for a double node, is exactly
\[
 B_{jk;\ell}=\eta(4-c_\ell^2)\Gamma_{jk\ell},
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{jk\ell}=\phi_N(F_jF_kF_\ell).
\]
The triple trace is symmetric, strictly positive precisely when
\(j+k+\ell\ge D\), and otherwise zero. The proof uses the existing
positive Newton multiplication table and a finite coefficient reversal;
it supplies explicit factorial sums for every coefficient.
On the first supported boundary,
\[
 \Gamma_{jk\ell}=\frac{N^2}{H_jH_kH_\ell},
 \qquad H_r=\frac{S_r^4}{S_{2r}}.
\]
The odd simple coefficient is \(\Gamma_{jkJ}\), with no artificial
derivative channel.

Every remaining \(F_\ell\) coefficient is also explicit. Besides the
ordinary logarithmic derivatives below index \(\ell\), it retains
the alternating tail
\[
 e_m'(c_\ell)=(-1)^{m-\ell}
   \frac{S_{\ell+m}S_{m-\ell-1}}{s_{2\ell+1}S_m^2},
 \qquad \ell<m\le D-\ell .
\]
These terms cannot be recovered by discarding the repeated roots.
The theorem also proves the corresponding support rule for any
finite canonical product of physical rows, using the actual
zero rule at Newton collisions. It does not give a sign or lower
bound after the prescribed multiplication crossing.

## Uniform size and nonzero amplitude of the positive triple trace

The [triple-row pressure theorem](research_physical_triple_row_pressure.md)
gives a quantitative result for those same original coefficients.
It first rewrites the exact sum symmetrically:
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathbf j}=\frac1N
 \sum_{\substack{0\le r_i\le j_i\\\sum_i r_i\ge D}}
 \frac{\prod_i S_{j_i+r_i}\prod_{i<h}S_{r_i+r_h}}
 {\prod_i S_{j_i-r_i}\prod_i S_{r_i}^3 S_{\sum_i r_i-D}}.
\]
For \(\mathbf x\in[0,1/2]^3\), \(\sum_i x_i\ge1\), let
\(\mathcal G(\mathbf x)\) be the maximum of the explicitly defined
log-sine action in that note over
\(0\le t_i\le x_i,\ \sum_i t_i\ge1\). Uniformly on every
nonzero physical triple,
\[
 \log\Gamma_{\mathbf j}
   =N\mathcal G(\mathbf j/D)+O(\log N).
\]
The lower bound uses one actual supported integer term obtained by
rounding each maximizing coordinate upwards. It applies at support
and fold boundaries as well as in the interior.

The action decomposes into nine ideal-tetrahedron volume functions.
For \(0<x_i<1/2\) and \(\sum_i x_i>1\), its unique maximum is
strict and has negative definite Hessian. Uniformly on compact
subsets of this region, the sharper statement is
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathbf j}
  =N^{-3}\mathcal A(\mathbf j/N)
      e^{N\mathcal G(\mathbf j/N)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad \mathcal A>0.
\]
The amplitude is explicit and analytic. Its normalization retains
the shift \(\sum_i r_i-D=N(\sum_i t_i-1)+1\); omitting this
shift would change the leading coefficient.

These estimates apply directly to \(B_{jk;\ell}\) through its exact
positive-trace formula. They do not estimate the inserted-normal
observable \(\phi_N(G_jF_kF_\ell)\), whose alternating tail remains.
In particular differentiating the continuous degree parameter in
\(\mathcal G\) is not an identification with that original normal.
Nor does the nine-tetrahedron expression identify the action with
the volume of an arbitrarily partially filled knot complement.

## Actual derivatives and cancellation near the midpoint

The [full-normal fold calibration](research_triple_row_fold_full_normal_calibration.md)
compares the original triple trace with a specified polynomial saddle
window. Write \(X_j=(j+1/2)/N\) and \(C(X)=2\cos(2\pi X)\), so that the
midpoint is exactly \(X=1/2\). For a compact set
\[
 K\Subset\{0<x,y<1/2,\ x+y>1/2\},
\]
there is a fixed neighborhood of the closing midpoint and a positive
gap \(\gamma\) on which the same polynomial \(W_{jk,N}\) satisfies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \phi_N(F_jF_kF_\ell)&=W_{jk,N}(c_\ell)
       +O\!\left(N^B e^{N(\mathcal G(X_j,X_k,X_\ell)-\gamma)}\right),\\
 \phi_N(F_jF_kG_\ell)&=W'_{jk,N}(c_\ell)
       +O\!\left(N^B e^{N(\mathcal G(X_j,X_k,X_\ell)-\gamma)}\right).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The second line concerns the original spectral derivative at a double
root. The odd simple root requires only the first line. This theorem
does not assert estimates for derivatives in the two bulk incoming
variables.

The polynomial is an actual restriction of the positive Newton sum to
a fixed interior saddle box. Its holomorphic asymptotic is
\[
 W_{N,B}(C(X_1),C(X_2),C(X_3))
   =N^{-3}\mathcal A_c(\mathbf X)e^{N\mathcal G(\mathbf X)}
      (1+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})),
 \qquad \mathcal A_c>0
\]
on the real parameter neighborhood. Centering the degrees changes the
earlier amplitude by
\(\mathcal A_c=\mathcal A\exp(-\tfrac12\sum_i\partial_{X_i}\mathcal G)\).
The saddle stays strictly inside the feasible polytope even at the
midpoint. At the simultaneous midpoint,
\[
 t_i^*=\frac{\arctan 2}{\pi},\qquad
 \operatorname{Hess}_{\mathbf X}\mathcal G=-4\pi I_3 .
\]
There the same polynomial approximates all eight required mixed first
jets. Its even angular dependence gives a holomorphic spectral
function near \((-2,-2,-2)\), without dividing by a vanishing angular
derivative.

The proof explicitly includes the high Newton indices activated by
a first derivative. Their absolute action is
\[
 \chi(X,t)=\mathcal J(X+t)+\mathcal J(t-X)-2\mathcal J(t),
 \qquad X\le t\le1-X.
\]
As \(X\) tends to \(1/2\), this band forces \(t\) to \(1/2\), where
its action agrees with the positive action on a proper boundary
face. Strict interior maximization provides a uniform gap. This
is the source-specific reason that the omitted normal terms are
small; agreement of the values on a dense grid would not suffice.

The [finite fold-row theorem](research_triple_row_fold_alias_suppression.md)
applies this calibration to the original trace. Put
\(H_{jk,N}=T(F_jF_k)\), \(t_\ell=\pi-2\pi X_\ell\), and
\(M(x,y)=\mathcal G(x,y,1/2)\). For every fixed signed integer \(p\),
there is a small fixed width \(T>0\), a midpoint cutoff
\(T_N=T+O(N^{-1})\), and \(\delta>0\) such that
\[
 \left|
 \eta\!\sum_{\substack{\ell\text{ double}\\0<t_\ell<T_N}}
 \left\{(4-c_\ell^2)(R^pH_{jk,N})'(c_\ell)
                  -c_\ell(R^pH_{jk,N})(c_\ell)\right\}
 +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}(R^pH_{jk,N})(-2)
 \right|
 \le N^{O(1)}e^{N(M(X_j,X_k)-\delta)} .
\]
The crossing power may have either sign or be zero. The constants
are uniform for \((X_j,X_k)\in K\) and both level parities.

To prove it, the exact crossing values and normals are represented by
\[
 \rho_{N,p}(t)=q^{p(N-1)^2/4}e^{ipNt^2/(4\pi)} .
\]
The symmetric angular contour for the calibrated polynomial is
\[
 \frac{\eta N^2}{2\pi i}
 \oint_{\partial([-T_N,T_N]+i[-H,H])}
 \frac{\sin t\,\rho_{N,p}(t)W_{jk,N}(-2\cos t)}
      {\,2-2\eta\cos Nt\,}\,dt .
\]
It includes both lifts of each double node and counts the odd central
value once. On horizontal sides its denominator supplies
\(e^{-NH}\); on vertical midpoint sides it supplies \(e^{-N|h|}\).
The strict real maximum and the sufficiently small fixed width pay
the crossing growth on all four sides. The actual value and normal
errors have their own exponential gap. The proof leaves every row
outside the specified window in the original sum.

The all-eight-jet calibration also gives a strict gap when all three
boundaries are closed over midpoint windows with any fixed signed
crossing powers. Terms with at least one boundary outside those
windows are not covered. Neither theorem proves a nonzero coefficient
for a charged critical point or a lower bound for the complete knot
scalar.

## A single positive coefficient for arbitrarily many value rows

The [positive coefficient theorem](research_physical_products_positive_coefficient_saddle.md)
works for every fixed number \(m\) of physical value rows. The
Jacobi matrix for \(F_j\) has eigenvalues strictly above \(c_0\).
Writing their differences from \(c_0\) as \(r_{j,b}>0\), one has
\[
 F_j(c_0-z)=\prod_{b=1}^j(1+z/r_{j,b}).
\]
List the \(N\) roots \(c_a\) of \(P_N\) with their actual
multiplicities, and put \(d_a=c_0-c_a\ge0\). For
\(s=\sum_i j_i\), \(k=s-(N-1)\), set
\[
 a_{\mathbf j}=\prod_{i,b}r_{j_i,b}^{-1},\qquad
 H(x)=\frac{\prod_{i,b}(1+r_{j_i,b}x)}
                   {\prod_{a=0}^{N-1}(1-d_ax)}.
\]
The original full trace, including its repeated-root data, is exactly
\[
 \phi_N\!\left(\prod_iF_{j_i}\right)
                   =N^2a_{\mathbf j}[x^k]H(x).
\]
This gives another proof of the known positive support rule
\(s\ge N-1\), and a new one-dimensional estimate of its size.

The unique positive saddle radius solves
\[
 k=\sum_{i,b}\frac{\rho r_{j_i,b}}{1+\rho r_{j_i,b}}
                 +\sum_a\frac{\rho d_a}{1-\rho d_a}.
\]
This is the mean of an exact sum of independent Bernoulli and
geometric variables. For each fixed \(m,\varepsilon>0\), uniformly
when \(k\ge\varepsilon N\), the saddle stays in a fixed compact
subinterval of \((0,1/4)\), and its variance \(V_N\) is bounded
above and below by positive multiples of \(N\). Interlacing after
deleting a small fraction of Jacobi rows proves this even when
some input rows reach the midpoint.

Fourier inversion gives
\[
 \phi_N\!\left(\prod_iF_{j_i}\right)
 =\frac{N^2a_{\mathbf j}H(\rho)\rho^{-k}}
         {\sqrt{2\pi V_N}}(1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
The positive geometric factors bound the characteristic function
away from its central arc. Near zero, the odd cubic term integrates
to zero and the remaining Gaussian error is relative \(O(N^{-1})\).
Adjacent coefficients consequently have ratio
\(\rho^{-h}(1+O_h(N^{-1}))\) for every fixed integer \(h\).

For every polynomial \(q\) of bounded degree and bounded coefficients,
this also proves the original observation formula
\[
 \frac{\phi_N(q(C)\prod_iF_{j_i}(C))}
      {\phi_N(\prod_iF_{j_i}(C))}
           =q(c_0-\rho^{-1})+O_q(N^{-1}).
\]
If the displayed polynomial value stays away from zero, its leading
coefficient is nonzero. The theorem does not apply to \(R^p\)
merely because \(p\) is fixed: its canonical degree grows with
\(N\). It also does not replace a boundary derivative row by a
positive value row.

## The pressure selects the original common characteristic

The [common-characteristic theorem](research_triple_row_common_characteristic.md)
connects the three-row pressure to the original Jacobi equations.
For \(0<x_i<1/2\), \(\sum_i x_i>1\), put
\(X_i=\cot(\pi x_i)\). The internal saddle satisfies
\[
 Y_i=\cot(\pi t_i^*)=\sqrt{X_i^2+L},\qquad
 L+\sum_{i<j}\sqrt{X_i^2+L}\sqrt{X_j^2+L}=1.
\]
The scalar equation is strictly increasing in \(L\), with derivative
at least four, and
\[
 0<L\le\frac{1-\sum_{i<j}X_iX_j}{4}\le\frac14.
\]
Its positive square roots specify the original real branch. The
gradient and common characteristic are
\[
 \partial_{x_i}\mathcal G=2\operatorname{arsinh}(X_i/\sqrt L),
 \qquad \zeta=2-\frac4L.
\]

For the ordinary external polynomial
\(\Gamma_q=\phi_C(q(C)\prod_i K_N(w_i,C))\), the exact source identity is
\[
 \mathscr J_{N,w_i}\Gamma_q=\Gamma_{Cq}
 \quad\text{for each }i.
\]
The full kernel forcing vanishes because it is divisible by
\(P_N(C)\) under the original trace. These are polynomial
identities, including all external derivatives.

The nonzero pressure asymptotic controls finitely many neighboring
physical values. Applying the exact recurrence to them proves
\[
 \frac{\phi_N(q(C)F_jF_kF_\ell)}
      {\phi_N(F_jF_kF_\ell)}
    =q(\zeta(\mathbf j/N))+O(N^{-1})
\]
for fixed-degree \(q\), uniformly on strict compact support with
bounded coefficient norm. Thus \(\zeta\) is measured by the actual
source, not inferred only from a formal critical equation. It lies
below \(-14\); it is an asymptotic observation ratio, not an extra
eigenvalue of the finite operator.

## The general row-product pressure and its height Hessian

The [scalar pressure theorem](research_physical_products_scalar_pressure.md)
evaluates the coefficient saddle for every fixed \(m\ge3\). Put
\[
 \Psi_x(w)=\int_0^x
  2\operatorname{arsinh}\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{2-w}}2\cot(\pi s)\right)\,ds.
\]
For \(0\le x_i\le1/2\) with \(\sum_i x_i>1\), the equation
\[
 \sum_i\arcsin\!\left(\tanh(h/2)\sin(\pi x_i)\right)=\pi
\]
has exactly one positive solution. It minimizes
\[
 A_{\mathbf x}(h)=\sum_i\Psi_{x_i}(-2\cosh h)-h.
\]
Its second derivative is strictly positive. The minimum
\(\mathcal G_m(\mathbf x)\) is strictly concave where all \(x_i>0\),
and extends continuously to zero and midpoint coordinates.

Uniformly over original physical tuples with
\(\sum_i j_i-(N-1)\ge\varepsilon N\),
\[
 \log\phi_N\!\left(\prod_i F_{j_i}\right)
        =N\mathcal G_m(\mathbf j/N)+O(\log N).
\]
The finite coefficient height is within \(O(\log N/N)\) of this
height, and the finite tilted variance satisfies
\[
 \frac{V_N}{N}
 =\frac{A_{\mathbf j/N}''(h)}{\tanh^2(h/2)}
                      +O(\log N/N).
\]
The normalization follows from the exact identity
\[
 a_{\mathbf j}H(\rho)\rho^{-k}
  =\frac{\prod_iF_{j_i}(c_0-\rho^{-1})}
          {\rho\,|P_N(c_0-\rho^{-1})|},
 \quad
 |P_N(-2\cosh h)|=e^{Nh}(1+(-1)^Ne^{-Nh})^2.
\]
Thus there is no undetermined additive constant in the rate.
With \(L=\operatorname{sech}^2(h/2)\), exponentiating the
inverse-sine equation gives an algebraic relation in \(L\) and
the boundary exponentials. Its real angle sum must remain
specified; the exponentiated equation alone permits other branches.

## Original mixed normals have the same uncharged pressure

The [full-normal contour theorem](research_physical_products_full_normal_coherent_contour.md)
now estimates the actual derivative rows in that product.
Write
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathbf j,I}
  =\phi_N\!\left(\prod_{i\in I}G_{j_i}
                         \prod_{i\notin I}F_{j_i}\right),
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{\mathbf j}=\phi_N\!\left(\prod_iF_{j_i}\right).
\]
For every fixed \(m,\varepsilon\), on
\(\sum_i j_i-(N-1)\ge\varepsilon N\),
\[
                    |\Gamma_{\mathbf j,I}|
                         \le C N^B\Gamma_{\mathbf j}.
\]
Every physical row is allowed in this upper bound; at the odd
simple node only its value is prescribed. If the differentiated
indices lie in fixed bulk intervals, the stronger result is
\[
 \frac{\Gamma_{\mathbf j,I}}{\Gamma_{\mathbf j}}
  =N^{|I|}
    \left(\prod_{i\in I}g(j_i/N,c_0-\rho^{-1})
                         +O(\log N/N)\right),
\]
\[
 g(x,C)=-
 \frac{2\operatorname{arsinh}(\tfrac12\sqrt{2-C}\cot(\pi x))}
      {4\pi\sin(2\pi x)}<0.
\]
Thus the leading mixed-normal coefficient is nonzero.

This proof keeps the alternating terms together. The original
Jacobi normal identity replaces a derivative row, inside the full
trace, by a polynomial cofactor and a fixed Ward representative.
The latter has the exact upper-minus-lower cut jump
\[
 \widetilde Q_{N,+}(2\cosh h)-\widetilde Q_{N,-}(2\cosh h)
       =\frac{iN}{2\sin(\pi/N)}\tanh(Nh/2).
\]
This is polynomial in \(N\). Cofactors remove finitely many
numerator factors from the positive coefficient product; the
denominator's Fourier decay remains.

The cut is paid explicitly. Its row action \(B_x(h)\) satisfies
\[
 B_x'(h)=\frac1\pi
  \arcsin\!\left(\min\{\coth(h/2)\sin(\pi x),1\}\right)\ge x.
\]
Hence the product cut action is increasing on the relevant support.
At its right endpoint the numerator is bounded by its value at the
negative saddle, whereas the Chebyshev denominator has a fixed
extra height. This proves an exponential gap for the entire cut,
including determinant zeros and the branch point.

On each strict bulk product chart there is also one holomorphic
scalar whose values and all \(2^m\) mixed first physical jets
approximate the original ones with relative error
\(N^{O(1)}e^{-\gamma N}\). Its contour uses the exact scalar
row correction, so there is no normal-interpolation error on
the retained arc. The allowed exponent is
\[
 \gamma<\min(g_{\rm arc},g_{\rm cut})-C\delta^2,
\]
where \(\delta\) is the real chart width. The earlier analytic
normal-connection constant restricts the complex chart thickness
but does not enter this physical error exponent.

The theorem concerns a product before an extra filling crossing.
It neither bounds unsupported rows by a zero value trace nor
continues the scalar to an arbitrary charged critical point.
The crossing's exponentially large cut jump requires its own
coherent contour argument.

## Analytic insertions beyond bounded polynomial degree

The [analytic Hermite insertion theorem](research_analytic_hermite_coupon_trace.md)
removes a degree restriction for a specified class of actual coupons.
Let \(a_N(C)\) be holomorphic on a fixed buffered disk containing
the physical roots and every relevant coefficient circle. Let
\(q_N\) be its degree-\((N-1)\) full Hermite interpolant, with
first derivatives at double roots and one value at the odd root.
Then
\[
 \frac{\phi_N(q_N\prod_iF_{j_i})}{\Gamma_{\mathbf j}}
       =a_N(c_0-\rho^{-1})+O(M_N/N),
 \qquad M_N=\sup|a_N|
\]
on the specified disk. The difference between the interpolant and
the analytic function is divisible by the full \(P_N\), so its
contour contribution is exactly zero.

For \(a_N=e^{b_N}\) with \(L_N=1+\sup|b_N|=o(\sqrt N)\),
the relative error is \(O(L_N^2/N)\). Such observations are nonzero
for sufficiently large \(N\), have the original exponential rate,
and remain in this class under any fixed number of ordinary
canonical products. No closure under the physical turn is asserted.

For a slit or meromorphic representative, the exact formula adds
the cut-bank and endpoint integrals and subtracts the nonphysical
pole residues. These contributions are source terms. The theorem
does not infer that they are small from agreement at the physical
nodes, and it does not apply the slow-exponential estimate to an
actual filling phase.

## A complete crossed trace for physical-row inputs

The [radial contour theorem](research_crossed_physical_products_radial_contour.md)
proves a nonzero asymptotic with the actual crossing retained.
Fix \(m\ge3\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and a signed integer \(|p|\ge4\).
Uniformly over every physical tuple satisfying
\[
              \sum_i j_i-(N-1)\ge\varepsilon N,
\]
the full original scalar
\[
                 Z_{p,N}=\phi_N\!\left(R^p\prod_i F_{j_i}\right)
\]
has a nonzero leading contribution. Zero and midpoint physical
indices are allowed under the stated sum condition. No external
derivative rows are inserted in this theorem.

For \(p\ge4\), set
\[
 S_{\mathbf x}(t)=\sum_i\Psi_{x_i}(-2\cos t),\qquad
 \Phi_{p,\mathbf x}(t)
      =S_{\mathbf x}(t)+\frac{ip t^2}{4\pi}-it.
\]
There is a selected critical point
\(t_p=s_p-ih_p\) with \(0<s_p<2\pi/p\), \(h_p>0\).
Its real action \(M_p=\Re\Phi_{p,\mathbf x}(t_p)\) is positive.
These assertions hold uniformly on the compact physical support.

The contour is constructed explicitly. For \(0\le s\le2\pi/p\),
minimize
\[
 A(s,h)=\Re S_{\mathbf x}(s-ih)+\frac{psh}{2\pi}-h
\]
over \(h\ge0\). The identity
\[
 S'_{\mathbf x}(t)=-\frac1\pi
     \sum_i\operatorname{arsinh}(\sin(\pi x_i)\tan(t/2))
\]
shows that \(A_{hh}>0\) throughout this strip. The resulting
minimum \(b(s)=A(s,h(s))\) satisfies
\[
 b''=-A_{hh}-A_{sh}^2/A_{hh}<0,\qquad
 b'(0)>0,\quad b'(2\pi/p)<0.
\]
Its unique maximum is the selected saddle. This is why the
threshold four appears: \(2\pi/p\le\pi/2\) gives the direct
convexity argument at every height.

The exact full-grid lens, with all closing derivatives retained,
represents this scalar by a lower arc from \(-\pi\) to \(\pi\).
Reflecting the radial height to the negative half subtracts
\(psh(s)/\pi\) from its real action. The real outer intervals
already have a strict gap; a small fixed depth preserves it.
At both endpoints the actual Jacobi root product bounds the
rows directly near \(C=2\). The full denominator
\[
 W_N(t)=\frac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-(-1)^{N-1}e^{-iNt})^2}
\]
is retained there. Away from the endpoints, its nonleading
aliases have fixed exponential decay. Consequently every
part outside the saddle neighborhood is strictly smaller
than the selected contribution.

The leading term uses the actual finite row logarithms:
\[
 \Phi_{p,N}(t)=\frac1N\sum_i\log F_{j_i,N}(-2\cos t)
                         +\frac{ip t^2}{4\pi}-it.
\]
Its critical point \(t_{p,N}\) differs from \(t_p(\mathbf j/N)\)
by \(O(\log N/N)\). With the original crossing carrier and
the specified Gaussian orientation,
\[
 Z_{p,N}=
 \frac{iN^{3/2}}{\pi}q^{p(N-1)^2/4}\sin(t_{p,N})
 \sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{-\Phi_{p,N}''(t_{p,N})}}\,
 e^{N\Phi_{p,N}(t_{p,N})}(1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
The square root has positive real part, and the coefficient is
uniformly nonzero. In particular
\[
                 \log|Z_{p,N}|=NM_p(\mathbf j/N)+O(\log N).
\]
Negative powers follow by exact conjugation. Both level parities
and the odd simple value are included in the original lens.

This establishes the contribution of a specified positive critical
point to the complete one-vertex trace. The next result handles
external first derivatives. Neither result identifies this action
with a knot-complement volume or controls subsequent turns and
closing of the remaining boundary labels. Those requirements are
essential for the general short-partial-filling theorem.
No conclusion for \(|p|<4\) is inferred.

## Boundary derivatives of the crossed trace

The [mixed-normal extension](research_crossed_physical_products_full_normal_packet.md)
keeps the hypotheses of the crossed trace theorem and allows any
subset of its physical value inputs to be differentiated. Write
\[
 Z_{p,N,I}=
 \phi_N\!\left(R^p\prod_{i\in I}G_{j_i}
                         \prod_{i\notin I}F_{j_i}\right),
 \qquad
 G_j(C)=\left.\partial_w K_N(w,C)\right|_{w=c_j}.
\]
Only repeated physical nodes carry such a prescribed derivative;
the simple node at odd levels still carries a value only.
Uniformly over the same positive support margin,
\[
                  |Z_{p,N,I}|\le C N^B |Z_{p,N}|.
\]
The original closing derivatives, including those of the crossing
factor, remain in this formula.

If the differentiated indices \(j_i/N\) stay in compact subintervals
of \((0,1/2)\), their leading multiplier is explicit:
\[
 \frac{Z_{p,N,I}}{Z_{p,N}}
 =N^{|I|}
 \left(\prod_{i\in I}g(j_i/N,C_{p,N})
                         +O(\log N/N)\right),
 \qquad C_{p,N}=-2\cos t_{p,N},
\]
where
\[
 g(x,C)=-
 \frac{2\operatorname{arsinh}
       \bigl(\tfrac12\sqrt{2-C}\cot(\pi x)\bigr)}
      {4\pi\sin(2\pi x)}.
\]
The selected spectral point stays in the half-plane \(\Re C<2\).
On the selected branch, the numerator has positive real part and
the denominator is positive for real \(0<x<1/2\). Thus the factors
are uniformly nonzero on the specified compact ranges.

The proof first substitutes the exact Ward--Jacobi representatives
of the normal rows inside the original trace. They extend the
same angular contour identity because their angular functions are
even and holomorphic on its interior. Away from the endpoints,
normal factors cost only powers of \(N\). Near the endpoints,
each derivative of a Jacobi determinant is bounded as a sum of
cofactors, without dividing by a determinant that might vanish.
This preserves every strict gap in the value proof. At the
remaining saddle, the known scalar normal connection gives the
displayed leading multiplier.

There is also one holomorphic function of all boundary variables,
locally on every compact subset of
\(\{\mathbf x\in(0,1/2)^m:\sum_i x_i>1\}\), whose physical mixed
first derivatives approximate all \(Z_{p,N,I}\) with error
\[
                     C N^B e^{-\gamma N}|Z_{p,N}|.
\]
It is defined by integrating the exact scalar row interpolation
over a fixed short saddle arc, with the crossing Gaussian and the
complete Fourier denominator retained. Every physical value and
first derivative agrees exactly on that arc. The error comes
only from its omitted complement.

This provides the boundary data for a possible next contraction.
It does not prove that the next contraction preserves the leading
term: its own phase, endpoints and closing derivatives still
require estimates. In particular, a local relative error need
not remain relatively small after an exponentially cancelling sum.

## Removing the positive-coefficient support condition

The [bounded minimax theorem](research_crossed_physical_products_bounded_minimax.md)
extends the actual crossed scalar, its mixed first normals, and
its local scalar interpolation to every fixed \(m\ge1\) and
\[
             |p|\ge4,\qquad \sum_i j_i\ge\delta N,
             \qquad \delta>0.
\]
The uncrossed trace may be exactly zero in this range. The proof
does not divide by it or use it to select the crossed saddle.

For \(p\ge4\), let \(a=2\pi/p\), \(H=1+2m/p\), and minimize
\[
 A(s,h)=\Re S_{\mathbf x}(s-ih)+psh/(2\pi)-h
\]
over \(0\le h\le H\), for \(0\le s\le a\). Here
\(S_{\mathbf x}(t)=\sum_i\Psi_{x_i}(-2\cos t)\) is the
original row action. On this rectangle \(A_{hh}>0\) and
\(A_{ss}=-A_{hh}<0\), uniformly when \(\sum x_i\ge\delta\).
The minimizing height is unique and Lipschitz. Its reduced
function \(b_H(s)=\min_{[0,H]}A(s,h)\) is strongly concave,
including where the height reaches the constraint.

At height \(H\), the inequality
\[
 |\tan((s-ih)/2)|\le1
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 A_s(s,H)\ge \frac{p}{2\pi}
                 +\frac{m}{\pi}(1-\operatorname{arsinh}1)>0
\]
prevents a maximum of \(b_H\) from lying on that boundary.
The signs \(b_H'(0)>0>b_H'(a)\) place its maximum strictly
between the two vertical sides. The lower height boundary is
also excluded there because \(A_h(s,0)=ps/(2\pi)-1<0\).
Thus the constrained optimization produces an actual interior
critical point of the original complex phase.

Its action is uniformly positive because
\[
                   M_p>b_H(a)=S_{\mathbf x}(a)>0.
\]
The old contour estimates apply to the full original trace on
this new bounded graph. They do not require the uncrossed support
condition. The same is true of the determinant-cofactor estimates
for every allowed mixed normal and the exact interpolation of
physical first derivatives on a retained saddle arc.

This removes the missing macroscopic row range for powers of
magnitude at least four. It does not give a nonzero asymptotic
when the entire degree sum is \(o(N)\), or establish a lower bound
after a second trace.

## Crossing powers two and three

The [smaller-power theorem](research_crossed_physical_products_two_three_radial_contour.md)
establishes the same complete scalar and boundary-derivative
conclusions for \(|p|=2,3\), retaining
\[
                   \sum_i j_i-(N-1)\ge\varepsilon N.
\]
Its new ingredient is a barrier that keeps the radial minimum
inside the region where the second height derivative is positive.
Global convexity at every height would be false here.

Write \(k_i=\sin(\pi x_i)\) and
\(r_k(t)=\operatorname{arsinh}(k\tan(t/2))\). Directly on the
original branches,
\[
 \operatorname{sgn}\Re r_k'(s-ih)
   =\operatorname{sgn}\bigl(1+(1-k^2)\cos s\cosh h\bigr).
\]
For \(\pi/2<s<\pi\), set
\[
 h_B(s)=-\log(-\cos s),\qquad
 \beta_k(s,h)=-\Im r_k(s-ih).
\]
Every nonzero \(\beta_k\) increases strictly up to \(h_B\), and
\[
 \sum_i\beta_{k_i}(s,h_B)
       \ge(\pi-s)\sum_i x_i>\pi-s\ge\pi-ps/2.
\]
Above the barrier each term stays at least as large as its
barrier value. Hence the radial equation
\(\sum_i\beta_{k_i}=\pi-ps/2\) has exactly one root below
the barrier. Its reduced action is strictly concave and selects
one saddle with nonzero Hessian.

At power two the radial graph reaches \(s=\pi\). The bound
\(h(s)<h_B(s)\to0\) gives \(b(\pi)=0\), while \(b(0)\) has a
uniform positive lower bound. This keeps the maximum away from
the endpoint. The actual contour is given a small positive
minimum depth; sufficiently close to each endpoint it has
constant depth. Jacobi determinant bounds then control the
entire endpoint pieces and the original vertical connectors.
The full Fourier denominator remains in the calculation.

The saddle stays in \(\Re C<2\), so the original finite-row
Gaussian coefficient and the scalar normal connection apply.
Both signs and both level parities are included. Low-support
inputs at these two powers, the unit powers, and subsequent
shared traces remain outside this result.

## Continuing an actual crossed block to the next boundary window

The [crossed-block continuation theorem](research_crossed_block_regular_saddle_source_window.md)
starts from the original polynomial
\[
 H_{p,N}(w)=\phi_{N,C}\!\left(
 R(C)^pK_N(w,C)\prod_{i=2}^mF_{j_i}(C)\right).
\]
Here \(\phi_N\) is the original closing functional, \(R^p\) is the
crossing factor, \(K_N\) is the original edge kernel, and the other
factors are literal physical value rows. The seed colors must satisfy
one of the two crossed-scalar ranges above. A holomorphic family of
nondegenerate child critical points is supplied separately, with
uniform positive geometry and negative imaginary part.

On its fixed continuation domain the proof constructs
\[
 B_N(w)=N^{3/2}q^{p(N-1)^2/4}a_N(w)e^{N\Lambda_N(w)}
                         (1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad 0<c\le |a_N|\le C.
\]
The phase \(\Lambda_N\) comes from the actual finite integrand and
converges, with buffered derivatives, to the selected geometric action.
At real physical seed colors, \(B_N\) approximates \(H_{p,N}\) and
its required first derivative with an exponentially small relative
error. The derivative calculation retains both moving-endpoint terms.
For a sufficiently short consecutive window \(I_N\), spectral Hermite
interpolation corrects that error exactly without changing the leading
coefficient. At an odd simple endpoint only the value is prescribed.

Consequently the original partial closing, with any original parent
factor \(P\), is exactly
\[
 \phi_{N,I}(P H_{p,N})=
 \frac{\eta N^2}{2\pi i}\oint_{\gamma_I}
       \frac{P(w)\mathcal B_{I,N}(w)}{P_N(w)}\,dw.
\]
All sides of the closed contour are included. This is equality of the
prescribed finite closing data, not equality with the original
polynomial off the physical nodes. In particular it supplies neither
a lower estimate for the complete next closing nor automatic
cancellation of differences between neighboring window representatives.
