## Removing a large endpoint term before estimating the trace

The [factorial wire calculation](research_factorial_wire_wrap_obstruction.md)
shows why bounding each untraced edge integral by its geometric
action cannot work throughout the positive geometric domain.
On an explicit open family, the short interval beyond the last
integer wire index contributes at a strictly larger exponential
rate. This occurs at both level parities.

The same calculation gives an exact remedy inside the original
trace. Write the wire index in this interval as \(x=1-s/N\).
For \(s\) in any fixed compact subinterval of \((1/2,1)\),
the large term is a multiple of the full spectral polynomial
\(P_N\). Modulo that polynomial the halfwire can be replaced by
\((-1)^{N-1}B_N(-s/N,t)\). The replacement and all its fixed
angular derivatives are bounded by powers of \(N\), even on
angular rectangles enclosing the entire physical grid.

Because the difference contains the full polynomial, the
replacement preserves values and first derivatives at repeated
roots, as well as the odd-level simple root. It can be made at
any finite collection of traced ends while keeping every other
factor and the original closing functional. Free boundary
polynomials are retained. Thus this particular exponential excess
can be removed before taking absolute values.

The remaining factors can still be large or cancel each other.
The result is neither a bound at the volume rate for the whole
source nor a lower bound for its geometric term. The angular
rectangle statement does not extend through \(s=1\).

Polynomial bounds on the physical values, first derivatives and
ordinary boundary polynomial over the entire high-index half of
the circle were already proved in the
[high-index boundary theorem](research_high_index_free_boundary_hermite_bound.md).
They retain the costs of nonzero wire height and complex boundary
angles. The new [endpoint calculation](research_wrap_endpoint_full_hermite_bound.md)
sharpens the bound on the real microscopic cap and identifies its
limit exactly. The shifted class tends to
\((-1)^{N-1}e_{N-1}\). Its values vanish at every physical root,
but its derivative at the outer double root is nonzero. With a
remaining factor \(A\), its prescribed closing is
\((-1)^{N-1}A(c_0)\), where \(c_0=2\cos(\pi/N)\).
Thus the endpoint cannot be discarded merely because
all its values vanish. This clarifies the normalization and does
not enlarge the previously proved domain of polynomial control.

## Exact evolution of the entire charged source

The [charge heat reduction](research_entire_charged_source_heat_reduction.md)
gives an exact scalar evolution for arbitrary original compiled
components, before any asymptotic branch is selected. Let
\(Z_N(\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\chi)\) be the original full trace with
crossing powers \(n_v\) and the specified charge coupons. Remove
only its known scalar carriers
\(C_{N,n}=\exp(\pi i n(N-1)^2/(4N))\), writing the result as
\(\widetilde Z_N\). Then
\[
 \partial_{n_v}\widetilde Z_N
       =-\frac{i}{4\pi N}\partial_{\chi_v}^2\widetilde Z_N.
\]
This identity includes the first derivatives at every repeated
physical root. The entire charge observation is faithful: in one
variable it has dimension \(N\), with a pair of functions
\(\cos(N\tau_a(1-\chi))\) and
\((1-\chi)\sin(N\tau_a(1-\chi))\) for each double root, and the
additional constant at the odd simple root. The second function
retains the normal direction that value-only interpolation loses.

For any real \(n\ne0\), the exact solution is
\[
 \widetilde Z_N(n,\chi)
 =\sqrt{\frac{N}{|n|}}\int_{\mathbb R}
      e^{-\pi Nr^2/|n|}
      Z_N\!\left(0,\chi+e^{-i\,\operatorname{sgn}(n)\pi/4}r\right)\,dr.
\]
The formula applies independently at every selected variable and
commutes with all ordinary free-boundary derivatives. Its initial
datum is the entire zero-power charged source, with the original
closing and every attached factor. For each fixed \(N\) the
Gaussian integral converges absolutely. Its charge lines can be
translated through any finite prescribed point, since the initial
function is entire and has only exponential-linear growth at
infinity. No physical-grid residue or factorial pole is omitted.

On a supplied regular classical branch, the stationary charge is
\(y_v=\chi_v-n_vt_v/(2\pi)\). Substitution recovers the original
quadratic crossing action exactly. The corresponding Hessian
determinant is the ratio of the original filled and zero-power
period Jacobians, including mixed signs and zero powers.
Thus this representation also retains the correct local Gaussian
density.

This is a different exact representation of the full problem.
The zero-power initial function has many coherent branches and
exact alias identities; one cannot insert just a formal geometric
term in the integral. A controlled expansion on a suitable charge
contour and a bound for its complement remain necessary. The
reduction does not prove noncancellation or a new filling family.

## A sharper bound and the cancellation it leaves unresolved

The [physical pressure theorem](research_charged_source_physical_pressure.md)
improves the absolute bound for a fixed same-index circle tree with
complete outside angles. If \(W(\mathbf s)\) is the sum of its real
edge actions, define
\[
 \mathcal P(\mathbf b)=
 \max_{\mathbf s\in[-\pi,\pi]^I}
       \{W(\mathbf s)+\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf s\}.
\]
The actual charged source, including every repeated-root derivative,
obeys
\[
 |Z_N(\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\chi)|
 \le C N^a\prod_v(1+|\chi_v|)
        e^{N\mathcal P(\operatorname{Im}\boldsymbol\chi)}
\]
uniformly for bounded real crossing powers. The positive sum of
the corresponding physical kernel values has exponential rate
\(\mathcal P\). This does not assert that the signed source has
that rate.

At a positive zero-power geometric point, let
\(\mathbf t=\mathbf s+i\mathbf h\), let \(\mathbf g\) be its
imaginary incidence returns, and let its induced charge be
\(\mathbf y=\mathbf A+i\mathbf B\). Write \(S_0\) for its selected
critical action and \(\mathcal E\) for the convex square energy.
The excess of the bound is exactly
\[
 \mathcal P(\mathbf B)-\Re S_0(\mathbf y)
 =
 \frac{\mathcal E(\mathbf s,\mathbf g)
              -\mathcal E(\mathbf s,\mathbf0)}{\pi}
 +\mathcal P(\mathbf B)-W(\mathbf s)-\mathbf B\cdot\mathbf s.
\]
Both terms are nonnegative. The first is strictly positive if
any imaginary angle is nonzero. Thus the positive physical
partition genuinely grows faster than the desired geometric
term at these complex targets. Improving polynomial prefactors
in an absolute-value estimate cannot remove that exponential
excess.

The same bound gives an explicit estimate for the complement of
a chosen region in the exact Gaussian evolution. The negative
Gaussian quadratic term controls sufficiently remote charge
values; the note states the precise inequality needed for a
strict exponential gap. This improves tail estimates once a
nonzero local expansion is known. It does not establish that
expansion at additional charges or prove arbitrary-short-filling
noncancellation.

## Continuing the original source from small positive charge

The [local heat propagation theorem](research_charged_source_local_heat_propagation.md)
now gives a quantitative way to continue an actual nonzero source
expansion through a small signed change of a crossing power.
Suppose the entire, carrier-removed initial source has
\[
 f_N(z)=N^\alpha e^{NS(z)}
              \bigl(a_0(z)+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})\bigr),
 \qquad a_0(z)\ne0,
\]
on a fixed complex charge disc. Suppose also that its whole
function obeys a bound of the form
\[
 |f_N(y)|\le e^{o(N)}(1+|y|)^p
                         e^{N(C+\pi|\Im y|)}.
\]
The note proves such a finite exponential bound directly for the
fixed same-index graph sources, including every physical first
normal and both level parities.

For a sufficiently small real power increment \(\delta\), the exact
Gaussian integral gives the actual expansion at
\[
 \chi=\Phi_\delta(z)=z+\frac{i\delta}{2\pi}S'(z).
\]
Its phase and leading coefficient are
\[
 S_\delta(\chi)=S(z)+\frac{i\delta}{4\pi}S'(z)^2,
 \qquad
 a_\delta(\chi)=
 \frac{a_0(z)}{\sqrt{1+i\delta S''(z)/(2\pi)}}\ne0.
\]
The square root is continued from one at zero increment.
The proof bounds the full exterior of the local integration
segment exponentially below this contribution. In particular,
noncancellation here follows from an estimate of the actual
integral, rather than an assumed coefficient for a formal saddle.
The original scalar carrier is restored exactly.

The same note justifies a fixed complex neighborhood for the
existing small-charge initializer. It uses the exact entire coupon
identity and the strict gaps for all mixed contour terms, aliases
and removed physical rows. Agreement on the physical charge
lattice alone is not used for this extension.

The domain restriction remains explicit. From a disc of radius
\(R\), reserving a margin \(\rho\) gives the output domain
\(\Phi_\delta(D_{R-\rho})\); the allowed step is bounded in terms
of \(\rho^2\), the global envelope and the local phase derivatives.
Successive steps retain the same initial angular labels
\(t=iS'(z)\). For a target with charge one, power \(n\), and
angle \(t^*=s-iH\), \(H>0\), its initial charge at a real base
power \(b\) must be
\[
 y_b=1-\frac{(n-b)t^*}{2\pi}.
\]
This point is generally complex. The proved initial neighborhood
must actually contain it; subdividing the power change does not
create new initial angular labels. The note's cumulative step
bound applies only to its stated conservative nested-disc
estimate, since characteristic images may expand or shear.
Thus this is a local nonzero source theorem, with global
short-filling coverage still open.

The [radial compactness theorem](research_radial_charge_compactness_and_corners.md)

provides a strictly feasible angle assignment at every
\(0\le\chi\le1\), with a common distance from the square boundaries.
This is a feasible comparison, not a scaled geometric solution.

Subtracting a small amount from one incidence at each selected vertex
and using the supporting inequality for the convex energy gives a
uniform bound on \(\sum_v H_v\), where \(t_v=s_v-iH_v\).
The positive incidence pairings then bound every real return and
every square-energy gradient. Thus the original tetrahedron shapes
stay in a fixed modulus annulus: they cannot tend to zero or infinity.
The closed minimizing angle assignment depends continuously on
\(\chi\), even where its positive geometric interpretation fails.

There is also a uniform lower height bound on every interval
\(\chi_0\le\chi\le1\), \(\chi_0>0\), wherever the positive solution
exists. A zero-height limit would force the same endpoint degeneration
at every vertex of its component. It either contradicts a complete
outside angle or makes every square of an isolated component attain
its maximal boundary energy. Replacing that component by the scaled
unit assignment strictly lowers its energy, contradicting minimality.
Consequently, for some \(h_0>0\),
\[
 H_v\ge h_0,\qquad |\sin t_v|\ge\sinh h_0,\qquad
 |\sin(t_v/2)|,\ |\cos(t_v/2)|\ge\sinh(h_0/2).
\]
The corresponding local observation factors therefore cannot vanish
along such a positive-charge approach.

What remains geometrically is a finite corner. If a square reaches
\((A,y)=(\varepsilon_A\pi/4,\varepsilon_y\pi/4)\), its limiting
signed gradient coordinates \(U=\varepsilon_A E_A\),
\(V=\varepsilon_y E_y\) must satisfy
\[
 U,V>0,\qquad \sinh(2U)\sinh(2V)=1,
\]
together with all original matching and period equations.
The full corner subdifferential allows a weak inequality instead;
its strict cases cannot be substituted for limits of actual positive
solutions. We have not excluded the equality case, or proved that
the positive-charge set connects the small-charge interval to one.
These bounds also require the supplied positive unit solution and
do not establish geometric coverage for arbitrary hyperbolic short
partial fillings.

The [full-grid lens identity](research_full_grid_lens_source_continuation.md)
is an exact result about the original finite quantum source, independent
of that geometric existence question. Its trace can be integrated along
any lower angular arc from \(-\pi\) to \(\pi\), with all original
physical rows, derivative terms and Fourier aliases retained. The
endpoint integrand is regular and vanishes there; no separate vertical
current or removed outer-row sum is needed. For an ordinary polynomial
spectator \(A\), its formula is
\[
 \phi_N(R^n\mathcal C_{N,\chi}A)
 =-\frac{N^2C_{N,n}}{\pi i}
   \int_\Gamma
    \sin t\,A(-2\cos t)e^{inNt^2/(4\pi)}
    \frac{e^{-iNt}\cos(N(1-\chi)t)}
         {(1-(-1)^{N-1}e^{-iNt})^2}\,dt ,
\]
where \(C_{N,n}=e^{\pi i n(N-1)^2/(4N)}\) and
\(\mathcal C_{N,\chi}\) is the canonical coupon with the stated
physical values and first derivatives. The identity holds at both
parities and is entire in \(\chi\). Reflection \(t\mapsto-t\),
rather than an unproved periodicity of the coupon or Gaussian,
produces the formula.

Applying it at every selected vertex gives an exact joint contour
for the complete compiled source, with the original polynomial
edge kernels and untraced boundary variables. Compact interior
deformations with each endpoint face fixed preserve this integral.
The existing small-charge proof also extends to real continuous
coupons on the same small box: its bounds require evenness, the
physical cosine bounds and the full alias formula, all of which
remain valid.

The [joint factorial version](research_joint_factorial_lens_relative_source.md)
then restores every paired Newton index as a period integral.
It works for both the original identity and turn kernels, arbitrary
fixed signed crossing powers, loops and repeated edges. All free
spectral endpoints retain their entire ordinary polynomials.
The angular endpoints are moved to
\(\pm a_N\), \(a_N=\pi-\pi/(2N)\), which still enclose the full
physical grid. The wire real parts lie in
\([-1/(2N),1-1/(2N)]\). The direct and reversed factorial
representatives are simultaneously holomorphic on this product
domain at any fixed finite heights.

There is an explicit reason that the factorial expression and the
finite Fourier polynomial expression give the same whole integral.
Their difference at a traced vertex is divisible by the original
spectral polynomial
\[
 P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad
 P_N(-2\cos t)\,
 \frac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-(-1)^{N-1}e^{-iNt})^2}=(-1)^N.
\]
After this exact cancellation the correction is odd and holomorphic
in that angular variable. Its primitive, starting at \(-a_N\),
also vanishes at \(a_N\). Telescoping the vertex replacements
therefore gives
\[
                 \Omega_{\rm factorial}-\Omega_{\rm Fourier}
                                      =d\Theta ,
\]
where the pullback of \(\Theta\) vanishes on every specified angular
endpoint face and every fixed wire-coordinate face. The statement
retains the first derivatives at double spectral roots, including
the angular ramification of the odd-level simple root.

Consequently compact joint angular-and-wire deformations with those
coordinate faces fixed preserve the original finite source, for
either representative. This permits work on the joint factorial
phase without first replacing an entire finite edge kernel by a
single geometric exponential. This fixed-face theorem alone does
not permit movement of the wire seam faces or deletion of the
relative primitive on the artificial boundary of a local patch.
The moving-seam theorem below retains the additional currents needed
for the former operation.

The remaining analytic step is a bound on the connecting part of
this actual joint cycle and a nonzero net geometric contribution.
The known local descending contour does not provide that bound.
Likewise, the geometric gap for specified Ward deletion currents
does not automatically bound an arbitrary connecting chain.

## Exact transport when the wire cuts move with the angles

The [moving-seam theorem](research_moving_wire_seam_source_descent.md)
extends the exact joint representation to wire contours whose
heights depend on the angular variables. It applies to the same
original compiled networks, with both kernel orientations, signed
powers and all untraced boundary polynomials retained. It does not
prove an exponential estimate for the transported integral.

Write \(\tau_e\) for translation of the continued index \(x_e\)
by one. The finite Fourier polynomial form is periodic under
this translation because every wire has exactly two halfwire
factors. For the factorial form, use its already proved primitive
\(\Omega_{\rm fac}-\Omega_{\rm car}=d\Theta\), and set
\[
 J_e=\tau_e^*\Theta-\Theta.
\]
These are specified differential forms made from the original
angular primitives. They obey the exact identities
\[
 \tau_e^*\Omega_{\rm fac}-\Omega_{\rm fac}=dJ_e,\qquad
 (\tau_f^*-1)J_e=(\tau_e^*-1)J_f.
\]
The second identity cancels the alternating defect at intersections
of two cuts. No additional higher-corner correction is required.

Let \(C\) be the joint chain cut along its wire circles, with
opposite faces paired by these translations and angular endpoint
coordinates fixed at \(\pm a_N\). Orient each lower wire face
\(F_e\) so that its paired contribution to the boundary is
\(\tau_e F_e-F_e\). Then
\[
 \int_C\Omega_{\rm fac}-\sum_e\int_{F_e}J_e
                              =\int_C\Omega_{\rm car}.
\]
For an admitted homotopy from the original product chain, multiplying
this expression by the original prefactor
\(N^{|E|}\prod_v[-N^2C_{N,n_v}/(\pi i)]\) gives the exact finite
source. This establishes equality coefficientwise in the entire
free boundary polynomial, including its derivatives.

There are nonconstant moving cuts inside the known holomorphic
domain. One may write
\[
 x_e=-\frac1{2N}+r_e+iH_e(\mathbf r,\mathbf s),
 \qquad 0\le r_e\le1,
\]
where \(\mathbf s\) parametrizes the angular contours and the bounded
smooth real functions \(H_e\) agree across all paired wire faces.
Interpolating their heights from constants keeps the real wire
coordinates in the original strip and gives an admitted homotopy.
The seam correction is generally nonzero because its pullback now
contains \(dx_e=i\,dH_e\).

A more restrictive symmetry can make the integrated corrections
zero. If the seam embeddings are holomorphic and even in every
angular variable on the required symmetric domains, and the angular
chains are full product lenses, the pullback of each primitive
current is odd and holomorphic in the angle whose trace kernel has
been canceled. Its integral is zero.

The permitted perturbations can also have fixed size as the level
varies. On the angular rectangle
\(|\Re t_v|<\pi,\ |\Im t_v|<T\), choose
\(h_e>T/(2\pi)+\delta\). For bounded holomorphic functions \(f_e\)
that are even in every angular variable, the embeddings
\[
 x_e=-\frac1{2N}+r_e+ih_e+\varepsilon f_e(\mathbf t),
 \qquad |\varepsilon|\sup_e\|f_e\|_\infty<\delta/2
\]
are admissible for every \(N\ge2\), with the same nonzero
\(\varepsilon\). Each factorial argument stays at imaginary
distance greater than \(N\delta/2\) from the real axis; the signs
reverse for reflected halfwires. The original canonical factorial
is holomorphic and nonzero on both nonreal half-planes. These
bounds also hold while an angular primitive is integrated with
the wire variables frozen. Thus the exact symmetry argument
applies on a domain of fixed size, including all paired wire
faces. This establishes no magnitude estimate and does not
assert that a local geometric wire contour extends to this
entire symmetry class.

The transport is finite because the primitive is explicit and
the translations commute, not because the analytic deck action is
nilpotent. In fact the exact halfwire period law gives
\[
 (\tau^*-\eta)^k B_N
   =P_N(-2\cos t)^k
     \left(\frac{(-1)^N}{4\sin^2(\pi Nx)}\right)^k B_N,
 \qquad \eta=(-1)^{N-1},
\]
which is not zero as an off-spectrum meromorphic function.
Removing a trace kernel in a primitive term also retains its
vertex and all its other incidence factors. It is not the scalar
graph deletion estimated by the earlier Bregman comparison.

Thus the next analytic comparison must include the actual seam
integrals, or establish a globally admissible symmetry that cancels
them. The local geometric Morse neighborhood and the convex boundary
gap do not by themselves estimate the remaining joint chain.
No new filling family or finite-exception conclusion is adopted here.

## An exact contour through a given positive geometric point

The [product-domain and wire-contour theorem](research_positive_wire_product_contour.md)
removes a specific continuation problem for the original same-index
network. Fix any positive edge configuration with traced angles
\(\Im t_v^*<0\). No restriction on the number of vertices or on the
signed powers is imposed. The theorem assumes this configuration;
it does not construct a positive solution for every short filling.

The stationary wire is determined by
\[
 a_v=\tan(t_v/2),\qquad
 q_{vw}^2=1+a_v^2+a_w^2,\qquad
 \cot(\pi x_{vw}^*)=q_{vw}.
\]
Independent real contractions of the endpoint tangents preserve
positive edge geometry. This permits a product of symmetric angular
domains containing both the entire real intervals \((-\pi,\pi)\)
and the chosen complex angles. On this product the discriminants
avoid the nonpositive real axis, so \(q_{vw}\) has positive real
part and \(0<\Re x_{vw}^*<1/2\). The domains are chosen independently
of \(N\), but narrow near the angular endpoints. A rectangle of
fixed depth would contain a simple square-root branch point for all
sufficiently large \(N\); the narrower domains avoid it.

The exact reciprocal-factorial divisor theorem supplies the next
step. Both orientations of the original halfwire are holomorphic
throughout
\[
 -\frac1{2N}\le\Re x\le1-\frac1{2N},
 \qquad |\Re t|<\pi,
\]
at arbitrary finite imaginary heights. Negative factorial arguments
can give zeros, but introduce no pole in this domain.
For each angle tuple, replace its wire interval by the two segments
from its fixed left endpoint to \(x_e^*(\mathbf t)\) and then to
its fixed right endpoint. A homotopy within this strip and Cauchy's
theorem preserve the original integral exactly. Full lower angular
lenses can pass through the specified angles. All original trace
normals, signed powers and free boundary polynomials are retained.

One can also insert a coherently oriented real Morse segment
\[
 F_e(X_e(\xi;\mathbf t);\mathbf t)
       =F_e(x_e^*(\mathbf t);\mathbf t)-\xi^2/2
\]
between two explicit connectors. The wire endpoints stay fixed, so
this construction has no wire-seam correction. The radius over the
full lenses may depend on \(N\); a separate compact neighborhood of
the target has a fixed phase-Morse radius.

Thus a representative of the whole original source can pass through
the positive stationary point with the local descending directions.
What remains is a bound on the connectors and the other angular
regions, together with the actual amplitude through the retained
factorial factors. Passing through the point does not establish
that its contribution survives their coherent sum.

## The periodic inverse-phase probe does not supply a lower bound

The [exact probe calculation](research_periodic_even_probe_trace_cancellation.md)
tests the proposed removal of the leading phase on the high-wire domain.
Let \(F_{\rm ev}\) be the sum of the original half-plane factorial
phases and signed quadratic Gaussians, before the linear trace phase.
There is an explicit wire character \(\zeta_N\), bounded independently
of \(N\) on fixed compact tubes, for which
\[
 p_N=\zeta_N e^{-NF_{\rm ev}}\prod_v2\cos(Nt_v)
\]
is exactly periodic in each wire and even in every angle. For a closed
fully traced network \(\zeta_N=1\). The factorial and cardinal formulas
for the period with this inserted probe agree exactly, including the
specified even moving contours.

For a closed graph with \(e\) wires and \(v>0\) traced vertices, the
absolute integral with its original normalization obeys
\[
 |\mathfrak c_N|\int |p_N\Omega_{\rm fac}|
       \le C N^{2v-e}.
\]
Nevertheless the corresponding signed observation obeys the stronger
upper bound
\[
 |\mathcal O_N|\le C N^{2v-e}e^{-\kappa vN},
 \qquad \kappa>0.
\]
This is an exact cancellation mechanism in the original full-Hermite
trace. The identity
\[
 2\cos(Nt)W_N(t)=1+2(-1)^{N-1}W_N(t)
\]
annihilates every angular term missing its trace kernel. The remaining
normalized amplitudes are exponentially close to \(2\pi\)-periodic.
On the full trace rectangle, horizontal sides are exponentially
small and paired vertical sides contain only that period defect.
The proof retains every derivative contribution at repeated spectral
nodes and the odd-level simple node.

This inserted observation is not the unweighted invariant. The
calculation shows why a polynomial absolute bound for this particular
periodic probe cannot certify the required nonzero contribution.
It supplies neither an upper nor a lower volume-rate estimate for
the unweighted source.

## What the first corner replacement would have to change

The [original edge-star calculation](research_regular_corner_original_edge_stars.md)
now follows the actual face maps at a regular corner with ordered shape
\(b=B>0,\ b\ne1\), while the neighboring disk page remains positive.
The base-edge star has four tetrahedra. Its link vertices, after
normalizing that edge to \((0,\infty)\), are
\[
 1,\quad b,\quad L=bD,\quad d,
 \qquad
 d=-B' \text{ at the pure seam},\quad d=-D' \text{ at the odd seam}.
\]
The primes denote shapes of the actual neighboring page. The distinction
between these two ordered seams follows from their three-point face maps.

If this star and the old apex-diagonal star have only their central
tetrahedron in common, their union is a seven-tetrahedron ball with eight
distinct developed vertices and twelve boundary triangles. Its developed
boundary is nevertheless not embedded at the corner: two of its boundary
edges are crossing diagonals of the same ideal quadrilateral. This
prevents an embedded positive replacement with exactly that developed
boundary. Changing only the diagonal inside the single original
octahedron also fails, because two of its prescribed boundary triangles
overlap along a zero-angle edge.

These statements specify why the two proposed small repairs do not
suffice. They neither forbid a larger replacement nor establish a new
filling case. A larger construction must change the relevant boundary
decomposition and retain the original peripheral curves; it cannot be
justified by counting four face occurrences without tracking which
tetrahedra meet each edge.

## Comparing the exact Newton formulas with the geometric phase

The [local spectral comparison](research_newton_spectral_legendre_adapters.md)
now proves the change of variables for the actual multiplication and
both signed crossing matrices. It matches their critical actions,
nonzero second derivatives in the eliminated variable, and leading
Gaussian densities. The multiplication formula holds on its whole
strict support, including high indices. At the multiplication point
where the angular coordinate has a zero derivative, the spectral
coordinate remains regular. This last fact concerns a multiplication
coefficient; it does not remove a degeneration of the final trace.

The signed crossing comparison needs a specific Fourier character.
Its spectral critical action differs from the recorded factorial
action by \(-2\pi i\sigma x\), where \(\sigma=\pm1\) is the crossing
sign and \(Nx\) is the integer output index. After multiplication by
\(N\), this difference exponentiates to one on every original summation
index. Off that integer grid it changes
the stationary equation, so the character must accompany any contour
argument. The proof also retains the order-one crossing scalar and
the offset \(-1\) in the complementary index \(N-1-r\).

There is an exact check at the closing operation. For the original
Newton basis and \(P_N(c)=2T_N(c/2)+2\),
\[
 e_r(c)e_{N-1-r}(c)
   =\frac{(-1)^N P_N(c)}{N^2(c_r-c)}.
\]
This is a polynomial identity after canceling the displayed factor;
it retains multiplicities at repeated roots. Together with the exact
residue formula for \(\phi_N\), it recovers both the primitive trace
phase \(-it\) and its leading density. Thus the comparison respects
the prescribed closure as well as the local matrices.

For a specified regular factorization at each selected vertex, these
identities compare the entire Newton critical point with the original
geometric critical point. The proof introduces one spectral variable
per local matrix. Internal Newton indices then force adjacent spectral
variables to agree. The elimination pairs each internal index with a
spectral difference; eliminating the indices alone would be invalid,
because that part of the Hessian is zero. The paired block is
nondegenerate. What remains is precisely the original angular action,
with its crossing constants and primitive trace charges.

This gives a local equivalence of critical points, not a new
short-filling source theorem. Three requirements remain: a suitable
regular factorization for every short component under consideration;
a nonzero coefficient of the resulting local contribution in the
original finite cycle; and control of the rest of the contraction.
The comparison does not carry the entire previously constructed
inverse-period contour to Newton coordinates by stationary
substitution: away from its center, that contour does not satisfy
the equations used for the substitution. The frozen long-filling
theorem and the currently proved knot families are unchanged.

## Positive geometry excludes algebraic singularities of proper prefixes

The [proper-prefix theorem](research_positive_primitive_prefix_regularity.md)
settles the algebraic part of the regular-factorization question above.
Suppose a selected vertex has a positive primitive geometric solution.
Write its angle as \(t\), its incident meridian increments as \(r_e\),
and its signed power as \(n\), so that
\[
                    \sum_e r_e-\frac{i n t}{2}=-\pi i.
\]
Comparison with the positive edge obtained by setting this endpoint
angle to zero gives \(\Re(r_e\overline t)>0\) for every incidence.
The full equation then implies \(\Im t<0\). For every nonempty proper
subset \(A\) of the incident factors, and every real allocated power
\(n_A\), its partial return
\[
 R_A=\sum_{e\in A}r_e-\frac{i n_A t}{2}
 \quad\hbox{satisfies}\quad
             0<\Re(R_A\overline t)<-\pi\Im t.
\]
The power term contributes zero to this real pairing. Consequently
all such returns avoid the values that make a Newton clock zero or
infinite, make its label integral, or cause a spectral-node collision.
The same inequality
excludes every factorial sine divisor at a multiplication gate.
For either sign of a single crossing, equality of its two label
exponentials would force \(e^{-i\sigma t}=1\), contradicting
\(\Im t<0\).

For an integer physical power and degree at least two, leave one
incident factor for the final complementary pairing. Any binary
multiplication of the other factors, followed by the signed crossing
layers, then has algebraically regular intermediate labels and
nonzero spectral fiber Hessians. No separate search for a favorable
ordering is needed for this conclusion. The degree-one endpoint is
outside the argument.

The qualification about asymptotic domains remains necessary. A
nonvanishing factorial sine does not put its argument in the original
factorial strip. The chamber calculation below now supplies the local
analytic expression outside that strip, retaining its Fourier factors
and continued logarithms. The prefix theorem itself supplies neither
positive geometry for every hyperbolic partial filling nor a coefficient
in the original cycle.

## Endpoint corrections preserve the full boundary norm

The [endpoint-current unit theorem](research_endpoint_matching_boundary_unit.md)
gives a separate finite noncancellation result. Insert the specified
one-step Ward currents on any vertex subset of a fixed circle tree,
retaining every shared boundary variable. At every level \(N\ge3\),
their exact joint matching polynomial \(\mathcal E_{S,N}\) is
nonzero at every physical boundary assignment, provided none of the
even current powers is zero. A zero even power gives the zero current
itself, so that exception is essential.

After extracting constant even-current factors and one common sign,
the polynomial is the determinant of a matrix with positive diagonal
Hermitian part. The actual Ward-coupon values give a lower bound
\(4\cos(\pi/N)\ge2\) for every entry of that diagonal, independently
of the signed powers. This proves nonvanishing before any exterior
contour estimate.

The conclusion retains the repeated roots. In the full tensor product
of the physical boundary algebras, \(\mathcal E_{S,N}\) is a unit,
and for \(b\) boundary variables its inverse satisfies
\[
             \|\mathcal E_{S,N}^{-1}\|_{\mathcal J,B}
                         \le C_{G,S}N^{2b}.
\]
Here the norm records every physical value and every mixed first
derivative required at double roots. The constant is uniform in the
current powers. For fixed powers the forward multiplier also has
polynomial norm, so multiplying a boundary state by this correction
preserves its exponential growth rate in this norm.

This does not prove noncancellation after closing the boundary. The
prescribed exterior functional can annihilate a nonzero boundary
state, even after multiplication by a unit. The unit theorem also
does not replace an arbitrary contour remainder by the specified Ward
currents, or give a zero-free inverse throughout a complex contour
window. These two new results therefore remove algebraic problems
inside the proposed argument while leaving the global scalar
contribution to be proved.

## Exact factorial formulas beyond the original strip

The [factorial chamber theorem](research_newton_factorial_chamber_atlas.md)
now describes every algebraically regular multiplication and signed
crossing near its specified labels. The earlier half-plane theorem
already supplies uniform asymptotics at every nonreal argument,
without restricting its real part. A real noninteger argument needs
an additional exact factor.

Write \(k<\Re\xi<k+1\), where \(k\) is an integer, and retain the
actual fixed index offset \(a\). For either indicated continuation
side \(\tau=\pm1\), the canonical factorial has the exact expression
\[
 G_N(N\xi+a)=
 N^{1/2}e^{NJ_\tau(\xi)+(a+1/2)J_\tau'(\xi)}
 \bigl(1-e^{\tau2\pi i(N\xi+a)}\bigr)^k
 U_N(\xi,a),
 \qquad U_N=1+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1}).
\]
The remainder is holomorphic and nonzero on a fixed local chart.
All zeros or poles of the displayed Fourier factor remain present.
This follows from the exact \(N\)-step factorial relation and the
existing strip estimate; it introduces no new interpolation of the
finite source.

The product of these factors also has a useful general property.
For finitely many nonconstant real-affine factorial arguments, choose
a common imaginary direction and expand each factor on the side
where its exponential has modulus less than one. Every nonconstant
frequency then has positive pairing with that direction. Consequently
the constant Fourier coefficient of the product is exactly one,
including when reciprocal factors occur or the affine arguments
are linearly dependent. A form that becomes constant after wire
identifications remains an explicit scalar and is not covered by
this conclusion.

The specified geometric action must still retain its original
continuation. If it differs from this chamber's action by
\(2\pi i(\lambda\cdot z+\gamma)\), the relevant wall coefficient is
the coefficient at frequency \(\lambda\). It cannot be renamed the
constant coefficient. The theorem neither computes that general
coefficient nor shows that the original finite residue cycle
contains the corresponding contribution. It removes a local
analytic-description problem, not the global cancellation problem.

In using this observation, the original lattice kernel must accompany
the wall factors. Already on a strict signed-crossing triangle all
factorial arguments lie in their original strip, so the wall
multiplier is \(1\). Nevertheless the proved spectral comparison
retains the character \(-2\pi i\sigma x\). That character belongs
to the lattice Fourier lift, and the crossing still has its nonzero
local Gaussian coefficient. Thus absence of a frequency in the wall
multiplier alone is not a vanishing test for the original geometric
contribution. Any general coefficient criterion must retain both
sources of Fourier characters.

The [positive-star construction](research_positive_star_real_factorial_wall.md)
shows why the real-chamber factors cannot be excluded using positivity
alone. For every fixed central integer power \(n\ge5\), and every
sufficiently large fixed degree \(d\), it constructs positive original
edge blocks with identical prescribed outside angles. Their central
returns satisfy the literal primitive equation. At the corresponding
two-leaf multiplication, \(x+y-z\) is real and belongs to \((-1,0)\);
all six other factorial arguments have positive imaginary part.
The proof is an exact positive-edge construction followed by a
real implicit-function argument. The choices are fixed before
the quantum level tends to infinity.

Every binary parenthesization of the identical leaves contains this
two-leaf multiplication when the resolution reserves one leaf for
closure and places all crossings after its products. Thus
reassociation alone does not remove the factor in that resolution.
The example prescribes noncomplete outside angles; it is not a
constructed knot exterior or a complete global filling. It also
does not exclude a different placement of the crossings. Its
conclusion is exactly that positive primitive local geometry does
not imply the original factorial-strip inequalities.

## The exact correction needed when inverting a boundary current

The [inverse-current calculation](research_endpoint_current_inverse_transport.md)
explains how the previously proved boundary unit behaves under the
actual closing operation. Its polynomial Hermite inverse gives an
exact identity in the finite algebra. Applying the Ward shift to a
product with that inverse retains an explicit commutator; the shift
does not obey a multiplication rule that would make this scalar
transport.

The analytic representative supplies a further exact check. For a
singleton odd current with one outside incidence, that representative
has a simple zero inside the lower physical angular window, at
distance of order \(N^{-2}\) from its real boundary. The proof uses
the fixed-argument gamma-product expansion and a simple zero of a
digamma expression. It works for either sign of the fixed odd power.
This is a zero of the analytic representative away from the physical
nodes, so it is consistent with the finite-algebra unit theorem.

Replacing the polynomial inverse by its analytic reciprocal alone
introduces a pole. The exact difference between those two
representatives has the opposite residue. After the original trace
normalization, the individual pole coefficient tends to a nonzero
constant, multiplied by the actual exterior polynomial evaluated at
that pole. Thus its contribution cannot be discarded solely because
the finite inverse has polynomial norm. Keeping both terms cancels
the extra pole exactly. A contour argument that retains this
correction remains possible; a reciprocal-only argument is not
justified by the boundary-unit theorem.

## One choice of logarithms for every proper composition

The [global proper-return phase theorem](research_global_proper_return_phases.md)
now removes the remaining ambiguity in continuing the local action
through the positive primitive domain. Its conclusion holds for
arbitrary degree and signed integer crossing powers.

Write \(H=-\Im t>0\). The earlier prefix theorem puts every proper
return in
\[
                 0<\Re(R\overline t)<\pi H,
                 \qquad |\Re t|<\pi .
\]
There is a useful explicit description of this domain:
\[
                   R=-\pi i u+itv,\qquad
                   0<u<1,\quad v\in\mathbb R.
\]
It is contractible, as is the domain for two returns whose sum remains
proper. At a vertex of degree \(d\) and total power \(n\), the primitive
equation becomes
\[
 r_e=-\pi i u_e+itv_e,\qquad
 u_e>0,\quad \sum_eu_e=1,\quad \sum_ev_e=n/2.
\]
Allocating a crossing power changes only the corresponding real
\(v\)-coordinate. Thus all proper intermediate returns remain in
the same domain.

On these domains the exact prefix formulas have no zero or pole,
and neither do the seven multiplication sine factors or the three
crossing sine factors. Contractibility allows one to fix their
logarithms globally. The proof calibrates them against the original
strict real multiplication and both signed crossing formulas, including
the additive constants. In particular, it constructs a single value
phase \(\mathcal B(t,R)\) with
\[
 \mathcal B(t,-\pi i-R)=it-\mathcal B(t,R).
\]
The multiplication and crossing phases then cancel at every internal
connection. Every permitted proper resolution gives exactly
\[
 \sum_{e=1}^{d}\mathcal B(t,r_e)
       +\frac{int^2}{4\pi}-it+\frac{i\pi n}{4},
\]
with the original crossing Fourier characters retained. Reordering
the multiplication or redistributing the signed crossing layers
does not change this marked action.

This supplies a general phase comparison rather than a list of
particular short components. It does not establish the coefficient
of that action in the original scalar. It also does not transport
the existing inverse-period contour: away from its center that
contour has return sum \(\xi-\pi i\), whereas the final complementary
identity above uses the primitive sum \(-\pi i\).
Degree-one traces remain outside this proper-subproduct chart.

## What a local Fourier coefficient can and cannot certify

The [marked-mode kernel calculation](research_marked_mode_lattice_kernel_gauge.md)
now combines the exact sampling kernels with the factorial chamber
factors. It applies on the actual allowed lattice support, including
nonrectangular supports, and keeps the subsequent original closing
functional.

For an unscaled integer coordinate \(Z\), every kernel
\[
            K_m(Z)=
              \frac{2\pi i\,e^{2\pi imZ}}{e^{2\pi iZ}-1},
              \qquad m\in\mathbb Z,
\]
has residue one at every integer. The difference \(K_m-K_0\)
is entire. Replacing the kernels on the original small product
circles therefore leaves the finite source exactly unchanged.
The statement uses holomorphy near each allowed lattice state;
it requires no extension to a bounding rectangle.

After choosing a fixed common side for the factorial arguments and
retained coordinates, the Fourier expansions have frequencies in a
pointed cone. One can choose the integers \(m_j\) so that any
specified integral geometric frequency is their first joint
frequency. Its coefficient, multiplied by the factorial wall factors,
is explicitly nonzero: only the first term of each kernel and the
constant term of each wall factor can contribute to it.

But changing just one \(m_j\) by the appropriate unit step makes
that very same frequency absent, while preserving the exact finite
source. This proves a limitation rather than a scalar lower bound:
nonvanishing of a local Fourier coefficient depends on the kernel
representation. The invariant question is whether the complete
original integration cycle retains the geometric contribution after
all its pieces are assembled. Entire kernel differences have zero
total original residue; their contributions on individual deformed
pieces need not be zero or small.

The proof also records the correction required for derivative
residues. Multiplying a double-pole kernel by an integer character
alone changes its first-normal residue. Differentiating the new
simple kernel instead supplies the exact lower-order correction and
preserves every required jet. Ordinary wire sampling followed by the
unchanged original closing avoids that extra modification.

Under the additional literal integer-affine and integer-offset
hypotheses, normalized wall-and-kernel Fourier coefficients are finite
signed integer sums independent of the level. A nonzero one has
absolute value at least one. This observation concerns those local
factors, not the analytic remainder or the final integrated invariant.

## A general geometric gap for the split deletion terms

The [ambient convex comparison](research_split_current_convex_action_gap.md)
removes the same-charge feasibility restriction discussed in the next
section. Assume that the fixed short component has a positive solution
of its original primitive filling equations, with the prescribed
outside angles. For every nonzero elementary current in a specified
even-factor implementation, every admitted deleted-forest angle action
with nonzero integer charges is strictly below the original geometric
action. This is a classical action comparison; it does not assume that
the entire quantum deleted source has already been bounded by those
actions. Write \(S\) for the selected filled vertices and \(n_v\)
for their original total crossing powers.

The new point is to compare energies on the full angle body before
imposing the filling rows. If \(z_0\) is the original positive solution,
subtract the supporting affine function of the energy there:
\[
 D_0(z)=\mathcal E(z)-\mathcal E(z_0)
                         -d\mathcal E(z_0)(z-z_0).
\]
Strict convexity and compactness give a positive minimum
\(\delta_0\) of this remainder on the boundary. The original period
equations give \(H_v=-\Im t_v^0>0\) and the exact identity
\[
 \mathcal E(z)-\mathcal E(z_0)
      =D_0(z)+\pi\sum_{v\in S} H_v(c_v-1)
\]
when the comparison assignment has charge rows \(-\pi c_v\).
The comparison charges need not be charges of the quantum source.
They enter only this supporting-plane identity.

For a nonempty deleted set \(C\subseteq S\), put each deleted real angle at
\(\operatorname{sgn}(n_v)\pi\) and set both incidences of every
deleted edge to zero. These are always admissible weak angle data.
The deleted row then has \(c_v=|n_v|/2\). Negative surviving charge
rows can be reflected without changing the energy or the outside
data. Write \(M_G\) for the original calibrated real action and
\(M_{\rm del}\) for the deleted assignment's angle-energy value.
The exact square-boundary energy gives
\[
 M_G-M_{\rm del}\ \ge\
 \frac{\delta_0}{\pi}
 +\sum_{v\in C}H_v\left(\frac{|n_v|}{2}-1\right)
 +\sum_{w\in S\setminus C}H_w(|c'_w|-1)>0
\]
for every admitted deleted assignment with \(|n_v|\ge2\) on \(C\)
and \(|c'_w|\ge1\) on the surviving selected vertices. Isolated
surviving rows remain imposed. If the deleted assignment set is
empty, the theorem assigns it neither a classical action nor a
quantum estimate.

There is an exact choice of Ward factorization which covers every
nonzero elementary deletion current by this inequality. For odd
total \(n_v\), retain the auxiliary half factor
\(\epsilon_v^*=\operatorname{sgn}(n_v)\); for even \(n_v\), use zero.
Then \(m_v^*=n_v-\epsilon_v^*\) is even. Currents at
\(n_v=0,\pm1\) vanish exactly, and every remaining deleted power
has \(|n_v|\ge2\). This factors the same original operator
\(R^{n_v}\); it changes neither the physical marking
\(\eta_v\) nor the surgery relation \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\).
The exact current is still the bounded scalar prefactor times the
unchanged deleted source.

The gap is uniform on compact families of positive solutions, hence
under sufficiently small changes of the outside angles. This is the
uniformity needed near complete outside angles when the remaining
cusps are subsequently filled with long slopes. The theorem requires
the positive original chart and does not supply it for every
hyperbolic short partial filling.

The remaining analytic task is now more specific. For this choice
of elementary currents, the positive deleted geometric actions
already have a strict gap. One must bound the whole deleted source,
including contributions not represented by those positive angle
assignments, and prove that the actual contour deformation introduces
only controlled terms. The nonzero geometric coefficient in the
original closed source is still unproved in general.

## When a deleted assignment preserves the original charge rows

The [endpoint-face criterion](research_endpoint_current_angle_face.md)
characterizes the stronger requirement that a deleted assignment
extend with all original unit-charge rows unchanged. The preceding
ambient comparison avoids needing this requirement for its chosen
split currents. This earlier calculation concerns the simultaneous one-step
Ward current, whose exact formula deletes a set of vertices and leaves
specified factors on the remaining graph. It does not identify every
contour remainder with that current.

Let \(C\) be the nonempty set of deleted vertices, \(n_v\) the original
signed crossing power at \(v\), and \(s_w=\Re t_w\) a surviving real
angle. Write \(d_C(v)\) for the number of edges from \(v\) to vertices
outside \(C\). The deleted angle assignment extends to the original
closed angle polytope, with each deleted angle at one of its spectral
endpoints \(s_v=\pm\pi\), if and only if
\[
 \bigl||n_v|-2\bigr|
   +\sum_{\substack{e=\{v,w\}\\w\notin C}}\frac{|s_w|}{\pi}
       \le d_C(v)
                    \qquad(v\in C).
\]
The sum includes edges to prescribed outside vertices. Every surviving
primitive filling equation must already hold, including at isolated
surviving vertices. If no such deleted assignment exists, the comparison
has no input.

The reason for this condition is elementary. An angle at \(\pm\pi\)
forces the incidence variable at the opposite end of each adjacent
edge to be zero. At the deleted end of an edge to \(w\), the remaining
incidence variable can range between
\(-(\pi-|s_w|)/2\) and \((\pi-|s_w|)/2\). Their sum must still satisfy
the deleted vertex's original filling equation. Adding these intervals
gives exactly the displayed inequality. Edges with both ends in \(C\)
have zero incidence variables at both ends and supply no capacity.

There is also an exact energy calculation. The energy of either square
factor of a deleted edge is constant along the square boundary and equals
\(G_{\rm Cat}/2\), where \(G_{\rm Cat}\) is Catalan's constant. Thus
each deleted edge contributes \(\pi M_\infty\) to the original energy,
where \(M_\infty=4G_{\rm Cat}/\pi\). The prescribed outside linear term
does not change: its restored incidences are zero.

Consequently the calibrated deleted energy value is exactly a boundary
value of the full problem. If the full problem has a positive solution,
its strict interior minimum gives
\[
 \mathcal M_{G\setminus C}(z')
       \le M_G-\Delta_G/\pi<M_G,
\]
where \(\Delta_G>0\) is the minimum boundary energy minus the interior
minimum energy of the original polytope. This comparison holds for
every compatible deleted angle assignment, not just a stationary one.
For a positive stationary deleted assignment, the value on the left
is its calibrated classical action.

To turn this into a quantum estimate, the deleted source must still
have a proved contour expansion and bounds on its complementary
contributions. Under those hypotheses the earlier grouped-current
formula retains the deleted exponential rate, with a nonzero leading
factor. The inequality then supplies the missing strict comparison
for that contribution. The angle calculation itself does not prove
those contour hypotheses or the survival of the full geometric term.

The feasibility test is substantive: if
\(|n_v|>d_C(v)+2\), the endpoint realization is impossible, even
though positive original solutions and nonzero current polynomials
can exist. Failure of the test is not a counterexample to a quantum
gap; it means that this particular convex-boundary argument cannot
establish it.

There is a separate caution about grouping contour terms. The
[exact logarithmic transport identity](research_gaussian_logarithmic_contour_transport.md#5-many-steps-leave-only-end-strips)
gives, for an arbitrary compiled exterior \(A\),
\[
 E_{n,N}(A)=2\{1-(-1)^n\}\,\phi_N(f_nA).
\]
Here \(E_{n,N}\) is the current from a full logarithmic turn,
not the one-step deleted current above. For odd \(n\) it is four
times the original source. Applying this identity at several vertices
preserves all remaining contractions. Thus an induction which declares
every translated current smaller solely because it is called a boundary
term would be circular. An even Gaussian factorization, with the half
crossing retained in its spectator, removes this particular full-turn
identity; it still requires estimates for its actual spectator and
the remaining deformed contours.

## Keeping the marked half twist separate simplifies the exact currents

The [even-twist source reduction](research_even_twist_ward_source_reduction.md)
now supplies the precise alternative mentioned above. Write the original
power as \(n=m+\epsilon\), with \(m\) even and \(\epsilon\) the retained
marked half crossing. In the filling convention this is
\(m=-2p\), \(\epsilon\in\{-1,0,1\}\). The Ward operator acts on the
even factor; the half crossing remains in the original spectator.

This gives an exact current before any asymptotic estimate. Set
\(\rho=2i\sin(\pi/N)\), \(c_0=2\cos(\pi/N)\), and retain the original
crossing scalar \(\kappa\). For an arbitrary exterior polynomial \(A\),
the current is
\[
                 \kappa^n(-1)^N mN\rho\,A(c_0).
\]
It is a value evaluation, so on a circle tree all edges incident to
that vertex evaluate to one. For any set \(C\) of such currents,
the result is exactly
\[
 \mathcal J^{\mathrm{even}}_{C,N}
   =\left(\prod_{v\in C}\kappa^{n_v}(-1)^N m_vN\rho\right)
                   Z_{G\setminus C,N}.
\]
Every surviving factor and the prescribed closure remain unchanged.
The coefficient is bounded independently of the level for fixed
powers; it vanishes if one of the \(m_v\)'s is zero. This implementation
needs no derivative matching expansion. It also has zero full-turn
current.

The half crossing has a canonical holomorphic exponential representative
on \(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\), with the same physical values
and first derivatives as the original polynomial. This representative
has no zeros. It therefore gives an exact analytic conjugation of the
finite Ward operator on a common chart. Its exponential contributes the
missing \(\epsilon\) to the action: the geometric filling equation
still contains the original total power \(n\). In particular, the
endpoint-face criterion in the preceding section must use \(n\),
not \(m\).

The note computes the correction at the edge of the logarithmic
window as well. Continuing a Gaussian without respecting the canonical
spectral sheet changes the finite operator by an explicit map supported
at \(c_0\), depending on both \(A(c_0)\) and \(A'(c_0)\). Thus the
analytic representative is legitimate on the stated charts, but
changing its sheet during a global deformation requires that correction.
The split operator also has a second characteristic branch; the proof
identifies the desired total-\(n\) branch and does not discard the other.

This is a simplification of the general source calculation. If a deleted
source has a proved upper bound, its split current inherits it directly
from the exact scalar identity. The preceding convex-boundary theorem
then gives a strict gap whenever its feasibility criterion holds.
The remaining task is to construct the original global deformation
with all its actual boundary terms controlled and its geometric
contribution nonzero. Neither of these new notes supplies that theorem.

## First-order cyclic transport with the original closing retained

The [first-order transport theorem](research_first_order_gaussian_jet_transport.md)
gives a concrete cyclic descent calculation for each even filling factor.
Introduce the eigenvalue coordinate \(w\), with \(z=w+w^{-1}\), and retain
the doubled roots:
\[
 \mathcal B_N=\mathbb C[w,w^{-1}]/((w^N+1)^2),\qquad
 \delta=w^N+1,\qquad \delta^2=0.
\]
The original Casimir algebra is exactly the subalgebra fixed by
\(w\mapsto w^{-1}\). At odd levels the fixed point \(w=-1\) has
only an invariant value; its extra logarithmic derivative is
anti-invariant. This recovers the original simple node rather than
introducing an extra physical derivative there.

Set \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\) and \(D=N-1\). Let \(U\) substitute \(q^2w\)
for \(w\), and let \(g_m\) be the normalized original Gaussian of
even power \(m\). Its first-order
equation is
\[
       (U-q^mw^m)g_m=m\delta p_D,
\]
where \(p_D\) is the idempotent at the last node of the chosen
logarithmic window. The right side has zero values and records the
derivative mismatch at that node.
An exact formula follows this term through any integer number of shifts,
including negative shifts.

The uncorrected multiplier has product \(1-m\delta\) around the
cycle. Thus dropping the normal term would make a unit solution
impossible when \(m\ne0\). Including it changes the multiplier to
\(q^mw^m(1+m\delta p_D)\), whose cyclic product is one. Its unit
solutions form a torsor under
\((\mathbb C[\delta]/(\delta^2))^\times\): any two solutions differ
by exactly one invariant unit. Inversion symmetry removes the
remaining \(\delta\)-freedom, and the original normalization fixes
the scalar. This determines the filling Gaussian, including its
first derivatives. It is a torsor statement for the filling factor,
not yet for the entire knot period.

One-sided transport also needs the correct closing functional.
At odd levels the unmodified closing has a kernel on the doubled
algebra, so it has no adjoint for a single spectral shift on that
whole algebra. The proof constructs two perfect extensions which
both restrict to the original closing on physical sources; inversion
exchanges them. Their exact adjoints compose as a group. In the
norm measuring values and first logarithmic derivatives divided by
\(N\), each \(k\)-step adjoint has norm at most \(3N\), independently
of \(k\). The estimate comes from one conjugation, rather than a
product of losses over successive steps.

This supplies exact first-order transport of an arbitrary retained
spectator with polynomial cost at both parities. It does not bound
the spectator's own exponential size. Nor does nilpotence give a
fixed-dimensional space of all currents: their shift orbit spans an
\(N\)-dimensional space before taking inversion invariants. The
geometric turn is another operation and has not been replaced by
the spectral shift.

Together, the new results give a simpler exact form of the deletion
terms, a general geometric action gap for the chosen nonzero currents,
and bounded
cyclic transport of the filling factors. The missing implication
remains global: the original closed source must have a nonzero
geometric contribution and all competing contributions must be
controlled for an arbitrary fixed short partial filling. No new
hyperbolic knot class or finite-exception conclusion is inferred.

## Why the transport bound does not yet control an attached component

The [turn-current calculation](research_turned_gaussian_current_norm.md)
checks the next operation in the actual source. It defines the turn
after a one-sided shift by using the original turn kernel and the
chosen closing extension. At odd levels this keeps an explicit
additional term from the auxiliary normal at the fixed point.
Thus the doubled-algebra transport can be inserted into the source
without inventing a new geometric turn.

There is an exact obstruction to estimating every intermediate current
separately in the same jet norm. A shifted Gaussian endpoint current,
projected back to the original inversion-invariant algebra, gives a
vector \(f_b\) with norm one whose original turn satisfies
\[
 \|\mathsf T f_b\|_N
    \ge \exp\{(4G_{\rm Cat}/\pi)N-O(\log N)\}.
\]
This holds at both parities and uses the original positive diagonal
kernel sum. The same current nevertheless has
\[
                         \phi_N(\mathsf T f_b)=0
\]
under the prescribed original closing.

Consequently the polynomial spectral-shift bound cannot simply be
multiplied through successive turns to obtain a polynomial bound for
a short component. The exponential response occurs within the module
generated by the actual endpoint current, so restricting to that
module does not repair this estimate. Its zero closing also shows why
the result is not a counterexample to the desired knot asymptotic:
the attached exterior and the cancellations in its contraction must
be retained in the estimate.

## A finite algebraic test for survival across leading-coefficient zeros

The new [coefficient-ideal lemma](research_filling_coefficient_ideal_certificate.md)
is an auxiliary implication, not an extension of the proved knot class.
It replaces the requirement that the leading coefficient alone avoid
every long tuple by a finite identity among several coefficients.
Write \(\epsilon_i=1/p_i\). After keeping known nonvanishing normalization
factors outside, suppose the **whole original scalar** has a controlled
expansion at the selected action with holomorphic coefficients
\(c_0(\epsilon),c_1(\epsilon),\ldots\), and all complementary terms have
a strict exponential loss. If
\[
       \sum_{j=0}^{J}g_j(\epsilon)c_j(\epsilon)
                       =\prod_i\epsilon_i^{\nu_i},
       \qquad \nu_i\ge0,
\]
holds as an identity of holomorphic germs, then at least one of those
coefficients is nonzero at every independently sufficiently long fixed
tuple. Its first nonzero order changes the power of \(N\), not the
exponential rate. The identity and the expansion must hold in every
level class; a proof for one parity is insufficient. The note retains
the source normalization, any orthant choices, and the separate proof
that the selected action gives the actual knot-complement volume.

Equivalently, with \(t=\prod_i\epsilon_i\), the ideal generated by the
coefficients must contain a power of \(t\). After inverting \(t\), this
says that the coefficient ideal is the unit ideal. This is a finite
algebraic target. Noetherianity alone supplies no such identity.
For one remaining cusp, any nonzero coefficient germ at a finite order
already has the required factorization. In several variables later
coefficients can remove a leading divisor; the note gives an explicit
algebraic illustration, without attributing that illustration to a knot.

The general short-filling problem still requires the actual expansion
and the finite identity. A nonzero formal geometric Gaussian does not
supply either for the prescribed closure. In fact the
[exact twist-period reconstruction](research_twist_period_insertion_growth.md)
shows why inspecting arbitrarily many coefficients of the wrong sector
cannot work: every inverse-power coefficient of its larger augmented
contribution cancels exactly when the fixed short source is recovered.
This example does not assert cancellation of the desired filled
geometric contribution.

The same review recovered several existing results and limitations;
they should not be proposed again as new advances:

- [Rational-chain reductions](research_rational_corridor_compression.md)
  and the [full affine normal form](research_definite_rational_corridor_normal_form.md)
  already handle arbitrary-length fixed rational chains by an exact
  boundary-matrix test. When its lower-left entry has absolute value one,
  a two-ended chain reduces to one edge and fixed shifts of its two
  remaining twist parameters. The retained circles stay distinct, so
  the frozen all-long theorem transfers in the original coordinates.
  A zero lower-left entry instead merges parameters and requires the
  separate infinite-fiber analysis.
- [Dominant-saddle transport](research_dominant_saddle_transport.md)
  already proves persistence under controlled relative-cycle transport.
  It still requires control at deleted divisors and ends, and does not
  construct that transport through arbitrary short fillings.
- [The original closing obstruction](actual_quantum_source_positivity_obstruction.md)
  excludes a faithful positive realization of the same closing map.
  Exact Ward equations and the scalar intertwiner line therefore do not
  replace a lower bound for the prescribed scalar.

The next substantive source theorem must address a general fixed short
component, with its original closing functional and complementary
terms. The coefficient-ideal lemma makes one possible nonvanishing
criterion precise; it does not remove those analytic requirements or
the collapsed-core obligation described above.

## The local geometric contribution and integer filling shifts

Three further written results separate the local nonvanishing question
from the problem of selecting that contribution in the original sum.
None extends the proved knot class yet.

First, the [primitive-filling Gaussian calculation](research_primitive_filling_local_gaussian_unit.md)
evaluates the leading coefficient of the local geometric contribution.
Let \(S\) be the selected vertices of the original circle tree and let
\(E_S\) be all edges incident to \(S\). The other boundary angles are
held fixed. Write \(k=|S|\), \(m=|E_S|\),
\(a_v=\tan(t_v/2)\), and
\(q_{vw}^2=1+a_v^2+a_w^2\), with the branches specified by the complete
geometric point. If \(J\) is the Jacobian of the primitive filling
periods, the actual local leading coefficient satisfies
\[
 A_0^2=\frac{(-8)^k}{16^m}
 \frac{
  \displaystyle\prod_{v\in S}a_v^2(1+a_v^2)^{d_v-2}
  \prod_{w\notin S}(1+a_w^2)^{d_S(w)}
 }{\displaystyle(\prod_{e\in E_S}q_e)\det J}.
\]
Here \(d_v\) is the degree in the original tree and \(d_S(w)\)
counts neighbors of \(w\) in \(S\). On the stated regular chart,
where the edge coordinates, selected \(a_v\), and \(\det J\) do not
vanish, this is a nonzero rational function. The square root is
taken on the marked local cover. The proof retains the original
Hermite trace, its Fourier charge-one coefficient, and the separate
endpoint currents. It also proves the local formal integration
statement: modulo formal integration by parts, the nondegenerate
geometric Gaussian has a nonzero leading class. This is a local
statement about a specified stationary point. It does not show that
the original global contour has a nonzero coefficient at that point,
or bound the contributions from the rest of the contour.

Second, the [continuous Ward calculation](research_continuous_filling_ward_derivative_current.md)
identifies an obstruction to obtaining filling derivatives from the
integer Ward identities. In the specified Gaussian continuation of
the full Hermite source, the original closing of the endpoint defect
is exactly
\[
             \kappa^{\varepsilon-2p}(1-e^{-2\pi i p}).
\]
It vanishes at every integer \(p\), but its derivative there is
\(2\pi i\kappa^{\varepsilon-2p}\). The derivative restores a value
current that integer specialization had removed. Thus one cannot
differentiate the integer deletion rule while continuing to discard
that current. In the reciprocal coordinate \(x=1/p\), the displayed
alias has an essential singularity at zero; it is not a holomorphic
coefficient germ of the kind used in the preceding ideal lemma.

Third, [independent integer shifts](research_independent_filling_shift_ideal.md)
give an algebraic alternative to assuming filling derivatives.
Let \(R=\mathbb C\{x_1,\ldots,x_b\}\), \(t=\prod_i x_i\), and let
\(I\ne0\) be the ideal of the actual holomorphic coefficient germs
in one level class. Put \(J=I:t^\infty\). If each independent shift
\[
 \sigma_i f(x)=f(x_1,\ldots,x_i/(1+x_i),\ldots,x_b)
\]
satisfies \(\sigma_i(J)\subseteq J\), then \(J=R\). Therefore
\(t^r\in I\) for some finite \(r\), giving the finite nonvanishing
certificate above. The proof takes the logarithm of the shift on
each finite Taylor quotient, uses Krull separation to recover
\(-x_i^2\partial_{x_i}J\subseteq J\), and then uses saturation to
remove \(x_i^2\). A nonzero differential ideal of convergent germs
contains a unit. Simultaneously shifting every filling is
insufficient: the proper saturated ideal \((x_1-x_2)\) is preserved
by that simultaneous shift.

This criterion still requires source identities. No independent
shift relation has been established for the actual scalar geometric
coefficients of an arbitrary short partial filling. A boundary twist
matrix does not by itself give such a relation after the prescribed
closing, changed action, and endpoint contributions are retained.
The whole-source expansion and its complementary exponential bound
also remain necessary.

## The convex energy constructs a finite geometric contour

The [inverse-period contour theorem](research_positive_period_inverse_descent.md)
adds a global consequence to the local Gaussian calculation. Its
hypothesis is that the fixed short partial filling has a positive
primitive solution in the original edge decomposition. It does not
deduce that hypothesis merely from hyperbolicity.

Write \(t_v=s_v+ih_v\), and let \(P(t)\) be the original primitive
period vector. At the geometric solution \(t^0\),
\(P(t^0)=-\pi i\mathbf1\). The existing angle energy \(\mathcal E\)
is defined on a compact polytope of angle assignments, with the
imaginary parts of these period equations imposed as linear
constraints. The new proof minimizes
\[
                    \mathcal E(z)-\xi\cdot s(z)
                    \qquad(\xi\in\mathbb R^{|S|}).
\]
There is a unique minimizer for every real \(\xi\). It is interior
exactly when there is a positive solution of
\(P(t)=\xi-\pi i\mathbf1\). Finite boundary points of this period
image correspond to unique limiting angle assignments with corner
degenerations. The entire period image need not be all of real space.

The decisive identity uses the original phase normalization:
\[
       \operatorname{Re}F(t(\xi))
          =m\psi(0,0)-\frac{\mathcal E(z_\xi)}{\pi}.
\]
Here \(m\) counts the included edges and \(z_\xi\) is the tilted
minimizer. The fixed outside imaginary angles are included in
\(\mathcal E\), so no unspecified boundary constant is omitted.
The geometric point is therefore the unique maximum of the real
action on this entire inverse-period slice.

Let \(\Delta>0\) be the energy difference between the minimum at
\(z_0\) and the minimum on the boundary of the angle polytope.
For any \(0<\delta<\Delta\), the sublevel
\[
 \Omega_\delta=
 \{\xi:\mathcal E(z_\xi)<\mathcal E(z_0)+\delta\}
\]
is bounded and star shaped, with smooth boundary and compact closure
inside the positive period image. Its image
\(\Gamma_\delta=t(\Omega_\delta)\) is a finite contour through
\(t^0\), with
\[
 \operatorname{Re}F\big|_{\partial\Gamma_\delta}
                  =\operatorname{Re}F(t^0)-\delta/\pi.
\]
Thus the geometry supplies a contour and a uniform boundary action
loss. This conclusion does not require all selected powers to be
large. It persists under small changes of the outside angles.

The original quantum sum has not yet been decomposed into this
geometric contribution and a smaller remainder. Such a decomposition
must keep the actual connecting faces, vertical trace currents, and
all wire indices until their original contractions have been taken.
The [full-wire obstruction](research_all_three_edgewise_contour_obstruction.md)
already shows that individual edge remainders can be larger than
their geometric contributions, even on positive charts. Some such
large terms cancel exactly at adjacent Hermite traces. Consequently
the missing estimate must address those joint contractions; the
new energy identity does not supply an edgewise estimate.

## Why the physical cut sums must be contracted before they are bounded

The [positive-tree cut comparison](research_positive_tree_cut_norm_obstruction.md)
rules out a proposed universal estimate for the smaller pieces.
Consider two adjacent selected zero-power vertices, each of original
degree four, with their six outside angles complete. This is an
already controlled positive zero-power source, so it provides a test
of the estimate without assuming an unproved short-power asymptotic.

Let \(M_\infty=4G/\pi\) be the complete edge rate, where \(G\)
is Catalan's constant. The original positive primitive solution has
rate \(M=7M_\infty-\mathcal E_*/\pi\). The new proof gives
\(\mathcal E_*>4>4G\), and therefore
\[
                        M<6M_\infty.
\]
Deleting the middle edge leaves two three-edge stars, each with its
own shared boundary color. Their complete rates sum to
\(6M_\infty\). Thus the full geometric rate need not exceed the
sum of those complete component rates. Positivity of the geometric
solution does not imply the proposed cut inequality.

The failure persists even when the full physical Gram weights are
retained. Set \(B_N(z)=K_N(z,-2)\), and expand the canonical
remainder of \(B_N(z)^3\) in the original Newton basis:
\[
             \operatorname{rem}_{P_N}B_N(z)^3
                         =\sum_r f_{N,r}e_r(z).
\]
The actual radical contribution on the middle edge is
\[
 T_N=\sum_{r<\lfloor N/2\rfloor} f_{N,r}^2
       =\sum_{a,b}W_{ab}B_N(c_a)^3B_N(c_b)^3.
\]
Here \(c_a\) are the physical double nodes and \(W\) is the exact
Gram matrix from the radical contraction. If \(A_N\) denotes the
same physical-color sum with \(W_{ab}\) replaced by \(|W_{ab}|\),
the new proof establishes, at both parities,
\[
 \log A_N=6NM_\infty+O(\log N),\qquad
              1\le T_N\le C N^q e^{N(M-\varepsilon)}
\]
for some \(\varepsilon>0\). In particular \(A_N/T_N\) grows
exponentially. The required cancellation occurs inside the signed
divided differences that recover each \(f_{N,r}\), before their
squares are added.

For this radical sector all high boundary indices disappear
algebraically: \(f_{N,r}\) only observes boundary indices at most
\(r\). The existing internal-high theorem therefore supplies the
coherent bound directly. No high-boundary comparison is needed.
The positive square representation uses the symmetric zero-power
source; it is not a positivity statement for arbitrary signed
fillings.

This changes the general strategy. Neither independent boundary
suprema nor absolute physical Gram weights can give the desired
universal remainder estimate. A calculation must keep the Newton
coefficients, their signed divided differences, or an equivalent
contraction that preserves this cancellation.

## Exact reduction of interacting cutoff and radical terms

The [collective cutoff theorem](research_cutoff_cluster_exact_reduction.md)
gives further identities before any absolute values are taken.
Put \(D=N-1\), \(m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), \(L=D-m\),
\(A=e_L\), and \(B=e_{L+1}\). The exact cutoff term on an
oriented edge \(v\longrightarrow w\) is
\(-s_{L+1}^2A(z_v)B(z_w)\). These terms arise from the original
low-kernel difference equation.

At odd levels, \(AB=B^2=0\), while \(A^r\), \(r\ge2\),
is the simple-node projector at \(-2\). Consequently a nonvanishing
eligible cutoff cluster is an outward star. A branching center
evaluates its entire spectator at \(-2\), and all remaining
observations use values only.

At even levels, \(B^2=0\). Every internal vertex of an outward
cutoff tree is evaluated at
\(c_*=-2\cos(\pi/N)\), with an explicit crossing scalar.
Only the root may retain a first derivative of its spectator.
On a general finite simple graph, a directed cycle with outward
trees is also allowed; it has no root derivative. All unchosen
edges and their shared variables remain in the spectator.

There is a stronger rule when full radical edges and cutoff edges
are expanded together. At odd levels, a radical edge cannot share
a traced vertex with any cutoff edge. At even levels, every eligible
connected mixed cluster is a tree with exactly one radical edge.
The cutoff edges point away from its two endpoints, and its radical
index is forced to the lowest radical polynomial \(B\). No sum
over that index and no spectator derivative remain in this mixed
cluster. This follows from the exact local products and a count of
incoming radical factors, rather than an estimate of their norms.

The observation cost of an even mixed cluster with \(\ell\) leaves
is at most a fixed constant times \(N^{2\ell-2}\) times the joint
physical-value norm of its remaining spectator. In particular a
mixed chain has cost \(O(N^2)\), independently of its length in
the exponent of \(N\). This statement concerns a fixed graph before
the level limit. The smaller component sources still depend on
that graph and retain their original powers.

These identities reduce specified corrections to sources with fewer
traced vertices. They do not show that every contour correction has
this form, give a strict geometric rate comparison, or determine the
coefficient of the geometric contour. The preceding cut example
explains why the resulting components must still be treated with
their coherent contractions intact.

The [exact Newton crossing transport](research_corner_newton_source_transport.md)
is already available for that purpose; it must not be proposed again
as a new representation. It expresses arbitrary fixed powers using
the original triangular crossing matrices, but even one such matrix
has exponentially large entries in the coefficient norm. Applying
it to an old zero-power remainder therefore requires a new estimate
of the full transformed sum.
