## Explicit initialized endpoint connection and all local pole weights

The [endpoint proof](research_terminal_phase_endpoint_connection.md)
uses the actual terminal phase Casimir
\[
 (C\gamma)_j=\alpha_j\gamma_{j+1}+\delta_j\gamma_j
                               +\beta_j\gamma_{j-1},
\]
where
\[
 \alpha_j=\omega(1-\tau^{-j-1}),\quad
 \beta_j=\omega^{-1}(1-\tau^{-j}),\quad
 \delta_j=2\omega^{-1}\tau^{-j}.
\]
The endpoint arrows vanish exactly. The polynomials \(p_j(z)\)
are normalized by \(p_0=1,p_{-1}=0\) and the first \(N-1\)
rows of \(Cp=zp\). Their actual final-row equation is
\[
 (C-zI)p(z)=-\frac{P_N(z)}{N\omega^{N-1}}e_{N-1},
 \qquad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2.
\]
Thus a geometric parameter off the finite spectrum does not
give an exact homogeneous finite eigenvector; the endpoint
source cannot be suppressed.

For \(G_N(t,z)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}p_j(z)t^j\), the exact polynomial
connection equation is
\[
 (1-t)^2G_N(t,z)
 -(1-\omega zt+\tau t^2)G_N(\tau t,z)
 =-\frac{P_N(z)}N t^N.
\]
The finite logarithm modulo \(t^N\) is explicit. At a physical
node \(c_s=\omega\tau^s+\omega^{-1}\tau^{-s}\), it gives the
degree-\(N-1\) product
\[
 G_N(t,c_s)
 =(\tau^{s+1}t;\tau)_{N-1-s}
                (\tau^{-s}t;\tau)_s,\qquad
 p_{N-1}(c_s)=\tau^{-s(s+1)}.
\]
The factor \(1-t^N\) that converts the intermediate rational
expression into this polynomial is retained. Spectral
differentiation of the finite connection, rather than
differentiation of a discrete label, supplies each true Jordan
normal. The resulting columns \(p(c_s),p'(c_s)\), with the odd
simple column when present, form the complete finite basis.

Write the endpoint resolvent as \(Q_N(z)/P_N(z)\).
The cofactor normalization and its derivative are exact:
\[
 Q_N(c_s)=N\omega^{-(N-1)}\tau^{s(s+1)},\qquad
 \frac{Q_N'(c_s)}{Q_N(c_s)}
                  =-\frac{p_{N-1}'(c_s)}{p_{N-1}(c_s)}
\]
at every double root. They follow from the tridiagonal
adjugate and determinant identities. No physical root
cancels out of this endpoint resolvent.

For a distinct double-node representative \(s<N-1-s\), put
\(\theta_s=(2s+1)\pi/N\) and
\(u_s=\omega^{-(N-1)}\tau^{s(s+1)}\). Its two pole coefficients are
\[
 W_{2,s}=u_s\,\frac{4-c_s^2}{N},
 \qquad
 W_{1,s}=u_s\left(
 \frac{2i\sigma(N-1-2s)\sin\theta_s}{N}
                                      -\frac{c_s}{N}\right).
\]
In particular
\[
 \frac{16}{N^3}\le |W_{2,s}|\le\frac4N,\qquad
 \frac1N\le |W_{1,s}|\le2+\frac2N .
\]
At the odd simple node the residue has modulus \(1/N\).
The value-weight lower bound uses the orthogonal real and
imaginary parts of the displayed expression; it does not
divide by an uncontrolled cofactor derivative.
Thus every local value and normal spectral block is coupled
to the prescribed endpoint at polynomial size.

For any function defined by full Hermite data modulo \(P_N\),
\[
 e_0^{\mathsf T}f(C)e_0
 =\sum_{\rm double\ s}
      \bigl(W_{1,s}f(c_s)+W_{2,s}f'(c_s)\bigr)
       +\text{the odd simple term}.
\]
This is the actual endpoint functional, including the
crossing derivative at a repeated root. Its summands remain
complex and can cancel. Alternating the two retained-face
operators also changes this initialized spectral basis;
the bounds on individual weights are not a lower bound for
that coherent composition.

For the literal same-sign corner baseline
\[
 B_\sigma(c,y)=\kappa^\sigma
        \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}a^{N-1-i}c^iy^{N-1-i},
\]
the phase vector is exactly
\(N\kappa^\sigma a^{N-1}e_0\).
Since \(\kappa^{2\sigma}a^{N-1}=1\), an allowed
retained-face word \(U\) has the exact scalar
\[
 \kappa^\sigma\ell_a(UB_\sigma)
                         =N(U_{\rm phase})_{00}.
\]
This identifies its finite initialization and closing without
an unknown normalization. It applies to the specified
cap-prepared source, not an unproved representation of
every knot diagram by a two-face word.

The final proof is pinned at
\(\texttt{0fd547a51c458e7f586b01a7de7ce5319695a95166fba031ae941e3785793850}\).
Complete author, peer and root reads cover this final and both
complete direct sources at matching pins \(68b1e668\) and
\(d1be51d8\). All calculations are written proofs; no
mathematical programs or numerical evaluations were used.
The general short-filling noncancellation theorem remains open.

## Removing the two spherical vertices of the crossing cellulation

The [lens-and-cone construction](research_free_sphere_vertex_lens_deletion.md)
starts from the literal four-tetrahedron crossing blocks, with their
two free vertices \(P,S\) and the knot vertex \(K\). For a diagram with
\(c>0\) crossings it gives a generalized ideal triangulation of the
same marked knot exterior with \(4c\) tetrahedra and only vertex \(K\).
Its meridian and preferred longitude are those of the original diagram.

At the first free vertex, a specified \(0\to2\) move inserts two
tetrahedra. In its spherical link these form an embedded two-triangle
disk, the closed star of a new link vertex \(A\). Write the rest of
the sphere as a disk \(D\). The balls \(P*L_P\) and \(A*D\) have the
same labeled boundary, so replacing the former by the latter preserves
all recorded boundary face maps. The replacement removes two
tetrahedra from the prepared cellulation. Every resulting tetrahedron
still has one \(S\) corner. The procedure can therefore be repeated
at \(S\), using a nonloop edge in its new spherical link. Repeated
global edge or tetrahedron incidences do not require distinct copies
of the corresponding quotient cell.

The final face-pairing prescription has no additional vertices.
Auxiliary subdivisions are used only to prove the relative PL ball
homeomorphisms. The second connecting edge is chosen after the first
replacement; no assertion about a preassigned second path is needed.

This is a topological result. The corresponding equality of full
quantum boundary tensors has not been proved. In particular the
original marked closing functional and its meridian currents cannot
be replaced by an ordinary cap selector. Positive developed
tetrahedra and the contribution of the geometric stationary point
also require separate arguments.

The proof is fixed at
\(\texttt{b2309660fabcbb5b196ec5df1c6cecb5e8edb0a7a2255129109e2957102020e0}\).
Its complete direct source is the crossing-tunnel construction at
\(\texttt{e836e8f4bb4fc0c67eeee286d3ad39e372546b369517ef903df8806551841154}\).

The [local-move refinement](research_free_vertex_deletion_by_local_moves.md)
gives a second, explicitly factored deletion. A lune followed by a
\(2\to3\) move subdivides any abstract link triangle at a fresh
link vertex whose global endpoint is an existing \(K\) vertex.
Another such subdivision and flip subdivides a link edge. Two
face-and-edge refinement rounds give an ordinary simplicial sphere.
Peeling the disk complementary to a \(K\)-anchored vertex star
then uses \(2\leftrightarrow3\) moves and exactly one final
\(4\to1\). During the \(P\) stage every tetrahedron retains at
most one \(S\), so the same procedure applies at \(S\).

This second output need not be the unrefined \(4c\)-tetrahedron
triangulation. The written count is at most \(4c\,64^2\).
No global vertex or peripheral covering is added. The proof is
fixed at
\(\texttt{08adacd45ce1559cec02d2d46cb892b5051d25ce7adec7ccf0060c7759b98028}\),
with the preceding lens-deletion proof as its complete direct source.
Its scope is classical: the original tensors have not been assigned
to these face maps, the terminal marked bubble identity is unproved,
and the refinements can create identically degenerate developed
tetrahedra requiring their own full source transport.

## The original paired-face adapter, its wire phase and fixed cut

The [literal adapter proof](research_kashaev_paired_face_boundary_adapter.md)
starts from Kashaev's published function (4.28), rather than choosing
a new tetrahedral state. Put \(d=N-1\), \(a^N=A\), \(b^N=B\), and
\[
 f(k)=a^{[k-1]}b^{[-k]},\qquad
 \Psi_{kj}=Q^{jk}f(k).
\]
The full paired-face map uses \(k=\alpha_--\alpha_++c\).
It has rank \(N\), with image the simultaneous-translation
invariants in the \(N^2\) face-pair space. Its inverse on that
image and its averaging projector are explicit. Its condition
number on that image is exactly
\[
 \left(\frac{\max(|A|,|B|)}{\min(|A|,|B|)}\right)^{d/N}.
\]
The cyclic seam is retained:
\[
 (S-a/b)f=\frac{B-A}{b}\delta_0.
\]
It restores monodromy one and cannot be removed by continuing
the geometric progression through the zero index.

For reversed face order and charges summing to one, the complete
finite sewing identity is
\[
 \sum_{\alpha_-,\alpha_+}
 \mathcal A_c(\alpha_-,\alpha_+;j)
 \mathcal A_{c'}(\alpha_+,\alpha_-;j')
   =N^2(ab)^dQ^j\delta_{jj'}.
\]
The two specified non-link edge factors cancel \((ab)^d\).
The original wire clock \(Q^j\) and the factor \(N^2\) remain.
Changing root branches produces an explicit additional phase
and index translation. The four-leg boundary expression retains
the full factor \(s_{05}^dN^4\).

The planar fixed cut in the original index basis is \(E_{00}\).
Its transported rank-one projector has entries
\[
 \mathcal E_{\alpha_-\alpha_+;\alpha'_-\alpha'_+}
       =\frac{f(k)}{N^2f(k')}.
\]
Tracing one face gives a circulant matrix. With \(t=A/B\),
\(h=[\alpha'-\alpha]\), and \(z_j=(a/b)^{-1}Q^j\), its entries
and, for \(t\ne1\), eigenvalues are
\[
 M_{\alpha\alpha'}=\frac{(a/b)^{-h}}{N^2}(N-h+ht),
 \qquad
 \lambda_j=\frac{(t-1)^2z_j}{N^2t(1-z_j)^2}.
\]
For \(|A|=|B|\) and \(t=e^{i\theta}\ne1\), this is a positive
density matrix with
\[
 \frac{\sin^2(\theta/2)}{N^2}I\ \le M\le I.
\]
These conditions can be met simultaneously at any finite number
of boundary vertices: choose \(z_0=-1,z_5=1\) and distinct
\(z_m=i u_m\), \(1\le u_m\le2\). Then
\(t=e^{2i\arctan u_m}\), so the lower bound is \(I/(2N^2)\).
Thus every positive one-face operator \(H\) obeys
\(\operatorname{Tr}(MH)\ge\operatorname{Tr}H/(2N^2)\).
This does not assert positivity or a lower bound for a general
operator acting on both faces. Other tetrahedral differences
need not stay uniformly separated as the number of vertices grows.

The proof is fixed at
\(\texttt{c430fd2714acdc7588003e1c18c60453e1ebe123bd7c0155d20a0eef639ec8ed}\).
Its complete direct definition is Kashaev's 1995 paper, archived
at PDF pin
\(\texttt{0baef40fa9934c9119af2c67252f8032e288c884da72eeaecf405bf91569cda9}\).
All these finite adapter identities hold at every \(N\ge2\).
The published tetrahedral model itself has an odd-level restriction.
The proof does not assume its nine-tetrahedron contraction formula,
identify the original meridian jets with decoration derivatives,
or establish the global charged source or geometric coefficient.

## The literal charged tetrahedron inverse and vertex bubble

The [finite charged-bubble proof](research_literal_charged_tetrahedron_bubble.md)
reconstructs Kashaev's 1994 definitions at odd \(N>2\), with all
central parameters and the indicated partial sums nonzero. It
proves the cyclic finite-sum normalization without assuming the
printed inversion or CG-duality assertions. For the original
normalizing functions,
\[
 \rho\bar\rho
 =\frac{(x_p x_r)^N}
        {N(x_{pq}x_{qr}-x_{pqr}x_q)}.
\]
The raw \(w\)-kernel contraction is diagonal: its off-diagonal
sums vanish by finite Fourier orthogonality, and its diagonal
sum cancels this exact scalar. Thus the printed opposite-orientation
kernel is the actual matrix inverse in the compatible branches.

Writing \(a=c_{01}\) and \(c=c_{12}\), the vertex-charge equations
and inverse-pair conditions give \(a'=-a,c'=-c\). The charged
product is therefore
\[
 T(a,c)\bar T(-a,-c)
       =\langle s_{02}\rangle\langle s_{13}\rangle I.
\]
Contracting the third face is a plain trace in these face indices:
\[
 \sum_{\alpha_0,\alpha_1,\alpha_2}
       T_u(s,c,\alpha)\bar T_u(s,c',\alpha')
 =N\langle s_{13}\rangle\langle s_{02}\rangle
                  \delta_{\alpha_3,\alpha'_3}.
\]
The local link passes along \(0\!-\!3\!-\!2\). Under the required
boundary routing, edge \(02\) is initially non-link and becomes
the replacement link segment after removal of vertex \(3\).
Its old non-link factor and that of internal edge \(13\)
cancel both brackets. The extra \(N^{-1}\) in the old vertex
measure cancels \(N\). These are exact scalar cancellations
with the full regular parameters retained.

cut, route the knot through \(P,S\), or cover singular

## The complete nine-tetrahedron boundary source and its normalization

The [nine-cell proof](research_nine_tetrahedron_boundary_source_reduction.md)
starts with the explicit 1995 kernels and the finite 1994
normalizing functions. It lists all fourteen internal face pairings,
the eight boundary faces, and the actual edge weights. There are
no interior vertices in this crossing ball. Its two tangle edges
have charge zero and its other four interior edges have charge one.
An explicit charge table works over every odd
\(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\), with arbitrary sector charges summing
to one and boundary charges \(h_m\) summing to two.

The nine Kronecker symbols impose one boundary condition and
eliminate eight internal sums, leaving six independent cyclic
indices. The resulting finite sum keeps every Gaussian phase
and all nine normalization factors. Its dependence on the
boundary faces is entirely through
\[
 k_m=\alpha_m^--\alpha_m^++h_m,\qquad \sum_m k_m=2.
\]
The boundary tensor therefore lies in the fourfold image of the
literal paired-face adapter. Applying its explicit inverse loses
no data and defines a unique array \(\mathcal R^\chi\).
The shift and phase relating all charge sectors are explicit.
This establishes the boundary quotient for this calculated source.
The subsequent complete evaluation below identifies
\(\mathcal R^\chi\) with the planar crossing up to an explicitly
retained scalar and charge phase.

Two normalization comparisons are also proved directly. First,
with lower indices interpreted as matrix rows, the 1994 charged
operator and the explicit 1995 kernel obey
\[
 T^{95}(a,c)=q^{ac}T^{94}(a,c),\qquad
 \bar T^{95}(a,c)=q^{-ac}\bar T^{94}(a,c).
\]
The complementary-charge bubble is unchanged, but the nine-cell
product retains its signed sum of \(ac\).

Second, take the canonical sector, boundary charges
\(h=(1,0,0,1)\), and boundary differences \(k=(1,1,0,0)\).
For each fixed odd \(N>2\), use ordered real decorations
\(z_i=L^{5-i}\) and positive compatible roots. After division
by the explicitly retained decoration factor, the nine-cell
tensor tends to \(q\) as \(L\to\infty\). A separate finite-binomial
calculation gives the corresponding planar crossing coefficient
exactly \(N^2q\). Thus
\[
 \frac{\text{specified nine-cell tensor}}
      {\text{unit-coefficient planar crossing expression}}
 \longrightarrow N^{-2}.
\]
No charge-convention phase remains in this chosen comparison.
The elementary cyclic endpoints, both finite normalization sums,
and every edge weight are included.

This disproves the unit-coefficient identity for the precise
combination of kernels and scalar functions used in the note.
The 1995 paper refers to the earlier scalar functions without
displaying a conversion, so a possible conversion must be made
explicit. This degeneration neither refutes a global invariant theorem
nor on its own proves a corrected array identity. The subsequent
evaluation proves the full array identity with an explicit
parameter-dependent scalar; it determines its modulus on every
distinct-real component without asserting constancy of its phase.
The subsequent global sewing proof below supplies the original cut
and complete normalization for its constructed closed source.

## Complete evaluation of the nine-cell crossing

The [full evaluation](research_nine_cell_canonical_crossing_evaluation.md)
starts from that literal six-variable source. For every odd \(N>2\),
every sector \(\chi=(x,y,\zeta,w)\) with \(x+y+\zeta+w=1\), and
every allowed set of boundary charges, it proves
\[
 \mathcal R^\chi_{\mathbf i}
 =C_N(\mathbf s)\,
   q^{3(h_1-1)/2+d_\chi+\zeta+w}
   R(\mathbf i\mid x,y,\zeta,w).
\]
Here \(d_\chi\) is the explicit phase in the source-reduction
proof, and \(C_N\) is the explicit product of finite normalization
sums and edge roots in equation (4) of the evaluation. Both are
retained. The identity includes every boundary index and every
zero of the planar weight.

Three exact cyclic beta convolutions evaluate three of the six
sums. Finite polynomial Fourier sums evaluate the remaining three.
The remaining coefficient is obtained from
\[
 F(X)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{m}{m\brack\ell}_q q^{a\ell}
       X^\ell(qX;q)_{a+m-C-\ell},
\]
where \(a=[-k_1]\), \(m=[-k_2]\), and
\(C=[k_3-1]+1\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\). Negative product orders mean
reciprocal finite products, as defined in that proof. Put
\(h=C-a-1\) and \(M=m-h\). The coefficient is zero unless
\(C>a\) and \(M\ge0\); on that support it is exactly
\[
 [X^{N-1}]F
 =q^{aM}\frac{p_m p_{C-1}}{p_M p_h p_a},
 \qquad p_j=\prod_{r=1}^j(1-q^r).
\]
A separate finite Fourier calculation of the specified planar
weight gives \(N^2q^{1-k_1}\) times this same coefficient, including
all its zeros. Cancellation of the four boundary adapter factors
then proves the displayed array identity. No published crossing
contraction or pentagon theorem is used as a premise.

For arbitrary six distinct real vertex decorations, with real odd
edge roots and the compatible positive divided-difference square
roots, the scalar satisfies the exact identity
\[
                         |C_N(\mathbf s)|=N^{-2}.
\]
The proof does not assume the real values occur in their label
order. It conjugates the literal finite sums, uses their exact
normalization product, and cancels all the remaining signed real
factors. A common injective real decoration is therefore available
for different crossing blocks. Its modulus contributes no
exponential growth for a fixed number of crossings. Its phase
need not be discarded or assumed constant.

This completes the local array comparison previously left open.
The global assignment and cut are supplied by the subsequent sewing
proof below. A lower bound for the geometric contribution after that
cut is closed remains a different question. In particular neither
finite comparison proves the assertion about
arbitrary fixed short partial fillings or the finite-exception
theorem. The frozen manuscripts remain unchanged.

## Literal normalized recoupling and the pentagon

The [recoupling proof](research_literal_clebsch_gordan_recoupling.md)
derives Kashaev's finite intertwiners and duals from the stated
matrices, rather than assuming the published duality and pentagon.
It first fixes the actual Gaussian frame: in that frame the
generators are \(D=P XZ^{-1}\) and \(E=Z^{-1}\), with
\(Z|j\rangle=q^j|j\rangle\) and \(X|j\rangle=|j+1\rangle\).
Raw finite Fourier orthogonality gives the inverse and completeness
relations for the normalized change of basis.

The two ways to reassociate three tensor factors are then compared
entry by entry. Their coefficient is precisely the specified
matrix dilogarithm, including its three-numerator,
one-denominator square-root factor and its finite normalization
sum. Comparing the five bases for four tensor factors gives
\[
 R_{12}(p,q,r)R_{13}(p,qr,s)R_{23}(q,r,s)
   =R_{23}(pq,r,s)R_{12}(p,q,rs)
\]
in the stated lower-indices-as-rows convention. This is an exact
odd-level regular-parameter identity. Charged global moves still
require their specified clocks, charges, face assignment and cut.

The [collision proof](research_nine_cell_protected_collision_valuation.md)

 \mathcal B_\chi\in h^{N-1}\mathcal O,\qquad
 \mathcal R^\chi\in\mathcal O .

Here \(\mathcal O\) is the ring of holomorphic functions on the

do not alter this conclusion. The resulting order of vanishing
cancels the inverse boundary adapter's factor \(h^{-(N-1)}\).

## Exact material-wire subdivision with the original cut

The [two-cell proof](research_literal_hamiltonian_wire_subdivision.md)
uses a ball made of two tetrahedra glued on two faces sharing the
actual link edge. Its two boundary disks are the paired triangular
faces used by the original adapter. The internal edge has charge
zero and is part of the knot, so it carries no ordinary edge weight.
The ball has no interior vertex.

The direct finite sum is first evaluated in an order in which the
kernel has a diagonal face output. The primary face Fourier maps
then put both boundaries in their actual paired adapter images.
The single-tetrahedron permutation factors are explicitly retained:
their product is one by the proved normalization identity
\(\rho\bar\rho=y^N/[N(z-x)]\). Their charge phases cancel for the two
neutral recipes. Finite cyclic endpoint products give the exact
physical matrix
\[
             K=N^{-1}Z^{-1},\qquad Z_{ij}=q^i\delta_{ij}.
\]
One charge recipe gives boundary charges \(1,0\); the other gives
\(0,1\). Thus either endpoint order under a single global vertex
ordering is available. No unproved permutation identity is used.

Joining two port disks contributes \(N^2(ab)^{N-1}Z\).
Its two ordinary edge weights remove the decoration power, and its
one new interior material vertex supplies \(N^{-1}\). Hence the
normalized joining matrix is \(S=NZ\). Inserting the ball changes
one joining into two, with the exact equality
\[
                         SK=KS=I,\qquad SKS=S .
\]
The prescribed cut is retained since \(K,S\) commute with \(E_{00}\).
There is no replacement by a uniform vector or a newly chosen trace.
An oriented crossing diagram can use charge one at each incoming
crossing end and zero at each outgoing end; two of each occur at
every crossing, and every joining has complementary charges.

The statement holds against fixed exterior physical arrays and their
specified paired adapters. If a new construction chooses different
decorations for its crossing ports, it must retain their actual
scalars \(C_N(\mathbf s)\); this wire identity does not prove those
scalars unchanged. Their exact modulus from the full crossing
evaluation is available separately. Nor does this subdivision prove
the further detours through the two global poles or transport a
selected geometric integration cycle.

## Changes of planar sector charges preserve the fixed ends

The [planar gauge proof](research_planar_sector_gauge_and_open_cut.md)
works directly with the specified planar weight. At a crossing with
cyclic edge colors \(i,j,k,l\), its corner charges are on
\((i,j),(j,k),(k,l),(l,i)\). Two admissible assignments differ by
\[
 a'-a=x_j-x_i,\quad b'-b=x_k-x_j,\quad
 c'-c=x_l-x_k,\quad d'-d=x_i-x_l
\]
for edge potentials \(x_e\) which can be chosen zero on both end
edges. The proof replaces each crossing by a small circle and
integrates the resulting increments on that plane graph. Crossing
and face sums kill every integral cycle; the vanishing of the
individual outer-corner differences fixes the same value at both
ends. No division modulo \(N\) is used.

All four finite-product arguments and their theta supports then
remain unchanged under \(j_e\mapsto j_e+x_e\). The crossing's
explicit prefactor changes by \(q^{-x_i-x_k}\), with \(i,k\) the
underpassing half-edges. Consequently the entire open array satisfies
\[
 F_{a'}(u,v)=q^{\Omega(x)}F_a(u,v),\qquad
 \Omega(x)=\sum_e x_e-\sum_{\text{under-half-edge occurrences}}x_e .
\]
This phase is independent of both end colors and every summation
color. In particular the argument retains the original fixed
\((0,0)\) closing. It does not authorize a different closing
functional or establish noncancellation.

Face and crossing sums count corner occurrences. Where four distinct
regions meet a crossing, this is literally the primary planar
definition; where a region repeats, the note defines its
occurrence-level convention explicitly. No ambiguity in the
primary \(V\times F\) notation is used as a theorem.

## The complete closed source for a braid presentation

The [global comparison](research_braid_cut_and_global_nine_cell_sewing.md)
constructs a closed charged tetrahedral source for any supplied
one-component braid presentation, with \(c>0\) crossings on at least
two strands. For every odd \(N>2\), it proves the exact finite identity
\[
 N^2 Z_{\rm lit}
   =\left(\prod_{v=1}^c N^2 C_N(\mathbf s_v)q^{\phi_v}\right)
                 O_\chi(0,0).
\]
Here \(Z_{\rm lit}\) includes the original factor \(N^{-1}\) for
every interior vertex, \(N^2\) is the specified closed normalization,
\(O_\chi(0,0)\) is the original fixed-zero planar source, and
\(C_N,\phi_v\) are the explicit local scalar and charge phase already
evaluated above. On the common injective real decoration,
\[
                     |N^2 Z_{\rm lit}|=|O_\chi(0,0)|.
\]
The equality holds even when the invariant vanishes at that level.
No division by its value or assumed nonvanishing occurs.

The proof includes the actual closing functional. First the exact
Fourier comparison with the enhanced quantum-group braid, including
the phase of the negative inverse, gives the open operator
\[
                 O_\chi(i,j)=q^{-i}\delta_{ij}O_\chi(0,0).
\]
The two end-edge factors are omitted from this \(O_\chi\); the
charge-gauge note's array includes both. The braid's closure shift
is absorbed into its sector charges. A direct gap sweep verifies
the face sums. Comparing the result with an admissible assignment
by the expanded-circle potential construction fixes both end colors,
because the unchanged outer path has zero corner differences.
This avoids assigning inconsistent values to repeated edges.

An admissible assignment itself is explicit: choose a rooted tree
in the black Tait graph and its complementary rooted dual tree.
Each crossing assigns its unit to the child endpoint in one of these
trees. Every bounded region receives one, and both root regions
receive zero. The proof counts corner occurrences.

The topology is also explicit. Slit the shadow's dual quadrilateral
sphere along the chosen cut side. The resulting disk has \(c\)
cells, \(2c-1\) internal sides, and two free sides. Its suspension
is the assembled crossing ball. Region arcs from one pole to the
other are single edges, not extra unvisited vertices. Inflating
each internal side to a bigon inserts precisely the two-cell
identity collar. This keeps all crossing ports distinct and permits
one global vertex order, including self-adjacent wires.

Each effective wire contributes \(NZ\), so the open scalar is
\[
 K_{\rm open}=N^{2c-1}\prod_v C_N(\mathbf s_v)q^{\phi_v},
 \qquad |K_{\rm open}|=N^{-1}.
\]
The \(c\) ordinary region edges cancel the \(c\) pole-edge powers
in the local crossing formulas. All these are actual contractions,
with the vertex and edge measures included.

The empty closing ball consists of two tetrahedra with the
four-triangle boundary left by the open source. Its knot route is
\(a-\mathsf P-\mathsf S-b\), using one of the two distinct pole
edges. It is a boundary-parallel closing arc; gluing gives the
original knot in \(S^3\), with link degree two at every vertex,
including both poles. The other pole edge and the cap diagonal
are ordinary edges, with the prescribed charge one.

The cap is evaluated directly. Its row is \(N^{-2}q^i\); it is
not replaced locally by \(E_{00}\). The two free face-index sums
give \(N^2\), while all four boundary vertices become interior
and give \(N^{-4}\). Its edge powers cancel exactly. Applied to
the proved open diagonal, it gives \(N^{-1}O_\chi(0,0)\).
Combining this with \(K_{\rm open}\) and the closed factor \(N^2\)
gives the displayed complete formula.

This resolves the constructed finite-source comparison at odd
levels, including the original closing. It does not establish
invariance for arbitrary triangulations, an even-level tetrahedron
state, a positive geometric development, or transport of the
geometric integration cycle. It proves no new volume identity for
a short partial filling. In particular the general large-level
lower bound and finite-exception theorem remain open.

\[
 C_{\rm pl}=Nq^{-1}\sum_i|i,i+1\rangle\langle i,i|,\qquad
 J_{\rm pl}=N(q^{-1}-1)\sum_iq^i|i,i+1\rangle\langle i,i|.

\(i+1\). The norms are exactly \(N\) and \(N|q^{-1}-1|\).

 (R_W)_{\rm can}
   =Nq^{-2i}\delta_{j,i+1}\delta_{k,i}\delta_{l,i},

## Beta elimination with every endpoint normal retained

For one of the three actual beta sums, the
[completed elimination proof](research_literal_beta_current_and_stationary_flags.md)
sets \(g_r=W_A(r)/\overline W_B(r+L)\) and uses the invertible
Fourier-diagonal map
\[
             (B_Lf)_K=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}q^{Kr}g_rf_r .
\]
Its unit column is the previously evaluated finite beta scalar.
Arbitrary attachments use the whole map and its inverse.
The cyclic raising shift is transported to an explicit rational
clock-shift operator \(A_L\). The original truncated shift is
\((I-P)A_L\), where \(P=\mathbf1\mathbf1^t/N\); the seam
projector survives.

More precisely, the specified polynomial lift is
\(\widehat B_Lf(k)=\sum_{r<N}g_rf_rk^r\).
Writing \(\mathcal T G(k)=G(qk)\),
\[
 \mathcal R=z(1-b\mathcal T)(1-xq\mathcal T)^{-1},
 \qquad
 \chi(G)=\frac{g_0}{g_{N-1}}[k^{N-1}]G,
\]
the exact transported cyclic shift is
\[
 \widehat B_LS\widehat B_L^{-1}G
             =k\mathcal RG+\chi(G)(1-k^N).
\]
Here \(x,b,z\) are the actual root ratios specified in the proof,
including the shift \(L\). The last term is required to replace
the degree-\(N\) coefficient by its cyclic constant. It is not an
adjustable choice of continuation.

For the unit input this yields
\[
 (1-kz)G_L(k)-(x-kzb)G_L(qk)
                        =(1-x)g_0(1-k^N).
\]
At \(k=\exp(2\pi iK/N)\), every positive \(K\)-normal of the
right side at an integer \(K\) is
\(-(2\pi i)^h(1-x)g_0\). Thus equality on the finite sample
alone would lose nonzero normal data.
The proof also transports integer moments and evaluation rows
in the three actual eliminations, retaining their shared indices.
Fixed words in the displayed shift, number and endpoint operators
have polynomial norm bounds, uniformly over all finite \(L\).
This does not assert a polynomial condition number for \(B_L\)
on every possible insertion.

On compact regular fixed-log root paths, the literal beta scalars,
tetrahedral normalizations and crossing scalar \(C_N\), together
with their inverses and fixed decoration derivatives, have
polynomial upper bounds. Hence they add no exponential action
on those specified paths. Arbitrary growing deck choices and
off-root quantum deformations are not included.

The classical stationary variable is
\[
 t_*=\frac{1-k}{1-kl},
\]
with the continued primitive
\[
 \operatorname{Li}_2(kl)-\operatorname{Li}_2(k)
       -\operatorname{Li}_2(l)+\operatorname{Li}_2(1).
\]
The five flags \((\infty,0,1,k,kl)\) give its literal five-term
boundary. The divisors \(k=1\), \(l=1\), \(kl=1\) are its zero,
product-seam and infinity degenerations. These are stationary
index flags, not the auxiliary global vertex decorations.
Their global peripheral-relative assembly and the original
analytic cycle map remain unproved. In particular the remaining
boundary-dependent \(0235\) ratio in the first elimination
must still be retained; opposite labels alone do not cancel it.

## The closing cap for an inserted open array

The [marked-cap proof](research_marked_cap_for_arbitrary_open_observations.md)
extends the constructed finite comparison to a supplied arbitrary
open array \(G(i,j)\) and a prescribed bilinear covector
\(\nu(G)=\sum_{i,j}\nu_{ij}G(i,j)\). The actual bare cap has row
\(N^{-2}q^i\). Inserting
\[
            D_\nu=\operatorname{diag}_{i,j}(q^{-i}\nu_{ij})
\]
therefore gives the exact marked formula
\[
                     N^3Z_\nu(G)=\Delta_N\,\nu(G),\qquad
 \Delta_N=\prod_v N^2C_N(\mathbf s_v)q^{\phi_v}.
\]
On the common real decoration, \(|\Delta_N|=1\).
The marked normalization \(N^3\) is kept distinct from the bare
closed normalization \(N^2\).

For the original fixed-zero planar observation this coupon is
\(E_{00}\otimes E_{00}\). After a general insertion the error
in replacing the marked observation by the bare closing is exactly
\[
 \Delta_N\left\{N^{-1}\sum_{i,j}q^iG(i,j)-G(0,0)\right\}.
\]
It vanishes on the proved scalar open array, but is not asserted
zero on wall or current insertions. An averaged cut from the
original balanced representation must be supplied as its actual
covector in these coordinates. Agreement on scalar cuts alone does
not make it the fixed-zero covector.

The proof gives every face-pair entry of the coupon, including
the inverse \(f(l)\) factors and both cyclic seams. Its operator
norm lies between
\((\kappa_a\kappa_b)^{-1}\|\nu\|_\infty\) and
\(\kappa_a\kappa_b\|\nu\|_\infty\), where the two adapter condition
numbers are uniformly bounded on fixed noncollision decoration
compacts. This transports the norm of the supplied observation;
it does not bound that observation if it is itself exponentially
large. It supplies neither an identification of the full analytic
negative-ray current nor a geometric coefficient.

## Uniform ray moments, including the last physical degree

The [ray estimate](research_uniform_full_dilogarithm_ray_transport.md)
uses the original full quantum dilogarithm and its selected negative
ray. For \(0\le a<N\), let
\[
 j_{\epsilon,a}
 =-\frac{\epsilon(-1)^{N-a}}{2\pi i}
   \int_0^1\Psi_\epsilon(\log r+i\epsilon\pi)
                              r^{N-a-1}\,dr .
\]
Its exact sign and branch are retained. Put \(b=N-a\),
\(c=\log2/(2\pi)\), and \(c_0=1/(2\pi)\).
The uniform endpoint expansion is
\[
 \int_0^1\Psi_\epsilon(\log r+i\epsilon\pi)r^{b-1}\,dr
  =\frac{\sqrt2\,e^{i\epsilon N\pi/24}}{b+i\epsilon Nc}
    -\frac{\mathbf1_{b=1}}{i\epsilon Nc_0}
    +O(N^{-3/2}).
\]
The second term belongs to the endpoint at zero when \(a=N-1\).
It is not omitted or absorbed into the error.
The upper endpoint has strictly larger modulus in this last case,
so the two cannot cancel at large levels. It follows that
\[
           c_*/N\le |j_{\epsilon,a}|\le C_*/N
\]
uniformly over all physical \(a\), for sufficiently large \(N\).
The proof does not exclude zeros at the finitely many smaller levels.

The full-function remainder and its logarithmic derivative are
uniform on the relevant logarithmic strip. A cutoff at \(r=N^{-2}\)
and one integration by parts control its contribution by
\(O(\log N/N^2)\), without assuming a bounded ordinary derivative
at zero. Two integrations by parts handle \(b\le\sqrt N\).
For \(b>\sqrt N\), combining \(r^{b-1}\) with the oscillatory
phase gives a uniform endpoint estimate. These are the two
overlapping estimates behind the displayed all-degree formula.

For every nilpotent contraction \(T\), with \(\|T\|\le1\) and
\(T^N=0\), the actual ray transfer
\(\mathcal J(T)=\sum_{a<N}j_{\epsilon,a}T^a\) satisfies
\[
 \|\mathcal J(T)\|\le C,\qquad
 \|\mathcal J(T)^{-1}\|\le CN e^{C\sqrt N}.
\]
The inverse bound is a finite triangular calculation. After
removing the specified common phase and \(N^{-1}\), consecutive
coefficients differ by \(O(N^{-1/2})\), except for the last
explicit endpoint seam. Multiplication by \(1-T\) makes these
differences the coefficients of a Volterra inverse. Counting
positive compositions bounds that inverse by \(e^{C\sqrt N}\);
the last-degree seam contributes only once since \(T^N=0\).

The original reciprocal-factorial ray diagonal has norm \(O(N^{-1})\)
and inverse \(O(N)\); the reflected factorial ray diagonal and its
inverse are \(O(1)\). All original reflections, phases and factors
of \(N\) are kept. Fixed products of these maps and unitary
Gaussian factors are therefore subexponential in both operator
directions. Cups, projections and the prescribed closing covector
are still their actual maps; invertibility does not give a
nonzero scalar observation.

## Full ray patterns and the original exterior observation

The [ray-pattern proof](research_full_psi_ray_crossings_and_nine_cell_boundary.md)
applies the full circle/ray coefficient decomposition to the nine
actual Euler and factorial atoms of each signed crossing. It
lists every phase, reflected index and factor \(N\).
The original support barriers bound every moment order by \(N-1\)
independently of the coefficients. Thus the replacements are
valid in the complete original source, with its actual cups
and caps and all shared indices.

Every modified crossing entry is an explicit two-index finite sum
with ordinary integer inequalities, not only congruences. Four
literal Fourier sums then collapse its paired-face replacement to
one modified physical matrix entry. For a positive crossing, for
example, set
\[
 u=[-k_1],\quad v=[-k_2],\quad
 a=[k_3-1],\quad b=[k_4-1].
\]
The boundary array is exactly
\[
 C_N q^{3(h_1-1)/2}s_{05}^{N-1}N^2q\,x^{b-u}
          \left(\prod_m f_m(k_m)\right)M_{v,u;a,b}.
\]
The negative crossing has its separately derived rotation and
inverse phase; its total sector phase is exactly zero.
No estimate for an inverse crossing is used in these direct
replacement formulas.

On fixed noncollision real decoration compacts, the full
eight-face norm is comparable to \(N^2\|M\|_{\rm HS}\).
For the pattern with rays at every atom,
\[
 \|M_{\rm ray}\|\le CN^{-3},\qquad
 \|M_{\rm ray}^{-1}\|\le CN^6e^{C\sqrt N}.
\]
There are three reciprocal diagonals, three reflected factorial
diagonals and three transfers. Their literal products prove
these estimates. The resulting eight-face arrays have a uniform
upper bound and a subexponential lower bound for their norm.
Neither is a lower bound for their signed exterior pairing.

That exterior is explicit as well. The proof prints the original
averaged braid covector, every pivot, the finite remaining-word
contraction at a selected crossing, and its inverse dual on all
eight boundary faces. The four paired fibers contribute exactly
\(N^{-4}\). It does not replace an inserted averaged observation
by a fixed-zero observation or invoke whole-cut scalarity.
For a fixed \(b\)-strand word with \(c\) crossings, its entire
all-ray scalar pattern satisfies the actual bound
\[
 |P_{\rm all\,ray}|
       \le |\chi_{\beta,N}|\,C_{\rm word}N^{b-1-3c},
\]
with the original external source line \(\chi_{\beta,N}\)
still retained. No such bound is claimed for all mixed patterns.

There is now an actual first beta operation on the same ray
chains. The proof gives the finite boundary coupon and moves it
to the original exterior covector before summing the internal
beta index. Its coefficients have inverse moment degree at most
\(N-1\); the original ray measure contains \(t^{N-1}dt\).
Consequently the inner endpoints are integrable and the finite
move commutes with the original joint integral and its matched
lip boundaries. The new formula retains the full \(0235\) ratio
with arguments \(K+L\) and \(K+L-k_2\), all source scalars and
the sector phase. It is not a substitution of a ray moment
for an unrelated internal tetrahedral factor.

This supplies a comparison of the actual analytic ray pattern
through that finite move while leaving the ray contours unchanged.
It does not identify them with a positive geometric contour,
bound every mixed pattern relative to the hyperbolic contribution,
or prove noncancellation of the complete source. Those remain
the critical tasks for arbitrary fixed short partial fillings.

## Polynomial transport and the complex-normal endpoint

For the original moments \(I_b\) defined above, the
[consecutive-moment proof](research_polynomial_ray_transport_and_normal_endpoint.md)
shows
\[
 |I_b-I_{b+1}|\le C N^{-2}\qquad(2\le b\le N-1).
\]
The factor \(r^{b-1}(1-r)\) vanishes at both endpoints; its second
derivative has uniformly bounded integral. Two integrations by parts
control its classical term, while one integration by parts controls
the full quantum remainder. The last seam, between \(b=1\) and
\(b=2\), remains separate.

Consequently the normalized moment differences are \(O(N^{-1})\)
away from that seam. The finite Volterra inverse now gives
\[
 \|\mathcal J(T)\|\le C,\qquad
 \|\mathcal J(T)^{-1}\|\le CN.
\]
This improves the earlier \(CN e^{C\sqrt N}\) bound. For the
all-ray crossing the inverse bound improves to \(CN^6\).
These estimates hold for the actual maps on their stated spaces;
they do not invert a cup, projection, or prescribed observation.

For \(\mathsf F_{Ka}=N^{-1/2}Q^{Ka}\) and
\(\mathcal K=\mathsf F\operatorname{diag}(j_a)\mathsf F^{-1}\),
bounded variation of the normalized coefficients and their reciprocals
also gives
\[
 \|\mathcal K\|_{1\to1},\|\mathcal K\|_{\infty\to\infty}
       \le C\log(eN)/N,\qquad
 \|\mathcal K^{-1}\|_{1\to1},\|\mathcal K^{-1}\|_{\infty\to\infty}
       \le CN\log(eN).
\]
In an actual beta transform \(B_L=\sqrt N\mathsf F\operatorname{diag}(g)\),
the weights cancel exactly in \(B_L\operatorname{diag}(j)B_L^{-1}\).
This cancellation requires the diagonal to act on that beta transform's
own input index. A general crossing insertion first needs its actual
boundary coupon.

There is also a limitation in a transverse complex direction.
Multiply the top ray integrand by \(r^{-\sigma}\), keeping its
integer lip prefactor. The resulting moment has a zero at
\[
 \sigma_{\epsilon,N}
 =\frac{\log(\sqrt2/\log2)+i\vartheta_{\epsilon,N}}{\log N}
        +O((\log N)^{-2}),
 \qquad
 \vartheta_{\epsilon,N}\equiv\epsilon N\pi/24\pmod{2\pi},
 \quad |\vartheta_{\epsilon,N}|\le\pi .
\]
The proof retains both endpoint contributions and applies Rouché's
theorem to their uniform holomorphic expansion. The original positive
Markov cell realizes this moment as a scalar multiplier of any
unchanged exterior. Thus this is a zero of a specified source group,
not a zero inferred from an auxiliary model. This Mellin parameter
has not been identified with peripheral holonomy.

## What the regular nine-cell stationary equations permit

In the [stationary calculation](research_nine_cell_regular_stationary_gate.md),
write \(U,V,T,R,S,Z\) for the six rescaled numerator shapes and
\(A,B,C\) for the three denominator shapes. Exact identities among
the shared auxiliary roots cancel all auxiliary coefficients in
the six limiting stationary equations:
\[
\begin{aligned}
1-U&=TR(1-B),&
1-V&=RS(1-B)(1-C),\\
1-T&=US(1-C),&
1-R&=UV(1-A),\\
1-S&=VT(1-A)(1-B),&
1-Z&=(1-A)(1-B)(1-C).
\end{aligned}
\]
On the regular chart all nine shapes are finite, nonzero, and
different from one. Put
\(P=U+T-1\), \(D=U+R-1\), and \(H=U-1+TR\).
Elimination gives
\[
 V=\frac P{UT},\quad S=\frac D{UR},\quad
 A=\frac H P,\quad B=\frac H{TR},\quad C=\frac H D,\quad
 Z=\frac{UH}{PD}.
\]
The denominators are nonzero under the stated hypotheses.
It follows that \(RSZ=A\), \(UVSZ=B\), and \(TVZ=C\).
Comparing these with the physical boundary monomials forces
\(\kappa_1=\kappa_2=\kappa_4=1\), hence also \(\kappa_3=1\).
For finite nonzero limits of the actual commuting shifts, the
associated shared meridian matrices are then \(-I\).

This excludes a noncentral geometric meridian from this regular
interior stationary chart. It does not exclude pole residues,
degenerate shapes, singular shift limits, or the completed signed
source. It gives no license to discard these boundary terms.

direct sources: \(\texttt{5aeecb0c}\), \(\texttt{495a2fde}\), and
\(\texttt{dcab795c}\). No mathematical programs were used.

## The finite boundary chart and its original residue

The [boundary calculation](research_nine_cell_pentagon_boundary_and_residue.md)
retains the finite level before taking any stationary limit.
All shared-root coefficients cancel from the exact consecutive
ratios after rescaling the shapes. The resulting rational chart
contains the factors \(Q,Q^2\) in the actual boundary monomials;
no finite nonzero limit of the auxiliary roots is required.

On the stated generic boundary-clock chamber, every entirely finite
limit of ratio-one points has
\[
 Z=A=B=C=0,\qquad
 R=(1-U)/T,\quad S=(1-T)/U,\quad
 V=(U+T-1)/(UT)
\]
on its torus part. The proof also includes all finite zero cases.
It gives the first normal equations when \(Z\) and \(U-1+TR\)
are of order \(Q-1\). Other scales and infinite-shape charts remain
outside that normal calculation. On the continued positive branch
the restricted phase is constant, and its fixed-log \(W(0)=1\)
normalization has value zero. This surface therefore cannot simply
be declared the physical three-parameter crossing action.

The actual finite elimination has a different, exact residue
description. For \(a^N\ne1\), an integer \(n\), and \(r=[-n]\),
\[
 \omega=\frac{Na^r\xi^{N-r-1}}
                 {(\xi^N-a^N)(1-\xi)}\,d\xi
\]
is regular at zero and infinity. Its residues at
\(\xi=aQ^v\) are \(Q^{nv}/(1-aQ^v)\). Thus the positively
oriented sum of sampling circles is equivalent, for this
differential, to the negatively oriented circle about \(\xi=1\).
For an arbitrary finite attachment, expand
\(Q^{nv}H_v=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}c_rQ^{-rv}\). The same identity retains
its full observation:
\[
 \sum_v\frac{Q^{nv}H_v}{1-aQ^v}
       =\frac{N}{1-a^N}\sum_r c_ra^r.
\]
This is the actual \(1345\) resolvent in the nine-cell evaluation.
It is a rational sampling identity, not an asserted deformation
of the original full-dilogarithm ray.

The subsequent coefficient calculation retains both ordinary
totals \(N-1\) and \(2N-1\). Their equality gives the otherwise
missing factor \(\beta_{0345}^{-N}\). With the original prefactor
unchanged, the remaining packet is exactly
\[
 c(\mathbf k)=
 Q^{Jv}\frac{p_{u+v}p_{J+u}}{p_vp_up_J},\qquad
 J,u,v\ge0,\quad J+u,u+v\le N-1.
\]
Its actual positive and negative crossing entries are
\[
 (M_+^0)_{u+v,J;\,J+u,v}=x^{-J-v}c(\mathbf k),\qquad
 (M_-^0)_{J,N-1-v;\,N-1-u-v,J+u}
       =x^{N-1-u-J-v}c(\mathbf k).
\]
The coefficients are complex. The retained factorials and phases
give the existing five-shape primitive, rather than a new
nonnegative state sum. The new statement locates its boundary
residue representative in the nine-cell source. It supplies no
lower bound after closing an arbitrary short component.

## A polynomially invertible matching transport on the full physical source

The [matching-unit proof](research_full_radical_matching_unit_transport.md)
retains both values and first derivatives in the original physical
algebra \(\mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N)\). Write
\(d=N-1\), \(m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), \(\eta=(-1)^d\), and
let \(c_a\), \(0\le a<m\), be its double roots. The normalized
nilpotents
\[
 \delta_a=\frac{\eta P_N(z)}{N^2(z-c_a)},\qquad
 \phi_N(\delta_af)=f(c_a),\qquad \delta_a\delta_b=0
\]
are part of the full physical source, not ordinary-color projectors.
Use the positive coordinate norm with orthonormal coordinates
\(f(c_a)\), \(\eta(4-c_a^2)f'(c_a)\), and the odd simple value.
Multiplication by each \(\delta_a\) then has norm one.

The high-index kernel has the exact expansion
\[
 H(z,w)=\sum_{a,b<m}W_{ab}\delta_a(z)\delta_b(w).
\]
There is an inverse-kernel identity on the double-node value grid:
\[
 E_{ar}=e_r(c_a),\qquad
 G_{ab}=K(c_a,c_b),\qquad
 G=EE^{\mathsf T},\quad W=G^{-1}.
\]
Here \(G_{ab}\ge1\), and the earlier coefficient bound gives
\(|W_{ab}|\le4m\). No polynomial condition number for \(G\)
is assumed.

For any chosen same-index edge \(e=vw\) whose endpoints are
actually traced, set
\[
 V_e=\sum_{a,b<m}\frac{W_{ab}}{G_{ab}}
                   \delta_a^{(v)}\delta_b^{(w)}.
\]
The quotient in this formula is entrywise. Then
\[
 K_e=K_{<,e}(1+V_e),\qquad V_e^2=0,\qquad
 V_eV_f=0\quad\text{if the edges meet}.
\]
Consequently, for the fixed chosen multigraph,
\[
 U=\prod_e(1+V_e)
   =\sum_{M\ {\rm matching}}\prod_{e\in M}V_e,\qquad
 U^{-1}=\sum_{M\ {\rm matching}}(-1)^{|M|}
                            \prod_{e\in M}V_e.
\]
If \(\nu\) is its matching number, both multiplication operators
have norm at most
\(\sum_M(4m)^{|M|}=O(N^\nu)\).
Thus the complete array and the low-index array are related
in both directions at polynomial cost, with no separate absolute
estimate of each high-index correction.

The comparison retains every attachment and signed crossing:
\[
 F=UF_<,\qquad
 \ell(F)=(\ell U)(F_<).
\]
The proof gives the entire transported closing row as a finite
matching polynomial on every physical color assignment, including
every mixed first derivative, crossing chirp, and odd simple value.
Its highest-normal components remain specified. There is no
replacement by a positive norm or a different trace.

This nilpotence has a precise boundary. It applies to the fixed
network after imposing the original algebra relation at traced
vertices. Ordinary free-boundary variables remain unreduced.
A later turn can send \(\delta_0=e_d\) to \(1\), so the radical
cannot be discarded before subsequent tangle operations.
Likewise, fixed crossing powers act by polynomially bounded shears
on these full jets:
\(\|M_{R^{\pm n}}\|\le1+|n|N\).
The raw tensor norm therefore has the same exponential rate for
different fixed powers; the scalar observation still carries
the filling-dependent cancellation.

### Near-identity transport with scaled first derivatives

The [scaled-jet corollary](research_semiclassical_matching_unit_corollary.md)
uses the same full physical algebra and closing, with local coordinates
\[
          f(c_a),\qquad j_a(f)/N
\]
and the unchanged odd simple value. Let \(\|\cdot\|_{\rm sc}\)
be their tensor Hilbert norm. Multiplication by \(\delta_a\)
has norm \(N^{-1}\), so the exact matching factors satisfy
\[
 \|V_e\|_{\rm sc}\le\frac{4\lfloor N/2\rfloor}{N^2}
                      \le\frac2N .
\]
The matching formulas for both \(U\) and \(U^{-1}\) therefore give
\[
 \|U-I\|_{\rm sc},\ \|U^{-1}-I\|_{\rm sc}
 \le\epsilon_N:=
       \sum_{\substack{M\ {\rm matching}\\M\ne\varnothing}}(2/N)^{|M|}
 \le(1+2/N)^{|\mathcal E|}-1 .
\]
For a fixed graph this is \(O(N^{-1})\), and the condition number
is at most \((1+\epsilon_N)^2\). The explicit bound also retains
its dependence on the number of chosen edges.

The original local row in these coordinates is
\((-\eta c_a,N)_{a<m}\), with the odd simple coefficient one.
Thus
\[
 \frac{\|\ell U-\ell\|_{\rm sc}}{\|\ell\|_{\rm sc}}
                    \le\epsilon_N,\qquad
 |\ell(UF_<)-\ell(F_<)|
                    \le\epsilon_N\|\ell\|_{\rm sc}\|F_<\|_{\rm sc}.
\]
Both the source and the row have been compared. The second
inequality is nevertheless absolute, not relative to the
possibly canceled scalar \(\ell(F_<)\).
Fixed signed powers satisfy
\(\|M_{R^{\pm n}}\|_{\rm sc}\le1+|n|\).
No derivative has been removed and no new inner-product formula
for the invariant is being assumed.

### An exponentially accurate analytic lift on physical windows

The [analytic lift](research_analytic_matching_unit_window_lift.md)
uses the exact unit \(U=\prod_e(1+V_e)\) above without changing its
physical data. Fix \(0<\varepsilon<4\) and a target complex compact.
On double nodes \(c_a,c_b\le2-\varepsilon\), the original positive
Newton values give, for a fixed \(\kappa>0\),
\[
 G_{ab}\ge e^{\kappa N},\qquad
 \left|\frac{W_{ab}}{G_{ab}}\right|
                  \le2N e^{-\kappa N}.
\]
The normalizing factors obey
\(|\eta(4-c_a^2)|\ge16/N^2\).
Thus all the required mixed first-derivative data of each \(V_e\)
are exponentially small, even for double nodes approaching \(-2\).
The odd simple node still has only a value.

On consecutive windows of at most \(\rho N\) distinct nodes,
the ordinary Hermite interpolation cost on a fixed complex disk is
\(\exp\{C\rho(1+|\log\rho|)N+O(\log N)\}\).
Choosing the fixed density \(\rho>0\) after the target compact and
\(\kappa\) leaves an exponential margin. Interpolating the actual
mixed derivative data gives polynomials \(v^\sharp_{e,N}\), and
\[
 \mathcal U_N=\prod_e(1+v^\sharp_{e,N}),\qquad
 \mathcal V_N=1/\mathcal U_N,\qquad
 \mathcal U_N,\mathcal V_N=1+O(e^{-\gamma N}).
\]
These are holomorphic on a buffered target domain, with the same
conclusion for every fixed derivative on a smaller compact.
Their full window jets are exactly \(U\) and \(U^{-1}\).
The reciprocal is the genuine analytic reciprocal; the finite
matching inverse is not substituted off the physical grid.

Consequently the original product-window residues satisfy both
\[
 \Phi_{\mathcal I,N}(F)
     =\Phi_{\mathcal I,N}(\mathcal U_NF_<),\qquad
 \Phi_{\mathcal I,N}(F_<)
     =\Phi_{\mathcal I,N}(\mathcal V_NF),
\]
with arbitrary original attachments, signed powers, mixed normals
and ordinary free variables retained. If a supplied local descent
period \(I_N=\int_\Gamma\omega_N\ne0\) has its nonzero Gaussian
asymptotic and
\(\int_\Gamma|\omega_N|/|I_N|=e^{o(N)}\), either analytic factor
changes it by relative \(O(e^{-\gamma' N})\).
This supplies local analytic transport, rather than an inference
from a norm comparison. It does not supply the chain \(\Gamma\)
in the original closed trace or control the complementary color
assignments, connectors and endpoint currents.

There is a useful consequence for choosing the local representative.
On the eligible product windows of the spectral repair theorem,
let \(K_N^\sharp\) be its geometric-action representative of the
full kernel. For one selected edge,
\(\mathcal V_NK_N^\sharp\) then has exactly the low kernel's
full physical window jets, with the same normalized action bound.
This follows from the two exact jet identities, rather than from
an estimate for the canonical low polynomial off the grid.
Consequently a factorial-cut collar of that canonical polynomial
is not an additional local requirement for this repaired window
source. The original closed window contour still has its exterior
sides. Patching different physical windows still requires their
actual differences, multiplied by every spectator. These global
terms are not removed by changing the local representative.

## The actual low kernel through its stationary wire fold

The [fold proof](research_actual_low_newton_fold_packet.md) treats the
original sum
\[
 K_N^{\rm low}(w,w')=\sum_{k=0}^{L}e_k(w)e_k(w'),\qquad
 L=N-1-\lfloor N/2\rfloor ,
\]
including its parity-dependent midpoint. The prior endpoint estimate
has denominator \(1-16/((w+2)(w'+2))\). Its zero is exactly the
stationary-wire fold
\[
 q_e^2=\frac{16-(w+2)(w'+2)}{(2-w)(2-w')}=0 .
\]
Here the positive stationary wire, defined by
\(\cot(\pi x_e)=q_e\), approaches \(x_e=1/2\).
This is a degeneracy of the wire projection, not an angular
filling equation or a knot classification.

Fix \(p\) in a compact positive interval, put
\[
 \epsilon_N=N^{-2/3},\quad
 w=-2-4p,\quad w'_N=-2-4p^{-1}e^{-\zeta\epsilon_N},\quad
 \kappa(p)=\frac{\pi^2}{3}(2+p+p^{-1}),
\]
and define the convergent relative period
\[
 I_p(\zeta)=\int_0^\infty e^{\zeta s-\kappa(p)s^3}\,ds .
\]
Uniformly on bounded complex normal sets and a small complex
neighborhood of the positive \(p\)-interval, the actual finite sum is
\[
 \frac{K_N^{\rm low}(w,w'_N)}
       {N^{2/3}e_L(w)e_L(w'_N)}
       =I_p(\zeta)+O(N^{-2/3}).
\]
The error has all fixed buffered \(p,\zeta\) derivatives.
The exact finite factors \(e_L\) remain in this formula.
With \(H(p)=\operatorname{arcosh}(1+2p)\), positive for real
\(p>0\), the two parities have the common normalization
\[
 N^{4/3}e^{-N[H(p)+H(p^{-1}e^{-\zeta\epsilon_N})]/2}
       K_N^{\rm low}(w,w'_N)
       =\tfrac14 I_p(\zeta)+O(N^{-2/3}).
\]
In particular
\(I_p(0)=\Gamma(1/3)/(3\kappa(p)^{1/3})>0\) on the real fold.

This is proved from exact backward ratios, not from a formal cubic
substitution. The summation layer is \(L-k=O(N^{2/3})\).
Its products have a uniform integrable bound
\(\exp(Cs-cs^3)\), where \(s=(L-k)N^{-2/3}\).
Taylor expansion of those products and a controlled Riemann sum
give the stated error and its derivatives.

The original increasing-index sum selects the positive half-line
with coefficient \(+1\). Its endpoint cannot be erased:
\[
              3\kappa(p)I_p''(\zeta)-\zeta I_p(\zeta)=1 .
\]
The right side is the retained midpoint contribution.
An ordinary homogeneous Airy equation would describe a different
source.

There is also a proved overlap with the original stationary-wire
Gaussian. Take real \(\zeta_N\to+\infty\) such that
\(N^{-2/3}\zeta_N^{5/2}\to0\). Let \(x_*\) be the actual
positive stationary point, \(H_e=-F''(x_*)>0\), and define
\(\Delta F\) by integrating the original logarithmic-ratio
derivative from \(1/2\) to \(x_*\). Then
\[
 K_N^{\rm low}(w,w'_N)
 =e_L(w)e_L(w'_N)e^{N\Delta F}
       \sqrt{\frac{2\pi N}{H_e}}\,
 \{1+O(N^{-2/3}\zeta_N^{5/2})+O(\zeta_N^{-3/2})\}.
\]
Thus the coefficient \(+1\) is established for an actual finite
source overlap, with its action constant and orientation fixed.
It is not inferred from convergence on bounded \(\zeta\)-sets.

The high-index part does not supply a second decaying half-line
pointwise. Its original physical normal contractions remain
separate coherent sums. Nor does positivity of the geometric edge
imply that this local coefficient dominates everywhere: the
archived radical-removed cutoff obstruction already rules out a
universal low-kernel packet. The full angular/current contraction
must still retain that cutoff contribution.

## Relative Stokes transport of the finite fold source

The [relative-cycle proof](research_actual_fold_relative_stokes_transport.md)
continues the actual low-kernel fold calculation, retaining its
endpoint forcing. For coverage, the cubic integral is a standard
rescaled Scorer function:
\[
 I_p(\zeta)=\pi(3\kappa)^{-1/3}
          {\rm Hi}\bigl(\zeta/(3\kappa)^{1/3}\bigr).
\]
The normalization follows directly from the
[NIST integral definition](https://dlmf.nist.gov/9.12.E20).
The classical special function is not a novelty claim. The source
comparison and its error range are the assertions needed here.

Let \(\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}\) and orient
\[
 J_k(\zeta)=\omega^k I_p(\omega^k\zeta)
    =\int_{0}^{\omega^k\infty}e^{\zeta s-\kappa s^3}\,ds,
 \qquad k=0,1,2 .
\]
Every \(J_k\) has forcing one in
\(3\kappa J_k''-\zeta J_k=1\).
Their differences are homogeneous saddle periods. The three
half-rays are independent relative classes; their sum is not
set to zero.

For \(0<\arg\zeta<2\pi/3\), the endpoint, positive-saddle and
negative-saddle periods are respectively
\[
 E=J_1,\qquad A=J_0-J_1,\qquad B=J_1-J_2 .
\]
For \(2\pi/3<\arg\zeta<\pi\), they are
\[
 E'=J_0,\qquad A'=J_0-J_1,\qquad B'=J_0-J_2 .
\]
Thus their exact transition is
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}E'\\A'\\B'\end{pmatrix}
 =
 \begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&0\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix}
 \begin{pmatrix}E\\A\\B\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The proof also gives the lower-half-plane and real-axis matrices.
It identifies the descending contours by following inverse
branches of the original cubic polynomial, including the endpoint
branch. No table of Airy connections is assumed.

The actual source \(J_0\) equals \(E+A\) in the inner sector,
and equals \(E'\) in the outer sector. Its positive-saddle
coefficient changes from one to zero. This occurs after that
saddle has become subdominant to the endpoint; it does not
contradict persistence of a strictly dominant saddle.

The comparison is resolved in actual finite kernels. For the
normalized \(\mathcal S_N\) of the fold theorem, one has
\[
 |\mathcal S_N(p,\zeta)-I_p(\zeta)|
 \le C N^{-2/3}(1+R)^B e^{CR^{3/2}},
 \qquad |\zeta|\le R\le(\log N)^{2/3}.
\]
Take \(R_N\to\infty\) with \(R_N^{3/2}=o(\log N)\).
The error is then smaller than either cubic exponential
mode, including the subdominant one. Linear combinations of
the three actual values
\(\omega^k\mathcal S_N(p,\omega^k\zeta)\), each with its own
exact finite normalization and boundary parameter, have the
corresponding descending-period asymptotics. Their transition
matrices are exact linear identities. They are not asserted
to solve the cubic differential equation at finite level.

On both sides of these walls the original edge still satisfies
\[
 \Re q_e>\sqrt{(\Re\tan(t/2))^2+(\Re\tan(u/2))^2}.
\]
All eight original shapes are therefore positive and regular.
This supplies an actual local source calculation showing why
positive shapes do not fix its saddle coefficient. The detunings
are not claimed to solve filling equations. The high-index
matching, angular/current integrals and final closing remain,
so this is not a vanishing statement about a knot invariant.

The final proof is fixed at
\(\texttt{7affecf451916ca9d403ab3a0489882d5086a42ac5b28e4dbfbf112b7208d427}\).
Complete author, peer, and root reads include all three unchanged
direct texts: finite fold \(\texttt{849e6264}\), unsummed phase
\(\texttt{b5441bb5}\), and original edge positivity
\(\texttt{da5129c7}\). No mathematical programs were used.

### Separation from the middle endpoint on actual filled paths

The [filled-path phase theorem](research_filled_path_middle_endpoint_phase_separation.md)
retains the action constant fixed by the original finite source.
Its middle polynomial has growing exponential \(e^{iNt/2}\)
at both level parities when \(\Im t<0\). Thus the actual paired
middle-endpoint action is \(i(t+u)/2\), and
\[
 \Delta(t,u)=\psi(t,u)-i(t+u)/2 .
\]
For any fixed \(H,K\ge0\) satisfying
\[
             \tanh^2(H/2)+\tanh^2(K/2)<1,
\]
put \(t=a-iH,u=b-iK\), \(0\le a,b<\pi\).
The original complete branch extends across this whole rectangle.
Its principal returns have imaginary parts strictly between
\(-\pi/2\) and \(\pi/2\). At the pure-height corner
\(\Im\Delta=0\), while
\[
 -1<\partial_a\Im\Delta<0,\qquad
 -1<\partial_b\Im\Delta<0 .
\]
Integration on the rectangle proves the calibrated inequality
\[
                    -(a+b)<\Im\Delta(t,u)<0
                     \quad(a+b>0).
\]
The intermediate points used to prove the inequality need not be
geometrically positive.

For the actual same-sign path family with \(n_v\ge3\) and
charges in \([0,1]\), the established height bound
\(H_v<23/20\) implies the rectangle condition at every edge.
Every active edge therefore has \(\Im\Delta<0\) on the full
charge cube. The all-negative mirror has the opposite sign.
This excludes a descending connection between this saddle and
this fixed middle endpoint, even where the endpoint has larger
real action. It is a restriction furnished by the actual filling
equations; the free-parameter fold example does not contradict it.

The already established wire-order and tangent-sector results
also put these actual edges away from \(q_e^2=0\). Neither that
distance nor the middle-endpoint inequality supplies a global source
coefficient. The zero endpoint is treated below. Logarithmic lifts,
aliases and the angular closing remain separate. Branching and
mixed-sign short components have not been reduced to this path family.

The final text is fixed at
\(\texttt{5e13a523b2cc7ccadc6aaf43bde0e277bafd076983a22bf0077b3e3ce9106cd5}\).
The complete final and all four direct texts were read at matching
versions: finite fold \(\texttt{849e6264}\), positive edge
\(\texttt{da5129c7}\), charge cube \(\texttt{d3806ceb}\), and real

### Separation from the zero endpoint and the two-endpoint wedge

The [zero-endpoint supplement](research_filled_path_zero_endpoint_phase_separation.md)
keeps the literal endpoint \(e_0(t)e_0(u)=1\), whose action is
zero. On the same height rectangle as above it proves
\[
 \psi(a-iH,b-iK)\in\{\Im z>0\}\cup(0,\infty),\qquad
 \Im\psi>0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ aH+bK>0 .
\]
Its real base is calibrated without an arbitrary integration
constant:
\[
 \psi(a,b)=\frac1\pi\int_a^\pi
       \operatorname{arsinh}\{\tan(s/2)\cos(b/2)\}\,ds>0,\qquad
 \psi(0,0)=4G/\pi .
\]
Along the simultaneous height path the original branches stay
regular, and
\[
 \frac{d}{d\lambda}\Im\psi(a-i\lambda H,b-i\lambda K)
       =\{H\Re r_t+K\Re r_u\}/\pi\ge0 .
\]
This derivative is strictly positive if \(aH+bK>0\). In the
remaining cases the action stays positive real: its height
derivative is real and nonnegative. These statements include
zero heights and zero real angles, with the same complete constant.

Together with the middle-endpoint inequality, every active edge
of an actual same-sign path with \(|n_v|\ge3\) therefore satisfies
\[
           0<\Im\psi(t_v,t_w)<(a_v+a_w)/2
\]
in the positive-power convention, with the mirrored inequality
for negative powers. This locates the saddle phase strictly
between the two specified endpoint phases on the entire charge
cube. It rules out both fixed-endpoint descending connections,
without a real-action dominance hypothesis.

The conclusion is about a wire with its endpoint angles held
fixed. A boundary contribution to the closed source may solve
different angular stationary equations. Its action is not
obtained by inserting the original geometric angles into the
endpoint formula. Such boundaries, logarithmic lifts, aliases
and the original closing still need a joint contour argument.
No new filling case or global lower bound follows here.

## A uniform angle comparison for wire-endpoint patterns

The [wire-endpoint proof](research_wire_endpoint_angle_comparison.md)
works on any fixed original graph with edge set \(E\), selected
vertex set \(S\), complete outside angles, signed real powers
\(n_v\), and a supplied positive unit-charge
solution \(X^*\). No new topological realization of an arbitrary
graph is inferred. Use the original angle variables
\[
 s_v=\Re t_v,\qquad g_{v,e}=\Im r_{v,e},\qquad
 \rho_v=\sum_{e\ni v}g_{v,e}-n_vs_v/2 .
\]
The ambient closed angle body has
\(|s_v|+2|g_{w,e}|\le\pi\) and its endpoint-swapped inequalities.
Let \(\mathcal E=4\sum_e(E_{P,e}+E_{Q,e})\), and define
\[
 D_*(X)=\mathcal E(X)-\mathcal E(X^*)
                     -d\mathcal E(X^*)(X-X^*).
\]
The parent rows are \(\rho_v(X^*)=-\pi\), and their full ambient
gradient is \(d\mathcal E(X^*)=\sum_vh_v^*d\rho_v\).
The Bregman remainder is nonnegative on the entire closed body,
with equality only at \(X^*\).

Delete disjoint sets \(E_0,E_m\) of wire interactions at their
specified zero or middle endpoint, and put \(D=E_0\cup E_m\ne
\varnothing\). The original endpoint actions are respectively
zero and \(i(t_v+t_w)/2\). If \(m_v\) is the number of middle
incidences at \(v\), the retained rows consequently have charges
\[
 c'_v=1-m_v/2 .
\]
Every selected vertex, its bound \(|s_v|\le\pi\), and its retained
row remain present even when it becomes isolated. This gives a
compact set of closed angle assignments, possibly empty. Their
angle action is
\[
 M_B=(|E|-|D|)\frac{4G_{\rm Cat}}\pi-\mathcal E_B/\pi .
\]
It is the real boundary critical action only when such a regular
positive critical realization has separately been supplied.

For a prescribed retained assignment, restoring the deleted
incidences to the original unit rows is possible exactly when
\[
 m_v\le
 \sum_{\substack{e=vw\in D\\\text{incidences at }v}}
                 (1-|s_w|/\pi)\qquad(v\in S).
\]
Indeed each missing incidence has the independent interval
\([-(\pi-|s_w|)/2,(\pi-|s_w|)/2]\), and their required sum is
\(-\pi m_v/2\). Loops count twice and parallel edges individually.
Every pure-zero pattern passes, with all restored incidences zero.

For any such extension \(X\), the original energy-volume identity
gives
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 M_G-M_B=\frac{D_*(X)}\pi+
                  \sum_{e\in D}\frac{V_e(X_e)}{2\pi}>0 .
 \quad}
\]
There is a single reserve uniform over all nonempty extendable
patterns and all their assignments. Let \(\delta>0\) be the
parent's minimum square-coordinate margin and
\(\kappa=(\delta/\pi)\sin^2\delta\), so
\(D_*(X)\ge\kappa\|X-X^*\|_2^2\).
Let \(v_\delta>0\) be the minimum of the unnormalized one-edge
volume \(V_e\) when its four square coordinates all have margin
at least \(\delta/2\). Then
\[
 M_B\le M_G-\varepsilon_*,\qquad
 \varepsilon_*=
 \min\{\kappa\delta^2/(4\pi),v_\delta/(2\pi)\}>0 .
\]
Away from \(X^*\) the Bregman term pays this margin. Near \(X^*\)
any one deleted edge has positive volume at least \(v_\delta\).
This proves the pure-zero comparison without assuming a
geometric solution on each retained component.

There is also an exact formula when the extension test fails.
Restore all missing incidences as zero, obtaining \(X^0\), and
write \(H_v^*=-\Im t_v^*>0\). The parent heights occur here,
rather than the heights of a re-solved boundary critical point:
\[
 M_G-M_B=\frac{D_*(X^0)}\pi+
              \sum_{e\in D}\psi(s_v,s_w)
                    -\frac12\sum_v H_v^*m_v .
\]
The real-angle function \(\psi(s_v,s_w)\) is the nonnegative
volume of the zero-incidence restored edge divided by \(2\pi\),
with its original complete constant \(4G_{\rm Cat}/\pi\).
Reflect each negative-charge boundary block before restoring
zero incidences to obtain the stronger signed identity
\[
 M_G-M_B=\frac{D_*(X^{\rm ref})}\pi+
       \sum_{e\in D}\psi(s_v,s_w)
       +\sum_vH_v^*\bigl(|1-m_v/2|-1\bigr).
\]
The last coefficient is negative only for \(m_v=1,2,3\).
If every selected count is zero or at least four, the same
uniform reserve \(\varepsilon_*\) follows even without the
original-row extension test. This is a charge reflection
argument on the angle body, not deletion of the original rows.

The theorem controls these closed angle actions. It does not
identify every actual quantum boundary current with one of them,
bound negative or singular sectors, or supply the geometric
coefficient of the closed period. The existence of the supplied
positive parent geometry must also be checked for an arbitrary
fixed short filling. These are still requirements of the
unchanged finite-exception target.

### The parent-height budget for shifted Fourier charges

There is an immediate written consequence of the same proof.
For a supplied closed retained assignment, replace its rows by
\[
 \sum_{e\notin D,\ e\ni v}g_{v,e}-n_vs_v/2
                  =-\pi(\ell_v-m_v/2),\qquad \ell\in\mathbb Z^S .
\]
Retain all angle bounds, isolated rows and the same nonempty
endpoint pattern \(D\). Define \(M_B\) by its same remaining
angle-energy formula. Reflect each negative effective-charge
vertex block, then restore zero incidences to obtain
\(X^{\rm ref}\). Energy and real-edge volumes are unchanged by
these reflections. The full ambient gradient identity gives
\[
 M_G-M_B=\frac{D_*(X^{\rm ref})}\pi+
       \sum_{e\in D}\psi(s_v,s_w)
       +\sum_vH_v^*\bigl(|\ell_v-m_v/2|-1\bigr).
\]
The first two terms are at least \(\varepsilon_*\): the
far/near argument proving that reserve uses no filling-row
constraint on the restored ambient assignment. Thus, with
\[
 B_*=\sum_vH_v^*-\varepsilon_*,
\]
one obtains
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 M_G-M_B\ge
       \sum_vH_v^*|\ell_v-m_v/2|-B_* .
 \quad}
\]
Every charge vector with weighted sum strictly greater than
\(B_*\) consequently has a strict action gap, uniformly over
its admitted closed assignments. The vectors not paid by this
bound lie in
\[
 \mathcal A_D=\left\{\ell\in\mathbb Z^S:
          \sum_vH_v^*|\ell_v-m_v/2|\le B_*\right\}.
\]
If \(B_*<0\), this set is empty. If \(B_*\ge0\), every member
obeys \(|\ell_v-m_v/2|\le B_*/H_v^*\), so it is finite.
Equality remains in the candidate set. Since all \(H_v^*>0\),
the weighted distance is proper on the integer lattice;
outside the candidate set it has a uniform positive excess
over \(B_*\). There are finitely many endpoint patterns, so
the same assertion holds after taking their finite union.

Bare finiteness of feasible angle charges was already elementary:
their bounded angle body gives
\[
 |\ell_v-m_v/2|\le
             (|n_v|+d_{E\setminus D}(v))/2 .
\]
The additional information is the parent-height action budget
and its strict quantitative loss, rather than a new finiteness
principle for the angle lattice. This concerns Fourier-charge
vectors at one fixed parent. It is not finiteness of exceptional
filling assignments. In particular arbitrary analytic aliases
have not been identified with these closed angle assignments,
nor have their amplitudes and original currents been bounded.

The underlying wire-endpoint proof is fixed at
\(\texttt{1c5abe425060f9d8f891bd72e260d912b2132b4c9ab270e813bd964551af7568}\).
The shifted-charge corollary is the additional written consequence
derived in this ledger above, rather than an alteration of that text.
Complete final and direct-source reads match the versions:
absolute calibration \(\texttt{669722d4}\), ambient supporting
identity \(\texttt{8e42b3e5}\), middle endpoint
\(\texttt{5e13a523}\), and original Newton kernel
\(\texttt{849e6264}\). No mathematical program was used.

## Moving the surviving angles using the deleted graph

The [relative-core proof](research_deleted_graph_core_endpoint_gap.md)
removes the need to preserve every surviving angle in the previous
completion test. Retain its fixed positive parent \(X^*\), complete
outside vertex set \(B\), selected vertex set \(S\), and disjoint
zero/middle endpoint sets \(E_0,E_m\). Put \(D=E_0\cup E_m\ne
\varnothing\), and let \(P\subset S\) be the selected vertices
incident to \(E_m\).

Suppose there is a set \(C\subset S\) containing \(P\) such that
every \(v\in C\) has at least two deleted incidences whose opposite
end is in \(C\cup B\). Let \(d_C(v)\) count precisely these
incidences, including both ends of a loop. The hypothesis depends
only on the graph, rather than on the powers or a particular
boundary angle assignment.

For any admitted closed boundary assignment \(X_B\), center each
block
\[
       (s_v,(g_{v,e})_{e\notin D,\ e\ni v}),\qquad v\in C,
\]
at zero. Negating one such block preserves the surviving energy:
its two edge squares are exchanged or simultaneously negated.
The midpoint with that reflection is its centered block. Convexity
therefore gives a new surviving assignment \(Y_B\) with
\[
                  \mathcal E_B(Y_B)\le\mathcal E_B(X_B).
\]
The intermediate boundary rows at vertices in \(C\) may change.
They are not constraints of this trial construction. Rows outside
\(C\) are unchanged and are unit rows, since all middle endpoints
belong to \(C\).

Restore the usable deleted incidence at \(v\in C\) as
\(-\pi/d_C(v)\), and every other deleted incidence as zero.
Each nonzero restored incidence has opposite angle zero and
magnitude at most \(\pi/2\), so all original weak square
inequalities hold. At a centered selected vertex the restored sum
is \(-\pi\); at an uncentered vertex no row has changed. This gives
an actual full parent-unit angle assignment \(X\), retaining every
selected row, including those made isolated by deletion.

The exact comparison has an additional favorable energy term:
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 M_G-M_B(X_B)=\frac{D_*(X)}\pi+
       \sum_{e\in D}\frac{V_e(X_e)}{2\pi}
       +\frac{\mathcal E_B(X_B)-\mathcal E_B(Y_B)}\pi
                         \ge\varepsilon_*>0 .
 \quad}
\]
The same parent-dependent \(\varepsilon_*\) from the preceding
proof works for every such nonempty pattern and every boundary
assignment. The first two terms have the old uniform reserve;
the third is nonnegative. No positive boundary critical point,
sign condition on the powers, or height estimate enters this trial.

The existence of \(C\) has a canonical graph test. In the deleted
graph repeatedly prune selected vertices of current degree zero
or one, while retaining all complete outside vertices as anchors.
The surviving selected set \(C_*\) is the unique largest set with
the displayed degree property. Any such set survives every
pruning sequence, and the terminal set itself has the property,
which proves order independence. A completion set containing
all selected middle endpoints exists exactly when \(P\subset C_*\).

Every pure-zero pattern passes with \(C=\varnothing\). If every
selected middle degree is zero or at least two, take \(C=P\):
its middle incidences alone supply the required degree. Thus
degree-three middle branching is covered here along with
degree-two components and all larger degrees. A middle-degree-one
vertex may also pass when zero edges provide a second connection
within the relative core. Failure of the core test is a limit of
this sufficient trial, rather than an action-gap counterexample.

This settles the entire classical boundary-angle maximum for the
stated graph class. The actual finite middle polynomial, its
second exponential, mixed normals, Fourier aliases and original
relative currents have not been replaced by this trial. Supplying
positive parent geometry for arbitrary short fillings and proving
the quantum source bounds remain separate tasks.

## The actual single-middle interface at both level parities

The [middle-leaf adapter](research_middle_leaf_half_charge_adapter.md)
retains the literal finite middle factor, rather than just its
growing exponential. Put
\[
 d=N-1,\qquad m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor,\qquad L=d-m,\qquad
 A=e_L,\qquad \chi_N=q^{d^2/4}.
\]
With the original full kernel and trace, the interface is
\[
       \mathcal L_{n,N}(\zeta)
          =\phi_N[R^n A K_N(\,\cdot\,,\zeta)] .
\]
The outside variable \(\zeta\) remains an ordinary polynomial
variable. Let \(h_{n,N}\) be the full kernel multiplied by the
Gaussian without its carrier,
\[
 h_{n,N}(z;\zeta)=
       e^{inN\arccos(-z/2)^2/(4\pi)}K_N(z,\zeta),
\]
and let \(I_{n,N}\) interpolate its values at all distinct
physical nodes. At odd levels set
\(\ell_{n,N}=[z^m]I_{n,N}\). At even levels put
\[
 Q_{\rm d}(z)=2T_m(z/2),\qquad
 \mathscr D_{n,N}=(h_{n,N}-I_{n,N})/Q_{\rm d},\qquad
 c_*=-2\cos(\pi/N).
\]
The exact full-normal identity, for every signed integer \(n\), is
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \mathcal L_{n,N}(\zeta)=
 \begin{cases}
 (-1)^mN\chi_N^n\ell_{n,N}(\zeta),&N=2m+1,\\
 2N(-1)^m\chi_N^n\mathscr D_{n,N}(c_*;\zeta),&N=2m.
 \end{cases}
 \quad}
\]
At even levels the next Newton node repeats \(c_*\), and
\(e_m=(-1)^mQ_{\rm d}/(2N)\). Its confluent coefficient is
therefore exactly the defect above. The Gaussian's derivative
at \(c_*\) is \(in/(2s_1)\), agreeing with the original crossing
normal. Thus the even formula consumes the required derivative,
rather than replacing it by value interpolation.

The existing whole-period half-charge theorem now applies to this
actual coupon at both parities. For fixed \(|n|\ge3\), every
fixed ordinary derivative has
\[
 |\partial_\zeta^k\mathcal L_{n,N}(-2\cos(u+iv))|
 \le C_kN^{a_k}
       e^{N\{M_{|n|}-c(1-\cos u)+Bv^2\}},
 \qquad |u|\le\pi,\quad |v|\le h_* .
\]
The constants depend on the fixed power. Negative powers use
the exact conjugation of the real kernel and physical crossing
data. The algebraic adapter holds also at \(n=0,\pm1,\pm2\);
this displayed analytic estimate is not claimed for those powers.

For a literal middle path whose internal original degrees are
two, internal contractions have no spectator left and equal
\[
 \phi_N(R^nA^2)=
 \begin{cases}
 R(-2)^n,&N\text{ odd},\\
 -2inR(c_*)^n/s_1,&N\text{ even}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The identity \(2s_1^2\sum_{a<m-1}(c_*-c_a)^{-1}=c_*\)
from the Chebyshev equation gives the even cancellation.
At fixed path length these factors have polynomial size.
The remaining endpoints with one retained edge transmit precisely
the coupons \(\mathcal L_{n,N}\). Multiple such coupons at a
common exterior variable stay multiplied inside its original trace.
For a retained edge directly joining two such endpoints, the
joint source has upper bound
\(CN^a e^{N\min(M_{|n|},M_{|p|})}\) when both powers have
magnitude at least three. This uses the original physical rows
and their central normal, rather than independent observations.

The proof does not bound the last exterior contraction against
an arbitrary short component. A branching middle leaf can retain
several incident kernels, producing the joint source
\[
       \phi_N\!\left[R^nA\prod_{j=1}^rK_N(\,\cdot\,,\zeta_j)\right],
                 \qquad r>1 .
\]
The one-interface theorem does not provide that joint estimate; the
joint theorem immediately below now does.
The literal middle term \(A\otimes A\) is also distinct from
the original cutoff forcing \(A\otimes e_{L+1}\).
Neither is an arbitrary quantum contour current by definition.
