## A middle factor with any fixed number of retained edges

The [joint interface proof](research_multileg_half_charge_source_bound.md)
treats the source that remains when a literal middle Newton factor
meets several original kernels. With the notation of the preceding
section, let
\[
 \mathcal C_{r,n,N}(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_r)
 =\phi_N^{(z)}\left[R(z)^n A(z)
                    \prod_{i=1}^r K_N(z,\zeta_i)\right],
 \qquad r\ge1,\quad n\in\mathbb Z.
\]
Both integers are fixed before the level grows. Only the central
variable is traced; all outside variables remain ordinary variables.
Put
\[
 \Psi(t)=\psi(t,0),\qquad \Psi(0)=M_\infty=4G/\pi,
 \qquad
 S_{r,n}(t)=r\Psi(t)+\frac{int^2}{4\pi}-\frac{it}{2}.
\]
For \(r+|n|>1\), the selected half-charge saddle is the unique cone
branch satisfying
\[
 nt_*+2ir\operatorname{arsinh}\tan(t_*/2)=\pi,
 \qquad \Im t_*<0,\quad |\Re t_*|<\pi.
\]
Write \(M^{1/2}_{r,n}=\Re S_{r,n}(t_*)\).

Every fixed ordinary outside derivative obeys the whole-period bound
\[
 |\partial^{\alpha}\mathcal C_{r,n,N}(
                   -2\cos u_1,\ldots,-2\cos u_r)|
 \le C_\alpha N^{a_\alpha}
       \exp\left\{NM^{1/2}_{r,n}
                     +m\sum_i|\Im u_i|\right\},
 \qquad u_i\in\mathbb C.
\]
In particular no outside strip restriction is needed for this upper
bound. At the complete outside assignment the proof gives a nonzero
Gaussian at both parities, with exponential rate
\(M^{1/2}_{r,n}\) and upper and lower polynomial amplitude bounds.
It obtains that coefficient from the original full-normal contour.

There is also a stronger estimate at physical outside nodes. Set
\(\tau_a=\arccos(-c_a/2)\) and \(g_a=1-\cos\tau_a\ge0\).
For every fixed multi-index,
\[
 |\partial^\alpha\mathcal C_{r,n,N}(
                         c_{a_1},\ldots,c_{a_r})|
 \le C_\alpha N^{a_\alpha}
  \exp N\left[M^{1/2}_{r,n}
          -c\sum_{i:\alpha_i=0}g_{a_i}\right].
\]
Only slots that have not been differentiated retain their Gaussian
loss. The proof does not differentiate an inequality sampled at nodes:
it interpolates in the differentiated slots and keeps the other slots
physical. This distinction is needed when subsequent traces require
mixed normals.

The even-level high correction is contracted before estimation. Its
rate is at most \((r-1)M_\infty\), and the uniform strict comparison is
\[
 M^{1/2}_{r,n}-(r-1)M_\infty
       \ge M_\infty-\operatorname{arsinh}1>0.
\]
Thus it cannot cancel the complete-outside leading term. The remaining
case \(r=1,n=0\) is exact: \(\mathcal C_{1,0,N}=e_m\). It has rate
zero and polynomial bounds, with no nondegenerate Gaussian asserted.

This replaces the earlier restriction to one retained edge and powers
of magnitude at least three. It does not supply a relative asymptotic
at arbitrary free outside parameters, a lower bound after an arbitrary
closing contraction, or a new knot filling theorem. The exterior
variables in this statement cannot be observed independently when
the diagram identifies them.

## The radical endpoint has the same selected half-charge rate

The [mixed low/radical proof](research_mixed_low_radical_coupon_trace_bound.md)
treats the second, distinct endpoint of the actual cutoff error.
With \(A=e_L\), \(B=e_{L+1}\), \(m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), define
\[
 \mathcal D_{r,n,N}(\boldsymbol\zeta)
 =\phi_N^{(z)}\left[R(z)^nB(z)
                         \prod_{i=1}^rK_N(z,\zeta_i)\right].
\]
Every outside variable remains ordinary. For every fixed
\(r\ge1,n\in\mathbb Z\) with \(r+|n|>1\), this source has the
same action \(M^{1/2}_{r,n}\) as the preceding \(A\)-source.
Its mixed physical derivatives satisfy
\[
 |\partial^\alpha\mathcal D_{r,n,N}(c_{b_1},\ldots,c_{b_r})|
 \le C_\alpha N^{a_\alpha}
 \exp N\left[M^{1/2}_{r,n}
           -c\sum_{i:\alpha_i=0}(1-\cos\tau_{b_i})\right].
\]
This improves the coarse rate \(rM_\infty\) obtained by taking
absolute values in the radical value formula.

The proof uses the literal identity
\[
 B(z)=p_N(z)A(z),\qquad
 p_N(z)=\frac{c_L-z}{s_m^2},\qquad s_m=2\sin(m\pi/N).
\]
Apply the original contour adapter to the multiplied function.
The multiplier is bounded with its derivatives on the entire
proved rectangle, so the complementary contour bounds persist.
At the selected saddle it is nonzero. At even levels its value
at the last physical node is zero; its derivative in the original
normal is retained. This kills the even high correction exactly.
At odd levels it kills the simple-node term at \(-2\).

For the complete outside assignment the common Gaussian prefactor
of the \(A\)-source remains unchanged, and its amplitude is
multiplied by \(p_N(-2\cos t_*)\). Explicitly the new amplitude is
\[
 b^B_N(t_*)=
 \begin{cases}
 -2\sin t_*\sin(t_*/2)/s_m^2,&N\text{ odd},\\
 2i\sin t_*/s_m^2,&N\text{ even}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Both are nonzero. The complete source therefore has a nonzero
leading term through both parities. The exact remaining case is
\(\mathcal D_{1,0,N}=e_{m-1}\), with rate zero and polynomial
bounds. Its nonzero physical values are confined to angles at
most \(2\pi/N\), so it also satisfies the sampled Gaussian
estimate. No saddle is assigned to this exception.

The radical value formula gives outside degree at most \(m-1\).
Interpolating only differentiated outside slots therefore retains
every undifferentiated loss. Consequently arbitrary finite mixed
products of \(A\)- and \(B\)-sources satisfy the full product and
original-trace theorem below, with the same incidence-sensitive
exterior norm and the sum of their half-charge actions.

This applies directly to the cutoff equation. If
\(\mathscr L e_j=c_je_j-s_j^2e_{j-1}\), Newton multiplication
telescopes to
\[
 (w-\mathscr L^{(z)})K_N^{\rm low}(z,w)
        =-s_{L+1}^2A(z)B(w).
\]
After the two endpoint traces with \(r,s\) attached original
kernels and signed powers \(n,p\), its exact source is
\(-s_{L+1}^2\mathcal C_{r,n,N}\mathcal D_{s,p,N}\).
Its upper action is therefore
\(M^{1/2}_{r,n}+M^{1/2}_{s,p}\), retaining the actual source
normalization. The remaining joint exterior still has to be
estimated, and this action sum has not been compared with a parent
filled volume. The theorem does not control the homogeneous
low-source solution or its global coefficient.

## Recovering the selected algebraic point from the two finite sums

The [period-ratio corollary](research_half_charge_period_ratio_geometric_coordinate.md)
uses both complete source asymptotics. For fixed \(r+|n|>1\), put
\[
 C_N=\mathcal C_{r,n,N}(-2,\ldots,-2),\qquad
 D_N=\mathcal D_{r,n,N}(-2,\ldots,-2).
\]
Both are nonzero at all sufficiently large levels. Their entire
carrier, exponential, logarithmic error and Gaussian normalization
agree. The ratio of their leading amplitudes is exactly
\(p_N(z_*)=(c_L-z_*)/s_m^2\), where \(z_*=-2\cos t_*\).
Consequently, through both parities,
\[
 \frac{D_N}{C_N}\longrightarrow
 \rho_*=\frac{-2-z_*}{4}
       =\frac{\cos t_*-1}{2}=-\sin^2(t_*/2).
\]
This is an asymptotic identity for the original sums. It is not an
exact identity for their finite-level ratio.

The limit is algebraic. Indeed let \(w_*=\exp(it_*/2)\), so
\(|w_*|>1\). On the original logarithmic branches,
\[
 e^{\operatorname{asinh}\tan(t_*/2)}
   =-i\frac{w_*+i}{w_*-i}.
\]
Exponentiating the original half-charge critical equation gives
\[
 w_*^n(w_*-i)^r=i(-i)^r(w_*+i)^r.
\]
For \(n<0\), multiplication by \(w_*^{-n}\) clears its negative
power. The resulting polynomial over \(\mathbb Q(i)\) is nonzero,
as evaluation at \(w=i\) shows. Thus \(w_*\), \(\rho_*\), and
\(z_*=-2-4\rho_*\) are algebraic. The actual period and its
unexponentiated critical equation retain the root selection.

This extracts the local critical coordinate from actual quantum
observations, with no unknown scalar normalization left in the
quotient. The polynomial above has not been identified with a
knot's \(A\)-polynomial. The result does not control a closed-knot
source or arbitrary adjacent short components.

## Retaining the interface losses in the original joint trace

The [product-and-trace theorem](research_half_charge_coupon_product_trace_bound.md)
allows any finite number of the preceding interfaces to meet shared
outside variables. A slot is one occurrence of an outside argument
in one interface. Assign every slot to a variable \(z_v\), count its
occurrences by \(q_v\), and form the ordinary product
\[
 T_N(\mathbf z)=\prod_\ell
 \mathcal C_{r_\ell,n_\ell,N}
       (z_{\sigma(\ell,1)},\ldots,z_{\sigma(\ell,r_\ell)}).
\]
Repeated occurrences within a single interface are allowed. Write
\(M_\ell=M^{1/2}_{r_\ell,n_\ell}\), with the exact exceptional
\((r_\ell,n_\ell)=(1,0)\) assigned rate zero.

For every mixed derivative \(\alpha_v\in\{0,1\}\), the physical-node
bound is
\[
 |\partial^\alpha T_N(c_{\mathbf a})|
 \le CN^A\exp N\left[
       \sum_\ell M_\ell-c\sum_v(q_v-\alpha_v)_+g_{a_v}\right],
 \qquad g_a=1-\cos\tau_a .
\]
A derivative hits one slot occurrence; it does not remove the loss
from every occurrence sharing the variable. This is why a variable
with at least two occurrences retains a loss even when its trace
uses a first normal.

Let \(E_N(\mathbf z;\boldsymbol\xi)\) be any ordinary joint exterior
polynomial, with arbitrary level-dependent coefficients and free
parameters \(\boldsymbol\xi\). If \(\mu_a\) is the original multiplicity
of \(c_a\), define its physical full-jet norm by
\[
 \|E_N\|_{N,c,\mathbf q}
 =\max_{\mathbf a,\ 0\le\beta_v<\mu_{a_v}}
 |\partial^\beta E_N(c_{\mathbf a};\boldsymbol\xi)|
 \exp\left[-cN\sum_v(q_v-1+\beta_v)_+g_{a_v}\right].
\]
At the odd simple node only the value is included. For arbitrary
fixed signed crossing powers \(p_v\), the original joint trace obeys
\[
 \left|\phi_N^{\otimes V}
       \left[E_N\prod_vR(z_v)^{p_v}T_N\right]\right|
 \le CN^{A'}e^{N\sum_\ell M_\ell}\|E_N\|_{N,c,\mathbf q}.
\]
The estimate is uniform in the exterior; no factorization of it is
assumed. All its free parameters remain ordinary.

The proof expands the exact physical residue formula
\[
 \phi_N(f)=\eta\sum_{\mu_a=2}
       [(4-c_a^2)f'(c_a)-c_af(c_a)]
        +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}f(-2).
\]
In a Leibniz term with exterior derivative \(\beta_v\), the interface
product can be differentiated at most \(1-\beta_v\) times at that
variable. Its surviving slot losses therefore pay exactly the
weight in the displayed norm. Original signed crossing derivatives,
trace coefficients and the number of physical full-jet rows cost
only fixed powers of \(N\).

This is an actual joint closing estimate. Its remaining requirement
is a bound on the particular exterior norm at the appropriate
geometric action. The theorem does not establish that bound, compare
\(\sum M_\ell\) with a parent filled volume, or give a scalar lower
bound. Thus it is not a short-partial-filling theorem.

## The original turn has a nonzero exponential cost in this norm

The [turn-gluing corollary](research_turn_gluing_cost_in_coupon_norm.md)
checks the precise operation needed to join open blocks. In the
original algebra, \(\mathsf T e_i=e_{N-1-i}\) and
\(\phi_N(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=N-1}\). If \(F=\mathsf T f\)
and \(G=\mathsf T g\), their original turn connection is
\[
 \phi_N(f\,\mathsf T g)
 =\phi_N(F\,\mathsf T G)
 =\phi_N^{(z)}\phi_N^{(w)}
       [F(z)K_N(z,w)G(w)].
\]
By comparison, ordinary output identification gives
\(\phi_N(FG)=\phi_N(fg)\). Thus the preceding product theorem
does not remove this turn by itself.

Each endpoint of the joining kernel has one interface slot.
For every fixed Gaussian constant \(c>0\), its weighted exterior
norm has the sharp rate
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
       \log\|K_N\|_{N,c,(1,1)}=M_\infty .
\]
The lower bound uses the unweighted value at the odd complete
pair or at the even last physical pair. The actual last-row
logarithm gives their rate \(M_\infty\). Tensor interpolation,
Markov bounds and the polynomial real bound on the high radical
give the matching upper bound. Normal weights cannot remove the
unweighted value channel.

There is also an exact way to keep the turned interface:
\[
 \mathsf T_z[
   \mathcal C_{r,n,N}(z,\zeta_2,\ldots,\zeta_r)]
 =
 [R(z)^nA(z)\prod_{i=2}^rK_N(z,\zeta_i)]
       \quad\hbox{in }\mathcal A_N^{(z)} .
\]
The other variables remain ordinary. This is a full physical-jet
identity in \(z\), rather than an off-grid polynomial identity.
It retains the middle factor inside the next contraction.

The norm result identifies a limitation of this proposed gluing
estimate; it does not give a lower bound on the actual contracted
scalar or contradict a possible joint source asymptotic. The next
assembly argument must retain the turn and its phases, or prove a
better estimate for the actual joint state.

## Polynomial turn cost on the actual low-degree source class

The [coherent turn-graph proof](research_low_degree_coherent_turn_graph_bound.md)
uses more information than a bound on unrestricted physical jets.
Let \(m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), and write \(a_r(f)\) for the
canonical Newton coefficients of a full original class. At odd
levels take the short data
\[
 u_N(f)=(f(c_0),\ldots,f(c_{m-1}),f(-2))^t;
\]
at even levels take
\[
 u_N(f)=(f(c_0),\ldots,f(c_{m-1}),f'(c_{m-1}))^t.
\]
There is an explicit real matrix \(B_N\), with polynomially
bounded entries, such that for every full class \(f\),
\[
 (a_0(f),\ldots,a_m(f))^t=B_Nu_N(f).
\]
The rows below \(m\) are the original bounded radical rows.
The last odd row is ordinary interpolation at the distinct
physical nodes. The last even row retains precisely the central
confluent normal. Thus no first derivative is added at the odd
simple node, and no required even normal is discarded.

For any polynomial \(p\) of degree at most \(m\), and any full
joint exterior \(E\) in the same traced variable, the exact turn is
\[
 \phi_N(E\,Tp)=u_N(E)^t\Gamma_Nu_N(p),
 \qquad \Gamma_N=B_N^tB_N.
\]
This follows from
\(\phi_N(E\,Tp)=\sum_r a_r(E)a_r(p)\), since \(a_r(p)=0\)
above \(m\). The matrix has polynomial upper bounds. It is
positive definite for the conjugated pairing, but that does not
make the original bilinear closing positive. No polynomial
inverse bound is claimed.

Apply this independently in every paired slot of a fixed tensor
graph. The exact graph contraction is a finite physical-data sum
whose edge matrices are \(\Gamma_N\). Loops pair distinct slots
of one tensor, parallel edges are allowed, and joint dependence
on all remaining variables is retained. Each contraction leaves
the degrees in other independent slots unchanged. For a fixed
signed insertion in the literal operation
\(\phi_N(R^kp\,Tq)\), the edge matrix is
\(U_{k,N}^t\Gamma_N\), where \(U_{k,N}\) is the original
value/central-normal multiplication matrix of \(R^k\).
It also has polynomial size. The edge phases are retained.

Every A-source has outside degree at most \(m\), and every
B-source has degree at most \(m-1\). The theorem therefore applies
to any fixed graph made from these actual source tensors. If
\(M_v\) is its vertex's half-charge action, with the exact
exceptional one-leg sources assigned rate zero, then
\[
 |\partial^\alpha Z_N(c_{\boldsymbol a})|
 \le C_\alpha N^{b_\alpha}
 \exp\left\{N\sum_vM_v
       -cN\sum_{\substack{h\ {\rm unpaired}\\\alpha_h=0}}
                   (1-\cos\tau_{a_h})\right\}.
\]
All internal physical values and central normals have already
been contracted. There is no extra \(M_\infty\) per internal
turn. After any identifications of the remaining slots, the
original full trace obeys the same weighted exterior estimate
as the product theorem, with action \(\sum_vM_v\).

This is a bound on an actual sector of the original graph source.
Compiling a marked vertex into its A/B source supplies one turn
on each outgoing slot. Sewing two slots by the turn leaves three
turns on their original edge, hence exactly one original kernel,
since \(T^2=1\). The identity tensorizes, including loops.
Thus untwisted sewing reproduces the original graph with an
A or B insertion at each compiled vertex.

The degree restriction must be checked before contraction.
An arbitrary extra factor depending on both incidences of an
edge can destroy it; a new multiplication or identification in
an input slot can do the same. The unmarked unit-charge source
has not been placed in this class. The theorem supplies neither
a parent-volume comparison nor a lower bound on a possibly
cancelling graph contraction.

## One low incidence on each edge suffices

The [degree-cover corollary](research_degree_cover_turn_graph_bound.md)
weakens the graph hypothesis. Let \(F_N\) be any joint tensor in
independent paired variables, and assume that on each untwisted
edge at least one incidence has ordinary degree at most
\(m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\). Its other incidence may have arbitrary
full degree. Then the same exact contraction formula holds:
\[
 Z_N=\sum_{\boldsymbol i}
 \left(\prod_{\{h,h'\}}\Gamma_N(i_h,i_{h'})\right)
 \left(\prod_h\mathcal E_{i_h}^{(h)}\right)F_N .
\]
Here every \(\mathcal E_i\) is one of the short physical data
functionals of the preceding theorem. At odd levels only values
are used. At even levels the sole additional datum at each
incidence is its last-double-node first derivative.

The proof expands the entire joint tensor before making any
estimate. An original edge equates its two Newton indices.
The low incidence kills every common index above \(m\).
This happens simultaneously on all edges, even for correlated
tensors or loops. The short coefficient adapter is valid for
the surviving indices at both ends, including the unrestricted
one. Applying it coefficientwise gives the formula and its
polynomial upper bound.

For an original graph of compiled vertex sources it is therefore
sufficient that the A/B-marked vertices form a vertex cover.
Unmarked tensors need not be replaced by marked tensors or
projected to low ordinary degree. Their actual short physical
values and central normals remain in the exact sum. Their
growth at those data is still to be estimated; the corollary
does not assign them a geometric rate.

For the oriented edge \(\phi_N(R^kf\,Tg)\), a sole low
incidence must be the \(g\) incidence. The opposite incidence
then uses \(U_{k,N}^t\Gamma_N\). Multiplying the sole low
incidence by \(R^k\) can destroy the truncation and is not
included. Untwisted edges have no such orientation restriction.

## A global source-preserving low-halfwire boundary map

The [boundary-pushforward proof](research_global_low_halfwire_boundary_pushforward.md)
works before the original wire periods are integrated. Write the
full cardinal halfwire and its literal truncation as
\[
 B(x,z)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}C_j(x)e_j(z),\qquad
 B_<(x,z)=\sum_{j=0}^{L}C_j(x)e_j(z),
 \qquad
 C_j(x)=\frac{\sin\pi N(x-j/N)}{N\sin\pi(x-j/N)} .
\]
Paired halfwires have finite integer Fourier band
\([-(N-1),N-1]\). Exact sampling gives constant mode \(K/N\)
for the full pair and \(K_</N\) for the low pair; the mixed
low/high products have zero constant mode.

At wire \(e\), let \(A_e\) be the full pair and let
\(Q_e=(1+\widehat V_e)L_e\) be the low pair multiplied by the
ordinary polynomial lift of the original matching unit.
Retain the ordinary remainder
\[
 \mathcal R_e=K_e-(1+\widehat V_e)K_{<,e}
          \in(P_N(z_v),P_N(z_w)).
\]
This is zero in the full physical tensor algebra, but can be
nonzero at ordinary free colors. If
\(A_e-Q_e=\sum_{k=-D}^{D}d_{e,k}w_e^{-k}\), then
\(d_{e,0}=\mathcal R_e/N\), and
\[
 \mathcal D_e=\sum_{0<|k|\le D}
                \frac{d_{e,k}w_e^{-k}}{2\pi i k},
 \qquad
 (A_e-Q_e)\,dx_e
   =d_{w_e}\mathcal D_e-\frac{\mathcal R_e}{2\pi iN}
                                      \frac{dw_e}{w_e}.
\]
Here \(w_e=e^{-2\pi ix_e}\), so the increasing original
period is clockwise and restores \(+K_e/N\).

Order any fixed network's wires. Telescoping their product
differences gives an explicit global form \(\Xi\) and a retained
joint ideal term \(\mathcal I\) such that
\[
 \Omega_{\rm full}-\Omega_{\rm corrected\ low}
      =d\Xi+\mathcal I .
\]
For an arbitrary wire-dependent co-source \(a\), the actual
identity is
\[
 a(\Omega_{\rm full}-\Omega_{\rm corrected\ low})
    =d(a\Xi)-da\wedge\Xi+a\mathcal I .
\]
Thus a wire insertion does not commute with this replacement
without its derivative term.

The finite Laurent primitives are periodic. Paired complete
wire faces consequently cancel even when their seams move with
the angles or other wires. Ordinary angular sides and partial
wire arcs remain. On a partial arc their contribution is the
difference of the actual endpoint primitive values. Those
values may grow at a wire escape; no bound is inferred from
the completed-period identity.

For a completed residue with an actual low-degree attached
state, the preceding coefficient calculus gives
\[
 (\phi\otimes\phi)(F K_<)=(a_m\otimes a_m)F,\qquad
 (\phi\otimes\phi)(F H)=\sum_{r<m}(a_r\otimes a_r)F .
\]
These are polynomial short-data rows under the one-incidence
degree cover, with the even central normal retained. They
bound those completed residues, not the partial primitives.
The corrected low residue remains \(K\), rather than a
deleted edge or a rank-one replacement.

## Partial-wire observations recover the full source at polynomial cost

The [boundary-observability proof](research_partial_wire_boundary_observability.md)
uses an actual original halfwire with the fixed left state \(1\).
For an arbitrary full class \(E=\sum_{r=0}^{D}a_r(E)e_r\), \(D=N-1\),
define
\[
 F_E(x)=\phi_z\phi_w[
        E(w)B(x,z)B(x,w)],\qquad
 \mathscr B_{E,N}(x)=N\int_0^x F_E(s)\,ds .
\]
The original Frobenius pairing gives exactly
\[
 F_E(x)=C_D(x)g_E(x),\qquad
 g_E(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{D}a_{D-j}(E)C_j(x),\qquad
 \mathscr B_{E,N}(1)=a_0(E)=E(c_0).
\]
Thus a complete period sees one coefficient, although the
partial boundary function retains the whole class.

At the \(N\) midpoints \(x_k=(k+1/2)/N\), the matrix
\(M_{kj}=C_j(x_k)\) is unitary at both parities. This follows
from its finite Fourier representation, including the
half-integer frequencies when a single halfwire is
antiperiodic. Moreover \(1/N\le|C_D(x_k)|\le1\).
Consequently
\[
 \sum_r|a_r(E)|^2
 \le\sum_k|\mathscr B'_{E,N}(x_k)|^2
 \le N^2\sum_r|a_r(E)|^2 ,
\]
with exact inverse
\[
 a_r(E)=\frac1N\sum_k
   \overline{C_{D-r}(x_k)}
       \frac{\mathscr B'_{E,N}(x_k)}{C_D(x_k)} .
\]
Conjugation here inverts the numerical Fourier matrix. It
does not replace the original bilinear trace by a positive
closing.

The primitive values alone are sufficient. Put
\[
 P_E(x)=\mathscr B_{E,N}(x)-x a_0(E),\qquad
 y_\ell=\ell/(2N),\qquad
 \mathscr D_N(E)^2
   =N|a_0(E)|^2+\sum_{\ell=0}^{2N-1}|P_E(y_\ell)|^2 .
\]
The periodic polynomial \(P_E\) has Fourier degree \(D\);
its \(2N\) samples therefore reconstruct it exactly.
Discrete Parseval and the anchored primitive estimate give
\[
 \|a(E)\|_2^2\le8\pi^2D^2\mathscr D_N(E)^2,\qquad
 \mathscr D_N(E)^2\le(2N^2+N)\|a(E)\|_2^2 .
\]
These inequalities apply to arbitrary level-dependent
sources. Thus the full Newton norm and this family of
actual partial-period endpoint observations have the same
limsup exponential rate.

For \(s\) opened wires the construction tensors without
factoring the exterior source. Its midpoint frame has
condition bounds \(1\) and \(N^s\) on coefficient norms.
It recovers all \(N^s\) joint Newton coefficients, so any
linear quotient retaining all those partial observations
must have dimension at least \(N^s\).

This gives an exact limit on the completed-residue
compression above. The actual class \(e_D=T1\) has zero
short data for every \(N\ge3\), including the even central
normal, but has partial density \(C_D(x)C_0(x)\ne0\).
Its complete period is zero. The degree-cover bound
therefore does not bound partial currents from short data
alone. This is an original inserted state, not a vanishing
claim for a reduced knot invariant.

The observation frame spans an entire real wire period.
It is not confined to the geometric window. Continuing it
to a fixed nonreal height can cost exponentially in \(N\);
factorial/cardinal seams on untraced angular chains remain.
No scalar lower bound or geometric growth rate is inferred.

## Putting the prescribed final trace inside the boundary frame

There is a direct application to an original remaining trace,
without inserting an unknown scalar into an artificial state.
Let \([F_N]\) be the full Hermite class of the partial source at
its prescribed final trace, and set
\[
 Z_N=\phi_N(F_N),\qquad E_N=T[F_N],\qquad
 \mathcal N_N=\|a([F_N])\|_2 .
\]
Canonical reduction here is at that actual trace; it is not
performed at an ordinary free boundary. The original turn
reverses Newton coefficients. Therefore
\[
 \mathscr B_{E_N,N}(1)=a_0(E_N)=a_D([F_N])=Z_N,\qquad
 \|a(E_N)\|_2=\mathcal N_N .
\]
The preceding endpoint-frame bounds imply
\[
 \frac{\mathcal N_N}{\sqrt8\,\pi(N-1)}
 \le\mathscr D_N(E_N)
 \le\sqrt{2N^2+N}\,\mathcal N_N .
\]
The data with \(P_E(y_\ell)\) replaced by the raw partial
periods \(\mathscr B_{E_N,N}(y_\ell)\), together with the
weighted complete period \(\sqrt N\,Z_N\), differ by a
triangular shear of uniformly bounded norm and inverse.
Thus the native source norm and this actual boundary family
have the same limsup exponential rate, with \(\log0=-\infty\).

The specified complete period remains a particular coordinate:
\(|Z_N|\le\mathcal N_N\). If \(\mathcal N_N\) is eventually
nonzero and its logarithmic rate converges to finite \(M\),
then its scalar rate equals \(M\) exactly when, for every
\(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 |Z_N|\ge e^{-\varepsilon N}\mathcal N_N
 \quad\hbox{for all sufficiently large }N .
\]
Equality of limsups alone is weaker. The boundary-frame theorem
does not prove this projection bound, identify \(M\) with a
hyperbolic volume, or identify auxiliary partial periods with
ordinary main-knot colors.

This corollary follows from coefficient reversal and the entire
observability proof at \(\texttt{8bfeabd5}\). Root and independent
peer checked every displayed implication, including the actual
trace reduction and the distinction between limits and limsups.
No frozen proof was edited.

## Exact branching forcing retains the actual child closures

The endpoint forcing in a source recurrence is not an independent
nonzero normalization. Let
\[
 \mathscr L e_j=c_je_j-s_j^2e_{j-1},\qquad
 \eta=(-1)^{N-1},\quad D=N-1,\quad S_D^2=N^2 .
\]
The original canonical turn satisfies the ordinary free-output identity
\[
 w\,TF(w)-T(\mathscr LF)(w)
     =\frac{\eta}{N^2}P_N(w)F(c_0).
\]
For \(j>0\) this follows by applying Newton multiplication to
\(Te_j=e_{D-j}\). For \(j=0\) the remaining term is
\((w-c_0)e_D=\eta P_N(w)/N^2\). This proves the identity
coefficientwise for every original full class, with all free
parameters retained. The factor \(P_N(w)\) is not dropped at an
ordinary free boundary.

In a rooted original \(K_T\)-tree, write
\[
 F_v=\operatorname{can}\left(
       R^{n_v}\prod_{j\ {\rm child}}H_j
                  \prod_bK_T(\,\cdot\,,w_b)\right),\qquad
 H_j=TF_j,\quad Z_j=\phi_N(F_j).
\]
Since \(K_T(c_0,w_b)=1\) as an ordinary identity and
\(H_j(c_0)=Z_j\), the actual forcing coefficient is
\[
 F_v(c_0)=\kappa^{n_v}\prod_j Z_j,
 \qquad \kappa=R(c_0).
\]
The prescribed parent closing is instead
\(H_v(c_0)=\phi_N(F_v)\).

These data can differ even on a literal source. A child \(F_1=1\)
has \(Z_1=0\), while a parent with this child and power \(n\) has
\[
 F_v=R^ne_D=\kappa^ne_D,\qquad H_v=\kappa^n1,\qquad
 Z_v=\kappa^n\ne0.
\]
Thus one cannot divide by the product of child closures or
declare the endpoint forcing a unit. This example concerns the
original local trace states, not a counterexample to a hyperbolic
knot volume identity.

## The surviving framing direction cannot be removed by a positive metric choice

Here is a direct linear-algebra consequence of the
paid principal stationary scheme. A complex symmetric
Hessian of rank \(r\) on complex dimension \(n\)
has, after complex congruence, matrix
\(\operatorname{diag}(I_r,0)\). For any nonzero
complex phase scaling, the associated real quadratic
form has inertia \((r,r,2n-2r)\). Hence no real
negative-definite subspace has dimension greater
than \(r\). In particular, if \(r<n\), its real
part is not negative definite on any real
middle-dimensional \(n\)-plane.

The soft principal phase retains the nonzero
complex centralizer tangent. Thus changing
positive coherent spheres cannot by itself
produce a full nondegenerate Gaussian maximum.
This includes the product-cycle tangent choices
in the complete
[adapted-polarization source](research_actual_coherent_polarization_transport.md).
That source already proves exact cycle changes
and their possible exponential metric cost;
those identities are not new here.

The conclusion is about this principal Hessian.
It does not forbid a transverse Morse--Bott
calculation with a genuine relative fiber period,
or additional control from subprincipal source
terms. A source-compatible treatment of that
fiber is needed before a transverse Rivin
Hessian can establish noncancellation.

the source reviewer independently checked it.

## The translated domains give a complete Fourier expansion with controlled tails

The [Fourier expansion theorem](research_oblique_top_fourier_aliases.md)
now rewrites the exact contour decomposition as
\[
 K_N=\sum_{\sigma\in\{\pm1\}^m}
       \sum_{r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^m}
 \int_{T_{\sigma,N}} I_N(z)
       e^{-2\pi i(q_\sigma-\sigma r)\cdot z}\,dz
       +\mathcal B_N,
 \qquad q_\sigma=q+\frac{\epsilon-\sigma}{2}.
\]
Here \(T_{\sigma,N}\) are the actual translated bulk
domains. The complete boundary-band, mixed-facet and
side-current integrals remain in \(\mathcal B_N\);
they are not an estimated error.

This is an exact Fourier expansion, obtained by
expanding the polarized cotangent denominators.
The charges \(q_\sigma-\sigma r\) partition
\(\mathbb Z^m\) without repetition. Each integral
has coefficient one. The geometric charge is
\(\sigma=\epsilon,\ r=0\), on the domain passing
through the geometric point. This coefficient is
not its local steepest-descent cycle coefficient.

The common nonreal framing also gives a uniform
factorial and ordinary-binomial expansion on the
entire translated top domains. Every length stays
in a fixed compact slit chart there. The full
amplitude is a holomorphic unit, with the literal
finite \(N-1\) binomial correction retained.
The absolute integral for each orthant's base
charge is bounded by \(CN^p e^{C_*N}\).

The extra Fourier index \(r\) has a uniform kernel
penalty \(e^{-\gamma N|r|_1}\), with \(\gamma>0\)
fixed by the selected heights. Consequently
\[
 \sum_{|r|_1\ge R}
       |\text{corresponding Fourier integral}|
 \le CN^p e^{C_*N}
       \frac{e^{-\gamma NR/2}}
            {(1-e^{-\gamma N/2})^m}.
\]
For every prescribed \(\Lambda>0\), a fixed finite
cutoff \(R\), independent of \(N\), makes the
discarded charge tail \(O(e^{-\Lambda N})\).
Thus the infinite bulk charge family has been
reduced to finitely many explicit integrals at
any requested exponential accuracy.

This does not estimate \(\mathcal B_N\), prove
positivity of any Fourier integral, or integrate
the geometric centralizer direction. In
particular it is a finite-charge theorem, not
the sought finite-exception theorem for fillings.

## The actual factorial function has an affine Legendre test

The [affine source proof](research_affine_legendre_actual_checkerboard_function.md)
rewrites the same checkerboard summand exactly using the normalized
factorial interpolant, with every Gaussian, pivot and endpoint
factor retained. At each crossing its five logarithmic rows are
\(U,U,Z,Z,2\pi i-U-Z\). The last row uses the exact factorial
shift; its compensating factor \(1-e^{-U-Z}\) remains in the
amplitude, including its removable endpoint value. The scalar
function being tested matches the original summand exactly.

The general theorem covers
\[
 W(x)=\sum_j\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{A_jx+ia_j})
             +\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+i\kappa^{\mathsf T}x+c,
 \qquad \operatorname{rank}A=\dim x,
\]
with real symmetric \(H\) and the retained real constant \(c\).
Writing \(\alpha=A\theta+a\), a proper radial minimum exists
precisely when
\[
 0<\alpha<\pi,\qquad
 -H\theta-\kappa\in
       \operatorname{int}\left(A^{\mathsf T}
                       \prod_j[0,\pi-\alpha_j]\right).
\]
Its value is the maximum of the sum of positive tetrahedron
volumes over the corresponding constrained beta-angle fiber.
The proof gives uniqueness, strict concavity, a nonzero contour
Jacobian and a calibrated compact radial homotopy. It extends the
individual-shape contour construction to rectangular affine
systems, including the actual factorial rows just obtained.

The test also detects a universal obstruction in this particular
source chart. For its displayed potential with zero added Fourier
character, the outer braid strand supplies a nonzero integral
circulation on which the zonotope support gap is exactly zero.
The gap telescopes around that actual strand for every point
of the positive-shape chamber. Thus this marked potential has
no finite radial minimum or interior critical point there.
A finite radial escape and its endpoint layer remain; positivity
of all five shape arguments is insufficient.

This does not exclude the original source's other logarithmic
characters. Adding the retained character \(2\pi i\,n\cdot x\)
shifts the support target. For the exterior circulation \(h\),
strict feasibility requires
\[
 0<2\pi n\cdot h<
 \sum_{j\in I}\left[\pi+\varepsilon
                       (\theta_{Z_j}-\theta_{U_j})\right].
\]
Here \(I\) is the exterior set of crossings, all of sign
\(\varepsilon\). Each retained character must carry its original
coefficient and cycle. Those coefficients,
the source's finite residue cycle and its endpoint currents still
require comparison. No knot-volume case or short-filling stability
theorem is added.

\[
 R(\xi,\eta)=-J(\eta-\xi)-J(\tau-\eta)-J(1-\tau+\xi),
 \qquad J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds.
\]
Thus \(\pi R\) is the strictly concave volume of the ideal
tetrahedron with angles \(\pi(\eta-\xi)\),
\(\pi(\tau-\eta)\), and \(\pi(1-\tau+\xi)\).
For any prescribed point a
fixed distance from the physical edges, explicit real weights
\(\lambda,\mu\) make
\(R+\lambda\eta+\mu\xi\) attain its unique global maximum there.
The entire capped matrix
\(Y=\operatorname{diag}(e^{\mu c})X\operatorname{diag}(e^{\lambda a})\)
then satisfies a Gaussian bound with the correct power of \(N\).

 c|\kappa|e^{NS_*}\le\|Yb\|_2\le\|Y\|_2

The incoming error is paid by the matching upper and lower norm

The [complex packet proof](research_opened_generator_complex_clock_packet.md)

\[
 \mathcal P_N(z)=\kappa e^{iN\vartheta_N(v_*)}
      e^{N\Phi_z(v_z)}
      \frac{(2\pi)^{3/2}a(v_z)}{\sqrt{\det[-\Phi_z''(v_z)]}}
      (1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
Here \(v_z\) is the unique nearby critical point, \(a\) is an
explicit holomorphic unit, and the determinant branch is fixed by
the oriented real Gaussian. The map \(z\mapsto v_z\) is locally
biholomorphic, with an explicit inverse. In particular its total
coordinate can have a nonzero imaginary part.

proof uses the exact sine-factorial and Gamma interpolants on a
protected complex cube. A finite cotangent-residue formula retains

 \frac{\mathcal P_N[K_{\rm tot};z]}{\mathcal P_N(z)}
       =x^2e^{-2\pi i\tau_z}(1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
Thus the selected total-clock value need not be unimodular. This
is a bilinear matrix-element statement with an algebraic output
row; it makes no positive-state spectral assertion. Original
annular partial resolutions containing the four packet supports

## The two Gauss factors now fuse before taking the meridian limit

The [whole-meridian fusion proof](research_complementary_gauss_meridian_fusion.md)
proves an exact source identity at every fixed width \(r\ge2\) and

actual reflected Gauss factor \(A_-(M)\) with the actual transported
complementary-degree factor \(B_+(M)\). The coefficient meridian in
the latter remains \(M\), while its underlying representation has
meridian \(M^{-1}\). This distinction is kept before differentiation.

Put \(d=N-1\), \(m=r+1\),
\(k_0=(-q^{-1})^rQ^{-T}\), and let \(\Theta_-(M)\) be the
original physical full twist at reflected meridian with precisely
its common crossing scalars removed. The identity is
\[
 A_-(M)B_+(M)\Theta_-(M)
   =a_N(M)D_N(M^m k_0^{-1})\,
                         \omega_{r,T,N}(M)I,
\]
where \(D_N(z)=(z^N-z^{-N})/(z-z^{-1})\), \(a_N\) is the
original opposite-source scalar, and
\[
 \omega_{r,T,N}(M)
   =k_0^{-1}Q^{T(T+r-1)}M^{r(2T-d)}
                          \left(\frac N{D_N(M)}\right)^r.
\]
The scalar frame and its inverse are uniformly bounded on any fixed
scaled disk \(M=e^{u/N}\), \(|u|\le\eta<\pi\), at fixed width.
Its actual first logarithmic derivative is \(r(2T-d)\); it is
not removed from the original finite part.

highest string. Their lengths are \(T-j\) and \(N-1-(T-j)\),
both in the physical range even when \(T>N-1\). Their reflected
intervals cover exactly one root orbit with one factor removed.
The actual full twist cancels the remaining integer label. The
generic calculation includes every multiplicity and extends as an
identity of analytic finite matrices, retaining all root Jordan
blocks. No inverse norm or off-grid scalar interpolation is used.

For regular Cartan blocks \(k_0^2\ne1\), the root product vanishes
but its genuine combined first normal is completely specified:
\[
 A_0B_1-A_1B_0
   =\frac{2mN^2Q^{T(T+r-1)}}{1-k_0^2}\,\Theta_-(1)^{-1}.
\]
Here \(A_1\) uses the positive-meridian low-factor derivative, and

blocks the root product is nonzero, and the separate formula retains
the full-twist derivative. Thus this is a whole-meridian result,
stronger than differentiating a root factorization or choosing an
inverse on a primary quotient.

An inserted matrix still has its exact ordered commutator term.

The [complementary boundary proof](research_complementary_gauss_boundary_branches.md)
calculates the actual high-degree Gauss factor after the exact
turnover and degree transformation. At every fixed width its first
column reduces to an effective highest-weight factor and the last
physical head. A finite telescoping identity gives a first-order
recurrence through every physical coefficient, including the final
one. No denominator at a resonant split sum is inverted.

\(\chi=Q^{-H^2}\). The exact normalized column is
\[
 G_T(\rho)=\left[
   \mathfrak g_T(C\rho)-\chi\frac{\mathfrak g_T(\rho)}
                               {(Q^{1-H}\rho;Q)_H}
                \right]_{\le T}.
\]
Both terms and the physical Taylor cutoff remain. Their phases are
zero and
\(\psi(\rho;C)=[\operatorname{Li}_2(\rho)
-\operatorname{Li}_2(C^{-1}\rho)]/(2\pi i)\), with explicit
nonzero amplitudes on a small disk. On strict sectors one term has
a proved exponential advantage. On the equal-rate set the difference
must be retained. In particular the actual vacuum contains
\(1-Q^{-H^2}\) and vanishes at infinitely many physical levels
even with \(H/N\) in a fixed strict angle chamber. This is a
matrix-entry cancellation, not a vanishing knot invariant.

The all-width connection is a fixed Taylor remainder of the same
reciprocal-product branch with \(H\) shifted by \(r-2\), plus
explicit polynomially bounded zero-phase terms. The physical prefix
lift is a divided difference; it kills the finite Taylor subtraction
exactly. This yields a nonzero actual boundary on separated sectors
with a strictly winning positive rate. It does not give a zero-free
whole polydisk or a full two-sided kernel.

The [normal decay proof](research_actual_gauss_normal_decay_tube.md)

 \mathcal K_B(\rho,\zeta)=G_N(\zeta)a_N(\rho,\zeta)+O(N^{-1}),

\]
Here \(G_N\) is the actual root column, \(C=Q^{-T-1}\), and
\(\lambda_G(0)=2C\). The annulus excludes zero; the second disk
is chosen after its buffers and the fixed exponential accuracy of
an analytic particular solution. On compact negative-activity
subsets of that disk, both the symmetric and physical matrix normals
are \(O(N^{-1})\), in the stated fixed vacuum normalization.

normal is \(1/\rho+O(N^{-1})\); differentiating the symmetrizing
gauge leaves \(1/(2\rho)+O(N^{-1})\) as the symmetric boundary.
The retained axis forcing propagates it in the microscopic layer as
\[
 \mathcal K_B(\rho,w/N)
      =\frac{e^{2w/(2\pi i)}}{2\rho}+O(N^{-1}).
\]
Thus the constant term obtained by extending the first-column normal
homogeneously is not the leading term of the actual full normal in
this region. The proof uses the exact finite forced clock equation,
an optimally truncated analytic particular solution, and direct
propagation from the actual boundary. Weighted Cauchy estimates on
nested annular domains control that propagation without an inverse
whose norm might grow exponentially. A separate reduction of the
evaluation disk controls every remaining finite coefficient.

small bound or a bound relative to the exponentially small root
kernel. It does not cover every product decay sector. The original

## The original binomial input is controlled on the full fixed-width boundary

The [coherent-boundary proof](research_fixed_width_gauss_coherent_boundary.md)
sums the original binomial input before making an approximation. It
applies to every fixed number \(r\ge2\) of remaining tensor factors,
with \((T+1)/N\) in a compact subset of \((1/2,1)\). It estimates
the actual vacuum row of \(A_N^{(r)}\) paired with that entire input.

The exact contraction is one constant-term integral
\[
 \mathcal C_{r,N,T}(\xi)=\operatorname{CT}_t G_r(t)
       \mathcal B_{r,N,T}(\xi_1/t,\ldots,\xi_{r-1}/t),
\]
where \(G_r\) is the actual normalized first-column polynomial
and
\[
 \mathcal B_{r,N,T}(z)=\binom{N-1}T^{-1}
      [u^T](1+u)^{N-1}\prod_{i=1}^{r-1}(1+uz_i)^{N-1}.
\]
Both expressions are finite. Thus all magnetic input indices have
already been summed, including their original binomial weights and
caps. No relative error from a monomial approximation is transformed.

Let \(p=r-2\), \(a=2/(2\pi i)\), \(b=(T/N)/(1-T/N)\), and
write \(\xi_i=\vartheta_i a_*^2/(ab)\), where the bounded complex
shape parameters satisfy \(\sum_i\vartheta_i=1\). On compact
subsets of a sufficiently small punctured sector
\(|\arg a_*|<\theta_0<\pi/3\), the actual boundary has a nonzero
asymptotic of the form
\[
 \mathcal C_{r,N,T}=N^{-p}
       \frac{e^{N\Psi}}{\sqrt{2\pi N\mathcal H}}
              A_r^\partial(t_*)A_B(\xi/t_*)\,(1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
Here \(\Psi=2a_*+O(a_*^2)\), \(\mathcal H=2a_*+O(a_*^2)\),
and both amplitudes are explicitly fixed nonzero functions. The
unscaled row still includes exactly
\(a_{00}^{(r)}z_r^T\binom{N-1}T\).

The sector restriction is necessary for this proof. The whole outer
circle has two bounds to compare: the selected exponential has rate
\(2\Re a_*+O(|a_*|^2)\), whereas the competing vacuum term has
rate at most \(|a_*|+O(|a_*|^2)\). The former dominates uniformly
only in a sector strictly narrower than \(\pi/3\). This comparison,
together with the actual inner coefficient-circle estimate, pays the
entire complementary contour. Its Gaussian coefficient is one.

This theorem concerns the full coherent vacuum boundary. The reverse
propagation theorem above now extends it to nonzero output activities
on a specified local domain. Neither theorem by itself proves a
meridian-normal, complex-degree or original closed-source conclusion.

The [marked functional-calculus proof](research_marked_gauss_functional_calculus.md)
passes from scalar reconstruction to an exact identity on the original
quantum representation. It covers every physical channel, including
the endpoint values and Casimir Jordan blocks, before taking meridian
derivatives. This is an algebraic and analytic definition result;
it does not supply a coherent-kernel or closing-functional estimate.

At a physical joint Cartan--Casimir value, the two auxiliary roots
have the form \(\{u,v\}=\{Q^l,Q^k\}\), with \(0\le l,k<N\).
The prescribed logarithms take the values \(x=l/N,y=k/N\).
On these fixed-\(N\) germs, exact finite-shift identities show
\[
 \mathcal S_N(u,v;c)-\mathfrak b_N(x,y;\mu)
       =(1-u^N)(1-v^N)\mathfrak r_N(u,v;\mu),
\]
with a holomorphic quotient. Symmetric descent includes \(u=v\).
The actual matrix identity
\[
 (1-u^N)(1-v^N)=K^{-N}W_N(K,\Omega)=0
\]
then annihilates the complete difference, including all Jordan
and moving-meridian terms. No large-degree principal-symbol
substitution is used.

There is an exact description of the zero channels as well.
If \(n=l+k<N\), the full localized Gauss matrix is a root unit.
If \(n\ge N\), it is \(1-M^{-2mN}\) times a holomorphic
invertible matrix. Grouping whole colliding Casimir clusters gives,
at each fixed \(N\),
\[
 A_N=\mathfrak G_N\bigl[(I-P_{\rm up})
                     +(1-M^{-2mN})P_{\rm up}\bigr],
\]
where \(\mathfrak G_N\) is holomorphic and invertible.
The projector groups these primary zero channels; it is distinct
from the upper Fourier coefficient sector. No uniform conditioning
or lift to an original total-intertwiner projector is asserted.

The marking cannot be suppressed. An individual logarithm deck
can have a genuine simple meridian pole on an actual double
Casimir block, with opposite radical residues for the two decks.
Their simultaneous shift has the regular scalar multiplier
\[
 d_{{\rm deck},N}(M)=
 \frac{1-M^{-2mN}}{1-M^{-2N}}
 =\sum_{a=0}^{m-1}M^{-2aN}.
\]
This is the inverse of the previously computed cyclic Green
multiplier. Its root value is \(m\), and its first
\(\partial_{\log M}\)-derivative is \(-Nm(m-1)\).
Making this simultaneous shift in the left Gauss factor while
holding the original right kernel fixed multiplies the full
original sewn source by this scalar. Any compensating change
must therefore be explicit.

The result fixes the exact function, its vanishing divisor and
its normalizations on the physical module. The neighborhoods and
primary projectors may depend on \(N\); their coherent kernels
and continuation along a geometric contour remain unestimated.
No additional knot or filling case is claimed.

## Exact strip pairing reconstructs the scalar function throughout the positive triangle

The [global strip proof](research_balanced_gauss_global_cardinal_strip.md)
extends the earlier reconstruction near \((1/3,1/3)\) to every compact
subset of
\[
 x>0,\qquad y>0,\qquad x+y<1.
\]
It proves a nonzero asymptotic for the full reconstructed scalar
polynomial, with coefficient one, on a fixed complex neighborhood of
each such compact set. Fixed derivatives and a small scaled meridian
disk are included. No physical operator or closing-functional
estimate is inferred.

The crucial simplification is exact. With
\(c_0=2\pi i\), \(c=e^{c_0(1+\beta)/N}\), and the previously proved
marked factorial \(F_N\), set
\[
 \mathcal B_{N,\beta}(x,y)=
 \frac{F_N(N(x+y)+\beta)F_N(\beta)}
      {F_N(Nx+\beta)F_N(Ny+\beta)}.
\]
Finite Chu summation reduces the original double Fourier projection
to a single cardinal projection of this same function. The exact
shift \(F_N(z+N)=(1-e^{c_0z})F_N(z)\) then pairs the two vertical
sides of one width-one strip. Both horizontal ends are retained
until their limits are proved to vanish.

The resulting current satisfies, on compact scalar logarithmic
strips and a sufficiently small fixed \(\beta\)-disk,
\[
 |\mathcal S_N(e^{c_0x},e^{c_0y};c)-\mathcal B_{N,\beta}(x,y)|
 \le C N^p|1-e^{c_0Nx}|\,|1-e^{c_0Ny}|.
\]
The proof bounds the current at every imaginary height, including
the endpoint layer of width \(1/N\). Its two orbit denominators
give an integrable exponential weight after the two sides are
paired. A positive apparent infinity rate from one side alone
therefore does not survive in this actual current.

On the positive triangle, the exact factorial ratio has positive
real action
\(\mathcal J(x+y)-\mathcal J(x)-\mathcal J(y)\),
where \(\mathcal J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds\).
The current bound is consequently exponentially smaller there,
also on a sufficiently small fixed complex neighborhood.
The leading term and actual meridian derivative agree with the
earlier calibrated local formula. The proof includes the upper
Fourier coefficients; it does not discard them before applying
the inverse projection.

## The actual upper source needs its complementary lower contribution

The [source-assembly proof](research_upper_gauss_normal_source_assembly.md)
tests the upper sector under the original paired closing functional,
rather than under an arbitrary mark. Write the actual routed map as
\(T=L\mathcal A R\), and split
\(\mathcal A=\mathcal A_{\rm up}+\mathcal A_{\rm lo}\) using the
full meridian Fourier coefficients. Keeping the original right
kernel, the left-upper contribution is exactly
\[
 \Phi_{{\rm up},L}(M)=D_N(M)\operatorname{Tr}
  [H(M)^{-1}\mathcal A_{\rm up}(M)\mathcal A(M)^{-1}B^\tau(M)],
 \qquad B^\tau=L^{-1}B_+L.
\]
The quotient \(\mathcal A_{\rm up}\mathcal A^{-1}\) is holomorphic
at completeness, but the retained \(H^{-1}\) can still have a pole.
Thus a vanishing upper root value does not remove its source term.

For every invertible actual three-strand braid and every \(N\ge3\),
the integer-degree pair \((0,2N-2)\) gives the nonzero residue
\[
 \operatorname{Res}_{\mu=0}
     \Phi_{{\rm up},L}^{\{0,2N-2\}}(e^\mu)
       =\frac{Q-Q^{-1}}{18}\,b_{\rm top}(1).
\]
Here \(b_{\rm top}\) is the original nonzero scalar braid action
on the all-top sector, including its framing factors.
The proof uses the exact top derivatives \(6/(1-Q^{-2})\) for
the full Gauss function and \(2/(1-Q^{-2})\) for its upper part.
Their ratio is \(1/3\); the bottom upper part is identically zero.

The full original degree pair is removable. Its lower contribution
therefore supplies precisely the opposite residue. This is a
mandatory cancellation inside the prescribed source, not a
singularity of the invariant or a knot counterexample.
No nonzero residue of the upper trace after summing every other
degree pair is asserted. The calculation rules out declaring the
upper source separately null or removable on each reciprocal pair.
It also explains why the first upper normal alone cannot determine
every finite part before assembly.

## The complete upper normal can grow exponentially after physical evaluation

The [physical conditioning proof](research_actual_upper_gauss_carry_conditioning.md)
settles a limitation of the upper-coefficient bound below. It evaluates
the entire prescribed upper first-meridian-normal sum on an actual
two-tail-head block. That evaluated matrix has exponential norm,
despite polynomial bounds for its Fourier coefficients and scalar
jets. This is not merely an example of an arbitrary nonnormal matrix.

For even \(N=2p\), let \(d=N-1\), \(f_a=(Q;Q)_a\), and
\[
 U_N=\left.
   \sum_{l+k\ge N}2N\frac{f_{l+k-N}}{f_lf_k}
           \mathcal D_{lk}(K,\Omega)
       \right|_{\operatorname{span}\{|a,d-a\rangle:0\le a<N\}},
\]
with the exact symmetric Fourier polynomials of the cyclic-divisor
proof. The actual total Cartan and tail pivot are one on this block.
For every positive diagonal physical metric \(D\), the theorem gives
the exact bound
\[
 \|D U_ND^{-1}\|_{\rm op}
 \ge p\left(\prod_{a=0}^{p-1}|(Q;Q)_a|\right)^{-4/p}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \log\|D U_ND^{-1}\|_{\rm op}
 \ge \gamma N-O(\log N),\qquad
 \gamma=-8\int_0^{1/2}\int_0^t
                    \log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds\,dt>0.
\]
The constants are independent of \(D\). This includes the binomial
coherent metric and diagonal factorial changes of coordinates.

An exact harmonic identity first computes the whole Casimir radical
multiplier, with all phases retained. Its actual Hermite frame then
expresses the matrix as \(F\operatorname{diag}(b_j)F^{\mathsf t}\).
A physical-row Vandermonde minor bounds the Gram determinant from
below; the product of its nonzero singular values proves the estimate.
Determinant Cauchy--Schwarz preserves that lower bound under every
positive diagonal metric. Thus cancellation inside the whole upper
sum has already been accounted for.

In the original Gauss factor its upper normal on this block is
\(-NU_N\); the factor \(H_dK^d\) has not been discarded. A norm-one
matrix-unit mark detects an exponentially large pivotal entry.
That mark may depend on the level and is not claimed to come from
a fixed braid or short filling. The exterior factors and the
unmarked closing functional can still cancel this contribution.
No knot counterexample or closed-source lower bound is asserted.

The conclusion for the research route is precise: the scalar
upper-sector estimate cannot be passed to the physical source
through a general polynomial-cost evaluation, even after diagonal
reweighting. The next estimate must retain the actual paired
source and its coherent cancellations.

## The inverse Fourier projection has a selected scalar branch with coefficient one

The global strip result above now extends this local reconstruction
to arbitrary compact subsets of the positive angle triangle.

The [cardinal reconstruction proof](research_balanced_gauss_cardinal_reconstruction.md)
estimates the full scalar Gauss polynomial after the exact inverse
Fourier transform. This is stronger than estimating its individual
triangle coefficients. There is a fixed complex neighborhood of
\((x,y)=(1/3,1/3)\) on which the polynomial is nonzero for every
sufficiently large \(N\), with a calibrated asymptotic and all fixed
derivatives.

Put \(c_0=2\pi i\), \(M=e^{\xi/N}\),
\(\beta=-2\xi/c_0\), and
\[
 H(x,y)=\mathcal J(x+y)-\mathcal J(x)-\mathcal J(y),\qquad
 \mathcal J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds,\qquad
 \Lambda(x,y)=\frac{\pi\sin\pi(x+y)}{\sin\pi x\sin\pi y}.
\]
Uniformly on a smaller closed complex neighborhood and
\(|\xi|\le\eta<\pi\), the result is
\[
 \mathcal S_N(e^{c_0x},e^{c_0y};Qe^{-2\xi/N})
 =\frac{\Gamma(1+\beta)N^{-\beta}\Lambda(x,y)^\beta}
          {\sqrt{2N}}
   \sqrt{\frac{\sin\pi(x+y)}{\sin\pi x\sin\pi y}}\,
   e^{N[H(x,y)+i\pi xy]}(1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
Branches are fixed by the positive real triangle.
The meridian factor and its derivatives are part of the theorem;
the quantum root is held fixed.

The proof constructs a nonzero holomorphic factorial expression
whose sample error is exponentially small, using a long
Euler--Maclaurin expansion with its remainder bounded. The exact
cardinal Cauchy formula then reproduces this expression with
coefficient one. Both single-boundary terms, the double-boundary
term, the sample error, and the entire complementary Fourier array
have strict exponential gaps. The finite Fermat numerators are
retained throughout. Thus the selected coefficient is proved for
the reconstructed scalar function, rather than assumed from its
formal action.

This does not establish reconstruction throughout the positive
triangle, put an arbitrary knot's geometric point in the stated
neighborhood, or estimate the polynomial after substitution of the
actual quantum matrices and contraction with their source.
Those are distinct remaining requirements. No new knot or filling
case is claimed.

## The actual Gauss factor has a closed divisor source and a controlled carry sector

The [cyclic-divisor proof](research_balanced_gauss_cyclic_divisor_source.md)
rewrites the literal finite Gauss factor of the opposite map, without
changing its exterior or closing functional. Put
\[
 Q=e^{2\pi i/N},\qquad c=M^{-2}Q,\qquad
 g_j(c)=(c;Q)_j,\qquad \delta=1-M^{-2N}.
\]
The balanced polynomial has the exact finite Fourier interpolation
\[
 \mathcal S_N(u,v;c)=
 \sum_{l,k=0}^{N-1}
 \frac{g_{l+k}(c)}{g_l(c)g_k(c)}L_l(u)L_k(v),
 \qquad
 L_l(u)=\frac1N\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}(uQ^{-l})^a.
\]
Symmetrizing the two interpolation factors makes their dependence
polynomial in the actual commuting Cartan and Casimir. The identity
therefore retains their Jordan data. It is not an evaluation only at
semisimple spectral points.

There is also a specified closed contour for this same source.
In the finite algebra
\(\mathcal B_\delta=\mathbb C[y]/(y^N-\delta)\), the basis
\(e_l=y^l/g_l(c)\) satisfies
\[
 e_l e_k=\frac{g_{l+k}(c)}{g_l(c)g_k(c)}
                   e_{(l+k)\bmod N}.
\]
With \(U_u(y)=\sum_lL_l(u)e_l\) and
\(W_c(y)=\sum_{j<N}g_j(c)y^{N-1-j}\), the original functional is
\[
 \mathcal S_N(u,v;c)=\frac1{2\pi i}
       \oint\frac{U_u(y)U_v(y)W_c(y)}{y^N-\delta}\,dy,
\]
where the contour encloses the entire divisor. At completeness its
poles merge at zero; differentiating keeps the double denominator.
For a product of any number of basis factors, a meridian jet of order
\(k\) sees only total windings at most \(k\). This associative
filtration is a statement about this algebra, not a reduction of every
braid contraction to multiplication in it.

The quantitative advance concerns the entire upper triangle
\(l+k\ge N\). Its coefficients vanish at \(M=1\), but their actual
fixed-grid first normals are
\[
 \left.\partial_{\log M}
       \frac{g_{l+k}(M^{-2}Q)}
            {g_l(M^{-2}Q)g_k(M^{-2}Q)}
       \right|_{M=1}
   =2N\frac{(Q;Q)_{l+k-N}}{(Q;Q)_l(Q;Q)_k}.
\]
Every such normal has modulus at most \(N/2\).
The proof reflects it to the reciprocal of a positive sine
q-binomial coefficient and proves that coefficient is at least one.
The exact meridian frames then bound the whole upper triangle by a
power of \(N\) on each disk
\(M=e^{\xi/N}\), \(|\xi|\le\eta<\pi\).
Every fixed meridian derivative has polynomial cost as well.
On compact reflected interior triangles this sector is exponentially
small, uniformly on the same disk.

Parseval carries these bounds to the scalar Fourier interpolant and
its fixed scalar jets on the thin annulus
\(e^{-R/N}\le |u|,|v|\le e^{R/N}\). On arbitrary scalar arguments,
the bound retains the explicit factors
\(\max(1,|u|)^{N-1}\max(1,|v|)^{N-1}\).
These estimates do not bound arbitrary evaluated matrix norms or the
original exterior contraction.

The complete source normal still differentiates the interpolation
factors and all original peripheral factors. An exact one-head
calibration shows why: the top channel has a zero complete Gauss sum
although its highest-transfer summand is \(Q\). Its true meridian
derivative is \(4/(1-Q^{-1})\), and half of the relevant normal is
missed by fixing the moving interpolation arguments.
Thus a nonzero summand does not supply a source lower bound.
The new bound controls one global coefficient sector; it does not
establish the reconstructed geometric contribution or add a knot or
filling case to the volume theorem.

## Exact algebraic meridian frames isolate all original first-normal insertions

The [meridian-frame proof](research_actual_meridian_source_frames.md)
gives a source-compatible algebraic adapter for the actual
meridian family. On a finite head define
\[
 h_a(M)=M^{-a}\frac{(Q;Q)_a}{(M^{-2}Q;Q)_a},
 \qquad D_h(M)w_a=h_a(M)w_a.
\]
Then \(E(M)=D_h(M)E(1)D_h(M)^{-1}\), including its
forced zero arrow, and the actual turnover satisfies
\[
 C(M)=\frac{D_N(M)}{N}\,D_h(M)C(1).
\]
The ordered total lowering operator and total raising
operator have different explicit diagonal frames.
The raising frame also conjugates the entire finite
prefix and quotient. Combining those identities
cancels the factorial meridian dependence of the middle
turnover and leaves one specified diagonal insertion
in the opposite-source map. The scalar
\((D_N(M)/N)^m\), the reversal, and both tail Cartan
factors remain explicit.

The frame is uniformly tame on the full physical
head space: on every fixed disk
\(|u|\le\eta<\pi\), \(M=e^{u/N}\), its norm and
inverse norm grow at most polynomially in \(N\).
The proof bounds the distance of every denominator
to the cyclotomic roots. Its first logarithmic
generator is the explicit diagonal
\[
 \ell_a=-a-2\sum_{j=1}^a\frac{Q^j}{1-Q^j},
 \qquad \|\ell\|=O(N\log(N+1)).
\]
These formulas retain the actual vacuum-normal
contribution rather than differentiating a root symbol.

The same adapter is proved for the literal original
crossings. For example, with
\(\mathcal J_i=J_i+J_{i+1}\),
\[
 R_i^+(M)=\frac{\kappa(M)}{\kappa(1)}
    M^{-\mathcal J_i}D_{h,i+1}(M)
                    R_i^+(1)D_{h,i}(M)^{-1}.
\]
The negative formula follows by taking its actual
inverse, with the checked flip accounted for.
Consequently every fixed original marked braid
has an exact first-normal expression as a finite
sum of root words with diagonal insertions.
The common crossing scalar, zero-framing line,
mark derivatives and original pivot derivative
are all retained. No cancellation of the
diagonal insertions along a word is assumed.

This gives the true first jet of \(T\), and hence
the actual residue and finite part of its source
normalization, in terms of root operators and
the specified insertions. Polynomial frame
conditioning is not a relative estimate on
a matrix entry or a closed scalar that may
cancel. In particular the new result does not
remove the extreme-coefficient or geometric
cycle problem. No additional knot or filling
case is claimed.

## The actual Cartan-coupled kernels and their compact convolution are controlled

The [coupled-flow proof](research_actual_coupled_euler_coherent_flow.md)
extends the one-head estimate to each literal coproduct factor
\[
 U_{i,N}(\lambda)=
   \sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\frac{\lambda^n(E_iK_{>i})^n}{(Q;Q)_n}.
\]
The tail Cartan matrices remain operators. Their binomial kernels
produce exact tail-coordinate shifts in the finite recurrence.
An index-dependent analytic-radius bound controls the low activity
degrees, and an original-metric Cauchy estimate controls all
remaining degrees. This proves a nonzero local kernel, with
relative error \(O(N^{-1})\), on every fixed compact complex
nonincident chart for sufficiently small activity. The phase
and its linear transport retain the Cartan half-step and the
\(N-1\) endpoint shift.

The [compact composition proof](research_capped_coproduct_compact_coherent_composition.md)
then controls the convolution of these actual kernels.
It uses an exact complex change of coherent sphere adapted
to each external pair. Those compact spheres are homologous
to the original ones and give the same finite resolution.
The local stationary point is continued from the identity.
The proof separately controls the whole complementary chain:
low powers retain a strict coherent-overlap loss, including
at cross-pair incidence, and the high powers have a Cauchy
tail whose decay pays the conditioning of the complex frame.

The resulting actual finite total Euler kernel satisfies
\[
 \sigma_N\!\left(
   \sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\frac{\lambda^nE_\Sigma(1)^n}{(Q;Q)_n}
           \right)
       =e^{N\mathcal S(\lambda)}b(\lambda)(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad \mathcal S(0)=0,\quad b(0)=1,\quad b\ne0,
\]
locally on each such compact chart, for small \(\lambda\).
The exact \(N\)-powers of the finite resolutions and
the complex Gaussian determinant are computed. The
positive Dirichlet real part is kept distinct from that
complex determinant. The retained root carry transfers
the product estimate to the actual total operator.

These results are at the complete meridian and fixed
quantum root. They do not differentiate the lowering
vacuum or the shifted denominator. They also do not
evaluate the later quotient and original closing row.
There is an additional source-incidence issue:
the opposite map contains the extreme degree
\(E_\Sigma^{N-1}\). A small-activity estimate for its
Euler generating polynomial does not by itself
determine that coefficient. The extraction contour
and its competing sectors remain to be controlled.
No new knot or filling case is claimed.

## The actual meridian normal is now controlled on both small half-planes

The [finite Euler normal proof](research_actual_finite_euler_first_meridian_normal.md)
computes a derivative that cannot be recovered from the root
value alone. For the literal finite family
\[
 E_{v,N}(t)=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\frac{t^n}{(vQ;Q)_n},
 \qquad E_N=E_{1,N},\qquad
 H_N=\left.\partial_vE_{v,N}\right|_{v=1},
\]
the exact first-normal equation retains both its vacuum
and its top term:
\[
 (1-t)H_N(t)-H_N(Qt)
       =E_N(Qt)-1+\frac{N-1}{2N}t^N.
\]
There is a fixed small radius such that the following
estimates hold uniformly on compact subsets away from
zero and the real axis.

In the lower half-plane,
\[
 -\frac{2\pi i}{N}\frac{H_N(t)}{E_N(t)}
      =\log N+\gamma+\Log\!\left(-\frac{t}{2\pi i}\right)
                                      +O(N^{-1}).
\]
Thus the actual derivative shares the root exponential
there, with a calculated \(N\log N\) prefactor.
The proof uses a cancellation-preserving analytic
multiplier estimate and the exact harmonic integral
containing \(E_N(0)=1\). A high-order finite-product
remainder and all high-index tails are bounded before
using that multiplier; a coefficientwise small error
is not mistaken for a relative error in a signed sum.

In the upper half-plane the answer is different:
\[
 |E_N(t)|\le Ce^{-cN},\qquad H_N(t)=1/t+O(N^{-1}).
\]
Here the original vacuum layer near the zero end of
the harmonic integral supplies the leading term.
At its other end the exact divided difference is
kept together. This gives a concrete example in the
actual finite family where the normal has a larger
exponential order than the root value.

The estimates include fixed argument derivatives and
explicit adapters to \(v=M^{-2}\), to \(M=e^{u/N}\),
and to the unscaled logarithmic meridian. They hold
the scalar argument \(t\) fixed. In an operator or
source application, the additional \(t(M)\),
\(E_A(M)\), quotient and closing derivatives still
have their own exact terms. No whole-source
noncancellation or additional volume-conjecture
case is inferred.

## A finite analytic transport now proves the actual one-head Euler amplitude

The [one-head flow proof](research_actual_one_head_euler_coherent_flow.md)
estimates the actual root operator
\[
 U_N(\lambda)=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}
                    \frac{\lambda^nE^n}{(Q;Q)_n}.
\]
For every compact complex coherent chart away from incidence,
it gives a fixed small \(\lambda\)-disk on which the normalized
kernel is zero-free and has an explicit nonzero leading
amplitude with relative error \(O(N^{-1})\).
All physical endpoint arrows remain.

This assertion is derived from a finite recurrence. In homogeneous
coherent coordinates put
\[
 I=w_0z_0+w_1z_1,\qquad
 \theta=w_1z_1/I,\qquad t=\lambda w_0z_1/I.
\]
The normalized polynomial satisfies
\[
 G_{j+1}=(1-\theta)G_j+(\theta+Q^{-1}t)G_j(\theta,Q^{-1}t),
 \qquad G_0=1.
\]
An analytic coefficient majorant proves convergence of the
actual logarithms for every \(j\le N\). A second positive
analytic flow controls the discretization error. The
Hamilton--Jacobi equation and its subprincipal transport
are therefore compared with the actual finite kernel,
rather than used as a formal amplitude prescription.

At time one the initial coordinate \(b\) is determined by
\[
 t=b\exp\!\left[\frac{2\pi i(\theta+b)}{1+b}\right].
\]
With
\[
 p=\frac1{2\pi i}\Log\frac{\theta+t}{\theta+b},
 \qquad
 \Delta=1+\frac{2\pi i(1-\theta)b}{(1+b)^2},
\]
where the ratio has its proved removable value, the result is
\[
 G_{N-1}(\theta,t)
    =e^{NV(1,\theta,t)}
       \frac{e^{-\pi ip}}{(1+b)\sqrt{\Delta}}
                     (1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
The phase is calibrated at the identity, and its mixed
derivative remains nonzero on smaller charts. The
\(N-1\) endpoint shift is included in the amplitude.
For example, at \(\theta=1\) the exact kernel is
\((1-(-t)^N)/(1+t)\): the proof keeps this cap and
correctly gives zero limiting phase there.

The result controls a genuine factor in the original
binomial coherent convention. It is at the complete
meridian and fixed quantum root. It does not include
the additional lowering-matrix vacuum derivative,
the shifted-denominator normal, or the full quotient
and closing contraction. No geometric-domain or
volume-conjecture filling conclusion follows yet.

## Root coproduct factorization now has an explicit exponentially small carry

The [capped factorization proof](research_root_capped_euler_coproduct_factorization.md)
uses the actual ordered terms
\(X_i=E_i\prod_{j>i}K_j\) of the lowering coproduct.
For total degree below \(N\), the finite Euler polynomial
of \(\sum_iX_i\) agrees exactly with the decreasing-index
product of the finite Euler polynomials of \(X_i\).
The remaining total degrees form a specified finite
carry; they are not set equal to zero by a generic
infinite-product identity.

The proof writes each nilpotent factor as the exponential
of its exact finite logarithm, bounds that logarithm and
its inverse in the original binomial metric, and estimates
the carry by an operator Cauchy bound. On a sufficiently
small activity disk, its absolute norm and all four
two-sided relative operator errors are exponentially
small. The decay rate can be made arbitrarily large
by shrinking that disk.

The bounds hold on the actual complex collar
\(M=\exp(u/\sqrt N)\), with bounded \(u\);
fixed meridian derivatives cost only polynomial
factors. On each compact complex coherent chart
the proof also computes the exponential conditioning
of normalized evaluation, and chooses the carry
rate to beat it. This is not division by a
possibly vanishing scalar kernel.

The denominators in this theorem are the fixed
\((Q;Q)_n\). In the actual shifted family
\((M^{-2}Q;Q)_n\), the additional first-normal
coefficient remains
\(-2\sum_{j=1}^nQ^j/(1-Q^j)\).
The theorem does not replace that family, estimate
the quotient pairing, or locate a geometric saddle
in its small-activity domain.

## The retained factorial factor has an actual selected complex saddle

The [factorial-kernel proof](research_factorial_coupon_small_activity_saddle.md)
now evaluates the actual retained diagonal factor \(ZG^{-1}\)
on a small complex sector. Its original binomial kernel is
\[
 H_N(s)=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}\binom{N-1}{a}
                \frac{(-s)^a}{(Q;Q)_a},\qquad Q=e^{2\pi i/N}.
\]
An exact constant-term circle expresses this polynomial through
the finite Euler polynomial. Comparing that polynomial with
the exponential of its finite logarithm bounds the missing
Taylor coefficients by an exponentially small relative error.
The original circle can then be chosen through a unique
strict phase maximum; no unproved contributing-cycle
coefficient is inserted for this factor.

Writing \(c_0=2\pi i\) and \(s=c_0a^2\), the result holds
for sufficiently small nonzero \(a\) in each fixed sector
\(|\arg a|<\vartheta<\pi/2\), uniformly on compact subsets
away from zero. In particular the proved domain includes
small positive real \(s\). On the selected branch,
\[
 s=\frac{y(e^{c_0y}-1)}{1-y},\qquad y=a+O(a^2),
\]
and the complete leading term is
\[
 H_N(s)=
 \frac{(1-y)e^{-c_0y/2}}
 {\sqrt{2\pi N\,[y(1-y)+(1-e^{-c_0y})/c_0]}}
       e^{N\Psi(s)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
\]
\[
 \Psi(s)=-\log(1-y)
          -\operatorname{Li}_2(1-e^{c_0y})/c_0,\qquad
 s\Psi'(s)=y,\qquad \Psi\longrightarrow0\quad(a\longrightarrow0).
\]
All branches and the nonzero coefficient are fixed by
the actual finite contour. The exact differential row
also has the upper-cap component \(y=1\). It was not
divided away; the selected contour estimate accounts
for the whole original polynomial on this domain.

This controls the previously retained factorial factor,
but its location in the full source matters. Turnover
places it on the original donor. Its contraction with
the upper column is therefore a different composed row,
and the bare kernel above cannot be substituted for it.
The actual quotient, turnover, other scalar lines and
complementary integrations remain. Neither this sector's
membership for a geometric frame nor a nonzero geometric
contribution to the full invariant has been proved.
There is no new volume-conjecture filling case.

## One actual upper boundary column now has a controlled complex kernel

The [upper-column proof](research_upper_euler_column_resolvent_chart.md)
gives an analytic estimate for an actual factor of the opposite
kernel. Let \(f_a=(Q;Q)_a\), let \(G\) be the donor diagonal
with entries \(f_a\), and let \(Y\) have entries
\(Q^{a(a+1)/2}\). Conjugate the donor alone by \(YG^{-1}\).
The original upper column then has the exact finite form
\[
 (v(\zeta)\otimes I)\widetilde S i_{N-1}
    =\zeta^{N-1}
                  (I+x^{-1}F_{\rm r}/\zeta)^{-1}.
\]
The inverse is a finite polynomial because the actual recipient
matrix satisfies \(F_{\rm r}^N=0\). Every recipient retains
its original binomial metric and top endpoint. The original
donor row and its input scalar are specified explicitly.
A negative-star companion has its own stated donor gauge.

This is more than a scalar finite-node formula. On each
fixed compact complex recipient chart away from incidence,
the proof controls all powers \(F_{\rm r}^n\), \(n<N\),
with an error \(C^n n^2/N\) in the normalized coherent
kernel. Summing the actual finite resolvent, for donor
coordinate sufficiently large relative to that chart,
gives a nonzero holomorphic leading factor and error
\(O(N^{-1})\). The argument retains the
\(d=N-1\) and \(Q\) shifts needed at projective endpoints.
It includes fixed meridian derivatives on smaller fixed
complex disks. No ordinary quantum-parameter derivative
is obtained by differentiating nilpotency.

The full opposite source still has a specified interface.
Turnover reverses the heads and moves the donor diagonal
to a last-head inverse-factorial factor:
\[
 T(M)=Nq_F(M)Z_mG_m^{-1}\mathscr C_m(M)
                      \widetilde S_m(M^{-1})i_{N-1},
 \qquad Z_mw_b=(-1)^bw_b .
\]
That factor has not disappeared against the first-head
quotient. Its coherent kernel, the fully paired geometric
domain, and the original cycle coefficient remain to be
controlled. In particular an arbitrary exterior row is
not replaced by the special evaluation row used to prove
the local estimate.

The result supplies one proved complex boundary block.
It does not prove a phase or nonzero amplitude for the
complete \(J\) kernel, and it adds no volume-conjecture
knot or filling case.

## The root trace equations now give an exponential estimate on real coherent windows

The [finite trace-separator proof](research_finite_trace_separator_and_opposite_characteristic.md)
constructs a fixed finite family of actual quantum trace
observables. It verifies their four-entry ordered Hurwitz
transport and computes their first-head quotients without
expanding a growing prefix matrix. Each resulting observable
has degree bounded independently of the quantum level.
Its complete-root coherent symbol is the corresponding
single, pair, or oriented triple trace.

The elementary trace-Gram reconstruction proves that these
data determine an irreducible ordered tuple up to one common
conjugation, including over complex local Artin rings.
Applied to the actual root kernel \(T(1)\) and the Laurent
residue \(\mathsf R\) of \(J\), they give exact homogeneous
operator equations. Their possible characteristic relation
matches the turned ordered character and reverses the
selected regular total-product eigenvalue. The finite
part \(J_0\) instead retains its explicit inhomogeneous
first-normal row; it is not included in that homogeneous
conclusion.

The [real coherent localization proof](research_exponential_real_coherent_intertwiner_localization.md)
turns those equations into an actual estimate. If one
bounded observable has classical values separated by
\(\eta>0\) at two real compact coherent configurations,
then every exact intertwiner \(L_N\) between its two
versions satisfies
\[
 |\langle\psi_y,L_N\psi_z\rangle|
                  \le C e^{-cN}\|L_N\|.
\]
The proof uses exact analytic amplitude differences,
nested Cauchy estimates for powers of order proportional
to \(N\), and the binomial distribution of the coherent
state. The probability tail is retained through the
power estimate. For separated real windows this also gives
\[
 \|P_{\mathcal C}L_NP_{\mathcal D}\|_1
       \le C N^{r_++r_-}e^{-cN}\|L_N\|,
\]
where the partial resolutions are the actual positive
coherent integrals. Thus this part of the transport has
an exponential estimate on the original real cycle.

The unknown full operator norm remains on the right.
The estimate neither reaches a complex geometric saddle
nor controls the inhomogeneous \(J_0\) row. The proof gives
an exact example explaining that distinction:
\(P=|d\rangle\langle0|\) has \(FP=0\), but at the
nonincident complex point \((1/w,z)=(0,1)\),
\(\sigma_P=1\) and \(\sigma_F\to2\pi i\).
Pointwise multiplication of these covariant symbols
cannot remove an endpoint contribution there.
No new volume-conjecture case follows.

The use of quantum traces or intermediate Casimirs is
not itself a novelty claim. The abstracts of
[Bonahon--Wong](https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.5250v4)
and [Crampé--Frappat--Poulain d'Andecy--Ragoucy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17677v2)
were checked for coverage of quantum trace maps and
braid actions on intermediate-Casimir algebras.
Their proofs are not premises of the finite calculations
or of the estimate above.

## The opposite kernel's finite recurrence has a controlled assembled normalization

The [forced cyclic-normalization proof](research_opposite_kernel_forced_cyclic_normalization.md)
factors the literal opposite kernel through an actual top-head
braid route and the finite operator
\(A_N=q_FE_\Sigma^{N-1}i_{N-1}\).
It computes \(A_N\) as its original finite balanced
hypergeometric polynomial, including the last coefficient.
Its transfer and clock contiguities have explicit extreme-tail
forcing.

Before restricting to the actual tensor module, both
identities retain the norm polynomial
\[
 \mathcal W_N(K,\Omega)
             =C_N(\Omega)+K^N+K^{-N}.
\]
On that module \(\mathcal W_N=0\), including on Casimir
Jordan blocks. The remaining forced cyclic equation has
the exact whole-orbit multiplier
\[
 \mathcal R_N(M)
     =\frac{1-M^{-2N}}{1-M^{-2mN}}.
\]
Its assembled inverse \((1-\mathcal R_N)^{-1}\) is a
bounded analytic unit on a fixed disk in \(u=N\log M\);
at \(u=0\) its denominator is \((m-1)/m\).
This controls the actual scalar normalization and its
scaled meridian derivatives. It does not bound the
individual clock denominators or the surviving
extreme-tail operator.

The proof also gives the exact recurrence for partial
coherent resolutions, retaining their coefficient
commutators and endpoint forcing. Replacing \(K,\Omega\)
by a geometric scalar argument does not preserve
\(\mathcal W_N=0\); its displayed off-spectrum term
must then remain. No scalar finite-node interpolation,
nonzero geometric amplitude, or cycle coefficient
is inferred. No new knot or filling case is claimed.
