## Degree-scalar changes of the opposite kernel leave the paired source unchanged

The [degree-frame calculation](research_degree_scalar_source_frames.md)
settles a specific ambiguity in using the opposite-polarization
kernel. Write \(D=(m-1)(N-1)\), and let \(U_k\) be its actual
integer-degree spaces. The already proved map \(J(M)\) sends
\(U_k\) to \(U_{D-k}\). If
\[
 F(M)|_{U_k}=f_k(M)I,\qquad
 f_k(M)f_{D-k}(M^{-1})=1,
\]
then replacing \(J(M)\) by \(F(M)J(M)\) preserves both exact
double compositions and the full paired source coupon. For
any intervening reduced mark \(B\), its paired matrix is
conjugated by \(F\), so its trace is unchanged. Arbitrary
marked-source Ward corrections remain required.

The proof classifies these scalar changes by the elementary
norm-one equation \(f=b/b^\iota\), where
\(\iota(k,M)=(D-k,M^{-1})\). On a fixed degree, a value
\(f(1)=-1\) needs a meromorphic \(b\); it cannot be represented
by a unit \(b\). This qualification is retained. The result
classifies this scalar orbit, not all solutions of the
operator equations.

For restricted coherent resolutions the change is equally
explicit: it conjugates the outer window. Thus a window
commuting with total occupation is unchanged, whereas a
general window retains its commutator correction. Analytic
degree gauges can have exponential size in \(N\); the
source identity does not turn this into a volume bound.
The useful conclusion is that a common degree-scalar phase
need not be fixed separately in the fully paired source.
The actual geometric phase, amplitude, cycle coefficient,
and complementary-chain estimates remain unproved.
No new knot or filling case is claimed.

## Arbitrary marked sources now have an exact forced transport with bounded normal depth

The [forced-source theorem](research_forced_source_and_opposite_kernel_transport.md)
extends the preceding homogeneous calculations to arbitrary finite
marked matrices. This is needed for the actual beta vacuum and for
restricted coherent resolutions: neither is silently declared an
intertwiner.

In the actual prefix frame, put
\(C_n=f_n^{-1}p_nS^{-1}ASi_0\). The first column of the exact
commutator \([E_\Sigma,A]\) gives the forced recurrence
\[
 C_n=-((1-Q^n)b_n)^{-1}[E_{\rm r},C_{n-1}]
           +((1-Q^n)b_n)^{-1}Y_{n-1}.
\]
The original pointed source depends only on this column. Ordered
trace-adjoint iteration therefore reconstructs it from its
constant term and explicit forcing currents. The scalar homogeneous
kernel is the already proved \(D_N(M)H^{-1}\), and is used as a
universal matrix identity, not only on admissible intertwiners.

An analytic Jordan frame for \(E_\Sigma\) improves the initial
meromorphic recursion. The difference between the original source
coupon and its homogeneous first-column coupon annihilates the
entire \(E_\Sigma\)-commutant. In the constant Jordan frame this
means that every block superdiagonal sum is zero. A specified
entrywise recursion solves its commutator equation, including the
last column. The resulting primitive \(\mathcal W_E\) has at most
a simple meridian pole, uniformly in pole order as \(N\) varies:
\[
 \Phi(A)=D_N(M)\operatorname{Tr}(H^{-1}C_0)
                 +\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal W_E[E_\Sigma,A]).
\]
No norm bound on this primitive is inferred. The grouped finite
parts require at most first meridian jets; the individual raw
recursion terms can have deeper poles and are not truncated.

The proof also computes the actual defect of the opposite-
polarization comparison for any marked \(A\):
\[
 B_+T-TB_-=
 q_F\bigl([A,E_\Sigma^{N-1}]
       -[A,F_\Sigma]\Lambda_FE_\Sigma^{N-1}\bigr)
                 \mathscr C i_F^{\rm ref}.
\]
Here \(\Lambda_F\) is the specified finite partial inverse with
\(F_\Sigma\Lambda_F=I-i_Fq_F\).
Combining the two corrections gives an explicit whole-source
identity
\[
 P_0\otimes g-P_{\rm opp}
       =[\mathcal V_E,E_\Sigma]+[\mathcal V_F,F_\Sigma].
\]
Every factor of these currents is given in its actual order.
Their marked rows propagate through sewn words by the literal
coproduct Leibniz identity. The complete opposite source coupon
has only a simple meridian pole; no such pole bound is imposed
on unassembled relative products or individual primitives.

The beta forcing is now tied to a literal coupon: the unit
Newton term is the reflected atomic state \((0,0,N-1)\), with
its original coefficient \(Q/N\); after factorial reflection its
third physical occupation is zero. Its transported prefix row
contains the full coproduct sum \(P_0S^{-1}\), rather than a
reset \(P_0\). The source theorem applies to that exact inserted
matrix with its nonzero Ward currents retained.

The local affine beta monodromy is likewise retained. Its full
orbit is
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}u^N-v^N&B_N(u,v)\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
At the balanced norm divisor the off-diagonal entry is nonzero.
Thus the forcing is a nontrivial extension; replacing it by a
regular homogeneous line would lose source data.
The actual balanced residue and Barnes normalization terms
remain in the proof. Their norm divisor has not been identified
with the global complete-meridian divisor, and none of their
sewn contributions has been estimated or cancelled.

This is a general algebraic source transport for fixed words,
including words after any prescribed short filling. It proves
neither the geometric relative-chain comparison nor the
finite-exception volume statement. The still required estimates
concern these actual retained currents and the selected complex
kernel, rather than an unspecified normalization scalar.

## The opposite polarizations now have an actual normalized source kernel

The [opposite-polarization proof](research_opposite_polarization_source_kernel.md)
constructs the missing finite map, rather than replacing one boundary
polarization by the other from a scalar eigenvalue calculation. With
the actual prefix quotient \(q_F\), section \(i_F\), total lowering
operator and balanced turnover, it is
\[
 T(M)=q_F(M)E_\Sigma(M)^{N-1}\mathscr C(M)i_F(M^{-1}).
\]
It descends through the quotient by \(F_\Sigma V\), intertwines the
reflected actual braid word and reverses the complete Cartan weight.
The exact double composition contains
\(H(M)=D_N(MK_{\rm r}(M))\), with every balanced scalar retained.
Thus \(J=H^{-1}T\) is normalized by the same inverse-Jacobian
coupon that fixes the original pointed source.

The two normalized kernels have an exact compact coherent
convolution equal to the original highest-cut pivotal scalar.
They have at most simple meridian poles. Their sewn matrix has
only a simple pole as well; its residue has zero full trace.
Writing \(J(e^u)=R/u+J_0+uJ_1+\cdots\), the proof gives
\[
 R^2=0,\qquad
 [R,J_0]=\frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon m}(K_0-K_0^{-1}),
 \qquad
 J_0^2-RJ_1-J_1R
       =\frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon}(K_0+K_0^{-1}).
\]
On every nonself reciprocal physical-weight pair the residue
has an explicit contracting homotopy. The first-normal
equivariance defect is retained: this contraction is not a
reason to set the modified source to zero.
Multiplying the full kernels recovers the original first-jet
formula. The apparent second derivative disappears from the
full trace by \(R^2=0\), rather than by deleting a polar term.

The actual map also reverses the full integer occupation:
\[
 T(M)U_k\subset U_{(m-1)(N-1)-k}.
\]
Generic invertibility and the degree-preserving actual half
twist therefore strengthen the earlier mod-\(N\) result to
\[
 t_k^\beta(M)=t_{(m-1)(N-1)-k}^\beta(M^{-1}).
\]
The finite graded character is reciprocal, and complementary
integer sectors cancel their scalar source residues within
each pair. This is a new consequence of the explicit map;
the earlier projective-occupation note deliberately did not
assert it without that map. An integer-sector projector has
not thereby been lifted to an analytic original
total-intertwiner projector through every root collision.

For a relative coherent window the proof retains the exact
operator \(P_{\mathcal C}T-TP_{\mathcal D}\), its signed
boundary transgression and every complementary chain.
Local triple products can retain double poles and second
meridian derivatives. The full compact cancellation does not
erase those local terms. In particular no geometric thimble
coefficient, reciprocal-geometric addition theorem or volume
lower bound follows from the finite correspondence.
The next analytic row is the characteristic/amplitude
comparison for this actual universal kernel and the estimate
of its geometric relative-window defect.

## Knot closure now gives an undamped convergent whole Frobenius period

The [undamped Frobenius-period theorem](research_undamped_frobenius_gaussian_source_period.md)
strengthens the damped construction below. The original rational
graded trace is now an absolutely convergent combined Gaussian
integral at zero grading. The proof does not assert that the
undamped infinite operator is trace class.

In the common positive Frobenius metric, write
\(y_\ell=\overline Z_\ell\) and let \(\Gamma_\ell^0\) be the
complete local transport matrices. The real part of the entire
closed Gaussian exponent is exactly
\[
             -\tfrac12\sum_{\ell=1}^L
                     \|y_\ell-\Gamma_\ell^0y_{\ell-1}\|^2 .
\]
A zero would be a parallel vector fixed by the full transport
\(\Gamma_\beta^0\). For a knot, this transport is the quotient
of an \(m\)-cycle strand permutation by its invariant line.
Its smallest distance from the eigenvalue one is
\(2\sin(\pi/m)>0\). Telescoping around the closed word gives
the explicit bound
\[
 -\tfrac12\sum_\ell\|y_\ell-\Gamma_\ell^0y_{\ell-1}\|^2
 \le
 -\frac{\sum_\ell\|y_\ell\|^2}
        {2L^2(1+(2\sin(\pi/m))^{-1})^2}.
\]
This is a global estimate on the assembled auxiliary cycle,
independent of \(N\) and its parity. A link with \(c\) components
instead has exactly \(c-1\) complex flat directions, explaining
why the knot hypothesis enters this argument.

The gap persists on a fixed complex disk in \(u=N\log M\).
It controls the polynomial carry factors, all fixed meridian
derivatives and the ends under bounded entire translations.
A holomorphic two-parameter argument identifies this undamped
integral with the already prescribed rational graded trace.
The original paired first-jet source follows with its actual
residue cancellation and every scalar line retained.

## The original source has a central full-trace and inverse-Jacobian formula

The [central-source proof](research_central_resolvent_compact_source_symmetry.md)
removes the need to reset a pointed cut when comparing the actual
Weyl turnover. Let \(U_{N-1}\) be the monic polynomial defined by
\(U_{N-1}(z+z^{-1})=D_N(z)\), and let \(\Omega_\Sigma\) be the
actual total quantum Casimir. For every analytic total-intertwiner
family, the original highest-cut pivotal source is exactly
\[
 \Phi_0(W(M))=\frac{D_N(M)}N
        \operatorname{Tr}_{\rm full}
           \left(U_{N-1}(-\Omega_\Sigma(M))^{-1}W(M)\right).
\]
The inverse is generic and meromorphic, with its continuation
prescribed by the analytic original source. This is not an
ordinary trace substituted for a modified trace without its
central coupon.

The proof computes that coupon in the actual triangular coordinates.
It also proves the full Chebyshev polynomial identity on the
Casimir through every root Jordan collision, using divided
differences along the finite first-head paths. Consequently
\[
 U_{N-1}(-\Omega_\Sigma)^{-1}
  =\frac{(\Omega_\Sigma^2-4I)U_{N-1}(-\Omega_\Sigma)}
          {(M^{mN}-M^{-mN})^2}.
\]
Its meridian pole order is at most two, uniformly in \(N\).
All matrix finite-part terms remain; terms with zero full trace
are not discarded from a relative chain.

There is an exact inverse-Jacobian interpretation as well.
The actual reduced weight traces are interpolated on the
monic Casimir polynomial \(p_M\), and their source is
\[
 (-1)^{N+1}N D_N(M)
       \sum_\chi\frac{t_\chi(M)}{p_M'(\lambda_\chi)}
  =(-1)^{N+1}N D_N(M)[\lambda^{N-1}]t_M(\lambda).
\]
Thus the selected coefficient and its sign are fixed by the
original quantum source, including the collision data.
No free normalization of a torsor period is introduced.

The central full trace has a compact coherent realization on
the original product of spheres. Its actual Weyl turnover
is an orientation-preserving map of those cycles plus an
explicit global rational exact-form current. The half-twist
return has its own specified current. Symmetrization therefore
gives the same original period with a literal compact
involution, retaining all Laurent and finite-part terms.

This does not prove that the two reduced geometric eigenline
contributions add. The compact turnover sends the
\(F_\Sigma=0\) polarization to \(E_\Sigma=0\); the actual
comparison between those relative chains remains.
Moreover the central coupon has its own order-\(N\)
loxodromic scalar character, which cannot be treated as a
unit amplitude. No geometric-cycle coefficient or volume
bound follows from the central trace identity.

## The regularized reduced Verma period is now an ordinary convergent trace

The [damped Frobenius-period proof](research_damped_frobenius_gaussian_source_period.md)
provides an analytic realization of the graded period, rather
than assuming that its undamped infinite trace converges.
The entire lifted word is a finite residue matrix of polynomial
creation operators followed by the symmetric-power action of
\(\Gamma_\beta\). Every carry lowers the total residue degree
by \(N\), so its creation polynomial has degree at most
\(m-2\), independent of \(N\) and of the word length.

At the complete meridian the Frobenius braid action factors
through the finite permutation group. Averaging its metric
gives a common positive Hermitian form for all generators.
On the finite residue space tensored with its bosonic Fock
space, damping by
\[
                 e^{-sJ/N},\qquad s>0,
\]
makes the actual lifted word trace class. This holds with
fixed meridian derivatives on a controlled
\(|N\log M|\le c s\) neighborhood. The finite-source coefficient
cost is at most exponential in \(N\); no unknown knot-word
volume estimate is inferred from that coarse bound.

Distributing the damping among the local factors gives an
absolutely convergent paired Gaussian integral, with explicit
Gaussian ends even under bounded entire translations.
The original finite residue indices and all carry polynomials
remain in this period. Its trace equals
\[
 \frac{t_f(M;e^{-s/N})}
      {d_\beta(x(M)^N;e^{-s})}.
\]
At completeness the denominator is
\((1-e^{-ms})/(1-e^{-s})\). The undamped value and its
meridian jet are recovered by the exact fixed-\(N\)
Abel/rational limit as \(s\) decreases to zero.

At positive \(s\), even a physical Casimir pair can have a
nonzero residue. Its determinant derivative is therefore
retained in the specified linear first-jet row until that
endpoint. The row is not called a finite part of a
meromorphic graded source with a nonzero residue.
No interchange of \(N\to\infty\) and \(s\downarrow0\) is made.
The positive metric is on auxiliary Frobenius variables,
not a proof of positivity on geometric shape variables.
The geometric-cycle and finite-exception problems remain.

## Internal finite caps now have an exact reduced Verma transport

The [reduced Frobenius-trace theorem](research_reduced_frobenius_trace_and_cap_transport.md)
extends the old untruncated Verma/Alexander mechanism to the actual

The lift is defined on a polynomial lattice independently of the

 \widetilde t_f(M;\tau)=

The full unit at \(\tau=1\) is

For a knot, its complete value is exactly \(m\), at both parities.
The equality initially concerns formal graded series; evaluation at

the stated Abel limit at the complete meridian. It is not an
assertion that the unweighted infinite Gaussian trace converges.

The derivative of \(d_\beta(x(M)^N)\) is retained in the first
meridian jet. Its extra term is the determinant derivative times

is \(m\) times the corresponding rational reduced-Verma first-jet
period. An individual off-circle geometric chain has not been
proved to satisfy that residue equation; its determinant derivative
cannot be discarded separately.

every fixed actual word, including a knot obtained after any fixed

The [complete-longitude proof](research_complete_longitude_sign_and_marked_derivative.md)
includes an elementary frame-cover argument for the classical fact
that the preferred longitude of a complete hyperbolic knot exterior
in \(S^3\) has eigenvalue \(-1\) in every determinant-one lift.
The argument uses the odd turning number of the single boundary of
a Seifert surface and checks the actual convention \(\mu=-H\).
It imports no proof of a quantum asymptotic statement.

Thus the old actual-source identity
\(dS_{\rm flat}=2\Log\ell_{\rm intr}\,d\Log M\) has complete
derivative \(2(2j+1)\pi i\), not zero. Centering that logarithm
would multiply its phase by \(M^{-(2j+1)N}\), whose value at one
is one but whose first derivative is of order \(N\).
That character cannot be dropped in a first-jet source calculation.
This sign is established classical coverage, with the actual
word/flag normalization and its consequence proved explicitly here.

The [marked reduced-action theorem](research_marked_reduced_action_meridian_parity.md)
then checks the additional boundary character of the new reduction.
It extends the rational free quotient to generic meridian, compares
the literal \(S_m^{-1}R_iS_m\) and reduced primitives, and calibrates
their meridian-only discrepancy by finite limits of their explicit
partial derivatives. It uses no asymptotic action of \(S_m\) on a
physical vacuum. Restoring the original \(m-1\) tail pivots gives
\[
 \exp\!\left(\tfrac12\partial_{\log M}S_{\rm red,flat}\right)
                 =(-1)^{m-1}\ell_{\rm intr}.
\]
The complete Bloch--Wigner comparison alone did not determine
this character.

An odd-strand presentation with regular total product is available
by the already calibrated positive Markov operations. In it
\(\partial_{\log M}S_{\rm red,flat}=2\pi i\,\nu\), with \(\nu\)
odd and hence nonzero. If an actual differentiable geometric trace
sector with nonzero amplitude has separately been established,
its first-jet term acquires the nonzero multiplier
\[
 \frac{\nu(k-k^{-1})}{2\varepsilon m}\,N .
\]
Here \(k\) is its actual remaining total Cartan symbol; the
regular-total condition gives \(k^2\ne1\).
This fixes a local closing-normal obstruction. It does not prove
that the sector occurs, identify physical Cartan-pair projectors
with geometric cycles, or prevent cancellation of different
selected sectors. No additional volume-conjecture cases follow.

 t_\chi(M)=t_{\chi^{-1}}(M^{-1}).

 \Phi_{\{\chi,\chi^{-1}\}}(1)
   =\varepsilon^{-1}
       \left((\chi+\chi^{-1})t_\chi(1)
             +m^{-1}(\chi-\chi^{-1})t_\chi'(1)\right).
\]
Self-reciprocal weights are counted once, as specified in the proof.

The negative factor uses no chirp and the factors

complex-segment remainder estimate gives leading
amplitude one, uniformly down to \(a=0\), on their

The [arbitrary-star word theorem](research_reduced_euler_star_complex_word_kernel.md)
then treats all recipients together. In the all-factorial

 K_a^\pm=H_\pm^a Z_a(h;p^\pm),\qquad h=2\pi i/N.

Here \(H_\pm\) is the actual linear characteristic, and

Every actual \(N\)-dependent coefficient and half-step

## The reduced geometric correspondence and its Bloch--Wigner value

The [resolved reduced-critical theorem](research_actual_reduced_braid_critical_scheme.md)
derives the new correspondence from the actual finite coefficients.
It factors each \(S_r\) into ordered finite Euler blocks,
keeps the exact multinomial phases and all cutoffs, and computes
their canonical equations directly. On the first resolved chart
\[
 A_1=1+p_1t,\qquad f_1=-t,\qquad
 e_1=-p_1^2t/(1+p_1t),
\]
the total original lowering coordinate is \(-t\).
At \(t=0\), the retained \(p_1\) is precisely simultaneous
upper-unipotent conjugation. It is not discarded at the
central new meridian.

The literal reduced boundary generator
\(\kappa S_{m-1}D\) agrees with the quotient of the
original \(R_1\) map on this level, including every later
meridian in an arbitrary tail. The other reduced
generators have the same direct comparison. If
\(K_\Sigma^2\ne1\), a possible unipotent closing seam
satisfies \(s(K_\Sigma^{-1}-K_\Sigma)=0\), so it
vanishes over local Artin rings. The reduced fixed
scheme is therefore the true braid fixed scheme
on \(F_\Sigma=0\), divided by that unipotent action.

The presentation lemma supplies regular semisimple
total product. For complete discrete faithful holonomy,
its loxodromic eigenline cannot be a parabolic fixed
point. This gives unit prefixes and unit remaining
physical \(f\)'s in the resolved section. Some \(p_j=0\),
\(A_j=1\) points remain and retain their Springer charts.
Under the existing explicit positive complete gluing
certificate, fixed-meridian rigidity then makes the
geometric reduced germ, after the one common momentum
quotient, a reduced point. An ordinary Hessian statement
requires an actual regular holomorphic phase chart;
the resolved correspondence alone does not supply one.

The [Bloch--Wigner comparison](research_reduced_word_bloch_wigner_comparison.md)
also fixes the single-valued regulator for this reduced
network. A positive \(S_r\) contributes
\[
 \beta_S=\sum_j([B_j]+[C_j]-[B_jC_j]).
\]
Its inverse uses the literal inverse graph, including
its Gaussian and sign. The input/output regulator
differential shows that the reduced and conjugated
original local expressions differ by a constant.
A generic real point of the common rational chart
calibrates that constant to zero.

Before closure the exact identity retains both ends:
\[
 D(\beta_{\rm red})=D(\beta_{\rm original})
       +D(\beta_{S_m})(z)-D(\beta_{S_m})(z').
\]
At the actual regular-total fixed point \(z'=z\).
Continuous Bloch--Wigner limits handle resolved shapes
equal to \(0,1,\infty\), using the pre-closure identity
rather than assuming nearby regular critical points.
The original marked fundamental-cycle comparison
therefore gives
\[
                    D(\beta_{\rm red})
                      =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K).
\]
This is a classical single-valued regulator statement.
It does not determine the marked holomorphic action
constant, a local quantum amplitude, a finite-cycle
coefficient, or the asymptotic source.

## The reduced physical support and its geometric endpoint obstruction

The [reduced flow theorem](research_reduced_braid_flow_faces.md)
uses the actual \(R,S,D\) graph, whose residual wires may
have several closed cycles. Every such cycle visits an
\(S\)-donor, since otherwise it would remain a separate
component of the original knot. An \(S\)-star reaches
every other cycle. The full directed graph is therefore
strongly connected. Summing directed cycles through
its edges constructs a strictly positive integral
circulation, and a fixed rescaling places every edge
between \(c_G(N-1)\) and \((N-1)/2\) for all large \(N\).
All intermediate donor and recipient bounds remain.

This does not place a geometric boundary pattern
inside that support. On the actual all-\(f\)-unit,
regular-total chart, let \(I\) be every clock-one edge.
The full \(S\)-junction equations give the necessary
zero-status rules with all partial denominators
retained. If \(I\ne\varnothing\), knot routing and
\(K_\Sigma^2\ne1\) force an open run of \(I\)-wires;
whole \(I\)-cycles may coexist and are retained.
Their complete summed budget proves
\[
 (T+2)\omega<N-1,\quad
 D_i\le\omega\ (i\in I)
 \ \Longrightarrow\
 D_e\le\omega\text{ for some }e\notin I,
\]
where \(T\) counts every physical and \(S\)-branch transfer.
Mixed lower/upper endpoints and long transfer aliases
remain. If \(I\) is empty there is no endpoint assertion.

Thus the reduced physical domain has a strict interior,
while a nonempty geometric clock-one pattern cannot
be isolated from additional nonunit-clock boundaries.
This directs the analytic work toward actual mixed
kernels, projectors and interface terms; a local
resolved optimum alone is insufficient.

## The actual reduced matrix norm is not a geometric source norm

The [resummed Markov calibration](research_reduced_markov_matrix_and_spectral_source_bound.md)
checks the new norm route against an exact presentation operation.
For two positive stabilizations of the one-factor identity, the
normalized original source is exactly one. The actual reduced
matrix on two factors nevertheless has diagonal coefficients
with modulus
\[
             \frac{s_a}{s_bs_{a-b}},\qquad
 s_j=\prod_{r=1}^j2\sin(\pi r/N),\quad a\ge b.
\]
The intervening transfer sum has already been evaluated exactly
by a finite Newton identity; this is not an unresolved positive
path majorant.

For \(3\mid N\), \(a=2N/3,b=N/3\), this diagonal has
logarithm \(Nc_*+O(\log N)\), where
\[
 c_*=-3\int_0^{1/3}\log(2\sin(\pi u))\,du>0.
\]
It gives exponential operator and Hilbert--Schmidt norm
growth with source still one. Positive diagonal metric
changes preserve the offending diagonal entry. A unitary
Fourier transform preserves those norms. This rules out
interpreting the reduced norm as an automatically sharp
geometric source size. It does not show that the same
excess is additive after an arbitrary hyperbolic exterior.

The exact Cartan-block trace does provide a stronger,
basis-independent upper estimate. If \(B_a(M)\) are
the fixed weight blocks of the actual reduced word,
analytic on \(|M-1|\le\eta/N\), then
\[
 |\Phi_0(W(1))|
 \le C_{m,\eta}N^m
       \sup_{\substack{|M-1|=\eta/N\\a}}\rho(B_a(M)).
\]
This uses the exact scalar kernel, its \(O(N)\) bound
on the meridian circle, the elementary trace bound
\(|\operatorname{Tr}B_a|\le\dim(U_a)\rho(B_a)\),
and the maximum principle for the original analytic
source. No eigenvector conditioning is used.
The spectral growth is not estimated or identified
with hyperbolic volume. Its relation to the coherent
geometric contribution remains open.

## The reduced source has explicit generators and an exact presentation adapter

The [reduced braid-source theorem](research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md)
makes \(B_0\) an explicit finite network. The constant-coefficient
map \(\mathcal B_m\) is an algebra homomorphism on actual total
intertwiners. For the original positive checked braid generators,
\[
 \mathcal B_m(R_i)=R_{i-1}\quad(i\ge2),\qquad
 \mathcal B_m(R_1)=\kappa S_{m-1}D_{\rm red},
\]
where
\[
 D_{\rm red}w_b=(-1)^b q^{b(b+1)}M^{-2b}w_b.
\]
The first formula uses the original crossings on the remaining
factors; the second uses their explicit triangular prefix operator.
Negative generators are their exact inverses. All original scalar
and framing lines and their meridian derivatives remain.

The scalar-kernel identity below also proves
\(\Phi_0(XY)=\Phi_0(YX)\) for actual homogeneous intertwiners
on the common-meridian root family. Indeed their constant
coefficients commute with the Cartan kernel, so ordinary
remaining-factor trace cyclicity applies. This does not
erase defects of arbitrary marked arrays or prove a
quantum-normal identity. It does permit actual unmarked
braid conjugation with the original pointed source.

There is consequently a general presentation improvement.
For any irreducible complete knot representation, explicit
Hurwitz conjugations and at most three positive Markov
stabilizations arrange a total meridian product \(P\)
with \(\operatorname{tr}(P)^2\ne4\). If \(P\) is a
noncentral parabolic, irreducibility supplies a parabolic
meridian with a different eigenline. Repeating it once
or twice changes the total product to \(H_j^tP\);
the trace is affine in \(t\) with nonzero slope, so
one of these choices is regular semisimple. A central
product needs one preliminary stabilization.

This uses the same knot and actual source. A finite
Newton identity gives the literal positive-stabilization
scalar \(\alpha=\kappa x^{1-N}\); the original
zero-framing compensation cancels it exactly. This is
not an additional normalization selected after the
calculation. A finite classical \(P_{21}=0\) frame is
then available. No assertion that all other shapes
lie in a common regular chart, or that a geometric
cycle contributes, is inferred.

Finally, if the actual reduced word is analytic on
\(|M-1|\le\eta/N\), its first derivative can be absorbed
in a genuine Cauchy collar bound:
\[
 |\Phi_0(W(1))|
 \le N^{m-1}\left(1+\frac{N}{m\eta}\right)
       \sup_{|M-1|=\eta/N}\|\mathcal B_m(W(M))\|.
\]
The functional costs only a polynomial in \(N\).
Estimating the actual reduced word and proving its
geometric noncancellation remain the research target.

## The universal kernel is scalar, and only the first meridian derivative remains

The [scalar-kernel theorem](research_scalar_prefix_kernel_and_first_meridian_jet.md)
improves the bounded-jet reconstruction below. The universal
rational kernel simplifies exactly to
\[
 \mathfrak h_N(k,\omega;M)=\frac{D_N(M)}{D_N(Mk)},\qquad
 D_N(z)=\frac{z^N-z^{-N}}{z-z^{-1}}.
\]
There is no remaining Casimir dependence, including on
nonsemisimple remaining tensor blocks.

The proof is finite and retains the original source.
In two independent generic colors, closed first-factor
Casimir paths give a polynomial in the second Cartan of
degree at most the path length. The highest coefficient
is independent of the second Casimir. Its actual pivotal
trace kills every degree below \(N-1\). Lagrange coupons
therefore determine the kernel up to one scalar moment.
A finite telescope calibrates that moment, including
its phase. Varying the second color then gives \(N\)
distinct Casimir interpolation nodes for a polynomial
of degree at most \(N-1\), proving the displayed identity.
No modified-trace theorem is a proof premise.

For a common-meridian actual intertwiner family, write
\[
 B=B_0(1),\qquad B'= \partial_M B_0(1),\qquad
 K=K_{\rm r}(1),\qquad
 \varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)(m-1)}.
\]
The exact original pointed functional is
\[
 \boxed{\displaystyle
 \Phi_0(W(1))=
 \frac{\operatorname{Tr}((K+K^{-1})B)}{2\varepsilon}
 +\frac{\operatorname{Tr}((K-K^{-1})B')}{2\varepsilon m}.}
\]
Its residue cancellation is the necessary identity
\(\operatorname{Tr}((K-K^{-1})B)=0\).
Both the derivative of the actual prefix transform and
the tail pivot are included. The formula is a meridian
identity at fixed \(q_N\); quantum normals still retain
the unreduced \(J_N\) row.

In the actual remaining occupation norm, \(K\) is unitary,
so the cost of this functional is uniformly polynomial:
\[
 |\Phi_0(W(1))|
 \le N^{m-1}
       \big(\|B_0(1)\|+m^{-1}\|B_0'(1)\|\big).
\]
This bounds the functional, not the two actual source
matrices. It supplies no lower bound for their weighted
trace. Uniform asymptotics and a surviving geometric
contribution remain open. The general finite-exception
volume theorem is not claimed.

## The pointed source needs only a bounded meridian jet

Two general source results now sharpen the long-band reduction.
They apply at fixed primitive \(q_N\) to analytic common-meridian
families of actual total intertwiners. They do not assume that
arbitrary marked arrays satisfy the homogeneous intertwining
relations.

The [commutant reduction](research_prefix_commutant_and_pointed_normal_functional.md)
gives
\[
 W'=S^{-1}WS=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}F_1^n\otimes B_n,\qquad
 K_{\rm r}B_n=Q^nB_nK_{\rm r}.
\]
The remaining lowering equation is
\[
 [\mathcal E_{\rm r},B_{n-1}]
  =-(1-Q^n)(MK_{\rm r}Q^{-n}-M^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1})B_n,
 \qquad [\mathcal E_{\rm r},B_{N-1}]=0.
\]
The original highest-cut, pivotal source is exactly
\[
 \Phi_0(W)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm r}
   \left(K_{\rm r}^{1-N}
       \sum_{n=0}^{N-1}x_1^{-n}F_{\rm r}^{\,n}B_n\right).
\]
Thus the constant coefficient at \(M=1\) alone loses
source information. A calibrated two-head Casimir coupon
has \(B_0(1)=0\), square zero, and original pivotal partial
trace \(N I\). Adding it to the identity preserves
invertibility while varying the pointed source. This is
a statement about the intertwiner/coupon algebra, not a
counterexample for a knot or for an actual braid word.

Off the finite resonant meridians, the displayed recursion
determines all \(B_n\) from \(B_0(M)\). Its trace adjoint gives
an explicit universal rational kernel in \(K_{\rm r}\) and
the full remaining Casimir. The original source is the
prescribed finite part of its pairing with \(B_0(M)\).
The initial pole-order estimate was \(N-1\).

The [bounded-jet reconstruction](research_bounded_meridian_jet_source_reconstruction.md)
now improves that estimate to two, independently of \(N\)
and the number of heads. It constructs total-Casimir
projectors and explicit highest seeds on a punctured
meridian disk. Their raising chains and exact lowering
dual rows reconstruct the full actual intertwiner.
There is only one spectral projector in each term.
At \(M=1\), distinct Casimir branches collide only in
pairs, so this projector has at most a simple pole.
The lowering-arrow product has at most one simple zero.
The complete source kernel therefore has pole order
at most two.

Concretely the original functional has the form
\[
 \Phi_0(W(1))=[t^0]\sum_a
   \operatorname{Tr}_{U_a}
       \bigl(H_a^{(2)}(1+t)B_{0,a}(1+t)\bigr),
 \qquad \operatorname{pole}_{t=0}H_a^{(2)}\le2.
\]
The matrices \(H_a^{(2)}\) are given explicitly and contain
the original cut and tail pivot. Hence only the meridian
jet of \(B_0\) through order \(\min(N-1,2)\) is needed.
Arbitrary multiplicities and absent weights are included.
No scalar Casimir specialization, positivity, or generic
modified-trace theorem is used.

This is a genuine fixed-order reduction of the exact
source problem. It does not bound the resulting coefficients
as \(N\) grows. Uniform asymptotics of the reduced source,
its comparison with the geometric relative cycle, and a
nonzero surviving geometric contribution are still needed.
Quantum derivatives must retain the unreduced off-root
prefix term \(J_N\); a meridian-jet identity is not a
license to discard that term. The frozen long-twist
theorem and its range have not changed.

## Framing infinity is an explicit source wall, with long bands retained

The [framing-infinity reduction](research_framing_infinity_prefix_source_wall.md)
connects the new prefix transform to the actual geometric framing
coordinate. With \(Z=x_1^{-1}L_1F_{\rm r}\), the exact identities are
\[
 S^{-1}K_1S=(I-Z)K_1,\qquad
 S^{-1}K_{\rm r}S=
       \left(\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}Q^{-n}Z^n\right)K_{\rm r}.
\]
The finite sum is the actual inverse of \(I-Q^{-1}Z\)
because \(Z^N=0\). Its order relative to the tail Cartan
factor is retained. The literal unilateral flag commutes
with \(S\), but its endpoint vector, the cut and the tail
pivot have their full transformed formulas. In particular
the constant boundary vector is not an exact eigenvector
of a nilpotent shift.

Choose a prefix with nonzero lower-left reference entry;
irreducibility guarantees one. Direct multiplication of
the selected-flag frame gives \(f_\Sigma=1+r^{-1}+O(r^{-2})\).
On the fixed-cut principal chart this forces
\[
 A_{\rm new}=-r^{-1}+O(r^{-2}),\qquad
 1-z=-\frac1{A_*r}+O(r^{-2}).
\]
Thus infinity approaches \(z=1\) in this specified
prefix transform. This connects actual operator coordinates
to the geometric wall, rather than assigning the framing
coordinate to an arbitrary Fourier radius. It does not
assert a uniform asymptotic for the growing matrix \(S\)
at that wall.

The source term there has an exact joint-band expression:
\[
 \sum_{a,b,b'}\sum_{n=0}^{a}
   \pi_N(a,b)Q^{-n}x_1^{-n}
   (W_N)_{(a,b),(a-n,b')}
   (F_{\rm r}^{\,n}K_{\rm r})_{b',b}.
\]
All original finite walls and pivots remain. Fixed-transfer
asymptotics do not evaluate this sum, which includes bands
with \(n\) proportional to \(N\).

There is a scalar polynomial comparison, but it is not
the joint-band contraction. If \(r=NR\) and
\(\alpha=1/(A_*R)\), the normalized scalar sum tends to
\((e^\alpha-1)/(\alpha-2\pi i)\), with its removable value.
At \(z=1\) the exact scalar sum is zero, not \(N\).
This illustrates why the finite numerator and the
environmental bands cannot be dropped. The source pairing,
its uniform geometric approximation and its nonvanishing
remain open.

## A source-preserving Fourier transition at a vanishing prefix minor

The [relative prefix transition](research_relative_prefix_fourier_transition.md)
now gives an actual finite adapter for the complementary classical
prefix entry. At a simple zero of \(P_{11}\), determinant one makes
\(P_{21}\) a unit. Its specified ordered quantum lift is
\(C=F_\Sigma K_\Sigma\). This finite operator is nilpotent at the
root, so a change of Fourier basis cannot make it invertible.
The correct replacement retains a boundary correction.

For any number \(m\) of original heads, put
\[
 Z=x_1^{-1}L_1F_{\rm r},\qquad
 S=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{Z^j}{(Q;Q)_j}.
\]
Here \(L_1\) is the actual unilateral lowering shift, and
\(F_{\rm r}\) is the ordered raising coproduct on the remaining
heads. The finite operator \(S\) is unipotent. At the root,
\(S^{-1}F_\Sigma S=F_1\). Off root the exact additional column
\[
 J_N=(Q;Q)_{N-1}^{-1}
          S^{-1}F_\Sigma^N(T_{0,N-1}\otimes I)
\]
remains, including all normal derivatives.

After the explicitly stated diagonal gauge and finite
Vandermonde transform, the complementary entry is exactly
\[
 \mathcal A C\mathcal A^{-1}
       =Y-u_Nv^t+\mathcal D_N.
\]
At the root \(u_N=\varrho^N u_0\) and
\(\mathcal D_N=0\). The correction has rank \(N^{m-1}\).
Its norm in the stated Fourier metric is \(|\varrho|\), equal
to that of \(Y\); a small central factor \(\varrho^N\) does
not justify discarding it. The evaluation radius \(\varrho\)
is kept distinct from the geometric framing coordinate.

All three prefix generators are transported, including the
full Casimir on the remaining tensor factors. In particular
the root identity before the final gauge is
\[
 S^{-1}\mathcal E_\Sigma S(w_a\otimes v)
   =w_a\otimes\mathcal E_{\rm r}v+
       w_{a-1}\otimes
       (M_1K_{\rm r}Q^{-a}-M_1^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1})v
\]
for \(a>0\), with the second term zero at \(a=0\).
Its exact Fourier version follows because the missing lower
endpoint is multiplied by a coefficient that vanishes there.
The prefix Casimir is generally nonscalar and is retained.
These root simplifications are not used for quantum normals.

The note also gives a partial inverse of \(C\), its two
explicit coupled endpoint projectors, and an arbitrary-source
trace row. The latter includes the marked commutator and the
off-root residual. Thus the original cut, masks, pivots and
scalar lines have specified images. No endpoint trace has

This resolves the finite algebra of the proposed change of
coordinates. Its local asymptotic matching to a geometric
generating function and the actual pairing of the boundary

## The complete endpoint support obstruction and its Fourier equation

The [boundary-propagation theorem](research_geometric_endpoint_boundary_propagation.md)
strengthens the earlier flow-face result below. Let \(I\) contain
every edge whose geometric clock equals one, let \(c\) be the crossing
count, and put \(d=N-1\). For every original supported state,
\[
 (c+2)\omega<d,\qquad
 \min(a_i,d-a_i)\le\omega\quad(i\in I)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \min(a_e,d-a_e)\le\omega
 \quad\hbox{for some }e\notin I.
\]
This includes arbitrary mixtures of lower and upper wire endpoints
and long unit-transfer aliases. Summing the flow equations over
the maximal clock-one wire runs makes internal long transfers
cancel. Transfers escaping those runs cannot be long if their
receivers stay strictly inside the complementary region. The
resulting budget contradicts the required drop along the runs.
Thus no physical sector has precisely the geometric unit edges
thin and every other edge farther inside.

This corrects the possible interpretation of the earlier discussion:
the conditional statement that such a strict sector would need
a long transfer has an empty hypothesis. Its unpublished note is
retained with a supersession notice, and is not an occurrence
argument. A large local matrix entry alone cannot establish that
the geometric contribution reaches the original closing functional.

For a fixed integer width \(B\), the
[Fourier-source equation](research_geometric_endpoint_fourier_annihilator.md)
records the support result without making an amplitude assumption.
If \(\sigma_e\) shifts the auxiliary Fourier variable by \(h v_e\),
where \(a_e=v_e\cdot k\) and \(Q=e^h\), the masked source satisfies
\[
 \prod_{e\notin I}\prod_{t=0}^{B}
       (\sigma_e-Q^t)(\sigma_e-Q^NQ^{-1-t})\,\Psi_N=0.
\]
This is an identity of the full finite parameter germ. In
particular all derivatives of \(Q^N\), the moving shifts, and
the original coefficient marks remain. The root-family principal
symbol is
\(\prod_{e\notin I}(\lambda_e-1)^{2(B+1)}\), a unit at the
specified geometric clock pattern. An explicit recursive formal
inverse therefore excludes a nonzero formal local WKB solution
there for this masked equation. It does not provide an analytic
bound, a decomposition into actual asymptotic components, or a
peripheral knot \(A\)-polynomial. Widths increasing with \(N\)
give increasing-order operators, for which no uniform inverse
estimate has been proved.

## Long-transfer matrices and their full normal factors

The [actual long-transfer calculation](research_actual_long_transfer_cross_collar_kernel.md)
gives exact crossing blocks between opposite finite head collars.
Writing the input as \((d-u,v)\), the unpermuted output as

At completeness the clock equation

 \mathcal L_{N,B,O}(\zeta)

now gives an analytic transition for the

whenever \(T_N^N=0\) and

lower bound without assuming a

geometric approximate eigenpacket.
Uniform local invertibility is
not a lower bound for its final
scalar contraction, and it does
not estimate the outgoing currents.

## A bounded regular framing period cannot be the entire normalized source

The [normalization constraint](research_regular_framing_period_normalization_constraint.md)
rules out a tempting shortcut in the general
framing comparison. A compact regular
\(r\)-chain with uniformly bounded mass,
including absolute multiplicities, and
uniformly controlled descending normal
collars contributes at most
\[
                    C N^{1/2}e^{N\Lambda}
\]
in the canonical reduced literal source.
This follows directly from its \(c\) normal
Gaussian variables, \(c+1\) lattice
coordinates, and actual \(c+1\) factorial/
binomial amplitude factors.

The already proved exact original
figure-eight source has asymptotic
\[
 K_N(4_1)=3^{-1/4}N^{3/2}e^{N\Lambda}
                                  (1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
Its complete cups, caps, Cartan factors
and reduced cut have no hidden external
\(N\). In the new braid presentation the
occupation-independent factors are unit
phases. Adding an old cut-average \(N\)
would double-count its normalization.

Consequently a bounded regular-chain
model cannot exhaust this known leading
term with remainder
\(o(N^{3/2}e^{N\Lambda})\).
This uses the example to test a proposed
universal source map, not to add another
individual volume-conjecture case.

More precisely, if a proved global
comparison has the form
\[
 K_N=u_N C N^{1/2}e^{N\sigma_*}
                             (P_N+o(N)),\qquad |u_N|=1,
\]
and the same scalar has nonzero
\(N^{3/2}\) leading magnitude, then
\(|P_N|\sim C' N\). A bounded signed
endpoint sum alone does not control
the normal error when the chain mass
grows or its support escapes.

The missing scale can therefore occur
through growing multiplicity or extent,
nonuniform endpoint/infinity layers,
or other same-action currents. The
theorem chooses none of these mechanisms
and proves no actual framing pushforward.
The local density and volume exponential
are unchanged. In particular an abstract
unit centralizer period cannot be
declared the normalized original source.

The [facet compatibility proof](research_actual_facet_seams_and_geometric_boundary.md)

       +g_\theta'(u)1_{e={\rm cut}}
                  =\sum_\nu t_\nu a_{\nu,e},
\]
modulo the exact incidence-transpose vertex gauges.

\(\operatorname{diag}(\exp(\sum_\nu t_\nu a_{\nu,e}),1)\).

over local Artin algebras. It does not continue

together with infinity. Their degrees are at

limits. The translated side prisms have
nonreal factorial lengths and are not
themselves such faces. Neither their periods
nor the original endpoint coefficients have

## The regular principal stationary scheme is the midpoint representation scheme

The [soft-cut stationary-source proof](research_soft_binomial_cut_stationary_source.md)
uses the actual weighted occupation array, not an assumed
asymptotic formula for a full coherent crossing kernel.
Its exact binomial ratio is
\[
 \frac{\pi_{N,a+1}}{\pi_{N,a}}
  =\frac{c_0-h-u}{u+h},\qquad
 c_0=2\pi i,\quad h=c_0/N,\quad u=ha.
\]
It gives the principal boundary action
\[
 g'(u)=\log((c_0-u)/u),\qquad
 g(c_0/2)=g'(c_0/2)=0.
\]
The constant is fixed by the trace-one binomial normalization.
The finite mean is \((N-1)/2\), so the exact occupation
center differs from \(u=c_0/2\) by \(-h/2\).
The principal statement does not delete that shift or parity.

The changed cut equation is
\[
 \frac{p_{\rm out}}{p_{\rm in}}=\frac{u}{c_0-u}.
\]
It must be combined with every internal stationary row.
The actual braid preserves the ordered coproduct functions
\(K_1K_{\rm tail}\),
\(e_1K_{\rm tail}+E_{\rm tail}\), and
\(f_1+K_1^{-1}F_{\rm tail}\).
Once the other tensor positions close, these identities
force the cut \(K,e,f\) to close too. Where either
\(1-A\) or \(1-x^2/A\) is a unit, the physical formulas
then force \(p_{\rm out}=p_{\rm in}\).
The new cut row is therefore exactly \(u=c_0/2\).

This is an equality of localized exponentiated principal
critical ideals with the full braid fixed-point ideal
plus \((u-\pi i)\), on the specified logarithmic sheet.
After a classical common-momentum frame choice, it is
the actual selected-flag knot representation scheme at
\(A=-1\). The midpoint-frame theorem supplies its
regular complete geometric point for every hyperbolic
knot and finite braid.

The finite source cycle is also specified: the cut
latitude circle and the intermediate compact coherent
spheres with all original factors. Their common diagonal
\(U(1)\) angle can be removed exactly by a change of
variables, giving integral one. This is distinct from
the residual geometric centralizer \(r\), which survives.
Neither endpoint/nonunit strata nor an additive Fourier
charge is removed by the localized ideal calculation.

In particular, this does not prove a uniform analytic
phase or nonzero amplitude for the full growing coherent
crossing kernels. A selected-column asymptotic cannot
replace their additional coherent sums. The relative
geometric cycle, its coefficient and the general
volume lower bound remain unproved.

The [midpoint-frame proof](research_midpoint_geometric_braid_frame.md)

\[
 F(r,s)=\begin{pmatrix}r&1-r\\s&-s\end{pmatrix},

\]

 (F^{-1}PF)_{11}
 =\frac cs r(1-r)+(a-d)r+d+bs.

At \(s=-2\), it could vanish identically only if

absent from the full primitive cusp lattice. Thus each
actual group-word prefix excludes at most two \(r\).

and \(3/2\) in this normalized cusp basis.

 \begin{pmatrix}-M&M+M^{-1}\\-2M&2M+M^{-1}\end{pmatrix},

The same finite chart remains regular on a sufficiently

## A binomial cut has a polynomially bounded compact framing density

The [binomial-cut proof](research_binomial_cut_framing_density.md)
replaces the single interior occupation by the trace-one probe
\[
 P_N^{\rm cut}=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}
       2^{-(N-1)}\binom{N-1}{a}T_a.
\]
For the original unmarked cut endomorphism \(C_N=F_NI\),
this computes exactly the same scalar \(F_N\), at every
level. The marked comparison is still its explicit Ward
commutator; its current has norm \(O(N)\) and every fixed
meridian derivative has polynomial norm on the stated
shrinking disk.

The whole compact normal-residue density is explicit. With
\(d=N-1\), it is the polynomial evaluation kernel
\[
 p_N(T)=\sum_{k=0}^{d}(2k+1)\mathsf L_k(0)
                                \mathsf L_k(2T-1),
\]
where \(\mathsf L_k\) is the ordinary Legendre polynomial.
For the actual diagonal coherent polynomial
\(\overline f_C(T)=\sum_a C_{aa}\binom daT^a(1-T)^{d-a}\),
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}(P_N^{\rm cut}C)
 =\int_0^1p_N(T)\overline f_C(T)\,dT
 =\overline f_C(1/2).
\]
Equivalently the full coherent symbol can be integrated on
the compact latitude circle \(T=1/2,\ |v|=1\). This is an
exact finite-matrix identity, not a stationary approximation.
The Legendre evaluation kernel is classical; the proof
derives its normalization for this original cut.

Writing \(m=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\) and
\(A_N=(2m+1)4^{-m}\binom{2m}{m}\), the exact bounds are
\[
 p_N(0)=p_N(1)=(-1)^mA_N,\qquad
 \|p_N\|_{L^2}=A_N\le2\sqrt N,\qquad
 \|p_N\|_\infty\le2N^{3/2}.
\]
Thus the entire compact real density has polynomial cost,
where the individual middle-occupation density had
exponentially large endpoint coefficients. Every fixed
real derivative is also polynomially bounded. The
normal pole order still grows with \(N\), and no bound
on a fixed complex neighborhood is supplied.

Equal density endpoints do not remove marked currents:
their exact pairing is
\[
 \frac1N\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal T_N((P_N^{\rm nor})')C)
 =(-1)^mA_N(C_{00}-C_{dd})+\overline f_C'(1/2).
\]
Both terms, the original product-current correction and
the off-divisor normal data remain. The latitude circle
has not been identified with the remaining geometric
centralizer quotient. Its source phase, transverse
pushforward and original relative cycle must still be
analyzed before it can give the required geometric
coefficient. No new filling case is claimed.

## Small raw filling residuals cannot be the general lower-bound mechanism

The [actual-source overlap comparison](research_actual_filling_quotient_overlap_separation.md)
shows why the positive quotient minimum below needs a direct
analysis. Let \(\rho_{\boldsymbol n}(H_N)\) be the fraction of
the raw source's squared norm lying on its target period line.
For two fixed filling tuples,
\[
 \rho_{\boldsymbol n}(H_N)
 \le
 \left[6^rN^{5r/2}
       \prod_i(1+|m_i-n_i|/2)\right]^2
 \left|\frac{\phi_{\boldsymbol n}(H_N)}
              {\phi_{\boldsymbol m}(H_N)}\right|^2 .
\]
This follows from the norm of the original closing row and the
full-Hermite crossing multiplier. If another filling has a
strictly larger exponential rate, the target overlap fraction
is exponentially small. This is a limsup upper estimate;
equality of rates would need an additional raw norm bound.

There is an unconditional source-exact application. The known
normalization packet has target zero filling \(\kappa^2\)
and alternate filling
\(Z_N=\sum_a|(Q;Q)_a|^2\).
An elementary sine-product estimate gives
\[
 \rho_0(H_N)\le144(3/2)^4N(3/2)^{-N/3}.
\]
This actual tangle inserts into any nonzero exterior without
changing the overlap fraction or the target knot. It is not
a new knot example or a substitute positive model.
The smallest nonzero kernel eigenvalue is
\(\lambda_{*,N}=N\sin(\pi/N)/((N-1)\pi)\).
The raw residual therefore satisfies
\[
 \sum_i\|K_iH_N\|_{\boldsymbol n}^{\,2}
 \ge\lambda_{*,N}^2(1-\rho_{\boldsymbol n}(H_N))
                         \|H_N\|_{\boldsymbol n}^{\,2}.
\]
Consequently automatic concentration of the raw source near
the period line is unavailable, even when the target identity
is already true. The minimized energy can still have the
correct geometric rate; it subtracts precisely the excess
directions responsible for this example.

## The filling problem has an explicit positive quotient minimum

The [canonical Hermite splitting](research_canonical_hermite_filling_kernel_split.md)
works in the full physical space
\(\mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2)\), including first
derivatives at the double roots. In the circle basis
\(L_j=(-1)^{j-1}U_{j-1}(z/2)\), its zero-twist operator is
\[
 K_0L_j=\frac{\sin(j\pi/N)}{j\pi/N}L_j .
\]
Its image is exactly the kernel of the original closing row.
Conjugation by the actual signed crossing gives the corresponding
operator \(K_i\) for any specified filling power in slot \(i\).
The inverse on its image has Hilbert norm at most \(\pi N/2\)
in the explicitly specified metric pulled back by that crossing.
The metric is polynomially equivalent to the circle coefficient
metric for each fixed filling tuple.

Here is a direct useful consequence for an arbitrary coupled
exterior class \(H\in\mathcal H_N^{\otimes r}\). Let \(P_i\)
be the orthogonal projection onto the one-dimensional kernel of
\(K_i\), let \(P=\prod_iP_i\), and let
\(\phi_{\boldsymbol n}\) be the original tensor filling row. Then
\[
 \boxed{\displaystyle
 \inf_{V_1,\ldots,V_r}
 \left\|H-\sum_{i=1}^{r}K_iV_i\right\|_{\boldsymbol n}^{\,2}
 =\|PH\|_{\boldsymbol n}^{\,2}
 =\frac{|\phi_{\boldsymbol n}(H)|^2}{N^{4r}}.}
\]
All operators and the metric are specified before evaluating
\(H\). This is a convex quadratic minimization in finite
dimensional vector spaces; the co-source image is not asserted
to be an ideal.

For completeness, put
\(E_i=(\prod_{j<i}P_j)(I-P_i)\).
These are mutually orthogonal projections and
\(\sum_iE_i=I-P\). The specified inverse \(G_i\) obeys
\(K_iG_iE_i=E_i\). Consequently
\(\sum_i\operatorname{im}K_i=\operatorname{im}(I-P)
=\ker\phi_{\boldsymbol n}\).
Orthogonal projection proves the displayed infimum, and
\(V_i=G_iE_iH\) realizes it with
\[
 \sum_i\|V_i\|_{\boldsymbol n}^{\,2}
 \le(\pi N/2)^2\|H-PH\|_{\boldsymbol n}^{\,2}.
\]
The minimizing residual is unique; its expressions by the
\(V_i\) need not be.

The remaining analytic problem is to estimate this minimum for
the actual exterior source at the geometric exponential rate.
Neither the inverse bound nor positivity of this quadratic
objective gives such an estimate. A source can lie entirely in
the image being subtracted. The general source lower bound and
the finite-exception volume theorem remain open.

\(\mu(w)=mw+B\), \(\lambda(w)=lw+D\), with \(B\ne0\).
Writing \(d=D/B\), commutation gives \(l=1+(m-1)d\).
For any primitive integer slope, including negative powers, the
whole word is
\[
 \mu^a\lambda^b(w)=m^al^b w+B t_{a,b},\qquad
 m^al^b-1=(m-1)t_{a,b}.
\]
The full projective matrix filling relation is \(t_{a,b}=0\).
The eigenvalue equation alone keeps an extra parabolic factor.
The note proves the corresponding saturation identity in the
regular peripheral ring; it does not recover the translation
coordinate by saturating an already eliminated A-polynomial.

On the actual centered complete chart, let \(V=U\tau\),
\(\Im\tau>0\), and \(\psi(s)=(e^s-1)/s\), \(\psi(0)=1\).
The exact whole factor is
\[
 t_{a,b}=(a+b\tau)
       \frac{\psi(aU+bV)}{\psi(U)}.
\]
Thus matrix closure forces a nonzero centered integer charge.
It also gives a quantitative lower bound on the slope translation
throughout a fixed small zero-charge region, in the normalized
affine frame. No unbounded conjugation or escaping source chart
is covered by that bound.

## Actual long-filled groups have a quantitative representation-volume gap

The [filled-group theorem](research_long_filled_group_representation_volume_gap.md)
removes the need to prescribe a Fourier label for the classical
comparison. Fix a complete hyperbolic core with its marked positive
geometric certificate; any earlier short fillings are part of this
fixed core. Fill any nonempty subset of its cusps along independently
sufficiently long primitive slopes, leaving the other cusps
boundary-parabolic. Every other admitted projective representation of
the actual filled group has signed volume at most
\[
 \operatorname{Vol}(M(\sigma))-
       \min\{\delta/2,\,3c_1/\ell_{\max}^2\},
 \qquad \ell_i=\sqrt{a_i^2+b_i^2},
\]
where the positive constants depend on the fixed marked core.
The remaining cusp condition is substantive; different source
decorations of one projective holonomy are not separated by volume.

The full matrix relation supplies the missing integer condition.
Its centered slope charge is integral. If it were zero, the
peripheral maps would be nontrivial translations with primitive
slope translation \(B_i(a_i+b_i\tau_i)\ne0\), contradicting
the filled-group relation. The charge comparison therefore applies
to every nearby competing filled-group representation. Outside
the fixed complete-holonomy neighborhood, near-maximal rigidity
gives the other part of the gap. The proof also verifies equality
of filled and pulled-back core representation volumes by explicit
cyclic solid-torus and cusp maps.

This settles the classical comparison for this geometric setting.
For a quantum source we still have to prove its full matrix
filling relations, action-volume normalization, boundary control,
and nonzero geometric coefficient. Neither exponentiated equations
nor the new volume gap supplies those source statements.

## Centered long fillings have a uniform representation-volume comparison

The [centered cone-path proof](research_centered_long_cone_representation_volume_gap.md)
starts from any fixed hyperbolic core supplied with the marked positive
geometric certificate. That core may already have short fillings.
The uniform peripheral contraction works throughout the real
charge cube and throughout a larger box
\(|q_i|\le\rho_*\sqrt{a_i^2+b_i^2}\). In this fixed centered chart,
write \(V_i=U_i\tau_i(U)\) and
\(a_iU_i+b_iV_i=2\pi i q_i\). The exact volume differential gives
\[
 \frac{\partial\mathcal V}{\partial q_i}
 =-\frac{2\pi^2q_i\,\Im\tau_i(U(q))}
              {|a_i+b_i\tau_i(U(q))|^2}.
\]
Consequently volume decreases strictly with each squared absolute
charge. This includes all cusp coupling and needs no comparison
between the different slope lengths.

All choices of signs of unit charges give the same underlying
representation, with different retained flags. Every nonminimal
tuple of nonzero centered integer charges has a positive
quantitative volume deficit for each fixed long slope tuple.
Near-maximal rigidity controls the representations outside the
complete-holonomy neighborhood. The same argument gives a
uniform gap along the entire centered unit-charge cone cube to
competitors satisfying those same centered equations.

This is a representation-volume theorem. It does not infer
centered charges from exponentiated peripheral data or from a
Fourier label on an uncalibrated source sheet. It also does not
transport a quantum contour or prove its geometric coefficient.
In particular, compactness of near-maximal characters does not
make their highest-cut field coordinates compact.

## Exact local occupation cutoffs have a quantitative complex-domain estimate

The [occupation-cutoff proof](research_literal_poisson_occupation_cutoffs.md)
now treats the actual three-mean crossing kernel. At either crossing
sign, keeping all four head occupations below \(N\) means
\[
 S_N=\{(n,c,d)\ge0:n+c<N,\ n+d<N\}.
\]
Its exact multiplier is
\[
 Q_{S_N}(t)=e^{-\sum t_i}
        \sum_{(n,c,d)\in S_N}\frac{t_1^nt_2^ct_3^d}{n!c!d!}.
\]
It acts on the unchanged coupled coefficient function. Three
independent scalar cutoffs would give a different projector.
Differentiation produces the exact outgoing-facet currents, with
their shared corner counted once.

For \(t=N\zeta\), a direct union-tail estimate gives an explicit
open complex domain containing the strict real occupation
polytope on which \(Q_{S_N}=1+O(e^{-\delta N})\), uniformly
with every fixed number of derivatives. This also holds for any
fixed finite product of these factors. Its scalar ingredient is
the classical bound
\[
 |1-Q_N(N\zeta)|\le
       \frac{(|\zeta|e^{1-\Re\zeta})^N}{1-|\zeta|}.
\]

The result supplies a conditional noncancellation estimate.
If a proved common contour has a nonzero contribution of rate
\(H\), its absolute integral has rate at most \(E\), and the
cutoff error satisfies \(\delta>E-H\) over that entire contour,
the projector preserves the leading contribution.
Neither existence of this common contour nor its cutoff-domain
condition is supplied by the estimate. The stationary arguments
are lifted logarithmic occupations, not just tetrahedral angles;
Rivin positivity alone does not verify these conditions.

## The scalar Borel sum has its exact finite-product normalization

The [pointed interval](research_q_pochhammer_interval_lattice_anchor.md)
is the ordinary q-Pochhammer ratio
\[
 \Pi_c(h,s,Z)=
 \frac{(Ze^{ch};e^h)_\infty}{(Ze^{s+ch};e^h)_\infty},
 \qquad \Re h<0 .
\]
Its exact shift equation and value at \(s=0\) give the literal
finite product at \(s=hL\). Whole Gaussian coefficients continue
polynomially to roots of unity; their factorial pieces must be
canceled before specialization. Off the lattice the same shift
equation permits periodic factors, so pointing alone does not
choose an analytic interpolation.

The [exact color summation](research_color_interval_exact_borel_sum.md)
also evaluates the canonical negative-ray Borel sum, rather than
merely comparing formal coefficients. For \(c=0,1\),
\(\Re h<0\), \(|Z|<1\), and \(|Ze^s|<1\), it proves
\[
 \frac1h\int_0^s\log(1-Ze^t)\,dt+
 \mathcal S_-V_c(h;s,Z)=\log\Pi_c(h,s,Z).
\]
The constant Bernoulli term and the original lower endpoint are
present. If the endpoint logarithm is normalized by subtracting
\(\log(1-Z)\), its principal factor \((1-Z)^{s/h}\) remains
separate. Other fixed integer offsets have an explicit smaller
summation domain.

This pays one scalar analytic comparison. The factorial lower
endpoint, a common meridian chart for mixed crossing signs, finite
projection walls and the assembled physical cycle retain separate
requirements. Scalar q-dilogarithm summation is an established
technique; this calculation supplies its precise adapter to the
literal source and makes no standalone novelty claim.

## A boundary-preserving flow continues scalar quantum exponentials

The [filtered convolution theorem](research_filtered_scalar_borel_convolution_flow.md)
constructs the scalar Borel exponential beyond the initial disk.
For the meromorphic derivative \(g=\partial_\xi\widehat V\),
deform its \(n\)-fold convolution simplex by
\[
 \dot\zeta_i=
 \frac{\operatorname{dist}(\zeta_i,\Omega\cup\{0\})}
      {\sum_j\operatorname{dist}(\zeta_j,\Omega\cup\{0\})}
                                                        \dot\gamma .
\]
Every original zero face stays fixed. On a finite path separated
from the explicitly finite additive set with bounded total action
length, the denominator has a positive lower bound independent
of \(n\). Pole distance, Lipschitz constants and Jacobian estimates
then give
\[
                       |g^{*n}|
                 \le M^n A^{n-1}/(n-1)! .
\]
Holomorphic endpoint collars and relative Stokes prove actual
analytic continuation, not only a pathwise estimate. Consequently
the convolution exponential converges normally, and
\[
 \mathcal B_0(e^V)=e^{v_0}
       \left(1+I_0\sum_{n\ge1}g^{*n}/n!\right)
\]
retains its original constant and primitive history.
Candidate divisors remain excluded even at parameter values
where residues cancel, giving joint parameter neighborhoods.
No unfiltered additive singular set is asserted locally finite.

## The original source has an exact phase surface at every simple Alexander zero

The [general phase-surface theorem](research_actual_borel_phase_surface.md)
removes the quadratic-node and scalar-annihilator hypotheses from
the local source construction. Its premises are the original finite
highest-cut word and a simple zero \(\alpha\ne0,1\) of its Alexander
polynomial. The regular hard-contraction estimate applies without
a nonzero quadratic soft coefficient.

For the source-derived analytic phase
\(f(z,x)=zx-\Psi_0(z,x,0)\), the pullback of the actual Borel
germ has the exact normally convergent continuation
\[
 \mathfrak b_m(z,x)=r(z)\left[
 \frac{a_0(z,x,m)}{f_x(z,x)}
 +\sum_{j\ge1}\frac1{(j-1)!}
   \int_0^x(f(z,x)-f(z,t))^{j-1}a_j(z,t,m)\,dt\right].
\]
The analytic coefficients obey \(\|a_j\|\le MC^j j!\).
On a small bidisk the action oscillation is less than \(1/C\),
so the integral terms converge to a jointly holomorphic function.
All original primitive histories begin at \(x=0\).

The numerator at \(f_x=0\) is the unit \(r a_0\).
Thus the exact pole divisor on this phase surface is \(f_x=0\),
and higher quantum corrections cannot cancel it. There is no
Morse or occupation-nonvanishing assumption.
Since \(f_x=z-\Psi_x\) has \(z\)-derivative one at the origin,
the critical divisor is one smooth graph \(z=\zeta(x)\).
If \(\Psi_0(0,x,0)\) first has term \(\tau x^{p+1}\),
then \(z=s^p\) gives all \(p\) nearby distinct critical branches,
each with an actual nonzero fold minor for \(s\ne0\).
Their leading clock ratios are the original
\(\exp(m\cdot\Theta(z,x_j))\).
The possibility \(\Psi_0(0,x,0)\equiv0\), equivalently
\(\zeta\equiv0\), is retained rather than excluded.

## The phase's critical graph is the attached irreducible character curve

The [general representation quotient](research_general_critical_graph_representation_quotient.md)
proves the exact analytic reduction of the original highest-cut
stationary ideal at every simple Alexander zero.
Its regular hard variables eliminate by unit matrices even at
\(z=0\), leaving
\[
                     aF(z,ab)=bF(z,ab)=0,\qquad
                     F=z-\Psi_x .
\]
The actual diagonal gauge quotient is therefore
\[
                       \mathbb C\{z,x\}/(xF(z,x)),
                            \qquad x=ab .
\]
No occupation coordinate, \(z\), or highest-cut projector is divided
out in that ideal reduction.

An explicit regular Gauss inverse identifies this quotient with the
nearby character germ. Trace projectors give a separating coordinate
\(\chi=x+O(zx,x^2)\). Thus \(x=0\) is the abelian curve, and
\(F=0\) is one smooth attached curve of irreducible characters away
from the intersection. The original stage marks evaluate to its
actual occupations.

Finite soft order is now exactly nonconstancy of the meridian on
that attached character curve. If its meridian is nonconstant,
its finite ramification order gives the \(p\) branches and actual
nonzero marked minors above. If the graph is vertical, it instead
parametrizes a nonconstant character family at \(Y=\alpha\).
The proof does not silently rule out this alternative.

## The original marked Borel source has a nonzero local fold minor

The [endpoint reconstruction](research_actual_marked_fold_borel_reconstruction.md)
uses the common-soft-disk factorial estimate to identify the actual
marked minor. This is a source statement rather than a formal
stationary-sector prediction, under the same simple two-branch
node hypotheses.

After the regular hard contractions, the exact formal source has
phase \(f(z,x)=zx-\Psi_0(z,x,0)\) and analytic amplitude
coefficients \(a_j(z,x,m)\) with
\(\|a_j\|\le MC^j j!\) on common disks for each compact clock set.
Exact residue extraction proves the identity of Borel germs
\[
 b_m(z,\xi)=r(z)\sum_{j\ge0}I_\xi^j
       \left[\frac{a_j(z,x(z,\xi),m)}{f_x(z,x(z,\xi))}\right].
\]
Here \(I_\xi\) starts at the original \(\xi=0\); equality follows
from the actual soft moments, with only finitely many terms at
each quantum order.

In a parameter-dependent Morse coordinate
\(v^2=\xi-\xi_g(z)\), retain its original base \(v_0(z)\).
For \(j\ge1\) every repeated primitive is exactly
\[
 \frac1{(j-1)!}\int_{v_0(z)}^v
        (v^2-t^2)^{j-1}
        a_j(z,x(z,t),m)x_t(z,t)\,dt .
\]
The factorial bound cancels its primitive factorial. This series
converges normally on a fixed small \(v\)-disk, jointly through
\(z=0\). All these terms are holomorphic in \(v\). The remaining
term has the explicit simple pole
\(r(z)a_0(z,x(z,v),m)x_v(z,v)/(2v)\).
Consequently the actual continued source has
\[
 b_m=E_m(z,\rho)+\rho^{-1/2}A_m(z,\rho),
                 \qquad \rho=\xi-\xi_g(z),
\]
with holomorphic \(E_m,A_m\), and
\[
 A_m(z,0)=\frac{r(z)}2
   e^{A_0(z,x_g(z))+m\cdot\Theta_g(z)}x_v(z,0)\ne0,\qquad
 \frac{A_m(z,0)}{A_{m=0}(z,0)}=e^{m\cdot\Theta_g(z)}.
\]
The original endpoint history is kept before taking the odd part.
No higher correction can cancel this leading pole.

The actual local marked minor and its leading clock character are
therefore paid. Neighborhoods may depend on a prescribed clock
compact. Identification with the hyperbolic component, global
transport to complete holonomy and the physical-cycle coefficient
remain open; no additional filling case follows yet.

## The quantum logarithm has a factorial bound in its deficiency

The [factorial-deficiency theorem](research_actual_symbol_factorial_deficiency.md)
controls the full ordinary normal-symbol logarithm, not just its
principal phase. After scaling the fields, its coefficients satisfy
\[
 \log S_h(h^{-1/2}Z,h^{-1/2}P,\mathbf t)
       =\sum_{a\ge0}h^{a-1}\mathcal P_a,\qquad
                         \|\mathcal P_a\|\le MC^a a!
\]
on fixed common meridian, field and independent-mark disks.
The same estimate holds after the regular hard contractions, as a
bound on the whole analytic soft-variable coefficient
\(\Psi_a(z,x,\mathbf t)\). The singular soft trace is not included.

The literal entry bound follows from analytic logarithms and the
Bernoulli power-sum formula. Its factorial is in
\(a=j+1-d\), not the full quantum order \(j\).
Gaussian translation and exact quadratic absorption reduce the
remaining estimates to connected graphs. At defect \(a\), their
vertices and edges number \(O(a)\); the pairing factorial and
vertex factorials together are bounded by \(C^a a!\).

Poisson means can vanish. A centered Poisson functional is represented
exactly by cross-Wick variables with potential
\(\sum_i u_i(e^{\Xi_i}-1-\Xi_i)\). Its quadratic inverse is a
unit even at \(u=0\). This pays the closure estimate on zero
coordinate faces without dividing by an occupation.
Finite normal products, original pivots/framing and stage marks
retain the bound.

of \(T_0\) or an occupation coordinate occurs. Analytic summation

## The source-derived local principal phase and leading clock map converge

The [analytic principal-phase theorem](research_actual_analytic_principal_phase.md)
proves convergence of the phase and linear clock map in the exact
formal hard-Wick reduction. It applies under the same simple
two-branch node hypotheses, including \(\sigma\ne0\).

The proof starts with the literal signed crossing entries. Their
highest index-degree logarithms are analytic integrals of
\(\log((e^s-1)/s)\) and the normalized color-product logarithms.
Connected Poisson moments have an analytic principal phase given by
\[
 u_i=U_i e^{\partial_iV(u)},\qquad
 F(U)=V(u)+\sum_i(u_i-U_i-u_i\partial_iV(u)).
\]
The implicit Jacobian is the identity at zero, including zero
coordinate faces. Finite normal-symbol composition and regular
trace contractions use the analogous Gaussian equations
\[
 u=a+K\nabla P(u),\qquad
 P_{\rm eff}=P(u)-\tfrac12\nabla P(u)^TK\nabla P(u).
\]
They require no inverse of the covariance or the highest-cut
projector. Independent stage marks are retained before their
original specialization to \(hm\).

Balancedness then gives a holomorphic soft phase
\(\Psi(z,x,\mathbf t)\). Its unmarked value and first mark
derivative match the exact formal coefficients of the earlier
reduction:
\[
 \Phi(z,x)=-zx+\Psi(z,x,0),\qquad
 \Theta(z,x)=\partial_{\mathbf t}\Psi(z,x,0).
\]
Consequently the small critical point and critical clock map
are analytic, with
\[
 x_g=z/(2\sigma)+O(z^2),\quad
 S_g=-z^2/(4\sigma)+O(z^3),\quad
 \Theta_g=\mu z/(2\sigma)+O(z^2).
\]
Thus the formal leading clock ratio is the Taylor series of
the nonzero analytic function \(\exp(m\cdot\Theta_g)\).

This removes convergence of the local principal phase from the
list of unpaid steps. It does not prove convergence of the quantum
amplitude, occurrence of the stationary sector in the analytic
source, identification with geometric holonomy, or its coefficient
in the physical cycle. No additional filling case follows yet.

## The literal inverse factorials already make the joint ratios boundary-exact

The [unreduced-ratio theorem](research_actual_unreduced_boundary_exact_clock_ratios.md)

                    \frac{(Q;Q)_{n_c+o_c}}

inverse-factorial denominator in the new-source coefficient contains

## Fixed occupations with nonzero displacement have no local node monodromy

The [fixed-occupation regularity theorem](research_fixed_occupation_boundary_borel_regularity.md)
handles a specified physical occupation \(a\) with nonzero determinant
displacement \(\mu_a\). Retain its independent mark \(s^a\).
The actual marked determinant is affine:
\[
                   D(Y,s)=A_0(Y)-sB_0(Y).
\]
At a simple Alexander root, \(\mu_a\ne0\) implies
\(A_0(\alpha)=B_0(\alpha)\ne0\). A fixed small \(s\)-disk therefore
has a determinant uniformly bounded away from zero near \(\alpha\).

Fixing \(a=r\), for any nonnegative integer \(r\), is exact extraction
of \([s^r]\) from the original graded source. The proof checks this
extraction through rational grading completion and proves a uniform
actual Gevrey bound for all clocks. Its Borel source \(b_r\) is
holomorphic on a fixed product disk through \((Y,\xi)=(\alpha,0)\).
In scaled variables it satisfies
\[
 |z\,b_r(\alpha+z,z^2\eta,\nu/z)|
   \le\frac{C_r|z|}{1-A|z|^2|\eta|}
               e^{C A|z\eta|\,\|\nu\|_1}.
\]
Thus these actual boundary sources and their canonical primitives
have zero monodromy around the local node. Explicit finite clock,
meridian and exponential reindex adapters preserve this regularity.

\(\mu_a\ne0\). It does not cover zero-displacement occupations,
arbitrary transfer facets, or all auxiliary Ward currents.

## Hard contractions give an exact formal one-variable source

The [hard-Wick reduction](research_actual_hard_wick_soft_reduction.md)
rewrites the original marked trace as a one-variable formal moment
functional. At the simple determinant pole, split its covariance as
\(\mathcal C=uv^T/z+G(z)\). The regular part \(G\) is contracted
first. Connected cumulants then give
\[
 \mathscr W_m(h,\alpha+z)
       =r(z)\mathfrak L_z
           \left[\exp\!\left(\sum_{j\ge1}h^jU_j(z,m;t)\right)\right],
       \qquad \mathfrak L_z[t^s]=s!z^{-s-1}.
\]
The identity is coefficientwise in \(h\) for the actual source.
No inverse of the highest-cut projector or logarithm of its trace
is used.

Each monomial of \(U_j\) satisfies
\(\deg_t+\deg_m\le j+1\), with \(\deg_m\le j\).
Consequently \(x=ht\) separates a clock-independent formal phase
from a leading amplitude exponential in a linear clock form:
\[
 -zt+\sum h^jU_j
    =h^{-1}\Phi(z,x)+A_0(z,x)+m\cdot\Theta(z,x)+O(h).
\]
The calibrated quadratic coefficient is \(\sigma\ne0\).
Its formal critical point has
\[
 x_g(z)=z/(2\sigma)+O(z^2),\quad
 \Phi(z,x_g)=-z^2/(4\sigma)+O(z^3),\quad
 \Theta(z,x_g)=\mu z/(2\sigma)+O(z^2).
\]
The leading marked/unmarked ratio in this formal stationary sector
is therefore \(\exp(m\cdot\Theta(z,x_g))\).

These are formal source identities. Convergence of the phase and
clock map, occurrence of this sector in the analytic marked minor,
and its physical-cycle coefficient are not asserted by this theorem.
The formal integral notation for \(\mathfrak L_z\) does not supply
an analytic integration contour.

clocks. For the original source, with \(Y=Qx^2\), let
\(\mathsf T:Y\mapsto QY\) and let \(\mathsf E_i\) translate \(m_i\)
by one. The literal crossing products give
\[
 D(Y,\mathsf E)\mathsf T\mathscr W_m
    =Q^{c/2}\mathsf E^{H/2}N(Y,\mathsf E)\mathscr W_m,
\]
where
\[
 \begin{split}
 D(Y,X)&=\prod_+(1-Y^{-1}X^a)\prod_-(1-YX^{-b}),\\
 N(Y,X)&=\prod_+(1-Y^{-1}X^{a-n})\prod_-(1-YX^{n-b}),\\
 H&=\sum_-(a+b-n)+\sum_+(-a-b+n).
 \end{split}
\]
The labels in each factor are their actual matching-lattice forms.
Pathwise parity makes \(H/2\) integral. The original scalar framing
contributes exactly \(Q^{c/2}\).

The external shift changes no support inequality, so its cleared
row requires no additional boundary factor. Near any
\(Y_0\ne0,1\), after \(X=e^{z\theta}\), both \(D\) and \(N\)
are units on a whole fixed bounded spectral polydisk for small \(z\).
Their inverses therefore preserve the actual Fourier-period kernel:
all polynomial moments still vanish after multiplication by a
function holomorphic on the filled polydisk. Nonvanishing only on
its boundary would not justify this division.

On the proved full-clock source charts this gives the convergent
actual Borel row
\[
 \widehat{\mathsf T}F
    =e^{(c/2)z^2I_\eta}
       \mathcal R(\alpha+z,e^{z\partial_\nu})F,\qquad
       \mathcal R(Y,X)=X^{H/2}N(Y,X)/D(Y,X).
\]
The primitive starts at the original Borel origin and retains its
history. This proves the analytic action on the actual source;
it does not assume a global exponential shift operator on arbitrary
functions.

The same rational map has
\[
 \mathcal R(Y,\mathbf1)=1,\qquad
 \partial_{\log X}\log\mathcal R(Y,\mathbf1)=\beta(Y).
\]
At the exceptional point \(\theta_*=\mu/(2\sigma)\), the identity
\(\beta(\alpha)\cdot\mu=-\alpha\) gives the correct first derivative
of the actual unmarked partner longitude. A full marked character
map at nonzero meridian still requires the internal equations.

## The classical meridian is an explicit change of path weights

The [clock-torus adapter](research_classical_clock_torus_meridian_adapter.md)
absorbs the whole classical meridian dependence into the independent
path marks. For fixed integral path coordinates \(k\), define
\[
 N(k)=\sum_{\rm crossings}n,\qquad
 U(k)=\frac12\left[
       \sum_{\rm negative}(a+b-n)-\sum_{\rm positive}(a+b+n)\right].
\]
Both forms are integral on the entire matching lattice. The parity
needed for \(U\) follows path by path from the original staggered
input/output signs. Write \(U=u\cdot k\), \(N=n\cdot k\).

At \(Q=1\), every path coefficient, excluding the retained scalar
\(Y^{c/2}\), is a constant times
\(Y^{U(k)}(Y-1)^{N(k)}\). Thus, for \(Y,Y_0\ne0,1\), set
\[
 \Lambda_i(Y;Y_0)=
       (Y/Y_0)^{u_i}
          \left(\frac{Y-1}{Y_0-1}\right)^{n_i}.
\]
The entire marked determinant, including the highest-cut projector
and the grading parameter, satisfies
\[
 D(Y,\tau,\mathbf z)
       =D(Y_0,\tau,\mathbf z\Lambda(Y;Y_0)).
\]
This is an exact rational identity before taking any local expansion.

For logarithmic marks, put
\(\beta(Y)=u+Y n/(Y-1)\). Differentiation gives
\[
 YD_Y=\beta(Y)\cdot D_t,\qquad
       \beta(\alpha)\cdot\mu=-\alpha,\qquad
       \mu=-D_t(\alpha,0)/D_Y(\alpha,0).
\]
At a simple Alexander root, the full displacement vector \(\mu\)
is therefore nonzero. The explicit vector
\(v=-\beta(\alpha)/\alpha\) satisfies \(\mu\cdot v=1\).
It supplies a normalized longitudinal clock
\(\lambda=\mu\cdot\nu\) while retaining all transverse marks.

The result is classical. It neither makes this substitution in the
quantum source nor reduces that source to one variable. Multiple
Alexander roots and the geometric closing coefficient remain outside
the statement.
