## Polynomial-log Cauchy densities have exponential continuation bounds

The [Cauchy-density estimate](research_polynomial_log_cauchy_continuation_bound.md)
controls analytic continuation without first bounding the separate
terms of a possibly canceling density. For
\[
 F(\theta)=
 \frac{A(\theta)+B(\theta)\log(1-\theta^{-1})}
                   {\theta^{r_0}(\theta-1)^{r_1}},
 \qquad \deg A,\deg B\le d,
\]
its norm \(M\) on a fixed outer circle controls its norm on any fixed
continued compact \(K\) away from the endpoints:
\[
              \sup_K|F|\le M C_K^{\,d+r_0+r_1+1}.
\]
The branch is retained and the constant may depend on the fixed
continuation chart.

To prove the bound, multiply by the displayed denominator. Its first
\(d+1\) negative Laurent coefficients determine \(B\) through the
Hilbert matrix \(H_{ij}=1/(i+j+1)\). A residue interpolation formula
proves \(\|H^{-1}\|_\infty\le2^{11(d+1)}\). This recovers \(B\)
despite its cancellation with \(A\), and then recovers \(A\).
Ordinary polynomial Cauchy bounds finish the continuation estimate.
Polynomial segment densities and endpoint derivatives fit this class.

Consequently degree and endpoint-pole complexity \(O(k)\), together
with a whole-density outer bound \(MA^k\), give a continued bound
\(M'B^k\). There is no \(e^{k\log k}\) loss, so a transverse power
series retains a positive convergence radius on each fixed continued
chart. Uniformity for moving endpoints is proved when they remain
separated; endpoint collision is not covered by that assertion.

This is a proved function-space estimate. The finite-core trace theorem
above now supplies membership and uniform complexity for the actual
marked coefficients. Their joint continuation uses the product-contour
extension and factorial clock bounds above.

## A logarithmic order bound holds for the whole original marked word

The [operator-logarithm proof](research_actual_source_natural_log_filtration.md)
gives a structural constraint for a general fixed braid word. Near a
meridian with \(Y\ne0,1\), each literal signed crossing has the formal
factorization
\[
 R_h\Gamma(L)^{-1}
       =\exp\left(\sum_{j\ge1}h^jD_j\right),
                 \qquad \operatorname{ord}D_j\le j+1.
\]
The same bound survives the finite word, its independent diagonal
marks, and the original pivots and framing. The statement concerns
the operator logarithm; it does not take a logarithm of the cut trace.

The proof first uses the literal crossing kernel. Its three classical
index sums are independent formal Poisson sums. The scalar logarithm
at order \(h^j\) has index degree at most \(j+1\). Connected
falling-factorial identifications give the same degree bound after
taking moments. A triangular calculation with the exact normal-symbol
product then proves the operator-logarithm bound. Commutators lower
differential order by one, which proves closure through the whole word.

For a normal-order \(n\) product containing \(v\) logarithmic
insertions, the actual highest-cut determinant trace has pole order
at most \(n+v+1\). A contribution to the coefficient of pole order
\(2n+1-k\) must therefore satisfy
\[
                          \sum_{i=1}^v(j_i-1)\le k.
\]
At most \(k\) insertions can have quantum order greater than one.
There can still be arbitrarily many order-one insertions; their
contractions have not been summed by this theorem. The highest-cut
projector remains in the original trace throughout.

The proof also records why a sum of point evaluations alone is too
small a Fourier space. For the exceptional profile
\[
 F_0(\eta,\nu)=r w^{-1}e^{a\lambda},\qquad
 w=\sqrt{1-4\sigma\eta},\quad
 a=(1-w)/(2\sigma),\quad \lambda=\mu\cdot\nu,
\]
the exact scalar quantum action \(Q\) adds at order \(z^2\)
\[
 I_\eta F_0=r\frac{e^{a\lambda}-1}{\lambda}.
\]
Its canonical one-dimensional Cauchy density is
\[
       -r\log(1-a/\theta)=r\int_0^a\frac{ds}{\theta-s}.
\]
Thus the connecting path is retained even for this elementary
operator action. This does not assert that a particular framing
term survives cancellation with the rest of a knot word.

The new bound controls which terms can occur. Its finite-core refinement
and the quantitative estimates above now give convergent outer spectral
continuation. A marked moving minor and the nonzero physical closing
coefficient remain unproved. No new filling cases follow from this
filtration or its current continuation consequences.

## The full marked source has a convergent Fourier representation

The [Fourier--Cauchy representation](research_clock_borel_fourier_representation.md)
turns the actual initial full-clock family into an explicit contour
period. Put \(h=z^2\varepsilon\), \(m=\nu/z\), and let
\[

      =z\,\mathcal B_h\mathscr W_{\nu/z}(\alpha+z,z^2\eta).

The uniform exponential type in \(\nu\) makes the Laurent series
\[
 g(z,\eta,\theta)=
   \sum_{\gamma\ge0}\partial_\nu^\gamma F(z,\eta,0)
                         \theta^{-\gamma-\mathbf1}
\]
convergent outside fixed circles in each spectral variable. On their
product \(\Gamma\), the exact identity is
\[
 F(z,\eta,\nu)
       =\frac1{(2\pi i)^d}\int_\Gamma
                       e^{\nu\cdot\theta}g(z,\eta,\theta)\,d^d\theta.
\]
At \(z=0\) this density is
\[
 \frac r w\prod_i(\theta_i-\Theta_i(\eta))^{-1},\qquad
 w=\sqrt{1-4\sigma\eta},\qquad
 \Theta=\frac{\mu}{2\sigma}(1-w).
\]
Its leading branch coefficient is exactly the Cauchy evaluation
\(f\mapsto r f(\mu/(2\sigma))\). This is the actual exceptional
character, expressed as a Fourier functional.

The operator action keeps the Borel primitive \(I=I_\eta\).
Internal clock translation and original index translation act on
density classes by
\[
 \mathcal E_i=e^{z\theta_i},\qquad
 \mathcal S_i=e^{zI\partial_{\theta_i}},\qquad
 \mathcal Q=e^{z^2I},\qquad
 \mathcal S_i\mathcal E_j
       =\mathcal Q^{\delta_{ij}}\mathcal E_j\mathcal S_i.
\]
Cauchy derivative estimates and the \(n\)-fold primitive factorial
prove convergence on buffered contours.

Two densities represent the same function when their difference has
zero integral against every nonnegative monomial. Thus a source equation is initially an
equation of density classes. The canonical representative keeps the
Laurent terms negative in every variable. An unprojected pointwise
equation, or localization near the exceptional evaluation at nonzero
\(z\), requires another argument. No physical contour or scalar lower
bound is obtained merely by taking this Fourier representation.

## The joint clock equations retain their original support boundaries

The [joint-source equations](research_highest_cut_joint_clock_equations.md)
give explicit relations before eliminating the internal indices.
Their source is the untruncated graded highest-cut word, extended
by zero outside its fixed rational support cone. For a lattice step
\(v\), take the proper ratio of the two supported summands. For each
support form \(\ell\), the translated boundary consists of finitely
many integer layers. The product
\[
 \Theta_v(Q,X)=
   \prod_{\ell(v)\ne0}\ 
   \prod_{r=\min(0,-\ell(v))}^{\max(0,-\ell(v))-1}
                         (1-Q^{-r}X^\ell)
\]
kills every layer on which just one summand is supported.
Multiplying the cleared ratio equation by this entire factor gives
an exact equation on the whole lattice.

Fourier marking sends \(X_i=Q^{k_i}\) to clock translation and
an index shift to multiplication by \(Q^{-m_i}\), with the original
noncommutative order. The equations then pass coefficientwise to
grading one and act on the genuine canonical full-clock source.
The external meridian shift changes \(\nu\) as well as \(z\) in the
rescaled coordinates; its exact coordinate formula is retained.

The highest-vacuum conditions and the literal forced crossing columns
are also kept. A boundary-clearing factor can vanish on an entire
forced face; such a ratio equation then gives no information there.
If a support form vanishes identically on the actual cone, its
equation \(X^\ell=1\) and the forced columns supply the corresponding
exact reduction. Non-forced zeros still require local analysis.
The proof does not invert all boundary factors or use unweighted
scalarity after inserting clocks.

Together the two results specify the actual analytic family and its
equations. Bounded analytic division of those equations near the
exceptional Fourier contribution, with all relevant faces and period
classes retained, remains unproved.

## The original hole contour is an explicit relative Morse cap

The [relative-cap proof](research_original_alexander_hole_relative_morse_cap.md)
now constructs the two-chain represented by an original Alexander-hole
term at a simple two-branch node. This is the actual hole in the
short-cutoff color formula, with its coefficient \(+1\), rather than
a separately chosen contour through the local saddle.

Write the regular source as
\[
 b(v,\xi)=E(u,\rho)+\rho^{-1/2}A(u,\rho),\qquad
 \rho=\xi+S(u),\qquad u=v-\log\alpha.
\]
An analytic Morse coordinate gives \(S=w^2\). On the double cover
\(\tau^2=\xi+w^2\), put \(y=\tau-w\), \(\zeta=\tau+w\);
then \(\xi=y\zeta\). The full original two-form
\[
 \Omega=\frac{L e^{L(R-\xi)/v}}{v(v-a)}
                    b(v,\xi)\,dv\wedge d\xi
\]
is holomorphic across \(\tau=0\): its apparent pole cancels against
the Jacobian. The observation pole \(v=a\) stays outside this local
construction.

The original cylinder \(\Sigma_R\) has its two boundaries in
\(\xi=0\) and \(\xi=R\). In their relative homology group it equals
the negative of the explicit disk
\[
 \Delta_R:\quad
 y=\sqrt R\,r e^{-i\phi},\qquad
 \zeta=\sqrt R\,r e^{i\phi},\qquad 0\le r\le1.
\]
Both endpoint fibers remain fixed. The integer coefficient is computed
by the winding of the upper loop in the annulus \(y\zeta=R\).
An explicit bottom disk and upper annulus give the exact identity
\[
 \frac{e^{-LR/a}}{2\pi i}\int_{\Sigma_R}\Omega
       =-\frac{e^{-LR/a}}{2\pi i}\int_{\Delta_R}\Omega.
\]
The added bottom disk and upper annulus have zero integrals because they
are complex curves carrying a holomorphic two-form. The local even-source
contribution also vanishes exactly. The disk projects to \(S=-Rt^2\), explaining its finite Gaussian
intervals and their endpoints.

This pays the original local relative class and its sign. Global
transport still has to retain the fibers \(\xi=0,R\), the observation
pole, and every other encountered divisor. Continuing the odd minor
alone does not perform that operation or assign a geometric coefficient
to the original closed invariant.

The domain required for a proposed continuation of this cap can be
stated explicitly. With the two continued inverse-action lifts, its
matching-disk coordinates would be
\[
 S(u_\pm(y))=-Ry^2,\qquad
 \rho=Rx^2,\qquad x^2+y^2\le1,\qquad
 \xi=R(x^2+y^2).
\]
The full source and its histories would have to be constructed on a
neighborhood of this swept region, retaining any additional divisors.
Continuation of \(A(u,\rho)\) on an unspecified small transverse disk
does not establish that domain. This is a remaining construction,
not a hypothesis already checked by the local cap identity.

## Higher-collision branches have their exact local action support

The [local action-support theorem](research_higher_collision_local_moving_action_support.md)
locates the nonzero higher-collision branches, under the actual
operator hypotheses in the continuation theorem below. On the
ramified meridian \(Y=\alpha+s^p\), let \(\ell_j(s)\) be a partner
root and define
\[
 S_j(0)=0,\qquad
 dS_j=\log\ell_j\,d\log Y,\qquad
 \rho=\xi+S_j(s).
\]
For each prescribed finite angular window and continued outer branch,
the actual source and all its histories extend throughout
\[
 0<|s|<b,\qquad 0<|\rho|<\delta|s|^{p+1}
\]
on the retained cover, after choosing \(b>0\) for that window.
The canonical branch has nonzero monodromy about \(\rho=0\).
Thus its local singularity is at the exact action
\(\xi=-S_j(s)\), and there is no additional singularity inside
that punctured cluster.

The proof starts with the joint outer annulus already constructed
below. It shrinks an explicitly anchored radial boundary while testing
its complex normal against every root of the actual symbol.
The derivative \(d\log Y/ds\), of order \(s^{p-1}\), is retained.
Both angular labels are needed; no finite sheet number is assumed.
The noncharacteristic extension theorem then continues the source
and its primitive and shift histories across each moving boundary.

There is a useful consequence for every other actual annihilator
holomorphic on this chart:
\[
                    Q_{\mathrm{cl}}(\alpha+s^p,\ell_j(s))=0.
\]
Otherwise its elliptic extension would remove the branch's nonzero
monodromy. This makes the local classical branch a property of the
source, rather than an artifact of one chosen annihilator.
It does not select a quantum right factor or identify this branch
with a hyperbolic representation.

The statement is local to a partner cluster. The meridian radius may
decrease with the finite angular window and continuation word.
Behavior at \(\xi=0\) on other sheets, a regular moving minor for
\(p>1\), and the global original contour remain separate questions.
This result proves no new knot-complement volume identity.

## The higher-collision seed continues as an actual joint source

The [general collision continuation proof](research_classical_verma_higher_collision_joint_continuation.md)
extends the ramified initial germ below along every fixed finite
Borel path avoiding zero and the \(p\) exceptional critical points.
The allowed transverse radius remains positive for each such path.
This applies for every fixed \(p\ge1\) under the displayed actual
operator hypotheses of the profile theorem; it is not an assertion
that those hypotheses hold for every knot.

For \(z=s^p\), \(\xi=s^{p+1}\eta\), write the actual source as
\(b(s,\eta)=\sum_k b_k(\eta)s^k\). Its leading transverse equation
has a first-order companion system in \(p\) scaled primitives and
one additional variable. On compact paths its matrix costs \(O(k+1)\)
and its forced inverse gains \(1/(k+1)\). Exact normal ordering leaves
at most one derivative of a lower transverse coefficient. The gain
therefore closes the full finite-shift forcing estimate, giving an
exponential bound in \(k\) and a convergent joint continuation.
All primitive histories begin at the original \(\eta=0\) germ.

The exceptional algebraic profile changes nontrivially around each
of its canonical fold loops. Joint convergence makes this monodromy
nonzero for all sufficiently small nonzero \(s\) as well. This proves
a branch of the actual source, beyond a branch of its exceptional
restriction. It does not yet locate its exact moving divisor, give
a regular minor there for \(p>1\), or determine a coefficient of the
physical scalar.

## The rescaled clock seed has an explicit nonzero exceptional character

The [rescaled-clock profile theorem](research_rescaled_clock_exceptional_character.md)
computes the actual initial family after \(m=\nu/z\),
\(z=Y-\alpha\), at a simple two-branch node. Retain the
highest-cut projector in the marked classical determinant
\[
 D(Y,t)=\det\!\bigl(I-L_\beta(\sqrt Y,e^t)T_0\bigr),\qquad
 T_0=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,\ldots,1),
\]
and put
\[
 \mu_i=-D_{t_i}(\alpha,0)/D_Y(\alpha,0),\qquad
 \sigma=A/(2B)\ne0,\qquad r=1/\Delta'(\alpha).
\]
Here \(A,B\) are the actual scalar node constants; the
determinant zero is simple. The convergent rescaled Borel
family of the next section has exact exceptional restriction
\[
 \mathcal G(0,\eta,\nu)=
 \frac{r}{\sqrt{1-4\sigma\eta}}\,
 \exp\left\{\frac{\mu\cdot\nu}{2\sigma}
                   \left(1-\sqrt{1-4\sigma\eta}\right)\right\}.
\]
The square root equals one at \(\eta=0\). This is an identity
of the actual initial germ, entire in the rescaled clock
parameters \(\nu\), not a chosen formal interpolation.

The proof uses the marked denominator \(D^{2n+1}\) of the
order-\(h^n\) source. Taking \(d\) derivatives of the marks
has highest pole coefficient
\[
 (2n+1)_d(\mu\cdot\nu)^d c_n,\qquad
 c_n=r(2n)!\sigma^n/n!.
\]
Every derivative of the holomorphic numerator or determinant
unit loses a pole. This includes all quantum-coefficient
derivatives. Combining the whole-clock factor \(1/d!\) and
the Borel factor \(1/(n+d)!\) gives an explicit double
series; a Cauchy-residue computation of the Catalan generating
function sums it to the displayed expression.

At \(\eta=1/(4\sigma)\), its odd square-root coefficient is
\[
 \mathcal A(\nu)=r\exp\!\left(\frac{\mu\cdot\nu}{2\sigma}\right),
 \qquad
 \frac{\mathcal A(\nu+\nu')}{r}
   =\frac{\mathcal A(\nu)}r\frac{\mathcal A(\nu')}r .
\]
It is nonzero for every complex \(\nu\). The original
highest-cut source therefore supplies genuine character
initialization on this exceptional scaled-clock family.
The corank-one determinant formula for \(\mu\) keeps \(T_0\);
neither averaging the marked cut nor assuming an algebraically
simple eigenvalue is used.

This character is on the exceptional divisor \(z=0\).
It is not yet a character of the full classical Ward algebra
at a nonzero meridian. Continuing the joint marked family,
retaining its actual boundary equations, remains necessary
for a geometric character map. No physical scalar lower
bound follows from this initialization alone.

## Full clock factors have a uniform initial Borel family

The [full-clock theorem](research_full_clock_initial_borel_family.md)
keeps the original highest cut and the fixed integral path-index
coordinates \(k\). Insert the whole factor
\(Q^{m\cdot k}=e^{h\,m\cdot k}\), \(h=\log Q\), and write
\[
 \mathscr W_m(h,Y)=\sum_{j\ge0}h^jW_{j,m}(Y),
                  \qquad m\in\mathbb C^s .
\]
This is a fixed marked word evaluation. Its full exponential is
retained; no bounded-degree approximation is made on indices of
size \(1/h\).

Every coefficient is polynomial in \(m\) of degree at most \(j\).
Its homogeneous degree-\(d\) part has Alexander pole order at most
\(2j-d+1\). For a meridian compact \(K\) avoiding the Alexander
divisor there are constants independent of \(j,m\) with
\[
 \sup_K|W_{j,m}|\le C_K e^{c\|m\|_1} A_K^j j! .
\]
The proof bounds the exact clock on the finite-sector Cauchy
disk \(|h|\le\rho/(T+1)\), where \(|k|\le C_\beta T\);
its cost is \(e^{\rho C_\beta\|m\|_1}\), independent of \(T\).
The actual determinant numerator has grading degree \(O(j)\),
so rational continuation to grading one costs only another
exponential in \(j\), independent of the clock.

At the specified simple two-branch node, put \(z=Y-\alpha\).
The pole-scaled initial family
\[
 \mathcal B_m^{\rm pole}(z,\eta)=
        z\,\mathcal B_h\mathscr W_m(\alpha+z,z^2\eta)
\]
is jointly holomorphic near \((z,\eta)=(0,0)\), entire in \(m\),
with an \(\eta\)-radius independent of \(m\). The sharper estimate is
\[
 |\mathcal B_m^{\rm pole}(z,\eta)|
       \le \frac{C}{1-D|\eta|}\,e^{C'|z|\|m\|_1}.
\]
It follows by extracting each clock degree on a fixed meridian
circle, then using its improved pole order. Thus the exponential
type vanishes linearly with \(z\). Equivalently \(m=\nu/z\)
gives a joint holomorphic initial germ through \(z=0\), entire
of finite exponential type in \(\nu\).

For each fixed \(m\), the exceptional restriction is exactly the
same nonzero profile \(r(1-\eta/\eta_*)^{-1/2}\) as for the
unmarked source. The restriction after \(m=\nu/z\) is a different
question, since the clock is then rescaled with the meridian.
The theorem does not continue either clock family through the
moving divisor, preserve this type under that continuation,
or establish character-valued clock ratios at finite nonzero
\(z\). The coarse clock pole bound also cannot replace the
sharper higher-collision analysis below.

## Higher finite collisions have an actual ramified Borel seed

The [higher-collision profile theorem](research_classical_verma_higher_collision_borel_profile.md)
extends the initial source calculation beyond a transverse pair of
classical roots. It assumes an actual holomorphic annihilator at a
simple Alexander root \(\alpha\), with \(P(Y,1)\equiv0\),
\(P_{YL}(\alpha,1)\ne0\), and
\[
 \partial_L^kP(\alpha,1)=0\ (2\le k\le p),\qquad
 \partial_L^{p+1}P(\alpha,1)\ne0,\qquad p\ge1 .
\]
The source equation also forces \(P_L(\alpha,1)=0\).
These are conditions on the displayed actual operator; a simple
Alexander root by itself does not assert them.

With \(z=Y-\alpha\) and \(r=1/\Delta'(\alpha)\), put
\[
 B=\alpha P_{YL}(\alpha,1),\quad
 C=\frac{\alpha^{p+1}}{(p+1)!}\partial_L^{p+1}P(\alpha,1),
 \quad \kappa=(-1)^{p+1}C/B .
\]
The actual rational-loop coefficients obey the sharper pole bound
\[
 \operatorname{pole}_\alpha W_j
          \le j+\lfloor j/p\rfloor+1 .
\]
At every multiple of \(p\) the indicated pole is present, with
\[
 [z^{-((p+1)n+1)}]W_{pn}
       =r\kappa^n\frac{((p+1)n)!}{(p+1)^n n!}.
\]
The proof uses the exact differential coefficients of the finite
shifts. Their top derivative vanishes at the node for orders
\(2,\ldots,p\); the first nonzero top derivative at order \(p+1\)
alone determines these highest residues.

After \(z=s^p,\ \xi=s^{p+1}\eta\), the scaled canonical Borel
series \(s^p\mathcal B_h\mathscr W(\alpha+s^p,s^{p+1}\eta)\)
is jointly holomorphic at \((s,\eta)=(0,0)\). Its exceptional
restriction is the explicit algebraic germ
\[
 r\sum_{n\ge0}\binom{(p+1)n}{n}
          \left(\frac{\kappa\eta^p}{p+1}\right)^n
   =r\frac{U(t)}{p+1-pU(t)},\qquad
 U=1+tU^{p+1},\quad t=\frac{\kappa\eta^p}{p+1}.
\]
It has nonzero inverse-square-root singularities at
\[
             \eta^p=\frac{p^p}{(p+1)^p\kappa}.
\]
The classical partners have Puiseux expansions on the same
ramified meridian chart; integrating \(dS_j=\log\ell_j\,d\log Y\)
shows that these points are exactly the leading coefficients
of the scaled negative actions \(-S_j/s^{p+1}\).
Thus the normalization and action scale come from the actual
source for every such finite collision order.

For clarity about coverage, there is a useful necessary test
from the first two actual normal equations. If
\(c_1=[z^{-3}]W_1\), then every holomorphic actual annihilator
at a simple Alexander root satisfies
\[
 \alpha P_{YL}(\alpha,1)c_1
       =\frac{\alpha^2}{2}P_{LL}(\alpha,1)r .
\]
Indeed the order-\(h\) equation gives
\(P_L(\alpha,1)=0\) and
\(P^{[1]}(\alpha,1)=\alpha P_{YL}(\alpha,1)\);
the coefficient of \(z^{-3}\) at the next order gives the
displayed identity. A vanishing cubic pole therefore excludes
the transverse \(p=1\) hypothesis for every such operator,
rather than merely for a badly chosen left multiple.
The higher-collision calculation addresses these distinct
initial seeds.

For \(p>1\), this theorem does not yet continue the joint germ
at nonzero \(s\) to those singular points. The exact moving
minor and cutoff results proved below for \(p=1\) cannot
simply be assigned to it. No physical coefficient, geometric
component identification or finite-exception conclusion is
inferred.

## An original Alexander-hole term has an exact observation-pole jump

The [original-hole transfer proof](research_original_alexander_hole_observation_jump.md)
computes a contribution from the original finite-color formula.
Let \(C\) be one counterclockwise Alexander-hole contour about
\(v_*=\log\alpha\), excluding \(0\) and \(2\pi i\), and let \(R\)
be its constructed short cutoff. Define
\[
 F_L(v)=\frac Lv\int_0^R
                e^{L(R-\xi)/v}b(v,\xi)\,d\xi .
\]
The original positive hole term is
\[
 H_{\rm out}(a)=\frac{e^{-LR/a}}{2\pi i}
                  \int_C\frac{F_L(v)}{v-a}\,dv ,
       \qquad a\text{ outside }C .
\]
The same integral for \(a\) inside \(C\) defines a holomorphic
function \(H_{\rm in}\). Here \(h=a/L\). Cauchy's residue formula
on two nearby contours gives the exact local transfer
\[
 H_{\rm in}-H_{\rm out}=U_R(a/L,e^a).
\]
All constants and the sign belong to the original source kernel.

In the actual simple-node chart, continuation around an endpoint
branch point leaves \(H_{\rm in}\) single valued and exchanges
the two canonical cutoff values. Consequently
\[
 H_{{\rm out},+}-H_{{\rm out},-}
       =-D_R(a/L,a-v_*) .
\]
The right side is the negative of the exact finite Gaussian
period already proved below. This is an unconditional local
coefficient and orientation for a term occurring in the original
color formula, rather than an assumed identification of a new
ribbon with that term.

It also shows exactly what is still missing:
\[
 U_{R,\pm}+H_{{\rm out},\pm}=H_{\rm in}.
\]
Local branch jumps cancel in this pair, as required by the
single-valued finite-color polynomial. This does not show that
the large-color geometric contribution vanishes: the retained
\(H_{\rm in}\) depends on \(L\), and its growth is not bounded
by its holomorphy. The scalar endpoint and all other contours
also remain.

There is a genuine relative-cycle issue in moving this hole to
the physical observation. In the actual local coordinates
\(S=w^2,\ \tau^2=\xi+S\), the fixed-\(\xi\) fiber is
\((\tau-w)(\tau+w)=\xi\). The original lifted loop has nonzero
winding in this fiber and does not bound there. Holomorphic
endpoint graphs have zero pullback of the integration two-form,
but their required fillings cannot be presumed. The global
chain relation and quantitative interior-current bound remain
necessary for a physical noncancellation theorem.

## The canonical minor and its leading connection continue along regular branch paths

The [regular-branch transport theorem](research_canonical_borel_minor_regular_branch_transport.md)
continues the actual odd minor, retaining all its initial coefficients,
along any compact lifted path on the same classical branch where
the displayed operator coefficients are holomorphic and
\[
 P(u,\ell(u))=0,\qquad d_g(u)=\ell(u)P_L(u,\ell(u))\ne0 .
\]
The logarithm and action are continued from the original node;
their branches and integration constants are not reset.
On a finite neighborhood cover of the path,
\[
 b_{\rm odd}=\rho^{-1/2}A(u,\rho),\qquad
 A(u,\rho)=\sum_{n\ge0}a_n(u)\rho^n,\qquad
 |a_n(u)|\le CD^n
\]
with one positive transverse radius after finite shrinking.
In particular \(a_0\) continues without a zero.

This is a convergence theorem, not a transport of formal WKB
coefficients alone. The actual odd equation gives the triangular
first-order equations
\[
 (d_g\partial_u+e_g)a_n+
 \sum_{j=1}^{n}
    \frac{L_{j+1}a_{n-j}}{(n-j+\tfrac12)_j}=0 .
\]
Normalize \(v_n=(\tfrac12)_n a_n\), then \(f_n=v_n/a_0\).
An integration by parts in the forcing removes one derivative,
including its center boundary term. Weighted Cauchy norms yield
\(\|f_n\|_n\le C D^n n!\); division by
\((\tfrac12)_n\) recovers an exponential coefficient bound for
the minor. The meridian chart radius is fixed by the regular
operator coefficients, rather than consumed as the transverse
radius changes. Finitely many overlapping charts therefore
continue the whole actual germ along the compact path.

The leading connection is also intrinsic to the source. For any
other actual annihilator initially defined on the common source
chart, with its coefficients continued along the same lift,
the exact odd equation forces
\[
 Q_{\rm cl}(u,\ell(u))=0,\qquad
 d_Qa_0'+e_Qa_0=0 .
\]
Where \(d_Q\ne0\), this gives
\[
 \frac{a_0'}{a_0}=-\frac{e_Q}{d_Q}
                =-\frac{e_g}{d_g},\qquad
 da_0=\Omega a_0,\quad \Omega=-\frac{e_g}{d_g}\,du .
\]
For rational quantum coefficients, \(\Omega\) is a meromorphic
differential on the selected algebraic curve. The horizontal
section itself is not asserted to be algebraic or to have
trivial holonomy. This defines the source's leading line
connection in its fixed gauge without choosing a preferred
annihilator.

The continued minor has a nonzero finite Gaussian period with
a small fixed \(\rho\)-endpoint \(\rho_0\). Its leading term is
\(2\sqrt\pi h^{-1/2}a_0(u)e^{S(u)/h}\) on facing sectors.
Its original Borel endpoint, however, is
\(\xi=\rho_0-S(u)\), which moves with the meridian. It has
not been substituted for the original fixed-\(\xi\) cutoff
or for the physical scalar. The proof continues the odd
minor, not the deck-even source or the complementary cycles;
it does not cross a discriminant endpoint.

## The canonical singularity is a regular square-root minor with an exact finite period

The [regular-minor theorem](research_canonical_borel_regular_square_root_minor.md)
closes the essential-singularity ambiguity left open by the
moving-branch theorem below. It concerns the same actual canonical
source at the same simple Alexander/operator node. With
\[
 u=\log(Y/\alpha),\qquad S(0)=0,\quad S'=\log\ell,\qquad
 \rho=\xi+S(u),
\]
there are jointly holomorphic functions \(E,A\), including at
\((u,\rho)=(0,0)\), for which
\[
 b(u,\xi)=E(u,\rho)+\rho^{-1/2}A(u,\rho),\qquad
 A(u,0)=\frac r\beta a(u)\ne0.
\]
Here \(r=1/\Delta'(\alpha)\), \(\beta^2=-1/\eta_*\) has the
original cover sign, and \(a(0)=1\).
The leading amplitude satisfies \(a'/a=-e_g/d_g\), with the
actual transport coefficients defined in the next section.
The square-root form is convergent and belongs to the original
source; it is not an assumed local model.

The proof treats a possible infinite Laurent principal part
directly. On the exact \(\tau=\sqrt\rho\) cover, write
\(c_k(u)=[\tau^{-2k-1}]b_{\rm odd}\).
The outer source bound gives
\(\operatorname{ord}_0 c_k\ge3k\).
After the exact action-coordinate change, the actual finite-shift
equation has \(L_0=0\),
\(L_1=d_g\partial_u+e_g\), and
\(\operatorname{ord}_{\rm diff}L_{n+1}\le n+1\), with analytic
coefficients. The retained history terms are holomorphic in
\(\rho\) and have zero odd projection. The equation therefore
gives the normally convergent coefficient identities
\[
 d_gc_k'+e_gc_k+
 \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(-1)^n}{(k+\tfrac12)_n}
                 L_{n+1}c_{k+n}=0 .
\]
Choose a nonzero \(c_k\), \(k\ge1\), minimizing
\(\operatorname{ord}c_k-3k\), and put \(m=\operatorname{ord}c_k\).
The simple source residue forces \(d_g\) to have a simple zero
and \(e_g=O(u)\). Thus \(d_gc_k'\) has order exactly \(m\);
every other term has order at least \(m+1\). This contradiction
eliminates all \(c_k\) for \(k\ge1\), including an essential tail.
Fixed-annulus Cauchy estimates justify the infinite equation
and coefficient extraction through \(u=0\). A joint Laurent
series then gives the holomorphic functions \(A,E\) above.

There is also an exact formula for the original canonical cutoff
difference \(D_R=U_{R,+}-U_{R,-}\). For small fixed \(R\),
with the original endpoint orientation,
\[
 D_R(h,u)=\frac2h e^{S(u)/h}
       \int_{-\sqrt{R+S(u)}}^{\sqrt{R+S(u)}}
                     e^{-t^2/h}A(u,t^2)\,dt .
\]
The shared lower lift cancels. The even part contributes an odd
integrand and cancels at the endpoints; the remaining differential
is holomorphic on the full local \(t\)-disk.

On any closed \(h\)-sector facing \(R\), choose a fixed full
complex \(u\)-disk with \(|S(u)|\) sufficiently smaller than
\(|R|\). Finite Gaussian estimates give, uniformly there,
\[
 D_R(h,u)=2\sqrt\pi\,A(u,0)h^{-1/2}e^{S(u)/h}
                          (1+O(|h|)).
\]
Thus the meridian need not be parallel to \(h\), and the estimate
is not confined to the earlier growing ray. The full local
expansion has coefficients
\((\tfrac12)_n[\rho^n]A(u,\rho)\); the finite endpoint retains
absolute exponential scale \(e^{-R/h}\). Only polynomial
Gaussian moments are integrated to infinity in estimating
remainders. No infinite continuation of the actual source
is assumed.

This proves the exact local action, singularity type and
nonzero coefficient of a canonical source period. It remains
necessary to continue to the geometric physical observation
and prove its contribution in the original finite invariant,
with all other endpoint and cycle terms controlled.
The theorem does not cover sources without the specified node.

## The actual cutoff jump has a nonzero leading amplitude at a fixed meridian

The [fixed-meridian amplitude theorem](research_canonical_cutoff_fixed_meridian_amplitude.md)
upgrades the previous logarithmic growth estimate to an asymptotic
with its actual leading coefficient. Let \(D_R\) be the difference
of the two specified canonical finite cutoffs, in
\(u=\log(Y/\alpha)\). Retain the partner root \(\ell\), action
\(S(0)=0,\ S'(u)=\log\ell(u)\), and nonzero canonical node constant \(C_*\).
Put \(\kappa=\ell'(0)\). On the same growing ray as the earlier
proof, choose
\[
 \Re(\kappa e^{i\theta})>0,\qquad
 h=e^{i\theta}\varepsilon,\quad
 u_*=e^{i\theta}T,\quad R=\varrho e^{i\theta}.
\]
For every sufficiently small fixed \(T>0\), with a sufficiently
small fixed cutoff \(R\), the actual source satisfies
\[
 D_R(h,u_*)=
 C_*h^{-1/2}a(u_*)e^{S(u_*)/h}(1+o(1)),
 \qquad \varepsilon\downarrow0 .
\]
The target is reached exactly for all sufficiently small positive
\(\varepsilon\), not just along a subsequence.

Here \(a\) is holomorphic and nowhere zero near the node,
normalized by \(a(0)=1\). If \(P\) is the displayed classical
symbol and \(P^{[1]}\) its actual first \(h\)-coefficient, define
\[
 d_g=\ell P_L(u,\ell),\qquad
 e_g=P^{[1]}(u,\ell)+\frac{S''}{2}
                   \{\ell P_L(u,\ell)+\ell^2P_{LL}(u,\ell)\}.
\]
Then \(a'/a=-e_g/d_g\). This apparent singularity is removable:
the order-\(h\) equation of the actual simple-pole abelian source
forces the precise subprincipal cancellation \(e_g(0)=0\),
while \(d_g\) has a simple zero.

The proof retains the first correction of the actual quadratic
Ore reduction on fixed analytic buffers, giving an \(O(h^2)\)
remainder. It initializes the exact growing solution with the
canonical overlap, rather than prescribing a new direction.
A Riccati comparison has a summable error \(o(1)\) along the
entire landing grid. The previously bounded actual endpoint
forcing remains exponentially small relative to that solution.
These steps preserve both the nonzero coefficient and its phase.

This result concerns the actual finite-cutoff jump on the stated
growing ray. It does not transfer that coefficient to the complete
root-of-unity scalar, identify the partner as hyperbolic, or
exclude an essential Borel singularity on the moving cover.

## The canonical branch locus is the exact classical action graph

The [moving-branch theorem](research_canonical_borel_exact_moving_divisor.md)
identifies the whole local branch locus of the actual canonical source.
Assume the stated simple Alexander node of the displayed actual
operator: \(\alpha\ne0,1\) is a simple Alexander root,
\(P(Y,1)\equiv0\), and
\[
 P_L(\alpha,1)=0,\qquad
 P_{LL}(\alpha,1)P_{YL}(\alpha,1)\ne0 .
\]
Set \(u=\log(Y/\alpha)\). Holomorphic division of the classical
symbol, followed by the implicit function theorem, gives
\[
 P(u,L)=(L-1)(L-\ell(u))Q(u,L),\qquad
 \ell(0)=1,\quad\ell'(0)\ne0,\quad Q(0,1)\ne0.
\]
Define the complete analytic action by
\[
 S(0)=0,\qquad S'(u)=\log\ell(u),\qquad
 \rho=\xi+S(u).
\]
The symbol factorization here is not a replacement of the quantum
operator by a factor. The full actual operator is used throughout.

For sufficiently small fixed \(b_*,R_*>0\), the canonical Borel
source continues holomorphically on the actual twofold cover
\[
 |u|<b_*,\qquad 0<|\rho|<R_*,\qquad \tau^2=\rho .
\]
Its deck monodromy is nontrivial for every sufficiently small
\(u\). Thus its exact inner branch locus is
\(\xi=-S(u)\). This is an identity for the complete analytic
action, extending the previous quadratic and cubic calibrations.
It does not prove a finite pole order at \(\tau=0\): an essential
singularity on that cover is still allowed by this theorem.

The proof starts from the actual Laurent resolution, which
already gives the source outside \(|\rho|\le C|u|^3\).
On a compact meridian annulus, deform that inner radius by
strictly increasing smooth profiles \(r(t)\), \(t=|u|\),
fixed near both annulus ends. They can be made arbitrarily
small at any prescribed nonzero target, while keeping
\(0<r'(t)<c t/2\), where \(|S'(u)|\ge c|u|\).
The normal ratio on their boundaries is
\[
 p_{\rm nor}=S'(u)-
       \rho\frac{r'(t)}{r(t)}\frac{\bar u}{t}.
\]
It meets neither the abelian nor the partner characteristic;
the other factors and logarithmic aliases remain separated.
The actual noncharacteristic extension theorem below therefore
extends the source and its histories across each moving boundary.
Nested domains, compactness and fixed end collars rule out a
first stopping parameter. The initial twofold cover and its
nonzero deck difference persist by analytic uniqueness.
No regularity of an unknown singular set is assumed.

There is also a source-intrinsic consequence. Every other actual
finite-shift annihilator with analytic coefficients near the node
satisfies
\[
                 Q_{\rm cl}(u,\ell(u))=0 .
\]
If it were nonzero at one of these points, the same extension
theorem would remove the canonical branch there, contradicting
its nontrivial monodromy. For rational classical symbols, the
irreducible algebraic factor containing this branch consequently
divides every such symbol after denominators are cleared.
This is classical divisibility, not a quantum right-factor
identity. It shows that the partner is forced by the actual
source, rather than introduced only by a chosen left multiple.

The theorem is local at the specified simple node. Identifying
this intrinsic branch with the hyperbolic representation branch,
continuing it to the physical complete-meridian observation,
controlling all other contour terms, and obtaining an original
scalar lower bound remain necessary. The arbitrary-short-filling
goal also includes cores with no such Alexander node.

## A convergent inverse extends the actual source through noncharacteristic boundaries

The [analytic inverse theorem](research_actual_borel_analytic_elliptic_inverse.md)
proves a local extension result for the actual canonical Borel source
\(b(u,\xi)\), where \(u=\log Y\). Write the displayed finite-shift
operator and its classical symbol as
\[
 \mathcal P=\sum_jp_j(h,u)T^j,\qquad Tf(u)=f(u+h),\qquad
 P(u,L)=\sum_jp_j(0,u)L^j .
\]
The coefficients are holomorphic near the point considered; the
integer \(j\) ranges over a fixed finite set. No unproved factor
of this operator is substituted.

At \((u_0,\xi_0)\), choose a constant tilt
\[
 \rho=\xi-\xi_0+p_0(u-u_0),\qquad P(u_0,e^{p_0})\ne0 .
\]
Let \(J\) be the local primitive from a known base \(\rho_b\).
The local operator
\[
 \mathcal A_J=\sum_j e^{jp_0}p_j(J,u)e^{jJ\partial_u}
\]
has a convergent two-sided inverse on buffered meridian disks
and short primitive paths. Its coefficients satisfy the refined
bound
\[
 \mathcal B_J=\sum_{n\ge0}\sum_{k\le n}
          a_{n,k}(u)J^n\partial_u^k,\qquad
 |a_{n,k}|\le C_0 C^n(n-k)! .
\]
The proof controls the deficiency \(n-k\) with weighted Cauchy
norms. After \(k\) meridian derivatives and \(n\) primitives,
the remaining factorial ratio is \(k!(n-k)!/n!\le1\), so the
series converges geometrically. A uniform \(n!\) bound at every
differential order would not give this conclusion.

The original primitives cannot be replaced by local ones without
correction. Their exact history polynomials and the exact shifted
semigroup are kept. They give
\(\mathcal A_Jb=F\), with \(F\) holomorphic through the local
\(\rho\)-disk and fixed by the original history. Applying the
inverse extends the actual \(b\), its companions and its equation
from a supplied product wedge. The proof also treats holomorphic
graph coordinates explicitly.

There is a concrete consequence for a real \(C^2\) boundary with
nonzero \(\xi\)-normal component and the noncharacteristic ratio
above. At inward normal distance \(\varepsilon\), its known side
contains a slab with meridian radius proportional to
\(\sqrt{\varepsilon}\) and primitive length \(O(\varepsilon)\).
The operator coefficients are estimated on a fixed coefficient
disk, so the convergence ratio is \(O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})\).
The actual source therefore extends across the boundary, provided
its one-sided joint continuation and histories are supplied.
Those histories may grow without bound as the boundary is
approached; only their finite bounds on each interior slab enter.

This is a proved extension tool, not an assumption that the
source already has a fractional-power singularity. By itself
it does not identify the remaining singular locus or remove a
cofactor that is characteristic in an inserted-moment system.

## The full marked certificate acts on the original Verma moments

The [marked certificate transport theorem](research_marked_verma_full_certificate_transport.md)
pays source compatibility for polynomial functions of the fixed
path-index lattice. Keep the highest cut, choose its integral
coordinates \(k=(k_1,\ldots,k_s)\), and weight each original finite
summand by \(\mathbf w^k\). These marks describe a fixed word
evaluation; they are not asserted to define a new knot invariant.

The whole finite certificate has no internal multiplication variables.
Divide its common central \(q^N+1\) factor before root specialization,
then sum the zero-extended array with these weights. Internal shifts
become \(\mathbf w^{-1}\) exactly, with all boundary terms retained.
At \(x=q_N^{L-1}\), the signed high-index barriers restrict every
surviving path to the ordinary color-\(L\) quotient. The ratio of the
root and ordinary framing factors is
\[
 x^{-Nc}=(-1)^{c(L-1)}=1,\qquad c=b-1-w_{\rm writhe}\in2\mathbb Z.
\]
This remains true for every externally shifted color. Infinitely
many root levels therefore give an exact generic-\(q\) identity
for the weighted finite-color sources, coefficientwise in the marks.

The marked classical word at \(x=1\) is a weighted one-cycle
permutation. Deleting the cut column makes it nilpotent, so its
graded determinant is one there. This proves the marked regularity
needed for all-color formal rigidity. Consequently the full
certificate acts on the actual canonical marked completion:
\[
 \mathscr P(h,Y,\mathsf T,\mathbf w^{-1})
                 \mathcal W(h,Y;\mathbf w)=0,
 \qquad \mathsf T f(Y)=f(e^hY).
\]
Here \(Q=q^2\) and \(h=\log Q\).
The source has rational meridian coefficients. An arbitrary
certificate may use the chosen square-root meridian sheet.

Taking derivatives at \(\mathbf w=e^{\mathbf t}=1\) gives a finite
triangular system on every bounded collection of moments
\(M_\gamma=\left.\partial_{\mathbf t}^{\gamma}
 \mathcal W(h,Y;e^{\mathbf t})\right|_{\mathbf t=0}\).
These are the canonical completions of the original insertions
\(k^\gamma\). The diagonal is the specified
graded-lex coefficient \(A_\alpha\) of the whole certificate,
and its right sides contain only earlier moments. The exact
specialization \(\mathbf t=hm\) also retains the full clock
\(Q^{m\cdot k}\), without truncating its polynomial moments.

This closes the previous root-to-Verma source-compatibility gap
for these marks. It does not prove that \(A_\alpha\) has the
isolated rank-two node of a different scalar operator; a scalar
right divisor cannot simply replace it in the moment equations.
Nor does the result yet continue the inserted Borel sources or
identify their ratios with geometric characters. It covers
polynomial index weights and the stated clocks, rather than
every noncommuting weight-zero coupon.

## The original complete-color value has an exact Cauchy-cycle decomposition

The [Cauchy-cycle theorem](research_canonical_shift_current_cauchy_cycles.md)
integrates the entire color-shift semigroup into an explicit kernel.
Write \(u=\log Y\), let \(b(u,\xi)\) be the canonical Borel source,
and let \(\gamma\) be a constructed finite path from \(0\) to \(R\).
On a common single-valued logarithmic meridian domain \(\Omega\)
containing \(0,a\), with \(h=a/L\), the actual shift endpoint is
\[
 K_L(h;\gamma)=\frac{L}{2\pi i}
   \int_{\partial\Omega}\frac{dv}{v(v-a)}
      \int_\gamma e^{L(R-\xi)/v}b(v,\xi)\,d\xi .
\]
The boundary has the positive domain orientation, including clockwise
hole boundaries. This is the original endpoint, with every derivative
and primitive retained, rather than a new model for it. Cauchy's formula
sums their factorials to \((1+t)e^t\); along the exact characteristic
\(u=a-sh\), its \(s\)-integral is the endpoint of
\[
 \frac{s}{(v-a)(v-a+sh)}
       \exp\left(\frac{s(R-\xi)}{v-a+sh}\right).
\]
This calculation also permits a characteristic path avoiding holes.

At \(a=2\pi i,\ L=N\), choose an outer circle
\(C_\rho=\{|v-i\pi|=\rho\}\), \(\rho>\pi\), avoiding the logarithmic
Alexander zeros. Remove small disks around the finitely many zeros
inside it, with counterclockwise boundaries \(C_\nu\).
The compact canonical Borel estimate constructs one common short
straight cutoff \(R=ir\) on this punctured domain. Define
\[
 \mathcal E_{N,r}(C)=
 \frac{Ne^{-R/h_N}}{2\pi i}
       \int_C\frac{dv}{v(v-2\pi i)}
             \int_0^{ir}e^{N(ir-\xi)/v}b(v,\xi)\,d\xi ,
 \qquad h_N=\frac{2\pi i}{N}.
\]
For every \(N\ge2\), the exact original complete-color value is
\[
 C_N(e^{\pi i/N})
 =U_R(h_N,1)+e^{-R/h_N}A_N(h_N,R)
       -\mathcal E_{N,r}(C_\rho)
       +\sum_\nu\mathcal E_{N,r}(C_\nu).
\]
Here \(U_R=h_N^{-1}\int_0^{ir}e^{-\xi/h_N}b(0,\xi)\,d\xi\),
and \(A_N\) is the scalar endpoint defined in the next section.
The initial term is \(1+O(N^{-1})\). The outer term is
\[
 O(e^{-\gamma_\rho rN}),\qquad
 \gamma_\rho=\frac1{2\pi}-\frac1{\rho+\pi}>0.
\]
The latter estimate follows from the exact circle maximum
\(\max_{C_\rho}\Re(i/v)=1/(\rho+\pi)\).
Every counterclockwise interior cycle has coefficient \(+1\),
fixed by the original source and boundary orientation.

This determines the source's cycle coefficients, but not their
geometric interpretation or asymptotics. The interior integrals can
still interact with the scalar endpoint, which need not be small at
the short cutoff actually constructed here. The large-cutoff scalar
bound below does not extend the canonical source to that larger
cutoff. If such continuation is constructed, its moving boundaries
and both banks of each meridian cut remain explicit in the same
fiberwise Cauchy formula. If \(\Delta_K=1\), the short-cutoff hole
sum is empty and the scalar endpoint remains. No geometric coefficient
or volume lower bound is inferred in that case or in general.

## A finite cutoff controls the original scalar endpoint at any prescribed rate

The [scalar endpoint estimate](research_scalar_color_endpoint_large_cutoff_bound.md)
controls one of the two terms in the exact cutoff comparison using the
original finite-color polynomial. For a fixed braid with \(b\) strands,
\(\ell\) crossings and writhe \(w\), put
\[
 m=b-1,\qquad c=m-w,\qquad D=7\ell+2m+|c|.
\]
If \(C_L(q)=\sum_j a_{L,j}q^j\), the literal signed crossing
matrices, quotient cut, pivots and framing give
\[
 \sum_j|a_{L,j}|\le L^m3^{\ell(L-1)},\qquad
 \operatorname{supp}_q C_L\subset[-DL^2,DL^2].
\]
These are coefficient upper bounds and require no positivity of
the knot polynomial.

Write \(C_L(e^{h/2})=\sum_n c_{L,n}h^n\). The exact scalar endpoint
\[
 A_L(h,R)=\sum_{k,n\ge0}c_{L,k+n}h^k\frac{R^n}{n!}
\]
is entire in \(h,R\), and
\[
 |A_L(h,R)|\le L^m3^{\ell(L-1)}
       \exp\left(\frac{DL^2|h|}{2}+L\sqrt{2D|R|}\right).
\]
The square-root cutoff dependence follows by applying
\((k+n)!\ge k!n!\) to each exponential \(q^j=e^{jh/2}\),
then bounding \(\sum_n x^n/(n!)^2\le e^{2\sqrt x}\).
At \(h_N=2\pi i/N\), one finite \(R=ir\), chosen sufficiently
large before taking the level limit, therefore gives
\[
 |e^{-R/h_N}A_N(h_N,R)|\le e^{-\Lambda N}
\]
eventually, for any prescribed \(\Lambda>0\).

On the physical imaginary \(h\)-axis the estimate improves to
\[
 |e^{-ir/h_N}A_N(h_N,ir)|
 \le N^m\exp N\left(\ell\log3+\sqrt{2Dr}-\frac r{2\pi}\right).
\]
Indeed, for \(n\ge1\),
\[
 \sum_{k\ge0}\frac{z^k}{(k+n)!}
   =\frac1{(n-1)!}\int_0^1e^{tz}(1-t)^{n-1}\,dt .
\]
For \(z=jh/2\), with integer \(j\) and imaginary \(h\), its
modulus is at most \(1/n!\); the \(n=0\) expression has modulus
one. Applying the same square-root series bound to each frequency
therefore removes the factor \(\exp(DL^2|h|/2)\).
This corollary was proved from the complete fixed endpoint note
by root and checked by its author. It still requires a sufficiently
large cutoff, rather than the short cutoff already constructed
for the generic source.

The exact comparison still reads
\[
 U_R(h,e^{Lh})-C_L(e^{h/2})
       =e^{-R/h}\{K_L(h,R)-A_L(h,R)\}.
\]
The new estimate pays the scalar term \(A_L\). Constructing the
canonical generic-meridian cutoff at that large endpoint, and
bounding its continued shift term \(K_L\), remain necessary.
The entire scalar function alone supplies neither construction,
and gives no lower bound for the original complete-color value.

## Node continuation forces an exact compensating endpoint jump

The [color-line compensation theorem](research_canonical_cutoff_colorline_monodromy_compensation.md)
connects the initial cutoff with both canonical sheets at a simple
Alexander node. The compact Gevrey estimate first continues the
actual Borel germ along a meridian path avoiding the Alexander
divisor. The resolved local source then permits an explicit
endpoint-sheet exchange while staying outside its unresolved
inner singular region.

Let \(\alpha\ne0,1\) be a simple Alexander root satisfying the
actual operator-node hypotheses, choose \(a=\log\alpha\ne0\),
and take a small cutoff \(R=\varrho a/|a|\). At color
\(L\), the two continuations end at \(h_L=a/L,\ Y=\alpha\).
The original polynomial and its scalar endpoint \(A_L\) are
entire and single valued. Subtracting their exact continued
cutoff identities therefore gives
\[
 K_{L,+}(h_L)-K_{L,-}(h_L)
    =e^{LR/a}\{U_{R,+}(h_L,0)-U_{R,-}(h_L,0)\}
    =C_*\sqrt{L/a}\,e^{LR/a}(1+o(1)),
\]
where \(C_*=2r\sqrt{-\eta_*}\sqrt\pi\ne0\) is the proved
canonical node coefficient, and \(r=1/\Delta_K'(\alpha)\).
Here the second argument of the local cutoffs is the displacement
\(Y-\alpha=0\), not the meridian itself.

Thus at least one of the two cutoff errors has size at least
a constant times \(\sqrt L\). The two errors cannot both stay
exponentially small under continuation. This conclusion does
not rule out accurate matching on one source-selected path.
It explains why the nonzero local cutoff jump cannot itself
be called a contribution to the finite invariant: its endpoint
jump compensates it exactly in the original observation.
A quantitative bound on the selected path remains unpaid.
Neither the physical complete-root endpoint nor a hyperbolic
component identification follows from this node theorem.

## Exponentially accurate matching with original colors growing as \(1/|h|\)

The [uniform large-color cutoff comparison](research_uniform_large_color_cutoff_match.md)
strengthens the fixed-color identity near the original meridian \(Y=1\).
For a short straight Borel cutoff \(0\to R\), any closed facing
\(h\)-subsector, and a sufficiently small \(u_1>0\),
\[
 \left|U_R(h,e^{Lh})-C_L(e^{h/2})\right|
       \le C e^{-c|R|/|h|}
 \qquad\text{for all integers }L\ge1,\quad 0<|Lh|\le u_1 .
\]
The constants are independent of \(L,h\). The range includes
\(L=O(|h|^{-1})\), with the meridian staying in a fixed initial
logarithmic neighborhood. No Alexander-node hypothesis is needed
for this initial comparison.

The proof bounds both endpoint amplitudes in the exact finite-cutoff
identity. In a fixed logarithmic meridian disk, the extra primitive
and derivative in
\(\partial_u I e^{sI\partial_u}b\) cancel their factorials.
Consequently its integrated shift amplitude is at most
\(M(e^{L|R|/d}-1)\). The actual finite-color analytic anchor gives
\[
 \sup_{L\ge1,\ |u|\le u_0}
       |C_L(e^{u/(2L)})|\le M_0,
\]
and hence its scalar endpoint amplitude is at most
\[
       \frac{M_0e^{L|R|/u_0}}{1-L|h|/u_0}.
\]
Choosing \(u_1\) small makes these two growing-color costs smaller
than the facing cutoff exponential \(e^{-\operatorname{Re}(R/h)}\).
The proof checks the common analytic domain throughout the entire
color-length shift, rather than applying a fixed-color germ identity
outside its stated radius.

This pays actual-source matching on the initial small color arc.
It does not connect that arc to the Alexander node or the local
fixed-meridian growing branch below. The endpoint discrepancy
remains explicit and must be transported with control.
The estimate does not reach \(Lh=2\pi i\), the complete-color point.
Thus it supplies no original Kashaev lower bound by itself.

## A nonzero action rate at a fixed meridian

The [fixed-meridian growth proof](research_canonical_cutoff_fixed_meridian_growth.md)
transports the canonical cutoff jump from its shrinking overlap
to a fixed target. Put
\[
 u=\log(Y/\alpha),\qquad
 \kappa=\ell'(0)=-2\eta_*\alpha^2\ne0,\qquad
 \mathcal A(0)=0,\quad\mathcal A'(u)=\log\ell(u).
\]
Choose a direction \(\theta\) with
\(\operatorname{Re}(\kappa e^{i\theta})>0\), and a small cutoff
\(R\) on that ray. For every sufficiently small fixed
\(u_*=e^{i\theta}T\), the actual canonical jump satisfies
\[
 D_R(e^{i\theta}\varepsilon,u_*)\ne0,\qquad
 \log|D_R(h,u_*)|
       =\operatorname{Re}(\mathcal A(u_*)/h)
                         +O(\log(1/\varepsilon)),
 \quad h=e^{i\theta}\varepsilon,\quad\varepsilon\downarrow0.
\]
Equivalently its size is bounded above and below by fixed powers
of \(\varepsilon\) times the indicated exponential. Thus
\[
 \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
       \varepsilon\log|D_R(e^{i\theta}\varepsilon,u_*)|
       =\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\theta}\mathcal A(u_*))>0.
\]
The target is fixed and reached exactly for every sufficiently small
\(\varepsilon\), not just on a chosen subsequence.

The actual quadratic reduction below first pays the complementary
modes. The proof then starts at \(u_0\asymp\varepsilon^\beta\),
\(1/3<\beta<1/2\). Cauchy's estimate on the canonical overlap
determines the actual two-component initial vector.
Its unwanted component is \(O(\varepsilon/|u_0|^2)\) relative
to the growing one. This cone remains invariant: the spectral
gap is proportional to \(|u|\), and the moving-frame error is
\(O(\varepsilon/|u|)\). Their accumulated scalar error is only
\(O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\). The actual additive cutoff forcing
is estimated against the same growing product and cannot cancel
the initialized contribution.

This pays fixed-meridian propagation in a local growing sector.
It neither identifies that sector with the physical root-of-unity
direction nor identifies the operator component with hyperbolic
holonomy. The cutoff jump has also not been identified with the
original complete-color scalar.
Global continuation, these source and component comparisons, and
the cases without an Alexander pole remain necessary for the
arbitrary-short-filling and finite-exception targets.

## The actual cutoff source has an exponentially accurate quadratic equation

The [quadratic Ore-reduction proof](research_canonical_cutoff_quadratic_ore_reduction.md)
removes the complementary modes of the actual operator on a small
meridian disk. It does not order their moduli or assume that the
extreme classical coefficients survive.

In \(x=\log(Y/\alpha)\), choose a fixed small cutoff \(R\) and
a source disk of radius \(\delta=c_0\sqrt{|R|}\).
The actual finite-cutoff primitive estimates give
\[
 \|U_R\|\le
 C\frac{\sqrt{|R|}}{|h|}
       \exp(C_2|R|/|h|).
\]
The constants in this type estimate are chosen before \(R\).
The classical operator factors locally as
\(Q_0(x,T)(T-1)(T-\ell(x))\), with \(Q_0(0,1)\ne0\).
Analytic coefficient correction on nested disks constructs
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal P}_h=Q_h\#\mathcal S_h+E_h,\qquad
 \mathcal S_h=T^2+s_{1,h}T+s_{0,h},\qquad
 \|\mathcal S_h-\mathcal S_0\|=O(|h|),\qquad
 \|E_h\|\le Ce^{-c\delta/|h|}.
\]
The quadratic is monic. The coefficient Sylvester inverse exists
by coprimality modulo this quadratic, even when the complementary
polynomial has vanishing leading coefficients.
Only meridian holomorphy of these finitely truncated factors is
asserted, not holomorphy at \(h=0\).

An analytic-scale finite Neumann identity estimates
\(f=\mathcal S_h U_R\) from \(Q_h f\).
It bounds the actual function \(f\); no initial projection of the
source is assumed. Since \(\delta\) is much larger than \(|R|\),
the source type is smaller than the exponential factorization and
inverse gains. The result is
\[
       \|\mathcal S_h U_{R,\pm}\|
           \le C_R e^{-\operatorname{Re}(R/h)}
\]
on a smaller disk in closed sectors facing \(R\).
The same quadratic and estimate hold for their difference.
Its canonical node profile therefore survives in a two-branch
quasiequation with the original cutoff error.

This result pays the complementary-mode issue near the node.
It does not itself transport the nonzero coefficient to a fixed
meridian, identify a geometric representation component, or compare
the cutoff source with the complete-color knot value.

\(\texttt{90db0237f4536495e7150109eae374ebbb12e2f7515b7c577322d07d2b9daae7}\).

## Canonical regularization through the node and a nonzero connection profile

The [cutoff regularization and profile proof](research_canonical_cutoff_node_regularization_and_profile.md)
now constructs two actual canonical cutoff functions \(U_{R,\pm}(h,z)\)
through \(z=Y-\alpha=0\), for a fixed small nonzero cutoff \(R\).
The primitive calculation uses the Laurent resolution below.
Its negative powers in the resolved integration coordinate are even,
so no logarithmic primitive occurs. The endpoint primitive series
converge and extend holomorphically through the Alexander divisor.
This proves joint holomorphy in \(z\), for \(h\ne0\), of the actual
finite integrals. It does not assert holomorphy at \(h=0\).

Their original operator currents also extend jointly through
\((h,z)=(0,0)\):
\[
       \mathcal P U_{R,\pm}=e^{-R/h}J_{R,\pm}(h,z),
       \qquad |J_{R,\pm}|\le C,\qquad J_{R,\pm}(0,z)=0 .
\]
The proof glues the actual currents on a fixed \(z\)-circle and
uses Cauchy's formula to extend them across the node.
Thus the endpoint defect is uniformly exponentially small on closed
\(h\)-subsectors facing \(R\).

Set \(\eta_*=B/(2A)\), \(r=1/\Delta_K'(\alpha)\), and choose
\(\beta^2=-\eta_*\) with the recorded endpoint orientation.
The uniform square-root-scale limit is
\[
 \sqrt h\,U_{R,\pm}(h,\sqrt h\,s)\longrightarrow
 -2\eta_*r e^{-\eta_*s^2}
                  \int_s^{\infty_\pm}e^{\eta_*v^2}\,dv .
\]
It follows from the convergent canonical source, with the original
finite cutoff retained. Their difference has the nonzero coefficient
\[
             C_*=2\beta r\sqrt\pi\ne0.
\]
In particular, on each compact \(s\)-set,
\[
 |U_{R,+}(h,\sqrt h\,s)-U_{R,-}(h,\sqrt h\,s)|
                         \ge c_K|h|^{-1/2}
\]
for every sufficiently small \(h\) in those subsectors.
This is a lower bound for a specified canonical cutoff source,
stronger than mere nonidentical vanishing of an analytic function.
It is not a lower bound for the knot's complete-color scalar.

There is a genuine growing overlap. For each \(0<\delta<1/6\),
put \(D_R=U_{R,+}-U_{R,-}\). The proof gives
\[
 D_R(h,z)=C_*h^{-1/2}e^{S(\alpha+z)/h}
           \{1+O(|h|^{1/2-3\delta})\},
 \qquad |z|\le |h|^{1/2-\delta}.
\]
Here \(S'=\log\ell/Y\) is the local action of the actual second
operator branch. The replacement of its quadratic part is justified
by \(z^3/h\to0\); it is not a fixed-meridian asymptotic.
The range includes \(\sqrt{|h|}\ll|z|\ll|h|^{1/3}\), where the
node profile overlaps ordinary semiclassical scaling.
Combining this lower bound with the uniform endpoint defect also gives
\[
           |(\mathcal P D_R)/D_R|\le C e^{-c/|h|}
\]
on the stated growing overlap, after reducing \(c>0\).
Indeed the profile can lose only \(e^{-C|h|^{-2\delta}}\), while
the cutoff defect has \(e^{-c_R/|h|}\), and \(2\delta<1\).
This is a relative operator residual, not a transported solution
error or an original-invariant estimate.

The local source-to-node connection has now been established for
these canonical cutoff functions. Transport to a fixed nonzero
meridian, comparison with the original complete-color source, and
identification of the operator branch with hyperbolic holonomy
remain open. The argument still requires an Alexander pole and
does not treat the \(\Delta_K=1\) part of the broad target.
No finite-exception theorem is claimed.

The final proof is fixed at
\(\texttt{8c28a3d3a7b11085c8e2b5966221501b632ea99600aae4db57e8bdf8cd4a9631}\).
Author, peer and root checked the entire final and both complete
sources \(\texttt{6a65d3f4}\) and \(\texttt{b3b1e424}\), with renewed
matching hashes. The displayed relative-residual corollary follows
directly from those two written bounds.

## A convergent Laurent resolution with a fixed small Borel cutoff

The [Laurent-resolution proof](research_classical_verma_borel_laurent_resolution.md)
strengthens the earlier continuation domains under the same actual
operator-node hypotheses. Put
\[
 s=(1-\eta/\eta_*)^{1/2},\qquad
 b(z,\eta)=\sum_{k\ge0}b_k(\eta)z^k .
\]
Every canonical coefficient belongs to the finite space
\[
 b_k\in
 \operatorname{span}\{s^{-1},s^{-3},\ldots,s^{-(2k+1)}\}
       \oplus\mathbb C[s]_{\le k-1}.
\]
There are no logarithms in any transverse coefficient.
The exact finite-shift forcing preserves this space. At even \(k\),
its leading operator has one compatibility condition; the actual
canonical germ satisfies it. This uses the source equations and
their analytic Borel germ, not a guess from the first few jets.

The Laurent coefficient sums are bounded by \(CD^k\).
The resulting source converges on
\[
       D|z|\max(|s|,|s|^{-2})<1,\qquad s\ne0,
 \qquad
 |b(z,\eta)|\le
 \frac{C}{|s|\{1-D|z|\max(|s|,|s|^{-2})\}} .
\]
It is regular at both lifts \(s=\pm1\) of \(\eta=0\).
The cluster monodromy is exactly twofold and nontrivial.
This pays the other-sheet return-to-zero issue left open by the
earlier punctured-path theorem.

There is also a convergent description in the original Borel variable.
With \(w^2=z^2-\xi/\eta_*\),
\[
 \mathcal B_h\mathscr W(\alpha+z,\xi)
       =\frac1w H\left(z,w,\frac{z^3}{w^2}\right),
 \qquad H\text{ holomorphic near }(0,0,0),\quad H(0,0,0)=r.
\]
For a fixed sufficiently large \(R\) and small \(\xi_0>0\), this
gives the continued source on
\[
 R|z|^2\le|\xi|\le\xi_0,\qquad
 |\mathcal B_h\mathscr W|\le C|\xi|^{-1/2}.
\]
Thus a small outer cutoff can now be chosen independently of \(z\).
The unresolved inner region has cubic scale in \(w^2\).
At each fixed nonzero small \(\xi\), the chosen endpoint sheet
extends holomorphically through \(z=0\).
No uniform cutoff-current estimate is inferred merely by replacing
the old cutoff in its crude norm bound.

One further exact evaluation resolves the next leading layer.
Writing the actual principal coefficients as
\[
 a_{11}=Bz+b_{11}z^2+\cdots,\qquad
 a_{22}=A+b_{22}z+\cdots,\qquad
 \mathfrak d=b_{11}-(B/A)b_{22}+(B^2/A^2)a_{33}(0),
\]
the new exceptional restriction is
\[
 H(0,0,u)=r\left(1+\frac{2\mathfrak d}{3B}u\right)^{-1/2}.
\]
For the actual second classical branch \(\ell(Y)\), define
\(S(\alpha)=0\) and \(S'(Y)=\log\ell(Y)/Y\).
The proof checks directly that
\[
 -S(\alpha+z)/z^2
       =\eta_*+\frac{\mathfrak d}{3A}z+O(z^2).
\]
Hence the second exceptional restriction agrees exactly with the
action-predicted cubic displacement.
The theorem does not identify the entire moving singular set as
\(\xi=-S(Y)\), or identify this branch with hyperbolic holonomy.
The broad target also includes \(\Delta_K=1\), where this pole
seed is absent. No arbitrary-short-filling lower bound is claimed.

\(\texttt{6a65d3f47544255c46e6cc5450d822b5b38cfccce591e5ad59e21d4c569be341}\).

## A nonzero analytic period with a controlled quantum defect

The [canonical cutoff-period proof](research_canonical_borel_nonzero_cutoff_quasimode.md)
now converts the nonzero Borel monodromy into a nonidentically-zero
analytic function. This does not require an infinite Laplace contour.

Fix a small nonzero \(z_0=Y_0-\alpha\). Take two continued Borel paths
with the same start and cutoff endpoint \(R\): one includes a loop
around the local singular cluster, and both then follow the same
simple exterior tail. Their actual finite Laplace integrals satisfy
\[
 \mathcal P(U_1-U_0)
       =e^{-R/h}(J_1-J_0).
\]
The construction retains a common meridian disk of radius
proportional to \(|z_0|\), the original operator, and every cutoff
current. With the polynomial-horn cutoff,
\[
 |R|\asymp |z_0|^{2-1/\kappa},\qquad
 |J_i|\le C|z_0|^{-1-1/\kappa}
 \quad (|h|<c|z_0|).
\]
On closed \(h\)-subsectors facing \(R\), the absolute defect is bounded by
\[
 C|z_0|^{-1-1/\kappa}
       \exp\!\left(-c_\sigma
                 \frac{|z_0|^{2-1/\kappa}}{|h|}\right).
\]
This cutoff exponential lies beyond the local quadratic action scale.
It is not a relative estimate for the integral.

The nonzero statement concerns the actual canonical density.
If the difference of its finite Laplace integrals vanished identically,
all contour moments would vanish. Their Cauchy transform would vanish
in the unbounded complement of the projected contour. Both sides of
the free exterior tail belong to that complement; its Cauchy jump
would then force the known nonzero Borel monodromy density to vanish.
This contradiction proves nonidentical vanishing on every meridian
fiber in the chosen smaller disk.

It also gives a nonzero class modulo \(e^{-R/h}\) times amplitudes
holomorphic at \(h=0\), when equality is required on a full punctured
neighborhood. The proof uses the entire function of \(1/h\) defined
by the finite contour and Liouville's theorem.
No quotient by arbitrary sectorially flat functions is asserted.

The result does not identify a leading nonabelian action, prove
nonzero values on the physical sequence, or compare this local period
with the original complete-color scalar. A nonzero analytic function
alone supplies none of those lower bounds.
The arbitrary-short-partial-filling and finite-exception theorems
remain open.

The final proof is fixed at
\(\texttt{e719589ee216e9ed30216c17916d5dbd9c834dfb905bf4359313ae32d55229af}\).
Author, peer and root checked the entire final and all three complete
sources \(\texttt{b3b1e424}\), \(\texttt{35347248}\) and
\(\texttt{67cbb4c1}\), with renewed matching hashes.
Frozen manuscripts and public documentation are unchanged.

## A finite Borel integral has an exact endpoint current

The [finite-Laplace proof](research_canonical_borel_finite_laplace_current.md)
constructs an actual analytic function from any finite continued
canonical Borel path \(\gamma:0\to R\) on a common meridian disk:
\[
 U_\gamma(h,Y)=\frac1h\int_\gamma e^{-\xi/h}b(Y,\xi)\,d\xi,
 \qquad
 \mathcal P(h)U_\gamma=e^{-R/h}J_\gamma(h,Y).
\]
Here \(\mathcal P\) is the actual finite quantum-shift annihilator.
The amplitude \(J_\gamma\) is holomorphic and bounded also at \(h=0\),
and the proof retains every path history, negative shift, analytic
coefficient and original gauge.

Writing the actual differential expansion as
\(\mathcal P=\sum_{n\ge1}h^nL_n\), its precise current is
\[
 J_\gamma=\sum_{n\ge1}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}
                  h^j I^{n-j}L_n b(Y,R).
\]
The finite-shift factorial and Cauchy estimates give
\(\|L_n b\|\le M C^n\).
If \(\gamma\) has length \(L_\gamma\), then
\[
 |J_\gamma|\le
       \frac{M(e^{C L_\gamma}-1)}{1-C|h|}.
\]
The source Borel equation also retains the cancellation
\(J_\gamma(0,Y)=0\).
This is an exact analytic recurrence with an endpoint defect;
no integration to infinite Borel distance is required.
Its defect is exponentially small only in directions where
\(\operatorname{Re}(R/h)>0\).

On a common disk containing \(Y=1\), each fixed positive color has
the further exact identity
\[
 U_\gamma(h,e^{Lh})
      =C_L(e^{h/2})+e^{-R/h}H_{\gamma,L}(h),
 \qquad H_{\gamma,L}(0)=-b(1,R).
\]
The amplitude is holomorphic at zero. This is a controlled cutoff
comparison, not equality with the finite polynomial, and the
constants may depend on \(L\). It is not yet a bound for \(L\to\infty\).
A path near an Alexander point is not assumed to share a meridian
disk with \(Y=1\).

The construction provides a weaker possible route than a full
Laplace summation theorem: a finite action window could suffice if
the endpoint error can be transported below the desired geometric
contribution. Such a transport estimate, the exact nonabelian
exponent and the original scalar lower bound remain unproved.

The final proof is fixed at
\(\texttt{b3b1e4246e2b5ed1b364585b8504edf8e0f1f1e15797f62f276fc4b89dca586f}\).
Author, peer and root checked the entire final and all three complete
sources \(\texttt{f88f5fc4}\), \(\texttt{6ba957d7}\) and
\(\texttt{67cbb4c1}\), with renewed matching hashes.
Frozen manuscripts and public documentation are unchanged.

## A uniform sectorial sum would fix the original finite-color source

The [uniform-sum identification proof](research_uniform_verma_sum_physical_source_adapter.md)
removes a separate local choice of period once the required analytic
sum has been constructed. Suppose a jointly holomorphic function
\(S(h,Y)\), on a meridian neighborhood of \(1\) and an \(h\)-sector
of opening greater than \(\pi\), has the canonical source as its
uniform Gevrey-one asymptotic expansion. Then, for every fixed
positive integer \(L\),
\[
                 S(h,e^{Lh})=C_L(e^{h/2})
\]
near \(h=0\). The proof preserves factorial remainders under the
substitution and proves flat uniqueness by an elementary vertical
Laplace contour. All scalar and framing normalizations are those of
the original source. No estimate uniform in \(L\) is inferred.

Any continuation of that pullback along its lifted color curve
continues the same entire finite-color function. At
\(h=2\pi i/L\), it would therefore recover the original Kashaev
value, if the candidate can be continued there. The meridian lift
\(u=Lh\) must be retained; its endpoint is not automatically the
initial sheet at \(Y=1\).

The analytic sum in this statement has not been constructed.
The actual normal gauge does not supply a regular transport inverse
at the anchor: if \(p(Y)=P_L(Y,1)\), then \(p(1)=0\), and the
first-order reduced transport obtained from the full normal operator is
\[
 Y(Y-1)p(Y)
          \left(\partial_Y+\frac{\Delta_K'(Y)}{\Delta_K(Y)}\right).
\]
It vanishes at least quadratically at \(Y=1\). Dividing that factor
from the first term does not divide it from the whole quantum
operator. The finite-color analytic anchor is also insufficient
for the stated product-sector hypothesis. Thus the remaining
construction is genuinely analytic; this conditional identification
does not supply a new volume theorem.

\(\texttt{51b8c31a4c1495575fa8426a1e807b217d86dce6dec60ca0c159895ad74889ea}\).

source \(\texttt{f88f5fc4}\), with renewed matching hashes.

## A quantitative continuation domain at large Borel distance

The [polynomial-horn estimate](research_classical_verma_borel_polynomial_horn.md)
quantifies the continuation below. On a fixed sheet, after bounded
detours and along outward rays in a fixed angular interval, its
canonical transverse coefficients satisfy
\[
 |b_k(\eta)|+\frac{(1+|\eta|)|b_k'(\eta)|}{k+1}
       \le C D^k(1+|\eta|)^{\kappa(k+1)}
\]
for a fixed \(\kappa\ge2\). Consequently the joint source is
holomorphic and polynomially bounded in the domain
\[
                  D|z|(1+|\eta|)^\kappa<1.
\]
The proof uses polynomial path weights instead of the earlier
exponential weights. The derivative endpoint has an additional
inverse time factor, so it obeys the same time budget as the
Volterra primitives. All constants are uniform along the chosen
unbounded rays.

For small fixed \(z\ne0\), this permits an original Borel cutoff
\[
 |\xi_{\rm cut}|\asymp|z|^{2-1/\kappa},
 \qquad \xi=z^2\eta.
\]
This cutoff is farther than the local quadratic action scale
\(|z|^2\). The allowed \(z\)-radius nevertheless tends to zero
at infinite Borel distance. No fixed-\(z\) full Laplace ray, moving
singularity formula, or original scalar lower bound is obtained.

## Joint Borel continuation and nonzero monodromy near an Alexander root

The [joint-continuation proof](research_classical_verma_borel_joint_continuation.md)
extends the pole-profile result below beyond the exceptional divisor.
Under the same explicit transverse-node hypotheses on a supplied actual
operator, the canonical germ
\[
 b(z,\eta)=\sum_{j\ge0}z^{2j+1}W_j(\alpha+z)\frac{\eta^j}{j!},
 \qquad z=Y-\alpha,\qquad \eta_*=\frac{B}{2A},
\]
continues jointly near \(z=0\) along every fixed finite path leaving its
initial germ and subsequently avoiding \(\{0,\eta_*\}\).
The permitted \(z\)-radius depends on the path and remains positive.

The proof retains the exact finite quantum shifts.
Their order-\(n\), derivative-order-\(\ell\) coefficients have the bound
\(C H^n Z^v/\ell!\), with \(\ell\le n\).
In the pole chart \(h=z^2\varepsilon\), the \(k\)-th transverse
coefficient satisfies two first-order Borel equations. A lower
coefficient \(p=k-s\) appears with a Volterra primitive of order
\(n-1\) and a polynomial of degree \(\ell\) in its Euler derivative.
Exact normal ordering leaves at most one actual derivative.
Exponential path weights make the primitives compensate the growing
Euler coefficients; the leading inverse contributes \(1/(k+1)\).
The resulting bound is
\[
 M_k\le C_0D_0^k+C_1\sum_{s=1}^kD_1^s M_{k-s},
 \qquad\text{hence}\qquad M_k\le C_2D_2^k.
\]
It includes the full integration history from the initial germ, even
on loops. This exponential bound proves convergence of the continued
\(z\)-series, rather than continuation of separate formal coefficients.

Choose a loop based at a small nonzero \(\eta_b\), winding once around
\(\eta_*\) and not around zero. At \(z=0\), the difference between the
continued and original germs is exactly
\[
 -2r(1-\eta_b/\eta_*)^{-1/2}\ne0.
\]
Joint holomorphy makes that difference nonzero for every sufficiently
small \(z\), including \(z\ne0\). Thus the actual canonical Borel germ
has nontrivial nearby monodromy; this is no longer only a calculation
on the exceptional divisor.

No return through \(\eta=0\) on another sheet is asserted.
The theorem does not locate the moving singularities for \(z\ne0\),
bound growth at infinite Borel distance, construct a Laplace sum, or
identify a geometric coefficient in the original knot invariant.
The actual operator's second branch has also not been identified as
hyperbolic holonomy in general. The arbitrary-short-partial-filling
and finite-exception theorems therefore remain open.

## The canonical Borel germ has an exact Alexander-pole value

The [pole-profile proof](research_classical_verma_borel_pole_profile.md)
now gives a convergent analytic object attached to the actual
canonical \(q\to1\) coefficients. Write
\[
 \mathscr W_K(h,Y)=\sum_{j\ge0}h^j W_j(Y),\qquad h=\log Q .
\]
For every compact set avoiding the Alexander divisor,
\(\sup|W_j|\le C A_0^j j!\).
The proof uses the finite total-index source on quantum disks of radius
proportional to \(1/(T+1)\), followed by its exact polynomial numerator
in the grading variable. Continuing that polynomial to grading one
preserves a single factorial.

Suppose \(\alpha\) is a simple Alexander root and a supplied actual
operator, regular there, passes the derivative tests below.
Set \(z=Y-\alpha\),
\[
 r=\frac1{\Delta_K'(\alpha)},\qquad
 A=\tfrac12\alpha^2P_{LL}(\alpha,1),\qquad
 B=\alpha P_{YL}(\alpha,1),\qquad AB\ne0 .
\]
Its ordered source equation forces
\[
 \left.z^{2j+1}W_j(\alpha+z)\right|_{z=0}
     =r(2j-1)!!(A/B)^j.
\]
Thus every allowed highest pole is actually present.
The fixed-circle factorial bound and the maximum principle make
\[
 \mathcal B^{\rm pole}(z,\eta)=
 \sum_{j\ge0}z^{2j+1}W_j(\alpha+z)\frac{\eta^j}{j!}
\]
jointly holomorphic near \((0,0)\), including \(z=0\).
Its exact restriction there is
\[
 \mathcal B^{\rm pole}(0,\eta)
           =r(1-2A\eta/B)^{-1/2}.
\]
No summation contour is chosen in this evaluation.
The one-variable restriction has nonzero square-root monodromy
at \(\eta_*=B/(2A)\). The relative classical action of the second
operator branch starts with \(-\eta_*z^2\).

The local transition class is already studied: statement-level
coverage includes Witten,
[Analytic Continuation of Chern--Simons Theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.2933),
sections 3.4.2 and 5.2.1, and the torus-knot expansions of
Hikami--Murakami,
[Colored Jones polynomials with polynomial growth](https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.2836),
Proposition 3.2. No new transition universality is claimed; their proofs
are not premises here.

The theorem proves neither joint continuation up to
\((0,\eta_*)\) nor a nearby singularity for \(z\ne0\).
It also does not identify a Laplace sum with the original finite
source or determine its geometric coefficient.
Those distinctions remain necessary for the short-filling theorem.

The final proof is fixed at
\(\texttt{6ba957d7a521524f370cb3bdd90ab30338bff8c13960ae6ca1825d08260c77d2}\).

source \(\texttt{f88f5fc4}\), with renewed matching hashes.
