## The original finite-color polynomials have a controlled analytic anchor

The [small-meridian estimate](research_finite_color_small_meridian_analytic_anchor.md)
now ties the formal classical series to the actual finite-color
polynomials on a small complex neighborhood of meridian \(1\).
For a fixed original one-component cut braid, there is \(R>0\) such that
\[
 C_L(e^{u/(2L)})\longrightarrow\Delta_K(e^u)^{-1}
 \quad\text{uniformly on }|u|\le R .
\]
In the coordinates \(h=\log Q\), \(Y=e^u\), let
\(\mathcal W_K(1-e^h,e^u)=\sum_jh^j a_j(u)\).
For every \(0<r<R\), the same proof gives constants \(K,A\) with
\[
 \left|C_L(e^{u/(2L)})
       -\sum_{j<J}(u/L)^j a_j(u)\right|
 \le K A^J J!|u/L|^J
\]
for all \(L\ge2\), \(J\ge1\), and \(r\le|u|\le R\).

The reason is visible in the original index paths.
Following the single knot component from its cut index zero,
every internal index is at most the sum of the crossing transfers.
Thus a sector of total index \(T\) requires at least \(T/(b-1)\)
transfers. Their color-product factors are uniformly small near
\(u=0\). Extracting part of this small factor leaves an ordinary
binomial column sum and a summable bound \(K_0{T+b-2\choose b-2}a^T\),
with \(a<1\), on a quantum disk of radius proportional to \(1/(T+1)\).
Cauchy's estimate gives the factorial remainder. The coefficient
tail beyond the actual finite-color cutoff is included.

This is an independent literal-source proof of established analytic
Melvin--Morton--Rozansky territory. The primary statement-level
coverage is Garoufalidis--Lê,
[Asymptotics of the colored Jones function of a knot](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508100),
Theorems 1.3 and 1.6, with their quantum variable translated to our \(Q\).
Their proof is not used.

The new estimate is local in \(u\). It permits exponentially small
differences with the same asymptotic series and therefore neither
selects a Borel sum nor proves continuation to \(u=2\pi i\).
No volume case or finite-exception conclusion follows.

The proof is fixed at
\(\texttt{946a0495603a1a0fc92965c8e70a99c403c4cfb22952cd6838cf3beb20c2f0ba}\).
Author/root and peer checked the entire final and its sole complete
source \(\texttt{f88f5fc4}\), with renewed matching hashes.

## An exact algebraic test for the Alexander collision

The [actual transport proof](research_actual_abelian_transport_and_symbol_collision.md)
uses the retained normal state \(v_0=(Y-1)/\Delta_K(Y)\).
For a specified actual left-ordered annihilator, with classical
symbol \(P(Y,\Lambda)\) and first quantum coefficient \(P_1\) in
\(h=\log Q\), put \(p(Y)=P_\Lambda(Y,1)\).
The order-\(h\) equation gives exactly
\[
 P_1(Y,1)=Yp(Y)
       \left(\frac{\Delta_K'(Y)}{\Delta_K(Y)}
                                      -\frac1{Y-1}\right).
\]
When the operator coefficients are regular at the points concerned,
\[
 (Y-1)\operatorname{rad}\Delta_K(Y)\mid p(Y).
\]
Thus the actual source itself forces a classical collision at every
Alexander root. A vertical classical factor can account for this
divisibility; no second geometric branch is inferred from it alone.

At an Alexander root \(\alpha\) of multiplicity \(m\),
\(P_1(\alpha,1)=m\alpha P_{Y\Lambda}(\alpha,1)\).
If the two directly checkable derivatives
\[
 P_{\Lambda\Lambda}(\alpha,1)\ne0,\qquad
 P_{Y\Lambda}(\alpha,1)\ne0
\]
both hold, the actual symbol has exactly a local pair consisting of
the abelian branch and a transverse second shift branch.
Writing
\[
 A=\tfrac12\alpha^2P_{\Lambda\Lambda}(\alpha,1),\qquad
 B_*=\alpha P_{Y\Lambda}(\alpha,1),
\]
the leading scaled equation at a simple root is
\[
 (A y'+B_*s y)'=0.
\]
The original normal residue is
\(r=(\alpha-1)/\Delta_K'(\alpha)\ne0\), so the prescribed algebraic
tail \(y\sim r/s\) forces \(A y'+B_*sy=B_*r\).
The calculation does not establish an analytic scaling limit or
identify this second operator branch with hyperbolic holonomy.

## The original classical source and its Alexander residue

The [classical Verma-loop proof](research_classical_verma_rational_loops.md)
extends the literal crossing-and-cut construction to \(Q=1\), without
introducing a level-one ADO invariant. In the natural squared meridian
\(Y=Qx^2\), it constructs the canonical formal series
\[
 \mathcal W_K(\delta,Y)=\sum_{j\ge0}\delta^j W_j(Y),
 \qquad \delta=1-Q,\qquad
 W_j\in\frac{\mathbb Q[Y^{\pm1}]}{\Delta_K(Y)^{2j+1}},
 \qquad W_0=\Delta_K^{-1}.
\]
Its restriction to \(Y=(1-\delta)^L\) is the original reduced,
zero-framed color-\(L\) polynomial for every positive integer \(L\).
Thus its order-\(j\) color coefficient has degree at most \(j\);
the top degree is the corresponding Taylor coefficient of
\(\Delta_K^{-1}\). The full formal source is fixed by these restrictions
and satisfies each supplied actual generic color recurrence.
Rational loops and the perturbative degree bound are established
Melvin--Morton--Rozansky results; no novelty is claimed for them.
Here their proof starts from the same original source as the all-root
construction.

Consequently an actual normal-state annihilator with nonzero classical
symbol \(B_{\rm cl}\) satisfies \(B_{\rm cl}(Y,1)=0\): its symbol has the
abelian shift factor. At every simple Alexander root \(\alpha\),
\[
 \operatorname{Res}_{Y=\alpha}W_0(Y)\,dY
       =\frac1{\Delta_K'(\alpha)}\ne0.
\]
This is a known, nonzero datum in the actual \(q\to1\) source.
It must not be substituted for the fixed-level residue
\(F_N(M_*)/\Delta_K'(\alpha)\), where \(M_*^{2N}=\alpha\);
that numerator is separate data.

The source constructed here is formal in the quantum parameter.
No analytic continuation across the Alexander divisor, contribution
on the hyperbolic branch, or scalar lower bound follows from the
nonzero residue alone. The arbitrary-short-partial-filling theorem
and the finite-exception theorem remain open.

## An explicit finite response for the actual affine equation

The [coefficient response proof](research_coefficient_green_finite_response.md)
now makes the bounded-dimensional reduction unnormalized and explicit.
Choose a fixed actual rational-coefficient normal annihilator, and
write its regularized coefficient equation as
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^{w}p_j(q_N,Q_N^{k-j})c_{k-j}=\beta_{N,k},
 \qquad R_N(Y)=\sum_{k=-AN}^{AN}c_kY^k.
\]
The shifted source has support in \([0,w-1]\).
Solve forward only where \(p_0(q_N,Q_N^k)\ne0\).
At each zero pivot retain its coefficient as a free coordinate;
also retain the compatibility equation at that row.
Retain all \(w\) equations above the upper support endpoint.
This gives an exact system
\[
 C_N\xi=b_N^{\rm eff},\qquad
 K_N=\gamma_N+\lambda_N\xi,
\]
in bijection with the entire supported Laurent solution set.
Its number of unknowns is at most
\((2A+1)\operatorname{span}_T p_0\), independently of \(N\).
The construction covers empty pivot sets and \(w=0\).
No unknown complete value is used to normalize the system.

The closing is unique on this system exactly when
\(\lambda_N\ker C_N=0\). In that case the actual terminal dual
is any solution of \(g_NC_N=\lambda_N\), and exactly
\[
 K_N=\gamma_N+g_Nb_N^{\rm eff}.
\]
Uniqueness is not assumed for an arbitrary supplied operator.
The existing rank-one saturated-line certificate is one
sufficient condition; otherwise additional actual pointing
must remain.

For rational operator coefficients, the existing torsion theorem
also makes the indexing explicit. After finitely many levels,
every zero pivot has the form
\[
 k=\frac{h/t+n}{b}N-\frac{a}{2b}
\]
from a contained curve \(q^aZ^b=e^{2\pi ih/t}\).
Only finitely many \(n\) can lie in the original support.
Integrality is periodic in \(N\); after a further finite threshold,
their number and ordering are fixed on each congruence class.
No parity or composite levels are discarded.

The effective entries retain products over \(O(N)\) regular
steps. Neither their conditioning nor a nonzero leading closing
numerator follows from fixed matrix size or affine pivot locations.
The original polynomial bound on \(\beta_N\) likewise does not
bound its propagated effective forcing. This theorem supplies
the exact response whose geometric asymptotics are still needed;
it proves no new volume case or finite-exception conclusion.

\(\texttt{89bfbd7ce9648eca0a57b981d493baeeef0cf2f19676e6e508f2341a2e251c49}\).
Author, peer and root read its entire matching final and all three

## The positive meridian energy measures the regularized Green response

The new energy can be reduced to the original regularized period
without dividing pointwise at its dense ordinary-color zeros.
Write \(f_N=S_NR_N+P_N\), where
\(S_N=1+\cdots+Y^{N-1}\), and use the coefficient \(\ell^2\) norm.
The original width \(\operatorname{supp}f_N\subset[-AN,AN]\)
and \(\deg P_N\le N-2\) imply
\[
 \|f_N\|_2\le N\|R_N\|_2+\|P_N\|_2,\qquad
 \|R_N\|_2\le 2(2A+2)\|f_N-P_N\|_2.
\]
The first inequality is finite coefficient convolution.
For the second put \(g_N=f_N-P_N\) and retain the exact identity
\[
 (Y^N-1)R_N=(Y-1)g_N .
\]
In each residue class modulo \(N\), the coefficients of \(R_N\)
are prefix sums of those of the right side, with zero initial
value below the Laurent support. Each chain has at most \(2A+2\)
positions. The prefix-sum matrix has norm at most its length,
and multiplication by \(Y-1\) has coefficient norm at most two.
Summing the disjoint residue chains proves the estimate.

Since \(\|P_N\|_2\) is polynomially bounded, the uniform frame
therefore gives
\[
 \frac1N\log\max(1,\mathcal Q_N)
 -\frac2N\log\max(1,\|R_N\|_2)\longrightarrow0.
\]
The maxima are necessary: no nonzero regular remainder or
positive exponential rate is assumed for every knot.
This is an equality of the clipped growth measurements, not a
calculation of their value.

The estimate reduces calibration of this energy to the actual
regularized response
\(B(q_N,Y,T)R_N=\beta_N\), with its specified source and selected
homogeneous part. The already proved fixed support and polynomial
bound for \(\beta_N\) do not bound that response or its closing
overlap. No pointwise estimate of \(1/S_N\) at an ordinary node
is used. The derivation uses the entire matching actual
regularization \(\texttt{d7efc1e6}\) and uniform frame
\(\texttt{e3af9486}\), read in full by root and peer.

## A uniformly stable positive energy from the original quantum normals

The [uniform Hermite sampling proof](research_ordinary_orbit_uniform_hermite_frame.md)
strengthens the reconstruction below.
Fix the actual Laurent support bound \([-AN,AN]\) and
\(H=4A+1\). For every Laurent polynomial
\(f(Y)=\sum_{k=-AN}^{AN}a_kY^k\), let
\(\mathscr E_N=N^{-1}Y\partial_Y\) and
\(\zeta_l=e^{2\pi i l/N}\).
There are constants depending only on \(A\) such that
\[
 c_A N\sum_k|a_k|^2
 \le \sum_{l=1}^{N-1}\sum_{h=0}^{H-1}
                  |(\mathscr E_N^h f)(\zeta_l)|^2
 \le C_A N\sum_k|a_k|^2 .
\]
The complete node and all its derivatives are absent.
The estimate holds for every \(N\ge2\).

Fourier transformation splits the full sampling map into alias
Vandermonde blocks of fixed size. Pairing residue \(r\) with
\(r+\lfloor N/2\rfloor\) separates their frequency nodes uniformly,
including the larger zero-residue block. Their column spaces have
a uniform angle gap. This proves that deleting the complete sample
loses at most a fixed fraction of the full sampling energy.
It is stronger than injectivity or a growing polynomial bound
for an interpolation inverse.

The proof also gives an explicit recovery row for \(f(1)\).
It requires only inversion of a known \(H\)-by-\(H\) matrix and
has Euclidean norm bounded independently of \(N\).
The minimum possible norm is bounded above and below by positive
constants. The row is constructed without using \(f(1)\).

For the original knot source \(f_N\), define the genuine combinations
\[
 B_{h,l,N}=N^{-h}
 \sum_{r=0}^h(-1)^r\binom hr
 [\delta^h]C_{l+rN}
   \!\left(q_N(1-\delta)^{1/(2N)}\right),\qquad
 \mathcal Q_N=\sum_{l=1}^{N-1}\sum_{h=0}^{H-1}|B_{h,l,N}|^2.
\]
The exact Alexander product rule is a fixed triangular matrix,
with diagonal one, between these combinations and the sampled
meridian jets. Therefore
\[
 \mathcal Q_N\asymp_{K,A}N\sum_k|[Y^k]f_N|^2,\qquad
 K_N=\ell_N B_N,\qquad \|\ell_N\|\le C_{K,A}.
\]
In particular \( |K_N|^2\le C_{K,A}^2\mathcal Q_N\).
This is a specified positive inner product and Cauchy--Schwarz
bound for the actual source. None of the colors supplied in this
energy is divisible by \(N\); high colors and the signed finite
differences are retained.
There is no asserted equivalence with the norm of all raw
quantum-normal data before taking those differences.

Both remaining analytic requirements are explicit:
the geometric exponential rate of \(\mathcal Q_N\), and a
subexponential lower bound for the actual closing overlap
\[
 \frac{|K_N|}{\|\ell_N\|\sqrt{\mathcal Q_N}}.
\]
The frame proves neither. Its constants depend on the fixed
presentation and are not uniform over unbounded twist words.
The arbitrary-short-partial-filling and finite-exception theorems
remain open.

\(\texttt{e3af94860ab3b76d600547931fd0f542757639197c6b36704b26e56194e3ad6d}\).
Author, peer and root read the entire matching final and its sole
complete proof source \(\texttt{6c9c3089}\), with renewed matching

## Exact recovery from a bounded number of ordinary-orbit normal orders

The [omitted-node reconstruction](research_ordinary_orbit_jet_reconstruction.md)
gives an explicit general source for the remaining scalar estimate.
Fix a braid presentation. From its literal crossing entries and
the original pivot conversion, its reduced meridian numerator
\(f_N(Y)\), with \(f_N(1)=K_N\), has Laurent support in
\([-AN,AN]\) for a fixed integer \(A\).
Set \(H=4A+1\) and \(q(\delta)=q_N(1-\delta)^{1/(2N)}\).
There are fully specified coefficients such that
\[
 K_N=\sum_{L=1}^{N-1}\sum_{h=0}^{H-1}\sum_{r=0}^h
 w_{L,h,r,N}\,[\delta^h]C_{L+rN}(q(\delta)),
 \qquad
 \sum_{L,h,r}|w_{L,h,r,N}|\le C N^H.
\]
The largest normal order is independent of \(N\).
None of the supplied colors is a multiple of \(N\).
The colors with \(r\ge1\) are genuine higher colors in ordinary
residue classes, rather than the polynomially bounded colors
strictly below \(N\).

The proof first applies the residue theorem to the original numerator:
\[
 \omega_N=
 \frac{Y^{AN}f_N(Y)}{(Y-1)S_N(Y)^H}\,dY,\qquad
 S_N(Y)=\frac{Y^N-1}{Y-1}.
\]
There is no pole at zero and no residue at infinity.
Its complete residue is \(K_N/N^H\), so all the other residues
recover that value. Each uses at most \(H-1\) ordinary-point
meridian derivatives. The local coordinate
\(Y=Q_N^L e^{t/N}\) bounds the resulting coefficients uniformly
without inverting a growing Vandermonde matrix.

Every derivative is then replaced by an exact genuine-color identity.
Writing \(g_N=f_N/\Delta_K(Y^N)\), one has
\[
 (Y\partial_Y)^h g_N(Q_N^L)
 =\sum_{r=0}^h(-1)^r\binom hr
            [\delta^h]C_{L+rN}(q(\delta)).
\]
This follows from the original integral-color curve
\(Y=Q_N^L(1-\delta)^{r+L/N}\).
The product rule restores all derivatives of the Alexander
factor; it is not replaced by its value one before differentiation.
The total weight at normal order \(h\) is \(O(N^{H-h})\).

The \(h=0\) portion has polynomial size by the actual ordinary-color
bound. The higher-order portion is a complex signed row whose
noncancellation still needs proof. The existing positive Fourier
norm sees the zero-jets and the unknown complete value; it does not
bound this higher-normal row from below.
This theorem therefore locates the missing data in finitely many
normal orders of the same source, without proving a new volume case
or the arbitrary-short-partial-filling theorem.

The final proof is fixed at
\(\texttt{6c9c3089b93204ae6b7045265ece6deac1552563de806dae3810392c239c028d}\).
Author, peer and root read its entire matching final and all three
complete proof sources: \(\texttt{b1148936}\),
\(\texttt{46e984e3}\), and \(\texttt{d7efc1e6}\), with renewed
matching hashes. Derivative recovery and color-to-ADO recovery
have prior statement-level coverage in Murakami and Willetts;
no broad novelty is claimed for those principles or Hermite interpolation.

The ordinary-node divisor must also be retained when using this row
in a geometric asymptotic. In the actual decomposition
\(f_N=S_NR_N+P_N\), the polynomial \(P_N\) has controlled size.
The same residue calculation, applied to the regular part, gives
\[
 N R_N(1)=
 -N^{H-1}\sum_{L=1}^{N-1}\sum_{a=0}^{H-2}
 \frac{b^{\rm reg}_{H-2-a,N}(\zeta_L)}{a!}
                 (\mathscr E_N^a R_N)(\zeta_L),
 \qquad \mathscr E_N=N^{-1}Y\partial_Y,
\]
where
\[
 b^{\rm reg}_{j,N}(\zeta)=[t^j]\,
 e^{At}\zeta e^{t/N}(\zeta e^{t/N}-1)^{H-2}
                    \left(\frac{t}{e^t-1}\right)^{H-1}.
\]
The omitted part is exactly \(P_N(1)\), rather than a discarded
error from the residue calculation.
This is a direct consequence of the full matching reconstruction
\(\texttt{6c9c3089}\) and actual regularization
\(\texttt{d7efc1e6}\), read in full by root and peer.

The bulk symbol of this specified row can be computed explicitly.
If a supplied regularized local jet at \(\zeta_N\to\zeta\ne1\)
has normalized profile \(e^{\kappa t}\), its leading local
multiplier, after the displayed \(N^{H-1}\), is
\[
 -\zeta(\zeta-1)^{H-2}
                    \binom{A+\kappa-1}{H-2}.
\]
Indeed, for every nonnegative integer \(d\), the change of variable
\(z=e^t-1\) gives the exact identity
\[
 [t^d]e^{ut}\left(\frac{t}{e^t-1}\right)^{d+1}
                         =\binom{u-1}{d}.
\]
This computes the row's symbol; it asserts neither that an actual
geometric jet has the assumed profile nor that its slope meets
the displayed zero divisor. In particular the bulk formula cannot
be applied to nodes approaching the complete point without a
uniform edge argument. A smooth nonvanishing WKB ansatz for the
unregularized \(f_N\) across ordinary nodes would omit its exact
\(S_N\) factor. The reconstruction does not remove the need to
initialize the original regularized geometric contribution.

## A coefficient bound with type of order N log N

The [scaled-meridian proof](research_scaled_root_verma_polynomial_gevrey_type.md)
improves the level dependence of the estimate below.
For a fixed braid presentation of any knot, let \(k=x_0^N\)
stay in a fixed compact subset of \(\mathbb C^*\) on which
\(\Delta_K(k^2)\ne0\).
For both fixed-\(x\) and fixed original meridian
\(M=-q_Nx_0\) normals, the actual rationally continued source satisfies
\[
 |V_{N,j}(x_0,1)|
 \le C_0N^A e^{BN}
            \bigl(C_1N\log(eN)\bigr)^j j!.
\]
Here \(j\) is the order in \(\delta=1-q^{2N}\).
The constants are independent of \(N,j\) and of the choice
of the root \(x_0\); their complete formulas depend only on
the fixed word, the compact set and its explicit determinant
minimum. At the complete original meridian, take
\(x_0=-q_N^{-1}\), so \(k\in\{1,-1\}\) and that minimum is one.
This source estimate imposes no long-twist or Conway restriction.

The proof groups each full color product into cycles of length
\(N\). Choose the root factor nearest to zero. Its size is
\(O(N^{-1})\); the product of all other root factors is a
geometric sum of size \(O(N)\).
Their perturbations are controlled by the elementary reciprocal
root-distance sum \(O(N\log(eN))\).
Thus a complete cycle has a bounded product, even at an exact
root zero. The Gaussian factorial quotient retains its head
factors and every carry. Both crossing signs are estimated
directly from their actual finite-sector entries.

For a sector of total index \(T\), Cauchy's estimate is applied
on
\[
 |\delta|\le
 \frac{\rho}{N\log(eN)(T/N+1)}.
\]
The resulting coefficient bounds can be summed on a moving
grading circle \(|\tau|=\exp(-s/N)\).
The exact numerator degree is \(O(N(j+1))\), so continuation
from that circle to \(\tau=1\) costs \(\exp(O(j+1))\).
Using a fixed small grading circle was the source of the
earlier exponential-in-\(N\) loss in the Gevrey type.

The Borel transform therefore has a guaranteed local disk
of radius \((C_1N\log(eN))^{-1}\).
There is still no remainder estimate for a summation representing
the original period at grading one, no global Borel continuation
and no nonzero geometric coefficient.
In particular, the prefactor \(e^{BN}\) has not been related to
hyperbolic volume. At the complete point the order-zero coefficient
already equals \(K_N\); its precise exponential rate is not
determined by this upper bound.

## Explicit factorial coefficient bounds for the same completion

The [source estimate](research_all_root_verma_gevrey_bound.md)
now supplies analytic bounds for the canonical completion below.
It estimates the actual signed Verma word, ordinary pivot and
framing. It does not replace the source by a positive model.

Write \(V_{N,j}(x,\tau)\) for its coefficient of
\(\delta^j\), where \(\delta=1-q^{2N}\), \(x\) is the Verma
meridian coordinate and \(\tau\) records the total closed index.
On a compact annulus in \(x\), there is an explicit small disk
\(|\tau|\le t_0\) on which
\[
 |V_{N,j}(x,\tau)|\le K_0K_1^j j!,
\]
with \(K_0,K_1,t_0\) independent of \(N\).
For total index \(T\), the original finite sector is estimated
on the disk \(|\delta|\le\rho/(T+1)\).
The Gaussian polynomials, both signed crossings and the varying
pivot give an exponential bound in \(T\).
Cauchy's estimate then costs \((T+1)^j\); summing this against
the small grading weight gives the factorial bound.

The exact rational continuation has denominator
\(D_N(x,\tau)^{2j+1}\). Its numerator has grading degree at most
\[
 (b-1)(N-1)+2jN(b-1).
\]
Polynomial continuation therefore gives, on any specified compact
set avoiding the determinant zeros,
\[
 |V_{N,j}|\le \mathcal K_N\mathcal C_N^j j!,
\]
with explicit constants depending only on the word, parameter
bounds and the actual minimum of \(|D_N|\) on that set.
There is a separate proof for normals at fixed original meridian
\(M=-qx\), or fixed \(Y=M^2\); holding \(x\) fixed is not silently
identified with either of these paths.

Consequently the Borel series
\(\sum_j V_{N,j}\xi^j/j!\) is locally holomorphic at every fixed
level. At the complete meridian, \(D_N(x_*,\tau)=1\), but the
proved continuation cost still permits
\(\mathcal C_N=\exp(O(N))\).
This is a bound on the certified Borel germ, not a statement
that the actual radius has that decay. It proves neither
continuation along a ray nor a Laplace formula for the source.
In particular it gives no uniform remainder at the geometric
scale and no nonzero geometric contribution.

Gevrey regularity for knot quantum series has prior coverage in
Garoufalidis--Lê, [arXiv:math/0609618](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609618),
Theorems 5--7. The present estimate is proved directly for the
specified source and records its parameter and level dependence.
No general novelty claim for Gevrey regularity is made.

## A canonical completion of the original period at every root

The [all-root Verma proof](research_all_root_verma_normal_rationality.md)
now extends the original untruncated source beyond its root value.
Fix \(N\ge2\), let \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\), and put
\[
 \delta=1-q^{2N},\qquad q=q_N(1-\delta)^{1/(2N)},\qquad
 Y=M^2 .
\]
Write \(\Delta_K(t)\) for the symmetric Alexander polynomial with
\(\Delta_K(1)=1\), and \(\mathfrak F_{N,K}(Y)\) for the actual
reduced whole meridian state. There is a canonically specified
formal period
\[
 \mathcal W_{N,K}(\delta,Y)
   =\sum_{j\ge0}
       \frac{P_{N,j}(Y)}{\Delta_K(Y^N)^{2j+1}}\,\delta^j,
 \qquad P_{N,j}\in\mathbb Q(q_N)[Y^{\pm1}],
\]
whose constant term is exactly
\[
 \mathcal W_{N,K}(0,Y)
   =\frac{\mathfrak F_{N,K}(Y)}{\Delta_K(Y^N)},\qquad
 \mathfrak F_{N,K}(1)=K_N(K).
\]
This uses the original reduced source and its ordinary pivot,
framing, and meridian path. It introduces no unknown scalar
normalization. The series is formal in \(\delta\); convergence
has not been proved.

The construction retains the same graded infinite Verma trace.
At order \(j\), an upward residue carry costs at least one normal
order. In a closed head path, upward and downward carries
balance, so all surviving carry cycles have a finite budget.
Every such contribution is a polynomial differential insertion
of order at most \(2j\) in the classical Frobenius variables,
followed by the original linear Burau substitution.
The first-block-zero projector and the original graded trace
are retained. Their trace is a finite combination of at most
\(2j\) derivatives of a determinant inverse. This gives
the power \(2j+1\), without inverting the deleted Burau matrix.
All other apparent meridian poles cancel because every coefficient
of the original grading series is Laurent polynomial in the meridian.

There is an exact comparison with actual finite-color quantum
normals, rather than only root values. In the genuine integral
color \(L\), the Verma tail of indices at least \(L\) is invariant.
A high-index flag cannot disappear along either signed crossing.
The knot has one component, so such a flag would eventually reach
the open highest index zero. Thus no contributing path enters
the tail, even before taking the root or its normal coefficients.
On the color \(NR\) curve this gives
\[
 \mathcal W_{N,K}\bigl(\delta,(1-\delta)^R\bigr)
   =\mathcal C_{NR}\!\left(q_N(1-\delta)^{1/(2N)}\right)
                      \quad(R=1,2,\ldots),
\]
as formal series, where \(\mathcal C_n(q)\) is the original
ordinary reduced zero-framed color function. In particular its
order-\(j\) coefficient is a single polynomial in \(R\) of
degree at most \(j\). It is determined by \(R=1,\ldots,j+1\).
Its coefficient of \(R^j\) is exactly
\[
 \frac{(-1)^j}{j!}(Y\partial_Y)^j
       \left.\frac{\mathfrak F_{N,K}(Y)}
                         {\Delta_K(Y^N)}\right|_{Y=1}.
\]
No nonzero lower bound for this coefficient is asserted.

The full completion is presentation independent. In logarithmic
coordinates, the integral colors give infinitely many distinct
lines through the same point. A homogeneous Taylor coefficient
restricts to a polynomial in the line's slope; its vanishing at
all those slopes forces it to vanish identically. Rationality
then recovers the entire meridian coefficient from that germ.
The same argument, using odd \(R\) to retain the original
meridian lift, proves that every supplied actual generic color
annihilator acts on this completion. No evenness assumption on
the operator coefficients is used.

All-root loop existence and recurrence compatibility have prior
statement-level coverage in Garoufalidis--Wheeler,
[arXiv:2603.01619](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01619),
Theorem 1.3 and Corollaries 1.5 and 1.9. Their statements were
checked for coverage; their proofs are not premises here.
The contribution to these notes is the independent proof for
the literal graded source, with its determinant exponent, all
carry cycles, finite-color normal restrictions and exact pointing.
No novelty is claimed for the general existence statement.

## A perturbative degree constraint on the actual source

The [direct degree proof](research_actual_perturbative_color_degree_and_wall_test.md)
makes an additional necessary source condition explicit:
\[
 C_j(e^h)=\sum_{n\ge0}p_n(j)h^n,\qquad \deg_jp_n\le2n.
\]
This is the weak perturbative bound, not the stronger
Melvin--Morton assertion. At order \(h^n\), each original
unpermuted crossing has total generator degree at most \(2n\).
PBW straightening, inverse crossings and the actual pivots preserve
that budget. The knot's one-cycle cut contracts tensor words to
one ordered product, without a separate dimension trace.
Its highest-weight entry and the original framing correction
therefore give the displayed bound for every integral color.

For the multiplicative wall modification in the bounded-normal
source note, the limiting multiplier is exactly
\[
 H_{J,m}(j)=
 \left[1-\prod_{r=1}^J\left(1-\frac{j^2}{r^2}\right)\right]^m,
 \qquad \deg H_{J,m}=2Jm.
\]
If \(p_k\) is the first nonzero coefficient of \(C_j-1\) and
\(d=\deg p_k\), the modified first coefficient has degree
\(d+2Jm\). Thus \(d+2Jm>2k\) excludes that modification
as the color family of a knot. This repairs an omission in the
list of structural constraints tested against that construction.
It does not negate its stated algebraic properties or exclude
an affine modification matched to perturbative data.

sources: original cut polynomiality \(\texttt{d471549b}\) and
bounded-normal source \(\texttt{6a464af6}\), with matching hashes.

## Finite perturbative agreement does not fix the complete growth

The [regular affine construction](research_loop_regular_source_wall_surgery.md)
shows why the preceding degree constraint does not supply source
rigidity. It uses the already proved actual figure-eight Newton
family as a seed, to test a proposed general inference. It is not
another knot-volume case or a claim about a new knot invariant.

For every prescribed finite color prefix \(1\le j\le J\), loop
order \(b\), and meridian normal depth \(m\), there are fixed
integer Laurent polynomials defining
\[
 \widetilde F_N(Y)
   =H(Y+Y^{-1}-2)F_N(Y)+P(Q_N,Y+Y^{-1}),\qquad
 H(z)=(1-(1-z)^L)^m,\quad L\ge2b+1.
\]
The generic colors are changed by the same affine formula.
They remain integral Laurent polynomials, retain that entire
generic-color prefix exactly, and retain the original loop
expansion through order \(b\), including its Alexander diagonal.
At every further order \(n\), the loop coefficient still has
integer numerator and denominator dividing \((1-z)^{2n+1}\).
The perturbative degree bound, Weyl symmetry, ordinary root-value
bounds, and every fixed jet in the actual tame initial color
window also survive.

The interpolation is integral even though all color nodes coalesce.
Write \(\varepsilon=Q-1\) and
\[
 B_J=\prod_{j=1}^J(z-\delta_j(\varepsilon)),\qquad
 \delta_j=Q^j+Q^{-j}-2=O(\varepsilon^2).
\]
In the free quotient over \(\mathbb Z[[\varepsilon]]\),
\(z^J\in\varepsilon^2\mathscr A\). Reduction of a bivariate
formal series therefore converges and preserves its
\(\varepsilon\)-order. The Newton series reduces to its exact
finite prefix. Taking a monic polynomial remainder corrects the
prefix without losing any of the prescribed loop orders; no
loss depending on \(J\) is necessary. The proof also reconstructs
all integral rational loop coefficients of the seed directly
from its Newton sum, without an imported rationality theorem.

Nevertheless the complete values and the first retained large
normal are exactly
\[
 \widetilde F_N(1)=P(Q_N,2)\longrightarrow1,\qquad
 [(Y-1)^{2m}](\widetilde F_N-P)
                   =L^mF_N(1).
\]
The seed's positive complete exponent has moved to a higher
meridian derivative while its new complete exponent is zero.
The construction also has integral Newton coefficients.
It does not retain the full original quantum operator, all
perturbative coefficients simultaneously, or the prescribed
complete observation. On the open set where \(H\ne0\), rational
gauge transport retains the geometric characteristic factor;
that does not supply a comparison at \(Y=1\).

This identifies a concrete requirement for a useful torsor
comparison: it must preserve the selected complete source,
including its boundary lattice. A fixed scalar rational
normalization \(UF+V\) does preserve any positive complete
exponent when \(U(Q,1)\not\equiv0\); its value, inverse, and
the additive term have only polynomial cost along \(Q_N\).
Here \(H\) vanishes identically along \(Y=1\), so that condition
fails despite regularity at \((Q,Y)=(1,1)\). Arbitrary
level-dependent matrix units are not covered by this scalar
normalization statement.

## The actual terminal adjoint and a conserved color-cut pairing

The [pointed adjoint proof](research_pointed_main_color_adjoint_cut_flux.md)
now gives a Green identity for the original main-color recurrence,
including its full bounded-jet repair at singular steps. Write its
scaled finite system as
\[
 M_Ny=b_N,\qquad
 M_N=\begin{pmatrix}I_0\\H\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 b_N=\begin{pmatrix}b^{\rm in}\\0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \ell_Ny=Z_N=\langle K\rangle_N .
\]
Here \(I_0\) prescribes the fixed small-color jets, and \(\ell_N\)
selects the constant jet at the complete color. The existing
kernel-annihilation theorem implies that the terminal adjoint equation
\[
 M_N^*p_N=\ell_N^*
\]
is solvable even when higher jets are not unique. Its solutions form
an affine space over \(\ker M_N^*\). Every solution satisfies
\(p_N^*b_N=Z_N\); no unknown value is supplied in defining this
adjoint equation.

Write \(p_N=(\alpha,v)\) and
\((Hy)_j=\sum_{i=0}^d A_i(j)y_{j+i}\). At a color cut \(c\) define
\[
 \mathcal W_c=\sum_{j\le c<j+i}v_j^*A_i(j)y_{j+i},
\]
with the original recurrence ranges retained. Its change at an
initial color is \(\alpha_c^*b_c^{\rm in}\), its terminal change is
\(-Z_N\), and it is constant elsewhere. Consequently
\(\mathcal W_c=Z_N\) at every cut between the initial packet and
the complete color. Each pairing uses only a fixed number of blocks,
but includes every retained normal component.

Geometric weighting preserves this identity term by term: columns
are multiplied by \(w_j\), recurrence rows by \(w_j\), and adjoint
rows by \(w_j^{-1}\). If the weighted adjoint is instead assigned
an unscaled unit terminal source, its flux is \(w_NZ_N\).
The recovery factor \(w_N^{-1}\) must remain in any growth estimate.

This separates the required dual from the positive-energy row.
The latter equals the weighted initial source, has zero recurrence
component and zero cut flux, and does not solve the terminal adjoint
equation. Energy positivity therefore supplies no lower bound for
the conserved complex pairing. The new identity retains the correct
two boundary data; their geometric connection and exponential rate
remain unproved. It yields no new filling class.

## What the positive determinant terms retain

The [termwise minor calculation](research_pointed_gram_termwise_source_minors.md)
tests whether coefficient positivity supplies a different route to
the lower bound. For the actual pointed matrix let
\(r=\operatorname{rank}M_N=n-\nu\), where \(\nu\le B\) is
bounded independently of the level. Choose row and column sets
\(J,S\) of size \(r\), and let \(R_k\) select an original
constant color. Set
\[
 \Delta_{J,S}=\det(M_N)_{J,S},\qquad
 T_{J,S,k}=
 \det\begin{pmatrix}(M_N)_{J,S}&(b_N)_J\\R_{k,S}&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Consistency and \(\ker M_N\subset\ker R_N\) give the exact
termwise identity
\[
 T_{J,S,k}=-C_k(q_N)\Delta_{J,S}.
\]
If the selected full rows are independent, they span the row space
and permit subtraction of the observation row. If they are
dependent, adjoining the consistent source preserves that dependence,
so both determinants vanish. Thus the formula includes every term,
not just an invertible selected submatrix.

The positive coefficient expansion is precisely
\[
 q_\nu=\sum_{J,S}|\Delta_{J,S}|^2,\qquad
 d_\nu=\sum_k\sum_{J,S}|T_{J,S,k}|^2 .
\]
There are at most \(\binom n\nu^2\le n^{2B}\) denominator terms
and at most \(n^{2B+1}\) numerator terms. In particular a largest
denominator minor has at least a polynomial fraction of the
denominator mass. A nonzero denominator minor retains every
constant-jet column; only normal coordinates can be omitted.

For any selected family \(\mathcal F_N\),
\[
 \frac{\sum_{\mathcal F_N}|T_{J,S,N}|^2}{q_\nu}
   =\theta_N|\langle K\rangle_N|^2,\qquad 0\le\theta_N\le1.
\]
For a largest denominator minor, \(\theta_N\ge n^{-2B}\).
The original terminal scalar is therefore present in each positive
term. Controlling denominator mass alone supplies no terminal lower
bound; the source border must also be estimated. Ordinary-color
terms together have only polynomial size. A separate triangular
evaluation or geometric estimate of a bordered minor remains a
valid possible route, but has not been proved here.

## Exact continuous filling needs growing differential complexity

The [rank/width proof](research_continuous_filling_rank_fourier_width.md)
treats the actual scalar \(Z_N(s)=\phi_N(R_s)\), where \(R_s\)
is the original full-Hermite Gaussian interpolation, agreeing
with every signed integer power. With \(m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\),
\[
 Z_N(s)=\sum_{a<m}e^{is\omega_a}(A_a+isB_a)
          +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}e^{is\omega_m},\qquad
 B_a=\eta(4-c_a^2)\gamma_a\ne0 .
\]
After its prescribed scalar dephasing, its frequency exponents
in \(t=e^{\pi is/N}\) are exactly \(f(a)=a(a-D)\).
Their early consecutive gaps are \(N-2a-2\).

Suppose a nonzero exact differential annihilator has normal form
\[
 \sum_{|k|\le B}t^kP_{k,N}(\partial_s)
\]
of order \(r\). The coefficient polynomials may depend arbitrarily
on \(N\). Put \(K=\max(m-B-1,0)\). The first \(K\) shifted
frequencies are isolated from every other shifted source
frequency. Each forces both \(P_{k,N}(\mu_a)=0\) and
\(P'_{k,N}(\mu_a)=0\), since its actual source coefficient
has a nonzero linear term in \(s\). Hence
\[
 r\ge2K,\qquad r+2B\ge2m-2 .
\]
At width zero the exact minimal order for this particular
constant spectator is \(N\).

More generally allow \(P_{k,N}(s,\partial_s)\) to have rational
coefficients in \(s\), and measure \(B\) after a chosen common
denominator clearing in \(s,t\). Frequency isolation still makes
each nonzero differential block annihilate \(K\) independent
actual exponential-polynomial functions. The solution dimension
at an ordinary regular point gives
\[
 r\ge K,\qquad r+B\ge m-1 .
\]
Arbitrary meromorphic coefficients hiding additional exponentials
are not included. All assertions concern identities of the
specified analytic continuous-filling family. They do not constrain
a main-color quantum difference equation, a system whose cleared
width grows with \(N\), or a proved asymptotic geometric quotient.

This closes a specific proposed shortcut, rather than providing
a new lower bound. The exact source still has to be transported
in a geometry-weighted class with its actual co-source and
boundary currents.

## The actual even complete row on the whole fixed slit domain

The [relative slit theorem](research_even_complete_low_slit_relative_transport.md)
removes the half-plane restriction for the even complete low row.
For \(N=2m\), let \(J=m-1\), \(\Omega=\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\),
and retain the actual polynomials
\[
 F_{j,N}(w)=K_N(c_j,w),\qquad
 L_N(w)=\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}e_k(-2)e_k(w).
\]
For every fixed compact \(\mathcal K\Subset\Omega\),
\[
 \frac{L_N(w)}{F_{J,N}(w)}=1+O_{\mathcal K}(N^{-1/2}).
\]
Every fixed ordinary derivative of the error has the same bound on
compact subsets. Consequently \(L_N\) is nonzero there for all
sufficiently large even levels. With the logarithm normalized by
positivity at \(-2\),
\[
 \frac1N\log L_N(w)\longrightarrow
 \widehat\Psi(w)=\int_0^{1/2}
 2\operatorname{arsinh}\left(
       \frac{\sqrt{2-w}}2\cot(\pi s)\right)\,ds
\]
locally uniformly, with every fixed derivative. The complete angular
normalization is \(\widehat\Psi(-2\cos t)=\Psi(t)\).

The proof starts from the actual bulk row ratio, rather than an
assumed growing solution. It transports the ratio to a layer of
width \(A\sqrt N\). There an exact normalization of the Riccati
recurrence has a fixed disk on which its derivative has modulus at
most one; the total displacement of the disk center is
\(O_A(N^{-1/2})\). These estimates reach the last physical row.
The original alternating interpolation formula then gives the
displayed relative error by Abel summation. Earlier rows are
exponentially smaller by the already proved all-row slit logarithms.

This controls the actual low row on fixed complex paths whose real
part can exceed two, provided they avoid the removed ray. It gives
only \(o(N)\) logarithmic error on general slit compacts. No finite-level
zero-location theorem, shrinking-cut estimate, or full-kernel radical
bound is asserted. An exact local logarithmic phase can now be
recentered at its own nearby saddle; occurrence and domination of
that saddle in a given original contour still require proof.

## Holomorphic representatives and an exact phase-weighted Hilbert model

The [Bergman jet-quotient proof](research_bergman_jet_quotient_phase_transport.md)
replaces a formal choice of representatives by a precise Hilbert
construction on the original finite algebra. Fix \(R>2\) and
\[
 D=\{z:|z|<R\}\setminus[2,R).
\]
Here \(N\ge2\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(\eta=(-1)^{N-1}\), and
the one-variable algebra is
\(\mathbb C[z]/(P_N)\), \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\).
All distinct physical nodes lie in \(D\), with distance to its
boundary at least \(c_RN^{-2}\). Let \(J\) collect every original
double-node value and first derivative and the odd simple value.
For several traced variables use the full mixed tensor jets.
Only these traced variables are quotiented; ordinary exterior
parameters remain ordinary.

For a holomorphic phase \(\Phi\) on \(D^s\), define
\[
 \|f\|_{\Phi,N}^2=
       \int_{D^s}|f|^2e^{-2N\Re\Phi}\,dV,\qquad
 |a|_{\Phi,N}=
       \inf_{Jf=a}\|f\|_{\Phi,N}.
\]
The functions with zero full jets form a holomorphic vanishing
ideal. Its intersection with this weighted space is a closed
Hilbert subspace. Multiplication by \(e^{-N\Phi}\) is an onto
isometry to unweighted Bergman space. Hermite interpolation after
this gauge proves that \(J\) is onto, even if the weight itself
is unbounded. Thus every original full jet class has a unique
least-norm representative.
Write \(\mathcal Q_{\Phi,N}\) for the full tensor jet algebra
with this quotient norm.

Let \(G_0=JJ^*\), \(S_0=J^*G_0^{-1}\) and \(P_0=S_0J\) in
unweighted Bergman space, and let \(\Gamma_\Phi\) be multiplication
by \(J(e^{N\Phi})\) on the finite jet algebra. The exact formulas are
\[
 S_\Phi a=e^{N\Phi}S_0\Gamma_\Phi^{-1}a,\qquad
 P_\Phi f=e^{N\Phi}P_0(e^{-N\Phi}f),\qquad JP_\Phi f=Jf,
\]
\[
 G_\Phi=\Gamma_\Phi G_0\Gamma_\Phi^*,\qquad
 |a|_{\Phi,N}^2=a^*G_\Phi^{-1}a .
\]
In particular the projection has norm one and preserves the
actual physical jets, rather than merely projecting to a
polynomial band with changed data. The finite section formula
also proves holomorphic dependence on every ordinary exterior
parameter, despite the Hermitian norm's parameter dependence.
Unbounded products are not presumed to stay in the Hilbert
space; products preserve jets whenever the stated integrability
or bounded-multiplier hypothesis is satisfied.

The squared inverse cosine
\(\tau(z)=\arccos(-z/2)^2\) is holomorphic on this slit domain,
including the removable fold at \(-2\). Put
\[
 \theta_n(z)=\frac{in}{4\pi}\tau(z),\qquad
 m_{n,N}(z)=\chi_N^n e^{N\theta_n(z)},\qquad
 \chi_N=q^{(N-1)^2/4},\qquad \kappa_N=q^{(N-1)^2/2}.
\]
This holomorphic function has exactly the full original
\(R^n\) values and first derivatives:
\[
 m_{n,N}(c_a)=\kappa_N^n(-1)^{na}q^{na(a+1)},\qquad
 \frac{m_{n,N}'(c_a)}{m_{n,N}(c_a)}
       =\frac{in(N-1-2a)}{4\sin((2a+1)\pi/N)}.
\]
At the odd simple node only its value is required. Hence every
signed physical crossing acts as an exact isometry
\[
 M_{R^n}:\mathcal Q_{\Phi,N}\longrightarrow
               \mathcal Q_{\Phi+\theta_n,N}.
\]
The same holds for joint phases and all signed powers in several
variables. The metrics change in this statement. Original Jordan
blocks have not been made unitary in a single fixed positive
metric, and the Gaussian is not asserted to equal the canonical
polynomial away from its jets.

For the unchanged original closing row \(\ell\), all normal and
cross terms are retained in the exact dual formula
\[
 \|\ell\|_{\Phi,N,*}^2=\ell G_\Phi\ell^*,\qquad
 |\ell(a)|^2\le
           (a^*G_\Phi^{-1}a)(\ell G_\Phi\ell^*).
\]
The unweighted Gram entries are mixed derivatives of the
Bergman kernel at the physical nodes. The row includes the
original residue functional
\[
 \phi_N(f)=\eta\sum_a\{(4-c_a^2)f'(c_a)-c_af(c_a)\}
                +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}f(-2).
\]
Transporting both the source and the inverse-dual row preserves
their scalar exactly. Holding the prescribed closing fixed at a
new filling instead leaves its phase-dependent dual norm to be
estimated. The twist isometry does not remove that dependence.

The mean-value inequality and Cauchy's formula give polynomial
evaluation costs for \(e^{-N\Phi}f\), including all mixed normals:
\[
 |\partial^\alpha(e^{-N\Phi}f)(c)|
       \le C_{\alpha,s,R}N^{2|\alpha|+2s}\|f\|_{\Phi,N}.
\]
Ordinary derivative bounds additionally contain phase derivatives.
For the displayed crossing phases those have polynomial size at
the nodes. Such a bound is not asserted for an arbitrary
holomorphic phase with uncontrolled boundary derivatives.

The source compiler remains exact on the least-norm ranges:
an original finite operation \(A\) is represented as \(S_\Psi AJ\),
and \(JS_\Phi=I\) makes compositions exact. Estimates for a
general turn or for these compositions do not follow from this
identity. Nor does the construction assemble separately repaired
windows into a globally controlled representative. Its new role
is a defined phase-dependent space for the original source and
closing, with exact signed-crossing transport and an explicit
weighted Cauchy inequality. Their geometric norm bounds and the
nonzero scalar coefficient remain to be proved.

### Exponentially small matching transport in every phase norm

The quotient construction has an immediate additional consequence
for the analytic matching lift. Use only the full mixed jets on
the selected product of physical windows, denoting this map by
\(J_{\mathcal I}\). The same gauge and Hermite argument defines
its least-norm quotient. Its dimension is the product, over traced
variables, of twice the number of selected double nodes plus the
number of selected simple nodes.

Take the windows bounded away from \(c=2\) and sufficiently short
as in the analytic lift theorem. Choose its buffered polydisk to
contain the fixed bounded Bergman domain. Its genuine analytic
factors have
\[
 J_{\mathcal I}\mathcal U_N=U_{\mathcal I},\qquad
 J_{\mathcal I}\mathcal V_N=U_{\mathcal I}^{-1},\qquad
 \|\mathcal U_N-1\|_\infty,\|\mathcal V_N-1\|_\infty
                      \le\delta_N=Ce^{-\gamma N}.
\]
The bounded-multiplier estimate above, applied with no phase
increment, therefore gives
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|M_{U_{\mathcal I}}^{\pm1}-I\|_{\Phi,J_{\mathcal I}}
                             \le\delta_N .
 \quad}
\]
The constants are independent of every holomorphic phase \(\Phi\),
including joint or level-dependent phases. This assertion is
fiberwise; keep the windows fixed when using holomorphic exterior
parameter dependence.

For the exact original window source
\(F_{\mathcal I}=U_{\mathcal I}F_{<,\mathcal I}\), it follows that
\[
 \|F_{\mathcal I}-F_{<,\mathcal I}\|_\Phi
            \le\delta_N\|F_{<,\mathcal I}\|_\Phi,\qquad
 \|\ell_{\mathcal I}M_{U_{\mathcal I}}^{\pm1}
                      -\ell_{\mathcal I}\|_{\Phi,*}
            \le\delta_N\|\ell_{\mathcal I}\|_{\Phi,*}.
\]
The reciprocal source estimate also holds. Every original
attachment, signed power and mixed normal remains in these
classes. The scalar consequence is still only
\[
 |\ell_{\mathcal I}(F_{\mathcal I})
                  -\ell_{\mathcal I}(F_{<,\mathcal I})|
 \le\delta_N\|\ell_{\mathcal I}\|_{\Phi,*}
                         \|F_{<,\mathcal I}\|_\Phi .
\]
It is not a relative estimate for a possibly canceled scalar.
No assignment outside the windows has been controlled.
This corollary follows from the two exact jet identities and a
bounded multiplier, without transferring a canonical off-grid
polynomial estimate or changing the observation.

## The exact Rivin source and its angle optimization

### Coverage of quiver coordinates for closed arborescent sources

A coverage check found a relevant existing framework:
Stošić and Wedrich,
[*Tangle addition and the knots-quivers correspondence*](https://arxiv.org/html/2004.10837),
Eq. (1), Definition 2.1 and Corollary 1.2, claim quiver expressions
for all arborescent links. This check concerns their statements and
definitions; their proof is not assumed here. Their column-colored
HOMFLY convention also needs its stated conversion before comparison
with the original symmetric-color Jones/Newton source.

There is an elementary definition-level comparison. For a symmetric
integer matrix \(C\), put \(Q=q^2\) and
\[
 Z_C(\mathbf x)=\sum_{\mathbf d\ge0}
       \frac{(-q)^{\mathbf d^{\mathsf T}C\mathbf d}
                    \mathbf x^{\mathbf d}}
            {\prod_i(Q;Q)_{d_i}} .
\]
Let \(y_i\) multiply \(x_i\) by \(Q\). The ratio of consecutive
coefficients proves directly
\[
 H_iZ_C=0,\qquad
 H_i=1-y_i-(-q)^{C_{ii}}x_i\prod_jy_j^{C_{ij}}.
\]
For \(i\ne j\), the last monomials commute because
\(C_{ij}=C_{ji}\); each also commutes with the other \(y_i\).
Thus the displayed \(H_i\) commute. No theorem from the paper
is needed for these coefficient identities.

At a primitive \(N\)-th root of \(Q\), first truncate to total degree
below \(N\). Every denominator is then nonzero, and
\((Q;Q)_{N-1}=N\). If \(Z_{N-1}\) denotes the homogeneous top
part, the actual finite source has the endpoint equation
\[
 H_i Z_{<N}
 =-(-q)^{C_{ii}}x_i
                   \left(\prod_jy_j^{C_{ij}}\right)Z_{N-1}.
\]
Indeed all lower coefficients cancel as before; only the degree-\(N\)
raising of the retained top part remains. The infinite series has
not been specialized wholesale at a root of unity.

For knot conventions matching the paper's formula, the reduced
color coefficient is extracted as
\((Q;Q)_n[x^n]Z_C(t_1x,\ldots,t_mx)\), with all grading
monomials and signs retained in \(t_i\). An independent equality
with our original framed source is still required. Individual
\(y_i\) do not preserve this scalar specialization, so its actual
one-variable annihilator needs compatible elimination as well.
No geometric component, period coefficient or root-value positivity
follows from this definition check. These are possible alternative
coordinates for the existing problem, not a replacement objective.

### Exact endpoint observations and their retained derivatives

The [endpoint proof](research_physical_packet_endpoint_cosource.md)
starts from the physical packet recovered by the residue calculation.
Put \(d=N-1\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), and
\(p_j=\prod_{r=1}^j(1-Q^r)\).
For \(0\le u\le d\), let
\[
 A_u(J)=\frac{p_{J+u}}{p_Jp_u},\qquad
 C_u(J,v)=p_uA_u(J)Q^{Jv}A_u(v),\qquad
 0\le J,v<N-u .
\]
The finite binomial identity gives
\[
 B_u(z)=\sum_{J=0}^{N-u-1}A_u(J)z^J
       =\prod_{r=u+1}^{d}(1-Q^rz),\qquad
 C_u\mathbf1=Ne_0,\quad C_u^{-1}e_0=N^{-1}\mathbf1 .
\]
For any supplied diagonal coefficients \(d_J\), their exact Fourier
transform \(\widehat d_s=N^{-1}\sum_Jd_JQ^{-sJ}\) therefore gives
\[
 \sum_Jd_JC_u(J,v)
 =N A_u(v)\sum_{a=0}^u(-1)^aQ^{a(a+1)/2}
              {u\brack a}_Q\,\widehat d_{[-v-a]} .
\]
All cyclic carries and original complex phases remain. A quadratic
diagonal attachment retains its literal finite Gauss sum, including
the half-character at odd levels. That diagonal alone is not a
whole original crossing power.

The proof places this row on both signed physical crossings. Write
\(x=-e^{-\pi i/N}\), \(D_x|j\rangle=x^j|j\rangle\),
let \(S|j\rangle=|j+1\rangle\) with \(S|d\rangle=0\),
and let \(P\) flip the two heads. For the scalar-removed original
matrices, with their scalar restored whenever the crossing is used,
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}_1[((S^uD_x)\otimes I)PM_+^0]
       =N|u\rangle\langle0|,\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}_2[(I\otimes S^uD_x)PM_-^0]
       =Nx^{d-u}|d\rangle\langle d-u| .
\]
These identities implement the specified endpoint observation
against an arbitrary unchanged exterior. The clock, shift and flip
are mandatory insertions. The fixed-\(u\) matrix \(C_u\) ranges
across physical degree blocks; its inverse is not an inverse crossing.

Before sampling, the actual diagonal
\(\operatorname{diag}(1,z,\ldots,z^d)\) gives the polynomial
\(p_uA_u(v)B_u(Q^vz)\). It determines all clock derivatives.
Every inactive band value is a simple zero, whose first derivative
is nonzero. Thus those derivatives cannot be recovered by
differentiating a band formula which has already been sampled.

For \(u=0\), the positive cap equals \(N|0\rangle\langle0|\)
at \(z=1\). Its first logarithmic derivative is the full-rank
diagonal matrix
\[
 \mathcal N=\frac{Nd}{2}|0\rangle\langle0|
       -N\sum_{v=1}^d\frac{x^{-v}}{1-Q^v}|v\rangle\langle v|,
 \qquad
 \mathcal N^{-1}=\frac{2}{Nd}|0\rangle\langle0|
                  -\frac1N D_x(I-Z),
 \quad Z|v\rangle=Q^v|v\rangle .
\]
It satisfies \(\|\mathcal N\|\le N^2/2\) and
\(\|\mathcal N^{-1}\|\le2/N\).
This is a controlled local source derivative, not an identified
meridian deformation. After closing with a scalar knot exterior,
such inserted-clock derivatives remain scalar multiples of the
same unknown invariant. Indeed at these odd levels \(x=Q^{d/2}\);
Fourier orthogonality gives
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}\!\left[
   (F_N I)\sum_{v=0}^d x^{-v}B_0(Q^vz)|v\rangle\langle v|
                  \right]=NF_Nz^{d/2}.
\]
Local full rank therefore supplies no scalar lower bound.

\(\texttt{328032033298763a828a18fccbfa7f53bb7c52064387b79176ae70926d420906}\).

### Combining the original horizontal and vertical corner terms

The [combined-current proof](research_combined_low_kernel_corner_cancellation.md)
addresses the actual low-kernel endpoint rate, rather than replacing
that kernel by its classical density envelope. Let \(G=(V,E)\)
be a fixed loopless simple graph without isolated vertices,
\(d_v=\deg v\), \(n_v\ne0\) the fixed powers, and \(H_v>0\).
Assume
\[
 \lambda_v=(d_v+|n_v|)/2-1>0,\qquad
 R=\sum_v\lambda_vH_v .
\]
The existing all-vertical theorem has a nonzero coefficient at rate
\(R\) for the bare low-kernel graph. In particular its internal
kernels cannot be assigned zero exponential cost.

The original trace also contains the adjoining horizontal pieces.
Near the dominant endpoint use \(t=\sigma_v\pi-ih\),
\(\sigma_v=\operatorname{sgn}n_v\).
Both pieces have exactly the same holomorphic Gaussian source form.
Their orientations at \(h=H_v\) are opposite. If
\(a_v=H_v-i\sigma_v\delta_v\),
\(b_v=H_v-\delta_v\), with fixed sufficiently small
\(0<\delta_v<H_v/2\), the exact combined chain is
\[
 \mathfrak H_v+\mathfrak V_v
 =\sigma_v\int_{a_v}^{b_v}\omega_{v,\sigma_v}
    +\sigma_v\int_{b_v}^{H_v}\omega_{v,-\sigma_v}.
\]
The second integral retains the other branch of the paired
vertical current. Its form is
\(\omega_{v,-\sigma_v}=e^{-N|n_v|h}\omega_{v,\sigma_v}\);
it has not been discarded. Cauchy's theorem gives the first
connector inside the same holomorphic neighborhood.

After the exact low kernels are divided by their known exponential
factors, the phase in each coordinate is
\[
 \Phi_v(h)=\lambda_vh-in_vh^2/(4\pi).
\]
On the new connector write \(h=H_v-s-i\sigma_v t\),
\(s,t\ge0\), \(s+t=\delta_v\). Then
\[
 \Re\Phi_v(h)-\Re\Phi_v(H_v)
 =-\lambda_vs-\frac{|n_v|}{2\pi}t(H_v-s)
 \le-\delta_v\min\{\lambda_v,|n_v|H_v/(4\pi)\}.
\]
The other vertical branch has loss at least
\(|n_v|(H_v-\delta_v)\). Tensoring these exact replacements
keeps all coupled kernels and gives
\[
 |\mathcal J_N^{\rm corner}[A_N]|
 \le C M_N N^{2|V|-2|E|}e^{N(R-\Delta)},\qquad \Delta>0.
\]
Here \(M_N\) is the actual supremum of the polynomial attachment
on the fixed larger complex neighborhood; an exponential attachment
cost remains in this factor. For the bare graph \(M_N=1\).
The explicit \(\Delta\) is the sum, over vertices, of the smaller
of the two losses just displayed.

Every endpoint integration-by-parts coefficient at the removed
corner cancels, including mixed derivatives of coupled edge
amplitudes. The chain identities also hold at lower-dimensional
corners, with their exterior factors unchanged. The corresponding
strict bound requires the stated condition for the induced graph
and its actual attachment norm.

This proves that the earlier excessive upper-corner rate does not
survive in this combined local source. It does not compare
\(R-\Delta\) with the geometric action, control the new external
endpoints or remaining contour, or estimate the separated high
radical matching terms.

\(\texttt{796abcc8e660f4a9764a187a0e6c57a1125a33ee8febace433f2b2c878feae9f}\).
Complete author, peer, and root reads include both unchanged direct
texts: original full-period source \(\texttt{3f74b982}\) and
low-kernel asymptotic \(\texttt{e9261e46}\).
No mathematical programs were used.

### The angle optimization in physical coordinates

The [crossing-frame calculation](research_rivin_role_frames_and_bridge_angles.md)
gives a direct local connection. After an explicit positive change
of the overstrand and understrand frames, each signed crossing
coefficient is its original phase times a positive square root of
two tetrahedral angle weights. A change of role along a strand
requires an explicit sine-factorial connector. The complete matrix
identity retains these connectors, the highest-weight pin, the
trace pivots and the boundary derivatives. Thus the two-cell
interpretation does not silently change the original contraction.

After the existing exact overbridge summation, these factorials
combine particularly simply. In the
[complete-source angle formulation](research_charged_source_angle_optimization.md),
there is one variable for each incidence between an event and an
anchor. The sum at every event and every anchor is \(d=N-1\).
Consequently the entire set of clocks and block monomials is the
integer lattice of a fixed bipartite transportation polytope.
With \(k\) events, the exact scalar takes the form
\[
 K_N=\chi_N N^{k-1}\sum_n \Omega_N(n)
                  \prod_{\text{incidences }a}S_{n_a}^{-1},
 \qquad S_j=\prod_{\ell=1}^{j}2\sin(\pi\ell/N).
\]
Here the sum has the original incidence constraints,
\(|\Omega_N(n)|=1\) is the full prescribed phase, and \(\chi_N\)
is the unchanged external normalization. The closing events are
included: their two factorials multiply to \(N\), so their
magnitude is exactly one.

Removing the phases gives a positive comparison whose exponential
rate is proved, along all levels, to equal
\[
 \max_{x\in\mathcal P}\mathcal V(x),\qquad
 \mathcal V(x)=-\sum_a J(x_a),\qquad
 J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin(\pi s))\,ds .
\]
The normalized incidence sums in \(\mathcal P\) are one. The
function is concave; each event row decomposes explicitly into
ideal-tetrahedron volumes divided by \(\pi\). A rounding argument
preserves both sets of incidence sums at every level. The fixed-clock
positive radius bound has exactly the same constrained entropy as
its dual, including tight faces and degenerate block lengths.

The new [phase-loss theorem](research_charged_block_holonomy_rate_loss.md)
estimates the original coefficients before replacing their phases
by absolute values. Its basic positive polynomial is
\[
 B_{L,N}(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{L}
     \left|{L\brack j}_{q^2}\right|t^j
     =\prod_{r=0}^{L-1}(1+q^{2r-L+1}t),
 \qquad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad 0\le L<N.
\]
For every positive radius \(\rho\) and every angle \(\theta\),
\[
 |B_{L,N}(\rho e^{i\theta})|
 \le C N^C B_{L,N}(\rho)
 \exp\left\{-N\frac{\rho\sin(\pi L/N)}
                    {\pi(1+\rho)^2}(1-\cos\theta)\right\}.
\]
The constant is independent of the length and radius. Zeros,
endpoint lengths and radius escape do not invalidate the bound;
they can make its explicit rate loss vanish. The proof compares
the exact product with an arc integral and controls its logarithmic
zeros uniformly, at a cost \(O(\log N)\) in the logarithm.

For a full charged graph the resulting loss is the minimum, over
the original vertex phases, of the sum of these edge losses.
A cycle whose actual phase product differs from one forces a
quantitative loss; the stronger theorem retains the entire arc
integral, not just its cosine lower bound. This is a general
phase-sensitive bound for the specified coefficient. Applying it
to all original clock sectors gives a fixed-dimensional variational
upper bound for the complete scalar, with the order
\(\sup_{\text{lengths}}\inf_{\text{radii}}\max_{\text{phases}}\).
No interchange of these extrema is assumed. The bound applies to
any fixed signed braid in the original source conventions and
requires no long-twist hypothesis.

This establishes a concrete connection between the exact quantum
source and angle-volume optimization, with cancellation contributing
an explicit correction to the upper bound. It does not yet identify
that bound with the knot complement volume. On the positive chamber,
the bridge entropy is the volume of a cyclic ideal bipyramid. The
incidence sums give its axial and candidate equatorial angle sums;
the actual global face pairings, polar-edge equations and peripheral
marks still have to be established. A nonzero contribution under
the original closing functional is a further requirement.

There is also a useful exact check on what the auxiliary clocks
can achieve. With one event per crossing, let \(u\) be the total
understrand transfer and \(v\) the overstrand output. The clock
ranges over \(v\le h\le u+v\). At fixed remaining charges its full
phase is linear in \(h\), including all downstream and closure
feedback, so
\[
 \sum_{h=v}^{u+v}
 \frac{q^{Ch}}{S_{h-v}S_{u-h+v}}
       =\frac{q^{Cv}}{S_u}\,B_{u,N}(q^C).
\]
The actual coefficient is
\(C=N+\sigma(u+1+2J)\), where \(J\) is the original understrand
input and \(\sigma\) the physical crossing sign. The product on
the right has magnitude \(S_{J+u}/(S_JS_u)\), and its phase
restores precisely the original physical crossing. Summing every
singleton clock therefore returns the original conserved-weight
matrix contraction, with the original closure. It does not create
a positive formula for that remaining contraction.

The complete joint phase and its physical stationary correspondence
are now derived in the new note above. Fixed-clock cycle holonomies
alone see only variations of the split charges. The additional clock
derivatives include their feedback phases. Their polar-angle formulas
are explicit, but a direct face pairing of the positive incidence
bipyramids is still not proved. The original closing evaluation and
its geometric contribution remain the decisive issue.

The case studies have not established the general partial-filling
theorem. Their reusable
outputs include exact finite-source identities and obstructions to
replacing the prescribed scalar observation by a positive norm. Their
individual contour bounds remain valid in their stated domains, but no
proved reduction makes a list of \(3/4\)-words exhaustive for general
short partially filled tangles. Even a theorem for every word in those
two symbols would still leave other powers, signs, branching compositions,
and degenerations.

A new case calculation is justified only if it proves a lemma used in
the general partial-filling theorem, decides a stated hypothesis of that
theorem, or treats a case in a proved exhaustive reduction. Extending
another interval for an individual word does not meet that standard by
itself. The next task is to determine what survives arbitrary fixed
tangle operations while retaining the actual closing functional,
its nonzero geometric contribution, and control of the remaining sum.
The existing
[observation criterion](research_source_adapted_observation_composition.md)
states sufficient estimates; it does not establish them for arbitrary
partial fillings. The
[scope audit](research_finite_exception_scope_audit.md)
also explains why unresolved short cores with infinitely many parameter
preimages cannot be put into a finite exceptional list.

Two general results have now completed written proof and source review.
Neither uses a list of crossing patterns.

The [high-index boundary estimate](research_high_index_free_boundary_hermite_bound.md)
bounds the entire canonical Newton polynomial, rather than only its
values at distinct spectral roots. Uniformly for
\(1/2\le\Re x\le1\), it gives
\[
 |\partial_z^k\widetilde B_N(x,-2\cos u)|
 \le C_k N^{6+2k}
       \exp\{\pi N|\Im x|+(N-1)|\Im u|\}.
\]
It holds through zero index height, at both level parities, and with
every fixed boundary derivative. The product estimate applies to any
fixed set of free incidences in an original finite network, including
several incidences sharing one boundary variable. The exact unreduced
boundary polynomial and its height costs remain present. This supplies
a general upper estimate for a previously uncontrolled part of the
index period. It does not compare the remaining integral with the
geometric action or prove a nonzero coefficient. Author, separate peer
and root completed the entire proof and direct-source implication
reviews at SHA256
041ba93916ffb71d5549286538c24302d89f80b0f1936ea928f6dd3eaf490ac7;
the two direct-source hashes match the proof.

The [bounded-order auxiliary source theorem](research_partial_tree_bounded_smoothing_source_order.md)
applies to every fixed partially filled circle tree with a free vertex
and arbitrary signed fixed powers. In the specified auxiliary family
\(P_N(z)=s\), with the physical crossing polynomials held fixed, its
full free-boundary polynomial is nonzero and has
\[
 \deg_s F_N\le\sum_{v\ {\rm filled}}(\deg_T(v)-1).
\]
Thus a nonzero auxiliary derivative survives after all internal
contractions, at an order bounded independently of the level. Explicit
dual Newton moment vectors give the corresponding statement for
observations. This is not the physical meridian deformation, and the
nonzero derivative need not be the zeroth one. It therefore supplies
no lower bound for the original closing scalar or its geometric
coefficient. Author, separate peer and root completed the entire proof
and its direct-source implications at SHA256

The [boundary correspondence theorem](research_rivin_jones_split_boundary_source_equivalence.md)
now applies to every fixed short component built by the original finite
Conway operations, with arbitrary signed crossing powers. Its external
matrix contraction determines the complete ordinary Newton boundary
polynomial. The prescribed closing functional, crossing-sign reversal,
cup and cap scalars, and derivatives at repeated roots are explicit.
At a free vertex, the construction first retains independent variables
for every incident edge. Each variable then has degree below \(N\),

This last step preserves boundary products whose degree exceeds

There is now a general lower bound for the coefficients of each fixed
signed full-twist block. This is the first positive estimate obtained
from the present fusion step. Write the full canonical polynomial as
\[
 r_N(z)^{2p}\bmod P_N(z)
       =a_0+\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}a_n\,2T_n(z/2),
 \qquad R^{2p}=\kappa^{2p}r_N(\Omega)^{2p}.
\]
For every fixed \(p\ne0\) and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the
[bulk coefficient theorem](research_fused_twist_real_branch_symbol.md)
proves
\[
 |a_n|\ge c_{p,\epsilon}/N
 \quad\text{whenever}\quad
 \epsilon N\le n\le(1-\epsilon)N
\]
for all sufficiently large \(N\), without parity or coprimality
restrictions. The original scalar \(\kappa^{2p}\) has modulus one.
The proof keeps the repeated-root derivatives throughout. Its
uniform two-term expansion is
\[
 a_n=\text{an explicit finite Gaussian contribution}
       +\frac{ip\,q^{-p/2}}{N\sin(\pi n/N)}
       +O_{p,\epsilon}(N^{-2}).
\]
After removing a unit phase, the Gaussian contribution is
\(N^{-1/2}\) times a quantity depending on finitely many residue
classes. When that quantity is nonzero it dominates the remainder.
When it vanishes, the displayed \(N^{-1}\) term is nonzero and
dominates the \(N^{-2}\) error. This is a lower bound for actual
specified coefficients, rather than existence of some nonzero
coordinate. Author, separate peer and root have read the full proof
and its direct-source implications at SHA256
e569817c0444b41cdc1030c1e60a36567d6d83e7f2247dccd16c902705eb15ae.

The underlying [full-Hermite reciprocity identity](research_full_hermite_gauss_reciprocity.md)
expresses the whole original twist operator using exactly \(2|p|\)
real Fresnel branches, independently of \(N\). Grouping the original
integer charges converts their linear normal weight into an explicit
periodic sawtooth; it cannot be dropped. The identity retains the
original exterior and closing by finite-dimensional linearity.
Its principal values and all parity phases are specified, including
the cases in which the value-only Gauss sum is zero. Author, separate

SHA256 ccd241bfcd15e9855ea9aaa10e65c84697874c36149d894edf3ff8dfa2300ee1.

There is now an alternative
[fixed-contour complex-color identity](research_complex_color_mordell_gauss_reciprocity.md).
For a nonzero signed integer \(p\), let \(\sigma=\operatorname{sgn}p\),
\(L_\sigma=e^{i\sigma\pi/4}\mathbb R\), oriented by its real parameter,
and use the original \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\) and
\(\kappa=q^{(N-1)^2/2}\). Put
\[
 F_z(t)=e^{2\pi ipN(t-1/2)^2-2\pi izt},\qquad
 \mathcal M_p(z)=
       \int_{L_\sigma}\frac{F_z(t)}{1+e^{2\pi iNt}}\,dt,
\]
\[
 \mathcal G_p(b)=
  \frac{e^{i\sigma\pi/4}}{\sqrt{2|p|N}}\,
       e^{-\pi ib-\pi ib^2/(2pN)},\qquad
 I_p=\{\min(0,2p),\ldots,\max(0,2p)-1\}.
\]
For the specified entire value transform \(H(z)\), the exact identity is
\[
 H(z)=\kappa^{-p}\left[
  e^{-2\pi iz}\sum_{r\in I_p}(-1)^r\mathcal G_p(z-Nr)
       +\sigma(1-e^{-2\pi iz})\mathcal M_p(z)\right].
\]
The original normal transform and coefficient are
\[
 D(z)=\frac{ipN}{\pi}H'(z)-pNH(z),\qquad
 \mathfrak a(z)=\frac{ip}{\pi}H'(z)+(1-p-z/N)H(z).
\]
At an integer \(n\), the Mordell term vanishes from \(H(n)\), but
its derivative contributes
\(-2|p|N\kappa^{-p}\mathcal M_p(n)\) to \(D(n)\). Hence the actual
coefficient for \(0\le n<N\) is
\[
 a_n=\kappa^{-p}\left[
    \sum_{r\in I_p}(-1)^r(1+2p-r)\mathcal G_p(n-Nr)
           -2|p|\mathcal M_p(n)\right].
\]
This retains the original repeated-root derivatives. The missing
finite coefficients remain \(a_N=a_{N+1}=0\); the entire interpolation
at those arguments must not replace them.

The tilted integral is absolutely convergent and entire in \(z\).
Translating its line from \(a+L_\sigma\) to \(b+L_\sigma\), where
\(a<b\) avoid the half grid, gives exactly
\[
 \mathcal M_{p,a}(z)-\mathcal M_{p,b}(z)
   =\frac{\sigma}{N}
      \sum_{a<(j+1/2)/N<b}F_z((j+\tfrac12)/N).
\]
Consequently a joint contour change for several original twist slots
has a fixed integral representation and specified residues. The
normal terms, neighboring operators, and prescribed closing remain
in their original order.

Complex-color analyticity, differentiation, and finite exterior
contraction were already established by the paired-segment formula
below. The additional result is absolute convergence on a fixed
contour, with the displayed translation rule. It supplies no new
geometric lower bound. Its elementary absolute envelope already has
rate \(\pi|p|/4\) at normalized color zero, while the previously
proved full-circle endpoint symbol has linear rate
\(\pi|\operatorname{Im}\beta|\) at nonreal normalized color \(\beta\).
Neither estimate identifies the selected surgery action. The
unresolved estimate remains a coherent one for the attached short
component, its contour residues, and its prescribed closing.

The complete final proof and its direct-source implications were
checked by author, separate peer, and root at SHA256
5a813a6f394c6688f52d112ef6835bf774c110eaaba0fb62fd34b54601484f54.
Both direct-source versions are the matching reciprocity and coherent
Gaussian versions recorded immediately above. The comparison uses
complex-color fusion at
002f6e8170760ec084a7cafb43da00eb936b2da7ecc05310560cbfa658438693
and circle endpoint noncancellation at
e1ae2813bf81a737554370fea5849ec71e1999fe7af0fa422b8ab48d0017ca83.
No mathematical code or numerical check was used.

The lower bound concerns the first-kind Chebyshev coefficients.
The following results now treat their actual ordinary-circle
differences, the specified complex continuation, and the entire
prescribed exterior. None infers survival of the closing sum from
entrywise nonvanishing.

The [ordinary-circle calculation](research_fused_twist_circle_coefficients.md)
keeps the canonical endpoint convention in
\(\beta_j=(-1)^j(a_j-a_{j+2})\). It gives a uniform expansion
through an \(O(N^{-4})\) remainder on every compact interval of
normalized interior colors \(t=(j+1)/N\). The Gaussian term is
explicit, and the first remaining term is
\[
 (-1)^j\beta_j
 =\text{the explicit Gaussian difference}
   -\frac{2ipq^{-p/2}}{N^2}
                  \frac{d}{dt}\csc(\pi t)+O(N^{-3}).
\]
For every fixed \(p\ne0\), this proves a lower bound \(c/N^2\)
away from a finite, explicitly defined set of real resonances.
It also proves why an unrestricted lower bound would be false.
At the exact center, for \(N=2m\),
\[
 \beta_{m-1}=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \gcd(|p|,m)>1;
 \qquad |\beta_{m-1}|=m^{-1/2}\ \text{otherwise}.
\]
Any other eventual exact zero in a fixed interior interval must lie
in an \(O(N^{-3/2})\) neighborhood of an irrational noncentral
resonance specified by finite chirp sums. The proof excludes
additional zeros at rational resonances and treats the identically
zero Gaussian terms using their retained normal terms. This is
a classification of possible local coefficient cancellations,
not a classification of exceptional knots.

The [complex-color formula](research_complex_color_fresnel_fusion.md)
continues the original midpoint sum, rather than formally continuing
its real sawtooth. In each of its \(2|p|\) branches, the interval
indexed by \(m\) carries the necessary factor
\(e^{-2\pi i\zeta m}\), where \(\zeta\) is the complex color.
An exact finite formula on a grid of \(2|p|N\) points proves that
each branch is entire and retains the original endpoint currents.
The formula commutes with fixed boundary derivatives and finite
exterior contractions.

For this specified continuation, the
[complex circle theorem](research_complex_circle_endpoint_noncancellation.md)
also gives a two-sided estimate. On every fixed compact set of
nonreal normalized colors \(\beta\),
\[
 |b_N(N\beta)|\asymp N^{-2}e^{\pi N|\operatorname{Im}\beta|}.
\]
Here \(b_N\) is the entire original circle difference; its physical
complete-color coefficient retains the required half weight.
The leading symbol is the derivative of
\((p+1-\beta)/\sin(\pi\beta)\) in the upper half-plane and of
\((p+\beta-1)/\sin(\pi\beta)\) in the lower half-plane.
Their nonvanishing follows from the nonnegative energy of an
elementary Robin boundary problem. This proves survival of the
endpoint contribution in the whole local coefficient. Its linear
exponential action is not the geometric surgery action, and the
estimate is not uniform as the color approaches the real axis.

Most directly relevant to composition, the
[prescribed-exterior formula](research_fused_twist_prescribed_exterior_period.md)
now contracts with the original exterior before grouping the Fourier
charges. Let \(A_j=\Lambda(L_j)\) be that exterior's physical color
list, set \(c_h=A_{N-h}\) and \(c_{-h}=c_h\), and form
\[
 F_N(z)=\sum_{h=-(N-1)}^{N-1}c_h e^{2\pi ihz},
 \qquad E_N(z)=\sinh(2\pi iz)F_N(z).
\]
The reflected list is a definition using the same physical colors;
no symmetry of an unproved exterior continuation is assumed.
The theorem expresses \(\Lambda(R^{2p})\) as exactly \(2|p|\)
ordinary improper Fresnel integrals. Each amplitude retains both
\(E_N'/(2\pi iN)\) and the original linear normal weight, written
as a periodic sawtooth. The original zeros at \(z=\pm1/2\)
justify integration by parts without discarded boundary terms.
The formula holds for scalar observations and unreduced ordinary
boundary polynomials, with all fixed Hermite derivatives and
ordered compositions.

On every integration interval there is an exact identity between
this amplitude and the original integer charge plus a total
derivative. The zero-charge interval therefore integrates to zero
exactly. If a genuine exterior asymptotic has a nondegenerate
stationary point in another interval, the leading multiplier there
is the original charge times the exterior's leading coefficient.
The latter coefficient and the contribution of its contour still
require proof for arbitrary fixed short components. The new formula
preserves that question in the full closing sum; it does not answer
it by a local coefficient estimate.

There is an exact comparison with the earlier resolvent approach.
Write \(P_N(s)=2T_N(s/2)+2\) and
\(V_N(s)=P_N(s)(s-\Omega)^{-1}\), interpreted as its polynomial
numerator. The divided Chebyshev identity in
[the resolvent note](actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.md#3-exact-positivity-of-the-full-homogeneous-resolvent-numerator)
gives
\[
 F_N(z)=(-1)^{N-1}\Lambda(V_N(-2\cos(2\pi z))),\qquad
 E_N(z)\,dz=\frac{i(-1)^{N-1}}{4\pi}\Lambda(V_N(s))\,ds,
 \quad s=-2\cos(2\pi z).
\]
Thus the Fourier endpoint at \(z=\pm1/2\) is the previously studied
spectral endpoint \(s=2\). Its boundary value vanishes, but its first
derivative need not:
\[
 E_N'(1/2)=-8\pi i(-1)^{N-1}
                         \Lambda((2-\Omega)^{-1}).
\]
The known local bounds on that resolvent do not bound its entire
exterior contraction at the filled volume rate. This comparison
also explains why the new nonreal-color lower bound cannot simply
replace the missing geometric contribution: it estimates the local
endpoint before precisely that contraction. The Fourier formula
and the resolvent formula retain the same unresolved source data.

The exact compiler identifies the operation still needing an estimate.
Represent the exterior row as \(\Lambda(f)=\phi_N(a_Nf)\), where
\(a_N\) is its canonical polynomial of degree below \(N\).
The root-character identity then gives
\(F_N(z)=N^2a_N(-2\cos(2\pi z))\).
Thus the new Fourier formula still contains the original boundary
state. Multiplication by fixed signed crossing powers and products
of already controlled boundary states have their existing
[preservation theorem](research_boundary_crossing_packet_preservation.md).
The physical quarter-turn does not preserve that class without
additional hypotheses, as Section 7 of that theorem proves using
original sources.

In a turn with a twist \(2p\), the local charge phase, wherever the
proved canonical-product comparison applies, has the form
\[
 S_m(z)=2\pi ipz^2+\sum_j W_j(2\pi z)+\psi(2\pi z,u)-2\pi imz .
\]
Here \(W_j\) are the child boundary phases and \(\psi\) is the phase
of the original Newton turn kernel. At the complete boundary their
evenness gives \(S_m'(0)=-2\pi im\). The zero-charge term vanishes
exactly, so the surviving stationary points are displaced from zero.
The long-twist proof brings the selected point into the neighborhood
where the source is controlled. For arbitrary short powers we still
need to control the original turned source along a contour reaching
that point, with nonzero leading coefficient and a strict bound for
all complementary contributions. The source polynomial is
canonicalized only in the contracted variable; the outside ordinary
boundary variables stay unreduced. None of the new entrywise
estimates supplies this missing turn estimate.
