Two additional calculations explain why the fusion was necessary.
The [positive-chart sewing calculation](research_rivin_jones_positive_chart_sewing_obstruction.md)
shows that consecutive original positive crossings force reciprocal
shared shapes, so their two existing strict positive charts cannot
both apply. It also retains a nontrivial logarithmic seam after an
order-\(1/N\) change of Fourier radius. The
[complex-color endpoint calculation](research_fresnel_circle_endpoint_dominance.md)
shows that even the actual circle difference retains a nonzero
endpoint term whose exponential rate exceeds that of the projected
interior Gaussian saddle at fixed nonreal color. Neither calculation
asserts that these terms survive the full coherent closing, or that
a fused positive geometric description is impossible. Their complete
written proofs and directly used sources have been read by author,
separate peer and root at versions
7809489b46a1eb50accca9910428ca929fd98622734060e39b42e1e2070c7910
and ac050f044cf4b6f561f6caca670cb0fc0d34513acc3c55c011ba05c659c16a0d.

still needs a complete estimate; the interval \([7/8,1]\) is
already covered. Two left connections also remain for \(4,4,3\):
the existing complete left-connection theorems assume \(4,4,4\).
The subsequent whole-period assembly therefore remains open.
The [exact second-period decomposition](research_mixed_443_second_period_remaining_paths.md)
now identifies those missing contributions and proves a strict
exponential bound for every other complementary path.
For \(4,4,4\), the complete first sum is now bounded on the
selected second segment \([9/20,1/2]+i/100\).
These advances do not yet enlarge the proved knot family.

open; the factor estimate alone does not bound the product.

second-coordinate arcs and their connecting contours to be bounded.

contour remains before the first numerator zero. Concavity and

from finite summation remain present. Comparison after attachment
to the full endpoint factor is still a separate requirement.

quadratic upper bound from concavity, an integral estimate for

for a cancelling quantum sum.

There is now an [exact coefficient formula](research_mixed_complete44_newton_terminal_coefficients.md)
for the completed first sum. It is adopted at version
a860f5e71584be7858695b61707668fc3c03bdee1630d3d2cdf24151f36a68d3,
after the author, separate peer and root read the entire proof
and its five direct source implications, with matching versions.
This is an algebraic identity at every level, rather than a new
asymptotic estimate.

Put \(r=e^{-2\pi i/N}\), \(P_j=(r;r)_j\), and
\(p_j(Y)=(rY;r)_j\), where
\((a;r)_j=\prod_{h=0}^{j-1}(1-ar^h)\).
For the original endpoint polynomial \(U_{1,N}(w,X)\), define
the already existing reversed terminal expression by
\[
 \mathcal V_{1,N}(w,X)
 =\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}
       \frac{X^{-k}p_k(X)U_{1,N}(w,r^k)}{P_k^2}.
\]
The completed prefix then has the exact expansion
\[
 f_{44,N}(w,Y)
   =\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}
       \frac{\mathcal V_{1,N}(w,r^j)p_j(Y)}{P_j^2}.
\]
The proof is the product identity
\(P_jp_k(r^j)=P_kp_j(r^k)\). Both sides vanish when
\(j+k\ge N\), so it also proves the formula at the support
boundary. In particular each coefficient retains the cancellation
inside a complete original terminal expression.

At a physical second node \(Y=r^b\), only
\(j\le N-1-b\) survives. The next conditional kernel has the same
termination. Their product is therefore an exact two-index finite
sum over that square; the note records its phases and normalization
explicitly. This representation combines the two Fourier terms
of the complete physical transfer. It does not identify a physical
subsum with either separate contour term.

The unresolved estimate is now also expressible as a bound for
these terminal coefficients on real physical arguments, correlated
with the remaining factorial factors and the actual geometric
action. The existing terminal supporting plane is calibrated on
its stated complex contour and cannot simply be applied at these
real nodes. The coefficient identity alone supplies neither the
required upper bound nor noncancellation of the next sum.

the contour cuts. A separate upper contour bounds the positive-height
corrections, with the exact period multiplier retained.
The complete cap and both original Fourier weights are included.

Thus the same real first-interval estimate has a proof that does
not use the new critical branch or its paired critical-action
transport theorem. This is useful for further work: transporting
a chosen contour may remain possible where following a critical
point becomes difficult. The note proves this only on the stated
rectangle; it supplies no general transport theorem, lower bound,
or additional knot-volume identity.

The [exact reflected inverse](research_mixed_exact_reflected_inverse_transfer.md)
is adopted at version
63396ac56d3f6fe7e6f2888afc40ca1a6f533e230f489a8268b98c88c75ee8b0.
The author, separate reviewer and root read the full final proof,
all four direct source implications and the three comparisons with
earlier project results; the hashes match. The new algebra starts
with the finite Newton evaluation matrix
\[
 B_{ab}=\frac{P_{a+b}}{P_aP_b}\quad(a+b<N),\qquad
 B_{ab}=0\quad(a+b\ge N),\qquad
 P_j=(r;r)_j,\quad r=e^{-2\pi i/N}.
\]
It computes \(B^{-1}\) explicitly. After the necessary fixed
phase change, reflection about \(a+b=N-1\) gives that inverse.
The normalized three- and four-type transfer matrices preserve
one explicit indefinite Hermitian form.

For the type-three kernel, the result also gives an exact inverse
at complex arguments:
\[
 C_N^-(X,Z)=\left(\frac ZX\right)^{N-1}
        C_{0,N}(r^{-1}X^{-1},r^{-1}Z^{-1}),
\]
\[
 \sum_{b=0}^{N-1}C_{0,N}(X,r^b)C_N^-(r^b,Z)
       =\frac1N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(Z/X)^k.
\]
Both Fourier bands and the factor \(1/N\) are part of the identity.
For the complete \(443\) contraction, the note derives the
corresponding conserved pairing with its exact factor \(N^3\).
The form is indefinite, and the same proof exhibits exponentially
large and small eigenvalues of the positive type-three kernel.
Consequently the inverse identity alone gives neither a positive
norm bound nor a lower bound for the prescribed knot scalar.

Earlier notes already established indefinite conservation and
the distinction between a positive norm and the required closing
observation. The additional results here are the explicit physical
inverse, its extension to complex arguments, and the complete
contraction's normalization. No external novelty claim is made.

The next obstacle is to control the second summation with this
first sum kept intact. Local asymptotics alone do not propagate
the needed error estimate: an attachment can amplify errors
which are small only near the geometric critical point. A
general induction therefore needs bounds on the whole remainder
which remain valid after each attachment. Such bounds have not
been proved for arbitrary adjacent short blocks. The new
first-period result does not establish finite exceptions.

The assignment quantifier is important. In the original tree and path
classes, [an exact padding construction](research_original_tree_padding_equivalence.md)
repeats each represented knot on infinitely many assignments of one
larger admissible template. Consequently, cofiniteness for every
template in these classes would establish the identity for every
represented hyperbolic knot. A finite list of untreated reduced knots
cannot be treated as a finite list of exceptional assignments.

The strongest completed two-boundary result used here is the
[ordinary two-boundary theorem for the path \(343\)](research_mixed_symmetric_343_full_boundary_kernel.md).
It concerns the exact polynomial
\[
 Z_{343,N}(w_L,w_R)=v(w_L)^T A_3A_4A_3v(w_R),
 \qquad A_n=JM^n,
\]
with the original crossing matrix, Newton basis and full Hermite
trace. On a fixed complex neighborhood of \((-2,-2)\),
\[
 Z_{343,N}(\mathbf w)
 =C_{N,4}C_{N,3}^{\,2}N^{-3/2}
   \mathcal B(\mathbf w)e^{N\Theta(\mathbf w)}
   \{1+O_{\mathrm{hol}}(N^{-1})\},
 \qquad \mathcal B(\mathbf w)\ne0.
\]
The scalar factors have modulus one. The remainder estimate applies
to the whole finite polynomial, through both parities, so this gives
an eventual lower bound at the same exponential rate. At complete
boundary colors, \(2\pi\Re\Theta(-2,-2)=V_{\rm cells}\), the volume
of the corresponding selected geometric region with its original
marking.

The theorem also controls both entire real boundary-color intervals:
\[
 |Z_{343,N}(-2\cos\theta_L,-2\cos\theta_R)|
 \le CN^A
 e^{N\{M_g-c(1-\cos\theta_L)-c(1-\cos\theta_R)\}},
 \qquad M_g=\Re\Theta(-2,-2),\quad c>0.
\]
This estimate is what makes the result useful for further composition.
Together with the local nonzero coefficient, the negative boundary
Hessian and the marked boundary deformation, it verifies the
hypotheses of the existing
[finite-kernel composition theorem](research_finite_two_boundary_kernel_closure.md).
A fixed sequence may now contain arbitrarily many of these \(343\)
blocks, separated by independently sufficiently long signed powers.
For a fixed finite collection of eligible blocks, the common threshold
is independent of the length of the fixed sequence. The sequence and
all its powers are fixed before taking the level limit.

This is not stability under arbitrary short partial fillings.
Adjacent short blocks without the required long separators still
need their own whole-source estimates. Nor does the boundary
polynomial alone identify a closed knot invariant: the original
ordered closure, component condition, primitive slopes and reduced
zero-framing normalization must be retained when applying the
geometric composition theorem. The finite-exception goal remains
open.

specified first-end collar is also controlled. The other departures
from the allowed physical boundary windows still require estimates.
Even a complete theorem for these positive words would leave arbitrary

The absolute-row arguments use rational polynomial inequalities and,

level parities and the prescribed boundary-color neighborhoods remain
in the resulting pair theorem.

contour terms or the full finite sum. The completed central proof versions

The [complete selected four/three estimate](research_mixed_selected_four_three_early_complete_source.md)
now includes every remaining cap contribution, ordinary real-index range
and contour correction. It bounds the original product
\(U_{1,N}C_{0,N}d_N(X)X^{-N}\) by its unchanged geometric affine
rate minus \(1/2000\), with an arbitrarily small rate tolerance.
The first real coordinate ranges over \([.1,.22]\) at height
\(7/625\); the second remains in \(P\) at its actual height.
Both level parities, the whole real ordinary-color interval and fixed
small complex color neighborhoods are included. The proof version is
`c0f4532b`.

The high-index argument here bounds the sum of absolute row values.
It uses positive first height to make the once-wrapped rate decrease;
the preceding index range is transported using the derivative at every
maximizing row. This differs from the cancellation argument needed at
negative first height. The cap's true endpoint estimates remain separate
throughout.

The [complete selected four/four estimate](research_mixed_selected_four_four_early_complete_source.md)
is also established, in proof version `760ab93c`. Here the first
coordinate has height \(1/100\), and the product is
\(U_{1,N}C_{1,N}d_N(X)X^{-N}\), with its original outgoing
factor \(|d_N(Y)|^{1/2}\). The same early rectangle and gap
\(1/2000\) apply. Every physical summation index, endpoint term
and correction from the finite-sum contour formula is included,
for both level parities and the stated ordinary-color domains.
The high-index estimate uses the positive first height and negative
second height to bound the whole high block by its rate at the
half-index. The central contour terms require a separate argument;
they are not inferred from the high-index estimate.

The [assembly of both first Fourier terms](research_mixed_selected_early_boundary_assembly.md),
version `0643c85c`, now combines either completed pair with the rest of
an eligible word. On the enlarged rectangle, the selected term is
exponentially smaller and the unselected term retains the original
nonzero leading coefficient. The proof uses the original stationary
equations to cancel the outgoing linear term. Its extension through
the already controlled middle keeps the stated separation and right
boundary hypotheses. These remain restricted integrals.

There is now further progress on the left connection for an initial
four/four pair. The [zero-height face proof](research_mixed_selected_four_four_zero_height_face.md),
version `fe99fcef`, bounds every individual contour profile and the
complete finite source at first coordinate \(1/10\), with gap
\(1/1000\). It integrates a positive horizontal derivative and uses
that gain to control the change of height. The true cap endpoints
are estimated separately.

The [positive-height envelope](research_mixed_first_positive_join_convex_envelope.md),
version `b1f18bb`, retains every contour term, physical row and Fourier
alternative in one upper bound that is convex in the first height.
For four/four, the zero-height profile bound and the already completed
height-\(1/100\) bound therefore control the whole intervening
vertical segment, with gap \(1/2000\) before the prescribed
tolerance. The second coordinate stays at its geometric height.
This uses convexity of the proved envelope, not of the modulus of a
finite Laurent polynomial.

The [real first-interval proof](research_mixed_four_four_real_first_interval.md),
version `b848eb00`, also controls \([\rho,1/10]\) for any fixed
\(\rho>0\). Every retained joint profile increases toward
\(1/10\), with derivative greater than \(1/3\), so the same

endpoint is handled by a minimum-arc integral and its original

zero. Both first Fourier terms, all rows, both parities and the
ordinary-color neighborhoods are included. Extending this bound to
zero is now established by the
[endpoint continuation proof](research_mixed_four_four_real_first_endpoint.md),
version `4ceec7f8`. The exact finite source is a Laurent polynomial
whose largest absolute exponent is at most twice the level. A fixed
small-arc Chebyshev estimate extends the bound from an interval away
from zero to the endpoint, with an arbitrarily small exponential
cost. The resulting bound holds on the entire real interval
\([0,1/10]\), with gap \(1/2000\), for both first Fourier terms.
The outgoing factor is kept as a multiplier, including at its zeros;
no uniform estimate as a moving cutoff tends to zero is assumed.

The [negative-height connection](research_mixed_first_four_four_negative_height_face.md),
version `f5059830`, is also established. At real first coordinate
\(1/10\), it bounds the unselected finite source throughout the
vertical segment from its actual negative height to zero. The same
convex envelope contains every contour correction at both ends,
including the upper ordinary contour at height four. The endpoint
comparisons retain a positive gap
\(\gamma_{44}=\kappa(a_1-11/50)^2\) below the original geometric
affine rate. This completes both vertical connections at the left
face for an initial four/four pair.

The [connected left-contour theorem](research_mixed_initial44_connected_left_contour.md),

All later integration coordinates still lie in their stated
controlled intervals. The two first-coordinate paths end at different

A [right endpoint estimate](research_mixed_four_four_periodic_right_endpoint_collar.md),

The exact finite integrand is periodic in the first coordinate.
Polynomial continuation first extends the estimate a small distance

contour's endpoint and that neighborhood unresolved.

For an initial four/three pair, the
[zero-height estimate](research_mixed_selected_four_three_zero_height_face.md),

The [real-interval theorem](research_mixed_four_three_real_first_interval.md),

\([0,1/10]\), with gap \(1/2000\), for both first Fourier terms.
It retains every row of both finite factors. The argument first
transports the complete upper bounds to any fixed positive left
endpoint, then uses the degree bound for the exact Laurent polynomial
to reach zero. The high-index comparison includes each possible

point accounts for the whole sum.

The [negative-height connection](research_mixed_first_four_three_negative_height_face.md),

Their [connected-contour assembly](research_mixed_initial43_connected_left_contour.md),

The two first-coordinate paths start at zero, pass through their

On the right, the
[cap estimate from one half to seven tenths](research_mixed_first_four_cap_lower_right_horizontal.md),

This bounds the complete first cap and its Fourier weight by their

action.

The
[complete four/four pair estimate up to one half](research_mixed_initial44_right_half_interval.md),
version `309d6869`, is now author-frozen and adopted after its full
independent proof and direct-source review; all ten source versions
match. At the actual negative first height it controls the entire
unselected pair for \(9/20\le x\le1/2\), while the next coordinate
remains in \(P\) at its actual height. The estimate retains the whole
first Fourier weight and the outgoing modulus halfweight. Its rate is
\[
 \Lambda(z)-\frac{8\kappa}{9}(z-b_0)^2
             -\kappa(9/20-a_0)^2,\qquad \kappa=1/2500000,
\]
up to an arbitrarily small prescribed allowance.
The physical rows are transported jointly with each complete cap
profile. For the central integral, a Hessian comparison extends the

No new critical point or new action normalization is introduced.
The selected first path, later height changes, and remaining right
intervals are not supplied by this theorem.

The new [lower-right action comparison](research_mixed_initial44_lower_right_action_calibration.md),
version `ef0079ed`, is now adopted after the full author and separate
proof/direct-source reviews, with all six source versions checked.
It bounds the original conditional critical action on
\([1/2,7/10]+ic_1\). At one half, the maximum along a horizontal
private contour is convex in its height; the critical height minimizes
that maximum. The already proved fixed-height supporting plane
therefore bounds the moving critical value. The original algebraic
multiplier then makes this value decrease to the right. Combined
with the complete cap estimate, this gives the asserted rate
\[
 \Lambda(z)-\kappa_R(z-b_0)^2
            -(\kappa+\kappa_R)(1/2-a_0)^2,
 \qquad \kappa_R=8\kappa/9 .
\]
This is a comparison for the cap multiplied by the critical
exponential. The other finite conditional contour contributions
are not included in this assertion. They are controlled by the
complete continuation theorem recorded below.

The [lower-right physical-row comparison](research_mixed_initial44_lower_right_physical_rows.md),

profile together with a real conditional row. A separate trigonometric
inequality covers the small physical cap indices, which were not

cap endpoint groups use their own constant ceiling and a bound on
its possible growth. The result pays the conditional end blocks and
the real endpoints of the remaining contour through real part
\(7/10\). It does not itself estimate the complex central integral.

The [other first Fourier term up to one half](research_mixed_selected44_right_half_interval.md),

corrections. This supplies the specified horizontal segment for

A [complete continuation from one half to seven tenths](research_mixed_initial44_lower_right_complete_pair.md),

The [complete positive-height continuation](research_mixed_selected44_upper_right_complete_pair.md),

The rate is at most the original joint geometric supporting plane

Proposition 2 of the same note gives a separate estimate for the

There is also a new [reduction to finitely many boundary problems](research_mixed_exact_clean_cut_finite_boundary_reduction.md),

loss to reduce positive words in three and four of arbitrary length
to bounded-length end configurations and finitely many short words.
The required estimates for those boundary configurations are stated

The [conditional action across the incoming unit circle](research_mixed_four_conditional_positive_incoming_action.md),
version e8608019, is now adopted after the full author and separate
proof and direct-source reviews. It enlarges the algebraic incoming
domain from \(|X|\le1\) to
\[
 \Re X<0,\quad \Im X\ge0,\quad
 |X|^2+\Re X\le1,\quad |X|^2(3-2\Re X)\ge1 .
\]
The original cubic still has exactly one simple upper-half-plane
root on the original logarithmic lift. Its incoming action multiplier
lies strictly in the upper half of the unit disk. Consequently the
critical action decreases when the incoming logarithmic coordinate
moves right or up. This includes the rectangle
\([1/2,7/10]+i[-39/500,1/100]\), so the positive height of the
other first Fourier term no longer lies outside the action theorem.
The proof uses a new exact identity in the real-multiplier exclusion;
it does not extend the finite-sum estimate by assumption.

The [sharper original cap-plane floor](research_mixed_initial44_sharper_half_face_floor.md),
version eeb48098, has completed the author, separate peer and root
proof and direct-source reviews, with all four source versions
matching. At an actual initial four/four reference it proves
\(\Re T'(a_*)>-1/3\), where \(T\) is the original bare cap action.
The bare and allocated comparison planes at one half consequently
exceed \(183/200\), improving the former \(149/200\) floor.
The action normalization is unchanged. This strengthens a geometric
comparison constant; it is not itself a finite-source extension.

The [boundary optimization and positive-metric comparison](research_mixed_clean_cut_boundary_norm_obstruction.md),
version 0f99f381, is now adopted after the complete author, separate
peer, and root proof and direct-source reviews. All ten source
versions match.
For each fixed actual word, it writes the joint boundary supremum
as an exact allocation of the occupation budget between the two
disjoint target windows. The opposite boundary can be left at its
geometric reference, so the proposed uniform nonpositive comparison
requires the corresponding one-sided signs. Overlapping reference
halos remain fixed data and are not replaced by independent ones.

The same note proves a limitation of a positive inner-product
approach. At the actual type-four cap, any Cauchy estimate at the
coherent exponential rate would need a metric whose best condition
number relative to a positive diagonal metric grows at rate at
least \(1/6000\). The proof uses an actual summand lower bound,
not a loose upper envelope. This does not rule out a metric that
encodes cancellation and has that conditioning accounted for.
It rules out obtaining the required rate from a subexponentially
conditioned change of a diagonal norm.

The new [diagonal rate comparison](research_mixed_initial44_diagonal_rate_transport.md),
version bef465fb, has completed the author, separate peer and root
proof and direct-source reviews, with all five source versions
matching. It proposes a way to return the first variable from
its negative height to the real axis while increasing its real part.
Along that specified path, the conditional critical action decreases
at rate greater than \(1/4\), whereas the real cap profiles grow at
rate less than \(31/140\). Their combined rate therefore decreases
by more than \(1/35\). The note also gives derivative comparisons
for the ordinary real rows and the retained negative-height cap
contour.

These derivative bounds propagate only estimates already established
at the starting point. They do not supply a missing initial bound
for a central real-row contribution. In particular the upper cap
Fourier correction, and the side integrals created by moving that
contour higher, still require a comparison with the geometric rate.
The note does not claim a complete connection to the real axis.

The [two height connections at one half](research_mixed_initial44_half_face_height_connections.md),
version 4d83ce42, are now adopted after the full author, separate
peer and root proof and direct-source reviews, with all twelve
source versions matching. They bound the complete unselected factor
from \(1/2+ic_1\) to \(1/2\), and the complete selected factor
from \(1/2+i/100\) to \(1/2\). The proof compares the cap and
conditional critical action by height convexity. Physical low rows
are convex as well; high rows use separate monotonicity arguments
below and above height zero. The full conditional upper bound
includes every remaining row and contour correction.

This result avoids the unpaid diagonal correction: the original
contours may return to the real axis at one half. It does not
retroactively prove the diagonal connector. Its real-face corollary
also retains the additional \(1/50\) upper-alias reserve and
\(29/200\) true-end reserve needed for the following transport.

The [real continuation to seven tenths](research_mixed_initial44_real_right_horizontal.md),

full proof/direct-source review, with all seven source versions
matching. It is now adopted. For both first Fourier terms, the
complete initial four/four pair is bounded on \([1/2,7/10]\)
at height zero by the original joint geometric rate minus
\(\delta_R/2\), up to an arbitrarily small prescribed allowance.
The proof transports the cap and critical action, then treats
every ordinary physical end row, cap tail and sampling correction.
The finite selected monomial is retained; its modulus is one on
this real segment.

Thus both rightward paths can now run from their respective
plateau endpoints to the half face, return there to the real
axis, and continue to \(7/10\). The real interval from there to
the already controlled small neighborhood of \(1\) remains
unproved for this complete source. Earlier estimates for a
type-three cap or a terminal cardinal function concern different
finite sources and do not supply that missing interval.

The [connected right-contour assembly](research_mixed_initial44_connected_right_contour.md),
version cfda9bcc, has completed the author, separate peer and root
proof and direct-source reviews, with all ten source versions
matching. It combines the new right pieces with the established
left paths. For each of the two original first Fourier summands,
the first coordinate now follows a specified connected path from
zero to \(7/10\). All later retained coordinates remain
unselected on their original plateaux. The sum over these paths
has the same nonzero coefficient, original action and
\(N^{-3/2}\) power as the original restricted plateau integral;
the added contributions are exponentially smaller. The exact
terminal scalar, both path orientations and every shared halfweight
are retained. This is an enlargement of the controlled integral,
not the whole first period or a new knot-volume theorem.

The [unit-circle branch continuation](research_mixed_four_conditional_unit_incoming_branch.md),
version b6c8fdaf, has completed the author, separate peer and root
proof and direct-source reviews, with all three source versions
matching. It continues the original conditional critical point
through every real incoming coordinate \(1/2\le a<1\), with
\(\Im Y<0\) and \(\Re Y<1\). The cubic retains exactly one
simple upper-half-plane root, and that root remains strictly before
the incoming numerator wall on the original zero logarithmic lift.
The proof uses exact real-root and ray exclusions. There is no
uniform distance from the wall as \(a\) approaches one. This
removes the old algebraic branch-domain cutoff on the remaining
real arc; the complete finite-source comparison there is still open.

The [unit-circle multiplier theorem](research_mixed_four_conditional_unit_multiplier.md),
version 4d73d905, has also completed the author, separate peer and
root proof and direct-source reviews, with all three source versions
matching. On that same full incoming semicircle,
\[
 0<\left|\frac{v-X}{1-X}\right|<1,\qquad
 \partial_a\Re\Theta
       =\log\left|\frac{v-X}{1-X}\right|<0 .
\]
The new boundary exclusion handles a multiplier in either half-plane.
It therefore does not assume the old vertical monotonicity, whose
upper-half-plane hypothesis need not survive on the added arc.
The original critical action decreases throughout every real interval
\([a_1,a_2]\subset[1/2,1)\). This is an action comparison;
the cap and all finite conditional corrections on the remaining arc
still require their own estimates.

The [critical-root endpoint factorization](research_mixed_four_conditional_unit_endpoint_factorization.md),
version 7eeb4d31, has completed the root author readback and separate
full proof/direct-source review, with all three source versions
matching. Uniformly for outgoing parameters in any compact subset
of the same domain, the original upper root satisfies
\[
 v=X+(1-X)^3 f(X,Y),\qquad
 f(1,Y)=\frac1{Y-1},
\]
with \(f\) holomorphic and nonzero near \(X=1\). Hence its
action multiplier is exactly \((1-X)^2f(X,Y)\).
This specifies the singular part of the original horizontal action
derivative without a new action evaluation or normalization.
Combining it with the continued numerator factorial shows that the
joint rate of a fixed regular cap point and the conditional critical
exponential decreases near the endpoint. The endpoint neighborhood
is chosen before the level limit. This does not supply a calibrated
starting value on the intervening arc or the missing complete
conditional row and contour bounds.

The [endpoint normalization of the original action](research_mixed_four_conditional_unit_endpoint_action.md),
version f3c70561, has completed the author, separate peer and root
proof and direct-source reviews, with all four source versions matching.
The original complex action tends to zero as the real incoming
coordinate tends to one. This follows directly from its defining
primitive: the two upper-endpoint constants cancel, and the primitive
at zero has its original value zero. No new additive constant is chosen.
Writing \(\delta=1-a\), the resulting expansion is
\[
 \Re\Theta(a,y)
 =-2\delta\log(2\pi\delta)+2\delta
       +\delta\log|1-Y|+O_K(\delta^2),
\]
uniformly for outgoing parameters in each compact subset \(K\) of
the stated domain. Together with strict horizontal decrease, this
proves \(\Re\Theta(a,y)>0\) for \(1/2\le a<1\).
It fixes the endpoint value of the critical phase; it does not
establish dominance of that phase in the complete finite sum.

The [positive cap bound on the far right interval](research_mixed_initial44_far_right_physical_envelope.md),
version a676bfee, has completed the author, separate peer and root
proof and direct-source reviews, with all ten source versions matching.
For \(7/8\le x\le1-\rho\), where \(0<\rho<1/8\) is fixed,
the complete first cap has an absolute upper rate \(223/240\).
The inner endpoint coefficient is kept as its original signed sum;

For the next conditional factor, a separate real-variable comparison
reduces every low physical row to its rate at incoming coordinate
\(1/2\), and every high physical row to the half-index rate at that
same incoming coordinate. The original calibrated comparisons cover
the index ranges \(0\le j/N\le2/25\) and \(1/2\le j/N<1\).
Combining them with the cap bound gives a uniform additional
\(1/400\) rate gap for these two blocks, with both first Fourier
choices and the original outgoing halfweight. This includes every
cap index, both level parities and the ordinary-color extensions.
The intervening conditional indices are not covered by this result.
In particular it does not yet complete the right interval.

Two additional comparisons have completed the required proof and
direct-source reviews. The
[critical-term comparison](research_mixed_initial44_far_right_critical_calibration.md),
version b5cc74f6, strengthens the original cap marginal to
\(\Re T'(a_*)>-11/40\). Its original half-face plane therefore
exceeds \(223/240+1/1200\). The complete positive cap bound,
the calibrated critical action at the half face, and horizontal
action decrease give a strict gap for the cap times the critical
exponential throughout every compact subinterval of \([7/8,1)\).
All five source versions match. This assertion estimates the
critical term only.

Separately, the
[thin conditional contour near one](research_mixed_four_conditional_near_unit_endpoint_source.md),
version 08e567ae, controls the complete conditional polynomial by
the maximum of its original critical action and explicit remaining
physical-row rates. All seven source versions match. If
\(\delta=1-a\), its retained prewall interval is
\([\delta/2,\delta-\delta^4]\), with contour heights
\(\pm\delta^2\); the critical height is \(O(\delta^3)\).
The proof retains all joins, weighted corrections and postwall
rows. By itself it does not bound the additional physical middle
block by the geometric action.

The newer [complete far-right pair theorem](research_mixed_initial44_near_endpoint_complete_pair.md),
version 4a481d13, resolves that physical-row comparison directly
on the larger fixed interval \(7/8\le x\le1-\rho\), for every
fixed \(0<\rho<1/8\). The full author, separate peer and root
proof and direct-source reviews are complete, with all five source
versions matching. It bounds every original conditional row before
summing, so a conditional contour is unnecessary on this interval.

The key comparison retains the outgoing parameter exactly. For
\(\ell=2/25\), every middle physical rate satisfies
\[
 E_x(t)<E_{1/2}(\ell)-\frac{59}{47000},
 \qquad \ell\le t\le1/2,\quad 7/8\le x\le1 .
\]
After the incoming numerator wall, the sine-binomial entropy
inequality reduces the row to its rate at \(x=1\); the outgoing
integral then cancels against the calibrated low-cut rate.
Before the wall, Jensen's inequality and an integrated upper
derivative bound pay the remaining short interval. Combining
these with the earlier low/high comparisons covers every integer
\(0\le j<N\), at both level parities. The complete cap, both
first Fourier choices and the original outgoing halfweight
therefore have rate at most
\[
 \Lambda(z)-\kappa(z-b_0)^2-2\delta_R-\frac1{400}+\tau .
\]
This is a bound for the full finite pair. The interval
\([7/10,7/8]\) remains outside it, as do later-coordinate
departures from the controlled plateaux.

For the intervening interval, the
[fixed lower-cut theorem](research_mixed_four_unit_arc_fixed_lower_cut.md),
version a2e6a56f, has completed the root author readback and
separate full proof/direct-source review, with both source versions
matching. On the whole real incoming interval \([1/2,7/8]\)
and the actual outgoing container, the original critical point
satisfies \(2/25<\Re s<1-a\) and \(1/5<|v|<2\).
The proof excludes a smaller real part by an argument comparison
at large height and elementary modulus inequalities at the remaining
heights. Compactness gives strict uniform cut margins. This supplies
a possible contour domain, not a finite-source bound.

The [upper-cap alias endpoint comparison](research_mixed_initial44_upper_cap_alias_endpoint.md),
version adcb2a0a, has completed the author, separate peer and root

The [complete intermediate conditional bound](research_mixed_four_conditional_intermediate_real_source.md),

### Earlier transfer with an auxiliary outgoing coordinate

The complete transfer for the specified initial \(343\) blocks now has
its original nonzero geometric leading term while both boundary
variables vary. More precisely, take an actual complete word in powers
three and four, beginning \(343\), with at least five vertices.
Its geometric reference supplies the third outgoing coordinate \(z_*\).
The [two-variable transfer theorem](research_mixed_next_transfer_complex_neighborhood.md)
proves, on a fixed complex neighborhood of \((-2,z_*)\),
\[
 T_N(w,z)=N^{-2}A(w,z)e^{NP(w,z)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad A(w,z)\ne0.
\]
Here \(T_N\) is the complete finite transfer of the first three blocks,
\(w\) is its incoming ordinary color, and \(e^{-2\pi iz}\) is its
auxiliary outgoing coordinate. The functions \(P\) and \(A\) are the
original geometric action and leading coefficient. The formula holds
along both even and odd levels, with a holomorphic relative error
whose every fixed mixed derivative is \(O(N^{-1})\) on smaller
neighborhoods. It includes every physical row and both Fourier
sectors. Both remainders outside the exact local integral are
exponentially smaller than its geometric term.

The nonzero coefficient gives an eventual lower bound
\(cN^{-2}e^{N\Re P(w,z)}\) on every fixed smaller neighborhood.
This follows from the relative error, without assuming positivity of
the original quantum coefficients.

The same complete transfer now also has a bound over the entire real
incoming-color interval. At its fixed geometric outgoing coordinate,
the [incoming angular-decay theorem](research_mixed_next_complete_incoming_angular_decay.md)
proves
\[
 |T_N(-2\cos\theta,z_*)|
 \le CN^B e^{N\{\Lambda_*-c(1-\cos\theta)\}},
 \qquad -\pi\le\theta\le\pi,\quad
 \Lambda_*=\Re P(-2,z_*),\quad c>0.
\]
It also gives a fixed complex angular strip with a quadratic cost in
the imaginary part. Thus the result now controls every incoming real
color, not only a neighborhood of complete color. The outgoing
coordinate in this bound remains fixed.

This is a result for an open three-block tangle at boundary parameters
arising inside the specified longer words. It does not evaluate the
whole longer word or the knot invariant after closing. Further
composition and ordinary closing require bounds for the remaining
boundary sums, including values outside this neighborhood. Stability
under arbitrary fixed short fillings remains open, so the
finite-exception target above has not been reached. In particular,
the theorem does not establish the volume identity for every knot
whose diagram begins with these three blocks.

### Earlier approaches to the adjoining contribution

The following paragraphs record the comparison problems that preceded
the complete-transfer theorem. They remain useful alternative
approaches, but their unproved sufficient inequalities are no longer
obstacles to the specified reference calculation. The new proof instead
uses the physical zero-frequency anchor and the endpoint-dominance
inequality described below.

Before that proof, the current analytic task was the following.
For the retained complete reference
of the words beginning \(343\), the original transfer equals its known
nonzero geometric integral plus one coherent lower-boundary observation,
up to an error with a proved exponential gap. Equation (32) of the
[full-tail energy theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_full_tail_weighted_energy.md)
gives that observation with its original normalization. The entire
inverse-transformed cutoff forcing is bounded below the geometric rate,
and the upper exterior value vanishes by exact physical termination.
The remaining lower-boundary product had not been bounded at the required
rate. Its exact Chebyshev modes \(k\ge\lceil15N/32\rceil\) are now
bounded below the geometric rate, including their attached outgoing
coefficients; the lower modes were unresolved. There was a proved coherent saving
\(\delta>0\) in its
inner factor, and its complete outgoing factor has the original action
rate \(\Re\mathcal S(1/2,z_*)\). The outstanding sufficient comparison
is
\[
\delta>\mathfrak M_3+\Re\mathcal S(1/2,z_*)-\Lambda.
\]
This particular sufficient inequality has not been established. The
reference calculation is now settled by the different comparison below;
the remaining global boundary-sum estimates and arbitrary short partial
fillings still need proof. The algebraic resultant below
does not certify avoidance at the actual marked reference.

The full inner source now has the required upper bound on the reflected
domain. This discharges hypothesis (H) in the negative-contour criterion:
every remainder in the outer Fourier observation is exponentially
smaller than its nonzero local Gaussian, uniformly on each fixed
\(\delta\in[\delta_1,1/2]\), where \(\delta_1>0\).
The whole-observation assembly is recorded separately below.
The further comparison with the attached outgoing coefficients is now
proved by endpoint dominance; it is not a consequence of the Fourier
theorem alone.

The outgoing action now supplies a stronger input estimate for that
comparison. The exact insertion for the complete trailing interval is
polynomially bounded on a closed spectral ellipse of height \(9/50\),
by the sharper tail estimate below (the earlier height was \(1/8\)).
On larger ellipses its full exponential cost is the explicit action
maximum \(\mathcal P_Z(h)\) defined in the
[action-weighted Green theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_action_weighted_green_ellipse.md).
Attaching the outgoing factor before applying the global test gives
the sufficient criterion
\[
\mathcal P_{Z_*}(R)+\max\{0,\mathfrak M_3-c(r,R)\}<\Lambda,
\]
where \(c(r,R)\) is the proved analytic residual rate. This more
flexible comparison is also unverified.

A finite Fourier inverse now provides a second way to make this
comparison. It solves the exact low-frequency equations, retaining
the higher input coefficients and eleven generated boundary modes.
For an admissible increasing Fourier weight \(W\), its sharper
residual exponent is
\[
\mathcal G_W(\alpha,Z)=
\max_{0\le t\le\alpha}
 \{\mathcal E(1/2+t,Z)+W(t)\}-W(\alpha),\qquad\alpha<1/2.
\]
The sufficient inequalities are
\(\mathcal E(1/2,Z_*)<\Lambda\) and
\(\mathfrak M_3+\mathcal G_W(\alpha,Z_*)<\Lambda\).
The zero-free-symbol theorem below now enlarges the available class
of weights beyond those obtained from a positive real part. It also
computes the supremum of the saving available to that class as an
integral involving the roots of one explicit Laurent polynomial.
The required comparison with the original actions has not been proved.

The complete outgoing polynomials now have an absolute action theorem.
They are zero-free on the actual outgoing region, their successive
ratios follow the stable recurrence branch, and the literal terminal
value fixes their exponential rate. A separate continuation of the
original dilogarithmic primitive identifies that rate with the original
selected action on the middle interval. The new complex amplitude
theorem strengthens the two-sided bounds to a relative asymptotic with
an explicit nonzero leading coefficient and the original logarithmic
phase. It keeps the different boundary constants at even and odd
levels. These statements concern the actual outgoing polynomials;
they do not by themselves bound the signed contraction with the inner
periods. Positive nodal Cauchy estimates for its actual Green insertion
retain the full central inner exponential cost.

## Latest results and their present scope

### Arbitrary interiors with fixed boundary windows

The [exact closing-loss theorem](research_mixed_clean_closing_edges_completion.md)
removes a restriction in the earlier interior estimates. After summing
the terminal variable exactly, a word of length \(m\) has \(h=m-1\)
retained integration coordinates. With the conservative cuts
\(p=16\), \(q=m-15\), every coordinate in
\(F=[17,m-17]\) can now range over the full period and carry any
allowed Fourier alternative. The first sixteen and last sixteen
retained coordinates remain in \(P=[.22,.45]\), with the zero
Fourier alternative selected there. These conditions apply for
\(m\ge34\); the theorem also states the general safe-cut version.
The width of the boundary windows does not grow with the word.

The proof retains an exact loss that the earlier argument discarded.
Let \(D\) be the synthetic interior cost, and let \(A_p,E_q\)
be the two sums of synthetic closing defects. The original occupation
\(p_i\in[0,1]\) equals one whenever an interior symbol is selected
or outside \(P\). The new inequality is
\[
 D\ge-A_p-E_q+\kappa\sum_{i\in F}p_i,
 \qquad \kappa=\frac1{20000}.
\]
All four potentially nonzero closing edges remain ordinary plateau
edges throughout the comparison. Their losses are not used by the
charges assigned to the free interior. They can therefore be retained
in full, and cancel the closing terms in the physical boundary
comparison. No optimization error or smallness assumption on the cut
values is needed.

The two complete boundary estimates then apply to the original
terminal-contracted finite sum, including its scalar, Fourier terms,
endpoint rows and factorial weights. Every additional sector with a
selected or nonplateau free symbol is exponentially below the geometric
rate, with gap at least \(\kappa/2\) after the finite prefactors are
absorbed. Adding those sectors to the already controlled unselected
plateau preserves its nonzero leading coefficient, action and
\(N^{-3/2}\) power, at both level parities. This remains a restricted
portion of the original sum: the physical boundary windows are still
constrained.

There is also an extension allowing the complete first-end collar,
all four first-pair types and the original first/second Fourier
choices. The intervening prefix targets lie in their proved domains,
and the opposite contracted boundary stays in \(P\). Its existing
strict loss now propagates across an arbitrary interior without a
small-cut or long-corridor assumption; the final gap is \(3/250\).
The analogous uncontracted statement retains the genuine local
condition on the opposite boundary. Neither version covers an
additional uncontrolled symbol earlier in the physical prefix.

The [stationary-row transport theorem](research_mixed_unwrapped_stationary_high_row_transport.md)
applies to every actual first pair in a positive three/four word of
length at least three. Write its fixed-height targets as
\(a=x+ic\), \(b=z+id\), with
\(1/10\le x\le11/50\) and \(11/50\le z\le9/20\).
The numbers \(c,d\) are the heights of the original geometric
solution. Neither their signs nor the sign of the ordinary private
critical height is restricted in this theorem.

For the original ordinary row \(R_{j,N}(a,b)\), it gives
\[
 |U_{\alpha,N}(w,X)|\,|d_N(X)|^\alpha |d_N(Y)|^{\epsilon/2}
 \sum_{j=\lceil N/2\rceil}^{\lfloor N(1-z)\rfloor}
      |R_{j,N}(a,b)|

       e^{N\{\Gamma(z)-\gamma_*+\tau\}}.
\]

types are \(3+\alpha,3+\epsilon\), and \(U_{\alpha,N}\) is
the entire first cap. The function \(\Gamma\) is the original

\[
 \gamma_*=\frac{(a_0-11/50)^2}{2500000}.
\]

point; one remains available for continuation in the ordinary color.
The estimate includes both level parities, zeros of the finite
products, and every fixed ordinary-color derivative on a smaller
fixed complex neighborhood.

The main argument is a comparison of maxima. Before \(s+z\)
passes one, the exact stationary-row equation bounds its first
shifted numerator from below. The derivative of the combined cap
and ordinary rate with respect to \(x\) is then positive at every
stationary maximizing row. The two row endpoints are handled
separately: the half row already has a strict deficit, and the
upper endpoint cannot maximize because moving left increases its
rate. Taking the maximum over all rows and all cap contours
therefore preserves the comparison, even when maximizing rows
switch or become degenerate. The cap's true index endpoints have

\([4/25,11/50]\).

remaining strip \(1-z<s<1-x\), and the bound for the latest
rows still needs its calibrated joint last-row comparison. Those
are distinct obligations from central-contour estimates and from

### Exact limitation of original-turn almost-invariance

The [turn-defect theorem](research_rational_word_turn_isotropy_obstruction.md)
concerns every original rational-word state \(f_N=W_Ne_0\),
where \(W_N\) is a word in the genuine turn \(J\) and signed
crossing powers. The full original Frobenius relation gives
\(W_N^*JW_N=J\), while \(e_0^*Je_0=0\). Consequently
\[
 f_N^*Jf_N=0,\qquad
 \|Jf_N-\lambda f_N\|^2=(1+|\lambda|^2)\|f_N\|^2.
\]
For a unit phase \(\lambda\), the relative defect is exactly
\(\sqrt2\), independently of level and word. A unitary Fourier
change of coordinates preserves it. A nonunitary change retains
an explicit condition-number cost.

The original reflected contraction without the turn is exactly
zero, whereas inserting the turn gives the positive Newton norm
squared. The specified cap observations are different contractions
and are not asserted to vanish. A positive unrescaled average of
word conjugations that gives the turn a fixed positive weight also
has a positive trace-norm defect on these pure states. These facts
exclude the proposed automatic almost-invariance argument for the
original turn. They do not exclude a localized Gaussian estimate
for another operator or a separately controlled observation.

### Two deductions for the general short-component problem

The [finite-contour boundary criterion](research_finite_contour_boundary_loss_transfer.md)
separates the boundary-color estimate from the construction of a
contributing contour. On a fixed compact wire strip below the half
index, the original factorial inequality gives strict angular decay
for every exposed free-boundary factor. It applies to the unchanged
main contour, complete aliases and caps. The omitted physical rows
require an additional check: an index \(x>1/2\) can cost
\(\chi(x)=V_0(1-x)\) when the free color moves away from completeness,
where \(V_0\) is the complete-color Newton entropy. This cost is sharp
at the entropy level. Below the half index the cost is zero.
If the omitted absolute profile gaps absorb these charges, the full
source has the required real-boundary decay and complex-strip bound.
The coefficient bound must be established separately from the Newton
factors; a complete-color zero or a cancellation cannot certify it.
Thus a suitable complete contour proof need not be followed by a
new outside-angle cover for each tangle. The criterion does not
construct that contour or prove its nonzero coefficient.

[finite-depth reduction for actual open words](research_mixed_actual_open_full_alphabet_completion.md).

three/four word, including the selected alternatives, seams and
right-half rows. The geometric reference remains the actual open-word
reference. The existing occupation inequality
\(D\ge\kappa\sum_i p_i\), with \(\kappa=1/20000\), bounds the total
deviation of a nearly minimizing interior configuration. In a long
buffer one can therefore choose a six-symbol interval with small
deviation. Its symbols lie in the unselected plateau, where the
mixed Hessian bounds the cost of cutting. Cutting near both ends
and removing the intervening synthetic block is legitimate because
that entire block has nonnegative defect.

More precisely, reserve \(0\le\theta<1\) of the occupation loss and

triples fixed. Write the infimum as \(V_\theta\). If

 0\le V_\theta^{[d]}-V_\theta
 \le \frac{B_\theta}{20m},
 \qquad d=3+6m,\qquad m>B_\theta.

The finite constant \(B_\theta\) depends on the original local source
bounds, not the word length. Short intervals, including overlapping

### What the cyclic theorem gives to the Fourier approach

The [exact doubling calculation](research_mixed_cyclic_reflection_and_open_boundary_pairing.md)
distinguishes the two relevant finite quantities. For the original
matrix word \(B=A_{n_1}\cdots A_{n_m}\), with \(n_j\in\{3,4\}\),
the covered same-sign cyclic double is
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(BB^T)=\sum_{i,j}B_{ij}^{\,2}.
\]
The positive Gram double is instead
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(B^\dagger B)=\sum_{i,j}|B_{ij}|^2.
\]
Conjugate transposition reverses the order and the crossing signs,
so the latter is a mixed-sign word outside the proved positive
cyclic theorem. The inequality between the two quantities gives
only a lower bound on the Gram norm. It supplies neither the upper
bound needed for the boundary argument nor a lower bound for a
specified boundary evaluation. Their strict finite discrepancy does
not establish different exponential rates.

The specified boundary scalar does have an exact positive expression:
\[
 |v(w_L)^TBv(w_R)|^2
       =\operatorname{tr}(B^\dagger E_LBE_R),
 \quad E_L=aa^\dagger,\ E_R=bb^\dagger,
 \quad a=\overline{v(w_L)},\ b=v(w_R).
\]
These rank-one boundary matrices retain their original normalization.
Estimating this expression at twice the geometric action would be
useful, but positivity alone does not establish that estimate.
Ordinary-color Fourier integration also introduces its actual Newton
moment matrix; replacing it by the identity would discard a cost
that has not been bounded.

Some reflected cases are already covered. The
[repeated reflected-block identity](research_repeated_reflected_block_positive_moments.md)
converts the single-block Gram trace exactly into the positive word
\(W_r=A_2^{r-1}A_{r+2}\), with its scalar retained. Its sharp cyclic
rate is known for \(r=2\). At \(r=3,4\) the words become
\((2,2,5)\) and \((2,2,2,6)\); the positive three/four theorem does
not cover them. This existing reduction therefore does not supply
the missing general estimate, and it does not remove the boundary
matrices from the specified scalar above.

resolved by the full assembly above; the intermediate estimates
are retained to explain the proof's dependencies.

The [right row-curvature theorem](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_right_row_curvature.md)
and its [finite-current application](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_right_inner_low_and_far.md)
now control the entire inner path from first angle
\(2\pi/3-i/10\) to the original right endpoint. The result
includes the far horizontal, final vertical, and the discarded
far physical samples with their normal derivatives. It holds
at both parities, for every real incoming color, and on fixed
ordinary neighborhoods with a smaller gap.

The key comparison retains the outer factor. Along the proposed
path \(K=\pi K_g/(2\beta)\), its half-rate is \((K_g-K)/2\).
The new row bound gives a low-segment rate which, after adding
this half-rate, is strictly below
\[
 \frac{321}{200}-\frac{2261}{554400}<\frac{M_g}{2}.
\]
After the finite prefactors and continuation costs are included,
the complete low/far integral has gap \(1/500\) in a fixed
ordinary incoming neighborhood.

The [positive path through the inner saddle](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_wider_positive_saddle_path.md)
also now has a complete source estimate. Its geometric part
is bounded by the selected action. Its endpoint part is
controlled at first depths at most \(7/10\), while the
contribution at greater depths remains an explicit maximum.
The [strict-region edge theorem](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_wider_edge_packet_and_vertical.md)
supplies the nonzero bare-edge asymptotic needed to compare
its critical value with the row norm. Convexity then bounds
the right-face vertical by its endpoints. The new low-row
estimate controls its lower endpoint.

The remaining positive-path issue is the high-depth endpoint
rate. An additional written argument reduces its maximum to
the value at the selected inner critical point; that reduction
and the required comparison with the available closing rate
are not yet adopted as a completed theorem here. The whole
negative inner connection has a separate newly written proof
whose review is also pending.

These results do not yet bound the full intermediate right
outer integral. Besides finishing the inner estimate, the
outer path still has to reach the already controlled region
starting at \(4\pi/5-i/100\). No new closed-knot identity or
finite-exception theorem is asserted.

### Full edge restoration and a shorter remaining right connection

Two further estimates now apply to the original finite closing
calculation. First, the
[edge-restoration theorem](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_right_edge_restoration.md)
extends the incoming deletion bound to outgoing real angles through
\(2\pi/3\). Its proof uses the original physical rows on the spectral
half-plane \(\Re z<2\), including the extra odd-level term. On the
proposed path
\[
 u=\beta-iK,\qquad K=\frac{\pi K_g}{2\beta},
                  \qquad \pi/2\le\beta\le2\pi/3,
\]
let \(c_{\rm out}=(2\beta/\pi-1)K\) be the combined rate of the
outer crossing and trace charge, and put
\(B(u)=(M_g-c_{\rm out})/2\). The full inner trace \(Q_{n,N}\)
and the trace \(Q_{n,N}^{<<}\) with both adjacent edges shortened
satisfy
\[
 |Q_{n,N}(w,u)-Q_{n,N}^{<<}(w,u)|
                   \le C e^{N(B(u)-1/25)}.
\]
The bound holds on fixed complex neighborhoods of the whole real
incoming-color interval, for every signed integer crossing power
and both parities. It controls the restoration error; an upper
estimate for the shortened trace itself is still required.

Second, the [complete-column norm theorem](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_complete_column_norm.md)
proves
\[
 \|M_N\mathbf e(-2)\|_2
 =2^{-5/4}3^{-1/8}N^{-3/4}e^{N\lambda_*}
                         (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad
 b_2+1/9<\lambda_*<175/216.
\]
Here \(M_N\) is the original crossing matrix, \(\mathbf e\) contains
every Newton evaluation, and \(b_2\) is the established real
Newton exponent. The proof estimates both ends of the index range
directly and applies a positive discrete Laplace argument to the
interior. It also bounds \(M_N^3\mathbf e(w)\) near complete color.
The [resulting far-right estimate](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_earlier_far_right_connection.md)
controls the complete original closing integral from
\(4\pi/5-i/100\) to the original right endpoint, with gap \(1/50\).
This improvement uses fixed neighborhoods of the complete incoming
colors; the earlier all-real incoming far-right theorem remains
valid on its original, shorter interval.

Consequently the single unestimated outer connection can now be
taken from \(\pi/2-iK_g\) to \(4\pi/5-i/100\).
The following additional deductions have also completed their
proof and source checks:

- The [central vertical segment](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_center_height_join.md)
  has gap \(1/50\) in the available rate for one inner factor.
  Its estimate includes the geometric and endpoint parts of the
  finite-edge upper bound.
- The [signed central source bound](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_wider_signed_central_source.md)
  handles negative first angles by an exact exchange of the two
  edge variables and gives the explicit reflected action loss.
- The [endpoint estimate at depth \(7/10\)](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_right_endpoint_sector_budget.md)
  is strictly below the closing rate along the proposed curved
  path. It concerns a specified partial inner integral.
- The [continued geometric phase](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_wider_phase_hyperbola.md)
  decreases strictly along that path, on its original logarithmic
  branch.

The last two statements must not be combined by replacing a
maximum on a fixed-depth contour with the value at its saddle.
Those quantities can differ. A contour through the actual inner
critical point still needs simultaneous geometric and endpoint
estimates, together with its low and far completion. The outer
path from real angle \(2\pi/3\) to the controlled \(4\pi/5\) region
also remains to be estimated. No new closed-knot identity or
stability under arbitrary short partial fillings follows yet.

### The far-right connection is now controlled

The [far-right connection theorem](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_right_far_connection.md)
removes another part of the remaining closing integral. Evaluating the
original phase comparison at real angle \(\pi/2\) gives
\[
 M_g>\frac{321}{100}
       +\frac{(\pi/2-\beta_g)^2}{8\pi}.
\]
Here \(M_g\) is the real part of the geometric closing action, and
\(\beta_g\) is the real part of its critical outgoing angle. This
improves the earlier lower bound \(M_g>307/100\) without changing the
action or its normalization.

The stronger bound makes the existing complete matrix and Newton-vector
estimates sufficient on the path from \(19\pi/20-i/100\) to the original
right endpoint. The absolute value of its full integral is at most
\(C e^{N(M_g-1/20)}\). This includes all finite summation indices,
both level parities, and fixed complex neighborhoods of the real
incoming-color intervals. The proof and its source checks are complete
at dd3322925c80e58eaf22af936e5653945532f1b6de6b4044c047d92348211835.

Together with the left-side estimate below, this leaves one intermediate
right-hand integral, from \(\pi/2-iK_g\) to
\(19\pi/20-i/100\), where \(K_g\) is the depth of the geometric
outgoing angle. The exact finite integrand is holomorphic below the
real axis, so this path may be deformed within that half-plane.
Its integral has not yet been bounded below the geometric exponential
rate. Cancellation with the known nonzero middle contribution is
therefore still possible on the evidence proved so far.

Further written arguments concern a central vertical joining segment,
a sharper complete-column norm, and decrease of the continued geometric
action along a proposed curved path. They are not used in the established
closing identity here. In particular, a bound for the selected action
does not automatically bound the finite sum: an upper bound obtained on
a contour at fixed depth may have a larger exponential rate. The
remaining task is to construct and estimate a contour for the complete
finite sum, controlling its endpoints and the additional terms in its
exact sampling formula.

Thus the restricted long-twist knot theorem remains the existing
closed-knot result. The present short-twist calculation has not yet
produced a further closed-knot volume identity, and the general
finite-exception statement remains open.

### Only the right connecting integral remains in the symmetric closing

The [upper-outgoing inner theorem](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_upper_inner_packet.md)
proves the complete inner-three asymptotic for
\(u=\beta+iK\), \(0\le\beta\le\pi/2\), \(0\le K\le7/10\).
Its phase and crossing power remain those of the original
\(+3\) source. The argument conjugates only a bare edge
identity; it does not conjugate the crossing or the whole trace.
The resulting Gaussian coefficient is nonzero. The proof also
bounds the complete function uniformly over every real incoming
color, with any fixed positive allowance in its exponential rate.

That full incoming-color bound is what pays the intermediate
negative interval of the outer contour. Exact angular evenness
turns its inner factors into values on the upper outgoing
rectangle. The original closing phase has a strict quadratic
loss on this interval. Allowing for both inner estimates,
ordinary polynomial continuation and all prefactors leaves
a gap of \(1/100\) below the geometric rate \(M_g\).
The far-left theorem supplies the other part of the same
connection, with gap \(1/20\). Thus the whole left connecting
integral is exponentially smaller.

Combining this with the original two-current identity gives,
on a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of both complete
incoming colors,
\[
 Z_N(\mathbf w)
 =C_{N,4}C_{N,3}^{\,2}N^{-3/2}
 B(\mathbf w)e^{N\Theta(\mathbf w)}(1+O_{\mathrm{hol}}(N^{-1}))
 +\mathcal C_{R,N}(\mathbf w)
 +O(e^{N(\Re\Theta(\mathbf w)-\epsilon)}),
 \qquad B(\mathbf w)\ne0,\quad\epsilon>0 .
\]
Here \(Z_N\), the unit-modulus crossing scalars \(C_{N,n}\),
the geometric action \(\Theta\), and the literal right current
\(\mathcal C_{R,N}\) are exactly those defined in the
[two-current assembly](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_two_remaining_currents.md).
To express the new left error relative to \(\Re\Theta(\mathbf w)\),
shrink the incoming neighborhood so that
\(|\Re\Theta(\mathbf w)-M_g|<1/200\). The left error then
has relative gap at least \(1/200\); take the minimum with
the already proved error gap in that assembly.

### The opposite-height edge now has a complete source theorem

The [opposite-height edge theorem](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_opposite_height_high_edge.md)
allows the first angle to lie below the real axis and the
outgoing angle above it. On the independent high-angle box
specified there, the original shortened sum has upper rate
\(\max\{\Re\psi,(H+K)/2\}\), with any fixed positive allowance.
Where \(\Re\psi>(H+K)/2\), it has a relative asymptotic with the
original nonzero Gaussian coefficient. The latter statement is
uniform on compact subsets, with independent complex parameter
neighborhoods.

The new argument proves that the real row profile has exactly
one maximum. Individual factors need not be monotone; the proof
bounds their total logarithmic derivative wherever the product
force is at least one. A separate boundary calculation excludes
a right-side local maximum in the half-plane containing the
saddle. These two facts give the required main contour, while
the exact sampling identity retains the two other contour
integrals, endpoint caps, and every physical row.

The nonzero coefficient has a further useful consequence.
When the saddle rate exceeds the endpoint rate, taking
exponential rates in the exact row Cauchy--Schwarz inequality
bounds that saddle rate by the two row-norm rates. This
deduction would not follow from an upper envelope alone.

### The original two-current decomposition

The [outer-contour assembly](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_two_remaining_currents.md)
gives a precise remainder problem for the three consecutive
blocks with crossing powers \(3,4,3\). On a fixed complex
neighborhood of both complete incoming colors, the original
closing sum has the form
\[
 Z_N=C_{N,4}C_{N,3}^{\,2}N^{-3/2}
       B e^{N\Theta}(1+O(N^{-1}))
       +\mathcal C_{L,N}+\mathcal C_{R,N}
       +O(e^{N(\Re\Theta-\epsilon)}),
 \qquad B\ne0,\quad\epsilon>0.
\]
All functions and contours in this identity are specified in the
note. The first term is the asymptotic of the entire middle
horizontal segment, not just a germ near the stationary point.
The two remaining terms are integrals of the complete original
finite functions along the left and right connections to that
segment. The far-left and upper-inner theorems above now
bound the whole left connection. Only the right connection
remains unbounded at the required rate.

Four estimates give this assembly. The
[local outer calculation](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_local_outer_packet.md)
uses the actual geometric Hessian to prove a nonzero Gaussian
coefficient, with its original scalar and two independent boundary
variables. The [horizontal comparison](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_horizontal_concavity.md)
proves strict concavity of the closing phase on the full positive
horizontal segment, so its complement of the local interval has
a strict gap. The [polynomial extension](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_center_bridge.md)
carries that bound across the imaginary axis to a small fixed
negative interval. Finally, the
[far-boundary estimate](research_mixed_symmetric_closing_far_boundary_payment.md)
uses the complete crossing matrices and Newton-row profiles to
bound every removed far sample, its first derivative, and the
short endpoint currents. It retains both parities and every
term in the rational sampling kernel.

The actual middle angle now satisfies
\(2\pi/5<\beta_g<\pi/2\), \(17/30<K_g<7/10\).
The original action has \(\Re\Theta(-2,-2)>307/100\);
the far-boundary terms are below that rate by \(1/20\).
The real part of the leading action retains its original marked
cell-volume interpretation. A lower bound for the complete
closing sum still requires controlling the right connecting
integral or otherwise ruling out cancellation with it.
Thus this assembly does not establish a new knot-volume theorem
or stability under arbitrary short partial fillings.

### Positivity gives a lower bound for a complete two-step diagonal

The [two-step diagonal calculation](research_mixed_next_half_input_two_step_critical_curve.md)
gives a setting in which the proposed positivity argument works for
the entire finite sum. Let \(r=e^{-2\pi i/N}\),
\(M=\lceil N/2\rceil\), and let \(K_{ab}=C_{0,N}(r^a,r^b)\)
be the physical matrix for the conditional kernel with crossing
power three. Its exact Gram representation gives
\[
 C^{(2)}_{00,N}(r^M,r^M)
   =(K^2)_{MM}
   =\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}|C_{0,N}(r^M,r^a)|^2 .
\]
Every summand is nonnegative. A lower bound from a small set of
indices therefore remains a lower bound for the complete diagonal.

The original half-input action, denoted by
\(\mathcal S_{\rm h}(y)\), has a unique nondegenerate real maximum
at a point \(39/100<y_0<2/5\). The extended outgoing asymptotic
described below reaches this point with a nonzero coefficient.
Summing its squared modulus over the nearby physical indices proves
\[
 C^{(2)}_{00,N}(r^M,r^M)
 \ge c_*N^{-1/2}
       \exp\{2N\Re\mathcal S_{\rm h}(y_0)\},
 \qquad c_*>0,
\]
for all sufficiently large even and odd levels. The proof retains
the odd-level shift \(M/N=1/2+1/(2N)\). It needs no upper estimate
on the omitted indices, because those indices only increase this
diagonal sum.

This is a lower bound for an auxiliary composition that occurs in
the transfer analysis. Its exponent has not been identified with a
knot-complement volume. The actual fourth-block calculation requires
complex outgoing parameters, where this sum-of-squares identity no
longer applies. The new note derives exact rational equations for
the stationary points of that composition, but continuation of the
contributing cycle and comparison with the geometric action remain
open. It also proves that the half-input composition has a different
stationary point from the original geometric four-block contribution.
Substituting the latter point would therefore give the wrong
stationary-phase calculation.

The proof and source checks are complete at
6d62635e470aebe2c32d6d3f862a5a9379590f4e4951e467fb4ffb7c76c256a7.

The [complete diagonal theorem](research_mixed_next_complete_two_step_diagonal.md)
now strengthens this lower bound to an asymptotic for the entire
sum:
\[
 C^{(2)}_{00,N}(r^M,r^M)
 =N^{-1/2}|a_{\mathrm{par}}(y_0)|^2
      \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{d_0}}\,
      e^{2N\Re\mathcal S_{\mathrm h}(y_0)}
      (1+O(N^{-1/2})).
\]
Here \(d_0=-(\Re\mathcal S_{\mathrm h})''(y_0)>0\), and
\(a_{\mathrm{par}}\ne0\) is the original amplitude with the
physical half-row shift at the relevant parity. The proof extends

### Both edge deletions are controlled for every integer crossing power

The [integer-power deletion theorem](research_all_integer_crossing_edge_deletions.md)
extends the outgoing-tail estimate to every signed integer power

It also controls deletion of the incoming high rows after the
other edge has been shortened. The exact radical contraction
consumes the derivatives at double physical roots; the remaining
crossing values have modulus one. Consequently the constants do
not grow with \(n\). Odd middle rows, the simple root, and fixed
ordinary incoming derivatives are retained.

There is an exact expression for the outgoing upper rate:
\[
 \mathscr E(K)=K/2+\psi(iK,0)
       \le2b_2+K/2+K^2/(4\pi),\qquad K=|\Im u|.
\]
Here \(\psi\) is the original complete-edge action. The equality
comes from evaluating the convex dual of the physical-row
profile: its maximizing angle satisfies
\(\tan(v/2)=\sinh(K/2)\). It is the maximum of an absolute
upper profile, not an asserted rate of the signed error.
The incoming deletion has the smaller rate
\(\Re\psi(u,0)\le\psi(iK,0)\) on \(|\Re u|\le\pi/2\).

For the three-crossing kernel at complete incoming color, this
reduces the full source to the trace with both edges shortened

still has its original derivatives and signs. Its central and
complementary contour estimates have not been supplied by this
deletion theorem. For other powers, comparison of the same
absolute error with their respective geometric actions remains
necessary.

### Retaining all three crossing entries improves the next-attachment bound

 E(z,a)=J(z)-J(a)-J(z-a),\qquad

       \{V(y)+E(z,y)+E(z,a)\}.

Here \(J,V,c\), and the output profile \(B_\beta\) are the

 F(a)-F(1/2)\le V(a)-V(1/2)\quad(a\ge1/2),
 \qquad
 F(1/2)<2c+V(1/2)-\pi/720 .
\]
Thus the Fourier envelope still has its maximum at half input
and zero frequency, with a strictly smaller ceiling.

### An explicit upper bound after the next attachment

The [two-step Gram and Fourier theorem](research_mixed_next_two_step_gram_fourier_bound.md)
now bounds the entire propagated right contribution after appending

row and the full outgoing polynomial, on arbitrary compact sets of
the complex output \(W\), uniformly in real incoming color.

Here is the resulting exponential ceiling. Put
\[
 J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du,\qquad
 c=-2J(1/6),\qquad V(a)=-2J((1-a)/2)-J(a),
\]
and let \(\Gamma\) be the charged action from the proved inner

 B_\beta(W)=
 \max_{0\le s\le1}
 \left\{\int_0^s\log|1-We^{-2\pi iu}|\,du-(1+\beta)J(s)\right\}.
\]
The propagated right contribution is bounded by a polynomial
factor times
\[
 \exp N\{\,\Gamma(1/2)+V(1/2)+2c+B_\beta(W)+\epsilon\,\}
\]
for every fixed \(\epsilon>0\). The complete two-step kernel
has an exact Gram factorization. Cauchy--Schwarz bounds that
factorization; the original positive Fourier transition then gives
a two-variable maximum. The proof shows that this maximum occurs
at zero Fourier frequency and incoming index \(N/2\) in the
limiting coordinates. It does not assume that the four-type
kernel or the original quantum sum is positive.

This supplies a concrete bound to compare with the next conditional
geometric action. That comparison is still unproved, and the
other propagated remainder and the complement of the next local
integral still need estimates. The maximum above is a maximum
of an upper bound, not the exponential rate of the signed sum.

### The complete finite transfer has its geometric leading term

The [endpoint-dominance proof](research_mixed_next_positive_transition_endpoint_dominance.md)
shows that every Fourier mode has combined upper rate at most that
of the zero-frequency mode:
\[
 \mathcal D(t,Z_*)+\Gamma(1/2-t)
       \le E_0(Z_*)+\Gamma(1/2),\qquad 0\le t\le1/2.
\]
Here \(\mathcal D\) bounds the outgoing Fourier coefficient,
\(\Gamma\) is the rate of its inner observation, and \(E_0\) is
the outgoing rate at physical index \(M=\lceil N/2\rceil\).
The inequality is strict for \(t>0\). The physical anchor below
places the right-hand side strictly below the geometric rate
\(\Lambda=\Re\mathcal P_0^+(-2,z_*)\). Summing the exact finite
modes, and retaining the separately bounded terminal modes, gives
\[
 |\mathcal R_N^+(-2,Z_*)|
       \le C\exp\!\left(N\left(\Lambda-\frac1{4\cdot10^{13}}\right)\right).
\]
This is the entire adjoining contribution. Its coefficients need not
be positive. Positivity is used only for the transition weights that
give an upper bound on their magnitudes.

The [transfer assembly](research_mixed_next_complete_reference_transfer_asymptotic.md)
combines this bound with the original local stationary-phase formula
and the already controlled remainder. The local coefficient is
nonzero, so exponentially smaller terms cannot cancel it. This proves
the complete asymptotic stated at the start of this record, rather
than just an upper estimate or a local stationary-point calculation.

stationary point; \(L_{N,k}\) and \(R_{N,k}\) are the portions of the
horizontal contour on its two sides; \(V_{N,k}\) is the vertical
connector. The last term is the sum over the excluded physical nodes.
All five terms retain the original finite-source normalization.

For every fixed \(\delta_1>0\), uniformly at frequencies satisfying
\(\delta=1/2-k/N\in[\delta_1,1/2]\), the local term satisfies
\[
 G_{N,k}=N^{-1}B_{N,k}e^{N\mathcal S(\delta)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad 0<c\le |B_{N,k}|\le C.
\]
The function \(\mathcal S\) is the selected complex action and
\(\Gamma=\Re\mathcal S\) its exponential rate. The coefficient
includes both reflected contributions. At zero Fourier frequency
their exact factor is two, so they reinforce each other in this
local integral. The physical remainder satisfies
\( |E_{N,k}^{\mathrm{phys}}|\le C e^{N(\Gamma(\delta)-1/100)}\).

This local theorem by itself proves a nonzero contribution to an
exact decomposition. The subsequent contour estimates now bound all
remaining integrals below its rate, as explained below.
The written proof and its source dependencies have completed root
and independent readings at
6f2b155eee54cfd8a930d9af146ab96c3de277aac70d2de51b5f8318523f45ab.

and bounds the expansion on a surrounding ellipse. Choosing a narrow

It applies to complex coefficients; positivity is not assumed.

### The inner asymptotic now holds on the full selected curve

The [combined inner theorem](research_mixed_next_selected_curve_inner_packet.md)

\[
 Q_N^{\mathrm{sh}}(u_\delta)=
 C_{N,3}N^{-3/2}\mathcal A(u_\delta)e^{NS(u_\delta)}
                      (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad 0\le\delta\le1/2.
\]
The original Gaussian coefficient \(\mathcal A\) is nonzero, uniformly
on this compact curve, and the estimate includes both level parities.
The proof bounds the complete remaining contour before dividing by
the leading term. It therefore proves nonvanishing of this finite
inner source for all sufficiently large levels throughout the curve.
The exact outer radical identity licenses this shortened source
inside the outer observation; it does not assert equality with the
full source at arbitrary complex angles.

The estimates below now cover the entire right-hand current in the

\(u_\delta=\beta_\delta-iK_\delta\), \(0\le\delta\le1/2\).

In particular, they do not replace the full second kernel by a shortened

Write \(t_*(u)=a_*(u)-iH_*(u)\), and let

 \pi/2-iH_*\ \longrightarrow\ 2\pi/3-iH_*
 \ \longrightarrow\ 2\pi/3-i/10
 \ \longrightarrow\ a_0-i/10
 \ \longrightarrow\ 5\pi/6-i/10,
 \qquad a_0=\arccos(-13/20).
\]
Its four estimates are:

### Restoring the full outgoing edge preserves that asymptotic

A separate [trace calculation](research_mixed_next_outgoing_tail_trace_restoration.md)
now proves the full-source version. If \(Q_N^{\mathrm{full}}\) retains
both complete kernels in the original inner trace, then
\[
 |Q_N^{\mathrm{full}}(u)-Q_N^{\mathrm{sh}}(u)|
       \le CN^A e^{N(2b_2+|\Im u|)}
       \qquad (|\Re u|\le\pi,\ |\Im u|\le1/2).
\]
Here \(b_2<7/12\) is the original real Newton bound. The proof contracts
each removed row exactly. At even levels those rows are in the
radical of the physical algebra. At odd levels the middle row requires
a separate formula, including its simple-node value. The remaining
coefficients are polynomially bounded; no cancellation is assumed
in this estimate.

On the selected curve, \(K_\delta<2/5\) and \(s(u_\delta)>331/200\),
so this difference has a fixed exponential gap below the inner
leading term. Consequently
\[
 Q_N^{\mathrm{full}}(u_\delta)=
 C_{N,3}N^{-3/2}\mathcal A(u_\delta)e^{NS(u_\delta)}
                       (1+O(N^{-1}))
                  \qquad(0\le\delta\le1/2).
\]
This establishes the full original inner asymptotic on the curve,
including nonvanishing. It is a bound on the difference of the
ordinary functions, stronger than their earlier equality inside
one outer observation.

The same strip estimate, combined with the existing full-source
packet near zero, gives a genuine complex-disk packet for the
shortened source, with derivatives of its normalized remainder
controlled on smaller disks. Extending those analytic estimates
to a complete outer integration contour remains separate.

 K_\delta>\frac{20\pi}{113}\delta,\qquad
