### The far outer nodes are controlled, with both reflected charges retained

The [outer localization theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_far_nodes_and_paired_contour.md)
bounds the absolute contribution of every original physical node with
\(|u|\ge3/2\) by \(Ce^{N(\Gamma(\delta)-1/100)}\), uniformly over
the full frequency interval. It uses the actual nodal inner source,
its original normal weights, and the complementary phase bounds
\[
 K_\delta<\pi\delta/3,\qquad \Gamma(\delta)>M_3-34/275.
\]
No complex continuation of a list of nodal errors is used.

For the remaining finite sum, put
\[
 H_N(u)=\frac1{1-\eta_Ne^{-iNu}},\qquad
 f_{N,\delta}(u)=a_N(u)Q_N^{\mathrm{sh}}(u)
       e^{N(3iu^2/(4\pi)-i\delta u)},\qquad \eta_N=(-1)^{N-1}.
\]
The original parity amplitude is \(a_N(u)=\sin u\) for even levels
and \(\sin u\sin(u/2)/\cos^2(\pi/(2N))\) for odd levels.
Reflecting the exact finite sampling rectangle leaves its bottom
and right currents with the paired integrand
\[
                    H_N(u)f_{N,\delta}(u)(1+e^{-2iku}),
                    \qquad \delta=1/2-k/N.
\]
This retains the complete sampling denominator. At \(k=0\), the
last factor is exactly two. On a fixed neighborhood of the selected
saddles with \(\delta\) bounded away from zero it is uniformly
nonzero, including integer sequences approaching \(k=0\).
Thus this particular reflected pair does not cancel locally.
The remaining bottom and right complex currents are not yet bounded
at the selected action, so this is not a global non-cancellation theorem.

The localization and exact reflection theorem is adopted at

### Positive change-of-basis weights give a sharper Fourier upper bound

The [exact transition theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_positive_chebyshev_transition.md)
rewrites every coefficient of the original attached outgoing polynomial as
\[
 f_{k,N}(Z)=(-1)^{M+k}
       \sum_{d=k}^{U}q^{M+d}\beta_{d,k,N}C_{M+d,N}(Z),
 \qquad \beta_{d,k,N}>0.
\]
Here \(q=e^{i\pi/N}\), \(M=\lceil N/2\rceil\),
\(U=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\), and \(C_{b,N}\) is the original
terminating outgoing polynomial. The note defines every weight by
finite sine products, including the different odd-level formula.
The weights are positive; the terms being summed remain complex.
This identity therefore supplies an upper bound, not a lower bound
or a proof of non-cancellation.

For \(J(v)=\int_0^v\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds\), put
\[
 H(x,t)=J(2x)-J(x-t)-J(x+t)-2J(1/2+x),
 \qquad 0\le t\le x\le1/2.
\]
The weights have uniform exponential rate \(H(d/N,k/N)\), with
only polynomial errors. Thus, if \(\mathcal E(a,Z)\) is the
original outgoing action,
\[
 |f_{k,N}(Z)|\le CN^A e^{N\mathcal D(k/N,Z)},\qquad
 \mathcal D(t,Z)=\max_{t\le x\le1/2}
       \{\mathcal E(1/2+x,Z)+H(x,t)\}.
\]
For every fixed \(0<t<1/2\), this is strictly smaller than the
previous ceiling \(\mathcal E(1/2+t,Z)\). At zero frequency the
ceiling remains \(\mathcal E(1/2,Z)\). The improvement has not yet
been shown sufficient for the full outer observation.

The theorem is adopted at
68aad94365bf6a9f6ff8e3070e74c3e147ccabaf6845118c82adfe89a4fe1fab
after complete author, root, and independent proof readings.
No mathematical numerical evaluation was performed for these results.

### An exact dual sum retains the outgoing complex phases

The [dual-source theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_dual_hypergeometric_source.md)
gives a common terminating basic hypergeometric formula for the outgoing
Fourier coefficients. At odd levels it first takes a finite difference,
then retains the exact inverse of that difference in the observation.
The resulting Dirichlet polynomial cancels the odd radical's sine
factor algebraically. Both frequency sectors and the original outside
normalization remain.

This also gives a low-degree algebraic equation for candidate coherent
stationary points. With \(t=k/N\), \(x=d/N\),
\(Y=-e^{-2\pi ix}\), and \(h=4\sin^2(\pi t)\), the limiting consecutive
summand ratio equals one only if
\[
 (1-Z)(1+Y)^4-hY(2-Y-Z)(1+Y)^2
                    +h^2Y^2(1-Y)^2=0.
\]
The derivation keeps the complex outgoing recurrence root, rather than
its modulus. Roots at excluded denominators and roots on a different
recurrence branch are not selected by this equation. It is not an
identification with a knot's \(A\)-polynomial, and does not by itself
give a contributing contour or an asymptotic formula.

The exact finite identities and principal-ratio statement are adopted at
c4da73e92e6634940c3fd8902ad22f3e9cfa4f725e1ba73f1beeb85e3c403d6b
after complete author, root, and independent source/proof readings.

### The highest modes of the complete attached observation are bounded

The [terminal-mode theorem](research_mixed_next_combined_action_terminal_mode_payment.md)
proves a finite-source estimate for the complete reference words
beginning \(343\). Write the original attached polynomial as
\[
 F_N^+(X,Z_*)=\sum_{k=0}^{U}f_{k,N}(Z_*)T_k(-X/2),
 \qquad U=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1,
\]
and keep
\(\mathcal L_N(F)=\phi_N[R_N^3e_MQ_N^{\rm full}F]\).
Then, after including the original scalar \((\kappa_N^2N)^{-1}\),
the absolute sum of all terms with \(k/N\ge15/32\) is
\[
 O\!\left(e^{N(\Lambda-1/1000)}\right).
\]
The exact highest coefficient and both level parities are included.
This bound uses the full real inner source and the original outgoing
action; it does not require a global quantum asymptotic along the
continued charged curve.

The new input is the elementary terminal estimate
\[
 \mathcal E(1-\delta,Z_*)\le
 \delta\left(1+\log\frac{5}{2\delta}\right),\qquad
                  0<\delta\le1/2.
\]
The actual half-line root obeys \(|\mathcal L(a,Z_*)|>
(2\sin\pi a)/10\). Integrating this inequality from the original
zero terminal action gives the displayed estimate. On
\(0\le\delta\le1/32\), it yields
\(\mathcal E(1-\delta,Z_*)<11/64\), which combines with the
written bounds \(M_3<121/63\) and \(\Lambda>419/200\) to leave
a strict gap greater than \(1/500\) before polynomial absorption.

The same note distinguishes a real rate maximum from a complex
gluing equation: stationarity of
\(\mathcal E(a,Z_*)+\Gamma(1-a)\) imposes only
\(|\mathcal L(a,Z_*)|=e^{-h_{1-a}}\).
The additional argument equality and original logarithmic charge
remain necessary. Moreover the outgoing rate is a coefficient
ceiling, not a proved complex phase for that coefficient.
Neither a geometric gluing identification nor a bound for the
remaining modes follows from real stationarity alone.

The theorem is adopted at

after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.

### A finite upper bound now reaches beyond the inner half-angle

The [selected right-edge envelope](research_mixed_next_selected_right_edge_upper_envelope.md)
proves, for the literal shortened second kernel,
\[
 |K_N^<(a-iH,u_\delta)|
 \le C_\tau\exp N\!
   \left(\max\left\{\Re\psi(a-iH,u_\delta),\frac{H+K}{2}\right\}
                                                        +\tau\right),
\]
uniformly for \(\pi/2\le a\le2\pi/3\), \(2/3\le H\le1\),
\(u_\delta=\beta-iK\), and \(0\le\delta\le1/2\), at both parities.
Every physical row, endpoint group, cap and sampling correction is
included. The proof permits the endpoint rate to exceed the saddle
rate, so it does not require a relative asymptotic for this kernel.

Its [cut-guard input](research_mixed_next_selected_right_edge_cut_guards.md)
uses the actual stationary equation to prove
\(K<\beta/2\), \(|\cos u_\delta|<1\) for positive \(\delta\),
and \(H(u_\delta)>2/3\). These correlations control both factorial
cuts beyond \(\pi/2\), including the new part with negative cut
coordinate. The real wire profile has one maximum. A subharmonic
sublevel argument and the exact finite sampling formula then give
the upper envelope above.

For the inner right-hand current, the geometric part of this bound
has the existing horizontal phase loss. The endpoint part requires
comparison of
\[
       \Re\psi(a-iH,0)+\frac{H+K}{2}+\frac{3aH}{2\pi}-H
\]
with the actual inner action \(s(u_\delta)\). The newer action-sector
theorem above now supplies this comparison, and the subsequent three
segments connect to the old far region. The present envelope theorem
remains a finite-kernel upper bound on its stated interval; the whole
current uses those additional results.

### The full canonical source now has a specified packet radius

The [certificate-radius theorem](research_mixed_next_full_three_certificate_packet_radius.md)
gives an explicit unevaluated formula for an admissible radius
\(r_{\rm full}>0\), using the original power-three certificate's
recorded root, local-region and Hessian margins. It concerns the
full canonical polynomial \(P_{3,N}(0,u)\) on a neighborhood of
the closed disk \(|u|\le r_{\rm full}\), including its normalized
holomorphic remainder and fixed derivatives on smaller disks.

The proof bounds the change of the free factorial factor, constructs
the perturbed critical point by a quantified contraction, and pays
the faces added by translating its local integration cube. It retains
all nineteen original contour surfaces, the full discarded polynomials,
their normal terms and both parities. No shortened source is substituted.
No saved interval endpoint was numerically combined or reevaluated.

This supplies an eligible radius expression for the whole-frequency

comparison. The theorem is adopted at

### The moving right-hand current is controlled on an explicit quarter-disk

The [quarter-disk current theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_explicit_quarter_disk_current.md)
now estimates the fixed current and its entire vertical connector.

 |\mathcal R_N(u)|\le C e^{N(\Re S_3(0,u)-r)}
 \qquad
 (\Re u\ge0,\ \Im u\le0,\ |u|\le r),
\]
at both level parities. The constants and domain are derived from
the original cubic guards and the full-row slit-plane estimates;
no critical point or saved enclosure was numerically evaluated.

Substitution in the existing single-current assembly proves the
original nonzero packet on this closed quarter-disk for the source
with its first edge full and its second edge shortened at
\(U=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\). The amplitude, action and crossing
scalar are unchanged. This resolves the moving connector locally.
The global current over the full selected charged curve remains
to be bounded.

This distinction in the source matters: the shortened polynomial
agrees with the full canonical \(P_{3,N}(0,u)\) at double physical
nodes, but the two polynomials differ off the grid. The theorem
does not supply a full-\(P_3\) disk radius for the whole-frequency

### A fixed right-hand current is bounded at every physical output

The [fixed-height current theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_fixed_height_right_current.md)
uses one path at the complete inner critical height \(H(0)\), with
the original shortened kernels, crossing, sign and full sampling
denominator. Its output is an ordinary polynomial
\(\mathcal R_N^0(X)\) of degree at most \(U=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\).
The all-row slit-plane bound proves a common gap at all \(U+1\)
double physical nodes, including the nodes outside the earlier
positive-half-period packet. Interpolation therefore uses a complete
set of values of this one polynomial.

Writing \(t_3=a_3-iH(0)\) and
\(\varepsilon_0=(\pi/2-a_3)^2/(16\pi)>0\), the result gives
\[
 |\mathcal R_N^0(-2\cos u)|
   \le C N^4
        \exp\{N(M_3-\varepsilon_0)+U|\Im u|\}.
\]
In particular it has a fixed strict gap below \(M_3\) on
\(|\Im u|\le\varepsilon_0\), at both parities.

The original moving current satisfies the exact identity
\[
       \mathcal R_N(u)=\mathcal V_N^0(u)
                               +\mathcal R_N^0(-2\cos u),
\]
where \(\mathcal V_N^0\) is the vertical connector from height
\(H(u)\) to \(H(0)\). The quarter-disk theorem above bounds
that connector locally; its global estimate remains open.
Moreover the proved gap is below the complete action \(M_3\);
comparison with the varying selected action is still required.
This is a bound on a literal finite current, but it does not yet
bound the whole moving current. The theorem is adopted at
6f5a45805c83881ff84573a523072e35f2213d9323f2a6d245711b03128c6c7f
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.

### The continued phase has quantitative horizontal descent

The [horizontal-descent theorem](research_mixed_next_charged_curve_horizontal_descent.md)
and its [extension to both angular halves](research_mixed_next_charged_curve_two_sided_descent.md)
strengthen the phase continuation below. On
\(|\Re u|\le4/3\), \(|\Im u|\le1/2\), the original
return \(f(u)=\operatorname{arsinh}(c(u)\tan(u/2))\) satisfies
\[
                    \Re f'(u)>1/50,\qquad |f'(u)|<3/2.
\]
Thus the phase along each horizontal line through the selected
point \(u_\delta=a_\delta-ih_\delta\) obeys
\[
 \Re\Psi_\delta(a-ih_\delta)
      \le\Gamma(\delta)-\frac{(a-a_\delta)^2}{100\pi},
                         \qquad -4/3\le a\le4/3.
\]
The proof also gives explicit positive losses at the horizontal
endpoints and \(M_3-\Gamma(\delta)\ge\pi\delta^2/900\).
The selected point is the unique maximum on this whole horizontal
segment; both endpoints have fixed positive losses even at
\(\delta=0\). These are phase estimates with the original action
constant. They supply the required horizontal Gaussian geometry, but cannot
replace a bound for the finite source, its connecting contours or

### The selected stationary point continues through every frequency

The [charged-curve theorem](research_mixed_next_selected_charged_curve_full_interval.md)
now proves that the original geometric stationary point continues uniquely
and without degeneracy for \(0\le\delta\le1/2\), where
\(\delta=1/2-k/N\). For positive \(\delta\), it remains in
\[
             0<\Re u_\delta<4/3,\qquad -1/2<\Im u_\delta<0.
\]
The proof retains the original cubic sheet and logarithmic action. It
excludes roots on all four sides of this fixed rectangle, checks the
single root entering its corner at \(\delta=0\), and applies the
argument principle with multiplicities. In particular the selected
critical value obeys
\[
 M_3-\Gamma(\delta)=\int_0^\delta(-\Im u_s)\,ds>0
                                      \qquad(\delta>0).
\]
Its identity with the selected oriented algebraic factor also continues
through this interval. No assertion that this is the nearest root of
the factor is needed.

This settles continuation of the candidate phase. The finite quantum
coefficient is still proved to follow that phase only on the small

### The conservative whole-frequency comparison reduces to one action excess

The [constant audit](research_mixed_next_whole_frequency_constant_audit.md)
extracts the real angular coefficient \(c_{\mathrm R}=1/200\) from
the original source proof. It also constructs explicit complex-envelope
constants in terms of any eligible full-packet radius \(0<r\le1/4\).
The certificate-radius theorem above now provides one such radius
as an explicit unevaluated expression in the original certified
margins. A radius for the algebraic phase alone cannot be used
in its place.

For the resulting coefficient \(\gamma(r)>0\), the already proved
outgoing action loss makes the whole-frequency maximum exactly
\[
 \max_{0\le t\le1/2}
 \left\{M_3+\mathcal E(1/2+t,Z)-\Lambda(Z)
                            -\gamma(r)(1/2-t)^2\right\}
  =M_3+\mathcal E(1/2,Z)-\Lambda(Z)-\frac{\gamma(r)}4 .
\]
Thus this particular sufficient criterion is a comparison at zero
frequency, with every outgoing coefficient still included. Neither
the sign of the action excess nor a sufficient quantitative margin
has been established. A proof that the excess is nonpositive would
suffice without assigning a numerical radius; a positive excess
would have to be compared with an adequately quantified saving.
Failure of this conservative criterion would not exclude a sharper
Fourier estimate or cancellation in the full insertion.

The audit and its written estimates are adopted at
365a4273716e485f03674eedb58baee4ac04429014c8cb5e956a7a79c044787e
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.
No mathematical evaluation or certificate replay was performed.

### A direct Fourier bound now covers the whole frequency range

The [whole-frequency cosine theorem](research_full_single_vertex_whole_frequency_cosine_bound.md)
uses the complete source directly. For every fixed nonzero inner
power \(n\) and every fixed integer outer power \(m\), it proves
\[
 \left|\phi_N[R^m e_M\widehat Q_{n,N}T_k(-X/2)]\right|
 \le C_{n,m}N^{a_n+1}
       \exp\!\left\{N\left[M_n-\gamma_{n,m}
                        \left(\frac12-\frac{k}{N}\right)^2\right]\right\},
 \quad 0\le k\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor ,
\]
where \(\widehat Q_{n,N}(-2\cos u)=P_{n,N}(0,u)\) is the original
full canonical polynomial. If \(c_n,B_n,b_n\) are the established
constants in its whole-period complex envelope, the proof gives
\[
 \gamma_{n,m}
   =\min\left\{\frac{b_n}{2},
      \frac{1}{4(B_n+m^2/(16c_n))},\frac{c_n}{4}\right\}>0.
\]
The constants may depend on the fixed powers.

The exact parity fold is followed by a sampling rectangle of height
proportional to \(1/2-k/N\). The integer spacing of the frequencies
keeps the sampling denominators uniformly bounded even when this height
is of order \(N^{-1}\). Both horizontal alias groups and both vertical
currents are retained; the vertical estimate uses the sign of the
Fourier character together with the sampling kernel. All omitted
physical nodes have an absolute gap. This proof uses the full source
envelope and never separates a pointwise packet error.

For the actual cubic insertion, the resulting sufficient comparison is
\[
 \mathfrak M_3+
 \max_{0\le t\le1/2}
 \left\{\mathcal E(1/2+t,Z_*)-\gamma_{3,3}(1/2-t)^2\right\}
       <\Lambda .
\]
The exact outgoing Fourier expansion and its established coefficient
bounds justify this criterion, including every coefficient through
the last degree. The strict inequality has not been proved.
Positivity of \(\gamma_{3,3}\) is not enough to conclude it.
The theorem is adopted at
24ed707af29a5a15e5f2302210ae492d8256c5b5548145dce31de19dbbd2c489
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.

### The original Fourier coefficients follow the selected geometric branch locally

The [near-half cosine-response theorem](research_mixed_next_near_half_geometric_cosine_response.md)
now proves a source-specific coefficient estimate beyond the nearest-root
restriction of the generic inverse. Define
\[
 \mathcal O_{N,k}
   =\phi_N[R^3e_MQ_N^{\rm full}T_k(-X/2)],
 \qquad \delta_k=\frac12-\frac{k}{N}.
\]
For a fixed sufficiently small \(\delta_0>0\), it establishes
\[
 |\mathcal O_{N,k}|
     \le CN^{-1}e^{N\Gamma(\delta_k)}
       \qquad(0\le\delta_k\le\delta_0).
\]
Here \(\Gamma(\delta)\) is the real part of the original charged
critical value
\(S(u_\delta)+3iu_\delta^2/(4\pi)-i\delta u_\delta\).
The stationary point is the selected geometric branch. Its exact
loss is
\[
 \mathfrak M_3-\Gamma(\delta)
       =\int_0^\delta r_+^{\rm out}(1/2-s)\,ds,
\]
which is strictly stronger near zero than the nearest-root integral
for the full symbol.

On each fixed interval \(0<\delta_1\le\delta_k\le\delta_0\),
the theorem also gives a nonzero \(N^{-1}\) Gaussian leading term,
with its original complex action and all parity scalars. At even
levels the endpoint \(k=N/2\) is exactly zero and is not included
in the nonzero assertion.

The proof starts with an exact reflection of the physical-node sum
onto its full shifted or unshifted angular grid. It then applies the
finite sampling kernel \(1/(1-\eta e^{-iNu})\) on a rectangle whose
vertical edges are grid midpoints. Every sampling alias, cutoff edge
and removed original node has a proved exponential gap. The inner
packet is kept as an exact bounded holomorphic amplitude during this
step; no pointwise relative error is summed separately. Only the
surviving integral is expanded at its saddle.

The same local argument applies to every fixed nonzero signed inner
power and every fixed integer outer power, with an interval depending
on that pair. Only the cubic pair is identified here with the
degree-eleven factor. No uniform interval over all powers, full
outgoing-insertion bound or finite-exceptions theorem follows.
The result is adopted at
19a62beac1f4e2ef3c900d18d402c316b2cf098cd7c32753924824fe2aedcc02
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.

### Direct Fourier estimates can use the full analytic source and a paid real tail

The [nodal-tail theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_nodal_tail_gap.md)
checks the exact identity

sum over original nodes with \(u_j\ge u_0\), including their
consumed-normal weights, is at most
\[
 C N^{a_3+1}
   \exp\{N[\mathfrak M_3-c_3(1-\cos u_0)]\},
 \qquad c_3>0.
\]
The bound permits arbitrary real Fourier carriers and applies at

### Changing grids gives an exact rank-one correction, but an exponentially large inverse

The [opposite-grid transport theorem](research_mixed_next_opposite_grid_rank_one_transport.md)
distinguishes two constructions that cannot be substituted for each other.
On canonical polynomials of degree less than \(N\), put
\(P(X)=2T_N(X/2)+2\), \(\eta=(-1)^{N-1}\),
\(\gamma=4\eta/N^2\), and let \(\phi\) be the original Frobenius trace.
The ordinary cubic operator reduced modulo \(P-4\) is
\(\mathcal D_4^{\rm ord}=\mathcal D_0-\gamma\,1\otimes\phi\).
Transporting opposite-grid multiplication through the original turn
and crossing instead gives
\(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_4=\mathcal D_0+\gamma\,1\otimes\phi\).
Their characteristic polynomials are respectively
\(P(z-2)+4\) and \(P(z-2)-4\).

In particular the ordinary opposite-grid operator is invertible at
every level. Its constant-source solution, however, is an exact scalar
multiple of the original complete inner polynomial. The established
physical-node asymptotic therefore proves
\[
 \|(\mathcal D_4^{\rm ord})^{-1}\|_{\infty\to\infty}
       \ge cN^{1/2}e^{N\mathfrak M_3}.
\]
Here the norm is the supremum on \([-2,2]\) of the canonical
polynomial. It is not a norm of opposite-grid values alone and is
not a lower bound for the final signed observation. This excludes a
polynomial inverse estimate based only on the small opposite-grid
forcing. The theorem is adopted at
e61eff349f74fca353ea5682c97b237b550050ec74dda934c142853925984d60
after full author and independent source/proof readings.

### The complete outgoing source has a nonzero frozen boundary component

The [root-evaluation theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_fredholm_root_evaluations.md)
expresses the winding-one forward range condition as a contour integral
or a divided difference of the positive Fourier generating polynomial.
Repeated roots are included. Its artificial constant Fourier weight
cancels exactly against the rescaling of the symbol roots. The full
block has the outgoing half-input action ceiling \(E_Z(0)\); blocks
starting at a positive macroscopic index have an explicit action
saving. This result is adopted at
cf48af3535fc99a4ffb1df782e3cc42e8d0445a2fe7fb16d87a81474cd62512d
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.

The [normalized-source theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_normalized_source_and_compatibility.md)
now shows that the full-block ceiling is attained by this specified
functional. With \(\alpha_{M,N}=(-q)^M C_{M,N}\) and
\(L_0(Z)=\mathcal L(1/2,Z)\), the entire original polynomial satisfies
\[
 \frac{F_N^+(X,Z)}{\alpha_{M,N}(Z)}
   =\frac{1}{1-L_0(Z)(X+2)/4}+O(N^{-1})
\]
uniformly on the closed spectral ellipse of height \(1/8\), at both
parities and throughout the stated output rectangle. The proof controls
the complete finite tail relative to the nonzero first-row anchor.
Writing \(d=\sqrt{1-L_0}\), \(\omega=(d-1)/(d+1)\), and denoting the
twelve unshifted inside-or-crossed roots by \(\sigma_j\), the forward
compatibility has leading multiplier
\[
       \frac{1}{d\prod_{j=1}^{12}(1-\omega\sigma_j)}.
\]
This multiplier is uniformly nonzero. Thus the full frozen component
has exactly the outgoing half-input exponential rate and cannot supply
an extra exponential saving by itself. The actual hard endpoint reverses
the symbol; its correlated boundary responses still have to be controlled.
The result is adopted at
51f699be90c3a9ceea0f7b4eb96ff38ece62c865fb6dbd97dfb6e4d7d6c99029
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.

### A regular half-step factor now preserves the original scalar observation

The [Frobenius source lift](research_mixed_next_half_step_frobenius_source_lift.md)
proves exact adjoints for the regular half-step maps between the two
spectral quotients. For \(S=4\sin(\pi/N)(1-X/2)\mathsf D\) and
\(\mu=2\cos(\pi/(2N))\), it gives
\(\mathcal L+2=\mu^2-S^{\mathrm t}S\).
With \(U=TR^3\) and the complete original source \(Q\), every original
test \(g\) satisfies
\[
 \phi(gQ)=
 \mu^{-2}\langle SU^{\mathrm t}g,SU^{-1}Q\rangle_{\rm opp}
       +\frac{\mathfrak f_N}{\mu^2}\phi(g).
\]
The source coefficient is exactly the original parity forcing.
The transpose and pairing are bilinear, not positive Hermitian ones.
The transformed factors still contain the full turn kernel, so the
identity alone supplies neither a local oriented factorization nor a
cancellation estimate. This result is adopted at
30f84b2b480a32281c8aff1475b0e776898bd17988ebc7ae0e707e60b0260f59
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.

The [locality theorem](research_mixed_next_half_step_cubic_lift_nonlocality.md)
also resolves one limitation of this particular lift. Every nonzero
ordinary output value of \(SR^{-3}T\) requires at least \(M\)
original Hermite jet slots, hence at least \(\lceil M/2\rceil\)
distinct original nodes, where \(M=\lceil N/2\rceil\).
The proof uses exact annihilation of all input polynomials of degree
at most \(M-2\) and Hermite interpolation; at even levels it must retain
the central first derivative. Thus this lift has no formula using
a number of original sampling nodes independent of \(N\).
The result is adopted at
d973b46128b7929cae8bbab61b68b36977b23fcc310353542d9dae0b305c9a17
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.
It does not rule out another factorization or an estimate on the
actual source and test together.

### Progress in the finite Fourier calculation, and the estimate still missing

The latest work has not established the volume identity for a new knot
family or proved the finite-exceptions theorem. For the complete
reference calculation described above, the geometric contribution has
a nonzero leading coefficient. Its comparison with the remaining
signed boundary contribution is still unproved. The stronger theorem
would additionally require estimates with the tangle boundary variables
free, followed by stability under arbitrary fixed short partial fillings.

The [regular half-step calculus](research_mixed_next_outer_regular_half_step_calculus.md)
now gives polynomial average and divided-difference maps between the
original and opposite spectral grids. These maps retain the endpoint
values and derivatives required by the two defining ideals. Their ordered
compositions recover the original Askey--Wilson operator exactly. The
literal oriented translation also has an odd reflection term, which
cannot be discarded. This result makes the proposed doubled-grid
calculation well defined; it supplies no bound on its inverse or on the
remaining signed observation. It is adopted at
`083adf70c447e713d7f5fe6f1bfb41f490b33c6227e5b8ad495489795085a594`
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.

The next two questions are concrete: can the original finite transport
and its final scalar evaluation be carried through the oriented
factorization, and can the resulting boundary contribution be shown to
have an exponential rate below the geometric contribution? Neither an
almost-invariant-vector estimate nor the required noncancellation bound
has been proved. The manuscripts remain frozen.

### The doubled grid has a specified original source and an explicit small forcing

The [doubled-grid theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_doubled_grid_half_step.md)
constructs an exact algebra for the half-step required by the
oriented symbol factors. With \(q=e^{i\pi/N}\), it is
\[
 \mathcal B_N=\mathbb C[\zeta^{\pm1}]/((\zeta^{2N}-1)^2).
\]
The half-step \(\zeta\mapsto q\zeta\) exchanges the original
and opposite grids. Reflection \(\zeta\mapsto\zeta^{-1}\)
has invariant algebra
\[
 \mathbb C[X]/\{P_N(X)(P_N(X)-4)\}
 \simeq\mathbb C[X]/(P_N)\oplus\mathbb C[X]/(P_N-4),
 \qquad X=-\zeta-\zeta^{-1}.
\]
The proof retains all double-node derivatives and the simple
endpoints at both parities. A single half-step does not preserve
the even subspace, so the cover alone is not a descended operator.

The original complete inner source has a canonical ordinary
representative \(Q_N^{\rm full}\). Its formerly unspecified
ordinary defect coefficient is now computed exactly:
\[
 \mathcal D_{3,N}Q_N^{\rm full}(X)
 =-\frac{\eta\kappa^3}{N^2}
       \{P_N(-2)+P_N(X)\},
 \qquad \eta=(-1)^{N-1},\quad\kappa=q^{(N-1)^2/2}.
\]
The degree-\(N\) coefficient of \(\mathcal D_{3,N}X^{N-1}\)
is exactly \(-1\), while the original Frobenius trace gives
\([X^{N-1}]Q_N^{\rm full}=\eta\kappa^3/N^2\).
These two identities prove the formula without numerical evaluation.
On the opposite grid its forcing is \(8\kappa^3/N^2\) at even
levels and \(-4\kappa^3/N^2\) at odd levels. On the entire real
angular circle its modulus is at most \(8/N^2\).

This computes an actual extra source term of the cover; it does
not bound the solution or its signed observation. An exact oriented
factorization and transport with the original endpoint conditions
remain to be proved. The theorem is adopted at
`0cc541295d0562af9d235e4d27f7e1cb329a2fdc14569629ef76b3b0cccbaa37`
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.

### The geometric factor has a larger directional region, but range conditions cannot be omitted

The [directional-root theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_oriented_root_barriers.md)
normalizes the two polynomial factors to winding-zero Laurent
symbols \(a_+,a_-\), with \(p=a_+a_-\) and
\(a_- =\overline{a_+}\) on the real torus. Near frequency one
half, the nearest outer root of \(a_+\) is the selected geometric
branch. The closer unselected outer root of the full symbol belongs
to \(a_-\). Reflection exchanges the two factors. This locates
the different branches but does not permit deletion of one factor.
The result is adopted at
`4d950280fcc4984a38a85300605647eff037e2d0165a33148c61b64a7152cb5b`
after author and independent full source/proof readings.

The [range-condition theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_oriented_factor_range_conditions.md)
tests this possible simplification. Just beyond the first unwanted
root crossing, the frozen half-line symbol has winding one. Its
operator is injective with a one-dimensional missing range; its
right-hand side must satisfy one explicitly stated linear condition.
The reverse half-line instead has a one-dimensional kernel. Moreover
the product of the two compressed factors differs from the compressed
product by an actual boundary matrix: it is supported in the first
five rows and columns, and its entry \(K_{4,4}\) is exactly one.

There is also an exact finite-source test. At each level \(N\),
the attached polynomials \(F_N^+(\cdot,Z)\), as \(Z\) varies
over any open set, span their whole degree-\(U\) target space.
Thus no fixed proper subspace can contain the entire outgoing
family, including after a fixed surjective compression. This rules
out an automatic parameter-independent range condition; it does
not rule out a condition depending on \(Z\), an additional boundary
term or an exponentially small incompatible component.
The range and span results are adopted at
`6f6a411d7788f2727e3261195bb2a8e46871c631d6f86fab5b2cbb26ed2507a5`
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.
No mathematical numerical evaluation was used in these results.

### The characteristic polynomial splits on a double cover, but the nearest endpoint root is unselected

The [degree-eleven factorization](research_mixed_next_outer_degree_eleven_factors.md)
gives the exact quadratic norm
\[
 v^3z^{11}p(z,v)=B(z,v)^2-4v^3z^8(z-1)^6,
 \qquad v=w^2.
\]
The explicit polynomial \(B\) is given in equation (6) of the
note. On this parameter double cover the two factors are
\(\mathscr F_\pm=B(z,w^2)\mp2w^3z^4(z-1)^3\).
The transformation \(w\mapsto-w\) exchanges them. This is a
specified quadratic cover of the symbol parameter, with no asserted
identification with a knot's A-polynomial or quantum invariant.

For \(w=e^{i\pi t}\), \(0\le t<1/2\), one factor has six
roots inside the unit circle and five outside; the other has the
opposite counts. Their roots are reciprocal conjugates. It follows
that the root-distance function \(r(t)\) can be determined from
one degree-eleven polynomial. At \(t=1/2\), each factor has a
triple root at one and its other eight roots remain off the unit
circle. These are exact algebraic and argument-principle deductions.
The factorization is adopted at
`b5793f83ec635753a592f6497787f7d11231f9fb15765c0ab6b718f6e4e1351d`
after author and independent full source/proof readings.

The [endpoint-root theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_symbol_endpoint_roots.md)
then proves the sharper statement
\[
 r(1/2-\delta)=\frac{4\pi}{37}\delta+O(\delta^3).
\]
It computes all six roots approaching the unit circle and separates
the remaining sixteen. The closest pair comes from the unselected
root \(c=-1/2\) of
\(4c^3-3c-i(4c^2-1)=1\), and its conjugate. The original
geometric action uses
\(c_+=(1+2i+\sqrt{5-4i})/4\), whose associated symbol root has
strictly larger distance from the unit circle near this endpoint.
Consequently replacing the nearest-root function by that selected
action branch would be incorrect.

The optimal-weight supremum also has the exact limiting form
\[
 \sup_{\alpha<1/2}\mathcal J_Z(\alpha)
 =\min_{0\le t\le1/2}
 \left\{E_Z(0)-E_Z(t)+\int_t^{1/2}r(s)\,ds\right\}.
\]
This equality follows from monotonicity and continuity; it does not
authorize an inverse at the endpoint frequency. A sufficient
strict action comparison has still not been proved. The endpoint
theorem is adopted at
`aa0a17aec890cfe3951feaafd14a0c35b0d809a348181009e497cdc02dcdee90`
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.
No mathematical numerical evaluation was used in either result.

### A zero-free symbol suffices, and its roots determine the available saving

The [zero-free-symbol theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_zero_free_symbol_weights.md)
proves a uniformly bounded inverse for the actual finite compression
under the condition
\[
 p(u-is,t)\ne0\quad
 (u\in\mathbb R,\ 0\le t\le\alpha,\ 0\le s\le\lambda(t)),
 \qquad \alpha<1/2.
\]
Here \(p\) is the full original scalar symbol, and the positive
Lipschitz weight \(\lambda\) is constant near zero frequency.
The real part of the shifted symbol need not remain positive.

The proof treats both ends of the finite Fourier interval using an
explicit factorization of a scalar Laurent polynomial of winding
number zero. At zero frequency, the inverse convolution has enough
exponential decay to remain bounded after conjugation by
\(e^{\eta|k|}\). Finite overlapping windows combine these model
inverses into a lower singular-value bound for the complete leading
matrix. The original operator differs by \(O(N^{-1})\) in the
same weighted norm. The even subspace, the eleven generated output
frequencies and the original parity-dependent forcing are all retained.

This gives a specific next comparison instead of an unrestricted
search for weights. Put \(\zeta=e^{iu}\). Multiplying the Laurent
symbol by \(\zeta^{11}\) gives the explicit degree-22 polynomial
in equation (26) of the note. Define
\[
 r(t)=\min_{\zeta:\,p(\zeta,t)=0}|\log|\zeta||.
\]
Its roots occur in reciprocal-conjugate pairs, and \(r\) is
continuous and strictly positive on every compact interval below
frequency \(1/2\). The displayed zero-free condition is exactly
\(\lambda(t)<r(t)\).

Write \(E_Z(t)=\mathcal E(1/2+t,Z)\). The supremum of the
saving in our residual estimate, over the admitted weights at a
fixed cutoff \(\alpha\), is
\[
 \mathcal J_Z(\alpha)=
 \min_{0\le t\le\alpha}
 \left\{E_Z(0)-E_Z(t)+\int_t^\alpha r(s)\,ds\right\}.
\]
Thus the stated sufficient action inequalities admit a cutoff and
weight at a fixed actual reference exactly when
\[
 E_{Z_*}(0)<\Lambda,\qquad
 \sup_{0<\alpha<1/2}\mathcal J_{Z_*}(\alpha)
     >\mathfrak M_3+E_{Z_*}(0)-\Lambda.
\]
The strict supremum margin first selects a fixed cutoff and then
a sufficiently close Lipschitz approximation below \(r\).
These are criteria for the proved residual bound; no value or
sufficient sign for the root integral is asserted. Uniform boundary
estimates and arbitrary short partial fillings remain separate work.

The proof is adopted at
`b499a21141be11650f30b94498626e01383c9493edd670e4ef38e5ec985e11d6`
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.
No mathematical numerical evaluation was used.

### The positive-real-part criterion has a finite total gain

The [total-weight theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_positive_symbol_total_weight.md)
proves that every increasing Fourier weight obtained from
\(\Re p(u-i\lambda(t),t)>0\) satisfies
\[
 W(\alpha)=\int_0^\alpha\lambda(t)\,dt<1/6,
 \qquad 0<\alpha<1/2.
\]
The exact central derivative is
\(p_u(0,t)/p(0,t)=-8\tan(\pi t)\). Applying the strip Schwarz
lemma to the whole symbol gives
\(\lambda(t)\le\pi\cot(\pi t)/16\); its highest Fourier
coefficient gives a second uniform bound below one. Integrating
these two necessary restrictions proves the displayed total bound.
The written proof includes the elementary rational comparisons.

The actual residual formula has \(\delta_W\le W(\alpha)\),
because its minimum includes frequency zero. Thus this particular
sufficient criterion cannot pay an actual excess of at least
\(1/6\). No such lower bound for the actual excess has been
established, and a smaller excess does not by itself construct a
sufficient weight. This theorem does not limit inverses based on a
zero-free symbol without the positive-real-part assumption, and it
does not show failure of the signed cancellation itself.

The proof is adopted at
`1da609fb923f2d0c99edf6ad48d749b07d0882dbe619d00fc5bbfe3a41c6c5e9`
after full author, root and independent source/proof readings.
No mathematical numerical evaluation was used.

### Direct complex-symbol positivity limits the weight near the last frequency

The [endpoint restriction](research_mixed_next_outer_complex_symbol_endpoint_restriction.md)
proves that the sufficient condition
\(\Re p(u-i\lambda(t),t)>0\) for all real \(u\) forces
\[
\lambda(t)<\frac{2\pi}{23}(1/2-t)
\]
in a fixed, presently unquantified neighborhood below \(t=1/2\).
The proof uses the exact square expression for the principal symbol,
its highest Fourier coefficient, and two explicitly negative tests
of its cubic degeneration. It is a restriction on this particular
positivity test. It neither supplies an admissible weight nor bounds
the accumulated gain over the rest of the interval, and it does not
rule out the required attachment inequality.

This prevents treating the remaining distance to the endpoint as a
free source of cancellation. A quantitative comparison must keep both
the actual outgoing profile and a certified admissible weight.

### A sharper outgoing tail bound enlarges the available input ellipse

The [sharper tail theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_sharper_tail_and_ellipse.md)
proves \(|\mathcal L(a,Z)|<4/5\) on \(5/6\le a<1\) for the
original stable outgoing ratio. It excludes that circle using the
actual rotated complex characteristic, then selects the interior
branch by its zero limit at the terminating endpoint. The corresponding
finite ratios are at most \(81/100\) for sufficiently large levels,
uniformly through the last physical row and at both parities.

Together with the original middle action inequality this gives
\[
\mathcal E(a,Z)-\mathcal E(1/2,Z)
 \le-\frac{205}{1134}(a-1/2),\qquad1/2\le a\le1.
\]
The sharper piecewise lower bound for the loss is retained in equation
(15) of the note. Every coefficient of the degree-\(U\) Green insertion
therefore decays at least as \(e^{-205k/1134}\), up to a fixed
polynomial factor in the level. This proves a polynomial bound on the
closed spectral ellipse of height \(9/50\), including the original
highest coefficient. The complete attached input has rate
\(\mathcal E(1/2,Z)\) throughout that ellipse.

The larger input domain does not certify an inverse weight of the same

### The full Fourier operator can be inverted below the endpoint frequency

The [full-shift inverse theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_full_shift_low_frequency_inverse.md)
keeps all seven original leading shifts. Its symbol is positive on
the whole real angular circle for every fixed frequency band
\(|k|\le\alpha N\), \(\alpha<1/2\). A finite window argument
proves coercivity of the compressed matrix, including its
non-Hermitian coefficient variation. On a fixed even Hardy strip the
original finite operator differs from this leading-shift operator by
\(O(N^{-1})\), with no derivative or strip-width loss. This gives an
inverse for the corresponding compression of the actual operator.

For a polynomial input, the low Fourier coefficients of the residual
vanish exactly. Above the solved band, the operator contributes at
most eleven further cosine modes. All higher residual coefficients
are the original input coefficients. The eleven generated modes are
bounded as outputs of the inverse; they are not discarded or identified
with the input tail. The same polynomial test retains the original
three endpoint zeros, full Hermite transpose and parity forcing.

The [variable-frequency weight theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_variable_frequency_weight.md)
combines this inverse with the actual outgoing coefficient profile.
Writing \(E_Z(t)=\mathcal E(1/2+t,Z)\), it gives
\[
|\mathcal L_N(F_N^+)|\le C_\tau N^{A_\tau}
 \left\{e^{NE_Z(0)}+
 e^{N[\mathfrak M_3+\mathcal G_W(\alpha,Z)+\tau]}\right\},
\quad
\mathcal G_W=\max_{0\le t\le\alpha}(E_Z(t)+W(t))-W(\alpha).
\]
An explicit admissible weight is supplied, so this is an actual family
of finite estimates. Its quantitative adequacy is not established.
In particular the low input mode imposes the necessary condition for
this sufficient bound
\[
W(\alpha)>\mathfrak M_3+E_{Z_*}(0)-\Lambda.
\]
The small outgoing rate at the highest frequencies alone does not pay
for the generated boundary modes.

The [complex-symbol weight theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_complex_symbol_weights.md)
improves the admissibility test. If
\(p(u,t)=\sum_{\ell=-11}^{11}p_\ell(t)e^{i\ell u}\) is the full
principal symbol, the relevant real quadratic form involves
\[
\Re p(u-i\lambda(t),t)
 =\sum_\ell p_\ell(t)\cosh(\ell\lambda(t))e^{i\ell u}.
\]
Consequently a sufficient coefficient loss uses
\(\sum_\ell|p_\ell(t)|(\cosh(\ell\lambda(t))-1)\), which is
quadratic in a small weight. The proof also handles the reflection
at zero frequency and the long downward entries of the actual finite
operator. Direct positivity of the displayed complex-shifted symbol
is allowed when it gives a better bound than the coefficient estimate.
Neither criterion has yet produced the required strict action gap.

These three proofs are adopted after complete author, root and separate
source/proof readings, at hashes
\(\texttt{7b11e96c482d3c435e3fac0d9a488d0025aae31e2ec9d806949858031381b84c}\),
\(\texttt{09caa456c9f27ca22a91521a64c24ded42b4bad7546b591696daaaa82212bfcf}\),
and
\(\texttt{858546c9a2762175c32c1ef7b6dd62385051335a613665c9ff1848e0af711ff1}\).
No mathematical numerical evaluation was used. The endpoint band
\(\alpha=1/2\), arbitrary short partial fillings and the finite-exception
claim remain outside these theorems.

### An explicit cancellation exponent and a correlated boundary comparison

The [variable strip-loss estimate](research_mixed_next_outer_variable_loss_analytic_probe.md)
replaces the previous unspecified analytic constant by an explicit
integral of the original leading shift coefficients. If
\(\sum_{j=-3}^3a_j^0(u)v^j\) is the principal Laurent symbol of the
regularized adjoint and \(m_0=\sum_j a_j^0\), put
\[
K(s)=2\pi\sup_{|\Im u|=s}\sum_{j=-3}^3
 |j|\left|\frac{a_j^0(u)}{m_0(u)}\right|.
\]
For fixed \(0<r<R\) within the proved zero-free strip and any fixed
\(\eta>0\), the exact finite construction gives the residual exponent
\[
c_\eta(r,R)=\frac1e\int_r^R\frac{ds}{K(s)+\eta}.
\]
The strip losses vary with height. Their fixed positive reserve absorbs
the finite-level coefficient errors, while the exact finite transpose
retains the original endpoint conditions and both parity forcings.
The sufficient comparison is
\[
\mathcal P_{Z_*}(R)+\max\{0,\mathfrak M_3-c_\eta(r,R)\}<\Lambda.
\]
It remains unproved. In particular the explicit integral is not being
treated as an adequate bound merely because it is positive.

The [harmonic disk reduction](research_mixed_next_attachment_excess_harmonic_disks.md)
also preserves the correlation between the outgoing action and the
geometric action of the original \(343\) attachment. Its half-input
conditional phase extends holomorphically to \(0<\Re z<1/2\).
The original geometric output stays in that strip on both complete
external parameter disks, so the action excess
\[
\mathfrak E(b)=\mathfrak M_3+
 \Re\{\mathcal S_{\rm h}(z(b))-\Pi(b)\}
\]
is harmonic on neighborhoods of those disks. Here \(b\) is the next
incoming geometric coordinate, \(z(b)\) is the original third output,
and \(\Pi\) is the original attachment action with its absolute
normalization. At each eligible actual reference this excess is exactly
\(\mathfrak M_3+\Re\mathcal S(1/2,z_*)-\Lambda\).
Its maximum on either disk occurs on the boundary circle. Its derivative
is nonzero, but that fact gives no sign or quantitative margin. The
two boundary inequalities still require proof. The phase continuation
does not enlarge the domain of the finite outgoing estimate.

Both deductions are adopted after complete author, root and independent
source/proof readings. Their frozen hashes are respectively
\(\texttt{b5dba638946a0752318f8ac8cc54b327c79032b460a50ea8f6ea47d7c598c973}\)
and
\(\texttt{623ebfda0574d46a7e10e851d27a9fd48a8910543691a58a8d819a882878be47}\).
No mathematical numerical evaluation was used. The preceding goal turn

### The outgoing polynomial has an explicit nonzero leading coefficient

The [complex amplitude theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_complex_amplitude.md)
starts with the exact recurrence for the complete outgoing polynomial
and its literal terminal value \(C_{N-1,N}=1\). The corresponding
diagonal inverse satisfies a scalar Riccati recurrence. Its stable
solution admits a uniform first correction, with an \(O(N^{-2})\)
error through the last row. The proof propagates this error by an
actual contraction; distinct characteristic roots alone are not used
as a substitute for stability.

Multiplying the exact ratios and retaining the finite sine product
gives the complex leading coefficient. On the original middle interval,
with \(a=b/N\), the result is
\[
C_{b,N}(Z)=N^{-1/2}\sqrt{2\sin(\pi a)}\,
 \mathcal B(a,Z)e^{N\mathcal S(a,z_*)}
 \{1+O(N^{-1})\},\qquad Z=e^{-2\pi i z_*}.
\]
Here \(\mathcal S\) is the original selected action, including its
additive constant and logarithmic branch; \(\mathcal B\) is the
explicit nonvanishing exponential in equation (6) of that note.
The estimate is uniform on the actual outgoing parameter region.
At the boundary \(b=M-1\), the shift from \(a=1/2\) produces
the factor \(\exp(-\delta_N\partial_a\mathcal S)\), where
\(\delta_N=1\) at even levels and \(\delta_N=1/2\) at odd levels.
Fixed derivatives of the normalized relative error satisfy the same
\(O(N^{-1})\) bound on a smaller fixed complex neighborhood.

This establishes nonvanishing for the outgoing polynomial itself.
The remaining correction still contains the coherent sum
\[
\frac{1}{\kappa_N^2N}\sum_{b=M}^{N-1}(-q)^b\lambda_b
 C_{b,N}(Z_*).
\]
An individual \(O(N^{-1})\) relative error cannot simply be discarded
inside this further signed sum. Its required exponential bound remains
open, as do the free-boundary and partial-filling extensions.

after complete author and root source/proof readings and a separate

### The outgoing action enlarges the analytic domain of the exact insertion

The [action-weighted Green theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_action_weighted_green_ellipse.md)
proves that the stable outgoing ratio has modulus less than

\mathcal E(a,Z)-\mathcal E(1/2,Z)
 \le-\left(\frac18+\frac{53}{37800}\right)(a-1/2),
 \qquad1/2\le a\le1.
\]
Here \(\mathcal E\) is the original anchored outgoing action, equal
to the real part of the explicitly continued critical value.

The proof uses the exact complete Green column on \([M,D]\).
Its insertion has degree \(U\); the previous insertion on
\([M,D-1]\) had degree \(U-1\). The new highest coefficient is
computed explicitly and retained. Every Chebyshev coefficient obeys

|\widehat\nu^+_{k,N}(Z)|\le CN^A
 e^{N\{\mathcal E(1/2+k/N,Z)-\mathcal E(1/2,Z)\}}.
\]
Consequently \(\nu_N^+\) has polynomial norm on the closed ellipse
of height \(1/8\), with a fixed coefficient reserve. This replaces

             \{\mathcal E(a,Z)+h(a-1/2)\}.
\]
For \(h\le1/8\), this maximum equals \(\mathcal E(1/2,Z)\).
For larger heights it records the outgoing cost that must be paid
for a stronger analytic test. The exact complete-source reduction

### The global test extends to every fixed signed odd inner power

The [general odd-inner probe theorem](research_odd_inner_global_analytic_probe.md)
applies to every fixed odd integer \(n\), positive or negative, and
every fixed integer outer power \(p\), including zero. It constructs
the sufficient endpoint polynomial
\[
Q_{|n|,N}^{\rm rev}(z)
 =\prod_{\nu=0}^{|n|-1}(z-c_{U-\nu}).
\]
The original full jet maps show that each shift factor consumes at
most one of these endpoint zeros. This proves ordinary divisibility
for the entire conjugated adjoint, including the odd simple node,
without assuming the earlier three-power endpoint classification.

After this regularization the principal multiplier is positive on
the full real angular period. Its exact endpoint values are
\(16^{|n|}\) and \(4^{|n|+1}\). The global analytic construction
therefore gives an exponentially small residual for every such
fixed pair \((n,p)\), with constants allowed to depend on them.
The exact source forcing remains \(4\kappa^n/N^2\) at even levels
and zero at odd levels.

The final estimate retains the actual physical norm of
\(Q_{n,N}=TR^nF_N^{\rm cap}\). It does not supply a sharp geometric
ceiling for that norm or an adequate volume-rate comparison for a
new power. This is a general analytic ingredient for the short-filling
problem, not a volume theorem for a new knot class. The positive-symbol
argument does not cover even inner powers.

The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{e1034616122a11fc463a127bcf6dbff5ef8d0a9dac1c6b5b6c99c2848bca3cdf}\),
after complete author/root source and proof readings and a separate
full source/proof review. No mathematical numerical evaluation was used.

### A global analytic test gives a fixed coherent exponential saving

The [global analytic probe theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_global_analytic_probe.md)
constructs the adjoint test on the entire angular period. Ordinary
polynomial divisibility removes the grouped apparent poles at both
ends, and cosine-polynomial approximation extends that fact to even
periodic analytic functions. The principal multiplier is positive
on the whole real circle, including its two endpoints, so it has a
fixed zero-free complex strip.

The actual finite operator differs from multiplication by that
function by \(O((N\eta)^{-1})\) when a strip width \(\eta\)
is spent. A finite Neumann construction then gives an exponentially
small residual. Crucially, its test retains the three endpoint zeros
and the full Hermite transpose. There are no artificial interior
matching boundaries. For the actual Green insertion, the exact
identity is
\[
v_M=\mathfrak f_N\,\phi_N(R^3e_Mh_N)
       +\phi_N(R^3e_MQ_N^{\rm full}\rho_N),
\]
where the original forcing \(\mathfrak f_N\) is zero at odd levels
and \(4\kappa_N^3/N^2\) at even levels. The first term is
polynomially bounded and the residual \(\rho_N\) is exponentially
small on the whole physical interval. The resulting estimate is
\[
|v_M(Z)|\le C e^{N(\mathfrak M_3-\delta)},\qquad \delta>0,
\]
uniformly on the actual containing outgoing region and at both
parities. This saving is obtained for the signed original trace,
by using its exact recurrence before taking absolute values.

The absolute outgoing theorem below fixes the other factor's rate.
For the original interval \([M,D-1]\), its cutoff boundary can be
replaced by the complete boundary value as well: the same literal
low-index difference has rate at most \(1/200\), and the already
proved bound for \(v_M\) pays that replacement. This uses the old
test on \([M,D-1]\); it does not identify it with the different
test on \([M,D]\). Thus the remaining correction is bounded by
\[
C N^{-3/2}
 e^{N\{\Re\mathcal S(1/2,z_*)+\mathfrak M_3-\delta\}},
\]
up to the previously paid errors. The sufficient strict comparison
with \(\Lambda\) is stated at the front of this record.
Existence of a positive \(\delta\) does not establish that comparison.
Repeating the analytic construction does not amplify the saving
without spending further strip width or paying a larger-strip norm.

The global test theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{cb47c9d87949e276615443150b2da2260fec5bb09d3780039b90b322cd14eeb8}\),
after complete author/root source and proof readings and a separate
full source/proof review. No mathematical numerical evaluation was used.

### The original outgoing action now has absolute finite upper and lower bounds

The [absolute outgoing theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_absolute_anchor.md)
extends the resolvent comparison through the last physical row.
Near that row the omitted frozen link is small, with an error
\(O(N^{-3/2})\), so the relative \(O(N^{-1})\) ratio estimate
remains uniform. Multiplying the exact ratios backwards from
\(C_{D,N}=1\) gives
\[
|C_{b,N}(Z)|\asymp\frac{S_b}{N}
 \exp\left[-N\int_{\max(b/N,1/2)}^1\log|m(a,Z)|\,da\right].
\]
Here \(m\) is the first diagonal of the frozen half-line inverse,
and the two comparison constants are uniform. The sine product is
kept exactly, so the initial value has scale \(N^{-1/2}\), at both
parities, with no unspecified exponential normalization.

The [terminal action normalization](research_mixed_next_outgoing_action_terminal_normalization.md)
proves that this anchored rate is the original real critical action.
The critical point continues to zero as \(a\uparrow1\). Its shifted
argument may leave the original factorial strip, so the proof uses
the explicit upper-half-plane primitive
\[
g_+(v)=i\pi(v-v^2)
 -\frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{2\pi iv})-\pi^2/6}{2\pi i}.
\]
It agrees with the original primitive and has \(g_+(0)=g_+(1)=0\).
Thus the original critical action tends to zero at the terminal end,
and its real part is exactly the anchored recurrence integral.
No finite contour is asserted to cross the factorial wall.

Combining these two results with the finite relative-action theorem
gives, uniformly on the actual outgoing rectangle and for
\(M\le b\le D-L\),
\[
cN^{-1/2}e^{N\Re\mathcal S(b/N,z_*)}
 \le |C_{b,N}(Z)|
 \le CN^{-1/2}e^{N\Re\mathcal S(b/N,z_*)}.
\]
The same estimate holds at \(b=M-1\), with action evaluated at
\(1/2\). This proves an actual finite conditional growth rate and
nonvanishing. It does not identify a limiting complex leading
coefficient or estimate the signed inner-period contraction.

### The actual Green insertion is bounded on a fixed complex ellipse

The [finite Green localization theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_finite_green_localization.md)
uses the retained finite energy margin to improve inverse-entry
decay to \((126/125)^{-|i-j|}\), with the original sine-product
weights included. Applying this bound to the exact reverse-Newton
expansion of \(\nu_N\) gives exponentially decreasing approximation
errors in polynomial degree. The original double-node interpolation
has polynomial norm at both parities.

Consequently the Chebyshev coefficients of this particular insertion
obey \(|\widehat\nu_{k,N}|\le CN^5(126/125)^{-k}\). The full
polynomial is bounded by \(CN^6\) on the closed ellipse

analytic domain for a phase-preserving estimate; it does not remove
the nonzero central value or bound the signed trace by itself.

### The selected action now controls actual finite outgoing ratios

The [finite outgoing ratio theorem](research_mixed_next_finite_outgoing_ratio_transport.md)
starts from the complete polynomial
\[
C_{b,N}(Z)=\sum_{k=0}^{D-b}
 \frac{(r^b)^{-k}(r^{b+1};r)_k(rZ;r)_k}{(r;r)_k^2},
\qquad r=e^{-2\pi i/N},\quad D=N-1.
\]
Uniformly over the actual outgoing rectangle and both level parities,
\[
\frac{C_{b,N}(Z)}{C_{b-1,N}(Z)}
 =e^{\partial_a\mathcal S(b/N,z_*)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
\qquad M\le b\le D-L.
\]
The proof expresses the exact ratio as a trailing resolvent diagonal.
After including the sine-product metric, a constant half-line
recurrence approximates that diagonal to \(O(N^{-1})\). The inverse
decay controls the distant terminating row. The small half-line root
is then identified with the original selected branch, with the signed
and unsigned conventions kept distinct.

In particular the actual finite sequence satisfies
\[
\sqrt{s_b}\,|C_{b,N}/C_{b-1,N}|\le251/252
\]
for all sufficiently large levels. Its ratio to \(C_{M-1,N}\) has
the exponential rate
\(\Re[\mathcal S(b/N,z_*)-\mathcal S(1/2,z_*)]\), with uniform
upper and lower multiplicative constants. The absolute initial value
and the coherent inner-period contraction remain outside this theorem.

The proof is adopted at

after full author/source readback and a separate full source/proof
review. No mathematical numerical evaluation was used.

### Exact trailing determinants and a zero-free complete outgoing source

The [trailing determinant theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_trailing_determinants.md)
extends the finite energy through the natural last row \(D\), whose
upper coefficient is exactly zero. For every \(M\le b\le D\),
\[
\det(\mathcal J_{[b,D],N}-ZI)
 =(-1)^{D-b+1}\left(\prod_{h=b}^{D}A_h\right)C_{b-1,N}(Z).
\]
Thus the original complete finite polynomial has no zeros on a fixed
neighborhood of the actual outgoing region. The exact diagonal and
column Green identities retain every original scalar and phase.

The cutoff in the remaining lower-boundary value can also be replaced
by its complete value, with an exponential gap of \(1/7\) below
\(419/200\). The resulting boundary product is exactly
\[
qA_M a^{\rm all}_{M-1}(G_{[M,D]}^{\rm t}\lambda)_M
 =\sum_{i=M}^{D}\lambda_i a_i^{\rm all}.
\]
The determinant denominator cancels in this equality. Hence a
determinant norm alone cannot supply the missing cancellation estimate.

### The actual Green insertion retains the central positive-metric cost

The [boundary Green obstruction](research_mixed_next_boundary_green_positive_metric_obstruction.md)
writes the remaining test value as the original nodal trace
\[
v_M=\sum_{j=0}^{U}\mu_j Q_N^{\rm full}(c_j)\nu_N(c_j,Z),\qquad
\nu_N(\xi,Z)=\sum_{b=M}^{D-1}G_{b,M}(Z)(e_b/e_M)(\xi).
\]
At the last double node, literal Newton zeros give
\(\nu_N(c_U,Z)=G_{M,M}\). Strict finite accretivity bounds this
diagonal away from zero. The known complete inner packet there
therefore forces the best possible positive nodal Cauchy cost to be
at least \(cN^{-7/2}e^{N\mathfrak M_3}\), where
\(\mathfrak M_3>9/5\).

This rules out reducing that particular cost by choosing better
positive nodal weights, even weights depending on \(Z\). It does not
give a lower bound for the signed trace or for its product with the
outgoing boundary value. The finite energy also does not produce an
almost-invariant vector: the actual sequence carries its specified
boundary forcing.

### The complete remaining source is one lower-boundary observation

The [full-tail energy theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_full_tail_weighted_energy.md)
extends the outgoing inverse through index \(D-1\). A second scalar
rotation gives positive energy on the physical tail. Joining the two
rotations introduces only an explicitly bounded \(O(N^{-1})\)
commutator, and the estimates remain uniform where the sine factors
approach zero. The inverse norm remains at most \(20\sqrt{10}\)
in the original sine-product metric.

For the retained outgoing sum, the exterior value \(a_D\) is exactly
zero. The transformed forcing still has gap \(1/25\) on this longer
interval. The previously bounded high physical band can be restored
because its proof bounds the outgoing rows by absolute values before
the terminal observation. These facts give
\[
 \mathcal T_0[F_N](-2,Z_*)
 =I_{{\rm geom},N}
  +\frac{qA_Ma_{M-1}(Z_*)}{\kappa_N^2N}
       \sum_{i=M}^{D-1}G_{i,M}(Z_*)\lambda_i
  +O(e^{N(\Lambda-\epsilon_0)}),
 \qquad \epsilon_0>0.
\]
Here \(G=(\mathcal J_{[M,D-1],N}-Z_*I)^{-1}\),
\(a\) is the original signed outgoing sequence, and \(\lambda\)
is the original inner period vector. Thus both original Fourier
sectors and all source normalizations remain in the identity.
The one remaining product is \(a_{M-1}(G^{\rm t}\lambda)_M\).
Neither the inverse norm nor the available separate absolute-value
bounds suppress that product. No full-transfer asymptotic is asserted.

### The entire inverse-transformed cutoff forcing is now bounded

The [transformed forcing theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_transformed_forcing_bound.md)
applies the weighted outgoing inverse to the original inner period
vector. Its full cutoff forcing has rate at most
\(419/200-1/25\), strictly below the geometric rate

inverse; it does not reuse a bound for the old literal pairing.

The key improvement is a uniform bound on the original periods.
The complete physical inner values have rate at most

 \frac{419}{200}
 -\left(\frac{121}{63}+\frac7{60}+\frac1{200}\right)
 =\frac{83}{1575}>\frac1{20}.

After tolerances and polynomial factors, the theorem keeps gap

### Three exact compatibility conditions for the alternative adjoint construction

The [cokernel theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_three_cokernel_periods.md)
identifies the global image of the endpoint-constrained radical
adjoint as the common kernel of three explicitly normalized period
functionals. It gives an exact inverse on that image, without a norm
bound. The three relaxed recurrence solutions are distinct from the
full physical Hermite solution space, which has dimension zero at even
levels and one at odd levels.

The natural projection onto remainders supported at the three far
nodes is exponentially ill-conditioned on the odd subsequence, with
rate at least \(\mathfrak M_3-8/5>1/5\). This prevents that particular
projection from supplying a cheap generic bound; it does not rule out
a controlled inverse with another complement or a bound for the actual
coherent source. The theorem is adopted at

### The algebraic parametrization extends to every fixed crossing word

The [crossing-word conic theorem](research_crossing_word_principal_conic.md)
uses the original crossing and turn identities as polynomial
automorphisms of the trace surface. For every fixed word, its principal
period curve is the inverse image of the same explicitly parametrized
conic with trace \(-2\). This gives polynomial coordinates in one
parameter, together with a polynomial inverse on the curve.

The original Newton chart has rational inverse
\(x=-(V-2)/(X+Y-4)\), \(z=(X-2)/(Y-2)\). Its excluded
divisor is retained explicitly. The proof shows that no word's curve
is contained in that divisor, and that fixing any \(x\ne0,1\)
always leaves a nonzero polynomial equation of finite degree. Thus
the principal common-root construction need not be rebuilt for each
choice of fixed signed crossing powers. Branch selection, quantitative
separation, and the ordered finite-operator estimates remain separate
requirements; no new volume identity follows from this algebra alone.

### A positive energy estimate for the original outgoing equation

The [outgoing energy theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_weighted_energy.md)
uses an explicit unit-modulus row factor to make the off-diagonal
part of the signed outgoing recurrence self-adjoint in the positive
metric \(\sum_b S_b|a_b|^2\), where
\(S_b=\prod_{j=1}^b2\sin(\pi j/N)\). Its complex diagonal is
retained. A written trigonometric concavity estimate then gives a
uniform positive real part after one fixed scalar rotation.

For every middle Dirichlet interval, both parities, and every outgoing
parameter in the original containing region, the exact inverse has
norm at most \(20\sqrt{10}\) in this metric. Its entries satisfy
\[
 |(\mathcal J_I-Z)^{-1}_{i,j}|
 \le40\sqrt{10}\sqrt{S_j/S_i}\,
       e^{-\gamma|i-j|},\qquad \gamma=\log(1+1/2400).
\]
The sine-product ratio is essential. The source sequence is driven

periods produces a new test vector, so the old bound for the literal

### The common-root obstruction has an exact rational parametrization

The [rational trace theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_principal_rational_trace_locus.md)
replaces the implicit degree-eleven period equation by
\(xF(p)-D(p)=0\). Here \(x\) is the original point of the physical
middle arc, and
\[
 A=p(p^2+p+2),\quad B=p^2+1,\quad C=p+1,\qquad
 D=AB-C,\quad E=AD+B,\quad F=D+AE.
\]
Every solution corresponds to exactly one original period root;
the formulas are
\[
 x=D/F,\qquad z=-A^2/E^2,\qquad
 Z=F^2+1-AF/E.
\]
The proof reverses two trace recurrences from the conic where the
final trace is \(-2\). It checks every denominator: for physical
\(x\), none of \(A,D,E,F\) vanishes. It makes no assertion that
the eleven roots are distinct.

Consequently the full exceptional outgoing set is the image of the
explicit compact real algebraic locus \(D/F\in\mathcal X\), where
\(\mathcal X\) is the physical unit-circle arc. This is an exact
description of all common roots, including nongeneric ones. It does
not yet exclude the actual marked reference from that set, select
which roots can contribute to the finite sum, or supply a finite
operator estimate. Those are the questions now being tested against
the original conditional critical equation and its logarithmic lift.

 |H_N^{\rm all}|+|H_N|
 \le C_\tau N^{A_\tau}
            \exp\{N(\Lambda-17/10+\tau)\}.

### The endpoint and interior tests now have a proved global match

The [overlap theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_global_overlap_test.md)

### A generic parameter criterion for the principal elimination

The [principal Bezout criterion](research_mixed_next_outer_principal_bezout_criterion.md)
defines the exceptional outgoing set \(\Sigma\) by requiring a common
root of the two principal polynomials at some point of the compact
physical middle arc. Its nonzero leading coefficients give a uniform
root bound. Removing finitely many coefficient and discriminant
exceptions leaves finitely many analytic root branches; all exceptional
fibers are retained. Consequently \(\Sigma\) is compact, has planar
measure zero, and has empty interior.

For each compact set of outgoing parameters disjoint from \(\Sigma\),
the thirteen-dimensional Sylvester coefficient map supplies uniformly
bounded classical Bezout coefficients and their fixed derivatives.
This is a criterion in the ordinary complex parameter plane. It is
not complex Zariski openness, a density statement about knots, or proof
that the actual marked parameter avoids \(\Sigma\). It also leaves
the ordered finite-operator errors, transformed forcings, and endpoints
to be controlled.

### The constrained operator extends analytically through the complete color

The [central regularization theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_central_regularized_operator.md)
factors the test as
\(h=\prod_{a=U-2}^{U}(z-c_a)g\), and cancels the rapidly varying
radical factor using its exact shifted sine or cosine ratios. Individual
shift coefficients still have poles. The full operator on even analytic
functions nevertheless extends through them: ordinary polynomial
divisibility, approximation on the shifted circles, and the maximum
principle give a uniform proof at both physical parities.

The limiting multiplier is even and entire, has value \(4096\) at
the complete color, and is positive along the imaginary axis. On a
fixed small disk the actual grouped operator differs from multiplication
by that function by a Cauchy small-shift estimate. A finite Neumann
construction therefore gives a local test with the three endpoint zeros
exactly and a residual bounded by \(e^{-cN}\) times the full analytic
input norm.

The displayed guaranteed exponent does not yet pay the volume budget.
Its formula and radius choices give
\[
 c<\frac{\log4}{96\pi}<\frac1{192},
 \qquad E_*+\Re S_3(0,0)-\Lambda>\frac{287}{1500}.
\]
The second inequality uses the adopted lower bound
\(\Re S_3(0,0)>9/5\) and the exact definition
\(E_*=\Lambda-2413/1500\). Thus applying this particular residual
bound by absolute values with the uniform input ceiling \(E_*\)
does not prove a gap. This is a limitation of the certified estimate,
not a lower bound for the actual residual. A sharper estimate, retained
cancellation, or a sharper actual central input bound is needed.
The local theorem alone does not supply a global polynomial test.
The overlap theorem above now supplies that match, with all resulting
residual rows retained; it does not strengthen the exponent in this
comparison.

after complete author/root readback and separate full source/proof review.

 (X+Y+V-6)^2+(X-2)(Y-2)(V-2)=0.

### An exact algebraic alternative leaves eleven fixed-degree observations

The [finite Newton remainder theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_finite_newton_remainder.md)
uses the three endpoint conditions to define an ordinary polynomial
map
\[
 \mathfrak B_Nh=e_M^{-1}
       (R^{-3}\mathcal D_{3,N}^{\mathrm t}R^3)(e_Mh),
 \qquad
 h\in\prod_{a=U-2}^{U}(z-c_a)\,\mathbb C[z].
\]
The operator here uses its ordinary polynomial realization; the
division is exact before quotient reduction. It raises every nonzero
test's degree by eight, with a nonzero leading coefficient of modulus
one. Consequently every ordinary polynomial has a unique decomposition
\(H=\mathfrak B_Nh+\mathcal R\), with \(\deg\mathcal R\le10\).

For the actual insertion the construction stays below degree \(N\).
In the original normalized Newton basis it is a twelve-term descending
elimination, and the resulting original trace is exactly the parity
forcing plus eleven fixed-degree observations. All new endpoint defects
vanish on the constructed test. The remainder depends on all of the
outgoing coefficients, not just their first eleven values.

A written coefficient bound for this elimination is exponential and
too large for the required volume estimate. The fixed dimension of the
remainder therefore does not prove suppression or nonvanishing of the
original transfer. The theorem is adopted at

The [complete-color reduction](research_mixed_next_outer_complete_color_layer_reduction.md)
applies the actual interior inverse to the entire insertion \(H_N\).
For any fixed \(0<\delta<\pi/2\), it eliminates all intermediate
colors. The far colors and the far boundary of the adjoint identity
are controlled by the original full-kernel bound at rate \(8/5\).
The forcing term is also controlled. Their combined contribution to
the original transfer lies below its geometric rate by a fixed
positive amount.

What remains is an exact sum over \(0<u_j<\delta\). Its first three
coefficients have explicit corrections from the solved adjoint;
every other coefficient is the original \(H_N(c_j,Z_*)\). These
corrections have bounded norm relative to the original insertion
and exponentially decreasing dependence on distant interior data.
This follows from an entrywise decay bound for the actual banded
inverse, with no approximation to the source.

The layer still contains a number of colors proportional to \(N\).
Its coefficients have not acquired an analytic continuation merely
because their norms are bounded. Its signed sum is not yet estimated
below the geometric rate. In particular the three corrections must
be retained in any proposed central reflection or contour argument.
