### The positive-symbol calculation extends to every signed odd inner power

The [odd-crossing theorem](research_odd_inner_crossings_positive_symbol.md)
gives an exact square representation for the original principal
symbol. Writing \(C=\cos(u/2)\), \(k=\cot(u/2)\sin(v/2)\),
\(h=\cos(v/2)\), define
\[
 w_0=1,\qquad w_1=k-h,\qquad w_{n+1}=2kw_n+w_{n-1}.
\]
For every integer \(n\), the leading symbol is exactly
\[
 d_n(u,e^{iv})=4+4C^2(-1)^{n+1}w_n^2.
\]
The proof is the determinant identity for this two-term recurrence,
applied to the original ordered crossing recurrence. Thus every
fixed signed odd inner power has symbol at least four at every real
frequency. Any fixed integer outer power rotates the character and
preserves this inequality. The actual finite-width adjoint therefore
has the same interior inverse bound \(1/3\), for arbitrary nodal
inputs, with the exact parity forcing and all boundary terms retained.

The statement concerns fixed powers and fixed interior intervals;
its constants need not be uniform as either varies. It does not pay
the endpoint contributions. Even inner powers are not covered by
the positive-symbol conclusion: the power-two symbol already has
real zeros. The theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{7cb28ceade66edd8477715caec4a9204c2dcda0740e915fd6ccfcaeefa2c0eba}\),
after full root/author readback and separate actual-source/proof review.

### The interior adjoint now has an exact bounded inverse

The [interior inverse theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_interior_dirichlet_inverse.md)
turns the all-frequency symbol inequality below into a finite-matrix
estimate. On every fixed compact interval of angles inside \((0,\pi)\),
the actual weighted adjoint, compressed by zero extension of its test
sequence, satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\langle f,A_{I,N}f\rangle\ge3\|f\|_2^2,
 \qquad \|A_{I,N}^{-1}\|_{2\to2}\le\tfrac13
\]
for sufficiently large levels of either parity. The proof uses finite
Fourier orthogonality on sliding windows. Their exact overlap bounds
the error from the varying coefficients by a constant times
\(N^{-1/2}\).

The inverse applies to arbitrary nodal data, including the entire
actual polynomial insertion \(H_N\). It removes the approximation
residual and degree restriction from the earlier interior construction.
Exact summation by parts leaves the original parity forcing and at most
twelve outgoing boundary terms. The source values outside the interval
are retained; only the test sequence is extended by zero. Neither an
endpoint bound nor the desired full outer exponential estimate follows
from the interior norm bound.

The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{e1b713461bacdf263c07c3baa21de67960fae5e5e2735e5c400c009c987afddf}\),
after complete author/root readback and separate full source/proof review.
No numerical evaluation was used.

### Three exact endpoint conditions remove the derivative obstruction

The [full endpoint theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_adjoint_radical_endpoint_conditions.md)
computes the transpose on the original algebra, including the first
derivatives at double roots and the simple root at odd levels. For a
radical test \(R^3e_Mh\), its output remains in the radical if and only if
\[
                 h(c_U)=h(c_{U-1})=h(c_{U-2})=0.
\]
The three conditions concern values of the test polynomial, not its
derivatives. The proof gives the exact triangular endpoint map at each
parity and the full trace identity when these conditions are not imposed.
In particular agreement of shortened and complete source values cannot
be used to replace the complete source derivatives in that identity.

This identifies the finite endpoint obstruction, but does not show that
the actual insertion is in the resulting adjoint image or bound a
solution there. The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{9cde443d65bfdc41104ffe9e78ce4e4540ec998b53681923f99fd42a5d436d71}\),
after complete author/root readback and separate full source/proof review.

### A single algebraic square controls every real Fourier character

The [all-character symbol theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_all_character_symbol.md)
strengthens the constant-mode calculation below. The leading symbol
of the original seven-term operator satisfies
\[
                         d(u,\zeta)\ge4
           \qquad(0<u<\pi,\ |\zeta|=1).
\]
The proof keeps the correlation between the two shift symbols.
After a change of variables, the required difference of squares
is itself the square
\([2\cos u+2-P(P+1)^2]^2\); the physical range fixes the
sign of the unsquared expression. No numerical exclusion or
case-by-case root computation is used.

The exact outer weight ratio identifies the actual adjoint
character as \(-e^{3iu}\). A Fourier factor \(e^{ibu}\)
rotates this to \(-e^{i(3u+2\pi b/N)}\). The inequality therefore
includes both characters in every actual Chebyshev mode of
degree less than \(N/3\). Their finite coefficients have uniform
analytic bounds on a common fixed interior chart. The same leading
positivity holds if the fixed outer crossing power is changed,
while retaining this inner source.

The theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{c88ba98093fc147f5acfcf1790aa5b6f0f26edda6d741d2efc7c55315942e55e}\),
after complete author, root, and separate full source/proof reviews.
It supplies no endpoint estimate or global inverse by itself.

### The constant outer mode has an exponentially accurate interior reduction

The [constant-mode symbol theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_constant_mode_symbol.md)
computes the leading coefficient of the actual weighted adjoint,
including the crossing phase and the half-step of the physical grid.
It proves that coefficient is at least \(1/4\) throughout
\(0<u<\pi\). On every fixed compact interior interval it also
proves the actual finite coefficient bounds needed to construct
an analytic approximate solution of the adjoint equation.

The [local probe theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_local_adjoint_probe.md)
applies the existing Ward construction to those coefficients.
It produces a bounded test function with exponentially small
residual. Exact finite summation by parts then writes the original
constant-mode sum on that interval as its parity forcing, two
explicit endpoint contributions, and an error bounded by
\(e^{-c_JN}\) times the original sum of absolute values.
The forcing is zero at odd levels and bounded by \(256/(3N)\)
at even levels. The same construction gives an exact identity
for the error sequence of any approximate inner solution.

The endpoint contributions have not been suppressed. The positive
constant \(c_J\) depends on the fixed interval and analytic bounds;
it has not been shown large enough to meet the outer budget.
Shrinking intervals at the physical endpoints and characters with
degree proportional to \(N\) are outside these two statements.
Thus this is a proved local way to retain cancellation and correlate
errors, with the remaining terms explicit, rather than a completed
outer estimate.

The symbol theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{ef07c25bb23cf52763d8ef19d145be14b4abd69445df321b6cdb6d78697ee7cc}\),
and the actual local application at
\(\texttt{81acea1bc5255eaa72b6ac031d6b8b692ed1c40421c6beaf19e34b4118d7ec07}\).
Both have complete author/root readback and separate full
source/proof review. No numerical evaluation was used.

### A complete upper bound now covers the other physical colors

The [remaining-color theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_upper_physical_majorant.md)
proves, for every fixed \(\tau>0\),
\[
 |Q_N(u_j)|+|Q_N^{<<}(u_j)|
 \le C_\tau
 e^{N\{\Re S(\pi/2)-\kappa_0(u_j-\pi/2)+\tau\}},
 \qquad u_j\ge\pi/2,
\]
at every original double physical node, where
\(\kappa_0=\operatorname{arsinh}(\sin(\pi/8000))/\pi>0\).
Together with the nonzero asymptotic below for
\(0<u_j\le\pi/2\), this gives pointwise information on every
node used by the outer sum.

The proof fixes the inner contour at the critical height for
\(u=\pi/2\). The exact physical-row profiles decrease with the
outgoing angle, so that one contour works for the entire remaining
half-period, including the zero row near angle \(\pi\).
The full endpoint vertical, all removed first-normal samples,
and the complete first-edge restoration are bounded explicitly.
Both level parities and the odd central contribution are retained.
No critical-point continuation into the new outgoing interval is
needed for this upper bound.

The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{6fd4d8c0d67e184312f0d1106b112ac00a965f7d40716aae8ac7b502eb709c18}\),
after complete author, root, and separate source/proof reviews.
It is not a nonzero asymptotic for the new colors, and its rate
does not meet the outer budget near \(\pi/2\), as proved below.
The remaining task is a bound for the coherent weighted sum,
with its actual insertion and error sequence retained.

### The physical inner values now satisfy a closed seven-term equation

The [exact recurrence theorem](research_mixed_next_physical_inner_seven_term_recurrence.md)
gives a fixed-order difference equation for the original complete
inner output. Its forcing is exactly zero at odd levels and
\(4\kappa_N^3/N^2\) at even levels. The ordinary polynomial
equation also retains a scalar multiple of the physical relation;
it is not silently made homogeneous away from the physical nodes.

At interior double nodes the complete and shortened outputs have
identical values. Those actual values therefore obey the same
seven-term recurrence. The endpoint statement remains the full
polynomial equation, including its original first derivatives at
double roots. No agreement of the shortened and full derivatives
is inferred from agreement of their values.

The theorem also computes the exact adjoint for the complex weights
in the remaining outer sum. Summation by parts retains both endpoint
contributions. Applying this identity to an approximation and the
exact sequence gives an equation for their error with its actual
residual and boundary data. This supplies constraints on the error
sequence beyond the pointwise relative asymptotic. It does not yet
give a bounded adjoint inverse or an exponentially small outer error.

The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{49cd08c5759bd6669d3cbf1a7e661d60188639c9added0c973659c4723d0a21a}\),
after complete author, root, and separate source/proof reviews.

### A positive self-adjoint norm cannot supply the required outer bound

The [norm obstruction](research_mixed_next_outer_self_adjoint_norm_obstruction.md)
classifies every positive inner product that makes the reduced
recurrence operator self-adjoint. Each is diagonal in the distinct
physical-node basis. Even after optimizing all its weights, the
product of source and dual observation norms is at least the sum
of the absolute nodal contributions. An actual node approaching
the complete color has exponential rate greater than \(9/5\),
which exceeds the outer budget \(B_f=77/50+\pi/50\).
Thus this entire class of Cauchy--Schwarz estimates is insufficient,
already for the constant outer mode. This conclusion does not
lower-bound the signed outer sum.

The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{ddad67e85205d7d637ea4ab156f4e67938aacdc6aaed86213e8128d55d8a1849}\),
after complete author, root, and separate source/proof reviews.

The obstruction is not confined to colors near zero. The
[midpoint action theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_midpoint_action.md)
proves the strict original-phase inequality
\[
                        \Re S(\pi/2)>B_f+1/50.
\]
It uses a positive second-edge height curvature that the earlier
action floor did not need. Together with the physical-color
asymptotic and exact outer weights, it gives an absolute nodal
contribution exceeding \(e^{N(B_f+1/100)}\) near \(\pi/2\).
Consequently removing the small-color endpoint does not make
termwise absolute estimates sufficient. Cancellation must also
be retained in the middle of the color interval.

This proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{34442eec4aa7f7a77a9a2c0dcdaac74776fceb9b7d92456d64d9d664c46e6157}\),
after the complete author/root readback and separate full review.
These two obstructions concern proposed bounds, not the truth
of the volume identity or the size of the actual inserted sum.

### The complete inner asymptotic now holds at physical colors in half the interval

The [physical-color theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_physical_outgoing_packet.md)
proves the full inner asymptotic
\[
 Q_N(u)=C_{N,3}N^{-3/2}\mathcal A(u)e^{NS(u)}
                         (1+O(N^{-1}))
\]
uniformly at the original double sampling nodes
\(u=\pi-(2j+1)\pi/N\) with
\(0\le j\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\) and
\(0<u\le\pi/2\), and separately at \(u=0\).
The original coefficient satisfies
\(\inf_{[0,\pi/2]}|\mathcal A|>0\). Both level parities,
the full first edge, and the original Hermite trace are included.

At these nodes, the second shortened kernel is exactly a physical
row polynomial. Its previously established slit-plane asymptotic
therefore bounds the last right-hand contour contribution with the
correct two-variable phase. The physical grid has a half-step:
the row profile corresponds exactly to \(u+\pi/N\); returning
to \(u\) changes the action by only \(O(N^{-1})\).
A horizontal phase gap and a vertical monotonicity argument make
that entire remaining contribution exponentially smaller than the
nonzero geometric term. This completes the inner sum on the stated
nodes; it is more than an isolated stationary-point calculation.

The theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{c43064953e7d3bfa92a6ecc05725719661e45d0b6bfca76fe1b78a28c68de4f3}\),
after the complete author/root readback and separate full source/proof
review. No numerical evaluation was used.

The result does not include outgoing nodes above \(\pi/2\), a complex
neighborhood of the outgoing variable, or outgoing derivatives.
Moreover, its pointwise relative \(O(N^{-1})\) error cannot be passed
through an oscillating outer sum without a bound on the resulting
weighted error. The outer sum and stability under arbitrary fixed
short fillings remain unproved.

### An exact recurrence can be transported through the outer sum

The [operator transport theorem](research_mixed_next_short_kernel_outer_operator_transport.md)
proves an exact identity for the full inner and outer Hermite traces.
An inserted polynomial in the outer spectral variable can be moved
to the inner variable as the same polynomial in the conjugated
difference operator. The actual outer factor annihilates the
shortened kernel's recurrence forcing at both parities.

This identity retains four explicit endpoint integrals when applied
to an open angular path. They cannot be discarded: a fixed-path
current has degree at most \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\), whereas every
nonzero polynomial annihilated by the outer factor has degree at
least \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor\). Thus the recurrence forcing vanishes
under the outer observation, but a nonzero open-path current does
not vanish for that algebraic reason. Bounds or an exact signed
cancellation for the retained terms are still needed.

The theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{38df410463523eb05f3e9bed696f63bdbfda20ff03b72950a9664945d8c08068}\),
after complete author, root, and separate source/proof reviews.
It supplies no bound for polynomials in the difference operator
whose degree grows with the level.

### For general complex outgoing values, one explicit inner current remains

The [single-current assembly theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_single_remaining_current.md)
is adopted at
\(\texttt{2c5be7138aed7dabbb06f04010c602ee095fa8ceb62ec213e75e4d628aa95421}\).
It gives the original full-first-edge inner trace as
\[
 Q_N(u)=C_{N,3}N^{-3/2}\mathcal A(u)e^{NS(u)}
                  (1+O(N^{-1}))
          +\mathcal R_N(u)+O(e^{N(\Re S(u)-\epsilon)}),
 \qquad \inf_{\mathcal U_+}|\mathcal A|>0 .
\]
Here \(\epsilon>0\) is uniform, and the only unestimated
current is
\[
 \mathcal R_N(u)=
 -\frac{N^2C_{N,3}}{\pi i}
 \int_{\pi/2-iH_*(u)}^{\,5\pi/6-i/10}
       g_N^{<<}(t,u)W_N(t)\,dt .
\]
The integral can follow any path in the open lower half-plane;
its value is path-independent there. The source remains exactly
the product of the two kernels ending at
\(U=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\). The complete crossing, Fourier
denominator, both parity conventions, and the odd central
contribution remain in the derivation.

A uniform exponential gap for this current would complete the
inner asymptotic throughout the complex outgoing domain. Such a gap
is now proved on the physical subset stated above, but remains
unproved for general complex outgoing values. The outer trace and
stability under arbitrary fixed short partial fillings are still
subsequent requirements. The entries below retain the intermediate
results and their individual scopes, including earlier descriptions
of the remaining work that the later theorems have partly settled.

### The negative middle interval and the right far region are controlled

The [mixed-height edge theorem](research_mixed_next_shortened_edge_mixed_height_packet.md)
proves the original shortened-edge Gaussian uniformly while the
first angular height changes sign. The saddle can pass through the
real sampling line. The proof moves the unweighted main integral
through that saddle and estimates both complete Fourier corrections
on separate fixed contours.

Two new comparisons make this possible: the real row profile has
one maximum, and a right-boundary local maximum can occur only in
the half-plane opposite the saddle. Together with the original
cut and endpoint bounds, these facts give the required main path.
The coefficient, phase constant, endpoint terms and both level
parities are retained.

The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{fb885dd5c25d49f2b0cdf03eb8d2ce05d303bb90fcc8523cb800832b940c4b07}\).
Its final section pays the previously missing negative middle
angular interval. The signed-box first-edge comparison transfers
that absolute bound to the unchanged product with both kernels
shortened.

The [right far-region theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_right_far_region.md)
also pays the complete path
\[
 5\pi/6-i/10\longrightarrow T_N-i/10
                          \longrightarrow T_N-ih_c
\]
with gap \(1/50\), including its full original trace prefactor.
It uses the actual slit-plane kernel estimates, a calibrated
real complete-end bound, and the stronger action floor.
The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{d610fce6cd5f9e4786606796bff247b88e48e6021f85b3542178a4d3dc93ba9e}\).

The only angular contribution still unestimated in this inner
decomposition runs from \(\pi/2-iH_*(u)\) to \(5\pi/6-i/10\).
Its integrand is the literal product of the two shortened kernels
with the original crossing and Fourier denominator. The outer
trace and arbitrary fixed short partial fillings remain later
obligations.

### A stronger action bound pays a fixed strip of second-edge rows

The [action-floor and top-row theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_action_floor_and_top_rows.md)
proves
\[
 \Re S(u)>\frac32+\frac{853}{63000}
                    \qquad(u\in\mathcal U_+).
\]
It keeps the separate complete-end return estimate in the comparison
at \(\pi/2-iH_*(u)\), rather than replacing both edge terms by the
same weaker real-corner bound.

This larger margin has a finite-source consequence. There is a fixed
\(\delta>0\) such that every subset of the second-edge rows
\[
 \left\lceil N(1/2-\delta)\right\rceil
                   \le j\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1
\]
has absolute traced contribution at most
\(C e^{N(\Re S(u)-1/20)}\). The original complete terminal
insertion theorem supplies the bound; uniform continuity of the
zero-safe Newton potential at its half index controls the insertion
and outgoing coefficients. The estimate holds with either the full
or the shortened first edge. Arbitrary-subset first-edge tail errors
also have the stronger gap \(1/4\).

The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{0cb4e2f7d2c77b4e6a0c60391a00cecad02b11da8800980c3280c1b62d161adb}\).
The further second-edge cutoff is an optional exact traced reduction.
It has not replaced the shortened-kernel integrand used in the
current contour decomposition. In particular no previous partial
Gaussian is transferred to the further-truncated integrand without
a separate proof.

### The complete left connection is controlled

The [left-connection theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_left_connector.md)
bounds the full path from the original negative far endpoint down
to the critical height and then horizontally to
\(-\pi/2-iH_*(u)\). Its absolute current, including the original
\(N^2/\pi\) prefactor and exact Fourier denominator, is at most
\(C e^{N(\Re S(u)-1/5)}\). The full vertical part has the stronger
gap \(1/2\). Both level parities are included.

The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{0981672faffc8d4cb94848a59ce01eeeb9627110e05fed16a2664ba8c27f930f}\),
after complete author/root readback and separate source/proof review.
It uses actual finite-kernel upper bounds, not only the phase
comparison. The remaining unestimated pieces of the inner contour
are the middle negative horizontal and the right connection.

### The shortened kernels have a global bound from their physical rows

The [slit-plane source theorem](research_mixed_next_first_short_edge_slit_plane_bound.md)
continues the normalized logarithmic asymptotics of every physical
row to \(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\). The finite Jacobi
determinants put all row zeros on the removed real ray. Their
logarithmic derivative bounds give compact normal families, and
the previously proved Riccati normalization determines every limit,
including both limiting endpoint rows.

Exact interpolation at the double physical nodes then proves, for
every fixed tolerance \(\tau>0\),
\[
 \sup_{v\in\mathbb R}|K_N^<(t,v)|
       \le C_\tau e^{N(\Re\psi(t,0)+\tau)} .
\]
The first angle can run through any fixed positive compact rectangle
below \(\pi\), with height at most one. Polynomial continuation in
the second angle adds at most \(|\Im v|/2\) to this rate. These are
bounds for the actual finite polynomials at both parities; they do
not assert a nonzero asymptotic at a complex second angle.

The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{efe1c1c89bb01f5a0aca9468917595926648780bca265f73000ede095f432e7b}\).
The separate
[shortened-source transfer](research_mixed_next_inner_three_short_pair_source_transfer.md),
adopted at
\(\texttt{a835236285224a9df4ac41451c84882609b44b223eaa2c7c359f0f48518bccae}\),
retains the already proved partial Gaussian, center, far-negative
and complete endpoint estimates after shortening the first edge.
Its exact remaining-current decomposition is equation (30).
The left-connection theorem above now pays one of those three
currents.

### The first edge can be shortened after taking its original trace

The [first-edge tail contraction](research_mixed_next_inner_three_first_edge_tail_contraction.md)
proves a new exact reduction. Write
\[
 Q_N(u)=\phi_N\!\left[R_N^3K_N(\,\cdot\,,-2)
                         K_N^<(\,\cdot\,,-2\cos u)\right],
\]
and let \(Q_N^{<<}\) have both kernels replaced by the finite sum
ending at \(U=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\). On the actual outgoing
parameter domain,
\[
 Q_N(u)=Q_N^{<<}(u)
                 +O\!\left(e^{N(\Re S(u)-1/300)}\right).
\]
The functional \(\phi_N\) is still the full original Hermite trace.

At even levels, every deleted first-edge row is in the radical
and its traced contribution is an explicit sum of physical values
with bounded coefficients. At odd levels, rows above the middle
vanish at the complete endpoint. The remaining middle row has a
separate exact contraction through the double nodes and the simple
node \(-2\); the latter has coefficient one. The absolute sum of
all these terms has rate at most \(b_2+2/3<\Re S(u)-1/300\),
after absorption of polynomial factors.

The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{b31ac2d1cbf5f0e3ab4b71b36af9718151bced51e6959ee32b26ccf7fac5dfe6}\).
The remaining product has ordinary spectral degree \(2U<N\).
This reduction removes the first edge's high-degree growth from
the inner-contour problem. It is a traced estimate, not a
pointwise equality of the old and new kernels, and its error has
not yet been passed through the outer trace.

### The positive phase is controlled up to the far angular cut

The [positive-horizontal phase extension](research_mixed_next_inner_three_positive_horizontal_phase_extension.md)
continues the original phase with its constant and logarithmic
charge unchanged to every fixed positive angle below \(\pi\).
It proves quantitative horizontal concavity through \(2\pi/3\)
and a strictly negative horizontal derivative thereafter.
Thus the selected inner critical point is the unique maximum
on the entire positive horizontal, including the original far cut.

The proof is adopted at
\(\texttt{a643c0878b4a4c23010f3d15731e72907c55cb0f19639b9dba922b57235f4e1c}\).
This settles the phase comparison along that path. The actual
finite kernels beyond \(\pi/2\), and the paths from that horizontal
to the far endpoints, still need source estimates. The phase
inequality alone does not estimate those contributions.

### A nonzero contribution from the original inner integral

The [partial inner-integral theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_partial_horizontal_packet.md)
combines the positive-horizontal estimate and the center bound. Let
\(\mathcal P_N(u)\) be the original angular integral along
\(-\eta-iH_*(u)\le t\le\pi/2-iH_*(u)\), oriented from left to right.
Uniformly on the specified compact outgoing-parameter domain,
\[
 \mathcal P_N(u)=C_{N,3}N^{-3/2}\mathcal A(u)e^{NS(u)}
                      (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad \mathcal A(u)\ne0 .
\]
Here \(S(u)\) is the critical value of the original inner phase,
\(C_{N,3}\) is its original scalar of modulus one, and
\(\mathcal A(u)\) is the explicitly computed Gaussian coefficient.
Its modulus is uniformly bounded away from zero.

This statement concerns the actual finite kernels and the exact
Fourier denominator at both parities. It controls an entire
specified part of the original integral, including the center
and every higher Fourier term. It does not yet give an asymptotic
for the full inner trace: contributions from the unestimated
parts could still cancel it.

The adopted proof is frozen at
\(\texttt{03482ac7f06246db3c162965360e8f3ff596b1339b1b07522cc4947f149aa8ad}\).

### Part of the negative interval is also controlled

The [far-negative source theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_far_negative_source.md)
estimates the full angular integrand on
\[
 t=-a-iH_*(u),\qquad 5\pi/12\le a\le\pi/2 .
\]
Its absolute integral, including the original trace prefactor,
is at most \(C\exp(N(\Re S(u)-1/10))\). The proof continues the
exact finite polynomial from a real interval and retains the
odd-level cutoff correction. It does not assume that a local
complex asymptotic remains valid at the reflected angle.

The adopted proof is frozen at
\(\texttt{c33f32be5385f98eea72a77eab211bf77229007d905b3edf598e753b4e93b057}\).
For the full inner trace, the unresolved negative middle interval
is now \(\eta<a<5\pi/12\). The connections from the controlled
horizontal segments to the far endpoints also remain to be
estimated. The outer trace and stability under arbitrary fixed
short partial fillings are later obligations; neither follows
from these two results.

### The positive inner horizontal and its center are controlled

The [positive-horizontal edge theorem](research_mixed_next_shortened_edge_positive_horizontal_packet.md)
extends the complete shortened-edge asymptotic to
\[
 t=a-iH_*(u),\qquad a_L\le a\le\pi/2,
 \qquad u\in\mathcal U_+,
\]
for any fixed \(a_L>0\). The saddle may leave the first quarter.
The proof uses the two sublevel components to choose its upper
descent paths, and a new complete lower rectangle to bound all
lower Fourier terms. It retains the original saddle sheet and
has the simpler coefficient
\[
 a_e(t,u)=\frac1{4\sqrt{D_0}\,W^{1/4}},\quad
 D_0=A+B-AB,\quad W=AB/D_0,\quad
 A=\cos^2(t/2),\ B=\cos^2(u/2).
\]
The powers are fixed on their right half-planes and agree with
the original normalization.

The theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{2ec3d95d28876b2fb3c6129303b698c8f190f02fafe8b70023465b66b635be7e}\),
after author readback and complete root and separate source/proof
reviews. Together with the existing full first-edge bound, it
controls the actual two-factor source at its original phase
throughout every such positive horizontal interval.

The [center continuation theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_center_bridge.md)
then bounds the whole original angular integrand on a fixed
interval \(-\eta\le\Re t\le\eta\) at height \(-H_*(u)\).
Its proof uses the exact degree bound \(d_N<3N/2\).
After setting \(x=\tan(a/2)\), multiplication by
\((1+x^2)^{d_N}\) turns the source into a polynomial of degree
less than \(3N\). Chebyshev continuation from a fixed positive
interval gives an arbitrarily small exponential cost across
the center. Restoring the exact Fourier denominator cancels
the height cost and leaves a uniform strict gap.

This theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{0ddff6c7a588128a32f862e113f4e8253d9da6f3e56a4fc3bc5955cab02f7097}\),
after full root source/proof readback and separate review.
It estimates the actual finite source at both parities without
assuming a Gaussian expansion at a wire saddle on the real
sampling line. The odd central physical contribution remains
in the original trace.

The far-negative theorem above controls another part of the
negative angular interval. The remaining central-contour
obligations are its middle interval and the connections from
the controlled horizontal to the far endpoints.
The outer trace and arbitrary fixed short partial fillings
remain subsequent problems.

### The complete inner endpoint terms are now bounded

The [inner boundary theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_far_samples_and_verticals.md)
proves a uniform lower bound \(\Re S_3(0,u)>79/63\) on
\(\mathcal U_+\). All original angular samples sufficiently close
to \(-\pi\) or \(\pi\), including their first derivatives, have
absolute sum below this action by a fixed positive amount.
Both complete endpoint vertical integrals satisfy the same
comparison. The final gap is \(1/500\), at both level parities.

The proof uses the full first edge and the exact shortened second
edge. Uniform bounds for the Newton polynomials control their
values on a fixed far spectral interval. Markov's inequality
controls the required derivatives, and polynomial continuation
controls the small vertical segments. No cancellation within
these boundary terms is assumed.

The theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{15a38af35c84cacc940f11a7c22675748d5f9da7fc19424573116dcdbf77c685}\),
after author readback and complete root and separate source/proof
reviews. It leaves the exact lower angular contour integral;
its interior, including the odd-level central contribution,
has not been discarded or estimated by the boundary theorem.

### The inner saddle and its right-hand contour segment

The [horizontal concavity theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_horizontal_concavity.md)
proves, for the original reduced phase
\[
 \Phi(t,u)=\psi(t,0)+\psi(t,u)+\frac{3it^2}{4\pi}-it,
 \qquad
 \Re\Phi_{tt}<-\frac1{4\pi},
\]
throughout the independent box
\(0\le\Re t,\Re u\le\pi/2\),
\(-1\le\Im t\le0\), \(-1/2\le\Im u\le0\).
At the actual critical height \(H_*(u)\), this gives
\[
 \Re\Phi(a-iH_*(u),u)
 \le \Re S_3(0,u)-\frac{(a-a_*(u))^2}{8\pi}.
\]
The phase theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{a1e8eb57a7cf867b58c607b5c8d590c5a3ba00d3cba44642fd42456ff4c3298f}\).

The separate [right-segment source theorem](research_mixed_next_shortened_edge_right_segment_packet.md)
extends the complete shortened-edge asymptotic along the horizontal
from the actual saddle to a fixed real part \(a_R<\pi/2\) beyond
every \(a_*(u)\). It retains all finite terms and gives independent
complex neighborhoods and normalized derivatives. The full first
edge remains eligible there by its existing complete-end theorem.
This result is adopted at
\(\texttt{7feaa5b8137ca887b688a0b170bb4f1fd47aa39b628118cc9fa23193e007a2b7}\).
Both adoptions include author readback and complete root and
separate source/proof reviews.

Together these results estimate the actual angular integral on
that segment and a fixed short extension to the left of the saddle.
It has the nonzero local Gaussian coefficient written in the
outer-fold note, while its portion a fixed distance to the right
is exponentially smaller. The exact angular Fourier denominator
is retained; its higher charges have an additional height penalty.
This is a contribution from part of the inner contour. The later
positive-horizontal and center theorems above control its positive
left continuation and a neighborhood of the imaginary axis.
The remaining negative angular portion and the connectors to the
far endpoints still need finite-source bounds. The full inner
trace, outer contraction and arbitrary-short partial-filling
theorem remain open.

### The negative horizontal has a strict phase gap

The [negative-horizontal phase theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_negative_horizontal_phase.md)
continues the original edge phase to the signed first-angle box,
with its principal returns, closed derivative form and constant
unchanged. A uniform bound on \(\psi_{tt}\), together with the
quadratic crossing factor, gives
\[
 \Re\Phi(-a-iH,u)-\Re\Phi(a-iH,u)
                  \le-\frac{5aH}{7\pi}.
\]
At the actual critical height, horizontal concavity then yields
\[
 \Re\Phi(-a-iH_*(u),u)
 \le\Re S_3(0,u)
       -\frac{(a-a_*(u))^2}{8\pi}
       -\frac{5aH_*(u)}{7\pi},
 \qquad 0\le a\le\pi/2 .
\]
The two losses give a uniform positive gap, including at \(a=0\).
The theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{fd3f89e30e108e1b9911d0bcb55f0948b41b2c91ffa3aadefa894ea4224fd347}\),
after author readback and complete root and separate source/proof
reviews.

This phase comparison does not yet estimate the corresponding
finite second edge: after using evenness, its two angular heights
have opposite signs. A bound for that mixed-height finite kernel
is still required. The full first edge already has a polynomial
upper bound at its original action on the larger box, from
[the complete-edge gap theorem, Corollary 3](research_internal_pair_complete_edge_gap.md);
its bound at the reflected first angle follows from its real
polynomial coefficients and the calibrated Schwarz symmetry.

### The complete shortened second-edge asymptotic is established

The [upper-continuation theorem](research_mixed_next_shortened_edge_upper_continuation.md)
closes the remaining contour estimate for this edge. For
\[
 u\in\mathcal U_+
 =\{0\le\Re u\le\pi/2,\ -1/2\le\Im u\le0\},
\]
let \(t=t(u)\) be the original selected cubic branch. The original
finite sum now has the uniform asymptotic
\[
 K_N^<(t,u)
 =\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1}
           e_j(-2\cos t)e_j(-2\cos u)
 =N^{-3/2}a_e(t,u)e^{N\psi(t,u)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad a_e(t,u)\ne0 .
\]
Here \(\psi\) and \(a_e\) are the original action and Gaussian
coefficient, with their constants and branches unchanged. The
estimate holds at both parities and on a fixed open neighborhood
of the compact graph \(\{(t(u),u):u\in\mathcal U_+\}\) in two
independent complex variables. Every fixed derivative of
\(N^{3/2}e^{-N\psi}K_N^<-a_e\) is \(O(N^{-1})\) on a smaller
fixed neighborhood.

The new ingredient is a planar sublevel argument. The continuous
real factorial rate is subharmonic across its cuts. Its two side
boundaries each have one connected region below the saddle value,
and no other point can be a local minimum. The maximum principle
then forces the two descending saddle sectors into different
components. The right sector therefore connects to the already
bounded right endpoint. Compactness gives paths with a uniform
gap, which bound the entire upper Fourier denominator. No
positivity of the quantum summands is assumed.

The theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{b655d894a75f0744b5935f781996a386d9e78f1fe4a00ab503978842f2aa2542}\),
after author readback and complete root and separate source/proof
reviews. In particular this finite kernel is nonzero for all
sufficiently large levels, and its logarithmic growth divided
by \(N\) converges uniformly to \(\Re\psi\) on the stated compact
family. This conclusion concerns the edge kernel, not the full
Kashaev invariant.

The next missing theorem concerns the complete inner angular
trace. Its local saddle now has both required edge asymptotics
on an independent complex neighborhood. Its removed samples
and endpoint integrals are bounded by the theorem above; the
remaining interior still requires a global bound. The outer contraction and stability
under arbitrary fixed short partial fillings remain further
obligations. No new knot-family volume theorem or finite-exception
theorem follows yet.

### An exact fold separates the two outer estimates

The [outer fold and inner-source formula](research_mixed_next_outer_fold_and_inner_source_lift.md)
is adopted at
\(\texttt{5aab98669016b0de450270300ca8e678e26c4862b6ba8b9e222cd8110e3f9ed9}\),
after author readback and complete root and separate source/proof
reviews. Oddness converts the negative lower outer contour exactly
into a positive upper contour with the opposite orientation.
The center connector vanishes because the outer annihilating
factor removes its pole, including at odd levels. The complete
right endpoint integral remains present with its original sign.

On a positive upper point \(u=a+iH\), the explicit outer factors
supply the decay
\[
              e^{-N\{H/2+3aH/(2\pi)\}},
\]
apart from a fixed polynomial factor and the unchanged inner
kernel and outgoing polynomial. This permits a different estimate
on that half; it does not require a second geometric asymptotic
there if an absolute bound suffices. Such a bound is still missing.
Degree continuation alone can use up the \(H/2\) saving.

The same note writes out the full inner angular trace. Its
odd-level central pole remains, since this trace has no outer
annihilating factor. The new edge theorem supplies the hypothesis
of its local Gaussian calculation. The subsequent inner boundary
theorem bounds its removed derivative samples and complete endpoint
integral; the remaining interior contour still needs estimates.

### The contour reduction and its endpoint estimates

The [real-cut obstruction](research_mixed_next_first_quarter_real_cut_obstruction.md)
proves that the former internal real cut cannot be estimated separately
at the geometric rate. At the actual complete parameter, its real
action is strictly larger than the selected saddle action for every
eligible cut. This is a failure of that proposed estimate, not a
counterexample to the volume identity.

The [joined-contour formula](research_mixed_next_shortened_edge_joined_contour.md)
removes this artificial cut exactly. It expresses the original finite
second-edge sum as its known local Gaussian integral, two continued
contour integrals, and endpoint terms already bounded below the
selected exponential rate. It retains every original Fourier correction
and applies at both parities. The obstruction and the joined formula
have completed author readback and separate full source/proof reviews.

The [entire lower continuation](research_mixed_next_shortened_edge_lower_continuation.md)
is now bounded below the selected exponential rate by a fixed
positive amount. The proof uses the decay of the exact lower Fourier
denominator and does not assume an estimate for the upper continuation.
It is adopted at
\(\texttt{79a0e9fb0c9b8d22819cc0acbf4495664f2c6608ca6430bbde9a2c2c0732503c}\),
after author readback and complete root and separate source/proof
reviews. All Fourier corrections and both level parities are included.

The
[upper-region inequalities](research_mixed_next_shortened_edge_upper_terminal_regions.md)
now prove horizontal decrease at every height for \(1/3\le\Re y\le1/2\),
and along both cuts starting at numerator zeros. They also prove
that the incoming angular depth exceeds the outgoing depth and
bound the right boundary below the saddle action up to the height
of the outgoing zero. These results are adopted at
\(\texttt{b1b8cac36a0e6bb16252b0327311b6fe3aeec17fde13abe3d1aafd32682076a3}\),
after author readback and complete root and separate source/proof
reviews. They do not assign a starting action bound to either zero.

These inequalities supply the cut and endpoint information used
in the completed upper-continuation theorem above. The full inner
trace and central outer contour estimate are separate questions.

### Jensen's inequality gives the strongest current outgoing weights

The [Jensen extension](research_mixed_next_middle_jensen_spectral_ellipse.md)
improves the variable-ellipse estimate below. Instead of bounding
the spectral logarithm by its linear argument, average inside
the concave logarithm first. With
\[
 c=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2\pi},\qquad
 \lambda=-\log\cos(3\pi/20),\qquad
 \beta(h)=\log(1-c+c\cosh h),
\]
the complete outgoing observation of product degree \(\ell\)
has the spectral factor \(e^{\ell(\beta(h)-\lambda)}\).
Every original physical row, contour current, parity correction,
and small-index subtraction keeps its previously proved bound.

The resulting actual coefficient estimate is
\[
 |h_{b,N}|
 \le C_\tau N^{A_\tau}
       e^{N(E_*+\tau)-dI_J(b/d)},\qquad
 I_J(\rho)=\sup_{h\ge0}
       \{\rho h-(\beta(h)-\lambda)_+\}.
\]
The scalar penalty is the logarithm of the positive exponential
sum
\[
       \frac c2 e^h+(1-c)+\frac c2 e^{-h}.
\]
These positive weights describe the majorant; the quantum
coefficients themselves remain complex.
The new rate strictly exceeds the preceding rate \(I(\rho)\)
for every \(\rho>0\). At the maximal degree it is exactly
\(I_J(1)=\lambda+\log(2/c)\). Although that endpoint optimizer
is at infinite height, the finite-source proof uses a single
fixed height cutoff depending on the allowed rate error.
Its error is uniform through \(b=d\).

The theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{53e5117a9facd1793ece0ffb097bfe9f6fa4bfbb366cf6f3fc5d9c25b982ee20}\),
with complete root and separate source/proof review and author
readback. It gives the sufficient remaining estimate
\[
 \max_{0\le b\le d}
       e^{-dI_J(b/d)}|\mathcal L_N(T_b(\,\cdot\,/2))|
       \le C N^B e^{N B_f},
 \qquad B_f=77/50+\pi/50.
\]
This estimate is unproved. The constant mode receives no new
weight. In particular these coefficient improvements do not
remove the need for a coherent inner-kernel estimate: the
previous positive-majorant obstruction already uses retained
low rows and the constant outer mode.

### A positive action gap pays the remaining physical half endpoint

The [shortened-edge endpoint theorem](research_mixed_next_shortened_edge_endpoint_gap.md)
proves a uniform comparison on the independent two-angle box
\[
 t=a-iH,\quad u=b-iK,\qquad
 0\le a,b\le\pi/2,\quad 0\le H\le1,\quad 0\le K\le1/2:
 \qquad
 \Re\psi(t,u)-\frac{H+K}{2}>\frac{11}{252}>\frac1{25}.
\]
The original action and its additive constant are retained.
Its two inverse-hyperbolic-sine derivatives avoid their cuts
throughout this box and form a closed holomorphic one-form.
The displayed difference is nonincreasing in both angles and
strictly decreasing in both heights, so its minimum reduces to
one corner. Along a prescribed height
path to that corner the real action increases. Its real starting
value is exactly \(-5J(1/6)>50/63\), which proves the gap.

The actual continued cubic family lies inside this box.
Its physical half-endpoint rate is exactly \((H+K)/2\).
Continuity of the integrated logarithms and the uniform finite
Newton-product estimate therefore give a fixed \(\delta>0\) with
\[
 \sum_{j=\lceil N(1/2-\delta)\rceil}^{\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1}
 |e_j(-2\cos t(u))e_j(-2\cos u)|
 \le C e^{N(\Re\psi(t(u),u)-1/50)} .
\]
This bounds the sum of moduli for those actual rows at both parities;
it also bounds every subset of them. The odd middle row is absent
because of the exact outer annihilator, not an asymptotic omission.

The theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{ebc7b10eee43535efba159220c4c39702343a146b3278eaba937aa2ee0c391fc}\),
with complete root and separate source/proof reviews and author
readback. The subsequent joined-contour reduction, described above,
retains the intervening rows in two continued integrals and removes
the artificial right-cut contribution. A separate gap at the real
face \(x=1/3\) has not been proved and is not assumed in that
reduction. Neither the complete inner trace nor the central outer
contour estimate has been proved.

### Optimizing the Fourier coefficient weight over spectral ellipses

The [variable-ellipse theorem](research_mixed_next_middle_variable_spectral_ellipse.md)
extends the outgoing product estimates to every fixed spectral height,
uniformly over bounded height ranges. Put
\[
 c=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2\pi},\qquad
 \lambda=-\log\cos(3\pi/20),\qquad
 g(h)=c(\cosh h-1)-\lambda .
\]
An outgoing observation with product degree \(\ell\) has upper bound
\(C_\tau N^{A_\tau}e^{N(E_*+\tau)+\ell g(h)}\) on the ellipse
of height \(h\). Every original outgoing row and contour term is
retained. In particular the small-index subtraction is bounded
separately; its cost relative to \(\ell g(h)\) is independent of
the spectral height.

Extracting each coefficient before summing product degrees gives
\[
 |h_{b,N}|
 \le C_\tau N^{A_\tau}
       \exp\{N(E_*+\tau)-dI(b/d)\}.
\]
The note gives an explicit piecewise formula for \(I\).
If \(h_0=\operatorname{arcosh}(1+\lambda/c)\) and
\(\rho_0=\sqrt{2c\lambda+\lambda^2}\), then
\[
 h_0>\frac12+\frac1{300},\qquad
 I(\rho)\ge h_0\rho+\frac{(\rho-\rho_0)_+^2}{3}.
\]
For the second inequality, the note proves
\(I''(\rho)=1/\sqrt{c^2+\rho^2}>2/3\) above \(\rho_0\),
with matching value and derivative at \(\rho_0\).
Thus high frequencies receive an additional quadratic penalty
as well as a stronger linear penalty. All optimizing heights
lie below \(\log3\), so the optimization does not use nonuniform
constants.

The theorem is adopted, with complete source/proof review and
author readback, at
\(\texttt{d1638d660062f79e05543289e385253de1e62082fd9fe7e0410b31d4faf841b6}\).
It supplies stronger weights for the remaining signed operator.
It does not prove the weighted operator bound, a noncancellation
statement, or a new knot-family volume identity.

### The outer trace annihilates the upper second-edge rows exactly

The [exact low-edge reduction](research_mixed_next_outer_exact_low_edge_reduction.md)
removes an entire previously unestimated block from the actual
remaining outer functional. Put \(m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\),
\(M=\lceil N/2\rceil\), and \(U=m-1\). In the original physical
algebra, multiplication by \(e_M\) annihilates every \(e_b\) with
\(b\ge m\). At odd levels this includes the middle polynomial
\(e_m\), although that polynomial is not itself in the radical.
The proof identifies the annihilator exactly:
\[
 e_M f=0\ \text{in }\mathbb C[x]/(2T_N(x/2)+2)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \prod_{j=0}^{m-1}(x-c_j)\mid f .
\]

Consequently the second edge in the remaining functional may be
replaced by the literal sum
\[
                 K_N^{<}(x,t)=\sum_{b=0}^{U}e_b(x)e_b(t).
\]
The first edge, crossing factors, and complete inner trace remain
unchanged. This is an identity before an asymptotic estimate, with
arbitrary polynomial spectators. It also retains every ordinary
boundary derivative.

The contour formula has been derived again for this shorter
kernel. Its far physical samples agree term by term with the
old ones, and both new endpoint currents have the same proved
exponential gap. The complex kernel itself is different, so
the separate central integrals are not identified.
This eliminates the need to pay the complex upper-row ceiling
for this second edge. The low right-hand rows, full inner trace,
and central outer integral remain unestimated at the required
rate. Source and proof review, including author readback, are
complete at
\(\texttt{76524c28bdbafafe8922993093e3e5b4447ec033e4b0dd3928295047bfde797a}\).

### The retained second-edge contour and the limits of its reflection

The [first-quarter contour theorem](research_mixed_next_two_angle_bare_first_quarter_contour.md)
works on the positive half of the actual complex outer rectangle.
It puts the selected wire stationary point strictly inside the
upper first quarter and proves strict horizontal concavity there.
The original finite interpolation gives its nonzero Gaussian
coefficient. The entire low physical endpoint is below that action,
and every Fourier correction, weighted side, and unweighted join
is either below the action or bounded by one explicitly retained
right real-cut value. The rest of the physical sum remains literal.
The theorem is a decomposition, not yet a complete kernel asymptotic.
It is adopted at
\(\texttt{2226900d2118e37848c0d3aae263a3ac4de8d1d5048fc5a83c0b850a5ca1a0c2}\).

The complementary [reflected-factorial identity](research_mixed_next_two_angle_factorial_alias_domains.md)
retains every original zero and reciprocal-factorial branch.
It proves the reflected comparison throughout the wire interval
for real outer angles. It also proves why that comparison cannot
simply be extended to the whole interval after moving the outer
angle into the positive lower half-plane: near the right endpoint,
the reflected lower profile can exceed the upper one after its
Fourier penalty. This does not show that it exceeds the stationary
action. It requires a separate endpoint or tail estimate.
The note is adopted at
\(\texttt{57794ee07d3c14a36b3fcb802fb022abc0729edafb290d375a57938dcdf5e4fc}\).
Together with the exact deletion above, the remaining second-edge
problem concerns its retained low rows and their complex contours.

### A common polynomial for arbitrary positive crossing power

The [stationary trace identity](research_two_edge_stationary_chebyshev_trace.md)
expresses the original two-edge stationary equation as
\[
 \mathscr P_n(c)=T_n(c)-iU_{n-1}(c)=\cos(u/2),
 \qquad c=\cos(t/2).
\]
Here \(n\) is the positive crossing power and \(T_n,U_{n-1}\)
are the Chebyshev polynomials of the first and second kind.
An explicit determinant-one matrix product has half-trace
\(\mathscr P_n(c)\). The original logarithmic charge is retained
by continuation from the prescribed branch; the polynomial
equation alone does not choose that charge.
The identity is adopted at
\(\texttt{2f4ce35d1729af574c8d482f63ee3a6304c9573f400c146fe2296ce7030be4d3}\).

The [critical-point theorem](research_stationary_chebyshev_critical_geometry.md)
proves that every critical point is simple and lies strictly in
the upper half-plane. For \(n\ge3\), its real part lies strictly
between the extreme zeros of \(U_{n-1}\), and its imaginary part
is less than \((n-1)/n\). The polynomial zeros are also simple
and strictly upper. These are exact consequences of a dissipative
rank-one matrix and the Chebyshev differential equation.
The theorem is adopted at
\(\texttt{93541f6cc4d1d191a4c3047f7c693cbf4dc8f728ae1c89118e8610717a6be3f7}\).
No critical-value half-plane theorem or arbitrary-power finite
asymptotic is inferred from these location bounds.

### Exponential decay of the actual outgoing Fourier coefficients

The [fixed spectral ellipse theorem](research_mixed_next_middle_fixed_spectral_ellipse.md)
now controls the outgoing polynomial on the filled ellipse
whose boundary is \(\xi=2\cos(\theta+i/2)\). The bound has
the same exponential rate as the earlier estimate on the real
interval. It applies to the exact finite polynomial, including
the small physical rows, both level parities, every contour
current, and both joining segments.

Write its Chebyshev expansion as
\[
 H_N(\xi,Z_*)=\sum_{b=0}^{d}h_{b,N}T_b(\xi/2),
 \qquad d<N/3,\qquad E_*=\Lambda-B_0-1/50 .
\]
Here \(N\) is the root-of-unity level, \(T_b\) is the
Chebyshev polynomial characterized by \(T_b(\cos\theta)=
\cos(b\theta)\), \(\Lambda=\Re\mathcal P_*\) is the selected
geometric action rate, and \(B_0=2383/1500\).
The new conclusion is
\[
 |h_{b,N}|\le C_\tau N^{A_\tau}
       \exp\!\left\{N(E_*+\tau)
                        -\left(\frac12+\frac1{400}\right)b\right\}.
\]
These are the actual coefficients after the outgoing sum.
The proof first bounds each finite product on the ellipse,
with a further factor \(e^{-\ell/400}\) in its product degree
\(\ell\). An angular and radial comparison of an integrated
logarithm proves the bound throughout the outgoing upper
sector; the exact reflection identity supplies every lower
contour. For the low physical rows, an increasing combined
rate reaches the already controlled real cut. Applying the
outgoing proof to each product preserves the degree gain.
Cauchy's coefficient formula then gives the displayed decay.

The full written proof, author readback, and separate source
review are complete at
\(\texttt{dc656300238775a26ac4af0309b7be66405334b93e0ca60b12d4c895dfdfd1b6}\).
No mathematical numerical evaluation was used.

The exact outer reduction is also complete at
\(\texttt{cbbc62951666d06e0ae77b29f49f563d91c2024dc8da900ae996144d7db39dab}\).
If \(\mathcal L_{N,b}\) denotes the original signed functional
applied to \(T_b(\xi/2)\), a sufficient remaining estimate is now
\[
 \max_{0\le b\le d}
 e^{-(1/2+1/400)b}|\mathcal L_{N,b}|
       \le C N^B e^{NB_f},\qquad B_f=77/50+\pi/50 .
\]
This is weaker than the previously proposed maximum without
the exponential weight. The weight comes from the original
outgoing coefficients. The estimate is still unproved; a
direct bound for their signed combination would also suffice.

Two accompanying deductions clarify the alternatives.
The [exact Newton coefficient identity](research_mixed_next_middle_exact_newton_coefficients.md)
recovers the original physical outgoing kernels when the
polynomial is multiplied by its radical factor. Its positive
tail bound is relative to a sum of row moduli and supplies no
additional coherent action estimate. Separately,
[the thin-strip obstruction](research_mixed_next_three_outer_mode_thin_strip_obstruction.md)
rules out the proposed pointwise majorant for the largest
unweighted mode on the inherited small contour neighborhood.
It does not rule out a bound for the signed response or the
new estimate with the actual coefficient weights.
Their completed source and proof reviews attach respectively
to
\(\texttt{d8b58688c4da4237ac9cc5073fb32e0601d1326aab52dc9d71cee2070618ed48}\)
and
\(\texttt{3cc8db2cdade85a30b3ba27ee8362635e8c326fe7d02dba49182cdffb88a263a}\).

These results change the estimate to pursue, but do not yet
exclude cancellation in the complete transfer. Stability under
arbitrary fixed short fillings and the finite-exceptions
statement remain open. The manuscripts are unchanged.

### The far angular samples and both endpoint currents are now bounded

The [outer-boundary theorem](research_mixed_next_outer_far_angles_and_verticals.md)
pays every physical sample with
\(|\theta|\ge11\pi/12+O(N^{-1})\) and both complete vertical
endpoint currents. It retains an arbitrary polynomial insertion
through its supremum on the fixed ellipse above. The radical
factor vanishes at each physical node, so the original derivative
trace differentiates that factor; no unaccounted derivative of
the insertion remains.

The proof first bounds every Newton polynomial on the terminal
strip of height \(2/3\). Combined with the original terminal
operator, this gives the full inner kernel rate \(8/5\) on the
far real interval. Polynomial continuation supplies a fixed
small endpoint height at which both vertical currents have rate
at most \(8/5+1/1000\), times the insertion norm. For the actual
outgoing polynomial, the complete boundary contribution is
\(O(e^{N(\Lambda-1/200)})\).

The source and proof reviews, including author readback, are
complete at
\(\texttt{5e64e4909b55107431d13fcbff92f41776ff101757c5a9f7eb70ae2d8ea1408d}\).
The only remaining part of this outer observation is its lower
contour integral, with the endpoints at the proved small height.
Its interior may be deformed farther without creating another
endpoint current. That integral has not been bounded.

The [positive Newton-envelope obstruction](research_mixed_next_three_outer_mode_newton_envelope_obstruction.md)
shows why one simple estimate is inadequate: at the real angular
coordinate \(\pi/3\), taking absolute values in both bare inner
kernels exceeds the required rate even for the constant outer
mode, for the specified inner heights through \(4/5\).
This is a lower bound for that positive majorant, not for the
signed kernel. Its completed proof reviews attach to
\(\texttt{39a496e713991adc992e5a02a040d165c8583a61439db180ad59495611bb25c7}\).
Work on the central integral therefore retains the inner
kernel's cancellation.

### An algebraic continuation of the central critical point

The [inner critical-point theorem](research_mixed_next_inner_three_cubic_continuation.md)
continues the original stationary point throughout the fixed
outer rectangle \(|\Re u|\le\pi/2\), \(|\Im u|\le1/2\).
Here \(u\) is the outer angular variable, \(t\) is the inner
angular variable, and
\[
 C=\cos(u/2),\qquad v=2\cos(t/2)
\]
satisfy the exact cubic
\[
               v^3-2iv^2-3v+2i-2C=0.
\]
The selected root is the unique root with \(\Re v>3/2\).
The proof excludes the cubic's branch values from the parameter
domain and proves explicit root bounds. These retain
\(0<\Re t<\pi/2\), \(-1<\Im t<0\), and
\(|\cos(t/2)|<1\), as well as the original logarithmic
charge. The reduced stationary Hessian never vanishes on
this compact family. The action keeps its original additive
constant.

This continuation has one direct finite-source application:
the entire critical family lies in the proved domain of
the complete \(K_N(t,0)\) edge theorem. That edge therefore
retains its nonzero asymptotic uniformly on this family.
The second edge \(K_N(t,u)\) and the complete signed inner
trace still require estimates. Algebraicity and nondegeneracy
alone do not prove that their selected critical point
contributes to the finite sum.

The theorem and its source review are complete at
\(\texttt{8a8ef3f93a4ab44724d43f7bb9b15c5f8210d4649f79d1f0d4c0ec277801f41a}\).

trace does not automatically extend to these modes: multiplication
by a spectral polynomial changes the internal indices and the
oscillatory phases.

The current obstacle is therefore a bound for this last signed

### Exact analytic control of the physical-index amplitude

The [exact amplitude theorem](research_mixed_next_middle_exact_analytic_amplitude.md)
has completed its source and proof reviews at
\(\texttt{9d7de2f97562ac3010fdfcbb263dcb149727f244421415b81879433508fabead}\).
It concerns the original physical-index sum
\[
 W_{jk,N}=\sum_{n=\max(L,j,k)}^U
       q^{-(k+1)n}\frac{S_n^3}{S_{n-j}S_{n+j+1}S_{n-k}},
 \quad L=\lfloor N/6\rfloor,\quad U=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1,
\]
where \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\) and
\(S_a=\prod_{\nu=1}^a2\sin(\pi\nu/N)\).

The exact normalization is
\[
 W_{jk,N}=q^{-(k+1)U}a_U^{j,k}\,
                    \mathfrak G_N(j/N,k/N),\qquad
 a_U^{j,k}=\frac{S_U^3}{S_{U-j}S_{U+j+1}S_{U-k}}.
\]
The finite function \(\mathfrak G_N\) is defined by an explicit
sum of backward products, including the original lower endpoint.
Its numerator zeros reproduce the physical stopping indices.
For every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), this entire function is
uniformly bounded on a fixed complex neighborhood of
\([0,1/2]\times[\varepsilon,1/2]\), with every fixed derivative
bounded on smaller neighborhoods. It converges there to
\[
 \frac{1}{1-e^{i\pi t}\cos^2(\pi\eta)\cos(\pi t)}.
\]
The important estimate is for the exact finite function, not
for a replacement by this limit.

The proof controls products close to the upper endpoint by
contraction. Farther products have a uniformly negative integrated
logarithmic rate: a real Newton-profile inequality and a monotone
log-sine integral give that gap. A uniform finite-product estimate,
including numerator zeros, preserves the gap under small complex
shifts. Thus the complete tail is controlled before the remaining
indices are summed. No coefficientwise approximation error is
discarded after an oscillatory observation.

This removes the previous obstacle to treating the physical-index
factor as an analytic amplitude in a joint contour argument.
It does not estimate that remaining contour integral, prevent
cancellation with the geometric contribution, or establish
stability under arbitrary short partial fillings. The original
endpoint \(U\) is essential to this theorem; restoring the
previously removed physical half-band must use the complete
source bounds, rather than an unsupported estimate on its
individual internal summands.


### Restored source and outgoing contour bounds

The [restored-middle identity](research_mixed_next_three_restored_middle_large_indices.md)
now supplies that exact use of the old endpoint. It writes the full
transfer as the geometric integral plus the old whole-middle
physical sum restricted to \(j>\lfloor N/64\rfloor\) and
\(k>\lfloor N/4096\rfloor\), with exponentially small error.
The restoration uses the identity
\[
 \text{high }j,\text{ high }k
 =\text{whole node}
  -(\text{all }j,\text{ low }k)
  -(\text{low }j,\text{ high }k)
\]
on the removed physical band. Each term on the right has a bound
with precisely the required subset scope. Its proof is complete
at \(\texttt{5da7c55d24823b78dc2afe43a7281f66104f6aa413ead7d2a2ab9eb9dccff401}\).

A stronger [outgoing-domain theorem](research_mixed_next_middle_outgoing_half_disk_amplitude.md)
now controls the exact amplitude on contours of any height.
Writing \(T=e^{2\pi it}\), the normalized amplitude is an exact
polynomial \(\mathcal A_N(\eta,T)\). For \(\eta\) in a fixed
complex neighborhood of \([1/64,1/2]\), it satisfies
\[
 |\mathcal A_N(\eta,T)|
 \le C\max(1,|T|^{U-L})\quad(\Im T\ge0).
\]
Equivalently, for \(0\le\Re t\le1/2\),
\[
 |\mathfrak G_N(\eta,t)|
 \le C\exp\!\left\{\frac{2\pi N}{3}(-\Im t)_+\right\}.
\]
Upward outgoing-index contours therefore have no additional
exponential cost from this amplitude. Downward contours have
the explicit cost displayed above.

The proof bounds every finite product on the boundary of the
upper unit half-disk, then applies the maximum-modulus principle
to each exact product. Its outgoing zeros lie on the unit circle,
so reflection gives the exterior bound without changing the
internal complex parameter. The absolute sum of the products
remains controlled. Nonvanishing and the rational limiting
factor are asserted only on the unit half-disk, not its exterior.
The final author extension and all proof reviews are complete at

### Exact transfer reduction and removal of small internal indices

The [complete transfer reduction](research_mixed_next_three_complete_transfer_middle_reduction.md)
is now proved at the actual base reference for the compositions
in powers three and four beginning \(343\), of length at least five.
It retains both Fourier coefficients and gives
\[
 \mathcal T_0[F_N](-2,Z_*)
   = I_{{\rm geom},N}+\mathscr S_N^{\rm rem}
          +O(e^{N(\mathcal M_*-\epsilon)}),\qquad \epsilon>0.
\]
Here \(N\) is the root-of-unity level, \(\mathcal T_0\) is the
original conditional transfer, and \(\mathcal M_*\) is the real
part of its selected geometric action. The specified geometric
integral satisfies
\[
 I_{{\rm geom},N}
   =N^{-2}\mathcal A_0 e^{N\mathcal P_*}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad \mathcal A_0\ne0,\quad \Re\mathcal P_*=\mathcal M_*.
\]
Its algebraic error remains in the integral's asymptotic; it has
not been called exponentially small. Every other contour term,
the whole filter correction, and the separate correction at the
retained physical nodes are accounted for in the reduction.

now estimates every expanded summand with \(j\le\lfloor N/64\rfloor\),

the signed terminal trace intact before taking absolute values.
The proof combines its existing operator bound with elementary
sine-product estimates. The resulting absolute subset sum has rate
at most \(419/200-1/32\), whereas the actual action exceeds

Apply this theorem only after the disjoint physical-band and
small-outgoing-index removals in the transfer reduction.
The remaining sum then has precisely the indices
\[
\begin{gathered}
 \lfloor N(1/2+\delta)\rfloor+1\le b<\lceil5N/6\rceil,\qquad
 n=N-1-b,\\
 \lfloor N/64\rfloor<j\le n,\qquad
 \lfloor N/4096\rfloor<k\le n .
\end{gathered}
\]
The index \(b\) labels the original physical node, \(j\) its
internal evaluation after radical contraction, and \(k\) the
outgoing row. The fixed \(\delta>0\) is the width supplied by
polynomial continuation from the vertical bound. The summands
and their phases are exactly those in the small internal-index
note, equation (4). Replacing \(\mathscr S_N^{\rm rem}\) by this
triple sum changes only the exponentially small error; for
example the new gap may be \(\tfrac12\min(\epsilon,1/32)\).

### The nonzero geometric contribution now extends to the whole lower half-contour

The [complete lower-half theorem](research_mixed_next_three_actual_complete_lower_left.md)
applies to the original composition words using powers three and four,
beginning \(343\), with length at least five. It uses their actual
coupled critical points. The length-three terminal word and words of
length four are outside this new theorem.

The first integration path is now covered in full. The
[initial interval and taper](research_mixed_next_three_actual_incoming_initial_taper.md),
the central estimate recorded below, and the
[right path](research_mixed_next_three_actual_incoming_right_path.md)
retain the complete finite kernels and the original integration
normalization. The corner is estimated by deforming its combined
oriented integral. The
[bounded preceding-factor theorem](research_mixed_next_three_actual_bounded_prefix.md)
also controls the original cardinal-filter correction.

With the notation defined in the assembly note, the resulting
lower-half integral satisfies
\[
 I_N^{\rm lower}
 :=N\int_{[0,1/2]+ih_y}\mathscr D_{0,N}(w;y,z)\,dy
 =N^{-2}\mathcal A_0(w,z)e^{N\mathcal P_0^+(w,z)}
       \bigl(1+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})\bigr),
 \qquad \mathcal A_0\ne0 .
\]
Here \(\mathscr D_{0,N}\) is the complete density after the first
integration, \(\mathcal P_0^+\) is the original geometric critical
action, and \(\mathcal A_0\) is its original Gaussian coefficient.
The formula holds at both level parities and on the prescribed local
parameter neighborhoods. At fixed parameters it gives a genuine lower
bound \( |I_N^{\rm lower}|\ge cN^{-2}
e^{N\Re\mathcal P_0^+}\) for all sufficiently large \(N\), with \(c>0\).
This lower bound follows from the nonzero leading coefficient and the
relative error estimate.

The complete finite Fourier observation still contains three signed
contour integrals in addition to this contribution: the remaining
lower interval and two upper intervals. Equation (20) of the assembly
note defines their signed sum \(\mathscr R_N^{(3)}\); equation (23)
gives the exact reduction up to an exponentially smaller error.
Neither of the two original sampled Fourier coefficients has been
discarded. A sufficient next result is an exponential bound for
\(\mathscr R_N^{(3)}\) strictly below the geometric rate. It is enough
to bound their signed sum, but that bound has not been proved.

Thus the new theorem establishes a nonzero contribution for a
specified integral in the actual family. It does not yet establish
noncancellation in the complete quantum sum, a new knot-family volume
identity, or stability under arbitrary fixed short partial fillings.
The manuscripts remain frozen.

### Conditional complete next type-three estimate at shared radius at most 7/10

The [complete central estimate](research_mixed_next_own_three_deep_radius_complete_central.md)
now includes every summation index of the next type-three factor.

\((3,4,3)\), with incoming and outgoing real coordinates in
\(P=[11/50,9/20]\), shared real coordinate
\(0\le q\le11/50\), and shared radius
\(13/25<R=|Y|\le7/10\). The imaginary parts remain those of the
actual reference. The additional radius condition is now known
to exclude every intended ordinary reference. Under the stated
conditional hypotheses,
\[
 |U_{0,N}(w,X)C_{1,N}(X,Y)d_N(Y)C_{0,N}(Y,Z)|
 \le CN^B e^{N\{\Lambda_{123}(z)-10^{-11}\}} .
\]
The notation is the same as in the lower-interval results below:
\(U_{0,N}\) is the first cap, \(C_{1,N}\) and \(C_{0,N}\) are the
two complete finite kernels, and \(d_N\) is the shared Fourier
weight. The function \(\Lambda_{123}\) is the unchanged reference
action bound. There is no outgoing halfweight for type three.
Both parities, all real ordinary colors, and vanishing numerator
factors are included. The central incoming integral keeps its
original measure; the corresponding fixed-base local derivative
estimate has deficit \(10^{-12}\).

The new step controls the previously untreated upper indices.
Writing \(v=1-j/N\), their continuous exponential rate satisfies
\[
 E_0(1-v;y,z)\le
 \max\{L_0,E_0(4/5-q;y,z)\},
 \qquad 0\le v<q+1/5,
 \quad L_0=-\log R+2\pi(\Im z)_+ .
\]
Both quantities on the right already have the required bound after
the first factor is attached. A centered logarithmic-integral
comparison proves this inequality through \(v=3/10\); a positive
derivative carries the other indices to the previously bounded
interval. Uniform finite-product estimates then give the actual
finite-sum bound. This replaces the earlier missing interval at
\(R\le7/10\); it does not require a lower bound for an individual
terminal row.

There is also a reusable
[attachment theorem](research_mixed_next_three_deep_radius_bounded_prefix.md).
If a preceding factor \(V_N\) satisfies, uniformly on its domain,
\[
 |V_N|\le C_\tau N^{B_\tau}
             e^{N(2383/1500+\tau)}
 \quad\hbox{for every }\tau>0,
\]
then on the same shared and outgoing domain,
\[
 |V_Nd_N(Y)C_{0,N}(Y,Z)|
 \le CN^B e^{N\{\Lambda_{123}(z)-1/200\}} .
\]
This permits the already bounded correction polynomial and several
discarded first-factor groups to be attached to the complete next
block wherever their original domains apply. It does not assume
that \(V_N\) has nonnegative coefficients. Derivative conclusions
require a corresponding neighborhood bound on \(V_N\).
