The [original-invariant assembly](research_repeated_two_block_kashaev_volume_theorem.md)
completes the fixed four-block example. For the original cylindrical
closure of the list \((2,4,2,3)\), whose fraction is \(29/17\) in
our convention,
\[
 |K_N(\mathcal K)|
   =N^{3/2}\mathcal D_*e^{2N\mathfrak s}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad \mathcal D_*>0,
 \qquad
 4\pi\mathfrak s=\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus\mathcal K).
\]
The statement uses all sufficiently large integer levels, including
both parities. In fact the invariant is nonzero at every \(N\ge3\).

The new ingredient is the
[relative core identification](research_repeated_two_block_core_boundary_word.md).
Its dual handles cancel geometrically to a genus-two handlebody.
Tracing the four boundary punctures gives the full free boundary
homomorphism of the reflected rational half-word, not only its trace
character. The standard Dehn lemma, applied to the explicitly
identified nullhomotopic cap curve, gives a separating disk. The two
remaining annular cores are primitive in the resulting solid tori.
This identifies the actual rational tangle.

The doubled face map differs from the original physical turn by
the half-lattice translation \(K\). Each of the three such translations
extends over the trivial tangle by an actual rotation, and conjugation
extends it over any rational tangle. Absorbing this specified map
therefore identifies the complete double with the original knot
exterior, allowing orientation reversal. The argument retains the
endpoint permutation; it makes no assertion about a preferred
longitude or a transported ribbon.

The quantum normalization is also explicit:
\[
 K_N(\mathcal K)=\theta^{-w(\mathscr D)}\kappa^3\mu_{2,N},
 \qquad
 \theta=\kappa^{-1},\quad |\kappa|=1,\quad
 \mu_{2,N}=\|(M_N^2)^*M_N^2e_0\|^2>0 .
\]
Here \(w(\mathscr D)\) is the writhe of the actual blackboard
diagram. The physical reduced cut, already included in the
Newton closing row, introduces no additional factor of \(N\).
The previously proved full norm asymptotic and calibrated regulator
now equal the volume of the same knot complement.

This completes one fixed knot. It does not establish a theorem for
arbitrary repeated blocks or arbitrary fixed short fillings, and no
novelty assertion is made from this example alone.

### For next type four, the lower interval now starts at zero

The [complete lower-left theorem](research_mixed_next_complete_lower_left_four.md)
now controls the entire first incoming integral for
\(0\le q=\Re y\le11/50\), at the actual negative shared height,
when the next factor has type four. With the original notation
\[
F_N(w,Y)=N\operatorname{CT}_X[U_{0,N}(w,X)C_{1,N}(X,Y)],
\qquad
\mathscr D_{0,N}=F_N(w,Y)d_N(Y)C_{1,N}(Y,Z),
\]
its finite bound is
\[
|\mathscr D_{0,N}(w;y,z)|\,|d_N(Z)|^{1/2}
\le CN^B e^{N\{\Lambda_{123}(z)-10^{-12}\}}.
\]
All first incoming pieces, the complete next kernel, both parities
and all real ordinary colors are included. The new corner theorem
is used as its combined oriented integral.

The proof also retains the original cardinal correction and the
denominator \(1-Y^N\). The correction's disk rate \(77/50\)
is below the bounded-prefix threshold \(2383/1500\), so that
theorem applies on this interval with the full next factor.
The denominator stays uniformly away from zero because
\(|Y^N|\le e^{-\pi N/500}\).

Fixed outside derivatives are obtained from the assembled finite
polynomial. Squaring the weighted product gives degrees at most
\(2(N-1)\) in the ordinary color and \(3(N-1)\) in \(Z\).
The proved polynomial continuation argument therefore supplies a
fixed complex neighborhood with an arbitrarily small rate loss.
The outgoing halfweight is removed only near its actual nonzero
packet. The normalized filtered integral on
\([0,11/50]+ih_y\), with all fixed outside derivatives, is
\(O(e^{-10^{-14}N})\).

Adding this interval to the previously controlled central and
shoulder intervals preserves the original nonzero asymptotic:
\[
N\int_{[0,1/2]+ih_y}\mathscr D_{0,N}(w;y,z)\,dy
=N^{-5/2}\mathcal A_1(w,z)e^{N\mathcal P_1^+(w,z)}
                     (1+O_{\mathrm{hol}}(N^{-1})),
\qquad \mathcal A_1\ne0.
\]
The original action and coefficient are unchanged.

For this next type, the remaining signed contour has three terms:
\[
\int_{[1/2,1]+ih_y}K_N\,dy
-\int_{[s,11/50]+iH}K_N\,dy
-\int_{[9/20,1-s]+iH}K_N\,dy,\qquad H=1/100.
\]
Here \(K_N\) is the unchanged filtered meromorphic kernel and
\(s>0\) the original upper seam cutoff. Equation (17) of the new
theorem gives the exact original transfer minus its geometric
contribution and these three terms, with a controlled error whose
constant is reduced to include the new bound. The signs and both
Fourier coefficients remain. The signed sum above is still open.

This extension is for next type four at all its actual reference
heights. The newer type-three theorem above completes the analogous
lower-left term under the additional restriction \(R\le7/10\).
Its larger-radius case remains open.

### The earlier extension to the next half boundary applies to both types

The [complete boundary-interval theorem](research_mixed_next_complete_lower_right_shoulder.md)
now bounds the whole first incoming integral when the shared real
coordinate lies in \([.45,.5]\), at its original negative height.
The initial segment, left taper, central interval and combined right
tail are all included. After attaching the complete next tangle and
its original weights, the bound has a strict exponential deficit
\(10^{-11}\) below the unchanged reference-action plane.

The proof also retains the old Fourier filter and estimates its
correction polynomial against both alternatives for the next
tangle. Consequently the interval \([.45,.5]+ih_y\) is now removed
from the remaining signed contour. The complete lower integral
over \([.22,.5]+ih_y\) has the original nonzero Gaussian coefficient.
Here \(h_y=\Im y_*\) is the shared coordinate's fixed negative
reference height. This extends the interval on which the complete
source is controlled; the other complementary intervals remain open.

The [complete next-block estimate](research_mixed_next_lower_right_shoulder_next_block.md)
extends the calculation to the shared boundary coordinate
\(q\in[.45,.5]\). The first boundary coordinate remains in
\(P=[.22,.45]\), as does the outgoing coordinate; all three retain
the imaginary parts of the actual ordinary reference. On this
domain the full finite integrand satisfies
\[
 |U_{0,N}(w,X)C_{1,N}(X,Y)d_N(Y)C_{\beta,N}(Y,Z)|
       |d_N(Z)|^{\beta/2}
 \le CN^B e^{N\{\Lambda_{123}(z)-10^{-11}\}}.
\]
Here \(U_{0,N}\) is the complete first-cap polynomial,
\(C_{1,N}\) and \(C_{\beta,N}\) are the original finite sums for
the two adjacent blocks, and \(d_N\) is their original Fourier
weight. The flag \(\beta\in\{0,1\}\) records the type of the next
block. The function \(\Lambda_{123}\) is the unchanged affine
bound obtained from the actual reference action, defined in the
complete lower-interval theorem below. This is an upper bound
with a strict exponential deficit; it is not a new volume identity.

There is an important reason to estimate the adjacent factors
together. The last physical row of the next block retains a
separate exponential term. After multiplication by the preceding
block and the full shared Fourier weight, its dependence on the
shared variable is \(g(s+y)-2g(y)\), where \(g\) is the original
logarithmic primitive and \(s\) is the first block's summation
coordinate. At every nonpositive imaginary part of \(s\), the
real part of this expression strictly decreases as \(q=\Re y\)
increases from .45 to .5. The estimates at .45 therefore continue
to control it. Positive-height contour terms are first compared
with their controlling nonpositive-height or real-cut terms at
the same \(q\). They are not transported using an inequality
outside its domain.

The [incoming right-tail theorem](research_mixed_next_lower_right_shoulder_incoming_right_tail.md)
also controls the entire remaining right-hand chain of the first
boundary integration:
\[
 [.45+ih_a,.5+ih_a]\ \cup\
 [.5+ih_a,.5]\ \cup\ [.5,1].
\]
Here \(h_a\) is the first boundary coordinate's actual negative
reference height. The two pieces meeting at .5 are replaced
together by the other two sides of an exact Cauchy rectangle.
The proof retains every physical row, Fourier remainder and
connecting segment, and includes both alternatives of the next
block's estimate. Its integrated bound has the same
\(10^{-11}\) deficit.

Two additional written results supply ingredients for this
extension. The [closed half-output theorem](research_mixed_four_conditional_closed_half_output.md)
proves that the original cubic critical point, logarithmic branch
and calibrated action inequalities remain valid at \(q=1/2\).
The [small-index taper theorem](research_mixed_next_right_shoulder_taper_upper_currents.md)
proves the required curvature at every relevant contour height
on the added small-index range of the left taper. Its conclusion
controls the specified contour terms. The
[complete initial and left-taper proof](research_mixed_next_lower_right_shoulder_incoming_left.md)
supplies their main and physical-row comparisons. Its moving lower
cut is calibrated by varying the shared coordinate at each fixed
point of the taper. On the initial real segment, a positive
derivative transports every retained cap and conditional contour
profile to its controlled endpoint. Both arguments keep the
complete following tangle attached.

Combining the pieces gives the entire first incoming integral.
For the final signed expression, let \(K_N\) be the original
filtered meromorphic kernel defined below, \(H=1/100\), and
\(s>0\) the existing fixed upper seam cutoff. What remains is
\[
\begin{split}
 &\int_{[0,.22]+ih_y}K_N\,dy+
  \int_{[.5,1]+ih_y}K_N\,dy\\
 &\qquad-\int_{[s,.22]+iH}K_N\,dy
         -\int_{[.45,1-s]+iH}K_N\,dy .
\end{split}
\]
The signs, original factors of \(N\), and both Fourier coefficients
are retained. No bound at the needed rate has yet been proved for
this signed sum. The new assembly uses the minimum of the old
central, old upper-seam and new boundary-interval error reserves.
It proves neither the full next-transfer asymptotic nor stability
under arbitrary short compositions.

### What Fourier reflection now gives

There is also an exact
[right-rectangle reduction](research_mixed_next_right_paired_terminal_insertion.md).
The closed right-hand contour is one original terminal-three
trace with a single coherent polynomial insertion, plus a
controlled first-coordinate deletion. The insertion has degree
less than \(N/2\) in both its ordinary variable and the output
variable. The full terminal-source proof gives
\[
|\mathscr R_N^{\rm cl}|
\le C_\tau N^{A_\tau}e^{N(M_{\rm term}+\tau)}
       \|\mathcal I_{\beta,N}(\,\cdot\,,Z)\|_{\rm strip}
       +CN^A e^{11N/6}.
\]
Here \(M_{\rm term}\) is the original terminal-three action,
and the norm is the supremum of
\(|\mathcal I_{\beta,N}(-2\cos\theta,Z)|\) on
\(|\Im\theta|\le\log2\). Every phase in the insertion is
retained before this norm is taken.

This is a reduction to an explicit polynomial norm, not yet
a bound for that norm at the needed rate. The desired open
horizontal difference also has two vertical terms and an
even-level half-grid correction. The exact identity keeps
all three; none is discarded because its length is small.
The note is frozen after full source and proof review at
\(976f8bf4f46aa7011c8973e20e5335b914e9bc7a4cf5c76c1f0044a5aa2c56c1\).

The [recoupling corollary](research_mixed_next_right_insertion_recoupling_and_norm.md)
identifies this insertion more concretely. It is exactly
\(\kappa N\mathcal T_{1\beta}[\Pi_I U_{1,N}]\), where
\(U_{1,N}\) is the original four-twist cap and \(\Pi_I\) retains
the right-hand set of physical nodes. The projection must remain:
removing it would give a different, complete two-block message.

The highest Newton coefficient of the projected insertion cannot
cancel with the other retained nodes. Cauchy's coefficient formula
therefore gives an exact lower bound for its angular-strip norm.
At the physical test output \(Z=r^{N-1}\), the old strip norm is
at least \(2^{N/2}/N\) for even levels, with the corresponding
explicit odd-level factor. Thus a polynomial norm bound on the
whole containing output disk is impossible. This test does not
belong to any proved actual geometric output family and does not
contradict the needed exponential action budget.

The same terminal-source proof permits the smaller strip height
\(h_{\rm tr}+1/(n+1)\), where \(h_{\rm tr}\) is its original
trace height and \(n=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\) is the insertion's
degree bound. Cauchy derivative costs remain polynomial in \(N\).
This improves the auxiliary norm used in the upper estimate,
while leaving an exponential norm comparison at actual outputs
to be proved. The corollary is frozen after full source and
proof review at
\(b9b48ba9c977a081c2d7be9846c086ebad41f697132fb6e299e6635f3798de54\).

The [exact reflection identity](research_mixed_next_lower_complement_exact_reflection.md)
has now been checked against the original finite polynomials. It
exchanges the two Fourier coefficients that make up the attachment
sum. It also changes the following tangle's kernel, reverses the
factorial weight, and reverses the set of physical nodes removed
by the existing filter. The equation for the reversed weight has
an explicit forcing term. Deleting that term would give the zero
polynomial, so it cannot be omitted in a comparison.

This supplies an exact alternative expression for the remaining
right-hand integral. It does not yet estimate that expression:
the previously proved upper-contour estimate concerns a different
kernel and weight. The identity therefore gives a possible route
to a bound, but by itself removes none of the remaining contour
terms. The current type-four and type-three counts are stated above.

A separate [paired-left reduction](research_mixed_next_paired_left_physical_reduction.md)
now gives a checked exact identity. It expresses
the difference of the two left-hand integrals as a partial sum
over the original physical colors and two vertical connecting
integrals, up to already controlled corrections. The partial
sum and connecting integrals still need a joint bound.

The [moving-cut theorem](research_mixed_next_moving_left_cut_gaussian_balance.md)
shows exactly how this partial sum changes when its vertical
connecting integral is moved. Write \(Q_N(c)=S_N(c)-V_N(c)\),
where \(S_N(c)\) retains the physical colors to the left of a
half-grid cut \(c\), and \(V_N(c)\) is the upward integral at
that cut. The residue theorem gives its change as the lower
horizontal integral minus the upper horizontal integral.
Before the cut reaches the saddle neighborhood this change
is exponentially small. Across the saddle it has the original
nonzero Gaussian transition, including the original power of
\(N\) and its complex coefficient. At the nearest half-grid
to the saddle it gives one half of that coefficient, with
relative error \(O(N^{-1/2})\).

This is a propagation theorem for the actual signed finite
sum and its connecting integral. It leaves the initial value
\(Q_N(c_{0,N})+V_N^{\mathrm{deep}}\) undetermined, where
\(c_{0,N}=(\lceil .22N\rceil+1/2)/N\) and the second term is
the remaining seam integral below height \(-.01\). Thus it
locates the required initial bound without supplying it.

The [forced-weight theorem](research_mixed_next_reflected_forced_weight_bound.md)
also controls the complete reciprocal-factorial polynomial
throughout the reflected right-hand domain, including both
real radii and the full actual negative depth. On the original
closed upper half-annulus it has arbitrarily small exponential
rate. Its forcing term is retained. Under exact reflection
the selected inverse power cancels the apparent depth cost
of the reversed weight. The prefix and the following
conditional kernel still need a coupled estimate; the weight
bound alone does not remove the right-hand integral.

The [upper-alias branch theorem](research_mixed_next_lower_right_upper_alias_branch.md)
now identifies another feature of this right-hand interval directly
from the original cubic. At the incoming half face
\(X=-\rho\), \(5/8\le\rho\le1\), and for
\(\Im Y>0,\ |Y|<1\), the equation
\[
v(v-X)(v-Y)=X(v-1)^3
\]
has two upper-half-plane roots, counted with multiplicity.
At each real-radius endpoint \(Y=\pm R\), \(1/2<R<1\),
a simple positive real root enters that half-plane when the
shared coordinate enters \(1/2<q<1\).
On the original logarithmic sheet, these local branches satisfy
\[
Q_t=-2\pi i,\qquad \partial_t(Q+2\pi it)=0.
\]
Thus they belong to the first upper Fourier alias. The original
primitive gives real alias action zero at both boundary radii
and strictly positive action just inside the interval.

This result neither labels the two branches globally nor proves
that either contributes to the finite sum. Near a boundary it lies
to the left of any fixed positive private-index cut, so it does
not contradict an estimate on a retained middle rectangle.
It shows which additional endpoint and Fourier terms a direct
continuation of the first conditional factor must keep. The
reversed-product estimate and the signed contour comparison
remain open. The proof is frozen at
\(4f28582ee1a2906a078ec38a39f1a435db40be2319400bbf7c140f311418d3b6\)
after full root and separate algebra, sheet and source review.

### Concavity under composition and the lower-left main profiles

The [cotangent criterion](research_cotangent_concavity_under_composition.md)
puts the main phases in a common explicit concavity domain:
each real coordinate may range from \(1/6\) to \(1/2\), with
absolute imaginary part at most \(27/250\), using regular
limits at the half boundary. On compact subsets away from
that boundary it gives a positive lower bound for the negative
real Hessian.

For phases having the stated sum of pair terms and nonnegative
own-term weights, that lower bound is preserved when internal
critical variables are eliminated. With a fixed lower bound
on edge weights and every free vertex incident to an edge,
the bound can be chosen independently of graph size. The
determinant and Schur-complement identities were already used
in earlier notes; the new result combines them on the enlarged
common domain. It does not show that critical points for every
short filling exist in that domain or that the original
integration cycle contributes there.

The [joint lower-left profile theorem](research_mixed_next_lower_left_joint_main_profiles.md)
now uses this domain for the original two adjacent conditional
phases. It retains the full shared Fourier allocation, clips
the low main indices upward to \(1/6\), and proves a strict
supporting bound on \(0\le\Re y\le.22\). The original real
low and half-index profiles are now included as well. The
main-profile proof combines concavity near the old central
interval with an explicit positive derivative in the shared
real coordinate. To calibrate the next real cuts, it first
clips the first main index downward to \(5/12\), where that
same joint derivative remains positive up to the old face.
The first real half-index value is bounded by its value at
the original negative main height by an explicit vertical
argument comparison.

These comparisons keep the first incoming and final outgoing
real coordinates in their original central plateaus. They
prove bounds for all combinations of the two main profiles
and their original real low and half cuts. Their finite-sum
consequences, including the newly controlled contour
remainders, are stated next.
The four-piece signed remainder displayed above, and the
finite-exception goal, remain unresolved.

### Complete low finite blocks and continuation through the seam

The [low-block theorem](research_mixed_next_lower_left_low_physical_blocks.md)
has now converted part of the preceding profile estimate into
an actual finite-sum bound. In the first conditional factor it
retains every row \(0\le j\le\lfloor N/8\rfloor\); in the
next it retains every row through the original cutoff
\(3N/20\) or \(N/8\), according to its type. Each positive
sum is bounded by its real-cut profile. The zeroth rows,
which equal one, are included explicitly.

After attaching the entire first cap and the complete forced
Fourier weight, the product of these two low blocks lies
strictly below the required action rate on the full closed
interval \(0\le\Re y\le.22\), at every actual negative
reference depth. This estimate concerns a literal portion
of the finite source, with all its normalization factors.
The Fourier-weight upper bound is proved through the seam
by combining its exact forced radial recurrence with its
regular-strip estimate.

The [factorial continuation theorem](research_factorial_symbol_across_inward_seam.md)
also extends the original conditional-row interpolant across
\(\Re y=0\) at these strictly negative heights. An exact
integer shift moves the argument into the previously proved
strip. The trapezoidal expansion of the finite product
preserves both the original action and its amplitude.
This extends the specified low-by-main integral estimates
to the same closed interval. It does not replace the forced
Fourier polynomial by a reciprocal factorial at the seam.

The [complete current theorem](research_mixed_next_lower_left_complete_currents.md)
now includes both middle blocks. It estimates every horizontal
Fourier remainder, every weighted vertical side, and both
unweighted joins for each conditional factor. The original
half-grid cuts, all Fourier frequencies and the factor \(+N\)
are retained. The factorial continuation and the separate
forced-weight bound make the estimates uniform through
\(q=0\).

Together these results bound the literal product in which
both conditional indices range over
\(0\le j<\lceil N/2\rceil\), with the complete first cap
and original weights attached. Its deficit below the
unchanged action plane is \(10^{-11}\); local normalized
fixed derivatives retain a deficit \(10^{-12}\).
This includes the whole first incoming central interval,
with its original integration measure.

### Both complete conditional sums are now controlled for a next type four

The [central completion](research_mixed_next_lower_left_central_four_completion.md)
removes the restriction to indices below one half when the next
factor has type four. For every actual ordinary reference, set
\(a=x+ih_a\), \(y=q+ih_y\), and \(z=u+ih_z\), keeping its
original heights fixed. With \(x,u\in[.22,.45]\) and
\(q\in[0,.22]\), the result is
\[
 |U_{0,N}(w,X)C_{1,N}(X,Y)d_N(Y)C_{1,N}(Y,Z)|
 |d_N(Z)|^{1/2}
 \le CN^B e^{N\{\Lambda_{123}(z)-10^{-11}\}}.
\]
Here \(X=e^{-2\pi ia}\), \(Y=e^{-2\pi iy}\), and
\(Z=e^{-2\pi iz}\). Both conditional sums and the cap are
complete. The estimate includes both level parities, all real
ordinary colors, the original central integration measure, and
the closed endpoint \(q=0\). Local normalized fixed derivatives
retain a deficit \(10^{-12}\).

The proof first uses the
[upper-row comparison](research_mixed_next_lower_left_own_four_upper_rows.md):
the absolute sum of the upper rows is bounded by the larger of
its half-row and last-row rates. The
[next-last comparison](research_mixed_next_lower_left_next_four_last_row.md)
then controls the whole next factor when the first index is below
one half. The
[first-last comparison](research_mixed_next_lower_left_first_last_four_reduction.md)
controls the remaining pairs except for the pair of last-row
rates. Its half-row argument allows an increase of \(1/2250\)
and pays it from the already proved \(1/2000\) half-row margin.
It does not assign a numerical value to an unspecified last-row
margin.

The final pair has a simpler dependence on the shared variable:
only \(\nu_R(q)=-\Re g(q+ih_y)\) varies, where
\(R=e^{2\pi h_y}\). Its maximum occurs at
\[
 q_R=\frac{\arccos(R/2)}{2\pi}\in[1/6,.22].
\]
At that point, the first real row with index fraction \(1/8\)
exceeds the first last-row rate by more than \(27/500\).
That low row paired with the next last row already has a proved
bound. This comparison controls the last remaining alternative
at every shared depth. The same argument bounds the two last-row
rates for a next type three as well, retaining its positive
outgoing-height term; it does not estimate that factor's
intermediate upper rows.

The [bounded-prefix theorem](research_mixed_next_lower_left_bounded_prefix_four.md)
now gives a common estimate for many of the remaining discarded
contributions. Suppose a preceding factor \(V_N\) has a uniform
upper rate at most \(2383/1500\), with a polynomial prefactor and
arbitrarily small rate tolerance. On the whole same interval
\(0\le q\le.22\), with a next type-four block, it satisfies
\[
 |V_Nd_N(Y)C_{1,N}(Y,Z)|\,|d_N(Z)|^{1/2}
 \le CN^B e^{N\{\Lambda_{123}(z)-1/100\}}.
\]
The next sum is complete. The preceding factor can be a whole
polynomial, an absolute row sum, or a previously bounded contour
contribution; its own bound must be proved in each application.

At \(q=.22\), the old marginal calculation supplies a margin
greater than \(1/50\) for every controlling next profile.
The main and real low profiles increase toward that endpoint.
The real half profile can increase by at most \(1/2250\) in the
other direction. For the last profile the maximum possible
increase is less than \(1/125\). To prove the latter statement,
write its excess as
\[
 M(R)=\int_{\arccos(R/2)/(2\pi)}^{11/50}
                 \log|1-Re^{-2\pi is}|\,ds.
\]
Differentiation shows that \(M\) increases with \(R\).
At \(R=1\), the concave tangent bound for
\(\log(2\sin\pi s)\) at \(s=1/6\) gives
\(M(1)<44/5625<1/125\). Thus the original margin is sufficient;
no unspecified last-row margin is assigned a numerical value.

This theorem controls the existing positive low and upper first-row
groups on the incoming corner rectangle. It also controls the
entire old Fourier-filter correction polynomial on this shared
interval, because that polynomial has disk rate \(77/50\).
It does not by itself bound the remaining first main integrals
or any next type-three upper sum.

### The first incoming corner is now controlled for type four

The [initial and left-taper theorem](research_mixed_next_lower_left_incoming_initial_taper.md)
now bounds the complete first source on the real segment
\([0,1/10]\) and on the sloping segment from \(1/10\) to
\(11/50+ih_a\), for every \(0\le q\le11/50\).
The complete next type-four sum stays attached. Its finite
deficit is \(10^{-12}\); the stated local normalized derivatives
retain a deficit \(10^{-13}\).

The new lower index cut is \(\ell(x)=7/100+x/4\). It reaches
the original cut \(1/8\) at \(x=11/50\), where the central
estimate applies. Direct differentiation transports the cap and
low-row profile along this cut. The proof also includes the
entire middle sum and all its connecting terms. Upper physical
rows are divided between a half-row comparison, a last-row
comparison, and an explicit positive upper bound that satisfies
the bounded-prefix theorem. No endpoint-only theorem is assumed
when both outside real coordinates are small.

The [right horizontal theorem](research_mixed_next_lower_left_incoming_right_horizontal.md)
controls the complete density on
\([9/20,1/2]+ih_a\), with deficit \(10^{-11}\), on the same
shared interval. A fixed cut at \(1/20\) separates a positive
low block that satisfies the bounded-prefix estimate. The

### An explicit complete hyperbolic manifold realizes the four-block rate

The [five-core face theorem](research_repeated_two_block_five_core_faces.md)
extracts five tetrahedra from the existing saved subdivision and
lists their face identifications. The core has two annular ideal
ends and a four-punctured boundary. Its two internal edge products
are identically one; its six boundary products are
\[
 p,\quad p,\quad p^{-1},\quad p^{-1},\quad -V,\quad -V^{-1}.
\]
An explicit boundary gluing to the oppositely oriented conjugate
core gives ten positive tetrahedra and a single torus cusp.
The actual stationary equations \(|p|=|V|=1\) give every
multiplicative edge equation. Positivity and the torus-link
Gauss--Bonnet sum then force every edge-angle sum to be exactly
\(2\pi\).

Completeness is also proved for this explicit double. The developed
face maps give a boundary-parallel loop in one annular end with
nonidentity parabolic holonomy
\[
                         Z(t)=-\frac{u^2}{t-2u}.
\]
This is an actual loop on the doubled torus link. Its peripheral
holonomy group is abelian and centralizes that parabolic, so all
peripheral similarities have linear part one. The cusp triangles
therefore form a compact flat torus and a complete hyperbolic cusp.

For the resulting explicitly defined manifold \(\mathcal M_{\rm dbl}\),
the earlier calibrated regulator identity now proves
\[
 \operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal M_{\rm dbl})
   =2\{2D(u)+2D(u(1-u))+D(-V)\}
   =\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|Z_{2,2,N}|.
\]
At this stage the relative core marking and doubled boundary map
had not yet been identified with the original capped word
\((2,4,2,3)\). The new boundary-word theorem and original-invariant
assembly above now complete that step. The earlier face theorem
remains unchanged, with its original scope and hash; the separate
topological proof supplies the previously missing homeomorphism.

### The positive-moment calculation now has an analytic input for composition

The [canonical row-source theorem](research_repeated_two_block_canonical_row_source.md)
puts the repeated two-crossing operators in an exact symmetric
matrix form. With \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\),
\(S_j=\prod_{\nu=1}^j2\sin(\pi\nu/N)\), and
\[
 B_{ij}=Nq^{-ij}\frac{S_{i+j}}{S_i^2S_j^2}
 \quad(i+j<N),\qquad B_{ij}=0\quad(i+j\ge N),
\]
the actual capped moments are
\[
 \mu_{m,N}=e_0^*(\overline B B)^m e_0=\|W_m\|^2,
\]
where \(W_m\) is obtained from \(e_0\) by applying
\(B,\overline B,B,\overline B,\ldots\), in that order.
The original closing scalar and its phase are unchanged.

The previously proved \(W_2\) coefficient asymptotic now holds
for a specified canonical interpolation on a fixed complex
neighborhood of every compact interval in \((0,1/2]\).
The proof includes the extra rows that become nonzero away
from integer indices. The exact factorial reflection supplies
a continuous upper exponent through their moving zero wall.
On the real interval their rate is at most zero, whereas the
retained contribution has a strictly positive action. This
strict gap persists in a fixed complex neighborhood.

This provides a genuine holomorphic input to the next operator.
It does not identify arbitrary nonphysical indices with colored
knot values. An induction for all repeated moments still needs
control of the subsequent critical branch and every complementary
row and contour term.

### The four-block stationary point closes the actual knot representation

The [five-shape construction](research_repeated_two_block_five_shape_layer_dictionary.md)
follows the original cap and four signed crossings in the half-word
whose doubled scalar is the positive moment for \((2,4,2,3)\).
It records all eight limiting tetrahedral shapes: three flat
limits and five surviving positively oriented shapes
\[
 u,\quad u,\quad u(1-u),\quad u(1-u),\quad -V.
\]
The branch \(u\) and outgoing coordinates \(p,V\) are the same
ones selected by the complete finite-sum asymptotic. An explicit
regulator calculation proves that the sum of these five volumes
is its calibrated half-action, with no unspecified additive constant.

There is now also an exact closing argument for the original
representation. Let \(F=TR^{-2}TR^2\) be the actual half-word
on characters, and let \(I=T\circ\) complex conjugation.
Then \(FI=IF^{-1}\). At the stationary output \(b=F(c)\),
\(|p|=|V|=1\) says \(I(b)=b\), so
\[
 TF^2(c)=\overline c.
\]
The right side lies on the original closing cap. The original
finite meridian matrices remain irreducible through the
intermediate coordinate escape. The faithful four-punctured
cap argument therefore gives the literal closing inverse-pair
relations. This proves a boundary-parabolic representation of
the actual capped word, not only an abstract character satisfying
the critical cubic.

The volume theorem for the original knot remains open. The later
five-core face theorem above constructs a complete hyperbolic
double, but its relative tangle marking and closing map have
not yet been identified with the original knot. The original
representation, positive shapes and matching regulator do not
by themselves establish that topological identification.

### The remaining conditional sum has been reduced to one integral

The latest source estimates concern appending a third short tangle
to the already treated pair \((3,4)\). They do not yet prove the
volume identity for the resulting triple.

The problematic internal kernel is the original finite sum
\[
 C_{1,N}(X,Y)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}
       \frac{X^{-j}p_j(X)p_j(Y)}{P_j^3}.
\]
Here \(r=e^{-2\pi i/N}\), \(P_j=(r;r)_j\),
\(p_j(X)=(rX;r)_j\), and \(X=e^{-2\pi ia}\).
The incoming coordinate ranges over
\([1/2,7/10]-i[0,9/125]\). The outgoing coordinate now
includes the negative heights required by the actual next tangle.
The index \(j\) here is internal to this kernel; it is not the
Newton coefficient index in the earlier prefix estimates below.

Two direct finite-product estimates control the
[upper rows](research_mixed_conditional_lower_output_upper_block.md),
\(j\ge\lceil N/2\rceil\), and the
[low rows](research_mixed_conditional_lower_output_low_block.md),
\(j\le\lfloor2N/25\rfloor\). Both estimates hold on the whole
outgoing unit disk. They retain the complete first cap.
After multiplication by the actual next kernel and its Fourier
weight, the two groups are exponentially smaller than the original
supporting action. This comparison uses the existing action
normalization, including the weight's forcing term.

The [middle-source reduction](research_mixed_conditional_lower_output_middle_reduction.md)
also controls both horizontal and all four vertical cotangent
remainders. Thus, with the original canonical interpolation \(T_N\),
\[
 C_{1,N}(X,Y)
   =N\int_{\ell_N}^{b_N}T_N(s;a,y)\,ds+\mathcal E_N,
\quad
 \ell_N=\frac{\lfloor2N/25\rfloor+1/2}{N},\quad
 b_N=\frac{\lceil N/2\rceil-1/2}{N}.
\]
The error \(\mathcal E_N\), multiplied by the complete cap and
actual next factors, has a strict exponential gap; after the
original normalization, integration and fixed differentiation,
the stated gap is \(1/400\). This is a complete finite-source
reduction on the stated incoming rectangle and ordinary-next
plateau, not a bound for the whole next transfer.

The same note proves by algebra and elementary trigonometric
inequalities that the original critical point satisfies
\[
 2/25<\Re s_*<1-\Re a,\qquad
 |\Im s_*|<\log(5)/(2\pi).
\]
The phase is strictly horizontally concave before the incoming
numerator wall throughout that height strip. No critical root
was numerically evaluated.

The [complete deformation proof](research_mixed_conditional_lower_output_gaussian_deformation.md)
now also retains and bounds both unweighted connecting sides.
The local contribution is
\[
 G_N(a,y)=N^{-1}\mathcal B(a,y)e^{N\Theta(a,y)}
                       (1+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})),\qquad
 \mathcal B(a,y)\ne0,
\]
with the original phase and normalization. Its remainder has two
bounds: one is exponentially smaller than this conditional action,
with all outside factors retained; the other is already
exponentially smaller than the next tangle's supporting action.
Those bounds cannot be combined into a relative asymptotic for
the complete conditional polynomial without another comparison.

The [unselected incoming-corner theorem](research_mixed_next_unselected_incoming_corner_union.md)
now completes that comparison on the required replacement contour.
It first extends the supporting-plane inequality to the incoming
half face. A convex maximum over the private index height then
bounds the moving critical action by that fixed-reference plane.
This uses convexity before eliminating the private variable.
The complete cap and the original logarithmic action can then
be transported along
\[
 1/2+ih_a\longrightarrow7/10+ih_a\longrightarrow7/10.
\]
Both errors above are now controlled on this contour as well.

Cauchy's theorem therefore bounds the entire original union
\[
 1/2+ih_a\longrightarrow1/2\longrightarrow7/10
\]
with a strict gap, for every outgoing coordinate in the actual
lower plateau \(P+i h_y\), \(P=[.22,.45]\).
The stated local normalized gap, including fixed derivatives, is
\(10^{-10}\). The estimate concerns the union and retains its
cancellation; it does not estimate the two original pieces
separately. It is an ordinary-next result, not a terminal
extension. The new initial, left and right estimates above now
control the full incoming complement on the lower central interval.
The lower period outside \(P+i h_y\) and the selected middle
coefficient still have separate obligations. No full third-tangle

### Positivity now gives a stronger lower bound for actual capped words

The [repeated-block identity](research_repeated_reflected_block_positive_moments.md)
uses the original crossing matrix \(M_N\), original closing vector
\(e_0\), and
\[
 H_{r,N}=(M_N^r)^*M_N^r.
\]
For the specified repeated reflected words, their actual capped
scalar is exactly a unit complex factor times
\[
 \mu_{r,m,N}=e_0^*H_{r,N}^{\,m}e_0>0.
\]
The equivalent positive crossing list repeats
\((2,\ldots,2,r+2)\), with \(r-1\) entries equal to two,
and reduces the final entry by one. For even \(r\), the stated
closure is a knot. This is an exact noncancellation result with
the actual cap; it does not extend to arbitrary unequal caps.

The [interior-coefficient theorem](research_repeated_two_block_interior_cap_seed.md)
goes beyond the first Jensen lower bound. For \(r=2\), it proves
a complete nonzero asymptotic for an interior coefficient of
\(H_{2,N}e_0\), retaining the full finite sum and every contour
remainder. Write
\[
 J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds,\qquad c=-2J(1/6).
\]
For each sufficiently small fixed \(t_0>0\), the coefficient has
an action \(\mathcal S(t_0)>c\). Positive moment ratios then give
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}N^{-1}\log|Z_{2,m,N}|
 \ge mc+2(m-1)\bigl(\mathcal S(t_0)-c\bigr)>mc
 \qquad(m\ge2).
\]
The [full half-interval theorem](research_repeated_two_block_half_interval_packet.md)
extends that coefficient asymptotic through every physical row
\(0\le n/N\le1/2\). It bounds the complementary half separately,
and proves that it is exponentially smaller than an actual
interior coefficient. Consequently, with the same selected branch,
\[
 \mathfrak s=\max_{0\le t\le1/2}\mathcal S(t),\qquad
 \lim_{N\to\infty}N^{-1}\log|Z_{2,2,N}|=2\mathfrak s.
\]
This is a sharp rate for the full original capped word
\((2,4,2,3)\), not a cyclic trace or a selected summand.
The completed proof also shows that the maximizing index is unique,
lies in \((0,1/4)\), and has strictly negative second derivative.
It gives the full asymptotic
\[
 |Z_{2,2,N}|=N^{3/2}\mathcal D_*e^{2N\mathfrak s}
                   (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad \mathcal D_*>0,
\]
with an explicit Gaussian coefficient and concentration of the
actual squared coefficient masses around that index.
It also gives
\[
 \liminf_N N^{-1}\log|Z_{2,m,N}|
       \ge 2(m-1)\mathfrak s-(m-2)c\qquad(m\ge2).
\]
The higher moments still have only these lower bounds.
The knot complement's hyperbolic volume has not yet been
identified with the sharp rate \(2\mathfrak s\).

There is now an absolutely calibrated regulator expression:
\[
 2\pi\mathfrak s=3D(u_*)+2D(p_*)-D(p_*u_*).
\]
Here \(D\) is the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm,
\(p_*=e^{2\pi it_*}\), and \(u_*=e^{2\pi ix(t_*)}\) is the
original selected upper root of
\[
 u^3+(p-3)u^2+2u-1=0.
\]
The primitive's constant and its logarithmic lift are fixed in
the proof. The existing mixed-word representation dictionary
gives this same cubic and outgoing momentum
\(V=-(1-pu)/(p-1)^2\); outer stationarity says \(|V|=1\).
The new five-shape construction above closes the original reduced
representation. The geometric cap attachment and the marked
fundamental chain remain to be established. The representation
and dilogarithm value alone do not certify them.

### The scale needed to observe the geometric state

The representation-theoretic approach now has a sharp test on an
actual source for which the volume identity is already established.
This supplies information about the proposed lower-bound method;
it does not extend the list of proved knot families.

For a fixed even crossing block, let
\(\alpha_N=M_N^{2k}\mathbf e_0\), \(k\ge2\), and let
\(a_N=\alpha_N/\|\alpha_N\|_2\).
The original reflected-pair theorem gives
\[
 \|\alpha_N\|_2=\exp\{N\chi_k+o(N)\},\qquad
 \chi_k=\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus\mathcal K_k)/(4\pi)>0.
\]
The [growing-observation theorem](research_original_growing_cap_observation.md)
considers the projection \(P_{L,N}\) onto the first half of the
Newton coordinates together with the last \(L+1\) coordinates.
For every sublinear width \(L_N=o(N)\), it proves the exact rate
\[
 N^{-1}\log\|P_{L_N,N}a_N\|_2\longrightarrow-\chi_k.
\]
Thus even the entire first half together with a growing opposite
endpoint window detects exponentially little of this particular
geometric state. Any subexponentially bounded observations confined
to those coordinates have the same upper-rate obstruction.
The original two-cap Casimir observations through degree \(o(N)\)
are included. Reconstruction of this actual state from those
observations requires exponential amplification.

The theorem also determines precisely when a larger coordinate
window succeeds. Let \(x_k\in(0,1/4)\) be the previously established
location of the reflected norm maximum, measured backward from
the last index. Let \(B_k\) be its original increasing coefficient
action on \([0,x_k]\), with \(B_k(0)=0\) and \(B_k(x_k)=\chi_k\).
If \(L_N/N\to\delta\), then
\[
 N^{-1}\log\|P_{L_N,N}a_N\|_2
 \longrightarrow B_k(\min\{\delta,x_k\})-B_k(x_k).
\]
For \(\delta>x_k\), the omitted norm is exponentially small.
At \(\delta=x_k\), only the zero exponential loss is asserted;
no limiting mass fraction or polynomial reconstruction bound is
deduced. These are coordinate projections, not arbitrary signed
closing operations.

### Why approximate Casimir invariance does not select the source

The [exact resolvent calculation](research_original_casimir_resolvent_rate.md)
works for the original Casimir matrix at every fixed nonreal
parameter \(z\), without assuming a knot state.
It proves
\[
 \lim_N N^{-1}\log\|(C_N-zI)^{-1}\|_2=I(z),
\]
where \(I(z)=0\) outside the disk \(|z+2|<4\). Inside that disk,
\[
 \begin{split}
 c_z&=\frac{4-|z|^2}{2(2-\operatorname{Re}z)},\qquad
 x_z=\frac1{2\pi}\arccos(c_z/2),\\
 I(z)&=\int_{x_z}^{1-x_z}
       \log\frac{2-2\cos(2\pi x)}
                    {|2\cos(2\pi x)-z|}\,dx>0 .
 \end{split}
\]
The proof uses the literal bidiagonal inverse, uniform sine-product
bounds and an exact sign calculation. A normalized inverse column
has Casimir residual \(\exp\{-NI(z)+o(N)\}\), while its first-cap
observation vanishes exactly. These constructed vectors belong to
the actual operator; they are not claimed to be crossing-word states.

At the geometric value \(z_k\) of the reflected source, its
unit-growth equation gives \(x_{z_k}=x_k\). This relates the
geometric character to the precise coordinate threshold above.
It does not identify the resolvent action \(I(z_k)\) with the
crossing-source action \(\chi_k\), or give the missing signed
closing coefficient.

The practical implication is specific. A useful near-invariance
argument must retain enough of the interior geometric state and
prove its coupling to the actual closing row. Small Casimir
residuals and endpoint control alone cannot supply that coupling.

The exact middle-coefficient calculation was also pursued before
taking absolute values. Its outgoing Newton observation satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{CT}_Y[p_{D-n}(Y)C_{\beta,N}(Y,Z)]
 =\sum_{b=0}^{n}
       \frac{\nu_{n-b}^{-1}}{P_bP_{n-b}}C_{\beta,N}(r^b,Z),
 \quad \nu_j=(-1)^jr^{-j(j+1)/2}.
\]
Each backward step therefore restores a complete conditional
source at a new physical index. Combining these observations
with the quotient weights returns the full divided-difference
source; it does not impose a new support cutoff. No estimate
for the remaining middle contraction has been obtained this way.

The existing [dominant-saddle transport theorem](research_dominant_saddle_transport.md)
already addresses preservation of the top relative cycle through
ordinary Stokes events. Its global quantum-cycle and boundary
hypotheses remain the relevant unresolved conditions. Neither
analyticity of the finite family nor the new resolvent calculation
verifies them.

### Both end bands of the selected coefficient are now controlled

The new estimates concern the attempt to append a third short tangle
of power three or four to the already treated pair \((3,4)\).
They do not yet establish the full asymptotic for either triple.
The existing knot-family conclusions are unchanged.

Write the complete prefix in its original Newton basis,
\[
 F_N(Y)=\sum_{i=0}^{D}a_{i,N}f_i(Y),\qquad D=N-1,
\]
and let
\[
 \mathcal S_{j,\beta}[F]
   =N[Y^{jN}]\{F(Y)d_N(Y)C_{\beta,N}(Y,Z)\},
 \qquad j=0,1.
\]
Here \([Y^k]\) denotes Laurent-coefficient extraction; \(d_N\)
is the original reciprocal-factorial interpolation polynomial,
and \(C_{\beta,N}\) is the complete next-tangle kernel.
The exact transfer is \(\mathcal T_\beta=\mathcal S_{0,\beta}
+\mathcal S_{1,\beta}\). All factors and their normalizations
are those of the linked source notes.

The [low-index theorem](research_mixed_next_selected_low_newton_band.md)
bounds the contribution to \(\mathcal S_{1,\beta}\) from
\(i\le\lfloor N/25\rfloor\). After normalization by the original
geometric exponential, it and every fixed mixed derivative are
\(O(e^{-N/1000})\). The proof uses the exact polynomial quotient
by \(Y^N-1\), with the incoming cap coefficient kept intact.

The [high-index theorem](research_mixed_next_selected_high_newton_band.md)
does the same for \(i\ge D-\lfloor N/16\rfloor\), with the stronger
bound \(O(e^{-N/200})\). The essential step is to retain a
complementary sine factorial in the incoming coefficient until it
cancels a denominator in the quotient. Bounding those factors
separately would lose the estimate. Both results cover the stated
ordinary families and the actual matched terminal bases, both
parities, and the specified complex neighborhoods.

These are bounds for contributions to one Fourier coefficient.
They do not give pointwise estimates for a truncated prefix.
In particular, define
\[
 F_N^{\mathrm{middle}}
 =\sum_{\lfloor N/25\rfloor<i<D-\lfloor N/16\rfloor}
                       a_{i,N}f_i.
\]
The exact remaining problem can now be written
\[
 \mathcal T_\beta[F_N]-I_{\mathrm{geom},N}
 =N\int_{\Gamma_0\setminus J_*}F_Nd_NC_{\beta,N}\,dy
   +\mathcal S_{1,\beta}[F_N^{\mathrm{middle}}]+E_N,
\]
where \(Y=e^{-2\pi iy}\), \(\Gamma_0=[0,1]+ih_*\) is the original
lower period, and \(J_*\) is its original local geometric segment.
Both have increasing real orientation and are fixed at the base
reference when differentiating. The term \(I_{\mathrm{geom},N}\)
is the exact local integral, whose nonzero asymptotic coefficient
was already established. The normalized error \(E_N\), including
fixed mixed derivatives, is \(O(e^{-N/1000})\).

Crucially, the lower integral retains the full \(F_N\).
This assembly uses neither the earlier cardinal filter nor an
unproved asymptotic for \(F_N^{\mathrm{middle}}\).
The displayed integral and middle coefficient are not yet
controlled at the required rate.

### The upper endpoint arcs now reach the prescribed height

The [upper radial source theorem](research_mixed_next_upper_radial_seam.md)
extends the earlier small seam neighborhood to a fixed tube around
the entire segment \(Y=e^{2\pi h}\), \(0\le h\le1/100\).
It estimates the complete selected density, including the original
prefix, every row of the next conditional kernel, and the polynomial
forcing in \(d_N\). It holds for all actual ordinary and terminal
next-three and next-four references, both level parities, and the
specific older filtered prefix.

The proof uses exact paired numerator factors. For \(R\ge1\),
\[
 a_j(R)=\frac{|p_j(R)|}{|P_j|},\qquad
 a_j(R)\le R^{N-1},\qquad
 R^{-j}a_j(R)\le R^{(N-1)/4}.
\]
The identity \(d_N=N^{-1}\sum_j p_j/P_j\) also gives
\(|d_N(R)|R^{-N}\le1\). Thus the entire selected product acquires
at most \(5\log R/4\) in its exponential rate. The stronger
geometric action bounds below exceed this cost with a fixed margin.
A direct finite-product perturbation bound gives the fixed complex
tube; its width does not depend on \(N\).

The [top-arc removal theorem](research_mixed_next_top_seam_arc_removal.md)
applies this estimate at the actual upper height \(H=1/100\).
Keep \(h_*<0\) at the geometric critical height and the original
filtered kernel
\[
 K_N(y)=
 \frac{N F_N^{\rm mid}(w,Y)d_N(Y)C_{\beta,N}(Y,Z)}{1-Y^N},
 \qquad Y=e^{-2\pi iy},\quad Z=e^{-2\pi iz}.
\]
For a fixed sufficiently small \(s>0\), the remaining signed
integral is exactly
\[
 \mathscr R_N^{\rm short}
 =\int_{([0,1]+ih_*)\setminus J_*}K_N\,dy
  -\int_{[s,\,11/50]+iH}K_N\,dy
  -\int_{[9/20,\,1-s]+iH}K_N\,dy .
\]
Here \(J_*\) is the already established local geometric segment
on the lower period. The full transfer differs from
\(I_{\rm geom,N}+\mathscr R_N^{\rm short}\), after normalization
by its original geometric action, by
\(O(e^{-N\Delta/64})\), where \(\Delta=59/440000\), including
fixed mixed derivatives.
The geometric contribution has its unchanged nonzero leading
coefficient.

The remaining sufficient assertion is that this signed remainder
is exponentially smaller than the geometric contribution.
Its lower interval still includes the negative-height endpoint
regions. Its two upper middle intervals remain unestimated.
The complete third-short-tangle asymptotic and the general
finite-exceptions theorem are therefore still open, and no new

### An exact algebraic expression for the selected coefficient

The [Newton quotient calculation](research_mixed_next_selected_wrap_quotient.md)
gives a second route to the upper remainder. Write the original
prefix as \(F_N=\sum_i a_{i,N}f_i\), where \(f_i=p_i/P_i\),
and divide the complete product by the period polynomial:
\[
 f_i d_N=(Y^N-1)Q_i+R_i,\qquad \deg R_i<N,\qquad
 Q_i=\sum_{m<i}q_{i,m}p_m.
\]
The note derives every coefficient of this quotient. Summation
by parts in a terminating quantum-binomial sum gives the exact
all-level bound
\[
 |q_{i,m}|\le
 \frac{S_{i-m-1}}{N^2}+\frac1{N S_{m+1}},\qquad
 S_j=|P_j|,\quad 1\le i<N,\quad0\le m<i .
\]
The resonant last row \(i=N-1\) is handled separately.
The selected Fourier coefficient is then exactly
\[
 N[Y^N](F_Nd_NC_{\beta,N})
 =N\sum_i a_{i,N}\sum_{m<i}q_{i,m}
                       \operatorname{CT}_Y[p_m C_{\beta,N}].
\]
This retains the coherent original coefficients and the complete
outgoing observations. The corresponding total contraction is
not yet bounded below the geometric exponential rate.
In particular this calculation does not establish positivity or
noncancellation of the selected coefficient. The frozen note
\(194380e5\ldots\) has full root and separate proof/source reviews;
no numerical evaluation was used.

The [filtered contour theorem](research_mixed_next_filtered_meromorphic_seam.md)
then removes an apparent difficulty at the sampling nodes. The
previously fixed filter makes the numerator vanish at every node
in this neighborhood, so the poles of \(K_N\) there are removable.
Boundary estimates and the maximum modulus principle bound the
quotient itself, including at those nodes. Both vertical sides can
be moved exactly to half-grid positions next to the periodic endpoint.
Their short central portions are exponentially smaller than the
geometric contribution.

For the ordinary next-tangle references, the resulting reduction is
\[
 e^{-N\mathcal P_\beta^+(w,z)}
 \{\mathcal T_\beta[F_{34,N}]-I_{\rm geom,N}
                         -\mathscr R_N^{\rm long}\}
       =O(e^{-N\Delta/64}),\qquad \Delta=59/440000,
\]
with fixed mixed derivatives on smaller fixed neighborhoods.
Here \(\mathscr R_N^{\rm long}\) is an explicitly oriented integral:
it contains the remaining bottom and top intervals and the lower
and upper portions of both vertical sides. Moving the sides also
adds horizontal intervals at the original heights; these are
included in this remainder and have not been estimated.

The unresolved assertion is still that this signed remainder is
exponentially smaller than the nonzero local geometric term.
The new estimates therefore do not complete the third-short-tangle
theorem and do not enlarge the established knot families.
They close the small endpoint neighborhood for all the stated
output types. The longer vertical portions and complementary
horizontal intervals require further estimates.

### The preceding central-contour reduction

The first incoming integration is now complete on the central
selected segment of the second contour. The
[complete-prefix assembly](research_mixed_next_complete_prefix_selected_segment.md)
combines all six oriented parts, including the corner estimate
below, and proves a finite exponential loss \(1/2000\) for
\(F_{34,N}d_NY^{-N}C_{\beta,N}\), with its original outgoing
allocation. This is the entire prefix polynomial on that segment.
It still leaves the complementary second-variable integrals.

Those two Fourier remainders now have a single exact representation.
The [paired meromorphic rectangle](research_mixed_next_paired_meromorphic_rectangle.md)
uses the already established physical-index filter
\(F_N^{\rm mid}\) and the kernel
\[
 K_N(y)=
 \frac{N F_N^{\rm mid}(w,Y)d_N(Y)C_{\beta,N}(Y,Z)}
      {1-Y^N},\qquad Y=e^{-2\pi iy}.
\]
The removed physical values are zeros of \(F_N^{\rm mid}\),
so their poles in this representation are removable. The
residue theorem gives the complete filtered transfer as the
counterclockwise integral over one rectangle enclosing exactly
the retained nodes. Its bottom contains the known geometric
stationary segment; its top contains the selected central
segment just estimated. All four vertical half-sides remain.

After subtracting these two segments and restoring the small
filter correction, the exact result is
\[
 e^{-N\mathcal P_\beta^+(w,z)}
 \{\mathcal T_\beta[F_{34,N}]-I_{\rm geom,N}
                      -\mathscr R_N\}
       =O(e^{-N\Delta/32}),\qquad \Delta=59/440000,
\]
including fixed mixed derivatives on smaller fixed neighborhoods.
Here \(I_{\rm geom,N}\) is the already proved local integral with
nonzero leading coefficient, \(\mathcal P_\beta^+\) is its original
action, and \(\mathscr R_N\) is the explicitly oriented remaining
boundary integral of \(K_N\). Thus an exponentially smaller bound
for this one signed remainder would complete the local next-transfer
asymptotic. That bound is not proved. The same note gives an exact
cardinal-polynomial example showing why bounds at the deleted
physical nodes alone cannot estimate the new vertical sides.
Their coherent source must be retained.

A separate
[algebraic transport theorem](research_mixed_four_conditional_algebraic_transport_domain.md)
extends the type-four critical branch and its action monotonicity
to
\[
 \Re X<0,\quad\Im X\ge0,\quad |X|\le1,\quad
 |X|^2(3-2\Re X)\ge1,\qquad
 \Im Y<0,\quad\Re Y<1.
\]
The original cubic has one simple upper root on this domain, with
the original zero logarithmic lift. Its incoming multiplier
\(w=(v-X)/(1-X)\) satisfies \(\Im w>0\) and \(|w|<1\).
Consequently moving the incoming coordinate rightward or upward
decreases the real action. This includes actual negative outgoing
heights and requires no lower bound for \(|Y|\).
It is an action theorem: a complete finite-source estimate on the
enlarged domain remains separate.

rectangle as the conditional branch. Their logarithmic equations
keep their zero lifts and both critical points remain
nondegenerate. This is a statement about the critical phases;
it does not place their finite-source contours inside an
already proved endpoint domain.

The [upper-half estimate at negative incoming height](research_mixed_conditional_negative_height_upper_half.md)
now bounds every physical conditional summand with \(j\ge\lceil N/2\rceil\)
throughout the required displaced parameter rectangle. If \(\Theta\)
denotes the original conditional critical action, the complete sum of
their absolute values is at most
\[
 C N^B\exp\{N(\Re\Theta-1/1400)\}.
\]
The proof keeps the radial contribution of the outgoing numerator
and uses a positive lower bound for the complementary incoming
logarithmic integral. For the first part of the incoming interval
it uses the stronger action bound already present in the real-arc
proof. All physical upper-half rows, both parities and numerator
zeros are included. The result also controls fixed derivatives on
smaller complex neighborhoods.

This is an estimate for part of the original finite sum, not a new
knot-family theorem. On the deepest face, the new full theorem now
includes the interval \(1-\Re a\le j/N<1/2\) in its retained contour
and pays all its connecting pieces. The endpoint coefficient is
also controlled near the actual
real-incoming cap critical path, as above; its complete outer cap
and the product of the two factors still require their own estimates.
The theorem for separated short pairs of powers three and four,
with sufficiently long remaining twists, is unchanged.

For the remaining cap estimate, the
[wrapped-row transport theorem](research_mixed_cap_wrapped_row_transport.md)
improves the complete positive bound for private rows past their
incoming wall. Their rate is at most

 h(1-a)\le101/125-\frac95(a-1/2)^2
                      \qquad(1/2\le a\le7/10).
\]
Each row retains its complete endpoint coefficient. Reflection
handles the upper private half, and the true endpoint rows have
their own bound below this rate. The comparison with the cap's own
critical action is now proved by the wall-action theorem above.
The left private contour corridor and the remaining outer-cap
contributions still require estimates.

The [deeper endpoint theorem](research_mixed_endpoint_cap_rectangle_deeper_extension.md)
extends the complete original endpoint asymptotic to a fixed

          [27/100,49/100]+i[-3/50,1/25].
\]
The new depth is obtained by transporting the already established

coefficient. It works with either sign of the auxiliary critical

Both integer parities and fixed joint derivatives are included.
This is an extension of the complete coefficient theorem.
The actual-path theorem above now supplies containment of the
real-incoming critical path and the missing private interval
along that path. The full outer-sum estimate remains.

The [conditional branch theorem at negative height](research_mixed_conditional_negative_height_branch.md)
now covers the full proposed incoming rectangle
\(1/2\le\Re a\le7/10,\ -9/125\le\Im a\le0\).
The selected root is unique in the upper half-plane, simple,
and remains on the original zero logarithmic lift. The proof

is strictly negative on the retained regular index interval.
This removes branch collision and a crossing of the incoming

The [conditional height-monotonicity theorem](research_mixed_conditional_height_action_monotonicity.md)

This result and the root bounds are algebraic and analytic

The proposed displaced contour now has a complete bound for one

Both integer parities and the original integration measure are

The [moving-cut transport theorem](research_mixed_next_incoming_staircase_transport.md)

For the endpoint coefficient needed in a coherent cap estimate,

The lower rows increase to the lower cut, and the upper rows

Its uniform action floor \(1511/2000\) therefore pays that

The deeper endpoint theorem supplies the cut comparisons and

The [incoming connector estimate](research_mixed_next_selected_incoming_connector_envelope.md)
now bounds the complete original source on its vertical segment from

A local change to the critical-action coordinate gives a two-endpoint

The [complete conditional continuation](research_mixed_real_arc_complete_conditional_packet.md)
now proves
\[
 C_{1,N}(e^{-2\pi ia},e^{-2\pi iy})
   =N^{-1}\mathcal B(a,y)e^{N\Theta(a,y)}

on a fixed complex neighborhood of

This extends the complete finite conditional factor across the whole

The [whole-cap upper theorem](research_mixed_real_arc_complete_cap_upper.md)
now proves a uniform strict upper rate below

 \widehat M=\frac{203}{200}-\frac{1303}{7680000}
\]
on the entire interval \(1/2\le a\le7/10\), for all real ordinary

 e_0=\frac14-\frac{i\log2}{4\pi}.

Its internal critical point is real. All revived rows, the two

The [conditional curvature bound](research_mixed_half_face_conditional_curvature.md)
sharpens the comparison at the incoming half face. Maximizing

 \bar q''(x)<-\frac{2\pi}{3},
 \qquad 11/50\le x\le9/20.

Thus its former supporting-line estimate improves by
\(\pi(x-1/4)^2/3\). With the selected factorial halfweight,

Subtracting the following affine action leaves a concave

 \frac6{37}(a-1/2)+\frac{15}{16}(a-1/2)^2.

It bounds the complete conditional finite sum using its proved

A [new quadratic protocol](research_mixed_half_face_saved_quadratic_protocol.md)

After full static reviews and a frozen manifest binding 399
files, the sole prescribed calculation completed. Its

The calculation used only exact rational arithmetic on the
old stored lower bounds.
The [outcome record](research_mixed_half_face_saved_quadratic_outcome.md)
preserves the complete inventory and distinguishes insufficient

Thus the stronger analytic estimates have not yet established

The [fixed-height product estimate](research_incoming_fixed_height_row_contraction.md)

The [exact incoming row contraction](research_incoming_finite_row_contraction.md)
gives a finite-level version of transport from the half-face

 \exp\!\left\{-\frac{\pi^2j(j+1)}{2N}(a-1/2)\right\}.
\]
This is an exact product inequality, obtained by integrating its
logarithmic derivative. It contracts every positive diagonal

and it leaves the low rows and rows past the numerator wall

The [joint source theorem](research_mixed_half_face_joint_source_packet.md)
puts the two complete finite factors on one fixed complex parameter

 F_N(a,w,y)=U_{0,N}(w,e^{-2\pi ia})
                      C_{1,N}(e^{-2\pi ia},e^{-2\pi iy})
          =N^{-2}\mathcal D(a,w,y)e^{N\mathcal P(a,w,y)}
                       \{1+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})\},
 \qquad \mathcal D\ne0.
\]
Here \(a\) is the incoming coordinate, \(w\) the ordinary color,
and \(y\) the outgoing coordinate. The neighborhood contains

\(.22\le\Re y\le.45,\ 0\le\Im y\le.01\).
Continuing the incoming coordinate retains the physical rows which
vanish at even levels at \(a=1/2\) but revive when \(a\) moves.

The [incoming transport theorem](research_mixed_half_face_incoming_transport.md)
now proves
\[
                 \Re\mathcal P_a(1/2,-2,y)<-\frac{22}{53}
\]
throughout that outgoing rectangle. The derivative has an exact

Its modulus bound gives the strict negative sign without evaluating

\[
 N\int_0^\ell F_N(a+s,w,y)\,ds
    =-N^{-2}\frac{\mathcal D(a,w,y)}{\mathcal P_a(a,w,y)}
       e^{N\mathcal P(a,w,y)}
                       \{1+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})\}.
\]
All fixed normalized parameter derivatives and both parities are
included. This controls a genuine short piece of the incoming path.
Its endpoint term can cancel with an adjoining piece when their
common artificial cut is removed; the theorem does not settle that
assembly, the original vertical join, or the macroscopic interval.

The [general incoming transport calculation](research_mixed_half_face_general_incoming_transport.md)
continues the original critical phases throughout
\(1/2\le a\le7/10\). Two cubic equations determine the continued

This gives a continuation of the phases, not of the finite-source

                 e=\frac14-\frac{i\log2}{4\pi}.
\]
It lies outside the rectangle used by the complete cap proof,

The [uniform phase-decrease theorem](research_mixed_half_face_global_phase_decrease.md)

\[
 \left|\exp\{\mathcal P_a(a,-2,y)\}\right|<\frac{15}{16},
 \qquad
 \Re\mathcal P_a(a,-2,y)<-\frac1{16}
 \quad\left(\frac12\le a\le\frac7{10},\ y\in\mathcal Y\right).
\]
Thus the original critical action decreases uniformly along
the whole remaining real incoming interval. This removes the
phase-sign obstruction without a numerical calculation. The

above now handle the two finite factors throughout this interval.
What remains for this part is the stated comparison with
the geometric action and the original connecting path.
The cap upper theorem obtains the control actually needed
here without claiming a full relative cap asymptotic.

The [complete cap theorem at the incoming half
face](research_mixed_half_face_complete_cap_packet.md) now proves

 U_{0,N}(w,e^{-2\pi ia})
   =N^{-1}\mathcal B_{\rm half}(a,w)

 \qquad \mathcal B_{\rm half}(a,w)\ne0,

on a fixed complex neighborhood of \((a,w)=(1/2,-2)\).
Here \(a\) is the incoming boundary coordinate and \(w\) is the

The proof compares both original cuts with the cap's own critical

This local theorem does not extend throughout \(1/2\le a\le7/10\),
and comparison with the action of the following geometric piece is

Its own action also has the

 \Re\mathcal T_{\rm half}(1/2,-2)
       <\frac{203}{200}-\frac{1303}{7680000}.
\]
The proof retains the decrease from the real-index maximum to the

This scalar estimate alone does not decide the selected geometric

The [scalar comparison note](research_mixed_half_face_scalar_envelope_obstruction.md)
records the exact sufficient inequality, including the remaining

the critical coordinates or improve the estimates.

The [fixed saved-data comparison](research_mixed_half_face_saved_affine_protocol.md)
has now been executed once, after static review and freezing its

transport the saved boundary data to the full disks.

The [recorded outcome](research_mixed_half_face_saved_affine_outcome.md)
is inconclusive. All 4,096 comparisons completed: 1,498 lower

and every insufficient certificate is retained; no retry or

These are conservative lower certificates, so their insufficiency
does not disprove the actual critical-action inequality. It does

The complete local finite-source asymptotics and the uniform
phase-decrease theorem above are unchanged. This calculation adds

The [complete conditional theorem at the incoming half
face](research_mixed_half_face_complete_conditional_packet.md)
now proves an asymptotic for the whole original polynomial
\(C_{1,N}(-1,Y)\), not just for its central integral. For
\(Y=e^{-2\pi iy}\), with \(.22\le\Re y\le.45\) and
\(0\le\Im y\le.01\), it gives
\[
 C_{1,N}(-1,e^{-2\pi iy})
   =N^{-1}\mathcal B(y)e^{N\Theta(y)}
                  \{1+O_{\mathrm{hol}}(N^{-1})\},
 \qquad \mathcal B(y)\ne0 .
\]
The cubic equation for the internal critical point has a unique
root on the required half-plane branch, and its original logarithmic

action bound \(\Re\Theta>13/24\) control every omitted physical
row, both full residue remainders, and the main integral's connecting
segments. The proof includes odd levels, where the upper rows do not
terminate. It is therefore a noncancellation theorem for this complete
conditional factor. Together with the complete cap theorem above,
it gives nonzero asymptotics for both factors at this boundary value.
Their final contraction and comparison with the geometric action
remain separate.

There is also an [independent proof of the small-seam
bound](research_mixed_endpoint_seam_direct_reflection.md). For every

satisfies
\[
 \sup_{\substack{-2\le w\le2\\|Y-1|\le\zeta}}
 |\partial_w^k\partial_Y^m H_N(w,Y)|
       \le C_{\eta,k,m}N^{B_{\eta,k,m}}e^{\eta N}
\]
for every fixed derivative order \(k,m\), at both level parities.
An exact factorial reflection identity makes it possible to move
the middle part of the sum to a tall contour; the physical end
ranges and both residue corrections are bounded separately.
This repairs an application that had relied on a continuous-index
asymptotic outside its proved range. It establishes the required
upper bound near \(Y=1\), but does not prove that broader asymptotic
or assert nonvanishing near the seam.

The [allocated action bound](research_mixed_next_allocated_action_floor.md)
recovers additional room from the already established radius-dependent
following-family comparison. With the original incoming halfweight
included, the geometric action is greater than
\(9/5+439/2112000\). The selected-contour estimate can consequently
accept a polynomial whose unit-disk exponential rate is \(25/16\),
instead of \(77/50\). The input of that comparison is the next
internal coordinate \(s_3^*\); the more distant external parameter
\(s_4^*\) is kept distinct.

This stronger comparison pays the
[replacement lower private side](research_mixed_next_lower_private_cut_source.md).
The literal complete endpoint sum, with all reflected terms and
carriers retained, has rate below \(5/6\) on
\(e=1/8-i\eta\), \(0\le\eta\le11/200\), for every real incoming
coordinate \(1/2\le a\le7/10\). After the adjacent conditional
factor and the original selected weights are included, the finite
gap is \(1/300\). Adjacent residue rectangles at matching heights
cancel their shared side at \(e=.27\) exactly. Thus that artificial
side can be removed and replaced by the newly controlled one.
The horizontal path from the replacement side to the previously
proved endpoint rectangle remains unbounded. The note also proves
a genuine endpoint asymptotic on a thin strip over \([1/8,.27]\);
its width is not asserted to reach the full descent.

These results remove specific boundary obstructions and establish
nonzero coefficients for two complete factors. They do not settle the complete

finite-exceptions theorem. In particular, controlling the replacement

The [new lower-index estimate](research_mixed_next_low_private_middle_arc.md)
removes another specified part of the original finite sum. Write
\(a\) for its incoming boundary coordinate, \(e=j/N\) for the
internal index of the first cap, and \(t=k/N\) for the adjacent
conditional index. On \(1/2\le a\le7/10\), the terms with
\(e\le1/8\) have a strict exponential gap after multiplication by
the actual following factors and their prescribed outgoing weight.
The proof combines two curvature inequalities before maximizing and
uses the retained conditional polynomial's degree, which is less than
\(N/2\). This smaller degree reduces the cost of moving the outgoing
variable outside the unit circle. The resulting finite gap is
\(1/120\), with a smaller gap for fixed normalized local derivatives.
The estimate holds at both level parities and keeps each complete
endpoint coefficient before taking absolute values.

Together with the earlier upper-index and conditional-end estimates,
this leaves the real joint region
\[
 \frac12\le a\le\frac7{10},\qquad
 \frac18<e<1-a-\delta_*,\qquad
 \frac1{16}<t<1-a-\varepsilon .
\]
Here \(\delta_*,\varepsilon>0\) are the fixed widths removed near the
factorial walls. This describes the remaining real integration
region, not the entire outstanding proof: the initial vertical
incoming segment and the other connecting and outgoing pieces still
need their stated comparisons.

The [fixed-cut obstruction](research_mixed_next_half_face_fixed_cut_obstruction.md)
shows why simply lowering the internal integration contour is
insufficient. At the unchanged lower cut \(e=27/100\), a retained
conditional row makes the joint exponential profile exceed the

There is also a new [local critical-point calculation at
\(X=-1\)](research_mixed_half_face_cap_critical_point.md).
Its critical equation is an explicit cubic,
and its chosen root belongs to the original endpoint branch with
zero logarithmic lift. The note derives a nonzero Gaussian
contribution for a specified central integral. The complete cap
theorem above supplies the subsequent proof that this contribution
dominates the other parts of the finite cap. None of these latest
steps changes the established knot-family theorem.

The [paired localization theorem](research_mixed_next_low_cardinal_paired_localization.md)
removes one unnecessary requirement from the local next-source
argument. The low physical input interval was already bounded after
the two Fourier contributions were added. Its unselected central

kernel; the selected central segment had an earlier bound. If
