respective complements, the exact identity
\[
 R_0(E)+R_1(E)=\mathcal T(E)-G_0(E)-G_1(E)
\]
bounds the sum of the complementary corrections. Initially \(E\) is
the cardinal polynomial of the removed low physical input interval
and \(\mathcal T(E)\) its complete finite transfer. The theorem also
applies to the full correction for the older \(11/12\) filter:
it removes \(a\ge\lceil23N/24\rceil\), the low \(b\)-interval,
and \(b\ge\lceil11N/12\rceil\), with their overlaps retained.
The two contours
may differ: each central segment is subtracted from its own full
cycle. No claim of pointwise cancellation between different paths
is needed.

This result holds at the actual ordinary next-output references
and on fixed local neighborhoods, with the original boundary
derivatives and both level parities. It does not give the same
paired bound at every independent outgoing plateau coordinate.
It also does not estimate the complementary source that remains
after filtering. The full \(343\) and \(344\) asymptotics are still
open, but separate complete-sector bounds for this filtering
correction are no longer required for that local assembly. The
argument does not cover the newer \(8/9\) filter, whose available
correction bound is larger.

The [weighted coefficient theorem](research_mixed_next_low_weighted_coefficient_bound.md)
also estimates the actual signed incoming combination, rather than
an arbitrarily chosen vector. Its coefficient norm has exponential
rate below \(999/500+\epsilon(\delta)\), leaving \(21/500\)
before tolerances below the established next-action floor \(51/25\).
The outgoing Newton evaluation has an exponentially growing dual
norm, so this estimate alone does not control that evaluation.
The note gives the precise remaining cost and bounds the actual
exterior cardinal multiplier without assuming it is nonzero.

There is now an [exact Gram description of the complete selected
response](research_mixed_next_selected_response_gram_structure.md),
including its distinct adjoint observation and a finite Cauchy
formula on the roots \(Y^N=-1\). The positive Gram matrix
\(\mathsf A\), formed from the original conditional kernel,
satisfies a rank-one displacement equation for its lowering
operator \(\mathcal L\). In the resulting
\(\mathsf A^{-1}\) metric, the normalized original input
\(\zeta=\sqrt N\,d_N\) satisfies
\(\|(I-\mathcal L)\zeta\|=N^{-1/2}\) exactly. This is a statement
about that specified operator. The original diagonal phase
operator sends the same vector to an orthogonal vector in the
same metric. The outgoing evaluation cost is also retained, so
these identities do not assert invariance under all transfers or
a lower bound for the completed invariant.

The [uniform incoming-family theorem](research_mixed_next_low_node_family_packet.md)
extends the coefficient and Fourier estimates below from the first
incoming node to every \(B=r^b\) with \(0\le b\le\delta N\), for one
fixed \(\delta>0\). Here \(r=e^{-2\pi i/N}\), and \(b\) labels the
original root-of-unity boundary values. An exact sampled identity
supplies the boundary value before the recurrence's zero multiplier;
the proof estimates the indices after that zero separately. The
coefficient vectors are asymptotically scalar multiples of the
first-node vector. One common phase correction consequently gives
an explicit Gaussian Fourier asymptotic and a nonzero prescribed
zero mode for the whole family.

The qualification about the observation is essential. The two
Fourier sectors have opposite leading coefficient packets, and
their combination can cancel those packets. For a signed sum over
incoming nodes, the family theorem reduces the leading coefficient
to an explicit scalar sum but does not prove that scalar is nonzero.
The almost-invariance estimate therefore supplies a lower bound
for a specified Fourier observation, not yet for the contraction
defining the knot invariant.

The [complex source equation](research_mixed_column_exact_complex_equation.md)
also distinguishes the sampled recurrence from the equation needed
for contour deformation. The specified Laurent-polynomial
continuation \(\mathcal V_N(X)\) obeys
\[
 \mathcal L_N\mathcal V_N(X)
       =-\frac{\kappa^2}{N}\frac{1-X^{-N}}{X-1},
 \qquad |\kappa|=1,
\]
where \(\mathcal L_N\) is the second-order difference operator
defined in that note. The right side vanishes at every sampling
root except \(X=1\), where its removable value is \(-\kappa^2\).
It can be exponentially large inside the unit circle. Its own
first-order equation gives an exact homogeneous annihilator for
the enlarged system, with the forcing factor retained. This is
an equation for the original finite source; it has not been
identified with a knot's quantum \(A\)-polynomial.

For the forcing in the outgoing type-three equation, the
[positive Gram identity](research_mixed_next_actual_forcing_gram_bounds.md)
now gives its exact circle norm as a fourth moment of \(M^*M\),
where \(M\) is the original crossing matrix. The known second and
third moments bound that fourth moment from both sides. In
particular the complete forcing is exponentially larger somewhere
on the circle than at the positive seam value. The same identity
gives an explicit bound depending on the output angle, but the
present output enclosures include its worst angle. Positivity at
one boundary value and a whole-circle norm bound do not settle
the actual outgoing evaluation.

These latest results improve the analytic control of the finite
sums. They do not enlarge the knot class in the established
long-filling theorem, and they do not settle the full three-tangle
words \(343\) or \(344\).

The [full cumulative Fourier theorem](research_mixed_next_low_cardinal_full_fourier_packet.md)
now gives a nonzero asymptotic on every fixed compact interval of
coefficient indices \(0<j/N<1/2\), on both sides of the maximum.
It estimates the complete initialized vector
\(\mathbf a_N=(a_0,\ldots,a_{N-1})\):
\[
 \|\mathbf a_N\|_2\sim C N^{-5/4}e^{N A(x_*)},\qquad C>0.
\]
Here \(A\) is the real exponential profile of the original Fourier
column and \(x_*\) is its unique nondegenerate maximum. After removal
of the explicit phase and normalization to unit norm, the resulting
vector \(\zeta_N\) satisfies
\[
 \|\mathsf S\zeta_N-\zeta_N\|_2
       =\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{2N}}+O(N^{-1}),\qquad
                    \alpha=-A''(x_*)>0,
\]
where \(\mathsf S\) is cyclic shift by one index. Every Fourier
coefficient on \(|m|\le T\sqrt N\) has its explicit leading
Gaussian asymptotic. In particular the prescribed zero mode has
magnitude at least \(cN^{-1/4}\). The
[earlier peak-window theorem](research_mixed_next_low_cardinal_peak_window.md)
only gave band mass and existence of some mode for the full vector.
The stronger result retains the explicit phase correction. Its
zero-mode observation is not the outgoing evaluation used by the
knot invariant.

The new boundary input is the
[exact terminal coefficient](research_mixed_next_low_cardinal_terminal_anchor.md)
\[
                  a_{N-1}=d_N'(1)/N,
\]
where \(d_N\) is the original reciprocal-factorial interpolation
polynomial. Its unit-disk bound makes this endpoint exponentially
smaller than the interior peak. Summing the actual recurrence from
both ends proves exponential decay outside every fixed neighborhood
of that peak. A smooth next-order ratio, obtained from the original
second-order recurrence, then improves the full-vector relative error
to \(O(N^{-1})\), enough to determine the prescribed Fourier mode.
The boundary constant is estimated from the original sum throughout.

The [exact outgoing equation](research_mixed_next_low_cardinal_outgoing_equation.md)
expresses that Newton evaluation as the unique polynomial solution
of a forced finite \(q\)-difference equation with a specified boundary
value. Its forcing is an original two-tangle conditional polynomial;
the top-degree term and the homogeneous solution are retained.
The [function-norm theorem](research_mixed_next_outgoing_response_norms.md)
now inverts the outer factor with only polynomial norm loss, including
its actual homogeneous coefficient determined by \(d_N'(1)\).
For the remaining type-three factor, it also determines the sharp
worst-case disk amplification:
\[
 \log\|(I-\mathcal L)^{-1}\|_{R\to R}
       =N\Xi(R)+O_R(\log N),\qquad
 \Xi(R)=\max_{0\le u\le v\le1}
       \{J(v)-J(u)-(v-u)\log R\}.
\]
Here \(\mathcal Lf(Z)=(f(Z)-f(r^{-1}Z))/Z\),
\(r=e^{-2\pi i/N}\), and
\(J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds\).
This exponent is positive for \(R<2\), including the relevant
output radii. The monomial witness proves that an arbitrary forcing
cannot be transported with polynomial loss alone. It does not prove
that the actual forcing incurs that loss. Its specific cancellation
is still the analytic issue.

For the ordinary-next contour calculation, the
[joint cap estimate](research_mixed_next_coherent_cap_far_arc.md)
extends the controlled real incoming arc from \([13/16,1]\) to
\([7/10,1]\). It keeps the dependence between the incoming angle
and the private summation index before maximizing. On this part of
the source, the remaining real main integral is restricted to
\([1/2,7/10]\).

On that remaining interval the
[private-row theorem](research_mixed_next_wrapped_private_sector.md)
now bounds every private cap index \(e=j/N\ge1-a-\delta_*\),
for a fixed \(\delta_*>0\). Here \(a\) is the real incoming coordinate,
with \(X=e^{-2\pi ia}\). The retained conditional polynomial has degree
less than \(N/2\) in its outgoing variable, so moving that variable
to the selected circle costs only half the former degree bound.
This pays the complete indicated region without deforming a contour.
With the earlier conditional-end estimates, the remaining real
source has
\[
                  a+e<1-\delta_*,
                  \qquad a+t<1-\varepsilon,
\]
where \(t=k/N\) is its conditional index and
\(\varepsilon>0\) is the existing fixed cut width. Both indices
therefore stay a fixed distance from the factorial boundaries.
The initial vertical connector, the other outer contour pieces,
and the assembly of the complete Fourier coefficients still
require estimates.

These results do not yet establish the volume identity for a
three-tangle short component \(343\) or \(344\). The established
knot theorem still permits the specified separated adjacent pairs
of powers three and four, with independently sufficiently long powers
at the remaining vertices. Arbitrary short partial fillings and
finitely many exceptional assignments remain open.

## Extending the pair to a third short tangle

The next attachment is now written as an exact finite sum in
[the attachment formula](research_mixed_three_four_next_conditional_attachment.md).
It applies to both the words \(343\) and \(344\), where the digits
denote the original integer powers. Because the existing pair ends
in four, both attachments contain the complete factor
\(d_N(Y)(1+Y^{-N})\). The formula includes the intervening Gram
contraction and both Fourier coefficients. It does not require a
further Fourier transform of the prefix.

Two estimates now reach the boundary-coordinate domains selected by
the following tangle. The
[outer-row comparison](research_mixed_four_upper_rows_following_domains.md)
controls the high physical indices by their half-row and last-row
values and the low indices by the original central cut. It permits
either sign of the incoming height. The
[outgoing-radius bound](research_mixed_transformed_following_four_radial_majorant.md)
controls the complete complementary contour on the ordinary and
attached type-four domains, including terms that no longer vanish
when the outgoing color is complex. These are bounds for the finite
sums, with their zeros and fixed derivatives retained.

The complete two-tangle sum is now controlled on that correlated
family of geometric boundary values. The
[following-family asymptotic theorem](research_mixed_three_four_following_complete_prefix.md)
proves a nonzero leading term for the entire finite polynomial,
with every other part of its incoming contour exponentially smaller.
This extends the earlier result near the isolated pair's coordinate
\(z_*\) to the boundary values imposed by the next tangle.

There is now also a
[local asymptotic for the next attachment](research_mixed_three_four_next_local_source.md).
For both \(343\) and \(344\), the integral near the geometric critical
point has a nonzero leading coefficient. This statement uses the entire
two-tangle polynomial and the complete next conditional sum. It applies
to the specified ordinary and terminal reference families. It is a
lower bound for this local contribution, not for the completed invariant.

The [interior theorem for arbitrary words](research_mixed_retained_prefix_unselected_plateau.md)
extends this calculation to every fixed positive word in powers three
and four. It evaluates the full interior box for the Fourier choice
that takes \(1\) from each factor \(1+X_j^{-N}\). The leading
coefficient is nonzero, and the remainder of that box away from the
critical point is exponentially smaller. The conditional action also
gains more than \(1/6\) at each ordinary attachment. These estimates
give a common argument for every word length; they do not include the
other Fourier choices, the outside contour, or the final closure.

Several further estimates control parts of the next attachment's remainder.
The [binomial end bound](research_mixed_three_four_next_binomial_end_bound.md)
now controls the second incoming indices \(b\ge\lceil11N/12\rceil\),
extending the earlier last-four-percent bound. It sums over the first
incoming index before taking absolute values. Both Fourier coefficients
are already combined in this finite sampling identity.

The [terminal-insertion theorem](research_mixed_next_high_coefficients_terminal_insertion.md)
now extends that combined physical range to
\(b\ge\lceil8N/9\rceil\). The high Newton polynomial vanishes at
every distinct spectral root, so its exact full trace retains only
values of the remaining kernel at the first \(N-b\) roots.
An entire polynomial insertion into the original terminal-three
contours controls those values. The proof includes the removed wire
rows, removed angular nodes, both root multiplicities, and every
retained contour term. It gives coefficient rate \(153/100\) and
combined next-source rate \(203/100\), below the actual action floor
\(51/25\). The fixed normalized derivative gap is \(1/200\).
This proof uses the complete source before taking absolute values;
it does not assign a bound for the full kernel to an uncontrolled
partial sum.
The high-index coefficient bound is also uniform when the second
power in the \(33\) product is replaced by any signed integer:
after the exact radical contraction, that power contributes only
unit-modulus values at the retained roots. This uniformity concerns
the specified coefficient range, not a whole-word asymptotic.

For the narrower final band
\(b\ge\lceil99N/100\rceil\), there is now a
[separate bound for both complete Fourier coefficients](research_mixed_next_high_cardinal_whole_sectors.md).
It applies to any subset of that band, before or after the
first-coordinate deletion, on both ordinary and terminal next-reference
families. The proof controls the cardinal correction on the entire
coefficient circle, including its divided-difference term. Each error
has rate at most \(203/100\), below the actual common action floor
\(51/25\); fixed normalized derivatives have gap \(1/200\).
This gives a narrower filtering operation that is valid in each
whole coefficient. The wider \(11/12\) band is still controlled
only after the two coefficients are combined.

The [first-coordinate theorem](research_mixed_three_four_next_sectorwise_first_end.md)
also permits removing \(a\ge\lceil23N/24\rceil\), separately from
each complete Fourier coefficient. Its proof bounds the removed
polynomial throughout the second variable's unit disk, then uses the
exact interpolation polynomial and Cauchy's coefficient formula. A
separate positive estimate bounds the whole corresponding rectangle
of physical indices. It therefore also controls its overlap with the
second-coordinate deletion. The complete source is reduced to
\[
        0\le a<\lceil23N/24\rceil,\qquad
        0\le b<\lceil11N/12\rceil
\]
with an error exponentially smaller than the original geometric
contribution, including fixed derivatives on the stated neighborhoods.
The truncated first-coordinate polynomial retains the same local
asymptotic and nonzero leading coefficient as the complete \(34\)
prefix. This removes actual finite-sum terms without assuming
nonnegative coefficients.

There is now a
[fixed low-index interval theorem](research_mixed_next_low_physical_interval.md)
for both next letters. It proves that, for some fixed \(\delta>0\),
the sum over \(0\le b\le\lfloor\delta N\rfloor\) is exponentially
smaller than the actual geometric contribution. The prefix is summed
coherently before taking its modulus. Together with the earlier
high-index deletions, the remaining physical rectangle is
\[
        0\le a<\lceil23N/24\rceil,\qquad
        \lfloor\delta N\rfloor<b<\lceil11N/12\rceil .
\]
This holds on both the ordinary and terminal next-reference families,
for all real ordinary colors and on small complex complete-color
neighborhoods, with fixed derivatives and both level parities.

Using the new terminal-insertion bound, the physical rectangle can
be narrowed further to
\[
        0\le a<\lceil23N/24\rceil,\qquad
        \lfloor\delta N\rfloor<b<\lceil8N/9\rceil .
\]
Section 5 of that theorem constructs its exact cardinal polynomial,
including the overlaps with the first-coordinate deletion. Its
correction to the full prefix has unit-disk rate \(509/300\),
strictly below \(7/4\); hence the same nonzero local prefix and
next-attachment coefficients survive, with normalized local
prefix gap \(1/25\). This is a second filter. The stronger
\(77/50\) correction bound on the entire selected contour,
discussed below, still belongs to the earlier \(11/12\) filter.
Neither filter has yet supplied the missing complete-sum estimate.

The new input is a
[bound for the low Newton coefficients of the complete \(33\) polynomial](research_three_crossing_low_newton_coefficients.md).
Inserting the \(b\)-th Newton polynomial into the earlier pendant
proof costs a rate \(\epsilon(\delta)\to0\) when \(b\le\delta N\).
An exact tridiagonal transport controls the coherent outer sums;
the original contour integrals acquire a bounded polynomial
amplitude. The proof therefore retains the parts of the old
argument that relied on cancellation. The
[kernel and action comparison](research_mixed_next_low_index_kernel_margin.md)
supplies the other factor and a strict reserve \(59/440000\)
before choosing \(\delta\) and the finite-rate tolerances.
It retains the previously dropped positive terms
\(-\Re g(y)-\beta\Re g(s)\) in the actual action.

The insertion now also has an
[exact formula at every physical index](research_three_crossing_all_index_prepared_amplitude.md).
Its coefficients are finite sine-factorial sums, with different
harmonic supports below and above \(2b=N\). The boundary forcing
has a particularly simple interpretation: it removes the first
\(b\) coordinates of the prepared vector exactly. After the
original reversal, the prepared three-index sum therefore has
the additional cutoff \(k\le N-1-b\). This gives an explicit
formula and contour upper profile for the remaining middle
indices. It does not yet bound the new cutoff current or the
transported preparation error below the required geometric action.

The middle rectangle also has an exact polynomial representation.
Remove its two second-coordinate ends by the original cardinal
projections from the first-coordinate-truncated prefix, and call
the resulting polynomial \(F_N^{\rm mid}\). The complete transfer
of this polynomial is exactly the displayed rectangle. Its
difference from the full prefix has unit-disk rate at most \(8/5\),
below the prefix action \(>7/4\) at every matching reference.
Consequently it retains the same local prefix expansion and the
same nonzero local next contribution. This is a statement about
the finite source, not only its stationary equations.

Separately, the
[first-collar estimate](research_mixed_three_four_next_first_collar.md)
controls the specified small interval near the first incoming endpoint,
for both Fourier choices, when the second real coordinate lies in
\([.24,.363]\) and the third vertex is ordinary. These statements
have different domains. The
[selected right-segment theorem](research_mixed_second_selected_first_three_right_segment.md)
also controls the whole product when the first incoming real coordinate
runs from \(.45\) to \(.5\), at its actual height, and the second
coordinate stays on the selected interior segment. It includes all
rows and contour terms of its finite factors and both alternatives
in the Fourier weight. It applies to the ordinary-next reference family.

The [selected left-transition theorem](research_mixed_second_selected_first_three_left_transition.md)
now controls the first-coordinate path from \(1/10\) to
\(11/50+ih_a\), while the second coordinate remains on the same
selected interior segment. Its full-product estimate has a strict
exponential loss and includes every physical row and contour term.
The proof and its source dependencies have been checked. Together with
the interior and right-transition estimates, this covers more of the
first-coordinate contour; it does not control the second coordinate's
outer contour. The
[initial-interval theorem](research_mixed_second_selected_first_three_initial_interval.md)
now also covers the entire first real interval \([0,1/10]\),
on that same selected second-coordinate segment. It pays the
true cap ends separately at all real colors.
The [final real first-coordinate arc](research_mixed_next_selected_final_first_arc.md)
is now controlled as well: the complete original source on
\(a\in[13/16,1]\), with the second coordinate anywhere on
\([.22,.45]+i/100\), has a finite gap \(1/1000\) at the
original ordinary-next supporting plane. This is a continuous
contour estimate and uses no off-grid termination. Its key scalar
identity is
\[
 \max_{0\le t\le1}
 \{J(t-v)+J(v)-J(t)\}=J(v)-2J(v/2)\le v\log2,
 \qquad v=1-a.
\]
It bounds each incoming product while keeping the original endpoint
sum coherent.

There are now two additional reductions on the remaining real
first-coordinate interval \([1/2,13/16]\). The
[conditional end-range theorem](research_mixed_next_selected_first_wall_rows.md)
bounds all rows \(j/N\le1/16\), and all rows at or beyond
the factorial boundary \(a+j/N=1\), with fixed collars at both
ends. It retains the rows that can be nonzero between sampling
points. After multiplying by the complete cap, the lower rows have
unit-disk rate \(18167/12000\) and the rows beyond the boundary
have rate \(2249/1500\); both are strictly below \(77/50\).
The existing selected-source comparison therefore pays these
actual finite terms on the whole selected second-coordinate segment.

For the retained conditional rows, the
[real-integral reduction](research_mixed_next_far_half_conditional_aliases.md)
now pays every Fourier remainder, including both full vertical
sides and the two horizontal sides of a fixed rectangle. It uses
the original factorial interpolation \(T_N\) and gives
\[
 C_{1,N}^{\mathrm{mid}}(e^{-2\pi ia},e^{-2\pi iy})
       =N\int_{\ell_N}^{u_N(a)}T_N(t;a,y)\,dt+\mathcal A_N(a,y).
\]
The error \(\mathcal A_N\), multiplied by the complete remaining
selected source, has finite gap \(1/1000\).
The proof bounds the vertical phase derivative by \(9\pi/5\)
above the real axis and from below by \(-15\pi/8\) below it.
The cotangent remainder contributes decay \(2\pi|\Im t|\),
so both full vertical errors are controlled by the already paid
real cut values. The horizontal errors at heights \(\pm2\)
have rate less than \(2269/1500<77/50\).
This is an exact finite-contour argument, with both parities and
the original scalars retained.

The real main integral in that formula is still unestimated.
If it is subsequently deformed, its unweighted connecting segments
must remain in the argument. Thus the outstanding work on this
part of the source is now this main integral and its first-coordinate
assembly, rather than additional conditional Fourier remainders.
The first-coordinate vertical connector and the second-coordinate
noninterior pieces also remain open.

A separate [exact coefficient reformulation](research_mixed_next_lowered_word_dual_observation.md)
has been proved and checked. The original basis change cancels the old final
quantum factorial before the next transfer. For the prefix \(34\),
the remaining coefficient row belongs to the word \(33\). This
expresses the next transfer as a specified linear observation of a
boundary polynomial already studied in full. The observation retains
the repeated-root derivatives in the original trace. Bounds for the
polynomial's values do not automatically bound this observation or
prevent cancellation in it. The
[complete-trace bound](research_mixed_next_three_complete_trace_bound.md)
gives an explicit whole-source upper estimate and keeps the vertical
endpoint term in its inverse-crossing contour. Its broad upper
estimate has not been shown smaller than the required geometric
action; it supplies no complete-sum lower bound.

The complete next attachment still extracts two exact Fourier
coefficients. We must control their combined remainder and prove that
their sum retains the nonzero geometric contribution. Some pieces
can be bounded separately; the paired localization above controls
the older filtering correction only after the complements are added.
In particular,
no volume identity for a three-tangle short component, or stability
under arbitrary short partial fillings, follows yet. The selected-pair
knot theorem below remains the established extension of the
long-filling result.

The distinction between the two coefficients is now an
[exact polynomial identity](research_mixed_next_cardinal_sector_separation.md).
For a degree-\((N-1)\) correction \(E\), let \(I_N(Ed_N)\)
be the degree-\((N-1)\) interpolant of its product values on
the original root grid, and write
\[
 Ed_N=I_N(Ed_N)+(Y^N-1)Q_E.
\]
The selected coefficient of its transfer is exactly
\(N\operatorname{CT}(Q_EC_{\beta,N})\). The unselected
coefficient is the physical correction sum minus this same
quantity. The note gives \(Q_E\) explicitly, including its
sampled derivatives and all off-diagonal index pairings.
Thus the extra estimate needed for separate coefficient control
is identified without assuming that the small physical correction
bounds either coefficient on its own.

The [low-cardinal response theorem](research_mixed_next_low_cardinal_coherent_response.md)
now identifies this correction with cumulative moments of the
original three-crossing Fourier column \(\gamma=MJM^3e_0\).
Already at the first physical node, the two outgoing sums have
normalized row coefficients \(a_j\) and \(1-a_j\). The original
nonzero asymptotic of \(\gamma\) proves that, for
\(j_N=\lfloor N/4\rfloor\),
\[
 \max\{|a_{j_N}|,|a_{j_N-1}|\}
       \ge cN^{-3/2}e^{NA(1/4)},\qquad A(1/4)>0.
\]
Thus polynomial bounds for each normalized correction row are
false, even though the two coefficients add to one at every row.
This excludes a proposed coefficientwise shortcut. It does not
make either complete outgoing sum large: cancellation among its
different rows remains possible and still needs to be estimated.

The [cumulative endpoint theorem](research_mixed_next_low_cardinal_endpoint_packet.md)
goes further on every fixed physical index interval strictly before
the maximum of the original Fourier profile. It evaluates the whole
cumulative coefficient \(a_j\), rather than only its adjacent
difference. Backward geometric summation gives a nonzero leading
coefficient. With the original quadratic root written as
\[
 u(t)=\frac{1-\sqrt{4e^{2\pi it}-3}}2,\qquad t=j/N,
\]
that coefficient simplifies to \(1/(1-u(t))\).
The same calculation identifies its inner response exactly with
the original conditional source \(C_{1,N}(r^j,1)\) and fixes the
absolute action \(I(t)-2J(t)-i\pi/12\), including the endpoint
phase at both parities. The note gives the full outgoing row
amplitude and rational parametrizations of its necessary critical
equations. It does not replace the discrete cumulative source by
an unproved complex interpolation, extend the packet through its
turning point, or estimate the complete outgoing sum.

For the filtered polynomial the unselected remainder can be stated
as one coherent integral. Let
\(\Gamma_y=[0,1]+i\Im y_*\), and let \(J_*\) be its already
controlled local stationary segment. What remains is an exponential
gap for
\[
 N\int_{\Gamma_y\setminus J_*}
 F_N^{\rm mid}(w,e^{-2\pi iy})\,d_N(e^{-2\pi iy})\,
 C_{\beta,N}(e^{-2\pi iy},Z)\,dy.
\]
Such a bound would complete this coefficient of the filtered source.
It has not been proved, and its second coefficient still needs a
complete comparison. The second-coordinate deletions were paid only
after combining the two coefficients; they do not compare each
filtered coefficient with its original counterpart separately.
In particular, deleting physical indices does not delete the
corresponding real interval from this contour.

That additional check has now been completed on the
[whole selected central segment](research_mixed_next_filtered_selected_plateau.md).
For the ordinary-next reference families and both next letters,
replacing \(F_{34,N}\) by \(F_N^{\rm mid}\) on
\([.22,.45]+i/100\) changes the selected integrand by an
exponentially smaller term, with a finite rate gap \(1/1000\)
and the original outgoing supporting plane. The proof sharpens
the correction's unit-disk rate to \(77/50\), retains both
alternatives in the exact Fourier weight, and uses the sign of
the actual geometric marginal to control the whole interval.
This pays the filtering correction on that segment. It does
not supply a missing bound for the original full-prefix integral
there, extend to a terminal third vertex, or estimate either
complete coefficient. The newer paired localization supplies the
combined complementary correction for the older filter near actual
ordinary outputs. The complementary retained source itself remains
unestimated.

Older cyclic contour estimates also have narrower reference domains;
they cannot be imported into this half-chain without a new proof.

## The moving action can be studied on one complex parameter domain

The [general pre-Gram curve theorem](research_mixed_arbitrary_prefix_pregram_curve.md)
identifies one global geometric branch for every nonempty positive word
in powers three and four, on the same two typed input disks. Both the
initial auxiliary parameter and the last leg are one-to-one holomorphic
coordinates. The last-leg derivative is bounded above and away from
zero independently of the word and its length. Consequently the
outgoing geometric neighborhoods, and the bounds for derivatives of
their actions, can also be chosen uniformly on compact input sets.
The absolute action constants remain word-dependent. This is a theorem
about the geometric branch, not an asymptotic theorem for every finite
sum.

For the fixed \(34\) prefix, the more specific
[following-reference curve](research_mixed_three_four_following_critical_curve.md)
applies these coordinates to the available remainder bounds. The
original endpoint equations and rational transfer retain every
logarithmic lift and action constant. The first attached leg need not
be treated as an independent external parameter.

For the initial and complementary contour pieces, the resulting
comparison reduces to the boundary arcs and clipping chords of four
explicit domains in one complex variable. The proof uses harmonic
and subharmonic maximum principles. It also permits different valid
source bounds on different boundary pieces, by applying maximum
modulus to the same normalized finite polynomial. The boundary signs
required a separate argument, completed below.

The [angular remainder estimate](research_mixed_transformed_following_four_angular_majorant.md)
strengthens the complementary-contour bound by retaining the outgoing
angle and its correlation with the height. Its uniform ceiling on
the required ordinary and attached type-four domains is \(2281/1250\);
the note also gives a sharper bound depending on the outgoing
coordinate. Conversely, the
[height-derivative calculation](research_mixed_three_four_following_action_direction.md)
shows that lowering the outgoing height worsens the action margin
against one valid, coarser radius bound. Thus the radius improvement
alone does not justify downward transport of the previously proved
gap. Neither statement decides the sign of the sharper action
comparison on the actual following family.

The [fixed two-center calculation](research_mixed_three_four_following_action_diagnostic_protocol.md)
has now enclosed the original five-variable critical points and their
absolute actions at \(c_3=7/20-i/100\) and
\(c_4=3/10-13i/250\). In both cases the geometric action exceeds

and the initial-interval ceiling by more than \(7/125\).
The [saved interval result](../repro/results/research-mixed-three-four-following-action-centers-attempt01.json)
retains both inclusions and all comparisons. These strict inequalities
pay those two remainders at the prescribed references and on sufficiently

The [fixed full-circle attempt](research_mixed_three_four_following_boundary_diagnostic_protocol.md)
has now been executed and retained as

Every one of the 1,024 original boundary intervals has strictly positive

contains all 2,048 comparisons and retains every input binding. The

The [two-remainder theorem](research_mixed_three_four_following_remainder_gaps.md)
uses the maximum principle to prove both inequalities on the full

initial incoming interval and the complementary contour are uniformly
exponentially smaller than the actual geometric action throughout this

below; the next attachment remains a separate problem.

The [central-contour theorem on the following family](research_mixed_three_four_following_plateau_source.md)
now proves more than the existence of a critical point. Throughout all

\(N^{-3/2}e^{N\mathscr P_{34}(c)}\). The rest of that segment is
exponentially smaller. The proof combines the complete first-cap and
ordinary conditional estimates, removes a Fourier weight whose
nonvanishing is already proved, and uses the original critical equations
to cancel their linear terms. Each holomorphic integral uses a contour
fixed at its base reference. Both level parities and fixed derivatives
are retained.

This settles the central segment on the new family. The
[moving lower-cut theorem](research_mixed_three_four_following_left_moving_cut.md)
also resolves the mismatch between the earlier \(3/20\) transition
and the available ordinary estimate at \(1/8\). The new cut is
\(s(x)=39/400+x/8\), so it reaches exactly \(1/8\) when the
incoming coordinate reaches \(x=.22\). A direct derivative inequality
controls every complete cap profile along that moving face. It bounds
the whole lower physical sector by the original action minus a fixed
positive amount. The same proof establishes horizontal concavity and
vertical convexity on the enlarged conditional rectangle.

The [complete left-transition theorem](research_mixed_three_four_following_left_taper_source.md)
now adds the central main term, both horizontal aliases, every vertical
side, and the full upper physical sector. Original argument bounds
control the aliases; the actual critical equations cancel the cap and
conditional linear terms. The resulting gap applies to the whole
\(U_{0,N}C_{1,N}\) product on the fixed-base left transition, with
both parities and fixed derivatives. The
[right horizontal theorem](research_mixed_three_four_following_right_segment.md)
likewise controls the entire product for \(.45\le\Re a\le.5\)
at the actual incoming height. Its proof uses the moving cut
\(s(x)=23/40-x\), joint concavity, and the original real-row bounds.
It includes the continuous convex limit at the numerator zero
\(\Re(a+t)=1\).

The [real-color extension of the left transition](research_mixed_three_four_following_left_real_colors.md)
also proves its bound for every real ordinary boundary color. The
proof uses estimates for the original coherent endpoint coefficients
and separate estimates for the extreme indices. It never assumes
that changing the color decreases the modulus of a signed sum.
This extension supplies the all-real bound needed when the pair is
inserted into a larger finite sum. The same note verifies the exact

The last contour comparison concerned the vertical segment joining
that height to the old fixed complementary path. The

for this segment keeps the outgoing-radius term

has now passed on every one of the 1,024 prescribed boundary intervals.

The [connector theorem](research_mixed_three_four_following_connector_gap.md)
extends these strict comparisons to the full reduced disks by a

All parts of the incoming contour are therefore accounted for in the
[complete following-family theorem](research_mixed_three_four_following_complete_prefix.md).
For the whole two-tangle polynomial, on fixed neighborhoods of the
actual outgoing sets \(q(K)\), it gives
\[
 f_{34,N}(w,e^{-2\pi iz})
 =N^{-3/2}\mathcal A_{34}(w,z)e^{N\mathcal P(w,z)}
      (1+O_{\mathrm{hol}}(N^{-1})),\qquad \mathcal A_{34}\ne0.
\]
Here \(K\) ranges over the four stated ordinary and attached input
domains. The action retains its original additive constant, and the
estimate includes both level parities. In particular this is a lower
bound for the signed finite sum itself. It follows from a nonzero
Gaussian coefficient and exponentially smaller remainders, without
assuming nonnegative summands. The theorem also supplies an upper
bound with a positive angular loss for all real ordinary colors.

The remaining step for a third short tangle is to estimate both exact
Fourier contributions in its attachment formula and prove a nonzero
leading coefficient for their sum. No such conclusion is inferred
from the new lower bound before that coefficient extraction.

## The complete polynomial after the boundary transform

The [complete transformed-prefix theorem](research_mixed_three_four_complete_transformed_prefix.md)
now proves a nonzero asymptotic for the entire transformed three/four
polynomial near the original pair's last private geometric coordinate
\(z_*\). Write
\[
 f_{34,N}(w,Y)=N\operatorname{CT}_X
                [U_{0,N}(w,X)C_{1,N}(X,Y)].
\]
Here \(U_{0,N}\) is the complete first-cap polynomial and
\(C_{1,N}\) is the original conditional finite sum; both are defined
in the linked theorem. The coordinate \(w\) is the left ordinary
boundary color, whose complete value is \(-2\). On a fixed complex
neighborhood of \((w,z)=(-2,z_*)\),
\[
 f_{34,N}(w,e^{-2\pi iz})
   =N^{-3/2}\mathcal A_{34}(w,z)
        e^{N\mathcal P_{34}(w,z)}(1+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})),
 \qquad \mathcal A_{34}\ne0.
\]
The action has its original additive constant and belongs to the prefix
before the final Gram contraction. The normalized error and all its
fixed mixed derivatives are uniform on smaller neighborhoods. Both
level parities are included. Thus this is an actual lower bound for
the complete transformed polynomial, not only a bound for its norm or
one selected contribution.

The proof divides the incoming contour into five successive pieces.
The [central plateau](research_mixed_three_four_transformed_plateau_source.md)
has the nonzero two-variable Gaussian coefficient. The
[real initial interval](research_mixed_transformed_real_initial_interval.md),
[left transition](research_mixed_three_four_transformed_left_taper.md),
[right interval](research_mixed_transformed_right_strip.md), and
[complementary path](research_mixed_three_four_transformed_complement_calibration.md)
are all exponentially smaller on the same action scale. Their integrals
sum exactly to the original polynomial.

The missing support issue is resolved in this local theorem. At a
physical outgoing index, some transform rows vanish. At complex
\(z_*\), they reappear. The new upper-row estimates retain every
one of them. A useful general ingredient is the
[asymmetric endpoint comparison](research_mixed_transformed_left_upper_rows.md):
for a specified independent domain of two angles and negative heights,
the entire upper half of the three-factorial row rate is bounded by its
half-row or last-row value. Its proof uses reflected arcs and elementary
monotonicity, without a new numerical evaluation. The half row is paid
by a pointwise geometric source estimate, and the last row by a separate
bound on the complete cap.

Removing the terminal endpoint factor in this argument is an exact
operation on each retained interpolant. The factor is known to be
nonzero on the relevant neighborhood. No estimate for the already
summed terminal polynomial is divided by that factor.

The next obligation is to prove bounds at the boundary references
selected by subsequent short attachments, including their competing
contour regions. Those references are not asserted to lie in the
neighborhood just proved. The final Gram contraction and the complete
type-four factor \(d_N(Y)(1+Y^{-N})\) must also be retained. The
existing arbitrary-letter theorem closes the local phase and leading
amplitude equations, but does not yet establish the corresponding
whole-source estimates. Arbitrary short components with branching
vertices remain beyond this result. The finite-exceptions target and
the frozen manuscript scope are unchanged.

## Exact reductions cover entire parameter fibers

The [kernel reduction theorem](research_exact_reduction_kernel_saturation.md)
transfers any proved full boundary kernel through the original zero
and unit reductions. It preserves the entire ordinary polynomial,
including its derivatives, up to an explicit scalar of modulus one.
For example,
\[
 E_{(2r,0,3-2r,4),N}=E_{(3,4),N}\qquad(r\in\mathbb Z).
\]
After the required marked rotations are carried into the neighboring
tangles, the selected-pair knot theorem therefore covers every
assignment in these fibers with the same sufficiently long surviving
powers. The canceled powers themselves need not be bounded. More
generally, the longness conditions apply to the surviving affine sums
of the original parameters. This enlarges the covered assignment
strata, without claiming new knot types merely from different
presentations. Irreducible short words remain a separate problem.

## Current result and its scope

The [selected-pair long-filling theorem](research_three_four_component_long_fillings.md)
now proves the original Kashaev volume identity for a further class
of marked partial fillings. In any fixed admissible original circle
tree with at least one edge, select disjoint connected components
consisting of two adjacent vertices of original degree two. Their
ordered powers may be \((3,4)\), \((4,3)\), \((-3,-4)\), or
\((-4,-3)\). All remaining powers may then be chosen independently
sufficiently long, with unrelated signs and magnitudes. The number
of selected pairs is arbitrary, and the remaining vertices may branch.
The original carriers, strand tracing, knot condition and absence of
internal closed components are retained.

The new [full boundary kernel theorem](research_mixed_three_four_full_boundary_kernel.md)
is what permits this assembly. It proves the nonzero holomorphic
asymptotic on a fixed complex neighborhood, strict real boundary
curvature, decay over both entire real boundary periods, and the
quadratic complex-strip estimate. The proof includes the first-half
source with all real colors and the
[all-real complementary contour](research_mixed_three_four_complementary_real_colors.md).
Exact finite traces replace each selected pair by that entire
two-boundary polynomial. The remaining source satisfies the existing
complex-phase long-filling theorem, and the marked geometric boundary
germ supplies its original volume. The final nonzero prefactor has
power \(N^{3/2}\), and the limit holds along all integer levels.

This extends the proved class of selected components. It does not
prove the finite-exceptions target: arbitrary irreducible adjacent
short strings and short components containing branching vertices
remain to be handled. Exact reduction fibers reaching a proved
component are covered by the preceding reduction theorem. The new
longness threshold belongs to this fixed component assembly; the
bound of eight from the separate path-family theorem is not asserted
for it. No numerical computation was needed for this extension beyond
the single saved action enclosure described below. The manuscripts
remain frozen.

The [finite-gluing remainder theorem](research_calibrated_remainders_under_finite_gluing.md)
also gives a general upper-bound tool. The original Hermite trace
acts with only polynomial cost on unreduced products of degree
\(O(N)\). A remainder with local exponential gap \(\delta\)
therefore survives arbitrary fixed signed gluing if the loss between
the sum of its local reference rates and the actual composed action
is smaller than \(\delta\). This theorem states that comparison
explicitly; it supplies neither a nonzero main coefficient nor the
missing comparison for arbitrary short contexts.

## The complete short-block calculation

The ordinary short pair \((3,4)\) now has a nonzero asymptotic for
its **complete original finite sum** at complete boundary colors.
The [complementary-contour theorem](research_mixed_three_four_complementary_contour_completion.md)
closes the estimate that was missing from the first-half calculation:
\[
 Z_{34,N}(-2,-2)=\kappa_N^3N^{-3/2}\mathcal A e^{N\mathcal S}
                         (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad \mathcal A\ne0.
\]
Here \(Z_{34,N}=v(-2)^TA_3A_4v(-2)\) is the original
two-boundary observation, \(\mathcal S\) is its geometric critical
action, and \(|\kappa_N|=1\). The statement holds along all integer
levels. The remaining contour is exponentially smaller than this
term, so it cannot cancel its leading coefficient.

The decisive additional input was a sharper enclosure of the original
action, not a change of invariant. A single prescribed interval
calculation proves \(M=\Re\mathcal S>27/10\) and places the
critical height in \((-7/200,0)\). These bounds leave enough room
for the existing coefficient estimates. The new proof estimates all
transform indices directly on a vertical connector and the remaining
real half-circle, with a uniform gap \(1/300\). It retains each
complete private endpoint polynomial before taking absolute values.
There is no substitution of a sampled-root bound for an open contour.

The [computation record](research_mixed_three_four_half_face_witness_outcome.md)
distinguishes two conclusions. Its six lower witnesses did not refute
the proposed upper-bound criterion, so that diagnostic remains
inconclusive. Independently, its certified action enclosure combines
with the written upper bound \(\mathcal E(1/2;0)<529/200\) to
establish the physical middle-sector comparison. The full continuous
contour theorem uses a separate direct argument.

This complete-color calculation alone did not supply a component
that could be inserted into another source. The full boundary
estimates and marked assembly above now provide that insertion when
the remaining powers are sufficiently long. Stability under
arbitrary fixed short partial fillings, and hence the
finite-exceptions goal, remains open. The existing path-family knot
corollary with effective twist magnitudes at least eight remains
available with its original scope.

## Supporting estimates and earlier stages

The latest
[assembly theorem](research_mixed_three_four_first_half_assembly.md)
joins the seam, real small-angle interval, left taper, geometric
plateau and right extension into the complete first half of the
original ordinary \((3,4)\) contour. If \(I_{-,N}\) denotes
that segment with the original scalar, it proves
\[
 I_{-,N}=\kappa_N^3N^{-3/2}\mathcal A e^{N\mathcal S}
                  (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad \mathcal A\ne0.
\]
Here \(\mathcal S\) is the original geometric critical action,
and \(M=\Re\mathcal S\). The exact observation remains
\(Z_{34,N}=I_{-,N}+I_{+,N}\), where \(I_{+,N}\) is its
complementary contour segment. The estimate needed to prevent
cancellation by that complementary contribution is supplied by the
new full-contour theorem above. The first-half theorem by itself did
not provide it. The notes below record the supporting estimates and
earlier reductions, including questions that were open when those
individual notes were written.

The latest completed estimates remove both extreme transform-index
ranges on the entire incoming circle, at every height needed by the
actual contour. The
[global transform-end theorem](research_mixed_three_four_global_transform_ends.md)
proves a gap \(1/20\) below the original geometric action after
multiplication by the complete first factor. Its finite binomial
identity bounds \(p_j(X)/P_j\) at every radius; the existing estimates
for sums of moduli of whole endpoint coefficients then give a global
first-factor ceiling. Exact termination controls the opposite end.
The result holds for every real ordinary color, as well as on small
complex neighborhoods of the complete colors, with all fixed ordinary
derivatives and both parities. It estimates only these extreme rows;
central cancellation is still a separate problem.

There is a separate elementary bound for the cap's own extreme
private indices. The
[real-circle index-end lemma](research_mixed_cap_real_circle_index_ends.md)
uses the exact reflected factorial identity to prove
\[
 \frac{|p_{N-1-m}(X)|}{|P_{N-1-m}|}\le2^m
                                  \qquad(|X|=1).
\]
It gives a rate \(3/5\) for those complete rows of either cap,
uniformly in every real ordinary color and every incoming angle.
The bound includes the seam \(X=1\) and needs no division by an
outgoing-angle factor. These are private-index ends, distinct from
the outer transform-index ends in the preceding theorem.

The complete ordinary \((3,4)\) product is also controlled
on the added incoming interval \(9/20\le x\le1/2\), at its actual
critical height. The
[moving-boundary theorem](research_mixed_three_four_moving_transform_cut.md),
Theorem 4, proves
\[
 |U_{0,N}(w_L,e^{-2\pi i(x+ic)})
       V_{1,N}(w_R,e^{-2\pi i(x+ic)})|
 \le C N^B e^{N(M-\gamma)},\qquad \gamma>0,
\]
where \(M\) is the original geometric critical action. The estimate
retains both ordinary colors near their complete values, their fixed
derivatives, every physical row, all contour corrections and both
level parities. The
[real-color extension](research_mixed_three_four_right_strip_real_colors.md)
now makes this a bound on the entire real ordinary-color square,
with a remaining positive strip gap and losses
\(c_L(1-\cos\theta_L)+c_R(1-\cos\theta_R)\).
It lifts the complete source estimates before spending any part
of the strip gap; a local complex-color result alone would not
justify that extension. Neither statement bounds the whole
incoming circle.

Two analytic improvements complete this interval. The
[correlated-radius comparison](research_mixed_three_four_private_right_correlated_radius.md)
uses the same transform radius in the moving face and its reference,
reducing an unnecessarily large cost. The other improvement moves
the lower transform cut from \(t=.15\) to \(t=.6-x\). Along this
boundary the shared primitive cancels from the derivative, and the
coupled action decreases by more than \(1/20\) per unit of \(x\).
The additional contour pieces are controlled by a positive horizontal
derivative and separate convexity in the two imaginary coordinates.
The proof applies these comparisons to an explicit partition of the
finite sum; it does not omit the new endpoints.

The supporting
[joint-curvature proof](research_mixed_three_four_right_strip_joint_curvature.md)
bounds the terminal main rectangle after multiplication by the
whole first cap. The
[face and alias transport proof](research_mixed_three_four_private_left_right_extension.md)
also controls the weak private-left face, the real right-transform
face, and every penalized terminal alias anchor. These are
comparisons with the original coupled action, not a change
to a Fourier closing. They preserve strict exponential gaps.

The [upper-transform comparison](research_mixed_three_four_upper_transform_half_face.md)
separately controls the complete physical upper triangle at
the incoming half face. Its proof uses the actual absolute
triple-row bound and the whole first cap. The
[radius comparison](research_mixed_incoming_half_circle_radius_comparison.md)
extends the incoming right-semicircle numerator estimate to

The remaining real-face transport costs have now been proved.
The single prescribed

retains every original reference cell and all eight families.
Six families have strictly negative upper bounds after the transport
cost is added: both previously controlled faces and all four corners.
The real transform face \(t=.15\) and private face \(e=.49\) were

All 15,288 selected comparisons and the complete inherited coverage
were checked; the source, roots, phases and derivatives were not

abd1f98e09312ba8c6ceffcb88478a8f031730cc845f31e483e8bd143612ea14.
No rerun or refinement was used. That fixed-cost comparison alone
did not control the added interval. Its six-of-eight outcome remains

 |U_{0,N}(w_L,e^{-2\pi ia(x)})

The previously proved

The [real small-angle theorem](research_mixed_three_four_real_small_angle_source.md)

There is a separate advance for the exact sampled-root formula.
The [physical far-sector theorem](research_mixed_three_four_physical_far_half.md)
proves

 \kappa_N^3 N\!
 \sum_{b=\lceil5N/6\rceil}^{N-1}
 U_{0,N}(w_L,r^b)V_{1,N}(w_R,r^b)
 =O\!\left(N^B e^{N(M-1/200)}\right),
 \qquad r=e^{-2\pi i/N}.
\]
It also bounds the sum of the absolute differentiated terms,
on fixed ordinary-color neighborhoods and at both parities.
The proof uses exact terminating supports and a bound on whole

They do not identify it with a continuous arc; any contour

An additional
[incoming-height inequality](research_mixed_three_four_far_half_height_transport.md)

It keeps the original logarithmic branch and chirp. Positive-height
aliases and the comparison with the paired action remain outside
