The [physical middle-sector reduction](research_mixed_three_four_physical_middle_reduction.md)
gives a separate sufficient test for the sampled range
\(1/2\le b/N\le5/6\). It keeps the transform index real and
deforms the complete private sum. The resulting explicit upper
envelope is
\[
 \mathcal E(v)=\overline Q(v)+
  \max_{.1\le t\le v}\{A(t)+J(v)-J(v-t)-2J(t)\},
 \qquad v=1-b/N.
\]
Here \(\overline Q\) is the proved physical first-cap bound,
and \(A\) is the maximum of all five private-contour profiles.
The envelope is increasing in \(v\), with a quantified strict
decrement away from \(v=1/2\). Thus the single comparison
\(\mathcal E(1/2)<M\) would bound this whole sampled sector.
That comparison has not been proved. Its possible failure would
show only that this bound loses too much transform cancellation,
not that the desired volume limit fails.

For the current one-circle strategy, the outstanding region is now
the complementary far incoming half with its complete transitions.
An explicit representative runs from \(a=.5+ic\) to \(a=1\)
with linearly decreasing height. The source is an entire periodic
function of \(a\), so its complementary integral depends only on
these endpoints; any replacement path still needs a bound for its
complete contribution. On the alternative sampled-root representation the sector
\(b/N\ge5/6\) is already controlled, whereas the middle far sector
still needs its estimate and any conversion must keep the sampling
terms. These are two representations of the same original
observation, not interchangeable partial bounds.

None of these results is yet a whole-circle ordinary-pair theorem,
and they add no knot family to the proved results.

The preceding completed result concerns a Fourier representation. It does not
enlarge the proved knot family. The
[internal-chain theorem](research_internal_two_crossing_chain.md)
already establishes the complete ordinary two-boundary asymptotic
for every fixed same-sign power-two chain, including the adjacent
pair. Keeping these two statements distinct avoids counting a
second representation of a covered block as new knot coverage.

The complete adjacent-pair boundary asymptotic is now proved with
two independently varying Fourier parameters. The
[joint kernel theorem](research_mixed_two_adjacent_joint_outer_packet.md)
establishes
\[
 h(x)^T A_2^2 h(y)
   =N^{-1/2}\mathcal C(x,y)e^{N\mathcal S(x,y)}
                      (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad \mathcal C(x,y)\ne0,
\]
uniformly on smaller bidisks in a fixed complex neighborhood of
\((x_0,x_0)\), along all integer levels. Every fixed mixed
derivative of the normalized error is also \(O(N^{-1})\).
Here \(A_2\) is the original power-two operator, \(h(x),h(y)\)
are its actual Fourier boundary vectors, and \(\mathcal S\)
is the unchanged critical action of the exact merged source.
The theorem includes every original physical row, both parity
lattices, both infinite sampling corrections, and both entire
outer side integrals. It does not identify an arbitrary prescribed
knot closing with this kernel or its Fourier derivatives.

The proof first establishes the
[complete equal-parameter assembly](research_mixed_two_adjacent_outer_total_assembly.md)
from three estimates, each for an exact finite source or an
explicitly discarded part of that source.

1. The [absolute truncation bounds](research_mixed_two_adjacent_global_central_truncation.md)
   remove all physical total indices \(m/N\le1/2\) and, for
   every remaining total, all inner indices
   \(\lvert j-m/2\rvert>N/5\). Their combined error is at
   most a polynomial in \(N\) times \(e^{N(M-1/500)}\),
   where \(M=\Re\mathcal S\). The
   [original diagonal-side estimate](research_mixed_two_adjacent_physical_diagonal_strip.md)
   also pays the final total-index interval near \(1\).
   These estimates precede outer cancellation.
2. The [retained inner finite sums](research_mixed_two_adjacent_all_height_central_packet.md)
   have a uniform nonzero Gaussian asymptotic at every finite
   complex total height, with both parity choices kept.
   Their factorial arguments remain regular on both upper
   and lower contours. The elementary modulus comparison
   works whenever the stated external radius and angle
   conditions hold; it is not a numerical check at the saddle.
3. The outer real phase has its unique maximum on the
   horizontal contour through the original critical point.
   On every vertical side its real part is convex as a
   function of height. Together with the exact parity
   sampling weights and the original factorial tails,
   this bounds the complete side integrals below the
   critical rate. Each parity contributes half of the
   same Gaussian coefficient, so their leading terms add.

The earlier obstacle about carrying a physical
\(O(N^{-1})\) inner error through an oscillatory outer sum
is therefore resolved for this boundary observation:
the inner estimate is proved on the actual complex contour
before the outer integral is estimated.

The [independent-parameter inner proof](research_mixed_two_adjacent_independent_inner_packet.md)
then moves the inner critical point by an exact finite contour
identity. It bounds both lattice corrections, every endpoint
segment, and the original complementary rows. The joint kernel
proof applies this estimate on the bounded outer contour; the
strict original physical and contour gaps persist by uniform
continuity. Its infinite tails are checked separately using the
exact factorial formulas. The actual outer main path is moved
through the continued critical point with both endpoint connectors
retained. This proves the independent-parameter statement rather
than inferring it from diagonal values.

There are also complementary exact constructions. A
[symmetric full-width interpolation](research_mixed_two_adjacent_half_to_full_total_packet.md)
equals the entire original inner sum at every physical
total index, because its added rows vanish through the
original reciprocal-factorial zeros. It has a complete
complex asymptotic at nonnegative total height. Its
[modulus criterion](research_mixed_two_adjacent_golden_ratio_inner_dominance.md)
uses an external radius greater than the golden ratio.
That representation can meet numerator poles on lower
contours; the completed outer proof uses the central
truncation above, whose lower contour has no such poles.

The earlier proposed absolute bound on the whole raised
two-variable square is
[false](research_mixed_two_adjacent_raised_corner_obstruction.md).
The new proof does not use it. The
[complete-cycle cancellations](research_mixed_two_adjacent_complete_cycle_cancellation.md)
and [symmetric endpoint identity](research_mixed_two_adjacent_symmetric_total_cycle.md)
remain valid alternative formulas, as does the
[complete left-current bound](research_mixed_two_adjacent_left_total_current_payment.md).

The [exact ordinary-observation formulas](research_mixed_two_adjacent_ordinary_observation_adapter.md)
explain what an additional boundary summation changes. They retain
the full Fourier periods and all derivatives at repeated spectral
roots. At the proved Fourier center, the complete ordinary
observation has a nonzero phase gradient. Thus its asymptotic
cannot be obtained by leaving that center fixed. The ordinary
pair is nevertheless already covered by the internal-chain
theorem; this calculation does not reopen it.

The next genuinely uncovered positive internal pair has powers
\((3,4)\). Its exact ordinary-color source is
\[
 \mathscr P_{3,4,N}(w_L,w_R)
 =\kappa^3N^2\oint
       \mathcal U_{0,N}(w_L,X)\mathcal V_{1,N}(w_R,X)
                                      \frac{dX}{2\pi iX}.
\]
Here the two factors are the explicit finite polynomials in
[the terminal-coordinate reduction](research_mixed_reversed_cap_assembly.md),
equations (1), (9), and (13); the whole terminal coordinate has
been summed exactly. The complete ordinary boundary values are
\(w_L=w_R=-2\). The geometric critical branch, its local
nonzero contribution, and some complementary-region estimates
are established in the earlier mixed-source notes. The remaining
task is a bound on the rest of this exact circle integral below
the geometric exponential rate, uniform for nearby ordinary
boundary values, together with the whole real-boundary decay
needed for further fillings. A theorem for a differently prepared
Fourier observation does not establish these bounds.

There is also an exact warning against an unrestricted composition
argument. Write \(\mathsf T\) for the original coefficient reversal,
\(\mathsf R\) for canonical multiplication by the crossing, and
\(\operatorname{can}\) for reduction in the full Newton algebra.
The source \(F_N=\operatorname{can}(R\,\mathsf T(R^2))\)
has the already proved concentrated asymptotic, whereas
\[
       (\mathsf T\mathsf R\mathsf T)F_N=\kappa R
\]
has unit-modulus values on the physical grid. Thus this operation
does not preserve the entire class of concentrated sources.
The proof is in Section 7 of the ordinary-observation note.
This limits a proposed method; it does not disprove a knot
volume identity.

The [rational boundary-transport calculation](research_mixed_two_adjacent_rational_boundary_transport.md)
now makes the matching problem explicit for the completed Fourier
kernel. If \(X=e^{-2\pi ix}\), \(W=e^{-2\pi iy}\),
\(U=e^{-2\pi ia_\#}\), \(V=e^{-2\pi is_\#}\), and
\(p=e^{\mathcal S_x}\), \(q=e^{\mathcal S_y}\), then
\[
 p=UV\frac{1-U}{1-V},\qquad
 q=UV\frac{1-V}{1-U}.
\]
The note gives the rational inverse, its preserved differential
form with the incoming orientation reversed, and the precise
matching condition when kernels are joined. It also proves that
two copies cannot be joined by leaving their critical point at
the present Fourier center. The new branch and its full contour
must be controlled; the rational identity alone does not do this.

The proposed positive-norm lower bound also needs the correct
exponential normalization. In the
[original coefficient calculation](research_complete_boundary_coefficient_transport.md),
Fourier orthogonality gives a positive norm after reversing one
crossing power. The desired same-sign source is a bilinear
pairing. Section 7 proves that, even in an already solved
long-power family, their ratio is exponentially small:
\[
 \frac{|w_n^{T}w_n|}{\|w_n\|^2}
       =C_n e^{-N\Delta_n}(1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad \Delta_n>0.
\]
Thus almost invariance in that unmodified norm is not a universal
lower-bound mechanism. A useful replacement must retain the
correct exponential cost of the overlap, or justify a changed
contour and positive form. Neither the positivity statement nor
this counterexample settles the mixed \((3,4)\) source.

The strongest completed knot-family statement remains
[Corollary 5 of the path assembly theorem](research_uniform_path_trace_assembly.md):
the original auxiliary graph is a path, every auxiliary vertex
is filled, the original signed crossing powers satisfy
\(\lvert n_v\rvert\ge8\), and strand tracing gives one knot
component with no internal closed component. Arbitrary short
partial fillings and finitely many exceptions per template
remain open. The manuscripts remain frozen.

## Exact source and preceding one-block results

This section records the earlier stages of the Fourier proof.
The whole-source estimates for its two-free-Fourier-boundary pair
are now supplied by the current theorem above. The distinct
ordinary \((3,4)\) problem remains open.

The adjacent Fourier composition has an
[exact two-variable source with its intervening crossing already summed](research_mixed_two_adjacent_merged_source.md).
For the original two power-two blocks,
\[
 h(x)^TA_2^2h(y)
 =e^{\pi i(N-1)(x+y)}
   \sum_{u=0}^{N-1}\frac{p_u(X)}{P_u}
                          C_{0,N}(r^u,W),
\]
where \(r=e^{-2\pi i/N}\), \(X=e^{-2\pi ix}\),
\(W=e^{-2\pi iy}\), \(P_u=(r;r)_u\), and
\(p_u(Z)=(rZ;r)_u\). The same note gives the explicit
two-index triangular factorial sum and its complete rectangular
residue representation. Every original boundary derivative
and complementary color remains. It also pairs the first
variable's opposite contour sides exactly, retaining the
level-dependent boundary factors and both convergent infinite
currents. These are exact identities; their uniform bounds at the
critical action are now supplied by the joint kernel theorem above.

For equal original Fourier endpoints \(x=y=x_0\), the
[critical-point theorem for this merged source](research_mixed_two_adjacent_critical_corridor.md)
proves a unique original critical point in
\(1/3<\Re a,\Re s<5/12\), with the correct logarithmic lift.
The real Hessian is negative definite throughout that complex
strip. The entire central rectangle therefore has an explicit
nonzero \(N^{-1/2}\) Gaussian contribution, continuing to nearby
endpoint pairs. By itself this local calculation does not estimate
the complete finite pair. The joint kernel theorem above supplies
the complementary-contour estimates that were missing at this stage.
The critical incoming height is greater than \(1/20\), so the
small interpolation neighborhoods below cannot simply be assumed
to reach it. The direct two-variable source is regular at that
critical point.

The all-power-two run similarity and its full ordinary
two-boundary estimates were already established in the earlier
internal-chain theorem. The new formulas keep two Fourier
boundary states free. They do not add a knot family or turn
either local description into lower bounds for every prescribed
closing.

The completed one-block advance is a
[jointly holomorphic local representative of the complete conditional sum](research_mixed_three_fixed_cutoff_holomorphic_packet.md).
For every real incoming reference \(a_0\in[.267,.433]\), choose a
fixed cutoff slightly larger than \(a_0\). The resulting finite
reciprocal-factorial sum, with its exact second-period subtraction,
defines \(\widetilde C_{N,R}(a,y)\) on a fixed complex neighborhood
of \((a_0,x_0)\). On that neighborhood it has a nonzero asymptotic
\[
 \widetilde C_{N,R}(a,y)
   =N^{-1/2}\mathcal C_J(a,y)e^{N\Phi_1(a,y)}
                                       (1+O(N^{-1})),
\]
including every fixed mixed derivative of the normalized error.
At the relevant physical incoming nodes it agrees exactly with
the original \(C_{0,N}\), with the output still free. The proof
retains both entire endpoint currents, their two reflected period
factors, the infinite tails, and the connectors needed to move the
contour through the continued critical point. Two nearby admissible
cutoffs give representatives differing by an exponentially smaller
term, also after normalized differentiation.

This is a local interpolation theorem. It does not identify the
representative with \(C_{0,N}\) at unsampled incoming arguments,
does not replace the original incoming normal derivatives, and
does not assert an estimate on the whole earlier complex incoming
rectangle. In an actual attachment, only the specified local node
sum may use this estimate; its complementary node sum and the
original joining matrix remain.

The preceding
[complete nonzero asymptotic for the twice-crossed source at physical incoming colors](research_mixed_three_physical_input_complete_packet.md)
holds uniformly for
\(267/1000\le b/N\le433/1000\) and for the outgoing parameter
\(y\) in a fixed complex neighborhood of the original reference,
\[
 C_{0,N}(r^b,e^{-2\pi iy})
   =N^{-1/2}\mathcal C_J(b/N,y)
       e^{N\Phi_1(b/N,y)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad \mathcal C_J\ne0.
\]
The coefficient and the absolute action are explicit. This proves
matching upper and lower bounds for the complete finite function,
at both level parities, with all fixed normalized outgoing
derivatives. Restoring the exact crossing factor gives the
corresponding \(N^{-3/2}\) asymptotic for the entire original
Fourier boundary after two negative crossings.

The proof now accounts for the whole summation contour.
The [raised-contour comparison](research_mixed_three_left_cycle_right_contour.md)
proves that its real phase decreases throughout the part beyond the
central critical strip. It also bounds the entire right weighted
current and the right joining segment, including the infinite tails.
The [right endpoint value](research_mixed_three_left_cycle_right_endpoint_gap.md)
has a gap greater than \(1/20\), while the retained
[second-period correction](research_mixed_three_real_input_action_gap.md)
has a gap greater than \(1/25\). Together with the completed left
estimates, these facts leave one nonzero Gaussian contribution.

The incoming values in this physical-row theorem are \(b/N\).
The fixed-cutoff theorem above now supplies the chosen local complex
interpolation; it does not change the meaning of incoming
derivatives of the original polynomial. A subsequent actual signed
attachment still needs a complete estimate of its own.

The proof starts from the
[exact connection formula for the complete finite source](research_mixed_three_left_cycle_initialized_source.md).
For every \(N\ge2\), every physical incoming index \(0\le b<N\),
and every outgoing parameter \(y\) in the stated strip,
\[
 C_{0,N}(r^b,W)
   =N E_N(y)L_{b,N}(W)-N(W^N-1)I_N(b/N,y),
 \qquad r=e^{-2\pi i/N},\quad W=e^{-2\pi iy}.
\]
Here \(E_N\) is the original reciprocal factorial,
\(I_N\) is the complete second contour period, and \(L_{b,N}\)
is an explicit degree-\(b\) polynomial given by a terminating
quantum-factorial sum. The formula keeps the free outgoing
parameter and every physical incoming color. It follows from
exact cancellation of the contour-moment forcing against the
true final row of the finite sum. The initial value is fixed
by a growth argument that excludes all nonconstant periodic
factors; agreement at physical colors alone is not used to
infer off-grid equality.

The multiplier \(W^N-1\) may have exponential size and remains
part of the proved action comparison. The complete polynomial
asymptotic is now established on the physical incoming family
specified above. Noncancellation of the actual adjacent
contraction still requires proof.

The preceding results concern cancellation after two negative crossings.
Write the exact finite boundary function as a particular solution of
its difference equation plus a homogeneous solution \(H_N\).
There is a second homogeneous solution \(I_N\), defined by an explicit
contour integral. The
[period-pairing theorem](research_mixed_three_fourier_conditional_homogeneous_period.md),
Theorem 5, computes the determinant
\[
 \mathcal W_N(a,y)=
 H_N(a,y)I_N(a+1/N,y)-H_N(a+1/N,y)I_N(a,y)
\]
exactly and proves that it is nonzero throughout the stated complex
parameter domain for \(N\ge5\). Thus the two solutions remain
independent at neighboring boundary parameters. The proof also fixes
the periodic factor that the difference equations alone leave
undetermined: growth estimates for the original integrals exclude
every nonconstant Fourier mode.

The [second-period asymptotic](research_mixed_three_fourier_conditional_second_period_packet.md)
then gives
\[
 I_N(a,y)=N^{-3/2}B(a,y)e^{N\Psi(a,y)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad B(a,y)\ne0,
\]
on the stated rectangle containing the actual type-three incoming
parameters. This estimates the whole integral, including its infinite
ends. An exact cancellation of the contour kernel's poles permits a
vertical contour on which the real part of the phase is strictly
concave. There is a unique maximum, with a nonzero Gaussian
coefficient.

These two results give a lower bound for a specific combination:
\[
 H_N(a+1/N,y)
 -\frac{I_N(a+1/N,y)}{I_N(a,y)}H_N(a,y)
 =-\frac{\mathcal W_N(a,y)}{I_N(a,y)}.
\]
The right-hand side has an explicit nonzero leading term. The
[absolute action calibration](research_mixed_three_fourier_calibrated_homogeneous_observation.md)
identifies its exponent with the selected left critical action,
including the additive constant. The resulting coefficient is
nonzero and its power is \(N^{-1/2}\). Since the displayed ratio
is uniformly bounded on smaller parameter neighborhoods, at least
one of the two neighboring values of \(H_N\) has this exponential
size, up to a fixed constant. This is a lower bound for a
two-component state. It does not yet give a lower bound for the
combination prescribed by an arbitrary knot closure.

The [extension to every physical color and exact composition formula](research_mixed_three_homogeneous_period_full_node_composition.md)
also retains all boundary values needed to join short pieces.
For two adjacent power-two blocks, their intervening matrix is
explicit and includes the original crossing and turn. It cannot
be replaced by a positive inner product. The merged-source theorem
above now sums that interface exactly. Estimating the resulting
two-variable source, with its prescribed final closing functional,
remains the next substantive step.

There is now an exact check on which observations belong to the
original finite algebra. At physical color pairs, the
[moment calculation](research_mixed_three_second_period_physical_moments.md)
expresses the second-period matrix as
\[
 \mathbf I=\frac{1}{2\pi iN^2}\mathbf H+\mathbf R,
\]
where both \(\mathbf H\) and \(\mathbf R\) have cyclotomic entries.
Consequently an algebraic closing row, even after the actual
intervening crossing matrix, cannot annihilate \(\mathbf I\) while
retaining a nonzero \(\mathbf H\) contribution at that physical
output. This follows from transcendence of \(\pi\), not from an
asymptotic estimate. The earlier analytic two-point observation
therefore cannot simply be substituted for the prescribed closure.

We have also proved an
[alternative contour representation of the same finite block](research_mixed_three_factorized_cycle_and_finite_state.md).
It subtracts an explicit periodic multiple of the second period
and simplifies the joining terms. The full physical node matrix
is unchanged. A corrected version also agrees with the original
function at every physical incoming color while keeping the
outgoing parameter free. Exact cardinal reconstruction retains
the original Fourier band and all derivatives; directly
differentiating the replacement would give different incoming
derivatives. Thus this representation is available for the
actual source, with its full sampling corrections. Its complete
critical-contour estimate is now proved on the physical incoming
family above. The new fixed-cutoff representative supplies a
jointly holomorphic estimate near each real incoming reference.
The subsequent signed attachment, including the complementary
colors and the original closing operation, remains unproved.

No new knot family follows from these latest calculations.
The [proved path-family statement](research_uniform_path_trace_assembly.md),
Corollary 5, still requires every selected original crossing power
to have absolute value at least eight, together with the stated
strand-tracing hypotheses. Arbitrary adjacent short pieces and
finitely many exceptional assignments remain unproved.

The earlier complete calculation after three negative crossings
remains available in the
[connection formula](research_mixed_fourier_negative_three_connection.md).
At nonreal incoming parameters an endpoint correction can supply
the leading term; at physical color values it vanishes exactly
and an explicit product remains. In the actual path word this
operation changes the last power from four to one, whose marked
reduction was already known. The two-crossing operation changes
it to two. Isolated powers therefore should not be counted as
new knot-family results.

The complete original Fourier right cap now has a nonzero leading
asymptotic at every actual incoming reference of type three or four:
\[
 V_N^{\rm F}(x_0,e^{-2\pi ia_*})
   =N^{-3/2}\mathcal A_*e^{N\Phi_*}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_*=\frac{2\pi\,\mathfrak b_*}{\sqrt{\det H_*}}\ne0.
\]
Here \(\Phi_*\) is the original unallocated phase at its critical
pair, \(\mathfrak b_*\) is the nonzero coefficient of the exact
row interpolation, and \(H_*\) is its negative two-variable Hessian.
The determinant root is fixed by the Gaussian integral, with the
original orientation. The
[full-source theorem](research_mixed_fourier_right_cap_full_asymptotic.md)
defines every factor and proves the formula along both integer
level parities. It gives matching upper and lower bounds for the
whole finite expression, rather than only its local critical term.

For incoming type four, the original Fourier-weight comparison
proves that the auxiliary incoming weight is nonzero at the actual
reference. The proof removes that weight only there, after estimating
the complete remainder. It makes no such division at possible zeros
elsewhere in the target interval. The result is a boundary-function
theorem; it does not by itself identify a new family of knot
invariants or establish the finite-exception goal.

The complete right-hand part of the outgoing Fourier integral is
now controlled. The proof in
[the right-horizontal completion](research_mixed_fourier_right_horizontal_completion.md)
keeps the upper retained Fourier term together with both of its
positive-height sides. Translating their complete contour moves the
two imaginary coordinates in opposite directions. The shared
factorial stays below its real support wall, so this representation
introduces no diagonal poles. Exact finite-source estimates control
the infinite end uniformly in the quantum level.

The four boundary integrals are all included. The retained endpoints
start at already bounded real cuts. At the left outgoing endpoint,
an exact change to a higher retained contour supplies bounded initial
profiles. At the right outgoing endpoint, the period identities give
two left-seam integrals, one with the retained Fourier kernel and
one without it. Moving the latter to the original negative critical
height preserves the complete source. Their rates can increase by
less than \(1/80\), which is smaller than the available reserve.
The [right-endpoint proof](research_mixed_fourier_right_endpoint_shear_comparison.md)
then bounds the full infinite connecting integral.

Combining these facts with the completed small-index and nonpositive
contour estimates leaves only the central outgoing interval:
\[
 I_N^P=N\int_{11/50}^{9/20}S_N^<(z+i\Im q_*)\,dz,
 \qquad
 |d_N(X)|^{\eta/2}|V_N^{\rm F}-I_N^P|
     \le e^{N(B_\eta(x)-\delta_c/16)},
 \quad \delta_c=\frac{1}{2500000\cdot2500}.
\]
All original scalar factors and both level parities are retained.
The full-source theorem then removes the remaining inner contour
corrections and evaluates the two-variable Gaussian.

The [complex-parameter extension](research_mixed_fourier_right_cap_holomorphic_packet.md)
now proves the same formula on a fixed complex neighborhood of each
actual reference. Its coefficient is holomorphic and nonzero, and
every fixed derivative of the normalized relative error is
\(O(N^{-1})\) on smaller neighborhoods. The proof first chooses
uniform cutoffs for the infinite contour ends, then preserves the
strict estimates on the bounded parts. Translating the main rectangle
to the moving critical point retains all four boundary faces. Thus
the nonzero contribution persists under small boundary perturbations;
it is not merely an asymptotic at one isolated parameter value.

There is also a [bound across the incoming plateau](research_mixed_fourier_right_cap_full_plateau_plane.md):
the complete finite boundary function, with its original incoming
weight, lies below the tangent-plane rate with a quadratic loss,
up to any prescribed positive rate tolerance. This supplies the
terminal factor required by the Fourier-ended boundary-window
comparison on that domain. It does not supply the full neighboring
window comparison at arbitrary contour heights or the ordinary
closing functional.

The [compensated right-boundary estimate](research_mixed_fourier_right_boundary_shallow_taper.md)
now combines that complete cap bound with the neighboring ordinary
factors and the original pinning fee. It proves quadratic decrease
on the unselected central interval and extends to a fixed shallow
taper of the physical suffix. The extension retains all induced
neighbor-height changes while protecting the cut and its coherent
continuation. It has a positive exponential reserve away from the
central interval. Together with the existing left estimate, this
pays both compensated boundary expressions on their stated shallow
unselected domains. Selected contributions, deeper tapers and the
remaining physical periods are still outside those estimates.
Attachment to arbitrary short pieces and the finite-exception
conclusions remain unproved; no new knot family follows yet.

For the high retained indices, the
[incoming-height theorem](research_mixed_fourier_incoming_height_transport.md)
now gives an estimate through the entire nonpositive height reset
and across the full right taper. The proof compares each exact
incoming Newton product while keeping its whole outgoing Wall
contraction. Its allocated rate decreases by at least
\(9\pi/25\) times the height increase. The right-taper comparison
retains the plane at its original endpoint \(x=.45\), together
with the explicit marginal terms still owed to the neighboring
factor. A separate phase inequality lowers main and other
nonpositive-height profiles by at least \(\pi/10\) times the
incoming height increase. Positive-height corrections and the
complete compensated low-index source are not supplied by these
statements alone. The subsequent whole-source assembly below now
includes the positive-height corrections as well.

The [central phase estimate](research_mixed_fourier_right_cap_half_incoming_sheet.md)
also extends to incoming real part \(1/2\) at the actual
nonpositive height. On the added strip its negative real Hessian
is positive semidefinite; the original strictly positive Hessian
on an initial part of each segment preserves an explicit quadratic
loss. The old coefficient is multiplied by \(1989/4489\) for
type three and \(171/196\) for type four. Raising the incoming
height adds the preceding \(\pi/10\) decrease. This controls
the central phase through the full right taper, while retaining
the remaining complex marginal and contour corrections.

The [all-height transport lemma](research_mixed_fourier_incoming_taper_all_height.md)
proves that raising this incoming height never increases a retained
phase, even on the positive-height contours. On those positive-height
pieces, increasing the incoming real coordinate from \(.45\) to
\(.5\) is favorable as well. An exact finite-product argument
supplies the required numerator upper bound through the new
\(s+a=1\) wall, including its zero. These statements transport
individual valid profiles. The
[complete right connector](research_mixed_fourier_right_taper_shear_connector.md)
now also bounds the negative-height replacement path: its comparison
with the left outgoing taper is independent of the incoming parameter.
The extended main sheet, transported real cuts and vertical convexity
therefore provide its initial bound. The original exact period
identity and uniform factorial remainders then control the entire
infinite connector, including both of its terms.

There is now a [whole finite-source upper bound on the full incoming
right taper](research_mixed_fourier_right_taper_small_rows.md),
Corollary 3. The physical indices are partitioned before estimation:
the small rows increase to a controlled cutoff, the central rows
retain their full contour decomposition, and the high rows keep
their complete outgoing contractions. Every outgoing vertical
current, endpoint segment, right return and infinite end is included.
For the original nonpositive incoming height \(c\),
\(.45\le x\le.5\), and \(c\le h\le0\), the bound is
\[
 |d_N(e^{-2\pi ia})|^{\eta/2}
 |V_N^{\rm F}(x_0,e^{-2\pi ia})|
 \le C_\tau N^{A_\tau}e^{N\{\mathfrak B_\eta(x,h)+\tau\}},
 \qquad a=x+ih,
\]
where
\[
 \mathfrak B_\eta(x,h)=
 \max\{B_\eta(.45),B_\eta^{\rm ext}(x)\}
       -\pi(1-\eta/2)(.5-x)(h-c).
\]
The two planes retain the original reference action and marginal;
the extended plane has the explicit curvature coefficient
\(\chi_\eta\) above. In particular this controls the endpoint
\(x=.5,h=0\), rather than only a shallow neighborhood of the
plateau. The comparison of this maximum with the complex tangent,
after the neighboring ordinary factor and boundary compensation
are included, is still unproved. The result is an upper bound,
not a new nonzero asymptotic or a knot-family extension.

The [stronger height estimate](research_mixed_fourier_right_taper_uniform_height_credit.md)

\[
 \min\{\pi(h-c)/10,\,
       \pi(1-\eta/2)(.5-x)(h-c)+1/280000\}.
\]
It is positive even at the real taper endpoint. However, the

The algebraic description now holds at finite level as well.
The [exact boundary difference theorem](research_mixed_fourier_exact_boundary_difference_system.md)
derives two ordered difference operators directly from the original

is a free rank-one module; fixing one coefficient gives exactly the

statement, valid also over the specified localized cyclotomic ring.
The operators have order bounded independently of the level, and
their commuting symbols are the polynomials of the

The already proved asymptotic selects their local critical branch.
The original short-filling trace remains a different operation;

The [exact closing interface](research_mixed_fourier_boundary_closing_interface.md)

complement of the new stationary contour needs its own exponential

of the diagonal Fourier boundary mark: the former has a nontrivial
Jordan block, whereas every scalar function of the latter is
diagonalizable. This rules out that substitution, not a general
noncommuting operator treatment of the closing integral.

That noncommuting treatment is now explicit at finite level.
Section 5 of the same closing-interface note writes the actual
crossing as a finite triangular polynomial in the Fourier-index
lowering operator, followed by its exact diagonal phase. It proves

crossing calculus. The lowering operator has nilpotence index \(N\),
so its nilpotence does not give a bound uniform in the quantum level.
The same formulas recover the original ordinary Casimir as an
explicit invariant of this ordered transport; arbitrary ordinary
evaluation still retains its last-row forcing.

For the present boundary function, the
[zero-index projection theorem](research_mixed_fourier_zero_index_projection_gap.md)
pays that endpoint correction on a fixed complex neighborhood of

\(f_0(y)C_{1,N}(X,1)\), and the completed physical seam estimate
puts it exponentially below the full selected action. The result

Indeed the exact first-crossing formula is
\(\mathsf P_0\mathcal M_1G=\kappa G(0)f_0\) for every

The [crossed-endpoint identification](research_mixed_fourier_crossed_endpoint_terminal_source.md)
now expresses this observation as an existing ordinary terminal

 Z_N(a,0)=\mathcal V_{1,N}(2\cos(\pi/N),e^{-2\pi ia}).
\]
The proof uses the first Newton node and the Fourier cardinal
value at zero; no asymptotic continuation to the unit circle is

Fourier action still requires a comparison. The same note proves

The [signed crossing recurrences](research_mixed_fourier_signed_crossing_coefficients.md)
now describe the exact first Fourier coefficient after every fixed

support and all crossing scalars. This coefficient is a specified

Two signed runs now also have analytic endpoint bounds. After
[one negative crossing](research_mixed_fourier_negative_one_projection_payment.md),

where \(d_N^\star(X)=\overline{d_N(1/\overline X)}\).
Root orthogonality proves this identity with the original Gram

are exponentially small near each actual reference.
These are comparisons with the original cap action. A nonzero
asymptotic and action comparison for the complete crossed function
are still needed before either estimate can be iterated.

There is now a [complete finite-source reduction after two negative

\[
 \mathcal M_{-2}Z_N(a,y)
   =\frac{\kappa^{-2}e^{\pi i(N-1)y}}{N}
            C_{0,N}(e^{-2\pi ia},e^{-2\pi iy}).
\]
Here \(C_{0,N}\) is the original type-three conditional polynomial,
and \(\kappa\) is the original crossing scalar. The identity retains

Thus this particular full crossing problem reduces to a single

lies outside the supplied conditional-packet domains; the old

An [exact critical-point criterion](research_mixed_three_conditional_root_criterion.md)
addresses the resulting quadratic. Write
\(P=\cot(\pi a)=p+i\alpha\) and
\(Q=\cot(\pi y)=q+i\beta\). Provided \(p,q>0\) and
\(|\alpha+\beta|<2\), the original cotangent strip contains
exactly one critical point if and only if
\[
 p^2+q^2-(p+q)(\alpha q-\beta p)>0.
\]
On that domain the point is simple, holomorphic in the parameters,
and solves the original equation with zero logarithmic lift.
The [actual-input comparison](research_mixed_three_conditional_actual_input_subdomain.md)
now proves this inequality with reserve \(1/400\) for every actual

in the cotangent coordinates on the whole containing rectangle;
no roots are sampled. General terminal type-four inputs remain
unresolved. The older interior \(44/444\) bounds require ordinary
vertices beyond the final incoming leg, so they cannot be imported

The [complete endpoint-current theorem](research_mixed_three_fourier_conditional_endpoint_current.md)
also gives an exact decomposition of this conditional sum into

This does not compare it with the new crossed action. The

There is also a
[closed second-order difference equation](research_mixed_three_fourier_conditional_difference_equation.md)
for this entire conditional polynomial. Its explicit forcing is

The [particular-current theorem](research_mixed_three_fourier_conditional_particular_current.md)
now separates that forcing from the remaining period exactly:
\[
 C_{0,N}(X,W)=H_N(a,y)
       +\frac{(1-W^N)(X^{-N}-1)}{N^2}A_N(a,y),\qquad
 \mathcal L_{N,W}H_N=0,
\]
\[
 A_N(a,y)=-\frac{1}{(W-1)(X^{-1}-1)}+O(N^{-1}).
\]
The second term is defined by an explicit convergent contour integral,

The earlier real zero-mode integral alone did not solve that equation:

Its regular interior index phase has no stationary point when

 \mathcal M_{-3}Z_N
 =\mathcal P_{-3,N}
  +\kappa^{-3}N^{-3}e^{\pi iDy}

The bracket is holomorphic with the same error order for every fixed

On every fixed negative incoming-height neighborhood, including all

 \mathcal M_{-3}Z_N(a,y)
  =\kappa^{-3}N^{-3}

There is a corresponding packet with phase \(-\pi iy\) and opposite

The [exact nodal contraction](research_mixed_fourier_negative_three_nodal_contraction.md)

 I_N^{\rm hor}=N\int_c^{\beta_N}S_N^<(u+i\Im q_*)\,du.

The [neighbor-height reduction](research_mixed_first_attached_neighbor_height_credit.md)

The [coherent contour argument](research_mixed_prepared_cap_coherent_contour_completion.md)
now proves an asymptotic for the entire original prepared three-four
boundary function, near the original alternating Fourier parameter
and complete ordinary color:
\[
 v_N(w)^T A_{3,N}A_{4,N}h_N(y)
 =\kappa_N^3N^{-1}\mathcal B_{\rm cap}(y,w)
        e^{N\Phi_{\rm cap}(y,w)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad \mathcal B_{\rm cap}\ne0.
\]
The first cap is summed before taking absolute values. Its exact
polynomial remains in the three-index contour formula throughout.
This keeps the cancellation lost by the unsuccessful private-face
estimate. Every outer lattice correction and every connecting contour
now has a strict exponential gap. The proof uses the existing fifteen
successful comparisons, the cap's proved source envelopes, and an
elementary bound for its true-index endpoints; no new evaluation was
needed. Both level parities and fixed derivatives are retained.

This is a lower bound for the actual finite boundary function, not
only a nonzero coefficient of a formal local integral. Its asymptotic
is local in the outgoing Fourier parameter.

The [output-profile transport theorem](research_mixed_prepared_cap_full_period_profile_transport.md)
now also supplies an upper bound over the entire outgoing Fourier
period. Changing that parameter changes only the original outgoing
incidence. The proof adds this exact change to each already controlled
source profile, retaining its last index, complex height and loss.
Their compact maxima define a weight with the correct action and first
derivative at the reference. A finite periodization respects both level
parities. Patching this weight to the actual local phase and adding a
prescribed small slack away from that chart gives
\[
 \sup_{z\in\Lambda}|G_N(x_0+z)|e^{-NW_\varepsilon(z)}
       \le Q_\varepsilon N^{-1}e^{NM},
 \qquad M=\Re\Phi_{\rm cap}(x_0,-2).
\]
Here \(\Lambda\) is the whole real period together with a small
complex disk at the reference. The weight is defined by the original
source profiles, not by unknown values of the finite function. No
profile maximum has been newly evaluated.

The [two-block kernel estimate](research_mixed_paired_kernel_full_period_profile_transport.md)
now gives the corresponding upper bound with both boundary Fourier

The [Fourier-curvature theorem](research_mixed_fourier_profile_curvature.md)
now strengthens the reference comparison. The exact boundary incidence
has horizontal negative Hessian
\[
 -\Re d^2\ell_a(x)=c(a,x)(da-dx)^2+d(x)\,dx^2.
\]
On the specified original interface interval both coefficients are
positive and \(d(x)>\pi\). The full prepared central profile therefore
has output curvature at least \(\pi\); the paired central profile
has external curvature at least \(\pi/4\) in each boundary variable,
including its exceptional summed-index region. The existing gaps
control every nonmain profile on explicit smaller intervals. Hence the
complete transported paired rate satisfies
\[
 \mathcal B_{\rm coh}(\theta,\theta)
       \le M_{34}-\pi\theta^2/4
\]
there. This controls a genuine interval, with no new source evaluation.
It does not settle the rest of the Fourier period.

The missing operation is now more precise: prove that an admissible
weight for this actual source remains controlled under the full
attachment operator, including the input outside its local chart.
The weight just constructed has not been shown to satisfy that
inequality. There is, however, now a separate
[invariant phase neighborhood for the actual prefixes](research_mixed_actual_prefix_finite_step_phase_transport.md).
In retained-leg coordinates it contains the actual prepared \(34\)
phase and is preserved under \(34\) attachment. The stationary

\(.084\); Schwarz--Pick gives contraction \(14/15\) for the gradient
error in the displayed hyperbolic norm. The proof retains every
original action increment and a nondegenerate Fourier polarization.
Thus a source induction in this retained representation has no further
phase-proximity requirement. An induction using the older small
Fourier-kernel bidisk must still justify its moving seam domain.
Neither statement estimates the full finite-source remainder.
The completed knot-family scope and finite-exception target are unchanged.

The [single-letter extension](research_mixed_actual_prefix_arbitrary_letter_phase_class.md)
now allows arbitrary orderings of the two block types, rather than

function on the union of the two typed disks; its gradient norm
includes their different radii. The exact stationary response is
pullback of the incoming gradient error by the stationary input map.
Schwarz--Pick therefore gives contraction \(61/64\) for either
letter, uniformly in the preceding word. The local Gaussian
coefficients also form an invariant class: their logarithmic
derivatives satisfy \(M_{\rm out}\le M_0+(61/64)M_{\rm in}\),
and their normalized multipliers have fixed positive lower and
upper bounds. Both actual one-letter seeds belong to this class.
Every action increment and the original \(N^{-3/2}\) retained-current
power are preserved. This completes local phase and leading-symbol
transport for arbitrary three/four words; it does not control the
remaining terms in the full finite quantum sums.

The [localized finite-level remainder theorem](research_mixed_localized_current_remainder_transport.md)
now completes the corresponding local error estimate. It integrates
the exact original row on a fixed small translated box around each
critical point. After retaining the exact scalar multiplier at every
step, its normalized analytic remainder stays in an
\(O(N^{-1})\) ball for arbitrary sequences of the two block types,

This requires fixed inner input domains and a common enlarged output

There is now a
[critical-point existence theorem](research_mixed_fourier_boundary_critical_existence.md)
for every nonempty positive three/four prefix ending in four, with

The point is unique, nondegenerate and has the original logarithmic

The [exact source and local-current theorem](research_mixed_fourier_prefix_local_current.md)
connects these points to the original finite functions for every such
fixed prefix, without requiring a long alternating tail. If the word
has \(m\) letters, of which \(k\) are four, its local current is
\[
 \mathcal M_N=\kappa_N^{m+k}N^{-1}\mathcal B
                         e^{N\Phi}(1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad \mathcal B\ne0.
\]
The proof gives the original symbol explicitly and retains both
parities and fixed boundary derivatives. The power \(N^{-1}\) follows
from the exact matrix normalization: each four-crossing block carries
one factor \(N\), while a shared-boundary contraction carries none.
This theorem concerns the integral near the proved critical point.
The rest of the finite sum has not been shown smaller for every word,
and the relative error is asserted for each fixed word only.

The [coherent main-sheet theorem](research_mixed_fourier_prefix_coherent_main_sheet.md)

This controls the central sheet and its nonzero leading coefficient
uniformly at the level of the phase inequality. The finite-level

The theorem does not replace the boundary terms in the existing

Section 5 of the same note proves why the remaining step cannot be
replaced by more tests of fully real absolute face bounds. For an
all-four chain, moving every integration coordinate from its critical
height to zero increases the real phase by an amount growing with
the length. Moving one coordinate to the outer boundary has only a
bounded local cost. Consequently, for sufficiently long chains the
raw phase on that real face is greater than the critical action.
This is a proved limitation of that decomposition, not a failure of
the signed finite sum. A general propagation argument must retain
cancellation in the interior blocks as well as in the first cap.

The [Fourier-ended boundary reduction](research_mixed_fourier_ended_boundary_windows.md)
retains this interior cancellation and isolates two finite boundary

Each boundary estimate must include the adjoining interior loss and

therefore supplies a finite family of estimates uniform in the quantum
level, not a finite numerical test or a new knot-family theorem.

The [correlated right-endpoint theorem](research_mixed_fourier_right_cap_correlated_endpoint.md)
gives the appropriate reference family explicitly. At a last-four
vertex, put \(S=e^{-2\pi is}\), \(Q=e^{-2\pi iq}\) and
\(Y=e^{2\pi ix_0}\). The last stationary equation is
\[
 Q^2-(1+Y^{-1}-S)Q+(Y^{-1}-1)=0.
\]
The actual root is the unique one inside the unit disk. Rational
formulas recover \(S\) and the incoming exponent from \(Q\);
the typed-image filters force the original logarithmic equations,
with no extra branch choice. This gives an exact, locally
unramified parametrization of the actual last-vertex family.
Its first two displayed independent-disk counterexample arcs are

The [half-plane branch theorem](research_mixed_fourier_endpoint_halfplane_branch.md)

A [direct bare inner-contour proof](research_mixed_fourier_right_cap_bare_inner_contour.md)

including the short interval to the left of \(.24\). The original
ordinary row estimates each have gap \(1/2000\); the exact change
of actions therefore leaves gap \(1/35000\) for each of these two

The [saved-margin deduction](research_mixed_fourier_right_cap_last_row_saved_margin.md)

record reconstructs coverage and parses the existing bounds; it

The [outgoing-contour theorem](research_mixed_fourier_right_cap_outer_contour.md)

 W_{n,N}(Y;Y)=\mathcal A(n/N,Y)e^{NI(n/N,Y)}
