They do give a uniform phase loss \(1/500\), and a complete
finite-source loss \(1/1000\), on a plateau edge with a selection
when both height fractions are at least \(4/5\). This last
consequence uses exact rational inequalities and the existing
source theorem.

A [certified five-cycle example](research_mixed_right_maximum_transport_obstruction.md)
shows that lowering the largest right-transition coordinate need not
increase the phase, even at the actual correlated geometric heights.
Its derivative is less than \(-.003\) at an interior target with
all real coordinates at least \(.22\). Thus the left minimum-level
argument cannot be extended to the right by merely reversing the
direction. A net estimate for a group of blocks remains possible;
the example does not contradict any completed source bound or volume
identity.

A [three-vertex geometric enclosure](research_mixed_neighbor_conditioned_critical_boxes.md)
now bounds critical coordinates according to their neighboring types.
Its 512 boundary products and 4,778 cells passed both the 256-bit
author check and a fresh 320-bit replay. These bounds retain the
original logarithmic branch for every cyclic word, including lengths
one and two. They help retain the correlations needed when two
incident right-transition blocks are estimated together.

A [reference-extension lemma](research_mixed_height_coupled_reference_extension.md)
also controls targets whose heights depend on the reference. It proves
an explicit rectangle-width correction to a boundary comparison;
the uncorrected harmonic argument would not apply. Its [paired right-transition application](research_mixed_paired_right_transition_support.md)
now passes all 2,048 reference boundary products at 256 bits and a
fresh 320-bit replay of all 68,903 saved cells. It controls the two
unselected blocks at one transition coordinate and pays the costs
of the two exterior plateau blocks. This gives a strict loss for an
isolated transition with plateau neighbors; arbitrary overlapping
transition groups and selected terms remain separate.
The [diagonal-height extension](research_mixed_selected_height_reference_extension.md)
now permits prescribed selected heights and every actual Fourier
branch. Its exact Laplacian and curvature argument are proved, but
the selected boundary support estimate is still open.

A [selected seven-cycle example](research_mixed_selected_minimum_flow_obstruction.md)
also shows that the corresponding selected minimum-level flow can
decrease immediately below the four-fifths height threshold. Its
derivative is less than \(-.8\), with the original neighboring
height relations and the correct Fourier branch retained. The same
note proves a useful positive fact: throughout the transition strip
\(.1\le x\le.22\), \(0\le h\le.014\),
\(-\Re g(x+ih)-2\pi h>3/40\). The factorial alternative therefore
strictly dominates the forcing alternative there. This simplifies the
selected comparison but does not make the decreasing flow monotone.

The [enlarged positive cap](research_mixed_early_selected_source_cap.md)
now supplies the complete finite-sum asymptotic when the selected
height rises from zero at real coordinate .10 to .014 at .12, and
then stays constant. The whole 161-product cover passed at 256 bits;
a fresh 320-bit replay verified the same 71,240 cells without new
subdivisions. All original midpoint contributions and aliases remain
in this estimate. On the corresponding
[earlier contour](research_mixed_early_selected_transport.md), the
selected Fourier correction is constant as minimum coordinates move
from .12 to .22. This removes the derivative obstruction from that
part of the path. The [78 additional local derivative domains](research_mixed_constant_selected_height_transport.md)
have now passed the complete 256-bit check and a separate 320-bit
implementation, covering the same 817,218 leaves and every recorded
monotonicity reduction. The separate 192-domain replay is complete as well. Together these
local results and the existing transport argument prove the
selected-term bound on \([.12,.45]^m\): every nonempty selection
has finite exponential loss at least 1/200. No further geometric
assumption is needed for that particular region.
The early interval is handled by the direct estimate below. Combining
it with the later transition, low or right coordinates, and the right
transition still requires further estimates.

The [early block theorem](research_mixed_early_transition_support.md)
now gives a direct comparison on that first interval. One real
coordinate may lie in [.10,.12] and its neighbor anywhere in
[.10,.45], with independent small heights and every actual Fourier
branch retained. Its phase loss is 1/100 after reserving the full
oriented cost of a neighboring plateau height change. The proof uses
the two positive triangle forms to obtain real concavity and height
convexity, then finite tangent bounds and a subharmonic comparison in
the reference parameters. All 64 boundary products and 251 cells
passed at 256 bits and in a fresh 320-bit saved-cover replay.

The [early/plateau assembly](research_mixed_early_plateau_clusters.md)
uses that reserve for every arrangement in
\(([.10,.12]\cup[.22,.45])^m\), with every original selection.
Each changed plateau incidence has a unique neighboring early-block
credit. When both ends of a plateau block change, the largest residual
cost is .0168255; its two adjoining early losses total .02. This
leaves a uniform positive margin at arbitrary fixed cycle length,
including lengths one and two. The complete finite integral off the
plateau is therefore smaller by at least 1/2000 in exponential rate,
and this restricted region retains the original nonzero central
coefficient. Combining early coordinates with the later transition,
or with coordinates below .1 or in the right region, remains open.

The [fixed-early transport reduction](research_mixed_frozen_early_transport.md)
now specifies the next local inequality. Early coordinates stay fixed;
a position between two early positions also stays fixed, since both
its incident blocks are already controlled by the stronger early
estimate. That exclusion is necessary: the real three-cycle with
types (3,4,3) at (.1,.219,.1) has middle rate derivative less than
\(-3/20\). Original-logarithm self-maps verify this without an
approximation to the geometric reference heights, because all target
heights are exactly zero. After excluding those isolated positions,
the endpoint bound and the transport implication are proved, but the
required local derivative inequality remains open. The case where
the moving center has no early neighbor now has a
[complete fifty-domain calculation](research_mixed_frozen_outer_half_stencils.md):
132,360 leaves passed at 256 bits and in the separate 320-bit
implementation. Combined with the now completed 192 and 78 domains,
this supplies that case of the derivative inequality. The case with one early neighbor requires the
[correlated-height comparison](research_mixed_one_early_neighbor_transport.md),
whose complete 175-chart cover has now passed the canonical 256-bit
check and the separate 320-bit implementation. Together the four
local families supply every admissible moving-center case. The
[full left-region theorem](research_mixed_full_left_region.md) therefore
retains the original nonzero central coefficient after summing every
selection over \([.1,.45]^m\), at every fixed cycle length. Its
error is exponentially smaller, with rate loss
\(\min\{1/2000,\mu/1600\}\), where \(\mu>0\) is the
established plateau Hessian bound. This does not yet include regions
that mix these coordinates with low or right coordinates. A position with two
early neighbors remains fixed, as proved above.

The new comparison uses two geometric bounds that are already
established. A [type-four position followed by type four](research_mixed_four_before_four_height.md)
has right-leg height below -.048, while the
[middle of three consecutive type-four positions](research_mixed_three_consecutive_four_height.md)
has height below -.053. Their proofs enclose original five-position
window solutions on complete external rectangle boundaries, then use
holomorphy and uniqueness to reach every actual cyclic word. The first
512-product result passed both original-logarithm and independent
sine/cotangent implementations; the stronger 256-product subset was
rechecked independently on every saved cell. These are geometric
inputs to the phase estimate, not assertions about a finite sum.

An [exact reflection of the physical indices](research_mixed_physical_index_folding.md)
also gives a Fourier alternative. The three-crossing kernel has a
factorial reflection identity, and its positive Gram form compares
the whole right-half trace with a weighted left-half trace. The
four-crossing kernel acquires a different weighted coefficient
kernel. The exact difference contains a matrix whose norm has
positive exponential rate, so it cannot be dropped as a small
reflection error. These are identities of the original finite sums;
the note retains the diagonal weights and explains why a physical-grid
identity cannot simply replace a Laurent function on a deformed contour.

On the earlier independent contours, the [assembled result](research_mixed_selected_right_taper_support.md#5-all-selected-subsets-on-the-region-above-22)
controls every original Fourier term on the whole region \([.22,1]^m\),
for every fixed cyclic word of three- and four-crossing blocks. Its
contribution has the same nonzero geometric leading coefficient as the
central integral. Partitioning into the constant-height portion, the
right curved portion and the right half-period gives an exponential
loss of at least \(1/160000\) for every contribution except the
uncorrected central one. The proof includes adjacent curved coordinates,
all Fourier subsets and the actual polynomial part of each Fourier weight.
The all-small box is now exponentially smaller as well. The remaining
outer integral on those independent contours is contained in configurations with a coordinate below
.22 and a coordinate above .10. It could still cancel the contribution
just proved; this is not a theorem for the whole period.

The [assembly with both right curved coordinates included](research_mixed_unselected_right_taper_products.md#3-a-whole-unaliased-integration-region)
now evaluates the term without additional frequencies on the whole
region \([.22,1]^m\). It has the same nonzero geometric leading
coefficient. Partitioning each coordinate into the plateau, the right
curved portion and the right half-period gives a strict exponential
loss on every box except the all-plateau box. The proof includes
adjacent coordinates on the curved portion and budgets the small
Fourier-weight errors for the whole word. This extends the earlier
[plateau/right-half assembly](research_mixed_right_half_block_bound.md#5-an-unaliased-integral-that-can-now-be-assembled).
The additional-frequency terms on that larger region are now included
by the stronger assembly stated above. Its new local inputs are the
[selected central-block bound](research_mixed_selected_plateau_support.md)
and the [selected right-contour bound](research_mixed_selected_right_taper_support.md).
For each smooth expression in a true Fourier weight, real concavity
bounds its maximum by a quadratic at a rational trial point. Convexity
in the contour heights reduces the whole curved portion to height
endpoints. The proofs retain the dependence of each unselected target
height on its reference height. The older
[plateau clamping theorem](research_mixed_plateau_alias_clamping.md)
continues to give the stronger loss \(|S|/150\) on the all-plateau
box itself, for a nonempty selected set \(S\).

We have also proved a [local bound on part of the left curved
contour](research_mixed_left_taper_tilted_hessian.md). For an unselected
four-crossing block, its left real parameter may lie in \([.15,.22]\)
while its own parameter lies in \([.24,.45]\). The complete block is
exponentially smaller than its geometric tangent-plane estimate by
at least \(1/2000\). This comparison uses straight complex segments
from the geometric reference point; it does not assume concavity after
substituting a curved contour.

There is also a [global algebraic root theorem](research_mixed_global_cotangent_roots.md).
For both crossing types the conditional critical equation has exactly
one simple root in a specified cotangent strip, for every pair of
parameters in one common domain. The proof excludes roots on the
boundary and counts them at a single exact base point. It fixes the
original logarithmic lift and applies throughout both quadratic contour
profiles away from their endpoints. Thus root existence no longer
requires a separate rectangle calculation at every point. Controlling
the complete finite sum through that root requires an additional argument.

The [closed-boundary extension](research_mixed_closed_cotangent_roots.md)
now includes an outer angle with real part one half while its neighbor
is complex. The selected root remains simple, its logarithm keeps the
original zero lift, and the negative real Hessian remains positive.
This supplies the endpoint needed by convex complex parameter domains.
It does not by itself supply a finite-sum bound on those domains.

There is also a [height-minimization theorem](research_mixed_minimizing_height_transport.md).
On a fixed product of real and imaginary parameter intervals, a
holomorphic phase with negative definite real Hessian has a unique
height minimizer above each real point. The minimized real phase is
strictly concave, even where the minimizing height reaches a fixed
boundary face. Where the minimum is interior, writing
\(\Phi''=-A+iB\) gives \(Dh=A^{-1}B\) and the reduced Hessian
\(-A-BA^{-1}B\). If the original finite sum is bounded by this
phase throughout the product, its exact contour can use this graph;
the geometric coefficient is unchanged. This applies to the proved
unselected central product. It is not a theorem for shrinking height
intervals: the note gives both an elementary counterexample and an
obstruction in the original homogeneous four-crossing phase near real
angle .1414. Thus extending the method into the left transition still
requires estimates on the sloping boundary and on the whole finite sum.

That argument is now proved for [every real pair of neighboring
parameters](research_mixed_all_real_conditional_packet.md). On every
compact \(K\Subset(0,1/2)^2\), the original conditional sum satisfies
\[
 \mathcal L_{\epsilon,N}(a,b)
 =N^{(1-\epsilon)/2}B_\epsilon(a,b)
       e^{NQ_\epsilon(s_*;a,b)}\{1+O_K(N^{-1})\},
 \qquad B_\epsilon(a,b)\ne0,
\]
where \(\epsilon=0,1\) denotes the three- or four-crossing type and
\(B_\epsilon\) is its original, explicitly normalized Gaussian
coefficient. This holds at all integer levels, with every finite row
retained. The proof covers both signs of the critical height and is
uniform when that height passes through zero.

The [half-endpoint extension](research_mixed_half_endpoint_conditional_packet.md)
now gives the same assertion on every compact subset of
\((0,1/2]^2\). The proof checks the boundary root count, strict phase
inequalities and the exact finite-source contour at an outer parameter
equal to one half. It retains the same nonzero Gaussian coefficient.
The canonical interpolated sum is covered at every integer level;
an exactly half-period physical color occurs only at even levels.

The proof proceeds through four general statements. The algebraic root
theorem fixes the critical point and its logarithm. A [left-half
phase argument](research_mixed_real_conditional_contour_geometry.md)
and a [circular second-difference inequality](research_mixed_negative_height_full_period.md)
show that the geometric point dominates the entire horizontal period.
The [factorial continuation theorem](research_lower_half_factorial_continuation.md)
controls shifted arguments beyond one period, with exact midpoint
moduli at both ends of the finite index range. Finally a [full residue
rectangle](research_mixed_global_lower_conditional_packet.md), together
with its upper-height extension, keeps the original zero mode and both
Fourier remainders. The upper period multiplier is retained explicitly.
Thus the proof can handle cancellation even when the sum of absolute
values of the original rows has a larger exponential rate.

This real-parameter source theorem does not assert dominance at every
complex point of the outer taper. It is uniform on compact real sets,
not at a parameter tending to zero with \(N\). Nor does its nonzero
coefficient settle cancellation after the remaining outer summations.

The [complex-neighborhood stability theorem](research_mixed_real_packet_complex_stability.md)
now gives an open complex neighborhood of every fixed compact real
parameter set, with the same nonzero full-source asymptotic. It proves
this by perturbing every original contour current, including the exact
right-midpoint multiplier and both Fourier remainders. The neighborhood
is not asserted to contain the prescribed taper heights. A separate
[rational cotangent example](research_mixed_complex_horizontal_obstruction.md)
shows that root uniqueness on the much larger cotangent domain does
not imply domination on the entire horizontal contour: its right-end
rate can exceed the selected rate. The smaller taper domain is not
decided by that example.

An [exact coupled-contour theorem](research_mixed_coupled_outer_graph.md)
allows each outer height to depend on its two neighbors. If a coordinate
is at most .22, a particular cutoff makes both arguments of every
incident inner sum real. The new real-parameter theorem then applies
away from zero. The deformation preserves the complete finite Laurent
integral, and its Jacobian is bounded independently of the level. It
does not preserve the previously proved upper bounds on the real phase.

There are now [two proved obstructions](research_mixed_left_support_obstructions.md)
to simple absolute estimates on this region. First, taking absolute
values of the individual inner rows can exceed the geometric tangent
rate. Second, on the proposed coupled contour, an actual seven-block
all-four example has a coherent finite-density rate exceeding the
geometric rate by a number between .0093 and .0095. The source and
weight asymptotics are valid at that example, so this second failure
is not an artifact of an unjustified saddle approximation. It rules out
pointwise absolute domination on that contour. It does not rule out
cancellation in the integral or a different contour.

The full cyclic sum, the boundary conditions needed for the knot
invariant, and arbitrary short twist patterns are not yet settled.
In particular these latest local and cyclic results have not enlarged
the proved family of knots described below. The frozen manuscripts
have not been changed.

For every fixed cyclic word in threes and fours, the
[central integral theorem](research_mixed_central_outer_integral.md)
now evaluates the entire part of the original unaliased outer integral
whose real coordinates lie in \([1/4,2/5]\). Its leading coefficient
is nonzero. The proof uses complete inner finite sums on
[independent parameter rectangles](research_mixed_central_conditional_rectangles.md)
and a uniform positive Hessian. It proves exponential decay throughout
that central cube away from the selected critical point; no inner
endpoint or Fourier correction is discarded.

The earlier [central alias theorem](research_mixed_central_alias_gap.md)
bounds every additional-frequency term on that smaller cube as
well. Moving each selected four-type contour to height \(.014\)
costs at most \((25/2)(.071)^2\) in its optimized action.
The actual Fourier polynomial supplies a larger penalty, even where
its interpolation remainder dominates the factorial continuation.
The resulting loss is at least \(1/125\) per selected variable.
The proof allows every real coordinate to readjust; it does not
assume that the shifted maximum stays near the old critical point.
It extends the earlier
[local decomposition](research_mixed_local_outer_contribution.md),
[reoptimized action estimate](research_mixed_reoptimized_alias_action.md)
and [shifted conditional-sum theorem](research_mixed_shifted_conditional_packets.md).

Consequently the exact cyclic trace is its nonzero geometric central
term plus an explicitly defined exterior remainder and exponentially
smaller central corrections. For each additional-frequency subset,
deform its whole period first and then remove the same real cube
\([.22,1]^m\); the sum of the integrals over the remaining regions
is the exterior remainder. There are no unrecorded joining contours.
Bounding that remainder below the critical exponential rate is the
remaining cyclic problem. The central contribution can still be
canceled by it. Even a full cyclic result would require the original
boundary conditions before it could be applied to a knot invariant.

There is also an exact [periodic graph contour](research_mixed_outer_graph_contours.md)
that keeps the established central heights and reaches height zero on
the right half of the Fourier period. It applies to each original
finite Laurent polynomial, including every additional-frequency term.
The joining sides cancel by periodicity, and its Jacobian is bounded
independently of the level. Its existence does not establish
dominance of its central contribution.

The [triangle-Hessian criterion](research_mixed_plateau_accretivity.md)
now provides strict real concavity of the eliminated phase on the
larger constant-height box \([.22,.45]^m\). Its proof starts from
the established holomorphic conditional root, proves positivity of
the real part of each triangle Hessian by an exact cotangent identity,
and preserves that positivity under a complex Schur complement.
The bound is uniform in the cyclic word length. With the actual
unselected Fourier-polynomial estimate, this gives the full unaliased
asymptotic on that box. It also justifies the larger plateau of the
periodic graph. It makes no concavity assertion after substituting
a curved height graph. The additional-frequency estimates use the
separate clamping argument below.

The [clamping argument](research_mixed_plateau_alias_clamping.md)
bounds each of the two possible exponential expressions in an actual
Fourier weight separately. Mixed derivatives are positive. The signs
of the derivatives on selected faces therefore allow the upper
coordinates to be lowered to .4 without increasing the required
upper bound. Raising the lower coordinates from .22 to .25 costs
at most \(3|S|/5000\). Combining this with the smaller-box theorem
leaves the strict loss \(|S|/150\), including the Fourier error.
Every inequality used for these derivative signs has a saved rational
interval witness; a separate 320-bit implementation reproduced all
58,621 witnesses. The written concavity and clamping proof explains
why these finite inequalities control every fixed cyclic word.

The [larger conditional-source theorem](research_mixed_transition_conditional_rectangles.md)
now controls the whole original finite inner sum when both neighboring
real parameters lie in \([.22,.45]\), at all the original and selected
heights. It establishes a new holomorphic root on the larger product,
retains every row and contour correction, and proves the nonzero
asymptotic with its original normalization. It supplies the full
finite-source input to the enlarged-plateau argument above. The
remaining left portion below .22 still needs its complete comparison.
The right curved portion is now included in the assembled theorem.

The [wider asymmetric extension](research_mixed_asymmetric_wide_conditional_packets.md)
evaluates the complete four-crossing conditional sum when its left
real parameter lies in \([.15,.22]\) and its right one in
\([.24,.46]\), at all the stated original and selected heights.
It extends the earlier [narrower domain](research_mixed_asymmetric_low_conditional_packets.md).
The proof controls every finite row and both unequal-height Fourier
corrections, and retains the nonzero leading coefficient and original
normalization. Its logarithmic root and normalized asymptotic agree
with the plateau theorem where the domains meet. The joined domain
contains the straight segments used in the left-contour comparison
stated above. That comparison is proved for unselected variables in
its stated ranges; the whole extended domain does not automatically
satisfy the same upper bound.

A [right-side extension](research_mixed_right_guard_conditional_packets.md)
similarly evaluates each complete conditional sum when one real
argument lies in \([.45,.50]\) and the other in \([.22,.45]\).
Both block types and both argument orders are included, at every
stated selected and unselected height. This provides the finite-sum
asymptotic needed to compare the right curved contour with the geometric
contribution. Existence of that asymptotic alone does not establish
the comparison. A [one-coordinate comparison](research_mixed_right_taper_tilt.md)
now proves an exponential loss of \(1/80000\) for the complete block
with its allocated Fourier weights. The proof integrates the Hessian
along a straight complex segment: positive curvature before real
coordinate .45 outweighs the possible negative curvature afterward.
The written argument and a separate 320-bit run have been checked.
It concerns unselected variables and does not cover two adjacent
coordinates on the right curved contour. The [two-coordinate theorem](research_mixed_unselected_right_taper_products.md)
supplies that remaining case. It extends the complete conditional sum
to the independent square \([.22,.50]^2\), controls both complex
directions in the Hessian, and integrates the resulting early and late
curvature bounds. The complete allocated block again loses at least
\(1/80000\). Summing the original tangent planes cancels their linear
terms at the cyclic critical point; this proves the larger unselected
integration-region result stated at the beginning of this record.

The [endpoint and seam estimates](research_mixed_boundary_strip_bounds.md)
now bound the complete local finite kernels near the ends of the Fourier
period, including their actual reciprocal-factorial weights. One estimate
holds in an explicit strip of half-width \(10^{-6}\) without changing the
original contour height. These are absolute bounds, not yet bounds relative
to the geometric critical value. To compose them through an arbitrary
word, the dependence on the neighboring angle must be retained: taking
independent worst-case values can lose the required exponential gap.

For a [type-three block with a type-four left leg](research_mixed_43_endpoint_support.md),
that comparison is now proved at the tapered right endpoint and on a
fixed neighborhood of it. The complete local source has a strict
loss of \(1/2000\) below its original geometric supporting plane,
uniformly over all reference parameters and the full unselected
height range \([-.057,0]\) or selected range \([0,.014]\).
The proof bounds the absolute sum of every row before extending
the endpoint to a neighborhood. Its
[source support grids](research_mixed_endpoint_support_grid.md)
and the reference comparison are separate outward covers, followed
by an independent replay. A [separate theorem for the other seven
orientations](research_mixed_all_endpoint_support.md) now completes
the endpoint estimate for every three- and four-crossing block.
Its raw bounds include the seams, all heights on the taper, both
Fourier alternatives, and both endpoint representatives in the
geometric plane. Thus every such endpoint has a fixed neighborhood
with a strict geometric loss; intermediate angles require the
additional arguments below.

The source optimization has been reduced further. On the right
half-period, the actual Fourier weight has no exponential rate at
height zero. Its [angular extrema](research_mixed_right_half_source_reduction.md)
are explicit; with the other half-weight included, the general
[candidate equations](research_mixed_angular_support_candidates.md)
have degree two or six, with their endpoints and Fourier branch
changes retained. At right angle \(1/2\), each expression in the
actual Fourier maximum is
[strictly concave in the row and neighboring angle](research_mixed_right_half_concavity.md)
on \(0<u<1/2,\ .13\le y\le.5\), and convex in the contour
height. Thus the maximum on this region can be bounded by two
height-endpoint problems and rigorous tangent estimates.

The [geometric supporting slopes](research_mixed_geometric_support_slopes.md)
now satisfy \(-1/5<\Re p_a,\Re p_b<1/4\) for every actual cyclic
three/four word. Here \(p_a,p_b\) are the derivatives of one
conditional critical action, with its two incident Fourier half-weights.
An outward calculation on three neighboring blocks and a separate
sine/cotangent replay prove the bounds. They supply the hypotheses
of the right-half reduction: for rows \(u\le1/2\), the other angle
\(y<.13\) and the extra interior right-angle maximum can both be
eliminated analytically.

The [core support comparison](research_mixed_right_core_support.md)
now compares the remaining lower-row maxima and the complete-period
row value with the original geometric plane. It includes both
orientations, both Fourier alternatives, and the full ranges of heights
on either of the two proposed taper contours. Concavity gives 750
rigorous scalar upper bounds; the correlated three-block reference
comparison covers all 512 boundary products. An independent calculation
using the original signed heights reproduces every scalar bound.
The support gap exceeds \(1/500\), leaving a finite-source gap of
\(1/1000\) after the Fourier tolerance.

For the upper rows, the [endpoint reduction](research_mixed_high_row_endpoint_reduction.md)
proves that, at right angle \(1/2\) and other angle
\(y\in[.13,.5]\), the row exponent has a single minimum on
\([.5,1]\). Its maximum is therefore at \(u=.5\) or \(u=1\),
both already included in the core comparison. The proof retains
the original reciprocal factor and treats the logarithmic product
zeros. Together these results control all rows on this core.
The [remaining small-angle upper rows](research_mixed_small_angle_high_rows.md)
also admit a complete reduction: their maximum occurs at
\((u,y)=(.5,.13)\), at the original height, for every height
needed on these portions of either taper. The proof combines a
monotonicity estimate near the half-row with one compact strict
inequality for the distant rows. It includes the positive-height
Fourier term in the branch subtraction; dropping that term
separately would not justify the argument.

These estimates now assemble into a [complete local right-half
theorem](research_mixed_right_half_block_bound.md). Whenever either
outer angle of a block lies in \([.5,1]\), its original finite
kernel, with both allocated Fourier weights, is bounded below its
geometric supporting plane by an exponential gap \(1/2000\).
All summation indices, all allowed selected factors, both taper
choices and arbitrary fixed cyclic three/four words are included.
The remaining global problem concerns the blocks with both angles
in the left half-period and how their bounds combine around the word.

The [two-right-angle theorem](research_mixed_two_right_source_bound.md)
now proves the full local comparison when both target angles lie in
\([1/2,1]\) at height zero. The exact angular reduction leaves
four corner values, whose row maxima have explicit algebraic
maximizing parameters. A complete reference cover proves a gap
greater than \(1/50\), leaving a finite-source gap of \(1/100\)
after the Fourier error. Every original row and every choice of
selected half-weight is included. For a fixed cyclic word of
\(m\) blocks, the integral of the absolute value over the all-right
box is therefore at most
\[
 C N^A\exp\{N(M-m/100)\},
\]
where \(M\) is the real part of the original critical action.
The linear supporting terms cancel by the actual stationary
equations. This settles that whole exterior box for every
additional-frequency subset; it does not settle regions with
one right-half neighbor and one left-half neighbor by itself.
Those local configurations are covered by the assembled right-half
theorem above; its global use still requires bounds on the other
blocks in the same word.

The parameter bounds are uniform in word length. Every type-three
critical leg lies in \((.30,.39)+i(-.03,.02)\) by the
[three-vertex window theorem](research_mixed_type_three_window_strip.md);
every type-four leg lies in \((.27,.33)+i(-.057,-.001)\) by the
[type-four window theorem](research_mixed_cyclic_critical_height_bounds.md).
The [refined type-four estimate](research_mixed_type_four_height_refinement.md)
improves the upper height to \(-.02\) for every actual cyclic critical
leg. It uses the original block map on the already proved rectangles,
with a complete outward boundary cover and a separate sine/cotangent
replay. It changes neither the finite-source definition nor the knot
scope.
These bounds exclude the explicit
[endpoint obstruction on an earlier, larger domain](research_mixed_conditional_image_contours.md).
A separate [operator bound](research_arbitrary_twist_conditional_endpoints.md)
controls the highest conditional rows uniformly in every signed crossing
power, with a rate tending to zero as their fractional width shrinks.
It does not control the whole observed word.

The [separated operator calculation](research_mixed_wrapped_operator_factorization.md)
also puts every additional-frequency insertion in the original
crossing coordinates. An explicit unitary Fourier transform expresses
its middle matrix through divided differences of reciprocal factorials.
Relative to the positive three-crossing expression, the insertion is
strictly upper triangular. The full operator has rank \(N-1\)
and is already nonnilpotent at \(N=2\). These identities specify the operator that an
approximately invariant-vector argument would need to control; they
do not provide such a vector or an exponential norm bound.

The [exact row-window calculation](research_mixed_wrapped_geometric_window.md)
now rules out one proposed norm shortcut. If \(\mathcal E_N\) is the
relative correction operator defined there and \(\Pi_N\) restricts its
indices to a shrinking window about \(Nx_0\), containing a growing number
of indices, then
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}N^{-1}\log\|\Pi_N\mathcal E_N\Pi_N\|_2
 =\int_0^{x_0}\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt .
\]
This rate is positive at the geometric index \(x_0=2/3\).
The calculation also gives exact finite formulas for contractions with
the neighboring crossing matrix, including the endpoint terms of a
restricted sum. Thus a useful vector estimate must exploit these
particular phases and contractions. Restricting the indices alone
does not make the correction operator small.

At a boundary, the [three-crossing cap theorem](research_mixed_three_first_cap_packet.md)
now gives a nonzero asymptotic for the whole original cap at actual
outgoing root-of-unity indices. The
[Fourier replacement theorem](research_mixed_three_first_cap_fourier_reduction.md)
then expresses its original polynomial remainder exactly inside the
next full contraction. It retains an extra reciprocal-factorial weight
and an additional-frequency term. Its replacement polynomial has a
genuine complex asymptotic near the real outgoing interval. Quantitative
control on distant complex boundary configurations and the new full
boundary correction are still needed.


The completed short-chain theorem proves the volume limit for the original finite sum
of every fixed homogeneous chain of length \(m\ge3\), with crossing
power three at each selected vertex and both outside ends complete.
The [full propagation proof](research_three_larger_source_propagation.md)
preserves the nonzero local asymptotic and bounds on the entire internal
Fourier period through any fixed number of attachments. The
[closing theorem](research_three_larger_source_closure.md), together
with the separate [three-vertex](research_three_chain_three_closure.md),
[four-vertex](research_three_chain_four_closure.md)
and [five-vertex](research_three_chain_five_closure.md) proofs, gives
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}
 \log|v(-2)^TA_N^mv(-2)|=\operatorname{Vol}(M_m),\qquad m\ge3.
\]
Here \(M_m\) is the marked partially filled manifold with the two
outside ends complete. The coefficient of the leading exponential
is nonzero, its polynomial prefactor is \(N^{-3/2}\), and the result
holds at both level parities. Written proof reviews and outward
arithmetic checks cover the closing inequalities. Its marked
application to knot complements after further fillings is described
below; the scalar statement alone does not supply that identification.

The [outside-color theorem](research_three_chain_outside_boundary_decay.md)
now supplies decay over all real boundary colors and a quadratic bound
in a fixed complex strip, with a nonzero holomorphic local asymptotic.
Its written proof and the inherited cap-domain certificates have been
checked. The proof obtains the boundary loss in the original cap
contours and preserves it through attachment without an accumulating
error in the exponential rate. These are the analytic estimates needed
to compose the short chains with later fillings.

The [marked component theorem](research_three_chain_short_filling_stability.md)
now makes that application. In the original circle-tree construction,
selected components may include any fixed number of homogeneous paths,
each of fixed length at least three, original degree two at every selected
vertex, and two distinct outside vertices. Each such path may use power
\(+3\) throughout or power \(-3\) throughout. They may occur alongside
the previously proved graph components. Independently sufficiently long
remaining signed powers give the original Kashaev volume identity for
the knot complement, along all integer levels. The proof retains the
original carrier parity, knot-component test, boundary degrees and
primitive filling curves. It does not treat mixed signs within one path.

The general finite-exception target remains open. The
[original-tree padding theorem](research_original_tree_padding_equivalence.md)
also makes its strength precise: adding two original crossing circles
creates a zero-filling slice on which each old assignment has an
infinite fiber, all representing the same knot. Universal cofiniteness
per template would therefore prove the identity for every hyperbolic
knot represented by the original circle-tree class, with no exceptions.
The same holds for paths. This implication uses the original grammar,
not an enlargement of the class or a change from assignments to knot
types. Untreated reduced knots on such fibers cannot be counted as a
finite exceptional list. General mixed short paths and arbitrary short branching components
remain outside the new source theorem.

For mixed short powers, the [three/four interface calculation](research_three_four_source_interface.md)
now gives an exact one-crossing kernel and finite Fourier transport
identities. It certifies a positive alternating geometric reference
and a strictly negative real Hessian for its local angular phase.
This reference is more than \(.035\) from the old Fourier center,
and its two vertex gradients are opposite and nonzero. At level three,
an exact nonreal trace ratio rules out making the power-four vertex or
the alternating period positive Hermitian by scalar normalization and
similarity. These facts specify why the existing homogeneous argument
cannot simply be reused. Both full local kernels are now controlled
near that reference, as described below. A mixed quantum asymptotic
still needs control of the ordinary end factors along a full joined
cycle and estimates for the entire remaining source. The periodic
geometric reference alone does not provide these estimates.

The [exact crossing transport](research_crossing_cauchy_transport.md)
now determines the one-crossing kernel by a forced first-order difference
equation and its cyclic boundary condition. The forcing is explicit;
discarding it would leave only the zero solution on the regular domain.
The resulting finite Green formula retains both level parities. Its
closing denominator can be exponentially small, so this algebraic
determination does not by itself bound the kernel. A crossed pole also
has an exact residue and a nonzero local expansion. At the alternating
three/four reference, however, stationarity of that residue with the
old three-vertex phase requires an intermediate parameter of modulus
greater than 1.30, outside the domain of the old packet theorem.
A separate Pascal-matrix estimate controls the extra cost of a crossing
on one deleted corner; it is not an estimate for an entire mixed word.

There is now a quantitative estimate for the full crossing kernel.
An explicit one-variable entropy criterion gives an all-order expansion
by its first finitely many matrix rows and an exponentially bounded tail
after any fixed positive fractional row cutoff. It holds over the whole
input period at either nonzero height. At the alternating reference,
the leading term is the rank-one endpoint contribution. The moving-pole
term is exponentially smaller there, including at the required exterior
intermediate point. A proof of the geometric term must therefore combine
the crossing with its neighboring source before discarding the larger
endpoint contribution.

The [exterior product construction](research_exterior_crossing_phase.md)
removes the local domain obstruction. Exact inversion of the second
finite product gives a three-variable stationary phase at the required
point. Its negative real Hessian is bounded below by \(2I\), and its
local Gaussian density is nonzero. Eliminating the index variables gives
the original power-four characteristic equation. A connected complex
continuation fixes the phase constant exactly, so the local critical
action equals the original angular action. Shifting the entire finite
wire period below the real axis also gives an exact starting expression
for the whole sum in this exterior chart. That construction alone
does not determine the coefficient of its local contribution in the
full finite cycle. The exact summation and two-index contour argument
below supply the full power-four kernel through a different expression
of the same finite sum.

A further [exact finite calculation](research_power_four_finite_source.md)
combines the two kernels before estimating either one. Integrating the
intermediate Fourier variable selects a triangular set of coefficients.
A finite binomial identity then sums one index exactly, leaving a
symmetric two-index formula for the original power-four vertex.
It retains the original scalar and all level parities. Its selected
critical indices both lie inside the original denominator charts.
Thus the larger crossing endpoint term no longer has to be estimated
separately from its cancelling partners.

The [full power-four theorem](research_power_four_source_packet.md)
now proves the resulting local asymptotic for the original, undeleted
kernel. On a fixed complex neighborhood of the alternating reference,
\[
 V_{4,N}(x,y)=\kappa^2N^{-1/2}a_4(x,y)e^{N\Xi_4(x,y)}
                  (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad a_4(x,y)\ne0.
\]
Here \(\Xi_4\) is the original geometric angular action, including
its absolute constant. The conclusion holds at both level parities
and with every fixed boundary derivative. The
[real-index argument](research_power_four_real_complement.md)
reduces the entire triangular complement to four concave edge curves
under explicit algebraic inequalities on the boundary parameters.
Its rate is below \(.841\), while the selected action exceeds
\(.8562\). A separate contour argument keeps every index side and
every nonconstant cotangent mode; its negative real Hessian is positive
definite on the entire deformation rectangle. Thus the Gaussian
coefficient actually occurs in the full finite sum. The written proof
and an independent contour replay have been checked; a further root
replay at 384-bit precision reproduced all 16 side products.
This establishes a local building block for mixed powers, not a
whole-boundary theorem or an arbitrary mixed-word knot invariant.

The [full power-three theorem at the same reference](research_three_vertex_mixed_reference_packet.md)
now gives
\[
 V_{3,N}(x,y)=\kappa N^{-1/2}a_3(x,y)e^{N\Phi_3(x,y)}
                (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad a_3(x,y)\ne0,
 \quad \Phi_3=\Xi_3+i\gamma.
\]
The real constant \(\gamma\) is the original homogeneous calibration
constant, continued through an explicitly checked connected branch
domain. This theorem uses the full vertex without deleting its
endpoint corner. Its real-index complement has rate below \(.651\)
near the reference, whereas the selected action exceeds \(.6562\).
All 16 products of index contour sides and every Fourier alias have
strict gaps; an independent 384-bit replay reproduced their bounds.
Thus both original vertices have nonzero local coefficients at the
same geometric reference. This neighborhood cannot be silently
extended to the homogeneous power-three center, where the undeleted
corner has a larger rate than the geometric local contribution.

Two further results concern composition itself. The
[joint Hessian theorem](research_mixed_three_four_joint_coercivity.md)
places both unsummed vertex phases in one explicit chamber and proves
\(-\Re\mathcal F_n''\succ I\) there, for \(n=3,4\). Adding
these quadratic forms preserves the bound when boundary variables
are identified, without a loss depending on word length. Eliminating
the index variables by their critical equations also preserves a
positive bound, by a complex Schur-complement identity. The alternating
geometric reference is stationary for every alternating finite word
with its external Fourier boundaries fixed there, and for even cycles.
The theorem does not locate the critical point of an arbitrary word
or control the integral outside the chamber.

The [exact shared-boundary calculation](research_mixed_wire_exact_contraction.md)
goes further at the level of the finite sum: it performs each entire
Fourier integration algebraically. In a common boundary basis, the
contraction matrix has entries
\[
 \Gamma_{jk}=\frac{Q^{jk}(r;r)_{j+k}}
                  {(r;r)_j^2(r;r)_k^2}\quad(j+k<N),
 \qquad \Gamma_{jk}=0\quad(j+k\ge N),
 \quad Q=e^{2\pi i/N},\ r=Q^{-1}.
\]
The finite q-Vandermonde identity proves this at every level. It
expresses every fixed mixed word, including its original ordinary
boundary polynomials, as a finite contraction with no residual Fourier
integrals. Its interior coefficients have positive sine-product
magnitudes and a known quadratic phase. On a cycle the cross term is
\(\pi\sum_vj_v(i_{v+1}-i_v)/N\), with explicit additional diagonal
quadratic phases at the four-crossing vertices. Thus the suggested
Fourier viewpoint is an exact representation. The weights and finite
support still couple the indices; Plancherel alone does not give a
lower bound for the specified boundary value. Controlling that
oscillation remains the substantive mixed-word problem.

The [contracted-phase theorem](research_mixed_contracted_phase.md)
now gives the full interior symbol of this exact cyclic sum, including
its \(N^{-m}\) density, the order-one phase at four-crossing vertices,
and the absolute phase constant. Its negative real Hessian has a
bound independent of word length on a fixed central index chamber.
For alternating words the original geometric stationary point and
the logarithmic lifts are identified. These are local statements
about the original contracted phase; they do not discard the rest
of the finite sum. The [focused record](../repro/results/research-mixed-contracted-phase.json)
contains 36 exact identities, 11 outward comparisons, and two
connected-branch calibration cells.

The [complete-boundary calculation](research_mixed_complete_boundary_sum.md)
also expands the original open word, with every fixed ordinary
boundary derivative, into positive sine-product weights and an
explicit quadratic phase. It retains the endpoint index sums and
cancels the endpoint carrier phases exactly. The regular endpoint
critical equation and its selected complex root are proved, and
the full open phase has a strictly negative real Hessian in the
regular chamber. Its proposed Gaussian power \(N^{a+b-3/2}\) for
boundary derivatives of orders \(a,b\) remains conditional on a
valid deformation of the complete source. The
[exact checks](../repro/results/research-mixed-complete-boundary-sum.json)
cover 20 symbolic identities, 193 original finite normalizations,
and 29 signed boundary-jet positivity identities.

The [complete-boundary coefficient theorem](research_complete_boundary_coefficient_asymptotic.md)
now proves that the selected endpoint saddle contributes to its whole
original one-dimensional sum. Uniformly for physical \(e=j/N\) in
any compact subinterval of \((0,1/2)\), every fixed ordinary
boundary derivative has a nonzero asymptotic with power
\(N^{k-3/2}\). Exact factorial interpolation, both endpoint strips,
all vertical sides and both lattice aliases are retained, at both
level parities. This strengthens the earlier stationary-point result;
that theorem concerns physical outer indices. Its
[focused checks](../repro/results/research-complete-boundary-coefficient-asymptotic.json)
contain 13 exact identities and 72 original finite-product asymptotic
diagnostics. The uniform theorem follows from the contour proof.
It also gives adjacent-index transport for the actual boundary vector:
\(b_{j+1,N}=R(j/N)b_{j,N}(1+O(N^{-1}))\), with an explicit
algebraic multiplier \(R=XU/(X-U)\). This controls the stated
relative difference; it does not establish a common approximately
invariant vector for all interior operators or its closing overlap.

The [complex-index boundary theorem](research_complete_boundary_complex_index.md)
now supplies one specified holomorphic continuation of the full
boundary coefficient near \([1/5,9/20]\). Its fixed finite sum
retains every ordinary boundary derivative and both parities.
The additional rows vanish at physical indices; their off-grid
smallness is proved before deriving the uniform nonzero packet.
The exact finite generating equation keeps its original forcing,
including \(-4(1-Y^N)/N^3\) at even levels. The
[focused record](../repro/results/research-complete-boundary-complex-index.json)
contains nine exact identities, five positive scalar margins,
148 grid/operator checks and 54 complex asymptotic diagnostics.

The [full interior-index extension](research_complete_boundary_full_index_interval.md)
now proves both the physical coefficient asymptotic and that same
canonical continuation for every compact interval \(I\subset(0,1)\).
Above \(e=1/2\), an exact derivative-ratio calculation gives one
nondegenerate horizontal maximum without assuming global concavity.
Both vertical currents and aliases retain strict gaps; convexity
of \(J\) controls every additional physical row above the midpoint,
and revived rows have rate at most zero. The nonzero coefficient,
power \(N^{k-3/2}\), both parities and all fixed ordinary jets are
unchanged. The [focused record](../repro/results/research-complete-boundary-full-index-interval.json)
contains 13 symbolic identities, seven critical-lift diagnostics
and 120 original finite-sum comparisons; a fresh 180-digit replay
also passed. The same canonical source now has a nonzero packet jointly in the
outer index and the ordinary boundary color near complete color
\(-2\), with all fixed derivatives. The neighborhood is fixed but
its size is not quantified to cover an arbitrary complex first-cap
critical point. The new ordinary-color statement passed written and
code review and an independent 180-digit replay, including 36 complex
color diagnostics; those diagnostics supplement the uniform contour
proof rather than replace it.

The [first-cap critical theorem](research_mixed_first_cap_critical.md)
now locates the original zero-logarithm-lift saddle of both vertex
types for every real outgoing index in \([.2,.45]\). The complete
outward covers have 52 type-three and 64 type-four intervals; a fresh
384-bit replay passed. A positive two-variable Hessian proves uniqueness
on the full regular chamber and gives a coherent local contour.
There is also a precise warning about a proposed outer cutoff: at type
three and outgoing index \(.2\), the already-resummed phase at the
physical outer index \(s=1/2\) exceeds the selected cap action by more
than \(.011\). That wall must be retained in a source deformation or
controlled by cancellation. This earlier result is a critical-point
and local contour theorem. The subsequent
[whole type-three cap proof](research_mixed_three_first_cap_packet.md)
retains that wall: it sums the original outer index exactly by a
terminating quantum-binomial identity before estimating the remaining
index. Its coefficient is nonzero, with level power \(N^{k-1}\) for
the \(k\)-th ordinary boundary derivative, and the conclusion holds
jointly near complete ordinary color. Type four is not covered by
that cap theorem.

Away from the physical outgoing grid, the original cap polynomial is
the remainder of \(N d_N K_N\) modulo \(X^N-1\), where \(K_N\) is
the fixed replacement polynomial defined in the
[Fourier reduction](research_mixed_three_first_cap_fourier_reduction.md).
For a following Laurent factor with exponents in \([-N+1,0]\),
the full circle integral of that remainder is exactly the integral
of \(N d_N K_N(1+X^{-N})\). This is an identity at every level and
radius, retaining all ordinary boundary derivatives. The
replacement \(K_N\) has its own proved complex asymptotic; equality
on the root grid is not used to infer an off-grid asymptotic for
the unreduced product.


There is now a [global real-entropy theorem](research_mixed_real_index_entropy.md)
for every cyclic three/four word. The unique absolute-rate maximizer
has every leg in \((.26,.39)\), and the complement of

\[
                         [1/4,2/5]^{2m}
\]

loses more than \(10^{-4}\) relative to that real maximum, uniformly

power of \(N\). The [checker](../repro/results/research-mixed-real-index-entropy.json)
verifies 13 exact identities and seven outward inequalities. This
is an absolute-sum theorem, not a lower bound for its oscillatory
counterpart.

The distinction is necessary: an
[explicit all-length obstruction](research_mixed_absolute_complement_obstruction.md)
shows that, for every alternating cycle with \(k\ge2\) pairs, a

already has exponential rate greater than \(k\sigma+1/80\), where
\(\sigma\) is the selected geometric action per pair. Its
[22 outward comparisons](../repro/results/research-mixed-absolute-complement-obstruction.json)
certify one rational configuration and a bound valid for every
such length. Thus the real-entropy complement gap cannot be used
as a geometric-rate complement bound. The signed sum still requires
cancellation or a legal deformation retaining its phase; this
obstruction makes no claim against the desired mixed-word asymptotic.

There is now an exact way to preserve cancellation while summing one
whole index family. The
[conditional-leg identity](research_mixed_conditional_leg_sum.md)
replaces a three-vertex conditional by a polynomial coefficient,
\(L_0(a,b)=N[z^a](rz;r)_a(rz;r)_b\), with no root-of-unity alias.
It also gives a positive Hermitian Gram interpretation of that

retain both parities and the original cyclic matrix products.

The [full-circle conditional theorem](research_mixed_three_conditional_circle.md)
then proves a nonzero asymptotic for that entire three-vertex sum,
uniformly when \(a/N,b/N\in[1/5,9/20]\). A paired-factor
inequality puts the unique global Cauchy-circle saddle on a fixed
short arc and controls its entire complement. Thus every original
conditional endpoint is already included, even when a neighbor is
\(.24\), the value in the absolute-complement obstruction. The

check its universal inequalities and normalization. This is a theorem
for physical integer neighbors.

Its [complex-neighbor extension](research_mixed_three_conditional_complex_neighbors.md)
constructs a fixed lifted contour near each real neighbor pair.
The exact Gamma-factorial interpolation agrees with the full
physical coefficient, and its entire far arc and both connecting

packet with uniform neighbor-derivative estimates. A finite family
of patches covers the real square. These patchwise continuations

include 12 exact identities, 120 Barnes-interpolation diagnostics

The [full four-vertex conditional theorem](research_mixed_four_conditional_packet.md)
also controls its entire physical sum for
\(a/N,b/N\in[1/5,9/20]\). It proves a unique zero of the

There is then a [canonical complex-neighbor continuation](research_mixed_four_conditional_complex_neighbors.md)
of the four-vertex conditional, defined by a single fixed \(N\)-term

Its [record](../repro/results/research-mixed-four-conditional-complex-neighbors.json)

There is now also a separate
[canonical three-vertex theorem](research_mixed_three_canonical_conditional.md).

The [universal localization theorem](research_mixed_cyclic_critical_localization.md)

The [sharper critical-domain theorem](research_mixed_cyclic_critical_height_bounds.md)
now bounds every type-three leg by the disk
\(|z-(.35-.01i)|<.083\), with \(-.065<\Im z<.068\), and every

                 .27<\Re z<.33,\qquad -.057<\Im z<-.001.
\]
The first image estimate passed 6,994 two-angle cells. The stronger

The [broad-image obstruction](research_mixed_conditional_image_contours.md)
retains an actual last row of the canonical type-three conditional

the exact last-row identity and the rate inequality with ten exact

passed. This rules out the proposed termwise bound on that whole
auxiliary domain. It neither proves cancellation fails in the sum nor
places this example at a cyclic critical point. The new critical
bounds exclude both offending inputs. The full packets on the smaller required domains are now proved
below. Control of the remaining outer aliases is still separate.

The [critical-image packet theorem](research_mixed_conditional_critical_images.md)
now proves the complete canonical conditional asymptotic at every cyclic
mixed critical configuration. Its parameters retain their correlation:
for the original two-leg root \((s(a,b),t(a,b))\), the conditional
arguments are \((a,t(a,b))\), or the opposite orientation. The external
domains are the sharper type-three disk and type-four rectangle above.
The proof keeps the entire fixed finite sum, including revived endpoint
rows, both cotangent aliases and all connecting sides. Its Gaussian
coefficient is holomorphic and nonzero, with power
\(N^{(1-\epsilon)/2}\) for type \(3+\epsilon\), at both parities.
The author and independent 320-bit replay cover all 42 boundary pieces
and 4,838 affine root cells in both orientations. The replay checks
58,056 endpoint inequalities and 154,816 horizontal alias inequalities.
Only after the global branch and coefficient are established does a
maximum-modulus argument extend the normalized expansion across each
full parameter product. This closes the conditional source-domain gap.
It does not estimate the remaining outer torus, the conditional kernels
at reflected outer parameters, or a complete mixed-word observation.

An [exact torus-composition identity](research_mixed_conditional_torus_composition.md)
also replaces the remaining cyclic root sums by global
Laurent-polynomial integrals on arbitrary nonzero circle radii.
The original diagonal gauges cancel exactly. There is no outer
alias at a three-weighted variable and exactly one explicit wrapped
alias at a four-weighted variable. Its matrix is strictly upper
triangular of rank \(N-1\); it is not a rank-one error.
The [1,852 exact checks](../repro/results/research-mixed-conditional-torus-composition.json)
include original cyclic matrix words, all relevant Fourier bands,
the forced interpolation identity and full constant-term scalars.
The same theorem now includes the whole original ordinary boundary
polynomials of open words: exact endpoint factors replace the two
cyclic end factors, and the Fourier bands retain precisely the same

with literal original words at derivative orders \(0,1,2\) at both
ends; the proof retains every derivative order and arbitrary complex
boundary colors. No asymptotic for the new endpoint polynomials is inferred.

The [Fourier-weight theorem](research_mixed_fourier_weight_continuation.md)
then proves that the exact interpolating weight \(d_N(e^{-2\pi iz})\)
equals the reciprocal Gamma-factorial with relative error
\(O(e^{-N/200})\) on the whole rectangle containing the type-four
critical disks. Its residue proof retains both midpoint sides,
both horizontal sides and the original forcing. The

checks nine symbolic identities, 50 exact finite identities and

or knot-volume theorem is asserted.

The [reflected-alias budget](research_mixed_alias_reflection_budget.md)
uses the sharper type-four depths to lower every nonempty wrapped alias

past its proved domain. The exact local factorial density loses at least

The [coherent endpoint deletion theorem](research_mixed_coherent_endpoint_deletion.md)
controls the highest conditional rows as one original operator block.
For types three and four, its final row has exactly norm \(\sqrt N\),
and a block of \(\lfloor\eta N\rfloor+1\) rows has rate at most
\(\eta\log(2e/\eta)\), which tends to zero with \(\eta\).
The proof keeps the original repeated-root normal directions and the
ordered product telescope. Its checker passed 1,397 exact source

A bound for a whole observed word still needs its surrounding factors.

The [arbitrary-twist extension](research_arbitrary_twist_conditional_endpoints.md)
proves the analogous vanishing-rate block bound uniformly in every signed
crossing power, even if the power depends on the level. It uses the exact

binomial majorant; it does not identify this multiplication matrix with

Its 6,897 exact identities and three symbolic checks retain that factor.
Neither the small operator rate nor this observation identity alone
bounds a complete mixed word or identifies its geometric volume.

There is an [all-level restriction on a possible operator proof](research_mixed_three_four_operator_obstruction.md).
No single positive inner product, even allowing separate scalar
normalizations, makes both vertex operators positive Hermitian.
Their relative insertion is similar to the original crossing matrix;
three of its eigenvalues already prevent accretivity at levels at
least seven, and the original first-normal Jordan block prevents a
unit-normalized contraction at every level. These statements rule
out those exact changes of metric. They do not rule out approximate
invariant vectors or estimates for a particular coherent boundary
observation; such estimates would still have to control that

The source proof now extends from paths to **branching circle trees**.
For every filled vertex let \(d_v\) count its original incident edges,
including edges to unfilled vertices. The
[branching theorem](research_degree_controlled_network_source.md)
requires
\[
                    |n_v|\ge\max\{8,4d_v\}
\]
at every filled vertex. Its proof uses a contraction estimate for the
coupled period equations, a componentwise bound for changes in the
critical action, and estimates for every remaining term of the exact
finite trace. The bounds depend on the local degrees, without a loss
that grows with the length of a path or the number of branches.
For the original marked circle-tree construction, filling all auxiliary
vertices and passing the literal knot-component test gives Kashaev's
volume identity along all integer levels. Arbitrary abstract graph
sums are not assigned a knot interpretation.

A different
[degree-and-power criterion](research_network_degree_power_source.md)
proves the full source expansion when
\[
                       n_v^2+d_v^2\ge4096
\]
at every selected vertex. This permits arbitrary fixed powers, including
zero, at adjacent vertices of degree at least 64. The proof places the
entire partial-charge family in \(|t_v|<1/10\); a degree-weighted
Taylor estimate then controls all vertical parts of the trace, including
those at zero power. This removes the earlier requirement that the
selected high-degree vertices be nonadjacent. The two criteria are
separate sufficient hypotheses on the selected graph; no theorem here
allows choosing between them independently at different vertices.

A separate mixed theorem now permits a vertex-by-vertex choice between
\(|n_v|\ge\max(8,4d_v)\) and \(n_v^2+d_v^2\ge512^2\).
This allows a sufficiently high-degree short vertex beside moderate
long powers at its neighbors. Its larger second threshold is essential
to the proof as written; the homogeneous threshold 64 has not been
proved for this mixed situation.

The [whole-boundary theorem](research_network_whole_boundary_decay.md)
now gives all these sources exponential decay away from their complete
outside colors over the entire real period, together with a quadratic
bound in a fixed complex strip. This supplies the boundary estimates
needed for later composition, at the positive-seven and signed-eight
path thresholds as well as in the two graph regimes. The literal
outside polynomial degrees and all first normal derivatives are kept.

Consequently the new
[componentwise partial-filling theorem](research_componentwise_short_filling_stability.md)
allows any collection of disjoint connected selected components, each

boundary vertex. The theorem preserves the original parameters and
proves the original Kashaev volume identity, with a nonzero leading
coefficient. In particular, arbitrary fixed powers at connected
components of original degree at least 64 are now allowed regardless
of component size. The earlier sufficient degree bound proportional
to the number of selected vertices is unnecessary in this range.

Their scalar and matrix comparisons can be replayed together with
`python3 repro/run_research_checks.py network-source-constants`.
They do not settle arbitrary low-degree short components, so the
finite-exception conclusion remains open.

The short-path analysis now has a direct Fourier result with a
nonzero coefficient. For a three-crossing vertex, the original
transformed finite sum has a large endpoint corner which prevents
the desired local geometric approximation. Sections 7--10 of
[the traced-vertex proof](research_traced_three_vertex_endpoint.md)
remove that entire corner and bound the resulting change **after
the original complete-ended chain has been contracted**. Its
exponential rate is below the geometric rate by more than \(1/15\),
for every fixed homogeneous three-crossing chain.

The retained vertex has a nonzero holomorphic asymptotic on a fixed
complex neighborhood of the homogeneous wire point. This uses an
[exact interpolation of the denominator products](research_root_pochhammer_interpolation.md),
the original sine-factorial interpolation, and estimates on every
side and alias of the local lattice contour. The
[exact action calculation](research_homogeneous_three_action_calibration.md)
evaluates the original eight tetrahedron volumes as four regular
ideal-tetrahedron volumes. It fixes the absolute geometric action,
rather than matching it numerically.

There is also an answer to the almost-invariance question at this
local level. Normalize the actual retained coefficient array in
\(\ell^2\), and let \(T_1,T_2\) shift its two indices by one. Its
translation residuals are \(O(N^{-1/2})\), while its unitary
two-dimensional Fourier transform satisfies
\[
 |\widehat f_N(0,0)|
       =\left(\frac{24}{7}\right)^{1/4}N^{-1/2}
                       (1+O(N^{-1})).
\]
The exact finite-product ratios prove the almost-invariance;
the complex Gaussian integral separately proves the nonzero
coefficient. Almost-invariance alone would not imply that lower
bound. These are the transformed indices of one retained vertex,
not an assumed invariant vector for the crossing operator.

The [local composition theorem](research_three_vertex_local_composition.md)
now composes these packets for any fixed chain or cycle. In a
cycle, its coefficient is exactly the independently known full
spectral coefficient
\(\rho^{m/2}/(1-\rho^m)\), where
\(\rho=(5-\sqrt{21})/2\). The
[global modulus theorem](research_three_vertex_global_wire_bound.md)
now gives a stronger conclusion: the absolute summand entropy on
the entire retained index triangle and Fourier torus has a unique
maximum at the homogeneous point. Every fixed complementary wire
region therefore has a strict exponential gap. This proves the
full-period retained kernel asymptotic with homogeneous Fourier
endpoints, and an absolute complementary estimate for cycles.
It does not identify a cyclic network with a knot or substitute
Fourier endpoints for actual complete outside colors.
Small changes of the two contour heights preserve a complementary
gap, but the modulus envelope then exceeds the optimized real part
of the actual critical action by a positive quadratic term. The
unequal-radius proposition computes that term explicitly. It must
be included when comparing the full sum with a displaced cap
contribution.
The [interior localization theorem](research_three_path_interior_localization.md)
puts every sufficiently deep geometric edge of an actual
homogeneous three-crossing path inside any prescribed neighborhood
of the homogeneous point, uniformly in path length. Its stronger
boundary-decay estimate now gives
\[
 |t_v-t_*|\le C q^{\min(v,m+1-v)},\qquad 0<q<1,
\]
where \(m\) is the number of vertices and the constants do not
depend on \(m\). The proof uses strict convexity of the original
geometric energy and a direct estimate for the inverse of its
block tridiagonal Hessian. Thus the geometric effect of the two
ends decreases exponentially with distance from them.

An [explicit contraction theorem](research_homogeneous_three_geometric_contraction.md)
now gives numerical constants independent of chain length. Solving
one original vertex equation while holding its neighbors fixed
preserves the rectangle
\[
 1.3\le\Re t\le1.82,\qquad .82\le-\Im t\le1.21.
\]
The simultaneous update contracts the maximum of the real and
imaginary coordinate errors by \(5/8\). Its fixed point is the
original positive geometry. A discrete comparison then gives
\[
 |t_v-t_*|_\square\le
 \left(\frac{8-\sqrt{39}}5\right)^{\min(v,m+1-v)-1}.
\]
Here \(|z|_\square=\max(|\Re z|,|\Im z|)\). This also gives a
certified finite-iteration approximation to every chain, without
inferring a general statement from samples of path lengths.

The [complete-ended one-vertex theorem](research_homogeneous_wire_complete_cap.md)
now supplies a genuine quantum boundary input. Near the homogeneous
internal Fourier coordinate, with the original complete outside
color, its full finite sum has a nonzero leading term
\[
 W_N(x,u)=C_{N,3}N^{-1}A(x,u)e^{NS(x,u)}
                (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad A(x,u)\ne0.
\]
This includes both level parities, the original repeated-node
derivatives, and bounds on the discarded physical rows and contour
ends. The derivative \(S_x\) at the homogeneous coordinate is
nonzero. The actual boundary therefore changes the stationary point;
it cannot be replaced by a fixed homogeneous endpoint. The cap and
the [retained vertex](research_three_vertex_directed_packet.md)
now have proved uniform asymptotics on the same explicit complex
parameter region. The [first attachment](research_three_cap_first_attachment.md)
certifies their coupled stationary point there and gives a nonzero
Gaussian coefficient for the restricted integral through that point.
The outgoing phase derivative is smaller. The phase and source
induction results described below now specify a repeatable class,
but placing the actual end source in that class remains necessary.
The [exterior-cap estimates](research_three_cap_wire_complement.md)
now control the exterior wire intervals and both vertical segments
used in moving the first attachment contour to its critical height.
For the vertical segments, the cap rate is at most \(1.2638\),
and the retained-vertex rate is less than \(0.6474\). Their sum
is below \(1.9112\), whereas the certified critical action is
greater than \(1.9113\). These bounds concern the original finite
functions, with both parities and their outside derivatives.
The [central-source theorem](research_three_cap_central_source.md)
now completes this first attachment. It bounds the discarded angular
pieces, the real summation indices outside the central square, every
vertical index contour and every nonconstant cotangent contribution.
The remaining joint integral has exactly one geometric critical point
and a nonzero Gaussian coefficient. Hence the whole original wire
period has the asymptotic previously proved only for its small central

This conclusion also holds after restoring the deleted corner of the
vertex. The [Fourier-boundary error estimate](research_three_chain_fourier_corner_transfer.md)
uses the exact transformed cardinal vector on the entire horizontal
Fourier period. For the first attachment its error rate is below

proved output is the original finite function
\(v(w)^TA^2h(y)\), with a nonzero holomorphic asymptotic near
the outgoing Fourier coordinate \(y=x_*\), and with every fixed
ordinary derivative at the complete outside color \(w=-2\).
The same error argument applies to arbitrary fixed words of retained
vertices. Separate results below now provide whole-period bounds
and one further full attachment. The corner-error estimate alone
does not justify iterating a local asymptotic along an arbitrary chain.

There is now an explicit domain for the retained kernel needed in
that iteration. The [bidisk source theorem](research_three_vertex_bidisk_packet.md)
proves its nonzero asymptotic for both Fourier variables within

larger exact corner \(\lfloor N/40\rfloor\). The source error
from that deletion remains more than \(1/20\) below the complete

The [phase-transform theorem](research_three_phase_graph_transform.md)
also gives a class of holomorphic phases on this disk that is

action constants. The
[quantified first-attachment theorem](research_three_prepared_cap_quantified_source.md)
now proves the original prepared source's nonzero asymptotic uniformly

the restored corner. The proof estimates the entire original input
period, then moves all four central integration heights together.
Concavity on the horizontal rectangles and convexity along this
joint height change control every connecting face. The square
containing the disk is used to over-cover the errors; the asserted

The estimates needed for an induction are now available. The
[global real-period bound](research_three_vertex_capped_gaussian_bound.md)
gives a quadratic loss in the distance of each real Fourier variable
from the selected point, with the distance capped at \(1/100\).
The [joint height bound](research_three_vertex_weighted_height_bound.md)
also allows the output height to move. Its exponent is
\[
 2c+13(\Im w)^2-\frac32
       \min\{\operatorname{dist}(t,\mathbb Z),1/100\}^2,
 \qquad x=x_h+t,\quad y=x_h+w.
\]
This is a single global bound on the original absolute summands;
it is not obtained by adding unrelated real and imaginary estimates.
Its proof reduces the global maximization to a strictly concave
three-variable problem and certifies the critical branch over the
entire height interval. A separate source theorem extends the
[retained input rectangle](research_three_vertex_input_rectangle.md)
to real width \(1/100\), while preserving imaginary width

Together these give a
[source induction theorem](research_three_source_tail_propagation.md)

original-source packet on the \(1/200\) disk, and the full-period
envelope
\[
 |F_N(x_h+t)|\le C N^b
 \exp N\left\{\Re S(x_h)+|k_0|H v(t)-\frac{29}{20}v(t)^2\right\},
 \qquad v(t)=\min\{\operatorname{dist}(t,\mathbb Z),1/100\}.
\]
Every further retained attachment preserves these conditions and
the nonzero coefficient. The proof estimates both real annuli,
the remaining real period, and every join of the central contour.
It then establishes the required real-period envelope for the
outgoing source, so it can actually be repeated.

There is now a [whole-period bound for the first prepared source](research_three_prepared_cap_period_bound.md).
Two global supporting planes, applied to strictly concave functions,
bound the full outgoing real period by a polynomial times
\(e^{1.91164N}\). They retain the two contour joins and the
original corner error. Together with the proved disk packet this

with \(H=.03\), including the whole annulus between \(.005\)
and \(.01\). This is an actual finite-source bound; its gradient
is still too large for the induction theorem.

The [first additional attachment](research_three_first_entrance_source.md)
is now proved for the full original source. Its exact Fourier
integral gives \(v(w)^TA_N^2\widetilde A_Nh(y)\), and the
separate corner estimate restores \(v(w)^TA_N^3h(y)\) without
changing the nonzero leading coefficient. The asymptotic is uniform

The proof controls the incoming real annuli using the wider actual

The [real extension](research_three_first_entrance_real_extension.md)
now enlarges that packet to the real interval of radius \(.009\).
It uses the original retained kernel on a larger domain, certified
critical-input contours, and separate bounds for the principal
incoming term and its absolute error. A sharper calculation at the
actual central critical point improves the gradient to
\(|h_2(0)|<.0057\), while \(|h_2'|<.18\) on the disk and
the larger real interval. Writing \(M_2=\Re S_2(x_h)\), the
full-period bound is now
\[
 |F_{2,N}(x_h+t,-2)|\le CN^b
 \exp N\left\{M_2+|k_0|(.0057)v(t)-\frac{29}{20}v(t)^2\right\},
 \qquad v(t)=\min\{\operatorname{dist}(t,\mathbb Z),.03\}.
\]
The intermediate estimate retains positive slack below \(.000077\);
the proof explicitly pays for it when deriving this stronger bound.
The gradient is above the old induction threshold \(1/2500\), but
the [full larger-source theorem](research_three_larger_source_propagation.md)
now preserves both the asymptotic on this union and the estimates on
the complementary periods. Two attachments bring the actual source
into the older, smaller-gradient class. This proves the required

The new original-source and phase certificates are grouped in
`python3 repro/run_research_checks.py three-source-entrance`.
Their individual checks and separate replays have passed; the runner
also validates the listed paths and their order.

Once two actual end sources have entered this class, their
[full-period closure](research_three_small_source_closure.md)
has a nonzero leading coefficient as well. Its proof keeps the

The entrance and induction arguments now give this construction for
every fixed length at least ten. The stronger
[larger-domain closure](research_three_larger_source_closure.md)
works before the two extra attachments at each end and lowers the
