now extends the prepared source to a directed complex rectangle.
It proves the needed nonzero expansion on the actual closing contour,
using a lower bound for its phase before converting the absolute
complement estimates to relative errors. The full original period and
ordinary outside boundaries are controlled, giving length four as well.

The [three-vertex proof](research_three_chain_three_closure.md)
uses the two original end factors and the middle vertex in one
six-variable integral. An exact full-period identity removes the
exterior wire intervals before absolute values are taken. A concavity
argument bounds the entire real-index complement. The remaining
integral is moved simultaneously to the geometric critical heights,
with every connecting face retained. Its leading coefficient is
nonzero, all omitted terms have strictly smaller rates, and the

gives estimates over all real outside colors, using the uniform
physical-row bound for each end factor. This supplies length three

The [all-length chamber theorem](research_three_chain_geometric_chamber.md)
now treats every chain of at least three power-three vertices with
the actual complete outside conditions. The geometric contraction
reduces its proof to finitely many certified reference paths and a

selected summation variables lie in explicit fixed rectangles; both
ends lie in the domain of the proved cap asymptotic. The theorem
then identifies these geometric points with the critical points of
the original quantum phase. This identification keeps the selected
algebraic roots and the logarithms themselves, not only their
exponentials.

Keeping the summation variables instead of first eliminating them
gives a particularly useful estimate. Write \(\mathcal G_m\) for
the combined phase of a chain with \(m\) vertices, \(z_c\) for
its geometric critical point, and \(z\) for the vector of all
integration variables. On the specified central product of real
intervals, with imaginary parts fixed at those of \(z_c\),
\[
 \Re\mathcal G_m(z)\le
 \Re\mathcal G_m(z_c)-\frac{|z-z_c|^2}{40\pi}.
\]
The constant is independent of chain length. The proof sums the
[positive quadratic forms of the local Hessians](research_three_vertex_joint_concavity.md).
It establishes a unique central maximum and a nonzero leading
coefficient for a small integral through it, for every fixed length.
This local argument alone does not prove that the original finite
sum has that leading term. The full propagation and closing arguments
now supply the complementary-contour estimates for lengths at least
six; the direct three-, four- and five-vertex proofs supply the remaining
three lengths.

The [absolute action calibration](research_three_chain_action_volume_calibration.md)
now supplies the geometric normalization for every such chain. It
places all the selected algebraic index solutions in one connected
holomorphic chart. On that chart, the retained critical phase differs
from the original angular phase by one purely imaginary constant;
the exact homogeneous calculation fixes its real part. Summing the
original incidence phases, with the two complete end conditions,
therefore gives
\[
 2\pi\Re\mathcal S_m=\operatorname{Vol}(M_m),\qquad m\ge3.
\]
Here \(M_m\) is the original marked partial filling with both outside
ends complete. The volume constant is no longer an unresolved step
for this family. Combining it with the full propagation and closing
proofs gives the complete-boundary finite-sum volume limit for every
fixed \(m\ge3\).

There is separate global preparation in the
[internal-projection theorem](research_homogeneous_chain_internal_projection.md).
It removes endpoint ranges of the intermediate matrix indices after

then has a small factor on both sides. The resulting full-source

There is also a new

for positive paths whose selected powers are at least three.
Keeping the actual unit-disk and phase restrictions on neighboring
cosines gives an activation cost less than
\(5811/5000<M_\infty-1/1000\), independently of path length.
The analytic reduction leaves two explicit boundary arcs; outward
interval certificates and a separate replay cover their full

That general open-chain theorem remains open; the homogeneous
power-three result for lengths at least three is the narrower theorem

A separate [alternating-observation estimate](research_radical_observation_boundary_decay.md)
gives a strict exponential loss for every original radical
insertion, and for the neighboring midpoint cutoff insertion,

and quadratic complex-strip bound. It uses the original alternating

For arbitrary fixed signed paths with \(|n_v|\ge2\), the
[charge-interval theorem](research_charged_corridor_wide_contour.md)
also gives a nonzero full finite-source asymptotic on
\(\epsilon\le\chi_v\le1/10\); powers of magnitude at least three

are included. Here \(\chi\) is the explicitly defined analytic

The full finite-source argument now applies to **arbitrarily long
fixed paths with every signed crossing power of magnitude at least
eight**, without a long separator between selected vertices.
The [path source theorem](research_uniform_path_trace_assembly.md)
retains the original powers \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\), every original
trace derivative, and both quantum-level parities. When all
auxiliary vertices are filled and the original component tests
give a knot \(K\), it proves
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|\langle K\rangle_N|
                  =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K),
                  \qquad |n_v|\ge8 .
\]
The signs and magnitudes can vary independently. The path and
its powers are fixed before the level tends to infinity.
This is a theorem for the original ordered circle-tree path
construction, not for every Conway composition. Positive powers
at least seven are also covered at the source level when the
stipulated complete outside endpoint is retained; that existence
hypothesis has not been removed to assert an all-selected
power-seven knot theorem.

The argument controls the entire sum. The critical point supplies
a nonzero Gaussian term. Endpoint currents have a strict gap,
and complementary physical rows lose more at their incident
edges than the change in critical action caused by setting
their charges to zero. These are local comparisons, so the
proof does not accumulate an uncontrolled error with path
length. The detailed new inputs are described below.

This still leaves the finite-exception goal open. For example,
fixing one untreated power of magnitude below eight leaves
infinitely many choices for the others. Arbitrary short groups,
their degenerations, and the broader template class remain
outside the path theorem.

There is now a full two-boundary source theorem for **every fixed
integer pair \(n,p\ge7\)** and its mirror. The powers are fixed
crossing data; the quantum level \(N\) tends to infinity.
[Theorems 6–7 of the pair proof](research_internal_pair_combined_contour_reduction.md#7-the-full-source-for-every-fixed-pair-of-powers-at-least-seven)
give
\[
 \mathcal P_{n,p,N}(u,v)
 =C_{N,n}C_{N,p}N^{-3/2}\mathcal A(u,v)
           e^{N\mathcal S(u,v)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad \mathcal A(u,v)\ne0.
\]
This is the original finite source, with both level parities,
all original trace normals, and uniform ordinary boundary derivatives
on a fixed neighborhood of the complete colors. At completeness,
\(2\pi\Re\mathcal S(0,0)\) is the volume of the original marked
partial filling. The theorem also gives decay across the whole real
outside period and a quadratic bound in a fixed complex strip.

The proof closes the cancellation problem for this family of blocks.
It combines the local Gaussian with a complete estimate of the
remaining source. In the connecting angular regions the two trace
heights move together; convexity controls that common deformation.
The contour homotopy fixes its boundary and retains the exact
two-form, so no independent mixed-height corner or endpoint term is
discarded. Both wire sides, both vertical wire segments, the
discarded indices, and the grouped angular endpoints have strict
exponential gaps.

Two uniform comparisons make this possible. The
[geometric proof](research_real_pair_geometry_and_tail_gap.md#7-a-global-comparison-for-real-trace-angles)
gives \(2\pi\Im x_*<2/15\) and \(\mathcal M(n,p)>163/50\).
It also bounds every real mixed reflected region at that wire
height by \(391/120\), leaving a gap of \(1/600\).
The action lower bound uses monotonicity and a rigorous interval
certificate for the original \((7,7)\) period equations; it is
not inferred from a sampled numerical solution. The other gaps
come from written convexity, reflection, and finite-source bounds.

The [uniform composition theorem](research_internal_pair_three_kernel_compositions.md#8-one-separator-threshold-for-all-positive-pairs-of-powers-at-least-seven)
now supplies one separator and closing threshold for **all**
ordered pairs \(n,p\ge7\), their mirrors, and the previously
established \((3,3)\) blocks. The threshold is independent of
the pair powers and of the number and order of insertions.
The proof first establishes uniform estimates for isolated
vertices as their powers grow, then proves the corresponding
uniform gluing lemma with both outside variables retained.
Two large-power ranges and a finite remaining square cover
the entire pair family. Each resulting word and all its powers
remain fixed before the quantum level tends to infinity;
amplitudes and starting levels need not be uniform in that word.

There is also a proved family with a zero separator. The exact
marked simplification
\((n,p,0,r,s)\mapsto(n,p+r,s)\) retains a physical half-turn.
The [zero-join corollary](research_internal_pair_three_kernel_compositions.md#9-what-an-exact-zero-power-join-does)
controls these blocks when the positive outer powers are at
least seven and the merged power exceeds one common threshold.
No estimate putting that threshold below fourteen has been proved.
Neither result permits every adjacent short word or turns
infinite fibers of original filling assignments into a finite
exceptional set.

The next source estimates concern connected paths rather than
separated pairs. The
[path geometry and action bounds](research_unsummed_network_phase_coercivity.md#6-a-common-central-domain-for-positive-paths-of-power-at-least-seven)
put every critical angle in \(|\Re t|<19/20\),
\(|\Im t|<3/10\) for the established positive charge family
with powers at least seven. Removing a charge increases the
stationary action by less than \(1/10\) per incident edge.
The [full-edge complementary-angle estimate](research_path_mixed_trace_currents.md#8-a-stronger-centered-loss-for-a-removed-incidence)
now supplies a larger loss, \(21/200\), at each removed
endpoint whose real angle has magnitude at least \(\pi/2\).
Its other endpoint may range over the entire complex rectangle
\(|\Re t|\le\pi/2,\ |\Im t|\le3/10\).
It retains every original index and ordinary derivative.
If both endpoints are removed, it retains both losses.
Thus this local comparison has a reserve exceeding \(1/200\)
per affected incidence, independently of path length.

The [mixed-current comparison](research_path_mixed_trace_currents.md#9-vertical-current-monotonicity-at-powers-of-at-least-seven)
controls every subset of endpoint currents at the level of
the original phase on that wider rectangle. Theorem 3 of the
[full edge-kernel proof](research_bare_kernel_thin_rectangle.md)
now establishes the corresponding nonzero expansion for the
**actual finite kernel** throughout
\(|\Re t|,|\Re u|\le\pi/2\),
\(|\Im t|,|\Im u|\le3/10\).
It treats all omitted Newton indices and separates the constant
and nonconstant terms of the exact cotangent contour.
Three fixed wire intervals cover the parameter box. Their
right-endpoint gaps are proved by
[a rigorous interval certificate](research_bare_kernel_wide_endpoint_gaps.md):
separate harmonicity reduces the full parameter regions to
48 boundary faces, and outward mean-value bounds verify
1,240 closed cells covering those faces. The remaining
contour comparisons are analytic inequalities.
This supplies the missing finite-sum estimate in the path
assembly and proves the two scopes stated at the beginning
of this record.

The scalar comparisons for these developments can be replayed with
\(\texttt{python3 repro/run\_research\_checks.py path-source-constants}\).
The seven checks save their exact or outward interval margins and
dependency hashes. The uniform source, contour and marked
composition arguments remain written proofs.

The Fourier approach now also has an
[explicit positive inner product](research_fourier_lower_bounds_and_almost_invariance.md#18-the-canonical-positive-form-in-full-physical-coordinates)
on the full space of physical values and first derivatives.
In these coordinates the original closing is
\(\langle\overline y_n,y_p\rangle_G\), whereas the positive norm
is \(\langle y_n,y_n\rangle_G\).
The distinction matters: a proved family has an exponentially small
ratio between the required closing and the norm. A change of
coordinates that preserves the original pairing leaves that ratio
unchanged. Thus positivity supplies norm bounds, but a lower bound
for the desired overlap still needs a separate argument.

For homogeneous three-crossing chains, the
[original spectral formulation](research_positive_three_crossing_cycle.md#8-reciprocal-weights-and-an-upper-bound-for-the-whole-open-source)
now retains the actual boundary weights and their reciprocal relation
at odd levels. A separate estimate, valid at both parities, bounds the
entire two-boundary polynomial and its ordinary derivatives with rate
\((2m+1)c+M_\infty\) for a fixed chain of length \(m\).
It uses the physical crossing eigenfunctional with its first-normal
identity to remove one costly inverse-crossing norm. Here
\(c=2\int_0^{5/6}\log(2\sin\pi x)\,dx\) and
\(M_\infty=4G/\pi\), with \(G\) Catalan's constant.
This is a bound on the actual source, but its rate is not proved sharp.
The boundary weights have different phases even on the part of the
spectrum above one. Neither a positive spectral measure nor the
nonzero geometric leading coefficient follows from this calculation.

Two further checks delimit possible estimates. Exact discrete
summation by parts in the
[support-restriction note](research_pair_regular_support_cells.md#8-an-exact-kernel-antiderivative-and-its-amplification)
retains a boundary term that cannot be bounded by treating the
restricted sum as the full sum. The
[holomorphic comparison](research_physical_normal_defect_packet.md)
also shows why one proposed constant bound on a complex ellipse
cannot yield the needed exponential gap: enlarging that ellipse
reaches a region where the actual function exceeds the proposed
bound. Neither observation is a counterexample to the volume
conjecture. They identify estimates that cannot justify the
remaining step.

There is now a nonzero starting family for continuation in the Fourier
charges. The [small-charge source theorem](research_small_charge_path_source.md)
inserts the specified Chebyshev polynomial
\(T_{N-j_v}(-w_v/2)\) in each original trace. For every fixed positive
path with powers at least three, it proves a uniform asymptotic with
an explicit nonzero coefficient when
\(j_v/N\in[1/640,1/320]\). The proof estimates the complete finite
source: the other Fourier charges, vertical contour terms, removed
physical rows, and first normal derivatives are all retained. This
establishes an initial contribution near the complete point. It does
not yet transport that contribution to charge one, where the coupon
is one and the original unmodified source is recovered.

On the smaller interval \([1/4000,1/2000]\), the theorem extends to
any fixed finite graph carrying the specified same-index edge
kernels, with no isolated selected vertex, and permits every fixed
signed integer power, including zero. Its small critical point is
constructed directly, without assuming a global geometric
continuation for those powers or a knot realization of the graph. The
[Gaussian preparation estimate](research_fourier_lower_bounds_and_almost_invariance.md#16-gaussian-preparation-is-now-proved-for-the-small-charge-source)
then proves an independent positive norm and an
\(O(N^{-1/2})\) relative annihilation residual for the actual
rescaled horizontal integrand. The associated Gaussian oscillator
has gap at least \(1/(5\pi)\). Thus the initial almost-invariance
has a source-level proof. Extending these estimates to charge one,
while controlling the other contour contributions, is still open.

The [analytic charge family](research_dominant_saddle_transport.md#9-an-exact-analytic-coupon-family-and-the-proved-initializer)
interpolates these insertions by their full physical values and first
derivatives. It therefore supplies an exact finite family between
integer charges, with the trace contour and its poles fixed for each
level. At charge one the companion terms add; their transition near
that endpoint has a uniformly nonzero, explicitly retained amplitude.
The earlier dominant-saddle continuation theorem could transport the
new initial coefficient if its relative-cycle and global bounds were
verified for this family. Those hypotheses remain open. Analyticity
of the finite family does not provide them.

The [charge equation](research_current_free_aw_crossing_transport.md#10-a-closed-recurrence-for-the-original-charge-observations)
now gives a recurrence for the actual one-edge source, retaining its
free boundary color. Its order is independent of the level and its
outer coefficients never vanish. The physical charge relations reduce
its solution space to two dimensions, including at physical boundary
colors. The original endpoint condition selects one line; the other
line consists of a source with zero physical values and nonzero first
normals. This is an exact algebraic selection of the original source,
not yet a lower bound for one of its charge observations.

There is now a positive Fourier norm that can be computed sharply
for any fixed graph carrying the specified same-index kernels. The
[charge-increment theorem](research_charge_increment_graph_norm.md)
takes differences between charges separated by one period, eliminating
the first normals exactly. Parseval turns their squared norm into a
positive sum over physical values. Its rate is twice the sum of the
unfilled edge rates, independently of every integer crossing power.
This proves a genuine lower bound for the whole charge vector. An
already settled three-crossing source has a central observation
exponentially smaller than that vector's norm. Thus bounded Fourier
projection and positivity alone cannot supply the desired scalar
lower bound; the change in geometric action has to be accounted for.

For one charged edge with a real free color, the
[source reconstruction](research_physical_normal_lift.md)
now recovers all charge observations from the period increment by an
explicit operator of polynomial norm. Inverse Fourier transformation
recovers the double-node values; the last Jacobi row recovers the odd
simple-node value that the increment misses. The already proved
relative normal formula then supplies every required derivative.
This settles reconstruction on the original source line in that real
interval. The remaining lower bound concerns one row of the resulting
Fourier operator; bounded reconstruction of the whole vector does not
bound that row from below.

The local value equation now has a positive boundary formulation at
the actual complex geometric colors. The
[maximum principle for cosine phases](research_geometric_phase_maximum_principle.md)
proves \(\Re w<7/4\) throughout the positive-path charge cube,
uniformly in the path and its powers. Thus every ordinary Jacobi
inverse there has norm at most \(5\), for \(N\ge16\). The
[exact Fourier boundary problem](research_physical_jacobi_charge_boundary.md)
transfers this estimate to the period increments in a positive metric
whose condition number is at most \(N/2\). Its original endpoint
forcing is retained. When the other endpoint is subsequently traced,
the Ward representative also retains every required mixed normal
while bounding the relative normal by \(O(N^6+N^2\log N)\).
These are estimates for the original values and trace data; the
positive boundary observation is not the final closing functional.

There is a quantitative reason that the local growing solution has
a nonzero coefficient. The
[physical-row Riccati theorem](research_physical_row_riccati_transport.md)
proves a strict contraction of the actual consecutive row ratios in
a common right half-plane. Away from the row endpoints, those ratios
follow the selected characteristic root with error \(O(N^{-1})\).
Their products equal the exponential of the original edge-phase
difference times a holomorphic factor bounded above and below by
positive constants. The normalization comes from the original row
\(F_0=1\). The endpoint argument also fixes the absolute rate:
\(\log K_N(c_j,w)=N\psi(\tau_j,u)+O(\log N)\), with
\(w=-2\cos u\), on interior physical rows. The
[last-row theorem](research_last_physical_row_riccati.md)
extends this absolute estimate to the last physical row, with every
fixed free-color derivative. An exact positive-real barrier controls
the ratios where the two limiting roots approach one another.
At odd levels the endpoint is precisely the complete color.
At even levels the
[low-index complete-end theorem](research_even_complete_low_kernel.md)
uses exact Chebyshev interpolation to obtain a relative error
\(O(N^{-1/2})\) from that physical row. Summation by parts controls
the cancellation of its alternating interpolation weights.
The original low complete-end kernel consequently has a nonzero
holomorphic factor of polynomial size at both parities.
The separate [radical calculation](research_even_complete_radical_asymptotic.md)
proves that the full bare kernel can have different odd- and even-level
rates at a complex free color. Thus the low-sector qualification cannot
be removed on the whole spectral half-plane.
For actual complete-ended positive pairs there is a stronger result:
the [pair-specific complete-edge gap](research_internal_pair_complete_edge_gap.md)
gives \(H<107/100\) and
\(\Re\psi(t,0)-H>1/500\) on a common angular box containing
their selected points. The full complete-end kernels have the
nonzero geometric factor there at both parities. The parity
counterexample lies outside that box.

These bounds now supply the independent normalization needed for
[local Gaussian preparation](research_internal_pair_local_gaussian.md)
at **every fixed integer internal pair \(n,p\ge3\)** with complete
outside ends. The actual rescaled mixed density has a positive
limiting norm and relative annihilation residual
\(O(N^{-1/2})\); its local integral has an explicit nonzero
coefficient multiplying \(N^{-3/2}\) at the geometric exponential
rate. These sharper conclusions use Section 7 of that note and
hold on a fixed complex bidisk in the outside colors. The discarded outside
radical sectors are exponentially smaller after their original
traces, by the existing pair gap. This local statement alone does
not prove the full pair asymptotic: its shared-wire and trace contour must
contain that local piece with nonzero coefficient, and the combined
remaining currents must be controlled. The separate
[free-boundary edge theorem](research_pair_free_boundary_kernel.md)
now supplies the full edge factor on a fixed complex neighborhood of
the outside color, with its explicit nonzero Gaussian coefficient,
both level parities, and ordinary outside-color derivatives. Its
proof uses the original finite Newton sum, a single-maximum contour
in the tangent coordinate, and bounds for every endpoint and
cotangent alias. This removes the edge-normalization obstruction.
The joint two-trace cycle is now controlled for \(n,p\ge7\)
by the assembled theorem above; it remains untreated in general
over the whole range \(n,p\ge3\). The same
edge theorem also bounds the full real outside period with a strict
angular loss and extends that bound to a fixed complex strip,
including ordinary outside-color derivatives.

The [combined contour reduction](research_internal_pair_combined_contour_reduction.md)
now removes the original real tails and writes the retained pair
as sixteen exact currents, bounded by one explicit function of
the shared index and both trace angles. The localized Gaussian
has coefficient one in this decomposition. The reduction alone
does not exclude cancellation; Sections 6–8 now complete that
argument and its boundary estimates for \(n,p\ge7\).
The [endpoint-taper theorem](research_internal_pair_endpoint_taper.md)
does exclude the two shared-index endpoint collars: jointly
decreasing the wire and trace heights puts every current there
below \(2M_\infty+1/200<M_{n,p}-1/200\). This works for every
fixed positive pair, with full outside kernels and ordinary
normals. The exact trace identities remain valid when the
heights depend on the wire coordinate. The middle wire band
requires the further comparisons described below.

The [angular-tail transport theorem](research_internal_pair_angular_tail_transport.md)
also bounds the entire omitted set of original physical trace
rows on the shifted Fourier circle. It first proves the sharp
complete-end tail bound through color \(2\), using positivity
of the exact physical-row recurrence coefficients. An elementary
geometric estimate gives \(2\pi\Im x_*<3/4\). Separate exact
Fourier reconstructions of the two half-band sources then put
their omitted angular rows below \(M_{n,p}-1/100\). This result
uses complete outside colors and retains every original normal.
The [grouped connector theorem](research_internal_pair_grouped_angular_connectors.md)
now supplies the needed additional bound for folded angular
connectors. It pairs each connector with the whole other trace
in an exact identity. At complete outside colors, all these terms
have rate less than \(2.51<M_{n,p}-1/100\), for every fixed
integer pair \(n,p\ge3\).

The [joint wire-alias comparison](research_internal_pair_wire_alias_reflection.md)
and [negative-angle reflection estimate](research_internal_pair_negative_angle_reflection.md)
also bound two competing densities in the regular factorial
region. They retain the original crossing phases and finite
trace denominators. Their reference is the upper positive-angle
absolute density, which still requires a global bound.
The mixed region, where one trace crosses a factorial branch
boundary and the other does not, remains unresolved. The
[exact reflected-current identity](research_internal_pair_reflected_current_identity.md)
shows that its moving residues are original physical values;
discarding them would change the finite source. Thus these
comparisons do not yet prove the general pair theorem.

One additional part of the original finite sum is now bounded
directly. The [triangular first-normal formula](research_pair_triangular_normal_region.md)
retains the terms where the Newton value is zero at both selected
physical rows but both first derivatives contribute. For shared
indices \(j/N\le1/4\) or \(j/N\ge49/100\), this entire portion
has a strict gap greater than \(1/100\) below the pair's geometric
rate, uniformly in the fixed positive powers. The proof uses a
positive magnitude envelope, not positivity of the signed sum.
The intervening band and the terms with only one such derivative
still have to be treated together with the rest of the source;
no separate smallness assertion is made for them.

There is now an exact way to combine those derivative terms before
estimating them. The
[normal-difference trace identity](research_trace_normal_defect_positive_form.md)
subtracts the derivative of the value interpolant from the actual
first derivative. It cancels the artificial triangular boundary
exactly. At even levels its crossing operator is a positive
Hermitian Pick kernel; an explicitly weighted subspace has the same
property at odd levels, while the unrestricted odd formula retains
its endpoint correction. The original pair contraction still has
its phases and bilinear closing functional.

This operator also has an exact transport law. If \(U_t\) is the
original diagonal crossing evolution and \(G_N>0\) is its
infinitesimal observation matrix, then
\(H_{n,N}=\int_0^nU_t^*G_NU_t\,dt\). Its energy is an integral
of squared ordinary interpolation observations. The signed trace
has a separate exact formula multiplying observations at times
\(t\) and \(n-t\), without conjugation. Both formulas retain the
specified source and all first-normal contributions. The latter
formula is the one that still needs a lower bound.
At a full level-dependent observation time, the exact identities
\(H_{N,N}=N\operatorname{diag}G_N\ge2I\) at even levels and
their weighted odd counterpart do give a uniform or polynomial
lower bound. These times grow with the quantum level; they do
not prove a lower bound for a knot with fixed twist coefficients.

The [small-eigenvalue theorem](research_pick_form_small_eigenvalues.md)
shows why positivity alone cannot finish that argument. For each
fixed positive power, this actual even-level operator has unit
vectors with nonnegative entries and quadratic form at most
\(nN^2e^{-N/(1024\max\{n,1\})}\). The proof cancels low moments
on physical colors near \(-2\); it does not identify the original
source with those vectors. A useful lower bound must control the
specified source and its closing observation, not every vector.

The [complete-source observation estimate](research_complete_source_pick_observation.md)
now proves an exponential loss for the actual complete-end vector
in this positive energy, for every fixed positive horizon at
even levels. Its further Theorem 2 now proves a nonzero leading
coefficient for the original alternating observation at every
fixed real \(n\ge3\). The exponent is the action of the
complete-end leaf at charge \(1/2\), constructed directly from
its scalar period equation. The resulting positive energy has
the sharp asymptotic \(C_nN^{-2}e^{2NM_n}(1+O(N^{-1}))\), with
explicit \(C_n>0\). This result includes the physical tails,
vertical contours, and earlier-time part of the energy integral.
It gives a lower bound for the specified observation at its
correct rate. The original signed pair uses a bilinear
convolution rather than this positive square, and that
distinction remains essential.
The [odd-level observation theorem](research_odd_half_charge_observation.md)
now gives the corresponding nonzero coefficient at odd levels.
It uses the full distinct-node interpolation and accounts for
the simple complete-color endpoint by its exact angular residue.
The additional top-degree trace term is evaluated explicitly;
its pair product has rate below \(2M_\infty\). This is not
a positive-energy theorem for the unweighted odd observation.
The [pair action comparison](research_pair_half_charge_action_gap.md)
now proves that both actual colors of every fixed positive
pair \(n,p\ge3\) lie beyond the corresponding half-charge
observation contours, with a strictly larger direct action.
The exact residue formula therefore gives a smaller
interpolation correction to the geometric first-normal term
on a fixed neighborhood. This supplies a normalized local
source statement for the full interpolation defect at both
level parities. It does not justify dropping the correction
on the entire contour.

The [uniform physical-color estimate](research_physical_normal_defect_packet.md)
now determines the interpolation derivative defect at every retained
color, at both level parities. Its rational leading coefficient is
nonzero throughout the physical interval. The
same theorem now extends holomorphically to a fixed neighborhood
of every interval \([-2,2-\delta]\), \(\delta>0\). Its tapered
observation contour retains all added connectors and yields an
explicit logarithmic-potential bound for the exact reduced trace.
This avoids a substitution of finitely many asymptotic terms
before an increasing-order divided difference. The
[free-boundary extension](research_free_boundary_half_charge_observation.md)
retains this coefficient on a fixed complex neighborhood of the
complete outside color, including every fixed ordinary derivative.
It also proves decay across the whole real outside period and a
quadratic growth bound on a thin complex strip. These are estimates
of the original finite source; they do not yet survive an arbitrary
signed contraction of the shared internal index.

For every fixed positive pair of integer powers \(n,p\ge3\), the
[outer-index theorem](research_real_pair_geometry_and_tail_gap.md)
now removes the shared indices \(j/N\le1/50\) and
\(j/N\ge12/25\), after the original trace has been taken. Their
total absolute contribution is at most a polynomial times
\(e^{N(M_{n,p}-1/50)}\), where \(M_{n,p}\) is the pair's
geometric rate. The proof compares the pair action with the two
half-charge actions, using a continuous real-power family. Its
angle comparison uses a downward-crossing barrier; the earlier
incorrect rotated-sinh identity and global monotonicity argument
have been replaced. The middle interval is now controlled for
\(n,p\ge7\); these tail estimates alone do not settle it for
every pair in the larger range.

At even levels, the
[exact Fourier cell decomposition](research_pair_regular_support_cells.md)
removes the nonphysical rows separately in each cell. Joining the
cells leaves explicit boundary terms. Their cancellation matters:
even for the already settled pair \((3,3)\), one of the three terms
in a boundary jump has an absolute-integral rate larger than the
full pair rate. They therefore cannot all be bounded separately
by the desired rate. A different shortcut also fails: the
[certified positive pair \((7,3)\)](research_pair_truncated_ray_obstruction.md)
has a shifted factorial zero between the real wire interval and
the direct tangent ray, inside the retained middle interval.
The exact polynomials are entire, but the complete-edge proof
using one zero-free logarithmic phase cannot be transferred
unchanged. These conclusions locate two specific cancellations
or contour changes that a general pair proof must handle.
On the original double-pole contour, the
[regular right-hand horizontal region](research_internal_pair_right_horizontal_bulk.md)
with \(1/4\le\Re x\le12/25\) already has a strict gap by joint
concavity. The estimate now extends to the closed factorial walls
and a fixed reflected width, with both wire heights and all four
sign choices for the trace angles. It still does not include full
vertical connectors or the projected-kernel terms introduced by
the block representation.
On the left side, the
[both-reflected contour estimate](research_internal_pair_reflected_current_identity.md#5-when-both-trace-factors-are-reflected-the-real-contour-has-a-gap)
has real rate less than \(751/300<M_{n,p}-1/60\), giving a
\(1/120\) gap on nearby contours of small positive trace height.
The same note proves favorable height descent on the lower wire
for powers at least three, and on both wires for powers at least
seven. These phase comparisons do not evaluate the connectors
created by a height change. The
[left mixed-region estimate](research_internal_pair_reflected_current_identity.md#7-a-mixed-region-that-can-be-kept-near-the-real-contour)
now permits exactly one reflected factor when \(\Re x\le1/8\):
the real rate is below \(5953/2400<M_{n,p}-19/480\), and a
\(19/960\) gap persists on nearby contours. The other trace angle
is unrestricted within the retained real interval. This is an
estimate of the original double-pole density, including its full
complete-end factors and selected normals, through both parities.
It does not cover the connecting contours or the projected terms.
The remaining mixed interval \(1/8<\Re x<1/4\) cannot all be
handled by making both heights small: Section 6 gives actual
\((3,3)\) densities of rate greater than \(2.9\) near the mixed
corner, while that pair's full rate is less than \(2.6\).
An asymmetric contour or cancellation before taking absolute
values is therefore necessary there.
Section 8 supplies one such local asymmetric estimate: near zero
regular trace angle, retain that trace at a height between \(3/5\)
and \(107/100\), while the reflected trace and wire have small
heights. The resulting gap is \(911/30000\), throughout the
compact reflected angular region. This includes the actual
\((3,3)\) height. It is a height criterion, not a lower bound
for every geometric height, and does not yet control all regular
angles or the connecting contours.
The [finite grouped-jump diagnostic](../repro/results/research-grouped-pair-shared-face-diagnostic.json)
also cautions against assuming that combining just the three terms
is enough. For the original \((3,3)\) source, the grouped-to-third-term
ratio at level 96 is approximately \(-1.03739-0.02016i\), with
agreement between 150- and 220-digit calculations. This is finite
evidence only. It motivates retaining cancellation across cells
or along a contour, rather than asserting an unproved gap for
each grouped jump.
Proposition 5 of the cell note gives an exact alternative: freeze
the support on each of finitely many blocks and cancel all internal
shared faces before estimating. The restored reflected factorial
region has width at most the chosen block width plus \(1/(2N)\).
The block seams and the interpolation-observation terms still
require bounds; the identity alone does not provide them.
Section 7 now gives two exact alternatives for those terms.
One retains a support-projected polynomial in the original trace,
or equivalently a nested Cauchy integral with its diagonal residue.
The other restores the omitted original first-normal rows before
the block residues are taken. Both preserve the necessary
cancellation; neither proves that the corrections are small.
Section 8 gives an exact discrete antiderivative of the physical
projection weights. It rewrites each projected source as one
boundary term and a sum of successive differences of the original
normal defect. For constant input the difference sum vanishes,
making the cost of the boundary explicit: at a cut \(L=N/3\),
the projection has growth rate greater than \(8/25\), although
the corresponding uncut projection is polynomial on the same
thin contour. The constant input is not the prescribed knot
source. It proves that the holomorphic packet bound alone cannot
control this operation, even with an \(O(N^{-1})\) relative error.
The actual difference sum and cancellation between blocks remain
necessary.

Separately, the
[complete-source crossing overlap](research_complete_source_crossing_overlap.md)
is computed at both parities: its normalized matrix coefficient
tends to \((1-it/2)^{-1/2}\). The unmodified vector is therefore
not almost invariant under any fixed nonzero crossing. Its
infinitesimal defect is \(O(N^{-1})\) at time \(1/N\), but
iteration to a fixed time produces a positive limiting defect.
These statements identify which norm and which operator can
support the proposed representation-theoretic argument; they
do not replace the missing signed lower bound.
The [original recurrence's spectral projection](research_fourier_lower_bounds_and_almost_invariance.md#17-the-actual-resonant-projector-can-be-exponentially-large)
now gives another quantitative restriction on that strategy.
At odd levels its eigenvalue zero is separated from the other
eigenvalues by \(4\sin^2(\pi/N)\), but at power three the
projector has norm at least
\(cN^{-3/2}e^{NM_{3,3}}\). An exact Green identity retains a
rank-one term whose coefficient is the desired original closing
scalar; its complementary Green operator has lower rate
\(2M_{3,3}\). At even levels the actual forced inverse has norm
at least \(cN^{5/4}e^{NM_{3,3}/2}\). These facts follow from
the literal matrices and the already proved \((3,3)\) source.
They show that an inverse eigenvalue gap of polynomial size does
not supply a polynomial norm bound in the original coordinates.
Any useful positive metric must also control the source and the
closing functional after changing coordinates.

For transport in the Fourier charge itself, the
[complete-boundary characteristic calculation](research_charge_characteristic_two_mode_block.md)
identifies an isolated pair of growing modes for every power
\(n\ge3\). Their moduli cross at charge \(1/2\); the geometric
mode alone is not protected by modulus ordering. The corresponding
finite spectral projection changes by \(O(N^{-1})\) per step on
compact interior charge intervals. This is not a bound on accumulated
source error: other modes grow faster, and the block meets additional
modes at the charge endpoints. The missing estimate still concerns
the original source's coefficient in this block and its final
normal-weighted Fourier observation.

The [central-readout calculation](research_central_readout_half_plane_zeros.md)
shows why the last distinction is necessary. For every level
\(N\ge3\) and every signed power, the original central polynomial
has a zero inside the positive Jacobi half-plane, even though every
physical value and endpoint transmission there is nonzero. These
zeros have not been placed on the actual geometric locus. They rule
out an inference from accretivity alone, rather than a lower bound
proved using that additional geometric information.

The Fourier lower-bound approach now has an exact positive example
for arbitrary fixed chain length. The
[three-crossing spectral-moment theorem](research_positive_three_crossing_cycle.md)
proves \(M(JM^3)M^{-1}=\kappa M^*M\). For the specified capped
word \((3,\ldots,3,2)\), the original quantum sum is therefore
\(\kappa^{m-1}\langle e_0,(M^*M)^m e_0\rangle\), with a positive
spectral measure and proved exponential lower bounds. The cyclic
contraction has a sharp asymptotic from the Gaussian operator limit.
These statements remove cancellation for those particular
contractions. They do not determine the cap's sharp geometric rate
or make a general two-boundary pairing positive.

The [exact cap recursion](research_positive_cap_fourier_recursion.md)
now writes these moments as finite Fourier convolutions, with their
initial cap and both polynomial projection terms specified. Its clock
intertwiner is tridiagonal; the apparent endpoint term cancels
algebraically. If \(H=M^*M\) and
\(W=(M-M^T)^*(M-M^T)\), it also proves, for every fixed \(r\ge2\),
\[
 \frac{\|H^re_0-W^re_0\|}{\|H^re_0\|}
                =O_r\bigl(e^{-N(v-c)/2}\bigr),
\]
where \(c\) and \(v\) are the proved second- and third-moment rates.
This is a relative estimate for the original cap vectors. The
remaining upper convolution has complex coefficients, so the
positive weighted norm that follows it still needs a sharp lower
bound. No higher-moment volume equality is inferred from this
replacement.

The [fourth-moment coefficient estimate](research_positive_fourth_cap_observation.md)
now improves these cap lower bounds. One specified coefficient of
\(H^2e_0\) has an exact finite-sum expression with a unique maximum
of its absolute summand and a stationary complex phase. Its nonzero
Gaussian coefficient gives
\[
 \langle e_0,H^4e_0\rangle\ge c_4N e^{wN},
 \qquad w\simeq1.504207135>3/2.
\]
Together with the sharp third-moment rate \(v\simeq0.906072448\),
positive-moment log-convexity yields the lower rate
\((m-3)w-(m-4)v\) for every fixed \(m\ge4\).
This strictly improves the previous lower rate at every such length.
The proof follows an actual quantum coefficient; it does not discard
its oscillating phases. The fourth moment's sharp rate and the
corresponding volume identity remain undetermined.

There is now a sharper actual cap estimate. The
[third-moment theorem](research_positive_three_crossing_cap_seed.md)
proves exactly \(\langle e_0,H^3e_0\rangle=\|MJM^3e_0\|^2\),
where \(H=M^*M\). The full Fourier profile of the vector on the
right was already proved, so this identity supplies a sharp third
moment and stronger lower bounds for all longer fixed capped
chains. It also proves that \(He_0/\|He_0\|\) remains far from
the leading eigenspace, despite the uniform spectral gap.
For other matching original caps,
[positive transport](research_positive_three_crossing_cycle.md#6-transporting-independently-proved-source-norms-through-positive-blocks)
gives a lower bound directly from the known input and next-crossing
norms. These are genuine source estimates. Identifying their sharp
rate with hyperbolic volume and controlling different boundary
vectors are still required for a general volume theorem.

On the geometric side, the
[fractional-charge theorem](research_positive_path_fractional_charge_cube.md)
now continues the positive stationary solution through the entire
charge cube for integer powers at least three. It proves
\(\partial F/\partial\lambda_v=\pi H_v\) and
\(\sinh H_v<\sqrt3\sin a_v\). Thus the cost of activating an
adjacent pair is exactly the integral of its two heights. The
[pair-activation comparison](research_positive_path_pair_activation_gap.md)
reduces a universal edge gap to two finite support inequalities.
Both original unrestricted searches exhausted their subdivision
budgets without full coverage; neither produced a certificate.
The sector-restricted scaled inequality is now established: the
complete 77,088-box certificate passed its separate 160-bit replay.
Together with the written small-height proof, it gives
\(H<\min\{59\chi/50,23/20\}\). The
[scaled-height consequences](research_scaled_pair_activation_consequences.md)
prove a strict deletion gap when the two adjacent powers are both
at least four, or either is at least ten. They also prove a gap
for every connected run of at least two deleted edges, with all
powers at least three. The isolated types \((3,j)\),
\(3\le j\le9\), and their reversals remain unresolved by this
comparison. Quantum estimates for the remaining components and
the coefficient of the main cycle remain separate requirements.

The sector-restricted affine verification is unfinished. The stronger cosine-phase bound
\(\tan^2\arg\cos(t_v/2)<1/2\) gives a further reduced geometric
domain. Its [separate verification](research_pair_height_phase_cap_verification.md)
has an independent replayer; full coverage is still pending.
The older runs have been retained. The reduced-domain assertion,
if certified, gives the needed geometric height bounds directly;
it would not prove the older unrestricted support assertions.
The separate small-height part has a written proof through height
\(3/100\), with exact rational verification.

The [cutoff-current calculation](research_radical_path_sector_gap.md#7-the-middle-newton-polynomials-on-the-whole-real-period)
now has a useful positive Fourier expansion: the middle Newton
polynomial has nonnegative coefficients and polynomial size on the
whole real angular period. Consequently every nonempty collection
of literal cutoff forcing edges reduces, at polynomial cost, to
whole-boundary bounds for components with fewer selected vertices.
Adjacent forcing edges are included. If the pending pair-activation
certificate and those smaller-component bounds are available, every
such forcing term has a strict gap below the full geometric rate.
This is an induction for these specified error terms. The joint
low-index source still needs its own contributing-cycle theorem.

The [collar estimate](research_wire_cutoff_collar_localization.md)
extends this reduction to a cutoff spread over Newton indices within
\(\epsilon N\) of the middle index. Each removed or forcing edge
costs at most \(\exp(2N\omega(\epsilon))\) times a polynomial,
where \(\omega(\epsilon)=-2\int_0^\epsilon\log\tan(\pi r)\,dr\)
tends to zero. The remaining factors are original components with
fewer selected vertices and unrestricted real boundary colors.
Thus an independently proved geometric deletion gap survives a
sufficiently narrow cutoff. This conditional remainder estimate
does not supply the contributing cycle for the retained sum.

The [maximum-height theorem](research_positive_path_height_bound.md)
now gives \(0<-\Im t_v<23/20\) for every positive integer-power
path with all powers at least three, independently of path length.
The proof uses the period equation at a vertex of maximum height,
a harmonic support inequality on a quarter ellipse, and a finite
outward interval certificate. Together with independent block
contractions in the convex energy, it gives the
[uniform activation budget](research_edge_cut_energy_comparison.md#7-consequences-of-a-uniform-height-bound)
\[
 F_\Gamma(\mathbf1)-F_\Gamma(\lambda^T)
       <\frac{23\pi}{20}\sum_{v\in T}\frac8{n_v+5}.
\]
Here \(F_\Gamma\) is the minimum square energy and
\(\lambda^T\) makes exactly the vertices in \(T\) complete.
For a cut edge with endpoint powers \(n,p\ge3\), this proves
the required geometric action comparison whenever
\(\max(n,p)\ge562\), with no restriction on the other old
positive powers beyond three. The same estimate applies to
matchings. Turning it into a quantum remainder bound still
requires the whole-boundary bounds for the remaining components.
It does not produce their nonzero geometric coefficient.

There is a more precise obstruction to using a separate local
Gaussian at every short vertex. The
[traced three-crossing calculation](research_traced_three_vertex_endpoint.md)
proves that, near the homogeneous positive geometry, the full
vertex kernel has leading rate \(\log2\), which exceeds its
geometric vertex action by more than \(0.047\). Its leading
term is an explicit endpoint function. The next exact Fourier
contraction can cancel its apparent exponential growth.
Thus even taking the original trace at each vertex is insufficient
to justify a product of local geometric asymptotics. Bounds for
composed pieces must retain this cancellation.

The [polynomial cap chart](research_polynomial_cap_chart_and_product_closure.md)
also gives an exact finite transform through the original cap,
including its scalar and parameter derivatives. It closes under
the step \(JM\), but a single \(M\) introduces an additional
diagonal character. A degree argument excludes exact closure of
the canonical three-crossing source by a bounded number of
factorial factors with bounded-degree shift ratios. Forced
systems with a fixed number of channels remain possible.

The [one-crossing theorem](research_one_crossing_gaussian_window.md)
now determines the normalized Gaussian operator obtained from the
original crossing matrix, with convergence in Hilbert--Schmidt norm.
Its leading singular value is simple and separated from the others by
an explicit gap independent of the level. An explicitly prepared
Gaussian therefore has a proved nonzero one-step amplitude. The
original cap does not have this preparation: its projection onto that
leading singular vector is exponentially small. An exact example also
shows that discarding relatively small tails can destroy the next
inverse-crossing estimate, even when the original endpoint value is
retained. These results locate the additional input needed for a
spectral lower-bound proof.

The [Gaussian frame formulas](research_gaussian_frame_newton_transport.md)
give an exact positive resolution of the identity, explicit signed
crossing kernels, and the original initial and closing functions for
every finite word. They supply a common representation in which to
study that preparation. A positive frame identity alone does not
control the signed closing coefficient.

Two exact calculations further specify this operator route.
For every level at least three, a nonreal cyclic product of three
entries of the original Gram matrix survives all positive diagonal
weights and phase changes. Thus those changes alone cannot supply
an entrywise nonnegative kernel. The
[boundary condition for an adjoint trial](research_complete_boundary_coefficient_transport.md#a-boundary-condition-for-an-independent-adjoint-trial)
also shows that a useful norm lower bound requires an exponentially
accurate cancellation in a specified endpoint row of the original
four-step recurrence. A small residual in an interior Gaussian
window is insufficient. These statements leave non-diagonal forms
and globally controlled transport available; they identify what
such constructions must prove.

The [network phase theorem](research_unsummed_network_phase_coercivity.md)
now gives a strict quadratic decrease away from a critical point
on an explicit convex domain, for any finite graph with the same
Newton index at both ends of each edge. It estimates each incidence
directly and does not insert complete-boundary terms at interior
vertices. At every regular positive geometric configuration, a
different local change of wire coordinates gives a nondegenerate
Gaussian, even outside that convex domain. These are general phase
results. They do not prove that the original finite integration cycle
contains that Gaussian. An exact positive-edge example in the note
shows why positivity alone cannot justify the unchanged horizontal
contour.

For the mixed phase with its complete-end contribution, the
[height-order extension](research_mixed_phase_height_extension_and_wire_order.md)
removes the earlier comparison between the wire and vertex heights.
The new geometric half-plane bound supplies two of its remaining
real-domain inequalities. The
[coupled wire-order theorem](research_positive_path_real_wire_order.md)
now supplies the last inequality at every actual geometric critical
point of a positive path with powers at least three, throughout the
charge cube. Its proof first shows that each active cosine has modulus
less than one, then uses the period equations to exclude a wire passing
either endpoint coordinate. Every original factorial argument
consequently stays in its regular real strip at the geometric saddle.
The earlier independent-angle counterexample is excluded by these
coupled equations; it was not a filled-path example.

The [horizontal-concavity theorem](research_positive_path_horizontal_concavity.md)
also places every such saddle in the original joint angular rectangle:
\(\Im\tan(t_v/2)>-1\) for every active vertex. This improves the earlier
sufficient power thresholds six and eight to three for this geometric
conclusion. The continued angular phase has a unique maximum on that
rectangle, and the full mixed phase of a two-vertex piece with complete
outer ends has its saddle in the known convex concavity domain. These
statements apply to paths of arbitrary fixed length. They still do not
estimate the other parts of the exact finite contour or prove its
coefficient on the central geometric cycle.

The [pinned coefficient equation](research_complete_boundary_coefficient_transport.md#9-the-pinned-green-equation-and-its-exact-adjoint-test)
now incorporates the original endpoint normalization at both
parities. Its spectrum and one specified inverse-matrix entry are
independent of the crossing power, although the actual source norms
have different exponential rates. Its natural adjoint trial does
not give the missing norm lower bound: the small residual comes
with a still smaller forcing overlap. Thus an operator proof must
control the relevant vectors and matrix elements, beyond those
scalar spectral data.

The [terminal-splitting deduction](research_affine_reduction_fibers_and_core_obligation.md#8-a-terminal-splitting-inside-the-original-circle-tree-class)
also sharpens the original parameter obligation. Adding two vertices
to any fixed circle-tree template gives one enlarged template whose
zero-twist slice has exceptional set equal to the old exceptional
set times the integers. Cofiniteness for this one enlargement would
therefore settle every hyperbolic assignment of the smaller template.
This deduction preserves paths and original filling coordinates.
It explains why an unresolved fixed short core cannot simply be
placed on a finite exceptional list.

The [internal pair theorem](research_internal_pair_three_full_boundary_packet.md)
now proves the full original two-boundary asymptotic for the adjacent
crossing powers \(3,3\), and for their mirror \(-3,-3\).
Its leading amplitude is nonzero, both level parities are included,
and its real exponential rate is the marked partial complement's
hyperbolic volume divided by \(2\pi\). The proof uses the exact
Fourier constant coefficient
\[
 \mathcal P_N(u,v)
   =N\int_{iY}^{1+iY}W_{3,N}(x,u)W_{3,N}(x,v)\,dx.
\]
On this shifted circle, the geometric critical point supplies
a nonzero Gaussian term; every part of the complementary period
has a strict rate gap. Both outside boundary variables remain
free, with a whole-period angular bound and a quadratic complex-strip
bound. This resolves the coefficient problem for this fixed internal
block. Arbitrary connected groups of short vertices remain open.
The [reproduction script](../experiments/reproduce_internal_pair_three.py)
runs its five finite interval certificates.

The [composition corollary](research_internal_pair_three_kernel_compositions.md)
allows any fixed number of these internal pairs, with either sign,
separated by sufficiently long signed powers and followed by a long
closing power. One common finite threshold works independently of the
number and order of the pairs. The original carrier congruences and
knot-component test remain part of the statement. The threshold is
not yet given numerically; the value \(64\) from the all-long path
theorem cannot simply be substituted.

The pendant same-sign pair of powers \(3,3\), and its mirror,
now has the nonzero original boundary contribution and the
whole-period estimate required for subsequent long turns.
Its [closing theorem](research_three_crossing_long_closing_fiber.md)
therefore settles all but finitely many original values of its
one remaining filling parameter. It also permits arbitrarily
many such fixed pendant pieces in the specified composition
class. This does not yet settle arbitrary connected short pieces.

The [Fourier lower-bound analysis](research_fourier_lower_bounds_and_almost_invariance.md)
now gives precise sufficient conditions in terms of the actual
phase variation and a weighted spectral gap. It also proves that
these conditions cannot be applied at the raw absolute-sum rate
of the settled pair: cancellation lowers that rate by a fixed
positive amount. A general lower-bound proof must retain this
cancellation or estimate the norm of the actual complete-color
Fourier vector. The positive comparison partition used in the
Cauchy upper bound does not supply that norm.

The [Gaussian observation criterion](research_shifted_gaussian_observation.md)
now states the exact additional requirements for an operator proof
on a shifted Fourier contour: independent exponential norm growth,
small relative Gaussian annihilation residuals, and a smaller
contribution from the complementary cycle. The standard Gaussian
spectral gap then forces a nonzero bilinear coefficient. These
requirements follow from the already-proved packet for \(3,3\);
obtaining them directly from the quantum equations for arbitrary
short components remains open.

This failure is not confined to an unreduced state sum.
The [local phase theorem](research_three_crossing_real_period_newton_bound.md#7-the-local-phase-can-force-cancellation-in-the-newton-coefficients)
shows that a nonreal derivative of the local boundary action,
together with the proved smaller coefficient-norm rate,
forces exponential cancellation among the actual Newton
coefficients. The settled adjacent pair meets these hypotheses.
In its marked peripheral coordinates the derivative is determined
by the cusp shear. This rules out a proposed lower-bound
mechanism in that basis; it does not obstruct the volume identity.

The [joint path theorem](research_uniform_path_trace_assembly.md)
now proves the nonzero original finite-source contribution for
every fixed nontrivial circle-tree path with
\(|n_v|\ge64\) at all selected vertices. The signs may differ
and the magnitudes need not be comparable. When all auxiliary
vertices are filled and the original component test gives a
knot, this proves the original Kashaev volume identity along
all integer levels. A free endpoint retains a nonzero
holomorphic expansion and a whole-period bound with angular
loss \((1-\cos u)/200\). Retaining both endpoints gives a
nonzero two-boundary kernel with prefactor \(N^{-3/2}\),
additive angular losses and a quadratic complex-strip bound.
An internal short pair needs this two-boundary information.
It is now supplied for \(3,3\) by the separate internal pair theorem
above; it does not follow from the pendant-pair theorem.

The new step is joint control of an entire path. The earlier
isolated-vertex theorem already allowed powers of this size,
but its separate local estimates did not prove this composition.
The [partial-charge estimate](research_positive_path_partial_charge_bounds.md)
bounds the action change at removed vertices by less than
\(\sum d_v/800\). The
[original trace comparison](research_path_mixed_trace_currents.md)
gives a loss greater than \(\sum d_v/600\) at those same
vertices. Every remaining mixed contour term has a strict gap,
using the proved
[full kernel on a thin rectangle](research_bare_kernel_thin_rectangle.md).
These comparisons leave the geometric Gaussian coefficient
nonzero, without requiring nonnegative real-source coefficients.

The geometric solution itself exists for arbitrary signed
\(|n_v|\ge8\) by the same partial-charge contraction and
original marked completion. The quantum conclusion presently
uses the stronger bound sixty-four. Neither statement settles
an arbitrary group of smaller powers, or yields finitely many
exceptional assignments per template.

There is now a proved reason that the path proof cannot be extended
to powers three by enlarging its bare-edge chart. The
[power-three obstruction](research_bare_kernel_power_three_obstruction.md)
shows that the full kernel is dominated by its first-normal endpoint
sector at an explicit positive geometric point. Actual internal
edges of sufficiently long finite all-three paths approach this
point. The kernel's rate is strictly larger than its geometric
edge action there. This does not contradict the volume conjecture:
the subsequent original trace can cancel that endpoint sector.
It does require those cancellations to be grouped before a global
upper or lower estimate is applied.

The [edgewise obstruction and contracted-current estimate](research_all_three_edgewise_contour_obstruction.md)
make this requirement more precise. On an all-three path, all but a
bounded number of internal edges lie in the region where the full
individual edge kernel exceeds its geometric rate; the bound on the
number of exceptions is independent of path length. Adjacent leading
endpoint factors nevertheless vanish under the original traces because
their product is square-zero in the physical algebra. Removing those
terms still leaves a midpoint cutoff current. After its two original
endpoint traces are performed, that current is bounded by a polynomial
times the real-boundary norm of the graph with that edge removed.
For a path this is the product of the two open component bounds.
Thus the same strict comparison with the two component rates would
control both the radical contribution and the midpoint current.
Neither comparison nor the coefficient of the remaining homogeneous
solution has been proved for every short path.

The [one-sided Hermite representation](research_one_sided_hermite_projection.md)
provides an exact alternative for doing that algebraic grouping.
The whole source is one specified multivariable coefficient of a
polynomial of degree less than \(2N\) in each selected angular
variable, or equivalently its value at zero times an explicit
power of \(-(-1)^{N-1}N^2/2\). The construction retains every
original crossing and first normal. It does not create positive
coefficients or establish the needed exponential lower bound.

The [full radical contraction](research_high_newton_radical_contraction.md)
now groups the entire nilpotent high-index sector before estimation.
Its original first-normal traces become physical evaluations with
explicit coefficients of modulus at most two. On a graph, only
matchings of radical edges survive, and each matching is bounded
by a polynomial times an original partially evaluated source.
All incident edges and remaining traces are retained. This removes
the apparent off-grid exponential inflation of that sector.
The remaining estimates concern the physical-color contractions
and their comparison with the filled geometric action.

The resulting Gram matrix is positive definite, but has an
exponentially small least eigenvalue. Odd crossing powers cancel
its alternating signs while leaving their quadratic phases.
Consequently this reduction does not yet supply a source lower
bound. The [actual-source Hardy norm example](research_one_sided_hermite_projection.md#6-an-actual-source-with-a-large-hardy-norm-and-a-small-evaluation)
also shows that an exponentially large positive norm can coexist
with a polynomially small closing evaluation in this representation.
Its closure has zero volume; it rules out an unqualified norm
comparison, not a lower bound that includes the actual change
of hyperbolic volume.

For positive paths, the
[convex-energy identity](research_edge_cut_energy_comparison.md)
puts a separate needed pair-removal comparison in the form
\(F_{\rm full}<F_L+F_R+4G\).
The identity relating each minimum \(F\) to the absolute action
is proved; this strict gluing inequality remains open.
It must not be confused with the physical-color quantum bound
just described.

For the internal pair \(3,3\), one strict comparison is now proved.
The [radical-sector estimate](research_radical_path_sector_gap.md)
shows that its complete geometric action satisfies
\(M_{3,3}>2M_\infty+1/100\). An explicit feasible-angle trial
and seven exact rational inequalities prove this bound.
The entire radical contribution has rate at most \(2M_\infty\),
uniformly over both real outside boundaries, so it has a strict
gap. The [traced cutoff estimate](research_bare_kernel_power_three_obstruction.md#6-the-midpoint-forcing-after-the-original-internal-pair-trace)
also bounds the remaining midpoint forcing at that same smaller
rate, including the even-level central first normal.
Both error estimates persist on a small complex boundary neighborhood.
These two sector bounds did not by themselves prove that the
geometric coefficient survives. The full pair theorem now proves
that conclusion by estimating the mixed Fourier source on its
entire shifted period, without assuming a bare low-kernel packet.

The geometric comparison now extends to every real pair \(n,p\ge3\)
with complete outside boundaries. The same variational argument
proves interiority throughout this quadrant, and the same explicit
trial gives \(M_{n,p}>2M_\infty+1/100\). The
[real-power interpolation](research_real_power_source_transport.md)
keeps the full original crossing values and first normals, with
polynomial bounds uniform on compact power intervals. Consequently
both the radical and midpoint estimates persist along the path
from the proved long pair \((64,64)\) to \((3,3)\).
Its exact parameter equation still contains an uncontrolled bulk
insertion. The new proof treats the endpoint \((3,3)\) directly;
it does not prove survival of the coefficient along this whole path.

The [complete-boundary coefficient recurrence](research_complete_boundary_coefficient_transport.md)
gives another exact formulation. The internal pair is the bilinear
sum \(w_n^{\mathsf T}w_p\); for equal powers its Fourier version
is the integral of a square, without complex conjugation.
The vector \(w_n\) satisfies a uniquely normalized finite
difference equation. At power three its leading equation has
four distinct roots at every interior real index, but this does
not select the contributing asymptotic branch. Reversing one
power produces the positive norm \(\|w_n\|_2^2\), rather than
the same-sign invariant.

There is now a proved limitation on using that positive norm.
For every sufficiently large fixed integer \(n\), the opposite-sign
pair has geometric rate larger than the same-sign pair by
\(16\pi^3/n^6+O(n^{-7})>0\). The same-sign bilinear sum is therefore
exponentially smaller than \(\|w_n\|_2^2\), although its own
geometric coefficient is nonzero. This rules out a general
phase-coherence lower bound in the original coefficient norm.
The proof also quantifies the exponential conditioning needed
for a pairing-preserving change of coordinates to restore
coherence. It leaves appropriately weighted complex contours
available. The internal pair theorem uses such a contour for powers
three, retaining the original bilinear coefficient instead of replacing
it by the positive opposite-power norm.

The individual low kernel cannot replace that joint solution.
Its exact difference equation has cutoff forcing whose off-grid
rate exceeds the geometric edge rate at the power-three point.
In contrast, [discrete Parseval applied to the actual radical](research_high_newton_radical_contraction.md#7-fourier-bounds-for-the-original-radical-polynomials)
gives a Fourier coefficient norm at most \(\sqrt{N-1}\) for every
radical basis polynomial, and polynomial bounds over the entire
real period. These statements explain why contraction and the
choice of contour matter.

A [certified frozen-collar calculation](research_edge_cut_energy_comparison.md#5-the-two-new-vertices-cannot-be-the-only-variables-changed)
also rules out proving the general energy comparison by moving
only the two newly filled vertices. Even their optimal adjustment
can cost more than \(4G\) when the old halves are held fixed.
Any such constructive gluing proof must let some old collar
coordinates relax. The unrestricted energy comparison remains open.

Two uniform composition results are now available. The
[recursive tree theorem](research_recursive_high_valence_source.md)
uses one sufficient internal-degree threshold independent of tree
size and depth; internal powers are arbitrary and terminal powers
have magnitude at least two. The
[fixed-domain turn theorem](research_fixed_domain_long_power_turns.md)
instead permits chains of arbitrary fixed length, with an initial
terminal power of magnitude at least two and one common lower bound
on the magnitudes of all subsequent powers. Their signs are arbitrary.

The [combined tree theorem](research_hybrid_tree_filling_closure.md)
now permits these two operations in one tree, with thresholds
independent of its size, depth, and branching. The
[two-boundary block theorem](research_finite_two_boundary_kernel_closure.md)
also allows arbitrarily many short powers \(2\) or \(-2\) along
a path, provided successive short turns are separated by eligible
long powers. Both statements include the final scalar closure and
the original Kashaev volume identity under the stated knot conditions.

The [two-class reset theorem](research_alternating_long_and_nonzero_turns.md)
now removes the restriction to those two short values. There is one
threshold for alternating long powers and arbitrary nonzero powers,
independent of the intervening integers and the fixed word length.
The proof restores a fixed bare-edge class after each long turn;
it does not require the intervening powers to come from a set chosen
in advance.

For arbitrary same-sign chains of powers \(2\) or \(-2\), an exact
marked reduction replaces each pendant chain by one terminal twist,
and a new interpolation estimate also gives the unreduced chain's
full boundary asymptotic. The mixed pendant pair with powers
\(2,-2\) now also has a complete boundary asymptotic, proved directly
for its original finite polynomial, and its complete rate is exactly
the volume of the specified augmented complement. The original
peripheral curves and its full geometric deformation are now identified,
so the literal closure satisfies the volume conjecture for every
sufficiently large fixed odd final twist of either sign.
Connected cores with other adjacent powers and
the reductions caused by terminal powers \(0,\pm1\) remain.

There is also a specified family containing both short powers
\(-2\) and \(-3\). The
[binary-chain reduction](research_binary_negative_corridor_positive_reexpression.md)
replaces a pendant word consisting of runs of \(-2\), separated
by single \(-3\)'s, by a positive continued-fraction word and one
crossing at its remaining boundary. The new powers are the old
run lengths plus two or three. If these powers satisfy the proved
long-turn bounds, the original pendant has a nonzero full boundary
asymptotic, and every sufficiently long signed closing twist gives
the original Kashaev volume identity. There may be arbitrarily many
separating \(-3\)'s. This is a consequence of the existing long-word
theorem and an exact marked tangle identity; it does not estimate
an arbitrary short component. The free closing power changes by
\(a\mapsto a+1\), so distinct remaining assignments are retained.

There is now a complete boundary theorem for
[every nonzero power at an isolated degree-two vertex](research_all_nonzero_degree_two_fillings.md).
Both neighboring boundary variables remain free, and the estimates
include the whole real period and a fixed complex neighborhood.
Consequently the two-boundary version of the same-sign
\(2\)-crossing chain is covered at every fixed length as well.
This removes the entire missing degree-two power range. It does not
yet estimate an arbitrary connected group of different short powers.

The [isolated-vertex theorem](research_isolated_vertex_coverage_and_assembly.md)
is now complete in every degree: its exact condition is
\(d+|n|>2\). The analytic estimates cover the unbounded parameter
range, and the remaining 6,369 pairs all passed the common contour
certificate. A separate checker verified the complete parameter set,
hashes and rational subdivisions of all 121,011 contour domains.
Thus arbitrary nonadjacent fixed short fillings in this domain can
precede independent long fillings at the remaining vertices.

The resulting
[finite-pattern deduction](research_finite_short_patterns_and_exceptional_dimension.md)
places every untreated assignment in that domain on one of finitely
many slices fixing an adjacent pair of powers. In a surgery box of
radius \(H\), there are \(O(H^{d-2})\) such assignments for a template
with \(d\) vertices. This is a finite set when \(d=2\); it need not be
finite when \(d>2\).

Two further reductions now help with the connected short regions.
The [rational-corridor theorem](research_rational_corridor_compression.md)
gives an exact test for replacing a fixed rational tangle between two
attachments by one internal twist and constant twists at its ends.
For its boundary matrix
\(G=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\),
with \(c\ne0\), the test is
\(a\equiv d\equiv\epsilon\pmod{|c|}\) for one common
\(\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}\). The theorem retains the boundary half-turn,
arbitrary attached tangles, and the original integer parameters.
For disjoint corridors passing this test, the surviving parameters
undergo an injective translation. The isolated-vertex theorem
therefore applies after the reduction. The test does not cover
every rational corridor.

The more general
[continued-fraction normal form](research_definite_rational_corridor_normal_form.md)
does cover every nonintegral rational corridor. It replaces the fixed
word by a chain of negative powers of magnitude at least two, together
with fixed twists at the ends and the prescribed proper rotation.
The exact quantum identity includes its scalar power of
\(\kappa_N\). Thus a full boundary theorem for these uniform-sign
chains would transfer to arbitrary rational corridors; the existing
single-vertex theorem supplies the unit cases. The normal form
does not itself prove that boundary theorem or eliminate branching.

There is an explicit geometric result for these normalized chains.
The [negative-corridor variational theorem](research_negative_corridor_variational_bounds.md)
proves that the minimum is interior if every selected negative
power has magnitude at least three. The criterion is independent of
the path length. Its proof classifies all possible corner minima,
then combines the filling equations with a strict direction for
nonnegative incidences. Analytic inequalities reduce the possible
corners, in this range, to adjacent magnitudes three and four or
three and five. A complete rational interval certificate excludes
both remaining compact angle domains.
This establishes the positive solution of the original logarithmic
period equations at complete outside boundaries and unit filling
charges. The [pointwise completion theorem](research_positive_point_marked_completion.md)
now identifies this solution with the actual original marked
hyperbolic filling. A positive contraction to the complete cells fixes
the full peripheral periods; only its endpoint has to satisfy the
filling equations. The [cell-volume identity](research_positive_edge_volume_identity.md)
then gives the absolute hyperbolic volume from the stationary action.
Neither result supplies the coefficient of that solution in the
quantum period.

The [attached-pair geometry theorem](research_attached_even_reflected_pair_geometry.md)
now supplies a common complex boundary disk \(|u|<1/100\) for
every original degree-\((1,2)\) pendant pair whose two powers have
independent signs and magnitudes at least four. An explicit feasible
point has energy strictly below every boundary point, uniformly in
those powers and in the outside angle. The positive solution has
the original primitive slopes, absolute volume, and a uniformly
nonsingular boundary response. This differs from the closed reflected
knot: the second vertex keeps its outgoing edge and return term.
The quantum boundary estimate for the intermediate powers remains
unproved.

The same note proves a general sign lemma for interior positive
solutions on any original incidence network. Reversing all real
angle and incidence variables at one selected vertex leaves the
unconstrained energy unchanged. Strict convexity and the full
positive-charge filling equation then force its imaginary core
angle to be negative. Thus this sign is a consequence of the
original positive period equations, rather than an additional
hypothesis of the marked-completion theorem.

Theorem 15 of the negative-corridor variational note includes
arbitrary chains of magnitude three, and arbitrary mixtures of
the larger negative magnitudes.
The original selected-path hypotheses and complete outside ends
are retained. The
[exact interval replay](../repro/results/research-negative-three-corner-exclusion-root.json)
covers both entire angle rectangles with 104 rational subrectangles;
each violates a necessary period or outgoing-incidence inequality.
It treats terminal equality separately. Magnitude two remains
outside this geometric theorem.

The [original minus-two period equations](research_negative_two_chain_original_periods.md)
now have explicit solutions at every corridor and pendant length.
Their half-angle cosines satisfy a Chebyshev recurrence; the proof
retains the full primitive charges, regular face coordinates and
strictly negative imaginary parts of the selected angles.
Positivity of every original tetrahedron now follows for every
sufficiently long complete run, by Theorem 9 in Section 12.
Its proof bounds all indices in the middle uniformly and then
checks the finitely many end indices by their exact limits.
The resulting length threshold is existential. Shorter lengths
are not all covered by this argument. In a mixed negative
path with all magnitudes at least two, the same note also proves
