that the negative endpoint of any possible corner must have
magnitude exactly two. This locates the remaining folds but does
not justify removing a minus-two run from the original geometry.
The first edge of every selected pendant chain is now proved
positive. More generally, nonpositive imaginary parts of both
original endpoint returns imply positivity of all eight shapes
in an edge; the proof integrates the mixed Hessian of the
Euclidean norm. One return direction has the required sign
throughout the explicit pendant chain. The other is the inequality
(49), now proved uniformly for sufficiently long complete chains.
An exact
rational example with a complex outside boundary shows why
positivity cannot simply be propagated from one end without
using the other boundary condition.

Section 11 now eliminates any such run with both outside
half-angle cosines retained. A single Chebyshev equation
determines its parameter, and explicit formulas retain the two
original endpoint returns. The possible vanishing denominator
is excluded on the actual quadrant domain by a discrete
Dirichlet-eigenvector identity. On the calibrated regular branch,
the reduction gives exactly the boundary crossing shifts and the
new central primitive charge. It does not automatically give a
nondegenerate positive reduced chart: an example has positive
original cells while the reduced central angle is zero. These
formulas make the boundary matching exact.

Section 13 strengthens this to a uniform interior-positivity
theorem with both boundary values retained. If the two outside
half-angle cosines stay in a compact subset of
\(\{\Re z>0,\Im z\le0\}\), every sufficiently long run on
the specified small-center branch has positive original interior
blocks. Only the two attaching blocks remain to be checked.
The proof retains their return values and primitive slope shifts.
It does not solve the neighboring filling equations, prove the
attaching blocks positive, or supply the required quantum estimate.

For the binary negative chains just described, the complementary
positive presentation gives another geometric conclusion without
a long-run assumption. Its powers are all at least three, apart
from one isolated power two already covered by the terminal theorem.
The positive-cell geometry and absolute volume therefore follow
in the new marked presentation at complete outside boundaries.
This does not assert that every cell in the original negative
presentation is positive. Quantum asymptotics for these chains
are presently obtained only when the complementary word satisfies
one of the proved composition theorems.

The original-cell criterion also now covers a path with one
terminal magnitude two, all other magnitudes at least three,
and magnitude at least six at the terminal's neighbor. Section 10
of the [minus-two period note](research_negative_two_chain_original_periods.md)
proves that a corner with a negative incidence at such a terminal
would require its neighbor to have magnitude at most five.
The proof uses the terminal's exact real and imaginary filling
equations; the last excluded case is settled by elementary rational
bounds. This extends the geometric theorem at a terminal, while
general internal runs of twos and their quantum asymptotics remain.
The [complementation criterion](research_binary_negative_corridor_positive_reexpression.md)
also shows precisely why repeated whole-corridor complementation
alone cannot eliminate every internal two in the fixed outside frames.

The volume comparison has also been strengthened. Section 8 of the
[cell-volume note](research_positive_edge_volume_identity.md) gives
an explicit quadratic loss away from the selected positive angles,
and a loss of \(\pi\) times the core length for each added positive
integer filling charge. The comparison retains the original edge
relations. Section 9 proves the signed action-volume identity along
regular continuations of the same marked cells. When the original
primitive filling relations kill the peripheral matrices, the
representation-volume inequality bounds these critical actions by
the actual filled volume. Singular charts, other edge relations and
the coefficient of a critical point in the quantum sum remain outside
these conclusions.

The [near-maximal volume theorem](research_near_maximal_representation_volume.md)
now gives a uniform strict gap for regular critical representations
outside any fixed neighborhood of the complete holonomy. Its proof
allows the representations to vary or escape: volumes approaching
the maximum force convergence to holonomy after conjugation.
With a supplied positive complete ideal triangulation, relative
rigidity gives the gap for every other boundary-parabolic
representation. This is a known rigidity phenomenon, with an
independent proof and attribution in the note. It still groups all
decorations and logarithmic lifts of the same complete holonomy;
it does not prove their coefficient in the quantum period.

Corollary 4 extends this comparison to a small real box of free
boundary angles at one fixed integer partial filling. It requires
a positive complete triangulation and the original regular
geometric critical germ, with every remaining cusp parameter
specified. The signed boundary correction vanishes on that real
box, giving a uniform gap from every different regular critical
representation. This argument keeps the filling fixed throughout;
it does not apply filled-manifold rigidity to a nonintegral filling
path. Complex boundary angles and the coefficient of the geometric
contribution still require source estimates.

There are also new exact boundary equations for the quantum source.
The [primitive-cap factorization](research_quantum_cap_primitive_source.md)
uses three invertible sparse coordinates to carry every original
crossing and turn. One cap factor has a simple zero eigenvalue,
and its closing minor is an exactly normalized product of two
neighboring original source values. Multiplying by the second
factor recovers the full repeated-root cap and its modulus-square
normalization. The neighboring value can vanish while the desired
source is nonzero, so it cannot be divided away without proof.

For the primitive bidiagonal coordinate and the first even
crossing denominator, the
[weighted Green estimate](research_elementary_weighted_green_transport.md)
is sharp for every forcing vector. After explicit factorial weights,
the inverse norm is exactly
\([2\sin(\pi/(4N+2))]^{-1}\), hence proportional to \(N\).
In the ordinary norm these inverses have exponential growth, with
rates computed in the same note. The weighted bound therefore
controls elementary boundary errors while retaining their
exponential cost; it does not allow arbitrary compositions to be
treated as polynomially bounded.

For a complete run, a stronger cancellation identity is now proved.
The [crossing-run Schur construction](research_crossing_run_quantum_continuants.md)
replaces a fixed even run by a tridiagonal system with \(m\) internal
channels. After reordering by the original color, its full endpoint
response is \(N^2\mathcal R_{m,N}\), apart from a unit scalar.
The [cyclotomic determinant theorem](research_cyclotomic_endpoint_monodromy.md)
proves that \((-1)^N\mathcal R_{m,N}\) is positive definite with
the exact eigenvalues
\[
       \left[4\sin^2\frac{(2k-1)\pi}{4m+2}\right]^{-1},
                         \qquad k=1,\ldots,m.
\]
They are independent of the level. Its proof uses a finite
quantum-oscillator identity and a cyclic block determinant;
reflection pairs the original colors at both parities.
Thus the entire endpoint response has upper and lower bounds
proportional to \(N^2\), despite exponential growth at intermediate
colors. A specified off-diagonal entry may still vanish. The
original caps and turns must be shown to select a controlled
pairing when several runs are joined. This remains an operator
result, and does not enlarge the proved volume-conjecture class
or change the exception count above.

The distinction between that endpoint map and the actual state is now
explicit. In the [resonant run construction](research_resonant_crossing_run_source.md),
the original column \(M^p\mathbf e_0\) is the residue at the clock
eigenvalue one. This adds a last-channel boundary term which is absent
from the bounded endpoint problem. The residue fixes the initial
vector and its scalar. For every fixed signed power, all subsequent
original coefficients obey an exact recurrence in
\(\lceil|p|/2\rceil\) coordinates. Its apparent color poles cancel,
and all coefficients are bounded polynomials on the physical circle.
The same construction recovers every matrix column and all free-boundary
normal derivatives.

The [two-run recurrence](research_two_run_source_transfer.md) then
retains an actual turn and the complete signed color sum in
\(\lceil|a|/2\rceil\lceil|b|/2\rceil+1\) coordinates. The last
coordinate accumulates the original bilinear pairing. Thus powers
\((-4,-5)\) give a seven-dimensional recurrence for the original
scalar, rather than a substitute positive contraction. The recurrence
has been checked against every original paired-color contribution
before the scalar sum. Its whole-product asymptotic is still needed.

The [characteristic and reset theorem](research_crossing_source_characteristic_and_reset.md)
proves that each limiting source characteristic polynomial recovers
the original transported cap symbol, including its square and all
elementary factors. It also proves a nonzero initial mode on a fixed
small color interval for every signed power. For even powers its rate
is an explicit eigenvalue integral together with the original sine
factorial. For odd powers the initial classical mode is the constant
root minus one, and the actual coefficients there are bounded above
and below by positive constants. These are local color statements;
they do not continue a selected mode around the entire circle.

Finally, the [full-period source identity](research_two_run_monodromy_source_jets.md)
expresses the actual two-run scalar as a specified zeroth, first, or
second derivative of a marked matrix entry. The order is the number
of even crossing powers. A characteristic polynomial omits this
entry, and an unmarked analytic similarity can remove it even while
fixing the boundary frame at the physical point. Any extension of
the cyclotomic determinant theorem must therefore keep the marked
boundary vectors and the relevant derivatives of the conjugating
matrix. The original source is now located exactly in that data;
its geometric exponential rate remains unproved in general.

The [resonant monodromy theorem](research_resonant_source_monodromy_characteristic.md)
now supplies the classical polynomial for the actual source,
including its last-channel boundary condition. For every nonzero
signed power, the complete quantum product has exactly the same
characteristic polynomial as its classical transfer evaluated at
the \(N\)-th power of the clock, with the level-parity sign stated
in the theorem. This includes odd powers. The proof uses cyclic
block determinants and an explicit quantum-oscillator relation;
the second boundary term and its scalar are retained throughout.
For two runs the parity signs cancel. Consequently the denominator
of their exact affine transport equation is a fixed classical
polynomial \(D_{a,b}(x^N)\), independent of the level apart from
that substitution. Here \(x\) is an auxiliary color coordinate;
this statement does not identify it with a meridian eigenvalue.

For every even run, the [simple-spectrum and marked-kernel
theorem](research_even_run_simple_spectrum_and_marked_kernel.md)
now gives a stronger description of the backward period. Its
characteristic polynomial is exactly that of the classical
backward channel matrix at \(x^N\), with the stated parity sign.
After subtracting its common scalar pole, the whole matrix is
polynomial of degree at most \(N\). A disjoint-sector argument
proves that its classical Jacobi spectrum is simple on the full
closed auxiliary disk. The exact quantum spectral projectors
therefore extend holomorphically across that disk, including zero.

At the physical reset the original endpoint state is precisely
the zero-eigenvalue line. Its left-right pairing is the exact
nonzero value \((-1)^NkN/q\), so a specified projector column
recovers the original state with no normalization ambiguity.
This follows from a determinant derivative and the original
source equations. It supplies the selected quantum line and
marked section, not just its characteristic polynomial.
The norms of these projectors away from the reset, the growth
on partial color intervals, and pairings at subsequent turns
still require estimates. Eigenvalue collisions are now excluded
for this family; changes in modulus ordering are not excluded.

The [odd-run theorem](research_odd_run_simple_spectrum_and_marked_kernel.md)
now proves the corresponding simple-spectrum and normalized-kernel
statements for every odd signed power. More strongly, its selected
line has a unique primitive polynomial vector satisfying the exact
color transport equation and the original cap normalization. Every
source coefficient is a value of this vector at a root of unity,
times a specified phase. The proof constructs a cyclic average,
clears its invariant denominator, and removes the common polynomial
factor without changing any physical value.

The [odd scalar recurrence](research_odd_primitive_scalar_recurrence.md)
also reconstructs that vector from one scalar difference equation,
of order bounded by the fixed crossing power, together with every
original cap condition. For powers three, the primitive polynomial
is explicit. Its reversed coefficients are the classical
Rogers--Szegő polynomials evaluated at one, and discrete Parseval
gives the original reflected norm exactly. A separated coefficient
mode proves a positive exponential lower bound. The literal
reflected closure in this odd example has two components; this is
source information and is not a new knot volume theorem.

The [full three-crossing profile](research_three_crossing_full_coefficient_profile.md)
now gives substantially more control of this original column.
Its exact first-order equation has a one-crossing forcing term.
The known nonzero endpoint fixes the scalar, and reciprocal
factorial tails prove that on each closed interval of upper-half
colors the coefficient is a single scalar times
\(q^{j(j+2)}S_j^2\), with exponentially small relative error.
The full column also has a relative \(O(N^{-1})\) Euclidean-norm
approximation by its explicit factorial vector, through both
parities. This yields the sharp positive reflected-link norm.
The exponentially accurate statement is presently at the discrete
colors; moving it through a further signed operator or a boundary
kernel of degree growing with \(N\) requires retaining its exact
inhomogeneous current.

The [full boundary-current calculation](research_three_crossing_boundary_current.md)
now retains that current at every polynomial degree. For the adjacent
pendant pair with powers \((3,3)\), and its negative mirror, it gives
a unique endpoint-forced system with six diagonals. Its coefficients
are explicit in the original color variable and its determinant is
exactly a unit. A cofactor formula then expresses the entire ordinary
boundary polynomial as a determinant with two lower and four upper
diagonals, including the derivatives at repeated physical roots.
The associated classical curve has an explicit rational parameter;
its intersections with the free boundary reduce to two quartic
equations. The proof and the original-matrix checks include the
prescribed forcing at the final color. Neither the unit determinant
nor the classical curve bounds the inverse or proves a nonzero
geometric contribution. This is an exact reduction of the next
short-pair problem, not a further volume theorem.

The [geometric branch calculation](research_three_crossing_pendant_geometric_branch.md)
identifies which quartic root belongs to the original negative pair.
If \(\tau=-2\cos\alpha\) is its inner selected trace, the full
primitive equations give
\[
 (\tau-2)^2(\tau^2-2\tau+2)=2i\cos(u/2).
\]
At the complete outside cusp, its root is the unique one in
\(|\tau-(0.944+1.303i)|<0.001\). Exact rational root isolation
and positivity select it, and the original outgoing meridian and
longitude agree with the rational curve on a fixed holomorphic
germ. Thus the geometric branch, its marking and its volume
normalization are now determined. Proving that its contribution
survives in the endpoint-forced quantum determinant remains open.

The [kernel and endpoint-sector calculation](research_three_crossing_kernel_and_boundary_tail.md)
also gives a reason to estimate the composed source before taking
absolute values. For every integer crossing power \(p\), let
\(E_{p,N}\) be the high-degree half of its original terminal
polynomial. Off the real boundary, on compact sets with
\(|\Im w|>1\), this entire sector is
\(\kappa^p e_{N-1}(w)(1+O(N^{-2}))\), including fixed
holomorphic derivatives. At \(w=-2\cos u\) its exponential
rate is \(|\Im u|\). Yet after any one original closing twist,
its contribution has the uniform bound
\[
 \bigl|\phi_N(R^a E_{p,N})\bigr|\le \frac76N^2
 \qquad (a,p\in\mathbb Z).
\]
This follows from an exact bilinear sum and the proved original
low-color bounds. Thus the exponential size of an intermediate
boundary sector need not be its size after closing. The estimate
does not extend automatically through another turn or an arbitrary
attached tangle. The same note gives an explicit finite product
formula for the first boundary kernel, with its full central
forcing retained until the cyclic iteration is complete.

The [three-crossing Fourier theorem](research_three_crossing_fourier_packet.md)
now proves a lower bound for actual Fourier coefficients of the
original column after removing its specified quadratic phase. The
normalized vector is \(O(N^{-1})\)-close to the positive envelope
\(S_j^2/\|S^2\|_2\). Its Fourier coefficients have an explicit
nonzero Gaussian profile in every window \(|m|\le T\sqrt N\);
in particular its constant coefficient is asymptotic to
\((2/\sqrt3)^{1/4}N^{-1/4}\). Its cyclic-shift defect is
\(\sqrt{\pi\sqrt3/N}+O(N^{-1})\). Positivity and the controlled
error prove the coefficient lower bound; almost-invariance alone
would not do so. The original turn reflects and shifts this window
exactly. The next crossing is now controlled as described below;
the prescribed final boundary observation is proved by the separate
local boundary theorem described below.

For \(\alpha=M^3e_0\), the
[next-crossing source theorem](research_three_crossing_next_step_profile.md)
chooses an exact finite scalar \(A_N\) for which
\(\alpha-\kappa^3A_Nh\) is polynomially bounded in every coordinate.
The original vector \(\gamma=MJ\alpha\) satisfies a second-order
recurrence with known nonzero endpoint values. A direct reverse-triangle
estimate gives a coefficient lower rate strictly above \(1/3\),
whereas the original crossing operator has norm rate strictly below
\(1/3\). The propagated error is consequently exponentially smaller
than that actual coefficient. The exact scalar is necessary: replacing
it by its leading asymptotic would lose the polynomial remainder.

The [dominant-profile proof](research_three_crossing_next_crossing_dominant_profile.md)
retains the endpoint forcing and proves a nonzero complex amplitude
on both outer halves of the color interval. The
[global Fourier theorem](research_three_crossing_next_crossing_fourier.md)
then bounds the middle interval and proves a unique nondegenerate
maximum at \(x_*\), where \(2\cos(2\pi x_*)\) is the unique real root
of \(z^3-2z^2-z+3=0\). After its explicit phase correction, the
normalized actual output has
\[
 \widehat v_N(m)=
 (4\pi/a)^{1/4}N^{-1/4}e^{-2\pi imx_*}
 e^{-2\pi^2m^2/(aN)}(1+O_T(N^{-1/2})),
 \qquad |m|\le T\sqrt N,
\]
where \(a=-A''(x_*)>0\) and \(A\) is the explicitly defined
growth function. Its shift defect is
\(\sqrt{a/(2N)}+O(N^{-1})\). This proves a second nonzero Fourier
window in the original source, through one additional crossing,
along all integer levels and at both signs.

The [boundary-pairing audit](research_three_crossing_boundary_pairing_audit.md)
keeps the distinction between a norm and the actual observation explicit.
The short pair uses
the coherent contraction
\(F_N(w)=(M^3\mathbf e(w))^{\mathsf T}(M^3e_0)\).
Its two Fourier factors are not supplied by the one-vector norm
theorem. At \(w=-2\), the first two original summands already have
different phases for every \(N\ge10\), ruling out a direct positive
diagonal pairing. The output profile and its nonzero amplitude are
therefore inputs to the boundary proof, not a replacement for that
proof or for the finite-exclusion goal.

The next-crossing result now also reaches the actual complex clock
needed by that contraction. The
[marked saddle calculation](research_three_crossing_geometric_remaining_saddle.md)
identifies the geometric point with the endpoint-selected recurrence
branch, retains the required Fourier alias, and proves that the local
two-variable Hessian has negative definite real part. The required
clock is
\(X_*=1/(\tau^2-3\tau+3)\), where
\((\tau-2)^2(\tau^2-2\tau+2)=-2i\) and
\(\tau\) lies near \(0.944-1.303i\).

The
[lower-half-disk transform bound](research_next_crossing_lower_half_disk_error.md)
applies to arbitrary original input columns. It shows that polynomial
input errors remain polynomial on \(0<|X|\le13/20\),
\(\operatorname{Im}X\le0\), including fixed derivatives on interior
compact sets. This region contains \(X_*\). It therefore controls
the entire exact remainder, rather than continuing an \(O(N^{-1})\)
real-grid approximation without an error estimate.

Using that bound, the
[complex next-crossing theorem](research_three_crossing_complex_next_step.md)
proves for the actual finite polynomial
\[
 G_N(X)=N^{-1/2}\omega_N B(X)e^{NS(X)}(1+O(N^{-1}))
\]
on a fixed complex neighborhood of \(X_*\), with \(B\) holomorphic
and nonzero and \(\Re S>1/20\). The exact factorial sum has a
quadratic stationary equation. Strict horizontal concavity,
vertical convexity, both real tails, and the full upper/lower
residue corrections give its global one-variable contour proof.
The scalar inequalities and the zero logarithmic lift are certified
by outward rational arithmetic. The original polynomial forcing
and the noninteger factor \(X^{N-1}\) are retained.
The action and leading amplitude agree exactly with the specified
continuation of the original recurrence profile: the proof fixes
the additive action constant and the square-root sign. It therefore
also proves the actual canonically interpolated column \(\gamma\)
near the complex color required by the final geometric saddle.

Thus analytic continuation of this intermediate source, with a
nonzero coefficient at the required complex clock, is now proved.
The remaining operation is the full double sum
\(F_N(w)=\mathbf e(w)^{\mathsf T}JM^2\gamma\).
The [global preparation estimate](research_three_crossing_global_preparation_error.md)
now carries the exact factorial replacement through this entire
contraction. Its remainder has rate below \(3/2\), including all
original colors and ordinary boundary derivatives. The same note
removes the outer real color ranges, leaving
\(1/10\le j/N\le1/2\) and \(1/10\le i/N\le2/5\),
with an error rate at most \(4507/3000<153/100\).
The [absolute action calibration](research_three_crossing_action_volume_calibration.md)
identifies the selected stationary rate with the original partial
exterior volume divided by \(2\pi\); this rate exceeds \(153/100\).
Its proof retains the boundary correction while continuing to a
zero-volume degeneration.

The [full local boundary theorem](research_three_crossing_full_boundary_asymptotic.md)
now proves the geometric contribution in the original finite sum:
\[
 F_N(-2\cos u)=\kappa^2\omega_N C(u)e^{NW(u)}(1+O(N^{-1})),
 \qquad C(u)\ne0 .
\]
It holds on a fixed complex neighborhood of \(u=0\), along all integer
levels, and retains all fixed ordinary boundary derivatives.
The exact cellwise residue identity gives the principal integral
coefficient \(+1\). Seven horizontal estimates and the complete set
of 144 mixed-current inequalities put every other contour below
the selected rate. This supplies the nonzero coefficient that the
action calculation alone could not determine.

The [whole-period theorem](research_three_crossing_whole_period_source.md)
also proves the required global upper bound, with real angular
coefficient \(1/4000\). Its proof uses two Newton color cutoffs,
39 additional boundary inequalities, and the direct far-period
matrix estimate. It gives the thin complex strip and strict phase
curvature required by the existing closing theorem.

Consequently the
[long-closing theorem for the adjacent pair](research_three_crossing_long_closing_fiber.md)
settles the actual original filling fiber \((2,2,p)\), with the
outside carrier \(\eta\) fixed, whenever \(|\eta-2p|\ge B\)
for one finite threshold \(B\). At most \(B\) integers remain
untreated in that fiber. The mirror has fixed inner fillings
\((-2,-2)\) with the mirrored carriers. Both statements concern
the original Kashaev invariant along all integer quantum levels.

The same note also permits arbitrarily many copies of either
adjacent pair as pendant leaves in the existing hybrid tree
construction. There are common finite thresholds for the enlarged
family, independent of the number of copies: each attaching vertex
still needs sufficiently many children or a sufficiently long power.
That pendant theorem alone supplies no two-boundary placement.
The separate internal pair theorem now provides the required
two-boundary source for this block. Other connected short regions
remain, so the full finite-exclusion goal on an arbitrary fixed
template is still open.

The [lower-bound comparison](research_fourier_lower_bounds_and_almost_invariance.md)
separates this Newton-coefficient vector from the full
complete-color Fourier state. The latter already satisfies
\(\widehat c_N=K_Nu_N+e_N\), with \(e_N\perp u_N\) and
\(\|e_N\|^2\) bounded by a polynomial. Its absolute shift defect
is therefore polynomial. An exponential lower bound on its
actual positive norm would prove the needed lower bound on
\(K_N\). The positive comparison partitions currently provide
Cauchy upper bounds instead. The note gives precise spectral-gap
and observation hypotheses for using almost-invariant vectors,
and a direct lower-bound lemma for a controlled positive envelope.

The [original observation calculation](research_original_almost_invariance_and_observation.md)
shows why those hypotheses cannot be suppressed. Actual geometric
Casimir quasimodes have exponentially small overlap with the
original cap rows. An exact adjoint approximate mode of
\(C-qX\) has an exponentially small residual, but its overlap with
the specified endpoint forcing is equally small. The adjacent-pair
equation has a natural Hermitian form of exactly known indefinite
signature; its full boundary value is a specified inverse matrix
element, not a positive quadratic form. These results identify
the estimate still needed and do not add a finite-exclusion theorem.

For even powers, the [cyclic descent theorem](research_even_run_cyclic_descent.md)
constructs an algebraic holomorphic vector on the whole auxiliary
disk. Its only additional scalar extension is a specified root
\(a_{k,N}(X)^N=\psi_k(X)^{-1}\), where \(\psi_k\) is a
nonvanishing classical function and \(\psi_k(1)=1/k\).
The original coefficients are exactly its root-of-unity values
multiplied by the universal quantum factorial, a phase, and the
bounded factor \(k^{j/N}\). Common zeros away from the physical
orbit can be removed by an invariant polynomial, giving a
nowhere-zero algebraic frame with the same original coefficients.
The finite cyclic descent is the classical Hilbert 90 mechanism;
the source normalization and explicit sampled functions are proved
in these notes.

Thus all nonzero signed powers have specified functions giving
their original coefficients, rather than just a characteristic
curve or an unspecified solution line. This is progress toward the
torsor approach. It does not yet determine the exponential size of
those functions, or prevent cancellation when they are paired at a
turn. In particular, these descent results do not reduce the
exceptional-assignment count stated above.

The [selected scalar-period theorem](research_two_run_selected_scalar_period.md)
now carries this restriction through an actual two-run closing
pairing. For every nonzero signed pair giving a one-component
closure, the normalized tensor section turns the full affine
matrix equation into one scalar cyclic equation. Its only
denominator is \(1-\chi(X)\), where \(\chi\) is the product of
the two selected classical periods. All other matrix resonances
are removable in this specified scalar projection. An explicit
finite sum gives its numerator, including every physical color,
and its value at \(x=Q\) recovers the original invariant with the
full phase. The first or second reset coefficient is also fixed.
For a mixed odd/even pair, the selected denominator is independent
of the odd magnitude; its influence remains in the polynomial
section and numerator. Thus the denominator alone cannot give
the invariant or its volume. The remaining scalar sum still
requires a growth and noncancellation proof, and this result is
not a theorem for arbitrary inputs or general free boundaries.

The source-jet note also checks the actual outside arcs. Their
two-run closure is a knot precisely when at least one crossing
power is even. In these cases the denominator equals one on the
physical clock orbit and the affine row is regular there. The
original invariant is its specified first or second derivative.
Thus the classical denominator has been determined, while the
growth and noncancellation of the marked numerator remain the
analytic problem. These exact identities do not yet add a new
case to the volume theorem or reduce the exceptional set.

There is now an exact way to determine that numerator as well.
The [marked Laurent numerator theorem](research_two_run_marked_laurent_numerator.md)
proves that it is the unique solution of an explicit forced
matrix difference equation. Its Laurent coefficients satisfy a
finite linear system with bandwidth independent of \(N\); the
number of coefficients grows linearly with \(N\) for fixed powers.
All resonant coefficient equations are retained. The original
two-run invariant is exactly
\[
 \mathcal Z_{a,b,N}
   =\kappa^{a+b}\bigl(1+P_N(Q)w_0\bigr),\qquad
                  Q=e^{2\pi i/N}.
\]
Here \(P_N\) is that uniquely determined Laurent row, \(w_0\) is
the original reset vector, and \(|\kappa|=1\). Thus the remaining
limit concerns an explicitly specified polynomial evaluation;
it does not require choosing an unspecified solution of an
annihilating operator. The same note identifies the possible
poles over a simple classical denominator root with a finite
marked period on its cyclic invariant line. It does not prove
that period nonzero or estimate its growth. The required volume
asymptotic, including cancellation in the displayed evaluation,
remains open for the untreated cases.

For opposite even runs, there is a further source-specific
noncancellation result. The
[reflected-period theorem](research_reflected_run_marked_period.md)
proves that a unit-modulus cyclic mode has marked period
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^N |(u_j)_k|^2
       \ge \frac{48}{49^k-1}\sum_{j=1}^N\|u_j\|^2>0.
\]
The original tridiagonal equations prove the inequality without
dividing by a color weight. For every fixed pair \((2k,-2k)\)
and every level, the classical characteristic curve supplies
such a mode. Hence the actual affine row has nonremovable
poles at the corresponding auxiliary clocks; they cannot be
canceled by its numerator. One of these poles is within
\(\pi/N\) of the physical reset, which also rules out a common
fixed holomorphic disk in that auxiliary coordinate. This is
noncancellation of a specified resonant period. Its hyperbolic
rate and its comparison with the original scalar evaluation
still require proof, so it does not enlarge the finite-exception
theorem.

Section 6 of the [selected scalar-period note](research_two_run_selected_scalar_period.md)
now proves that such a pole also occurs in the actual selected
source line for every reflected even pair. Its positive cyclic
observation sum gives a polynomial lower bound on the leading
Laurent coefficient after division by the selected vector's squared
norm. This normalization is necessary: a zero-free invariant change
of frame can change the absolute residue exponentially while fixing
every physical source coefficient. The theorem therefore retains
the remaining comparison with the physical source.

The [backward source theorem](research_even_run_backward_source_growth.md)
now determines the actual endpoint vector for every positive even
crossing power. Its leading projections onto all nonconstant
Neumann path modes are explicit and nonzero. A separated dominant
mode then gives the original coefficient asymptotic on a fixed
short color interval. Consequently the positive reflected source
\(\phi_N(R^{-2k}T(R^{2k}))\) has strictly positive exponential
growth for every fixed \(k\ge2\). The same note gives a rigorous
upper envelope over all colors. The sharper comparison below now
identifies the full logarithmic rate.

The [middle-color contraction theorem](research_even_run_middle_color_contraction.md)
controls a different part of the same equation. Across the middle
half of the colors, every backward channel vector contracts at a
uniform exponential rate, up to one fixed prefactor. The estimate
holds for every physical input column, without selecting an
eigenvalue branch. For \(k\ge2\) internal coordinates, the sharper
bound is a factor \(1-1/(64k^2)\) for each pair of successive
steps, once \(N\ge2048k^2\). Its proof combines the strict
first-row loss with the elementary energy estimate for a tree
joining the two parity classes of coordinates. A local observation
matrix then bounds the whole vector by \(k\) adjacent original
coefficients. Consequently the full reflected norm is comparable,
with constants independent of \(N\), to the sum over its two
outer color quarters. The interior of the middle interval is
exponentially smaller.

The [uniform low-color theorem](research_original_low_color_bound.md)
now removes the lower quarter as well. For every signed integer
crossing power, its original Newton coefficients have modulus at
most \(\sqrt2\) on the first quarter, independently of the level
and even when the power depends on the level. The whole first half,
up to the last distinct physical node, has an explicit \(O(N)\)
bound. The proof uses ordinary divided differences of the unit
physical values and an exact telescoping sine-weight identity;
it makes no unsupported estimate on double-root derivatives.
Combining this with middle contraction shows that the reflected
even source has the same logarithmic rates as its upper color
quarter alone. Its upper rate is therefore bounded by the maximum
of the backward envelope on \([0,1/4]\).

The [sharp reflected-growth theorem](research_even_run_sharp_reflected_growth.md)
now proves that the selected original mode attains this maximum.
Before its normalized modulus falls below one, it strictly exceeds
every other mode. Its modulus crosses one at a unique point
\(x_k\in(0,1/4)\); afterward every mode has normalized modulus
less than one. The original endpoint coefficient is nonzero, so
the lower estimate and full-source upper estimate agree:
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
   \log\phi_N(R^{-2k}T(R^{2k}))=2B_k(x_k)>0
 \qquad(k\ge2).
\]
This holds through every integer level and for both crossing signs.
The [geometric-point calculation](research_even_reflected_run_geometric_point.md)
also proves that this critical point solves the two original
primitive filling equations and gives eight positive tetrahedra.
The corresponding literal reflected closure is a hyperbolic knot,
and its reduced Kashaev invariant has the modulus of the displayed
positive scalar. The [spectral transgression](research_reflected_even_spectral_volume_transgression.md)
now proves equality of the integrated rate with that absolute volume:
both actions have real-parameter derivative \(4\eta_k\varphi_k\)
and limit \(8G\) at infinity. The proof controls the moving logarithmic
endpoint and fixes the integration constant.

Consequently the [reflected even knot theorem](research_reflected_even_kashaev_volume_theorem.md)
proves the original Kashaev volume conjecture for
\(C(R^{-2k}T(R^{2k}))\) at every fixed integer \(k\ge2\),
through all integer levels. It also covers every original four-path
assignment \((m,0,-2k-m,2k)\), by the exact marked zero reduction.
For fixed \(k\), this includes infinitely many assignments of
one knot; those fibers have been treated rather than discarded.
The theorem still does not supply the boundary function or
noncancellation required after an arbitrary additional turn.

The [fixed-insertion theorem](research_even_reflected_casimir_insertions.md)
identifies additional original quantum data with this same geometry.
The full Newton coefficient column concentrates exponentially near
the unique spectral maximum. It is an approximate eigenvector of
the actual, nonnormal Casimir matrix, with limiting value
\(z_k=-2\cos(\varphi_k-i\eta_k)\). For fixed polynomials
\(P,Q\), the exact normalized inserted scalar therefore tends to
\(\overline{P(z_k)}Q(z_k)\). Fixed colors on the two original
filling cores recover their geometric holonomy characters, in the
transported disk framings, and have the same volume rate. These
fixed-degree conclusions do not provide bounds for degrees growing
with the level or for a further signed filling.

The [forced Green theorem](research_even_run_forced_middle_green.md)
extends middle contraction to every original input column, including
its resonant diagonal forcing. Its exact inhomogeneous formula
retains these sources, and it gives quantitative lower amplification
and upper localization bounds for the input-clock average of actual
outputs. Finite Fourier orthogonality identifies that average
exactly. A coherent output has the corresponding upper bound,
but no lower bound follows by averaging. The turn reverses the
response weights, which can differ exponentially. Moreover an
invertible crossing can send a legitimate arbitrary input to a
single middle color, so coherent localization cannot hold for
all inputs. The next composition theorem must use the prepared
input produced by the preceding tangle.

For opposite even runs, the [marked Stein energy
identity](research_reflected_laurent_stein_energy.md)
reshapes the original affine row into a Hermitian matrix equation.
At the physical clock its Green matrix is positive definite for
\(N\ge2k\), with inverse norm bounded by an explicit polynomial
in \(N\). Its prescribed quadratic form is the original reflected
source. Elsewhere its inertia is the stable/unstable eigenvalue
count of the actual monodromy. For every \(k\ge2\), the Laurent
numerator is indefinite on an open auxiliary arc. Thus a globally
positive Fourier symbol for this particular numerator is unavailable;
the physical positive identity and its polynomial inverse bound
remain valid. No signed joining or volume asymptotic is inferred
from that inverse bound.

There is now an [exact local system for an arbitrary rational
word](research_rational_word_local_source_system.md), including
every free input column and each turn. It uses a triangular pair
of color indices and a fixed number of internal coordinates per
crossing run. The equivalent finite generating-function equations
retain their explicit endpoint currents. A rank argument explains
why arbitrary free inputs cannot, in general, be processed by a
causal recurrence with a number of states independent of the level.
These are exact source identities. They supply the object to be
estimated, not a replacement for its asymptotic or a new
finite-exception conclusion.

The [free-boundary interpolation theorem](research_free_boundary_cardinal_factorial_comparison.md)
addresses a different issue. On every fixed compact rectangle
\(0<\alpha\le\Re x\le\beta<1/2\), the canonical Newton interpolation
and its sine-factorial expression differ by an exponentially smaller
term near the complete boundary. The proof controls the full
polynomial and all prescribed first derivatives, using exact Fourier
folding and an estimate of the discarded frequencies. This permits
the actual factorial phase in that part of the exact network
integral. It does not control the whole integral after cancellation.
An exact highest Fourier coefficient shows why the same estimate
cannot simply be extended around the entire index period.

The [turn-trace identity](research_turn_trace_residue_density.md)
also expresses the original closing functional as an ordinary matrix
trace with an explicit invertible density. That density is indefinite
and has its own exponential rate, so it does not turn the signed
source into a positive trace problem. The
[endpoint-normal calculation](research_endpoint_normal_cap_rate.md)
similarly shows that a contour endpoint term can have a larger rate
than the original source. It gives an exact example with a removable
unit crossing. These results rule out two shortcuts; they are not
additional volume-conjecture cases.

For terminal pieces, a
[common intrinsic trace domain](research_terminal_intrinsic_trace_domain.md)
is now proved. The selected root is the inverse of
\(P_p(k)=kU_{p-1}(k)\), where \(U_{p-1}\) is a Chebyshev
polynomial. On the upper half-plane in
\(w=i\cos(u/2)\), this branch takes values in the first quadrant
and its square satisfies the Schwarz--Pick inequality. This
continues the selected geometric phase to \(|\Re u|<\pi\).
It does not continue the quantum asymptotic to that whole strip.
The real part of the peripheral derivative can become negative
there, so a composition proof needs a domain adapted to the actual
gluing maps.

Finally, the [simultaneous-current formula](research_grouped_endpoint_current_matchings.md)
groups all endpoint derivatives into matchings of the removed
subgraph. On the entire original tree, the same product-rule
calculation gives a sparse determinant for each physical spectral
assignment. Summing these determinants retains the original
coherent source exactly. This organizes all first normals, but
does not prove cancellation bounds for that sum.

The [kernel difference equation](research_edge_kernel_difference_and_endpoint_bound.md)
makes this last question more explicit. It identifies the physical
kernel rows with a classical Askey--Wilson recurrence, and proves
the full polynomial equation with its physical-relation error term
retained. Its [extension to every physical color](research_all_color_path_normal_bound.md)
now proves \(H_{jk}\le\gamma_j\gamma_k\) for every pair of double
spectral roots. The full derivative determinant therefore has a
polynomial lower bound at every color assignment of a same-sign
path with powers of magnitude at least two. More generally, the
same statement holds on a filled tree whenever
\(\operatorname{diag}(|n_v|)-\operatorname{Adj}(G)\) is positive
definite. The proof includes every original first normal and both
level parities. Cancellation between different color assignments
remains: already the terminal power \(-2\) has an individual color
of rate \(M_\infty\), while its entire source has rate \(M_\infty/2\).
The determinant result is not a lower bound for that coherent sum.

There is now an exact formula for the coherent scalar of any fixed
rational word, rather than just its separate color contributions.
Let \(W_N\) be the original word in turns and crossings, let \(L_N\)
be the turned multiplication matrix, and set
\(D_{W,N}=W_N(L_N-c_0I)W_N^{-1}\), with
\(c_0=2\cos(\pi/N)\). The
[normalized-cofactor theorem](research_rational_word_normalized_cofactor.md)
proves
\[
 N^2|\phi_N(W_N1)|^2
   =(-1)^{N-1}
       \det D_{W,N}[\{1,\ldots,N-1\},\{0,\ldots,N-2\}].
\]
The matrix in this determinant has bounded bandwidth for a fixed
word, independent of \(N\); its entries are uniformly bounded.
All original derivative data and the normalization are retained.
The [weighted crossing transport](research_current_free_aw_crossing_transport.md)
provides the exact difference operators behind that assertion,
including the forcing at a free boundary.

The determinant has a limiting singular-value distribution, but
this alone does not determine its logarithmic growth. An exact
example in the cofactor note proves that distinction within the
original source: the word \(W_N=T R^2\) has closing scalar of modulus
one, whereas its bulk logarithmic mean is strictly positive.
An exponentially small singular value accounts for part of the
discrepancy. Thus this determinant formula does not yet extend the
volume theorem to arbitrary neighboring short twists. It gives a
precise alternative formulation of their cancellation problem.

The [cap-symbol factorization](research_rational_word_cap_square_factorization.md)
also computes, for every fixed rational word, an explicit integer
Laurent polynomial whose square is the non-elementary part of the
classical cap equation. It keeps the trace-coordinate label and
gives a simpler expression for the spectral upper bound. The
terminal counterexample survives this factorization, so its
logarithmic mean cannot be substituted for the scalar growth.
An [exact negative-pair calculation](research_negative_pair_diagonal_gauge_obstruction.md)
also rules out converting the general closing matrix to a real
matrix by diagonal row and column rescaling. It leaves methods
using coupled matrix blocks open.

There is nevertheless a positive energy for one elementary
conjugated cap. The
[path-Laplacian identity](research_elementary_cap_path_laplacian.md)
changes \(M^{-1}LM-c_0I\), by explicit unitary left and right
factors, into the Laplacian of a path with edge conductances
\(4\sin^2((j+1)\pi/N)\). Its Green matrix and all principal
cofactors are explicit. Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz gives a lower
bound \(8/(3N^2)\) for every nonzero singular value, at both
parities. This proves polynomial control of the elementary
inverse. General word transport is a nonunitary similarity,
so these bounds cannot be multiplied to obtain the missing
coherent-source estimate.

The current geometry and finite-source statements have independent
written checks and reproducible calculations. The
[full-normal replay](../repro/results/research-all-color-path-normal-bound-root.json)
uses 150-digit arithmetic and the defining Newton polynomials.
The [positive-cell replay](../repro/results/research-positive-edge-volume-identity-root.json)
compares eight Bloch--Wigner volumes, an explicit dilogarithm
primitive and integration of the original meridian form.
The [corridor replay](../repro/results/research-positive-corridor-completion-root.json)
solves sixteen original primitive systems and checks 900 positive edges
along their contractions. These finite calculations supplement the
proofs; they do not establish the quantum limit.
The [weighted-transport replay](../repro/results/research-current-free-aw-crossing-transport-root.json)
and [cofactor replay](../repro/results/research-rational-word-normalized-cofactor-root.json)
use 150-digit arithmetic and the original crossing matrices.
The [path-Laplacian replay](../repro/results/research-elementary-cap-path-laplacian-root.json)
also uses 150 digits, checking nineteen levels and 219 principal
cofactors against the original matrices.
The [action-comparison replay](../repro/results/research-circle-tree-action-comparisons-root.json)
checks the charge inequality, signed volume formula and a logarithmic
loop. None of these finite checks substitutes for the corresponding
written proof or for an estimate of the whole quantum period.

## What the finite-exception statement requires

An estimate that applies when every twist is sufficiently long misses
infinitely many assignments as soon as there are two parameters. For
example, one coordinate can remain equal to two while another tends
to infinity. The missed set has density zero in expanding boxes, but
it is not finite.

In terms of the original integer filling parameters, the change in
quantifiers is substantial. The all-long theorem applies when
\(\min_i|p_i|>B\). A finite-exception theorem would supply a finite
\(B_*\) and apply whenever \(\max_i|p_i|>B_*\), among assignments
giving hyperbolic knots. Thus even one coefficient tending to infinity
must eventually suffice, with arbitrary fixed values at all other
coordinates. The constants can depend on the template and its fixed
half-twist pattern. Neither condition concerns the quantum level:
every filling assignment is fixed before that level tends to infinity.

[The partial-filling reduction](research_finite_exceptions_under_partial_fillings.md)
gives the precise sufficient condition. Fix any short coefficients,
prove the volume identity when all remaining coefficients are
independently sufficiently long, and retain this statement under
further fixed partial fillings. At each step there are finitely many
short choices and one fewer free parameter. A finite tree of these
choices then leaves only finitely many complete assignments. The
thresholds may depend on every coefficient fixed earlier; no common
threshold over all partial fillings is required.

This is a reduction of the problem, not a proof of the required
stability theorem.

## Every fixed original terminal power is now covered

The new boundary estimates cover every signed terminal power
$|n|\geq2$. Here a terminal vertex is a vertex of degree one in the
original circle tree. Its source is kept as a function of the remaining
boundary angle, so that the result can be used inside another
contraction. A closed-knot asymptotic alone would not suffice.

The proof has three parts:

| Terminal power | Proof of the complete boundary estimate |
|---|---|
| $|n|=2$ | [An exact one-index formula and its contour estimate](research_two_crossing_terminal_filling.md). |
| $3\leq |n|\leq31$ | [The three-crossing proof](research_three_crossing_terminal_filling.md) and [one common interval certificate for powers four through thirty-one](research_terminal_powers_four_through_thirty_one.md). These control the selected saddle, every contour boundary, and the original lattice corrections. |
| $|n|\geq32$ | [One analytic proof for the entire unbounded range](research_terminal_large_fixed_powers.md), using the edge expansion near the complete boundary and a strict bound outside it. |

Each result gives a holomorphic asymptotic with a nonzero leading
coefficient, a global decay estimate for real boundary angles, and
a thin complex-strip bound. The sums retain every index and every
first normal derivative at a repeated spectral root. They apply to
both parities of the integer level. The crossing power is fixed before
the level tends to infinity.

Two common ingredients made the extension possible. The
[exact rational trace formula](research_exact_complete_trace_contour.md)
sums all positive Fourier charges before estimating them. The
[uniform factorial and boundary estimates](research_uniform_factorial_and_boundary_decay.md)
remain valid through moving zeros and provide decay in the unfilled
boundary angle. The detailed estimate for the retained edge is in
[the weighted edge proof](research_weighted_edge_contour_bound.md).

The exact identities for terminal powers zero and $\pm1$ are also
available. Zero gives cap splitting. A terminal power $\pm1$ can be
deleted while shifting its neighbor's power by $\mp1$. Those are
finite tangle identities, with the original marking and framing
correction retained. They do not automatically settle every knot
that can remain after a splitting or deletion.

## The resulting volume theorem

[Terminal fillings followed by independent long fillings](research_verified_terminal_fillings_and_long_remainder.md)
proves the following statement. Fix an ordered circle-tree knot
template with the prescribed strand matching. Choose any collection
of its original terminal vertices, leave at least one vertex, and
give those terminals arbitrary fixed signed powers of magnitude at
least two. All independently sufficiently long fixed signed powers
at the remaining vertices then satisfy the original Kashaev volume
identity. The threshold may depend on the chosen terminal powers.

The proof uses the entire finite source and gives a nonzero
$N^{3/2}$ leading term. Its exponential rate is the volume of the
actual knot complement: the primitive filling curves are retained,
and the absolute volume constant is fixed along the cone deformation
from the complete blocks. The
[filling theorem for a complex boundary phase](research_long_fillings_complex_boundary_phase.md)
allows the complex phase produced by terminal elimination; it does
not assume that its imaginary part is quadratic.

Thus entire infinite families with short terminal twists are now
treated. This is a partial-filling extension of the long-twist
theorem. It is not yet stability under every short partial filling.

## A finite-exception case is completed

[The two-circle corollary](research_two_circle_finite_exceptions.md)
does give finitely many untreated assignments for a fixed one-edge
template. Both vertices are original terminals. Fixing either short
power of magnitude at least two is therefore covered by the theorem
above; powers zero and $\pm1$ give only cap or two-strand torus
closures and do not produce hyperbolic knots. Taking the maximum of
the finitely many thresholds for the remaining short values leaves
all untreated pairs in one finite square.

This uses no threshold uniform over all terminal powers, and it
counts the original filling assignments. It is a completed special
case of the target. The argument does not extend to a tree with an
untreated short internal vertex.

The marked simplifications give another precise consequence. On a
three-vertex path, fixing any one of its powers to \(1\) or \(-1\)
reduces the other two parameters to a two-circle family by an
injective affine change. Each of these six slices therefore has only
finitely many untreated hyperbolic assignments. A zero power on that
three-vertex path gives only torus or unknot closures. The
[scope calculation](research_finite_exception_scope_audit.md#3-what-exact-simplification-can-transfer-safely)
proves these statements with the original rotations retained. They
do not establish a finite-exception theorem for the entire
three-parameter family.

## Short chains that can now be treated at every length

Consider a pendant chain of \(k\ge1\) vertices whose powers are all
\(2\sigma\), with \(\sigma=1\) or \(-1\). The
[marked chain identity](research_repeated_two_crossing_chain_reduction.md)
replaces it by one terminal of power \(-\sigma(k+1)\), and shifts
the neighboring power by \(-\sigma\). The proof uses the actual
four-endpoint boundary maps, carries the rotations of attached
branches, and retains the quantum framing scalar. It therefore
identifies the filled knot complements as well as their invariants.

The replacement terminal always has magnitude at least two. Any
collection of disjoint pendant chains of this form can consequently
be fixed first, with independently sufficiently long powers at the
remaining vertices. This proves the volume identity for entire
families of short adjacent twists, of arbitrary fixed chain length.
The same reduction applies when the remaining diagram meets the
recursive tree theorem's degree condition.

There is also a new estimate for the actual boundary polynomials,
proved in
[boundary multiplication](research_boundary_crossing_packet_preservation.md).
Suppose a source has a nonzero holomorphic leading term near its
complete boundary angle, and is exponentially smaller away from that
angle on the whole real period. Multiplying by any fixed crossing
power in the original Hermite quotient preserves these properties.
The proof controls the complete Fourier tail of the product and its
value-and-derivative interpolation; every repeated-root derivative
is retained. The canonical product differs exponentially little
from multiplication by the corresponding analytic Gaussian on the
real period and on a fixed small complex disk.

Applying this estimate after the chain identity gives the canonical
free-boundary asymptotic for every same-sign chain above. The angular
decay and complex neighborhood can be chosen independently of the
fixed chain length, using the uniform terminal theorem. This is
stronger than merely replacing the chain after it has been attached
inside a closed trace.

The same argument handles a fixed finite product of such concentrated
sources, followed by a fixed crossing power. A corresponding
unrestricted statement for quarter-turns is false. For example,
the concentrated terminal source \(H_p=T(R^p)\), \(|p|\ge2\),
turns back into \(R^p\), whose values have modulus one at every
physical spectral root. It cannot have both a nonzero leading
asymptotic near zero and strict exponential decay at the other
angles. A further composition theorem must use the geometric
conditions on the actual attached pieces, or also handle sources
without strict concentration. Arbitrary mixed-sign chains and general
short connected regions remain outside the present conclusion.

For instance, the three-vertex slice with powers \((2,-2,c)\),
where \(c\) is independently long with the knot parity, needs a
different argument from the same-sign reduction. The separate
analytic and marked geometric proofs below now settle its original
closure. General neighboring short powers are still untreated.
Nor can every intermediate
piece with no positive-volume boundary asymptotic simply be
discarded: its further attachment may still produce a hyperbolic
knot. These are precisely the sorts of fixed short assignments
that a general finite-exception proof must treat.

## Every nonzero isolated degree-two filling

An internal degree-two vertex has two remaining boundary variables.
Its original source is
\[
 P_{n,N}(u,v)=\phi_N^{(t)}[R^nK_N(t,u)K_N(t,v)].
\]
[The new theorem](research_all_nonzero_degree_two_fillings.md) proves,
for every fixed nonzero integer \(n\), a full expansion
\[
 P_{n,N}(u,v)=\epsilon_{n,N}N^{-3/2}
       A_n(u,v)e^{NS_n(u,v)}(1+O_n(N^{-1})),
 \qquad A_n\ne0,
\]
on a fixed complex bidisk. It also proves exponential decay away
from the complete boundary angles on the whole real torus and the
corresponding thin complex-strip bound. The constants may depend
on \(n\); both level parities are included.

The proof for magnitudes three through thirty-one uses an exact
reduction of the contour estimates. Once the trace angle is fixed,
the two wire variables are independent. Their three-variable phase
is the average of two copies of a scaled two-variable phase. This
averaging controls every combination of wire corrections provided
each wire penalty is scaled as well. The trace contour is written
first, so no unestimated interior deformation is introduced.
The same construction applies at arbitrary degree; its hypotheses
and proof are in
[the contour lifting theorem](research_scaled_wire_contour_lifting.md).

For the twenty-nine missing degree-two magnitudes, one parameterized
outward-arithmetic computation proves all nineteen required contour
bounds per power. It also certifies the algebraic critical point,
the local Hessian, and the discarded wire gap. The written proof
then checks the exact factorial domains, original trace normals,
all lattice charges, the nonzero Gaussian coefficient, and the free
boundary estimates. The full batch has been replayed at 210-bit
precision in
[the retained certificate](../repro/results/research-internal-degree-two-contours-all-root.json).
This is a proof of bounds for the full original polynomial, not a
fit to large-level numerical values.

The powers \(1\) and \(-1\) need no contour estimate of this kind.
If \(M\) is the original crossing matrix, \(J\) is Newton reversal,
and \(\kappa_N=q^{(N-1)^2/2}\), the braid relation gives
\[
 JM^\sigma=\kappa_N^\sigma M^{-\sigma}(M^{-\sigma})^T,
 \qquad \sigma=\pm1.
\]
This reduces the source to the bare edge with one canonical boundary
crossing on each side. The proved boundary multiplication estimate
applies, with exact cancellation of the scalar carriers. The marked
tangle identity retains the appropriate physical half-turn.
The existing proofs for magnitudes two and at least thirty-two
complete the nonzero integer range.

The consequence for an internal chain of \(k\) equal twists
\(2\sigma\) is now unconditional at every fixed length:
[the exact two-boundary reduction](research_internal_two_crossing_chain.md)
replaces it by power \(-\sigma(k+1)\), with the recorded boundary
crossings and rotations. The full estimate follows from the theorem
above. The previous untreated lengths two through thirty are no
longer exceptions to this source theorem.

There is also a degree-independent simplification of one contour
step. For every \(d,|n|\ge1\) with \(\max(d,|n|)\ge3\),
[the outer-angle argument](research_all_degree_outer_angle_gap.md)
proves that the original real angular nodes \(|t|\ge2\pi/3\)
have a gap greater than \(d/30\) below the selected action.
It uses the termwise kernel bound and the symmetry and monotonicity
of the classical action. The remaining central contour estimates
are now supplied by the completed generic certificate described below.

The wire cutoff can now be uniform as well. The
[uniform action-gap proof](research_uniform_isolated_wire_gap.md)
shows
\[
 M_{d,n}-(d-1)M_\infty>1/6
\]
for every allowed isolated integer pair except
\((2,1),(2,-1),(3,0)\), where this difference is exactly zero.
Consequently one interval, \([1/128,63/128]\), gives an omitted-wire
gap greater than \(1/60\) in every nonexceptional case. The proof
uses action monotonicity, the degree-power symmetry, and elementary
integral bounds; it does not scan the degrees or powers.
The three equality cases already have separate exact or zero-subtree
arguments. This removes a case-dependent cutoff from the remaining
central-contour work.

For the finite remainder
\[
 3\le d\le127,\qquad 1\le n\le63,\qquad
 d^2+n^2<\max(1024,128d),
\]
the [generic contour proof](research_generic_isolated_contour_certificates.md)
uses nineteen inequalities in two variables, with the wire penalties
scaled by \(d\). Exact averaging lifts these inequalities to the
full \(d\)-wire source. The
[completed manifest](../repro/results/research-isolated-scaled-all-manifest.json)
contains all 6,369 pairs. The separate
[archive check](../repro/results/research-isolated-scaled-all-integrity.json)
verified all hashes, the exact parameter set, and the subdivisions
covering 121,011 surface domains, with 6,389,640 accepted rational
boxes. It checks the recorded coverage independently; it does not
reevaluate the analytic interval inequalities. Those were evaluated
by the frozen outward-interval proof engine in the certificate run.
Negative powers follow by conjugation. Along with the terminal,
degree-two, zero-power and unbounded-range proofs, this establishes
the full condition \(d+|n|>2\).

## The mixed pair: a boundary asymptotic and its complete volume

For the fixed tangle word \(T(R^{-2}T(R^2))\), let \(Z_N(u)\)
be its original canonical boundary polynomial evaluated at
\(-2\cos u\). The
[mixed boundary theorem](research_mixed_two_crossing_boundary_theorem.md)
proves, on a fixed complex disk,

\[
 Z_N(u)=A(u)e^{NS(u)}(1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad A(u)\ne0.
\]

The statement holds through every integer level, with holomorphic
control of the error. It also bounds the full real boundary period
by a polynomial factor times
\(\exp N\{\Re S(0)-c(1-\cos u)\}\), for some \(c>0\), and
extends the estimate to a fixed complex strip. These are the analytic
properties required for attaching the tangle to another source.

The proof begins with an exact two-index sum. Its contour identity
has nine terms, including the combined vertical sides with their
nonconstant multiplier. A horizontal maximum argument gives the
selected contribution, and rational interval certificates bound
every other contour term strictly below it. The resulting rate is
\(\Re S(0)=1.22659310939050\ldots\). The numerical value is a
description of the exact selected action; it is not the justification
for identifying that action with geometric volume. The sign-reversed
word satisfies the conjugate theorem.

There is also an
[exact recurrence and action curve](research_mixed_pair_fourier_transport.md)
for the same source. A third-order recurrence, together with its
terminal values, determines all transformed Newton coefficients.
Its characteristic curve is exactly the first stationary equation
of the original sum. Eliminating both stationary variables gives an
explicit degree-five equation \(\mathcal Q(w,P)=0\), where
\(w=e^{iu}\) and \(P=e^{-2\pi S'(u)}\). The logarithmic branch,
resultant factors, and source normalization are retained. The marked
geometric comparison below now gives its peripheral interpretation:
in the positive-carrier chart, \(m=P/w\) and \(\ell=w^2\), so the
selected germ satisfies \(\mathcal Q(w,wm)=0\). This is a constrained
eigenvalue germ of the augmented link, with its main cusp complete;
it is not asserted to be the minimal A-polynomial of a filled knot.

The [positive subdivision](research_mixed_two_crossing_positive_subdivision.md)
now identifies the complete rate exactly. The specified augmented
complement \(M\) retains one crossing circle and has two cusps.
A recorded sequence of local triangulation moves starts from its
literal diagram and gives nine positive ideal tetrahedra. Their
shapes lie in the field defined by \(X^3+2X^2+1=0\).
Exact edge equations, angle bounds, and cusp similarity equations
give the complete metric. Five dilogarithm identities then prove

\[
 2\pi\Re S(0)=\operatorname{Vol}(M)
             =7.70691180281012665\ldots.
\]

Combining this with the nonzero asymptotic proves
\(\lim_N(2\pi/N)\log|Z_N(0)|=\operatorname{Vol}(M)\).
This is a volume limit for the original boundary polynomial of
the mixed tangle; it is not a closed-knot invariant assertion.

The volume theorem for its independently long attachments also
requires the selected deformation to be geometric, with the
original oriented meridian and disk longitude. This comparison
is now proved. The
[peripheral transport proof](research_mixed_two_crossing_peripheral_transport.md)
now carries explicit curves from the original diagram through 56
local triangulation moves. It checks their homology at every move
and computes their complete periods exactly. The clockwise diagram
longitude has ratio \(1+1/Y\); the source collar has ratio
\(-1-1/Y\). Their cubic minimal polynomial excludes an unrecorded
integer shear or a multiple of a primitive curve. One relative
orientation is reversed, and must be translated explicitly.

The [ordered representation proof](research_mixed_word_collar_representation.md)
now completes that comparison. It derives the group of the outside
crossing-circle piece directly from the five original diagram
crossings, with the rational tangle's four boundary generators
specified by their actual diagram arcs. The meridian is the inverse
of the clockwise oval generator; the longitude is the boundary of
its twice-punctured disk. The cap representation and the full labelled
leaf matrices then give exactly the two source critical equations.
The complete cusp polynomial selects the geometric representation,
and the local gluing theorem identifies the whole deformation germ.

For the literal closure by \(R^c\), with \(c\) a sufficiently large
fixed odd signed integer, the scalar source therefore has a nonzero
\(N^{3/2}\) leading term and its action is the volume of the resulting
hyperbolic knot complement. This proves the original Kashaev volume
identity through all integer levels for this infinite mixed family,
and for its mirror. The original primitive filling coefficient is
\(p=(1-c)/2\); no change of framing or longitude is suppressed.
An [independent exact replay](../repro/results/research-mixed-word-collar-representation-root.json)
checks the diagram endpoints and the rational matrix and cusp identities.

For attachment inside larger trees, the
[pure-carrier proof](research_mixed_pure_carrier_geometry.md)
constructs the actual three-cusped complement with its original
marked periods \(U_0=-2\pi S'(u)\), \(V=2iu\). Its complete positive
subdivision has the same volume as the odd-carrier complement.
The [relative disk argument](research_marked_pants_seam_isotopy.md)
then identifies the original embedded twice-punctured disk with
the geometric attaching surface, preserving its ordered boundary
curves. This uses a specified relative isotopy theorem, rather than
inferring an embedded surface from its boundary traces.

The [hybrid tree extension](research_hybrid_trees_with_mixed_pendant_seeds.md)
therefore permits arbitrarily many mixed blocks and their mirrors
as pendant pieces, together with all terminal powers of magnitude
at least two. One pair of thresholds works independently of the
number of pieces and the tree depth: each remaining vertex must
have sufficiently many children or a sufficiently large absolute
power. Each mixed piece has one free boundary and counts as one
child. The theorem does not use it as an internal two-boundary
kernel and does not allow arbitrary short powers at the other
low-degree vertices.

The representation argument also has a general statement for any
rational word with its four boundary labels retained, once its
complete base representation is established to be geometric.
This general lemma does not prove a nonzero asymptotic or select an
integration cycle. Those analytic requirements remain separate for
other short words.

## One turn with a threshold uniform over all terminal powers

The [uniform large-power turn theorem](research_uniform_large_power_turn.md)
treats an infinite family without a separate contour certificate
for each member. There is a finite \(B_*\) such that the original
boundary polynomial

\[
                    T(R^bT(R^a))
\]

has a nonzero holomorphic leading asymptotic, whole-period angular
decay, and a fixed complex-strip estimate whenever
\(|a|\ge2\) and \(|b|\ge B_*\). The threshold and domains are
independent of \(a\), and the two signs are unrestricted. Both
powers remain fixed before the integer quantum level tends to
infinity. The starting level and polynomial prefactors may depend
on the two powers.

The proof applies more generally to any input family with common
holomorphic phase bounds and full boundary estimates. It retains
the endpoint current in the exact trace formula. A contraction
locates the selected critical point at distance \(O(|b|^{-1})\)
from zero, with depth and action loss \(O(b^{-2})\); the original
tails retain a fixed larger gap. The amplitude is explicitly
nonzero. Control of the imaginary quadratic part is essential:
a previously inserted crossing of power \(-b\) could otherwise
cancel the new crossing exactly.

The [marked geometric corollary](research_large_power_turn_marked_geometry.md)
also applies after one common enlargement of \(B_*\). The uniform
terminal geometric chart and the one-child gluing theorem identify
the selected phase with the original partially filled complement.
Its meridian and disk longitude are retained, and the cone path
fixes the absolute volume constant. Thus the boundary evaluation
has the volume of that complement as its limiting rate.

In a larger ordered circle tree, this gives a volume-conjecture
theorem for finitely many disjoint pendant paths with original
degrees one and two, powers \(|a|\ge2\), \(|b|\ge B_*\), and
independently sufficiently long powers on the remaining circles.
The selected paths may share an outside circle; its carrier is
inserted once. The threshold for the remaining fillings may
depend on the fixed template and selected powers. The original
parity and strand tracing must give a knot.

This theorem alone does not justify uniform iteration along chains.
Its proof may reduce the complex neighborhood at each application.
A stronger estimate now resolves this particular loss, as follows.
Neither result settles the infinite families where \(b\) stays
small and \(a\) grows.

## Arbitrarily many long turns with one threshold

The [fixed-domain turn theorem](research_fixed_domain_long_power_turns.md)
proves that one finite threshold works at every step of an arbitrarily
long fixed chain. Start with \(F_{0,N}=T(R^a)\), \(|a|\ge2\), and
form

\[
 F_{\ell,N}=T(R^{b_\ell}F_{\ell-1,N}),\qquad
                           1\le\ell\le k.
\]

There is a single \(B_*\), independent of \(k\), \(a\), and
the choices of signs, such that \(|b_\ell|\ge B_*\) at every
step gives the full nonzero boundary asymptotic on one fixed
complex disk. The phase bounds, curvature bound, and whole-period
angular loss are also common. The relative error constants and
starting quantum levels may depend on the entire fixed word.
Every power and the chain length are fixed before \(N\to\infty\).

The new ingredient compares the complete edge kernel at a real
integration angle \(t\) and complex outside angle \(u\) with
its phase \(\psi(0,u)\) at that same outside angle. It proves

\[
 |K_N(t,u)|\le CN^d
       \exp N\{\Re\psi(0,u)-\gamma_e(1-\cos t)\}.
\]

The first derivative needed by the original trace satisfies the
corresponding bound. Consequently the outer trace terms retain a
gap without shrinking the outside disk. A second estimate restores
the angular loss for the full central kernel. The envelope identity
and an explicit Schur complement give the same phase and curvature
bounds after every turn. This makes the induction independent of
the number of steps.

The original one-child geometric composition also iterates on this
disk: each new cone path stays strictly inside the previous piece's
positive chart. Its older primitive slopes remain fixed, and the
new carrier and remaining longitude have their original meanings.
This proves the marked boundary interpretation for these chains.

There is also a common threshold for the final scalar closing
trace. Enlarging \(B_*\) once to include it gives a knot theorem:
for every fixed admissible original circle-tree path, an initial
terminal power \(|a|\ge2\) and all subsequent powers, including
the final closing power, of magnitude at least \(B_*\) satisfy

\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|\langle K\rangle_N|
                       =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K).
\]

The threshold is independent of path length, the initial power,
and all subsequent signs and relative magnitudes. The original
half-twist pattern and strand tracing must give one knot and no
internal closed component. The full source has a nonzero
\(N^{3/2}\) leading coefficient through both level parities.
Section 7 of the fixed-domain theorem proves the last trace with
its original normalization and primitive closing slope.

Short turns are still excluded. The theorem does not turn the
density-one result for arbitrary fixed templates into a cofinite
statement: a single small internal power can still occur in
infinitely many untreated assignments.

## Long powers and large branching in the same tree

The [combined tree theorem](research_hybrid_tree_filling_closure.md)
chooses finite constants \(M,B\) before choosing a tree. Every
nonroot terminal has a fixed power of magnitude at least two.
At each other vertex, including the root, either its number of
children is at least \(M\), or its power has magnitude at least
\(B\). Under the original framing and knot-component conditions,
the resulting knot satisfies Kashaev's volume identity. One pair
of constants works for every fixed finite size, depth, ordering,
and branching pattern.

The proof first fixes the common phase and boundary estimates.
Large branching then determines \(M\). At vertices with fewer
than \(M\) children, the sum of their phase derivatives has a
common bound depending on this already fixed \(M\); that bound
determines \(B\). After either operation the outgoing phase
returns to the original common estimates. The sum of the child
bounds therefore does not accumulate with depth. The raw products
retain their larger polynomial degree until the original trace
is taken, so no derivative at a repeated root is lost.

This is a volume theorem for arbitrary finite circle trees with
the displayed restrictions. It leaves infinitely many assignments
where a vertex with few children has a short power.

## Repeated short turns separated by long fillings

The [finite collection of two-boundary pieces](research_finite_two_boundary_kernel_closure.md)
provides a different extension. In addition to the bare edge
\(K_N(s,u)\), use the complete two-boundary polynomial

\[
 P_{b,N}(s,u)=\phi_N^{(t)}
       [R^bK_N(t,s)K_N(t,u)],\qquad b=2,-2.
\]

These two short pieces already have their full asymptotic,
global boundary estimates, and original marked geometry. An
exact change in the order of the finite contractions gives

\[
 T(R^bT(R^nF))(u)
       =\phi_N^{(s)}[R^nF(s)P_{b,N}(s,u)].
\]

This identity retains all derivatives in the trace. It permits
the short middle vertex to be evaluated first. The next long
filling then takes place within that piece's proved small
boundary chart; no continuation of a local edge approximation
to the old short-filling contour is required.

The theorem applies to any finite collection of two-boundary
pieces with the stated full estimates. Its two centered bounds
follow from those hypotheses, and their constants are common to
the collection. Consequently one threshold works for an arbitrary
fixed sequence of the operations

\[
 F\longmapsto T(R^nF),\qquad
 F\longmapsto T(R^{2\sigma}T(R^nF)),
       \quad \sigma=\pm1,\quad |n|\ge B.
\]

The initial source may be any terminal \(T(R^a)\), \(|a|\ge2\).
A final long closing trace gives the original Kashaev volume
identity with its nonzero \(N^{3/2}\) leading coefficient. The
short turns may recur arbitrarily often, with either sign, but
are separated by long powers in this construction. The threshold
is independent of the fixed number of such insertions.

There is an additional seed obtained by taking \(F=1\): the
kernel itself supplies the necessary curvature and angular loss.
This proves the full boundary result for \(T(R^{2\sigma}T(R^a))\)
whenever \(|a|\) exceeds one common threshold. It does not allow
an arbitrary short turn immediately after an arbitrary short
initial terminal.

The geometric proof keeps the middle primitive filling of
\(P_{2\sigma}\) fixed while filling its input circle. Each new
carrier is inserted once, the outside longitude stays primitive,
and the cone path gives the absolute volume normalization. Thus
the repeated short-turn result includes the actual knot invariant
and complement volume, rather than only a formal phase identity.
It removes infinite families of short assignments but does not
treat arbitrary adjacent short clusters.

## Long powers separated by arbitrary nonzero powers

The [reset theorem](research_alternating_long_and_nonzero_turns.md)
now gives a uniform statement without a prescribed finite set of
short powers. Start with any terminal \(F_0=T(R^a)\), \(|a|\ge2\).
There is one finite \(B\) such that every fixed word
\[
 F_j=T\bigl(R^{b_j}T(R^{n_j}F_{j-1})\bigr),
 \qquad b_j\ne0,\quad |n_j|\ge B,
\]
